reviews.comment: Dr. Anu is a kind and courteous professor. We read three novels, multiple articles and other pieces, and watched two films. Most of class is discussion based, whether it be whole class or small group. A couple writing assignments, but she is not a very hard grader on those. Her personality shines through every day.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment:
Dr. Anu is really passionate about the material being taught to students. She also makes the class genuinely fun and engaging, while also clearly conveying key concepts to students. For classwork, there is a bit of writing to do, especially with the final project, but as long as you actually put in effort, it's more than manageable.

10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr. Anu is a lovable professor who genuinely cares about her students. She gives thoughtful feedback on every assignment, and also sets up students for success outside of the classroom. As long as every assignment is completed, students should receive an A. Dr. Anu is by far the best professor I've had at my time at UW, we are lucky to have her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: She has a very unique teaching style I've never experienced before that took a while to get used to, but holding on was worth it. She encourages collegiality a lot and group discussions are a big part of the class which was fun. I did have to purchase her book and write a review on it for my final though, which felt a little strange to do.
Manageable reading, a little more than average writing, and wonderful and personable discussions. Focus on group work and working with peers.
Participation is important for this class. This class requires some readings. Lectures are engaging, & are most of the content.

Professor Taranath is warm and friendly. Essentially if you show up to class and respond to her/your classmates, you will do well. Had to read 3 books and a few other short readings. No book reports, just discussion posts on canvas and in-class journalling and discussion. Her lecture style is very engaging and she clearly cares about her students.

She cares for students and wants you to pass, communicate clearly if you have any needs, and she'll help make a plan. Lots of readings, which can be difficult but questions are vague and open to lots of accepted interpretations. Lots of class and group discussions/projects. Great lectures.

This is a seminar class so group discussion is simply just part of the class. There will be many opportunities throughout the quarter to work within groups. Dr. Anu herself is rather kind and personable, I personally didnt have issues communicating problems with her.

I had the privilege to have Anu as a professor on my study abroad program and she is easily one of the best professors I have ever had at UW. I had yet to meet a professor who cares about her students as much as Anu does and she creates a safe space in her classes to allow for personal reflection about difficult topics. Could not recommend more!!!

Dr. Anu is experienced, knowledgable, and passionate about what she teaches. She wants to give every student a 4.0 if they all apply themselves. To her, English is subjective and there are almost no "wrong" answers. However, if you have a differing opinion, you don't really get a chance to voice it and she sometimes comes off as hypocritical.

I recommend anyone needing/wanting to take a diversity credit to go with Dr. Anu. Although her teaching style is unique, I personally enjoyed it, and felt it was a nice change in comparison to my other lecture/essay heavy classes. She is extremely bright and fosters some interesting discussions. My only issue was with the emphasis on group work.

Dr. Anu is one of the most amazing professors I've had the privilege of having so far at the university of Washington. She is kind, respectful and creates an amazing and safe environment to learn in. 100% recommend her and her class's. Her lectures are inspirational, deep, insightful, and leave you many times more knowledgeable than before.

Anu is great!! I learned about so many things that never even crossed my mind before. it also made me reflect on my life so much from being in her class so far this quarter. She is so understanding and sweet<3

I told her, "My learning needs are not being met." She disregarded this and basically told me to drop her class. She said multiple times, "This is a conversation you need to have with yourself, not me." This felt extremely dismissive and disrespectful. I felt like she did not care about me as a student. After I left the zoom, I cried... in public.
she'd make a great high school teacher since she has no idea what she's talking about or how to properly and respectfully speak to students in their mid-twenties :-)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Took this class as an elective as the course content looked interesting. Quickly found an absurd workload of 100+ pages a week plus 4 pages of reading responses weekly. More work than classes in my major. Teacher is very understanding and cares about students, workload is just excessive if taking as an elective or for fun. Overall 4/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: So much in-class discussion in this class. Really touchy-feely. Expects a lot of reading done for discussions, but graded on few assignments this quarter. Lots of group projects and talking about the hypothetical. She cares deeply about her students. Not a lot of practical application. This whole class was pretty much just processing trauma.

Dr. Anu is an amazing instructor. Very knowledgeable, approachable, and humble. Our class was mostly discussion based and student driven. Class content was based equally on readings and larger questions about community, equity, race, etc that are very relevant to our daily, real lives. Reasonable workload and very engaging class. Take her classes!
A true inspiration. Her lecture style is like no other person. Very humble, intelligent, and stretch stretch stretch your thinking!
She gets you to see outside the box. If you really absorb what she teaches you this class will change the way you look at the world.

I loved her class. I learned a lot from the readings and the classes were well paced for reflection/lectures. I think anyone who has a passion for people and literature would take away a lot from this course. This class was definitely inspiring and I can't see myself ever forgetting it.

I would take any class she taught again. Inspires you to be better as a person. Class materials were used and taught how to think outside the box. Being in class is incredibly important because her lectures are more of a conversation and discussion with class. Do yourself a favor and take her class whatever subject it is.

Dr Anu is an incredible teacher and knows how to get the best from her students. Our class was so interesting and she helped us learn about the literature, the countries, themes, and ourselves in only four books. If you have the chance, take her classes.

I've taken post colonial lit and the Bangalore  study abroad with Dr. Taranath and believe she is one of the most influential professors I've ever had. You learn and engage beyond readings and quizzes. She discusses race, sexuality, gender, disability, etc. in a valuable way. It makes some uncomfortable/defensive but she is kind in her approach. :)

Anu Taranath is a good teacher, but the substance itself of what she teaches is lacking. She preaches a form of moral relativism and throws around empty buzzwords such as patriarchy and white privilege. I would consider at least one of the books we read in this course to be propaganda: fallacious reasoning and twisted "facts."

Anu will challenge you to be a better human being.  The class forces you to re-examine your beliefs and to view the world through a whole different lens.  I've been to private school, public school, community college, and am currently a Junior at UW. This is the best class I've taken in my entire academic career. 10/10
Dr. Taranath is an incredible professor! I would gladly retake this class over and over again and I'm confident I would continue to prosper intellectually.

I took this class just for the credit it offered however, I feel so privileged and fortunate that I made the decision to take it. This was an amazing quarter for me and any class taught by Dr. Taranath is most worth it. You won't regret it! If I could continue taking classes with her or attend her lectures just for fun, I would in a heartbeat!

All of these ratings are correct, Anu is amazing. This is why I'm already registered for another course with her. She is passionate, fair, and an overall global world citizen. Take at least one class with her if you can!

When I read posts saying that Anu would "change your life" I was really curious...  I took her class to experience this miracle of a teacher myself.  She's LEGIT!  I learned so much from Anu.  I rated "1" for easiness because of the critical thinking involved, but as long as you give an honest effort, she's a really easy grader.  Take this class!
Take her class!

Amazing, passionate teacher! Anu forever changed my views of the world and how I see things. Her classes are amazing, and the literature that she teaches are outside the usual 'canon' and fascinating. Highly recommended. I learned so much from her.
This woman will change your life. Enough said.

Hands down best teacher I have ever had. Taking classes from lecturing professors will be impossible after one of Anu's classes. She cares about what she does and she cares about you. If you take her class you will do well and it will hurt in the best way. If you dont take her class, you are missing out on the biggest opportunity.
Values her students. Extremely helpful. Challenging material, but will definitely make you think and re-evaluate a lot of things!

I've took a very wide range of classes at UW, but I was never as intellectually challenged or inspired as much as I was by Prof. Taranath. I'd recommend everyone take a class from her, no matter the subject. She'll make you want to be a better world citizen.
Great teacher! I would have her again in a flash!

She absolutely the best teacher I've had. I've taken her 3 times. She's brilliant, articulate, and unrelentless in her standards for a socially just classroom, and world. She is an incredible woman, and I have the highest respect for such a gifted teacher. Prepare to un-learn. Take her class.

dr. taranath is absolutely brilliant and inspirational. she really cares about her students, encourages them to share their thoughts and makes each class highly relevant, engaging, challenging! definitely take her class!
AMAZING. mind-blowing class. you will leave a changed person.

Anu is a great teacher. She will put your perceptions and ideas to the test. Every day in class was a challenge that caused me to really stretch my capacity to analyze and criticize both the literature and the underlying assumptions that were brought to the table. Take a class from Anu if you really want to learn something!
awesome...with a dash of prejudice
Taranath taught an amazing class and gave us a great forum to share our ideas
No Comments
Very on the go feeling almost rushed vibe to lectures. She makes a lot of mistakes during lectures so pay attention. Very warm personality that may suit some better than others.
Do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: the textbook is so bad and the prof doesnt give all details during lectures so u are forced to read it
nice person but just could not teach at all like I learned genuinely nothing from lectures
Don't understand how this professor still has a job. don't take this class

If you care about your GPA and sanity, don't take her. Her lectures are disorganized, she teaches new material right before exams, and the homework has random curveballs. When most of us failed the first midterm, she blamed us instead of taking responsibility for being a terrible professor.

Her lectures were disorganized, explanations were vague, and she rarely clarified confusing concepts when students asked for help, SUPER disrespectful towards students asking questions. Doesn't prepare enough resource to help us succeed in our exams and blame our "study habits" when the Median was 15/40. Please don't take this class.
just don't.
Not very respectful and goes at a faster pace, although she shouldn't. Holds students to a higher comprehension level than they actually are at and blames them for it.

She does a basic intro of a topic but to really understand it for at least me I had to read the textbooks. Of the 50-minute lecture I'd say only 30 minutes is actually course related. I also had a problem with the course organization, but that might be a curriculum problem from UW instead of her.

She displayed a shocking lack of emotional maturity and professionalism in class. She exhibited childish behavior, including passive-aggressive remarks and a tendency to "rage quit" the lecture whenever things didn't go to plan. It was evident that when faced with criticism or any challenge to their approach, they would shut down completely.AVOID
Whats the point of studying if the content won't show up on the exam? Whats the point of taking the exam if none of the content was covered in the studies?

Exams are sadly nothing like practice exams, however, often reflect weekly written homework assignments. Lectures were directly from the textbook, and I often found myself understanding the material better when I taught myself. Office hours are very helpful for homework problems, and she'll directly check your work :)

Tough grader and not enough time on the exams. The review guide is not close to what the exam is going to look like. Lectures are pretty chaotic. Two-hour office hours once a week and no TAs available to help ever.

I would NOT take Heald! Her lectures were extremely disorganized. It was very clear that she knew the material, but when it came to class, I felt she was just reading from the textbook. She would often spend a whole class explaining topics that could be summed up in 5 minutes. She is an extremely harsh grader and gets very stingy on the test.
Better off just reading the textbook and watching Thomas Carr on Youtube to learn and understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are useless because they are regurgitations of the textbook. The exams make up more than 80 percent of your grade. The exams also had no study guide and were never provided, it also have questions meant to throw you off and destroy your score, also never enough time to finish comfortably. The syllabus is VERY dry. Worst class ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not the GOAT. tough to read the board even from the third row. Homework isn't bad but webwork is really bad, no WebAssign. Said she taught this course 10 times but felt like her first. Use Thomas Carr's Youtube lectures, the true Math 207/8 GOAT. Confusing and doesn't cover or explain topics well. Has good proofs and theorems to put on note sheet.

The GOAT. 
Her tests are not only fair but refreshingly straightforward, and her lectures? Absolutely unmatched. Andy doesn't just teach—she transforms the entire learning experience.
Honestly, Andy is the kind of teacher you'll talk about for years. If you get the chance to take her class, DO IT! It's not just a class—it's life-changing.

The material itself is manageable, but the course is disorganized. There's a lot of homework and almost no resources available. She answers questions but definitely judges you for them. Be prepared to learn everything on your own. She misses a lot of content in her lectures.

Avoid taking her class if possible! Her lecture notes are very unclear and I always have to Youtube the math concepts. The exams are very time consuming and account for 82% of the entire grade. Many of my friends and I struggled to finish her exams because the problems were so lengthy and tedious.

Lectures are 100% copy and paste of info in the textbook completely useless to attend. Exams and midterms don't have a guide, syllabus is so weak, no information about what to expect. Final exam felt like it tested your mental endurance instead of knowledge (lots of calculations in a short amount of time). anyone else will do brothas and sistas.
she is chuzz

I would never recommend Heald to anyone. She is so condescending when students ask questions. Always late to lecture and doesn't seem to care. In office hours, I saw another girl try to get help. When Heald did not answer the girl's question well and she tried to ask for clarification but Heald ignored her until there was no time left.

Some of these comments are very unjustified. Andy Heald is an excellent professor. Any time someone asks a question in lecture, she explains the concept comprehensively. Compared to the other profs, her exams are much lighter and easier. If you don't come to lecture, it will be difficult-so come! I would wholly recommend her to anyone taking 208.

The most frustrating professor I have ever had. She is condescending to student questions, terrible at teaching concepts, and forgets to teach concepts entirely to certain sections of the class ("Oh yeah, I forgot I only taught that to the 8:30 lecture"). 

Writing T(u)+T(v)=T(u+v) instead of T(u+v)=T(u)+T(v) does get you 10% off your midterm.

I made an account just to make a rating because some people gave some extremely unfair ratings.

Yes the exams are weighted very heavily. Yeah, its annoying. Whatever.

Every other complaint is ridiculous. These people think that anytime you see a question that was not exactly on the homework, it somehow covers "completely unrelated topics"....

Prof Heald is a decent math professor. Although I attend lecture, I often don't have any idea what is going on, so I watch Thomas Carr on YouTube. Exams aren't too difficult, but they are account for way too much of the grade. Midterm/Final = 82% of total grade. That said, these are a bit out of her control and rather at fault of the department
She is not a good teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a really awful professor with teaching in mass. she never provided any class material and previous exam archive. real exam is much harder than the  practice exam she provided. she likes to write her class on a awful yellow paper which makes people hard to catch up, the percentage of the exams is 84%, while tons of homework only worse 16%..

Their lectures are all over the place. They fully expect you to write proofs on exams in class without giving you the proper toolkit. Office hours are a mess and flooded due to the limited availability of the professor and course staff. Highly don't recommend this professor if you want to get a solid foundation in linear algebra.

Grading criteria for exams are incredibly unreasonable and strict. You can get points off even though you wrote down the correct answer. Some content on the exams was never covered in the lectures. Clearly a tough grader and her lectures are extremely disorganized. DON'T TAKE HER CLASS!!!!!!

Our class average for the first two midterms were roughly 60-70%, and 82% of your grade comes from exams (including the final). Professor is a nice person, easy to make conversation with, except her lecture recordings are a bit hard to see since she writes on a yellow legal pad. Her lectures are straight from the textbook--watch 3b1b, very helpful.

Worst professor I've had, hates technology for some reason so there are no notes or any resources posted. Randomly changes the examples she's writing on the whiteboard halfway through class and exams have content that we never covered. Avoid taking 208 with her at all costs!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The grading criteria for the exams are insane. Also, exams are very tight on time
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great, hilarious and very friendly professor that makes lectures enjoyable. Lectures were not recorded so you have to make sure that you can attend the lectures.
She holds zeal but course is disorganized. The homework grader is very strict and the test review is completely irrelevant with the test.

Andy is a really great person but as a math lecturer, she isn't great. Expect to learn and flesh out a lot of concepts on your own, especially when doing Webassign. The class isn't that bad but her lack of preparing for lectures and midterms makes it more difficult to succeed in.

She's a nice person, but not a great lecturer. Her lectures are pretty disorganized, and doesn't release lecture notes. However, she follows the textbook closely, so it's simple to keep up by just reading it. Most people stopped attending lectures by the end of the quarter, and just read the textbook to learn the material. HWs aren't too bad.

This professor was late to almost every lecture. When they did show up, they weren't very prepared and used most of the class period to teach things unrelated to the course just because they think it's fun.The homework was sooo difficult for no reason and there was a lot of it. The TAs weren't on track with the lectures, so quiz sections sucked.

Often arrived late to class and the lectures were disorganized. She knows her stuff reasonably well and office hours were somewhat helpful. Be prepared to spend a lot of time outside of class learning to make up for poor quality of lectures, but its doable to do well.

Heald appears to be a very nice person. However, she was consistently late to our lecture and very unprepared. She would often get halfway through an example, then erase the whole thing, wasting 10 mins of a 50 min class. Also, it was pretty clear she did NOT want to be teaching this course, and her lack of caring showed in her lectures.
Amazing professor and person. Would definitely take again! Thanks for a wonderful first quarter, Andy!

Professor Heald is nice but not a good lecturer. She's almost always late. Her lectures are disorganized and rushed. She frequently gives incorrect examples, then either rushes a new one or just moves on. She also always runs out of time. Many of us started attending a different professor's lecture in order to understand the material.

Professor Heald's nice but not the best. Always late, notes unprepared, and her examples are off. She makes up problems, realizes they don't work, erases and starts over, wasting time. Office hours are messy and always late, too. Just not a smooth learning experience.

Doesn't give clear explanations or good examples. Also doesn't post lecture notes. Is unorganized when teaching the material. Always keeps teaching after the class period is over and is often late.  Also the final is 40% of our grade.

She seems like a very nice person, but her faults aren't worth it. She often comes to class late, and even when she is slightly early to her own lectures, they are rushed and unorganized as she constantly messes up the examples to the point where we run out of time because we had to repeat them. Not a bad person, but needs improvement as a teacher.

Good late policy and generally nice, but became my most disliked professor. Would sometimes be late, skip steps in problems (mostly easy algebraic steps, but sometimes too many at a time), rush important ideas because of disorganization, un-tech savvy, and sometimes had rude or unforgiving tone to students having a hard time understanding material.

During lecture, they would go through a problem and realized they messed up somewhere. Lectures felt unprepared and a lot of the time, we would run out of time mid problem and then they'll move onto the next chapter the next day. Also skips a lot of steps in the problem and assume you understand whats going on
301 is definitely a difficult class w/ tons of proofs but prof.Heald is great. Her lectures were very clear and she cares about her students.
Professor Heald is enthusiastic about her teaching, and she cares about her students. Lectures are amazing and very clear, HWs are highly related to lectures w/ fair workload.

Her lectures tended to be disorganized and she went on tangents of things we didn't necessarily need to know for the midterms. She was very lenient about accepting late work which I appreciated. There was written homework on top of WebAssign which I had never had before. Exams weren't too difficult and pretty straightforward.

Andy was a pretty good instructor. I had her spring 2021 when things were online, and I surprised myself by getting a 4.0 in differential equations. She's pretty clear in her lectures and her exams were slightly harder versions of example problems from lecture. Take notes, ask questions, and memorize those Laplace Transforms and you'll be golden.
Run away!!! She is garbage.

Professor Heald is caring and enthusiastic about her teaching. She explained things well and was always available to answer questions. She was a little disorganized, though -- for example, she sometimes forgot to bring her laptop to class and lectures were often pretty rushed near the end.

First half of the class is a piece of cake before relations, after this topic there is a huge difficulty spike. Overall, she was a fine prof but towards the end I feel like me and most of the class were lost. Exams were fair, she made the first one too hard but was accommodating by offering extra credit. I feel like her lectures could better

Andy explains everything clearly in lectures and gives many examples, so I don't use the textbook at all. They are generous with extensions and late work and give feedback on work. They post optional practice problems every week and we do them in groups on Zoom. Tests are easy. Andy is really chill and friendly too. Nice, low-stress class.

Shes a super fun and chilled out professor who helps with homework and answers all your questions. Lecturee may not be the most organized or anything but all the material is still put across so I found it super helpful!

Took Heald for 308 AND 394, 394 online and 308 in person. Fairly easy grader and seems caring but otherwise very lazy at teaching. Most of the class is group work clearly because Heald can't be bothered to prepare anything else; "lectures" are done on the spot (early on in class Heald specifically said they had no time to make ppts!). Rating 2.5/5.

Has no structure to her lectures, offers practice problems then works through them on zoom while standing in front of her work. Doesn't explain why anything works and doesn't adequately explain the topics of the class. Get ready to go on khan academy to try and understand anything that is happening in the class.

horrible group work, horrible lecture, but trying really hard to get points of from short exams and final. Ask students to write T/F questions for short exams and grade on quality of question. We here to learn analysis not how to write good questions.

Not a great class, most of the actual "class time" was just doing group work, and she would consistently make mistakes and not really teach us anything. The actual lectures were done through videos made by another professor that were slow and boring. Plus, we had a huge focus on quiz grades, such that each question was essentially 10% of our grade

Consistently unprepared for class. Uses majority of class time for "Group Work" that does not benefit many learning styles. Likes to ignore questions, or give minimal answers. She stands in front of the board, so that note takers can't write down what is written, then erases what was written before anyone has a chance to note. Teaches the book.

Seemed not prepared to teach materials in class. Professor Heald wasted a portion of class time to figure out the calculations that were supposed to be prepared earlier. And she sometimes does not finish important explanations in class. Materials are not hard but takes a lot of your time to figure out things by yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Best math professor, scratch that, best professor I've had at UW. She really does love what she is teaching and it shows.
It was a great experience with her in Math324, a solid and passionate teacher who is able to clearly clarify most of the contents. Recommended!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Solid teacher in the Math department. She truely cares for her students and explains the concepts in class very clearly. Very helpful during office hours so definitely go if you are struggling. Homework is quite hard and so are the tests, but you do get a note sheet, which is nice.

Took math 300 with her and it was great. I considered dropping the class before the quarter even started because of her low ratings and Im very glad I didnt. She is enthusiastic, a great professor and it is easy to succeed in her class if you put in the work.

Super enthusiastic about math and great to have as a prof! It's clear what class expectations are and she's very understanding about students being busy - ask for an extension on a homework assignment and you'll probably get one. Lectures often work through a proof or two. The class is hard but she makes it as easy to succeed as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The teacher is nice and cares a lot about her students. However the final exam she wrote was extremely difficult.

Homeworks are tedious and long, but they are relatively easy and help you work through the math. Great in class at providing different viewpoints and easier ways to think of the complicated math. Very accessible outside of class, really wants her students to learn. Class is very difficult, but she makes it as easy as possible to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Homeworks are really hard and are intentionally desinged to make you think. Quizzes and midterm are relatively easy and straightforward. But final was painful. Do not underestimate this class even though it is about probability.

I'm honestly shocked by the other reviews. I really liked her! I thought her lectures were really clear and the exams/quizzes were very reasonable. The weekly quizzes were a bit stressful, but they seriously helped check my knowledge. They were also only worth 10% of the final grade and she gave lots of extra credit opportunities!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Pretty much just copied out of the text book and couldn't answer questions or give any more insight to undergrads. Always alluded to more advanced topics when trying to clarify and then got flustered. She is passionate about math but just not a good teacher. Worst upper level math teacher I've had
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Incredibly passionate about this subject which is good, but she basically just talks at you. There was no real learning because you're trying to keep up with everything she's saying. There are quizzes each week and she doesn't give enough time on them. She purposely makes the exams hard, and she's not very helpful. I would avoid her if possible

There isn't enough space to properly review the course here, but I'll try to hit on a few basic points:  Pros: *Positive attitude, clearly interested and wants to share knowledge Cons: *Few office hours (but standard for UW) *Lectures can be abstract and meandering, few applications *Use of WebAssign automatically docks pts from any review I give
Terrible Experience in 308 in every aspect. Bad teacher, rude, fairly hard tests when the course material itself wasn't that bad.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS EVER. Math 308 is known to be a very interesting class but it was such a big mistake taking it with her, she doesn't teach at all. first 10 mins she gives 2 theorems and tells us to do the worksheets in group, when ask questions, she rather asks rhetorical questions. Not worth it at all, please avoid taking her class.

Very boring lectures, all you get is the introduction of a theory, the proof of that theory, and few examples of the theory. So nothing you can't find in a textbook. Midterms weren't too bad and she graded easily.

She was nice and gave a bunch of examples for each new topic/theorem. Always responds to emails and is helpful in office hours. Midterm and final were fair. The material can be hard if you're new to modular arithmetic though..
One of the best professors I have had. he knows what he is talking about and explains things very well, would definitely recommend him over any other physics prof I have heard of.

Very kind and knowledgeable professor. He makes lectures easy to understand and has problems similar to exam questions that don't try to trick you. Paying attention in class and doing practice problems will help you succeed.

This is the best professor I have ever met. He is a really great lecturer that his office hours and his lectures really matters so much in learning this course. The class take participation points by pollEv so attending lectures really matters. There is a little bit of in-course discussion in this course. Love Professor al-Binni Forever.
very willing to answer questions in class, after class, and on EdStem. structure and tests were very fair
Very nice teacher. You can tell he's trying his best to help everyone understand the concepts

His lectures are very detailed and uses a lot of examples. Sometimes he demonstrates with experiments that are interesting. I blame the class itself for being difficult and a weed out class, but he's pretty good at explaining concepts out. If you don't do the readings (or just don't understand physics too well) you may struggle.

Kind lecturer. Always tries to answer as many questions as possible and help students understand. Sometimes struggles to get to the point and overexplains, which can get confusing, but he means well. He takes his time moving through the content. Keep pace, pay attention, and you will do fine. Tests were fair.

Physics is hard regardless, but Dr. al-Binni's lectures make it easy to understand. He is very helpful during office hours and will take the time to help with any questions without making you feel bad. Exams are hard, but going to office hours and doing practice exams is helpful.

Al-Binni was a really nice professor who was always willing to help students when they needed help. Always was in a positive mood and made learning a tough topic like physics feel a little less extreme. The exams were not easy but if you do the practice exams and know the content, you should do well in the class.

Al-Binni is a good teacher for the time he spends actually teaching. To my taste he gives too much lecture time waiting for students to answer online questions or do discussions (in which people often say nothing). This could be because I took his earliest class. He really shines when you ask follow up questions.
will do well if you do practice problems and read textbook

She very much cares about her students and their success, and is very accomodating, highly recommend.

This class was alright. Course content interesting and not a lot of assignments. However, I didn't love how this class was set up and taught. Ta's were very hard to reach and rarely responded to emails, if I could rate the Ta's on here I would probably give them a 1/5. Class is basically just a 300 person seminar, kind of felt like a waste of time.
I LOVE this professor. She is so passionate about what she talks about, and her lectures are always engaging with the other students in the lecture hall. She's a great person to talk to as well!
Great class, lectures are always interesting. Professor Frost is very laid back, and chill professor, Would take her class again :)

Lectures always cover interesting topics and are heavily discussion-based as the majority of class consists of her asking for students' opinions. Clearly has a lot of passion and experience which always makes class and projects engaging.

Super passionate, interesting, and caring prof. Also brought in great guest lecturers all the time. Even with a larger class size we spend most of the lectures in big discussion mode. Lots of reading and I was nervous about there being lots of complicated legal jargon, but Frost made it super comprehensive and I learned a lot.

Prof. Frost was awesome. Her lectures were fun, and she really tried to have us question our belief system. We had 5 speakers from different parts of the legal system, which was very cool. This was an eye-opening class that was very well structured. There are 2 papers, but both are simple and graded fairly. No exams, weekly reading reflections.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really easy class, attendance is not mandatory. I went to about 8 lectures this whole quarter. Feels like a high school class, but you definitely learn a lot about how society and media interact. There's one group project, but it's' extremely easy. Other than that, its pretty lightweight and 10/10!

This class was easily the best I've taken at UW. The slides are empty but that's because there's so much discussion in this class and it makes it all the better. Two papers in this class, but the second is just adding onto the first with more theories you've learned which makes it pretty simple. 100% recommend if you enjoy sociology/criminology.

I've also taken her SOC371 Criminology class last year. Her class is EXTREMELY easy. Lots of readings (you can just skim) and It'll be really boring if you're not interested in the topic(s). Besides that, she's the most thoughtful and accommodating professor I've met at UW, same for the TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lecture style/presentations can feel a bit unstructured, as she often talks naturally and jumps off of her students' responses/input. The topic is interesting, and her experience working in the justice system brings a knowledgable and interesting perspective. A lot of guest speakers which is helpful in changing it up and keeping us engaged.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Frost is the best, I have taken her for a few soc classes and I highly recommend. She has good lectures and slides, never has too hard of tests and is a really nice person. Her classes are interesting and fun, but not too much work. I took her classes 2020,2021 and it was all asynchronous lectures. Def take her class if you are considering.

Ann Frost is a great professor, makes her lectures concise and interesting, doesn't waste your time and is really organized which makes being successful in her online class easier. She is super caring and willing to work with students in order to make sure they understand her material. If you are considering a class w Ann Frost, definitely take it.

Ann Frost is one of the best professors I've had in my four years attending the UW. She is NOT a perfect professor, however she cares very much for her students and is very accommodating to students when issues come up. Those upset with Ann Frost I find, are students who don't understand different teaching styles. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Although the grading criteria for the exams can be a little harsh, I LOVED this class. Frost will completely change the way you think about the criminal justice system, but is still completely respectful of all ideas and assigns extremely interesting readings! It was easily one of my favorite classes at UW. Totally recommend.

Professor Frost was great! Its pretty easy to do well in the class if you attend lecture and do readings. Quizs were easy to prepare for with study guides. Fair grader. Super great to connect with outside of class - has lots of great advice and experience to share!!!

Very nice lady who clearly loves interacting with students. Make sure that you know all of the readings super well or you will not pass her exams. If you are not interested in reforming the criminal justice system, don't take this class. Has a couple guest lectures who really make the material she is teaching come to life.

I couldn't really tell you anything I learned in this class. Her lecture slides are unhelpful and the readings you do outside of class are so long and they are rarely talked about again. The tests are hard. The options are like a) this b) that c) those d) this and those e) this and that f) all the the above g) none of the above Super hard

The material of the class is so fascinating, but the way it was presented made me uninspired. Frost is nice, but her lectures were very disorganized and it took her a while to get it together. The grading scale is ridiculous and the test format changed 3 times. It felt like it was being taught for the first time ever.

This class was disorganized and unclear. Concepts we were supposed to know on tests were never clearly defined ahead of time and the formatting of tests changed every time abruptly through the quarter. The final prompt was written poorly and not clear in how it would be graded or on what the expectations were. Overall seemed disjointed.

I like her as a person, but as a teacher she was not good. Frost did not get organized until WEEK 6 of the quarter. The teaching style was all over the place, and there were a lot of miscommunications between frost, the TAs, and the class. The exam style was also changed 3x. Kind of disappointed because others had great things to say about her.

The material itself is straightforward and not that difficult. However, be prepared to answer questions on exams that test extreme details of the readings. The grading scale is also absurd, with 2 points out a hundred dropping exam score GPA by 0.1 (a 98+ is a 4.0, and a 90 is a 3.5)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honestly, she is one of the best professors at UW. Super down to earth and genuine. Her class is mostly discussion-based. And, different from most of the profs who also based their lectures on discussions, she takes answers from students SERIOUSLY and elaborate based on those answers, not just brushing over briefly and moving on.

I think she tried really hard to make the class interesting and engaging at the expense of giving us actual content some lectures. She doesn't post lecture slides so if you any of the small amount of information provided make sure you go to lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She was really nice. But the tests are written so specifically, that you need to write exactly what she wants. And the grading system was terrible. You need to attend lecture, other wise you'll miss out on weird details she'll test you on. Quiz section is mandatory and the only reason I passed. Really reading heavy too, you gotta do them to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Love Professor Frost's classes! I've taken three with her and want to take more. She's a great lecturer and has great exam formats, normally pick 14 out of 17 short answers. I definitely look for her classes every time I go to register!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: She is an amazing, knowledgeable professor.

Her slides have barely any content and are very sloppy. She wastes class time by rambling about examples instead of actually fully explaining concepts. Going to quiz section was only reason I learned anything concrete. This class is appealing to some because it has barely any workload, but lectures are extremely boring. Tests are straightforward.

It seemed like professor Frost did not care about the content she was teaching. She had very dry and boring lectures. The tests were pretty easy. Make sure you are very detailed in your short responses on the tests!!!

She does not record her lectures so you have to show up everyday. Also she doesn't like using the mic so you have to ask her to use it or else you won't be able to hear her. She gives out long readings but you can live without reading them because she goes over them in class. For tests you have to write definitions verbatim to her definitions.

SHE'S ABSOLUTELY AMAZING!!! This was my first time taking a class with her and she had a "mom" vibe - caring and funny while giving some good lectures! She's very personable and friendly, encouraging students to send in requests for songs even. The tests were pretty easy and you MUST SHOW for lectures or else you'll struggle!

This class is impossible to get a good score on. This was my first time taking a class with her and if you are not a veteran student for her, she will give you horrible grades. Unless you know her style and how the tests are, the quarter will be torture!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's a super friendly person, and pretty funny; but she goes off on so many tangents it takes up most of the class time. The problem is, the exams come DIRECTLY off the slides - I'm talking word for word. You'll get points off on the exam for getting the answer right, but not answering in verbatim what it said on the slides, which is ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I love this woman. She is HILARIOUS and also so helpful if you want to object a grade or try to understand class concepts more. She has advised me on several independent study projects and written me a letter of rec. I am eternally grateful to this woman for he passion and inspirational personality. She grades medium-hard but tests are a breeze.

Great lectures! Super clear and easy to understand. Frost is so easy-going and will tell you how it is while staying true to the facts. Not very many assignments, relevant content, and overall pretty interesting. I recommend.
This was my favorite class. Professor Frost is extremely kind and cares about her students. We just had one short two-page paper, midterm, and final. If you study her slides, you will get an A.
Very knowledgeable and helpful instructor. She is very well versed in her field. Also, a helpful and approachable professor

Ann is a sweetheart of an instructor. If you are considering her summer 14 seminar on wrongful convictions you should sign up. You will be graded on contribution to discussions, 2 small reading presentations, and 3 papers (3-5, 3-5, 6-8 pg). She's very knowledgeable about the subject & it seemed like every class I had something to look forward to.
AWESOME professor- easy class. 2 classes a week, reading discussion based. LOTS of assigned reading, can be repetitive, but reviewed over extensively during class discussion.
Amazing TA! Hands down one of the best in the poli-sci department. Have had her for two quarters and she is stellar!

Hands down the best TA from the Political Science Department. I like her teaching style: she gets straight to the point. I wish every professor at UW had the same teaching style like hers. I strongly recommend having Ann as your TA. She's amazing.

Ann is so incredibly nice. I have never had a more knowledgeable, kind, and helpful TA. I have had her for two different classes now and I learned a lot from her. If you have the option to be in her section, I absolutely recommend her!

Doesn't accommodate for anything, including the studio class most of us were taking. Most of what I learned was from the textbook. Most effort in this class was put into the note sheet for the exam because we were expected to write about details she barely covered in lecture (made it very hard to actually learn anything)

This is for class ARCH 351. Scary bad teaching style, I understand she is filling in for another teacher on sabbatical but it's astounding how little she can say on a building. The words symmetrical, solid, and masonry were the extent of vocabulary. Literally baddd tests, longest note card ever and it still won't help. So rude too.
Bad bad bad save yourself
Not a good professor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ann is so sweet and such a wonderful teacher! She cares so much about her students and wants to see everyone succeed. She gives excellent feedback and despite pushing her students to be the best they can, her expectations are not unreasonable like they often can be with architecture professors.
Tough quizzes. Long lectures

Very boring professor and the lectures are long and dragged out. The questions in the quizzes were very subjective and specific to what is on her mind not what's on the lecture. The lecture slides are only pictures so you have to write down pretty much everything she says. Class would be much better if she wasn't teaching it or writing the quizzes.
NOT EASY A FOR THIS CLASS!!!!!HARD TEST!!!!!BORING CLASS !!!!!QUIZ DIDN'T REALLY CONNECT TO HER CLASS, YOU HAVE TO READ THE BOOK. WASTING OF TIME FOR A 3 CREDIT CLASS.
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FOR A GPA BOOST. HER TESTS ARE HARD AND SHE IS THE WORST TEACHER
Terrible lecturer! She really struggles to keep her audience awake. Hopefully she will know about it one day. ONCE AGAIN, DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU WANT EASY 3.0 AND ABOVE. :)

She probably knows that her class is not attractive at all, so she just makes the quizes entirely  on the lectures, means you cannot find useful information in any other ways, even on her own lecture slides and the textbook. She's just trying to force everyone  going to her class to listen to her 2 hours' nonsense.

If you are taking this class for a GPA boost, look elsewhere! The lectures are fast-paced, off topic, and confusing, and the tests are even worse!  The questions are vague and opinion based. She posts her lecture slides, but they have no information on them, only pictures, making it difficult to study.  Don't waste money on the book.
It's almost like she wants to prove people this class is not supposed to be easy by making super ambiguous tests. Do not take it.

Definitely dropping this class. Very boring to listen to. Quizzes are ambiguous. She expects you to understand and remember small details that she very quickly mentions in lecture. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU WANT EASY CREDITS.

The class is pretty boring. She doesn't have much caption on lecture slides, so when you want to go back and study the slides, you may not know what they were about. She has 17 questions on each quiz, so if you miss some then you won't be able to get a good grade. The less questions on the quiz, the more difficult they are.

Those looking to take this class for easy VLPA and GPA. Don't. A 95% is a 4.0 and wading through her ambiguous quizzes and lectures can only get you so far. This class is not a lot of work, merely an exercise in trying to interpret her often contradictory words. If you look in between the lines, this class is about Architecture, sparingly.

This teacher goes through some of the slides extremely fast & expects you to know it for the quiz.Her quizzes aren't reflective of her lectures & are general w/ multiple correct answers (gl guessing). She expects you to read her mind haha.I don't recommend this class for a 3 credit class, it isn't a GPA booster, boring & is extremely time consuming

I took take this class for 3 credit elective and thought how hard can it be. However it was one major mistake. Her lectures are boring and her quiz are super duper hard. You will have to read & pay extra attention to details because she will ask you most unexpected questions possible. I don't recommend taking this class if you want a GPA boosters.

Clearly knowledgable about architecture, and really nice, but lectures are dry, boring, and often rushed with no review of past concepts or their relevance moving forward. Online quizzes are infuriating and almost never align with lecture material...a really bad way to gage student's learning and knowledge. There are better architecture courses.
WORST TEACHER I HAVE EVER MET IN UW! The quiz totally based on her own opinions. NEVER EVER TAKE THIS CLASS if you really want to learn something and get a high GPA.

She's one of the worst lecturers I've ever encountered. Constantly forgets what she's talking about or some real important points in the slides (mostly no words just pics) because she wouldn't put notes on the slides. Her quiz has little/nothing to do with the lectures or the book. She thinks she's covered it all but erhhhh...

In architecture class and decide to look up my teachers rating (7 weeks into the quarter), Ann Borys. And wow!... All the coomments are spot on! Borys lectures off of slides, giving information which is 30% useful for tests and 70% useful for not this class. So many side topics! unbelievable. Not that hard of a class if you study with friends *hint

If I had a choice between attending wsu and attending her class I would pick wsu because at least I'll learn something there. Quizzes are based on opinions, the teacher is so boring that you will cry yourself with tears of blood, but even a hospital will not save you from the endless torture of attending the class and listening to her just to pass.

Take it with another professor. She assigns way too much work for a 3 credit class and she isn't an easy grader. Every class was torturous. She reads off of her computer as she lectures like she hasn't taught the class before and hasn't prepared. Seriously, take it with someone else.

Not a great professor. Her lectures are filled with random tangents and the slides she uses are often dark and unclear. The quizzes are based off of her opinion and answers are not readily available in the book.
She makes the lecture boring. It is not too hard class, but needs group of friends to understand the materials better.
The class overall was very interesting for me, but listening to her talk was quite draining.

classes are a bore. she breezes through slides without mentioning much but then puts it on the study guide to know for quizzes. She WILL test you on things she says in passing and often times two choices seems likely.  Make sure to read ur notes carefully and be able to compare different buildings and you should get a good score.

Class was horrible. Tests are based on things she mentioned in a passing fancy, or worse, on things that she NEVER even mentioned during class. And she sighs too many times to count when she talks. Does not lecture well at all

most assignments involve coding, which i had no experience with prior, but i didn't have a ton of trouble getting them done. the professor is very entertaining and throws in random jokes in lectures and assignments which makes the class more fun
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I actually have no clue why she is rated so low. She is very witty and easy to understand and gives plenty of resources to understand assignments(there were no exams), and all the grading criteria were very fair. She is actually also so funny too. Deserves a better score on here imo. Learning Rstudio isn't hard if you just lock in for like 3 hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I really liked the way Anne taught this class. They kept a lot of the information up to date and relevant. And struck a nice balance with incorporating their opinions into the course (because ethics) but not in an overwhelming way. The workload was also very manageable and realistic, and they are a very understanding and generous professor.

Dr. Wagner was hard to understand with her thick German accent. She also goes on rants about how the earth is flat using advanced statistical methods, which although illustrative of the problem, seems fake.

Took the online, j take the in-person class with someone else. 98% is an A, their lecture videos are long, there's like 4-5 videos per assignment to watch (but the code never aligns with the assignment, you have to j figure it out), and there's "hidden questions" so even if the autograder gives full points, you lose points in the actual grade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Actively in this class, but wanted to review! I'm not a stats person and I suck at coding, but I've had no issues in this class. 5-6 video lectures per week is a lot, but they cover interesting content + the homework is straightforward if you go through the content. I enjoy her jokes/comments in lectures and if you reach out to her she's so sweet!

Anne is the best professor ever and I highly recommend her. On an unrelated note, did you know just anyone could leave a review on RMP? Even the professor themselves! How silly, but as said, not related to this otherwise glowing recommendation.

Her lectures are long and don't always cover how to EFFECTIVELY translate that info over to R. She's kind and is helpful 1 on 1 but there're too many students to be able to always get that experience in OH. Her content isn't as cohesive and her discussion assignments are also unclear with exactly what they want making you lose points. Class is mid.
what a nice teacher

The lectures are awful but the class isn't that difficult. Lectures always turn into random rambling and she somehow finds a way to talk about her political views in everything she tries to teach. I eventually stopped watching the lectures and learned the material online instead.

I had some issues with my homework, but I contacted Anne and was able to resolve it right away!
A lot of people are saying her class is confusing/unorganized, but I doubt they reached out for assistance. Watch the lectures, do the homework, and you should do fine. The low rating for Anne is not justified.

Honestly, I'm glad this class is over. There's an autograder that just sucks at grading homework, and most of the content did not even make sense. Somehow the lectures made that worse. Also, the write-up assignments are very unclear and disorganized. 
I had to take this course for a credit; if you don't have to, then save yourself the trouble.

There's a huge disconnect between lectures and assignments. The professor overcomplicates concepts and I was really confused 90% of the time. I'm having a bad time and I need to understand the content in this class because I am a stats major and this is supposed to be foundational stats.

lectures were not as helpful as it should be, had lots of unrelated stuff. my grade was only saved by my wonderful TA, he would walk through my wrong answers then updated my grade to be better which encouraged students to go to office hours to learn from their mistakes. worst 8 am ever. tests every 2 weeks in QS and the final is in lecture hall.
stupid class. canvas so disorganized and the assignment instructions make no sense.

Very nice, but lectures are long winded, rambling, unedited, and unclear in lecture. Lectures do not cover what you need for assignments and often there feels like there's a big disconnect between the lectures than work. Not a super difficult class, but definitely not made any easier by Anne

Ok professor. Lecture videos are long, and the prof isn't very helpful on Ed discussions. The TA Office Hours were much more helpful and I used it to basically learn all the class material. Agreeing with another review -- there is a large disconnect between the lectures and the assignments, which made homework much harder than it needed to be.

Content is ok, lectures are overly long for what the content is and somehow doesn't fully cover how to do hw problems.  The autograder is useful for feedback but super problematic to be honest just based on how confusing it is.  Luckily the course load isn't bad and async is nice.  Could work on making lecture content more translational to R.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Highly recommend taking this asynchronously. Anne was engaging in her lecture videos and kept really clear communication with her office hours. Check EdDiscussion often, and it helps to have a bit of basic knowledge on RStudio before beginning. More coding than you think, but a great class to get your stats requirement out of the way.

She's nice enough and the content is not too hard. Her lectures are incredibly long though, and I feel she could make them shorter. Its now week 7 and I still haven't had a single grade entered in Gradescope or canvas so my grades are a mystery.
Anne if you see this please grade my assignments

Really enjoyed this class! Prof Wagner is super nice and helpful, also has a cute cat who makes a lot of appearances. Honestly, textbook is also super helpful but she does a lot of examples in class which is nice. 10/10 would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lectures are very slow and mostly skippable, definitely do all the assignments because even missing a couple can really tank your grade.
Lectures are prerecorded, usually a few years old, with questionable quality. However, the course as a whole is pretting interesting and focuses on modern topics of AI.
Very chill class--just a lot of weekly homework, but nothing terribly difficult. He is very sweet, but be prepared for the instructions of every single assignment to make 0 sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: literally so much busy work. a 500 word essay every week and 5 discussion posts. the most disorganized class i've ever taken. course materials are scattered throughout canvas and never in one central place. DO NOT take this class.

SOC 225 Data and Society, great course for any major programs with data science option requiring ethics component, makes broad connections, prompts own independent critical thinking. Course makes Sociology basically human-centered applied statistics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: SOC331 is probably the worst class I have ever taken. The lectures were just so boring. The assignments literally never made any sense and I don't understand what we were even doing with google sheets. I went to ask for help once and he had horrible breath and I never talked to him again. The whole class was incredibly awkward, especially the final
GOATTTTTTTTTTT
Insane amount of work! Hundreds of pages to read every week, 5 discussion posts, and more. Worse work load ever, especially for a 3 credit class. Would not recommend.

I took the 3-credit option with no lab, and there was so much work given each week that it should have been 5 credits. The content was interesting and none of it was hard, but it was time-consuming and a lot of busy work. I would take another online class for an easier time unless you need this to fulfill a specific requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: WAY TO MUCH WORK for the 3 credit option! Plan to spend the whole day working on the class or at least one hour a day. Consists of long lectures, 5 discussion posts, and 2 replies for each discussion + a reading response that consists of 5+ long readings every week. On top of that, there are 3 memos Basically a 5 credit class with no lab. No exams.
(I took the 3 credit version w/out lab) layout of the class is very straightforward, grading is simple. I only had to think about the class maybe an hour every week

Hard to understand and goes on tangents easily. So far my least favorite professor but I also don't like chemistry. Hard to follow and you need to self teach a lot, he doesn't teach what you need to practice on ALEKS. Nice guy but not the best teacher.

He is very excited and knowledgeable but he is not good at conveying information in lectures and goes off on lots of little tangents that don't contribute to the class. I ended up not attending class after the first midterm and instead watched the recorded lectures so I could skip or focus on specific parts, and that improved my next midterm score.

Not the best teacher, but Bo Zhang makes Chem 152 very survivable. Straightforward tests if you pay attention in lecture and do your quiz section packets. Lectures are pretty dull and hard to follow, but not impossible.

had fun taking his class. he specializes in electrochemistry, so there was a lot of focus given to that unit. the lecture slides are really wordy and i found them difficult to understand sometimes. the quiz sections were really helpful, and the exams were very similar to the questions on the quiz section practice packets. really good class overall.

I hesitated to take Bo Zhang's class because of the negative reviews, but I'm glad I did. All of his tests align with his PowerPoints, worksheets, and practice problems, and you can honestly just learn from his recordings. His tests are super straightforward, and he actively encourages students to ask him questions and form relationships with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bo Zhang is a nice person, but is not the best when it comes to teaching content. His lectures are too wordy, with little to no explanation on the concepts. His lectures contain all the important equations, but doesn't explain coherently the fundamental concepts on using them. I would not recommend him for 152.

It's pretty tough to sit through his lectures. His expectations of your work is through the roof. The tests were blindsiding and nothing like the practice exams. Read the book for exams and homework. The average is set pretty high, which is awesome.

Not the best professor. Lectures were confusing and quick. The examples were not great. It was easy to tell he cared more about his research than his teaching, as he missed two lectures for his research.  In the end, this class helped me to lose all interest I had in Chemistry.  Tests were impossible to study for.

Zhang is a really nice guy. Unfortunately, this is just one of those classes where you have to spend TONS of time teaching yourself material in order to do well. Sure, you can go to class, but making sure you have the book /workbook is crucial, as well as no social life so you have plenty of time to study! Yay!

Nice guy. I attended the lectures for the first half of the class. After the first midterm, I ended up skipping lectures because everything he discusses are in his lecture notes, which are online, and in the book. I ended up with a 3.7 because of self-studying. His tests had one random question, so be prepared. Overall, ok prof.

He is a really nice guy who cares about his students. His accent is difficult to understand but his notes make up for it. I did terrible in 142 but much better in 152. As long as you study his quiz questions and lecture notes you'll do fine.

He does have an accent which can throw people off and he also isn't super clear at conveying ideas from his slides. But, his notes are on point as it is all taken from the book. All I can say is read his notes, read the book and study all the practices problems from quiz sections. Do that, and you'll get above average on all exams no problem.

Horrible at teaching. He cannot connect ideas together in a coherent manner despite being really good at the subject himself. hes one of the those guys who gets it but cant convey that understnading to others. ala a teacher. A sweet man though who has good intentions.
i had a horrible prof in chem 142 but turns out 152 is ok with prof zhang. his exam is easy if you study the quizs and take notes in lecture. choose Chelsea Hess as TA and you won't regret this.

Straight up worst teacher i have ever had. His english is poor, but thats not why he is unclear. He just spends way too much time on theory and does way too few example problems. There is 0 reason to go to lecture, if anything it makes things more confusing. I would suggest using the time you should be in class to go over his lecture powerpoints.

A very mediocre professor. He seems to be really intelligent and knowledgeable, but when it comes to actually teaching, he lacks clarity, and his classes are really boring. You can get a good grade without attending lectures. His tests can be really hard or super easy. Very unhelpful. His homeworks are straight from the text book.
Not that great at conveying what we needed to know. Often times I mistook extra time on a slide as an emphasis...but it wasn't. Nice guy though.

Bo is a great teacher. I did horrible in 142, and heard 152 was even harder. He sucks at talking, but so what. He makes his points clear, and has almost no tricks on his tests. His midterms and final were far easier than the other 152 section. Take prof. zhang, you will not regret it.

He's nice and easy. His tests are exactly same as his examples in his slides and practice tests. Slides are useful, but his explanation confuses u, so i recommend not to go to the class but read slides for sure.
His tests are very straightforward. he is so beautiful

Very relatable.He is very nice though never actually spoke to him. His tests are very similar to his reviews he puts out and they aren't hard if you study topics on the review and pay attention during lecture. Many aren't too respectable which appalled me, he tries his best so just listen and learn and you'll do fine

This class is slightly difficult because Prof. Zhang has an accent. He is, however, quite knowledgeable, and his demeanor is pleasant. There has been a couple of incidents where he has not controlled the class completely, but those are not too noticeable. His tests are much easier than the homework. Practice midterms mirror the actual ones nicely.

He is a really sweet Asian man. It is difficult to understand him and the lectures are boring but the book is really helpful. His practice exams are also really similar to the test, which is really helpful.
He was okay. The tests were hard but doable with study. Read the book and do practice exams.  Not the best at lecturing but he has the heart to help and tries his best.

This class was challenging, and the prof was of little help.  Mostly it was luck on having a good TA that decided your grade.  The average grade for the tests was somewhere around the middle 50s, and the average for the class around the middle 60s.  The curve can hurt you, and premeds are not guaranteed good grades.
No Comments
This class is not extremely challenging. If you know the practice midterms then you will be fine on the tests. Although there is usually one curve ball question.

Hardest class in the department, but she's a really good lecture and loves discourse. Make use of office hours and asking questions. May seem a little intimidating but is very nice and passionate about what she teaches.

Prof. Traxler is very charismatic, but her lectures do contain a lot of material so be prepared to take good notes because the tests will pull heavily from examples presented during lecture. She is not the most tech savvy, so a lot of our recordings never made it up to the website, so attendance is mandatory if you don't want to miss anything.

Traxler is super passionate about the things she teaches and that shows up in lecture. She likes to go on the confusing but albeit fun ramblings about various subjects that you'll need to detangle later. She's pretty available during office hours, although she can be a intimidating. Nonetheless she deeply cares about her student and it's fun.

Knowledgeable and enthusiastic of subject. However, overly-detailed lectures often felt pointless attending (DO attend), grandiose vernacular that could otherwise be said simply (what is she even saying?), makes exams unnecessarily hard. You will only pass if you know Every. Single. Component. of her PP slides. Great, but would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I could tell she likes her field however, her lectures were disorganized. I noticed her circling around the same idea over and over constantly adding in bits of information but losing most of the class along the way just from the amount of info. I think she would have clearer and better lectures if they were stepwise and concise. Class was ehhh

HARD class. No lecture record so very important to go to classes+take good notes. Traxler talks fast, hard for note taking even with printed lecture slides, which only were uploaded the night before sometimes even the morning right before lecture. I asked a prof to fix this but no change! Nice & enthusiastic, but I learned more from Kendall & labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Beth Traxler is one of my favorite professors I've ever had. She is incredibly passionate and has a very unique teaching style. She is not afraid to engage you as an individual and makes you feel like she appreciates you being in her class. It is so cool to be able to be taught by a master in the field. Always left her lectures feeling inspired.

Professor Traxlers questions are really tricky and take a lot of time to read. Wished I had realized that sooner and left her questions till the end instead. Make sure to practice memorizing the material ahead of time because you will not pass this class by studying the last week of a test! Study every day!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Microm 410 was SO boring. That being said, Traxler is clearly passionate about bacterial genetics and while she claims to be explaining clearly, her lecturing voice is super annoying and she accentuates every. single. word as if it is the most important... the MC tests are hard and knowing every single detail is important.

She doesn't care about students at all. Never reply emails even though she said in the lecture that "feel free to send me an email if you have any questions. Her lectures are not organized at all. Sometimes I don't even know what she's talking about

Dr. Traxler lectured quickly but effectively taught the material. You have to really pay attention but she does a good job of explicating. She also is really great to talk to outside of the class if you are interested in bio/microbio

You can tell she is very interested in the material when she talks but that is not the problem. Their are clicker questions that she writes the morning off that half the class doesnt understand but they still get graded. She goes over complex material 2 days before exam. Confusing when she talks, very unprofessional.

410 was an incredibly difficult class intended for future researchers, not for biopre-med students. You must memorize EVERYTHING on the slides! (A few words that seem like unimportant tidbits will end up a test question.) Long and tricky exams, not graded on a bell curve. People sleep during her lectures. Take 301302 instead!
Difficult course, but the prof was very enthusiastic and well organized

Prof Traxler did her section 2nd to Parsek, so just by comparison she was so much better. She really seems to care about the topic and sounds excited to be teaching it. Test can be difficult but as long as you pay attention to lecture or listen to the audio cast a few times its really a do-able class. Straight up memorization.
Decently engaging and class was quite easy.
if i could go back in time i would drop this class just so i would never have to be taught by evans.

Quiz sections are optional aside from the midterm. Prof Evans does really care about the topic but the lectures do get boring at times. She is very nice though and quite understanding. Pretty easy class, I did not read the textbook once but I do recommend going to lectures if you don't read the textbook.

I took Sociolinguistics, an incredible course for those interested in linguistics. She is a tough grader and there are research assignments throughout the quarter. If interested in studying under her, I recommend speaking to her about what she expects on exams because she is particular. Go to class, it'll help. Take if serious about linguistics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: rubrics and assignment guidelines all incredibly unclear. clearly passionate, but lectures were poorly paced and often boring. the only reason i didn't drop this class was because i needed the credit, and it wasn't even a hard class. despised her teaching style and every single assignment made me want to bend my laptop in half.

Passionate about her subject and getting the class to participate. Weekly assignments/quizzes are easy and not timed. However, the midterm was bad. Idk if that was the TA's grading, but somehow I managed to get a 74 while getting 90-100 on everything else including a 95% on the final I didn't study for. Took down my grade to a 3.6 (91).

I don't understand Evans hate. I took COM 233 for the credit and prepared for her to be a bad professor, and I was very pleasantly surprised. Everyone complaining about attendance mattering, just go to class, you pay for it bruh. You have weekly quizzes which are easy if you pay attention. She was funny and nice. Convinced everyone here is lazy.

Worst linguistics class I've taken by far. Very boring and unclear lectures and things were often poorly explained. Quizzes have questions that are too dense, poorly worded, and impossible to finish in the given time. Attendance is done very poorly, and it will drop your grade a lot.

This was one of the worst courses I've taken while at the UW. It was at 8:30, which already bugged me but it was a mandatory 8:30 which made it even worse. I really don't understand her grading system, one day I had a 98, I had to miss one class for personal reasons, and it dropped down to a 92. Check rate my professor before you take the class! 😭

Prof Evans did not provide clear criteria for the assignments and her grading depended on her mood. She never seemed prepared for the day's lecture and even forgot her own dissertation research. I would not suggest this course to anyone who wants to stay interested in sociolinguistics.

I really like the professor, she clearly enjoys what she teaches, but the organization of the class and tests are poor. I enjoy the content, but the tests make this class far more stressful than it needs to be. 15 min / 15 questions and DENSE questions written to make you fail. Sometimes quizzes are on holidays and weekends.

I'm a junior and this might be the first class I don't receive a 4.0 in. It's that unforgiving. The way that things are weighted, you can only miss about 11 points the whole quarter without dropping below a 95%. I'm not even kidding. Tests are extremely difficult despite the content being seemingly easy.
