This actually ended up being one of the toughest and most impossible classes Ive ever taken at UW. I currently have a 3.7 and am pretty sure Im still going to fail this class because of the final. 15 minute 15 q LONG quizzes every week worded to make you fail, id work so hard and never got 100%. Cumulative 80 questions 80 mins final IN PERSON.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Although the class is organized and flexible, the downside of that is that you must hold yourself accountable to go through the extremely bland pre-recorded lectures and long readings. It is disappointing to see her lack of effort in connecting with her students and making a fun format.

Honestly, out of my entire college career this is probably the worst class I've ever taken. Despite reading every single chapter and studying for every single quiz, you'll most likely still fail. The way that she words her quizzes feels like she wants you too fail. Do not take if you don't need to. 0/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This professor thinks it's a good idea to teach students only with the textbook, give about zero resources for studying, and only host office hours for students to ask her "questions". I thought some of my other professors handled teaching online badly, but this is a whole extra level of garbage. I did not pay tuition to read a book.

Her chapter tests are difficult as hell. Despite putting in hours of reading, taking notes (verbatim) from her lectures, she twists the words around in her quizzes to throw you off. It's like she wants you to fail. I would definitely suggest not taking her class if you don't have to.

Have to study 2-2.5 hours a week at most, majority of grade is on weekly quizzes. Her feedback and email replies are super condescending and unforgiving. Asked her a question about content and provided quotes from the textbook and from her lecture asking for more clarification and she told me to go back and reread it.........
Lots of tests. She didn't know her materials well. The recording lectures are so mediocre and she makes the interesting materials sound boring. AVOID.

Tons of tests, all the information is given in class but she posts the powerpoints online. She's a little condescending at times but the lecture material was interesting. You really do have to study for those tests, though, because they're a massive chunk of your grade.
Talks down to students and has very unclear grading. Assignments are easy but tests are tricky despite content taught being simple.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Class material is really easy, but the tests always have a few questions that are poorly written. This sucks because missing one question brings down test grade by 4%. There is no EC and also NO CURVE! I am in the higher percentile for test scores yet I only have a 3.5 at this point in the quarter. Great Lecturer, but her grading system sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A lot a lot of readings to do, and skipping a few class wont hurt your grade. Assignment can be complicated and difficult to finish for some kinds of people. She is really specific on things that she wanted just be careful of that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class LING 233 is somewhat interesting, and the multitude of online tests make it an easy A. However, Betsy was a bit of jerk and came off really condescending in lectures. She's good enough at explaining concepts, but I wouldn't take her again. Lectures aren't really mandatory but she does use Poll Everywhere.

Professor Evans is okay, my biggest issue with her is that she kind of talks down to students, never had a prof do this before but just made me feel always inadequate. As for the class it's fine (didn't learn much) but unforgiving. If you work/have other commitments, your grade will fall if you accidentally forget one thing, lots to keep track of.
Poll everywhere in lecture. Final is okay if you study the quizzes and assignments. Really passionate and fun prof.
A great proffesor. Lecture can be useful, but skipping a couple won't hurt. Weekly quizzes with all answers found online. One final test and if you study the quizzes, you will be fine.
She really loves what she does!!

One of my fav profs. Super engaging, funny and really just wants everyone to learn (she will slow down/go back if people don't understand concepts). Online quizzes/hw is super easy as long as you go to lecture/skim the textbook. No essays. Final is also pretty easy even without a study guide. Quiz section is a waste of time/not mandatory. Easy A

She is an excellent professor who cares about her students and is passionate for teaching linguistics. There are no written assignments (except for one) where we had to talk about which motivations for studying dialects interests us the most. That was hard for me because I had to find reasons for studying dialects and finding evidence to support

Not the most easy/interesting class but it's ok. Prof Evans is really passionate about what she's doing but cares a little bit too much when people talk during class. The online tests are ok but the time limit is really tight, and the final was kind of confusing since there's nothing to begin with- no study guide, just the tests we took.

You have to come to class on time or else you will feel targeted by her. I think she holds grudges. 8 online test that are very confusing as well as 9 online assignments. Make sure you are clear and concise with your free response answers because she grades hard. Also, its hard to get a good grade. I was there everyday, got 87% which is a 3.2.

Worked my butt off. Scored above everyone else on the exams (according to the catalyst statistic) and received a 2.1. I feel very sorry for anyone who scored lower. Gosh. This course should be curved. Clearly not everyone absorbs everything and we all do our best. Professor error?

Tests every 2 weeks, attending class is essential to getting kick ass grades, her tests are confusing, and somewhat detailed. She's a very nice person, funny, and concise. No extra credit assignments are offered, lecture slides weren't available online. Interesting class, difficult to get a good grade though

I had her for LING 432 (socio I) & LING 433 (socio II). I didn't do so hot in 432, but I did much better in 433. She doesn't give tests. But she does have weekly writing assignments (whic turns into a final research proposal). It was a very USEFUL class especially for those who are going into grad school. Let's you know what's expected in academia.

This Ling/Anth/Com course was quite easy. The textbook will help you (Wolfam's American English). Grades are based on tests (4 plus a final) and attendance to lectures is NECESSARY as almost all the test questions are based off lecture (which are very repetitive). Dr.Evans is a very nice and funny, and there is lots of help you can get if needed.

I really love her as a professor, she explains everything clearly and really tries her best to make linguistic interesting. However, I don't like how she does not post her slides online, so you really have to attend her lectures. Overall, I love her class.

her class is really hard but she's an interesting lecturer. she's very picky about what she wants you to know so if you have ethical problems w/regurgitating whatever your prof says, don't take her class.

I enjoyed her a lot - and have learned so much from her. The tests appear to be easy, but since there are only 7-8 questions, it's so easy to get a low score.  On top of that, she is a very harsh grader!  So I got low grades on my tests even though I felt confident in the material. I don't think my grade accurately reflects what I learned.
literally the worst teacher I've ever had. she wants you to fail
She is hilarious.

This class should be avoided at all costs. (unless linguistics is your major). Boring lectures, would not post notes online, felt like she was talking to us like 1st graders. Not a great class for general elective. Don't waste your time.
No Comments

This class had a midterm, final, weekly quizzes and in-class activities, so it requires pretty regular review (as with Patty's other classes!). Patty was very considerate by allowing up to 2 quiz drops. The organization of examples and information on her lecture slides can get confusing, so be sure to attend class to see how she explains them.

Yes, she doesn't record her lectures. You're in college paying thousands for the class, feel like that should be a motivator to go to class. Her lectures aren't super exciting, but I learned more about statistics in her class than any stats class I've ever taken. I hated stats in high school, and this class made me feel like I'm actually good at it

I'm an ISE major so I have taken a lot of random classes that have nothing to do with my major, and I've had a lot of bad professors. Patty is the best. Exams will only ever have things that shes covered in lectures, never any curveballs. Her slides are simple and get to the point. If you miss class, catching up is very easy.

Weekly quizzes are the only way to force participation, because her lectures are so boring that no one would engage with her slide-reading. Exams are long, hard, and tricky with tough grading. She uses office hours to engage the class since she doesn't cover everything in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Nice and explains concepts decently well when they are about lean, but on the technical such as simulation it is much harder and the classes often are so anti-recording there is little available resources to review if you miss class. Also despite her carefree nature she is a rather harsh grader, sometimes projects pile up and need so much work.

She is a very nice person but a horrible professor. Her assignment documents and grading criteria are hilariously vague, yet despite that she is a strict grader. She is very difficult to access and most of the time will not help you. She is busy with her job outside of teaching, but she really should devote more time to her classes.Class wasnt hard

Prof. Buchanan is extremely kind and cares about every student's success. Her lectures were informational but also slightly boring. Content seemed to be more challenging for people without prior statistics knowledge, as it's a pretty fast-paced course, but the course was overall manageable.

Prof. Buchanan truly cares about her students. She is accessible outside of class, personable, and tries her best to be a great teacher. Regardless, her years in academia and industry have left her somewhat tone-deaf about her students. Expect a passionate teacher who will leave you questioning her grading methods and 1on1 communication style.
Very good professor. The nicest professor you could ever have in your 4 years of campus life. Extraordinary in both teaching and communication with students.

I love Patty, I just didn't do as well bc i do not get econ. Ind E 250 was so much better than taking econ 200 with all the finance bros. She is such a mom, you get a partner for quizzes, and she wants you to succeed. Take it.

Best lecturer I've had at UW so far. Incredibly nice, funny, sweet person that genuinely cares about your learning. Even though the room is quite big, it never feels scary to ask her a question in class because she always gives great answers that don't make you feel stupid for asking them. Knowing Excel pretty well helps a lot.

Patty is a very good professor, always accessible and remembers the names of all her students, caring about them a lot. Slides are laid out extremely well, and she walks through several examples to make sure we all know how to do problems. Her tests, however, tend to have trick questions on them which I did not appreciate. Don't take STAT instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Patty is by far one of the best professors I've had thus far. Stats was a completely new subject to me and a class outside of my major, but she made things easy to follow and helped me to understand what was going on. Lectures were lots of fun, and the structure of using quizzes rather than midterms alleviated a lot of stress

Patty is amazing!! Very understanding and lenient, she'd push back homework when we fell behind in class material to give us enough time to complete the homework. Clear presentation of materials, and gives thorough explanations when asked. The quizzes are very straightforward, and once I remembered the practice exams existed my scores went way up.

Buchanan is honestly one of the best professors I've had at UW. Class is pretty straight forward, but she'll go the extra mile to explain something to you if you're having trouble outside of class, feel like she truly cares about the students. Extremely kind and lectures are pretty easy to understand for most part. Definitely recommend
One of the best classes
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very good professor at what she teaches, but material itself isn't very interesting. Gives good lectures and goes over a lot of examples which is helpful but can be hard to pay constant attention. Tests are fair and she gives lots of hints/prep material for exams. Very nice, and if you need help she is very helpful.

Professor Buchanan is very caring and teaches the class well. The material up to the first midterm with probability is the most challenging but it is easy after that. Do her practice exams and the homework and you'll be fine.

shes a great professor. her powerpoint slides are very clear and organized. she really cares about her students, she often sends out email to clarify some confusion or posts extra flowchart to help students. shes also funny, often brings up real life scenarios. she gives reviews before every exam and gives many hints too. Highly recommended.

The biggest thing I liked about her was how she was very caring and reasonable. She provides a lot of resources that will allow you to do well and her tests are very similar to the practice exams she provides. It shows that she cares despite knowing that barely anyone showing up to class (Panopto). Content isn't hard but don't slack off too much.

Not the most challenging IND E class but very interesting with this professor. She is the most caring and effective teacher at UW I have encountered. Very respectful and tries her best to avoid dry lectures even when the material seems miserable. Overall, I would absolutely take a class with her again, by far my best prof. at UW.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: Great professor, good at answering questions and explaining concepts. If you pay attention in class and do the homework the class is fairly easy; just a standard statistics class with mostly  engineering-oriented word problems. Prof is flexible about homework deadlines and eager to provide help when needed, and lectures are somewhat entertaining.
Definitely avoid. Lectures were incredibly boring, and I was never sure whether she knew what she was talking about. It was an easy class, but I don't feel like I learned much at all.
Class was very straightforward, expectations for tests were extremely clear, lectures and reading were both very direct to all assignments.

I took him for Critical Filipino American History. He was a great welcome to my first ever quarter at UW. His lectures are hilarious and its easy to understand when he talks about his own experience. Though, he provides a ton of reading and quizzes afterwards. The quizzes are slightly easy if you pay attention in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bonus assignments are not dependent on the lecture. He provides all the information you need for quizzes (which consist of vocab words and general ideas we learn in class) and isn't a tough grader, just use your own ideas and words. He likes it when his class talks.

wonderful professor!! bonus was the first professor i connected with on campus and he truly cares about connecting with his students. that being said, his course was definitely unorganized and admittedly left leaning, as many other reviewers noted. still, he is a wonderful individual and i would love to spend more time learning from his teachings

Professor Bonus was very knowledgeable and always tried to make class interesting. One thing I'll say is be prepared to read A LOT. I should've expected this for a history class but I didn't realize how it'd be difficult sometimes with other classes and stuff. You should get a decent grade if you do the work on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super dry, boring, and made us buy multiples of his own books just to read one half of one chapter in each. Enjoy those extra royalties, I guess that's what you mean by "Bonus"!

Bonus is one of those radical far-left professors that make UW the memeable school it is. He openly hates on anyone who isn’t a minority student, explicit in his disdain for white people. If you’re a minority but have white friends, prepare to be made uncomfortable; Bonus thinks you should only be friends with other minorities.

Bonus is one of the best AES professors I've taken! I really enjoyed his class and found the course extremely interesting. While he does talk really fast, he always takes questions at the end of lecture for clarifications. I took this class online, so it was probably a lot easier than in-person since he modified his final to a 1-pg reflection.

Professor Bonus is one of the best professors at UW. He's very welcoming, understanding and hilarious! He tells the best stories and made going to lecture fun and worthwhile. He explains what material will be on the quizzes and tests and is available to answer any questions. Definetely would recommend taking his classes.

HIs class is very disorganized and is too fast paced. He does not provide panopto recordings nor does he provide the lecture slides used in class. He goes through the slides very quickly and if you miss something on a slide, you're kinda screwed. The material is very radical and can sometimes be misleading. This class is very bias toward the left.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Rick Bonus obviously loves what he does. Only complaint is that he goes too quickly and there is no panopto or posted slides to look at later. Otherwise, hes funny, relatable, and cares about his students. Would recommend this course as it is informational and not particularly difficult or stressful.

I love the content of the class. it is very interesting. but this teacher has ruined it for me and does not want to help you at all. he is very unorganized and the midterm was unbelievably hard. there are four books to read and around 7 very long articles. pop quizzes on the readings as well as weekly homework and two huge presentation projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He's really funny so you won't be bored during his lectures. He doesn't take attendance but he doesn't post his PPT or he has pop quizzes during the lecture so it's smart to go to every class.. if you go to the lecture and memorize the vocabs before exams you will be fine! He also gives many extra credit opportunities.

Bonus class is so much fun because he is very funny! However, he sucks at going over the slides. He has a powerpoint but doesn't show his slides while talking he just tells you what to write then when he is done he will show his slide which makes it confusing sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: If you want to do well in this class, just make sure you know the general concepts and also every single detail mentioned. Dr. Cookson is an alright professor, but my god, the structure of this class is ridiculous.  If you want a good grade, memorize everything (consistent active recall!!!), and if you want to keep your sanity, avoid this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I didn't entirely hate this course but it was really challenging. The content was pretty interesting but they don't provide you with any study materials and it is so hard to memorize all of the content. Just brute memorization of a bunch of different bacteria with no good way to do so is near impossible. Plus 90% of your grade is exams
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class works by two midterms and one final. Each midterm is about 22.5% of your grade, and the final is around 44%. Each lecture is taught by a different professor, which makes it difficult to study. This is just a pure memorization class. Avoid it if possible. If you do take it, make flashcards, go to class, DON'T FALL BEHIND!

While Dr. Cookson is a kind man who seems to be very passionate about his job, the same cannot be said about him as a teacher. The structure of this course is the worst that I have ever experienced. We cannot see what we got wrong on the exams, there are no assignments, and very few practice questions are given to help prepare. Take at own risk.

Dr. Cookson is pretty funny and is a good lecturer. However, he only gives about 5 lectures out of the whole class. The rest of the class is given by guest speakers. The class itself is pretty difficult with a lot of material to cover. If you aren't good at memorization, you probably won't do well. Basic understanding of micro bio is a must.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Worst Micro elective at UW. DO NOT take this course thinking it's an easy class. Even though he proclaims that even non-micro majors can ace his class and he wants everyone to get a 4.0 this is far from it. You get a bunch of different guest lectures and they create the test questions. Overall terrible, disorganized, and unnecessarily hard class.

Preparing for exams can be a bit overwhelming because there's so much material. Tests aren't impossible if you really pay attention to details. Unfortunately it may take messing up on first exam to figure this out, so a 4.0 is likely out of reach. I thought the lecture class format was great with the various experts that lectured.

My comments are more related to the course rather than a specific lecturer. There are a number of guest lecturers and they come up with their own questions. Really hard to grasp what each lecturer focuses on which makes studying harder. There is A LOT of contenT. There was one lecture that had almost 60 PowerPoint slides... A lot of memorization...

he's a great speaker, however, he only teaches one or two of the main lectures and leaves the rest up to the guest speakers. the guest speakers write their own questions on the tests and it becomes super confusing with all the different formats. hardest class I've taken at UW. don't believe him when he says you need no science background for this
I just wished he used powerpoint slides, he's very disorganized. He's an AMAZING speakerpresenter though. Just hard to follow.

He is great for telling you stories and giving you great "review" lectures. His handouts are an absolute mess, and he skips around and isn't very organized and on topic. Sometimes I wish he used a powerpoint, only to keep in on track during lecture. He is funny, though! Just be prepared for difficult exams.  He did have a great bowtie though.

Oh, you handsome bow-tied man, I wish I could have taken all my classes from you! Cookson is like a force of nature. He knows what he's talking about, his lectures command your attention, and he's not just reading powerpoint slides. Honest and funny. Sadly, he only does the intro lectures and then it's all guest speakers on each topic.

He's entertaining, knowledgeable, and overall a great professor. I was worried because people said the class was hard (and it is), but he's a great professor that cares about his students. I plan on taking him again for management 300. You'll need the textbook for quizzes but not exams.

One of the best classes I've taken at uw. Lots of readings and long lectures but they're both super engaging, especially the lectures. Grades are just made up of exams/quizzes but as long as you pay attention in lecture and do the readings you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Probably the only professor that could make an hour fifty minute lecture interesting. Very helpful and seems like he cares a lot. If you read the student notes youll do fine

this is one of the worst classes i have taken at uw. because of this class, i have genuinely doubted my ability in school because he purposely makes his class so difficult for no reason. if you cant spend every waking moment studying for this class, then dont take it with him! you are not given any practice to bounce off of for tests, just lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The best (and hardest) course I've taken so far. I was actually excited to go to class because his lectures were so engaging. I worked extremely hard to end up with a 3.9 but I also discovered my interest for law so it was worth it. If you don't read the textbook you probably won't pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tod is one of the best teachers I have ever had, I am not a foster student but this class if one of my favorite I've ever taken. All you need to do is go to class and pay attention in lecture, because all the quizzes and tests are 99% lecture content. His lectures are super interesting and it makes the class really fun
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Reading the 5-rated reviews, I have a suspicion that Tod writes them himself; they sound a lot like how he talks in class, and I don't know anyone who has such good words for him.

Don't trust the other reviews; some of Tod's lectures are interesting, but he is the worst professor I have taken in terms of grading. His tests are already hard on their own, and he subtracts points if you get questions wrong. Only take if you want to dedicate most of your time to his class.

Tod is probably one of the best teachers I have taken by far. His lectures are super entertaining, he has great communication with his students, and always seeks what's best for you. His exams and quizzes are very tricky. This class is a lot of memorization. When taking quizzes and exams, read everything correctly; he purposely makes it tricky.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took him abroad during the Summer, and he was a great professor; he is very engaging. The exams require studying, but as long as you pay attention in class and read the readings he requires, you will be fine!! It is a great class and Tod is a professor you should experience at least once while in Foster!
Don't take his class! i nearly diagnosed mental illness because of this class, especially when you're not a native speaker!

Awesome professor and super entertaining. He is very passionate about what he teaches and makes it intriguing to learn. Has a lot of tricks up his sleeves for quizzes and exams so stay up to date with the course pack and readings! Quizlet was a lifesaver. Would definitely take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tod is the best lecturer at UW. The class is difficult but you get the grade you work for if you study hard. Lectures were entertaining and examples using students were hilarious and helped reinforce concepts. Getting to know Tod is such a treat and conversations with him are never boring. Highly recommend doing his Early Fall Start in Australia!

Best professor in the business school, hard class and lots of memorization, concepts are not to difficult but lots and lots of memorization. Great stories and in class examples, gets the class involved, incredibly interesting class and would definitely take it again

Even though this class made me decide to go to law school, it did kill my GPA so decide if u wanna take this class wisely. tests are very hard and really theres only so much you can study for, theyre just very detailed and theres some trick questions in there so be careful and thoughtful. Other than that the class is SO fun and interesting.

Tod is an amazing professor to get to listen to while sitting through lectures. He keeps all students very engaged and makes learning interesting. However, his quizzes and tests are harder than I have ever experienced. Towards the end of the class I started figuring out the way he writes tests. Read the true or false questions word for word!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fantastic teacher and amazing content. You can typically miss 3 questions on quizzes and still get 100%, which is nice and can make up for a lack of study guides. Quiz and test questions can be quite tricky, but after a quiz or two you get a feel for what kinds of things he may ask.

Class is entirely memorization, the better you are at that, the higher the grade you will get. The key is to memorize entire lectures for the exams /quizzes. He has a very clear grading criteria. His questions are designed to trick you, pay attention to the wording.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tod is extremely talented at engaging students in lecture. The concepts covered are very relevant and interesting, and he is very knowledgeable. That being said, the amount of work in this class is overwhelming, his grading is harsh, and success hinges on memorization. Create flashcards of everything covered/assigned and you will be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: quiz every week

Quizzes and exams require STUDYING! Do not let yourself fall behind in this class. Tod is a great professor with great lectures, but do note his exams are difficult. I recommend reviewing the content before and after each lecture to avoid having to cram it all right before an exam. Despite the heavier workload, I would take his course again!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Sit near the front and you will be super engaged because Tod is one of the best lecturers at the U. Don't fall behind on the readings and you will do fine in the class. This class is graded on 4 quizzes, a midterm, and a final. Keep in mind that every MGMT 200 course is graded on a curve with a median ~3.0 so you will get the grade you work for.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 3 years at UW, this is the first class I've made an effort to go to every lecture because they are actually engaging and beneficial. You can solely rely on the lectures and course pack and will be set. All tests are COMPLETELY memory based, so don't forget to note everything, questions r made to trick you! No canvas is annoying but not impossible.

Tod is a super interesting lecturer. I learned a lot. But be prepared to take lots of notes. His FEW exams are very Memory based. There is also only a few things that count toward your grade so make them count. But he seems like a smart and energetic guy. Always enjoyed coming to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of typos in his lectures, exams, and instructions overall. It makes it hard to take seriously the extreme expectations he imposes on his students when his work is so careless. Only pro is that his lectures are usually interesting. Overall, dreaded going to this class because of the confusing content and lack of preparation materials.

Most unclear course I have ever taken. As someone with a very high GPA, I maintain this through actually understanding every concept I learn for every class. It is impossible to do that here. Understanding concepts does not get you anywhere, as it is solely a memorization course of absurd amounts of information and random details.
The quiz will seem really hard at first but keep up with the texbook, coursepack reading and lecture note and you will be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had at UW. Tod is extremely engaging during lectures, making it worth attending class. While he's a tough grader, he presents the content in such an interesting way that preparing for tests feels manageable.

The lectures are fast-paced and challenging, but Professor Tod makes the class engaging with great guest speakers. Prepping with unstuck ai and the textbook can help you stay on top of the demanding grading. Definitely worth taking if you're up for the workload.

He gives helpful resources you can download and review. I studied hard for this class, and this class had a strong impact on me!! I loved the subject and found areas that I was passionate about. Not to mention the BEST lecture at uw in my opinion - very engaging with his stories and involving his audience. Tough grading system, be sure to know it!

I love Tod! I had him as our study abroad faculty, and Tod taught us many things about Australia that we didn't know about outside the business setting. He was caring and funny and would went out with us often to create bonds. *This is not a traditional lecture course.

Amazing lectures but goes through a lot really fast. Exams were hard and you have to know your stuff for the quizzes. Hated how all the lecture notes were on ONE 200 pg word instead of ppts bc "the class content changes too fast" and refused to change it despite a TA offering to do it. It made it hard to study for. don't get behind on readings!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class is tough but Professor Bergstrom explains concepts well and gives excellent anecdotes and stories to make concepts stick. Classes are definitely packed full of information and there's a ton of terms but the information is easy to understand. Both the quizzes and tests are hard and if you don't know the info, you will NOT do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very engaging during lectures, approachable, and funny. Quizzes and tests are fairly easy as long as you go to class, pay attention, and memorize vocab from the class. There may be pop quizzes, but only if people stop going to the lecture (which is highly suggested, because he might test you on examples only given in class).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tod is great at presenting and engaging with the class. The textbook readings are the exact same as the lectures, so please don't waste your time on them. Quizzes and exams will only reflect lecture material and the course pack articles/cases. Memorization is the best way to prepare for quizzes. The grading system on quizzes is strange, so beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: FYI - other students complaining about the course difficulty should try taking a STEM class at UW and then reassess. Tod worked tirelessly to organize an extensive list of guest speakers for a Boeing 737 Max case, which made the class quite special and rewarding. He goes above and beyond for the students, and Foster is lucky to have him.

Took him for MGMT200 and 320, one of the best professors I've ever had. Amazing lectures that you don't want to miss. The class is not as hard as people make it out to seem. Tod wants you to memorize broad concepts so simply studying definitions will not get you very far. I think this is where most people fall short.

Super nice guy, very passionate about the topics. Grading is brutal and destroys your self-esteem. Beware his grading policies on T/F questions, I literally got a 0/30 on the first quiz because of it. Very knowledgeable but has crazy high standards.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible Canvas page and hypocritically high standards for students that he does not live up to himself. Boasts about the high-stakes nature of the class, yet it's clear he hasn't evolved as a teacher in 20+ years. Despite this, he manages to exhibit an unbearable ego. Would not recommend and by far the worst class experience at Foster.

I'll just say that he's a great guy and he's passionate about teaching but his structure promotes memorizing lots of content over learning:
No canvas structure or slides.
Penalises students for getting the wrong answer.
Harsh grader.
He goes through content extremely fast and most of the time students can't keep up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really appreciated how he was always energetic and passionate about making these lectures as interesting as possible for everyone. However, his grading is pretty tough so be prepared for that, and the quizzes/exams are even tougher. Stay on top of the class by doing all the readings, showing up to lectures and tons of notes and you'll be prepared
Great professor, fun lectures, honestly the material is not as hard as some people make it to be.

I came into this class expecting it to be extremely difficult, but it wasn't bad at all. His grading is pretty fair, and he no longer does pop quizzes. His lectures are very engaging & you can tell he's passionate. There isn't that much reading either. Just put in the time to read the textbook and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Excellent lectures. Extremely difficult tests and quizzes. Tod is great, but I fully expect to receive a very low grade in the class.

Such a fun class. Tod really knows how to give engaging lectures. Lots of content to remember, but if you put in the work you will be fine! Four quizzes, one midterm, and one final make up your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tod is an amazing lecturer, he knows how to make the content relatable. There are no more pop quizzes in the class, but the quizzes are still very difficult as you can lose points for guessing incorrectly on T/F. Your grade mainly relies on the tests/quizzes, so it's worth picking up good study habits for this class so you can do well on them.

His tests try to trick you and he will subtract additional points for guessing so you might as well not answer at all. His grading seems EXTRA harsh and lecture notes + canvas is completely disorganized. Many of his examples also revolve around s*x and female dancers (almost every class) which has made many female students uncomfortable.

I'll keep it simple. As of now, he does NOT do pop quizzes. He grades you on 3 of your best quizzes (out of 4). There is a midterm and final (non-cumulative). Yes, he is an amazing lecturer and I love his speeches, but be warned, his questions on quizzes and exams are tough! Take him if you don't care about grade and want to learn, if not stay away
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tod was a natural great lecturer in any kind of scenario. He was able to make the law languagle the most beautiful poem in the world  through using well designed examples. Tod had quite a lot readings and assessment pretty fun readings tho. I would genuinely accept a lower gpa if i am learning from a professor like TOD

Class is alright, too much information. There is no example of past tests and quizzes, that make students have a rough time studying. He also got this penalty rule with T/F questions which is kinda annoying. Personally, I just don't like how the class structure. If you are like me, taking 4 classes and working, please don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Incredibly dedicated, intelligent, kind, and inspiring.  One of my favorite profs I've had here.  Also had him for 320.  My younger brother came to visit before admissions decisions were released, and after finding out he was waitlisted Tod helped him personally with his appeal.  Genuinely so thankful for Tod and his passion for teaching!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tod had extremely interesting guest speakers and lecture content but his quizzes and tests are extremely difficult. Expect to spend a lot of time studying for his class and reviewing notes. Attendance is not mandatory as all lectures are recorded but his content is so engaging you will want to go to class.

Tod has great lectures, but that's the only great part of his class. His class favors students who has free time to spend it reading, reviewing lecture material and memorizing. If you are a working student, a parent or have a lot of responsibilities outside of school, avoid his class at all costs.

Tod is the best professor I have had at UW! His lectures are entertaining and informative. However, the tests are hard and there are a lot of questions on details only briefly covered in class. Overall if you study a lot and do the readings, you will get a ton out of this class. I can't wait to take MGMT 320 with Tod!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Tods was the best class I've taken at UW so far! The lectures were super interesting and he explains tough information so it was easier to digest and learn. Would 100% recommend his classes to anyone and would definitely take his class again. Beware of the POP QUIZZES though, there's 4, and 2/4 are announced before class. Best teacher at Foster!
He is a good lecturer but beware of the quizzes. The questions try to trick you, are over small obsure details, and he has a negative point punishment for true/false questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: One of the best professors at Foster. Passionate. Knowledgable. Lectures are very engaging. Materials are relevant and useful. Great guest speakers. Exams are based on lectures so pay attention in class and take notes.

This is the second class I've taken with Tod. This course is easier than MGMT 200, less reading and enough cross over from the previous class that the pace doesn't get uncomfortable, but Tod is just as engaging. If you have to take this class take it with Tod.
Someone remind him this isn't law school.

reviews.comment: His teaching style is a complete mess and it is incredibly difficult to study for this class. There are also lots of reading material. reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Amazing professor, just brilliant. Great lecturer, really knows the law since it's his day job. Be prepared to do lots of reading and pay attention in class.

He does have biases towards students HOWEVER all grading for exams are done anonymously. His TAs (who grade exams) do not know whose exam it is.
I thoroughly enjoyed this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Tod is a fun, passionate, and very smart professor who wants his students to succeed. His lectures were so engaging and memorable, which helped me stay very attentive, learn a lot, and do good on exams. I am also more interested in law now all thanks to Tod. My one regret is not participating as much in class, which I recommend everyone to do.

Tod is an amazing professor, maybe my favorite professor at UW. His lectures are very interesting, engaging, and helpful. Pop quizzes sucked but weren't actually too hard if you did the readings and attended lectures. It's hard to do well in the class but the whole class experience and Tod's relevant work stories made up for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Most engaging and entertaining professor in Foster. Extremely difficult class with a high workload, but worth every bit of effort. Very fair grading style and he blind grades exams and papers, so no favoritism. 320 with him is amazing, and the themes are captivating. You won't take a more influential class than 320 with Tod (200 is good too).

Tod's exams are cruel and he absolutely plays favorites, but he is a very engaging lecturer and knows his stuff. Has lots of stories and connections that make long classes interesting. Reasonable and clear expectations that can be met if you just do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I <3 Tod. His class is hard for sure but his lectures make up for it, and he is very up front about his class format and what is expected. Get ready to work hard but the results are worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is the worst teacher I've ever had. There are extremely few instances where you receive a grade (4 pop quizzes and 2 midterms). I can't believe pop quizzes still exist in modern times. The midterms are extremely long and challenging. You have to memorize an unholy amount of info. Be prepared because Tod doesn't care about you at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: please save yourself your money and time and do NOT take professor bergstroms classes. He is a poor professor and picks favorites from his class. he sets his students up for failure and does not care about his students, unless he favors you. I have never hated a class as much as this class and wish i never signed up for it.

one of the worse classes ive taken ever. it was incredibly hard and the professor did very little to actually help the students. he also made class mandatory with random pop quizzes and still expected those with covid to come into class. DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS CLASS PLEASE DO NOT TAKE!!!!!!!!!!!!

Tod is by far the best lecturer I have had at Foster. He is knowledgeable and passionate about law. However, this class was stressful, and there were 4 pop quizzes throughout the quarter and demanding exams. Listen to his lectures (write everything), go to CLUE, and do quizlets, and youll do well. I highly recommend Tod!

reviews.comment: Tod is an amazing lecturer and really smart. it's just too much. i don't really think that he should be lecturing with a mask off in a pandemic. we're forced to go to class because we have pop quizzes and the class has no online/live zoom option either. tests are set up for failure

TOD IS THE BEST

reviews.comment: I didn't know real pain until I took this class. Help.

Tod is one of my favorite professors at UW. This class is hard, no doubt, but getting a good grade in this class is still feasible. Need to stay on top the reading. Be familiar with the concepts and tests in law. Those are a big part in the tests. Also you need to be comfortable to find details in story problems to apply the appropriate tests.

reviews.comment: Tod is by far the best lecturer I have ever taken. He explains almost every concept with hilarious anecdotes, and I learned more material than I ever have in a class before. There are four pop quizzes (one is dropped) and exams are extremely difficult, but his class is worth it. You have to work HARD, but everything is always fair. A gem for sure.

Tod is an amazing professor who puts so much time and effort into making class interesting. 320 is very similar to 200 except there are more guest lecturers and a group project. I would recommend taking 320 the quarter after 200 or as soon as you can because there is some overlap in material and you get used to the pop quiz format.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tod is an awesome lecturer, gives hilarious and interesting examples that are relevant to course content, and answers questions well. Each lecture has a LOT of content so take notes beforehand so you can catch what he says that aren't on the slides. Pop quizzes are rough b/c of the way things are graded but do the readings and you'll be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof. Bergstrom cares about his job and is extremely passionate about what he teaches. He is engaging even during online classes. Would recommend.

First of all, don't take this class if you're lazy. Tod is challenging but he is easily the best professor you'll have in your time at UW. He's a great lecturer, gets amazing guest speakers, and knows how to keep you engaged for the full 2 hours. There are pop quizzes and you absolutely have to do the readings for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His lectures are entertaining but he's a tough grader and gives pop quizzes. Make sure you always do the readings and watch the videos before class! Also buy a course pack, for some reason it's optional and I made the mistake of not buying one. For midterms and finals, pay CLOSE attention to what guest speakers have to say and take many notes

I hate his class. He has no understanding for his students, especially during this time. I didn't feel supported and felt like his pop quizzes were so hard I was being set up to fail. reviews.comment: This is one of the toughest classes I have taken, but it's definitely worth it with Tod. Tod is extremely smart and shares interesting stories from his work as a prosecuting attorney. His experience as a professor and from his practice makes learning and memorizing law much more doable. Expectations are clear-get ready for lots of reading!

Tod Bergstrom has been my favorite teacher at the UW so far. His class is hard and I spent many hours reading each week and he gives pop quizzes which essentially makes class mandatory if you want to do well. His tests are hard but they are extremely fair. His lectures are some of the best Ive been too, and he is extremely intelligent and it shows

Best professor I have ever had. He is extremely knowledgeable and gives amazing insight into his thought process on many legal situations. reviews.comment: Tod is great and knowledgable. His class itself is pretty difficult and challenging, but you learn a lot. However, I would say that he's not very considerate of students or some of his comments.

reviews.comment: Tod is the best professor I've had at UW so far. It's so relevant to society and incredibly eye-opening. It's worth taking at UW, don't do it online just for the sake of getting a 4.0.

reviews.comment: I loved the class and Tod doesn't make the lectures boring at all. reviews.comment: Best professor at UW. All of the material you need to learn is clear cut. Good and easy to follow course pack. If you do the readings right before class the pop quizzes are easy. Tod is a knowledgeable professor with clear criteria and expectations for his students and is able to hold the class's attention despite the late night lectures. reviews.comment: This professor's lecture is really amazing, however, his tests and quiz are really insane super difficult.

reviews.comment: Tod is the best teacher that I have ever had. His lectures are incredibly entertaining and memorable, and the material in the course is really fascinating. The admissions team weights this class the same as an elective.

reviews.comment: Ive gone through 2 years at UW and hes been by FAR my favorite prof. Pop quizzes suck, and his tests just rail you, but if you put in the work youll do relatively well bc of the curve. Just do the reading and go to class.
