reviews.comment: Amazing professor but it's the hardest and most demanding class i've taken. I don't regret taking it with him though. Everything is so applicable to life in general. If you are considering taking another professor to make this course a bit easier, i wouldn't recommend that. It's not often you get a chance to have an amazing professor like Tod.

Tod is a real G when it comes to teaching, but this class is very hard. Honestly I hated my life for 3 months, but lectures were extremely engaging. Once you get through the class, you will know a lot about law which is cool. Beware of Pop Quizzes, so you gotta show up to class or else you will get railed. He's the best for the class though!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: By far the best professor or teacher I've ever had. Engaging, funny, and very rational. This class requires constant reading, note taking, and studying because of his pop quizzes; but the class is well structured and organized. Tod knows what he's doing and you will get out of this class whatever you put into it. Worth the extra work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: By far the most engaging professor I've had here at the UW. Class is hard - give yourself LOTS of time to review his lecture notes and content (and DON'T skip) and remember ALL the small stuff and the legal tests and you'll do well. Tod makes you work for it but doing well in his class is the most satisfying feeling. Also pop quizzes - study hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: You'll want to go to every lecture, regardless of a pop quiz. You'll feel a need to impress him if you're in his class. Its a tough class but, very manageable if you put in the effort. Do the assigned readings the night before, review hours before lecture. Study HARD for the tests, it will be worth it. I got a an extra point for participation too

Tod has by far the best lectures I've ever been to. Very engaging, never got bored, great examples. You MUST read all the assigned material, as there may be a pop quiz on it. He does not announce when the will be until about 2 minutes before the quiz. The quizzes and exams are quite challenging as it is a Foster weed out class. Highly recommend him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Similar to Law, do not take Tod's class if you just want to fulfill the core requirement; he will make you work hard for your grade. 320 with Tod is only offered winter quarter, so it would be wise not to take a heavy course load with this class. Brings in great guest lecturers. Awesome guy. As always, lots of reading + difficult pop quizzes/exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: easily the hardest class i've ever taken. Memorization is NOT enough, you truly have to think like a lawyer. this class may tank my gpa, but bergstrom was fascinating and really knows his stuff. Will miss his personality but not how hard this class was.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: The best professor I've taken at UW over the course of two years. He really cares for his students and inspires me to really question and understand application of law in our society. He genuinely cares for students, he's relatable, and his stories of crimes gone wrong made the class so enjoyable. Just simply amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Tod is a BALLER - his "day job" is being a prosecuting attorney so he knows his stuff. This class requires A LOT of work - probably 10+ hours per week of readings/notetaking, and his pop quizzes are intimidating. Go to CLUE, go to lecture to hear his relevant, usually funny stories. I'll only end a little above average, but still love this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Todd is really cool. Very smart, knows what he's saying and keeps lecturers engaging and interesting although he's teaching a dry subject. Give's a lot of examples and is very welcoming/not intimidating although the subject and work load might be. I would 100% choose him for this class if I had the choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you don't read you will fail, and reading takes 7hours/week if you're gonna read thoroughly enough to do well on his 4 pop quizzes. Tests are written in a way that you don't just need to know the material, you need to be able to critically think about it. One of the best and smartest lecturers I've had, and the hardest class I've taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tod is the best professor I've had at the UW. He is engaging with his lectures, and is always willing to help and answer any questions. He actually applies a lot of the concepts to real world scenarios happening in real time, which again makes his lectures a lot more engaging. Dude is a beast
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: There are pop quizzes! but the lowest one gets dropped. the exams are so hard and alot of reading. But every class is so much fun and he makes it so engaging. Blind grading is done and that makes it so much more fair. There is so much reading so you need to start early. penalises for wrong multiple choice answer so beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Tod is by far the best professor I have had at UW. There's pop quiz so you kinda have to go to the lecture but you would want to go anyways. His lecturers are so fun and he used lots of real life cases. The class does require a lot of work but it is how law class is. You won't regret taking his class!

Tod is an amazing lecturer and knows exactly how to keep his students interested. He has a great sense of humor and has great stories to tell the class. You can also tell that he cares a lot about his students. His tests are quite difficult because of all the memorization involved, but nevertheless, he is a great teacher.

Tod is a fabulous lecturer and contributed so much to this course. He cares about the student success, he is a fair grader, and he just "gets it." He understands what we need as students, provide great examples in class to engage us, and take time out of his weekend to meet and get to know us. . He provided guidance to us to navigate the UW.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Favorite class I've taken at UW so far! Brings in real-world experience from being a prosecuting attorney, plus relevant news articles. Look forward to coming to this class every week. Pop quizzes force you to stay on top of your reading. Tough grader/writes difficult midterms. Don't let difficulty be a deterrent--his lectures are amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tod is a huge beast. Favorite professor I've had thus far. Very engaging and smart, used his own experience as well as real-world examples to make the class much more interesting.  Roll Tod

Tod is probably the best professor I'll ever have at this school. His lectures are engaging, he uses his real-world experience and excellent real-world examples to teach lessons, and he really cares about his students' learning. Very knowledgable about law and always fascinating to listen to. Always looked forward to this class. A+++

Tod is definitely one of the best professors I've ever had. He asked us thought-provoking questions, had awesome speakers in class, and gave interesting lectures. I would definitely take his class again just because he is awesome. Avoid Tod if all you are looking for is to fulfill the requirement -- he will make you work for your grade.

He is a difficult professor but I LOVED going to his lecture because they were never boring. Make sure you stay on top of the readings and take good notes on them! He gives pop quizzes to make sure people go to class. The exams cover so much material so make sure you start studying for the exams at least a week before.

Tod is a great professor who definitely knows what he's talking about. He interacts well with his students and gives clear real world examples to help his students better understand the concepts. There is a lot of reading assigned, but if you take the time to sit down everyday and do it, you'll thrive in his class.

Amazing lecturer and I looked forward to going to his class. He gives pop quizzes but if you do the reading they aren't all that difficult. The tests are harder than the pop quizzes but they are fair. I would recommend taking this class as long as you're ready to do the reading.

He is seriously an amazing lecturer. He puts a lot of passion and his lecture are very interesting and he always gives clear and real-world example. There are a lot of readings to do (both from the book and the course pack) and he does 4 pop quizzes (you can drop the worst one) on the readings for that class. I would recommend, but be prepared.

On average over a chapter a night plus course pack (dry, random, newspaper articles) audio homework and lecture notes, which he does pop quizzes on. He referencestests a lot on American politics. There are technically 3 exams which incorporate things from business law so if you transferred in good luck. Oh and  a 20 page group paperpresentation.

King County District Attorney teaching nights, shows how passionate he is about teaching. Great lecturer, slides are terrible tho (word documents). Grading  2 tests, group project and 4 pop quizzes which is how he gets people to come to class. Overall not too hard, minimal workload other than a lot of reading. Overall outstanding, passionate prof!
Very tough grader. I had a 3.6 average and this class alone dropped it to a 3.3.
Tod's an amazing lecturer. He is the main reason that I have decided to pursue law school. But his grading is keeping me on the fence about it.
For me as an international student, this class is hard as rock, but he is so passionate about the class. Listening him talking is actually a kind of enjoyment.
He covers quite a lot in lecture but even then, it's only part of the text. Prepare to spend a lot of time outside of class reading and memorizing concepts.

Probably one of the few classes where you'll learn a lot and still struggle to pass exams. He covers quite a lot in lecture but even then, it's only part of the text. Prepare to spend a lot of time outside of class reading and memorizing concepts.

This class was incredibly difficult. I learned a lot in this class that I'll use for the rest of my life. However, the way Tod set up the tests made them hard to study for. Try not to take this class unless you absolutely have to.

I enjoyed this class. Tod is passionate about the subject and you will leave the class with a lot of useful knowledge pertaining to law. Just don't expect a great grade unless you really commit to getting a 4.0. He writes glowing letters of recommendation as well.
He made the class much harder than it needed to be. Hope to never have Tod as a professor again.
Intense class but Tod teaches you everything he knows. He thoroughly enjoys the material. P
He is one of the best lecturers I've had at UW. He is passionate about the subject and he also blindly grades. The class is tough. You get out what you put in.

He's very passionate about the subject, and is a heck of a lecturer. However, the class is incredibly difficult. You are forced to keep up with reading because he gives four pop quizzes through the quarter and they account for a large chunk of your grade. If you want a great grade without much effort, this isn't the class for you.
Teaching 18 years for MGMT 200, Tod has great examples for criminal cases and he demonstrate the law through blind grading.

Great class and great lecturer. The tests are incredibly difficult (4 pop quizzes). You also lose points for wrong answers on true and false questions. Read the lecture notes before class. I repeat. Read the lecture notes before class. They really help. All in all, I learned a lot and really enjoyed taking this class with Tod.

Tod is one of the best lecturers I've ever been taught by. It is obvious that he knows what he's talking about. Plus, the two hour lectures rarely felt boring. But the pop quizzes are an absolute nightmare. My GPA dropped after taking his class. Try to focus on the stories he tells in class because they tend to be on the quizzes and midterms.

Tod is an awesome prof! He cares more about his classes than any other prof. that I've had. This class is a ton of work. There is a heavy reading load, and pop quizzes are extremely detail oriented and difficult. You will get out what you put in.

Haven't taken the final yet, but I can say that Tod is a great, great teacher who cares about what he teaches and his students. You will meet awesome guest speakers and Tod himself asks interesting, thought-provoking questions. He is the only teacher who blind-grades at Foster. The tests and quizzes are hard, but the class is worth the suffering.

definitely the last professor for international students. This drags my overall gpa from 3.9 to 3.6. Luckily I got admitted by foster this quarter, otherwise I don't know what I'm gonna do with this horrible grade. Lots of reading, however hard to digest for non native English speakers. I initially took this course because of scheduling, I regret..

GREAT teacher and great class but grade is based on 4 (pop)quizzes, 1 midterm, and a final. He makes his tests extraordinarily hard, and points are deducted for wrong answers in the multiple choice sections. But nonetheless, enjoyed the class. He is a very good professor.

Tod was an excellent lecturer. His speech was really engaging. But it was a hard class, the pop quizzes  were killing me! You need to do ALL the reading! Also, never skip 2nd hour of the class, he likes to exam the material we learned from 2nd hour. Tips: TAKE NOTE of all his STORY EXAMPLES was very important, since you will have essay exam.
Tough class, but rewarding. Tod is an excellent lecturer, and easy to relate to. Make sure to do all the readings.

Best professor & class I've taken at the UW.  Most engaging lecturer I've encountered.  Class is definitely harder and more work than the other management 200 classes however. Worth it if you want to learn.

Coolest teacher ever.His range of knowledge in his field is extremely vast due to his profession. Gives crystal clear examples to every cases which means lecture attendance is critical. Pop quizzes are killer though, you never know when one would turn up. Extremely hard class though I must say, you get minus points for questions you answered wrong.

Tod is one of the best professor I've every meet. His lecture can keep me awake even when I am extremely sleepy. He uses interesting examples and is a GREAT speaker. But his class is definitely not easy, though you'll do alright if you're welling to commit your time and effort into memorizing the readings and lectures.

#1 Tip: Read the lecture notes before class.  Also do the assigned reading, but reading the lecture notes helps drill the important info in in case of pop quiz. His lectures were entertaining so I didn't mind the late class times. He gives hilarious examples. Also really tries to get to know students! This class is tough but worth it!

Tod's class is difficult, but it has been the most interesting, engaging, practical, and rewarding class I've taken at UW. Pop quizzes are based mainly on examples from the reading, but tests are almost solely from lecture, so everyday attendance is mandatory. Great guest speakers and the hard work really paid off.

Def on of the best classes, and one of the most useful classes at the UW. The materials learned can definitely come in handy in this real world, and learning from him actually made me feel that i am smarter than the other kids.Tod is so cool and knowledgeable.Gives real interesting examples and cases and excellent clarity.Score well if study hard

One of the best classes at UW. Tod is an amazing lecturer and gives great examples. Your grade probably will not reflect how much you learn. It's a really hard class because there is a lot of reading and there are pop quizzes, but it's so worth it. I loved his class! Possibly convinced me to go to law school!
Best class I have taken in my 3 years at UW

AMAZING LECTURER! I won't lie, probably my favorite so far in my 3 years at UW. His use of examples are fantastic and memorable, so it really helps out when it comes to test time. Tests are pretty hard, but managable if you study moderately & go to class.  Take MGMT 200 with him, even though it is in the evening. Worth it!!!!

Hard class because of the pop quizzes and loads of reading, but in the end, it's totally worth it. I learned so much and the classes were very interesting! He's a great lecturer and class won't be a bore. His tests are hard to because he's usually looking for a specific answer... that's where memorization comes into play. Take his class!

Although his class was difficult (eg. his pop quizzes can be tough and his tests are tough), his exams are designed to give an almost perfect curve. His class was one that i looked forward to everyday because his lecturing is enjoyable and funny. Also, he is genuinely interested in his students. I would definitely take this class from him.

definitely not an easy class at all!! tons and tons of reading and sooo much memorization. tods super cool though. he really tries to get to know his students and makes it mandatory for you to go to coffee with him at the beginning of the quarter. great examples, you can tell he knows what hes talking about. its just really hard.
Great class, not an easy class, requires a lot of hard work, memorization, reading, and you must attend all the lectures, but definitely worth it.

Tod is one of the best professors at UW.  His humor, intelligence, and real life examples keep class entertaining.  Hard class, but if you study a lot you will do well.  You get out of it what you put into it.

The best professor I have ever encountered. The material requires a lot of memorization, but Tod makes the subject incredibly entertaining through his stories. He honestly cares about his students, during and after they take the course.
REALLY HARD CLASS, LOTS OF MEMORIZATION AND BEING ABLE TO APPLY THEM TO REAL LIFE SCENARIOS (AKA ESSAY QUESTIONS), FUN TEACHER, STUDY ALOT
not an easy, easy class. but he's a pretty cool guy. his pop quizzes are a killer though - know all the vocab.
Tod will be one of your most likeable teachers at the UW.  He is funny, witty and entertaining while at the same time never losing your respect for his intelligence.
Great class made better by a very interested and caring professor. Definately recommended esp. for non-business students wanting to get an overview of the law and our legal system.
freely gives out letters of recommendation

This guy is my hero.  He takes all of his students out for coffee.  He gets to know all of his students and he does an amazing job of portraying the material so all can understand.  he one of the, if not the best professor i have ever had.
Probably one of the best teachers. Don't be dissuaded by the evening classes. It is definitely worth it.
very engaging
Great instructor. Current prosecuting attorney. Very clear and precise. Course pack has all the lecture notes. Entertaining and interesting. Highly reccomended.
I loved professor loveless, my goat. always detailed what the tests would look like and gave a ton of resources for you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, 100% recommend. I didn't read the textbook, as the lectures were enough. Gives extra credit on homework if completed early and if you answer a question during Test Prep section. Very caring person, office hours are a great time to do homework. About 3 homework assignments each week and takes ~6 hours total.
His classes will not be easy, but he will support you the whole way through. professor Loveless values hard work and dedication in a way I have not seen before.

Very good lecturer with clear, consistent expectations for exams. His website had many helpful resources, including a large test archive that closely matched actual exams. WebAssign offered extra credit for early completion. I enjoyed attending class and found his real world examples engaging and helpful.

His online resources are amazing, and if you put effort, you'll do well! Loveless is caring and helpful, and we'll get you where you need to be if you put in the work. Math has always been hard for me but I found it doable and did alright.

Professor Loveless was great! Loved his resource page, engaging lectures, and definitely motivated me to show up to my 8:30 lecture. There's extra credit for homework if you start it two days early, but it is capped at 100% in the end. His midterms are on the easier side, and the test prep and worksheets given were very helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very good and interactive lecturer, homework is not too much but can be very challenging at times. Exams are reasonable difficulty, just a really difficult course.

Everyone uses his materials even when they don't have him. His online resources are detailed and well thought out. I really thought I was bad at math and not cut out for my major until my class with him. He makes learning math enjoyable and I look forward to what he will teach next. Attendance isn't mandatory but you will want to be there anyways!
Dr. Loveless, THE GREATEST PROFESSOR. Even though my major doesn't require 126, I'm starting to consider continuing to take his class

Loveless has been my favorite professor of all time at UW. Although 125 is a difficult course, Loveless truly has almost an infinite amount of resources for students to use. His lectures are clear, thoughtful, and engaging which genuinley makes me motivated to attend my 9:30 lecture with him. 10/10 prof.

Super nice and funny guy. You can tell he is passionate about his teaching and his students, and actually listens to feedback. The difficulty is pretty average for a math class but there are a ton of resources if you make an effort to use them.

I love his course its, very engaging and pretty funny, I can easily pay attention to his lectures. 
Everything is posted online, including recordings. 
He posts homework help and videos on the discussion board, and has exam archives and study material.
He is passionate and very willing to help.
Highest moutain, longest river

Take his class, period. I didn't even have Loveless for this class but his lectures are so good I attended anyway. It is clear that he genuinely cares about his students more than any professor should. He has tons of extra resources for outside of class, responds to students personally, and spends hours outside of class working on examples.
God among men when it comes to teaching calculus.

Regardless of which class you're taking in the sequence, he is a phenomenal professor. He walks through problems to completion and teaches at a steady pace, which is hard to come by at UW. Always opt for Loveless if you can; he is your best chance to truly understand calculus. I'd even go so far as to say he's the best professor I've had here.

I hate math with every fiber of my being but taking 120 with him actually wasn't too bad. I will say that there is a tonnn of hw, but he gives extra credit if you complete it 2 days early. I got the worst grade I've ever gotten in this class but that one's on me not him😔. His lectures are super engaging and informative and he always cracked jokes!
Andrew Loveless, you are my goat.

Holy, moly. Dr. Loveless is such a good professor. He's a funny guy, so its easy to stay engaged with the material covered in lecture. He'll stay up late at night answering every single question on the discussion board. I once noticed three people stuck on the same problem, so he made three separate videos for each person. Wow.

I did not click with his teaching style but others like him. I found that his lectures were not very clear. He teaches the very basic concept in class, but the homework expands on concepts in ways that are not on exams. Lots of tedious homework, but ygives EC if you submit it before 2 days before the deadline. Nice person, office hours are good.

The course its self was way more in-depth than any high school precalc class I had taken. He is a very kind, caring, goofy, and approachable teacher. He truly cares a lot about his students and as long as you attend office hours somewhat regularly, u will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Loveless is very nice guy with a lot of dad jokes. In Math 120, if you finished the homework 2 days before the deadline you get extra credit. Homework levels was very reasonable. I never felt overwhelmed in his class. He holds office hours really frequently which is very nice.  He really loves his job and that honestly makes his class the best.

Funny, kind, and willing to work with you no matter how little you may be able to grasp the concepts he's teaching. Even after doing absolutely terribly in his class, I love Dr. Loveless and would 1000% take classes taught by him again.

Outstanding professor. He really cares about his students and tries his best in every lecture. I skipped most of the lectures due to my knowledge of the material, yet the archive helps me a lot when preparing for exams. One thing I like most is that he uploads short but very useful summary videos to YouTube for us to study.

This was Dr. Loveless' first time teaching summer quarter and he absolutely knocked it outta the park. UW in the summer is usually pretty sleepy but it was so great to have a professor be so active and provide so many learning resources, I truly felt supported and always looked forward to coming to class. Thank you Dr. Loveless!

Absolutely amazing prof that genuinely cares about the students and that they actually understand. Took this as an online summer class but he was super accessible online (discussion board, YT, zoom reviews) so I was still able to keep up. The sheer amount of explaining he does for every question we can ask is proof he's absolutely goated!!

He explains well, but I'm taking his summer 126 course and he has all these office hours, but they aren't  helpful because he spends 30 minutes with 1 student and there is no time for me to ask questions. Office hours should be in person only, or he should give shorter responses or answer questions not related to the Course outside of office hours.
reminds me of my funny HS math teacher.
Just an all-around awesome guy.

Hands down the best prof I've ever had. The course content is a bit tough as it is calc, but he is INSANELY good at explaining tough concepts and is so so experienced. Definitely the best teacher I have had, especially in the calc series. Can't recommend him enough. Super easy to talk to, super helpful, and just a great guy. Highly recommend!

Certainly the best professor I've ever had, amazing lectures and truly cares about his students. He's incredibly active online and his YouTube videos and discussion posts will help you master any topic in the course. Has tons of office hours and will take the time to explain concepts to you till you understand them. Can't recommend enough, the 🐐

Legitimately the best professor I have ever had. Great lectures, clear requirements on homework, fair grading on exams. Still difficult, but that is the nature of the course. Hands down the most caring and dedicated professor I have ever had. If you put in the work you will succeed.
One of the best teachers I have ever had. Cares about his students learning and grades very fairly. Exam questions are always from lecture/homework content. Provides many resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great guy. big fan.

Picture this: two nights before the midterm, I was cooked. I went to bed praying I'd pass. The next morning, I suddenly understood the content. It had to be a miracle; Dr. Loveless must've visited me in my sleep. Ultimately, he's one of the few professors who truly cares about his content and students. I couldn't ask for a more Goated professor. 🐐

He's not a bad professor, but not what the ratings imply. I took Calc 3 after not taking Calc in a year or 2, very bad decision. He skips over steps he deems "necessary," which makes it hard to follow for someone who is practically relearning old concepts. He is very messy and unorganized, adding to why it's hard to follow. Offers office hours.

I have so much respect for how much Dr. Loveless goes out of his way to make sure his students are able to understand the material he's covering. Don't get me wrong the exams are hard, but you get out how much you put in which is rare for a math class at UW. He's goated, if you can take the whole CALC series with him.

Awesome time learning from him in the 100 calculus series, I am forever grateful that I was able to have in my first quarter at UW, his tests can be difficult but the learning behind them and the strategies to approach them that he covers are intuitive and easy to follow.
Great professor! Truly cares about his students, and the structure and material of the class are understandable. The best professor Ive taken so far at UW
It's too bad so many kids who are terrible at math take their frustration out on Dr. Loveless, because he is the goat.
I have him for Math 126 and genuinely one of the best professors I have had for the math intro series (along with Nichifor). Hilarious and cares for his students (amazing resources).

Professor Loveless genuinely cares that every student enjoys learning. While the knowledge I came into math 125 with made the class relatively easy for me, the key to success is indeed going through old exams. Follow his advice regarding exam studying. If you do so correctly, you'll find that his exams are predictable. Great professor!

Genuinely one of the best professors out there I think. He cares so much about his class and his students and has a bunch of really great + well-thought-out study materials. Would absolutely recommend.

He is as great as everyone says. Seriously the best math professor I have ever had, he explains things well, in-detail, and puts in so much effort so that students can understand everything he teaches. He was on vacation and STILL put out videos explaining the intuition behind homework problems when he saw that people needed help. Amazing.
Dr. Loveless is the goat, he actually cares about each and every one of his students. He uploads a lot of review material and extra practice.

Omg professor loveless is saving so many students every day, he's not even teaching 125 this quarter but he's still posting life saving lectures to help students prepare their finals and to understand concepts, I so much appreciate it, I think every department need someone like him
omg he saved my life, he's not even teaching math125 this quarter but he still post life saving lectures for final reviews and I so appreciate it, I think every department needs a Professor loveless
Literally my goat

Didnt have him as my prof but he hosted review sessions before exams even though he wasnt currently teaching it. His youtube videos are so helpful! Watching his videos taught me so much more than my actual prof. He deserves everything and I hope he gets a raise. Hes the GOAT.

This is a man in it for the love of the game. Tons of extra resources out of class to help you out. He is the absolute GOAT at mathematics. Stuctures his lectures very clearly

One time I swear on my life I was studying and I heard a "ba-a-a-a-a" down the hall and I thought to myself "is that a goat? and I got up and turns out it was just Loveless
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is such an amazing professor, probably the best professor I have ever had. I noticed how enthusiastic he is whenever he answered students' questions in the MIDDLE of talking. What's more, hadn't it been for his explanations, I would have never been able to understand MATH 126 content as well. Hope to take his class again sometime!!

I've never had Dr. Loveless as a professor, but he provides incredible resources for students in math courses, even those he isn't teaching that quarter. I recently attended a review session he hosted for Math 126, despite him not teaching the class, simply because he wanted to help. If you have the chance, I highly recommend taking his class!

I had Prof Loveless fall quarter for math 125 and he was amazing! He spent a lot of his free time holding review sessions. He has an amazing website with a lot of resources. Now, I am in math 126 for winter quarter and he followed up to everyone and held a math 126 review session even when we are not his students anymore. Most caring prof ever.

Andy Loveless is the greatest professor I've had at UW so far. Math 125 is very difficult but Andy does his best to make it manageable. He has made countless resources to support students through the calc series and even held review sessions for 126 when he wasn't teaching it. Really great guy!
Genuinely the most caring professor, he dedicates so much time to his students its wild. Dr. Loveless you are loved. The goat.
So so good!

Dr. Loveless was an amazing professor. He cares a ton about every student and their success, and is constantly pushing himself to improve, and help students improve. I would love to have him again.

Dr. Loveless cares a lot about his class, as shown in the abundance of support videos he provides. Please take his class guys, we love you Dr. Loveless, you are so friendly and caring, worrying about your students a lots. I love Dr. Loveless's teaching style and his small videos for explanations. He is funny and cares about your grade, even your mental health. He is the best math professor I've ever met. I hope people can treat him like he treats us! Love him!

Prof. Loveless is an amazing professor and his lecture is very fun to go to. He has his own website that provide tons of resources such as review notes or past exams to practice. Absolutely loved having loveless as a professor. Friendliest professor I have had yet he is such a sweet heart and cares so much about students. Andy Loveless is one of the best professors at UW. His extra materials to supplement the lectures were super helpful. If it were not for him, I would not have been able to succeed in this class. He is also incredibly funny. Once a Math 126 fan, always a Math 126 fan.

one of the best professors in the math department. prepares everyone for the webassign homework questions by going over some in class which is very helpful, and always gives detailed answers on every single question posted on discussion board. do not miss your chance to take a class with this professor!!
greatest professor of all time. made math 126 the easiest of the entire calculus series. take this professor for not only a free 4.0, but also for the knowledge you gain from his teaching style

Our class was very discussion-heavy. Dr. Babbie doesn't do much busywork, which I appreciate, just larger projects that we edit throughout the quarter. He is also very understanding with deadlines/extensions.
The kindest gentlest soul of any professor I've had. Anyone who leaves a bad review on this man is an opp and cannot be trusted with even the simplest tasks.

I normally don't write reviews, but Dr. Babbie is genuinely one of the best professors I've had at UW. reviews.comment: Such a nice and caring professor, very lenient with deadlines and grades as long as you communicate with him. Participation matters during class and discussions for homework, but it's light work, and you have creative freedom. He cares more about you putting in effort than the quality of the work, and he's very understanding. No exams.

I love Professor Babbie! I really enjoyed this class and his lectures. He's really funny and kind and he cares about your learning a lot. As long as you participate a bit in class and submit assignments you can easily get 100% in this class. We had weekly online discussions and 2 papers, all of which were basically graded by completion.

He grades on how much effort you put into the projects and not how well you write. Two projects in one quarter, no tests, have chance to revise to get a higher grade. Very friendly and easy-going, mostly supports all of your ideas.

Dr. Babbie was undoubtedly excellent. He clearly wants all students to succeed. He is understanding and caring, especially when unexpected things happen to you, and you need an extension. I was not very excited about the course topic, but his "off-topic" rants were very (and far more) interesting. Getting a 4.0 should be easy as long as you try.

Dr. Babbie one of my favorite professors! Be aware of class discussions and weekly discussion posts as well as papers. also, 1:1 meeting to discuss what we are planning to write about (u wouldn't waste ur time on a wrong draft + know what we were asked for) and allow us to ask as much of questions (which not all professors do). no regrets the BEST.

I was required to take ENVH 320 (technical occupational writing class) with Tyler. After 4 years at this university I can say he is one of my all-time favorite professors. Cool dude.

Amazing professor. Second time taking one of his classes. Incredibly understanding and flexible. Gives lots of feedback on papers and encourages improvement. Fun lectures and exciting materials. Would recommend any class that he teaches!

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, second time I am taking his class. Interesting lectures, he's really passionate about what he teaches. The class is really fun and there aren't too many assignments, definitely recommend if you need a W credit.

Tyler is the most chill and enthusiastic teacher I've met at UW so far! I thought ENGL 131 would be a standard gen ed class like all my friends were talking about when they took it, but this blew me away. Tyler is so into the things he teaches, and the readings he assigns are never unreasonably long. Thought provoking readings, fun discussions.

One of the best at UW, no doubt. Such a fun class and really makes it so that all students voices are heard. Very chill and willing to go off topic during lectures. Low pressure writing style, allows you to write in whatever style and however much you want. Coming from a fellow student, one of the best at UW!

Such a kind, gentle, caring person. In order to do well in his class, make sure to attend lectures and do the readings, but otherwise you'll have some of the most fun times in his lecture. Lectures are fun, and engaging, and he does his best to incorporate class ideas into lectures. One of the best profs no doubt I've had at UW, you'd be missing out if you don't take him.

He was a great professor and always enjoyed going to class and participating in discussions. I took his class for the W credit requirement but I had so much fun, and would definitely take more classes with him. *took engl 297 concurrently with clas 430
has super interesting lectures about the readings and clearly enthusiastic about what he does. very flexible grader; allows submissions + revisions up to finals week.
he's truly the best, i really recommend his class. he clearly cares about his students.

Dr. Babbie is one of my favorite prof at the UW. He's kind and soft-spoken but he also gives great feedback on your writing. Everything you would want in an English prof!

Dr. Babbie was one of my favorite professors I have had at this school. He is so passionate about what he is teaching, and he will do whatever is necessary to help you get the grade you want. I don't understand why Dr. Babbie doesn't have a perfect score on here. Honestly, the fact that people complain about his teaching style is more reflective of the kinds of students that are writing the reviews than on what kind of professor Dr. Babbie is. If you appreciate passion in your professors and care about learning, he's the best there is.

I took Dr. Babbie Spring 2020 so it was online but I loved him as a teacher. I was a little worried with the rating he has but he was great. Dr. Urbanski is a wonderful professor! I have taken two classes with her and they have both been great. Her lectures are entertaining and the tests are easy (if you study minimally and pay attention). I highly recommend her for history classes!

Professor Urbanski is an amazing teacher who makes history interesting to learn, no matter how dry it can get. She is a wonderful person who is passionate about teaching. She makes it very easy to excel in her class. Two papers, one midterm, one final. Both tests are open note. reviews.comment: She is a really delightful person, and you can tell that she is passionate about the topic. If you take the class, the textbook isn't really necessary, but the other books are. I never read the textbook and got by with a 95

reviews.comment: Prof. Urbanski is EXCELLENT! The lectures are very well-organized, she follows her syllabus, and she covers the course content within the allotted class period. Her class material gives a good overview of historical people, places, and events. Take her class for INSPIRATION, she makes history comes alive!

Professor Urbanski made a subject I had no interest in, the late Middle Ages, something entertaining and fun. You can tell that she cares a lot about what she's teaching, her enthusiasm is infectious. A midterm, final, and 2 papers. As well as 4 reading assignments. Don't buy the textbook if you don't want to, her lectures are great on their own.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Urbanski's class was by far one of my favorites at the UW. This is mostly due to her kind nature, her great sense of humor in lecture, and the passion she has for what she's teaching. She also has great TAs. At one time I had a bunch of assignments and when I told her this she gave me an extension without any hesitation.

One of my favorite professors so far. She is very energetic and engages you through her lecture which makes the content easier to understand. She knows what she is talking about and is great at communicating her knowledge. You do have to show up to the lectures and do the assignments but if you're interested in the content it really isn't that bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Charity's classes are awesome! She really makes the history come alive. I couldn't wait for the next class each time to find out more about what we were reading. She has very clear grading criteria and expectations and is fair. Highly recommend!

Professor Urbanski is hilarious and obviously loves teaching what she teaches. The lectures are a little fast paced, so be ready to write a fair bit. You also get the majority of your information from lecture. The readings can be long, but she does an excellent job of explaining them. I've had her for two classes, and am taking another!

Prof. Urbanski made what I thought would be a boring class, interesting and engaging. She is flexible and great at answering questions. Even though her tests and quiz sections were relatively easy, I learned so much more in this class than any of my other ones. I definitely recommend! However, get all the books and prepare to read and go to class!

reviews.comment: Urbanski is an amazing teacher who tries to make learning about history interesting. The lectures can get a bit dry and her powerpoint are difficult to follow but overall it's not a big deal. The exams have complete study guides you can use while taking. The 2 papers were the most difficult; although, the first one does have an optional re-write.
Prof. Urbanski is an amazing teacher. Definitely take a class with her if you have any interest at all in medieval history. She cares about students and you will enjoy coming to class!

Professor Urbanski is a fantastic lecturer. The two tests are very easy and if you do the readings and show up to quiz section the two essays are not that hard. She will always answer your questions and is very friendly. I would definitely take more of her classes. Overall a fun and easy A.

The course material is interesting and the readings are (usually) interesting as well. However, she has trouble keeping her lectures on time. By our midterm she was a full day behind in lecture. This is related to her tendency to go off on random tangents and take all questions.

This class you definitely have to show up to lectures and you have to do the assigned readings. I only had two tests and two papers. For each of the tests I got a study guide that she made the test from and got to take a full sheet of notes. It's an easy class if you show up and do the work. She is also a great lecturer, very clear voice.

She is a fantastic and engaging lecturer. For the midterm and final, she gives all possible exam questions *and* allows a typed, front and back cheat sheet. Makes it sound easy, right? Well, the analysis is what's emphasized. You really need to actually learn the material to do well, so you can synthesize the info. Paper grading is fair.

Took her for both HSTAM 112 and 365. She is easily the best lecturer I've had in my time at UW. Exams are easy but the papers she assigns sometimes aen't. That said, if you ask for help you will get it and she is always happy to help so long as it is not a question easily answerable by looking at the syllabus or the assignment handout
She is my favorite professor. Her enthusiasm really makes 2 hours go by fast. Highly recommended.
Lectures clarified reading material; good at emphasizing the big questions and issues; terrifically knowledgable; never arrogant or negative; excellent at encouraging and dealing with questions .
Great professor, really helpful, take this class if you can.

Urbanski is great. Like most history professors she has her quirks and her off days but overall she's a great professor. Really passionate about the topics and extremely helpful in showing you how to improve your writing. The class involves a lot of reading but she's good about clarifying anything that's confusing. Highly recommend.

Lectures were entertaining; however, breadth was emphasized over depth to a serious fault. Rigorous grading on essays and tests. Easy in-class reading questions rewarded student participation. Granted extensions. Friendly but firm.
Notes allowed for midterm and final. As long as you go to lecture and do the reading it is very easy. Be warned that it is a lot of reading. Make sure you start the note sheet early enough.
Funny and enthusiastic. Easy class with notes available for tests, she really just cares about you retaining your knowledge.

GREAT professor. Everything is very straight forward. If you do what she assigns, you will well. Class is mandatory, as it only meets once a week. She is super nice and has a great sense of humor. Super knowledgeable! Gives extremely helpful feedback on assignments. Take classes by her, she rocks!

Ok, Urbanski is extremely nice and very willing to be of extra help via office hrs and email. She is a great lecturer and funny as well, only negative thing is her course is more geared toward writing analyses rather than history, so if you aren't a strong writer, I would avoid. Other than that, she is awesome.

AMAZING professor.  I recommend that anyone with a love of Medieval history take her classes. She has a wicked sense of humor and if you ask questions she will go out of her way to explain clearly and concisely her arguments.

I personally wasn't very interested in the subject material, but she's really funny which makes lectures fun. She likes playing clips of tv shows and movies which is also nice! There's a lot of quiz section readings, but overall, the class is pretty easy and manageable.

Professor Urbanski's lectures are very interesting, and I really enjoyed them. There is a lot of reading, though. The readings combined with the two pretty long essays make this class a fair amount of work. It's definitely doable to get a 3.6ish though.

Very poorly organized class. Over half of your grade is dependent on essays, then on the very last day of class they teach you how they want them written. Thanks! Too little, too late. Makes you lose interest in the medieval period quickly.

Prof Urbanski's lectures are interesting but the emphasis on essays makes the class less about history and more about history writing than would be expected. Also, having taken both 300-level class and the 100-level class, I can say that the 100 level was much harder.
Lots of reading, but her tests are fair and her lectures are interesting.

One of the best professors I've had at UW. Class was enjoyable everyday, she knew her stuff...her powerpoints keep you attentive, and you have plenty of time to complete the assignments. Highly recommend.

Professor Urbanski is pretty fun and she has a sense of humor which makes class that much better, especially for the kind of work she does. She makes Monty Python jokes a fair amount. She can be disorganized though so you might need a little patience in her classes, such as syllabus changes and accidentally giving readings in medieval French.

I thought I was really going to enjoy the subject before starting the class, but the focus was not the student learning the material. She seemed to have little interest in whether or not we learned anything or enjoyed the class.

I learned a lot from lectures, but none of that was reflected into my grade. There's a disproportionate amount of emphasis placed on quiz section reading, so lectures were useless. They were painful anyway bc she would never stop a certain few people from taking up class time asking unrelated questions to show off. We ended up a week behind.

She is nice and passionate about the topic. But it is a hard class with a lottt of work. You do have to show up to class, and she calls on people randomly. Also sooo much boring reading. I don't know when teachers are going to understand that students do not enjoy or retain knowledge by reading 50 pages of a textbook.

Caley Cook is a highly-skilled journalist and one of the best professors I've had in the JPIC program. She taught me how to tell compelling stories through down to earth, simple language, and provided constant positive reinforcement in the feedback process. I would recommend her to any aspiring journalist who's looking to improve their craft.

I had Prof. Cook for 440 and Video Production. She is super approachable and truly wants the best for her students. If you are good at staying on top of your work, her class will be a breeze. She was my favorite teacher at UW because she pushed me to not just get an A, but create work that I am proud of. Take her class, you will learn a LOT.

Prof cook is my favorite teacher at UW. The effort level she provides to stay current, providing real world examples for class is unmatched. The content is fascinating and the exams are extremely manageable if you listen in class. She is so approachable and helpful inside & outside of class. Cook is an amazing teacher and person! Highly recommend!

News lab was scary yet transformative. Despite fears about deadlines/interviews, her engaging teaching made learning enjoyable. She prioritized student wellness, trusted our potential, and was honest & approachable. Her real-world experience & network enriched the class, helping students like me publish stories and grow personally/professionally.

Best professor at UW. Brings real-world legal and journalism expertise to class. Her engaging lectures make complex subjects like Mass Media Law understandable. She's genuine and supportive of her students! Her confidence and passion transform potentially intimidating material into an engaging learning experience. Opt out cold-call option too!

I took this class because I wanted to have more skills in videography and I left with more than that. I gained a greater appreciation with the craft and a better understanding of what kind of a journalist I wanted to become. I'm always going to be grateful of how graceful of how she guided me to become a better reporter!

Professor Cook is one of the best profs I've ever had. It's obvious to see her care for students and their learning. She views each of us as students and humans who have lives outside the confines of her class. That to say, she has clear and high standards, but not impossible. Engage in class, communicate with her & you'll be fine! And learn a TON!

this class is hard- I read everything and showed up to every lecture and took every note. it is A LOT. that being said, its been an incredibly interesting and informative class. I was really intimidated, but I put in the work and its paid off. prof Cook's lectures are actually really interesting and if you pay attention you will do well. good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Cook is AWESOME! After reading other reviews of COM440 I was definitely scared to take it, but I highly recommend it! The "exams" are somewhat difficult but if you attend class and put in the slightest bit of effort you will get a great grade! She is super kind and understanding. It is clear that she wants everyone in her class to pass!

Caley can be a bit intimidating at times, but she will make you such a better journalist. Know your stuff, do good work, and she will reward you with a good grade. You're in college, nobody is going to hold your hand. She is tough, but you will have editors and bosses like her in the future if you stick with it. 

Try hard, and you'll do fine.

Dr.Cook is tough! This was by far one of the hardest classes I've ever taken. I had to fight for my life daily to get that A. Make sure to read and take lots of notes. I hope for future classes you get lucky with a good TA because mine was amazing. The final had me crying for days on end, but I lived. Try your best and you'll succeed!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Caley's a tough grader but accessible outside class. You have to read the textbook for a better chance to get an A, and go to quiz sections to do good on weekly essays. The final will be hard but you'll do good if you have an outline ready to go. Quizzes aren't bad bc its open book. If you have a grade you think is wrong, tell her- she'll regrade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Caley Cook made me question whether I wanted to continue in my major and made me not want to pursue journalism. Every class included a snarky or rude comment spoken in a condescending manner and I've never had more anxiety being near a professor. RUDEST PROFESSOR IVE EVER HAD

While the course content is interesting, Caley's grading significantly dampened my experience. She is a hard grader, which I would not have a problem with if her grading criteria were made more transparent. Her grading feels quite nitpicky, and I can never quite figure out what she is specificially looking for in an assignment.

Caley is straight-forward and she points out the flaws of your work directly without any sugarcoating. But she's definitely the most dedicated professor I've ever met. She spends weekends to help us edit our stories and she's very responsive. You'll learning a lot if you take 362 with her. It's not an easy class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I've taken more than six COM courses so far, this is the worst. Caley was impatiently bad tempered, be it in person or by email. She is straightforward but without understanding what help you may need to go through difficult assignments and tests. Not worth the stress :(

This class is a total nightmare. The assignments take forever and even with diligent notes the tests are nitpicky and the lectures dont line up. Seemed like there was no communication between my TA and Caley and she was often snarky and in a mood, with answers that were highly unhelpful. Stay away at all costs, its impossible to succeed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was my favorite comm class ever. Not too hard if you put the work in.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Cook definitely knew what she was talking about, and explained the subject matter very well. Tests can be hard but it's not that difficult to do well if you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof cook is the BEST teacher I had. She is very knowledgeable on mass media law and how it has an impact on first amendment, courts, etc. Definitely recommend!

Avoid at all costs!!! While the content is interesting, the class is impossible to do well in as she lectures at you without helping to explain anything and never provides clear criteria on what you're graded on. She is super nitpicky and will just give you 0's if you don't define everything and plainly state it. Got over 85% which was barely a 2.5

Professor Cook was the reason I questioned my major a quarter before graduation. She was in a stressed/bad mood most of the time, and gave harsh/snarky comments all the time. She WILL have favorites and mistakes are traumatizing to go through with her. Even my TA disliked her and told me she got anxiety being around her.

Caley is a great and knowledgable journalist, but she will not help you unless you ask for it. ALWAYS CHECK THE SYLLABUS BEFORE YOU ASK HER ANYTHING. The grading and editing is pretty harsh, but COM 362 is probably the most important and applicable class in the journalism series.

I also studied abroad with Caley. Unfortunately, Caley was the worst professor I have ever had the displeasure of working with. I have never been so disrespected nor would I ever recommend taking one of her classes. Steer clear.

Experience is the hardest teacher and Professor Cook will make sure  you get plenty of that. You'll be pounding the pavement and getting stories published, but make a mistake and you'll pay for it. Little to no reading, but read enough to ask good questions and Cook will be there for you no more, no less. READ. THE. SYLLABUS.

I spent the last quarter on a UW study abroad program with Caley. Getting used to life in a foreign country was stressful enough and I felt very discouraged by her teaching style. Material was not conveyed very clearly and there was no room for mistakes. If you're looking for compassion or have a question, maybe wait until she is having a good day

I agree that syllabus details were confusing and deadlines/expectations were unclear. Great as a teacher and very knowledgable, but not very helpful and expects you to be able to do everything on your own with very little advice.

She's very engaging and passionate about what she does. Reading is necessary to excel in this class. She gives take home quizzes each week that help with the reading process. Great teacher, but challenging class.

She's one of the best professors I've had at UW. Her lectures are engaging and she's hilarious, i look forward to coming to class everyday. The chapter worksheets are helpful to learn from the text chapters without reading the whole thing. If you pay attention in class and do work you will do great in this class!

Really energetic and loves to try and connect with the students as much as possible, so much its annoying by the end of the quarter. She comes off a pretty nice and caring about each student most of the time but definitely has a cranky side. Moves with quick pace, too much readings, above average difficulty on exams and study guides aren't the best

Expectations and syllabus were confusing. You're expected to do a lot of things without really being told how. Forget some minor rule and you may be harshly chastised. You know how some teachers offer extra advice, help and general inspiration? You probably won't find that here.

I took this class over the summer so it was condensed. There was a lot of reading however that may be due to the shorter schedule, the professor however was helpful and graded very fairly in my opinion. Expectations were pretty clear. As long as you pay attention and do the assigned work you should do well with this prof.

Enthusiastic, young, friendly, but a hard grader. Can get snarky at times. Gives you pop quizzes on a week's worth of news, really hard to get a good grade. Has pointless, stressful, on-the spot class activities. You'll learn a lot but you won't enjoy yourself.

CC is great to work with, she has a ton of knowledge on the subject and occupation or journalism. Uses prezzies every class, uploads them at the end of the day, hand writes some notes on the board, lost of discussion, 5 short writing assignments, 2 exams, and 1 final paper. I found the information very interesting, would be hard if you do not.

Daniel is very nice professor but the content is heavy but, in order to pass the class, do lots of EOC's they help a lot witht the finals and midterm. Finals and midterms are nothing like the practice exams he gives out. I did lots of outside of work and still got a low grade, did not enjoy him that much but it was okay i guess.

Take Tylenol before exams and prepare for headache. The practice exams were nothing like the real one (time limit was also tough). Slideshow was pretty unorganized, but he was really funny and had cool in-class demonstrations. READ THE TEXTBOOK!! Lecture makes a lot more sense after reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course is challenging and this is going to be true with any CHEM 152 professor. Chiu is a very funny professor and often includes demos which are enjoyable, but he doesn't make the content accessible and I had to do a lot of work outside of class. That being said if you stay on top of the EOC's, lab and ALEKS you can do well.

Chem 152 is a difficult class content wise, and with prof. Chiu you need to put in a LOT of outside effort. Chiu does explain the concepts, but will sometimes skip over important details. Difficult and confusing exams, but okay partial credit. Work on the end of section textbook problems (not the challenge probs) to do well in class + worksheets.

His teaching style worked well for me. I had a 2.8 in 142 and my grade went up to a 3.5 in 152. While he often moves past slides, he does go back to them if they're important. The practice midterms and discussion sections corresponded to the tests. The grading on the tests was fair.

Lectures arn't always very easy to follow and it's not clear what readings he'll cover in each lecture. He has a tendency to lecture pretty fast and assume that once he says something, it is fully grasped, so reading ahead would be a good idea. Tests are pretty straightforward, very similar to practice tests he gives out. Overall not bad.

Tests are difficult, but they are fair and if you do the challenge problems in the textbook you'll be fine. He's really generous on partial credit since the questions are all FRQ and worth about 20 points a piece. He moves fast in lecture so be sure to pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Daniel Chiu is definitely not for every student. The standard deviations on our exams were insanely high, often being around 25, which showed a clear gap in understanding for the majority of people in the course. In lecture, not much is explained about the concepts taught. Practice exams and DS worksheets are NOT representative of what is tested.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chiu is very simply a little evil but also helpful and funny. This man loves to blow things up and give the least helpful answers possible in class. However, his office hours are good and he is a fair grader. Prepare to be confused for 50 minutes and then watch him make thermite at the end of class. His research is also really interesting.

I understood his lectures and they were pretty clear. Practice problems in the lectures made sense too. The issue is the fact that practice exams look absolutely nothing like the actual exams. Weekly worksheets and practice problems help to an extent but again nothing on the exams look anything like it. He made me consider switching majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His class sucks. Never take it!! His tests are incredibly hard and don't have much in common with the practice exams. His lectures are very boring, and he doesn't care about students' understanding.

Not sure why so many people are not a fan of him. In my opinion he is a harsh but fair grader. He only teaches you what you need to know, and he only tests on what he teaches. The labs line up with the units (unlike chem 142) and ALEKS is super relevant and helpful. He's definitely for a certain kind of student, but I like him.

TLDR: Wait a quarter and take someone else's 152 class if you can - 

In lecture he tends to talk about things in concept and his examples in practice aren't very clear either. Beware of the midterms, they are only 5 questions. My most recent one was 80% on a topic that he barely covered in any of the worksheets and homework, so it felt very unfair

Insane tests, fully FRQ and difficult. Very bad lecturer, don't even come to class, you'll learn more from the textbook or Google. Ruined my freshman year with how tough the grading was in this class. Take any other professor for this class. The stories about him are true.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Where do I even start... I am so glad I got this man as my prof. This guy is very respectable and seems like a good man. His practice tests are super helpful, and he is willing to help us learn. Also, I loved the in-class activities.
Highly recommend. Great guy, chill, absolute GOAT
This guy was awesome. Very chill. His tests are very similar to the practice tests. Also, for most of his lectures he did in-class demos which were awesome. Highly recommend.
He was great

His lectures are very confusing and unclear. He somehow goes both too slow and too fast at the same time, and jumps around slides before you can finish reading them. His tests were fair in my opinion. The questions are free response word problems and don't test you on conceptual ideas/definitions, just practice problems. Not a great teacher overall
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Organic chemist clears

Chem 152 is a very information-heavy subject and the lectures reflect this. Highly recommend attending lecture as the course is fast paced and dense. I personally did not use the textbook but many others recommend to read. Practice tests accurately reflect exam material. Lectures can get boring so make sure you pay attention.

Hardest exams I've ever seen. The grading was only determined by the exams as well as only like 10% for aleks. Lectures are very hard to follow as well. Overall a terrible experience 0/10 would not recommended if you can get any other professor try to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures can be hard to follow at times but if you are actively listening he makes sense. I have ADHD and so at times this is hard but the material/questions he goes over in class and the material we are given in quiz section are genuinely representative of the questions we are asked on exams.

Daniel Chiu teaches at a fast pace but if you keep up with the reading, pay attention in lecture, AND DO WHAT HE SAYS, you will do fine. He repeated over and over again to practice problems as preparation, and he seems to take his test questions from the back of the book problems which he led us to do. Very manageable, but definitely still hard.

Lectures are pretty boring but not required. Keep up with ALEKs and you should be good, make sure you do a LOT of review though to be able to solve all types of questions. Start making your note sheet for the exams early on so you don't get confused. Also study using the worksheets. Exams are difficult, make sure you understand the concepts.

Lectures are hard to follow and stay engaged in. Explanations are surface level and lots of extra work and self-teaching is needed outside of class to keep up. Tests are all free response and usually pretty tricky in regard to set up.

Lectures aren't great and the class requires outside work to keep up. That being said, tests are fair and align well with class material. They're difficult tests but partial credit is generous. Unfortunately, the textbook is going to be one of your best resources. As long as you keep up with the content, you should do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is a lecture heavy course. If you're confused on a concept during that lecture, he doesn't walk through it. Heto throw everything up on the slides at once and expects you to follow. What I did love about his class is that he allows a full sheat of paper, front and back for both midterms. For the final two pages front/back.

Just read off slides for lecture, tests were difficult, and TAs took weeks to respond to Ed. He is a funny person though and seems really nice, it's just the tests that give him the bad rep. Gives a light ALEKS load and allows cheat sheets on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was alright, the lectures were interesting at the beginning but they got boring due to his monotone voice. He does have good demos and he makes a couple jokes but the exams can be somewhat difficult. He does not respond in the ED Discussions so TA's are lifesavers.

Not the greatest lecturer, but the demos in class are really fun. Follow his advice and do lots of practice problems from the book. The tests are pretty similar to those problems. If you do plenty of practice beyond just aleks, you will do fine. Overall, I think what people say on here is fair, but he doesn't deserve the hate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Daniel Chiu is a funny professor that doesn't deserve the hate he gets. The tests are frqs and always similar to the end of chapter problems. He isn't the greatest lecturer but his office hours are invaluable. As long as you read the book and do practice problems you will do good in his class.

Nice guy but bad at explaining concepts, lectures are not engaging. Tests are really hard and questions are written confusing. He will include questions not covered in lecture on the test. Avoid if u can
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He doesn't teach well at all. He just reads off the slides he has. I learned more from the homework and labs. The practice exams don't help for the tests and sometimes problems on the tests are things that weren't discussed or taught how to solve. Avoid him if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: exams were confusing and not what you expect he expects you to answer them a certain way. Nice guy but lectures were slow and boring, he is not the best at explaining things in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Chiu was a very boring lecturer so go to lectures even if you're gonna fall asleep. His exams were pretty difficult and he expected you to solve each problem his way even if there happened to be another way. He didn't seem to care if his students were learning or understanding the concepts. Questions on ed-discussion were rarely answered.

Chem 152 Spring 2024-2025

Exams were very difficult, lots of curveballs. Very test heavy. 

There were only 5 FRQ questions on each of both midterms & 9 on the finals and didn't even give any practice material for the finals. Class is also curved.

Sometimes TAs take a while to reply on ED Discussion. 1-2 weeks before finals no TAs replied on ED.
You're better off self-studying than attending ANY of his lectures.

Not the greatest lecturer but is incredibly helpful during office hours, if you struggle with anything do not be afraid to approach him! A really sweet guy but his lectures could be better, he goes over practice problems quite quickly so you'll definitely want to review things outside of class. Has a ton of fun demos though!

this class is just really hard. Dr. Chiu is really kind you can't even be mad if you do bad because he is so willing to explain things, talk to him at the end of lecture and go to office hours! he will offer you help, you just have to go get it. lectures can be slow but he will do demos sometimes. nice dude hard class don't fall behind
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I taught myself through the textbook because while he does practice problems, for the overall topics, he doesn't rlly explain what it all means. this is also the first class i ever fell asleep in so hes quite a boring lecturer.  But he does like to answer questions during office hours so dont be scared to go. Overall id try to find another prof
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures can be a bit slow sometimes, but he does demos in class to try and keep it engaging. Sometimes explanations are a little unclear and not thorough enough, but if you ask at the end of class he will always clarify really well. Really easy to ask questions to though and overall nice guy! Keep up with lectures and aleks and you're good.

Chill dude but honestly not good at lecturing. I go to lectures and then review them and still somehow end up having to teach myself everything. He does demos which makes it better. He's funny at least but not good for learning basics I think. Avoid for gen chem.

He's ight. Lectures are boring but so is chem 152. He does demos and tries to make the class more engaging which is nice. Tests are hard and lots of aleks. You kind of have to sell learn a lot specially for tests.

not the nicest gen chem professor, but he's sweet and tests are doable even if you don't study hard. always have fun demo before the end of lecture. never went to his office hour so i thought i would get a 35 on a midterm but it turns out that i got a 80. his rubric save my life so take him if you can.

Lecture materials are very shallow and given examples don't really help with learning topics - Tests are unlike the one practice test given & much more difficult, Homework is tedious, abundant, and overwhelming. Expect to be learning on your own time, and foregoing time with friends to complete absurd amounts of ALEKS modules. Just don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests are impossible.

Chiu's lectures are very confusing. He talks very fast and almost brushes right past things and is hard to follow. You are only graded on ALEKS and Exams so there's little chance to boost your grade outside of exams. However he's very sweet and his in class demos are very fun. His practice exams are also very similar to the exams he gives

Chiu is not a good professer. His tests are hard - which is not what I am complaning about because 152 is a hard course. I will say that his lectures are extremely confusing and hard to follow. He doesn't explain concepts well, is always rushing, and glosses over practice problems. Take 152 with another professer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The tests are open note but borderline impossible. He glosses over major concepts and then shows an extremely hard math problem application of it and expects every one to understand. If no one gets it he makes a passive aggressive comment about how we need to figure it out and then moves on. He also makes the ALEKS due at 5pm which is just dumb.
tests are hard everything else okay for some reason

Chemistry 152 is a tough course, but Professor Chiu's engaging demos and jokes make the class more bearable. Though his lectures can be rushed, his willingness to help in office hours is invaluable. unstuck ai's practice problems were a lifesaver for exam prep.

152 is the hardest gen chem class but Chiu probably isnt to blame. Hes down to earth and in office hours hes great. Lectures may make you want to fall asleep, but his demos are fun, and at least hes easy to talk to. Still a demanding prof and class tho (Final average was 89/200, with a little studying i got 135).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lectures are straight forward and tests are well aligned with worksheets in discussion sections and problems from class. He is also very willing to help with any questions you have!

I personally really liked Dr. Chiu, especially compared to other professors for chemistry here. He is straightforward and clear in his lectures, and still has some sense of humor throughout them. Any class in the chem series is gonna be difficult, fast paced, and have hard tests, and I think that Chiu handles it very well. DONT FALL BEHIND!

Chiu is so fun and silly. His lectures can be a little boring sometimes but he does demos that really lighten it up. He makes an effort for all his students to have the capacity to prepare well for exams and is very good at answering questions. I wish I could take this class again! Would recommend.
Just reads off slides but goes to quick where you can't take notes or understand. Very monotone and not engaging. Have to spend large amount of time teaching myself.

Lectures are not very engaging and hard to follow. He goes through slides too fast for most people (me) to take notes, and he will do a lot of pointing with his laser instead of truly explaining. Admittedly, the content in this class is hard, but I would recommend taking chem 152 with another professor - you have to teach yourself with this prof.

Professor Chiu seems like a great and caring guy and is always making jokes and doing demos for the class. However, the good ends there. He should not be lecturing for a class that is already super difficult, because he simply is a terrible lecturer. He rushes through slides and jumps around while rambling on and making the class more confusing.
