Professor Doty is so sweet and very knowledgeable. Her research is pretty interesting too!

Exciting class, helps you learn many microbio & plant ecophysiology lab/field techniques. The professor's explanations & the hands on activities were invaluable. Dr. Doty let students work in her lab outside of class time, went out of her way to teach us about her exciting field of study & allow us to pursue undergrad research with her.

Very helpful professor who is, most of all, VERY enthusiastic about her field of study, which makes her lectures enthralling. Tests are long but not difficult, though they might require you to think about new matters. I would definitely recommend professor Doty.
BORING! Textbook is all you need.

I took the PNW Ecosystems class with her and Hinkley and had a great experience overall. She does talk quietly, so it is hard to stay awake, but the concepts taught are not all that difficult. Pros: no book, field trips, and an easy grade. Cons: you'll need coffee before class and she writes LONG, but easy, tests (one was ~3 hours)

Can go fast at times but is actually really good at explaining things. Learned a lot from this class. If you study for the tests a little bit they're easy. The Pre-test review sessions were pretty good too.
Don't bother with the lectures, just read the book and come for the tests. She is too boring to stay awake.
Not very interesting, goes through slides kinda quick and isn't very good at answering questions. Tests are easy though.

She will go through the slides in lecture so fast it will make your head spin, and then she wont even post all of the slides online! every other slide someone in the 150 person lecture would ask her to slow down, but she wont.
Very caring and nice prof although the class itself was not useful at all.

Dan is a great professor, respected and has been at UW for over 20+ years. If you get the opportunity to take his class, TA for him, anything, just take it. He has a wealth of knowledge, resources, and is one of the premier faculty at UW. He is such an amazing professor; if you have the opportunity to take a class with him, do not hesitate.

Prof. Grossman was fine, but the class itself was incredibly boring. Personally, I wish I hadn't taken the class, but I understand it could be helpful for others. He did a great job making sure the workload for this class was light and tried to diversify the material. However, I feel like the class could be 50 min instead of 80 min.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was very laid back. Each session was alumni presenting about their career paths and experiences. Prof. Grossman did a great job facilitating the conversation. This class was a great way to learn about companies and careers.

There was a lot of reading in this class, and the articles had unusual jargon terms. But Dan's in-class summaries helped me grasp the material pretty well. However, the articles were often over 20 pages long, and there were many we had to read each week. Considering CSE 480 is just two credits, this was a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: It could sometimes be hard to be motivated to go to seminar especially towards the end of the quarter, but I think Dan did a great job making every meeting worth going to. He is a well-organized and very caring guy.

While the seminar was boring at times, Dan did a good job organizing the sections. We had a mix of group discussions and panelists, including other UW profs. There was a lot of good information presented throughout each session. I also met a lot of new people. Overall, Dan is a good professor and I look forward to taking more CSE classes with him.
Good professor, seminar was a tad boring sometimes, but most of the time it was very fascinating and it was easy so long as you attend and participate
Took Dan for CSE DA seminar, very funny and easy to talk to. Keeps track of time and always makes a seminar that normally sounds boring fun!

Very fun class discussions that weren't stressful with my additional classes for the quarter. In every class, numbered notecards were handed out as you walked in so you talk with new people in discussion groups. Very accepting of student circumstances if you talk with him. He is passionate about the topics he teaches to the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This was a great class. Grossman explains everything well and has reading notes, recordings, and lecture slides if you miss something. There are 7 homeworks a midterm and a final. Each homework has some interesting parts and some tedium. You have to know your stuff for the exams. If you go to lecture you will learn a lot in this class and do well.

Professor Grossman gives great lectures and is clearly very passionate about this course! However, be ready to spend a significant amount of time on homework assignments. Overall, a good class, but very time consuming.

Good and enthusiastic professor, but his 341 class was quite demanding, as it is his favorite course to teach. 

However, if you end up disliking the material, the homeworks can be a ton of busywork, so I would recommend looking through the material and seeing if it seems interesting to you before deciding whether or not to take this course.
amazing lectures but very demanding
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Well Dan is a good professor but his expectations from this class are extreme because he did his PHD in programming languages. The material is very difficult Assignments are exponentially hard. Take his coursera course before this class which is basically the same and I didn't know. Not sure how he can have the same material in UW and coursera
I took him back in 2011, he was simply one of the best professors I had!

Really great guy and a great teacher. You could tell he really cared about the material and students' learning. Homeworks were time-consuming but manageable and helpful. Tests were difficult but if you studied you'd be fine.

The best professor Ive had in uw. He is just amazing. The lectures are indeed interesting and inspirational, I looked forward to each one of his classes all quarter. He is passinate about teaching and jumps up and down about the things he cares about. Highly recommend taking any class with him and in particular 341.
Great guy

Dan's lectures were engaging and extremely helpful. He clearly understood the topics he was lecturing on, and although this was only his second time teaching this particular class, I would not have guessed it if he had not told us. He expressed his intention to give us "hard but fair" exams, which I feel described our midterm and final accurately.

Great professor. CSE 341 was amazing and I'd recommend taking as many classes from Dan as possible. I also had CSE 351 with him. It was his first time teaching it and he still crushed it. He's so good that you'd learn in his class even if you tried not to.

Incredible teacher. Probably the best lecturer I've ever had. He really has good analogies and goes over things with a reasonable pace, but at the same time has the knowledge and experience from being a researcher to give answers to really complex questions. Tests are hard but in an intellectually stimulating way, as they require creative thinking
Dan's an amazing professor. His lectures are fantastic and really helpful, but his exams are also quite difficult.
Amazing class. I think it the Programming Languages class at coursera should be required for every engineer that wants to improve a lot his programming skills
exams were very fair, recommend going to TA hours a lot.
Prof has Analytical and clear delivery. He is excited and engaged by subject.  I learned a lot and enjoyed it.  Lots of time required for lectures + homework + code review.
Very strong and clear in subject. Teaching methodology is too good. Assignment quality and design is flawless.

He writes up notes for us, has videos of himself teaching, and he's relatively clear. I think he's had some planning problems this quarter so our assignments are a little scrunched together towards the end and he tries to pull off too much in lecture. But he's good enough.

He's an okay guy, but his planning skills are truly poor. Towards the end of the quarter, he had to hold us back after the bell to get through the content and lets the TAs cover the content that he can't get to. It's disappointing and insulting to us and the subject. I don't see why he is popular if this is how he "teaches".

Grossman is the best CS professor I have had so far. He is enthusiastic about the class content and very clear. He gets a few laughs every lecture and is generally pleasant to be around. Highly recommend.

If you are a CSE major and you have to look here to hear about how awesome Dan Grossman is, you must be living under a rock :)  He is enthusiastic, helpful, cares about students (he memorizes everyone's name). No books needed- helpful note provided. 341 is more his specialty, but I can't imagine him not being equally effective i

I took Engl 111, the material was interesting and thoughtfully chosen, and I enjoyed the assigned readings. I think she's a very engaging teacher; the two hours flew by. Her feedback is very clear and helpful, and if you need clarification, she's very willing to help! Great Professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: My advice would be to write poems with strange layouts, nonsensical prose, and no capitalization. She doesn't like much else. Duncan's feedback is difficult to get through, and there's a large amount of books for the class (not at the school bookstore) of which very little is discussed. Duncan's fine for the credit, but won't help you improve.

I wasn't wild about Anne and her teaching style. While this was a workshop driven class, I felt there could have been more information shared via lectures. Poetry is also just a very subjective thing, so sometimes it was hard to understand her feedback. You wrote 8ish poems, workshopped 3, and had to submit a portfolio of 5 (I believe).

Anne seems really passionate about her and does a decent job discussing the material of the class. I would recommend taking other professors for this class as her readings can be a lot longer and tedious than other professors and her grading can also be tougher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Laws is genuinely kind, thoughtful, intelligent, and engaging. My only big issue is that essentially all your grade is left up to the midterms and final, so if you're a bad test taker (like me), then your grade might be lower than in other classes because there are few ways to make up for scores with homework or other assignments.
This guy could make Watching Paint Dry 101 the most interesting class you'll ever take. Super passionate and caring professor.

"A nanosecond's a long f*cking time!" said while crouching on top of a desk, was my first introduction to Dr. Laws. He's awesome, super caring (the first professor I've ever had at UW who actually bothered to learn people's names before class started), and makes something already fascinating like astronomy genuinely entertaining to learn about.
literally my goat i shed a few tears in this class not even kidding
Very passionate teacher. There are weekly discussions which you need to make 1 post, 2 replies, and a weekly quiz and you write very freely for the posts. Very easy class for 5 credit.

By far the funniest, coolest, most caring professor I've had at UW. Concepts were well-explained and had me genuinely engaged and interested in astronomy. You WILL have to study for weekly in-person quizzes, but it's worth it. Lectures are recorded, but you won't want to skip anyway; he had us clapping and tearing up some days. SHOUTOUT CHRIS

Chris Laws was hands down the best professor I've had at UW. He is engaging, passionate, and super funny. It's super impressive and feels good as a student that he knows every single person's name in his lecture!

Easily one of the best professors at UW, gives great life advice, learns your name which no other professor has done, incredible lecturer, created an interest in astronomy for which i particulary had no interest, super approachable, understanding, can fall behind if you don't pay attention, but this is hard to do because of how good lectures are
Best professor at this school
He was absolutely amazing
Amazing lecturer, easy class. Take it

Great professor. He remembers every student by name. Very friendly and approachable. He often goes on tangents, but they kind of feel like a good break from complicated subjects. He was also very accomodating. My only complaint is that he often assigned a lot of reading. One week had 200 pages assigned. Just prioritize the lecture content.
Easy and simple but no extra credits and if you slip up in one of the 2 exams, then you can't save your grade. No extra credits and only selected HW assignments

Professor is absolutely amazing. He loves astronomy and his students very much. Very encouraging and ensures that every student does well in his class. There are weekly quizzes, lectures are recorded and uploaded right after class, review questions are available on canvas, and TAs are available for help. Don't slack off, the class is fast paced.

Amazing professor. Very passionate about astronomy, could not have asked for a better professor in this class. Super energetic and engaging in lectures and wanted to go to class because of that. Super lenient grading criteria too, its not hard to do well in this class

Laws is awesome. He's super funny, energetic, and entertaining. The class is more work than your typical intro class, and you gotta study a good amount. That said, both Chris and the TAs provide many resources and are very accessible, and they're genuinely chill and awesome people. Heck, Chris is the kinda guy I just wanna go fly fishing with.

Chris Laws is a fantastic professor. His lectures are entertaining yet informative and the material was diverse and detailed. There are no midterms or final, only weekly quizzes. The quizzes however, can be challenging but if you are engaged and attend the lectures, that's all you need to succeed in this class.

He clearly has experience teaching and clearly knows what he's talking about. He has a great team of TAs and the grading of quizzes are fair and generous. This class starts out easy but the concepts start to become more challenging and his lectures helped me understand them a lot easier. Would love to work for him in research some day.

I'm so glad I decided to take Dr. Laws's class. Astro101 is the best class I've taken, perhaps ever! Not only does he present the facts very clearly and concisely, he also finds ways to incorporate philosophical insights into each of the topics. His lectures are the highlights of my week. The Astro101 TAs are also amazing at answering questions.

I love Chris. Make sure you keep up with lectures if you want to do well on the weekly quizzes, and the quiz sections are very necessary. The quizzes are harder than you think they would be. The lectures are at times hard to follow so be sure to ask questions. It's not too hard but it's also def not a blow-off class.
Every week have a quiz. The answer will in the lecture and ppt. Almost every month have an opportunity to get extra credit.

I love them!! He is passionate about the field and that is apparent in his interesting, engaging, fun lectures. He cares a lot about his students and does everything he can to accommodate to us. I would recommend this class to everyone I know, it is only graded on 10 quizzes; there is no final! My only complaint is the TAs are tough graders.

Dr. Laws' class was so great. It wasn't too hard and I was always excited to go to class. He's from the south so when he lectures he straight up sounds like a really passionate southern preacher, but preaching about love and acceptance and the Universe. One of my favorite classes + teachers I've had so far at UW.

Prof Laws is so caring and passionate and makes an effort to know as many student names as he can, despite there being hundreds of students. He is such an authentic person who wishes the best for his students, and the TA's are very helpful in reviewing for quizzes. NO MIDTERM NO FINAL! weekly quizzes that are easy as long as you attend class.

Chris is such an incredible lecturer - he is so funny, so caring for his students, and always has something nice to say. His class is really well-organized and you can tell he puts a lot of thought into which TAs he chooses. I highly recommend going to office hours just to talk to him because he has so much knowledge to share!
Very nice man! The class was amazing. The content is not very easy for astr beginners like me (just took it for fun). But all the instructors are very accessible.

I really enjoyed this class! Chris is very charming and he's very passionate about the subjects he's teaching. Attendances for lectures are not mandatory. For quiz sections, you will be graded based on participation. There are weekly quizzes and no final. The quizzes are not very hard as long as you pay attention in class and go through the ppts.
No finals or mid terms, just weekly quizzes.

I took this class because I was curious of astrophysics and honestly, at first it was pretty stressful. It is a lot of material, but the lectures and the quiz sections made the quizzes a lot easier. The professor is genuinely caring. He wants you to succeed. He will forever be my favorite professor.

i took astro to get my QSR credits over with... i am SO not a STEM person and wasn't remotely interested in astronomy. laws and his truly awesome TAs made me not hate the class. lectures were funny and engaging because laws is genuinely passionate about astronomy and it's kind of contagious. shows a good professor makes all the difference.

It's clear he loves teaching the class, and his enthusiasm is shared by TAs and students alike. This is a class you don't want to miss regardless of your major. Reading the textbook helped with the weekly homework and the lectures answered the weekly quizzes. 95 is a 4.0 like most non-STEM intro classes.

Chris is the best professor anyone could ever ask for. He is the most romantic and heart-warming human being on the planet. He cares about students a lot, keeps telling us that he is here to help. I love that he always put on a suit and tie even though it's a remote class. He is super enthusiastic about what he does. And he has the coolest TA ever!
AMAZING!!! REGISTER THE CLASS NOW!!!!

absolutely amazing professor. they always come to class super energetic and you can tell he loves talking about astronomy. he is also super understanding with anything assignment related. there might be a little more assignments, but there is no midterm or final so i think that its worth it. PLS take any class you can with chris you wont regret!!

I absolutely loved taking Astronomy 101 with Professor Laws. Especially during the pandemic, he made the classes fun and I always looked forward to them. He is my favorite professor at The University of Washington so far! If you have the chance to take a class taught by him - do it.

Prof. Laws is amazing. His philosophy of weekly quizzes versus a cumulative final was so great and I think it helped me retain more material in the long run anyway. There are weekly quizzes on Fridays and homework assignments, along with one or two lab projects which are easy. I definitely hope to take another class with him if he offers it.

Most incredible professor I've ever had. Such a vibrant passion for teaching that cannot be matched! Quizzes are reasonable, but honestly quite interesting even when they get difficult. Chris is very accommodating and flexible, and cares about educating students rather than passing out grades. TAKE A CLASS WITH CHRIS BEFORE YOU GRADUATE

Chris is by far my favorite professor at UW! He provides the textbook for free and while you do read a lot, his lectures are so energetic they feel more like discussions. Grades were based on weekly assignments, with an optional final exam. While Covid probably altered the class, his character truly defined it. Best connection I've made!

Without a doubt, the absolute finest professor/person I have ever even heard of, much less met. The class itself is not difficult, but they're also not going to hand you an A. Do some light reading, watch the lectures, and do the relatively few/easy assignments they have and you'll get an A.

Chris' exuberance is contagious! Lectures are full of information but fun. Personable and profession, a fabulous teacher! Quizzes are hard-even after watching the lectures multiple times. Grading varies as it is done by TAs and grading team. Canvas is the best organized I have seen and very clear expectations. Book is free-lectures are everything
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Chris Laws is such a good lecturer and just a really good person. His lectures are very clear and you can tell the passion he has for astronomy. This class does take a decent amount of time and work but the clarity of all the instructions and the clear expectations make it a very enjoyable class.

Prof Laws is a very dedicated teacher who cares a lot about astronomy and his students. It's really nice having a prof who's so passionate about their subject. My only complaint is that there was SO much more work and really tough grading than I expected for a 101 class. Don't take if you just want a fun, easy intro to astronomy.
He's nice but it's really hard to get a good grade on weekly quizzes

Dr. Laws is probably one of the nicest professors I've had. He loves astronomy and gets really excited teaching it. He's also very available to students when they need him. that being said, his quizzes do take work. You need to be specific and include all of the details to get a high score. It's hard to get a 100% in the class.

He's so Amazing! One of the best professors I have met at UW. Even though the pace is kinda fast(but not too much), he can really teach everything well and understandable. there are a lot of details, but connected and clear-cut. A very humorous man and an inspiring professor!

Astr 101 is one of the best classes I have taken at UW. Professor Laws really cares about his students and you can tell he really loves what he is teaching. The lectures are interesting and informative, and the assignments are grading are fairly easy.

MY GOD IF YOU HAVE THE CHANCE TO TAKE ANYTHING WITH CHRIS LAWS, DO IT. This man is the sweetest, most caring prof I have ever had. He genuinely loves what he does and every student. I would die for him. As an avid anti-math and science student, I promise this is a 4.0 for anybody willing to do the work. REGISTER FOR THIS CLASS NOW!

Professor Laws is hands down the best professor I've had at UW. He is always there for his students and he cares about our success. We didn't have exams or finals, we have papers to write but they're not hard. After each paper, you will have conferences with him and he is so understanding, means no class for weeks! No way you will fail.

Absolutely enjoyed taking classes with Chris. He is great at lecturing, the content is super interesting, and he makes it clear what we need to know and what we don't for the weekly quizzes. One of those classes that I wish I can take again.

Dr. Chris Laws has been the greatest thing since sliced bread. His lectures are so good and interesting that I wanted to come to class even if it was at 10:30, which is still bedtime. Gives weekly quizzes and material is pretty interesting. He told us about aliens and supermassive black holes. 10/10 would recommend.

Amazing professor, class consisted of weekly quizes (friday's) and midterm & final were optional! He mentioned the average grade was an 83% however I had an incredibly difficult time even reaching above a 75%. He is one of the few professors that is actually interested in what he's teaching, also remembered all 200 of his students name, impressive

Dr. Laws is an amazing professor who really cares about his students and the course he teaches. His excitement and love for astronomy are contagious! The course itself is also extremely interesting and his lectures help explain everything that will be on the test and really help to clarify the readings. Highly recommend!

Chris is a very nice professor, but this class (at least for me) was hard and a lot of work that I did not expect. There are weekly quizzes that are tough and to do well you really need to do the multiple chapter readings. He said the avg. score is only 83%. Interesting stuff, but hard to get an A in.

Chris is clearly super excited to be doing what he does, and that creates a positive effect on the learning environment in both lectures and section (visited occasionally). This class isn't a super easy 4.0, but it's not difficult if you study at least 2-3 hours before each quiz. I started trying harder in the 2nd half of class & got myself a 3.8.

Chris gives some of the most amazing lectures. He is funny, inspirational, and charismatic. He makes it clear what needs to be known to succeed in the class. He really knows his stuff and comes to class everyday ready to teach and answer questions. The enthusiasm he presented everyday motivated me to do better in the class.

I am taking Chris' ASTR101. I have to say that this is the best professor I've ever met. 1. He CAN remember everyone's name in a 300 people class. 2. Optional Midterm and Final 3. No need for buying textbook Those 3 reasons are definitely enough for a 5 star professor lol

No participation in class thats tracked, quizzes are kinda specific so you need to go to class to get whats on them-half of its not in the readings (those really arent necessary either), midterm/final both optional, going to discussion section gives you good points for minimal effort, go to review sessions for quiz questions
Great teacher, I wish hed teach all of my classes. Id highly recommend him, he is one of the better teachers at UW.

Chris is a great teacher! Lectures are not mandatory, but are great! I managed to get a 4.0 without doing the reading and just studying the lectures the night before the quizzes (I attended each lecture). First 5 quizzes can add up to your mid term score, and last 5 quizzes equal your score on the final (optional, but easier than taking exam.
Really interesting class with a caring and passionate professor, would highly recommend.

Amazing professor! He really cares about his students. He uses a free textbook so we don't have to pay and he supplies the blue books for the exams. Plus the midterm and final are optional! It's an easy class but not an easy A. Be prepared to study for weekly quizzes! The 3 labs were easy but had hard questions. Don't start those the night before!

Do not take Laws' 101 class if you're looking for an easy 4.0. Laws himself is an incredibly good lecturer and the material is fascinating. However, you are graded harshly on weekly quizzes that are the majority of your grade. You have to remember every tiny detail from every lecture to even come close to getting 100% on quizzes. Take Astr 150.

I took this class in my first quarter of freshman year and it was the best class I've ever taken. Chris is caring and amazing. The lectures are not at all boring and if you do good on the weekly quizzes you don't even have to take the midterm and the finals!

I love him! Chris always gives the most inspiring lectures and I actually look forwards to attending his lectures. We have a quiz every week which is not bad since we can skip the final and the midterm if we do good on the quizes. Overall hes great and I would definitely recommend!

I love Chris. It is so great to have him be my first teacher at UW. He tries and can remember most of everyone's name. He is always inspirational and sometimes romantic, which makes me so happy and unwilling to miss any of his lecture. Go Chris!!!

Professor Laws is one of the best instructors so far. He makes learning the topic very fun throughout his lectures and answers any questions you have. He's also really straightforward about what you'll be tested on, and even gives you the mid-term and final questions pretty early on in the course. Labs are also graded by effort so don't stress out.

Chris is an incredible teacher. He learned the names of every student in my course and says hello when he sees you outside of class. He makes it easy to enjoy astronomy as much as he did, and that's coming from someone who, before this class, couldn't care less.

Dr. Laws is the best lecturer I have ever had. He REALLY cares about his students and will go to any length to help you learn the material. I'm an astro major so expected this to be easy, but I still spent up to 4 hours a week reading to prepare for the quiz. Not an easy A if you don't like reading about Astronomy, but is worth it and is super fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I'm graduating with CS this quarter but Chris' ASTR 101 has made me regret not majoring in Astronomy. He is THE best lecturer I have ever had up to this point, without a doubt. Knows everyone's name in a 300-student size class, which says a great deal. If you are at UW, you have gotta try one of his classes.

Prof. Laws had memorized everyones names before class even started, so as we walked into our first class of freshman year, we were warmly greeted with our names, which really meant a lot. If you put in work and participate in class, you'll get a good grade. Very inspirational and so far my favorite professor!

If I can I would marry this adorable old guy. He is the funniest professor ever.I took his astronomy 101 and it was not hard to get a good grade if you try and not procrastinate. He gave us weekly quizzes and all exams are optional. He is very helpful to all students. MOST IMPORTANT: He remembers all his students' name in the lecture. Literarily!
You didn't have to take the midterm or final if you were happy with your quiz grades. He remembers all his students names even after the class ends. Favorite prof at UW.

Not the easiest class. I honestly think his standards are really high. This class was supposed to be for reshman class, but he expects you to write like how expert writers would. DEFINITELY a LOT of homework, and A LOT OF reading. hated it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He is simply amazing! his lecture is awesome, mind-blowing every lecture! hes very passionate about this class and very caring to students. It's very easy to pay attention his class just because its so interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is the BEST PROFESSOR I've ever had in my LIFE! He is so caring and enthusiastic about his students and classes. I had two of his classes for fall quarter, and the experience was absolutely AMAZING! He remember EVERYONE's name! Honestly, If he can teach every single one of my class, school would be HEAVEN!

GREAT CLASS TO TAKE! DEFINITELY PUSHES YOU TO YOUR LIMITS, 3 PAPERS DURING THE WHOLE QUARTER BUT 3 DRAFTS OF EACH PAPER, FAIRLY EASY IF YOU PUT YOUR MIND TO IT. LAWS MAKES THE CLASS EXCITING AND BRINGS SNACKS TO CLASS. NOT A HARD GRADED CLASS.

Chris is the best professor I've ever met in UW. His passion to teaching made me love this English course, which should have been boring and tedious. He said this is only a class, I want to see how hard you push yourself to do "experiments" on your paper.  If you really like this course and make efforts, you won't get a disappointing grade!

He's a great person who genuinely cares about his students. However, he is a very tough grader. I've had my fair share of essays, and he is extremely picky about how you explain the topic at hand. He makes you work for your grade. But I feel like I've learned lots of helpful writing tips from him.  Overall, this is NOT an easy 4.0 class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Chris Laws is an awesome astro teacher. He has such a passion for the subject and it shows through in lecture. There is a quiz every week, so do the reading, but the midterm and final are optional. Not an easy 4.0 but definitely doable if you do the reading/go to lecture.

Fantastic Professor. Humor, ability, intelligence, he's got it all. Captivates you with his lectures and leaves you pondering many things at the end. Quizzes are a bit tough, as are exams, but if  you do the reading you should be fine. Also brought cookies to the final and tells great jokes. Best professor I've ever had, 10/10 would take again.

Truly cares about his students. He will make you work hard for a good grade. This means keeping up with the readings and really asking questions if you have any. He will know everyone names and he will be very enthusiastic in class with lots of jokes. Dont take bc you think a 101 class will be easy. He will push his students and is well respected.
He is dope.

Chris definitely cares about his students actually learning. He learns everyone's names by the first day of lecture, is always available to meet, holds review sessions, and answers emails quickly. There are quizzes based on a fair amount of reading every week, but you can sub your quiz grades for your midterm and final grades if you want!

PROF LAWS IS THE BEST!!!!! HE REMEMBERS ALL OF YOUR NAMES LITERALLY IN LECTURE. HOWEVER WEEKLY QUIZZES CAN BE A PAIN!! GET A GOOD TA AND WILL SAVE YOUR LIFE. YOUR QUIZ IS ALMOST EQUIVALENT TO YOUR GRADE. NOT AN EASY 4.0 AND LAWS WILL MAKE YOU WORK WORK WORK FOR IT!!!!!!!!!!

Professor Laws is an amazing professor, for an Astronomy 101 class he covers lots of material and tries to make sure that his students is able to understand them as much as possible. However, if you're looking for a class that is an easy A, this class is not it; there are weekly quizzes drawn from the reading along with other homework.

Honestly one of the best professors I've ever had at UW. He cares about student success and its evident. He leads weekly CLUE sessions on his own time to prepare students for his weekly in class quizzes and during his lectures you can tell how much he loves this subject. This class is a must take if you need a NW credit! Easy A with a little work.

Seriously one of the best, if not THE best, professor I've had at UW. He genuinely cares about the subject and your success in his class. Lectures never felt like they were dragging on and I always looked forward to them. If you are an astronomy major, just interested about space, or need a NW credit, take his classes. You will not regret it.

ASTR 301 with Chris Laws was by far the best off-major course I have ever taken. He has ways of explaining the material that just clicks, especially when it involves mindblowing concepts such as black holes. There are weekly quizzes and he requires a huge amount of detail, but if you pay attention and study accordingly you are certain to excel.
One of the best teachers I've ever had. You will have to work a decent amount but it's interesting and helpful.

Took this special topics course for writing in astronomy. Laws is by far the best astronomy prof in the department, and there's no question why he's received 2015's Distinguished prof of the Year award. He is inspirational, an great lecturer, cares deeply about his students and their success.

Chris Laws is by far the best professor I have at this university. He is funny memorable, and very dedicated to his students. The class is not an easy A, there is a weekly quiz which you need to prepare for, but if you do well on the quizzes then you can avoid taking the midterm and final.  Laws is willing to help any time, day, or for any reason

He's probably the best teacher I've ever had. His enthusiasm is through the roof and he genuinely enjoys his job and working with students. He grades on effort, so whether you're a really good writer or really bad your grade will depend on whether or not you actually tried. Fantastic professor, can't recommend him enough

Chris is by far one of the best teachers I've ever had, and my favorite so far at the UW. Not only is the subject interesting, but he is extremely enthusiastic about it. He is the most encouraging, helpful teacher I've had, he really believes that anyone can be involved in astronomy if they want to be. Also knew everyone's name first day of class!

350 characters is not nearly enough to describe what a great professor Chris is. Fantastic lectures, incredibly reasonable work load, and just an all around great teacher. His ability to break down complex concepts and explain them simply is unparalleled. Take his class. Any class of his you can find.

Even after 3 years of being at UW, I've decided that Chris is one of the best lecturers I've ever had. Even if you don't take his class, it's worth sitting in on just to witness him present the universe in a way that you didn't expect. That being said, the course is difficult. Definitely not an easy 4.0.
This guy is a wonderful mentor that loves what he teaches.

Hes a great professor. Hes very enthusiastic. I took his class for a freshman seminar which was supposed to be very easy. I'm now looking for other classes I can take with him because he was so great!

Was connected with ASTRO 150& helped explain astronomy concepts. Wrote 4 papers the whole quarter& had no testsquizzes. Responds quickly to emails. He learns everyone's name in a couple weeks, he cares about his students. He doesn't care about grades, he wants you to become a better writer. He brought snacks for the class. Easy A.

Chris is one of the most enthusiastic professors I have ever had. He loves what he teaches, and unlike most professors teaching a class of 200+, he really cares if you learn. He wants to share his excitement of astronomy with you, which is awesome. The weekly quizzes are NOT EASY. I repeat NOT EASY. Those recked my grade.

Let's be real. Dr. Laws is a  cool guy and definitely knows his stuff. But honestly, this class was stupid hard for being a 101 class. One quiz is worth 4% of your entire grade and there is one every week so if you mess up one you're basically screwed. So godspeed and good luck if you take this class. you're gonna need it. NOT AN EASY 4.0!!
Very nice professor, and helped me a lot with writing stuff.
He gives his best both in class and in office hours. He really wants every student to succeed, whether they are lagging behind or doing great. One of the best I've ever had.

Professor Laws was so personable and easy to talk to about assignments. Initially I was nervous about taking this class but I'm so glad I did! He's clear about what's expected of students and really encourages students to do their best. A great professor!

He really cares about the students' education.  He makes you go in for one-on-ones and I found those to be very helpful.  He's always willing to help you out if you are willing to reach out for help.  He is enthusiastic about his job, which is nice.  He loves astronomy and English.  An amazing teacher.  Dedicated yet thoughtful and caring.

Chris is definitely one of the nicest teachers I've had and you can definitely tell that he wants his students to succeed. With that being said, his one-on-one conferences are very helpful but they get dragged on to the point where you aren't even listening anymore. But overall, he was great and very enthusiastic.

Chris Laws was one of the worst teachers I have had to date. He goes on tangents while discussing in class and even though it is intro to astronomy based, he takes things way over beginners' heads. He is also very vague with paper reviews - Spent an entire one-on-one with him telling me my paper was awful without any real structural advice.

Absolutely best professor i've ever met. He's always enthusiastic about teaching and astronomy. He cares about every student too. And i'm so impressed that on the first day of class, he can name every one of 20 students in my class. He cares more about the efforts u put in than the quality.
Oh man, he's one of the best in UW.
He's very cool and generous, and will make you love astronomy.

DOC LAWS IS A BOSS. take this class, it's not the easiest class but he'll make you want to work hard for your grade. Amazing guy, amazing lecturer. No complaints. Worked my ass off and didn't get a 4.0 but to this day (a year & a half later) I still tell everyone he was the best professor i've had.

Chris is an extremely intelligent, fantastic, energetic professor who really loves what he does. He's one of the most caring, entertaining professors there is. However, do not expect an easy 4.0. The class is difficult to get a good grade in even if you work hard. However, the material is extremely interesting. Lots of reading though.

BEST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD AT UW. Honestly, he is incredibly enthusiastic about astronomy and wants you to learn as much as possible, he even invites everyone to astronomy trips to eastern washington to look through telescopes and such. Quiz and news reading every week. Not hard at all if you go to class and read a bit. Hes really funny too :D

He is the best professor I've ever had at UW. If you have the opportunity to take a class with him DO IT! He is so passionate about astronomy and he clearly loves teaching. You can only do poorly if you don't attend lecture/quiz section or just don't pay attention. It is, however, a lot of work, so be prepared! But it's all worth it.

Dr. Laws is very enthusiastic and loves to teach. He expects a lot of work, but also rewards students who put effort into each assignment. He also makes it a goal of his to get to know each one of his students, remaining flexible with schedule conflicts. If you show up for class and work hard you'll do well. He's a great professor!

Great professor.Really engaging even if you don't find the material that interesting.  Really tries to help students succeed and spends a lot of his own time so that he can be available.  Love this guy.
He made the class enjoyable and fun! Always available for help. One of the best professors I ever had!

The best professor at UW. He cares so much about his students. He understands that students have a huge workload from other classes, so he always extensions on due dates to accommodate to your needs. Best professor ever.

This man is the best professor I've had thus far. He is amazingly helpful and will go to great lengths to make sure that you get the help you need. He truly wants you to succeed, and it shows. He has high expectations but is still a fair grader. It's a shame I had him so early in my college career, because other professors pale in comparison.

This guy's a boss. He brings an unbelievable passion to class every day. He's probably the coolest teacher I've ever had. He's extremely helpful and very willing to work with you to help you succeed. His paper's are sometimes a little hard but that's the only possible downer to his class that I can think of.

He brings an amazing passion and energy to the class. He obviously loves the subject and he makes every lecture exciting. He also made tons of time for help when we needed it. Although it wasn't easy to get a 4.0 he made sure it was possible if you made the effort. He is a great professor. I definitely recommend any class he teaches.

It is obvious from the first day of lecture that Professor Laws is extremely passionate about astronomy and wants us to succeed in his class.  The class is challenging and not an easy 4.0, but it is interesting and Prof. Laws provides you with a lot of resources and gives a lot of opportunities to get extra help.  Def. take a class with him.

One of the BEST professors I have ever had. He challenges you but gives you plenty of resources and opportunities to succeed in the class. Highly recommended. He is a great professor but also an awesome person!!

Im a biology major and this has been my favorite class at UW so far because of Chris. He brings a high level of energy to class every day and keeps you interested. He gets to know you personally and has a clear understanding of your life outside of class by the time its over. Definitely take a small class with him if possible

best professor i've had. i had him for the writing link with astronomy. i hated the astronomy professor and wish he was teaching both. i probably learned more about astronomy from him than from prof larson. very passionate and engaging teacher. i highly recommend the writing link. the writing is hard but he is extremely helpful

This guy was awesome. He brought energy to class each day and was very understanding when it came to assignments and turning things in. I won't forget the time he walked with me from class to the UW libraries for my first time to help me get a book. This guy rocks and I loved him as an English teacher and could tell his passion for astronomy.

This guy is such an amazing professor. The class is so much work, but no one will try harder to make English interesting that Dr. Laws. He is so enthusiastic and he is such a great guy, if you go talk to him at office hours it is like you are talking to a friend. Class is a ton of work, but I'd say its worth it to have Laws as a professor.

I took Astronomy 101 with this professor and it was one of the best classes I've ever taken. He makes the topic fun and interesting. This is the only class where I've been able to continuously pay attention during lecture, and for that reason I never opened the book. He's also a great guy outside of class, so if you get the chance, go talk to him!
Best professor ever. Makes astronomy cool. Mike Solontoi is also another good TA.

The class as a whole was very interesting, and it was obvious how passionate Professor Laws is about astronomy. The weekly quizzes makes sure that you keep up with the reading, and the weekly astronomy readings are an easy way to wrack up credit. Overall, it was definitely a good class as long as you kept on track of your work!

Chris is the best professor I've had so far at the U. He is funny and lecture flies by. I learned an incredible amount in this class. Your TA is important, if possible get Daryl Haggard. Do the readings and pay attention in lecture on quiz days and you will do great. Definitely recommend taking this class with Chris!

Prof. Laws is amazing and funny. His class is difficult but you are making your money's worth in college. You learn lots of useful stuff. Weekly quiz are difficult. You have to pay close attention to lectures and textbook readings. You have to work hard in this class but Prof. Laws is just absolutely amazing. He is the BEST!!!

Chris himself was awsome, and so were all the TAs, very helpful. The only problem with his class is it was HARD! 10 quizes, weekly, 2 dropped, quizzes were VERY difficult, even if you read sometimes you fail. You have to keep up. 2exams, gives 8essays and on day of exam picks 2 along with some multiple choice. A LOT of work for an elective.

Chris is a great teacher and VERY passionate about astronomy.  The class is pretty challenging because of weekly quizzes that are pretty tricky and essay tests.  There are only two tests but you have to write two essays and do multiple choice! I was very time crunched even after studying all week!! But the readings help a lot.
Seriously, a great professor. Genuinely cares about the students and while the class is a lot of work, stay on top of the reading and you should do fine. Highly recommend this prof!
Awesome teacher--one of the best professors I've ever had.  He really makes the effort.  He is an excellent teacher and mentor!

This professor will change your view of astronomy.  Before I had no interest in astronomy, but his passion for the subject and the fascinating way in which he teaches makes it so interesting!  You should take any changce you can to take a class from him!

I thought he was a wonderful teacher.  Really cared if the students learned or not.  Even learned all the students names to make the classroom feel more personal. He was really cool and the class is easy if you get all your work done.

A wonderful teacher.  Really cared if the students learned or not.  Even learned all the students names to make the classroom feel more personal. He was really cool and the class is easy if you get all your work done.
Very passionate about astronomy, and very helpful in writing assignments. I enjoyed his class.
A guy who really loves astro. There are weekly quizzes which can be tricky, and mid-terms are essay based but you'll be fine if you read
a good teacher

Respectfully, he was an alright lecturer but his notes were disorganized and messy. Sometimes, there would be errors in his notes that he would miss but then go back and fix them once pointed out. His exams are fair and align closely to the style of practice exams he provides. Honestly, just do the practice exams and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Maly understands the course material and the exams reflect his lectures well. His practice exams are basically his old exams, which work very well for you to prepare for the midterms and final. Homework was very easy to complete so much of your grade is dependent on your exam performance. There is a drop system to help your grade too.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Going to be honest - I never went to lecture or quiz section after the first day and still passed with a 4.0. Maly gives so much practice questions similar to his exams that if you do those question + extra practice on your own, you will do well. His lectures are messy, and I found them never useful. Just pick up a textbook and practice lots!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He explains concepts well during lecture but notes are hard to understand. Midterms were similar to practice problems/exams he provided, + he was generous with partial credit but final was much harder than midterms w/ completely different material from practice or anything he covered in class. Would've rated him higher if it wasn't for the final.

Maly's good at explaining and will stop and answer as many questions as people have. His tests are the average difficulty for an ochem class and the people saying otherwise didn't study. Much more doable than the other 238 profs. Yes, his notes are unorganized but if you go to lecture that doesn't matter. Maly is awesome and the best 238 prof imo

Really good at teaching the mechs/rxns for the class--basically half the class, as after the 1st midterm it's almost all rxns. He loves his resonance, but it's super important for the rxns. Rough when it comes to material not about rxn mech tho. Beware of his super hard tests, do the practice tests, didn't read the textbook and it was alright tho.

This is the worst professor I have ever had, and I have never struggled so much in a class. The lectures, pointless. He goes through the slides that he has already written and just draws and thinks we understand. Tests are extremely difficult; you walk out of the testing room thinking you did well and receive the exact opposite a week later.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love Maly! He explains things very clearly. I don't understand why some people complain about him going too fast because you can just watch the recordings if you missed something. He gives us a break during lecture, and he covers all the material very well. I think he explains content a lot better than my 237 professor.

Genuinely the worst professor I have ever had at UW. Tests were extremely hard and the rubrics were very unfair. Lectures are so boring and pointless, he just goes on and on about as many topics as he can in 1 hour and 20 minutes. Average for midterms were around 50-60% while other CHEM 238 classes were higher and did retakes. Would not recommend.

Why does UW let this guy teach? He doesn't care about teaching at all and only wants to talk about his research. In one of his office hours I asked him for tips on solving NMR problems only to learn more about his research on the plasticity of signalling enzymes than I did on NMR spectroscopy (i didn't go back to any more office hours after that..)

His lectures are super disorganized, so the textbook will have to be your friend. The exams questions are practically hit or miss as he doesn't really like giving partial credit. He also often makes lots of mistakes. I went to office hours once to ask a question about williamson ether synthesis, but he ended up just talking about his research.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: nice guy, but the lectures are useless. worst lecturer i've ever had. super disorganized unfortunately and i feel like he just was scrambling during the lectures. you're gonna have to read the textbook and learn content from other means because you wont learn anything from him. tests were hard and had low averages but that's just a given with ochem

for CHEM 261/2:
super chill class(es)! the readings were kind of dense but you didn't really have to do them, and most quizzes were based on prelab questions. the final was the only kind of dicey part as it's an oral final where you have to get very specific with how you word things, but he grades it leniently. overall pretty enjoyable course(s)

literally crashed out after every lecture. notes were very disorganised and dense. mostly he'll just gloss over the important stuff and go in depth on random topics. 20% of exams were usually stuff not covered in class, but grading and practise was decent. barely passed with the curve. the content of chem238 is hard, DEF TAKE ANOTHER PROF!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures and notes were hard to understand, but he is caring and generous with the grading. He curves and drops parts of the exam, which definitely saved me.

Maly is among one of the best professors you could get for CHEM 238. He explains every concept and every mechanism very clearly, and provides a lot of practice worksheets for studying. His lectures are heavy on content - he doesn't ask the audience questions like Goldman or Lalic does but because of this you can get away with not reading the book.

This professor is especially kind, but he does not provide any (useable) lecture slides for note taking. He does not explain what will show up on the exam, and also goes over something very quickly that ends up being incredibly important for the exam. There was absolutely no class structure and not a lot of practice problems for extra help.

Nice guy, cares about the content and the students. Incredibly disorganized though and it was near impossible to follow his lectures. Tests are hard and tricky, and he does not go over everything that is on the test so there's unseen content on those. Get ready to teach yourself the course, don't rely on lectures. Would really not recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Maly was the definition of an interesting critter forreal. Definitely very smart, so smart that sometimes it's difficult to follow along in class, but his criteria are more than fair when it comes to grading. The assigned reading is dense and not super useful. Minus 1 pt bc he says "right" and "yknow" so often in lecture I started keeping a tally.

honestly goated. very clear what he wanted us to know with regard to exams, only thing that I heard people complain about was his lecture notes--they're kind of unorganized. but, this is a hard class, and he made it more clear for me at least.

Prof Maly was super enthusiastic and ready to clearly answer any questions, and his lecturing style, while different from other professors, allows him to talk about concepts more in depth. His practice exams are very similar to the real thing, concepts might just be presented in different ways. As long as you know the basics, you'll succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Maly is my favorite chemistry professor by far. His notes were a little messy, but it wasn't impossible to follow. He has very thorough and helpful explanations that don't feel like you're just getting information spewed at you for 1.5 hours. His tests are very fair, and he clearly enjoys teaching. I wish I could have him for every chem class.
Still one of the hardest classes, but Maly is an easier prof compared to other ochem profs at UW. If you want to do well, unfortunately go to lectures and come to office hours prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Notes were pretty disorganized. Required a lot of outside of lecture study time. Overall it was manageable but far from enjoyable. He didn't come to exams so we would occasionally start late and the TAs were often overworked by passing out tests. He loves resonance on his tests.

His lectures are very surface level and he often doesn't get to all the material he had planned, but he still expects you to know it for the exam. Several times he never finished the lecture and just told us to read the textbook to figure it out. His exams are very difficult and the averages are very low.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Doesn't get to everything in lecture and expects lots of outside reading. Be warned: things not covered in lecture are fair game on exams. Very surface level in his lectures and practice problems/exams are much easier than the actual exam. You're gonna have to teach yourself a lot of the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grade is dependent on only tests, hw doesnt count since its unlimited attempts and answers online. Test averages were very low, not reflective of what was shown in lectures/on hw. Partial credit isnt really a thing since most answers are right or wrong. Only 1 practice test per midterm/final so very limited resources to study on. High stress class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: At first, his teaching style may take time to get used to(his 'slides' are like in website format) but after few lectures, you'll get used to it. His exams are really straight forward so as long as you get the basics done, you're good. His curve was very generous at the end :3
Extremely unorganized canvas page and not that helpful in office hours, but tests were straightforward and slightly similar to practice material.

Midterm averages were pretty low, and he focuses heavily on synthesis while his lectures are very surface-level. Was plenty of practice problems but points were distributed weirdly on exams. I didn't prefer his lecture style but he had a generous curve at the end. Not bad, but didn't enjoy it either.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very tough exams that require a lot of extrapolating. Lectures don't go super in-depth but if you read the textbook and do practice problems it's not too much of an issue. Not the greatest professor but not the worst (would take him over Gelb any day).

Maly tends to skim material in lectures, but provides students with an adequate amount of practice problems (weekly) and practice exams (preceeding each exam) to make up for that, given a student reads the textbooks. Course grading policy was gracious, with hw/quizzes replacing the lowest midterm score or 2/3 of the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Maly's lectures are very confusing and hard to follow. It is very difficult to get good grades because your overall grade is only determined by 3 midterms and final. His tests are unfair because the practice material given isn't similar to what's on the test. A lot of the test questions were things we'd never really gone over before which was hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Barely any partial credit on exams and each question was worth a lot of points. You could get 90% of the question correct but mess up on one thing and that's 20 pts out the window. Quizzes r very easy compared to exams and he throw things into the exams that we hadn't learned or barely went over. Grade is entirely made up of midterm scores.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely not. Midterm average was a 50 because he refused to give any partial credit on whole-page questions (and marked people wrong for writing minor AND major product even though they showed they understood the concept). 1/3 of the exam was on one reaction and if you didn't get the first part right you basically failed the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Maly's lectures are a pain to get through and hard to follow. He didn't update the grade book once the entire quarter and practice exams were always way easier than actual exams, and points were always distributed really weird between questions on exams. If you get Maly, make sure you're good at teaching yourself.

Maly should get more credit than people give him. Even though his lectures are VERY fast paced, he can fit a lot of content in short lecture time. Straight-forward, and easy flow, repeats concepts that are important - heavy emphasis = will be on exam. Gives a lot of practice material (not common among all) that is similar to exams. Overall helpful

Maly is amazing! Straight forward easy to understand lectures, fair tests, no excess busy work or unnecessary information. He puts a lot of effort into providing extra practice problems/exams and is lenient about homework assignments (rare for o chem). Chem 238 is a hard class but Maly makes it bearable and less stressful :-)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fair, easy test (compared to rest of Chem department), give a lot of resources for practice, actually lets you know if you need to know something for a test
he sucks, his tests are extremely difficult and his lectures are a mess. it is impossible to follow his instructions and his office hours are useless

I had high hopes for Professor Maly but he seemed pretty uninterested in teaching. He didn't really care if students succeeded. Both the practice final AND real final were riddled with typos and mistakes. The TA's had to correct multiple questions and structures MID-EXAM and I ran out of time to finish. He's also inaccessible during office hours.

I didn't think he was bad until he set the average. Literally got significantly above average every test and got a B. Also, final was ridiculously tough. More than half of it was complicated synthesis problems. Mixed feelings about him.

Honestly I feel like he wasn't that bad. Sure he was ALWAYS late at uploading lecture notes and wasted a bunch of time in lecture teaching irrelevant material. Also taught us biosynthesis even though it wasn't on the exam (lol another time waster). However, he does cover everything in a somewhat simple manner. I think he's alright for a chem prof.

I had high expectations for Maly, but was very disappointed. Seems more focused on his own research than teaching and wanting students to learn. Inaccessible outside of lecture or scheduled office hours and online office hours are unhelpful, since they're online and this is ochem. If you learn through repetition of problems, take another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Not a great lecturer, doesn't seem to care if you learn or not and doesn't seem invested when answering questions online or in person. I had to rely on friends for practice problems from other professors because he only provides one practice exam for each exam and that's it. His exams are meant to trick you. Hardest professor I have ever had.

Barely goes into detail on material and provides hardly any practice problems for you. Tests are extraordinarily hard and there's nearly no grading criteria for them and the TAs grade the exams, so how many points you are awarded is up to them. You can get most of the question right and they will still take off 2/3 points for one mistake.

He only teaches reactions very briefly and doesn't give great practice problems. Rarely replies to questions on the discussion board, and gives a lot of extra information that is not helpful when learning the material the first time
Scatter brained, isn't clear with expectations, lots of mistakes in lecture not corrected.

I read the reviews prior to taking this class, and had high expectations for Maly, but now, 5 weeks into the quarter, I thought I should warn other people the way I wish I would have been. He throws material at you and basically leaves it up to you to teach it to yourself & rarely does example problems and basically leaves you in the dust for tests

Maly was the best o chem teacher I had throughout the series. His lectures provide everything you'll need to know for the exam and is very thorough when explaining mechanisms. His old exams are VERY similar, so just study as many of those as you can!

This country singer-like Professor is excellent and a prototypical professor! His tests are straightforward and he never puts foreign materials (except for rare bonus problems). Do what you're told, don't overthink problem and choose correct quiz section. He even allows advanced material and uncovered methods/reactions! He also gives sample exams!

Maly is my favorite Ochem prof. His lectures and explanations were quite clear and he'd answer any question raised. He didn't give lecture notes but you don't need them if you show up/watch Panopto. Tests were tough (avg 63/110) but straightforward if you study well. Exams covered lecture material only. Gave us helpful reaction sheets for test 2.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Maly is one of the greatest ochem professor that I've ever taken imo. Not going to lie though, his tests are extremely difficult and tricky. You're going to have to spend tons of time studying and learning his tricks. Nevertheless, he is one the professors here that I dearly respect and love. He has tons of office hours & is willing to help!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Maly has been my favorite Science professor by far. His lectures are incredibly clear and straight forward and he cares. He even made reaction summary sheets to study for exams. OChem is never easy, but Maly's tests were well written and each question had reasonable expectations of student knowledge. He never asked questions that were beyond reach.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a great professor. Super nice and cares for his students. ALthough he didn't post lecture notes for my class, I thought his outline was extremely organized. Not going to lie though, his tests were pretty tough and tricky, but he is an amazing test writer. Overall, he is the best chem professor I've ever had!

His lecture notes are very disorganized. For me, reorganizing the lecture notes myself helped a lot. From what I've experienced and what I've heard, he gives out at least one test that's very very hard (resulting in class average of 50% or below), and this screwed me over. Overall, not the worst, but not the best, either.

He just drops information in front of you and doesn't really do anything to help. If you aren't amazing at ochem, then you will struggle. When it comes to exams he gives to practice tests and thats it, no topics list or anything. By far the most unhelpful prof I've had here at UW.  Good luck to anyone with the misfortune of being his student.

While he is very knowledgable his teaching ability is dismal. Exams are extremely complex and not even close to the many of the practice material, or what is gone over in lectures. He is extremely hard to get ahold of and very limited in general help, you need to know exactly what you need help with if you expect any answer.

His tests are extremely difficult. Keep up with the practice problems every week. He tends to spend a lot of time on simple concepts, and then a small amount of time on the more difficult ones. Make sure you know all the small tricks and exceptions, he tends to test a lot on those.

I was excited about taking his class at first, but the class went quite fast toward the end. He tends to skip a chunk of concepts from the book (which is nice) and his mechanisms are a bit different. The tests are not bad if spend some times doing practice problems/ tests from any sources you can find. Avg is about 60%, sometime higher.

Organic Chemistry itself it really hard, but Maly is a good professor. It sucks because of the curve. The tests are difficult because you have to understand the special cases of a wide variety of synthesis. Not a vary organized lecturer, but he offers lots of practice problems that he created, which is nice.
He is very clear with what he expects you to know and not know. There are no surprises on exams, but the exams are definitely not easy. Pay attention and do all the practice problems he gives.
He's a great teacher! His tests are difficult because there are usually 2-in-1 reactions so make sure you have your reagents down. If you read the textbook and put in some effort, the A is yours!
I feel that, although he expects a lot from his students, he will often go the extra mile to help them out if they are motivated.  His explanations are also very good.  I would recommend him.
This guy is an epitome of a teacher. He grades all quizzes and tests by himself and really care about your learning. He makes sure to answer all of the questions before moving on. Highly recommend!

Apparently, this is the best you can expect from an ochem professor. He's not abjectly terrible like other chem professors I have had, but I don't think I'd make the stretch of calling him an amazing professors. His lecture style is helpful, and the tests aren't easy, but they didn't have averages in the 30-40% rage like other professors.

His lecture is pretty straightforward and clear. He does not provide screencasts but does provide podcasts. He gives you a lot of reactions, which is sometimes overwhelming. Overall he is a good prof, although his tests are rather difficult.

His way of teaching sucked for me. people say this class is easy, but when I took Andersen's class, I felt much more confident and knowledgeable. His scoring system for exams sucks too. While Andersen has a variety of level of questions with appropriate scores distribution, Maly doesnt do that. But definitely easy 3.3+ if that is what you aim for.

Loved him!! The fact that he didn't post lecture slides or screencasts really makes you pay attention during class - definitely made me a better student. I did really well in his class, and I generally get 3.3's in all chem classes. Go to class, take good notes, and do all his practice worksheets!!

One of the best professors I've had thus far. Maly is crystal clear and his explanations are great! He doesn't screencast though, so going to lecture is really important. He's a super smart guy and his test questions are sometimes tricky. But otherwise a very enjoyable class!

Maly is the best ochem professor I had! I really loath chemistry but he explains things very clearly and his use of examples are great. You're still going to have to put in a lot of work to get a good grade, but it's easier to manage with him as your professor if you hate chemistry like me.

The class was challenging, but teaches ochem VERY, VERY WELL! He makes complicated concepts understandable. He writes lecture notes on the overhead, so you write along with him. He doesn't screencast, which forces you to be in class. I LOVE THE WAY HE TEACHES! The one thing I dislike is he turns off the lights, which makes me sleepy all the time.

He was a great professor! Definitely made sure that you understand the important concepts and the mechanisms behind them so it isn't so much just straight memorization. The practice exams are extremely similar in format to his exams and the practice problems are helpful. If you pay attention and practice, it should be an easy class.

His exams are very doable if you practice enough. Do ALL of the book practice problems he assigns, twice if you can. This will really help you on exams. The quizzes are very easy, but you have to keep up with the material to do well on them. He posts podcasts, but not videocasts, of his lectures, so be sure to take detailed notes.

I have to admit Maly is good as people say he is. I tried much harder in Professor Boydston's 237 course and got 3.7. Here I got a 4.0!!! He makes good and fair decisions for specific policies. This quarter we had a blackout on our very final. He made the make-up final optional! Be aware, his exams are somewhat complex but fair.

Awesome professor!! His lectures really help you understand not just the reactions but the principles behind them and he really emphasizes patterns and trends in reactivity which helps so much! Every exam has at least one mechanism and one synthesis qustion but the practice exams are really helpful as are his lecture notes. Highly recommend.

Truly an impressive and effective teacher. His examples are interesting and stimulate understanding of the concepts. Office hours helped the most as well as his straight forward lectures and fair tests!
Best professor ever! Questions are hard but fair and lectures and office hours are extremely helpful. My grades went up to a 4.0 from a 3.1 in Chem 237 Boydston!

Hands down best professor ever! Changed my perspective of organic chemistry from downright terrible to actually enjoyable. Lectures were so clear and helpful, tons of office hours and practice problems. Wish every chem class was taught by him!

The very first chem teacher to ever make coming to lecture worth it.  Very down to earth and everything made sense.  I went from a 2.9 in CHEM237 with Andersen to a 3.6 with Maly.  A lot of mechanisms in his tests.  NO emphasis on nomenclature!  Reactions were the main point of his lectures and he offered other examples than just from the text.
Great professor. Very enthusiastic about the subject. His tests are difficult, but the practice exams are extremely helpful. Key to success: do his practice problems.

Maly is a great professor. Coming from Andersen, this is a HUGE step up. He really takes the time to answer students questions, and provides tons of office hours. This class improved my learning and interest level more than any other chem class I've taken. He's approachable, his explanations are very clear, and he is extremely intelligent.

One of the best chemistry profs I've had at UW. His explanations were excellent and all of the test material was covered in class. The exams are difficult, but not unreasonable. He expects students to work hard outside of class and practice the material. He was funny and upbeat in class and made ochem lecture enjoyable!

The fact that he cares about his students is shown through the amount of time he invests in the forum, answering Q's, being at every office hour, answering emails promptly, all while having other responsibilities. His passion & commitment to his students will make him one to remember. He exemplifies how an ideal educator should be.

This guy completely turned organic chemistry around for me. His lectures are very clear and informative, and the information sticks. I knew the material after lectures enough to ace the quizzes without consulting the book. While tests were difficult, if you read the book and do the practice problems (he posts a lot!), you will succeed. I'm really disappointed he isn't teaching 239 next quarter :(

Dustin is a really great professor. I had Andersen for 237, which was not fun at all. I thought I hated organic chemistry until I took it from Maly. He really makes everything seem so clear. GO TO LECTURE, and DO THE READING BEFORE IT! He really reinforces your learning well, but you need to put in the effort, too. Tests are difficult.

His lectures are clear and straightforward. He really takes a lot of effort explaining every reaction and concept in detail. This is one of the rare chem classes that I actually study with my in class notes. His tests are very hard: He loves to put complicated synthesis questions that requires you to draw knowledge from several chapters.

He was a good prof. and his tests were pretty straight forward (matched well to what you are told to expect on the exam). His practice exams, which he will post on the website, will give you the best indication of what to know. only complaint is his handwriting is horrid and it would probably be better to look at the book if he shows examples.

AWESOME professor! He really knows his stuff and answers any questions clearly. Also, ALL test questions are from lecture, so reading is pretty much a supplement for clarity (reading along with lecture was helpful for me). No nomenclature tested, but it's not hard to learn on your own. Quizzes = straight forward; don't make dumb mistakes though! =O

He redeemed ochem for me after taking it with Straumanis. Gives you everything you need to do well on the tests, was really nice and curved to a 2.8 because we had unusually high midterm scores. His tests come straight from lecture.

Pretty good professor, lectures were clear and test were fair. Make sure you pay attention to those "exceptions," they will show up on the test and trip everyone up except you :) I recall having to show atleast one mechanism on each exam so remember those as well. Overall an enjoyable course.

Maly is one of the best chem professors at UW. His lectures were incredibly clear and helpful and prepares you well for the tests as a majority of the test questions come from his lecture material. He doesnt cover nomenclature so it may be underdeveloped for future ochem classes. Quizzes are pretty easy. Highly recommended.
He is one of the best chem professors at the UW. His tests are very fair, not too easy and not too hard.

Maly is a funny guy and his lectures are pretty good. I always read the book, but you don't really need to after his lectures, only for clarification. His tests were extremely fair, not too hard. Quizzes are very easy. I wouldn't mind taking another class from him again
Dusty is the man. He made me love chemistry.

I think getting a good grade in this course can't just rely on the 50-minute class. It requires spending a lot of time and effort outside of class. However I think David is a very good teacher, especially his office hours really helped me solve many problems.
