Lots of demos and interesting topics, but lectures felt disconnected from labs and tutorials. I had to teach myself much of the material. TAs often couldn't answer questions. Exams were harder than expected with unclear expectations on what would be tested. Overall mostly read off of slides and barely elaborated

He's very friendly and his lectures are entertaining. He seems to be more helpful one-on-one so definitely approach him or go to office hours if you need help. Other than that, his lectures lack coherence and he doesn't always know what he's doing. For tests, expect a good amount of trick questions. He's just OK.

If you understand physics already this will likely be a fine course, but it is definitely a weed out one. The lectures are very fast paced and I feel like getting questions answered during lecture was not common and hand raises were ignored several times

He is very passionate and funny but seems disconnected from the course, creating exams that were increasingly more difficult than practice material. You will have to spend a lot of time outside of class working on this course. His lectures felt rushed, crammed, and all over the place. While he has a fun personality, he is not good as a teacher.
whatever lecturing talent hertzog might've had in the past is gone
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hertzog does an adequate job lecturing given how messy the 121 curriculum is. He's clearly an experienced lecturer, and does lots of fun demos. He does seem somewhat disconnected with the curriculum, especially the labs and tutorials. He writes difficult tests, and I've found the in class work isn't enough to prepare for the exams.
Professor Hertzog was great! I really enjoyed his lectures, he made them very engaging with lots of demos. At his office hours, he was very helpful.

Prof. Hertzog is funny and very passionate about physics, but his lectures aren't enough to understand the concepts if you fall behind in the readings. You will do fine in physics as long as you keep up with the textbook. Don't skip a day of reading. That's my only advice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, despite him not teaching in a while he did great! Goes in depth about lecture problems to make sure that everyone could understand them, gives out reasonable exams, and is amazing during office hours. Makes funny jokes and has fun demos, I definitely recommend him!

I respect the guy hes cool and all but my god I've learnt absolutely nothing from him. Every lecture is just nonsensical and no help. I feel like everything is easy to understand until he teaches it. I don't understand the good ratings. I think a decade away from teaching has really messed him up. clearly a smart guy and passionate. Just not good

Hertzog is not only a clearly brilliant guy, but he also makes it apparent how much he enjoys what he is doing not o my as a researcher but as a teacher as well. Very nice guy and know how to entertain without overdoing it too often. Lectures are very helpful but, because of this, you'll have to go above and beyond to beat the curve.

Really great lecturer- his sense of humor made the material way less stressful. Demos were also cool. You can tell he really enjoys his job. Physics tests are always hard, but if you're looking up this class, you probably already knew that. If you have to take phys 122, I definitely recommend taking it with him!

Very energetic during lectures.  He plays some music at the beginning.  He slowly and thoroughly goes over everything in his lectures and is extremely prepared for lectures.  He even posts answers for clicker questions and goes step by step when going through problems.  One of the best professors I've had at the UW!
This guy has great lectures that really engaged everyone in the room. Subject material is tough but he does a good job of setting and making clear expectations for the test. Great class.

Hertzog is hilarious.  He's a jolly guy and knows how to make people laugh.  Demos are useful, and he is very good at explaining.  Midterms were very fair.  I found the best way to prep for tests was to do the extra (unassigned/not mandatory) SmartPhysics homework

I hate physics, but this was by far my favorite class of the quarter. Hertzog makes lectures a ton of fun and keeps everyone laughing through all of the tedious math. It's hard, and requires a lot of outside work but his tests are very fair.

You can tell that he likes what he does but for me his lectures were all over the place. He would randomly start doing a demo and then switch back to explaining something completely different right after. He did everything VERY quickly and it was easy to get lost.
Dang this guy is so cooooooool.  I liked his class very muchhhh. Crazy how physics workssssssss. Kan't wait to take 122!         So many good lectures.

Hertzog is an incredible professor. He loves to make physics entertaining, but instead of just using demos and such as gimmicks, he explains them in a way that helps you fully understand the concepts. Fun guy, great teacher!

Coming from a bad 121 experience, thought 122 was going to be worse but Hertzog completely changed that notion. He is an excellent lecturer in tying in what we were learning to the class demo's which made attending lecture fun! He's got quite a sense of humor too. Study his clicker questions because those are what he base his exam questions off of.

One of the best professors that I have had at the UW. Coming off of 121, I was not very hyped up on physics but Hertzog rekindled my interest. He got a round of applause from the class after the last lecture, if that is any indication of his quality.

First off, this is a tough class. Any student taking it needs to be aggressive in their intent to learn the material. But if you invest the time into understanding it, everything falls into place, and it will be one of the most rewarding classes you've taken. David Hertzog will make sure of that. He is a terrific and enthusiastic professor

Physics generally makes me very depressed. HOWEVER, do exactly what Hertzog suggests and you will survive! He WANTS you to succeed. He is fair, willing to help, gives you resources, and puts a lot of effort into making physics less daunting.

having had Pedigo for 122, I can say that Hertzog is a much better Physics teacher.  He teaches for the tests instead of just going over the general ideas.  Often does example problems, which help a lot

Great professor all around. Engaging, has great demos and slides, also listens to studentsand adapts his class to make sure they learn. his tests are fair and he posts his notes online for ease of access and learning. One of the best teachers at uw in my opinion.

Great great professor. Does a good job with his power points and demos in order to communicate topics effectively. Having had Pedigo sub a couple times, Hertzog is DEFINITELY much better. Very funny guy... you can tell he loves his job.

His power points are easy to look at and take in. He communicates very well and makes sure the demos that he does make sense. His clicker questions focus more on understanding of concepts rather than understanding how to do basic algebra (good thing). He's definitely one of the better intro physics professors.

Amazing professor! He is very enthusiastic about the class and does a superb job explaining the concepts.  His slides are well organized and informational(you wouldn't need to read the book in this class,) and he is very wiling to help after class or during his office hours.  His tests are a lot harder than the homework questions though.

Physics 121 is a difficult class but Hertzog really tries to make the lectures interesting and clear. Make sure to do the pre-lectures before going to class because otherwise his lecture slides can be confusing and you will get lost. Also go to the study center if you are confused and meet with him because he really helps clarify things in person.
Great Professor. He explains everything clearly. No need to even open the book. He's also fun!

For somebody who hasn't taken physics before this can be an extremely difficult course. However, Professor Hertzog is always upbeat and excited about teaching the material. On the other hand the tests were ridiculously hard and the homework was a lot harder than anything he showed in class. You'll need to have plenty of extra time for this class.

Dabiri, while being a kind person, is not a great professor. All class material is screenshots directly from the textbook and all lectures are reading textbook slides and being told to "discuss with your neighbor". Often late to class, missing materials, and late on grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: EXTREMELY slow grader. Most take over 1 month from due date to be graded. If students have deadlines for assignments, someone's gotta give this man grading deadlines. No way to tell how you're doing, and no feedback provided on quizzes and homeworks. Lectures are just repeating the textbook (which is very good btw), which adds nothing.

Nice guy, TA's are pretty bad. Assgts take weeks for grading/feedback/solutions. 

Lectures straight from the powerpoint. In-person attendance dwindles from 50 people down to a syconphantic dozen that make the last couple of weeks like pulling teeth.

HW weighted as 65% of grade, 1 final takes up the last 35%, expect a C worst case scenario.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very relaxed, excellent speaker. Does assign a lot of "derive the known formula" problems, which I thought added nothing to my learning except frustration. Quizzes and exams were fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures are solid, but there are no solutions provided for tests, quizzes, and even some homework assignments. If you lose points, it can be really time consuming to figure out what you got wrong. Studying for the class is also challenging since the professor assigns problems from a different textbook than the one used for lectures.

Dabiri is genuinely a wonderful person. You can tell he really cares about his student's wellbeing and education. He does struggle with concision in lectures, but in small groups, he slows down and explains in an individually tailored way. He's a forgetful guy but is very approachable; when in doubt go to office hours or spot him on campus.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nice guy, terrible professor. Think he's been teaching since 2017, don't know how he still has a job. So unprepared, changes things last minute, SAYS he cares about students' feedback (promised to give us 1.5 hrs for midterm), but in reality doesn't care (gave us 50 min). Added quizzes to HW the day before it was due. Textbook is better than him.

Dabiri explained things very well and answered everyone's questions during class. Class sometimes went 15-30 minutes overtime (sometimes even 1 hr) which got annoying but nice he spent the time for us. Tests are tough but fair to the homework. He even made our final optional just bc someone asked him to. Overall, good professor and clearly cares.

Good teacher overall. Definitely recommend office hours because he is a much much better teacher in a one on one environment and is socialable. Textbook is a must. intro to fluids by anderson is a great book and you'll use it to learn most of the stuff on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Good solid class. Equations of motion were hard to understand when I first read through them, but after he explained them in class, I really understood them well. The class is a bit of work, but he gave us a method to learn better, and that is working well.

Professor Dabiri's lecture might be boring from time to time but he is really passionate about what he teaches. He uploads all his slides onto canvas and he is pretty accessible outside lecture. His tests overall were fair and he gave ample resource to prepare for them.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Although he's passionate about what he teaches and seems like a nice guy, his teaching is pretty abysmal. His lectures consist of him standing in front of a disorganized whiteboard talking to himself. Uploaded example problems and solutions consistently have errors in them, and the canvas page is never organized or up to date. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Lectures were glossed over review problems and slides were uploaded on canvas. Tests were much harder than these problems and most of the homework. Most test material was based off the labs because the TAs write and grade the tests and homework. A good TA is the key to passing this class, Dabiri was pretty much just the lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: very good instructor! He was always there for office hours, and often stayed longer if we needed him.  His lectures follows the book well, so there was no confusion in the material I was learning.  His tests were fair, and I feel he prepared us well for them.
This guy loves what he teaches. He posts lectures but no panopto videos. Come to office hours and he will dedicate himself to you. Tests were not easy but very fair; no trick questions.

excellent professor.  He explains the concepts well, and posts his lectures early enough that we can review them for class. He starts each class by reviewing where we left off from the last class, which is a big help getting me in gear for the class. We just took our first midterm, and I felt well prepared for it. I would easily recommend him.

One of the best professors I had.  I never realized how much I didn't know until i had to explain it to the person sitting next to me, which  then helped me to know what to go study. He was very approachable in office hours, and he gave me 100% every time I went  to office hours.

This professor is actually quite good.  A lot of students complained about discussing with your neighbor, but I found that it helped me to organize my thoughts, and find out things that I don't know, and to then take care of it.  He was always helpful in office hours, and as able to teach me well during office hours. I'd like him for my other class

Seems like a nice and smart guy, but he's not the best professor. Lectures are straight out of the reading you are assigned to and consist of him marking up examples (while not explaining them well) and telling you to discuss with your neighbor. Basically, his lectures are useless. Most of the learning comes from lab section. Get a good TA!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Wonderful person . . .alright teacher. He asks you to "discuss with your neighbor" a lot and cares that you work with others to arrive at an answer. You must read and understand the textbook to pass this class, for his lectures are basically a rundown of the same thing you already read in your textbook. ATTEND LAB SECTIONS, THEY SAVE YOUR GRADE!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Tough class. He is very passive in teaching. Relies heavily on slides, from which he will just circle and check things as if he is teaching from scratch. Dabiri clearly understands the content himself, but the way he teaches is very un-engaging. Your best hope is to study outside of class prior to lecture. Lab sections are helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He usually just reads off the slides given to him by the textbook, so lectures aren't that useful. There is a lot of homework every week. All the tests where either insanely hard or too long to do in the time allotted. Be prepared to learn a lot of the difficult topics on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: TAs can make/break the class. TAs make the exams and grade everything--NOT DABIRI. He never does problems by hand during lecture, only goes through the pre-made slides. Dabiri does not communicate with the TAs about expectations for the class. No clear grading criteria for exams either. Try to avoid Dabiri. Also, his office hours sucks. 0/5. PISA

Easily the worst professor I've had. Lecture is useless, he doesn't seem to review the information or look over the slides THAT ARE PRE-MADE by the software provider before coming. He basically garbles through 2 "example" problems per lecture and doesn't explain anything. He is frequently incorrect and the tests are unreasonable. AVOID. 0/5

He literally has the textbook slides copied from the company who produced them. And he just talks through the slides he didn't make, doesn't specifically show how to do practice problems. He always says turn to your neighbor and explain how to do the problem, which is a problem when he never explained the method in the first place.

Hes an enthusiastic professor who encourages participation among students, however I do not like his teaching style. He tends to go through the textbook slides and explains problems as he goes by circling, so he never actually does any problems himself. Because of this he doesn't explain the mindset and the process of going through problems well.

This is a tough class, and you have to be ready to participate to do well.  I had to put up with a lot of whiner classmates, and eventually worked on my own because I didn't want to put up with others who blamed the professor for their own failures.

One of the worst professors  I've ever had. Never did examples in class to help you. Lectures is him writing exactly what's on the book.  HW is insanely long for a 3 credit class.  HW assigned on a Friday and has to be done by Monday morning. Expect to put in 20 hours over a weekend to finish HW. DON'T take this class unless it is with another Prof

Most inconsistent teaching methods ever. Started as 30-90 minutes of posted videos to be watched prior to class then class was entirely review. It turned into a mixture of videos and class lecture, then strictly class lecture. Class attendance was the worst of any class I've ever had (518 avg). Only read the book, showed up to 25% of class.

He is hard but good, & is interested in making sure you're learning. He keeps us engaged in the class by having us turn to our neighbor & discuss what we are learning.  The weekly quizzes keep us from falling behind.  The 1st midterm was hard, but the 2nd was easier. If you take this class, be ready to put good time into it, but you'll learn a lot.

A great professor. You get used to the accent after the first week, never late to class, and her lectures were helpful and easy to follow. Tests were reasonable, although they make up 90% of your grade. A very good experience and I would definitely take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you get below the class average on the first midterm you are basically cooked, I scored 90% on both the second midterm and final and only ended up with a 3.0.
She is a good professor, and knew how to teach the content, but the first midterm was really long and hard, most people didn't finish on time. Then we didn't know what to expect for the other tests.

She has a strong accent. After a week or two, you get used to it. She doesn't teach the concept; she instead does problems. Her explanations are not good, but her tests are relatively easy sometimes. Tests are random, like they are easy, but there are too many problems, so you run out of time. Her lectures are def. not organized.

Professor Dos Reis is really good. As a student who has always been mid/a bit above average UW classes, I think that once you get used to her accent she's awesome. Her lectures are SO reflective of what is on the exams and the material she reviews in review sessions are actually the same material she tests on. Don't be scared by the other reviews

Wait pls disregard all the other negative reviews. She's actually great. Sure maybe a little hard to understand sometimes but her accent isn't even that bad, like definitely understandable just use your brain. She's very helpful in her office hours and I think genuinely cares about her students. She also has a dry sense of humor which is funny
Caring and willing to help. Lots of time for exams. Lectures lacked structure and clarity.

I honestly do not like dos reis so much so that I stopped going to her lectures and started to go to the lecture before mine (Prof Sanmarco). Even though I took Calc in high school, the way she taught made me forget everything I knew... I got better grades skipping and studying by myself than attending her lectures

Dos Reis spends the entire lecture doing two practice problems and explaining zero concepts which was incredibly unhelpful to my learning. I had to learn all the material on my own (textbook is great). Do not take her if you have never taken a calc class, you will be completely lost.
Genuinely Evil
take another professor

Dos Reis is an atrocious lecturer. She talks at light speed with a heavy french accent. She doesn't explain concepts well and her examples usually aren't of a comparable difficulty to what's on the homework or exams. I eventually just stopped going to her lectures and instead went to the section before mine.
She takes a whole lecture to explain one or two easy problems and test us in the harder versions of it and

Prof Dos Reis is legitimately such an engaging lecturer. She's so funny and really tries to make difficult concepts relatable to students. As a disclaimer, I did not take this class for credit, which is probably why I have such a positive view of real analysis.

Her lectures for 207 is pretty comprehensive and easy to follow. Apart from her strong french accent that can be hard to understand, she was able to explain the process and concepts well and clarifies people's questions effectively. Sometimes she comes late to the lectures which for a 50 minute lecture it can affect how much we learn by a lot.

Good professor at analysis course, especially in comparison with other professors. She has a heavy french accent, especially on the word thereom, but except that, she did great at lecturing and proving the theorems. But her exams are the hardest, and made up nearly 80% of all the points you can get for this course.

She's funny, engaging, and understandable. For me, her answers to questions were really helpful to build mathematical insight. The class was memorization and formula heavy, but I think differential equations as a subject tends to be a bit "hand-wavy" so I don't think that was a fault on her part. You need to do extra reading to solidify concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice and helpful in office hours but lectures are completely terrible. She is always 5-10 mins late to lectures, frequently gets lost in her own example problems. Going to lecture is a waste of time. Exams are not terrible but make up 90% of grade. Webassign homework is not very relevant to class problems. Avoid if you can't learn on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I thought her lectures were really bad and I just ended up doing all of the work on my own. The class isn't very hard in my opinion, you just have to be willing to put in the work. If you usually struggle in math, definitely take another section if you can.

Having Fanny Dos Reis my first quarter at UW was my, "welcome to college" moment. Once you get past her thick French accent, it is still hard to understand what she is teaching at times. I'm sure she means well in her teaching, but do not take Math 124 with her at the helm.

Quizzes have a large impact on your grade if you bomb them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would say, almost no homework which is great. But the pronunciation is somewhat "strange" I would say. It takes time for you to accommodate. Also, she sometimes forgets to record her voice on Panopto, which makes review being hard for us. She never uses PPT, always handwriting. You will easily get lost because you will forget about the question.
Consistently late and doesn't respect anyone's time. Constantly got lost in her own lectures and couldn't figure out where she made the mistake. One of the worst teachers I've ever had in my life.

most people overreact about the accent its really not an issue, however lectures are very unorganized and you'll be better off watching Thomas Carr lectures. Her tests are also ridiculously long and she would always be late getting them started so you will only have 45 minutes for a test that would take about an hour. in general DE is not that hard

Heavy accent, if English is not your first language lectures may be very hard to understand. Even if you can understand her, she frequently gets lost in her own lectures and confuses herself in example problems so it gets hard to follow. She is a few minutes late very often. Homework and class in general isn't super hard but the lectures just suck.

You need to completely disregard every other review of this professor. You will never have trouble understanding what she is saying. Her lectures and homework are well paced and easy if you attend lecture (or read textbook), and she is extremely willing to answer even the stupidest of questions--probably from the writers of the negative reviews.
She's kind of just not a good lecturer. Fanny Dos Reis is consistently late to class and the lectures make the material harder to understand (was better off just watching Thomas Carr on youtube).
never use PowerPoint, always hand writing, and always have time extension every class. The pronunciation is terrible and not easy to understand. The handwriting is unrecognizable.

Professor Dos Reis's lectures follow the structure of introducing a concept, then spending the rest of the lecture going over example problems. I disagree with a lot of reviews on this site, I found her accent easy to understand, and I found the examples helpful for understanding and completing the homework. Just depends on your learning style.

Going to lecture is a waste of time, you will have to learn and teach yourself the math sections on your own time. Lectures are not clear whatsoever and she does have a thick accent that is hard to understand. There was many times where she was even confused on what she was doing. Would not take her class.

Prof. Dos Reis was a decent professor; she was helpful during office hours and worked to ensure students understood the material. She wrote easy midterms, which hurt the curve and didn't prepare us well for the final, but you could easily score well on these! She also had an intense accent and sometimes used convoluted methods to approach questions

Final exam was unlike review material and noticeably more difficult than prior years exams, professor was basically useless and class could be done as effectively without her presence. No curve as well and partial credit was sparse.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her final was way harder than past finals, difficult to understand during lectures, you will need to learn in your own time don't waste time on lectures,

Genuinely the most horrific final. The midterms and example exams (from past quarters) that she provided were nothing like the exam. The rest of the class was manageable, but you're going to have to teach yourself the majority of the course (the textbook is great). Be ready for her to make multiple mistakes in lecture too
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her midterms and finals are wayyy harder compared to other professor's exams, which gave such an unfair disadvantage to us. Lectures also move very fast and are hard to understand.
She has a heavy French accent.

She can barely speak English; it's constantly hard to understand what the heck she's saying the majority of the time. Workload is the worst out of the Calc series. It's often hard to follow along in her lectures. The only pro about Fanny is that her tests are easier than the other teachers. I would strongly advise against taking her.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Consistently late to morning classes and explains topics in a roundabout and confusing way. She also insists on using a document camera, which made everything harder to see and understand. Class was paced poorly and I genuinely felt reading the textbook and doing online practice problems was more useful than going to her lectures.
Lowkey she not gonna teach anything

Prof. Fanny is an incredibly nice and caring person. I wasn't the biggest fan of her lecturing which is why I rated her a 4, but assuming you do the exam archives and homework, you will do great. I ended with a 4.0 and I studied a lot, and fortunately, Prof. Fanny's exams are very similar to the archives. Don't be discouraged by the other reviews.

Dos Reis was a very good professor. The class was hard, but so is every math class at UW (at least for me). She was always helpful when I emailed her with a question and was quite funny at times in class. Only down side is that she doesn't reply to emails on the weekend (good for her, bad for me lol). Would recommend!
Lectures were good and her office hours were helpful, but overall she is a tough grader so avoid if you can. Our class's final went so poorly that she lowered the passing grade by 8%.

Was almost always late to class. Didn't know how to use the doc camera, lighting and technology so everything she wrote was extremely hard to see. Very disorganized when trying to explain concepts and didn't link the theorems to example problems. The class felt rushed - she was always behind with material. Her exam reviews were not helpful

She is very disorganized and sometimes can't articulate her explanations and reasons for how and why she is solving a problem in a certain way. Her lectures were boring and she was always behind. Her lectures are very example heavy, she doesn't give the time of day to explain the theorems or how they work into her examples.

Very nice person but not a great teacher...Struggles to use a document camera and never seemed organized/ was often late to class, sometimes by 5-10 minutes. She knows the material well but all the examples covered in class were significantly easier than homework, which at times was ridiculous and TA's struggled to solve.

Lectures are practice problems. People hate but she is a good professor and a really easy grader. Biggest complaint is how she wrote during lectures. She would print out slides and write on them underneath the document camera, but the exposure was too high so nobody could ever see anything. Also meant you could never look back at lecture slides.

Prof. Fanny Dos Reis is a an amazing professor. She explains concepts very well during lecture and really cares about her students. All those reviews saying that "you can't understand her accent" are all pretty biased. But in the end it is math, the main way to get better at math is to do practice problems.
Her notes were very neat. Explained everything well. Didnt need to rely on the book much. Unlike Neal Koblitz in math 208
I got a 90% on the final. If i could then anyone could probs.

Professor Dos Reis covers the materiel well in class. The thing is to listen carefully.  She drops gems, great professional tips and advice from a PHD as asides.  She explains things in the lectures that the books just don't cover.  Well done.

I really liked Professor Dos Reis! She genuinely seems to care about her students and she is helpful in office hours. Her lectures consist of mostly practice problems- I recommend reading the textbook section prior to class as she tends to quickly jump into to new topics. Tests are fair and very much related to the problems done in class.
She is very nice and only wants to see you succeed. She gives a lot of partial points on midterm and exams. Lectures have lots of example problems. Definitely worth choosing her as your prof.

She's a really caring professor. Her lectures are a little fast-paced but she uses good example problems. I personally didn't do as well as I thought I would and wouldn't take her again, but others did really well. She gives a lot of partial credit and is very clear about what will be on the exams. Exams make up 90% of your grade, just beware

I think she is really a good professor, although her accent is a bit strange, but you will get used to it after listening to a few classes. Most of all, she is very clear and gives a lot of examples to help us understand new concepts and knowledge, I will definitely take her class again.

Wasn't a fan of her teaching style but she's very caring and is probably the easiest grader I ever had. As long as you show an attempt at the problems on the exams she'll give you a good amount of points.

She is absolutely an excellent professor. Her graphs are clear and show all the key detials. Her accent might be confusing at first, but it’s easy to understand if you get used to it. Her grading is excellent. She only deducts a half point off for calculating mistakes.

Would recommend! Haven't had any problem understanding her accent and find it kind of cool (anyone who understands English should be able to understand her). Cares a lot for her students and does want all her students to have a good grade. Easy grader. Very helpful in office hours. I mean math is a hard subject, you always have to spend extra time.

She tends to state steps rather than explain. It's hard to understand her accent and on top to try to comprehend steps without explanation. First 2 lectures was her showing the side of her face and I mean literally. Imagine if you were standing at the very front corner of the classroom trying to look at the board in the middle. Self study class.
she's a nice professor but horrible at lecturing. Hard to understand accent and her diagrams are impossible to understand. Handwriting is also pretty bad and all over the place.
Concepts easy to understand, helpful and nice to students.

Ridiculously easy grader. If you AT MINIMUM make a reasonable attempt for every question on the homework and exams there is absolutely no way youll fail. Strong French accent but those claiming that they cant understand a word she says, youre either disabled or just xenophobic. Not a great teacher by any means but extremely easy to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dos Reis is a very sweet and caring professor. But, this doesn't make up for the disheveled lectures and unreasonable exam questions. Her lectures are near impossible to follow and her typed up notes are also filled with errors. Part of me wishes I tried harder, but part of me feels like the instructor is also at fault.

She is very nice and cares a lot about her students. Homeworks and exams are very reasonable, but it's almost impossible to understand her lectures. I have had a lot of instructors with accents, but she was definitely the hardest to understand. She is great otherwise, but her class will be difficult because of her accent, which is very unfortunate.

Exams are not that difficult. She is very nice and caring and I had no issues understanding her accents. Lectures sometimes feel like a quiz section where we work together to prove theorems, very fun if you participate but easy to dose off if you don'. Very rigorous structure: we proved basically everything so we didn't get through a lot of content

Pros: VERY AVAILABLE outside of class Good amount of question for practice. Cons: Some accent. Question too Standard (Only basic knowledge, not stimulating) Class too Classis(prove thm, don't have personal style)
Professor Does Reis is incredibly caring and wants students to succeed, but her lectures are confusing and hard to understand. The amount of homework is fair and her tests are reasonable.
It's just weird. A lot of the time I don't know what she's doing.

Prof. Dos Reis' lectures somewhat follow the structure of the textbook, but in-class proofs are often different than the text. She does not spoon-feed proofs and instead has the class work together to solve a problem. Homework is difficult but there are not many assignments. Her accent is not hard to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: wish anyone who takes her class good luck, you might start to think about dropping out of math major after taking her brilliant class
She barely gives feedback. Her lecture is the worst one I've ever seen. Never take math course with her plz.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Fanny is very friendly and nice. lecture is well organized and easy to follow. exams exactly correspond to what she covered in class. you should be totally fine if you go to classes and finish all the homework
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very disorganized and wings all proofs based on classroom input. Sounds like a good idea but means we get sidetracked with terrible proofs that last days to finish. You never get hw back with feedback so you go into the tests blind if you are doing anything correct at all. Hardly ever responded to questions on piazza.
Best professor ever :(

Very disorganized, I gained very little from her lectures and mostly relied on the textbook and YouTube. Homework was very infrequent and tests were not hard. She does do in class quizzes so go to lecture for those. The material itself is not very hard, you just have to teach yourself a lot of it.

Everything about this course was unclear. It took me days just to find a syllabus and even longer to understand where she was getting her material from. Content very loosely related to textbook, prepare to be insanely confused. After class we all talk about how hard it is to understand her.

Her teaching style is very disorganized and lectures are not helpful as she only does practice problems to no end without teaching many concepts. Not very clear on due dates/ class schedule. Does assign reasonable homework.
She is a great professor. If you come to her office hour, she is really helpful! One homework assignment for a week, easy to do. Exams are fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--TEST HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: Disorganization - this is key. She lectures like she's doing her homework - no stopping, no explanation, just writing and dictating (as well as she can) what she writes. Also, terrible accent, not fluent in english. This plays a factor in her terrible lecturing ability.

Honestly not a huge fan of her. Extremely spacey and disorganized with grading and posting assignments, and answering emails or questions on piazza. It's actually very annoying as to how poor her communication is. Then I don't think her teaching is great either. Just kinda jumps right into class without prior explanations

Now I finally understand why her class always have open spots, DON'T take her class, her lecture is useless and she does not care if you understand the content or not, and she is super lazy, you don't get your midterms back until the end of the quarter and she doesn't even give you the answer for the midterm. She also doesn't showup to office hour.

Professor Dos Reis is very friendly and generally teaches well. Does a lot of examples to show you each and every way to approach the solution. She's always happy to stop and answer any questions you have. Occasionally jumps around while explaining concepts, just pay attention and you won't be too lost. Assigns very reasonable amounts of homework.

I'm a math major and I studied my tail off for this class. Despite having the solutions to the various problem times hardwired, I was not able to finish any of the exams due to lack of time. I thought the curve would save me, but as previously mentioned, the class is *not curved* so I did worse than expected. Lectures are fast, but useful.

Professor Reis is definitely a good instructor and does not deserve all the bad comments. Her lecture was clear in general and you could ask her whenever you have confusions since she was always patient with questions no matter in class or after the class. The every-week quiz and tests are quite easy. You will be fine if you do listen to the class.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. Her lectures were messy and all over the place, very unorganized, and her handwriting was extremely difficult to read. She's a great person and she's very nice and flexible with accommodations when needed, but she was still a horrible teacher.
Was very nice a good at explaining things. She was always willing to give you extra help in her office hours. Her accent may be difficult for some to understand.
Worst instructor ever. Only few students really listen and understand. Lots of mistakes on the notes.

take any other teacher over her, I mean it.  It was the worst teaching I have ever received in math (and possibly my college career and I'm in my 3rd year).  If you have a bad feeling about her the first couple lectures, it's right, get out & switch.    no background info, jumps right in and you're like ?? confusing lacks explanations jusbad

Professor Dos Reis is clear and very passionate about what she is teaching. If you don't understand something, go to office hours, she is very helpful! Do the suggested problems because she picks those problems for the weekly quizzes and tests. Overall, best math professor I've had at UW so far. Would recommend taking her class.

Her accent makes her difficult to understand and her lectures are EXTREMELY unorganized and confusing. She's obviously brilliant but she is a terrible lecturer. There is no fluidity  and it seems as though were learning completely unrelated topics in each class.

I learned that she is a very easy grader; however, she does not curve your final grade. Based on my experience from previous math classes at UW, grades were curved pretty heavily, so I was expecting a fairly high grade from this class. I was surprised and disappointed with the grade I got.
This professor is not good.

Mrs. Dos Reis is an incredible mathematician, very smart and very helpful. She has a very cool accent that positively adds up to her pleasant character. Would definitely take any other class taught by her. Eventhough, she goes over the material very fast, if you occasionally go to office hours, you'll do fine.

Very qualified, knows her stuff, but a terrible lecturer. First 12 of the course was review from 307 and 308, so easy to catch on. Second half was brutally challenging. Lectures were unorganized, online notes were useless. Had to research for notes online and do a lot of self studying. Easy grader. Course as a whole was not challenging, she was.
thick accent, boring class :/really difficult course and very fast paced.
Pretty easy if you go to class. If you miss class, get notes. Also she's got a bit of a thick accent so she's a little hard to understand.

Despite her being passionate about the content she teaches, she is not a good teacher.  Grading expectations are unclear, content taught in class is basic, but concepts that are tested in exams are a lot more complex. Very stingy on wording in exam responses. Side tracks often during lectures and lots of micromanaging as well.

A classic weed out course. Heavy emphasis on using the “exact phrasing” in your exam answers to get full marks. Ellie seems to be a generally nice person; her lecture style, however, is scattered, disorienting, and without structure.

Theobald really bugged me the wrong way when she says that there are really endless possiblitlites of answers that are right, but when in the exam, they are very, very, very specific about what they want. The exams are atrocious and so unclear what they really want. Prepare to do lots of outside work for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Theobald organized the course in a way that it was very confusing as to what knowledge would be required for quizzes. This also made it challenging to do well because they were wanting ultra specific answers on the quiz yet in class they would accept anything as a good answer. The content itself is quite mundane and I would not take again.

Class had required lectures, but they were ultimately not helpful and moved very slowly. Quizzes are less based on content knowledge and more on how closely you could match the wording in the rubric. What would be on the test was also unclear, they only said "anything from the past few weeks" rather than clearly stating the content.

The lectures most of the time did not help, but at least we didn't need to go over content that wasn't covered in lecture. The exams were okay, but I think some questions were ridiculous though, like you needed to be on par with the wording to get points. Profs were not that accessible, and the practice questions will be your savior!

Didn't really like this class. Lectures, readings, and exams felt disconnected, and tests expected super specific answers. Partial credit & regrade requests might as well be your best friends. Lectures weren't very helpful either. The class grading curve was also atrocious. Good luck if you're taking BIO 180 with her.

I went into this prepared to work hard, but all the work you put in doesn't matter. what matters is your ability to answer random data questions tangentially related to content. Only ridiculously specific answers get credit, so your grade is up to TA kindness. she doesn't provide actual content in lecture, she uses unreliable student responses.

Theobald has charisma, but not the kind needed for this class. She makes a whole bunch of noise just so say nothing of meaning. You're better off just reading the textbook and doing it all on your own than sitting through her lectures.

She is nice, but her teaching style is overly bubbly, like a teacher for younger kids. She also likes to interrupt when a student is speaking. Content is easy if you have a background, do practice Q's and analyze the answers wording + why they said it and you will do good.

She's a really nice person but just doesn't teach that well. I came in with bio knowledge so I didn't have to pay a lot of attention. Just use bio vocab and you're good on tests. Labs felt irrelevant at times though.

Theobald gets a bad rap but the reality is she is so much better than a lot of BIO department professors because she actually cares. She shows up to exams and comes to every lecture with a lot of enthusiasm and passion. I would 100% choose her again.

Professor Theobald is quite enthusiastic, but her teaching style doesn't work for everyone. The workload is heavy, with mandatory attendance and daily quizzes. While the TAs are great, the lectures can feel disjointed. For study prep, try using Unstuck ai alongside the textbook.

You know what. I wrote an immensely poor rating for Theobald when I finished her class in the spring quarter for 180, but now that I have Nemhauser for 200 I take it all back. I've been enlightened. I want Theobald back.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Theobald was such a kind, genuine professor, but her methods of teaching are very specific to a certain type of student. Her lectures have more examples than definitions, requiring knowledge of the concepts before going into the class. The workload is manageable, with readiness quizzes before each class. The TAs are really wonderful in lab!

I LOVE PROFESSOR THEOBALD! she was so lively and easy to learn from. I could easily remember anything she said because of how excited she was about it. To really succeed in her classes though, it is necessary to do the readings before class since she teaches class as if you have. Also heavy workload but very manageable. 100/10 would take again
Annoying hard to listen to during lecture. Exams graded harshly to what I exactly she wants to hear and her own made up definitions.

Lectures as if we are kindergarteners and teaches us the bare bones concepts but grades like we are experts. I think some people appreciate her "enthusiasm" but honestly it is distracting to the course. Lectures are really not very helpful imo and really would not recommend taking biol180 with her, take it with Mo Turner, i've heard she's better.

everything ppl have said, but DON'T TAKE HER, take biol 180 with Mo turner!! theobald teaches like an elementary school grader but grades like we are experts. exams drop your grade SO MUCH. she's a super frustrating non helpful lecturer especially for an intro class.

There's an overwhelming amount of work and weekly exams. Grading is very harsh and they will dock you for the smallest things. If you don't do it how they want, you get docked. Try to argue back for points? Nothing of substance. Theobald is a nice professor but the way the class is set up is horrible. Too much work for almost nothing of substance.

This class had mandatory lectures, grade group call in KANE 130, and reading quizzes every single day. The professor was sweet but her lectures were all over the place and virtually pointless. None of the topics flowed together or corresponded to each other when they easily could have making this class much more confusing than needed.
Hard to understand and lecture kinda not helping you really need to rely on your own to understand thing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Looks like a lovely and great professor at first, but as the quarter goes by her explanation of the lecture is kinda not helping and over the place. The exam is not easy but not hard also but the grading and her answer key sometimes kinda confusing leading to a big loss of point. She's a great professor but sometimes it she can be very confusing.

She uses outdated practice exams that are almost 10 years old, when asked for help avoided the questions and not even the TA's knew how to help when I showed the practice exams she gave out and said "w-t-f is this problem". Wastes class time on rants during exam prep days. If you can wait for another professor to teach this class then wait please.

Theobald is getting some hate but she's a nice person with a unique teaching style. Tbr you can quizlet every assignment, not open the book and show up to lecture and be fine for tests as long as you practice a little bit on things you don't know. first test is deceivingly hard tho, and things gotta be worded specifically, but can always drop one

This class is quite archaic in its teaching style, but somehow ineffective at the same time. Exam review sessions are a waste of time, and the lectures are often interrupted by students asking questions that can easily be googled. Overall, I can tell Elli is trying to do her best, but there are some key oversights that simply cannot be ignored.

Theobald is caring/enthusiastic, but teaches this class like a 1st grade teacher. She interrupts students by saying "yeah yeah" or "totally great" or "this is so fun" which prevents anyone from actually understanding the questions. Lectures don't explain things in useful ways (pictures only). Exams are fair but EXTREMELY time crunched.

Theobald is an enthusiastic caring and kind professor, but she has taught Bio180 in 2024 like an elementary school class. Labs are fairly useful and help to reinforce concepts. Exams are fair but very time crunched and graded on a mark scheme. She interrupts students in lecture by saying "yeah" or "totally great" and it's hard to understand.

she herself is a kind person but she gives 3rd grade art teacher, which isn't a bad thing but it is when shes teaching an intro class. she doesn't actually teach she expects you to know it due to the book readings but then says she doesn't like the book.. so its like bruh. Again nice person, but not a good teacher, you have to teach yourself

While Dr. Theobald has been recognized for her research on innovative anti-competition teaching practices, her application of them in her own classroom is flawed. Lectures are informative but not particularly interesting. She has also played a large role in the strict rules that now exist in the UW Bio dept. which discourage student advocacy.

Eli is a very nice, enthusiastic lady, but one of the toughest graders I've ever had. If you don't use specific key words in your answers on exams, you will lose points. There aren't a lot of resources for studying for exams, so take advantage of the lecture notes and anything else you can.
One of the worst professors I've ever had.

People hate her, but Theobald is very enthusiastic about science and makes incredibly boring lectures bearable. Bio180 as a class itself has weird wording on exams that tests your writing ability more than concepts, but that isn't because of her. As long as you put effort into learning how to write in her preferred manner, you will ace this class.

Dr. Theobald is a very nice professor who tries her best to excite you about biology. The objectives and material are clear most of the time. She is often too receptive to questions, so we have less time for content. It's also hard to decipher whether she's excited because an answer is correct or because the answer is wrong and helps us learn more.

Professor Theobald was nice, but I found this class asking us to do a lot of work. Make sure you read the readings for more in depth knowledge on key concepts you cover in lecture because it will be tested. Exams are tricky and do all practice problems necessary. She doesn't really teach that much in class, but will answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Fine prof. No real problems with the way she taught the class, and for the most part 180 is generally chill as long as you stay on top of things. The exams are kind of annoying and you can lose points for not going in-depth enough even if it's beyond what the question was asking you.

Very enthusiastic, passionate, friendly professor that always tries to make sure we use all available resources. Strict grading criteria, but prof encourages a cooperative learning space instead of a competitive one.

everyone who rated professor theobald poorly just didn't understand how the lectures would help and apply to the exams and the understanding of our knowledge. this teaching style definitely isn't for everyone but it is very effective. its a bit of a learning curve to understand how concise she wants the answers but once you got it down you're fine

you can tell that dr theobald is very passionate about what she does. it may seem like reading the assigned sections have nothing to do with lecture, but it does. reading it familiarizes you with the stuff and the lectures help you apply that knowledge. this teaching style might not work for everyone though
Dr. Theobald is an incredibly passionate and well-spoken professor. If you pay attention, show up to class, and do the homework you can easily get a 3.3 (which is good on uw stem standards)

Theobald is decent at explaining concepts and her class isn't very difficult. The grading system, is EXTREMELY picky, so be careful with how you word things. Do the practice problems and you'll be fine.
Professor is very enthusiastic and patient. Passionate and friendly and very direct.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Understand the concepts being taught in lecture? Great! Doing all of the assigned coursework? Way to go! Now go do a million practice questions, write your answers *exactly* as they appear in her answer key for exams, and you may have a fighting chance in her class.

I urge y'all disregard most of the negative ratings that people have given Professor Theobald. As long as you actually do the work for this class you should be fine. This is a relatively easy class. You may have to figure out how to word you answers, but practice exams make the format extremely clear. I can't recommend Professor Theobald enough

I don't usually write bad reviews for professors but we have just spent an entire 50min lecture talking about the ethics of textbooks instead of learning about actual biology when the final exam is in one week. She rarely teaches any content in class but expects everyone to know exactly how she would define complex biological concepts on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Her lectures are horrendous, she does not teach the material and goes on long irrelevant tangents that have nothing to do with the curriculum. The tests are all short answer and she grades on specific ansers that she wants but are extremely specific and not logical.

Professor Theobald is an extremely nice person, but her lectures are super confusing and have little to do with the exams. Tests are written response, extremely hard, AND are worth 55% of your overall grade. I definitely feel like the only way to succeed in this class is to make friends and figure things out together.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Theobald has very difficult tests but the labs and readiness questions are worth a lot and fairly easy points so it's not too hard to get a decent grade in her class

First time I've felt compelled to leave a poor review for an instructor. Dr. Theobald does her best to be engaging and says everyone can do well in her course - that's simply not true. Make no mistake: this is a weed out course. Exams are unnecessarily hard & graded excessively harshly. If you're able to, take Bio elsewhere & don't ruin your GPA.
She's really funny and really good at explaining things. Tests are quite difficult but the class is very welcoming and fun.

She does an excellent job making student understanding the concepts. However, her test has little relations to the concept she taught in class, it feels like a ACT science section test instead of a real biology test, the amount of reading is extremely difficult especially for international students. it is impossible to finish the test on you own.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very enthusiastic professor, however, is terrible at actually teaching the content on her own tests. Tests are supposedly open ended, but they are looking for ONE very specifically worded response. Read the textbook for content and do infinite practice problems to learn how to word your answer if you want a good grade. Otherwise take the L.

I ABSOLUTELY LOVED her! Don't let any bad reviews scare you about her class. The only people I have heard not like her class are those who do not like biology and are not willing to put in the work to do well. Easy to succeed if you want to learn and are willing to put in time and effort. Very caring, and enthusiastic prof, and not too much work.

She organizes the content pretty well, and test questions are reasonable. Minus 1 point because I simply detest ecology (and she failed to make it interesting like some extremely charismatic profs would be able to) and because a lot of concepts are oversimplified so I barely learned anything from the quarter.

She is passionate about biology and willing to help. But between dismissing questions she doesn't know the answer to, to having no clue about the answers to her own test prep problems, there are huge gaps in her lectures. Expect a lot of filler. Exams are free response and are graded based on specific words. Daily quizzes, weekly reflections

Textbook is very good. Theobald poorly conveys course expectations and the depth of content students. Exams are longgg and good luck interpreting the rubric. Well-meaning professor and lenient w grading drops, but goes on frequent tangents and is a little scatterbrained. Do a lot of practice problems, and don't bother going on exam review days

The content isn't hard - just the tests are. Dr. Theobald does a good job on teaching the content, making sure its digestible. If you understand the content, then you'll understand the test. However, do as many practice problems as possible to make sure you understand how to ANSWER the test. That's where many lost points.

The class is organized and you can get credit from various factors, not just exams. Since the class covers evolutionary bio, the grading criteria can be very subjective, so make sure you understand the content really well. PAY ATTENTION TO HER LECTURES - that's where most of the test content is. She was nice but could come off as patronizing.

Dr. Theobald is one of the kindest, most motivated professors I have met in the STEM field. Lectures cover the textbook, exams, and little things in between. She does everything possible to prep her students for exams. However, answers that may be accepted in class may not be accepted in the exam. Recommend going to office hours.
Professor Theobald was an amazing professor. Polls, labs, and RQ will save your grade do them!! Also exams are lecture heavy rather than textbook heavy which is good. Exam final isn't cumulative.

Fairly easy introductory biology course, if you read the textbook and can follow along in lecture. Exam problems can be challenging, but if you understand the concepts and what is being taught in the class, you'll be fine. I didn't really get that much out of lectures, but Theobald does great focusing on what's important.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is really energetic & does an amazing job engaging with the class. She encourages collaboration & really cares about biology. With that being said she would serve better as an elementary school teacher. At the very least someone please stop letting her write exams. Everything from the exam questions to the grading of exams is a mess

bio with Eli is horrendous. she's preppy & cares about bio but that doesn't make up for being a bad uni prof. in class you can argue multiple different points but the tests do not allow for this AT ALL. Her exam questions...wack. Her grading key...even more wack. would be an easy 4.0 without her absurd exams and petty grading key. good luck

Easyyy concept driven class. Although there is a textbook, I never read it and got above an 85 on all exams. Just attend lecture & you will be fine because she never tests you on things she doesn't mention in lecture. Tests are written, short response (be careful with how you explain things), but it was easy especially since she's a fun lecturer!!

Professor Theobald likes to talk really fast and her lectures felt very rushed. She really encourages peer collaboration and requires mandatory lecture attendance with polling points. However, I often felt like she wasted time during lectures talking about irrelevant information. I had to do most of my learning self-taught by reading the textbook.

Theobald is amazing professor and teaches well. Her practice sheets are fairly similar to her exams. Her lectures are very participation heavy and not the best for introverts/ heavily note taking students. She will push and desires for people to join study group. Her exams are hard but everything else is pretty much effort. Make sure to study well

Professor Theobald seems like a really nice person, but her class is so disorganized. Sometimes it seems like the practice questions aren't written by the same person that writes the exams. The lecture tries to oversimplify the material and the exams are much more complex. It feels like there is no way to actually know what will be on the test!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Theobald was one of the best professors I have had at UW, if not the best. Her tests are all short answer and very difficult at times, but somehow she makes the 400 person room feel like 30 when she's lecturing. Great teacher and the class is very future focused, which can be challenging because the whole class is application based.

Dr. Theobald is a pretty great professor. The lectures are interesting and cover the content well. Participation in class does matter in the sense that you have to poll in every lecture for attendance. Highly recommend taking the optional bio113 class and making a study group early on. Exams are a bit vague, but it is not that hard to pass.

Prof. Theobald is super duper nice and radiates mom vibes. Her lectures are easy to understand and she encourages cooperation amongst students. Exams are pretty long and short-answer, and graders often look for precise wording, so expect those to be kind of rough at first.

Theobald places a lot of importance in interacting with your peers, which is something I ended up really appreciating from the class and thought contributed to my learning. She is a clear and fair about her class policies, and does an excellent job of trying to create individual connections in a class of 500+ students.
would not recommend it. Her tests often are pretty semantic, it's not enough that you understand concepts you very much need to know the exact terms

She is very particular in terms of her grading when it comes to exams. You may answer a question correctly for the most part, but if you are even just one word off, then you will lose at least 50%. Additionally, her lectures are fairly dry, and surface level compared to the material you are learning

Eli is a super caring and passionate lecturer. She is very fair and sets out all her expectations so they are very clear. The class is set up so all information can be obtained though lectures although there is a textbook. This class was a fun learning experience and I highly suggest taking it while Eli is teaching.

Lectures are dry and exams are very toughly graded. Your answers have to use the exact words and sentences that are in the key. Her class is discouraging for students entering UW with a passion for biology. Changed my career path completely because of this class.

She needs Grammarly. You might know the answer but if you don't  speak theobaldian and get stuff wrong because the question is confusing not because you are bad at biology. The homework and labs are worth a lot but its easy, its not curved but if you do everything and get like a 65% on your midterms and final you can get about a 2.5

She's really nice, but her exams :) ARE SOOOO LONNNNGGGGG. We had 4 exams total, and only one time that we got all the questions answered. The exam might be different in person. Nice person, definitely a tough grader.

Professor Theobald was a very nice person and I enjoyed her lectures and TA's. She seemed to care for the success of her students. She is known to ramble occasionally and some of her lectures were contradictory.

Prof Theobald isn't the best lecturer and it often felt like we didn't get to the point of the lesson. Exams are often "8 questions" long but have multiple subsections that all require 1-2 sentence answers and grading criteria aren't clear at all. I highly recommend having a solid study plan in place for this class if you want to pass.
Lectures are engaging and fun. You can tell she cares about the students. Tests are very difficult though.

Lectures were interesting and also involved talking with those around you which helped me learn better. Theobald seems nice and accessible outside of class. Readiness questions are stupid and graded on correctness so just make sure to double check your answers. The in person exams were much harder than the online ones. Overall a doable class.

Professor Theobald can be a bit or miss for some students but I loved her teaching style. If you do practice problems and stay on top of the readings then you’re set for this class. Study groups are also really helpful. The professor genuinely cares about her students and she is super enthusiastic, I would totally recommend her as a professor!

Doing well in this class is not impossible if you have a solid AP Bio/Envir background. Theobald has difficult exams, but if you write fast, think fast, and know your stuff then you'll do fine. She is caring, compassionate and open to you reaching out if you need help. She plugs study groups a lot though, and they're kind of unnecessary.

Dr. Theobald is genuinely so enthusiastic and passionate about biology - my favorite professor at UW so far! The lecture content itself is not difficult to understand, especially with an IB/AP foundation, so it only required light book skimming. The exams are challenging and do focus more on theoretical concepts, so averages were around 65-70%

Theobald is a nice person but beware of her difficult exams. A lot of the material is not about what you know but how you can apply it to real world situations. There is a lot of statistics, interpreting of graphs, and designing hypothetical experiments. Use the study resources, read the textbook, and pay attention during lectures.

Dr. Theobald is the best professor I ever had. She is so caring, genuine and will not hesitate to go above and beyond for all of her students (and she has a lot!). Her lectures are so engaging and she is clearly passionate about 180. A lot of students criticize her exams but they are actually very straightforward if you practice. I love her!

Dr Theobald is by far the best professor I've ever had. Not only does she love the material she teaches, but if you ever need help (extra study problems, resources on campus, help discerning exams) she goes out her way to provide you with all you need. This class is difficult, but it's an introductory biology course and that's expected.

Both lectures and readings seem irrelevant to exam content. It is really about learning the main ideas and hoping you can apply them to arbitrary hypothetical questions on exams. Theobald is totally great and totally enthusiastic about the course which would be okay if she was actually as understanding or flexible as a professor as she portrays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: TOTALLYYYY AWESOME!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TOTALLY AWESOME
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Shes good but has flaws. Enthusiasm is there just not the teaching ability. Study the past exams she gives out, and the practice problems of the day and exam scores will be in the 70-80 average. Set aside some time in for the class for everything builds off each other. Class is not competitive so its up to you to get all the points possible.

She has a decent lecture that is straightforward and easy to understand. However, the class is exam-based, and the difficulty of the exam always goes well beyond her lecture. The exam is reading heavy requires people to have a deep understanding of the knowledge as well as a strong reading skill and the wording of the question is super confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't know why Dr. Theobald has such terrible ratings, she's actually great. She really cares about her students, has engaging lectures, and provides lots of opportunities to get points in her class. The class is not that bad, as long as you sign up for Bio 113 and put in time outside of class you should do fine.

This class was the worst experience of my entire college career. Eli makes herself out to be so compassionate, so understanding, but truthfully shes very impatient and does not take kindly to people who question her. She says the class is noncompetitive and she dropped out of college because of that but the HIGHEST grade on test 2 was 95%!! BS

Prof. Theobald is a lovely person, however this course was one of the worst experiences of my college career. Her teaching and grading style are difficult to grasp and I dont feel like I really learned anything in this course other than that I no longer wanted to major in biology. I would only suggest this for people ready to study a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The exams are HARD, but in my opinion professor theobald is such an amazing teacher that its worth it. Ive never had a teacher so friendly, positive, and eager to teach. She makes you want to learn and encourages any and all questions. I think a good attitude in a teacher really rubs off on students, and she has it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Overall, Prof. Theobald did a solid job teaching BIOL 180. Yes, the exams are tough and the grading is extremely controversial, but Prof. Theobald evidently cares, is excited to teach this course and helps provide many resources to support students. The exams aren't fun, but Prof. Theobald does her best.

Theobald is a great option for 180. I think any dislike for her comes more from the subjectivity of test answers and thats it. In person, she has lectures that makes sense and gives plenty of practice material for exams. She is willing to listen to student feedback and cares about how students are doing. Would take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Her lectures were useless, but the required readings were helpful. She really oversimplified the material, and her exams weren't necessarily difficult, but the majority of the time was spent trying to decipher her terribly worded questions. When people complained about the ambiguity she said: "Don't focus too much on what the questions are asking".

Don't do the readings, it's a waste of time. The content is easy, the tests are the not. It's keyword grading so if your wording is slightly off even if you understand the question, you lose points. Get yourself a good study group because the exams are group.
good luck lol
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She goes out of her way to make it seem like she is your friend but is the WORST grader I have ever encountered. Throughout the course we were encouraged to think creatively but on every single exam answers were expected to match her criteria word for word. It was pretty demoralizing to lose points repeatedly for things like that. My TA was great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The reading, the lecture, and the exam are not related at all. Did not learn anything from her class. Did not have enough time to finish all the questions on the exams.

Avoid taking this class at all costs if you can. The tests will make or break you. Not only does she not give enough time but grades questions on how well you worded the response the way she wanted them to be. You must be a fast typer, thinker, writer, as tests are timed and questions are long and also the scenarios given for each set of questions
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: she did not care if someone is cheating in our exams, she does not know how to teach, she does not follow her class policy, she has no credibility in her class, her exams are nonsense, it does not reflect your knowledge or ability, nightmare professor, please don't take her class, you will regret.

The information you learn in class is not sufficient enough to prepare you for the test and the tests felt like typing exams. The lectures are so repetitive and are just restating the reading you already read and the practice exams are way easier than the exam so it isn't really helpful as well. The grading is also super nitpicky and illogical.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Theobald genuinely spoke to us like we were children and always used a condescending tone. We learned no biology in lectures and all of the valuable info was from the textbook. Her tests didn't represent her lectures at all and you have to use specific terminology to even get partial credit. I've always excelled in bio, but she makes it impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The content overall wasn't too bad. The exams were a nightmare though. I had an awesome study group where we met 2-3 times a week to go over all the practice problems the class uploaded for us. It sucked when we did poorly, but we overall scored around the high 70s and low 80s on the exams. BIOl 180 is considered the worst out of the three.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's a great person and a good lecturer. The content itself is relatively easy/organized and similar to AP Biology. However, she is overly harsh and specific on her grading for exams. If you learn how to take her tests and answer in the way she wants, this class will be a breeze for you. Homework isn't long, and labs/pre-labs are insanely easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Class was easy to do okay, hard to excel. I took AP Bio in high school so take this with a grain of salt, but I thought grading was indicative of most bio tests; material isn't hard, most work lies in learning how to take the tests. Prof cares a lot about her students and tries to make lectures as engaging as possible-- Did a lot with what she had.

Prof Theobald is a caring person but that's about it. Her exams are the hardest I've ever taken since they're extremely specific and cryptically graded while lecture is not helpful as she oversimplifies the material. She is passionate about science, and her class got me to "think like a scientist" but that won't be enough for the rest of bio series

Sorry to say that she was the worst professor I've had at UW so far. Lectures are very disorganized and exams have the strangest questions. She is a very sweet person though, I just think her style of teaching is more suited towards younger childrenher lectures feel like how primary or middle school teachers teach science.

Theobald isn't a great lecturer. Her slides are messy and she never gave us clear answers to questions asked during lecture. HOWEVER, she does provide a lot of study materials and did alter her tests after students raised concerns. The topics aren't hard, but if you didn't word your answers the way she wants you to, you won't get points.

in class, professor theobald makes it seem very easy but the tests are very difficult. no matter how many practice problems you do, you never know exactly what will show up on the exams. the grading is also very unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She has a great and bubbly personality, so she would get a 5/5 if she were a kindergarten teacher.
