Literally never take her class she just writes and writes and expects u to know what shes talking about. Throughout the lectures its only the same 2 grown people who would answer her questions and people keep not showing up to her lecture bc she doesnt really teach. 0/5
Feels more like a handwriting marathon than a chemistry class — zero structure, just writing nonstop with no real teaching.

She's very kind, but her teaching style is extremely hard to follow. The lectures are disorganized, and she handwrites everything on the slides, which makes it hard to focus what she talked in lectures. Her handwriting is also difficult to read. You're basically left to teach yourself. If you need structure, this class will be frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She was extremely unorganized, every lecture had 40+ handwritten slides with scribbles and arrows that made it hard to follow. She mostly reads directly from the textbook with no additional explanation, and the lecture feels redundant. Always asking if we prefer 220 or 221, I would 100% choose 220. This was the worse course in this equence.

(took for 224!!!) gives note templates to fill out/follow along lectures with, but the lectures are pretty standard, has pollev questions during them for credit, so you can't skip too many. Felt weirdly passive aggressive sometimes towards students that would ask more high-level questions? Won't be mean to your face though. Exams are like the hw.

Dr. Ingalls is very sweet and she is accessible outside of class. That being said, her lectures are unfortunately extremely boring and dense. Reach out to her if you need help, she is always willing to meet outside of class... but her lectures are pretty unpleasant. Very kind prof though!

crammed way to much content into the course. Litterally writing non stop all class to the point where i was too busy focusing on taking notes so fast that i wasnt able to even pay attention to what she was saying or understand what she was talking about. horrible teaching style. class average on tests was C-, clearly the issue is the instructor.
Reads from textbook during lecture, doesn't answer student questions directly

She was very nice as a person. Taught directly from the textbook so reading the book helped a lot in understanding concepts. Exams were stressful but it was helpful to review homework and resources supplied. Nothing on exams was out of pocket. Very tough class and her teaching style didn't add much. Basically just study often and you'll do okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Ingalls had never taught this course before and I thought she did a great job! It was nice having a professor who taught directly from the textbook and her tests (minus the final) were always very reasonable. She provided a lot of time and resources outside of class for extra help, which was great given this was the accelerated course. Solid!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: avoid this professor at all costs... although she may strike you as a "nice" person, she is an incompetent lecturer. She lectures straight from the textbook, however, her exams are usually not reflective of what is learned through the text/lectures. Take CHEM237 instead.

While she was nice and clearly passionate about the subject, during lecture I found that she read off the slides a lot--oftentimes I felt like I learned a lot more from the TAs during quiz and lab sections.

You can tell that she knows a lot about the course content and she is very passionate about her subject. She is very enthusiastic about wanting to help her students, and there is a lot of support if you find the content difficult. However, she mostly just reads off the slides in lecture, and you will find that you learn a lot more outside of class.
Her teaching style was good, there were reading quizzes every night and lecture quizzes, but I found that helpful to help not fall behind, and to keep me accountable.

I found Prof Novitski to be a great lecturer and very passionate about ensuring students understand content. Good demonstrations and examples in class to help with understanding concepts. Definitely recommend attending lectures and doing work outside of class as it helps your grade very much. Tests are difficult but study hard and you can do well.
Prof. Novitski had good example problems in class and the curve and grading scale were fair!

I think Novitski was one of the best professors I've had so far. She's super knowledgable about physics and is a really good lecturer, I'm not really good at physics but she makes it super easy to understand. Just watch out for the tests as they are really difficult and the MCQ portion has questions that are similar to FRQs.

Highly underrated professor- most of the complaints against her have more to do with how college courses are run and less with her teaching. Her lectures were super nutritional and the course materials were highly organized and helpful. She was extremely open and receptive to feedback and used to tailor lectures. Don't be afraid to take her course!

Not a bad professor, some explanations are better than others. Not enough time is given to work on problems in class, so you'll have to spend plenty of time outside of class. Do as much practice as you can and make sure you can complete the practice tests within the time you'll get for the real thing (some patterns will be repeated).

the class structure is an absolute mess. furthermore, professor novitski is very unorganized in lecture spends long points talking about simple or irrelevant subjects while glossing over the much more challenging materials. finally, the class simple doesn't prepare you for the exams most people were pretty much clueless the entire quarter.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Novitski chooses quantity over quality with her lectures. You get very little time to answer her lecture questions and I relied on the textbook to learn. Is very condescending and asks for student feedback during lecture and literally DEBATES students mid-lecture. Can tell she is passionate and intelligent but fell short.

Not an awful lecturer, but goes way too fast so it's hard to keep up. No time to write ANYTHING down during lectures. Gives very little time on in class clicker questions, mostly I wouldn't get to the answer before she closed it and they're accuracy graded. Kinda condescending. Seems happy when students are confused and getting questions wrong.

Good lecturer, easy to follow along, learning catalytics (in class participation questions) make class participation graded but are good for knowledge checks. Content is presented a little quickly sometimes but the equations make sense and she is always happy to answer questions (actively pauses and encourages it).
an ok lecturer

she's really caring and incorporated feedback and student concerns she received into her lectures! the flipped classroom method is difficult to deal with overall though and i don't think that's a fault of the professor

Explanations are sometimes lacking, often just shows an equation and we are expected to understand it. Rarely works through problems. Course resources were good though, and the tests are curved pretty decently.

I was worried because of his rating at first, but he's a good lecturer who knows his stuff and is very willing to help you wherever you are in your learning. I enjoyed his class a lot, he gives memorable examples for games and makes an effort to know all of his students. Also, he is a fast responder to emails now!

Professor is fundamentally a great person and treats his students with respect. That is the first step in being a good mentor.

His teaching is entertaining, logical and oriented around economic frameworks. Game Theory is a hard concept, and he does a great job in connecting abstractions. 

His tests are hard, the class is hard, but he is good.
He is a really good professor with great sense of humor and he explains concepts well. The materials are definitely not easy but this class is worthwhile, studying game theory is super fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he did not explain the concept well and it has a lot math based equations. The grader is tough and fastidious. Avoid anycost to take it .
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Just dont.
Only tests. He doesnt respond to emails. Textbook bad prof.
He makes an effort.... thats it. Dont take.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Do not take
No idea who is giving this guy 5.0 stars. The prof doesnt know how to COMMUNICATE.
If you arent super technical and math oriented, this class will suck.
Super smart guy. Terrible professor. Makes the effort, fails so hard at explaining concepts to students. Extremely technical and entirely useless.
he is really good
hard but very rewarding. If you love econ and models, then take this class

I actually thought his teaching method was exciting and motivating. The material is difficult if you aren't willing to put in the time to read before classes. One of the hardest, yet most rewarding classes I've taken in Econ. He is also willing to bump up your midterm grade if your final grade shows that you've finally grasped most concepts.

He's like a teddy bear! And he's brilliant, takes a different approach to game theory than I've had in the past, more boring and dry than it could be. Also very micro intensive, brush up on your micro modeling. Otherwise he makes it easy to come to class.

Very good and clear professor. He isn't necessarily easy, but he knows the material and teaches it dry, expecting you to do the extra work to make it meaningful. He is genuinely interested in your learning and how you do it. I would definitely recommend him.
No Comments
Quite a difficult class, good at teaching. Sometimes she made her TAs teach instead.
Hardest tests and grading
Has a tendency to go on tangents gives random history lessons for a programming clsss
Grading seems kind of arbitrary. Points deducted off of labs without much explanation, and she also just rambles too much

Most of the content can be learned outside of class. Quiz sections are very important though. The regrades are very nice, however, the grading for the projects themselves felt very subjective. Sends very scary emails if you do anything against the forbidden code, even if you learned it in hs, which I think is excessive.

After a while I started watching lectures from previous quarters from when my friend took the class. Elba delivered poor quality lectures and was bringing up her personal life consistently in class. When you talk with her one-on-one her explanations are better, but as a lecturer, which is the primary job, she was really lacking.
Sometimes yaps a bit too much and goes over the same concepts redundantly, but overall decent. Lenient grader with a free extra attempt for basically every project.
Incredibly disorganized. Hard to follow her train of thought when she's lecturing. Talks down to students.
Lectures aren't helpful, but definitely attend quiz sections.

Grading on assignments can sometimes be unclear, however you LITERALLY get extra attempts with resubmissions. Final grade calculation is a little weird and ambiguous, so some people get blessed, others not. She missed a couple of lectures but it was bc Gigi had cancer soooo, its okay. She responds well and tries to help anyone that reaches out.

Elba and the TAs are very helpful and provide plenty of supplemental materials to help you succeed. Lectures move fast so make sure to do the pre-class materials (and you can always rewatch the recording if needed). I was not prepared for how harsh the grading would be in 122 after taking 121, but if you use resubmissions, you can get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Rough curve, which sucks because the class wasn't that bad

Elba is a wonderful professor. Her lectures were always clear, and she and the TA team provided helpful supplementary materials to improve our understanding of the material regularly. 12X grading is quite harsh, but resubmissions help to accommodate that. I learned a lot and enjoyed the class. I would totally take another class with Elba!

Honestly I cannot think of anything to criticize in this course. Elba and the TA team are AMAZING. They are all very enthusiastic and knowledgeable. An extremely well-organized course with a reasonable amount of very meaningful homework.

Elba is an incredible professor, it's clear she puts a lot of effort and time into her lectures, and the TA team is amazing as well! The grading is sometimes quite strict, but to account for that they have a resubmission process that allows you to make changes to your assignments for full credit. It was an amazing class overall, I would take again.

Elba is a great lecturer, she explains concepts with visuals and easy-to-understand language. Her quizzes and exams are slightly more conceptual but you'll be fine if you show up to lecture and do the pre-class work. The assignments are challenging but if you're genuinely interested in the field, it's fun.

Elba was an incredible professor. This was the first CSE course I took at UW (and in Java) and it was a smooth transition in with great resources to get me started. Elba and the TAs responded quickly and concisely on the ed board. I ended the quarter with a 4.0 and no AI warnings, those complaining here about AI warnings likely used AI.

Elba is energetic and kind, she provides good examples for concepts covered in class and is very open to further discussion outside of class. She and the TAs are understanding of external issues that cause a need to miss a quiz, and they overall want you to succeed. If you put in the time to study and use the resources provided, you'll get a 4.0.

Elba really cares about her students, she takes the time to come up with good examples for each lecture and makes each lecture engaging and interesting. The practice resources online are incredibly helpful for quizzes and homework, and the prof/ta's are easy to reach if you have any questions about the homework. Great class, would take again.

Spends a lot of time talking about her life and even military story, which feels really irrelevant — I'm here to study Java, not hear about that. Also expect to get academic misconduct warnings for almost every assignment, even if you did your work all by yourself.

Not the worst prof ever but spent more time trauma dumping and talking about her personal life than teaching. There's no point in going to lectures since you wont learn anything, just do the pre class and section work and you'll be fine.
Fun and a great professor, a great introduction to cs classes
Swearing in class, don't listen to any explanation, typing fast and minor grammar error = AI warning.

Elba as a professor great and engaging when she gave lectures. The grading criteria is very unclear however and getting an S as opposed to an E can mean 0.1 drop in your GPA at the end of the quarter. The content is easy to grasp as long as you go to lecture and section, but small mistakes can really tank your grade with quizzes and the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super sweet and nice professor. She gave me candies!! The grading Criteria and quiz are weird though.

The curve is crazy high this 25wi quarter. How can 2 S and 31 E in 33 letter grades be 3.8 and 1 S 32 E be 3.9? You should be perfect in all homework with your resubmission and only get at most 2 Ns to be dropped in 15 exam determined grades in order to get 4.0. lol
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Elba is an incredible professor! Her lectures are always fun and engaging, and she provides great examples to help understand the material covered. There's pre-class material provided that is quite helpful to understanding the lectures, and the quiz sections have good practice relevant to the assignments and quizzes. 10/10 would take again.

elba as a professor is great. i love the energy she brought to lectures and has understanding for students. content wise, lecture is basically unnecessary since the material is already covered in the pre class work and TAs in section go into much better depth.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Respected

reviews.comment: Elba is amazing! She is tough and has a no bs mentality but if you show her respect, she does the same back. She is passionate about what she does and cares about student's success. Talk to her and engage with the material as much as you can! She is on your side!

Lectures rarely go over all the material that needs to be covered and we hardly ever finish example problems because she spends most of the time talking about her personal life. Lectures are completely unneeded, you would be better off doing the pre class work and focusing on the quiz sections where the TAs tend to actually teach the material.

Internet memes. She incorporates internet culture into the class. Co-taught 122au with Miya Natsuhara, both gave the most engaging lectures to keep you tuned in. 

CSE12X TA grading is highly inconsistent at times though, which Elba does not necessarily have control over.
Enthusiastic and helpful

Of the classes I've taken at UW, professor Garza's pace was most like that of a high-school classroom. The material was easy to follow, but the lack of clarity in the grading system for CSE 12x meant that I sometimes felt I couldn't prepare appropriately for tests/assignments.

Elba (and Miya) were both amazing professors! As someone who came in with no experience in Java, and barely knowing conditionals, Elba made things very understandable (although I did do some extra practice to catch up to speed). Her office hours were also helpful (and included great snacks haha).

Elba is excellent. She explained CSE things with relatable topics and concepts. She was also enthusiastic and engaging. However, the course's grading system is strange, involving Es, Ss, and Ns and a range of Es and Ss to get a certain GPA. TA grading was inconsistent too. Despite the course's flaws, I enjoyed taking CSE 122 with her.

Garza is a fine lecturer. Unfortunately, the course is poorly designed. The grading system is weird and childish, quizzes are on paper and barely assess the important course concepts, and HW is graded more by whether your code comments than actual functionality. Furthermore, practice quizzes have many mistakes and HW grading is inconsistent.
If she does not swear during lectures, I'd give her a decent rating. Very inappropriate.
Co-taught 122 with natsuhara, they had good chemistry with each other and garza was a great professor in her own right, gigi is super cute and she also utilized great analogies and visualizations

Maybe not entirely the professor's fault (may be department), but the E/S/N strange grading system, with asinine "code quality" standards that deduct inconsistently across the board for the most absurd reasons, the least helpful feedback from TAs, and getting only one practice test per quiz (which has like 3 problems total) is crazy work.

Super smart, funny, and caring. You want to take a class with her--I promise. She is one of the best profs I've had by far, especially in CS. If you have a personal problem, she will go well out of her way to help you. In lecture and on the discussion boards, she's super happy to explain things in multiple ways and encourage everyone to participate

Garza is easily one of the funniest, most brilliant professors I've had. I first had her in her first quarter at UW. At the time, she was a perfectly adequate professor. But over the last two years, she has turned into something truly remarkable. Her growth has been inspiring to watch, and I will forever want to be her student again. Amazing prof.
Great class. Well organized, and everything is take home. Overall 5/5.

Awesome, down to earth, professional. 

A handful of labs and two take-home exams count for most of your grade, and the material is difficult if you don't have prior experience, but Elba is great.
Great professor! Well-organized class, clear expectations. All work is take-home and collaboration is encouraged on labs. Very chill class overall.

Elba was so good!! I had her au22 for cs121 (her first quarter teaching) & she was okay. She's gotten so good since then!! She's funny and so smart. She makes lectures engaging & fun to attend & is super willing to work with students to help them learn. She presents concepts in many different ways to help you understand. Take a class with Elba!!

If you're wondering whether to take a class that Elba teaches, don't worry about old reviews. Elba is funny, cares about her students, very communicative outside of class, always reminds students about deadlines, and is very responsive to feedback. I struggled with the material in 351, but enjoyed Elba and the structure of the class.

She is a really knowledgeable computer architect and truly cares about her students. Very reasonable course policies. In addition to office hours, you can make appointments to meet with her one-on-one if you have more private or less course-related questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor and very knowledgeable about CS. I honestly would not recommend taking this class if you're looking for an easy introductory class.

Elba was very enthusiastic about CS and that helped interest students. The one thing I will say though is that the homework difficulty fluctuated wildly from pretty easy to really difficult without much of a build-up. That said though, she and the TAs were very accessible on Ed outside of class to answer questions. I'd def take advantage of that

I really like Elba's slide organization as she went through how the algorithm worked step by step, especially about OOP. She is always available to answer questions, both in person and email. I enjoyed attending her lecture and most of the time fully understand the content after the lecture.
Nice woman but LORD this class took away my every will to live. Not beginner-friendly AT ALL! Never again.
Great teacher, recognizes her own mistakes and doesnt punish her students for them. Super helpful office hours and very caring in general

Elba is an amazing instructor. She and Matt make confusing concept sounds super fun and easy. So inspirational and she makes me happy the rest of the day after the lecture. The whole class is super organized and they constantly seek feedbacks.

After taking 12X series at UW, I have to say that Elba was the best CSE professor that I have met so far. Her slides are well-organized, and her time in class used to explain things and to guide us writing code was arranged reasonably. I think the most important point is that she was really passionate when teaching us, and this made me feel engaged

idk how she's only a 3.5 on here cus elba definitely deserves higher!! U can tell she really cares about the students and really tries her best to stay relatable with them w jokes n such. Also very accessible online and always responds to student questions via Ed. Grading scale kinda sucks but that's not her fault its a department-wide thing.

Average lecturer, delivered the material & her and the TAs were very responsive with questions about assignments and code. Love that she loves formula 1 but hate that you can't know your grade until the quarter ends.
I stopped going to lecture and just went through recordings under 2x speed, but go to section- CSE1XX TAs are generally goated.

Took CSE 122 with her and she was the best. Easy class with good lectures which are recorded, everything is found online, quizzes and projects are not too difficult. She answers questions well without sounding demeaning, and usually helps the person asking the question get to the answer by themselves instead of answering outright.

Elba's honestly not that bad, especially for CSE351 I think she was actually good. The class has a lot of new content that comes at you fast and can be hard to grasp, but Elba def knows her stuff. With regards to labs and homework, the TAs are pretty great. Try not to fall behind or miss small hws/readings - the class can be quite a rewarding one.

Underrated. Elba's a delightful lecturer that's got everything you'd want from a 351 professor - knowledge, industry experience, communication skills, and humor. She's quick though, so make sure to take out time for pre-lecture readings; otherwise, you'll be lost all lecture.
Very passionate about computer hardware and also understanding/flexible with grading. Would highly recommend her for HW/SW Interface.

Elba is honestly a pretty good lecturer. When it comes to grading and office hours, it's the TA's who do that so it doesn't really apply to her. The grading is pretty strict, but you get a chance to resubmit every assignment/ retake every quiz. Also, the final exam was super easy.

Idk what is up with these reviews she's actually so sweet and I think she did the best she could considering its a really big class. As long as you read the pre class work and go to your quiz section you'll be completely fine trust.

Like the other reviews, I agree that Elba is very condescending. I was scared to ask questions in class and she did not foster a forgiving requirement. Especially compared to Wortzman, who taught the class along with her in fall quarter, she definitely fell short.

Garza was the most condescending teacher I have ever had and consistently made us feel incompetent in our knowledge or that we know how to do everything better. She would often speak to us like we were in kindergarten or snap at us if we answered something wrong. Never really helpful outside of class and didn't take constructive criticism well

This was Elba's first quarter teaching a class at UW and I think she did a fair job. At lectures, she did seem a bit condescending, but she was overall fine to me. Teaching a class of 800 students is not easy and I think she did the best she could considering her experience and circumstances this quarter.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: she taught this course along with Wortzman. His lectures were driven with empathy towards students, but Garza was more cold. She moved through lectures fast and does not seem like she has her students' best interest in mind. The course material progressed quickly, and sometimes she failed to make us feel comfortable before moving on during lecture.

She is an okay lecturer but has the most condescending persona. She backhandedly shows that she has more skills than students and treats us as if we're incompetent/"should know better." She's cold and goes really fast over concepts and isn't willing to slow down by any means. The material itself isn't difficult but she doesn't make it any easier.

Lecture contents were interesting but poorly executed. She made many mistakes both in her handwriting and in slides, and many of them were not addressed unless a student noticed them. Especially the neural-network part of the lecture was disappointing, as we were not given enough lectures, and yet we were given an assignment with tightest deadline.
Lectures were detailed and in depth.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. Gives incoherent lectures and makes so many mistakes (verbally, written on the board, and in slides) and never clarifies what is actually correct. Super passive aggressive and will not accommodate you for anything. Only good thing about this class is she didn't come up with the assignments.

Dr. Frank was a very okay professor. She was rude to students in lectures which were boring and slow. Her notes were very mediocre. I learned next to nothing in this class (I had already taken MATH 208) but got a 4.0. Wouldn't recommend.

Dr Frank seems like a nice person, but her lectures were boring, notes often unintelligible, and both are riddled with mistakes that are fixed only when students point it out. Homework takes time but aren't hard necessarily. Exams lean conceptual and are proof heavy (expect to write a few proofs during both exams). The curve was great though.
I might get an A. Worked hard. Learnt a lot.
Would take again, but make time to prepare for classes.
We just had our test - fair. I heard there was a makeup test (nice).
Professor Frank is an excellent professor; she cares about the students and do extra effort to help them understand the material.
Dr. Frank explains the material in depth. She focuses on conceptual understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: NEVER TAKE HER CLASS!!!!!!! Her teaching skills were awful, and I had never seen a professor make a lecture so awkward. Most students never attended the class after 2 weeks. The most awful thing is that she will not provide you a detailed rubric about the grading standard. You never know why you lose your points.

If you can take a different teacher, do. She is out of touch with her students.

Shoutout Yiting Zhang (our TA) who CARRIED. So helpful.

What a joke of a class.  The class is extremely disorganized and too fast paced to learn anything. Literally left to learn everything on my own for the assignments, which are not even in sync with the topics being covered in classroom. I was really looking forward to this class as the topics looked cool but it has been a major disappointment
I have no idea why UW hired her.

do not take this class. you will learn nothing from this professor, and you will go bald trying to read her handwriting (i am not joking). The Piazza responses take forever, and the instructions on anything for the class are awful. EVERY LECTURE is copied from Professor Nathan Kutz's book, so you're better off just reading that book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is my first time in 4 years as a student writing one of these reviews because of how much of a joke this lady is. Lectures consists of copying word for word onto a board the course notes provided 3-4 years ago by Professor Kutz, during which she has a no phone policy and routinely blanks out and stares at the class for 3 minutes at a time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It can be seen that Professor Frank is young and inexperienced but shows a deep level of understanding of the material. She sticks to the rules, but at the same time is fair and caring. Be prepared to work hard in this class and learn a lot.

If you have a choice between her and someone else, take someone else. The other ratings summarize everything, super tough grader after answering barely any questions about the final with unclear grading expectations and no information about the curve and point distribution on the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Assumed that we knew differential equation, and logical notation, even though this course only requires calculus to take, assigns a homework assignment after the final, but has topics from that assignment on the final exam. The biggest issue were the lectures, too slow and messy, and would only teach proofs and properties, not the steps to solve it
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have never come across such an unqualified professor at UW. Lectures were illegible nonsense and useless. Had to self-study everything from other online sources. No practice exams, no note sheet, no given formulas, and no preparation for a very difficult final worth 30% of our grade. Read the other reviews and avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor ever, closest I've gotten to just dropping a class but then I'd have to take the class again and even if there's a small chance I get her as a teacher, I'm not taking that chance. Horrible handwriting, unclear grading, awfully worded homework, and the final wasn't on the stuff she taught us. Avoid at all cost

Great class if you want to self learn everything, lectures made everything more confusing. Canvas page is heavily disorganized, final is harder than any other previous class with negative points, no calculators, and no notes. DO NOT TAKE.

(2) since I have a lot to say. However, on a good note: this class is the *perfect* choice for those who enjoy completely self-learning the content. Because the lectures were absolutely pointless and only correlated ~20%, the rest you'll have to source online. Save yourself the grey hair and 10 years of your life, and DO NOT take this class.

Never. Have. I. Ever. Written. A. Review. This was probably the worst class I have EVER taken in my years at UW. Piazza responses arrive only a week later, usually being their personal favorite: “No.” NEGATIVE?!?! points on the final. You'll have absolutely no clue where you stand in the class and whether you're on your way to a 4.0 or failing (1)

I have never written a rating before, but this information would have been helpful for me earlier on.

I was confused from the first two classes. If you feel also feel this way with how Dr. Frank teaches, please take another course - it is not likely to get any less confusing. The provided materials did not prepare the class for the HW or final.

The worst teacher ever. Can't even be called a teacher cuz she didn't teach us anything. Her only effort was to write irrelevant stuff with messy handwriting in class and give "notes" like draft papers. Piazza questions never received accurate responses. Test ur ability to self-learn. Everyone was completely disappointed. Just don't take her class

She is always trying to teach you but at the end made you more confusing. The lecture is confusing and you have to learn everything yourself. At same time the final is hard and questioning something that is not emphasized both in lecture nor homework, but it worth 30% of your grade.
She is the worst professor I have ever had. She does not know to teach at all. Never take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely the only professor that has made me cry. The canvas page is disorganized, the due dates & curve are unclear, replies to comments and emails after a week. The lectures make me more confused and the notes are confusing, be ready to self learn everything. The final is unclear, and negative points for wrong answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Frank is nice and cares about the subject. Unfortunately, she is not a good professor. Her lectures are poorly paced, neither her or the TAs are accessible outside of class, and the final contains true/false questions where it is possible to get -1 points. The entire class is frustrated and confused, the study guide is sparse and curve unknown.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Frank is a nice person and clearly cares about teaching the content, but the lectures are way too convoluted to get anything out of. You will be self learning. She is a new prof, so this is to be expected. No equation sheet for the final exam is a little absurd, way too much to remember. Way too many proofs for an AMath class.

I don't usually write rate my professor ratings, but I needed to for Natalie. Her class is extremely difficult, and be ready to self-learn all of your content. She is extremely passionate about the content, but she often skips steps when teaching.  Also very HW reliant, with 70% of your grade based on HW and 30% based on a final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
It is so tough to follow the lectures and then apply that into the homework which is like 70% of the grade. The structure of the course was also really bad and honestly even though she genuinely tried teaching the concepts there was no enthusiasm so I never really learnt anything from the class, I just had to study everything on my own.

not happy.

She is a nice person but her lecture is hard to follow with her messy handwriting and this is the first time she has taught this course so she is unfamiliar with what she is teaching. Unlike other AMATH 352 courses have a final project, we have to take a final. The grade is mainly based on homework with 70% on the homework and 30% on the final.

Dr. O's class was one of the best I've ever taken. He is an amazing lecturer, the material is engaging and fun to learn.  There is a clear grading system, which is very generous. There are three exams, but your lowest one is dropped. I could not recommend this course more, it legitimately made me consider switching majors to astronomy.

Straightforward class with a very approachable and kind professor. Honestly, I stopped going to class, all the lectures are recorded, and they only count your participation grade from quiz section attendance, but I still found the exams pretty simple and easy regardless. Just rewatch the lectures and take notes as he goes along.
Great Professor! Very funny and it's obvious that he cares about the subject matter

Awesome class/professor. Lectures were recorded, but I attended anyways. Course is more wide than deep, but when I'd go to office hours with questions, he was great at explaining content beyond the course's scope. Tests were pretty one-to-one with lectures. Review your notes and you'll be fine. There's an online textbook, but he doesn't use it all.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor overall. Very funny and I like his voice/accent. Did find it hard to actually LEARN from the lectures at points, so my quiz section carried most of my learning. Lectures are 100% enjoyable so don't skip em. I would definitely recommend this guy, he will motivate you to learn more about astronomy. Tests were hard (somewhat).

This guy is super passionate about what he teaches. Everything he says will be on the exam is always on there, and there aren't any surprises. TA's we're both great when I took the class and they were always easily accessible. As long as you have a pulse you should be fine. Love this guy.

Oliver was the best professor Ive ever had for the best class Ive ever taken. if you are an astronomy major you need to take this class the trips to the observatory were so fun and while the coding for the final projects was brutal at times it was so worth it.

Such a charismatic and funny professor! Made learning the content really fun and provides ample opportunities for support/help for those with less scientifically-oriented brains. would recommend for anyone looking for a natural science credit from an outside major!

Professor O' is a captivating lecturer who brings astronomy to life. His engaging style and clear explanations make the material accessible. The textbook is optional, but study tools like Unstuck AI are helpful for exam prep. Overall, an enjoyable class if you're interested in the subject.

Dr. O was fabulous. He is so enthusiastic in lecture that it makes everyone interested in the subject manner. When more than half the class missed a test question, he removed it from the test, saying it was his fault he didn't teach it well enough. Tests are not too hard if you study, and labs aren't either. Great class, would take again.
Fantastic class, fantastic guy

Dr. O' is a very engaging speaker who knows his subject well. He appears to enjoy his students and his job. The concepts are clearly presented, and his tests correlate to his lectures. Grading-wise, he is fairly easy. I basically flunked the first test (65%) and still managed a 3.5 because of all the easy points available during the quarter.

His lectures are very fun to listen to and they cover pretty much everything you'll need to know. The textbook is necessary for the online class but only as supplemental material. Do the self checks, he takes questions directly from them for the exams. Take good notes and you'll be fine!
This guy has such positive energy. Total goofball and makes learning complicated concepts fun! You can tell he has so much passion for teaching and for science.
He is very passionate about what he is teaching and he tries to keep things intersting, do not expect this class to be light or easy. This is definitely not 101 level. (Winter 2023)
Amazing professor! The class was super enjoyable.

He is very funny and kind and his tests align with his lecture material which is rare for UW professors. Also his TA's are kind but his labs were graded weird, I did them with a friend but we would both receive different grades.

A passionate professor that makes the course very enjoyable! His course is abstract and more challenging but he does care about his students and is very accessible outside of lecture. I was able to get concepts cleared up and redo my labs during his office hours. Take this course if you are truly interested in Astronomy, not for easy NS credits.

Do NOT take this class. Very difficult concepts. Definitely NOT a 101 course. Quiz sections didn't even correlate with the lectures. HARSH graders. HARD midterm & final. Honestly- the guy doesn't know how to teach. I was confused the entire time. TA gave little to no help. Labs-unrealistic and difficult. Cried over how hard it was.

(Winter 2023 in person) Please save your time and do NOT take this class. The professor does not know how to teach. He skims over major topics in the lectures, and then expects you to immediately understand astronomy. This is a 101 class, but it honestly felt like a major requirement course. Walked out of lecture every day knowing literally nothing

Dr. O is a great teacher and person, but the online asynchronous course is very difficult. Even while doing all of the readings and watching the lectures, the quiz questions are very difficult. If you are REALLY into astronomy, I would recommend this class. If you are just looking for an easy NW credit, I wouldn't recommend this course.

The class is great if you like astronomy. You better read the book to understand anything. The wording on the quiz is a bit hard, but it should be simple if you can get the big idea out of the question. 

I like STEM, so ASTR 101 was easy for me. I don't recommend astronomy to people who hate STEM.

Labs and quizzes were graded heavily.

Overall The professor was good but DO NOT take this course if you're expecting something light and easy. Came in thinking it would feel like an intro class but in fact it took up more time than my classes in my major :/ Midterms were DIFFICULT. The concepts were interesting but the labs consisted of a lot of busy work
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr O was amazing! He started each class with a clapping exercise and improv. The course is pretty much all participation, and all of the activities that we had to turn in for a grade were very straightforward. We had 3 presentations during the quarter, and they were very manageable and fun to do! I would highly recommend this class!

Grading: HW 40 - Exams/Quizzes 60 Seriously if you read the chapters assigned and take a few notes you should do about a 10/12 on your quizzes and for review for midterms just do the review he provides and you should do just as well. Everyone that is an instructor/TA genuinely cares about the students and if you reach out you get a response fast!

I took this class online and it was a massive mistake. The quizzes don't make any sense, lectures are disorganized, I had no idea what I was supposed to be learning. Save yourself and don't take this class.
less than a quarter of the questions in the quizzes is covered in lecture. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS ONLINE. he basically doesn't teach. Even his recordings are very disorganized.

Fraser is an amazing professor and takes the time to learn the names of students who ask questions and engage in lectures. I found all of the content very interesting which made it easy to pay attention and retain information. However, the quizzes every week can be difficult, they are all short answer questions

I'm all for fairness but can't respect a curriculum with assessments that, even if asynchronous, don't pertain to course materials and demands highly extraneous work. Changing the curriculum in this way to address the issue of prior classes performing too well wasn't the right solution, and frankly unfair when not reflected to the in-person class.

I did not listen to the reviews based off of rate my professor for the online class, I fully regret it. The average of the weekly quizzes are so low and so unclear. None of the discussions or labs are relevant to the quizzes and midterms, all of this is bs. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!

This is the worst class I take.. The grading and the syllabus is unclear. He doesn't even teach and basically, you just have to study on your own by reading the textbook. Mid and Finals are super hard. This is not an 100-level class. Do not recommend taking online version
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THE ONLINE VERSION!!! I had friends who took it in person and said it was super easy, but the online version had a midterm and final, with the average being a 50-60% on both. His grading criteria was super unclear (never mentioned on in the syllabus), and kept saying there would be a curve.... there wasn't.

Professor Fraser is very kind and enthusiastic. I took his asynchronous, online Astronomy course. Pros: the lectures are engaging, he is accessible, and he offers a variety of assignments. Cons: the midterm and final were quite difficult. If you do all the readings and study, however, you should not have too much trouble getting an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was incredibly difficult online. The quizzes and tests have nothing to do with the lecture/lab/discussion content, and some material doesn't even seemed to be covered in the textbook. The TA's are harsh graders, even for discussion posts. I would definitely not recommend the online version of this class.

Was a very low effort class for me. No mid terms nor finals. Only weekly short essays that weren't too bad. Most of the subjects for essay can be found on his slides with extra research. The labs were easy (mostly bc our TA was very helpful). He's very passionate about what he's teaching!
The exams for his online course is HARD. Can't really find the answers from textbook or his lectures.

Every negative review seems to be about his online classes. Take ASTR 101 in person, he’s such a sweet guy and we had no midterm nor final! He made our quizzes (which I hated, but were doable) out of more points so our grade wouldn’t be hurt as much if we made small mistakes. One short essay quiz a week, three labs, three discussion paragraphs.

Gives almost no information in very short lectures and expects daily interactions with discussions and weekly quizzes. Many questions in the quizzes and midterms were not discussed in lectures and were not in the textbook at all. It feels like the professor barely skims over topics and then expects you to know astronomy instantly. Poorly run class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I regret taking this class. We have weekly quizzes, a midterm, a final, almost weekly labs, and weekly discussions. For discussions, you have to engage in it almost daily. Youll need to read the textbook or you wont do really well. The average gpa is 2.6. This is your warning to not take this class.

Dr. O is the best prof I've had at UW yet. He is so excited about teaching his students, you can tell that his job actually brings him joy and that just makes it so much fun to learn with him. He gets students involved and answers questions, and he is so sweet. You should say hi if you have him, he is the nicest.

Dr. O is such an amazing professor! I came into this class concerned because its presentation heavy, but no worries, he made every effort to make students comfortable and prepared for their projects. I highly recommend him to any curious honors students :))

Unlimited redo homeworks, easy but thought provoking discussion prompts, and a fun project at the end. Great guy, loved his lectures too! One of the easiest classes I've ever taken at UW. I looked forward to doing the work for this class every week, and one of the 'textbooks' was a video game which even had a plot! Amazing class!!

This class was pretty easy. The quizzes are like hw assignments so very easy. He gives you a whole day to complete it but they are on fridays so dont forget to do them. Very understanding and very funny guy.

Easier than most of my high school classes, I took ASTRO101 online. You do have to refer to the textbooks for notes but there is no final and only weekly quizzes & discussion sections. The pre and post-tests are a free 1% extra credit if you do them, the video game was surprisingly fun, HIGHLY recommend if you need an easy A.

I was really scared of taking this class because I did not know what to expect but wow, this professor is amazing. He is super caring and considerate about his students and COVID. He eliminated exams in this class and we only had to do quizzes which were super easy. He makes it super simple for students to learn, he is the best!

I highly recommend Dr. O as a professor. The class is very straightforward, and he really seems to care about his students. Definitely one of the best professors I've had that makes online class interesting.
This prof is really passionate about astronomy and it shows. It makes the learning more enjoyable. The class itself is truly set up to serve the students, and that makes a big difference.

Storytelling in the Sciences was the most useful class I have taken thus far as a STEM major. The content is fun and engaging, the grading is completely based on effort, and the projects--two presentations--are very low pressure. Would definitely recommend!

This man is amazing! He's my Honors Storytelling in the Sciences prof and he has single handedly made my freshman year great! This is really that one class that will give you a real sense of community as Dr. O does lots of improv & get to know you stuff over zoom! He's the kind of teacher who cares more about learning than grades! Easy & fun class!

Dr. O is a fantastic professor! I genuinely enjoyed every lecture, as he is so passionate about the subject matter and wants to ensure that people are learning. Hes a super nice guy and a great presenter. Definitely take his class!

Such a good guy. I suck at anything sciencey, but he was so kind and reassuring about it. Once I went to office hours and I was really confused about something, so I apologized and said I wasn't good at STEM. He told me not to talk like that, and that I was actually doing a great job. Awesome prof and really cares about his students.

The work is pretty straight forward and reading is not too much about a chapter every week. Reading is all the material you will get to study for the exam. He's probably a great prof. in person, but his online class is horrible and he's pretty disconnected from it. Exams are HUGE part of you grade. Their are 2 and you better pass one .
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I really like this course

Dr. O was such an amazing professor, definitely one of my favorites at UW so far. I took this intro class just to fulfill my last five natural world credits and going into it, I wasn't expecting much - I knew embarrassingly little about our planet and universe. But every lecture turned out to be very insightful and entertaining, I learned a lot!

Dr. O is a great guy who is very passionate about what he teaches. Very lovable guy and will guarantee to make you smile. He goes really fast and goes through slides with a lot of information fast. I recommend rewatching the Panaptos posted to really get the information, though. Easy material to follow if you just pay attention.
A wonderful teacher who makes you want to show up to class. Im not a B.S. Major but Dr. O made me almost want to switch :)

Overall a very nice, caring, respectable professor. Personally this class was difficult for me as I am not very gifted in physics, chem, and other sciences. Midterm and Final are difficult, but you can boost your grade through easy self checks and working hard on labs/projects in section. I suggest forming a study group to review with every week.

Professor O is a great Professor who shows a very obvious enthusiasm and passion for astronomy which makes lectures 100 times more intersting. Topic matter is also very intersting. The Professor is also very good at answering student questions and communicating. Great class!

Dr O is a really amazing lecturer! His classes are always interesting and very informative. He's very receptive to any questions & is happy to slow down or go over things again for clarity. Very nice guy. Wish I could take this class again

Best professor I've had since starting at UW. He's very understanding about situations outside of class. The topics for online discussion are very interesting once you get into it. His rubric is very straightforward; if you follow the rubric, you'll get 100% on assignments, no surprises. I wish he could teach all my classes.

I took this class online and THINGS HAVE CHANGED FROM THE PAST. This was the first year they had a better budget and more TA's. So the online material itself was not bad at all, BUT the MIDTERM AND FINAL WERE BRUTAL. NOTHING LIKE THE ONLINE MATERIAL/QUIZZES. I didn't use the textbook at all for the online part, but you need it for the exams!!!!

Solid professor and solid class. Some lectures are more fun than others but he is really good at keeping your attention. Some of his power points were a bit all over the place so I had to watch some crash courses on some topics, otherwise I really liked Dr. O!!
Very nice and explains topics well.

Very passionate and friendly. Makes funny jokes and sometimes brings in visuals so going to lecture is definitely worthwhile. The syllabus mentions getting 90% guarantees you at least a 3.0 which doesn't seem like much, but in the end the grading is not actually that harsh.

Super fun teacher and lecturer. Felt like some info that he lectured about was irrelevant to the tests and homework labs, but other than that I didn't really have any issues with his teaching! Could tell he cares about his students.
He knows his material. Good sense of humor, keeps class interesting. He also lets us create study guides in quiz sections to prepare us for the tests.

He's exactly what you want in an astronomy prof. He's weird and makes many many bad jokes in class but you really get his passion for the subject. He's just so excited! The class is easy but don't skip studying for the tests. If you go to class every time and ask questions if you're confused you'll be fine.

Dr. O is fantastic. He really cares about you as a person, trying to get to know you with assignments that help him learn more about you. Class was built entirely on presentation participation. Essentially public speaking class, but it is based more on effort than your own speaking skills. Very kind, relatable professor.

Dr. O is  a super caring and kind professor. If you get behind he is always available to help you. I find Astronomy hard to wrap my head around personally but, taking this class really helped me do better in my Astronomy class. Dr. O is one of the gems on campus.

Great lecturer! Always enthusiastic and energetic, really tries to engage with students. First half of the course is smooth sailing mostly but for the second half, material starts getting more difficult so keep up with lectures, read, or watch crash course (saved me for the final honestly) to back up that knowledge.

Dr. O was one of the most passionate and caring professors i've ever had. He genuinely cares about students learning and will make sure he is there to help you IF YOU ASK FOR IT.  I don't know why people rated him poorly before... He is honestly so kind and helpful but again you can't sit around and expect it to come to you, go ask him questions!
Dr. O is a very friendly and funny professor. His lectures are amazing, but the exams are not. Questions on the exams are really vague and he is not very clear about grading.

Even though this course was online, Dr. O. was extremely interactive and always available for students. These courses aren't for the procrastinator as there was definitely plenty of work weekly, but if you did the readings and short activities, it was simple. The midterms are based close to the quizzes, so there were no surprises.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Fraser was an enthusiastic person with a lot of passion for astronomy. However, his unclear lectures, lack of organization, clarity, and no study guides really made this class much harder than it needed to be. His exams asked very vague, unclear and weird questions... the content is much easier if you just watch crash course videos online.

Beware. Dr O is very nice, friendly,  funny, but lectures are confusing and unclear, forcing you to spend extra time self-studying the material (and still feel lost and frustrated). He tries to oversimplify concepts which just makes them even more unclear. He also doesn't give study guides & exams are tricky. NW credit? Better off taking ASTRO150.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. O clearly loves astronomy and so polite and such a sweetheart. He tries to make lecture interesting but it is probably the longest 50 minutes of my day. He's funny and really makes an effort to get to know his students but his lectures are confusing and all over the place and I really just learned mostly from the book and from section.

Easiest class I've ever taken, basically pass/fail. Doctor O is fantastic, super nice and understanding. The class is really applicable to real life and the presentation skills you learn are helpful for other classes. His accent is cool.

Fraser is definitely my favorite professor at UW. Very caring for his students and genuinely wants you to understand the material. His lectures are amazing and very interesting. Homework assignments were easy, and exams are manageable if you memorize facts. Would definitely take another one of his classes again.

Professor O is amazing! I would take his class in a heartbeat. He is kind and genuine and truly wants his students to do well and learn. I have only met two professors that are this genuine and caring. We need more professors and people like him!

Dr. O is great and really enthusiastic about what he's teaching. Lectures are engaging but sometimes not organized very well. Sometimes it is unclear what information is important and what information is not important.
Dr. O is the man. Loved his class and learned a lot. He is very helpful and responsive and definitely cares about his students. TAKE HIS CLASS.

Dr. O is awesome! It's hard to connect with students in an online course, but he really makes an effort to help and get to know you. He answers emails almost immediately, and is generous with his grading techniques. He makes the class informative, but easy to do well in.  He's an excellent professor!
He rocks. Need help? Contact him. Wonderful professor.

Dr. O is extremely passionate about astronomy, and loves teaching it and watching students learn. The class content gets progressively harder, eventually leading into concepts like relativity and light. Don't expect a 4.0 in the class, because a lot of questions on the exams are ambiguous. He's also super adorable, and the lectures are pretty funny

Dr. Fraser has a great personality, but I found the lectures to be disorganized  and unclear. He does most of his teaching orally, so it is difficult to go back and look at the lecture slides and understand. Also, the tests are very hard to prepare for because he does not give any practice tests. However, he is friendly and inspirational.

Such an awesome professor! I have always loved astronomy, and even though I'm going to a different direction for a career, he has truly inspired me to love astronomy even more! It's been awesome to share something with him (ie. if you take an astro photo) and see him share it with the class. He is really interactive and has a great teaching method!

Fantastic class, definitely go to lecture.  Even though he posts tons of helpful stuff online you should go just because he's enthusiastic, funny and excellent at explaining astronomy!  Otherwise labs are pretty easy and interesting, and the tests aren't anything to sweat too much about. Do the work, go to class, and it's an easy A and a fun time.

Learning materials are really exciting from which I can feel the passion of astronomists. Space images are beautiful and I'm pretty into the class. It's an easy class but I went deeper to learn more than what we need to get a nice grade. By the way, the lab video made me crazy once cuz I'd never made one before but not that bad:)
Super nice guy, very helpful, cares alot about his students. Also pretty easy if you pay attention and do the work assigned.

Hands down, Dr. O is amazing! I had him a year and a half ago, and he still remembers me (class size200). Loved his teaching style and helpfulness. Really tried to get to know the names of all the students who asked questions and talked to him. Convinced me to switch my major to astronomy and I couldn't be happier! Bonus: he's easy on the eyes ;)
Dr. O's really kind and the class is quite interesting.

Really, really great professor.  The material can be confusing if you haven't taken a lot of science lately, but he goes far out of his way to help you understand the concepts.  Very enthusiastic teacher (that's refreshing, right?) and genuinely nice person.  Tests aren't as bad as you'd think - he gives lots of prep material.

Definitely the most enthusiastic professor I've had so far. It's obvious that he knows a lot about astronomy, and is very eager to share his knowledge. Sections didn't often correlate with lecture material, but both were interesting and informative nonetheless. Highly recommended!

Dr. Fraser is a fantastic person who is very passionate about teaching and Astronomy. However, his lack of experience shows in his clarity of concepts and what to know as well as his test writing. It's not a difficult class, but don't expect a 4.0 due to some lack of clarity.

I had the online class so we learned entirely from the book. He made himself available during office hours or if you ever want to drop by. His office hours are very helpful in explaining the materials and assignments and it is how I was able to go from a 68% to ending up with a 4.0.

Dr.O's a bomb teacher with the an adorable quirky accent! He LOVES astronomy and teaching. He's a young prof who can relate to his students and his lectures are super amusing. His exams are harder than what I expected. But his review sessions before exams are VERY helpful. I wished I had another class with him! He made me fall in love with ASTRO!
He tends to go off topic a lot.

Probably because he's new but he put me to sleep almost every lecture (sometimes he was super funny). The quiz sections were more helpful since all he did in lecture was say the same things in the textbook. I'm sure he'll improve, he's not a bad prof, just inexperienced. Also, his slides felt disorganized.

Dr. O was hands down my favorite proff I've had!! Aside from his good looks & awesome accent, he does an amazing job teaching!! You can easily tell he is passionate about astronomy. One thing that sets him above other proffs is he tries to get to know students. Even though there were a lot of people in lecture he would do his best to learn names.

Dr. O is the best! His lectures are light and they're so much fun. He is funny, has a charming New Zealand accent, and is very passionate about Astronomy. He is also extremely nice and always there to help. He has all the qualities needed for a good teacher. I felt so sad when this class ended; I'm going to miss him so much!
Definitely do not recommend him if you only want this class for a 4.0 (which most previous astro 101 classes have been). His first year as a professor and he has A LOT of improving to do.

Dr O, is one of my favourite professors! He's so enthusiastic about the topic and will go out of his way to make sure you feel comfortable with the class. Not a lot of hw and tests aren't too hard. Over all it's his enthusiasm and clarity that make Astro 101 so great. I recommend him and his class to everyone!

I love this professor. He's young, he keeps lectures interesting, and he really wants to get to know all of his students. His exams aren't too hard, and there isn't much homework. He's really helpful and is good at explaining the material.
Very fair when writing exams and extremely enthusiastic about astronomy. Lectures are interesting and funny, too. Helpful when students have questions, and also is receptive to feedback.

This was the most frustrating class I've taken at UW. from to disorganized materials, unclear expectations with few rubrics, inconsistent grading, and her lack of response to any emails, though she is kind in person and willing to help if you meet with her directly.

Professor Fountain is an exceptional teacher who goes very in-depth about the cultural disparities in America. Her assignments gave unique insights to my learning and were very helpful. I personally loved this class a lot and it taught me many important skills. Very kind person!
I liked Professor Fountain's class a lot, it was insightful and I learned about a lot of new topics. It was not fully focused on natural sciences as the class said, but it was still very fun!

I took (ENGL 199) in the fall quarter.Rashenna Fountain was a very nice professor. There were 4 short assignments and 2 Major projects throughout the course and they were all very fun and creative. She also basically will give you 100 percent if you submit the short assignments and she is a very generous grader for the Major projects. Great teacher

She's a great professor. Her selection of readings will give you a well-rounded understanding of contemporary migration issues. Admittedly it is a lot of reading if you do all of them, but if you're a quick reader it'll be ok. She likes to have group discussions in class so you'll get to know your classmates better than in a regular lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: My favorite professor ever. While this class was quite reading dense, they are all interesting to some level, and she fits in a few documentaries that were really fun to watch. Going to lectures is a must, not only because it will benefit you in exams, but because she cares a lot about what she teaches and class time is quite fun.

I adore Professor Friedman!! Her class content was organized, interesting, and important. The books she required were well written and fun to read. Her exams were take home. She is also so kind, knowledgeable, and willing to help! She provides you with outside opportunities if you put in the effort. One of my favorite professors for sure!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She was so sweet and the lectures were so interesting. We even had guest speakers sometimes. All we had was three papers and she graded very generously. She even decreased the load of the last paper since she saw we were stressed from other exams. There was quite a bit of reading, but if you skimmed it right before (or during) class you'd be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While Professor Friedman is very knowledgeable about the subjects, she often goes into tangents about her personal experiences that don't support the lectures. She feels very dismissive of students who cannot attend her lectures and enforces participation via attendance.

Kathie Friedman is one of the sweetest individuals you will ever meet at UW. She's very clear on grading criteria from the beginning of the quarter, so you will know exactly what is necessary to get a 4.0. She likes for people to participate, but isn't pushy about it and genuinely cares about her students' learning. HIGHLY recommend taking her!

The class was online; surprisingly lighter workload. We only got 9 online discussions with the lowest score to be dropped. 2 papers (around 4-5 pages) for the entire. It requires a lot of reading on the online textbook. Skimming is possible but you may miss the key parts during the discussion. No revision allowed, so rather turn in late than rush.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Such a sweet and caring professor. She has so much valuable experience and is a really interesting person to get to know. I strongly recommend her class, especially online!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Friedman is one of the most caring professors I've had. She is really knowledgable and wants to make sure people engage with the material and participate in discussions. She is sure to help if you reach out to her outside of class.
Kathie is a very nice lady and super knowledgeable about immigration from many perspectives. She really does want you to succeed and is a fairly easy grader. I liked this class and do recommend her!

Kathie is a wonderful professor that I am glad to have had the opportunity to meet and work with. She genuinely cares about her students/the material and has such a passion for the topics she teaches. She is very knowledgeable about any and all things related to immigration, so ask away! I would definitely recommend her class, if you get the chance
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Friedman is wonderful. She knows her stuff about the history if Jewish women and is so open to her students' ideas and opinions. It is clear she enjoys teaching and cares about her students. I recommend taking a class with her!

Class was heavy on the reading, which was sometimes dry, but she graded papers very easily and was very open to alternative ideas. No tests whatsoever, but easy grading on the essays. Discussions were easy to bring opinions and experiences to and didn't always follow the readings. Instead they branched into personal experience.

Friedman is one of my favorite professors at UW. The class is engaging and interesting, and she definitely cares about her students and the topics she is teaching. Lots of reading but expectations are clear and assignments are reasonable. Take a class from her if you can!

Took JSIS 324: Really interesting class. Learned tons but you'll have up to 100 pages to read for one day, so depending on what other classes you're taking it may be a tricky fit. Kathie cares a lot about this subject and seems concerned about the class' view on things too.
No Comments
Her class was wonderful to take and she made learning enjoyable. The readings were always helpful, she never gave busy work, and she was always very clear on what she expected out of the class.

Definitely has her quirks, but I found her funny and entertaining. Did a great job providing examples and her lectures were helpful for a class that is pretty much just ECON200+ Many quizzes + midterm/final but nothing too difficult. Get on her good side by participating, but she will go off on random tangents every class and tell stories.

Hilarious teacher, I never snooze in her class. She comes in with the same iconic fit every single class. The readings were sometimes long, but she encourages students to ask questions and she does a lot of practice problems in class. Only thing I didn't like were her problem sets but it was very manageable.

Maloy is a hilarious teacher, I loved her personal and historic connections to work we were learning in the class. She cares to teach students and encourages student to keep trying. She gives a reasonable amount of work. This class is very similar to some topics from ECON 200 and there is some calculus, definitely a lot easier than ECON 200.

Basically micro, but 2 extra chapters. The first midterm is very easy, with a high mean sitting at around 86% for my section. We received some form of quiz/testing almost every week leading up to the final. No cheat sheets at all. Always talks about how hard her final is, gets old really quickly. Loves to talk over and cut off student questions.
Her class is definitely not easy so go to office hours! She is very helpful and wants her students to succeed. As long as you make an effort and get help, you will pass.

I feel that the homework assignments did not add much value to my learning. Many tasks felt repetitive or disconnected from the core concepts covered in lecture, and I did not find them effective in helping me better understand or apply the material.
Her teaching is poor, learned by studying lecture notes on my own time. Quizzes and midterms were easy, final was difficult.

The majority of the class is graded solely on weekly tests. Lectures were hard to pay attention to as she constantly rambled about unrelated topics. The midterm and final were all multiple choice, making it very annoying and difficult. Grading was often messed up, and the custom practice problem she occasionally assigned had errors.

Always rambling about her diet coke and but doesn't care to teach... Content was 95% Microecon review and then gives us 2 weeks to learn the actual content for the course. TAs grade u like they hate u: docking u off for smth that wasn't asked of in the question 😭

Frances is a professor who truly cares about her students. Yes, she may talk about things that are unrelated to class. However, if you just do the practice problems that she assigns with understanding, you will do more than fine. I had to do a lot of traveling this quarter and missed a lot of lectures, and I still felt really good about the class.
Our final was multiple choice. She docked everyone for not writing in the answer sheet, "I chose A because..." That's all I need to say about her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Someone fire this lady. quizzes/ exams 9/10 weeks of the quarter. Coming to class is useless bc she can't teach. Thinks her class is the center of the world. ALWAYS interrupts students' questions. Grading got messed up on every quiz. Disorganized class. Too much content. Take class at CC.

Nice person, but is so unorganized. Was still teaching new material on Thursday (a whole other chapter and a half) when exam was on Saturday, all bc she was running behind + in the same week gave a useless group project due day before the exam given Monday. We had no dead week to study. And those TA's grade quizzes like u ran over their dog.

DOES NOT NEED TO BE 2 hours long. 1/2 lecture is her yapping bout nothin. She just scribbles on the papers as she teaches. Quiz grading is terrible.Take's off points for not mentioning something that wasn't asked, or that you DID mention just not in vocab desired. Thankfully Exams are multiple choice and don't need to turn in HW. Doable class tho.

Frances is a great professor that truly cares if her students learn. Come to class having skimmed the textbook and you will succeed. Responsive to email and very helpful when you ask questions. If you keep up on your studying and ask for help when you need it, you will certainly do well in this class!
One of the few professors at UW that genuinely loves to host Office Hours and help out students.

This is the worst class I've taken at UW. The instructor seems unprepared, her examples don't match lectures, and practice guides differ completely from quizzes. The course relies only on confusing in‑person exams, and asking for help makes things harder. Avoid if you don't excel at tests or unclear teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I don't think even she knows whats she's rambling about half the time
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Super willing to help and answer questions

Professor Maloy is a kind and caring individual who values the success of all who enter her class room. She sets clear expectations for success in the beginning of the quarter and those who do not follow made that choice. Lectures are not as confusing if you do the reading/attempt the homework before hand. Go to class/office hours, do reading + hw.

Genuinely just one of the worst lecturers I've had at UW. I do think Professor Maloy cares about her students; she's great at responding to emails, and she is always happy to help out. However, her lectures are unbearable as she consistently goes on useless tangents and explains the course material in the most difficult way possible.
Don't listen to the flunk-outs, do the homework problems that she assigns and ask for her help during office hours and you will pass with flying colors.
great instructor!

If you took Micro and Macro Econ and the Math 111/112 sequence AT UW you will be fine. Its basically the same exact concepts, but yes, she rambles so bad it can be confusing, and learning the new concepts can be tricky because of this. Still, I never read the textbook and only relied on lectures (recorded yass). What saves her is that she's nice.

Frances is a nice professor, but her lectures can get a bit off track since she likes to ramble a lot. She overly complicates some extremely simple concepts and the only way I've been able to understand the content is by thoroughly reading the textbook first. She is nice and can be funny at times, but be prepared to put effort into this class.
Terrible at teaching, goes too fast, writes messy, draws and its very unorganized. Avoid at all costs.

Her lectures made no sense. She just babbles about random things that are off-topic. I stopped attending class because I found it to be a waste of time. She always had a lot of information in her lectures that she didn't explain very well, so I had to teach myself the concepts at home through reading the textbook and doing practice problems.

Overexplains spends too much time on proofs instead of teaching the formula, which confuses many. Changed her teaching style this qrtr after bad feedback. Tests are harder/dif than practice probs she suggests. Office hours help, though her explanations are still too detailed. Nice person but doesn't fit all learning styles esp if need lots of help
