She's a yapper, lectures can be a little all over the place. She will help you if you come to office hours and does care, but I think the way she explains is too confusing. Older, experienced people often have issues when lecturing because they have so much knowledge in their heads that they assume everyone understands them, which is not the case.
She is a tough but kind professor. Just pay attention and you will be fine.

It seems people are very harsh here. I personally found that attending class and completing assignments were more than enough to prepare me well for exams. While she is a direct communicator (which seems to be off putting for some students), she is extremely open to giving students second chances and taking their concerns about grading seriously.

Frances is a unique professor who can be a bit long-winded, but she genuinely cares about her students and is willing to go the extra mile to help them succeed. The class material is manageable if you stay on top of the homework and attend lectures. Unstuckstudy was a game-changer for my exam prep.

She doesn't get to the point in her lectures. She's not very good at teaching the material either because she gets off topic quick and then also expects everyone to immediately know how to interpret the graphs and doesn't give enough context on how to solve problems and doesn't go step by step, making it difficult to understand.
Homework is KEY to succeed in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: she cares about students a lot and is willing to help outside of class but man does she yap. she overcomplicates what she's teaching, and the teaching-style was just not it for me personally. def do the hw problems cuz they help A LOT and don't take this class at the same time as tod's 320 since the midterm and some quizzes were on the same day.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Frances is an extremely caring professor. She goes out of her way to hold extra office hours during finals week and quiz/exam weeks to help students. The midterm, final, and quizzes are extremely easy if you pay attention in class and do the practice homework problems. The medians are in the 90s, so don't make mistakes

Frances is definitely a character. She yaps a lot like everyone says, but honestly, she's not that bad of a lecturer. Some of her stories are a bit irrelevant, but they're also kind of helpful to visualize as examples at the same time. Textbooks are unnecessary, she covers everything during lectures. Exams were easy so the curve was pretty bad.

I am a junior at foster, and I dreaded taking this class. There are quizzes every thursday that start out easy but slowly get much more difficult. Professor Maloy gives you an easy midterm and a diabolical final exam. I walked out of my final upset and deeply disturbed.

Upper level econ class with an all multiple choice final is ridiculous. She changes originally written answers to be multiple choice so you loose out on partial credit. Same goes for most of the quizzes. She is extremely condescending when you ask her simple questions and goes on long tangents during lectures that waste time.

Nowhere as bad as the reviews say. She goes out of her way to hold extra office hours to help students out, and genuinely cares about helping students succeed.  If you pay attention in class, this class will be extremely easy. Do the HW problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She cool. Yaps a lot at times ngl (some of her stories are funny tho) and sometimes takes way too long to explain stuff but if you print out the slides for each chapter and take notes following along with what she writes you'll honestly be ight. 5 quizzes lowest grade gets dropped which was clutch, midterm way easier than final, just study for both

Frances is a really caring professor. She has fun stories that help concepts stick in my head better. Didn't feel like it was as hard as some others are saying, it was well balanced with effort to reward. Show up to class and listen, and as long as you understand her lectures, you will be fine.

She talked a lot about her personal life during lecture which made my class falling behind other sections. I mostly learned from doing homework practice problems. Easy quizzes, moderate midterm, hard final. Frances is supportive if need additional help. If you are good at algebra and understanding derivatives, you will do well in this class.

She talked over people many times when they asked a question in class. I thought she explained things well, especially during OH. She was very accessible with a lot of OH or through email. She does talk a lot about the same things over and over again. The exams and quizzes were hard.

Frances was fine. I agree with everyone who says she yaps a lot, which is very true. I found her lectures confusing at first, but after reading the textbook and practicing the problems the concepts were manageable to learn. If you can, participate in class because otherwise you will hear her yell "you guys should know this for your quiz" 7 times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She kind of just talks and talks and talks and talks about nothing at all. Nice lady, awful lecturer. Really hard to focus when half the lecture doesn't relate to course concepts. It's a shame that she's the only professor that teaches BECON300. If I could go back, I might have taken ECON300 for the same credit.

All she does is yap. Do prepare to read a lot and do the textbook problems because that's how you learn in this class, not from her. 2 group problems sets, 5 quizzes and two exams. optional HW but they help you understand a lot. Class could've been 30min - 1hr if she doesn't spend 2 hrs exaggerating and talking about non-sence.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I like Frances, but her teaching style does not work for me. She tends to overcomplicate the not so complicated concepts. Also, your grade is based solely on quizzes, tests, and an end-of-quarter group assignment. Homework is not collected

Super nice professor, she's giving grandma vibe fr. But in terms of teaching, I personally find it a little bit too redundant. Felt like she's sometimes overcomplicating stuff. She offers a lot of office hours but I don't find it that efficient cz she always ends up talking about something else. But again, super nice person and she cares about you

Maloy is a very nice lady. She really does care about her students and how they learn. That means that she often goes on long tangents about life stories or past students. When it comes to work, the class is pretty heavy. Quizzes can be hard to study. Homework is optional. Tests are very heavy. Take home project was easy with a group.

Gets a worse rep than she deserves, but definitely not my favorite professor. She cares about teaching and puts in effort. However, she isn't always clear in her explanations. Everything gets covered in lectures though, so textbook is optional.

Her class really isn't that bad as long as you do the readings, they help a lot with the weekly quizzes at least and they're not too long. She goes over everything that's on the midterm, final, and group assignments in class and gives you practice exams as well. She gets off topic a lot. The final isn't cumulative, but definitely more difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Idk what people are talking about she really isn't that bad. Her class is hard but she tells you exactly what to study and has practice problems available. She is also very accessible outside of class. She may be a little odd and she speaks very loudly but other than cutting off student questions, she wasn't rude or mean at all, maybe just quirky

Honestly, some of the reviews are semi-accurate but overall people are being dramatic. She clearly cares a lot and is always available. If you just put in effort before each quiz it's a lot easier to follow along because it all builds on itself. She's all over the place but don't be too scared to take the class, just keep up and you'll be fine!

First day of class was like we were supposed to know how to do everything already and it just goes downhill from there. Book isn't required but that's the only way to learn because Frances makes zero sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely the most difficult class I've taken at Foster and the professor did not make it easier. The professor often gets off-topic during lectures. She is very condescending towards students even during valid questions. Find a big study group because both the exams are very difficult. I barely survived and pretty much had to study everyday.

I have heard many people say that she is one of the worst profs. in Foster, but after taking the class she is not that bad. Just make sure to pay attention in class and do the homeworks/practice tests, and you will be prepared for the final. She mentions to read the textbook a lot, but I never did and did fine in the class. Overall a decent teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Frances is very knowledgable and you can tell she genuinely wants students to learn, but her teaching made it super hard to follow along in class. Tends to make out-of-pocket or shady comments but I guess that made lectures slightly more entertaining. Not an impossible course if you have a good support system and stay on top of readings.

Frances is one of the worst professors at Foster. She is incredibly condescending and has an extreme ego. She is a very bitter person. Her lectures are poorly structured with her often going on off-topic tangents. She overcomplicates the simplest concepts. The class is passable but you're better off reading the textbook and teaching yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Don't go to her class. Terrible lecturer, terrible penmanship (and you have to endure it every lecture since her slides are all written) Participation made lectures worse because it's mandatory. She does not wear microphones so don't expect the recordings would be good material to review.
She makes the material I already know confusing. I feel like she is reverse-teaching me. Her Crocks are her only redeeming quality.

Frances takes a long time to explain very simple concepts, and it seemed like our class time was not used effectively. Class is mostly review from previous ECON courses, but I left the course feeling more confused about what I thought I previously knew. I was not a huge fan.
A menace. Will look you in the face with a smile while talking down to you. Tread carefully around her.
Someone take those dogs away from her
don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Frances is kind of unhinged in an endearing way, but the class was a nightmare. Graded on 3 assignments, 2 tests, and participation -- which didn't seem to improve the quality of the class for anyone. Medians were very high, and many people clustered closely around the median. She obviously knows her stuff, but lectures were all over the place.
Frances is a very unorganized teacher, losing midterms no clear direction of the class. Most of the class lost interest after week 2, this lead to very empty classrooms

The worst lecturer I've ever had. I'm sure she is knowledgable, but she's so familiar with the material that she has lost touch with the fact that many students struggle with econ and need clear & concise instruction to succeed. She demands participation but responds in a condescending manner & fails to actually answer questions most of the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's a 3xx, not a baby 2xx. I average 3.3, so just avg. But I heard Q's that were just outright basic and drags the course progression. Econ is like math; it builds on top of other topics. Lectures are fine in my opinion. Yes, she has tech issues - just help her out. She sometimes goes off tangent, but I feel that engages some ppl more (not me).

Frances is honestly mean. She makes a lot of derogatory remarks while lecturing about things we "should" know already. As a disabled student, getting my accommodations fulfilled is an absolute nightmare. She doesn't know how tech works & refuses to learn. I'm talking Canvas, scanning docs, presenting, all of it. I'm scared to retake her class :'(

Most reviews about her are accurate, goes on many tangents. only graded by 4 assignments and 2 tests. The average midterm score was 50%, with only 17% of the class scoring above 80%. She fails to concisely explain topics outside of just the lecture slides. Spends more time bragging about everything she knows that actually teaching. Talks down alot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most of the reviews about Frances are true. She goes off on so many tangents and constantly interrupts students before they can finish their question and acts upset when students ask questions even though she requires LOTS of participation and its 7% of grade. Ik shes one of few professors that teaches BECON but I would avoid if possible.

Frances evaluates students fairly and clearly communicates student expectations. Grades are based on exams with low medians, but they are very doable if you put in the time. Tests are never a surprise if you do all the textbook problems.

Knows what she's talking about but teaches it rudely. Requires participation (which is graded opaquely) but condescends correct answers that are not what she's looking for. Participation includes email questions too, so she's always unreachable because she's flooded with student emails constantly. Gives 3.9+ roughly 4% of the time per UWGrades.

Goes off on way too many tangents. The whole class could be done in thirty minutes if she stayed on point. Also gets annoyed very easily and makes lots of small mistakes in class and on homework problems.

Although professor Maloy is highly knowledgeable in economics, I don't believe she should teach it because her teaching methods are mediocre at best. She tends to speak over students, yells during lectures, and is far too authoritarian. I feel like my tuition money was not well spent in this class.

The Professor is super passionate and knowledgeable in her field bu the way her class is structured (B ECON 300) is not that great. You will have to participate in every lecture to get the 40 points, with 30 points and almost perfect scores on exams I still ended up with a 3.5. Her class median was also super high. Just Participate ALOT.

Pros: Smart. Cons: Everything else. She talks over students, comes across as rude, blames others for her mistakes, not good w/ Zoom, Canvas is a mess, slow talker, goes on tangents. My least favorite UW prof so far. Once gave us a quiz without enough time, hardly anyone finished it, then tried to blame it on us instead of taking responsibility.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Probably the worst online class I have taken at UW. Frances is extremely stubborn and refuses to accept responsibility when she makes a mistakes instead deciding to shift the blame onto her students. She also required strong participation which is hard in a lecture that will lull you to sleep and is much easier to watch on Panopto at 1.5x speed.

Literally one of the worst professors I've had. Blames IT for technical ignorance (not uploading recorded lectures etc), Canvas page is a mess. She makes mistakes in every lecture, writes formulas wrong, does practice problems incorrectly, the homework answer keys are filled with errors. Interrupts our questions and is condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Terrible professor and makes the Canvas site an Easter egg hunt. The due date times are inconsistent (some days 11:59, some days 4:00). She posts assignments to canvas the week only a few days before due and changes everything about her syllabus. I would never recommend her to anyone.

Frances is tough, she is definitely condescending and definitely can come across as rude and so it really bothered me going to her class. However, she is VERY well versed in economics and I feel like I learned a lot from her class. The lectures are boring and it is hard to ask questions given her rudeness and tone at times but go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Frances requires you to talk in class for participation, but half the time when students ask questions she is unnecessarily condescending and rude. Midterm was multiple choice but final was all short answer, and she refused to give example short answer questions to prepare for it. Econ isn't that bad, but she makes it way harder than it should be.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She goes off tangents while lecturing which makes it hard to follow, and the final being all short response for an online format. With a lot of classes giving concessions for the pandemic, she gives absolutely NONE. take a shot every time she says "i've said that already, " in lecture.

She definitely knows her stuff, but can't convey it in a way students understand it. I remember she complained about students asking too many questions, but that's because people aren't following what she's saying. If she wants to get through the class more quickly, then she has to be more clear with her teaching. If you can, avoid taking her.

She sucks, straight up annoying and gets off topic 100% of the time. You could play a drinking game for all the times she says "um what". She also is a mean person and should no longer be a teacher, UW are you telling me there are no better options than this women
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is incredibly unorganized, unsympathetic, and online classes have been a NIGHTMARE with her. I've taken her for 2 Foster classes and she still remains a poor lecturer and either refuses to get better at Zoom/online tech or is in denial about being ass at it. She is unclear with grading rubrics, class expectations, and in-class participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Avoid. At. All. Cost. While available outside of class, she's still just hard to follow. She also yells the lecture at you. I'm not kidding. And she talks over us CONSTANTLY. You can't even get your question out. I spend 15 hours a week + study sessions and I'm still lost. Unless you love Khan Academy and stressing out, just do yourself a favor...

Her online class is very unorganized. The canvas page is a mess with any clear structure. The deadline may change often from the initial class schedule in the syllabus which makes things very unorganized. Long lectures, can go off-topic at times. Reading the textbook is often clearer/easier to understand than the lectures.

Frances is a really good lecturer! The homework is optional but I would recommend doing it and staying on top of it! If I had, I would've gotten a better grade for sure. She goes fast so it helps that it's recorded and you can go back and watch it to understand better. Participation counts- I wish I participated more! Solid professor if you keep up
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is not always the most organized, but she knows what she is talking about. Her explanations could be confusing at first, but with repetition, the concepts start to make sense.

Graded on a few things, including the ridiculous 6 minutes 20 points quizzes, 2 takehomes, and a midterm + final. She gets distracted easily and would ramble about unnecessary things during class time. A smart person, but not a really good teacher. Come to class because she doesnt really post her annotated slides, and participating is a doozy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Remote learning has not been kind to Professor Maloy. Let's start there. Frequently there are technical issues that are either blamed on "tech support" or even the class. One class went 45 minutes before she realized she was muted, despite chat and speakers trying to alert her. Other than that, her tests were lazy, copy/pasted from study guides.

I have no idea how her class is normally, but taking her BECON 300 class over zoom was a nightmare. Lectures were slow-moving but she yells "WHAT" a lot so it keeps your attention. Absolutely ridiculous 6-minute 20-point quizzes. Other than the quizzes I guess the course is alright but overall not a fun experience.

I took her 453 and it is a nightmare. the class are not that hard but she explained everything unclear and never gives NO practise and homework so you don't know what to expect om your midterm. Plus I learned nothing because 70% of the class is similar to 350. Her 300 is fine not because of her but because that is an easy course

Frances is very poor organizationally and in her teaching style. She is smart like other people have said, but her lectures and notes and inconsistent and unorganized. She does very poorly at adapting to the online school structure and instead of helping students and listening to their feedback she yells and them and gets defensive.

Professor Maloy is a good instructor who really does care about her students. She was very cognizant and responsive to the chaos of the world. She can get distracted and off-topic in lectures, but she knows the material very well and is effective at teaching it. Tests are pretty challenging. Overall, glad I took the course with her!

Overall a solid professor who teaches material well and makes it clear what you need to know for exams. She really showed how much she cares about her students and their wellbeing. If you have the chance, take the time to get to know her outside of class because she really appreciates building relationship with her students.

Frances is an amazing teacher. She truly cares about her students and wants you to succeed. She is open to answer any questions, she gives ample study materials, her lectures are straight forward and her tests are really a fair way to judge the material in class. Don't let these other reviews scare you, Frances is a great teacher for BECON300.

Frances is odd but after a while you begin to find her pretty entertaining. The class was straight forward and it wasnt like tests were out of nowhere. Just dont make any mistakes on problems worth a lot of points, thats where she kills you. Lectures were mediocre, lots of people stop going

Maloy was the most frustrating professor I have ever taken. Blows through topics in class without giving through explanations then she gets mad at you for asking questions in class. You need to teach yourself all the material to have a chance of doing well. I went into the class excited and left the final never wanting to look at econ again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: A lot of people don't like her, but I didn't think she was that bad when I took her. Just do your own work and read the textbook if her lectures are confusing (which they were to me). The class was quite interesting as well and is both concepts and calculations (which aren't bad) so be prepared to put in some work for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: People hate on Maloy cause she is intense but she is truly one of the smartest people I have ever met. Show up to class, take notes, do the problems and you will be successful. Her tests are never a surprise - meaning you just need to do her examples and you will be solid.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Iffy lectures and grade based 100% off tests. Her exams werent the most difficult (mostly conceptual), however her graders were relatively harsh and docked points for everything -40% off for not labeling a graph axis- for example. Overall, I would say shes a decent teacher but I personally would look for someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Maloy is not as bad as everyone says she is. She knows her stuff extremely well and is an energetic and enthusiastic teacher. However, she has a tendency to go on various tangents and draw attention to unnecessary details which detract from learning. After a few weeks you get used to this, so it's manageable. Make sure to study hard for all tests!!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture notes are so valuable so you have to go to class. Tests are lecture heavy and you won't pass if you don't go to class. She spends over half the time rambling about useless things. If you go to office hours, she will yell at you and condescend you. Just go to class, keep your head down, study, and it'll be an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is extremely knowledgeable, but not a very good teacher. I have no doubt that she's a highly adept economist; however, she moves way too quickly through her lectures without ensuring that the class is understanding her instruction. I thought maybe it was just me, but the vast majority of her students report feeling the same way.

Maloy is passionate about economics and knows what she's talking about. Her teaching style is lecturing for the entire class period and writing plenty of notes, which can be messy and isn't for everyone. If econ isn't your strong suit, you're a slow writer, or you like to actually work through examples in class, then this isn't the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The best word to describe Maloy is unkempt. She's actually not a bad teacher at all; a bit rambly at times but other than that, she gets the material across. Study from the lecture notes, do the homework, and you'll be fine. If you thought ECON 200 & 201 were a breeze, this is pretty much the same class with a little statistics added to it.

Graded on 4 things: two midterms, group project, and a final, so the best advice is to show up to class and take good notes, as she is very lecture-heavy. Very helpful during office hours. Doing well in this course requires doing the homework problems before/after lecture, and not waiting to review concepts. Curve is pretty high on first midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Maloy seems to teach everything in Foster, but econ is her specialty. She goes off on random tangents and it's easy to space out during class. She can be a little unclear at times and she isn't very good at answering questions. Very smart and can be helpful in office hours. Overall though, standard prof and if you put in effort you will do well.

Courseload is heavy. Exam is cumulative. The midterm exam is 8 pages long front and back PLUS a take home part. Lots of note taking. Exam is so much harder than what she taught in class. She's very smart but she should just stick with teaching Econ.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Frances is fast and loud. She steamrolls over questions and can be patronizing. Sometimes she takes simple concepts and makes them seem hard. That said, for people who learn well from lectures, have a solid Econ background, and can keep up, she's a great professor. Good lectures, and a manageable workload.

I have heard Maloy have a bad rep, but it is not true. If you pay the right effort in her class, you will get a good grade. Maloy definitely knows her stuff and her lecture and notes are very concise and to the point. Tips for those taking her class. Understand the stuffs instead of memorizing it. Her office hours are super helpful too! A++

I feel like people don't like Maloy just because she's a bit odd. She's a good professor who knows what she's talking about and is very open to helping you if you ask. She has her quirks but knows econ. Not an easy class but if you put the work in you'll be fine.

LOTS OF HOMEWORK, POP QUIZZES, AND READING. This class is hard.. especially with this professor. If at all possible, take it with someone else. If you can't, then be prepared to work very hard. The professor is knowledgable, but her teaching style isn't the most effective for some students. I would say that its either a hit or miss with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Frances is one of the professors that you pretty much have to take at some point at UW. She lectures from the white board, so you need to come to class to get notes. Besides her incoherent and lengthy lectures, she expects you to learn a lot on your own by reading and doing the homework. The exams aren't too hard, but this is a self taught class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Overall, Frances was a great teacher. She went through all the steps on the board, which was very helpful for me to learn the material. Yes she does have a crazy personality, but she is very kind-hearted in reality and does care about her students. Go to lecture, although which lecture doesnt matter. You can take a pop quiz from another class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I cannot believe this woman makes $120,000 a year for being this type of professor. She is extremely intelligent, but her demeanor is not good at all. She yells at people for asking questions, answers her own test questions wrong, and never inputs grades throughout the quarter. Make sure to take notes on examples and attend lecture for pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I was initially scared because of her reputation, but soon realized that people don't like to look past the surface. She is an incredibly smart lady and good professor. Yes, she's a "scary" New Yorker, but don't take it personally. Visit her in office hours with questions, she'll appreciate you. Her teaching style is clear;  it's on you, take notes
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Frances is an interesting lady. Her natural speaking voice is yelling, which can be quite intimidating. Then when you do participate or ask a question she interrupts you. She then assumes that since no one is participating that we haven't done the homework. Besides that, she does know what she's talking about and is a great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I liked her, but I also like economics. Others I've talked to say she talks too fast and doesn't hit the concepts home fully, but I thought she explained everything well and efficiently. Tells stories a lot & loves dogs. Hard to ask her questions, she kind of steamrolls over them and moves on. Tests are way too long for time given, you won't finish

Frances is a very smart lady. She is able to take difficult concepts, and make them into simple concepts. She has a fast paced teaching style; which is good if you ask me, because she is preparing her students for the real world. To be successful in her class I would recommend regular attendance and going to her office hours for additional help.

Maloy simplifies the complex you don't need a book she provides everything through canvas. Her lectures are far better than the book explanation. Pop Quizzes but if you listen you will know when it is coming. Talk to her about her dogs. You will get a bump if she likes you.  Love professors who teach you short cuts . I would take her again.

I took Maloy in Winter. In class multiple choice exam was hard; the take home essays were easier. The grading looked for specific key points to a question and if you missed it, you likely would get points deducted - it was fair, however. She returns the exams within a week which is very quick relative to the quizzes which may take much longer.

Maloy is the most condescending and rude professor I've at UW. She makes you feel stupid for simply asking a question and constantly critiques our generation. Teaching seems a chore for her and honestly I'm not sure why she's here. She makes the material seem impossible when most of it is common sense, but she does give pop quizzes and has no mercy

I've had Maloy twice (Fin423 and BECON300) - she takes everything you could possibly get confused on and simplifies it to elementary school language. Structure is always the same, 5-6 pop quizzes (drops lowest two) and midterm + final. If you want to understand thoroughly and not buy a book, take her. Also pretty funny!

She's very knowledgeable of the material -- that's for sure. She's a little crazy to be honest, but i keeps lectures interesting. She won't pull you along though. If you need help, go to her office hours. She is very helpful. She uses the book pretty heavily but also does a few topics different than the book, so I would advise going to class.

Goods and bads here. Maloy definitely makes herself available to you if you need extra help, but she often comes off as curt when you make a point to ask her extra questions. In class notes can get disorganized. Hard test to study for, do every HW problem throughout the quarter twice so it's fresher when reviewing for the final. Cramlose.

This is the best business core class I've taken. Clear and concise notes; fair exams; clear grading criteria. Lectures are interesting with Professor Maloy and she can explain the complex concepts to non-economics/finance majors clearly. Her class makes me want to switch to finance!

Although the material may be dry at times, they were never boring because of professor Maloy. She can explain things really well that a non-business economics person can easily understand. Her examples in class are crystal clear. Grading in exams are very fair. Make sure you understand the quizzes and if not visit her office hours!

She's probably one of the most down-to-earth professors I've had. Plus, she's hilarious at timesClass material is not hard at all compared to ECON300. She is very helpful and I recommend visiting her in office hours. Pop quizzes and some practice problems provided. Will definitely take her other classes!

There're only 2 tests and a few quizzes throughout the quarter, homework is assigned for studying but they're never collected. Grading is very fair. She goes over what's on the book so the book isn't really necessary, but if you're confused or want a supplement, it's a good resource. Teaches many different classes, would love to take others if able

She teaches similiar in all classes. As long as you are caught up with the reading and try doing your hw problems, you will be able to follow along on the lectures. Do hw problems REPEATEDLY and do not slack on the quizzes. She will take time to help and make sure you understand the concepts during office hours. Great teacher.

Frances is a great teacher. She understands the material well, explains it very clearly, and makes herself incredibly available for extra help. That said, she sometimes comes across as rude or harsh, especially to people who "don't participate." If you can handle her somewhat odd personality, her teaching style is very helpful and easy to follow.

Professor Maloy is interesting. I didn't do super well in ECON 200 or 201, but I found B ECON 300 to be straightforward. She uses Canvas a lot and offers plenty of office hours. Pop quizzes are easy... then got hard. The midterm was easy, the final was hard. If you struggle with concepts, just go see her. Participation helps -- she remembers faces!

Professor Maloy is interesting. I didn't do super well in ECON 200 or 201, but I found B ECON 300 to be straightforward. She uses Canvas a lot and offers plenty of office hours. Pop quizzes are easy... then got hard. The midterm was easy, the final was ehh. If you struggle with concepts, just go see her. Participation helps -- she remembers faces!
Study for the pop quizzes - they make up more heavily than you'd expect in your final grade.

Lectures are clear - I took good notes and did well on the exams. Always talks about her dogs. Btw, the in-class grader sucked - (s)he graded 3 of my multiple choice questions wrong; on the other hand the take-home grader rocked. (S)he seems to be very fair.
Tests are not too hard. If you put in effort then getting an A is completely doable. Lectures are engaging and useful.

Lectures tend to be all over the place, and she draws all over the whiteboard with no structure, so taking notes and reviewing them later can be frustrating. She is very bad at answering questions. It seems like questions are a burden to her, and treats them as a sign that you aren't caught up on reading and homework. Tests are hard too. Bad prof.

She was one of the only business school professors I did not like. She acted like it was a hassle when you ask questions and is not good at explaining things (ie. teaching). I love economics and the material was interesting, wish the school gave me a better teacher.

In my opinion she is a good professor. Although she likes to go off topic in class, I found he lectures interesting. Pop quizzes are not hard, but to take them you have to attend. She goes over the material before the quiz. One big minus: all the answers contain "all of the above", "none of the above", "a and b" and such. Course is not very hard.

Maloy's teaching style is casual and down to earth. She's a sweet person who clearly cares a lot about her students and helping everyone understand the course material. Test questions are drawn directly from lectures.

THE WORST TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD. I'm pretty sure she spent more time talking about past lovers and the comcast guy then actually teaching us. If she wasn't wasting our time with something useless and boring she was yelling at us for not doing the home work (that isn't required) and not reading the textbook three times. DO NOT TAKE
She is a character, but the class wasn't very difficult. Take some time to do the practice problems and you'll be good

This woman will make you work for that good grade, but if you're committed you will do well. Lots of HW, Reading, Exams are tough. Study the practice exams, read the textbook again, review all hw and you will be fine

I liked her teaching style up until the last week of classes. If she asks you to ask questions, DO NOT! You will regret it. I have never met such a condescending professor at FOSTER as her. I'm mad I gave her a positive feedback on teacher evals because we did them last week. Otherwise, she would've gotten a taste of her own medicine for me.

Probably the worst professor at Foster. She is smart and all, but her problem is she can't TEACH. She thinks that everybody is as smart as she is and goes over material very fast, expecting you to take extensive notes AND comprehend the lecture. She is not organized and sloppy. TAs had to make 2 corrections on the exam because of it. Don't take her

Prof. Maloy is one of the best at Foster.  She cares about you learning the concepts and will do her best to make you succeed.  Visit her during office hours and she'll make sure you understand the material before you leave.
Worst teacher I have had at UW. Very disorganized lecture. She asks for student input but then cuts them off to go on about her opinion. Very difficult to stay connected to the lecture.

427 = International Finance: I really like the way she lectures. She may be unorganized sometimes, but there is no way you'd get lost in her lectures. I'd say listening to what she says in class is way more important than taking notes because what she says during lectures go into more details than what she writes. Quizzes and exams are really easy.

If you enjoy economic and numbers you will love this class.  If you don't, this class will be incredibly boring.  Maloy is nice, though very eccentric.  That being said, I understand econ way more now than when I took Econ 200 and 201.

Professor Maloy is a sweatheart. She genuinely cares about her students and wants them to learn the subject. She said topics in her class will be asked in Job interviews... and this was true for me. She does get off topic sometimes, but this just means she is human. I highly recommend her if your you like dawgs because he loves dogs.

Overall pretty good prof. A little quirky with some weird sayings but she is friendly and knows her material. She is passionate about economics and finance and wants students to succeed. Very good at giving examples. Tests aren't that hard if you do everything she asks. Read the book, do practice problems, and take good notes

Frances is very knowledgable professor. She can explain complex issues by using life examples. The exams might seem hard if you didn't practice the assigned problems. Review the notes before class. Prepare and participate. She likes when the class is engaged. Frances is an easy going person compare to some professors in Foster.
Lectures are boring and the concepts presented are not clear. All the tests are multiple choice but they are not easy.

She knows her stuff, but that does not stop her from being one of the most obnoxious and irritating professors I've ever had  the displeasure of meeting. The class would have been decent if she didn't interrupt herself with meaningless phrases such as "Mmkay" and "Whatever". She also flies through material and doesn't use class time efficiently.

I won't sugar coat it, the class is difficult, and lectures are mandatory. Maloy may seem confrontational and aggressive, but she just likes to argue and have robust conversations. She really is a wonderful lady and wants her students to do well. VISIT OFFICE HOURS. She is a good professor.
Tough class, but she knows what she is talking about.

A poor educator. Very loud. Enjoys threatening the class with quizzes. Her excuses abound for the poor quality of the classroom experience... unprofessional. Also says mm-K which is very annoying. Lectures are solely on the whiteboard and she writes very small... get ready for a long quarter.
Not a good lecturer. I don't think she prepare for her lecture at all. She went to class and tell you about her life. Grade is mostly determined by midterm and final.

I have never complained about a professor because I think every professor brings a certain set of characteristics to teaching and making learning exciting. But Frances, holy crap. Worst class I have ever taken. Total waste of my time. She made a bunch of excuses to make it to class and goes on and on about things going on in her life. DO NOT TAKE!!

Pretty good prof.Her explanations are very clear and easy to understand. The tests arent that bad, but are sometimes tricky if you dont read the question carefully. Don't bother with the review sessions just do the book problems and the workbook problems from the book website. You should be able to scrape by with minimal work effort.

Frequently says "mmmKay" as previously stated, honestly I thought it was kinda funny. She is a nice person but talks ECON the whole time so explanations don't make much sense. Go to review sessions put on by the TAs to understand concepts, Tests are Math and very specific definitions, be sure to understand definitions entirely.

Review your 350 concepts before class. Lectures content: Teaches straight from the textbook, get your own 'cause you need to bring it to class. Challenge level: Tests are easy if you know your concepts well and know how to apply them. Generous grading. Final project is part of your final test grade, start early.

Im taking two classes with frances, and I like the way she lectures.Shes very passionate about the topics she covers. her tests and quizes are hard though. in a finance class, i expect to see more math and less wordy multiple choice questions.

I took her for becon and she was ok. I took her for finance and it was the worst mistake I have ever made. Her grading/teaching sucks! Her test questions come from a test bank from different textbooks, not the one you use-so problems are very different. You also have to take tons of notes in class. I would not recommend her at all! Worst finance te

I personally loved her! If you go to office hours and she knows you that helps a lot! M/C midterm and final -- lots of tricky questions so be careful! Pop quizzes -- attend class. Recommended homework helps with concepts. Take home group midterm and final can help your grade a lot! If you don't really try you won't get more then an average grade.

Frances is outrageously annoying. She says "mmmkay" like she is straight out of an epsiode of Southpark. Almost every example she gives is related to her dogs and how she leaves them in doggy day care. She has literally 2 sweaters that she alternates between, and she is completely disabled when it comes to technology.

Loud, disorganized, can be unprofessional at times. Show up to class and take good notes. Make it a point to visit her in the office, cos she doesn't respond quickly to emails (computer challenged). She often goes on tangents that further confuse complex questions. For her final practice Qd=Qs problems like your life depended on it!!

LOUD, will berate you w/ a smile on her face-has masochistic tendencies.  Will often "threaten" w/ pop quizzes if she feels class is being unresponsive(doesn't happen tho). Your grade is determined by midterm and finals- quizzes are small pts comparatively.  Will be nice in class "oh email me with your concern" only to not respond or do anything.

85% of grade determined by midterm and final.  Doesn't integrate numbers into explanations (all concept based.) Do not take this class if you want a good (3.7+) grade.  I missed 3 problems out of 75 on the midterm and got a 3.8.  She does know her stuff though...
Take notes in class word for word. Pay attention when she says "everyone makes does this wrong." You can't skip class and succeed.

Must be present to take pop-quizzes.  Gives group take-homes, which raise your grade.  Her in-class midterms are very hard (confusing M/C questions).  Lectures are pretty clear, tries to bring up the reading in class.  Goes on lots of tangents (20 mins of each class or so).  Not very helpful in explaining confusing concepts.

I enjoyed her class. She's a little crazy and talks really loudly, but she keeps it lively. She was a bit unorganized (ie on the list of equations we get for the exam, one of them was written WRONG and I caught the mistake... and shes a prof??) and a little unclear in emails, etc when you ask for help. Compared to other BUS profs, I recommend her.

Half of the material for the first exam (finance 350) was given on one day of teaching.  Almost nothing from the textbook was tested on, contrary to what she said.  No way to get notes if you missed a day.  She's there to help, but only if you want the same answer she gave in class.

Class can be a little difficult if you miss one class. You gotta take notes... and lots of notes too! Your hand will be tired after her class. As long as you take notes and study from your notes, you should do fine. If you don't like to take notes, don't take her class!

Class should have been called "How to use the HP-10B so you don't have to learn how to do math".  She would often go on tangents telling a room full of business majors how all investments were overrated.
He's very smart and very good at teaching and explaining things over and over if you don't get it. Exams are rough tho

Amazing lecturer, EVIL tests. Sometimes it feels like he puts the things you didn't study for on purpose. You will feel like you have the worst luck and that you might be genuinely a failure after his exams, but he is overall very good at explaining things and you will get a lot out of his lectures and talking to him outside of class.

Love Kendall!! The course is VERY memorisation-heavy, and test-heavy. Study EVERY sentence in the manual, as well as concepts/processes. He explains stuff very well though (but during class, no OH). Don't be scared to ask questions - but he walks you through if you're still confused. Though sometimes he feels a lil demeaning lol

Unlike other microm classes 411 requires deep understanding opposed to brute memorization. Dr. Gray is very helpful with giving alternative explanations and is patient if you are lost, making him very approachable. Also gives lots of good examples that reflect what will be on the exam!
Compassionate & incredible instructor. He is passionate & doesn't hesitate to answer questions and walk you through the smallest thing. Loved this class!

Very cohesive, clear lectures that actually really prepare you for what he asks on the tests (just make sure you take good notes and really understand the process behind what's happening). However, I was frustrated with his approach to answering questions in lab, as his go to is "think about it some more" instead of giving hints.

Exams and quizzes were extremely difficult and lectures (discussion sections) were run by TAs who are nice but not good at teaching. Long story short, I got 4.0 for the MICROM301 class (top 5 percent) but I barely passed this class. This should give you an idea about this class.

This class is HARD. Kendall runs the lab part of the class which isn't that bad. The TA's ran the discussion section and I disliked all of them. They were terrible at answering questions and when they do they try to make you look dumb. Weekly tests are very difficult and graded with a fine tooth comb. The TA's are what made this class so bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Kendall is a great professor. His lectures are kind of amazing - even if it was 'boring material', he just taught it so well that I was super engaged. When helping, he likes to lead students to a conclusion rather than tell them but you get help either way. He seems to genuinely care about his students . 411 is a uniquely fun microbiology class.

The guy's smart and kinda expects you to fall somewhere on that line of performance. He's GREAT at explaining things. The exams in 411 were BRUTAL but Kendall really gives you everything you need to work through the problems. I like to say that it all comes to down to the brain power you can muster in 1hr 20min of an intense 6-7page genetics exam

Rated 402 (Dec 20), back for 411, which is HARD. He only teaches lab lectures, is in some lab sections, but joins all lectures, can answer any question. My lab reports saved me from this major since 3 exams are SO tough. Tips:1/DO NOT MISS CLASSES/LABS/HWs! 2/ASK TO CONFIRM AS MUCH AS POSSIBLE esp on lab reports even DATA TABLE! Any point is worth!

Kendall is a great teacher but about as old fashioned as it gets. Nothing will be posted on canvas. His lectures are dense but easy to learn ONLY if you pay attention. It hurt me to give him a good grading since his classes are super hard and you have to give 100% literally 100% of the time... but he cares a lot. Smartest guy youll ever meet.

I enjoyed this lab! Hell guide u to find answers urselfneeded to ace his lab. Important:1)Understand why need to do each step+result if miss/mess it up! 2)Use key terms on tests & reports! 3)CLEAN microscope lens x7 even lens wipe look clean! 4)Study each lab test+dilution problem daily! 5)Terms mentioned in lecture will be tested! 6)Ask+confirm!

One of the best instructors I've ever had. You can tell that he is genuinely invested in student learning. He is very knowledgable and passionate about the subject material. Tests and quizzes are hard, but not unfair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Kendall is genuinely the best instructor I have had at the UW in any class, and that's saying a lot. The class is not easy by any means, but there is very little memorization required. The brunt of the work is in logic and problem solving. Kendall is excellent at explaining concepts and willing to help any student who asks for it.

One of the best professors at UW. His style of teaching is very clear, organized, and concise. Although, he isn't the main professor (only teaches lab) he keeps up with all the lectures and has no problem re-explaining concepts. You can completely trust his explanations, he is humble genius.
this class  is hard. i hope we got some practice problem to do before the exam. However he is an amazing professor. Every lab is interesting.

Amazing professor, but challenging. Not only did you have to memorize the lab manual, but you had to take the time to both understand the experiment and bridge connections with other experiments (this is the key for quizzesexams). Do well on the firstsecond lab report as the fourth one is impossible. Also try to master dilution problems. GLHF!

Hardest lab I've ever had! Not graded on a curve, and you will have to study a lot. Showing up and doing the lab projects doesn't matter for your grade, sadly, since you're tested on memorizing the lab manual. Very nice and helpful guy, though,
Great teaching style, so I was always excited when it was his turn to lecture. In the lab he was extremely helpful, but not so much that he gave away the answers or anything.

Dr. Gray only had a few lectures in our class, I enjoyed him thoroughly, and while I struggled very much in that class (due to the primary teacher Dr. Moseley) I actually did very well on the sections of the exams that covered Dr. Gray's material, really wish I could know how well I would do if I had him the whole quarter. Funny guy, seems cool.

Easily the best of the Micro301 professors.  His lectures and slides were clear and simple. He's easy to approach and ask questions and easily connects with his students. He only gives a few lectures for the Microm301, unfortunately, and the primary professor is terrible.  I wish he taught the entire course!

I love Kendall as an instructor. He's challenging and has really strong convictions about teaching style but dang you get some really hard as hell concepts in your head pretty efficiently with him. It's a pity he's not teaching 411 anymore since he really made the class but I'm jealous for anyone who gets him as a lab instructor.
Tests are not just memorizing, wo understanding the material is important.  I loved the class.  It was a lot of work, but i ended up with a good grade.

Good lecturer. Clear in explanations. But beware! He is known to be one of the toughest professors in the Microbiology Dept. with EXTREMELY difficult exams!  If it is NOT REQUIRED, I STRONGLY suggest you don't this class! It will SEVERELY impact your GPA. Nothing against Kendall but the meticulous grading and near impossible exams are a real pain!!

Offers clear and thorough explanations to concepts in class, pauses after each question to answer lingering questions and ensure that everyone is on the same page. However, workload is heavy, and is incredibly strict and stingy on extensions. Concepts explored in class also doesn't suffice to succeed in exams, need to put in extra work to do well.

Decent prof, nothing exceptional. He's genuinely a nice guy and makes himself available for questions after each lecture. He only had one office hour sesh on monday which was kinda annoying- but he was quite prompt at answering emails about math questions or logistics. DEFINITELY take in person. Not the easiest course but doable if you're proactive

He was not a bad professor, very interactive during class, you can tell he cares. At times his explanations were confusing, and you just had to know stuff. I came into calc 1 with no prior knowledge of pre calc, and did alright. Homework was most difficult, a lot of it and it being due at 6:30 PM. He's kind of funny.

For his first quarter teaching, he wasn't too bad. I will say that he expects you to know a decent amount of algebra in his lectures, especially when it comes to simplification or general algebraic manipulation, and that he sometimes doesn't finish his lectures in time. He is very kind though and can give great feedback and help during office hours

For starters, Giovanni is a good guy. He wants to help students understand the concepts. However, his explanations at time can be confusing, and often times, leaves students feeling a bit lost. Moreover, there is lack of practice material that relate to the lectures, aside from the homework.

His lectures, at least online, were nowhere near sufficient for the exams. He taught the most basic versions of the concepts and with the difficulty of the homework ramping up dramatically with only two days to do each one, so unless you hate sleep or free time be prepared to never put the textbook down if you want to do well. He means well though.

His lectures are very helpful, and he is always willing to help after class or during office hours. He frequently works problems on the board and walks through them step by step, often engaging directly with the class if students don't understand or need help. There is a lot of homework, but as long as you manage your time, you'll be fine.

This class ruined me. Tests were super difficult with no rubric or practice exam questions. I learned entirely from youtube and although I feel like I have a good sense of linear algebra my grade does not reflect that because you're entirely graded on exams. Lectures were super example heavy with little clarity on the concepts behind the examples.
I'd tell you to avoid him like the plague, but he'd just tell you that my statement wasn't precise enough and give me a 0/10.

While he definitely does care about how we do in the class and is willing to explain more about certain topics, the entire structure of the course is awful. Concepts are rushed and difficult to make sense of, and the exams are difficult and there's nothing to practice with other than conceptual problems and WebAssign.

Don't know what happened but this quarter's 208 was awful. He offers no help outside the class except his fully-online OH. He posted videos from another prof but his own gives so little explanation on concepts. His exams are challenging with no review guidance. Exam grading has no rubric.
He didn't finish his last lecture on the last chapter.

Giovanni's lectures on an already complex topic were confusing, with topics being introduced in an incomprehensible order. He'd spend too much time on simple concepts and rush through difficult ones. Exams were significantly harder than class or homework, with no practice tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture can be hard to follow and no lecture notes for review.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Inchiostro is clearly passionate about math, but sometimes his lectures were hard to understand and follow, but he always clarified things if you asked him. His tests were difficult and graded on very few questions, but he's willing to work with you and help out. Overall a great guy, and a decent prof.

I almost failed the course, but the dude's a respectful professor if you talk to him. He was very apologetic about me not being able to change my grade due to my neglect, so I do think he cares about his students.

He's okay for some but wasn't my cup of tea. His lectures seemed a little jumbled and inconsistent, he skipped over the most important theorem of the class, however, he was nice with answering questions. His final seemed extremely difficult compared to the midterms, luckily that meant there was a huge curve but just beware if you aren't test savvy.

Good professor. His way of teaching worked for me but I would say that it is not for everyone. He asks you to watch a video every time before class that covers the content material and does practice problems in class. Other than that the hw is minimal.  He doesn't have anything on canvas so you don't know your grade until they appear on myUW

Grading on tests is very rough, expect no partial credit. Lectures were expected to be watched before class and were not even his, not to mention unclear. His "lecture" classes were also unclear, problems we did were very complex and hard to understand. He did not do much teaching, making it hard to actually learn. No book used either
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yeah! good prof
good prof

They are new, so exams may be difficult, but they are the only math professor I've had who will spend as long as you need breaking a problem set down to elementary level if need be to ensure you understand it. There really are no stupid questions. Regardless of my final grade in this class I am a better student for learning from them Also very kind

Ask you to watch Youtube lecture and videos and using textbook, barely actually teaches knowledge mostly by selfstudy. Even though homework is not much, you can't have many errors or you will lose points. Don't even think of getting full grade on every week quiz, you won't be able because it is simply out range and have not enough time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Best prof in UW.

One of the best lecturers I've had so far. Her classes are extremely engaging, and she uses well-known cases to help you understand class content. You can get through the class without the textbook, her lectures are enough to help you succeed!

Weili is my favorite accounting professor I've had so far. Her lectures are super good at incorporating real world events, class discussions, and making sure people have a chance to share their opinions and understand content. She is super receptive to feedback and I'd happily take another class with her.
Amazing professor, class content could be a little hard if you take ACCTG 215 long time ago, but Weili really putting so much enthusiasm in the class.

Weili is the best accounting professor I've ever had! She ensures students have everything needed to succeed. Her 301 class was incredible! She makes accounting genuinely interesting and engaging. I gained so much knowledge, and her teaching style kept me captivated throughout. I highly recommend taking her classes!

My least favorite of the intermediate accounting professors but still good. Heavy on casework which doesn't translate much to exams. I relied a lot on the textbook to learn the content but I had a gap after taking intro (hardly read it in 302 and 303 as class explanations felt very clear.) Never felt super comfortable asking her questions.

Be prepared to teach yourself everything since Weili uses a flipped-classroom approach. She spent 99% of the class time discussing the cases, yet there was only one question about the content from the cases on the midterm and final. Be prepared to teach yourself everything from the textbook
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great class! Everything was well organized and I knew exactly what I needed to do to succeed. There were two group projects, one midterm and a final. This class is very case based; we were asked to read and attempt a case before almost every class. We never had to turn any of these in so it too the pressure off to get things exactly right.

Weili is the best accounting professor you can ever find! TAKE HER CLASS! She organizes this class very well: all the materials you need and assignments are clearly listed on canvas. Get ready to do many group projects, but they are really fun and inspirational. She shows us that accounting can be interesting and she is really nice and accessible.

Weili is the best! Her passion just makes you love accounting if you havent done so. Her class is very well organized and interesting. She really knows how to encourage and engage everybody into discussions. All the cases are so fun to work on although it can be challenging sometimes. I really learned A LOT from her class and from her.

Cases were time-consuming and difficult as you went in blind before learning the material in class. Curve was also brutal (the other students's fault though). I would have gone to class more had it not been at 8:30 am and 2 hours long. Weili is very caring and obviously incredibly passionate and knowledgable but this class was a slog.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I believe Weili is one of those professors you would love if you want to invest all your time into learning accounting. While she definitely loves to teach and attempts to be enthusiastic / engaging as best she can her lectures are incredibly dry and boring. She has has a mix of group / solo / and reading due each week that is time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is one of those rare professors that I would take ANY class from. Her energy is palpable and makes the topic incredibly engaging. She loves what she's teaching and works really hard to make sure everyone can be successful.

Weili is knowledgeable, personable, and put together a really interesting 440 class. The cases are interesting and most of the class is either discussions or brief lectures. The final financial statement analysis project is time consuming but worth it, and the overall workload is light compared to the 300 series. Great class.

Gelb is extremely hard to follow. Not only are his lectures confusing and disorganized, but he barely explains anything. If someone asks a question he is mean back. His "slides" are messy writing. I had to fully rely on videos to learn anything. He is pretty funny so I'll give him that. Our second exam average was a 37% which speaks for itself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you ask "bad questions" he gets kinda mean. Grades by your Z score/purely on curves, quiz sections ungraded. I think he's better suited for teaching higher level students and not a larger sophomore course. Requires a lot of self-studying. Very funny though, if not slightly offensive.

This man will not teach you the material you need to know. If you take his class, rely on the textbook and possibly other lectures. Like other folks have said, lectures are only helpful to know what will/wont be tested, as he spends a lot of time on topics that will not be on the exam. In my experience his exams are easier than other professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very disorganized lectures. No slides or practice exams & not accessible outside of class. Class average for a midterm was 37%. Exams weigh a lot and z-score depends on how well you do vs the average. Could have done more on my end, but also had to rely heavily on other teachers' practice tests, tutoring, and videos online. Would avoid if possible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Not recommended. Professor does not respond to emails (stated in syllabus), lectures are disorganized with no slides, and the midterm average was 37%. I had to rely entirely on YouTube to learn the material.

PLEASE DO NOT TAKE THE CLASS WITH HIM.

His lectures are only useful for figuring out what topics he'll omit from exams. Even major topics mentioned aren't guaranteed to appear in exams. If you find yourself in this course, rely on the textbook—it'll be your best friend. It's far more effective to teach yourself than to struggle with his confusing lecture style.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: DONT TAKE IT DONT TAKE IT I SWEAR DONT TAKE IT

do not take Gelb for 238. he provides no practice exams/ problems, told us he wrote a 'fair exam' and the average would be 60%. the average was 37% and tried to blame it on us. impossible to study for his class, lecture is no help and his exams are unpredictable. this class is ruining my gpa and my mental health.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: would rather have hitler teach me ochem

1. none of the stuff we learned was on the midterms.
2. he doesn't have lecture slides, he scribbles on his ipad
3. he talks about his time in jail SO MUCH, he thinks hes proud of that
4. doesn't wear shoes
5. doesn't show up during tests
6. doesn't provide his own practice midterms
7. class average 30%
8. all the 5.0 ratings are false
please like

to be successful in this class you NEED to do better than the average. when the average for every exam is a 40% its a little hard basically turning everyone in the class against each other. there is no partial credit given and most concepts learned and stressed during lectures will be irrelevant for exams. this class will make you lose your hair.

His course structure has changed significantly over time. This year, the grading felt more forgiving, and the overall workload was manageable. Expectations were clear, and the class felt more approachable compared to previous experiences. Test where very predictable. Gelb and  Maly is a yes
every single thing that's been said about michael gelb, good and bad, is true. do with that what you will.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Michael Gelb they could never make me have a concrete opinion about you.

the stories I could tell about this class... don't take it if you love your GPA or your self-worth but if you do, prepare for the most entertaining lectures you've ever sat in on. that said i woke up just this morning in a cold sweat after a vivid nightmare about his final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would take careful consideration before enrolling in this class. Some exam questions were pretty predictable, but others weren't and if you didn't have exactly the right answer partial credit was pretty much nonexistent. Classes were enjoyable because of Gelb's humor and what not, but didn't go over the material super well.

Gelb's lectures are lowkey kinda unorganized, but as long as you pay attention and write down the topics he mentions, and review it in the textbook, his class is actually super manageable. 

Super funny guy, willing to say when he's wrong. All the other people saying he's this or that, they just need to learn to stop taking things personally.

weird prof in a funny, refreshing way. love his special topics classes relating to course concepts. not the best at explaining basics but lectures are pretty engaging, and textbook should help fill in blanks. honest man, maybe too honest

Gelb the goat fr. Imagine getting free content outside of the textbook, it really do be double the value. You learn the textbook material on your own(which is easier than from him), and you learn how to make surfboards from scratch during lecture. He clowns students a lot, but I let it slide because he clowns himself too. He truly is one of a kind.

If I could give him a 0 I would. He forgot to print our midterms and got mad when people asked him questions after he made us write our answers on notebook paper. All that just for him to email us after that he was making us take it again the next week.

He makes fun of healthcare professionals that are not doctors and genuinely is kind of racist.

Like others have said; the first midterm was on the white board and another midterm had a 28/100 average. In my opinion: the adjustments made were fair. While disorganized, lectures are entertaining and sometimes hedirectly stated what would be on the exam, so watch them. If you go to other lecturers, or can self study Gelb's exams are the easiest.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: An awful experience. He didn't have lecture slides and just scribbled on the whiteboard so there was essentially 0 learning involved. He showed up late to the first midterm without the physical copy of it and decided to write it on the board (couldn't read handwriting and wrote the questions wrong). Then he left. Dropped the class right after.

The one problem I had is that his exams were unpredictable. It was VERY hard to tell what he was going to cover on each midterm. Midterm averages were anywhere from a 40-50% after partial credit. His lectures were terrible, but he makes the weirdest/funniest comments. If you're going to take his class, just know what you're getting yourself into.

PLEASE SAVE YOURSELF TIME, SANITY, AND MONEY and never take a class from Gelb. Single handedly the worst professor I've ever had, if I had space I could write a book, it actually makes me sick to think about it. No organization, no resources, no accountability, no preparation. I entered w a 3.9 GPA a barely got a passing grade

Singlehandedly the worst professor I've had at this institution. His Canvas page is a poorly written syllabus in which he essentially degrades his students. He does not post any helpful resources or study materials, even for exams. Forgot to print our first midterm and showed up late. Did not send out course evaluations. Do not take!!!

worst professor I've had at uw, lectures were all over the place and he had no slides and very few resources to help on canvas. No practice midterm provided for second midterm, average was a 28/100. Forgot to print the first midterm and had students attempt to write answers on paper after he wrote problems on whiteboard. terribly unhelpful.

Horrid professor DO NOT TAKE. He forgot to print off exams and just wrote on the whiteboard and immediately left so students sat on phones during exam. Says he doesn't believe in lectures slide and entire Canvas ONLY contains a syllabus. One of worst professors at UW easily.

Absolute worst prof. Came to the 2nd midterm only to find out prof arrived 15 min late and the exam was not printed out. We had to spend half of our exam time writing down the problems. He left as soon as he finished writing the barely legible problems on the board. This man does not care about you or your education. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!

If you're not interested in chemistry, don't bother. This class separates the strong from the weak. Orgo is infamously difficult and he explains everything nicely - I didn't even touch the textbook. Be confident and attend lecture - you don't have to teach yourself anything, although you should already be doing so if you're interested in chemistry.

One of my top professors at UW. Attend the class and ask good questions. He's quite a famous person and truly does want to help you - he just doesn't like repeated questions he's answered. Ask them a different way.

Exams are incredibly straightforward. Each question has some dead giveaway hints or subtle hints. In his words, Orgo "is like wordle."

He needs to retire or be fired by now. Made a student cry during a zoom lecture because we didn't know what he was talking about and couldn't read his child hand writing. Yells at students, talks about INAPPROPRIATE things, I had to drop his class just to hold back from saying things that need to be said to him. Awful human/prof. NEVER TAKE!!! :(
Terrible.

Do not take this class. He is very rude, condescending, and impatient with students. He disregards questions for being "easy," "something I already went over," and about "whats going to be on the exam." He posted 1 midterm for the entire quarter and adamantly refuses to provide the answer key. His lectures are unorganized, unplanned, and unreadable

I just started this class one week ago but I am absolutely appalled that this man is allowed to teach still. The way he speaks to students is so unbelievably disrespectful and discouraging, I will 100% be sending videos of his lecture recordings and going to the school. He also makes no sense during lectures so is totally unhelpful. AWFUL.

Gelb is probably the worst professor Ive ever met. I cant even understand where those positive ratings come from. He is a horrible lecturer. He is pretty rude and doesnt care about students at all. You might learn nothing even your grade looks fine. Chem 238 may not be that hard but he will make it 300% harder. Its not easy to teach yourself.

Besides being a terrible lecturer, Gelb is quite honestly probably the rudest person I have ever met. It's painfully obvious how little he cares about his students; he posted only one practice exam the entire quarter (with no answer key), and didn't even post our final grades on time, he posted them 3 days past the university's deadline. HORRIBLE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Our grade for the quarter consisted of ONLY the total homework grade, and three tests. His lectures are disorganized and unhelpful. He wrote our final the day before test day, and made fun of students. I stopped going to lecture after I did poorly on the first midterm,only read the textbook, and did FAR better. I taught myself this course. Terrible
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I can't do this anymore.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is INTERESTING and HILARIOUS in lecture. LOL. You can see that from the quite unprofessional syllabus (big LOL). He focuses on motivating students to learn chem, but offers little explanation to excel in class. Be sure to read the book for the concepts and take lecture for all the fun! Not recommended to those uninterested in chem or reading.
I have no idea what's going on but it's fun.

His lectures are HILARIOUS, I haven't touched the textbook a single time, if you go to lectures and take notes, you would be fine. He is legit the only reason why I survived quarantine. If you want to be his pet student, talk about surfing with him, he might even offer to take you on a surfing trip.
Absolute legend. Terrible lecturer but it'll be a fun two hours twice a week and you learn a lot about life
he is an amazing professor ochem is always hard, but if you focus on the class, you will be fine
don't take ochem with him unless you can teach yourself the entire quarter worth of material

Genius, but terrible lecturer/teacher. Lectures are random, but it's imperative to go because exams sometimes have q's that aren't ochem related, but are from his lectures. If you're the kind that doesn't get A's easily, opt for a prof that has a good rep.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: IMO, Gelb isn't a great lecturer.
