He is funny and he does introduce really interesting topics within and applications of organic chemistry, but as far as teaching the actual chemistry covered in this class/book, you're pretty much on your own. It's possible to do well in his class, but don't expect him to stick to his announced grading plan.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Gelb does not test many reactions in the book, he calls them"18th century chemistry that no one does anymore." His eccentric sense of humor leads him to ramble about toothpaste reserves and 6-walled jail cells--you will laugh and learn an enormous amount if you attend class. Study what he talks about and it is possible to score over 90% on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: It's hard to tell in class what is content and what is the side show. Lectures are hard to follow and only vaguely reference the book; material on exams stem from lectures, but sometimes seem like things we never covered. If you work hard and do that thing where you actually study daily, you may do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Gelb is the type of teacher that everyone dreads. He may be smart at research and world applications of chemistry, but he should not be a lecturer. His lectures were unorganized and rambling. Not a single lecture passed without him going off on a student for asking "something you should have known. This is so easy for me." Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: interesting
He's funny.

There are few times where a professor has made me so mad. His lectures were all over the place and sorta followed the textbook but not really making studying frustrating. He said some borderline inappropriate stuff in class. Thank god he had Panopto so I definitely would have failed. Not getting up at 9:30 for that nonsense.

Must review all of your notes from the lectures in order to do well on the quizzes + exams. The exams were fair and there were no surprises. His lectures are pretty clear, he likes to to go on rants about topics relating to organic chemistry, but I think it should be obvious to the student when and when not to take notes (he will tell you).

I have heard many stories about Gelb, and can see why many would not like him. His teaching however, has greatly improved recently. He follows the book well, gives plenty of extra explanations and has started making reasonable exams. I believe he is a professor worth taking

Very unorganized. Lectures are hard to follow. he will start talking about a mechanism and in the middle tell us about vampires stories. When the average on the test was a 42 he refused to acknowledge he may be at fault and said students need to learn to study more. He doesn't respect students Ignores requests for help from students in class/emails

His lectures are disorganized and unhelpful. The textbook was personally very helpful in compensating for what the lectures lacked. It was not an uncommon practice for him to spend the first fifteen minuets of a class correcting material he taught incorrectly in the previous lectures. Does not give partial credit lightly on tests and quizzes.
He is very unclear about everything and grades incredibly tough, the average was set to a 2.4. If you are trying to get a semi decent grade, take this class with another professor.
He's smart. Not suited to teach students. Teach yourself and expect the unexpected. Unorganized and unreliable.

No one will argue that Gelb is very smart, has interesting stories that somewhat relate the the content being taught, and has plenty of "professor humor." This will not help you understand the content. He doesn't want to be teaching and acts like it. He's super unorganized & frequently messes up and spends 15 minutes redoing what he already taught.

There is no doubt that Dr. Gelb has an exceptionally brilliant mind.   However, I believe this creates a substantial barrier between him and his students.  The level of disorganization is distracting.  He is entertaining and I would happily engage in discussions with him in an informal atmosphere.  However, I will never take a class from him again.

I know that Gelb is not popular on rmp, but he will likely be the best professor you will have at UW. If you come into the class expecting your hand to be held and having o chem spoon fed to you, DO NOT TAKE GELB. If you want to learn about chemistry in a way that a textbook can't teach, take Gelb. He is brilliant an will rock your world

Don't bother taking him. His lectures are unclear, goes off on tangents, talks about non relevant information, and says "anything said in lecture is fair game on the exam". First midterm was week 7, second midterm was week 9, and we had to convince him to put up a topic summary list. He doesn't want to teach, and he shouldn't be teaching.

Prof. Gelb is probably the worst professor I've ever had at UW. I'm sure he's a genius, but he can't teach at all. His handwriting is hard to read and the class is organized very poorly. He doesn't get that a 41% average on tests, and 3-410 on quizzes is a reflection of his teaching abilities; he blames it on the students not studying hard enough.

He's very funny sometimes- he told us where vampires come from. He starts lecture with "this wont be on the test" and then tells us something cool. But an awful lecturer. To add perspective others  havent said yet, my boss (I work in a lab) was talking about this 'Gelb' that he hated working with. But he thinksGelb could win the nobel prize.

Terrible professor. Very vague, unclear lectures. No online support. He didn't screencast his lectures, he didn't upload slided because he didn't use slides. He DID upload his hand written notes, wrongly oriented and ridiculously large so that they were totally impractical as well as being unclear and illegible. No homework. Very little guidance.

Professor GELB will leave you flummoxed and in awe. His profound expertise in alcohol dehydrogenase and styrofoam will inspire you to become a piece of styrofoam yourself. He does several demonstrations in class, and almost considered reacting phenylacetone with methylamine, a complex process.  This class is recommended for its depth. Take GELB.

Well, It is a honors class, and he is Gelb... You will learn about unicorns, figuring out problems if you are in prison for 20 years, bad jokes, pregnancy tests, his long thumbnail. He has a brilliant mind which is seen by his research. You are in a honors class so you will be ok... HE IS GELB, you will never forget what it means to have had GELB.
Worst professor ever. Not helpful at all inside or outside of class. Why is he still teaching?

He goes on a lot of in-class tangents, which I like but tend to throw people off. His tests are like mind-wrecking versions of a Sudoku. If you see him outside of class he can be very helpful, but it's hard to learn in lecture. He also makes a lot of jokes and picks on students, which I also think is hilarious, but YMMV. Oh there's no homework!
Completely worthless professor. Should not be teaching. Doesn't teach coherently, nor does he use the textbook at all. Is foul mouthed in class, and is late every single day.

Hilarious man, but you better have tons of outside help to actually understand the topic. Assumes you already know everything. Tells stories, does NOT teach, "you know in cartoons when they see double? That's real!"

really smart guy, but terrible teacher.  gets frustrated when the class doesn't get it, since the material is "so easy".  moves through material really fast in lecture and says "go home and think about it, it will make sense" gives fair partial credit on tests, but doesn't believe in study guides/practice exams

Weird but awesome. Judging by the preceding comments, students love him or hate him. Some of Richard Feynman's physics students probably thought he was a bad teacher. I think if you like chemistry, you'll like Gelb; if you don't...

Gelb may seem intimidating at first, but if you get to know him, he's incredibly helpful and will explain the concepts until all your questions are solved. His exams are fair, and if you go to lectures, you will have the capability of answering all the questions correctly. Gelb makes class interesting with his humor and knowledge--highly recommend!

Entertaining (and funny) guy but is awful at lecture. Goes off on tangents unrelated to the topic and digresses way too often. Then he crams everything before tests. We're a chap behind after the quarter ended. Tests aren't bad, tests you off lectures. Exam grading is very harsh but grades on a curve. If you're taking 336 with this guy, have fun.

Gelb is very entertaining. He doesn't use the book, so go to lecture and use that. If you pay attention in lecture, study your notes, and use his practice exams, you should do fine. I really enjoyed the class.
hea awful...worst proff i eva had! his notes are very unclear and his exams are pretty hard..sometimes the TA's cant even answer! hes smart but he just sucks at teaching!!

If you already know the material covered in this class, then you may enjoy it; but if you are hoping for a professor who will actually teach you the course material, look elsewhere. Gelb expects you to know info that he doesn't explain and isn't in the book, tests on material he hasn't covered, and calls it easy. Entertaining, but a crappy teacher.

Why!? Is all I could say while taking the class. From taking quizzes before he even taught the material. Or not even covering material that was going to be on the quiz or on tests. I've heard really good things about him but I didn't experience many. Very fair at grading though!

He writes equations literally in circles on the chalk board, and then says "See?  It's easy.  A monkey could do this."  Funny guy.  Fun to listen to (when he gets off topic... which he does), but he'll bring things up in the lecture that aren't in the book that my TA doesn't even understand, and give us a 20 pt question about it on the exam.
my fellow upper-middle class students: you've gotta love gelb, seriously. he's beyond our petty****.
just plain boring, doesnt give clear notes

The worst one. "Aaa mmm I forgot, I'll check it and then tell, mmm it's been a long time since I learned it, I should review then tell you. I will answer only the questions I like". Never checked anything out, never gave extra clarifications, never liked questions. Is that UW priority to keep him employed or to actually offer good education?
He will murder your brains and obliterate your soul.  He swoops in with carbonyl reactions and then rips out your heart with chicken.
Worst professor I have ever had at the UW. His exams are based on his lectures more than the textbook itself. He likes to go off topic a lot in class, doesn't send email with updates.

Best chemistry professor I've had at the UW.  Doesn't rely on the  book to teach the material, but actually contributes things himself.  Very good explanations, and doesn't pull anything out of left field on the tests; instead he sticks to what he's taught you.  Highly recommended.

Gelb enjoys talking about how to mix paint, being held at gun point to solve equilibrium equations, being trapped on the moon in a prison cell while doing equilibrium equations, and discussing how the volume of a hypothetical elephant can be calculated, but its not real Like resonance structures right? right? riight? He is HILARIOUS; will not learn

Prof Gelb has his flaws but he does care that his students learn. He's always happy to discuss extensions to test/class content and very reasonable on alternate answers to his test questions. He likes to go beyond the textbook and include applications and current (i.e. his) research.

Gelb is quite a character... but an excellent teacher for the motivated student. I owe my entire chemical intuition to Gelb. He absolutely expects that you understand the chemical concepts and tendencies behind reactions. Essentially, you dialouge about reaction mechanisms during class, and the tests consist of a "make this out of this" question.

A disasterously poor instructor, Gelb cannot stay on topic or in the apropriate scope (undergrad).  While *completely* worthless as an instructor, his research may one day save many, many lives.  He and we should be spared the pointless teaching reqirement. UW Chem fails to respect the undergrad and should rethink and retool.

Very unhelpful and unclear on the material presented in the lab.  Tends to go on tangents on other topics in chemistry and leaves you wondering what class you are in.  Very smart but he has difficulty with undergraduate level questions/issues.  Tests are pretty clear though and he will tell you exactly what you need to know beforehand.
also the worst teacher i ever had... he couldn't teach to save his life

Worst professor I've ever had (including undergraduate and graduate schools). I am now teaching college biology and would be ashamed to have exam averages of 10%!!! Some people should just stick to the research lab and leave the teaching to those who care!
Final grade almost fully dependent on 2 midterms and 1 final. Gives opportunity to retake up to 3 questions on midterms with no penalty for doing worse. Regrades are your friend, lol.

Final is almost fully dependent on final exam score. Gives opportunities to submit regrade requests on final and usually you can get points back if you make a good argument. Straightforward lectures and exam questions.

The exam being so indicative of your grade is genuinely so devious. Otherwise, his lectures were fine and to be honest his lectures were a repeat of prelab. Lab was alright and nothing difficult, just prepare and attend, do your postlab, and you're set. For final, review all procedure material and do the practice exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Has a weird final-heavy grading scale and wants very specific exam answers, which is super concept based. Having only one practice exam and not having him for 238 felt very detrimental because I have no idea what he wants from me. He's nice and my rating is mostly reflective of how his teaching style just does not suit me. Fight for your regrades!

I liked his course. Concepts were a lot clearer to me when he explained them vs. my actual chem 238 course. Very test heavy, but as long as you understand the labs and why each step is being done, you will be fine. Long exam, but similar to practice exam.

Professor Goldman is an excellent instructor who wants his students to succeed. His lectures are great; reading the textbook is unnecessary as you can learn all the material almost exclusively from his lectures. He's intentional about teaching logically and building on previous learning, making his course intuitive instead of rote-memorization.

This lab class has a ton of busy work, although the lab reports are generously graded. Just prepare for a lot of work along with the labs. The final exam was rough imo, just prepare way in advance. There's only one practice exam for the final, so not much study material for the final. If you are busy/hard schedule, consider taking this later.

I would just say his grading scale/policy is weird. You risk none of your hw, quiz and stuff count toward your grade, just exams. The exams are hard but partial credit can be given. Overall, if you are taking other hard classes/busy consider taking this later or if you find o chem easy you're solid.

He is a funny guy, which made 241 lectures a little more enjoyable. While the course itself was difficult, at least he was generous when it came to grading lab reports (giving us full credits as long as we get less than 2 marks off per section). It's slightly upsetting that he rounded our grades down instead of up, but otherwise he was great.
honestly id avoid him. his grading contract sucks and his exam questions are so confusing to figure out what he even wants

Lectures weren't very helpful. Gives too much work for a 3 credit class. Credit/no credit lab report grading system is unnecessarily stressful. Also most of the grade is pretty much decided by the final exam but the final was similar to his practice exam.

All the old comments are wrong; this guy is great. Larry always opens the discussion to questions and allows for humorous comments when given the time and opportunity. The exams are pretty difficult given as it is ochem, but he allows you to do a second chance which is super helpful for areas you're struggling in and for more points back. Awesome!

Take him! Grade is based upon exam scores BUT you have a 0.1 GPA boost for doing the homework and quiz sections. I thought grading, the exams, and courseload was extremely fair. He individually handles all regrades and was very kind and caring when doing them He offers supplemental videos instead of textbook readings that were very helpful to learn

I had Sasaki for 241 and Goldman for 242, and the only real difference is the final. Sasaki's is shorter and requires more understanding of mechanisms/reactions, while Goldman's is longer and more tedious, with questions about minute procedural details. Goldman's lectures were easier to understand but in my opinion neither were too useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a great lecturer and its easy to understand the content. The grading is forgiving with second-chance exams. However, being just 1 point under the 4 category and no curve gave me a 3.8. It just sucks there's no in between. I think it would be really great if the grading contract had room for getting 3.9, 3.7 based on test scores.

Take Goldman for labs I had him a couple years ago and the 242 course has gotten much better. His exams are pretty easy and the grading contract is really nice now. The only thing that sucks is that the final is weighted so heavy, its almost like whats the point of the labs? But goldman is lowkey the best ochem prof out of all of them.

Very funny professor, always starts class with a funny pre-class poll (ask for a fit check!) Somewhat strange grading system that relies almost exclusively on exam grades, but very generous second chance policy allows you to get significant points back.
Did a bi-weekly fit check at the beginning of most lectures creating a welcome learning environment. Highly recommended learning mechanisms which ended up showing on his exams. Good professor.

I have mixed feelings. He's honestly a great teacher and explains things very well, and certainly cares about the students. I didn't like his class structure though, he expects you to teach yourself something but isn't clear about you have to know for the exams. He also has contradictory standards. Not the best but not the worst, you'll survive.

Super good teacher, really good at explaining things if you ask him in lecture or in office hours. Lectures were helpful and he honestly talks about everything you need to know to do well on tests. Tests are definitely pretty hard, but his retake policy is super forgiving. Definitely cares a lot about teaching and his tests were tough but fair.

imo hes good at explaining things, but i had to rewatch most lectures to fully get it. i would take ochem again with him. retakes were usually very similar to the exam. he can come off as uncaring, but he will answer your question. like ive never heard him call a student dumb or weird if thats comforting!

He is a great lecturer overall, so you don't need to read the textbook, but it is helpful. He allows second-chance exams, but there isn't a curve, and the grading scale is a little messed up. To get a high grade, you can only miss a few points on exams, and doing the hw + quiz sections can only raise your grade from a 3.7 to a 3.8 at each cut-off.
Larry Goldman is bae and he gives retakes for 3 out of 8 exam questions for full points so any existing beef should be resolved after that tbh

This guy involves a lot of off topic materials for 237 (stuff from 238, 239) and shoves it in as if we were to alr know this. The grading scheme is extremely weird and insanely test heavy, you can technically get 3.9 without single hw. However, a single point difference in all exams can drop your GPA 0.2 points. So, lose 15, 4.0. 15.5, 3.8, no 3.9.

Lectures are not really bad but he mentions too many off topic materials (chem 238, 239 materials and sometimes even 400 level class topics), which is sometimes distracting. Also be aware of those out-of-textbook or lecture ppt materials in the lecture . He loves to put those on the exam.

People dislike him because the course is hard, but he does try his best to give examples and make the class as entertaining as organic chemistry can be. Some people can't look past their grade for the class, and blame the teacher for any possible shortcomings. Orgo is hard, just study, practice, and genuinely do the work assigned for the class.

He's a teaching professor who can't teach. Like if you're going to get a phd in chem and not do research at least be good at teaching (he isn't). This quarter is going badly as his lectures are confusing and he's no help at all in office hours. He blames the student rather than himself and gets frustrated when we don't understand concepts. AVOID
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The lab section was easy, just read the manual and you're good. But having a final exam be worth 70% is crazy work. He works to make sure that the exam is extra difficult too. He gets grumpy if class doesn't do well on the exam and he has to curve. Watching paint dry more entertaining than having to hear his unfunny jokes or be in his class.

Too many exams and you don't really learn ochem. 3 exams, 3 makeup exams (that are outside of class schedule so good luck if you can't make it), and a final. Test questions can be confusing. My advice is send in as many regrade requests as you can. you got nothing to lose and he will give back credit 50% of the time, even if it's borderline wrong

Professor Goldman is a good professor, but does not provide much practice for the most important part of the class (the exam). Additionally, the grading material is not very clear on the exam and would require the student to have extensive knowledge beyond the classroom. He also is not very excited/encouraging about the class.

Professor Goldman is a good professor, but his exams and grading material are especially unclear. The amount of work and practice to succeed in his class is a lot more than the average student, but he does have good notes and provides a lot of example problems and practice. I will also say, he  isn't very encouraging towards his students.

Lab 242 isn't bad in general in my opinion and goldman was alright teaching it. He's a funny guy but the final exam is hard and his grading scale is very confusing. The grading for his finals is also very weird, it's hard to get a good score because it's graded based on if you use very specific wording in your answers. Overall just mid.

He's a decent lecturer but comes off a bit snobby. He does a pretty good job of explaining the concepts, but the grading system is pretty weird, with the final making up 2/3 of the grades. The labs are time-consuming but not super difficult.

For an ochem class, you really didn't have to do most memorization. Goldman really emphasizes the logical basis that chemistry operates on. He more often tests about the stuff he says verbally than the stuff on the slides. If he repeats it a lot, it's going to be important for testing. Ask him for a fit check!!

I never write reviews, but Goldman comes across as someone who takes a certain joy in being pedantic and punitive. Having the final exam count for 2/3 of the grade in a lab course is especially strange, given how time-consuming the labs are and the fact that this course is meant to supplement a lecture series that already involves heavy testing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Redid his entire grading system so now there are exam retakes every week after the exam. Very tedious and draining because it's essentially an exam every week. Mentions insanely bizarre topics on his exams that are not covered anywhere else. Doesn't actually focus on ochem; focuses on wording and semantics. Glosses over concepts in class.

He's passionate & lighthearted. However, he has awful drawing skills (help 😩), and lacks teaching talent of explaining concepts well (unlike Forbes/Robinson). Adapting to his wack grading system took me most of the quarter. Some key details on the exams were barely covered in lecture, or even never mentioned!

Goldman is very frustrating to listen to sometimes - He makes things seem simple by the way he phrases his sentences and often does not explain things. The grading system for 241 is also a mess - He scales the exam down from 160 to 20 points. Why not just use a regular system that people actually like?
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loves conceptual questions - make sure you understand reasoning behind everything. Good lectures, also good at explaining things in office hours so def go to that. Fall 2024, there was partial credits + tokens, which worked out well for me and for majority of the class. Nitpicky with what answers he wants though, especially for concept. questions

Labs are fine but time-consuming. Grade almost entirely dependent on final exam. Not much practice problems give - just the 241 exam from the previous year. Grading scale is basically by 0.2 so every point on the final exam matters. Should be fine if you read lab procedures again and rewatch the lectures, but do make sure to study!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For Chem 242 Goldman clearly explained concepts and mechanisms that were allegedly going to be important for the (one) exam. Most of these concepts ended up being completely different and something you had never seen before, despite thoroughly understanding the lab. The lab itself is relatively easy, just time-consuming. Take good notes in lecture.

I had Goldman for 152 and 241, and while he was much better for 241 his lab manuals make it obvious that he does not work as a bench chemist. Having the final be worth 70% of your grade was insane as we spent 6 hours a week in lab, plus writing reports all for a mere 30% of our overall. All I can say is read the lab manual carefully.

Larry Goldman finds joy in sucking the life and hope out of his students. I would avoid him if possible but he has a monopoly over the ochem department. A LAB class where one test is worth 70% of your grade is INSANE- and then he doesn't allow for grade rounding, dropping your GPA by .2 points- he's kicking his feet and giggling as he does this FYI

I don't usually post on here but thought I really had to for this professor. the class is graded so heavily on the final test that its almost as if most of the work you do in the 3 hour labs twice a week amounts to nothing. the final exam was really hard, with almost no partial credit and no empathy/ understanding from the professor all quarter.

Doesn't allow any tech in labs-EVERYTHING has to be written in your lab notebook. Lab reports are pretty easy, mostly conceptual questions, and the expectations are very clear. Lets you drop 3 entire labs/discussion days, and there is some extra credit opportunities. Pretty average lecturer, your experience is more dependent on the TA you get.
Workload isn't a 3-credit course.

Supplemental videos before lectures, clear informative lectures, need to attend 7/9 quiz sections to bump up grade, worksheets not graded but helpful, practice midterms reflect actual exams, changed grading system to partial credit + tokens, likes to add a lot of conceptual questions on exams so make sure you actually understand the topics.
He doesn't care. dk other classes, 241 was silly for me.

Made ochem a lot less insufferable. The best chemistry professor I've had at UW so far. Changed his grading system so you get partial credit on exams now. Take him if you can. I used to struggle so much with chem but he just makes everything make more sense to me. Also very funny and personable guy who made class fun.
Tough grading but fair if you stay on top of practice problems. Lectures can be dry, so use Unstuckstudy and the free textbook to supplement. Doable with dedication.
Beware of his wrath

Definitely was easier for 242 than 241 and his grading system makes it easy to get a good grade as long as you do well on lab reports. Very willing to answer questions but sometimes comes off a little bit bluntly. He wasn't my favorite prof or the most warm or engaging guy, but I don't have many negative things to say about his class or workload.

The class is tough, but Larry is a great professor. Tests are more conceptual but going through the practice exams gives you a great idea of what to expect. Definitely try to take all Ochem classes with Larry if possible, it's worth it.

His class is a weed-out class. He skips some material but expects you to know it. There is a lot of writing on the test and little reactions. Lectures are good. The grading system is weird and no partial credit.

Goldman's grading system gets a bad rep but it's honestly not bad if you take the time to understand the concepts he teaches in class. I tanked one of the midterms but was able to use my tokens to correct my mistakes and went on to get a 4.0, so it is definitely achievable. His midterms are very fair and his lectures are pretty easy to understand.

Grading system sucks. All that matters is your exams, all the other work is pretty pointless if you aren't shooting for a 0.1 GPA difference. Did objectively alright on exams, but didn't get enough "pieces" per question so my grades were an awful reflection of what I knew. Huge mistake taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best at explaining material of the professors I've had in Ochem. Very weird grading system that has it's pros and cons. Very tough to get a good grade, but is the case in all Ochem courses. Doesn't curve. Still a nice professor who is interesting to listen to and funny at times.

I loved this professor. Ensure that you pay attention to EVERYTHING he says in lecture - it's all important. His practice problems were exactly like his tests so rely on those too - make sure you understand the why behind everything. Hes not the friendliest person so I'd ask TA's questions over him, but he's super clear with what he expects of you.

He seemed like he was indifferent, bordering on ambivalent, to all the students, but honestly pretty solid lectures. He helped me understand a lot of topics really well. He did get quite annoyed when people asked questions. Overall I didn't really like him, but I ended with a 3.9 due to the curve and had a good grasp on chem.

Exams were rough, so be ready for that if you're taking his o chem lab class. He doesn't give much practice, so my study method was finding past exams on the internet. However he does speak articulately, so pay close attention in lecture.

The grading system was weird but works well for you if you have a 75% understanding of the content, otherwise you're screwed. He was a decent lecturer but not super approachable and took a long time to respond to Ed posts. HUGE amt of work for this class but not rly his decision. The final was very fair- definitely do the practice tests posted.
VERY Tough Grader. Ok Teacher.

Goldman was a very harsh grader and doesn't regard student needs. It's very clear that he wants to reinforce that 152 is a weed out, as his curve sucks and it's very exam heavy. His lectures are good, however, he doesn't do that many write out examples that are seen on the exam, so the main form of studying ends up being ALEKS and the labs.

Lectures are hard to understand because he sometimes goes quickly on harder concepts. His bad handwriting makes it hard to follow him through problems. He requires very particular answers on tests to get full credit. His exams are mostly conceptual problems and does not test on actual problems, which can be hard to time manage. Get a tutor.

Goldman is a horrendous and bland lecturer, some find him tolerable but most do not. He is hard to follow, and I learned next to nothing. He gives 4 exams (you can drop one). Exams are very predictable (format is always the same) however it does not make up for his disorganization. I had an excellent TA and he is the only reason any of us passed.

I found that Professor Goldman isn't the best lecturer (his handwriting is very difficult to read), but his tests are fair. He provides practice exams that are similar to the midterms and great for studying with. His grading policy is the biggest plus for taking his class; having four midterms and dropping your lowest score was a great policy.

Goldman's grading contract may be scary at first however, it is really fair and gives you the opportunity to fix your mistakes. Your grade is pretty much entirely dependent on your test grades but there is lots of partial credit and as long as you get 2/3 of the question right you get full credit. Goldman is my favorite chem teacher so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just be prepared for all your exams, and exam corrections
Harsh grading system, don't take if you value your gpa, had friends that gotten 0.5/7 on exams that were worth 80%+ of your grade. The way he lectures is okay, but in my opinion doesn't explain well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy but his grading system is very unforgiving. Textbook isn't really needed, practice a lot (seriously), and master the fundamentals.
He's not a very interesting lecturer, and his grading system was not very forgiving.

DONT TAKE IF YOU ARE NOT PERFECT. GPA based ONLY on 33 exam q (1 point per). U get a full point if you get 80% of it right but NONE if even slightly below. One exam I got 1/7, even though if it was graded normally I scored a 65%. The way u learn to study for his class does not help for any class other than his, impt if u are going to study for mcat
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: dont.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Never had a more impersonal professor. His way or no way. Grading scale is DESIGNED to be unforgiving. GPA based mainly on exam points(33). Problematic when exam q's are graded all or nothing. He claims it's designed to show "mastery", but to get the point, you better know nearly everything PERFECTLY. Learned a lot, but my grade doesn't reflect it.

If u HAVE to take him, read the textbook (he says not to but it helps) but RELY on lectures. I went from a 3.5-4.5/7 to 6/7 when I started watching his lectures w textbook knowledge. Read the textbook before class (i took notes but it takes awhile) then class notes. Finish notes the WEEK OF and practice (not learn) before tests. GOODLUCK.

Prof Goldman definitely softens the blow of ochem, but he is a tough grader. Or, the TAs are. He grades based on a token system, which does work because students have higher GPAs overall, but his tests are very difficult. his rule is that you have to get 67-80% of the problem correct to receive the point, but there is no partial credit, which sucks

If you like the difference between a 3.6 and a 3.2 to be one question on a test then this class is for you. The threshold for a test question felt arbitrary, as well as if your explanation was sufficient. My test grades with standard partial credit grading were 85-90%, with his grading they were 75-80%. Condescending during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Larry is nice but the grading is insane. No partial credit (kinda). It sounds good at first. You'll get like 60% of the problem right but since you didn't get the 4/5 "pieces" they want for credit you just get a 0- no partial credit for the stuff you DID right. It KILLED my morale. So, you can get like 50% of stuff right but still get a 1/7 on exam

33 points total on all exams combined. Miss more than 2 points, you lose your 4.0. U do get 4 tokens total to redo questions. He has an all or nothing grading where if you get 4 out of 6 parts of a question correct, you get 0 points on it. Keep in mind each test is 7 points (final is 12). If you ace tests, take this class. If not, take Forrest.

Do not take Goldman. He is a good guy and makes himself accessible, but his tests are hard. He won't take any criticism of his grading system even though everyone hates it. There is no room for small mistakes; if you do badly on one test, you know your grade for the quarter. His lectures are pretty much just the book reinstated.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: DO NOT take if you value ur gpa. Having done fine in other 23X classes I had thought I would be fine and could rise above the grading scale but no :( 1 exam point determines a gpa difference of 0.2, so if you find exam-taking to be a weak point then AVOID. Grading system is extremely flawed and doesn't award you for the knowledge you DO show

Goldman gives good lectures and explains topics exactly as they will appear on exams. However, this means that you will need to but VERY familiar with the intricacies of a topic. On exams, there is a degree of forgiveness for small errors. Overall, the course drilled the fundamental topics and the tests were very fair.

great lecturer but he went entirely too fast and his grading system is wack. our test schedule was very stressful since we essentially had one every other week. homework and quiz section didn't even matter towards our grade so we were pretty much only graded off of the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grading system is very clear but overly stressful! He uses a system to receive points for an exam question where if you get at least 67% of the question right, you get the point. However, each exam is only 5 points. It is very possible to be slightly below the threshold and receive a 0/5. We had a test every other week.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE GOLDMAN! With the current grading system we have, all of our tests are out of 5. If you get a question >67% correct, you get the point. If less than 67, you don't. You can get a 65% on the test and receive a 0/5. Uses some weird token system to redeem points. Do not take him. Too complicated, unprofessional, and stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Labs were very enjoyable and reports were easy and short if you understood what was going on. Left early from 3 hr labs often. He is very knowledgeable and funny in lectures and he explains things very well. Due to the number of breaks in the quarter, we had one huge final at the end which was hard and points were deducted over small details.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: definitely a bit more work than a typical 3 credit class. however, goldman is easily one of the best profs in the department. hes super organized, consistent, responsive, and clearly has all his stuff together. his exams are super fair, but the pacing of lab reports could be better.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: There were 5 exams total (4 midterms 1 final), all of which were free response. All homework is done via ALEKS even though most ALEKS modules don't cover the kinds of things asked on exams. Grader's were pretty stingy with partial credit and took point off quickly. However lectures are pretty easy to understand and in class demo's were fun.

There are a ton of prelabs, lab reports, and small assignments to finish. My best advice is get them done ASAP. Labs were overall fun to me and my section didn't use the entire 3 hours each lab section. My biggest warning is the final. My grade dropped quite a lot because I did poorly. I would try to study as early as you can for it.

insane amount of work for a 3 credit class. we had 4 lab reports due the week before finals, and the webMO exercises he makes you use is incredibly annoying and time consuming for no educational benefit. almost every assignment is a waste of time.

Lab with Professor Goldman was well organized and I always knew to a certain degree what was going on. All class expectations are very clear and understandable and he provides a lot of supplementary material to help students understand. His final was also very fair because he provided a lot of practice material and drew his questions from lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Chem 152 is hard, 200 people lectures and ALEKS and everything. Dr. Goldman is more qualitative than quantitative when explaining things which is helpful. Tests are similar to worksheets and focuses on explanation, not math heavy. He has office hours 3 times every week which saved my exam grades.

Larry is truly one of the worst professors I've ever had at UW. His new grading system was so incredibly flawed and allowed for absolutely no error on exams. When questioned or critiqued on his grading system, he would lash out at students in a very juvenile way. It's truly a shame because he seems like a good person, but an awful professor.

Goldman is easily the best chem professor I've had so far at UW. His lectures are well designed and I rarely ever left lecture feeling confused about course content. Tests are totally fair and the grading system/overall class organization was very clear. Tests were also very much lecture and HW heavy, didn't focus much on the readings.
He writes very fair tests that targets broader understanding, and lectures/tests were not math focused at all. Super clear lecturer and a fair grader.

I love goldman he was an amazing lecturer, tests were super fair. He was very clear on what was important to know on exams and details that were not so important. Practice exams were very similar to tests. Will be taking for 239.
he had a new grading scale this quarter, which had some pros and cons however his lecturing and general exam content was very very clear and easy to follow, which I respect.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Goldman's exams are very clear and cover what was on practice exams and lectures. He's a great lecturer but also loves talking about hypotheticals which can get confusing. I had him during a year that he was trying a new grading system, so it may have been easier for me to get a high grade - regardless I still think he is very good.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good lecturer although with one topic he taught it backwards and confused me which hurt me a lot on the test. Weird grading criteria when I was taking the class but it worked out fine. Very accessible in office hours.

Goldman is one of the best professors I've had at UW. His expectations of what we needed to know for exams were clear & his lectures were easy to understand. Exams were fair. He tried a new grading system- can only get 4.0, 3.7, 3.5... The assignment category with the lowest score (usually exams) is your grade. I still recommend taking it with him.

Prof. Goldman is a solid choice for the first of the ochem series. He's extremely clear in what he expects you to know for the tests and gives you ample practice problems and practice exams that are comparable to the actual test. His specifications grading scale was a bit annoying (could only get 4.0, 3.7, 3.5, etc.) but it worked out in the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures were very clear. His tests were very fair & covered everything we needed in lecture and also provided supplemental material/practice tests to help prepare us for tests. Apart from his new grading system, which was all-or-nothing, Goldman was a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, really solid professor. Grading system was really weird for Autumn 2022 since he's trying out a new system, but lectures and quiz sections were great. Goldman's very clear in lectures, and doesn't use confusing terminology or anything, and the course overall is really well organized. Definitely read the textbook though, it helps!

Personally I really enjoy Goldman's teaching and lecture style. He is very to the point and his explanations & use of models makes ochem a lot easier to understand. He's testing out...weird grading policies right now but that was my only con of the quarter. Otherwise great professor!

Goldmanms alright. He lectures well and I liked that he focuses more on the qualitative rather than the quantitative w/ math. His grading system this quarter was new and kinda funky though, since each exam q. was graded pass/fail. Made the HW and stuff seem kinda inconsequential. If you need to take OChem, def not the worst choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Goldman is an eccentric man and comes off as snobbish to many. However he is an extremely effective lecturer and is a good teacher overall. I found myself learning more about CHEM239 topics from CHEM242 because of his explanations and thoroughness. He is however a hard tester and will give very challenging exams.

Goldman is overall a good professor and his lectures are alright, but very fast paced. His exams are very difficult to complete in 50 minutes, extremely conceptual and often times do not reflect the homework problems or practice exams. I've consistently gotten awful grades on his exams but did extremely well in chem 238 with a different professor.

His lectures are ok but he'll talk to you as if you're in kindergarten which can be really discouraging. I've had him for lecture and labs and his exams are pretty uniform but he'll intentionally ask about concepts he hasn't taught. TA asked him for extra material for our lab to prep for the final and Larry said no, so take at your own risk.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Goldman's class was difficult for sure, but he made sure that we were truly understanding the material. The exams made you think "above and beyond" from just the basics which was a struggle but now, in 238 and 241, I'm very grateful for this teaching style. He really prepares you to be successful in your next ochem classes.

Goldman's lectures were always very informative and prepared you well for the exams. His exams were very fair and he was a reasonable grader. Lectures were sometimes a struggle to get through but his witty comments kept it interesting.

Great lecturer, articulate, extremely capable of illustrating content, good office hours, clear expectations for what is going to be on tests, tests weighed heavily, decent curve. You will get out what you put into this class; Goldman is a good prof.

Goldman is my fav chem prof so far. He really cares about his students, and makes sure no question goes unanswered. To succeed in this class, I had to do the most but I feel like Goldman's teaching style is admirable in that if you put in the work you can succeed in o chem. I feel like he truly made the class interesting and is a good prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is the worst professor I've had at UW (and that's SAYING SOMETHING). He is rude to students and expects everyone to be as privileged as he was/is, and also randomly accuses most students of cheating on pre-labs. 241 was a 3 credit class but was too much work for even a 5 credit class. Don't take it at the same time as 238 or 239

To do well in Larry's class, you have to sell your soul to organic chemistry. 237 is the first in the series but he CONSTANTLY talks about future o chem classes & labs. Then, he puts future concepts we haven't learned yet on tests and calls them 'application' questions. He was good at teaching the basic concepts but made the exams SO hard. rip gpa

Do not take his class! He accused many students of cheating! Right before doing so he removed the sentence looking up figures and more info online encouraged from the syllabus. On top of that he was rude and condescending when questioned about anything. His exams were impossible to do well on if all you had was what he taught.

His lectures are extremely boring and the tests he does not prepare us for at all. He blames students for not completing labs on time when he doesnt cover everything we need to go through to even do the lab. Also, accuses many students of cheating on Chegg when they dont even have a Chegg account. Then he reports students to misconduct office.

Practice exams are nothing like the actual exam. Harsh grading, provides few resources, does not care about students. Accused and reported many students for cheating (Chegg) that he apparently caught by IP addresses. No flexibility with this being the first quarter of lab back in person, blamed safety incidents on "lack of preparation"

Goldman and Dunford are both on par w/ each other in terms of how well they explain the material + plan out the syllabus. Read/ skim the chapter before coming to class so that you can get the most out of opportunities to ask questions. Goldman is not rude about answering them, he actually takes time and effort to help his students which shows.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Bottom line: dont take any ochem series with this guy. Wait to take it with someone else next quarter.
Worst class to take at UW. His 0 teaching skills in addition to paranoid accusations of students cheating makes him unfit to teach.

Mediocre professor, with boring lectures and very specific test questions. Polls/lecture attendance are mandatory so make sure to attend those. Lab reports are pretty straightforward. The only downsides are that this professor is rude regarding any requests and condescending towards students' questions in class.

The curve is unforgiving in this class. Each lab you screw up is effectively a .4 GPA deduction. Goldman himself is an ok teacher and the exams are difficult if you don't know how to study for them - it's not like your regular chem classes where practice makes perfect. You have to understand the material but practice doesn't really help you.

Dr. Goldman is great and a must-have for the ochem series! His grading criteria are clear and he is very knowledgeable about the subject. He effectively transitioned to the online environment and had helpful slides. Watch the supplemental videos and attend office hours - you can gauge topics that are emphasized in class to prepare for exams.

His lectures are so boring and hard to focus on. Is sometimes very ruse and condescending, and often doesn't go over the actual steps to get to the answers of example problems. For more than half of 239, his go-to statement is "This is similar to a previous chapter, so just go revisit that." Learned absolutely nothing.

The structure of the class is good. As a lecturer he's mediocre... explains decently at times and not well at times. His exams are hell. Too long and heavy on synthesis problems. Takes forever to respond on Piazza. Just meh overall but not terrible. I did well on quizzes & HW but exam tanked my grade. I'd still take him over dunford though

Heard good things about him. Took him and he's kind of just meh at teaching and the way he talks is condescending. He's rude and hard to talk to and it doesn't feel like he cares. Does not respond to the question forums or if he does it's a few days after with vague responses.

Goldman is a solid ochem prof. his lectures are reflective of exam material and he doesn't deviate or throw curveballs at you. answers questions very clearly in lecture, not so much on piazza so be sure to ask there. heavy on synthesis problems so really understanding and practicing application is important. all in all fair, taking him again

worst professor i have ever had in my entire life. i took his class after hearing many good things. but after taking it, he would laugh at the class when we didn't know something? he is not interested in his students. if anything, go to Dunford. But i'm pretty sure dunford doesn't teach at uw. don't really understand why uw gets rid of good teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I felt like professor Goldman was extremely overrated and it was disappointing given the amazing things I had heard about him the previous quarter. He was very unfriendly with students in my opinion and very concerned about cheating. I didnt feel he taught mechanisms well and overall was merely an average lecturer.

Rude and petty and his lectures are way too fast. His exams are hard and even with piazza, he barely responds to you unless you go to office hours. His handwriting and explanations are a mess and he is very hard to approach. Best of luck to anyone taking him

Extremely overrated. He's an absolute awful and horrible prof. TAs be grading on ur grammar instead of what u actually know about chemistry and so I'm often confused on whether I'm taking an english class or an ochem class. Class international students unfriendly. (ps. didn't know ur comments could get deleted just because ur stating true facts)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Teaches as if you already know chemistry and never intuitively. Better resources exist but you'll get penalized bc grading criteria is too unclear. Exams are too difficult and long and rewards those who cheat. Blamed class when majority were wrong. No leniency. Worked way too hard for my grade. Class felt lose-lose. Wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Horrible teacher

Ochem lab courses 4.0 cutoff is 96. Our section did worse than expected, so he made the 4.0 cutoff a 93 which was nice. Average professor, lectures were vague and bland. Exams were open note. Use your completed postlabs from throughout the quarter during exams. Exam avgs were 68 & 65. Postlabs are worth more overall than exams, so do well on those.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Goldman's lectures are straight forward and to the point. All the material you need to know for the tests is presented in lab or lecture but not always heavily emphasized so it's important to study everything. I think he explains things in a very clear and understandable way and is definitely the best ochem prof I've had.

To be honest, I really enjoyed Goldman's class because I felt like his tests were very fair to his lectures! He also gave pre-lecture videos that helped me understand lecture topics more. Reading the textbook isn't necessary to understand the material. I'd say his teaching is a little mundane, but he does the job. I appreciate his organization!

Goldman is my least favorite professor. I NEVER learn anything from his class. This is my 3rd class with him and my opinion hasn't changed. He honestly doesn't care about his students and justifies the dept using your money for a single reusable lab video. He's rude and he tests you on stuff he talks about for 2 seconds, so take good notes.

His lectures are ok, he goes through them very fast and isn't the best at explaining concepts and answering questions. Despite doing all practice problems, exams, homework, etc.. and feeling prepared for exams his exams were unpredictable and were focused on material that would be taught later in the organic chemistry series.

I had really high hopes for Goldman, considering some of the reviews I read. His lectures were okay but he always seems to pull out random questions on his tests on material we didnt cover in the class (this includes material from later classes in the sequence we were not taught). SO FRUSTRATING!!! Honestly regret taking this professor.

I did all the homework and practice exams and felt prepared for lecture and the exam. However, the exams were completely different and more difficult from the practice exams or homework. You don't really know what to expect. If you answer exam questions with a different approach, he will still dock you off if it's not what's exactly in his key.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Goldman does not give a clear criteria on what you are really trying to learn. His lectures are very low energy/interest and almost have no correlation to the labs you are working on. He is slow to respond, negative, and rather rude with student inquiries. I found myself having to learn most of the class through my TA and other TA's.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took summer online with Goldman. His course is very well organized and has a clear criteria on what it takes to succeed. However, exams were very difficult and hard to complete on time. Had a 56% average on one exam. Otherwise, lectures were decent and I truly appreciate the effort he put to organize the class.

Lectures were very clear and understandable and office hours were super helpful to clarify any confusion. Tests were not difficult as long as you did all the practice problems and went to OHs to ask questions when you had them. He also provided extra credit for hw corrections. I highly recommend taking ochem with Goldman if you can.

Took this class during the Covid era where we had 5 exams and one drop for one of those 5 exams. Goldman is pretty basic he tries to explain the concepts as simply as he can. Sometimes he oversimplifies things and sometimes he talks too fast that I have to rewatch the lecture. Just make sure to do all the practice and rewatch lectures.

Honestly, the class was painful. Granted, ochem is usually hard, but Prof Goldman makes it doubly hard with vague explanations- he explains what is actually happening with what could happen, and gives the wrong explanation before the right one. Tests are harder than any material he gives you, including optional textbook practice. Nice man, but ouch
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Goldman is the WORST professor I've ever had. He's extremely petty and his exam was super difficult and long. He doesn't provide enough information to perform well on the labs so your grade is basically based on how helpful your TAs are. He's rude and will always call you out for not paying attention in class if you don't do well on a poll question

Dr. Goldman is the BEST ochem professor at UW. I took all three ochem courses 237-239 with him and I would do it again! Make sure you attend every lecture and engage with the class (it helped me stay focused since classes are long), also try to make it to as many office hours as possible (very helpful) and do a lot of practice. You'll do great!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Worst professorI have had during my time at UW. He is so paranoid about cheating that he said we were allowed to use online resources then penalized everyone who used an online resource. His lectures are dry and boring and he basically just reads the slides. Horrible explanation for questions asked. Unreasonable and disrespctful. AVOID

If u don't take ochem with him, then ur wasting ur time. Goldman is hands down the best professor. Do yourself a favor and trust me. Ochem in general is hard, but goldman makes it enjoyable. His example of applications are the best as well (how to make viagra for u college bois). I took 238 with him in person and 239 online and both were bombbb

He's quite conceptual so be prepared to explain concepts for a decent part of exams. You definitely have to go to class and pay attention (Ochem can be easy but you have to work at it). Make sure to study for exams (for exam 1: practice NMR!) and budget your time (especially for synthesis). If you do a lot of practice problems, the exams are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: (introducing Grignard reagent): So what can we do with a C-? Well, maybe not med school... legendaric food analogies and dad jokes. Perry@. Tbh, this is ochem, you have to pay attention in class because there is no such thing as guessing on ochem exams. Show up to lecture, actually work in quiz section, stop by office hours and you're all set.
He's very conceptual.

Goldmans class is pretty easy and this exams are not bad. Sometimes he makes you take things at face value, so if ur someone who needs to know the WHY, he might not be the prof for you. Hes a pretty straightforward guy and doesnt get too close with his students. dont expect to be his bff, but overall hes a solid lecturer with a generous curve

He gives great lectures, with additional metaphors and anecdotes to make connections between chemistry and daily life. Although the ungraded quiz section worksheets are tough, they help to prepare you for the exams. The class is extremely test-heavy, so study in advance and attend office hours!

He sets lectures up to promote active learning and often throws (dorky and funny) metaphors in to relate to concepts, but they seem to draw out often. I never felt like he wasn't making any sense though. His exams are straight forward for the most part, taking directly from lecture polls, practice exams, and quiz section worksheets.

Absolutely awful. Anytime you ask him anything about the course he's completely shut off to your reasoning and is rude about it. Final is crazy difficult and he takes pride in it failing students. If you don't want to teach, please don't. Take literally anywhere else.

Prof Goldman is paranoid about cheaters this quarter. He is saying over 15% of the class is cheating in some way. Many students have gotten zeros on their work because Prof Goldman thinks they cheated, but he has blinders on and won't listen to their explanation. He will think you are guilty and punish you before talking to you.

Larry flips through his slides extremely quickly and then just assumes we understand mechanism and reactions because they are similar to other mechanisms. His style of teaching makes it extremely difficult to do well on test. He spends lots of time discussing unnecessary information and then doesn't teach test material.

Lectures are extremely dry and boring (also applies to chem237), ochem lab lecture does not help lab AT all, which is why most people don't come. You're better off talking to your TA. Goldman got very salty about the fact that nobody wanted to come to class, so naturally he trolled the polls and sent out 2 VERY passive aggressive emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: First of all - don't worry about the textbook for the lab if you have Goldman. His lectures are brief and don't cover the most but his examples can be pretty helpful. The test at the end isn't too difficult either (as long as you look over the manual) but the TAs tend to do more of the work than Goldman anyways. Decent.

Goldman was a pretty good but middle-of-the-road professor. His lectures can be extremely dense and he doesn't always provide as many resources as students would like (saying we can do other things to prepare for our exams instead) but his tests aren't too hard considering the content and anyone can do well if they put in the work. Overall decent.

I had this professor for chem 238, 241 and I'm taking him again fro chem 239 and 242. He is a great professor. He provides you with all the resources you need regardless. He even posted lecture slides and resources from chem 237 for people to have a review source. He makes ponopto videos to any unclear concept. Clicker questions helps you a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The tags I used don't do the best job of describing Goldman, but I thought he was a really good prof. His lectures were very clear and he explained the concepts well. Open to questions during the lectures. I would definitely take him again!

I liked his teaching style, his power points were clear and analogies actually helped me understand what he means. He was very open about what he expected from us. The material and tests are hard, but that's because Ochem is hard. Make sure to pay attention to the lectures and do lots of review and practice.

Dr. Goldman genuinely cares about teaching and his students. He's NOT one of those chem profs who are only teaching so they can do their research. After every exam, he made a video explaining both versions of the key which was super nice. Funny dad jokes, great lecture slides, and reasonable exams for a challenging course. 10/10 would recommend.

He was a super good and organized professor with good explanations. Made weird smoothie analogies that surprisingly helped. Provided extra help when asked (extra worksheets) and holds helpful review sessions outside of class time. Tests were hard as they required us to understand why things were happening, not just how they happened but doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Goldman makes some cringy dad jokes but overall he knows his stuff. His tests are what you expect in any organic chemistry class. More conceptual and definitely a lot of spectroscopy.

Gave us midterms with questions we havent learned yet (for instance, gave us a question from chem 241. Were in chem237). Midterms had topics he hadnt gone over in class, or if he did, spent maybe 1 minute on a slide once. His midterms are unrealistic, unreasonable, unfair, and best of all? NOT CURVED!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: His lectures are super boring but focus mainly on the big picture ideas. I would highly suggest reading the textbook ahead of time because Goldman doesn't go into too many details on during lectures. Most of the polling questions are easier than the test so they are not a good indication of how well you are understanding the concept.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Larry was easily the best professor I had in the OChem series. He always took the time to answer questions thoroughly, work through example problems in class, and give plenty of feedback and clicker questions to help practice the material. Yes you will need to read the textbook occasionally to do well, but overall a very organized, approachable guy

Yeah OChem Classes are very hard as expected, but all I can say is goodboi grades all the exams for all (almost 1000) students, and gives us an actual grade even when there is a strike during finals week... Not like some other professors, we worked hard for a whole quarter, and then the 4.0 turns to a CREDIT. Very much appreciated, earned my 5/5.

Goldman is very goofy. His tests are as difficult as expected, averaging about 60-70%. He really seems to care wether students succeed or not, providing helpful hints for exams and review sections. I personally do not like his teaching style as he moves very quickly through lecture slides. He is not amazing but also not awful. Concept heavy!

honestly i just wanna know why Larry thinks we care about lab when he does zero to actually teach about the mechanisms, and then on top of that he rlly thinks it's ok to take off points for getting low yield when we tried our hardest to get a high yield but Larry doesnt care about that. all he cares about is his dumb "jokes" he tells. 0/10
Fair but pretty boring. His final is kind of tough. Lectures don't really tell you new information (it's all in the lab manual); the only reason to go is for the poll everywhere points.
reviews.rating_tags: SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great lectures, good grading! He actually means it when he says he doesn't want you to memorize things. He curves it really nicely, the curve ONLY helps your grade in his class (he boosts everyone's grade by a certain amount to make the average a 2.6/2.8, but doesn't lower anyones grade if the whole class does well like a lot of other classes do).

It's the department's fault the labs didn't match with 238, but it was unreasonable to expect us to read far ahead in 238 for his lecture. Most grade distribution comes from the final, which is long and entirely writing, so know post lab answers and why you did a step. TA office hours were the most helpful thing in this course!

Lab lectures are basically useless, he recites the procedures and expects you to know most things by the time of the lecture. Course was structured very badly, he taught it according to what he thought the 238 syllabus was (even tho he knew it changed). Doesn't really prepare you at all for labs or the final. Just hope that you get a good TA.

238 and 241 were not structured in the same order. Larry's solution was to read his 70 page powerpoint from previous years. Ain't nobody got time for that. Lectures were pointless, but of course he uses clickers. The class is fine and not hard to do well in, but wish someone other than Larry taught it.

Lectures were hard to follow and very dull. Larry also ignored students w questions a lot in lecture which was frustrating. Luckily the textbook is very detailed. The midterms are also pretty simple. If your TA is helpful this class is not so bad. Larry is not the most popular chem prof at UW so try to take it with Bryant if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Goes at a great pace! Really organized and well structured slides. Has extremely useful poll questions. You learn a lot by going to lecture.

238 and 241 two do not line up and so you go do the stupid experiment without knowing what's going on, and all Goldman says to do read his powerpoints to understand. Yeah bc I have time for that sir? You spend 7 hours in lecture/lab and then like 300 hours outside of lab. Worst time of my life

Great O Chem professor!! Super clear lectures and he always makes sure to provide extra study videos, exams, examples! He is always available to meet and you can tell he wants you to succeed! Great prof 10/10 recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best chem professors at UW. He's super nerdy and his lectures keep a good pace- not too slow as to be boring and not too fast that you don't understand anything. He polls the class for their opinions on classroom procedures. All around, a true bro.

His practice tests are generally easier than the actual test. Tests are also very long (10-12 pgs) and include both mechanism AND conceptual questions. Both 238 and 241 have clicker questions, so be wary of that if you tend to watch lectures online.

Definitely need to stay on top of the material and ask a lot of questions during office hours. If you do all of the practice problems and exams and come to office hours regularly, the class is not as difficult as it may seem. His exams always have small hints and clues to the answers too. Interested about the subject even though he talks fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: He was so interested in what we taught and was very funny. The labs were actually super easy, and don't be afraid of the unknown lab, it turned out to be a lot of students fave. The final was a bit tough but you only really need to understand why you add stuff so if you understand the science behind the labs, you'll do fine!

Larry knows his stuff, but does the bare minimum to teach you: he reads off his lecture slides verbatim (the manual/TA provide better context and info), he does ask Q's in lecture, asked questions yield patronizing responses. Make sure to study for the final early and befriend your TA. Also, figure out gradescope, it gave a lot of people trouble.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Even though Goldman is not a very good lecturer (he's way too fast), I took 4 classes with him (238-239, 241-242) because he's a very dedicated professor who would give you extra help if you ask for. His exams are surely long and can be tricky, however, unlike other professors, he would give you hints on the exam how to tackle the problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The lecture slides are well put together but he just reads them, or skips through them really fast as he summarizes. Not the fastest speaker but goes very fast to cover a lot of material. No real reason to come to lecture besides him having a nice voice that makes lectures more enjoyable in person than on Panopto. Watch out for final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Larry's a nice guy, pretty likeable and awkward. Tests are long and hard (NMRs for days), and there is a curve on the class but nowhere near as good as other teachers. You'd get a much better grade in a different class - but if you do take Larry always do the textbook review problems, there will be one question verbatim on the exam

This rating is only for 241. Lectures aren't really that helpful, but he gives an idea of what we should expect and do in the lab. He makes safety quizzes that are meant to trick students, a lot of the question choices are borderline correct/wrong which there really is no way to figure it out. Beware of the final exam, and it's not curved.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Terrible Professor, he is lazy, slides are directly from the book.  He adds nothing to the class you are better off not going to lecture.  Does not care about student learning.  Interrupts exams to ask if people are there.  The safety quizzes are bull, and SDS pages are crap.  Wish there was another option when I came to ochem labs.

Goldman is a really likable guy. Ochem is hard, that's a given, but he tries to be as accessible to students as he can. He gives a lot of examples, is open to working student questions and examples during lecture, and offers test review. He cracks a lot of dad-style jokes and his lectures are enjoyable. As good as chemistry gets.

Prof. Goldman has really clear and organized lectures (I learn best with a structured schedule). He talks pretty fast sometimes, but he does have a lot of material to cover! He's a very awkward and punny kind of funny. It's refreshing for such a long class. I never touched the textbook and studied by doing practice exams and quizzes and got a 4.0!

Good lectures, though he does not know how to pace the lectures, rushes through materials at the end. Great guy also, really cares about his students, holds review session before every test. Tests are fair but are really long.

Goldman is a great professor, he goes out of his way to give students online review sessions in the weekend prior to the midterms. There are a lot of practice homework, exams, etc. available to help you pass the class. Go take this class.

Best Chemistry professor I've ever had. His lectures are very easy to follow and will always offer alternate explanations if you ask. 2 midterms, 1 final, weekly group quizzes in quiz section. Homework is really easy to get 100% in because you get 10 tries per question and no points are deducted (other chem profs do this for Sapling).
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Goldman is a great professor. Everything about his class (exams, quizzes, final, etc.) was 100% fair. The practice exams were a lot like the real exams and the averages were fairly high for an ochem class (around 75%).  He really likes conceptual questions and mechanisms but highly emphasizes the things he deems important in class.

I took his class for CHEM 237 the first of the organic chemistry at UW and it was an awesome experience.   The professor Goldman is very enthusiastic about teaching and making sure that the students know the concepts needed for exams.  The whole class is non-curving, however, he changes curve accordingly and I was able to pull off 4.0.
Test is really long and hard compared to class. Really low average grade for the class.

The final was ridiculously long compared to the practice final, avg was low for a non-curving class. He is nice overall and tends to answer email really fast (maybe within one hour or two), so that's a plus plus about this class.

Reads directly off the slides so lectures aren't very helpful. He can be kind of cheesy, but mostly awkward. His practice tests are nothing like the real tests. Make sure you know the pre and post lab questions. Otherwise the class is pretty straightforward.

I love larry. He is my favorite professor at UW. He is never stumped and annoyed when students ask questions during lecture. Im not even a biology major anymore and im taking the second part of the OChem series just so i can have Larry as a professor again. His tests are not hard at all.

Dr. Goldman is one of the best Chem professors I've had at UW. He's clearly VERY intelligent. Gives great explanations, is very approachable, and makes some fun awkward jokes. Exams are pretty tough, but hey, its Ochem. Still fair and doable (except for the second midterm, which he admits he made too long, but he adjusted the curve accordingly).

Larry is the man. He cracks bad (good) puns and makes his lectures thoroughly enjoyable. Since the class is somewhat informal he is quick to answer any questions you may have at any given time during lecture, which is impressive.  Group worksheets (not graded) are atrociously difficult, but group quizzes are fair and help immensely. TAKE THIS CLASS

Very good teacher, explains topics in lecture very well. He never gets annoyed at questions and answers them clearly and in a different way than was presented in lecture. Group quizzes were great to understand different ways of going about problems. Tests are hard, but here gives partial credit and questions are fair.

He is a fantastic chemistry professor, his analogies for complex OCHEM concepts really helped me comprehend a subject that is not my strong suite. I would recommend him to any student interested in taking a chance with OCHEM!
best gen chem lecture in uw!
