Best professor I have had at UW! He is extremely clear, encourages questions, and always makes himself available. I had full confidence in his knowledge of the material and felt comfortable asking questions (I did this through canvas and got a response within the same day.) The course average is generally very high. Makes lectures enjoyable. :)

best chem prof I've had at UW. after suffering through terrible gen chem profs, he actually made me enjoy chem and made ocher much more understandable + manageable. i enjoyed lecture; he cracks bad jokes + legitimately wants you to learn + knows his stuff-- ask him anything and he'll know it. 224 is also easier than 223  if you know how to study.

He is the best chemistry teacher I have ever had. He takes time to organize this slides so that everything goes smoothly. The people who are complaining probably didn't realize that ochem is a hard class. I do agree that the weighting of the final was too much.

Very fair professor. His tests always covered material that was discussed in lecture. Slides were well organized and there was a clear order to the concepts being presented. Ochem is generally seen as a relatively tough class, but professor Goldman did his best to make it accessible and interesting to his students. Would definitely recommend.

He's a funny guy with interesting lectures, but not very nice, and he knows it. Multiple times in class he mentions having to go to the dean's office for saying something rude and HATES working with DRS, but they can't do much about him because he has tenure. Assigns a lot of boring reading; do not skip the thanksgiving lecture.

I don't regret taking POLS 307, but I wouldn't recommend it or any other classes with this professor. He brags about being tenured and close to retiring, and it honestly shows. He comes across as self-righteous, unapproachable, and not very helpful. Theres 130+ pages of reading a week across the five required textbooks. No online lecture slides.

Lectures were engaging and enjoyable—keeping in mind he's not very agreeable and extremely condescending. MUST do all the readings there's no getting around them and write at least 3/4ths of a page referencing each reading for weekly assignments and you will get 100s. Talk in section and go to lecture! Content was interesting, but he kinda sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Good luck! This prof's goal is to make you fail. Info on slides is intentionally wrong. Listen closely to lectures and take careful notes. TA's dock you points for no clear reason and agrue with factually incorrect data. Brags about how 50% of class failed midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Despite what many of the reviews on here have to say about Gill, he is an AMAZING professor. He puts an extensive amount of work and effort into coursework and lectures, and simply asks you to do what you paid to do. Yes, there is about 100-page readings and it can be a bit difficult to understand some concepts, GO TO OFFICE HOURS... youll do fine
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class is much harder than other 300–400 level political science courses, but not because of the material. The professor is unapproachable, unwilling to answer questions, and assigns a heavy amount of reading with little guidance. I'm not really recommend this class to you guys unless you want to ruin your emotional and your GPA then take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is mandotory as well as books, no free online ones lots and LOTS of reading. He is SO rude to talk to, makes you feel dumb when asking questions, go to TAs instead for any questions. If he grades anything of yours, GOOD LUCK, such a HARSH grader. Final exam has nothing to do with whats discussed in class.

You literally don't know what to expect on the midterm. Annoying trick questions, you have to take pencil and paper notes, and you can't access slides or a panopto outside of class. Things NEVER discussed in class are on the exams, which would be fine except there's no study guide at all (he claims the syllabus is a study guide).

Gill is an amazing lecturer. Easily some of the best lectures at UW. The issue is I am a DRS student. Gill does not seem to like DRS students. He grades DRS exams instead of letting his TAs do it, and he is a harsher grader than his TAs. I have lost points on exams for reasons unbeknownst to me, while friends answered the same and got credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Essentially accused me of using AI on my final paper (which I didn't). I didn't learn the grade of my final paper until a day after the finals. When I emailed him to try to appeal my grade, he never responded. I ended up having to get the department involved to get a reply, and his reply was condescending and curt. Don't take 270 with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gill is an intense guy that is very set in his ways. The class content was interesting, and he lectures well. I was lucky to be a student he liked, but I can't ignore his self-important attitude and rudeness to others. I am glad I took this class, but I would not take a class from him again. Also, as a DRS student he was not very accommodating.

Gill's class was entertaining but I recommend talking to your TAs and not him outside of class. He prefers male students and is self-important which is expected. The readings are fabulous but do NOT skip lecture, sections are fun, it is a full commitment money and time wise but it is worth it. This class will push you, know how to manage yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Gill is an amazing professor. His lectures are very interesting and provide a lot of information. There is a lot of reading, averaging about 100 pages a week, but the textbooks are all interesting. The content was so interesting, lectures and quiz sections are important for doing well. Tip: study the lists.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've had. Had him for 270 and it was fine because despite his extreme ego the class itself was interesting. In every personal interaction he has been incredibly rude and demeaning. I took him again for 307 and requested my blue book from my final, which he responded to by calling me functionally illiterate.

I took 307 with Gill and it's easily my favorite poli sci class at UW. Gill is a really great and engaging lecturer.  Definitely be prepared to read 100 pgs a week but his lectures summarize the important points really well. Also who on earth is spending money on the books required for this class??? Figure out how to get the books on the internet.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: All the reviews of this guy are mostly correct. He's got a rough exterior but really just is a nice guy underneath it all. Don't expect grace for simple mistakes. The quantity of reading was difficult to keep up with and forced me to skim instead of fully read and understand content.

Don't listen to any of the students' complaints about him, he's a great Professor. People complain he gives heavy readings and is a tough grader, why the heck are you going to university then, to play with your feet? You'll never become the best version of yourself if you don't take challenges. Uni is a great place to do that, so are his classes.

Took this class following his pols270 class and this was the most boring class ever. Has a thing for proper grammar but I read his book plus the books he recommends, its too wordy. you made your point 100 pgs ago. I read academic books in my own time. Restating points will occur. but alas political scientist are just HORRIBLE writers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Excessive use of textbooks (well over $100, his own textbook is used..) and LOTS of readings. Lectures are not recorded but 50% of the exam is based off of lectures, so do NOT recommend for any DRS students. I did well but it took EVERYTHING to get a 3.8, do not recommend for most people as it is very intense. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Rude and unhelpful. Made us read HIS poorly written book for class. Tests are not set up for student success.

He is by far the best lecturer I've had for a PoliSci class. He is able to keep the lectures interesting and entertaining throughout the whole course.
Reading requirements are ridiculous though 100+ pages a week.
Your grade is entirely dependent on how willing you are to buy the books (100$+) and how good you are at info dumping on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So hardddd! Need a lot of effort and a lot of exams to review, a lot of books to read.

A libertarian, and makes it clear via course material. He is pompous and rude, as others have stated. 
I was on good terms with him and received an A in the class, but that does not blind me to the fact that he openly embarrassed students like during the final, where he scolded someone for cheating on the essay loud enough so that we all heard.

Insane amounts of reading. Very very expensive. Do not take this class unless you want to read 150+ pages per week and spend well upwards of $100. So much effort. Interesting concepts and lectures though. Great TA's
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Yeah whatever the reviews arent wrong, hes pretty old-white-guy-who-thinks-hes-better-than-everyone-else but lectures were pretty good/important and readings (not hard to read) were a fair amount but usually worth it since he pulls smallish details from them sometimes for the test. Class isnt hard if you try, take good notes in lecture and readings

Condescending boomer who somehow manages to make simple concepts difficult to understand and doesn't seem to care much about the success of his students. Essentially told everyone that our votes “don't matter” without providing much nuance at all during election season. You would be best served taking other Poli Sci courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Gill is an engaging lecturer, though his high textbook requirements can be a burden. Using resources like unstuckstudy alongside the readings helps manage the workload. Overall, an interesting class if you can keep up.

My opinion of Gill was rather soured when I switched into the class late and he refused to be of any help. He's definitely a great lecturer, but he seems to care little about how student's actually do in the class and has a lot of boomer-esque attitudes. He's either very much your type of person, or not at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Condescending.

Funny professor with quite interesting lectures. Unfortunately the amount of books he requires in this class is just not reasonable at all. Never had a course in my 3 years at UW require this much, easily $100+. And most of the books are written by colleagues of his, so theres no doubt in my mind that they were chosen on purpose. Not for everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good lecturer & tests are clear. Lots of readings, but pretty interesting. Don't fall behind or you'll be screwed for finals week. This is my 2nd class with Gill, he is entertaining but the ego gets annoying. Graded by a midterm, final, essay, & section participation. Not a fan of the guy, but easy grader. questions are often lists from readings
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Gill is an extremely talented lecturer - he's organized, clear, and funny. This is my 2nd class with him, and both times he made seemingly "boring" topics interesting. He assigns a lot of readings, but all of them are good, relevant reads. He is very strict, but if you can follow directions you'll do well. He's a little offensive, I just ignored it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: My primary research focus is religion and politics. Despite waiting eagerly for this class, the professor's entertaining lectures are overshadowed by his tendency to humiliate students. He's a former nerd turned bully, likely compensating for insecurities, evident in his condescending demeanor and inflated ego.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I mean, you know what you're getting into. If you don't like his politics or his personality, take someone else. His lectures are superb, the content is fascinating, and his expectations are very clear. (Do the readings and be punctual.) He puts on quite a show in class, but I found him fairly personable one-on-one: the ego is mostly just an act.

Amazing lecturer but terrible with one-on-one. Lectures are engaging & he is very organized. On average, you will read 100 pgs weekly. 2nd half of the quarter, the readings get more difficult. Discussion attendance is mandatory (but they are for your benefit). Discussions talk a lot about readings. Not a full 5 because he is condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very condescending. The most amount of reading Ive ever had to do in a class, let alone he had us read many of his own or his colleague's works. The course work is super out of place with no structure to what he's teaching, just concept after concept. If you do all the readings and study terms, its alright.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Gill rambles a lot during his lectures about how he wants students to learn the concepts and not regurgitate useless information but then goes on to ask students to name specific keywords that he makes up on the exams. He doesn't give out lecture slides or a study guide and is somewhat standoffish when you ask for clarification on anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Very ramble-y lectures with lots of anecdotes because he tries to be funny, but covers very few actual concepts and everything is oversimplified. 
He is clearly a libertarian, and the bias shows through heavily in course material and readings. Ironically, he is also very paternalistic and dogmatic when it comes to course expectations.

Success in 307 after the midterm is entirely based on how many of his colleagues' books you can afford to buy. It is seriously an absurd amount of required books -- easily over $100 if you pay full price. Made me seriously resent the class. Otherwise, Gill is an amazing professor who conveys his love for his work in his lectures + class structure.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: 409: Gill brings a lot of enthusiasm to the material that makes his seminar entertaining. His course is well organized and you learn a lot. Be prepared to participate in class every day because that is a big part of the grade. Only a 4/5 because he can be very condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Gill knows what he is talking about and has clear instructions but his personality is probably the most difficult part of the class. You can get a good grade if you put in the work and his grading is pretty fair but be warned that he has a big ego and is very condescending.

Ignore the complaints about Prof. Gill; his grading scale is very lenient, expectations are clear, and he obviously enjoys teaching and tries to make "boring" topics fun. He's opinionated, but not intolerant as others claim. The class encourages you to think critically about religion--if you can't suspend your own biases, don't bother taking it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Gill really loves what he does and it shows in how he teaches his classes. As others have mentioned, he does have a massive chip on his shoulder and has very strong opinions. But if you can stomach his tangential lecture style, he seems to be a well-meaning professor that will meet you half-way. Give it your best and honest effort & you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Man, I'll never forget this class. I'm not sure about his other classes, but he teaches 270 masterfully. Super engaging and strong in his opinions, but always up for a discussion. The lectures always made me smile. Assignments were simple, fun, and the required reading was entertaining. Wish I could take again, highly recommend :).

Gill is definitely very knowledgable in his field but has VERY strict guidelines for students that can be unreasonable. His lectures are engaging as he integrates humor, but alternately his ego can make it feel like he’s just talking down at you. He’s not everyone’s cup of tea but the course as a whole was interesting, albeit VERY stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Oh wow I wish if I have made a better decision last year to avoid suffering from his class this much. I tried super hard and got a 80 on my last paper. There are points taken off for explanation not detailed enough oh what? You asked 3 questions in a row and wanted me to address all of them below 650 words? Expected me to define every single word

Taking his class is def my worst decision this year! If he ever checks this website, PLEASE! Put down your ego and listen to different worldviews! Stop being biased and seal yourself in that one outdated mind. Your paper prompts literally force me to answer in the way you like, but I am a human being who has my own thoughts.

Students need to pay a 5 points fee for any grade appealing lol, and he only returns you 3/5 even if you successfully appeal. If he rejects your appeal, you lose 5 points automatically. It is unbelievable and makes non sense to me. The most helpful advice is probably: he has a strong ego. Even if he is wrong, you better not to challenge him. ^^

I would say he is one of the worst professors at UW Pol S department. His arrogance makes me so uncomfortable lmao. He is biased and so crazy about economic concepts, in which he embeds economic mindset into his course policy.

speaks to his students like they are 12 He is demeaning and seems arrogant at times He says class is not mandatory but won't post slides during Covid, in which sick students should not be attending class. Full of himself and very biased; would only take if you want to hear his outdated viewpoints, not a multifaceted class!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hands down the best professor I have ever had. Wish I could take more classes with Gill. We are fortunate to have him here at UW. Every day is like an adventure coming to class, and you wont be let down. Very strict about deadlines and rubrics, but also reasonable with his assignments. You will NOT be disappointed!

Warning: Gill bans using laptops/tablets/smartphones for notetaking in his classrooms. I would not take his classes again solely because this rule. He does fantastic lectures but he is very strict. Be sure to read the syllabus and rubric carefully!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was absolutely amazing. I didn't get to know Gill personally, but his lectures were really interesting and engaging. The course content is super fun to learn because you are taught real life concepts. He is super funny and easy to understand, you can tell how passionate he is. I would take this class again and again!

Prof Gills 270 is one of the best classes Ive taken. Prof Gill is an amazing lecturer who knows how to make the material very interesting. He is very passionate about the material he teaches explains the material very clearly. It is a very writing-heavy class but deals with topics that are super interesting. Highly recommend.
Good prof. Love the hat.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Gill's class is an eye opener if you're interested in political science or religion. The lectures are engaging and Professor Gill is genuinely interesting and funny. The books you'll read in class are actually interesting to read and the text isn't dense or confusing. Read the content and watch the lectures and you will love this class.

the course was asynchronous which was nice and it was my second course with prof gill. He's a nice prof and knows a lot about what he does. There is a lot of work to do like weekly discussions/reading responses, and a paper in addition to the two exams. It can be tough if you don't fully understand the concepts but if you're interested I'd recommen
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This was my second class with Prof. Gill and I'm sad that I won't be able to take him again. He is probably the most passionate lecturer that I've ever had in college. Loves his subject and knows how to make it interesting for any student. He put so much effort into making his class engaging throughout the coronavirus shutdown, which paid off 100%.

Prof. Gill is probably the most passionate & innovative professor I've had to date. You can see how much he cares about his teaching through the way he describes concepts and connects assignments to real life. He's a great instructor for anyone new to economics. The course requires more thought than others but is worth taking.

Professor Gill is sweet and if you take his online classes, you can tell he really puts a lot of effort into his videos which I really appreciate. Sometimes, he explains it to you like a kid but personally, I don't mind and I like it. The concepts he teaches aren't too difficult, although the homework and exams aren't always straightforward.

Amazing online lecture setup, they're all prerecorded and the layout is very clear. Very interesting subjects and he knows what he's talking about. There are a lot of readings but you can get away with just skimming. About one assignment and a week but pretty short and easy if you watch lectures. need at least one discussion post a week, would rec.

Professor Gill is extremely knowledgable in his field. He will explain conceptual topics in ways that anyone can understand. As long as you put effort in and challenge any preconceived ideas you might have, you will do well in his class. Remember economics isnt for everyone. Professor Gills class is very market-based, which I actually love.

Probably the most interesting class I have ever attended. Prof Gill is a funny and interesting person, he made all his lectures damn crazy and fun to attend. All his lectures were recorded so don't miss out on any of them. All you need to do in this class is to be creative and punctual.
Never answered a question the entire quarter. You are just there to entertain his ego.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams are difficult he likes to put in a lot of things that were talked about briefly in lectures. Heavy readings and if you don't do them its going to be hard to pass, even if you do them it will be hard to pass. I had Christianna as a TA and she taught me more than Gill did make sure you get her for section its your only hope.

Professor Gill's lectures are the best I've ever attended and the amount of knowledge he's able to impart is really astounding. The class is reading heavy but all the readings are very interesting and he frequently incorporates his own research into the class as well. He's extremely funny, to the point, and makes content easy to grasp.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Gill is a firm believer in markets. He believes individual self interest will solve everything: the environment, organ donors, you name it. An intro Political Economy class should encompass all theories. Gill not only ignores Marx & Keynes theory,he outright dismisses them. The class should really be called "Intro to Classical Liberalism".
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: panopto and lecture slides were not uploaded and he required everyone to take handwritten notes. he gives a lot of real-life examples to help understand the concepts, which helped me learn the material much easier. very entertaining. more about understanding concepts and being able to explain them than memorization
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He supports price gouging and the privatization of natural resources. He completely ignores the fact that underprivileged people have been exploited at the hands of private property owners for centuries which has lead to the accumulation of wealth we see today. He speaks from a privileged perspective and will mock any student who challenges it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: There's a saying in the Poli sci circles ... you either love Gill or you hate Gill - and I freaking LOVE this man. He is HANDS DOWN my favorite professor in the department! The readings he assigns are phenomenal and he's a Solid lecturer. FYI he is a huge lockain along the lines of Hayek and mill - which is actually v beneficial to your learning

Enthusiastic, but the distance between this professor and his students is palpable. It seems he enjoys giving lectures but would prefer a different audience. He might have been a decent instructor 15-20 years ago, but he seems thoroughly checked out now. Course readings are underwhelming and expensive. Extremely lenient grading policy.
Very supportive, accommodating, and funny professor.
Gill is awesome. Lectures are fun, he is hilarious and you learn A LOT from going to class. Wish I could go back and take this class again!

I was really looking forward to this class (religion and politics, hello?), but Gill's teaching style ruined it. Attendance isn't mandatory, but he doesn't post his powerpoints online and goes through them super fast in class, tries to be funny but isn't, makes you buy his and his buddies' books for the class. + TA's don't really know how to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof. Gill's classes are always a treat, and this one was no exception. This seminar class featured excellent readings and incredibly strong discussion. By far one of the best classes I've ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: It's Gill. You already know who he is. 10/10

Prof. Gill gave a top-notch class, always with a new surprise around the corner. Lectures were entertaining and informative, and Prof. Gill challenged us to think critically and thoroughly. Lots of reading, but the books are pretty good, particularly Leeson's "The Invisible Hook". Prof. Gill makes you work hard, but it's 100% worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gill is funny and watching lectures are like watching a National Geographic documentary as in it is fascinating and educational. But there's a lot of essential reading plus the class doesn't actually cover politics like I hoped. But the class is irreplaceable in a way. Only a few people study this. Google economics of religion to test the waters.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you're looking to learn about politics get out while you can- this class is primarily econ. The professor is incredibly arrogant but lacks basic historical knowledge and teaching skills- his lectures only left me confused. He also has a hard time keeping his own political views out of the content, and often tried to pass off opinions for facts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Gill rants for a long time about scenarios that have no relation to the class. He uses outdated political economy examples that he has used for years. Not once has he tried to apply basic concepts to the present world, a time that is very interesting for political economy. His jokes are not funny either!
Took this class for early fall start. It was amazing and I would suggest incoming freshman take it! Not too difficult and very relevant to everyone's daily lives.

Gill is the best professor I've ever had, hands-down.  Definitely leans in a classically liberal direction along that of Hayek, which is unusual for UW.  Clearly distilled concepts with solid examples.  If you know the concepts from class and the readings, you shouldn't have too much trouble passing his tests.  Lectures are interesting and fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved this class! His lectures were engaging and he really cares about his students. It's difficult to study for exams if you don't read the books or attend lectures though.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Loved the class. Not so sure about Gill. My TA is really what is making it worth it for me. Doing the study guides is really what will get you a good grade. He makes zero effort to hide his political views, which is annoying, but it doesn't really impact his teaching. If you do the work, the class is not too bad though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Just took his EFS class and loved it.  Great professor with very straightforward tests.  Super interesting lecturer and he really cares about his topic.  Do the readings and pay attention in lectures and this class is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I had him for the EFS class, and he was great.  Its a lot of reading but the tests are straighforward- there are no surprises.  Not an easy class, but I wouldn't call it hard.  He's nice, funny, and understanding.  He is so interested in what he teaches and that makes him a great prof.  Just get ready to read, but his class is interesting.

Spends most of lecture making jokes about obscure things (Jack Black, Wood Carvings, Carnivals) and less time actually relating the stuff to political economy. Will give a clear definition and then spend 20 minutes going into a convoluted example that leaves you confused at the end of it. Incredibly biased!

He really cares about what he is teaching and whether or not the students understand it. He's a very engaging professor and highly recommend taking his class. He is also very helpful if you go to office hours.
Charismatic if unclear (at times), Anthony Gill makes a tough and relevant subject interesting and relocatable to students

Professor Gill is one of the best professors I have had at UW. The reading was reasonable, and he gives several examples of concepts through skits and creative explanations that are hard to forget. The test are very straight-forward as long as you go to class and section. Gill is very passionate about what he teaches.

Professor Gill is an amazing professor! His lectures are engaging, and he is very funny. Course material was interesting (connecting economics to religion). Quite a lot of reading, but with his reading guides he posts on Canvas, it is manageable. The midterm and final is very straightforward, and it is not out to get you. Overall, would recommend!

Prof Gill is really funny and kind of ridiculous. He is straightforward in lecture as long as you can figure out the relevance of his analogies. Easy weekly homework assignments and very straightforward midterm and final. Must do the reading! Tests are in class, written, and you need information directly from books and lecture.

One of the more unique classes I've taken, political economy 270 is either a love or hate class. Gill is an avid lecturer and his lecturesreadings are unique yet interesting at the same time.  Gill teaches from a very liberal point of view, if you agree with him you will enjoy this class. Pretty straightfoward tests with simple weekly assignments.
Best professor I've had at the UW, would definitely recommend! Lots of reading but you only need to understand the concepts and key points.
Professor Gill's classes are somewhere between stand-up comedy and a TED talk. Even if you disagree with his politics, he's a good professor and you'll still enjoy the class.

I liked Prof Gill's teaching style; he is super organized, clear, and his lectures are always entertaining. However, he is biased, and consequently, all of his materials are as well. He can be condescending, and makes it a point in his lectures (read: tangents). I differ from him politically, but still got a lot of value from his course.
Although a bit annoying, his lectures are very helpful and clearly lays out what is needed in order to do well

Always a lot of reading but, after taking 2 classes (307 and 280) from Gill, I would definitely recommend him to anyway. He always gives clear explanations with multiple examples. His tests are straight forward and he never tries to "trick" you. The large amount of reading is the only downfall but, most of the books are fairly interesting

I've taken 204, 270, and 307 with Gill, and 270 was my favorite. He's a great professor who is clear and makes great explanations and connections with the material. 307 is the most challenging, since the readings are a little more challenging than in 204 or 270. Overall, great professor - highly recommend taking a class from him!

Though he provides study guides, it's hard to take notes off of the readings and lectures. Both are hard to follow because of lame jokes and stories instead of concrete facts and explanations. Nothing is straight forward. If this class isn't required for your major, don't take it.

Prof. Gill obviously cared about the material and the amount that his students learned. However, he spent a lot of time going off on tangents and  examples rather than the actual material. The class  has a clear libertarian bias which seems to be taken too far at some points. With an average amount of work, you should have no problem doing well.

Gill is a very entertaining and fun professor. He makes his concepts interesting when they could easily be dry and chooses textbooks that are easy and genuinely a good read. He is also a lenient grader so there is a good chance you will end up with a pretty good grade if you put in the effort.
Definitely not my favorite professor. Demeaning in my opinion, and treats class like a 3rd grade level. Lots of people like him, but wasn't my style. Tries to hard to teach, and be a cowboy.

Very entertaining class and a great professor! A lot of reading is involved, but it's definitely worth it. I feel like I learned a lot from him and will be looking to take all of the other classes he offers. Class is NEVER boring with Gill.

Professor Gill was hand down amazing and entertaining!! :D Awesome and nice guy who really interacted with his students. Of course I had to study a bunch for tests but it was really interesting and I learned a lot in comparison to my science and math classes. The material sticks with you and he is so funny and has a great personality!

The amount of  reading and  information this professor expects students to know for exams is flat-out ridiculous. Don't take this if you're looking for a fun or easy class. The information presented is interesting but not worth the amount of effort required to do well in the class.
The class wasn't what I was expecting going in, but it was interesting and informative nonetheless. Gill is great at retaining student attention, and is very approachable.

Excellent professor. His lectures are always clear and easy to understand. He assigns a lot of reading, but nothing too overwhelming. His exams are reasonable and fair; not too hard, but you still need to attend lecture to get a good grasp on the content. He's really enthusiastic and also very funny! I highly recommend him!

Awesome prof! Randomly ended up in a poly sci class my freshman year due to my fig and Gill is awesome! Make sure you go to class, do the readings, and DISCUSS w/ classmates for the exams. He's an awesome guy and one of the best prof's I've ever had a UW. You do need to study for this class though!

I just finished up his 307 class this week and I learned a lot. Focuses primarily on Christianity, and has a small section on Islam. He brings interesting arguments to the table, but is so caught up in being a "rebel" that it's hard to take him seriously most of the time. He also LOVES white papyrus on black backgrounds...

Prof. Gill's lectures are almost always entertaining and make it easy to learn the material. He also uses a lot of games and small assignments that also help when thinking through the topics in this class.

Gill is the man.  Great teacher, energetic, fun to listen to, plus he wears a cowboy hat every day.  The tests aren't bad if you study and know your stuff. attendance is not mandatory but you will likely have a hard time catching up if you do not attend

Taken both 270 and 307, and I love both. Gill is an absolute riot, and he has a gift for teaching market economics with clarity. You will learn a lot, you will genuinely enjoy coming to lecture, and the tests are honestly not very hard. Even the readings (for 270) are fun, you will, like, want to pick up the book.

This professor is too caught up in trying to impress everyone and talk about how he is a member of the "intellectual" class to teach anything useful. I can't take hearing him talk about useless stuff all day, and his textbook is written straight out of a thesaurus, it's actually hilarious how hard this guy tries, but still sounds like a tool.

Absolutely the worst class and professor I've had so far. this was taught less like a pol s class, more like a history class. Impossible to know what the exams would look like. Lectures were boring, too long, and he would often go off on bitter rants about grad school, his personal life, or the past. Absolutely awful professor, avoid him!

I took this course online, and it was so clear and rather easy. There are weekly assignments, but they're not hard at all. Didn't read any of the textbooks all quarter, didn't need to. He makes a dry subject fun, and you'll get used to his unique humor.

I have now taken all three of Gills classes. Religion 307 was the most challenging, although I truly enjoyed it. The concepts are not far-fetched, or offensive. The term paper is graded harder than I think was necessary, but the tests are straight forward and not too challenging. I would recommend this class!

Gill continues to be one of my favorite professors at the University of Washington. This course was challenging at times, but Gill drills the concepts so you cannot forget them. Some people do not like his sarcasm, I though found it entertaining. The course is a little book heavy, but with attending the lectures and QS you will do great!

I've taken his 270, 307, and 204 classes and got a 4.0, 3.9, and 3.9 respectively. My favorite professor at UW. It's easy to do well if you attend lecture. I barely did any reading because he or the TA reviews the basics of each book. He's very enthusiastic and a hard-core libertarian - made me reconsider my liberal assumptions.

i had missed some of other classes in my uw life so far however i never missed any single lecture of his! he is just so enthusiastic! (even though he's very biased which made me feel offensive) i love all the materials he covered during the quarter! highly recommend his class! :)

One of the best professors I've ever had. He drills topics into your brain and it is very clear what to watch for on the tests. Speaking of tests, they are the most direct and straightforward you could imagine. Use the study guides and go to lecture and you'll do great

Lectures are interesting almost always  (assuming you like POL S). His ppt slides include tons of pictures and ppt transition. But during the later half of the quarter he started to seem...shall I say..a bit arrogant. Albeit he got a PhD so he could rightfully be, but a wee bit more modesty will gain him some respect from the more serious students.

I switched into Gills Comparative Politics class after the quarter began. I am so glad I did. Gill is intelligent, witty, entertaining, and is able to teach a large load of material without it being overwhelming. Attendance is a must in quiz section, and there is a lot of reading involved. I would recommend this class to all UW students!!!
Very funny and original, knows how to make fun of history and keep things entertaining.  I would definitely recommend him.

Gill goes out of his way to keep the class interesting and entertaining. He also enjoys playing music before and after class and has a very great selection (Queen anyone?!). This class is interesting and I highly recommend this professor!

Useful class that compares federalism vs. centralism, presidentialism vs. parliamentarism, and plurality vs. PR electoral systems. Also focuses on developmental paths of Britain, Germany, Russia, and others. Interesting guy for sure!

Gill is nice, funny, helpful and responds emails instantenously. He ties in all of the major concepts together so his students can see a bigger picture/pattern of development. I wont be taking RELIG POL bcuz it focus too much on Christianity, but it looks like a decent class. Prof knows a lot, and I learned a lot in his class. Gill, you're hired!:)

Prof. Gill is a great teacher, i highly recommend going to the lectures since that's where a lot of the test questions come from. He also drops hints and gives bonus question answers during lecture. He also is engaging and you can tell he is very passionate about teaching.

Gill is super nice/funny... content is weak. Don't take this class if you have any interest in Religion and World Politics. Contrary to the title, this is a course on Christianity (through the reductionist lens of Rational Choice) and Western (specifically U.S. and Western European) politics from an upper-class-white-evangelical-male persepctive.
Interesting lectures.  Likes to talk a lot about his books sometimes.  Circles in lecture sometimes but overall a good professor and fun to listen to.

Best prof I have had at UW and I am a junior now.  Extremely intelligent.  He is more than happy to accommodate students outside the classroom if they have an extended interest.  Yes, he is conservative.  I am liberal.  But debating/learning from him has broadened my horizons.  It's a silly reason to think less of a professor (or anyone). A++++++++

The class is essentially review for anyone who is knowledgeable about economics. His lectures are entertaining, but also sort of childish. The exams were not hard but you do have to go to class and read all the material. Gill basically takes examples straight from the lecture and the readings and puts them on the exam. Lecture notes are NOT online.

Interesting guy.  Unapologetically loud and abrasive but honest silly and self depricating enough to be tolerable.  Very easy class, but if you're interested in the topic gill provides a lot of outside input.  Lectures are entertaining if childish. Look through the website for useful content. Online test review guides are very comprehensive.

He's an okay professor though perhaps a tad overrated by poli sci students. I feel like the act gets a little tiresome but he is genuinely smart and has some great advice and information on his website

This is a professor for anyone who wants a laughably easy intro poli sci class. He teaches it as if you were in middle school, and doesn't hide his conservative biases very well (just look at the book he uses). He tries to make up for this by being cute and funny, which works for some but I felt like it was a huge waste of my time.

Funny. Creative. Enthusiatic. Engaging. Clear. His exams come from the textbooks, packets, and his lectures. He has REALLY COOL powerpoint slides for all the lectures but doesn't post 'em on his site so attending his lectures is a GOOD IDEA (otherwise you might be losing those IMPORTANT lecture-related question points on exam)!
Found him very interesting and engaging.  He made it clear in lecture what he thought was important.  I enjoyed the class a lot.
He's the whole package: brilliance, entertainment, helpfulness, clarity, and he looks like a cowboy!

Not the best of the best, but I get the impression that he is up there. He's kind of entertaining, but his antics become somewhat old and tiresome, especially involving an immaturely done final that really did make me mad. Overall I learned a lot about a variety of countries. I put in a solid effort and got a 3.4
Very grasping and entertaining lectures!
not what i expected in a poly econ class but i learned a lot more than i expectd to.  i had this class two years ago and i still keep usng it in my other classes and talking with friends and family
One of the best profs I've ever had!
great prof!
this guy simply kicks ass he is easy and I learned a lot in class if you get him be glad.

Always surprising, always funny, always prepared with powerpoint presentations (which he's prone to sneak in pictures of his son).  Great guy, brilliant orator, really knows his subject--just because he looks like an extra in 'Blazing Saddles' does not mean he's a dumb redneck.  His lectures were the best I've ever taken at UW.

Don't let Gill's cowboy suit fool you. He is a highly intelligent teacher (Albiet way too conservative) who puts forth the concepts of his class in a highly engaging way that makes you learn. His testing style is easy as you get questions in advance. However, his TA grading is based on a chart that makes it really difficult.

Gill is an interesting person. Though, I feel like I am being taught political economics from some guy that has never been off the farm. He is arrogant, his lectures are boring contentless. He does not teach differing views of political economics only his own. For an education avoid him like the plague. If you like attention ****s he's your man.

His the best teacher. He just made me more intrested in pol sc. he totally knows his job. i have not met  any professor better then him.  Hahah his story about his son is always entertaining..... .   Way to go Professor Gail.... ***big smile***

Great Prof! Kept his own political tastes out of an atmosphere where it easy to get off track and lost. Well thought out arguments, well explained, and alot of fun to have class with! Great class/ professor.
Classes are the highlight of my day, but I tried a few TA's and they all suck this year
My organs are bouys floating on a sea of gin
No Comments

Loves to make people laugh during his lectures.   He is very engaging and cares about the attentiveness of his students a lot.  Gives out prizes just for fun every now and then.  Learn about his little son, so yea definitely recomend him.
One of my favorite professors I have ever had, even though he was a little more conservative than I am.
Poli Sci as a Social Sci - great class! Funny, smart, engaging prof.  Highly recommend!

hardly ever went to class (too early) but he is very enthusiastic and passionate about what he teaches.. his lectures are very clear with fun powerpoint presentations. however he doesn't post his powerpoints, so if you must, attend class and you should get
Great teacher.  Perhaps the only un-biased prof. at UW?
This guy is a bad ass mother fffffffff
No Comments
I LOVE THIS TEACHER!  He began every class with funky music, his lectures were always hilarious, and he gives away prizes to students AT LEAST once a week.  AWESOME TEACHER!!!!
Freakin awesome class!
Most entertaining class I've ever taken.  He blasts music related to the topic, pretends to be a crazy cookie monster, and wears cowboy boots that look about three sizes too small.  What a stud!
I had him for POL S 204 and just had to take another class with him. Absolutely approachable  and the lectures are never boring. Love the daily cowboy hat he wears.
tests and quizzes hard. papers are subjective to his TA, seek help and he'll provide it. funny, good man, weekly assignments seem tedious but turn out to be helpful. pay attention and do the work.
The best teacher I had in college. Slightly irreverant, he makes the class fun *and* interesting.
Very good and organized lectures.  Puts a lot of effort into class and cares about his students!
Very funny, Class sucked though, but not his fault.  it was a stats class when it should have been a polisci class
No Comments
Drives in the carpool lane even though he's a single driver... What a bad man!
Awesome prof, wants students to learn, sense of humor is a must

Very cool dude, his lectures are very interactive and directly correlate with the work we have to turn in. He is very flexible with grading due to the extra credit assignments. No complaints here, definitely recommend taking his class.

Professor Groening himself is a great guy. He's super funny, very well spoken and knowledgeable. He can appear a little intimidating at first, but he's easy to reach out to or talk to during class. Just be aware that the class may be very different from what you expect, it's more of a commentary on society and technology than a study of film.
Professors teaching style is fairly up to date, and I'm sure most people who decided to take his class in the pass would feel the same way.

Just the sickest guy ever. Incredibly smart and he really cares about his area of expertise. If you pay attention to lectures and care about film/
TV you will love this class. He can be a little intimidating, but the best way to approach him is to just be yourself and be honest

Steve is kind of a firecracker, really knowledgable, will change the way you think about media. Appreciated the amount of time dedicated to feminist theory. Great variety of viewings. Class discussions are kind of a drag, but if u can get thru those, you can get thru anything. Recommend to anyone with an interest in television and cultural history!

Interesting guy with engaging classes. We had to do two discussion posts a week on assigned readings (these really added up) and it could be a bit overwhelming. He's pretty strict; no late work allowed and tech not permitted in class. He's happy to help with essays and ideas, quiz every class gave me a reason to be there.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Assignments were straight forward: in-class quizes, group discussions, written summaries every few weeks. Class itself was very interesting, really makes you think about media in a way you wouldn't think of. Stephen himself is a very interesting and smart professor, lectures and discussions are intellectually stimulating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Lectures would have been more interesting if I were passionate abt tv history. Chosen shows/episodes and readings/comprehension questions were doable and relevant. Small group discussions were painfully long but skipping brought grade down. Prof was knowledgable but strict about specifics (i.e. handwritten notes only). I enjoyed the final paper.

I liked the topic but not the way Steve ran the course
He is easy though
3/10

Nice and funny prof who is very passionate about TV studies. CMS 273 was quite easy, with most of the grade coming from 4 open note exams that are not difficult if you attend lecture. Readings can be difficult sometimes. Course content was OK, with lots of lecture on TV history and concepts without enough analysis of actual prestige TV shows.

Hilarious professor that knows his material. I learned a lot in this class that I find to be relevant today. Class-wise, we spent the first half of class on lecture, and the last half was spent on group discussion. There were no essays, just heavy readings for every class (20-50 pages), and group discussions. Attendance mandatory, no recordings.

Professor Groening is a sophisticated and well researched. Sometimes can be a bit challenging but that is exactly the point. If you are not willing to think critically and challenge yourself a bit then his courses may not be the ones for you. I've taken him twice and have enjoyed his lectures. Funny charisma as well, kudos to the prof.

God I love this man. Lectures are engaging, funny, and he always makes sure students fully understand the often difficult reading material in homework. Those who have difficulty with this class are those who don't do the homework, slack off on critical summaries, and then show up and are *shockingly* confused. Definitely get out what you put in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do not take a class with prof Groening, unless you're a CMS major. Just don't, lectured are boring, concepts are confusing, 274 is not what you think it is, this is a warning to all people at UW who just need their a&h credit, find another class!

Definitely not an easy A. He is a tough grader but he is very good at what he does. Very knowledgeable. It sucks that he doesn't record lectures so you have to be there every day. But the amount of work is reasonable and doesn't feel like busywork. He is a chill prof and overall very reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Steve is a super fun guy, he can go off on tangents which makes class long, but he is clearly very passionate about his work and students which shows. A large portion of this class is small group discussions so it is important to be there live. Definitely a fun class with interesting content, and a very achievable A.

Honestly one of the best CMS classes Ive taken. It was a good change of pace from watching films. Professor Groening provides a great catalog of television shows to view and discuss throughout the quarter. Theres a lot of dense reading so prepare to close read the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This is a early fall start course with 5 credits, named "How to Be a Person". Prof Steve is fantastic. It requires a lot of thinking and reading, but worth it. He is well-known and reasonable. It is so nice to take his course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: People asked me about online classes and what profs were best/worst from spring so I am putting Groening down for a no-take. even if you love a movie class, this guy is so boring and tells you 0 new and is useless on-line. In-person he was a little better but seeking him out is a joke that is not funny. He goes on + on in a monotone voice.

Really good lecturer and he clearly knows his stuff. The reading material is really dense so if you want an easy VLPA this is not the class. That being said, he goes over it in lecture and is available to answer any questions. I would only take the class if you are truly interested in the topic, but he makes that clear at the start of the quarter.

Steve is super entertaining and funny. His lectures are pretty wordy, but they are super helpful in helping you understand the concepts. There was a LOT of reading of essays and lots of writing. And hes a pretty tough grader, so be prepared!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Really interesting professor who is very knowledgable! Reading before each class and watching some shows. Easy discussions in class and he's really open to a lot of ideas!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Thinks he is funny but I dont really see it beyond it being forced. You cannot use your phone nor laptop which makes it difficult to take notes especially when it gets dark outside. Lots of reading and discussion questions. Not hard, just tedious, just go to class, take the quiz on the movie and leave otherwise be bored for 2 hours. 3 Papers total
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Steve is an awesome instructor. He's really knowledgeable, and can explain things clearly and pretty concisely. Also really helpful when you get stuck on something. His humorous style makes lecture extra engaging. Be aware the course isn't an 'easy VLPA,' but it is really informative, and gives you a good grasp on fundamental concepts in TV.

Stephen is a funny and engaging lecturer. The class pays relatively good attention. The problem is that his grading is very arbitrary. You will never be given full credit on one of the 4 essays you have to write. Nor will you get helpful feedback. If you take this course, do the readings and you may be fine, but I would look to an easier vlpa.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: if you're like me & love media/television studies, then I highly recommend steph's classes. i love his readings and no courses have been more valuable to me & my personal educational experiences than the two i took with him. BUT he can be really rude, is a petty & nonsensical grader, & actual in-class work often feels dull & unnecessarily dense.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This was the best class I've ever taken. The readings are difficult but Steve goes over them in lecture and answers any questions to help clarify. He is also is really funny and approachable. He gives good feedback on assignments. Be prepared to put effort in if you want to do well. Highly recommend this professor.
Steve is the best instructor I've ever had. He is funny and keeps the class interesting. Would definitely take another one of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Steve is a good teacher. However, the grading scale is tough. 4.0 is for 99-100 based on 100 points. Also, there's a lot of HW and the reading is kind a trick. But he is a really nice professor and approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I took the class "How to be a Person" for early fall start and it totally made me excited to be in college! Professor is kind and entertaining, and the class was interesting and engaging. There was a LOT of reading involved, but a lot of it was from novels (so a lot more entertaining than textbook readings).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I took his Early Fall Start class, How to be a Person, and it was awesome!! There's a lot of reading but he's good about covering interesting topics and mixing up the class routine
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The in-class material was very interesting, but Professor Groening made me dislike the class. His system of grading is not very fair for the amount of work we were expected to do.  I should have dropped the class as soon as he said that he never gives full points because grades don't matter. Also, the readings are extremely long and dull.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: very nice and helpful professor. gives practice tests every week graded for effort and helpful for studying. scantrons and exit tickets done in class so attendance is mandatory. tests are hard but there are a lot of office hours and tas are helpful

took autumn 2025, apparently was the worst qtr to take. exams did not match lectures and grade was HEAVILY based on group participation. prof jordt was very nice but not very fair while grading (whole class fell below curve and made us take another exam instead of curving). i guess dont take in autumn...

- Assigned graded group work
- Exams unlike practice (2nd exam was barely related to lecture material)
- Lots of office hours
- Class time spent doing graded scratch sheets and exit tickets with your group

yes she's nice but I don't know what she did this quarter because these exams have been pretty unrepresentative of the practice material. Honestly really difficult. The average was lower than normal for exam 2 so she had us take a second group exam to recoup points. Unsure if she changed something this quarter or if it has always been like this.

Prof. is very nice, but has made changes to the class recently that have made it worse. One of our exams had a significantly low average (with a perfect bell curve) and instead of adjusting this, made us take ANOTHER exam to get points back (unfair because you had to get 100% to have a proportional grade bump). Old grading system was better!!!

There is a pretty big difference between how the course is structured from a few years ago vs. now so don't based your expectations off of reviews from 2023. There is NO LONGER A CURVE and the gpa scale is harsh (I have an 83% -> 2.8 I have never had a grade this low at UW). Exams are NOT like the practice and she does like trick problems.

Going to be the voice of dissent here—Hannah is very approachable and nice, but she is extremely out of touch with her exams and they were in no way fair. The second exam was NOTHING like the practice problems and set us up for failure. Also, you are doing group work every class and on an exam too, so good luck if you don't have a good group.
best genome teacher

Love Prof. Jordt!! Super sweet and cares about her lectures + students, really makes sure you're getting the concepts. Gives a lot of practise material, and exams are pretty similar. Lots of group work w/ your quiz section though. Lots of chances to boost your grade w/ small assignments too.
Excellent professor with an emphasis on making learning as easy as possible

Professor Jordt was one of my favorite professors ever. Her lectures are super clear, thorough, and it is clear that she cares for students to succeed. She provides evidence-based research on the learning methods that best help students, and I recommend going to her office hours to truly do well in the class.

I loved Prof. Jordt and her teaching style. For this class poll everywhere was implemented and graded. You needed to attend class, but she made it worthwhile. There's a group cumulative final at the end which is really short and now worth much of your grade. The exams are tough, but if you attend class, you'll do fine.

Dr. Jordt is an AMAZING professor! One of the things I loved most about her class was that she would present relevant research studies and discuss common misconceptions related to genetics. The tests are quite difficult, but I found going to her office hours was most helpful in improving my grade over the quarter!

Professor Jordt is SO sweet. She's really into pedagogy (teaching theory) and it shows, she's great at teaching! Exams are pretty difficult but fair, just make sure to do the practice given. Lecture/section attendance is mandatory (they're both very useful though). She cares a LOT about her students and is always willing to help. Take 361 with her!

I absolutely adore her! She's great at explaining contents and her lectures are really helpful. She also gives fairly constructed exams that resemble her practice problems. As long as you pay attention in class and do the practice you should receive a decent grade. She also cares about her students. I highly recommend taking Genome 361 with her!

I took genome 361 with Hannah online during spring quarter 2021, and she was a TA for that class. She was super clear in explaining concepts and made a pretty difficult class more manageable. I made sure to show up to her quiz sections every week to get more help outside of lectures.
Lectures weren't bad. She contradicted herself a lot during lectures and wasn't very good at explaining answers to students. Grading curves are so high it's hard to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Such an amazing professor for GENOME 361!

One of the best lecturers out there especially with all the new difficult genetics concepts. Prof Hannah definitely knows what shes talking about and is always providing alternative ways to help you understand material. Shes very caring and helpful during office hours and wants to help you succeed too! Put in the effort and you'll do great! GL!

I took this class online over the summer and loved it. Lectures were so clear and informative, tests are straight to the point, and homework is useful in test prep. I received quick replies to all my emails and she was beyond helpful. You can tell she cares and I highly recommend her classes!

absolutely wondeful lecturer. the grading system was odd and and unclear, but the assignments were interersting and engaging. very knowledgeable about the topic and created the systems we used. lots of good insight into effective design + communication.

Wonderful lectures and course content as a whole are super useful for research, projects, and general data literacy. Assignments' grading is pretty hard and unclear, but you are practically guaranteed above a 3.5 if you put in just a little effort. No exams either!

Grading system is weird. You never start with the full points on an assignment and you have to "earn them back" through very clear extra effort on assignments. On the final project you start with 30/35 points (~86%) and have to go out of your way to earn the other 5. Content is interesting otherwise.

Great professor!
Neat schedule, but annoying/overwhelming to see so many not-really-required "required" readings
Tips
- Didn't realize there was a Textbook
- The Notebook is a different, interactive & free book.
- Lots of "required" reading, but if you focus on the assignments & in-class-practices (with some Notebook review) then you can ignore.

What a gem. Jeffrey is one of the best profs in the CS department. He is funny, knowledgeable, and very approachable. Clearly knows his subject matter, and one of the best at Data Visualization. Makes the class fun, approachable, and easy for people of all skill levels in the domain. Highly recomemnd you take his class, you won't regret it.
Absolutely loved her passion. She was a pleasure to have as a professor and she made sure you understood the material.

Honestly, she was a fine professor. This class was just an insane amount of busy work and the Canvas was horribly organized. And anytime I asked for help or feedback from the TAs I was only given vague responses that were almost never helpful. Her teaching style was fine. And I value the material covered, I just wish it was better organized.
Do not choose Graves

Jenny was a wonderful professor; her lectures always made the concepts easy to understand. She's very kind and helpful as well. Do every extra credit opportunity that's offered; they are so plentiful and you can easily get an A in this class with them. This class was very valuable and I intend to continue using what I learned in my future :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Class was hybrid and met once a week on zoom besides one in-person class. She was always super enthusiastic with lectures and a great presenter. She's also super accessible outside of class and gives lots of opportunities for either EC or earning missed participation points.

Such a W teacher she actually cares about her students and has always been respectful. So many extra credit opportunities that it would be hard to not get a 4.0 😂

 class itself is pretty meaningful if you don't know too much about finances.

This is my first time taking a business minor class and she made this class so engaging to where people who don't have a business/math background can truly understand the content. Retakes on quizzes are available until you get a passing grade. Tests/quizzes are open note and if you just study the material, you should pass. Very helpful and caring.

In my opinion, FIN 205 is a must-take class for all UW students, while it isn't the easiest class you learn A LOT of extremely useful information about managing your money. Jennifer is a really amazing professor who makes this class a lot more engaging than most other online classes I've taken. Please take FIN 205 you won't regret it I promise!!
Really kind professor who is also very knowledgeable. Her class wasn't too hard but did heavily rely on tests to make up your grade, so make sure to study well for those.
Extremely difficult

She jam packed all the materials for this class, which made us super difficult to track. The exams were horribly structured and the questions she assigned did not align well with the amount of time given to take the exam. The wording was super confusing and disorienting. Overall this entire class and the way it was structured was disorganized.

Jennifer is by far one of the best professors in Foster. She genuinely cares about her students, and her canvas is very well organized. Her homework/tests are difficult, but she gives you everything you need to succeed. TAKE HER CLASSES!

Jenny is really sweet, would highly recommend taking her class. Her lectures were half content, and half practice questions. It is a very math heavy/problem solving class, and she allows a cheat sheet for exams, but the tests are still pretty difficult, so I would suggest reviewing the practice problems she does in class!

She is very kind and caring. Her lectures and assignments are easy to follow along with. She doesn't force people to participate in discussions and allows cheat sheets for the exams. She is also very understanding and will provide extra help for your homework. I really enjoyed her class and almost switched my major to optmgt bc of her. TAKE HER!!!

Really nice professor who clearly cares about her students. It is evident that professor Graves is extremely knowledgable in her field. The content was easy and the lectures were informative and entertaining. Her slides, practice problem walkthroughs, and the diagrams she makes are super helpful. Cheat sheets allowed for tests which is nice.
Super student oriented and involved lecture. If anything content is too easy as you get massive cheat sheet on midterm and final
Great professor
best professor ive had in a while. teaching style extremely easy to follow and does not use overly complex words.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One of the best professors at UW. loved her class and the overall knowledge I gained. The class is challenging but she is passionate about her students learning the material and it shows. very much a slay

Professor Graves makes her lecture extremely practical and interesting. She cares about students and is always very responsive. As long as you attend class or watch recorded lecture and do hw, getting an A or A+ is easy.

Jenny is one of the best professors I have ever had. Her lectures are always super engaging and she ensures the class understands the content before moving on. Somehow I looked forward to an 8:30 class because of her lovely energy. Her professional background is also super cool. Of all my Foster professors she is a top three.

Jenny is a great professor. She is extremely nice and caring and makes lectures very entertaining for the subject matter. No textbook and all of the class material is very easy to follow. Her class is a little too easy for a Foster class which causes the median to be very high (92% for our class), so if you want a 4.0, you have to be near perfect.

Jenny was always super sweet and positive. Very willing to answer questions and let us use a page of printed/handwritten notes for exams. The content was a little challenging at times, so make sure to create connections with other students in the class for hw help. Exams were pretty similar to the lectures and hw, along with online canvas quizzes.

Professor Graves is amazing. The material can be complex at times but she always double checks to make sure everyone is caught up. There wasnt a single lecture wherein she wasnt super energetic. Its clear she enjoys teaching. Also shes kind of funny.

Fun, engaging, and optimistic in her pre-recorded lectures. Exams were harder than I thought they would be and you have to do practice problems from live lectures to do well. A background in Excel helps. I learned a lot about investing and building good budgeting habits. She was very approachable and wanted to help students succeed.

She's seriously one of the most caring professors I've come across at UW. She goes above and beyond to make sure students understand the content. The exams are very similar to the problem sets she assigned to us and she allowed us to use a double-sided piece of paper for notes.

We did not use any textbook but the PS and exams were relatively straightforward -- nearly everything you need to succeed in this class could be found in the lecture slides -- and the lectures were delivered in an elaborate and logical manner. Jenny is also a really caring professor as she would stay after lectures answering questions.

You're sent into tests and homework assignments blindly. Lectures are completely useless for quizzes and homework assignments. She prepares you for failure. Extremely disorganized and lacks depth. The textbook is completely irrelevant when doing homework assignments. Take another professor if you can.

The lectures can be pretty helpful but aren't the best when it comes to homework or tests. She doesn't really help answer questions you have either. I would feel confident in a test or assignment then I'd be graded below the median again and again. Chegg will be your friend for the homework and quizzes

Jenny is hands down the best professor I've had at Foster. She is so caring and kind, and incredibly knowledgable about operations, consulting, finance, and other key business topics. Canvas was extremely organized and assignment rubrics were very clear and fair. If you're going to take OPMGT take it with Jenny.

She is absolutely fantastic. Her financial literacy class is easy credit, sure, but it will legitimately increase your financial knowledge, even if you thought you were smart before. Most of all, you can tell she really cares for her students. It was one of the few classes I've ever been excited to attend in the morning. Thank you Jenny!

I thought the class was great and Professor Haddad-Fonda made the lectures very interesting. As a stem major, I was a little worried about taking a history class, but I felt that the class was extremely manageable and enjoyable.

Incredibly knowledgeable and gave the most engaging and fascinating lectures I've had. Tells funny history anecdotes and seemingly has an answer to every question. Don't be intimidated by his intellect, he is quite easy to talk to in office hours. Class is very manageable if you keep up with readings and take notes. Challenges you to think hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Haddad-Fonda is very knowledgeable and gives great, interesting lectures. He cares a lot about his students too, and is very accessible outside of class.

Lots of reading in the Decolonization class, was easy to fall behind. But Kyle's source choices are really varied and provided a great overview of many difference parts of French and British decolonization. Mostly discussions during class and reading outside, plus a couple open-ended essays. Would take again

AWESOME history professor. His lectures are very engaging. He is so knowledgeable and passionate about his subject, and I learned so much here. Essays aren't unreasonably difficult, if you know how to write. Do your readings, show up to class, don't be a bum. Take this class if you want to learn, not get an easy grade because he's one of the best.

LOTS of reading. Easy to get discouraged if you don't say the "right" answer when raising your hand to speak. Graded by a few assignments and because he is obviously an intelligent man, he has high expectations that are difficult to meet.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures and course material are amazing but good luck getting clear answers on expectations and rubric. Weighting is so heavy on certain things that there is no going back from one mistake. He seems to grade you a lot based on how interesting he finds you or your topic choice, rather than quality. Can be very hard to talk to, as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Haddad-Fonda is the most amazing history professor at the UW (Ive had him twice now). His class is extremely straight forward and all his classes follow the same structure. If you go to lecture and do the assigned readings (for this class, there were also pre-recorded lectures), its almost impossible to get lower than an A. Just study lol
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I was really excited for this class because of its course material! In fact, the lectures were actually pretty interesting- but man was I disappointed by the grading... Graded super harsh, and left no explanations as to why... Could be a TA issue but it's honestly a shame because I genuinely did enjoy lecture but the grading just ruined it for me.
He's very difficult to talk to and isn't very helpful when trying to get assistance on papers

I didn't dislike him, but I felt he could be rather pretentious at times. I would say he is my least favorite history professor I've taken in my college career. He isn't terrible and I did enjoy his class to a degree, but each time I spoke to him I felt discouraged afterwards, even for small things.

I am not a history student. I was nervous taking a 300-level history class, but Haddad-Fonda was amazing. There were a lot of readings, but you really just needed to listen in class (great lectures). The class presented a fair challenge. I missed a few classes, he was extremely helpful in ensuring I caught up. By far one of my favorite UW classes!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Fonda's lectures are hilarious and really informative. There's a lot of reading required for this class but I found that the notes I made in class were better to study from that the actual textbook readings.
