Honestly, while I would take him as a professor again, I wouldn't want to take this class because it is definitely too much work.

Not sure which class some of these commenters took. Dr. Fonda is a clear lecturer and all the class info is very well organized on the course website. He is helpful and approachable. The class is challenging (300 level history) with lots of reading and info to keep track of but grading is not unfair or arbitrary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Haddad-Fonda is an excellent, humorous professor.  To be fair, most of the sources are easy to read. His grading, so far, I believe is not really harsh. I saw some comments exhibiting negative opinions on his email sent after every exam and assignment; however, I would argue that what he mentioned in his comment is indeed correct and thoughtful

His lectures are very interesting and engaging, but the level of detail and knowledge you need on papers to get a decent grade is insanely high. The expectations for grading and writing papers are not clear, and the amount of work I had to put in outside class was not proportional to the amount of credits I'm earning. Extremely difficult class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Really difficult to work with as a professor. The lectures are great but he doesn't communicate expectations well at all and even if you follow his advice you'll get points deducted for not having an interesting enough topic. He's very elusive with answers to questions bc he doesn't actually want to help, he expects you to anticipate his meaning.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are interesting but the grading is questionable at best. There's an extreme degree of nit-picking and very subjective. If he doesn't like your topic or if he doesn't find it interesting you'll get points deducted. He sent an email to the class telling us our midterm essays were mediocre. It's a miserable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You need to be able to remember everything in the assigned reading and everything he says in class, I do mean EVERYTHING. I got 40 pts off for getting the date of an event wrong. He acts cool and chill in lecture and office hours but for a 300 level class with no prereqs this course is a GPA killer. Take at your own risk.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No meaningful grades until week 9 so I didn't realize how harsh he was going to be until it was too late. Save yourself the stress and take something else because this class simply isn't worth it.

Nebulous and arbitrary with expectations, doesn't provide feedback on quizzes. Assignments are graded harshly, must maintain detailed memory of lectures and reading material, come to class an expert on topics. Final is a cumulative Blue Book exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Says a lot and nothing at the same time, communication is a game and you must be able to read between the lines and anticipate his meaning. Gave great feedback on the overall structure and content of my essay but docked points for using contractions. He's a perfectionist with an ever-moving goalpost. Course needs prereqs.

Memorization of names, dates, and places critical. Must maintain strong connection to the assigned reading and lecture material. Must meet with him regularly and get his input to make higher than a C on papers. Final is a three part blue book exam containing three analytical essays. He expects high levels of dedication to his coursework.

lectures are great, but this is centered around an incredibly high level audience. Don't take this for credit- Eight assignments total, will assign papers worth 30% of your grade & grades aggressively.  Prof turns what is a very interesting period in history into a jumbled mess that requires lots of previous understanding. Needs prereqs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There's not many assignments but they're really intense. If you're taking it for the credit, I would recommend a different course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's an incredibly tough grader and will deduct 20pts for seeminly small things. I heard great things from people who had taken the class a couple years ago but I'm having a wildly different experience. This would be a great course for Cold War enthusiasts with mind reading powers and a photographic memory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: KHF is a very engaging lecturer, and he does a good job of fostering discussion in a class of 80. The workload is reasonable (three short essays, a few quizzes, and an in-class final) and grading is fair. Takes a real interest in his students.

Bad lectures, hard to follow, answered questions poorly, and with the lack of interaction from the class it was clear a very small portion was finding lectures useful. Rely on readings to teach you, I would recommend a good background in North African history, he wanted you to basically know everything before you come to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was interesting and he is clearly very thoughtful and knowledgeable about the subject. He did expect a high level of understanding and engagement from students which could be intimidating at times but he is always available to answer questions and offer advice. I would highly recommend office hours he is a great prof to connect with!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was challenging because prof Fonda assumed students already understood world history, with no foundation. Yes it's a HSTCMP class, but it focused much more on southeast Asia than any other region involved in the Cold War, so come prepared and you may have to do extra work to catch up.  However, he's hilarious and cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were all over the place. Does not use outlines, instead he just talks and goes on tangents for the whole class. Was one of the worst classes I have ever taken at UW.

Professor Haddad-Fonda is incredibly knowledgeable. His lectures are very interesting, long but never boring and pretty fun. This class is very lecture oriented so you have to have good note taking skills for sure, attendance not necessary but very helpful to attend all classes if possible. This class challenged me but I really appreciated it.

Professor Haddad-Fonda is the perfect professor for students outside of the history major if they want to take a history class. He is clearly an expert in the subject he teaches, provides hilarious relevant anecdotes, and is very available outside of class. He always gives students the benefit of the doubt. A+ professor. Wouldn't change a thing.

Professor Fonda actually gives a sh- which is really refreshing as a Pol Sci major. One example, though kinda small. We are in a junky classroom and the speaker system broke one class. Now he brings a small speaker so he can play us videos from the time period. Most professors would just replace the video with more boring lectures. Guy cares.

Professor Haddad-Fonda is so funny and witty with his lectures, it was such a treat to attend his classes. In his Modern North Africa course, you need to engage your writing and reading skills, but if you do the work, you should have no trouble being successful in it. He is quite passionate about the material, and it shows. I highly recommend.

An amazing professor! His lectures were really interesting (he is passionate and knowledgeable about the subjects) and the classes were organized very well. Despite not knowing a lot about history, after doing the homework I always felt prepared and could participate in class discussions. Overall this was one of the best classes I have ever taken!

An awesome prof!! You can tell he's passionate about what he teaches and he uses super interesting personal anecdotes during his lectures. Really understanding in the COVID era of university and chooses really useful and informative primary resources. Strooooongly recommend.

I loved the lectures, each one was interesting and I learned a lot of new info about a topic I was already well versed on. He was very accessible outside of class and helped so much with the many essays we had to write. The class was challenging and I had to work but it was very much rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: An conceptually easy course graded on a brutal scale w/ no clear criteria, 8 different submittables, competitive participation, passive aggressive teacher who can't answer questions and uses chatgpt for everything. Interesting and simple material presented in a way that makes you hurt.

Never seen a more biased teacher. Felt evident because of her highly subjective approach. The participation curve system might even be more flawed than classical Marxism. 80 students fighting for 55 curved points. Passive aggressive, like she is smiling but flipping you off behind her back. Would contemplate dropping out rather than take her again

Pros: Engaging class activities, helpful practice exams, and easy exams. Cons: Ineffective participation structure, unclear rubrics, contradictory grading, unhelpful panels, and an inability to answer student questions. Overall, it's an easy class, but the cons significantly diminish the class quality.

I don't understand the bad reviews. Yes, her participation critera made it so people would ask a thousand questions a class even though the questions really didn't matter, but I think the grading critera was pretty explicit, and the overall teaching quality was good. Too much hate not enough love in this world.
Unclear grading criteria, uneducated in subject matter, tough and biased grader, lectures just review textbook material, if you can try to avoid

She's a nice person and all but she really lacks credibility and prior business knowledge. She constantly wasn't able to answer class questions that would sound quite routine for a professor at this caliber of a school. Participation is unfairly weighted high, favoring those who aren't afraid to speak up at literally anything, for no reason at all.

Rubrics are subjective and ambiguous. Most of the reasons I was marked down in writing assignments involved the blanket comment "Need more". And if you write too well you will get the comment "Did you actually write this?" I wish I was joking (I'm not)
I agree with every other rating on this page except for the 5 because she wrote that one herself

Fine if u want a good grade. As long as u do well on ur assignments + REALLY easy exams, you'll do fine. However, there's a weighted participation system that benefits select students. Main takeaway: u won't gain much educational value bc she doesn't actually know anything about IBUS (was incapable of answering a single question this quarter).

I'd purposefully close my eyes when crossing the road b4 this class in hopes to get ran over before it started. Has less knowledge on topic than the students! It's competitive participation so ppl ask  questions to get points but she doesn't know how to answer the questions. Passive aggressive + grades tough yet can't teach ??? SAVE YOURSELF

Guidelines are honestly not clear enough for the group final report. Even asking for clarification never helps and it seems like she doesn't even know what her rubric is asking for. The participation points create an environment that does not reflect actual discussion or learning. If she dislikes you, she DISLIKES you.

Professor prioritizes class involvement, graded competitively, encouraging 40+ students to fight for participation. It derails class, wastes time, and prevents learning from the professor they are paying high fees to listen to. Teaching style is fine, but overall engagement is inequitable. Overall attitude and compatibility with students is low.

In my experience, the lectures did not provide much educational value, and I felt that the grading was quite harsh. I would not recommend taking this course if you are looking for a class that makes good use of your time and supports your learning

This professor has unclear and unfair guidelines for writing assignments. If you don't write like Edgar Allen Poe, don't expect to get above an 80% on any writing assignments. Students are pitted amongest each other due to her strict participation scale.

The professor is giving a presentation just like the same quality other students would make rather than a legit lecture. Not worth taking her class at all, the slides are messy and yet professor is just reading off the slides straight.

She can barely provide clear guidelines for assignments and changes her rubrics at the last minute. Makes SIGNIFICANT grading mistakes that dropped students' grades by an average of 8%, and a flawed participation system.

Proffesor Harrold uses a participation scale that doesn't promote inclusivity. Students are constantly adding information that isn't useful to class discussions. Specifically, there is this girl that waste 30 minutes of class time talking.

Gave extension because of the Superbowl! Rely on the lectures for this class. Writing wise this teacher is very particular regarding that, do not try to go out of the rubric. Participation do matter and is curved. Overall great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor is barely able to answer students' questions ans students in the class are weirdly motivated to show off thier knowlege in every class wasting roughly 30 minutes of class time. You get nothing out of it but bad grade since grade heavily relies on this class heavily relies on unfair participations.

He's a great professor overall and very nice. If you're taking his biodemography class, your grades are based on take-home packets and a final project. His lectures can get boring/dry sometimes. He does not use canvas but instead uses his own website. His grading standards can get unclear.

Oh my gosh. 10/10. He is one of the good teachers, not a lot of those. He cares, and is always always available to help outside of class. He literally gives you his phone number. I assume people give bad reviews because the classes are challenging... lol? If a course you are actually interested in is offered with Professor Holman 100% take it :)

Dr. Holman is a good professor who cares about the content and his students' success. The lectures are boring & dry though. I got a 4.0 hardly attending class. He just reads off the slideshows, which he always posts online, so no one really ever came to class. Your grade= 4 homework sheets (all content from slides) and one fun exploratory project.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class and Darryl as professor. He is very passionate about the subject and really wants you to understand. I highly recommend going to his office hours if you need help with problem sets. He's very approachable, responsive via email, and understanding. He's got some cool stories too.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is probably one of the best professors here! He actually cares if you do well in the class and he's willing to help you out until you understand the concepts. And he's a pretty easy grader; just as long as you show ALL your work and you're actually trying. Attendance isn't mandatory but it's a good idea to go. Also, he replies to all your emails
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: I truly enjoyed this class. Get ready to ready of course and be prepare for his unexpected fun times. Dr. Holman really cares about his students and he wants you to learn. Very helpful in his office hours and he will make time to fit your hours. His persona is the best part of the class, very spontaneous. I love his style and I would take again!

I actually enjoyed his class. As long as you attend and pay attention and ask questions of concepts you don't understand, Darryl is open to answering your questions until you understand. Yes, his lectures can feel a bit unorganized, but he really tries to create example to help students understand.

Had him for the evolution class. He's a little lazy and makes students do much of the grunt work. He tends to be a little obscure. He's an easy grader, though, and if you're motivated to learn on your own, you might enjoy the company.
This class should have been helpful for my research, but I learned little to nothing. Dr. Holman frequently was unprepared, and often ended class early.
Completely unorganized. Didn't have lectures prepared. Made students feel stupid when they didn't udnerstand

She is really sweet and passionate. I did enjoy her lectures, but the unit quizzes were very confusing and difficult for me. I know I wasn't the only one because the TA told me so, yet there wasn't a curve or anything on the questions that most of the class got wrong which is rly weird. The final was an improvement but quizzes were worded so poorly

Professor Jun is an extremely kind and caring teacher. She always made sure we understood the content and even learned most of our names. The slides are also very clear, and her lectures are easy to understand and engage with.

Professor Jun is an amazing professor! Sweet, kind, and gives feedback that doesn't make you feel belittled. Beware though, Professor Jun is the most toughest grader I have ever had in my academic career so utilize her office hours if you are struggling.

Professor Jun clearly cares about her students. The lectures can get long but she's quite enthusiastic so they're not too boring. The reading is average for a 200 level, and outside of one formal essay there wasn't much writing. She doesn't grade super easy though, so if you're not familiar with history writing definitely go to office hours.

I cannot recommend her enough. She is incredibly caring, easy to talk to, and deeply passionate about the material she teaches. The class itself is equally compelling, offering an intricate dive into the field of carework by blending theoretical frameworks with modern, lively examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: English 111 by Lahiri is dope simply put. She is consistently funny and unbelievably relatable. The assignments she puts out are unique and challenging but in a way that still manages to be fun. The class forces you to grow as a writer which is a cool and wholesome experience. Overall great.
She is super chill and nice. Deadlines were flexible and graded fairly. Definitely would recommend!

Ian Schnee is my favorite teacher at UW and I am taking another class from him next quarter. He makes the class very accessible and easy to succeed in. Quiz sections count as extra credit, his stance on active learning and in-class participation forces you to learn, and the content is relatively easy to understand.

Ian Schnee is my favorite professor at UW and I am taking another one of his classes next quarter because of it. He makes it very easy to do well with quiz section being extra credit, in class participation is worth a lot, and the content is relatively easy to understand. He is also very humorous and enjoyable which makes learning the content fun.

Ended up loving the class but beware if you're taking this class for a humanities-related credit. This course is designed for people in something like CS. Logic is basically math/coding before computers. Look up BOOL. I wouldn't have taken this class if I knew but it was valuable and I didn't end up doing that bad. Struggled HARD but rewarding.

Ian was a great professor- it was clear he loves what he does & wanted us to learn every lecture. Go to office hours- he's super accessible and wants to help you learn. You use the textbook he wrote himself which was clear & easy to follow. Assignments & tests were all reasonable as long as you put in your own effort. Highly recommend his class!

I have never seen a man so excited to teach every day. Probably the most enthusiastic professor I've had so far, and overall just teaches the subject really well. In all honesty, logic was a bit hard for me to follow sometimes, but Ian encourages students to try and be wrong which really helped. Just a fun guy honestly
A great professor who encourages students to think outside the box, 10/10

Fantastic individual. Lectures are fun and engaging, logic is fun. Just pay attention and do the assigned work, which is really quite reasonable. Test content is transparent and very chill. Prof. Schnee is a very friendly and open professor as well, he loves to talk, help out on whatever you'd need, and is very approachable!

I had Prof. Schnee for Phil 120 and 149 and absolutely loved him. As far as grading goes, in Logic, you really have to study for your desired grade. The tests have everything on it, but it is very managable and you get lots of practice in quiz section and in class.

I took Schnee for 120 and 149 this year. He built these courses with his own textbook, youtube lecture series, and practice materials. He supplemented lectures with lessons on metacognition and self-expansion, which were always captivating. Schnee, you offered me an onion this year. In my years at UW I've never met anyone like you.

Not many assignments (2 essays and a video review). Interesting lectures, watched good movies. You get 3 class skips. Final exam is multiple choice, doesn't weigh a lot and isn't hard. Do readings and watch a movie once a week. Overall, an interesting course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: For all in doubt about taking one of Schnee's classes, know that I made this account to give him 5 stars.
Legendary professor. Take him if you want to learn.

As a psych major girlie that was scared to take this class bc i'd heard horror stories, Ian is actually so sweet. He cares so much about his students - memorized over 300 names and faces and knew every single person on the first day of class. You've gotta work but this class is manageable and so rewarding. TAs and Ian are great resources for help!

we love ian! he made me want to be a philosophy major. super easy class, just go to section for extra credit and put average time into doing the work. he changed the curriculum so its easier now i think

Professor Schnee has been my favorite professor so far. He is funny and a very kind person who took the time to learn almost everyone's names. He rambles a bit but his office hours are super helpful. This is logical proofs heavy and it could be difficult at times. But utilizing office hours is critical. Also go to quiz section for extra points.

GOAT professor, he knew my name on the first day of lecture. Also he does metacognitive lessons to end each lecture, which is my favorite part of the class. It is a difficult class with logic proofs, more similar to 10th grade geometry class than a traditional philosophy class. if you struggle the TAs are great and Ian is great, and will help you.
missing lectures and slides

I would consider this class the ideal college class. Not too difficult, a few assignments per week with up to 10 tries on each, late work is accepted without penalty. Not too easy, a lot of content is covered and you can't just BS it without reading. He wrote the textbook, and it's actually decent with interactive stuff. Enjoyed and learned a lot.
Phil120 is super hard, but Prof Schnee does his best to help every student succeed. Logic is intuitive to some and not
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Schnee is enthusiastic, helpful, and kind! It is clear that he is very knowledgeable, which makes his office hours and Phil 120 rich and engaging. To succeed in Phil 120, attend office hours (for help on HW), don't fall behind on content (extremely crucial, Phil 120 is fast-paced), and attend section (for extra credit on midterm/final).

Tho it is true that this class has a heavy workload, I loved this class. The lectures can be confusing, but poll isn't graded on accurucy. The quiz sections saved me the most on the material, I recommend creating a gc in ur section to make hw go easier. Learning bool, fol, and prop were my fav, it like playing a puzzle game with logic.

This is the worst class at UW. Phil 120 is not an intro to logic course, but rather a 10-week accelerated study into every minor facet of formal logic. I believe that for this to truly be an intro class, it would have to cut out content and become a series. Schnee wasn't helpful when students were clearly lost, instead just belittled them as "lazy"

I was not expecting this course to be so difficult. Although this is a "intro level" course, the material was extremely advanced. Each week the material becomes more complex, I wasn't able to understand after week 4. Prof Schnee adds questions to exams aimed to trip you up or about content we haven't learned. Avoid this course if you don't need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Schnee is probably one of my favorite Philosophy profs in the department. He taught a class that wasn't easy, but was super helpful and patient. Furthermore, super accessible, and he gives out the textbook to his class for free, because he wrote it. I hate it when profs make students buy the text for the class when they've written it.

Ian was extremely enthusiastic, smart, and patient. I will say, logic is either something you get or don't, but he does a pretty good job at helping you. If you do all of the work on time and keep up with lectures, you should be able to do pretty well!

Ian is a really passionate and caring teacher and does a more than amazing job at explaining the content, however it is totally up to you to keep yourself caught up as falling behind can be really rough.

Ian is a great professor. His quiz sections are optional and you get extra credit on the midterm/final for attending. The material is pretty challenging but Ian really puts in effort to make sure everyone understands. He really wants everyone to succeed. Lowkey more of a math type class than philosophy though tbh

Professor Schnee will make you care about logic. He is totally engaging, wrote the textbook himself (and gives it to students for free), and really makes an effort to help students understand. I was warned that this class would be hard but if you do the reading (and there really isn't that much), this class is really easy.

Took two of his classes
Phil 149: Schnee's funny, knowledgable, great movie taste
Phil 120: had qualms with this class
- content was very tricky for a 100 level course, after week 4 I could not grasp the material
- the reading materials was much easier than the graded homework, bad for doing said homework

Would rec humanities ian, not STEM ian
Stay far far away from Ian Schnee

Relied too much on the terrible textbook that he wrote. The tests were so tricky, and they expected us to figure things out that we had never been taught. Prof didn't explain material properly. Also, the homework load was abysmal. WAY too much for an "intro" class. If you're looking for easy NSc credits don't take this class. Be smarter than me.

This class and his style is very much akin to enginnering so if you are SS get ready for a tough go. That being said he expects you to do the work and if you do it the gibberish makes sense. Also his office hours where very helpfull. Yes the midterm was busted but he gave us points back soo. Overall tough, but really well thought out course.

This class was painful. The textbook problems seem easy until you get to lecture and the prof gave us 1 minute to solve problems that were nothing like what we read about...and these poll ev questions were graded on accuracy. The tests were even worse, with concepts that were not only impossible to complete in the time given, but were never taught

The worst professor I have ever had. The pace of the class is way too fast with very little support. The material in the textbook is very simple and easy to understand but the mountain of weekly homework is much more difficult than the textbook meaning you have to figure out a lot yourself. The lectures would help if the pace was not so fast.

I took another one of his classes (Phil 149) and loved it and the way he taught it so I thought this class would be similar but I was fooled. He goes very fast through very complicated content then proceeds to get frustrated at everyone for bombing the midterm but doesn't think he's doing anything wrong. Don't take if ur looking for easy credits.
If I could give him a 0/5 I would. He does not care for his students whatsoever. These "great" ratings under his name are complete bots. Please don't take this class if you want to save your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Schnee's class was an excruciating experience. His lectures are nonsensical, and his homework quizzes are frustratingly difficult. He altered the class policy mid-quarter, and the Clue sessions are inconvenient for commuters. I caution against taking this class; if you choose to do so and fail, you have been warned.

This class was really interesting and Professor Schnee is a really engaging lecturer. The readings were never too long and I enjoyed most of the films. Professor Schnee uses Poll Everywhere to take attendance and the final exam is based almost entirely on content covered in lecture so attendance is pretty mandatory.

Ian is a great lecturer, so much so I never missed a class. Grading is very flexible and more than ample time is given to complete essays. This was my first philosophy class and I will be trying to take another of his.
I loved Professor Schnee! His class was so cool, he was engaging during lecture, and made he the content we were learning super interesting because of the way that he was teaching it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: You certainly have a lot to read but if you listen in lectures and read the textbook (which is AMAZING), then you'll do great. He genuinely listens and wants us to learn and love the content. This turned out to be my favorite class. His enthusiasm helps make lectures interesting as well.

Loved this class! Lots of French New Wave films but you also watch newer things like Bojack Horseman. The readings are all manageable + explained nicely in lecture. Courseload is pretty chill - 7 short essays, a few unlimited-attempt quizzes, a multiple-choice final. Prof Schnee is super knowledgeable and accessible if you have questions.

His class was an easy A, he is very kind and cares a lot about his students, always going out of his way to make sure students don't feel pressured from the work load of his class. There can be long readings but a lot of them are pretty interesting, as long as you know the gist of what is taught it'll be an easy 4.0.

5 short essays (you get to choose which ones you want to do throughout the quarter) and 2 required essays. Theres also a final exam, but if you do the reading and watch the films youll do great. Overall, Schnee is a great professor and definitely knows what hes talking about. The content is very interesting as well
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Schnee gives you lots of material, readings movies and more, and expects you to write a lot of papers, but if you have a good TA and show up to class youll get an A no problem. Lectures are fast with lots of interaction and engagement, so come to class with some ideas from the reading/movie. Pay attention in lecture and youll get it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: This was my first philosophy class at the UW and it made me fall in love with philosophy. Professor Schnee is so engaging with his class and you can tell that he truly cares about what he is teaching. He keeps the lectures lighthearted and gets everyone involved in a very comfortable way. 10/10 recommend anything that Ian Scnhee is teaching.

There's quite a lot of papers throughout the class, but you get to pick and choose which ones you want to do. He's a nice guy, and I found his lectures relatively interesting. You get unlimited attempts on the quizzes, so you should be able to get a good grade with minimal effort. Great overall experience, would totally recommend it.

Prof. Schnee is an amazing teacher! He is incredibly well organized, and the expectations are clear and reasonable. His lectures are short but informative, and his grading policy and assignments are built to maximize learning. Although the class is quite challenging, it's worth it if you like logic. *Class taken remotely due to COVID-19

If you enjoy movies and analyzing them, you'll love this. If you don't and you're just looking for easy credit, look for something else - you need to really love film and philosophical analysis to take this course. I didn't really enjoy the class and it really bored me, but Ian Schnee is super caring and passionate, and I don't fault him at all.
Very good.

This was my first PHIL class and even though it was all online and asynchronous, Prof. Schnee made it so entertaining and got me really interested in Philosophy. There are a lot of papers but they're short and it's easy to know what to expect, and the lectures and films are all amazing!!

It's such a great designed class for the combination of film and philosophy. I understood something via the big picture in philosophy which I was looking for via the details in psychology. Film as an intermediary, makes the philosophy class more appealing. Prof. Schnee is open minded and passionate. I am so happy for taking his class.

Had Dr. Schnee online for Fall 2020. His PHIL 149 course was really interesting, I liked the class a lot. It's a lot of writing, but there's a ton of flexibility with which assignments you choose to do. Some of the reading is pretty dense but he explains everything really well in his lectures. Overall a great prof and an interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ian is awesome, my first philosophy class and I really enjoyed it due to how interesting he made his asynchronous lectures. Would definitely recommend this to anyone interested in film or trying out philosophy. Prof. Schnee's videos sometimes let off a high pitched pop, destroying my eardrums and will to live, but other than that this class rocks!

he does not care about your personal problems. he WILL fail you if you have any. I was diagnosed with a rare neurological problem, he did not care and denied an incomplete, even though i finished everything else. told me he didnt care - i HAD TO make the final.

While this class was extremely difficult, from TAs I've heard Dr. Schnee's class is the easiest for PHIL 120. He is very passionate when teaching and does a good job with presenting the content. It is just that this class is very, very difficult.
Ian is a really amazing professor. I took this class when everything went online, yet he still managed to deliver lectures really well. There are lots of homeworks though, so be prepared to do those!

Honestly, such a great professor. The material was a lot but if you are willing to put in the work and not get behind, you will do well. The textbook is interactive and written by him so it wasn't too difficult to understand. He always has the student's best interest in mind so go to office hours and ask questions!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is great at leading discussions and imbuing knowledge to the class. The way he presented all the material made sense as a narrative of what philosophy is. Also, there was no textbook! Saves you money.

Ian is a truly amazing professor. The interactive online textbook he writes is very helpful and explains complicated concepts clearly and in details (if you read carefully). Homework counts as a big portion of your grade. You have a whole week to do it and two attempts for each, so as long as you put in effort you should have a fair grade already.

I really love the textbook (online). It's written by the professor himself and is FREE. The textbook explains things very clearly despite some minor mistakes. His lectures are OK. Very nice guy and answers questions carefully during office hours (very accessible, you can literally just go and ask questions right after lectures). Exams are not hard.

His textbook is completely online so there is no monetary requirement for taking the class. His lectures are fun and engaging. A real nice guy who genuinely wants to see all his students pass with flying colors.
He is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great guy, very fair and considerate. Will listen to what you have to say and will never make you feel bad for asking a dumb question.
One of the harder PHIL classes I took but very VERY worth it if you're interested in the subject (philosophy & film). Solid professor all around, plus he wrote our textbook.

Ian Schnee is an okay professor. He is definitely knowledgeable, but in this class is was way too much. There were 2-5 hour hw assignments with only a day apart, and if you work it is hard to keep up. In lecture he goes into so many tangents and his voice is a little annoying haha. Take him and see if you like it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Schnee is a great professor. If you have the chance to take one of his classes I highly recommend it. Be wary that there may be a lot of reading, random call, and some things in lecture may speed by faster than you may wish. That being said, he cares about your learning, your beliefs, and creates a good learning environment.

This guy legit is father of philosophy. You know why I love logic so much? this guy. This guy, god dang. I love it. Hes actually O.G and dope at teaching. Take his class and you'll learn a lot. Trust me bois.

Ian is very good at what he does. He wrote his own textbook for the class, which despite some bugs, was extremely useful (it's online and free). He is very receptive to student questions and never makes you feel stupid. Very accessible for office hours, and he is very aware that what he's teaching isn't easy. Course content was so-so in usefulness.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you're coming from a CS background and want to learn about proofs, this is the course. Ian literally wrote the textbook himself and turned it into a freely available interactive website. He's an amazing professor who cares about his students, would recommend.

Ian is great. Problem sets can be hard to finish but teamwork is allowed as long as no one is copying anything. If you have any questions in class, just ask and he'll explain it to you. He can be funny sometimes. And you're expected to read in advance to better understand the material. He speaks fast but always precisely points out what's important
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Ian Schnee is a great professor. I went to almost every one of his office hour with my stupid immature questions. He's helped me with those and even questions about philosophy major. I'm an intended phil major and taking this class has definitely prepared me for the future. You'll love him if you get his humor.
I love ian schnee!!

I think professor Schnee was a solid choice. He is funny and gives good lectures. However, I feel like I learned more course content and homework related work during quiz sections rather than lectures. You have to go to class because participation matters. The homeworks also take longer than they seem but I feel more prepped for CS / math proofs
one of the best class I've ever taken in uw.

The content for this course is very straightforward. Memorize everything and you will be very successful. It's just memorize and regurgitate. There is no room for discussion or playing with concepts and ideas. The information is also utterly useless outside of this environment, so I wouldn't recommend taking this ever unless you want to teach it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He does random calling in lecture after every clicker question, you can also pass. You can defend your answer to get the point even if you chose the wrong choice. Quiz on canvas before each lecture about readings. Really straightforward.
Great teacher; he always tries to understand students' questions even when they are unable to express what exactly they are confused about.
It was an absolute pleasure going to lectures! Always challenges his students and expects a lot but is also ready to help and is open for all questions.

One of the best professors I've had. Grades are hard but fair and every lecture has a lot of substance but incredibly informative. If you're ok going to lectures and doing the reading she will be amazing.

There's way too much homework and readings for a 200 level course. Ive taken multiple 400-500 level courses that had significantly less assignments. I was incredibly stressed the entirety of the quarter by the multitude of readings and content I was expected to read or view in a relatively short amount of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very passionate, kind, and understanding. She definitely cares about her job and her students. I struggled with my mental health that quarter but I talked with her and she helped me come up with a plan, and she checked in a few times to make sure I was doing okay and congratulate me when I managed to turn everything in. Wonderful person in general

Professor R-S is very kind, a soft grader, and perhaps the most passionate instructor I've ever had. I wasn't too impressed with her lectures and didn't think they were the most organized, but she clearly cares and gets really into it every day, so it was good in the end.

Prof R-S is so sweet. Her class was very enjoyable. Very dense readings but they don't expect you to understand everything. As long as you know the big pictures you should be fine. Learned a lot of stuff about colonialism and capitalism in Latin America. Hard class/content but she drops a couple of assignments which help boost my grade!

The readings are very deep and dark, they focus on the horrors of colonialism and capitalism. Leftists will enjoy this class. Very organized on Canvas! Asynchronous class! PARTICIPATE IN TA SECTIONS! I suggest you take notes there!

Great class and Prof. Rodriguez is a very enthusiastic lecturer who really knows her stuff. Its heavy on the reading, but Rodriguez will help break it down in her lectures and the TA should do the same. Emphasizes critical thinking skills over regurgitation. Much more hands-on then most classes I have taken at UW!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is a really good professor and I highly recommend taking her classes. Her lectures are clear and engaging and you can see she knows her stuff. The grading in this class is pretty easy in my opinion. You won't be able to get away with not turning things in but the work isn't that difficult so just do it and your grade will be good.

AMAZING. I adore Prof. R-S. She is the most engaging professor I've had at UW. Her lectures were so fascinating. The subject matter was often really heavy, but it was presented in a very engaging way. She's also truly so funny. An amazing prof, and I would love to take another class with her before I graduate.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Ileana is very funny and made class fun, but her manner of speaking and the course material were fairly disorganized and it was hard to take notes and stay on top of the material. The work is manageable and there aren't any big papers, but you have to do the reading. I liked Ileana a lot as a person but she's not the most compelling professor.
Very lecture-heavy. If you miss one class, be sure to have a friend to get the notes from because she does not post or record her lectures. Pretty interesting class, but it was quite time-consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her lecture style is crazy. She is impossible to listen to.

I enjoyed her lectures a lot and her class is very interesting. However, we need to read a lot and most of our grades come from the reading reflections. It's important that you write those reflections well. If you pay attention in class and take note, it is not a very hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: What a wonderful, wonderful class! I loved every minute of every lecture. You MUST take this class if you're at the UW.

She was a fantasitc teacher. She had a way of taking information that seemed boring or confusing and explaining it in a way that was easy to understand and interesting. Because of this class I want to pursue a diversity minor and take more classes about Latin American history.

Her lectures are a bit disorganized, but you can feel her passion in the subject when she lectures. Despite this being a two hour lecture class, she is able to keep students interested. I would definitely recommend this class to anyone. She is also actually cares for her students, making sure to remember all their names. One of the best professors.
Passionate, engaged, well informed.  Cares about teaching and her students.
Fantastic and passionate scholar. She really knows her stuff and makes history interesting and fun. Lots of reading, but worth it. Grading and tests are very straightforward.

She has unstructured lectures, she is willing to be helpful, but wants you to figure it out on your own. She does not say how she wants test questions answered so you are basically screwed unless you've taken her before. She takes time to learn names and cherishes class participation. I would not recommend her though if you're looking for an easy A

Lectures were hard to follow and difficult to take good notes to.  Too much time  was spent on useless and pointless class discussion. There is a lot of work involved but she is a fair grader. I strongly feel that this was the worst class I have ever taken at the UW based on her lecture style and her use of class time.
Good lectures.  I had more contact with her assistant, but she was helpful when I stopped by during office hours.  The grading was fair.  It wasn't an easy class.
Good professor!  This was the mandatory junior seminar for History majors.  Learned lots of new things, and was inspired to work and develop my own voice.

Ileana is the best teacher I think I have ever had. Her passion and knowledge of Latin American history rubs off on students. I wasn't very interested going into the class but I ended up getting excited to attend. She requires a lot of work and attendance but if you put in the effort you will do fine, she is very fair. I highly recommend her!

So much energy! I loved this class. Two hour lectures are long but she does a great job keeping them entertaining! I also loved how she got to know the names of every person in the class which demonstrates her passion for teaching and a desire that her students learn the material. Fantastic class!

Best professor I've had at UW. I wasn't too sure about taking a two hour history class, but her lectures are simply captivating. She's very objective and encourages critical thinking. Take her class if you can.

I've had her as a professor a few times because I love her brain so much! She is an enthusiastic professor and a critical thinker- which has been rare on UWs campus in my experience. I can't reccommend her high enough!!!

Truly inspired lecturer, she can hold an audience captive for two hours (if you're interested in the subject). Come every single day and take copious notes, otherwise you'll suffer during exams. She also offers some extra credit, which brought my grade to a 4.0 without perfect exam scores. Great reading material, funny, passionate lecturer.

Ileana is brilliant and a very talented, engaging lecturer. In contradiction to those who complain about the clarity of her lectures, she presents material very clearly, and a huge amount of it. She provides study guides for exams. Lots of notes to look through for studying, yes. You have to come to class. I highly recommend her, if you're serious.

Very energetic and passionate about the subject. Her voice, however, literally hurts my ears as she screams while she lectures. Demands participation in classes of 60+ individuals. She is a very kind person and will help you outside of class if you wish. Lectures are unorganized, very difficult to understand them.

Ileana is wonderfully enthusiastic and knowledgeable; she's capable of maintaining a classes interest for two and a half hours. however, as others have said, her lectures are unstructured; although I took copious notes, I found the midterm and final very difficult to study for.

Ileana is so enthusiastic it, but her lectures appear disorganized like a stream of conciousness. Her expectations are unclear, and everything is graded HARD. A great mind in the field, just not one I want responsible for my gpa.

Awesome. I wish she taught everything. Vary passionate about the subject, and her passion is contagious. Gives great, engaging, interesting lectures that you actually want to pay attention to. Her exams specifically the final tested on random information. It was about 95 questions and half of the questions were just memorizing cases/videos/in class activities. I think everyone low-key traumatized her because of here. She is not as bad as everyone makes it seem. Despite hearing negative comments about ruth, I actually really enjoy Ruth class. The class is based on lectures, in-class discussions, and activities, which really helped reinforce learning. Her class is really easy. There's nothing difficult to learn. Her exam is multiple choice and essay. It's all memorization basically. She also gives you an outline for the essay portion and grades it leniently.

She's not as bad as the reviews say. The only thing I don't like is that sometimes she doesn't fully get her point across. She tries to explain something but it's not very clear what she's trying to say. I wish she was more thorough in her explanation.

great. She takes roll attendance and there are reading quizzes often. they aren't hard though, you just have to read the assigned readings.

Prof. Huwe is very knowledgeable and a great facilitator. I have enjoyed every class in MGMT 404. The concepts in SWITCH that we read are very helpful in a professional set-up. She goes out of the way to ensure students understand a topic by explaining on the white board and by giving relevant examples. I highly recommend Prof. Huwe and MGMT 404.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I've always been on the dean's list at foster, so I feel qualified to state that Ruth is the WORST professor I've ever had, by far. She's unable to even structure a lecture, and her tests are based on using both the readings and lecture notes- even when the readings contradict what she says in lecture. Gives condescending answers to questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly, Ruth is obviously very experienced, but she will never let you leave without bragging about herself. I cannot count the number of times she talked about Boeing and Puget Power. The class overall, the reading quizzes are not bad, the midterm was OK. But her final project was not clear and confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Ruth is a solid professor with reasonable tests. She seems to know her stuff, but comes off as fairly arrogant. I would suggest taking it from Lee, as I've heard better things.

This class was definitely one of the most beneficial classes I took to prepare for the business world. Readings were manageable and relevant to corporate life, receiving feedback on group contributions was both unique and insightful, and the group business idea was a quality hands-on experience. Perfect elective for the Foster sales certificate.

Ruth is usually all over the place. I wanted to like her more than I ended up feeling about her, but she started to get sassy in conversations for no evident reason. although, she does have her biases, she does an above average job of being aware of them and usually doesnt stray to far from the center.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Huwe is a phenomenal professor who genuinely cares about her students' success both inside and outside of the classroom. She has years of real world experience in the corporate world yet encourages us to reach and think outside the box and be open to change and sustainability within the business environment.

Took MGMT 300 and 403 with Ruth. Really liked her classes because they are very interactive - the in-class activities really helped with learning the course material! Ruth also offered to go over our midterms to provide feedback so we can do better on the final (+ to review our resumes) - I improved from below avg. to the second highest in class!

MGMT isn't a hard class to teach; all you do is paraphrase the textbook in lecture. If this class was important to me, I would be frustrated that Ruth wastes A LOT of class talking about useless personal anecdotes. She also throws in weird test questions, which are often disputable if you challenge her on them. Curve is toughish. Class is a waste.

She lives in her own world, and often has commentary that makes me want to face palm. However, she's an engaging professor that has some relevant examples. I strongly disliked the in-class exercises/games, but some people seemed to enjoy them.

Ruth's classes are not for any student reading about her on this sight. In my experience she gave us a book and lectures every day and literally all of it ends up on the exams. I won't be taking a course from her again and advise other students to do the same. I will say she is very likable but I am myself not a fan of her course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Huwe's classes are interesting and engaging. I took three classes with her and each one had relevant activities, lessons and readings. Contrary to some earlier reviews, she doesn't play favorites. Your grade will reflect your work. She is fair in her assessments and feedback. I took many 'real life' skills out of each class. Highly recommend!!

Ruth is a dedicated professor who puts passion into her lectures. There's class discussions on readings each class, but the readings are either short or interesting. She's clear, she knows what she's talking about, and just overall a great teacher to have.

I've taken 4 courses with her (Mgmt301,302,303 and 322) and she is one of the best professors I have ever had. She gives a lot of useful feedback and is very dedicated to her students. I learned a lot of useful skills and knowledge from her classes than many other courses that I've taken. The reading is interesting and useful too.
An amazing teacher, really inspirational, she's fair, no midterms and finals, only some papers. She's well respected, knows what she's talking about and I learnt a lot.

Though the topics are interesting, Ruth is condescending in her attempt to seem well-versed and clever. She preaches self-reflection, but believes her way is the only way. NEVER use your phone in class. She's anal about cheating. She's picky about presentations. She favors the extroverted students. SO MUCH MATERIAL and reading. Hard to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Focusing too much on reading. Not practical stuff. Gets students to teach classes through presentations basically. Ignorant to many important issues and topics. Couldn't pronounce Xi Jinping which is important. Plugs her Morocco trip way too much - I would hate to be on a trip to another country with her. Grading criteria is not good.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hands down the best class I've ever taken at UW. The only class so far that I have learned things that I feel are actually useful to my future. We read Seven Habits of Highly Effective People as our class book if that tells you anything. Ruth is amazing and extremely intelligent. Yes she can be sarcastic - not a big deal at all in my mind.
If you're the type of student who reads these reviews, you're the type of student who should avoid Ruth at all costs. Take it with anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is rude, unprofessional. She once mocked a persons religion and down plays it by acting like she is joking but she really is not. She is unorganized and changes subject due dates and content at the last minute. She is picky and if you don't do something how she likes you will get docked points.

She knows her subject and is passionate about it. Other than that, very disappointing as a teacher. She's proud. Leads to hypocrisy and caprice. EG "quizzes will be ridiculously easy if you did the reading" to "I made the quiz extra hard to prep you for the exam." Wants original thought; praises regurgitation. She's strict. No electronics period.

MGMT 401 was one of my favorite classes I have taken so far at UW. I had full confidence in Ruth's knowledge and she exemplifies the material she teaches through her own leadership experiences. She is a very enthusiastic lecturer and provides you with an abundance of resource to help anybody become a better leader. I recommend this class to anybody

To sum her up pretty much she is clear, inspiring, caring and fun. She cares a lot about how much you understand the concepts. Loads of class room exercises to make a lot of friends. Her grading criteria is crystal clear and she gives specific feedback about what's missing. She has loads of industry experience so class examples are real and fun.

Professor Huwe is very energetic and really knows what she is talking about. I had her in three classes and in none of them I thought when is this class going to be over. Her classes are very interesting and rich in variety. For every paper or quiz she gives clear instructions such that I felt always treated fairly.

Ruth is one of those instructors that strives to get you to understand the concepts that she is teaching you. She's thorough and prepared. She genuinely cares about students. She's been doing this for a while and you can tell she is very familiar and comfortable with her material. She goes the extra mile, she's upbeat, and she's got a couple jokes.

Taking this class I didn't do super hot on the midterms because multiple choice is not my strongest area of expertise, but when I asked for help Ruth helped me out and actually cared about helping me.  She is fun and keeps the lectures going.  Never one time did I think "when is this class going to be over?"  she is also very invested in everyone!

Ruth is a very passionate and caring professor. She keeps class interesting with different activities, and she always provides real world examples to help you really grasp the concept. When you stop by for office hours she always says, "How may I be of service to you." That is how I would sum her up. She is there for you.

Participation is based on attendance (which technically isn't allowed). Midterm was 90 ?'s that required pure memorization of lecture slides, textbook, and other outside reading. Professor isn't very helpful and often uses a condescending and rude tone. Lectures are not online. Overall, a LOT of work but not terribly difficult. Wouldn't recommend.
EVADE HER
Loved her! The class was always interesting and I thought it was valuable stuff. She's an easy grader so let's see how the curve turns out...

It is really important to be in class and to read the assigned materials. As long as you do, the reading quizzes and tests are fairly straightforward.  There is also quite a bit of group work.  The lectures can be really interesting though, and she does a great job of using more hands on activities to keep class time from getting boring.
Great Class and professor
Must read chapters to prepare for quizzes (we had 7 throughout the quarter). You will learn a lot, but make sure you speak up or else she will mark you down.

Ruth is very passionate and knowledgable about this subject.  That being said, she is rater stern, stubborn, and hard to connect with.  However, she is a great teacher and the class is actually fairly easy as long as you go and are prepared.  There is one presentation and you must do the readings, but besides that a relatively light work load

Ruth Huwe was an awesome professor. Don't get me wrong, she isn't easy, but I learned more in this class than I was anticipating! She also tries her hardest to make the class content relevant and interesting, which of course helps you learn!

Ruth has been one of the best professors I've had at UW. She always comes up with innovative ways to help students understand topics and makes it fun to be in class. I would highly recommend taking Ruth's classes.

Ruth is one of the most passionate professors I know in the Foster Business School. She can be eccentric at times, but it is all because she knows her stuff and wants you to know it too. This particular class is really cool for those wanting to grow awareness as leaders and decision makers. Final paper is actually VALUABLE to me and my future.

Ruth teaches with energy &  confidence, and enhances the material with stories about her behavioral management research about her studies. She prints out her slides for you and really prepares you for her tests with lots of review. She's super helpful at her office hours, and I felt very comfortable going to her for academic and career advice.

Ruth has a very dry teaching style, and concepts are a little hard to distinguish.  Easy ideas, but the questions asked were VERY specific, which made very simple and easy material very hard to master.  She restructured the class mid-quarter, which made things more difficult.  I would say moving forward her class should be much easier than past Qs.
Extremely Rude! Avoid her!

Ruth is one of those teachers who goes out of her way to get to know her students. She is genuinely interested in making sure her students learn and have the tools to succeed. Ruth has acted as a mentor for me and helped me choose my career path. Her class was engaging and she employed novel teaching techniques to keep the class interesting.

Class materials could have been taught way better if she didn't treat students like 7th graders. She is extremely proud of herself for writing this one book that I can't even remember and loves going off the topic with that. The mgmt class is fun afterall, but I'm just saying it could've been better with a different professor.

Tests were challenging because she makes a list of new articles & youtube videos and expects you to know every single one of them, on TOP of textbook and class materials. However, what frustrated me more is her attitude. She becomes extremely rude when she is in a bad mood. Definitely the WORST class i've taken at UW. Trust me & DON'T TAKE her!

After each group presentation, she asked presenters a question that would lead back to one of her anecdotes about a former profession. This and other lecture stories had no benefit to the students. She doesn't clarify what she wants. She asked for hard copies of all group presentations the DAY OF presentations and looked at us like we screwed up.

I wanted to like her but seriously this class was super frustrating. She is not clear with assignments and did not like to clarify. The class material is very straight forward but tests were unnecessarily hard. Tons of memorizing from the book which she said she was avoiding..... And she takes attendance everyday.

Dr. Huwe has done a great deal of studies and papers, which she always will tell you. As far as professors go, I've had better, more engaging teachers that really wanted students to succeed. My biggest challenge when interacting with Dr. Huwe is that she was inconsistent in her instructions and in what she wanted from students - frustrating.

Dr. Huwe was easily the best professor I had at UW. She made her class/learning very enjoyable. She provided a variety of fun/new learning techniques including frequent group discussion and exercises. Because of these, I began to forget about my grade and enjoyed finding myself doing naturally well in the class, while actually learning something.

Ruth Huwe is an incredible professor & mentor. I truly enjoyed her management 401 course, as we discussed many things actually applicable to life in the business world and in general. As long as you follow the guidelines & directions of the course, you will not only learn a lot, but do well while doing so. Highly recommend taking one of her classes
Probably one of my least favorite class at the UW. I would not recommend her. The tests were straight forward but the essays must be done a certain way or else they are wrong.

As an exchange student at UW I took a course of Ruth Huwe. This class was definitely the most enriching experience. Putting theory into practice has never been more applicable. She knew how to make regular models fascinating and used the most interesting articles, movies and assignments. She was open to help students, I liked her a lot!

Ruth is an EXCEPTIONAL teacher! She makes her classes fun, engaging and informational. Her tests are straightforward because she actually wants students to read the materials since she chooses texts that are really fun to read and educational too. She's a teacher that knows her subject and is enthusiastic about it. One of the best teachers in HR!

I took Negotiations with professor Ruth! Amazing class and teacher. Highly recommended!  Up-to-date  lectures, readings and assignments.  Great teaching style and very thorough comments on papers. Easy to understand why you got a certain grade.  Ruth is friendly and really cares what and how you learn.  VERY Useful groupProject and inClass cases.

Highly recommended! Ruth Huwe?s classes are very rewarding, make you think and will drastically improve your writing and presentation skills. The class is engaging, has a fun discussion based atmosphere, and it is not impossible to get an A+. Ruth is very bright and supportive. Her classes were amongst my favorite at UW. Bonus- fun games in class!
Funny and fun lectures. Very laid back. Tests are very manageable as long as you study the slides and read the book. One of the more enjoyable classes I have had in the business school
She is interesting but her grading is so bias. Jeopardy is fun. Studied a lot for her class but her multiple choice exams are tough.
Awesome prof! So engaging!
Worst professor I have had at UW.

It's tough to separate feelings re: material & professor, but Huwe took me from uninterested to invested in OB. Lectures were engaging, slides were useful, difficulty was average, grading was fair. Huwe respects & engages you at the same level you offer the class. Classic case of getting out what you put in - bring your A game, seriously.
She is very enthusiastic and tries to keep lectures interesting and interactive. Tests are all multiple choice straight from the book, lots of memorization. Interesting class, I would recommend her

Class includes 2-pg paper, midterm, group presentation, and final. Tests are all multiple-choice and heavy on the book. She talks A MILE A MINUTE. Gives out copies of her powerpoint lectures in-class, doesn't post them online. Nice and passionate, but she grades hard on essay and presentation w/ little feedback.

Solid class, great class discussion. Ruth is easy to approach and really wants to help. Got really good feedback on presentations that was very helpful - both from the teacher and the class. Class was lively and engaging - keeps you on your toes, but in a good way. Definitely recommend.

Do not take this class if you care about grades...This professor cannot deliver a comprehensible lecture. She is all over the place. A scatterbrain. Trying to take notes is useless. Grading is biased. Be forewarned.
Absolutely the worse professor I have ever had.  As long as she is cashing checks from UW, I will never donate a penny to Foster.

This class is excruciatingly boring. Lots and lots of jargon, which is hard to keep straight. Be sure to read the textbook, especially the bolded words, the tests basically just test whether you remember those bolded words

Tests are straight forward mostly book and a couple questions on whatever else is covered outside so nothing tricky or ridiculously specific (ie memorize obscure areas of book).  She's nice and is very engaging to the class.  Grades hard on presentations and essays (80 is the median 4 essays, also grades in 10% incrm.).  Perfect scores are rare...

She teachers MGMT 401&403. If you like the type of prof. that challenges you and has high expectations from you, then she's the real deal. She respects her students, doesn't talk down to us, and she welcomes criticism and is not afraid to explain her ideas. IMO, contrary to others on this post, she is an amazing professor.
The worse instructor I have had at UW.

She's not as bad as people say she is. If Eng. is your 2nd lang. you'd better be prepared for some fast-ass talking cuz she's like a tornado all over the place when she's lecturing. You definitely need to buy the book b/c that's all she tests from. aside from that, she's an alright teacher that you can afford to take or avoid ~ purely average.
I strongly discourage you from taking this class with her.

This was my lowest grade in almost 4 years of college. It was a complete shock considering how well I thought I did. Her grading system seems to be completely random (for example giving me a 50% on class participation for missing only one class). Her teaching style is erratic & it seems like she is just "mailing" her lectures in. Do not take her!

Her grading is unreasonable low... Her expectations are unclear and she grades down on things she didn't tell the class she expected... She tries to come across as nice and friendly but it's all fake... Worst grade I have received in my 3 years of college.

All in all this was a really fun class and she suprisingly made it interesting. She likes to go off on her own stories here and there but other than that it's a pretty laid back class. Besides her stupid ass grading, I would say take her. But if you want to be safe, take it with someone else because her grading methods will screw you over!!

It's clear that she has taught this class for years, and it's gotten to the point where she is just on autopilot when she's teaching- completely dispassionate about her material or the students. Useless theory class. Just take it since it's a requisite for bschool students.

One of the worst professors I have ever taken a class from. She is very unapproachable. I went to her office hours to discuss grades, and she could not explain to me why I missed points. She is rude and I regret taking this class from her. I actually enjoyed the material, but she made the class horrible. Her grading style is biased and unfair. Plea

Ruth seems to be a very smart woman, though she refuses to listen to her students.  She stresses the importance of feedback (as a manager) yet she refuses to explain her feedback (aka: grades.) She responds to e-mails without reading what was asked, and even SHE doesn't understand her own grading scales. Too bad-she has potential to be a great prof

Worst professor I have ever had! I did not learn a thing from her lectures or homework! It was impossible to tie them back to the exams. Will not change grading even if the mistake was hers. Grading screws you over in the end. Someone who had a 55% still passed with a 2.8.  Fair? no. Avoid this instructor or you will probably hate her too...

I was very disappointed with Dr. Huwe.  She claims she is a good teacher but will not meet with students after or in between classes.  The highest grade she gave was a 3.5 even though they got 100 on almost every assignment while someone who never did any assignments still got a 2.8.  STUDENT BEWARE.  I have heard she is different for BCMU though.
Great teacher.  Fun.  Hot.
Ruth is an excellent lecturer. The info you cover in this class is all extremely useful. She can be a bit abrupt on a one-to-one basis, but I would reccommend her as an instructor.
one of the best professors i've ever had.
Dr. Huwe tests are all mulitple choice.  If you do well on this type of system.  Take her, she makes class very interesting.  Never had a "dull" day!
No Comments
No Comments

Excellent lecturer. Very easy-to-read lecture slide decks to review. No textbook. Topics covered aren't super challenging conceptually, but you need to know all of the theorems very well for exams. Exams have a high median, usually 80-90%, so there isn't a generous curve. Homework sets can be long (maybe 7-10 proofs) but are otherwise reasonable.
Prof. Novik is one of the best professors I had at UW. Extremely quick to respond to emails, great at explaining  concepts and is very friendly during office hours.
She's kind and very accessible

Prof. Novik is the best math professor I've had at UW. She's excellent at explaining quite an abstract subject and clearly enjoys doing so. Further, she's very accessible outside of class for help if you need it, and is just as welcoming and helpful in office hours. I would take her class again in a heartbeat.

Fantastic professor, first time in a while that I felt going to lectures was worthwhile. Proofs are interactive, she uses great examples and illustrations, and explanations are incredibly helpful. Lecture notes aren't provided before classes, which is a shame, but they are still helpful regardless. Overall one of the best math professors at the UW.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really helpful and understanding professor. Even though the course was difficult, going to her office hours made it much more doable and she explained topics in a very precise way.

Professor Novik is an excellent instructor. The course introduced many areas of mathematics that students go on to study after Math 300 in a way that is more useful than some instructors. She does not hold your hand in your work but provides places to start and honest feedback in a way that is fair and improves your work and thought process.

Good explanations and cares if you actually understand. Very approachable after class. Encourages people to work together and socialize. Combinatorics is pretty tricky but she does a good job of teaching it. Tests are fair and she makes it clear what topics we should know.

I'll be honest and say that the class is not very easy, but it's also not the hardest math class to take. If you need to fulfill your general math credits I would recommend Isabella. She posts her lecture notes online and the class is pretty straightforward.

She genuinely cares about her students and their understanding. She explains things in a intuitive and interesting way, with plenty of insightful examples. She is very approachable and polite, don't be afraid to ask questions in lecture or go to office hours.

Professor Novik was fantastic. You can tell she really cares about her students and is very available for help. Real Analysis is a hard class but she made it completely understandable by being very clear and answers questions. Highly recommend!
Professor Novik was great! She was very helpful and you could tell she really cared for her students. Highly recommend taking a class from her

This class was hands down the hardest course I took in my undergraduate degree in Mathematics here at UW, however she is a very nice lady and helped me out a lot. Go to office hours the minute you start having problems in the class because she needs to know. Also try to find other people you can study with because it will be a nightmare going solo.

She's just a cute old lady with an accent.  She gets excited about math and you can see her always smiling when she shows something new.  If you can deal with accents then I would recommend.  She shows difficult examples in class which prepare you for the tests

She was the WORST at explaining and always changed her answers during examples in class. She pretty much copied the entire textbook and just randomly writes her notes in class. Her tests and quizzes are extremely easy compared to the homework. I did well because I retook 125 after the AP test. She never makes sense during lecture. I don't recommend
Really insightful. Lectures were very easy to follow.

Math 126 is already a hard class. Thankfully, Professor Novik was helpful in lectures, answered a lot of questions, provided tons of practice problems for midterms, and kept a very steady pace. Lecture could be boring and the final was crap. But that wasn't entirely her fault. She's a pretty good teacher.

Fairly difficult course material; as has been mentioned, go through the material before class.  She teaches well and uses good examples, but section is probably more useful in helping students with the material.

She definitely has an accent, but once you get used to it it's not hard to understand at all. I honestly felt that attending lectures was pretty vital to my understanding the material. And while the quizzes and midterms were all very reasonable, the final was significantly harder and dropped my grade a lot even though i studied
She has a heavy accent but is pretty clear for the most part. You should learn the material before lectures, because she goes through a lot of examples so it's easy to get lost if you don't.
She is very well organized. Her lectures are pretty fast but as long as you do the work she tells you to, you'll get pretty good grades. Her review sessions are helpful.
