great prof. unless you don't follow along or do your work, you will do great in her class. she doesn't throw many curve  balls at you on tests or quizes.

Her lectures aren't very engaging and so even though she pauses to see if we need help, no one really knows or cares what's going on. Her tests are pretty easy and she is very helpful during office hours though.
She goes very fast in lectures...I was writing faster than I could comprehend! She always asked "any questions?" but the entire class would be flabbergasted. However her review sessions were helpful
Extremely confusing, lectures were useless... Learned more from my TA then her.
No Comments

I really enjoyed Professor Isaac's class this quarter. He is kind, He takes the time to provide helpful and insightful feedback on homework. I did not have any issues trying to meet for office hours or have to wait a long period for an email response. He is genuinely enthusiastic and cares about the students doing well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best English class ever taken here. Dr. Isaac is just so cool and chill. Such easy credits since his feedback is the best and his grading is not bad at all. One thing is that this class is mainly focused on participation so be ready to talk a lot every day.

I took ENGL 298. Workload was extremely light, no midterms and no final. Only one group project towards the end of the quarter. Attending class is mandatory and so is participation/ engagement. Extra credit was available. Professor Isaac is extremely sweet and understanding. I would retake this class in a heartbeat.

He is an incredible professor who is very caring and responsive. He thoughtfully addresses everyone's questions and brings in many interesting readings for class, making it possible to learn a lot. He invites guest speakers to share their insights. Truly, he is an outstanding professor, and his course is fascinating. Also, there aren't many works.

I went to a total of about 3 classes and still passed with flying colors. The content is actually very interesting for an intro but you basically learn nothing new. No exams, no essays, just a portfolio to submit with very lax grading. Not a bad teacher, just boring. Do not recommend if you want actually want to learn about education (ironically).

Professor Ikeru is a nice guy and very personable. Homework is very, very lax in this class, and Ikeru's lectures are not...super necessary to attend; you can do basically everything out of class. There are some cool guest lecturers though! This class is very much an intro and doesn't present a ton of novel information.

Very kind and caring and funny, although in person lectures felt very unnecessary. Class used ungrading, so we chose our grades at the end of the quarter based on how we felt we did in class, so a 4.0 is relatively easy. This class does have a volunteer requirement, so depending on the place you volunteer it will be a very different experience.

You can't learn anything from this class. Lectures once a week and he usually cancels the class. He just read the PPT and sometimes feels like he is not that familiar with what he is teaching. Weekly assignments are required but always been asked to write about the same thing/topics. I don't know what they are doing.

Prof Ikeru is a nice person I guess, but I barely learned anything in this class. There was only one lecture per week, and half of them got canceled. The professor would announce cancellations just an hour before class started. There were also a bunch of assignments that even he didn't seem to know the purpose of—it was a complete waste of time.

It's kinda hard to rate this one because I took his EDUC 240, but the class wasn't his. He was teaching some else's class. So he didn't make any of the assignments or anything. He is very understanding and engaging. Also only 1 class a week, but it was canceled half the time, so no one showed up. Also too much class discussion, not enough lecture
He's a chill dude who is such a theater kid. He truly loves his job and teaching so I would def take a class by him again. Slow at responding to emails though.

He is one of the most caring profs I have had here at UW, and there are a lot of them so that is saying a lot. He is flexible and works hard to make the work possible for every student. You must show up to class as group work is a large component of the class.

Attendance matters at the beginning to end since there are group presentations and projects, very flexible with schedule and very understanding, enthusiastic and funny, Mack is young and very friendly and loves his students with a passion! Get ready to read alot but the readings are very helpful in the long run!

I like how he delivers his thoughts and teaching. Lectures are useful, I believe you 'll learn something from his lectures and class materials! I had a lot of fun in his class. I gain new knowledge from the readings and enjoy reading these articles! I believe I'll bring takeaways from his class and put into practice. He is smart and well-educated!

I can see the efforts that he grows into his lectures. He is young, supportive and flexible. His lecture and he leave many positive impacts on me about learning. He did an amazing job in class preparations. He is capable of seeking a clarity in the communication with students. STRONGLY RECOMMENDED! Nice person, great teacher, fantastic instruction!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Mack cares about students' wellbeing as well. Other than offering academic assistance (multiple time slots of appointments availability can be found via Calenderly, he is happy to work with you), he is also glad to provide resources in mental health and safety areas. He is eager to assist students with achieving their goals.

Mack is a great human! He is passionate about teaching and proactive to give students feedback. Anonymous suggestions and different voices are welcomed, he will take consideration to make improvements. He is NOT a tough grader! Students are given the chance to revise their work. As long as you resubmit your work, this will get you a good grade.
Makes you read a lot, but I would say those reading are helpful. Good class organization. Passionate teacher. A little tough on grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: He was a good teacher for this class. Young, passionate about the subject, and really helpful in and outside of class.
This guy is pretty chill. 10/10 would recommend.

You can tell Charles cares a lot about what he teaches, and how it impacts his students. The course itself consists of readings at home and a short summary (200 words) before the lecture. The lecture was a full class discussion about the readings, based on opinions and the exchange of ideas. He is a great guy and showing up to class was beneficial.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Super awesome guy! He's fun, and has got a lot of great stories. The course content he selected was thought provoking and is transferable to the actions we make daily. Handles political themes with extreme nuance and care and makes a safe space for all students to share their unique thoughts.

The GOAT. Easily one of the most interesting and funniest professors I've had on this campus. Very engaging classroom atmosphere and is simply an incredibly chill dude. Regarding the course itself, work load is not that bad but could be quite some reading at certain times. However, def. a course worth taking if you're looking 4 writing creds & fun

Professor Ives was easily one of the best teachers I've ever had. He's very easy to talk to and very approachable, which helps when I had some confusion about assignments or other things. The classes are more seminar than lecture, but that helped with understanding the readings. Overall, I would highly recommend take one of Charles's classes!
He is the best! One of the most interesting classes I've taken, and it's super easy. Would 100% take another one of his classes again!

Charles is a legend. If I could, I would have Charles teach every subject. 
He is skilled at guiding conversations while allowing them to remain open-ended. 
The class has two reading + reflection assignments per week, plus a 2000-word final essay. 
Class is very, very discussion-based.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Favorite class so far! He is very encouraging and genuinely wants to hear everybody's perspective. It is a very discussion based class that always leads to really interesting topics/ideas. He is super sweet, engaging, and you can tell he enjoys teaching.

Discussion-based class, so he really encourages everyone to talk and share their ideas about the content. He is really good at keeping the discussion flowing and bringing up interesting points. Non-major, but found this class incredibly interesting. The readings were diverse and brought up discussion in my personal life.

Charles Ives is my favorite professor I have ever taken, and his class is what college is about. All the students who show up to class show up because they want to learn. Every class is discussion about the  reading assigned to it, and it always ends up interesting as most students participate and contribute. I would take any class he taught.

Charles is one of my favorite professors here, he is amazing at lecturing and guiding conversations. It's a good bit of reading but it's nothing too bad and he drops some assignments. If you talk during the class it only makes it better, coming from someone who hasn't taken a lot of PHIL classes. Genuinely an amazing class by an info-dumping man.

10/10 class and professor. Literally if Mater from Cars taught philosophy. Don't take it if you don't like participating or reading/writing. He listened to Preacher's Daughter per class recommendation, that's all you need to know

Charles was my favorite professor at UW. He makes you think about politics from all viewpoints, both left and right politics. Lectures are not required and there are 2 assignments due per week, a summary of the readings which is chill. The final is a paper but as long as you start early you can finish it easy. He is great for a writing credit!

This is the only UW class so far that I've felt pretty sad to see end. Charles knows how to teach and has a great depth of knowledge on the topic. Classes are fun and explorative. Discussions were lively and genuinely interesting. This class is a home run and will stick with me for quite some time. Thank you Charles Ives.

Charles is a great guy. Really enjoy his method of teaching. Class is outlined very clearly and workload is manageable. Classes are basically just discussions on the Republic. I found them to be very engaging and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: this class is so chill, it's always just discussions between him and us about the assigned reading that day. it's a lot of reading though (2 or 3/week) and there's an online discussion board and it kinda feels like a lot sometimes but he drops a few assignments. easy 4.0 class, just do the readings. no final exam, just a final paper.

phenomenal wonderful and fantastic professor, so funny. gave us snacks on the last day of class. lectures are marked as being crazy long in your schedule but he doesn't let them go too long, and knows how to lead a discussion to thoughtful points. very easy grader and overall a thought provoking class. already looking for ways to have him again!!
Grading is pretty clear if you do everything its an easy 4.0
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: I have taken two of Charles classes and he is such a great teacher! he offers lots of support and his class is moreso a discussion then a lecture. there is a bit of writing with one final paper but he is very lenient, he is such an awesome guy as well hearing his stories are so interesting. highly recommend his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had at uw. highly recommend it, he cares and wants you to do well in his class. his classes are discussion style which allows him to get input from the students. overall great teacher worth taking his class.
Charles is a great professor, he uses a lot of discussion-based learning which I really appreciated
Goated

It was a really interesting to experience his teaching style, clearly formed by a deeply held philosophy about human intelligence and growth. The experience still affects me and the way I think in a very positive way. Non-hierarchical, pretty much no due dates, very little structure but a lot of thinking :)

Charles was really a great teacher, you can tell he cares about the material hes teaching and how his students do in class. Attendance wasn't mandatory and class was discussion style, all homework assignments were all or nothing credit and he would let you resubmit till you got it correct (allows late work). Really overall a great teacher.
Charles is literally the best and idk why us Rate My Prof isn't higher. He's a funny and really intelligent guy. Would and am taking his courses again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Charles is by far my favorite professor at UW so far. He's very laid back and created a friendship with his students. There is a lot of reading but homework wise, as long as you try you'll get 100%. The final paper is big but he gives great feedback on the draft. Lectures are just talking about the reading and he almost always lets us out early
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Ives is really chill. He just wants you to engage with the material and you'll get a good grade. There are a lot of assignments and readings (2 per week) and they can get annoying to complete but he allows late work and excuses a couple. He is very kind and will work with you throughout the course to help you get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You read the whole republic with him and when you participate it is enjoyable, he reasonably grades and just wants to see you be a philosopher. He knows the republic well and is very helpful when you seek help.

Charles was the most impactful teacher I've had and will ever have. He prompts you to question your own beliefs and truths, as well as thinking about important aspects of our education system. Discussions are open ended and there isn't much structure, but very interesting. He is a fair/easy grader, and it's obvious he cares about his students.

Extremely open-ended philosophical discussion with your peers and Ives acts as a participant rather than a professor. He has a very unique style in which he grades you but does not actually teach you anything. There is no "lecture" but he describes classes as a philosophy student book club. I could read this material by myself and get as much out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: The best professor I have ever met so far in uw. He is not only teaching you philosophy but also inspiring you to think critically and creatively. He respects almost every idea from students.

I really enjoyed this class. I do not get where the student below me is coming from, because this class is easy. If you read the instructions correctly and do it right, you'll get an A. He wants the best for his students, you can tell from the way he interacts with us. & there are 2 reading assignments a week and a final essay!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: The grading criteria in this class are MESSED UP. If you forget or have an extra space in your citation, you get 0 for the HW which adds up a big chunk of the total grade. I cannot believe that every reading assignment's average grade is 60-70%. The TAs are also simply bad graders, often giving me 0 for mistakes that I did not make.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Charles is really chill but you may not learn a lot.

The class is beyond philosophy of education. So far, this is my favorite class at UW. The readings not only make you think about current education system, but also give insights to your own life. He grades fairly. He really care about students' opinion, and navigate fun discussion. Just take this class and enjoy,
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I hated philosophy and took this class just because I had to, but Charles showed me how great philosophy can be. His teaching style is not usual - he sees students like colleagues in a project (and respects them as such) and helps them develop their ideas without restricting them. That class might be the best one I took, and I'm a STEM major!

He cares about his students! He's very understanding and wants you to succeed. I believe he changes the structure of the class sometimes, but when I took it fall 2019, it mainly consisted of reading and discussing topics in class. At the end of the quarter we basically write a paper, but it's nothing too crazy or worrisome (and I hate writing).

Charles is literally the nicest professor ever! He deserves way more credit than what he's been given. I took his educ 210 class 2 times (you can take educ 210 up to 3 times bc topics/content change) only bc it's an easy 4.0 and the workload is so reasonable. The course counts as an I&S AND Writing credit, even though it doesn't mention W on canvas

Professor Charles is a very fun person. Though, when I entered his class I thought we would talk about current problems in education because that is what the heading said. This was more of a philosophy class. I am an education major and I thought I would learn actual problems in education. But overall, some of the readings are interesting.

As person, Charles is wonderful. He is clearly very smart, well-informed, creative, and he is pretty funny. However, Charles speaks and conveys his thoughts in a garbled and unstructured manner. The "classes" are more like a 2 hour student book club meeting with a wacky supervisor, rather than a class that is taught by an instructor.

Charles is so great, my favorite in the department. He wants you to think on your own and strives to create a learning environment for everyone. Complete the readings and interpret, you'll pass with an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The readings are kind of long but the material itself is easy to grasp and therefore going to class to discuss the reading may seem repetitive. However, the class is what you make of it, so engage in the discussion and you won't be bored! I was never stressed or overwhelmed and he is honestly easy going, friendly, and fun.

The readings were very long for each assignment, and frankly I just found the parts I needed for the questions since it was a waste of time. Charles had no idea what he was doing the entire quarter; he just talked about how there are different methods to teaching while not being able to teach a thing himself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Charles is super nice. Only 1 micro-essay per week (400 words max), and you could send the micro-essays to the grader before the due dates to see what you should change to receive good grades. Plus one group presentation (30 min total with 5-6 people). This is also a good chance for you to get W credit

different style of teaching some people love it, some people find it hard to follow his train of thought. Regardless he is very flexible and tries to cater to his students needs. Decent amount of time spent to two weekly quote collecting summaries and weekly review essays. Most annoying part of class is nerds who encourage him to make it harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Only enjoyed the class because of how easy the class is. He is very passionate about the subject, but it is difficult to really understand him when he goes off in tangents about life all the time. At most times he didnt teach us anything and the students of his class led the discussion.

First of all, he is simply not an instructor. He does not have anything planned, ever. He babbles about how much of a "different" approach he has on teaching, and never says anything relevant. Half of the class sat in the back and did homework for another class. I barely went to class, should have, but didn't since he led such awful conversations.

For his class attendance is important and is checked by answering the question of the day which you turned in on paper. He had us do readings for each class, with a short response turned in on canvas. In class he would go over those readings and talk about his life. Overall, if you want to get an A, show up to class and do writing assignments.
His office hour are super helpful

Charles has a unique philosophy of how school should work, and I think has an anti-establishment streak in him. It's almost like he doesn't believe he has the right to determine how good your thoughts are, so his class is what you make of it. Don't be lazy and blow it off; this guy's a genius and got me to see new perspectives. Very groovy.

Professor Ives is a nice man who is clearly new to teaching. During the entire quarter he only taught a few classes and left the rest to be taught by the students during "teaching week" which lasted the entire day every day ALL quarter(even the very last day). He literally didn't teach AT ALL. He also doesn't grade things in a timely fashion.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is an awesome professor if you want to get an easy A! He told a lot of stories about himself and was super funny. Just show up, read some articles and write some easy essays. You will do great if you come to class

Really cool guy who actually tries to make the course interesting and stimulating for all those who attend. Attendance isn't necessary as all the work/readings you must do can be completed outside of class. Do the papers, get feedback, & revise according to his suggestions and enjoy the easy 4.0.

Charlie is the cutest "professor" I ever met in UW. Taking his class is a strong motivation for me to go to school each Tuesday and Thursday... ^^This experimental-philosophy course is mostly discussion based so everyone is free to talk and even debate. His grading technique is also way too generous. Definitely recommended!

Charles' teaching style motivated me to get out the door every day for this class. He's dynamic in his teaching and he exudes genuine joy doing his job. He offers a unique perspective to teaching that other philosophy professors at UW simply don't have. His classes are experiments, so be open to defining expectations as the quarter progresses.

Grading criteria is super unclear, kept changing the structure of how we should should write our weekly essays, and then provided different rubrics in his feedback to justify a random grade. He rambles quite a lot during class (for most the class) which can get boring, you have one mandatory group project, he can get scattered with work/family life

Such a sweet guy. Goes off on tangents and mumbles to himself a lot, also talks about absolutely nothing for about the first 20 minutes of class. You leave not really sure what you learn but Charles is just so nice. He also lacks clear grading criteria so you never know whats gonna happen
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Charles is a super hilarious professor and he knows what he is teaching. Really nice and generous on grading. The class itself wasn't that fun but the professor is just so awesome.

Obviously has a passion and knowledge for history and philosophy, especially ancient philosophy. Keeps lectures and discussions entertaining, though his explanations may be wordy at times, it's probably because he's passionate about what he's teaching. Will work with you to make sure you succeed in the class. Overall great professor!

Charles is like an innocent little child. Has a deep affection for Platonic thought. Quirky, yet hilarious. He is quite charming, an unspoiled gem among a lackluster and uninspired Seattle Freeze. Willing to be flexible to see his students succeed. Gets excited about the smallest things. Yes, quirky, but also has a lion's heart. Highly Recommend!
Don't take this professor unless it's needed
Very unorganized, lectures are unclear

He's a very kind professor who is accessible outside of class a couple times a week. However, he is pretty disorganized, and his lectures can be hard to follow/understand. Definitely find the textbook somewhere.

Just didn't seem to know what he was talking about. Needed correcting many times throughout the quarter, and never really seemed sure of himself. Class was pretty easy, but just seemed like a waste of time. I got a 3.2 only because I forgot to do a couple homework assignments.

Prof. Ist. really struggles with communication, IMO. I often get the sense he hasn't looked at lecture slides since he gave the lecture a year before. He once spent 50min of lecture on rain gauge under-catch. Wording on HW is ambiguous and confusing. He seems personally like a great guy, and probably a great researcher, but not a great teacher.
Overall Good Professor.

Professor Knight didn't seem to really connect with the students, and it reflected in the lectures and assignments. The content was fine, but nothing could have prepared me for how irrelevant the final exam was from the class. The amount of reading wasn't too bad, but unless you memorize all of it word for word, the exam will be difficult.

Lectures weren't mandatory but if you didn't go you would probably struggle with the final. Thankfully they were all really interesting. There can be a lot of reading at times but overall it was manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Knight was awesome in so many ways. Entertaining, passionate, and kind. Participation is 25%, two essays (one graded by TA, one by prof.) and a final cumulative exam (30%). Every lecture slide is posted, but not recorded. But PLEASE attend because he is so interesting to listen to. Genuinely the best professor I've had at UW.

This is one of the best classes I have ever taken at UW. Prof. Knight is highly entertaining, and his lectures are excellent. Shakespeare is hard, but the class makes reading it way easier. I came in liking Shakespeare's works, and I know I will come out of this class LOVING them. I cannot stress enough what a privilege it is to take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Such a handsome lad. Oh yeah, also an awesome teacher with an equally awesome TA.

Jeff Knight is a great lecturer who is clearly passionate about teaching English. Even if you don't like Shakespeare at the beginning of the course, Jeff makes the class interesting and fun. I fell behind on reading a few times but the lectures always caught me up to speed. An excellent professor worth taking if you are interested in English!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jeff Knight made me love Shakespeare. He's a phenomenal lecturer who makes very dense texts approachable and relevant to people who might not even be English majors. He also appreciates Shakespeare's works as theater, not just writing, and that makes the class so much better. Be aware though: You must go to lecture and do all your readings.

I loved Jeff, and I loved this class! The only assignments are a few papers, and doing the reading before each class. Jeff is very passionate about the subject and he's super chill and easy to talk to, and his lectures are really interesting. He doesn't expect you to fully understand Shakespeare, but as long as you try that's what counts.

I def recommend this prof, he is very passionate about what he teaches and understands that Shakespeare is not easy to grasp, so he's patient plus he gives great and fair feedback. The only odd thing is that he actually has a final exam rather than just an essay. Yup, you get both, which personally I am not a fan of.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors I've had at UW so far! His lectures are always so detailed and insightful that it makes the readings all the more meaningful (and less tedious). It's the only class that has made Shakespeare make sense to me and challenges you think in contexts you never have before. Super funny and really cares for his students.
Avoid his class at all costs if it's not required
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. Jeff is super passionate about what he is talking about which for me, makes it better. All of the assignments were able to be from our perspective and he did not doc points if he disagreed with you. He is super considerate of circumstances and very nice. His class was very structured and super easy to follow.
Boring class with a boring lecture

Every other professor pales in comparison to Professor Knight's ability to teach during the pandemic. He shortened his lectures to the most important, interesting material, was flexible on deadlines, and structured the class to be accessible and fascinating. Truly one of the best I've had at UW. He made Shakespeare actually make sense.

Prof. Knight has a way of turning the most complex theoretical texts into something generative and easier to understand. If you follow the lectures and make an attempt with the readings, you'll be fine. He grades friendly (with feedback) and will usually implement a curve. Three tests, one video presentation and weekly discussion boards.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The readings are really long sometimes, but it is a class about reading theories. Even though the readings are hard, the tests are easy if you engage in the class. The lectures are beneficial because they go over the readings. He does a discussion page after every lecture, and one video presentation you pick to do on a recommended reading.
Maybe learn to how to turn on a projector and how to use Canvas before teaching any class involved with "technology".

The worst class I ever take at UW. Disorganized, not sure if he even knows how to use canvas lol. And please stop calling this class English literature and Technology, It has NOTHING to do with technology. He also gives ambiguous instructions. Overall super boring class, I would avoid it at all costs.

He sets very reasonable expectations. You may get exhausted by his volume of assigned readings, especially because they can get really dry. However, his lectures are great and he makes the class very straightforward and interesting. This isn't the easiest class to take in terms of hours required, but if you do the work, it's a great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Literally the best professor I've had at UW. Enthusiastic, interesting, amazing lectures (this coming from a person who usually skips when possible). Attendance is mandatory but worth it! Tests are super easy and the essays aren't bad as well. Highly, highly recommend.
As a creative writing and anthropology major, Prof. Knight is literally one of the best Professors I've ever had at UW. Inspiring, caring, engaging, worth all your time. Wonderful guy!!
One of my favorite professors at the UW. Really excellent lectures and good feedback on assignments. He will help you understand and appreciate Shakespeare even if you are resistant. Take his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This was my favorite class that I took at UW and I'm incredibly sad that I did not discover Professor Knight until the final quarter of my undergrad because I would have sought out other courses from him. Going into this class I thought I hated Shakespeare. Now that I am leaving it, I've learned to appreciate and even enjoy the 400 y/o plays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Loved this professor- one of my absolute favorites.  The class was fascinating and the textbook is now one of my favorites. Will probably take another of his classes. Clear expectations, readings can be dry but his lectures are not, and anything you need to know will be in lecture on slides. Strongly recommend.

Really enjoyed this class. It is his class for non-majors, and he has reasonable expectations. Class was interesting and engaging and he's funny. Got to work in the Special Collections library on a project which was fascinating. Would definitely recommend for majors and non-majors alike.

It's spring quarter now yet I find this seminar in fall so useful that I kept referring to my notes by then. Prof Knight's selection of reading is impressive, not to mention his clear and professional style. He's hilarious in a calm way and, REALLY nice if you take the class seriously.  Try to take his class even it's not your field
Amazing professor, probably my favorite at UW. Prof Knight really knows what he's talking about. Class discussions were always engaging and interesting. Attendance & required reading is a must!

Loved his Shakespeare after 1603 class.  Provided good historical background and grounded the class in the different performance approaches and media over the years.  He was very specific about expectations and gave you the tools to succeed.  Excellent professor would definitely take another class from him.

Definitely a good professor. He knows what he is talking about, gives good lectures, and knows how to be nice with workload. As long as you do any required reading and attend lecture, the class will be fun.

I loved her as a professor! Well spoken and had clear expectations in my opinion. Not a super easy class but if you pay attention, do the work, and ask for help when you need it you'll be fine. Prof is super friendly and loves to help so do not be afraid to reach out.

I disliked the lecture style. Slides were often changed mid-presentation or ignored which made taking notes or following the lecturer difficult.

Concepts were approached in weird abstract ways where the abstract methods of flux / Nernst equation was prioritized over the actual content.

Lectures rarely covered all content, so reading is necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, her lectures are very helpful. I would recommend that you rewatch some of them before test day. This class is in my opinion, much harder than 180 and 200. My one complaint is that one of our tests piled on a bunch of units, but generally, they were fair.

I honestly think she is a great professor. The grading is the exact same as the other bios but 220 is just harder content. As long as you put in the time to actually do the practice questions and review with the key you should be fine. I think what made people do worse in this class class was because of shorter tests each question was worth more.

Wastes time on random group calls during class, though they are for extra credit. The lectures go by super fast and it's hard to keep up even with iPad notes. Units don't flow into one another and jump between random topics. I 4.0ed BIOL180/BIOL200 and STRUGGLED to keep up in this class. Exams are very difficult unless you think exactly like her.
my last rating got removed i guess it was too mean... thats all i have to say. i had no trouble in 180 or 200 and this class TESTED me. avoid this prof if you can

Lectures are unorganized. Unit organization does not make sense for the type of physiology emphasized with each unit. Plus, some exams cover 2 units while others cover 5. Font on exams is like 7 point. No regrades on last exam, which they incorrectly graded for me!! No rounding above 0.5. They do not care about you in this class and it shows.

real chill prof, but lectures were a bit of a mess and confusing in a lot of aspects. her preclass homework system is surprisingly effective at forcing you to get familiar w/ content (as long as you do them). keeping up with lecture, doing the preclasses, and applying/practicing concepts yourself is really important to succeed in 220.

these other reviews are lowk melodramatic. this class is def harder than 180/200 but that's consistent across BIOL 220 classes. to do well you actually have to understand the concepts + apply them moreso than 180/200 which is why its harder. going to lecture + working thru all the unit packets (and UNDERSTANDING the key) will set u up for success

She is the absolute WORST lecturer I've EVER HAD. Slides are a COMPLETE MESS, she's so disorganized, explains in her own twisted way and expects you to understand, wastes half the class on "group calls". Instead of a study guide you get several 10+ page packets for each exam on what you should know, impossible to cover it all. This class is a JOKE

Tests are just as annoying as earlier biology classes except the content is actually difficult now, tests and lectures often have little correlation it seems, most readings require you to draw diagrams to submit which takes so much time, incredibly hard class, harder than any other intro series science class I've taken here and it isn't close.

Ruesink's goes fast during lectures that its hard to keep up. She has us talk with our classmates in small groups so many times instead of teaching the class. I dont recommend this proffesor if you actually want to learn. It sucks cause the topics were interesting. The exam questions were hard and not similar to the practive exams.

She's nice... that's all the good I can say. As someone who has NEVER struggled with bio 180/200 I was very surprised by how hard this class was. The exams are very different to the past bio courses and most of it tests you on how well you can use her weird concept maps/mass balance diagrams. Also, her cheat sheets aren't the best. Advice: Lock in

THE most unorganized lecturerer ever. Unclear notes, vague questions, and difficult to follow lectures. If you are not paying 140% attention in class at all times, you WILL be lost because her notes are THAT bad. TAs carry this class. External brains are tedious, vague, and a way of getting out of teaching fundamental material. Very frustrating!

The content is not hard. However, she piled on 5 units for a single exam when the first two had either 2 or 3 units. The practice exam packets we receive have many things we never learned in class. There are issues with the answer key. She doesn't upload her finished annotations in a timely manner, making it difficult to study.

I think professor Ruesink is great, but she definitely has a unique teaching style which is why I could the high difficulty/low quality ratings. The class is structured heavily around in-person lecture; focusing on refining your own thinking/logic and applying it to the concepts learned. If you are struggling go to office hours.

I liked the external brains, ~6 a unit that you draw out diagrams and answer very pointed questions instead of readings, which are then reviewed in class. Made test review easy. If you are not a textbook person it's very useful to do a few pictures than pages of textbook notes. Exams are short (~3 pages). My fav prof/class out of the intro series.

Wastes excessive lecture time on pointless group calls. Her slides are confusing and unhelpful, and exams test whether you mirror her phrasing rather than understand the material. The “external brain” assignments add little value, and her unconventional teaching methods would be far more effective if replaced with traditional readings.
Lectures are so pointless, she wastes so much time on the whole group call thing, neglecting actually teaching the content. External brains are pointless.

I love Jennifer!! She is such a diva and she wrote me LoR. Tests are not bad, not weighted heavy and you get a note sheet. The weekly textbook reading questions are the most annoying part but you can kinda fudge them if you're busy. loved the labs, always got out early. Pdf of the textbook is online. Hope to take another class t with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I dropped the class during week 2 just because i could tell that this class was going to be extremely hard. The expectations that she places on the class feels very unrealistic with a lot of busy work and the labs had so many aspects to it. The prof herself seems like a very nice person and a great researcher, but she should not be a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I have never met a professor that is willing to go the extra mile like Dr. Ruesink did for me. I had life events this qtr get in the way of my studies & she really helped me back on my feet when I struggled, something you wouldn't expect a weed out course professor to do. She is so approachable & provided so many study resources to the whole class.

I really liked her and thought she did a really good job teaching, which I think was a shared thought among classmates. She is also really caring and will explain a question very thoroughly. I only went to one of her office hours (w/ like 20 other people) and she remembered my name in lecture throughout the quarter. Sad to not take her class again

I honestly love Dr. Ruesink, one of the major reasons, is because she is so approachable. I felt like I could come up to her after class, or in one of her many office hours, and ask her questions. In her office hours before the exams, she would write out what you needed to know, and if you knew those processes, you would do well on the exam.

I'm going against the grain here, but I think Dr. Ruesink was a great instructor. This is coming from someone who did not do great in Bio 180 and 200; her teaching style helped me get a good grade in this class. She gives out tons of practice problems for the exams. The external brains work great for study material too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Difficult class, rushes through content, and patronizing at times. I was focused on never being wrong in lecture, instead of actually learning the content.  I put so much effort into this class for a mediocre grade. Course slides were disorganized; I was often confused on where one unit ended and the other began. The TA's saved this class big time.

quite literally the worst class I have taken as an undergrad. I took this and chem 223 at the same time and did astronomically better in the chem class, which is wild because I did terrible. She uses the same two mechanisms on every test and if you don't answer the test questions exactly how she did in lecture or how she would, you will fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures aren't that great. She rambles and goes off topic, it was hard to read her annotations, and goes too fast or too slow on certain topics. Exams kept getting harder. Highly recommend attending office hours to do well in this class. External brains were honestly a waste of time, didn't help much. There are required random group calls.

THIS CLASS WILL TANK YOUR GPA. She is the worst professor I have ever had. Her tests are impossible and there are no curves and no extra credit. It does not matter how well you understand the actual content, only the unhelpful strategies she comes up with. AVOID THIS CLASS!!!

This professor is terrible, you're forced to attend class every day and do the problems exactly how Ruesink wants, with mass balance reasoning every time. If you'd like to maintain a high GPA I highly recommend looking the other way.

External Brains (reading assignments) were very unhelpful to learning. Too many polling questions. Unprofessional near the end with the most snarky comments imaginable when students used drops in the quarter. Spent 60% of the lecture asking questions and not getting through the slides which rushed content at the end with no exam review.

Too many external brain assignments-you spend more time trying to complete them than understanding material. Ruesink and the course coordinator became increasingly rude and unprofessional as students started using drops. Spends too much making us discuss questions instead of lecturing leading to rushing content till right before an exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I was nervous bc of her ratings, but I loved 220 with her and it's solid proof that "bio intro series sucks" isn't a valid excuse for bad teaching. She goes above & beyond to connect with her students, & I even enjoyed the material I normally don't! Take every opportunity to engage with the material, even when it gets tiring, and you'll be set.

These ratings are surprising! VERY fun and kind. Accessible after lecture/in OH. Super approachable, OH were so helpful. I had a lot of questions/confusions but all were resolved at OH and labs. Some lectures were rushed due to the amount of content. Could drop 1/4 total exams. Harder course than past 180+200 tbh but still enjoyed w/Ruesink!

I don't ever write RMP reviews but this professor has been so disappointing that I am making the effort to write one. She is less concerned with actually teaching and is more concerned with people sharing out. External brains are too time consuming for the benefit you get out of them, and readings assigned are overly dense and not helpful.

Although this class was no easy A, Jennifer is very knowledgeable, understanding, and fun to work with/under. You don't necessarily need to attend lectures, but you must read every paper and make every discussion post if you want a good grade (2-3 shorter scientific papers a week). Great but challenging!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You teach yourself with vague & overly detailed/not detailed enough readings, then you watch the khan academy videos they assign to teach you the rest of the material. The tests are vague & left up to interpretation to screw you over. Lectures unhelpful and are 90% pollev questions and not real content so slides and lectures are useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She cannot teach to save her life (or yours). I am at a loss for words at how she became a lecturer at the UW. She is disorganized, rushes through content, and is very unhelpful outside of class. She expects us to know everything and refuses to elaborate on difficult content covered in the readings. I am basically teaching myself in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Clear example of just because you're knowledgeable in a certain area doesn't mean you can teach it. A 3 credit course she turned into a 100 credit course in terms of work, which was mainly pointless. AWFUL lecturer, can't even answer questions, replies with um im not sure. Exams are extremely broad, but expects "her" answers. AWFUL, DONT TAKE W HER
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: No extra credit whatsoever. Worst professor I've ever taken

Avoid this class if possible! The materials that were taught in class are completely irrelevant to what appears on the midterm. Her teaching ability is completely inabsorbable. If you want a class that gives you a headache and screw your GPA, enjoy the ride.

She's really a tough grader. The exams are insane. There was not enough time to work on most of the time, she was looking for answers that you would never think of or expect! Avoid this class if possible if you want to continue to love Biology
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If this was my intro to ecology, I would not be an EEC major. Dr. Ruesink is passionate and obviously knowledgable, but the course organization is terrible and the worksheets and exams are seriously opaque. I already had a background in the topics and I struggled with knowing what answers they were looking for more often than not. Skip this one.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is a really nice person but as a teacher is extremely confusing and disorganized. Slides are also a mess. Exams are VERY ambiguous and she grades unnecessarily hard. TAs also will tell you the answer in lab and then mark it as wrong when grading. Would not take this as a breadth class, there are better more interesting ones.

The professor isn't horrible, but the expectations are very vague (as well as 95% of the questions on exams and labs). As well - the TA's will literally help you during lab, and then mark you down on the same stuff they helped you with. They are also surprisingly picky (points) for a FOUNDATIONAL ecology course. Honestly turned me away from ecology

Class was a huge bore. The class is mostly based on the lab, so make sure you do well. Unfortunately, the lab is pretty boring. Her reading quizzes as well as actual tests are pretty vaguely worded, confusing, and hard to interpret. She likes to write a novel for pretty much each question. Otherwise, the actual content of the class is pretty easy.

I did not enjoy the reading quizzes, as the questions were very difficult to understand, and basically only enforced the reading vs. actually making sure you understood concepts.  Quiz questions were confusing as well.  However, she was really friendly and easy to talk to, and there isn't a final exam!

I enjoyed this class and got a 4.0 despite no previous interest in ecology. I did have issues with the pre-lecture on line reading questions, as many questions were worded ambiguously. In-class quizzes were easy. If you paid attention in 180, you've already covered >90% of the biol 356 material. Very little new info.

I enjoy ecology, but not when taught by this professor. Her reading questions (of which there are many) are poorly worded and ambiguous, and seem more about enforcing reading this specific textbook rather than actually understanding concepts. Lots of last minute changes to assignments and quizzes that lead to more confusion. Would not recommend.

This class was extremely frustrating.  Dr. Ruesink is super nice, but I thought her method of approaching ecology was incredibly confusing (she even got confused sometimes!).  All the exams are done with clickers, and the way she asks questions is very convoluted.
Come to class and pay attention and you will do great in her class. She understands better than any other professor how difficult ecology can be to describe. Do your best and you'll ace her class.

In my class we had two professors, the first exam had a higher than normal average and the second, which was the one after this professor started teaching was the one almost everyone BOMBED. She was unclear, there was no point to going to class because noone ever got the clicker questions right and the tests were horribly difficult.

Soooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooo confusing, clicker questions are weirdly worded and so are test questions. In some clicker questions she'll say one answer is more right than another so she'll have multiple right answers in the multiiple choice. WTF who does that??

She's so great, and extremely helpful. Just ask her if you're confused, and she'll make sure you know what's going on. She also is very integrated on campus happenings, research, etc. She pointed me to the UW farm meeting, how cool!

She tries and she's interested in how we're doing, and I like that. She listens to students. Unfortunately, her lecturing can include confusing wording and her clicker questions are in dire need of proofreading for ambiguity. Still, it's worth going to lecture, because you will learn some cool stuff.
Great teacher! Wonderful person but has very hard and constant homework... This is made up for because their are no exams or final!

She likes to have the class participate to demonstrate ideas and concepts, so her lectures are not that bad. One bad thing though is that sometimes she writes very vaguely in terms of meaning and she takes the overhead away too fast. So be prepared to take notes fast!!!
No Comments

She is a decent teacher, but not terribly captivating.  She puts note skeletons online, which is helpful for those who print out notes all the time, but not for those who take nnotes by hand all the time.  Middle of the road.

Good professor. Lectures are long and slides are dense, but he really engages with the material which makes it more interesting. Definitely recommend buying the textbooks, it makes studying and finding clear definitions of terms much easier.
The final is in-person at 8:30 a.m. and hand-written!!!

I agree with the disorganization, but he was very lenient and understanding. As long as you would write about your opinion or view and what you learned that's an easy A. A handwritten reflection is written at the end of every lecture. Many books were required BUT he goes over them. Just take notes. Very interesting and diverse.

Very passionate about the subject, really did change my mind ab some things I thought about Jesus. class was relatively disorganized but it was the first time this class was done. Reasonable grading, interesting lectures, many but interesting readings
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This was the first year that the class was offered and I think it's obvious with how poorly organized it is. The essay prompts are wildly vague yet you're expected to write four- to seven-page papers. He's a nice person and grades easy but it's just so boring. It felt more like he was preaching the Bible than teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is very passionate about what he teaches and genuinely interested in engaging students in conversation. But the assignments are poorly planned—his writing prompts are super vague and it seems that even he doesn't know what he wants the essay to be about, but then you're expected to produce a 4 page essay. His lectures can also be rambling.

Prof. Wellman is very passionate about what he teaches and is genuinely interested in engaging students in conversation. But he doesn't put a lot of planning into the class structure. The essay prompts are super vague and even he seems undecided about what he wants students to write about, but then you're supposed to write a 4 page essay from that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was interesting at first but slowly degraded into a disorganized mess. The amount of reading is ABSURD(200 textbook pgs in two days). The relevance of the reading is questionable. He didn't follow the syllabus, grading seems almost random. He struggled to remember things very frequently and I am worried he may suffer from memory loss.

Professor Wellman has been the only professor who seemed to actually care about his students. In his lectures he'd ask deep questions, and asked us to share with the people around us. If you are stuck in life, take this course. You will make it through this course by participating, and reading the materials. Would take this class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--So many papers

reviews.comment: There is a good amount of reading and writing but I would 1000 percent take this class again. The reading was enjoyable and fun to read in my opinion, it was not something that I would dread. Truly a professor that I think everyone should get to know. I am not religious myself at all and the course is not focused around that!

You have to really want to take this class and take it seriously if you don't want to dread it. There is a LOT of reading and a LOT of writing, but it's all reflection and you basically just talk about problems in your life. His lectures are good but can be long and a little boring at times. It's not too hard to get a good grade though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor wellman was great! We read a lot of books but the work was not hard and made you think a lot about your life. The class was called A life worth living and it was a truly amazing class!

Easy work but an excessive amount of it, nothing you actually gain anything from. Grades papers differently every time and unclear rubrics. Professor just talks about himself and teaches nothing. Mid way through the quarter here and wanting to drop

Signed up expecting to learn about religions, as one would. Instead, you get an arrogant professor who loves to hear himself talk about his own personal life philosophies and discuss nothing of religion. 2 hour lectures are beyond boring and required to attend in person. Grading and assignment expectations are unclear. BUSY WORK GALORE. Don't take!

Disorganized. Likes to talk about his feelings more than what we read. Whole class feels slapstick and like there's no guiding principle or body of knowledge being built. Really not my favorite. Stressful without the reward of useful knowledge.

Prof Wellman is a cool professor. He asks good questions and had great course material. 1-2 page paper due every week or so, and the final was also a take home paper. He is really passionate about what he does and what he believes in, so just show the same amount of effort and hell notice.

Lots of people liked him but hes arrogant and likes to hear himself talk. Unclear grading criteria on papers but the way the course is set up it didnt matter. It could be a problem for other courses that are graded on content. Lots of busy work and assignments due everyday in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Wellman is a cool professor and his RELIG380 class was much easier than I expected. His syllabus makes it seem like it'll be really hard to get a good grade in the class, but he is a nice grader so honestly, it's not too hard (plus he gives extra credit opportunities as well). His class will make you think sociologically about religion.

Wellman is a great, nice and very experienced Prof. He cares about his students. I took both JSIS 202 & JSIS 498 w/him Spring 16.  His lectures are amazing, and we learned so much. I am so glad I took his classes. Also, he's the only Prof. who @ end of quarter, invites all his students to his house - big diner. What a GREAT Prof. I really recommend

If you show up to every lecture and quiz section, you'll pass. Vocab quizzes every week and he sends the terms in advance. If you attend every lecture and pay minimal attention, you'll have no problem with the quizzes. 3 short essays, 1 term paper, pop quizzes, online final for 10% of your grade and quiz section participation, plus extra credit

Prof W is pleasant but isn't a great instructor. His lectures are good but most of the assigned reading had little to do with the subject at hand. Instructions and quiz q's were ambiguously worded and his explanations, when asked for help, were still unclear. He knows his stuff but it seemed that the course was thrown together without much thought.

Excellent professor! I took 501 with DR. Wellman and enjoyed a lot. Dr.  Wellman manages the 3 hours weekly seminar in super fun and productive ways. He is very engaging in the discussions and cares a lot about his students' learning and their intellectual challenges, too. I found him very kind, knowledgeable and approachable. Highly recommend!!

Covers politics, religion, and culture from many different parts of the world. Professor Wellman is engaging, and is constantly encouraging student discussion during lectures, rather than just talking at us. He isn't afraid to stir up debate, and is excited to listen to students' differing points of view. Very intellectual, thought-provoking class!
Excellent course, intriguing material and well taught by a dedicated professor.

I've taken three courses from Dr. Wellman and he's among the very best professors I've ever had the chance to learn from. Dr. Wellman cares deeply about student success, challenges students to think critically, and is an engaging and talented speaker. Take his classes, chat with him during office hours, and he will invest tenfold in your education.

Professor Wellman is a knowledgeable and interesting professor. Class material were not too hard and the discussion board was also helpful.  The professor is willing to listen to the students' thoughts and opinions and he always encouraged students to express their own ideas.

Really interesting scholar and fun person to talk to, but lectures in 202 were all over the place. Nonetheless, class is worth taking and he's definitely someone you want to talk to one-on-one or in small groups.

For me, James Wellman is the ideal of what a modern professor should be. He is there to educate, support, challenge, encourage, and foster students to reach their own best potential. He is charismatic and engaging, and somehow manages to make a 100 person lecture class feel like an intimate, socratic experience. Greatest professor at UW, hands down
Amazing human being and very good teacher. Was helpful in class and always there to help out. Also a great guy just to talk about life with. A lot of (interesting) reading though.

Though an interesting guy and clearly knowledgable, his lecture style is ALL over the place, and he spends most of class going off on tangents. Assignments were completely unreasonable and expectations were not clear. Would not take again.

Wellman's lectures often begin with historical context and evolve into meaningful interaction with the class. The open-ended approach almost always generates new perspectives, especially when students are personal and open-minded with their dialogue. W creates an environment where the course material hits home and feels relevant to real life.

Professor Wellman's lectures are a pleasure, conveying complicated ideas and theories in accessible form, while provoking thoughtful reflection. He likes to challenge students to reevaluate their assumptions, but is also very receptive to their arguments. He gives very direct and useful advice. He is truly concerned in seeing his students succeed.
JUST THE BEST GUY EVERY. SUPER-NICE AND RELATABLE AND BRILLIANT RELIGION PROFESSOR. Cultural interactions lectures can be a bit rambling, but overall a great prof.

Professor Wellman's teaching style is incredibly Christian centric for Western religions. For example, his example in lecture of what a religious tradition is: Donald Trump says he wants to make America great, which makes Americans want to be great. School shootings were his example of a ritual. His lectures are unclear and his style booming.

Awesome professor. Superbly knowledgeable about religion and highly passionate about what he teachers. You'll learn a ton about the subject matter from him and can gain excellent life and scholarly advice.
Very passionate and wants to inspire critical thinking.

Prof. Wellman is very passionate about this subject, and it shows.  In group talks, he was able to give opinions from a wide variety of backgrounds, and his comments were rarely biased.  I loved the class, it was very friendly and a great environment to speak with the prof. and students.
An amazing class and a teacher who cares about his students and wants us to learn from him, but also wants to learn from us!

Prof Wellman is a really interesting guy, you can tell he knows what he is talking about and he really appreciates when you can bring something new to the table. Also, he may seem intimidating but when you ask for help he is really nice and truly wants to help you!

Awesome class. Very interesting subject matter taught by a very funny, knowledgeable professor. Discussion based class allows for student participation and debate. This class involved a ton of reading, and his expectations for writing/arguments are high. Speaking with him one-on-one was extremely helpful for writing. Definitely would take again!
I am taking his class now and it's amazing. He makes you think critically.

If what you have to say is interesting, you'll likely get a good grade.  Lots of smaller assignments, so grade is more reflective of consistent work and not just one big final. In his lower level classes, his TAs do nearly all the grading.
amazing finals!
He was hilarious in class, and even though the lectures were almost two hours long I really enjoyed them. He did a great job making the content much less boring than it could have been.

Incredibly interesting class on Western Religion.  Class time was mainly spent discussing issues instead of actual dry teaching of religion which was interesting.  Wellman is opinionated but also welcomed others to express their opinions.  As long as you did what the syllabus asked, it was pretty easy to get a 4.0.

Wellman is the best professor I have had at UW. He is brilliant and funny and the course content was interesting the whole way through. He will change the way you see the world! I would suggest owning the textbooks but reading ahead is not necessary to do well in this class. Fairly low workload for a writing credit as well.

Great professor. Had such an interesting experience and fun time in Western Religions. Really goes out of his way to make sure his students are learning. In addition, his class discussions really expand your thinking on the topic.

Fascinating Class.  A great guy who cares about his students and really seems to value their insights. While my own beliefs were challenged he definitely created and open forum where ideas could be intelligently and respectfully discussed.
Wellman is a cool guy to talk to during office hours, he is very helpful too if you visit him. He is understanding, but is not a pushover. The research that he does is really cool.

Professor Wellman is one of the best at UW because of his interest in expanding and answering student's interests. I am not much of a talker in discussion, but he did a good job making sure everyone was comfortable while encouraging student engagement in discussion and to go beyond the classroom setting. If you want to learn, take classes from him!

Professor Wellman is great! You could tell he was enthusiastic about his class and the subject he taught, but I never felt as though he was steering the class one way or the other in discussion. He is  accessible and will do his best to challenge you with the material. He also makes an effort to really know you. I recommend taking a class from him.

I enjoy taking classes from Prof. Wellman. He challenges you and your thinking. He introduces new concepts that make you think long after class is over and he is open to debate. They are not the easiest courses but if you do what is required and come to class prepared, you will do well. I highly recommend taking a class from this professor.

Professor Wellman was one of my favorite professors at the University of Washington. While we share very different world views, Professor Wellman always made me feel comfortable enough to share my opinions and analyses. His teaching style is unconventional in a good way. He encourages participation and keeps his students energized. Great Professor!

Of all my years at the university of Washington, prof Wellman was one of my favorite profs. He asked questions that went beyond the classroom and encouraged raw and honest answers from his students. The character limits for this site limits the awesome things I could say about him. If you put in the effort, you will be set up for success.

Well informed professor of Western religions, who never missed an opportunity to push his student's boundaries and question the fundamental tenets of these traditions. His academic intentions can sometimes be misread by less academically adventurous students. For those seeking to grow in their understanding of the world, Wellman is a perfect fit.

Wellman is a professor who challenges his students and getting high grades in his courses is not easy, however, the challenge is certainly worth it. Wellman often asks tough and thought provoking questions. I really grew as a student in his courses and feel much more prepared for a career in international law.

Professor Wellman is authoritative, opinionated, and invested in his students. He challenges you to engage in class discussions (which is really the best way to learn on the liberal arts side of things). His critical perspective is what makes him such an effective instructor on American religions, and he'll push you to reexamine your own beliefs.
Wellman invited his classes to his home twice for a night of food and discussion. I was almost always engaged and intrigued by the class topics and his insight.

I have taken 5 classes with Professor Wellman. Professor Wellman's classes are fantastically easy to get A's in. That being said, they are also very interesting and I learn a ton every time. He is a masterful actor, constantly playing the devil's advocate to challenge students to think before they speak. He is a kind, caring, good man.

Prof. Wellman taught 2 of my most memorable classes at UW - SIS202 & SIS498. He is intentionally provocative and challenging in his teaching style, which may irk some students, but which others will find incredibly rewarding. Take a class from Prof. Wellman if you want to have your assumptions challenged and your worldview transformed.

Professor Wellman is a bit egotistical, he loves himself and boasts about himself and his accomplishments constantly. His lectures go off topic frequently and are disjointed,however he does have a lot of knowledge to share. Keep copies of everything, and email correspondences.

Very knowledgeable. Can be loud and wacky sometimes but it's all a part of his strange, yet entertaining sense of humor. Class is a decent amount of work, yet he is very patient and willing to answer all questions.

I've taken two classes with Prof. Wellman and they have both been favorites. He is controversial and wild, but above all knowledgeable and willing to be questioned. Nearly every lecture is a class-wide debate about religion. He knows how to make people think and how to get excited about learning about different religions. I would suggest him!!

Great group discussions- sometimes it was frustrating to try to figure out what was expected for assignments though.  Very challenging class, but worth it in the end.  He seemed genuinely interested in getting to know his students and took the class out to lunch once a week.

As an incoming freshman, I knew nothing about religion besides that from my own. The class was very reading & discussion based, and I learned a TON. I felt like I could always contribute, as long as I was able to articulate. I never felt like Wellman was pushing any "agenda", and as such I am still uncertain of his exact religious stance. Quality.

Wellman, a part-time pastor, plays the devil's advocate - while most of the books are liberal, many times he argues the neocon perspective which can cause frustration. He is enthusiastic, it is easy to pay attention in class, but he often speaks for minorities, (literally says, "I'm going to speak as a woman today") so I lost respect for him.

Worst professor I've had in International Studies. Arrogant, yet uninformed and self-righteous. He thinks he is "edgy", when really he uphold perspectives of the Middle East and Asia which are unacceptable. He speaks on behalf of minorities, various religions, and women and comes to terrible conclusions. Stick to religion, Wellman.

This teacher is extremely self self indulgent. Projects all statements (many opinion or his own world out look) as indisputable fact. Speaks for groups and religions he is not a part of, nor has ever experienced. This class was very difficult but if you are willing to struggle through all said above i would reluctantly recommend it.

Terrible. Terrible, terrible class. The lectures are really really really disorganized, there is no way to discern what he was talking about when you try to go back and look at your notes. The readings are also disjointed, the class itself had no point. He jumped around from tangent to tangent with no apparent reason and the final was ridiculous

The class itself would be very, very interesting with a different professor. Wellman is inappropriate and pompous, and has no reverence for serious subject matter. He is always lauding himself, but almost always lectures using other peoples' materials. It was so frustrating to hear him talk every week.

This is one of the best courses I?ve taken! Wellman is an awesome lecturer who knows how to engage a classroom and keep students interested in the lecture. I love how he incorporates class discussion with his lectures. He brings up thought provoking questions, so there is continually an interactive dialogue.
No organization whatsoever, and the course is a garbled mess of social and political theory with no unifying structure or theme.
WASTE OF MY TIME!
Worst class I've ever taken. Way too difficult for an introductory class. SIS 200 and 201 were nothing compared to Wellman's 202
Amazing, all around

I came into this class very excited to learn about cultures and theories. Wellman makes this class more confusing than necessary. I honestly have no idea what is going on and I do all the work and attend all the classes. HORRIBLE.

Very disappointed in his teaching. Professor uses unnecessary profanity and EXTREMLY controversial statements to engage his audience while sending them on a never-ending chase to weed out his tangents and to grasp what his point is.
If I had to choose between attending his lectures and gouging my eyes out...I would choose the latter.

This man can talk for hours and never say anything. Speaking in generalizations about society to an audience with no specific knowledge of history (which they desperately need and might hope to receive from an international studies course) is about as useless as explaining differential calculus to your cat.

Profanities could not express how much I hate this man's teaching. Rather than just teach us the material he goes on 50 minute rants with incoherent babbling disguised as intelligence. Then he tries to have a discussion in which he contradicts everything he just said. Waste of my time. Easy enough but if it weren't a degree req. I'd run screaming.

knows his stuff, good lecturer. fairly humorous. class is pretty easy-3 vocab tests, 5 pass/fail 2 pg essays. bam. lecture seems a little long, but he is hot so it is fine. i feel like i have a good foundation in xtianity, judaism, and islam.
Unlike his 201 class the reading here is mandatory because everything is based around it. Wellman is a professor that enjoys getting to know his students. He's the best I've had at UW.

Wellman is a very smart man and a good professor. lectures can be a bit dry with TOO MUCH info, he doesn't post them online so you have to go to class to get his notes. don't really have to read the books...easy ID quizzes and short papers. do well on the quizzes/papers and participate in section for a good grade. i got a 4.0 without much effort.

Incredible, introspective professor... very keenly aware of his own biases and worked diligently to assist in the combat of those belonging to his students. Fantastic perspectives on extremely important issues... very funny and entertaining. One of the best instructors I've ever had.

I like Wellman, I think he is engaging, funny, and spirited.  But if I didn't agree with him I think I probably would find that annoying.  I suspect his latest mission in life is baiting baby fundies, which is beneath him.  Still, it's a fun class which covers important issues and truths that EVERYONE should learn about.

I think Wellman tries really hard to be cool, and found myself bored. When people wasted my time by raising their hands in a 200+ person lecture I was annoyed when he answered and had a discussion. Mostly the people annoyed me rather than the teacher.

Professor Wellman was my first professor at UW and was absolutely phenomenal.  His style of teaching was remarkable- turning a lecture of 150 students into an intimate conversation.  Passionate both about his subject matter and his students, Professor Wellman even invited students to coffee after class on Wednesday to keep discussion going.

In my ten years at the UW Dr. Wellman is the BEST professor I've worked with.  He has an unmatched talent for engaging a room full of 200 people in meaningful conversation.  His lectures are always a blast--honest, funny and provocative.  He takes a serious interest in his students success outside of class.  He's a great mentor & friend.

Wellman is a good-humored professor with an obvious appreciation of the religions he teaches about (in my case, the Abrahamic). Attending lecture isn't a must--notes are posted online--but it's fun to go (bring your knitting though) and just listen to him get excited about religions. If you do the readings and write decently well, you'll do fine :D
He is very charismatic, and he goes off on funny tangents sometimes. He is very open for discussion! And open to being questioned, but be aware that he will demand that you defend your position.

I am a Comp. Relig. major so I have had my fair share of classes with Wellman. His dynamic & engaging teaching style is really to the benefit of his students. He keeps lectures interesting and engaging and has a ton of thought provoking questions. However his assignments are the same in all of his classes. Also his 205 class wasn't very well organi

Very interesting/funny man. First half of the class was excellent, although I lost interest in the second half. However, he changes his topics from quarter to quarter I hear. Highly recommended -- goes a little hard on Christianity -- which i absolutely loved -- may not be to everyones liking however

Kept class debates going while making sure that one side did not dominate.  From rumor the RELIG 205 class should be amazing too! He makes class interesting and you learn a lot.  There are papers and work to do but its awesome compared to most Prof's at the U

Great prof.  Very thought provoking.  Challenges you think and make solid statements/arguements in class.  Knows a ton and is very willing to get to know students despite the large lecture format.  Young prof and is pretty cool.
