Wellman was the best Professor I've had at UW.  Always willing to meet with students, made fair tests, had awesome discussion (even in a lecture format with 200 students). I wish all my profs were as good as him.

This is easily the best class I've taken at UW. Wellman's charismatic and interesting. He's very willing to help students out, he wants to make sure that everyone learns to the best of their ability. He gives a ton of information, but he makes everything interesting and applicable to the real world.
Wellman is an awesome professor.  Very intelligent, but still easy to understand.

Amazing teacher. The best class I've ever taken at UW. Prof. Wellman provokes the best discussion, even in a lecture of 200. He's really a great prof, his tests are fair, and you have the ability to prepare yourself for them.
shes so kawaii.
I really enjoyed this class. the professor is very caring and the class schedule is very clear.
There were very many monotonous assignments, and the class was really hard for a first language course in a sequence.

She subbed for my quiz section once; I had a lot of fun and learned lots. 102 is a little harder than 101. Pretty much the same rules. Learning a language is hard in general but she's always willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor for Korean 100 courses! Clear pronunciation + Korean handwriting, keeps my attention, and grading is fair. Make sure you attend every quiz section and lecture for participation!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: K102 was def harder than K101, but I still enjoyed the class. The biggest difference is the vocab quizzes including English to Korean, but a little more prep and you'll be fine. Kim is enthusiastic and wants to see her students succeed. Def take 102 if you want to continue ur Korean studies!

I had Prof. Kim for both my quiz section and lecture. This was very helpful due to her clear handwriting, pronunciation, and feedback. Attendance is mandatory-- if you miss more than 2 classes your grade will drop drastically. Korean gets more fast-paced as the levels go up so be ready to memorize a lot of vocab if you intend to go up to 103.

Great class if you want to learn Korean. You will get called on. Emphasis on speaking is great for learning languages in general. Didnt have her quiz section, but from the lectures it seems like she's a really good teacher. Lots of positive affirmation, and she'll always guide you if you are stuck on a sentence. Course moves fast, so study lots.

I feel that many people that have complained forget this is a language course so of course it won't be easy. If you are truly interested in the language and want to learn she is a great professor for that. There is a decent amount of homework but you have a week to do it and can finish it in an hour. The quizzes and exams aren't the hardest either.
very harsh with days allowed sick leave, even if it is a serious illness.

You can tell she's passionate about what she does. Focuses heavily on speaking practice, be prepared to be called on to read or speak. Definitely a difficult class, but as long as you do the work you'll be fine. I recommend studying Hangeul beforehand, because it's hard if you get behind on the reading part of it.

Loved it! It definitely helps if you've had some experience with Korean in the past (ex. learned hangul or have watch Korean TV), but overall the class wasn't too hard. She is more engaging in her quiz section than during lectures, but overall an enthusiastic professor. Write out your oral responses beforehand and you'll be fine.

Before starting school, I read her reviews, so I was a bit intimidated. However, her class was so much fun and I learned a lot during my Autumn quarter. I appreciate how genuine she is when teaching Korean. During the first week of the class, she said that she wanted to make Korean "Easy, Simple, and Fun." She highly emphasizes practicing out-loud!

Prof. Kim was so so nice and sweet. She cares about every single one of her students and it shows. She doesn't give harsh feedback and always tells students they're doing a good job. I had her for lecture and QS and she was amazing for both. If you're coming in knowing no Korean, you might have to put some extra time studying as it is fast paced.

Prof. Kim is a great professor and though she can be intimidating, she deeply cares for all her students and it shows in the effort she puts into lectures. The course material was difficult but that was to be expected- as long as you pay attention and take advantage of the resources she provides, you can succeed. I've taken her four times!!

The way the tests were weighted was very frustrating for their level of difficulty especially for the 50 minute quiz sections. After one quarter I felt much more confident in my Korean abilities I just didn't expect or find the workload fair. Don't expect any extra credit chances. Vocab quizzes are given during the lecture so don't skip them.

I took 4 of her classes. Homework is very straightforward. The 200 level classes are harder because there is more content to digest, it gets much easier once you have the grammar you learn in the 200 classes. Very fun class with an encouraging professor. Project heavy, but not with partners. Help is accessible. She presents outside opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class was very difficult. Unit tests every other week, multiple vocab quizzes within a week, two oral exams, and a written exam. Professor was very condescending while I was taking my oral exam. Made remarks that were completely inappropriate for a professor to say to a first year language student. She was nice to other students though...

Shes actually really amazing and caring. I was a little intimidated when I started 201 but she always made sure to comfort students & was really encouraging. The only thing I didnt like was how much speaking we needed to do, but since its a 200 level language class it makes sense. Honestly, I recommend taking her classes. I took her for 201 & 202
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Kim is so amazing! Her classes feel so warm and while you need to put in the work - it is a language class after all - she is so willing to meet and help you understand grammar and vocab. She is very sensitive to the students' needs and whether the class needs to slow down to take more time to go over a lesson point more deeply.

She is a really dedicated professor and very willing to help and care about the students, but she has the highest expectations for a 100 level class that aren't realistic. Her tests are hard, and she assigns a lot of other assignments/papers/projects. You will need to put the time in for this class if you take it.

Professor Kim is amazing! She does everything to help her students succeed, welcomes feedback, and does her best to build professor-student relationships as well as student-student relationships. There are lots of vocab quizzes, tests, and attendance is mandatory, but this is a language course so this isn't out of the ordinary. Highly recommend!

Have spent tons of time in this class. Too many tests and quizzes for a 100 level language class. She is not bad overall. Be aware there are BOTH project and presentation in this class, plus an oral exam AND a unit test during dead week. But can actually learn a lot if you are interested in Korean. Very time consuming for a VLPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: No curves on the tests at all. Schedules are not well-planned. Unit test, a presentation, an oral exam and the final exam all in two weeks. Lectures are too boring, and attendance is mandatory. We can learn much more during quiz sections.

Lots of tests on knowledge of vocab and grammar, but expected for a language class. It is helpful to see her outside of class time in her office and she is always happy to answer questions. While she seems strict, she is a relaxed grader if you put in effort. One of the only teachers I know that listens to feedback and adapts to student's wishes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Best professor you can find. Always available outside of class and happy to help. Does not judge any question. Extremely flexible and looks at review and improves based off of students suggestions. She is so funny and so precious. Everything in the class helps a lot with learning Korean and made learning Korean fun.

I love Professor Kim! She makes learning Korean very fun, and the weekly quizzes were good grade boosters. She is easily accessible outside of class and eager to help students do well. She always asks for feedback after tests and adjusts the following tests based off of what students say. Attendance is mandatory, but it is necessary to do well. :)

Professor Kim is an amazing teacher! You will learn a ton of Korean with her and make great friends in class. She is super engaging, approachable, and kind, and classes are always a lot of fun. Of course there is a lot of work in this class, but how else can you learn a language well without putting in work? I 100% recommend taking Korean with her.

I absolutely love Professor Kim! She honestly is the funniest and most caring professor I have ever had. She really listens to student's needs and try to make tests and projects fair for us. She always makes funny jokes during class too, so lecture is never boring.
Weekly quizzes, biweekly tests, project every 3 weeks, final during deadweek

Dr. Pfeiffer is an incredibly caring professor whose main concern is students engaging and learning the material. The grading criteria is crystal clear so if you complete the assigned work and follow directions you will get a good grade. Exams were straight forward and the grading was more than fair. Low stress class with meaningful topics.

Prof. Pfeiffer is understanding, helpful, and kind. Class was incredibly interesting. Each week consisted of readings, lecture videos, discussion posts, and reading response summaries + a midterm, a final, and a final paper. Midterm and final were 2 essay questions. Material was engaging. Favorite class (and professor) at UW so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: This class is really interesting and it is obvious that professor Pfeiffer is very passionate and knows what he is talking about. Attendance is mandatory and there are a couple of readings assigned each week, but as long as you show up to lecture and keep up with the readings and assignments, the exams should be smooth sailing.

There is a lot of reading but it's doable as long you understand the general idea. Do not use AI for his class. Final essay is a bit scary but it's doable as long you follow the rubric and communicate with him or your TA. Extra credit from the exam is based on how well you pay attention in class. Hilarious, lovely professor 10/10.

Learned a lot from his class. Well-respected, very knowledgeable with a sense of humor. Does great job explaining anthropological concepts and events. There are lots of reading! That's expected for an anth and global health class so I reccomend skimming or reading few sections if you can't get through all of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors at UW! Super passionate about medical anth and global health. Ya he assigns super long readings but they're for the most part super interesting. Assignments and exams are reasonable. Long lecture, but makes content engaging.
Don't use any sort of AI editing. Get ready for at least 80+ pages to read and approximately 3-hour lectures every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Pfeiffer is fantastic! Gives great lectures, assigns thought provoking content, and is flexible if you have accommodations. The final+midterm questions require you to be attending every class. The midterm and the final are in essay Qs, 5pg final research paper, and short weekly written papers on the assigned readings. Assigns 40 pages a week
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Pfeiffer is the best professor I've had at UW--super passionate and engaging, and makes you very inspired especially if you're interested in anth/public health. Very supportive and an easy-A class if you attend the lectures and pay attention. Highly recommend.
Unprofessional
Very knowledgable!
Fun CT CB b bcc

Professor Pfeiffer is hilarious and goes on tangents every 5 minutes, if that's not something you like maybe don't take him. While he heavily depends on structure from his TA, he is a wonderful professor and a super caring human being. He cares about his student's success and will accommodate you if you communicate your issues to him/the TA.
He is a great professor. Clear expectations, consistent due dates, and provides timely and helpful feedback. I would definitely take him again. Not a tough grad

I adore Professor Pfeiffer. He clearly cares about what he's teaching and cares whether or not you learn something. He is very helpful if you have questions and was very engaged with us. He gives very productive feedback. Lots of reading, but if you pace yourself, you'll be just fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lots of reading but they're very interesting and you just need to skim through them. The lectures were discussion-based and they were a little slow but inspiring. He is very passionate about what he teaches. He's very caring and accomodating– I was able to submit my final paper late.

Very knowledgeable in the field, predictable assignment schedule, clear expectations for students. Lectures could be a bit dense but always felt digestible. Cares a lot about his students opinions and health, would definitely take a course from him again!

Very seasoned in his field and considerate of course design during pandemic. Contents were quite straightforward. Grade consists of 10 reading summaries, midterm & final (2 short essay questions), and a research paper. His lecturing pace is rather slow yet deliberate, with a mildly sardonic humor on tangent events. Roughly 200 pages/ week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Midterm / Final are short answer. As long as you watch lectures and read, you will be good. Dr. Pfeiffer is a great person and professor. He is very encouraging of students interested in entering the global health field. Emphasizes public health as a branch of social justice.

Prof Pfeiffer is amazing - the dad you wished you had - full of passion + political fire about global health, stands up for what is right, and always encouraging you to think critically. He welcomes differing viewpoints and diversity, is very clear about grading criteria, and did an excellent job teaching online during COVID. Would recommend!
Loved this class with Pfeiffer. Super passionate and knows a lot about his field. Cares about students and encourages us to make a change in the world. Wonderful to talk to in office hours.

This class talks about some really interesting stuff and this prof is not afraid to say how he actually feels about certain things. He assigns ALOT of reading, but as long as you skim it you should do well in the class. Not that hard of a grader and tests were pretty fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. P is by far one of the best professors I've ever had at UW. He is deeply passionate about the subject material, but he's even more passionate about helping students learn. He has a sarcastic sense of humor which tends to keep lectures lively. There's a TON of reading for his classes, but if you skim the readings well you'll be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Week 2 of this class and there is way too much reading... im talking over a 100 pages for one portion of it. No way anyone actually reads all this. You need to be a good skimmer and be able to stay awake during some parts of the lecture. Material in class kind of seems like common sense
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: James is a great professor and he's incredibly passionate about the subject matter. Workload includes a weekly reading summary, 2 question midterm and final, and 3-5 page paper due at the end of the quarter. Gives a lot of extra credit opportunities. But there's A TON OF READING. On average the reading load is about 100 pages every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very passionate professor. All you do is read, do a weekly reading reflection, paper and two exams. Graded the exams fairly easily but there's only two questions. Offered a lot of extra credit. He was so into the topic which made it way easier to pay attention and understand the material. Definitely should skim the readings and go to class to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: All you freaking do it read! Great class, really educational and the teaching is so great, but only 2 questions on the midterm and final and the reading is so heavy!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved this class! It was the most interesting course I have taken at UW and it was all because of Pfeiffer's passion and personal connection to the subject! If you are at all interested in global and international health, I would strongly recommend taking this course. There is one midterm and a final paper and essay with long weekly readings.

The reading for this class is very heavy and can be repetitive. Dr. P. Is great though, he does current work in Africa and is very current on everything to do with AIDS research. This is a challenging class, there are grad students in this class as well, they do the same reading, but write a longer paper, be prepared to work.

He was very enthusiastic about this class and gave interesting lectures. There is a lot of reading for this class, but if you keep up you will better understand each week's topic and do well on the exams. There is a midterm, final and research paper for this class. Overall worth taking if you are interested in International health.

Great professor who genuinely cares about his students' success. His teaching breaks down hard concepts in an easy way. The class was hard, but you'll be fine if you do your homework and stay consistent. Learned a lot in this class, recommend.
Good lectures, fair tests, very approachable
Great professor. Made lectures interesting and interactive.

Jordan's cases are extremely unclear. He forgets tons of info and expects students to make the assumptions as his. How answers should be calculated is not communicated; does not do or teach clear financial modeling or allow access to his sheets. Lectures are extremely surface level and expects you already know complex ideas never taught. Nice guy

Jordan's teaching style isn't for everyone; he lectures for the entire 110 minutes (with a 10 minute break) and is using a very basic slide deck without any other forms of media. However, he is VERY generous when grading tests, so partial credit is almost a guarantee. He is also good at answering specific questions if you come prepared. Also funny!

Jordan was a great guy and teaches the material well and thoroughly. Exams and cases can be challenging, and the onus is definitely on students to work and study hard, but he gives you everything you need to be successful if you come to class and engage. Also very willing to help and answer questions if you put in the work.

I found myself having to reteach a lot of the topics when it came to studying for the midterm and final because the slides were a little confusing. However, Jordan does care about his student's progress and understanding. The cases were hard, but I would recommend talking in class rather than submitting the write-up, it saved me a lot of time.

Jordan is a nice teacher and is passionate about teaching FIN, however you'll be primarily studying based off whatever he puts in his slides during lectures and the practice problems after lectures, no textbooks. Be sure to choose good people to work on the case with because it's worth 20% of your grade. I personally wouldn't take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: his lecture style sucks, he doesnt explain how to do any of the math he just expects you to do it. He so nice and cares about his students and their learning experience it just sucks that he doesnt know how to teach finance and make it interesting.

Class is lecture heavy, but Jordan knows his stuff. He answers questions and genuinely wants to help. Paying attention in class makes it much easier to do problems. Cases were incredibly hard and made you want to cry, but they are graded very lightly. Offers TONS of partial credit on midterm and final. Office hours are too early, but a funny guy.

Young, chill dude. Just needs a lot more time to develop the ability to teach. 
There was little accessibility outside class. He requires attendance for every class, and doesn't post lecture recordings which I found frustrating as I was taking 4 classes and working a part time job. He does provide ample office hours though.

Jordan is an amazing professor! He is a great lecturer, posts plenty of practice problems, and has fair grading policies. The homework assignments are straightforward and his exams are doable. I learned a ton in his course and think he's one of the best finance professors at UW. I highly recommend you take his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ignore the poor feedback on this website - Jordan is one of the best teachers I've ever had. He cares about his students, puts an enormous amount of time and effort into his lectures, and teaches in a very clear and direct way that builds a solid foundation for future finance classes. Quick note: the cases are difficult, but they're graded lightly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I almost didn't take this class with Jordan due to all the reviews here, but I'm so glad I did. Jordan knows his stuff and wants students to learn. He's accessible outside of class, is a great lecturer, and encourages participation. There isn't much homework and he provides practice problems before the tests. I would recommend him to anyone.

Jordan's young & this is his first in-person class. It shows. Doesn't require a txtbook which is honestly more detrimental bc his lectures & assignments seem incomplete & I'm not learning. Is he kind? Yes! Does his current teaching style leave something to be desired? ABSOLUTELY. He's alright if FIN is your thing. He's got a lot of growing to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not sure what went wrong. I did my best and thought I understood the material until I got my final score back.

Decent prof; remember this was the first UW class he's taught. Nice guy + cares about the students. Not the best at explaining concepts but the lectures are two hours + dense material. Exams and group projects are tough + feedback wasn't great. TAKE THIS CLASS WITH FRIENDS. Group projects are challenging and getting a good group is key to success.
I felt I had a grip of the material until got my exams back. I studied so much for this class but not sure how much I really learned

If you love FIN as much as Jordan, take him. If you're a diff major, you'll probably struggle. He isn't the worst prof, but his lectures are unorganized and explanations can be confusing. He is passionate ab finance and cares about his students, but I think he just needs more experience teaching. In a few years I think he'll be great.

Jordan was an exceptional professor - clear grading, clear lectures, and cares about his students. All these 1-stars have to be from people who expected FIN 350 to be an easy 4.0... but it is not a marketing class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Terrible at explaining. Watch his lectures several times but he cannot teach better than some random dude on Youtube. Most stressful quarter of the entire college years. Doesn't put things in gradebook. Canvas page is very messy and confusing. Take him if you want to be stressed with lots of confusions of explanations :/
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was surprised to see only one star reviews. I assume they came from absolute bricks who couldn't take the heat. Jordan has great and clear lectures, relevant homework, and great people skills. Not to mention he throws up 150 pound dumbbells at the IMA.

I haven't chosen a concentration yet, and was v excited to take this class to see if I'd pursue finance. With that said, Jordan has made it feel impossible to like. His lectures are extremely confusing, and for being so young, his teaching style is very outdated. Worst prof I've ever had. I now hate finance. Don't take him if you have the option.

Avoid Jordan at all costs!! His lectures sucks. I had to look at youtube tutoring videos to study for my tests. His grades are never put in until like 3 weeks later. Only took him because he was the only choice for Finance class at UW. He doesn't go over any information that would actually help with the midterm. The worst professor I had at UW.

NEVER TAKE JORDAN NICKERSON FOR FINANCE. His lecture is not clear at all. He has only a few example problems that has nothing to do with the homework he gives us. I ask him to explain something in depth and he replies with "I don't know how to explain better." That's literally your job. No one in my class knew what was going on. DON'T TAKE HIM!!!!!
Show up to class, participate, and ask questions. Jessie cares deeply about the class and her students, but you need to be willing to engage and reach out when things are unclear.

i think this is a hard class for some people to garble with, it asks people to take a look at systems and race and then apply those concepts to yourself. But overall Jessie's contribution came from a place of knowledge about the unjust systems that the US is built off of. I think the class super informative
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is unorganized. Jessie is not open to opinions that differ from theirs. The grading is unnecessarily difficult. For the final group project, you are asked to pick a mutual aid group that fits the topic they give you. My group's topic literally did not exist, and then we were told we did the assignment wrong.

The class was very disorganized. Assignments were sometimes forgotten and posted just before they were due, yet they were still required. The final project, we were assigned niche topics with no choice. Our group met the rubric, but got a low grade due to a dislike of our assigned topic. Questions about ur grades answered after they were finalized.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Everything important was graded the last day grades were official/due and she refused to answer any questions regarding grading until after the grades were official. When asked about grading throughout the quarter, she was vague. Unclear grading criterias, untimely grading, and unfortunately a disorganized/uncoordinated teaching team this quarter.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super insanely hard final, but the midterms were ok. Pay attention to extra credit opportunities and go to the graded TA sections: every point ends up counting unless you're insanely good at math.
Absolutely one of the best math teachers I've had. Amazing lectures with notes, fair midterms and final.

Dr. Ostroff's lectures were amazing and explained the concepts really well. He was also really accessible outside class via office hours and very active on the Ed forum. I would definitely reccomend him!

Great professor. Clear explanations. Very active on discussion boards and answers everyone's homework questions quickly and with genuinely helpful advice. Very likeable. Clear instructions. All tests are very fair. You will enjoy taking his class.

Very knowledgeable, course was very clear. Writes great midterms, you know what to expect.
Best professor I've had at UW

One of the nicest Professor I've ever met, you don't see people like him often, especially as a Math Professor. He knows the way to teach and get everyone engaged and keep the class interesting. If you need to choose between him or any other Math professor, he is the one.
Good guy who is talented at teaching. Very good at clarifying things as well. The content would have definitely been made more difficult would it not have been for his well executed lectures.
Nice guy but I wish he covered topics in more detail, he really only goes over the most basic principles of the lesson and it makes the homework kinda hard

Profstroff was one of the best math instructors I have met. He has meticulously prepared the quarter's lectures to be clear, making sure every day ends with a clear learned topic. His exams were not too difficult and were based on what was learning in lecture. Truly appreciate this professor!

Lectures were easy to follow along with, may be hard to keep on track with the videos & hw, very test-heavy, tests were challenging but nothing you wouldn't be prepared for if you studied. I recommend doing previous tests and going to his online review session because he talks about specific tricks (that I found helpful) that may be on the test.

Prof. Ostroff had us watch pre-recorded lectures on our own time and used in-person lectures mostly as review and to further dive into the topics, which I can vouch worked really well for me. He's super engaging and funny and generally just a fun person to talk with. He's also almost scarily competent--his passion for math really shines through.

Genuinely one of, if not the most, active and accessible professors at UW. He answers questions the second they are posted to Ed. He has a great sense of humor. Course itself is easy if you put in the work. Loved his additional lecture on dots and boxes. Would definitely take again!
Extremely test heavy and curved really harsh, I've had many classmates drop it because of one mediocre midterm.

Really nice and sweet guy! Spent most of lectures going over practice problems and expected you to review the online prerecorded lectures before class which did add quite a bit of workload. Pretty good at explaining concepts and and overall great lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very exam-based: 85% of your grade is based solely on exams; 20% lowest, 30% highest, and 35% final. I don't understand why he disables the grading system on Canvas. The final are questions written by all MATH 126 professors so make sure the practice exams that you are using to study have those professors listed or you'll see some random question.

Fire professor, unironically one of the best I've had here. Great lecturer and funny guy, also super helpful during office hours. He's also flexible with letting you switch between in person and asynch classes. Just be aware that the midterms and final are worth the majority of your grade though I don't think that's his decision.

extremely cool guy! would rec the online ver. great, pre-recorded lectures and minimal hw. you can and should go in-person if you want!! pretty sure he didn't know i was asynch until the final (you take it in different rooms). go to office hours (jonah has 3 office hours a week! honestly really cool of him) and it's basically impossible to fail.
My roommates all had different Professors, after the fall quarter, I would say he's the best one. Even let me borrow his calculator on the final when I left mine at my dorm.

Sometimes good at explaining new topics, but he rarely uses actual 3D visuals(just some plain drawings) Sometimes explains things by just saying what he thinks they are, also pretty bad at writing midterm questions,write problems that never taught in lecture, which end up being like 30% of the points (I guess every math professor does this though)

Lectures often recap the pre-class videos, to the degree where you could arguably get away with not watching the pre-class videos at all. In my opinion, this isn't a bad thing: the lectures are clear and the worked examples in class are very useful. Lots of opportunities for asking questions and collaborating with others in lecture / quiz sections.
Neat straightforward lectures, helpful worksheets, helpful test syllabus material, and overall good energy!
For some reason i had a hard time understanding his pre-recorded lecture videos and the style in which he presented them.

Great professor. Clearly explains things in multiple ways, tabs out to Desmos to visualize ideas, midterms are noticeably less messed up than other professors. Chill class to just study and learn the material without too much stress. Take Ostroff if you can, and if you enjoy hybrid classes.

amazing professor :) hybrid class was online lectures & in person quiz sections -- online lectures were super great and clear! office hours are very helpful. take hybrid if u can with him. one of the best math profs at uw

Very great professor. The video explanations are very clear and the notes are easy to read. If you have a question, ask it on ed discussion and get an almost immediate response. One of the best teachers in the math department at the University of Washington. Don't miss out on taking his class if you like online classes.
Great lectures

Ostroff is THE BEST professor for Math 126. He gives the highest percentage of 4.0s (~15% compared to other professors only giving 12-15%), and is very lenient on grading (you only miss a point if you make a mistake). Online lectures mean that the average/median is lower but thats good if you watch the videos. His office hours are also fun to go to

Amazing professor, had him for hybrid section (recorded lectures in person quiz sections), lectures were extremely clear, sample problems given in lecture were pretty much what you'd need to know for the test. I'm not great at calculus, but the way he lectures is so clear. Responds to posts on Ed pretty much the second you post them. Take him!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ostroff is an excellent math instructor. His online lectures are engaging and he's super helpful in answering questions. I found unstuckstudy and ChatGPT helpful for preparing for the challenging exams. Definitely take this class if you're up for the workload.
Ostroff>>Loveless

I came in with a very weak calculus background. His explanations and help in responding to Ed questions and setting up office hours outside of allotted times when I couldn't make his normal times made a world of difference.

One thing I really like Professor Ostroff is that he always start the class with a very basic concepts and explanation to the main point of each day's lecture (i.e. motivation). Moreover, he always demonstrate a lot of examples that will be very useful in doing webassign homework and the exam problems. He made a very positive classroom environment

Solid math prof. I had him asynchronous for math 126 and lectures were crystal clear, and I'm not the smartest or best at math. He's also so accessible. I submitted a midterm regrade request on a random Sunday and precisely 3 minutes later he replied and reviewed my regrade. Phenomenal professor, phenomenal response time. You can't go wrong.

The best Calc instructor in UW I ever had. His lectures are interesting and professor himself is fun as a person. I took his hybrid session, and I never had to come to quiz section due to works in quiz section being accessible online. He has very generous grading system so it was very manageable despite being a weed out course.

The best math professor I've had, took his hybrid class and the lectures were entertaining and taught the content well, Profstroff is incredibly open to helping students and his midterms are extremely reasonable. A tough class, as all UW Math classes seem to be, but definitely not as difficult or exhausting as these classes with other professors.

I would 100000% recommend taking 125 with Prof. Ostroff. He is incredibly clear with explanations, he really cares about his students, and his lectures are super helpful; super super quick with responses through the online discussion board as well. Exam questions are very fair and he provides a tiny bit of extra credit. Thank you Prof. Ostroff!

I took Math 126 online with Professor Ostroff and I would highly recommend this course if you're the type of student who will stay on top of recorded lectures. His exams are very fair and easy to predict, I never felt that I was asked unreasonably difficult questions. I also found that 126 is much easier than 125.

Would 100% recommend taking 126 online as long as you have the self-discipline to keep up with the material on your own! Ostroff is incredibly clear, and his lectures are super helpful; also super quick with responses through the online discussion board. Exam questions can be a little unusual, since he likes to test for a deeper understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class online asych but I still really enjoyed the online lectures. Professor Ostroff was an engaging lecturer and good at explaining difficult topics. This class was hard and the HW took a while but that is true of all the math classes here. The tests were challenging but manageable if you did the HW, plus you got to bring a note sheet

Ostroff had great lectures and the homework wasn't too hard, but the midterms and finals were awfully hard. You can do practice midterms but they are also way harder than the homework, but I guess that's just how these stupid weed out classes are. In the quiz sections there is Q&A and practice midterms. The Q&A sessions were hit or miss.

I had Prof. Ostroff for hybrid math 126, so I never actually had a lecture with him in-person. That said, his lectures were extremely clear and well-done. As a result, there was never really a time where I felt like I would have needed to ask him a clarifying question, so I didn't mind the online lectures much. Great professor!

Took Prof Ostroff for two UW calc classes (124, 126). He is a great lecturer who gets to the point and is very friendly. Also quickly responds to questions whether that be on ed, email, or discord. Would highly recommend!

Absolutely love Ostroff! Everything bad I've ever heard about him had to do with the disastrous curve of the entire math department. Super helpful and explanatory. Also, he was perfect for the online format as he gave enough examples and eextra material to make up for the lack of quiz section. Take Ostroff if possible!!

After 124 and 125, I was ready to be over with the intro calc series and was expecting another horrible grade. Ostroff's class was not like my previous calc classes. I was able to keep up and really enjoyed the online format and organization. He explains concepts really well and the homework he assigns really helps with exam prep.

Ostroff was a great professor. I really struggle with math and he explained things excellently. I found that the homework could be pretty difficult and overwhelming, but that could because I am bad at math lol.

Professor Ostroff is awesome because he makes calculus easier to understand, he's very clear about what's expected, he answers questions very well, and he's just a very nice person as well. The only thing I did not like about this class was the WebAssign homework, but he doesn't control what problems are on there. But overall, great class!

This is the best math professor I have ever had. I took the online section for 126 and the lectures are amazing, weekly quizzes graded on completion, and extra credit opportunities. Jonah is very caring and very accessible (he even joined our class discord to help with questions). Make sure to do practice midterms and you should be fine.

Professor Ostroff's online 126 lectures are awesome! but just be aware sometimes it might be bc materials are out of date so you might see stuff he hasn't covered in webassign, then you might need to do while learning or read the textbook. There are also weekly practice quizzes which are graded based on completion, but not a big portion of grades.

Jonah is a great lecturer and I had no trouble keeping up even though the lectures were online. He is easily reachable outside of class and responds to emails and EdSTEM posts quickly. His teaching is very clear, I barely had to look at the textbook to keep up with the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ostroff is the best math prof I've ever had. He is thorough in explaining difficult concepts and is very helpful during office hours. His exams are brutally challenging, and there's no way around it, but he makes time for students after midterms to discuss their grades and next steps with them. Improved from a 40 on MT1 to a 59/60 on MT2!

Dr. Ostroff is an absolutely excellent teacher. His passion in mathematics as well as his thorough explanations reignited my enjoyment in math. He singlehandedly is the reason why I'm considering a Math relevant major.

Ostroff is a really amazing person but the exams are INSANELY difficult. The material covered in notes is more surface level / skimming and then test included deeper thinking and broader applications. A lot of the times there were questions that required you to recall one specific thing he said one time in lecture. Great guy, Hard tests.

professor ostroff is really nice and is good at explaining things. However the exams are very tricky and the online homework is kind of alot. it just depends if you are good at understanding math content or not. Otherwise he presents the class with alot of resources and help! you wont succeed unless you put in the work

Prof Ostroff really cares about his students and is probably one of my fav. professors. The class overall is not that bad as long as you attend the lectures. Occasionally his cats will make a guest appearance as well!

Despite the difficulty of the class Prof. Ostroff is an amazing professor. His office hours were great and he and the TAs were always willing to answer questions. The pacing of the content was a little weird, and his exams are pretty difficult, but he gives you a lot of resources and materials to work with to help you do well.

Jonah is amazing; willing to meet with individuals for specific help. He organized the list of content needed for exams and genuinely wants his students to succeed. He is the best professor I have had at UW. Exam questions can get tricky, but practice with those types of problems makes everything seem doable and more approachable.

Honestly the best stem prof I've had at uw so far. Math 126 is a lot of content and he did an excellent job of organizing materials and making it seem a lot more manageable (no wasted class time on stuff you don't need to know). Exams could be tricky but there's a whole archive of practice and resources to do well. Overall a great end to 12x

He is awesome and always willing to help you! I would recommend that you take professor Ostroff. However, since the Math 12X series is difficult you will have to put in some extra effort and time. Additionally, some of the test questions can be tricky/difficult, but professor Ostroff always is available for help.

Such an incredible professor! Math 126 is a very hard class but with Ostroffs explanations you are set! He is super caring and I would 100% recommend attending office hours he explains concepts so well and truly cares that you understand the material. Exam we’re definitely on the tough side but doing practice exams from the archive was helpful!

Professor Ostroff is a genuinely caring person who is very good at explaining things. His lecture notes are very helpful, and he is very reasonable with the workload. The course content itself was difficult, but that was just the nature of the content. He made students feel comfortable to ask questions and cared about students' learning.

Ostroff is by far the best math lecturer I've seen so far. I was initially disappointed to hear that 126 was going to be virtual all quarter, but he nailed the Zoom teaching and did a really great job visualizing concepts and answering student questions. He also has a good sense of humor, but doesn't let it get in the way of his lectures.

His lectures are very fun, and he makes the tough material of calc 3 a little bit easier. Sometimes you might not understand the content from the lecture, but showing up to his office hours will help a ton, especially if it's not right before an exam. Test questions are exactly like the homework and examples in lecture.

Amazing prof. Jonah is just honestly a very nice person and he clearly puts in a lot of thought and effort into the lectures. The lectures are structured in a way that is clear to understand. The tests are generous with partial credit if you use the right techniques. Also, he replies to emails fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The nicest guy in the world. The best at teaching. Take him if you can. Gem of this earth.

Not a math person and really struggled with this class, but Jonah and my TA were very nice and helpful. Hes approachable, funny, active on student discussion platforms, and good at explaining difficult concepts. However, 3 exams & lots of homework was challenging. Still, if I had to take a math class, Id want Jonah again in a heartbeat.
I mean, he has cats. What more can you ask

Jonah was super cool and his class was not that bad at all (the rate my professor page for him was not nearly as good before) - MATH 126 is a really difficult class, but Jonah intends to make your life easier. He answers every single question in chat, and he was always super helpful in-office hours.

Ostroff is a fantastic professor and just a cool guy too. Gives great lectures with lots of clear and useful examples. Tests are reasonable and manageable, especially with the test archive he provides.
Lectures are clear and helpful, but pay attention to examples and take notes. Most of your grade is midterms and finals, so just make sure to take the past exams as practice and you'll be fine.
The first math class I took in UW. Absolutely amazing. The homework load is not heavy and easy to get 100%. Do a lot of past papers prior to the exam and you will excel.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor, his lectures are clear and hes very nice and approachable in office hours. The midterms were tough because youre given a limited amount of time, but if you study and take good notes from lectures, the problems arent too bad.
He's great; make sure to pay attention to example problems because variations of those tend to show up on midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I REALLY LIKED JONAH, i was depressed when i took this class and still got a 3.4, he makes math126 easy to understand and his quizzes and exams are not too bad, just study and youll be fine. Hes kind of awkward but its funny, overall really nice professor I would take him again if I could. <3 u jonah

Prof Ostroff is a real good lecturer, they are clear and without unnecessary talks, 126 is totally manageable under his guidance. He proves everything so you can easily understand the conclusions. Though there are "midterms" every two weeks, but there are only three questions similar to what those in WebAssign.

Good choice especially for an online class. Lectures are long but rich and Prof Ostroff is accessible in many office hours. Homework was a bit heavy but not too bad as compared to previous classes in the series.

Prof Ostroff is a really great teacher and math 126 wasn't hard at all with him. The lectures were clear, the homework was a natural extension of the lecture material, the tests were reasonable, and best of all, in addition to regular office hours he'd also host live zoom sessions where he went over tough exam problems and answered questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Ostroff is a great professor and his lectures are clear and easy to follow. His exams are relatively difficult but if you use the study materials he provides you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Awesome lectures, and great grading system. Only gripe is that the exams were often pretty difficult, and didn't really match the exams in the archive. Just make sure you do the lectures and practice problems.

I only had Ostroff as a lecturer (exams were written by another instructor) but his recorded lectures were phenomenal. Engaging and easy to follow, even for someone like me who is not a math fan at all.
His lectures are great but his exams are really hard. do not recommend taking him unless you are extremely confident. I usually get a 3.9 / 4.0 in math but i got a 3.4 in his class.

He is a really good lecturer, but his exams are stupidly difficult. I did fine on them, but I feel like I'd be better suited if I just took another professor with easy tests. I studied a lot for each and every one of them. So TL;DR: He is a really nice guy and good lecturer, but it's prob. not worth taking him just because of his exams. I got a 3.6

Jonah is a nice guy and is really funny, but his class was pretty hard because not a ton of the homework concepts are covered in lecture so I had to teach myself a lot of the course. That said, that might be because of the strange circumstances from Covid-19. If you ask for help, though, he really does take the time to give you advice for studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: He explained the concepts really well which helped me visualize what was going on behind the calculations.

Really hard exams and no extra credit assignments. Tricky, time consuming questions on tests. If you get an average score you get 3.0 GPA if you get lower than average you get below 2.9 He teaches well but the grade you get is not worth it

Cant say I recommend this class. Maybe its not normally like this without the pandemic. But currently our exams each have three questions with one intentionally being a question that weve never seen before. As a result, doing all the textbook problems and dozens of past exams has not helped me to do well. You will be graded on your creativity.

I was surprised when I took this class with him considering his very high ratings on here. Don't get me wrong he's a nice guy but his lectures weren't anything special, not bad, but also not great. His tests however were much harder than most of the past exams and even felt borderline unfair. Not terrible, but also not worthy of a 4.8/5.

Ostroff was a good lecturer and explained the content well. However, his tests are quite hard so you got to study for them. Make sure you understand the content, not just the steps. Overall pretty good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His grading is really clear! And his lectures are great, well-structured! The exams are actually not that hard. Although some questions are tricky compared to other professors' exams, the questions are interesting!

Prof. Ostroff is a wonderful lecturer. He teaches the content extremely well. However, my only critique is that his tests are quite difficult in comparison to the other professors. I would take him again despite that, as his lectures were so well designed, making the multitude of topics in 126 cohesive. He is also hilarious!
Great.

Jonah is generally a nice person. However, he is not the best at teaching. I spent a majority of my time having to self learn the material because only about 60% was covered in lecture. And even the amount that was, was poorly explained. For the sake of your peace of mind, just take another professor and avoid suffering through one quarter.
great professor, clear lectures

I would not recommend Jonah's online Math 126 class, take it with another professor. He makes his tests overly difficult with at least one type of problem that he expects students not to be able to solve. His lectures did not go into detail or show the types of problems on the homework. He is hilarious and nice, but avoid his online math 126.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The best math proffesor i have had at UW! I feel like i learned a lot from this class. The exams are tough but he prepares you very well for them if you put in the time and effort. Very accessible outside class and on piazza.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Jonah is one of the smartest professors I've had at UW. Not only is he a math legend, he is always willing to help and answer questions. The problems he gives makes you smarter without realizing. Unlike some other reviewers, I actually found his class reasonable and quite enjoyable, though to be fair I don't usually struggle with math.

Great math lecturer for MATH126. His teaching is a little more concise for the content of the course so be prepared to think, but the way he teaches is very enjoyable and make you like the class. His exams are pretty challenging though but that also means there is room for some mistakes. I'd definitely recommend having him for MATH126:))))
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Avoid if possible. Jonah's lectures were easy and clear. However, when it comes to exams, be prepared to suffer. He was not particularly helpful in exam reviewing, only provided a few words when answering online. The fact that there were almost no past finals solving steps made everyone's final week harsher.

reviews.comment: super engaging, material wasn't difficult

DON'T TAKE HIM 1. His lectures do not explain most of the things on the homework 2. He does not explain based on the student's perspective. He skips a LOT of steps that will confuse you He is a funny guy but not a guy for your GPA
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Stroff was one of my best professors thus far, he really makes an effort to teach the course content and does it in multiple ways to help all of the students understand.

I do not recommend it at all. I understood the concepts and everything because his lecture videos were fine, but I did average or below average on tests because the problems on the tests were all new problems that he never went over. I bought the textbook just in case, but it did not help much.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: a great prof, super caring and really wants to see students succeed. hosts out of class exam review sessions the night before the exam and theyre super helpful! grading is a bit tough but you get a cheat sheet, lots of homework that doesnt really prepare you for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Jonah is the best!!! Very accessible. Lectures are concise, along with many examples. The best thing about an online class is pacing myself when to watch the lecture videos as well as having the time to pause the video and take notes / try to reason through the process. Also, this class is larger and usually has much lower medians. Take this class!

He's one of the most amazing lecturers I've ever known. However, no matter how adorable he is, the fact that his tests are way much harder than others' can't be changed. Also, this is not his fault but his curving is ridiculous. I have 90% but only end up a little bit above the median. WTF???

Jonah is a really good teacher, and is open and eager to answer any and all questions you may have. I found that going to office hours helps, as he is very good one on one, and will explain things to you until you understand it. That being said, you do have to do lots of work outside of class, but you should be fine as long as you stick with it.

He makes funny jokes that really soften the torturedness of math class. And he's really helpful, replying email super quick. Actually his class is not that hard compared to other sections. I highly recommend him and will take his other courses if possible!

He makes jokes and seems super likable, but then he makes the stupidest tests that are 10x harder than any of the other calc professor's exams and assigns literally 30+ homework problems twice per week. DO NOT TAKE.

Absolutely incredible professor! Jonah is hilarious, and many of my classmates and I begged him to teach 124/125/126 in the quarters we would need to take them so we could enjoy him again. The class is challenging for some, but Jonah is very helpful when answering questions and seems to really care for his students. Terrific guy!

Jonah is a very funny person, however the difficulty of the exams and the homework is nowhere near what he shows as an example in his lectures. So be prepared to not understand anything on the exams and homework.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is adorable, but this class is too hard and the curve is ridiculous. To get a 4.0, you have to get 99% correctness in every work!!!
Extremely good at explaining difficult math concepts. Best professor I've had at UW so far!

He was definitely the best professor I've taken for math. He was really specific about his tests and made sure his review sessions covered tricky questions for the past. Did quite well in class and would recommend for sure.

Ostroff is an amazing teacher!! His lectures could not be more clear and it's super easy to pay attention because he is actually hilarious. Also, all lectures are posted online along with panopto recordings so if you miss class it's still super easy to keep up with material.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Awesome teacher. Lectures were very easy to understand, sometimes I felt like he didn't go over enough examples as I got caught up on homework a lot, but he explains everything so well. Plenty of office hours. He also gave us 30 more minutes on our midterms than the other professors. Tests were pretty hard, I wish I studied way harder.
overall such a great professor!! his notes are clear and to the point, he explains everything so well and is funny. deadass, best math professor i've ever had.

Ostroff is a really great teacher - the best math teacher I've had at UW. He makes the concepts easy to understand, and if you don't understand, he is very accessible through online forums, email and office hours. The class is hard, as are all math classes at UW but Ostroff makes it bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: By far the best professor I've had at UW!

The best math professor I've ever had, hands down. His lectures were always interesting because he's pretty funny and he goes over so many practice problems. He also holds reviews sessions before every exam. Also, one of the only prof that shows ALL work on his answers for past exams. Exams were reasonable if you study his lectures and past exams.

Best math teacher I've had!! His lectures are always so clear since he broke each step down little-by-little. He also posted them online AND had panopto recordings. He kept the class interesting by putting spins on the math questions and inserting quirky jokes here and there. Was nervous to take this class, but ended with a 4.0!

He was a fantastic teacher, gave amazing study guides and accurate homework. He was clear about what students were being tested on and his tests accurately reflected his teaching. If you are not going to go to class make sure to panopto.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took Math 126 online with Jonah and loved it. Everyone warned me not to take an online calc class and the tests were challenging, but Jonah explains the material thoroughly and makes it way easier to understand than any other professor I've had. Bonus: His adorable cats sometimes made an appearance in lecture videos! :)

I enjoyed Jonah as a teacher. Homework doesn't always relate to the lecture, but the test sure do. Focus on the lectures near test time to get a good grade in this class. Also he can tell some pretty funny jokes and is very open to helping out students. Would recommend if you want a solid math teacher.

Dr. Ostroff is amazing! Highly highly recommend. I hope he teaches Math 124/25/26 classes because he made me actually enjoy trig which is something I never thought I would do. He is amazing and so helpful, a great lecturer. What a gem. Plus he adds great characters to story problems so that's pretty cool.

He made 308 so easy. He has the longest office hours I've seen in my entire UW life and he is also very funny. Posts all his notes online unlike other profs but I would still recommend going to class because he can really teach. I loved his nerd jokes. The only problem is that he's such a good prof no one is lost so you can't expect much curve

Jonah was the absolute best!! His lectures were so clear and understandable. He was so helpful in preparing for midterms and the final exam as he has review sessions prior! Also super helpful that all of his lectures are recorded on panopto! Hes not only a great teacher but hes just also an all around good, funny dude.

Jonah Ostroff is a Godsend. Coming from someone who does not like math, he brings so much clarity to the material we learn and is great at bringing math into a siple light. He is very accessible outside of class and hosts a study session for midterms and finals. Hilarious and approachable, 100% reccomend.

His lectures were very well put together and he made notes easy to understand. He went at a very good pace, so I never fell behind while taking notes. He gives lots of examples, which helps out a lot in the homework. He was super approachable and easy to talk to if you need help. I felt really well prepared for the exams. He wants you to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Jonah Ostroff is a god sent. He was very knowledgable on the course material and made math interesting. The notes he gave in class were perfect so there was no reason to even use the textbook. After years of math teachers who couldn't teach he really made me love math again. He also held review sessions before exams which were helpful.

Jonah's lectures are clear and aimed towards the homework most of the time. He makes lectures enjoyable and his word problems are sometimes fun to read as well. If you keep track of your work throughout the class, you should be fine. Just review your notes and do past midterms/finals & you are set to go.

Professor Ostroff is my favorite math professor at the UW. I had him for my first quarter of math and his explanations and course layout made it very easy to succeed. His tests are just what you would expect from the lecture materials; no trick questions or difficult methods that he just expects you to know or figure out how to do.

Love Jonah! He makes lectures fun and super organized. You can tell he cares about the subject and is super into whatever we are learning. The tests are pretty easy and he provides lots of opportunities to prepare. Definitely my favorite prof!
Good lectures

The Prof-Stroff! Jonah is extremely passionate about math and instruction. He's personable and extremely fair. His lectures are very well structured and he provides every resource for you to succeed. The one drawback is that his tests aren't the hardest, and people are very engaged in class, so the averages can be high. Ask about his math songs.

Try to get into his section if you can! Professor Ostroff is arguable the best mathematics professor at the university. He has good lectures and his tests are pretty fair if you do all a bunch of old exams. He also holds his own review sessions before tests, which are very helpful as well. A solid 10/10!!

I really enjoyed taking calculus 2 with Jonah. He was a very dedicated professor who really cared about helping students understand difficult topics. He also holds review sessions before tests which can be very helpful. I also felt that his tests were easy if you did the practice exams. I am just sad that he won't be teaching math 126 next quarter.

Professor Ostroff gives very clear engaging lectures. Tests are also very fair as well. As you long as you do lots of practice exams and make sure you use the study guides to study the right material, you will do fine. I'd give him a 10/10 and would definitely take his class again. If you get him, you will learn a lot and have fun in his class.

Charming and funny guy, really great at trying to make calculus easy to understand. His lectures go at a good pace, not rushing through the content or going too slow. His tests are a bit harder compared to the other math 125 profs, so that's worth looking out for.

Usually entertaining and engaging lectures. Be prepared to sink a decent amount of time into homework. About an hour per day. He does have an online homework discussion board that he maintains, so it is very easy to get help. If you can do the homework, you can do the tests. Tutorial sections are useless if you did the homework already.
He made math 120 really fun and understandable. Anytime someone would ask a question, he made sure you understood. His lectures are well worth attending, as they demonstrate the ideas well.
His lectures are rarely boring. He has great lecture notes and is very clear when explaining topics. Overall a great professor.

Seriously thank god for jonah. Made me not want to kms during math 120. He was really funny and explained everything thoroughly and clearly. He was really helpful outside of class too! Definitely go to the reviews he holds before exams. Take math with him if you can.

Jonah is by far the best math teacher I've ever had. Very clear and informative lectures with a nice inclusion of humor! He uses technology extremely well, which helps us students out immensely (in other words, he's not just going through a poorly designed PowerPoint). Additionally, he tries to make very relevant and applicable world problems!
Funny
Definitely recommend!

Missing lecture is not a good idea but you can catch up on panopto. Quiz sections is where attendance matters because they don't often take attendance but if you miss one of the few times your participation grade goes to hell.
He was clear at explaining things and always asked if anybody had any questions before moving on to a new topic. Go to quiz section, and you don't really need the course book.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He was always available to help outside of class and did his best to make the material as understanding as possible. Even in large lectures he took his time to answer student's questions, which was very helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is such a good professor! He explains the information in a really easy to understand way but he is also really cool. I think he might be the only math professor I know that included Game of Thrones and Hamilton references in a math final. Take his class if you can!

If you have to take PreCalc, do it with Jonah. He is hands down the best instructor in the math department, and makes this impossible course bearable. This class is designed to be heavy, but he tries to break everything down to easy concepts to build on. Utilize the practice problems and even the grad student tutors.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He was a good lecturer, really appreciated how accessible he was outside of class! Having all of the lectures on Panopto really made a difference, would highly recommend taking his class again!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is honestly the best professor I've had at the UW!!!

I took Jonah class freshmen year and he is so far one of the must caring and greatest professors in UW. His lectures are really good, homework may take a while at first, but then you'll learn how to study more efficiently. Not that hard to pass, but don't fall behind.

He is by far my favorite math professor. Lectures are extremely clear and his expectations are what he says they are. He's very approachable and in my opinion extremely smart. He gives daily practice problems that you can do that prepare you for future midterms but are not required to do. He knows what he is doing.

Jonah is probably one of the best professors at the UW math department. He's extremely brilliant and really cares about his students. His lectures are very funny but at times I didn't think they were as comprehensive as they could have been. I used the textbook to make up for the parts left out during lecture. Math 126 is hard but Jonah made it fun

Being honest- the math department isn't the greatest. That being said, Jonah is the diamond in the rough here. He goes through material at a good pace and is very clear. You know what to expect when you take his midterms. However, the finals are created by all of the math 120 professors so beware- this was my downfall.

One of the best lecturers in the math department. Lectures are easy to understand. He uses technology to make vectors make a lot more sense. Test are tough, but this is a calculus course, so it's expected.

Jonah   God  TAKE HIM IF YOU CAN. He is very clear, knowledgeable, and approachable and he makes math interesting and easy-ish to learn. I'm now considering applied math again because I've actually been enjoying math in his classes. A shining light in the darkness that is the math dept..

Jonah is an incredible lecturer. He is clear and concise and provides lots of examples that will help you with the homework. The homework load is reasonable. He is available for help not only through email and his office hours, but also his online forum which he updates regularly. He is one of the best professors I've had here at UW!

His lectures were extremely clear and straightforward. He provided relevant examples for every topic he taught. Attending his lectures will be a great help because he provides amazing notes that you will definitely want to refer to when preparing for his exams. Overall, Jonah and his team of TAs gave everybody the resources you needed to succeed.

Clear and concise with lectures. Stays after to answer any questions that students may have. Is willing to work with you until you understand material. Overall, the best Math 120 professor you can take at UW.

Probably one of the best professors/lecturers I'll have at UW. His lectures are so helpful and essential for doing well. He has great explanations too, and he's helpful during office hours. Definitely prepared us for the final exam too.

Jonah is one of the best math teachers I have ever had. He presents the material very clearly and is excellent at answering questions. This class made math very enjoyable to me. If you are taking Math 124-126 I would recommend trying to get into his section.

Math has really been a struggle for me since coming to college but Ostroff seems to want his students to do well. It requires a lot of work but as long as you reach out, he will do whatever he can to help. The TA I had was really good too! Quite a bit of homework, but in order to do well, you should definitely be completing it and then some!
Great professor, easy to understand lectures. The exams are difficult.
Very clear lectures and seems to be very helpful in office hours and the discussion boards.

Jonah is an amazing lecturer. He is funny and engaging and has a talent for making the material clear to understand. If you have a question he will stop immediately to make sure you understand and is very helpful during office hours. He also holds an exam review outside of class before every midterm and final, which is very helpful. #1 math teacher
Awesome!
Professor Ostroff always made lectures interesting and engaging. He is one of the best math professors I have ever had.

He is an amazing lecturer, by far one of the best in the math department! This class was really easy for me, since I had retaken it since high school. He gives about two homework assignments per week and each takes about an hour. Also, if you ever need help and can't make it to his office hours he will schedule an appointment at a time you need.

Took him in my freshmen year. Although I took calc before, he explains concepts really clearly and is easy to understand. He's quite humurous too and keeps the lectures interesting. He really cares about students and holds review sections and answers questions in class. Great Professor.

I've been fortunate enough to have him for two classes, and I absolutely love him! He makes learning fun, has a great sense of humor, and grades fairly. Definitely recommend his class to anyone and everyone!
Jonah is AWESOME. I loved his teaching style and he is so so smart. He provides lots of sample problems and exams and if you do them, you will do well.

Overall, really awesome professor. His lectures & examples are very clear cut and he keeps it interesting by cracking a few jokes once in a while. Definitely expect WebAssign homework, but he's always very reasonable about the time to turn it in. Midterms are hard, but you are in college!!! He's one of the best math professors here, take advantage!

Jonah is one of my favorite professors so far. He is very clear with his lectures notes and the examples that he provides in class. WebAssign is how he gives homework, and I believe that it is a decent amount of homework if it is spread out. Midterms and Final are fair if you do the homework and do a lot of practice problems.

He is very clear and organized in his lectures and shows helpful examples. The exams are hard mostly because they are long, so you need to really understand the material and do lots of practice exams. If you can do the problems quickly you can do well on the exams. The medians were about 70% . I would recommend him because he is a great teacher.

Jonah can relate to students amazingly and has a strong sense of humor. Lectures are perfectly clear, and while midterms are hard, the strategies he expects to solve his problems are completely reasonable. He gave out 4.0s to the top 10% of my class, only requires 90% on HW for full credit, holds his own review sessions and is easy to talk to.

Jonah is a great professor. I went into this class expecting it to be harder than Math 125, but I did way better in this class than in 125. He sometimes goes really slow and messes up a lot but he always offers extra help and it very nice about it. The tests were manageable and if you get an A on one of the two midterms you'll get an A class

Jonah is an amazing math professor. He cares so much about making sure all of his students succeed, providing lots of resources for studying and learning all the material for exams. That said, his exams are pretty tough. Definitely a time crunch, and there aren't very nice numbers. Other than that, I'd definitely recommend him.

Absolutely love Jonah. He's one of the most clear, understandable math teachers I have EVER had. He's one of my favorites. My boyfriend got him the quarter after me, and he loves the class too. He's an awesome professor, and super laid back. He's always willing to help, and his explanations are awesome.
Hilarious and enthusiastic professor, did an awesome job thoroughly explaining concepts. He was very dedicated to the success of his students.

Jonah is definitely the best teacher for Pre-calc at UW. He uses new technology for his lectures, is clear when explaining concepts, and his awkwardly hilarious personality makes class fun.  However, the homework is pretty hard but fortunately the midterms are easier than the homework.

I'm currently auditing this class, meaning taking it to prepare me for 124 not for credit and I could not recommend this class more. After dropping out of 124 within the first week because I felt like I didn't understand calc well enough this professor has restored my faith and love for math. Show up, take good notes, and you will succeed.
Jonah is so nice and If you see he teach the class, take his.

Jonah is an amazing teacher who genuinely cares about how you're doing in his class. He has a great sense of humor and explains the concepts in an easy way. Make sure to pay attention in lectures, take good notes, and practice old exams in preparation for midterms and the final.

I got a bad grade in this class but it is entirely my own fault. Jonah was an awesome teacher and he actually cared about how you did. Make sure to study. Just doing the homework will not cut it. And don't leave studying for the last minute either. Always available outside of class and on the forum so if you have a question ASK!

Funny and enthusiastic (but not overly so) guy, which made math somewhat more enjoyable. His lectures and explanations are very clear.  Does lectures on his iPad and uploads notes to his website, so it's okay if you miss classes sometimes, although it can be difficult to understand what steps are happening without attending lecture. Tests are fair.
Jonah's great! He's super helpful and explains everything really well. He's also really adorable. Definitely a great math professor to have.
If every math teacher were like Jonah, the world would be a better place, hands down. He is perhaps the best math teacher I've ever had, and is in general just a cool guy to talk to.
Jonah is the greatest man ever.
