Hands down the best math professor EVER! Unlike some other math professors I had in the past, he can actually understand and help students with their struggles in calculus. I got a 4.0 with a fair amount of study, wish he could be teaching 125 right now...

He is a really fun teacher to be around, maybe because he is young. He is very clear on lectures. The only downside is that he is a lefty, so you have to wait until he finish writing to see the notes. Other than that, he is a really great teacher.

Ostroff is the best professor I've had so far. He is always enthusiastic and helpful, and you can tell he wants you to succeed in the course. Also, the way he explains the coursework is thorough and easy to understand. 11/10 would recommend this prof.

I was one of those artistic people who would say "I hate math" every other day. It's thanks to Jonah that Calculus and I became friends. Seriously, Jonah is the best. I wish all other math professors were like him.
Jonah is a very cool and helpful Professor. He looks and does his math something like the young version of Albert Einstein. I would recommend his class.
Jonah is such a great professor! He makes lectures interesting and he tries to make the examples a bit more relatable. Definitely wish he was teaching 125.

Jonah was an awesome professor--one of the best I've had so far. He genuinely loves math and therefore presents the material in an enthusiastic way. He is able to solve/answer problems from different angles if a student is having difficulty understanding. He is also funny which made lecture more enjoyable. I recommend him hands down!
Coolest professor ever. He is so funny that I actually enjoyed going to class sometimes and his explanations are great too. Definitely recommend him for calculus.
Best math professor I've ever had! He's completely dedicated to his students understanding the material and is genuinely excited about teaching! Very approachable and a fair grader. Take his class!!!

Hands down, the best math professor at UW. The material is hard but Jonah made it engaging and exciting. His tests do not try to trick you and are extremely fair. He genuinely cares about his students. The first 3 weeks are demoralizing but it gets easier. Homework load is heavy and the math study center is your friend!

Jonah is by far my favorite professor at UW I think I will ever have. Even though I'm not the best at math and this class was difficult, I absolutely loved going to lecture. Jonah is very funny, enthusiastic, smart, and is a great teacher.

If you have Jonah, you are blessed. I have not taken math in a very lonngggggg time prior to his class and was worried at my ability to succeed but even without touching the ebook, and just attending lectures, I did way beyond imaginary! He is just so clear and takes baby steps before advancing, is so active on the HW form, and so easy to talk to.

Take Math 111 with Jonah!! He is a great, easygoing professor and he really cares about his students. If you ever have questions about class, exams, or homework he will answer your questions almost immediately on the online forum. Class averages tend to be in the 90s, but if you just go to lecture and take notes you will do good! Easy 4.0
Jonah is the best!

Jonah is AWESOME. Best professor I've had yet at UW.  He really cares about the success of his students and puts in a lot of extra time and effort between his discussion forums and extended office hours before tests. His lectures are very informative and he gives lots of examples. You always know what's expected of you! He's a great teacher.

Best professor I have had at UW, or in most of my other schooling. Very knowledgeable and so so interesting. Jonah is a great person and does his best with curves so everyone can do their best. His creative examples and home recorded songs make his class the best!! Would love to have my next math class with him.

Jonah is the best math professor that I have ever had! He made calculus enjoyable and easy to understand. It is obvious, he has a great love for the subject. His lectures are easy to follow, and his grading methods on tests are great. Also, he is very understanding with any problems you may have with the course. Plus he writes his own math songs!

Great professor! He has an amazing sense of humor. I took him for precalc and now taking him for math 124. If you come to class and do the homework you will do great the average of midterms in his class is usually around 80% at least in 124 its been around there. His grading is really nice too the lower midterm is weighed less than the better 1. :)
He was simply the best! Very understanding and truly wants his students to succeed. A refreshing change of pace from some of the other professors at such a large, public, research focused university.

Jonah is simply the best. Not only is a fantastic teacher, but he actually made me enjoy math lectures. The homework may be significantly more difficult than anything you've ever experienced, but worry not. His tests are pretty easy. 10+ for his office hours too. Go to them. My only complaint about Jonah is that he isn't teaching 125!!! Miss him!!

If I could take Jonah for every math class, I would. I knew most of the stuff already due to HS calc but still went to office hours/class because he's such a great guy. The worst part about him is he's not teaching 125 next quarter.

Best math professor that I could have asked for. He's hilarious and super nice. He is probably one of the only math professors that actually has way too many students show up to office hours because he's so helpful and easy to talk to.

Jonah made me love math! He is hilarious and I honestly felt he wanted to help you! If you could get Jonah as a professor I am positive you would learn something new. Great guy, even better professor!
He is a very good professor. He is really funny and he makes going to math actually fun. He is really good at his job and his lectures are really helpful.

Jonah is the best math prof. He is funny, helpful, and really nice. He really wants to make sure that everyone understands what he's teaching. Also, if you use the discussion forum on WebAssign it's REALLY helpful! USE IT! and TAKE HIS COURSE! He's a great guy

Lots of homework for this class, Dr. Ostroff does whatever he can in the lecture time but that usually isn't enough so Office Hours are encouraged. He is very helpful since concepts and homework can be difficult at times. Overall, not as bad a class as people make it out to be, just a lot of time put in.
AMAZING teacher! Very helpful! Class was VERY hard, had to put in a good 4 hours a day on homework, but Jonah made this class a lot more fun that it would have been!

Young, quirky teacher. Made class a little less boring with his pokes at humor. Very hard material and homework but the midterms and final were not as hard as the work. Spent a lot of time doing homework and had to go to CLUE a lot. But I ended up very happy with my grade and his teaching in general. He was the right guy to teach the class.

Jonah is a great professor. He tries to help his students as much as possible (it's the math department who doesn't give professors much leeway). He interested in math, and always has time to help his students. HIGHLY RECOMMEND. ATTEND ALL LECTURES.

Awesome teacher. He is probably the best math teacher there is out there at the U. Always looking out for the students and extending office hours to discuss grades and other concerns. Material is tough, but it's nice to know the prof cares and acknowledges it's tough as well. Love him and I know anyone else who takes his class will too.
If you ever take a math class, take it with Jonah. I hate math, but I at least can manage because Jonah is the professor. Very funny and is very helpful. would recommend.
He is very good at explaining the concepts in math 120. Moreover, He goes over a lot of examples, so don't ever skip class!!

He is probably the most helpful professor I have ever had! Any question, any time of the day, he is there to answer it! and me, not being so great at math he is the professor I needed. This class on the other hand, is not my favorite. I spend 5 hours each night JUST doing the mandatory homework... Its not Jonah's fault though. overall, HES GREAT

Really friendly, awesome guy. He's good-humored, he stays up late answering questions on the forum, and he has interesting and funny relevant stories during lecture. I'm really a fan of him, I think he's a great guy and great professor. Super hard class but that isn't his fault, it's just heavily condensed material.

Really great teacher.  It is difficult to keep up with the class, but that's the nature of the material and not a teaching issue.  He actually makes math funny and entertaining, and he is quite friendly and approachable if asked for help.
Great teacher that will help you really achieve a good grade if you actually pay attention in class. He goes over a lot of examples, so don't skip class!
Has really clear expectations, his lectures are engaging and provide everything you need to know, the best professor you could take.

The instructor is not very responsive and tends to engage more with fluent English speakers, making it harder for others to get help. Limited communication affected my understanding, and improvements in accessibility and equitable interaction are needed.
Kai come back to uw!!

best bio prof i've ever had. he's very nice, funny, and accessible outside of class. loves smash bros and kpop lmao. his exams are pretty easy and straight foward. his lectures are amazing so if you just watch and review you will be fine. he rarely uses poll everywhere so you can miss a lot of classes.

Kai was a great prof. He was both hilarious but professional and made lectures overall enjoyable. He was quite accessible out of class with his office hours. His exam were difficult for me but if you are able to study the lecture material and do his provided flow diagrams its quite helpful for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Kai is the best

I tried to take this class w a different prof before and literally could not handle the amount of work. But Kai really explains well and wants to make sure you understand. Def would suggest him if ur not the best with bio but need the credit
I am not interested in Kpop but still found his lectures to be extremely instructive. He was always clear about the content that would be on his exams, and was responsive to questions.

Kai is the best professor I've ever had! I highly recommend him, made material easy to understand and always provided good examples of the concepts. You have exams every other week which can sound daunting but he provides practice exams and study sessions beforehand which is extremely helpful. Ask questions, he always has good answers and listens!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor and nice guy. Lectures were clear and helpful. Despite being a 5-credit class, I only had 2-3 hours of homework and studying per week since the tests were easy.

Kai is one of the best, if not THE best, professors I've had the pleasure of taking at UW. I highly recommend his class to anyone as it was interesting and digestible. You can tell he really cares for his students and his work. Take LOTS of notes from lecture and study the study guides a few days before an exam and you will do amazing!
BEST PROFESSOR EVERR this class was very exam heavy but kai was amazing

omg I love kai. he made the lectures SO FUN and interactive and genuinely just such a funny and caring professor, he explained things the best way and made it easy for us to access him outside lecture. the class itself was not easy, but I think if it were another professor it would have been harder. you can really tell how intelligent he is.
I have loved Bio118 with Professor Kai! His lectures are super interesting, and he explains all the content clearly. I absolutely recommend this class!!

The professor makes lecture surprisingly interesting and will tell you exactly what you need to know for the exam. If he says to memorize something then he means it, and it will be on the exam. Also, attend office hours before exams because he goes over important relevant information.

He is an ok professor, but I think the majority of the reviews are written by K-Pop fans because that was all he really talked about (aside from content). The way he spoke about the exam made me think that they would be pretty simple, but our grades came out for the first exam and it definitely wasn't as easy as he made it seem.

Kai is easily one of the best professors I've had at UW. He is very passionate about biology and it shows through his teaching. He's also very approachable and readily available to answer questions. I have taken 2 classes with him and would take more if I could!

Kai is the nicest professor at UW. If you have the opportunity to take one of his classes, you definitely should. He's always willing to help outside of class time and offers many opportunities to learn effectively with his office hours, review lectures, and review sessions.His tests are fair and only based on material from lectures, no surprises.

LOVE KAI! He's an amazing professor who truly cares about his student's learning, is very enthusiastic and knowledgable about the course material. I took this course in the summer so there was a lot of content in a very short amount of time and Kai made the content a lot easier to comprehend. I would totally recommend taking his course if you can!
Best bio lecturer I've had!
Best bio lecturer I've had

professor kai, and the whole bio teaching team, have been so amazing. they're all knowledgeable and have lots of patience in answering questions and explaining them. lectures are clear and interactive. i highly recommend going to lectures everyday and participating. by far one of the best teams out there!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's so fun to listen to and makes you actually want to listen and participate. It is heavily dependent on you studying as there isn't homework, so make sure you know the material before the exam. He gives so many opportunities to study before exams, office hours, and study groups.

Kai is a brilliant professor and 100% worth taking. Exams are very straightforward and although there are not a lot of practice questions written by him, there is enough practice overall and if you understand the material well enough you won't need any other practice questions. He is also an extremely open guy and feels like a friend.

Great professor. He has a sense of humor, but he still genuinely cares that students learn. I haven't had many professors with both of these qualities. The way he sets up his lecture notes is clean and concise, and as long as you keep up you'll get something out of his class.

As an international student, I have to say that Kai is one of the BEST professors I have ever had. He's caring, understanding, and he always tries to make his lecture entertaining, but the most important thing is that he actually knows what he is talking about, and it even makes sense for a person who doesn't speak English as their first language!

Kai was an amazing prof! He explained concepts well and offered many options outside of class for study sessions and questions. There is a lot of content to study and all of the exams are in person (worth 80% of your grade), but one exam can be dropped. He does group random call, for extra credit, and has you discuss with your neighbor a lot.
Professor Kai made lectures fun and he broke down the material really well. By far the best course I took this quarter!!

Professor Kai is my favorite professor I've had this entire quarter. He has two help sessions per week to review content. BIOL 118 covers a lot but he does a great job of making it easy to understand and interacts with his slides. He is super nice and super caring and easy to reach out to. You can tell he is passionate about the subject.

One of the best instructors I've had. I would HIGHLY recommend joining all of his lectures because they are super interesting and clear. Class content is dense but Kai is great at setting students up for success with exam guides, practice exams, and Piazza.

Professor Kai has to be one of the most caring and enthusiastic professors at UW! He really does care about his students because he is clear on what will be on exams and does his best to make sure that his students understand the course content. Lectures are easy to follow IMO. He always starts his lectures with a Kirby picture haha.

Kai is a caring and empathetic professor who takes a lot of the stress out of the weed-out class environment. The concepts are broken down in an easy-to-digest way and I would highly recommend everyone who takes BIOL 220 to take it with Kai. Easily one of my favorite professors at UW.

Kai is a fantastic professor who aims to make lectures as engaging and interesting as possible. He obviously cares about his students and brings enthusiasm to lectures. Exams are very much lecture-based and tend to be much easier than practice problems. This leads to high averages while also being pseudo-curved, so keep that in mind.

Absolutely adored having Kai as a prof this quarter. Funny & overall caring. Explanations were clear and cohesive. Class organization was great. Flow diagrams --> very important to succeed!! External brains function almost as a flipped classroom model and can be time-consuming but are important as well. Would absolutely take another course w/ him!

Great lectures, funny, clear expectations. Uses a lot of flow-charts and visual diagrams on tests(which don't work well for me, hence not the best grade, but I'm in the minority there). Made lecture engaging. External Brain's are necessary IMO, do them!!!

Favorite biology professor ever. He is an avid Smash player, as well as KPOP fan, and hilarious overall during lectures. "Bettles." 

Unit packets aren't super helpful for studying, make sure you just practice your flow diagrams and really understand the concepts. Once he accumulates a few old exams to use as study material, those are more useful.

Really cares that you know and understand the material. Lectures are easy to follow and the material that you need to know for the exam is clearly stated. Would totally recommend taking a class with him.
Kai 10/10 best prof at UW.  You try and you will succeed.  Top tier explanations
Amazing lectures, very enthusiastic. Definitely not an easy class, but it's interesting and Kevin puts his soul into it. Easy to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great professor and extremely well spoken! Goes through lecture really fast, but it is definitely necessary so that he can cover all the content. Intimidating at first but is actually really funny and kinda shy in his office hours too. Definitely would take again!!

Professor Zatloukal is one of the best instructors I've had so far at UW. He is able to make relatively complicated concepts a lot more digestible and intuitive. I would highly recommend you take him for 311 specifically, as he is extremely knowledgeable and engaging on the subjects covered.

Kevin is knowledgeable and a good teacher, but the course structure hurts learning. In two classes the format was the same: weekly quizzes based on hw, yet graded hw arrives the night before quiz with no answer keys. There's no time to ask questions to actually learn from hw before quiz, and TA feedback is often unhelpful.

Kevin is a good lecturer and very knowledgeable, often providing insight from anecdotes regarding software development, which helps emphasize the importance of the concepts taught in class. However, since there is barely any programming involved (for AU25), it can be hard to see the real-world applications of the lecture content.

Good at lecturing. Kevin seems to care a lot about teaching, but he is quite stubborn about it. Weekly quizzes were alright imo, but often contained several mistakes that needed to be corrected. Feedback on homework and quizzes was not helpful, very generic. The things you learn in this class do not feel applicable outside of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He watered down the course so no one could cheat, there's no real homework and your grade is mostly determined by weekly quizzes and the final. Most of the stuff you “learn” is made up and I reckon isn't even really used outside class. For a software development class, there's literally no coding, which makes this class utterly useless.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Takes quizes this quarter, and maybe only this quarter. He's emphasizing on tests rather than improving teaching skills or students' understanding!
My man glazes Kevin 24/7 whenever his name comes up in our conversations (which is embarrassingly often). Other than that… no comment.
I'd show up to lecture even if I wasn't enrolled in his classes, the GOAT

hottest uw cs professor would go to lecture just to hear him talk. however this course was just mind numbing, incredible amounts of busywork and weekly quiz's in place of a midterm - i'd rather just have the midterm
weekly exam??
Confusing homework and tough quizzes every week.

He is very nice and understanding with any situations that may arise outside of class. Grading is tough on homeworks but sets the standard for exams. Feedback is always good too. His handwriting sucks though, it is nigh on illegible at times.

Kevin is very direct in his communication, which makes it easy to plan my workload. Unfortunately, his explanations are sometimes too abstract and one-sided. They need more examples outside of numbers, letters, and logic. TA feedback usually regurgitated instructions, making them a waste of time to read. Go to office hours and use the Ed board!

Such a great professor, even better as a person. One of the best professor I have ever had. The knowledge he posses on the materials he teaches is inspirational and makes you want to do better. Genuinely cares about the students and their situation, their perspective. Being a super accomplished person, he always wants others to do better.

Great professor. I've never had a professor as easily accessible as Prof. Zatloukal. His lectures are interesting and engaging. Tests are fair. HW can be tough, and grading can be a bit harsh, but overall quite manageable compared to other CS courses.

The professor skipped useful practice questions for homework ON PURPOSE and never gave us the answers. He said we would get "reference sheets" for the exam since we can't bring our own notes (other professors allow notes), but even with the test tomorrow, we still don't know what will be on these sheets or how many questions to expect on the exam.
Great lecturer and incredibly intelligent guy. Although his lectures were fast, he answered questions very well and was very organized outside the class. Tests were very reasonable.
Great lecturer but super nitpicky grading. Final was tough. Also very inspirational person. Great stories & background; I aspire to be like him one day!
great lecturer, good vibes all the time, and everything is straight forward for you to put in effort to get a good grade. Also amazing skin, need to know is skin care routine.

Kevin was a great lecturer. He had very dense, fast lectures that made them valuable to go to. A lot of support was available outside of class and he lived on the ed board. Content isn't too challenging, and the workload is fair. He's a very knowledgeable prof that you should take if given the opportunity.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Professor has a very smooth, calming, and angelic voice. Also pleasant to the eyes. 
100% recommend for asmr

Course content covered is a little much but absolutely doable, especially if you go to lectures. The lectures are high quality and understandable, and the only distraction is accidentally being hypnotized by Kevin's comforting voice.

Not that great of a lecturer, goes extremely fast so its very hard to understand him, often had to watch lecture recordings even after going to class. Not very helpful when asking questions, answers questions on Ed fast but it doesn't feel like he really answers the question. Very few practice resources for the tests.
Homeworks are graded harshly, but imo there is just too much content covered in this class
kz da goat

Kevin was great! I had to rewatch the lectures often to understand the content fully. Sometimes he would go fast, but the lectures/assignments were made well and built nicely off of each other. I did much better when I started early and went to office hours. Lastly, watch out for the final (Make sure you study and get good sleep).

- Great, clear lecturer, explains well, pauses for questions - go to lecture!!
- Replies fast on discussion board, tho sometimes get the feeling he doesn't always read thoroughly before answering
- May be slightly intimidating, but he just may not give off a very casual/outgoing/smiley vibe, has a sense of humor
- Fair final based off section/hw
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Knows his stuff. Opens each class with a joke, so you won't miss anything coming a few minutes late. Lectures on the faster side and occasionally talks about his programming experience. Has big, angel-like eyes.

This guy is an amazing, funny, and humble teacher. Genuinely a teacher that knows his stuff in and out, and goes of out his way to help students. I've had a great experience in 331 and would recommend anyone to take 331 with Kevin. Truly a goat.

Not to mention he's extremely fine ngl (stunner in person tbh)!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
He is a highly intelligent individual with a remarkable sense of humor. It's a pleasure listening to his lectures. This class is fast-paced and hard by nature, but you can definitely learn a lot from it. 
I have also never seen a professor answer questions on the online discussion board more frequently than him.

Kevin is a great professor and is always willing to help students with any questions. He is a true expert in the field too. However, I would suggest planning out around 12-15 hours a week on the course; it's hard to get a good grade and requires lots of time. Exams aren't too tricky--medium difficulty. HWs are much harder, at least the written part

I took 331 when he first redid it in Spring of 23. It was definitely difficult and took a lot of time (pulled many all nighters), since then I have heard it has gotten significantly better (less time consuming). His version of 331 was the most helpful class towards my internship. Great lecturer, lots of hw, hard tests.

The workload of this course is heavier than I think. In the last two weeks of 331 I gradually understood the meaning of all the things we did this quarter. He cared about his students and wanted his students to succeed. He gives you not only the skillset to make you successful, but also a vision for your future. Love Kevin!
Love him. Period.

This is the hardest class I've taken so far... however, as a teacher, he is very respectable and caring. I had a private post for some bugs where he kept responding to my questions for over two hours and after sending him my code files, debugged it and wrote me paragraphs of explanation about where I went wrong. Highly recommend.

top notch theory professor. amazing lecture and course quality, and spends more time answering questions out of class than the tas. 331 with the new structure is still a little bit wobbly as he is testing out a new set of homeworks and exams, some that are pretty long and a lot of work. highly recommend him, is one of my favorite allen school profs

Honestly, really difficult class for a 300 level - lots of work and not a lot of time for them and since its the first quarter with the new structure, the HWs and grading are unclear at times. However, the support for this class is amazing. the TAs are so helpful (I've never had a better TA set in my life) and Kevin answers on Ed so quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly great class despite the amount of work. He's a prof I found to really care about the topic he teaches. I never seen a prof respond to nearly all hundreds of messages he prob gets per day within 24 hours. It's a tough class, but considering how other tough CS classes are structured, he offers a lot of support. Tough love and all that

This class has been restructured this quarter and is experimental. The class is hard and definitely requires a huge time commitment and sleepless nights, so it really should have come with warnings. That being said, the prof definitely knows his stuff, and there's a lot of priceless info he teaches: changes my paradigm. Prepare to suffer but learn
Would give a 1 but he's handsome af
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Be prepared to not be able to sleep and do anything else besides your homework for this class.
Very strict about any late work, unclear lecturer, very long homeworks. Not much else to be said.

Super hard to understand how/when the examples on the lecture relate to homework, super vague homework instructions, EXTREMELY nitpicky grading despite the vague instructions. Expect to spend more time on this than any other class if you want a decent grade
As someone new to CS, I enjoyed his lectures and learned a lot :)

I've taken Kevin for both 311 and 331 now, and he is an enthusiastic and great lecturer. But at times he talks about the material at such a high level that you are bound to be confused. Grading is super nit-picky and tests are all HARD and too long to actually allow you to finish. But you won't fail with him as long as you show your trying.

He is a nice person who is ready to help you. But his lectures are really boring. It feels like he just "talks" throughout. Many people sleep half way through. Also, the course content is very ambiguous so it might be because of that. Overall, I really like him as a person but not the course and the style of teaching

He is a nice person who is ready to help you. But his lectures are really boring. It feels like he just "talks" throughout. Many people sleep half way through. Also, the course content is very ambiguous so it might be because of that. Overall, I really like him as a person but not the course and the style of teaching
Not a comp sci student, just sitting in on some 331 lectures. Easy on the eyes ;)

Lecture don't really help with homework assignments, going to office hours is so helpful. 1 homework assignment a week but it will takes you hours per problem. If you wanna do well on the exams, practice every single homework problem and go over section problems. Questions on the exam are identical to homework problems.
tough grader. you don't need to go to lectures, but you need to go to office hours and quiz sections because assignments are hard

He's a very good lecturer but he seems to rush through difficult and crucial materials like DFA minimization or converting NFA to DFA which requires me to review them through other Youtube videos. His Final is quite tough if you don't have a solid understanding of the homework.

311 is a tough class. The material is hard and the content moves way too fast. But none of this was Prof Zatloukal's fault and he did his best to make sure we understood everything. The homework was hard but excellent for understanding the material. The exams weren't easy, but we were well prepared and set up for success.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Kevin is a very good lecturer (more than just a soothing voice :-P). HW was time consuming however it makes up 60% of the total grade. Midterm and final exams were brutal but as long as you attend lecture and have a study group you'll be fine. Curve is better than you think.
I love Kevin. A real awesome teacher and I want to take other classes with him again. He sounds different in office hours than during lecture. 10/10 prof!

Only 8 home-works for the whole quarter. Gives an entire week to finish the homework. Attend the lecture and you'll be able to do the hw. His lectures are well structured and he takes time to answer every questions. The midterm and final were in class but the questions were very similar to the hw and the practice problems !!no surprises :) !! .
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Kevin is an excellent lecturer who made the course content clear and easy to understand. I genuinely enjoyed the class and I would happily take another with him!

Average 15-20 hours a week on homework for this class for myself and everyone I know. Between that and my other classes I don't have time to study so I'm flunking my midterms in other courses. This person will single handedly ruin your gpa. Most of the time spent on homework is trying to understand what the question is asking, rather than learning
Zaddy.
The lectures were full of him just writing out long equations and manipulating them by hand. If there is anything profound about Quantum Computing, he didn't express it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Kevin's voice is really soothing, and he is pretty funny. Nonetheless, his lectures sometimes are quite confusing and hard to follow tbh. The materials are interesting but Kevin's delivery might not sell them Additionally, the class can be quite frustrating for you if you care too much about points, believe me, the curve be nice and you'll be fine!

He definitely gives hard tests and homework compared to other professors, but explains concepts decently well though he talks really fast. Grading of 311 can only be described as "wack as hell" as it is so arbitrary where you lose points on. Kevin also adds a lot of supplementary side material into his slides that just confuse people.
Good professor
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really liked Kevin's lectures. His lectures are clear and I think compare to other courses, the pace of the lectures is not fast at all. Kevin is very nice during the office hours too. The curve fo the class is nice.

Kevin has a soothing and angel-like voice and his pitch is calming in that it usually goes really high up at the end of the sentence. I like him, but as for lecture, I do not understand anything and clearly I got annihilated by the tests. It is a hard class, and I don't think he does a good job teaching it.

Grading felt pedantic, and sometimes arbitrary. Lectures covered all the material, but often move through material way too fast, and never emphasized any part of the material than others. Some of the most critical subjects had almost no time spent on them, and his way of lecturing gave no indication of their importance. Overall, quite confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Kevin gets through the lecture material when he is supposed to and clearly has a deep understanding of all the topics covered in 311. At times it can be difficult to focus because he has a very smooth voice. The tests were moderately difficult but there was adequate preparatory material. Homework is very time consuming but it is possible to succeed
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Avoid for CSE311, takes off points even if you follow conventions taught in class. If you go into office hours asking why you lost points for something covered identically in an exam review two days earlier you'll just be told, "its only a few points". Those few points add up when it happens repeatedly, so unless you dont care about grades, avoid.
Dr. Z is a phenomenal person and outstanding instructor. He's a true expert in the field and will leave you hungry to learn more. I strongly recommend taking his classes whenever possible.
Absolute beast. Would take any class he's teaching. He's interested in making sure you learn, has incredible in industry and experience, is a humour savant and all round legend.

What I appreciate about this instructor is his willingness to help, unlike other professors who seem super nice at first but when you ask for help they either ignore the emails or say they can't help. Hard class like any other class, but he does his best to help

Kevin is the man.  He left the industry to teach at UW and he's extremely knowledge both about theory and how to practically use it.  He has a plethora of stories from the trenches and I would definitely take one of his classes again.

Pretty chill for a CS professor. His lectures are very clear and he follows his PowerPoints very closely. He explain the concepts very clearly. It seems like he only teaches 331 in the summer, but maybe that will change. Pretty typical for CS at UW. Best class to take after CSE 143. I STRONGLY suggest you take this before 332, because it is useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The course content was hard itself, but he gave clear and straight forward lectures. The exam questions were very often from his speech so COME TO CLASS (there was no recording). He is an expert in his subject. He gave prompt and really helpful email replies during the entire quarter. Hard exams but generous grading. Amazing instructor, Hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: One of the most well-controlled lecture halls I've been in. People actually participate and the 2 hour class flies by.
easiest A of my life, who cares about the rest.

this class is required for first-year transfers or anyone applying to the major it is manageable once you get used to the weekly flow biggest downside is strict participation with assigned seats and you can be marked absent if you do not engage even if you show up work is easy overall and your ta can really affect your experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
A lot of people expect INFO 200 to be more closely related to informatics / programming - which I understand is where the conflict surrounding it comes from - but I do feel that equity courses like these are genuinely necessary for everyone, in every field.

You get what you put in - the class is incredibly thought-provoking if you want it to be.

The class was easy, but a bit tedious at time. Very heavy on lecture and participation--attendance is graded. The information was interesting and I enjoyed Professor Wes a lot, but I wish we spent more time with them actually lecturing and learning and a bit less on group reflections.

We did all the homework during class, so there was barley any work to do outside of the lectures or sections. Attendance is mandatory, but all you have to do is google slides, submit journal entries, easy weekly online quizzes, and other small assignments. There wasn't a final for the class either.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Weekly quizzes, no mid terms or finals. Dr. Wes is an understanding professor, leading engaging discussions that are always interesting.

Wonderful Professor. Dr. Kim is very caring and inspirational, inspired me a lot and make me want to peruse in Informatics major. Completely changed my life, one of the best class I've ever taken. I feel connected to people, and I was motivated a lot. Appreciate Dr. Kim's support throughout each assignment and reading. Highly recommend! Easy 4.0

I like the class overall just be ready to read. It's important to attend lectures because most of the material we're graded on is covered there. The class is very easy, but it didn't feel like an informatics course. I was expecting to do things related to informatics, but instead, the main focus is on reading the books and showing up to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the easiest classes I have ever taken but I also learned nothing at all. You have to read a book and take quizzes on it but we barely talk about it during class, so it seems disconnected. The activities we did during class seemed like pointless busywork too. Professor Wes is extremely nice and understanding though.
Very discussion-based lecture. Weekly quizzes are okay. Overall an easy class.

One of the easier classes I've taken at UW. Dr Wes is ok prof. but the class overall felt like an extensive gender study / intersectionality class rather then 'research methods' Class is consists of discussion (Online / Inperson) and lots of reading and annotations. Dr Faucette the TA is chill but both section and lab DO NOT need to be this long
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Search up what black boxing in a tech context means. We are not allowed to say black boxing “bc we can't use black or white in this class” even tho there's NO racial affiliation at all. As a liberal some insane things have been said in this classroom. Asian women are fetishized bc ppl think Black is associated w Black men and White Asian women? wut

Dr King is very chill. You do need to go to class and pay attention (you get graded on it), but class is pretty easy. Lots of people in here complain about the class being "too woke," but understanding socioeconomic effects of information tech is literally the whole point of the class bro :| take technical foundations if you want less woke

Easy 4.0, if you show up. Almost entirely graded by attendance, and even then TA's look around to make sure ur paying attention for participation points, so take from that what you will. However, the content is interesting and you get to collaborate and talk a lot with other students. Dr. Wes knows what they're talking about.
was calm. chill fr.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy A but so boring and useless with mandatory 2 hour lectures twice a week and a quiz section. Only talked about racism and pronouns. No informatics and I haven't learn a single thing. Every class: 30 minute "mindfulness activity", 30 minutes making a slide in a group and the rest of the time is discussing social issues like bias with classmates.

The class had little to do with information system technology and foundational skills; it was rather focused on mostly the societal implications of AI systems.

The class itself was very straightforward, and quizzes and projects were no exception. Lectures were relatively boring.

Class was solid overall. I feel like we got a solid touch on the potential negative outlooks on AI through the lectures and the book. I just didn't care for the amount of time we had for our final, which was a group project that was with our whole lab section. We didn't start until about 5 weeks before finals and there wasn't a lot of direction.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Cannot understand those who give 1.0 or 2.0... Wes King is a great Professor in general. If humans can get rid of their electronic devices once in lecture and actively follow up with the lecture content...It's not that boring and useless...

Dr. Wes is a great human, who takes their students into consideration. This class had barely anything to do with informatics, and the time we did spend touching on it was to review a book. Lectures were spent doing ice breaker activates that were unnecessary and didn't teach anything, and our group project was very glazed over. Easy A though!

What a waste of time. Attendance is mandatory for two hour lectures where the professor rants about topics that have absolutely nothing to do with informatics. The quizzes are very hard because they include questions about specific details mentioned in a video or book or a comment that the professor made a week ago in lecture. Don't take this class
This class was a clusterfuhhhhh. Look, I'm liberal and all that but like the other student said, I HATE the things they talk about. It was very agenda-driven with almost zero informatics.
wouldn't want to take again

Participation is not mandatory but you would want to be there to collect artifacts for assignments anyway. The professor is chill, caring for students' social life and academic understanding/advancement. Assignments are easy, mostly just reading, giving your take on the topic, and discussing with your peers.

One of the easiest 4.0s I've gotten, however you need to attend lecture because of Wes's policy where you turn in your devices. Wes didn't explicitly state this at the beginning of the course, but if you don't turn in your device you will not do well. Assignments are easy and you don't need to pay attention during lecture, I just did homework.

I liked taking this class with Dr. King! I feel like any 2 hour lecture will be sort of boring, but I always found the content interesting. I loved the assignments in this class and overall it was a great experience. It was an "easy" A with interesting assignments. By far I most enjoyed the group project.
Dr. Wes is an incredibly kind person, but the lectures are so confusing and random. I have no idea what half the topics have to do with Informatics. I'm not complaining, though. Easiest A ever.

I am halfway through this class and I still don't know what "informatics" is. The class starts with turning in your electronics followed by a guided meditation. In class activities are unorganized, the only reason you should attend lecture is to have artifacts for your peer portfolio, but it's an easy A. Too many discussions about race and gender.
Dr. Wes is a caring professor who wants students to do well. I love how they bring up social issues in courses and for elective courses (like their internet dating class), this professor is great!

Wes is a nice person, but fundamentally fails as a teacher. Disorganized, has unclear expectations, and makes the class way too easy. Terrible at explanations of topics. Makes no effort to discuss readings or explain them.

I had lots of issues with the way Dr. Wes taught research methods. They seem to be a good teacher but had very, VERY confusing assignment guidelines, which sometimes contradicted lectures or readings. I will say Eli Wachter was an excellent TA, very nice person and clarified a lot of my questions - if they are still a TA, take them.

Most of the lectures felt like gender studies with a side of research methods when it should've been the other way around. For the final, our group basically relied on the two examples that we were given, because nothing from lecture helped at all. Os Keyes was an awesome TA, though. Labs with Os were more interesting and relevant to the class.

Wes is very passionate about info but went off topic frequently to more gender studies/social issues topics. Lectures were boring and unnecessary--everything you needed to know was in the textbook. Wes doesn't give tests or quizzes, which I appreciated for an intro info course. Labs were dedicated to the major projects which was nice.

Professor King was an okay professor, but lectures felt very repetitive and disorganized. They were also gone for like 2-3 weeks for conferences/COVID, so the TAs did half of the teaching. INFO 300 is a messy course and should be redone because it doesn't teach you much. The TAs were AMAZING and taught me a lot in quiz section. Shoutout to Os Keyes
The focus on social problems in this class is what convinced me to major in Informatics. Not too difficult but very insightful course.
Weird class. Easy but not super interesting. Nice teacher but I HATE the things they talk about. I'd take another prof for 200 instead.

He's a great guy and all, but what extremely killed it for me was the midterm paper in this class. I only got a 1.5-point boost on a paper I resubmitted. The professor and TA did not communicate how many points someone would get back for resubmission. That honestly felt like a waste of my time.

Felt like the professor did not put a lot of effort into this class. Lectures were regularly uploaded late even if they were recorded over a year ago. Participation assignments were busy work and usually had nothing to do with class content. TAs were helpful to teach content, I learned the most from them. Other than that, it's an easy class.

Dr. Wes takes the study of informatics and turns it into gender studies and social awareness class. I really wanted an informatics class and we learn just about the strangest things. Textbook is a compilation of random stories with spelling errors. Assignments are super easy but have nothing to do with informatics, take the other info prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: professor is very enthusiastic about invertebrates. labs and field trips are very fun, but after lab drawings and worksheets can take a while so don't fall behind. tests are pretty easy and you get a bunch of cheat sheets.

The class content was not hard at all, he did have midterms which were fairly easy as well. However lectures were long and difficult to get through. There would be random days that will have in class activities that are graded so attending would be smart.

There was a decent amount of homework which got tiresome halfway through the course. Labs are fun, but there is a lot of things to cover sometimes. The lectures are SO boring, but you have to go bc there are random in class assignments. Slides have no words on, just read the textbook and you'll be fine. Not enough organization for a zoology class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I did a study abroad program run by Ken and took 433, and cannot recommend him enough -- he was an entertaining lecturer, graded fairly, and emphasized getting used to reading academic papers and presenting in front of the class which I found helpful. He's a smart, funny, charismatic guy and I would love to take more of his classes in the future.

Quizzes are extremely difficult - you need to know the stuff or you won't pass.  All he does in lecture is drone on for two hours (better off studying material in your own time). Very poor communication (no office hours for prof or TAs, organization of field trip planning is unpredictable and short notice, does not reply to emails). Good luck...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible at lecturing, I can literally read the slides on my own and learn without wasting time with his boring lectures. good luck trying not to fall asleep. So much work for so little credits, very unorganized and unclear. Ken should just stay as a researcher and not a professor, he is probably the worst I have had.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Don't take this class. 1.5 hour incomprehensibly boring lectures (which are mandatory with no makeups), 3 hour labs twice a week with no organization, terrible communication of expectations, and nonexistent class structure. This class will frustrate you to no end because the professor is incompetent at his job. AVOID!!!!!!

Lectures are long but he clearly states what information is important and what may show up in the exam. There's A LOT of assignments in lab but it helps in studying what's discussed in the lecture. Lecture and lab exams are not that hard and have high averages. I got 4.0 and only attended live Zoom in the first half of the quarter.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: If you're thinking of taking Bio 434 to get it out of your way, don't. The work load is immense if you have other STEM classes going on. And the work is based on textbook, but the catch is, the answers are not even in the textbook, you're better off googling in the first place. Also, the sheer amount of work you have to do in class and lab is crazy
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I learned so much in this class. Thayer is a great professor and as long as you follow his code during lecture you will do great.

As someone who had no experience coding, I was intimidated going into this course, yet it turned out to be my easiest class. Thayer makes the class EXTREMELY beginner-friendly, with TA's always willing to help. No exams, only a final group project that consists of joining datasets (it's pretty short and easy with a decent group)

Lectures were clear and posted online (both recordings and slides) and optional readings provided. Easy to ask questions during lecture. No tests, grade is mostly the weekly assignments, weekly review, and final group project + extra credit opportunities. Many check ins for group project so you won't have an unfair grade. Great professor!

Overall the class experience was optimal. Thayer was a great professor the lectures were clear and thorough. The lectures covered 110% of the work in the assignment as he often completed the same thing needed in the lecture with a different dataset. Was always eager to answer questions and help students if they needed it.

This professor has boring lectures, but all the lectures are recorded and you can always read the lecture slides. Chill class with one final group project and there is no Finals. Even with zero coding experience, it's easy.
Best INFO 201 professor you can have. Easy 4.0 take his class if available!!!

Great Prof. Best prof in iSchool in my opinion. Took him for INFO 201 & 441. He breaks down things into a lot of detail, making sure you understand the very basic and fundamental of a concept. The assignments are good practice of what is taught in class and he is super super chill on deadlines too. He's really chill. Def recommend.

Thayer is a good guy, but his lectures were usually dense, and with class being 2 hours long it could be difficult to follow. You might have to teach yourself some r concepts so be wary of that. He provides office hours, TA help and there are resources online so as long as you try you should be fine. The content was very interesting to me.

Kyle was kind and I think he has taken steps to become a better professor overall. The class was enjoyable and relatively easy to follow. The course is beginner friendly and actually fun. My only complaints are that all grades came in at the very end of the quarter and the final website project was really rushed and thus difficult to execute.

Sometimes seemed a bit unprepared but his lecture demos were nice, he was also accessible to help during lecture and after. He is also a very understanding professor and does all that he can to help you succeed. Info 201 is a class that I recommend going to lecture for as it is very useful for getting help on the assignments!

This class is supposed to be about ethics, but Kyle made it about learning to code. Even if you have no coding experience, please take CSE 121 instead of this course, it will be much more useful. The assignments were barely put together as we were taking the class, and the professor was very distracted the entire time.

(TA, not student)

Although Kyle can be rather disorganized, he is very caring and understanding of his students. You really need to stay on top of your work in this class since there are so many weekly assignments to keep track of. However, Kyle is generous with extensions and understanding of students' circumstances.

Though Kyle seems a bit frazzled at times, he is kind and goes through demos in class which are very helpful. He is understanding when it comes to due dates and the regrade policy is great. For a first time coder it was tough (Google is ur BFF) but make sure to talk to the TAs and ask questions in class, and you should be okay and will learn a lot!

Although you will learn mostly through the textbook in this class, his lectures are good examples of how to program in R. He had a nice, clear grading syllabus that allowed redo's for more credit on assignments if you don't procrastinate. He was hard to get in touch with outside of class but listens to students need to push back a deadline.

thayer is understanding, but difficult to learn from. he tries his best and i appreciate that, but in the end he leaves u with not a lot of help, especially if youve never coded before like me. u have to google and pick up a lot of the slack urself outside of lectures. there are way too many assignments and hw, and it feels like youre drowning.

Lots of googling have to be done and not everything was taught in the lecture. The videos were entirely from last year and the quality was not too good especially with the audio. Very lenient with late days and lecture exercises but it can get a little annoying to do them.

Unreasonable and not accessible out of class which is pretty ridiculous because his lectures are recorded from over a year ago. Homeworks have included example problems to check your work with incorrect answers and hes generally just a bad professor who makes mistakes/stumbles during his recorded lectures and is too lazy to go back and fix them.
Good professor but he doesn't cover everything you need to know about the class and you have to google a lot of stuff while working on the assignments and group projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Much easier than cse 142/3 if you want to take an intro programming class. Homeworks are easy to get 95+percent if you just look at the rubrics and make sure you fulfill the criteria. Also reading quizzes are easy points. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Knowing code before this class is HIGHLY recommended. He goes over everything very fast and if you have questions he usually just tells you what to Google instead of the answer. That said, knowing code, this class is a breeze. No exams and hw has a clear rubric. And go to your quiz section! TAs help a lot with the base code for the hw.

His lectures give you the basics and you basically google the rest. Homework assignments were helpful and he was always willing to answer questions. No exams just homework and a final group project which was pretty fun. Overall, a solid class where I learned a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: INFO201 is already just a hard class because they say you can do well without knowing code but really you have to do so much outside research and reading to be able to complete the homework assignments. Big part of the grade is the group project so make sure you pick people who know code. Also the homework takes longer than you think so start early

Okay at lecturing, but fast paced and gave difficult homework and extremely hard tests. TAs were very picky when grading assignments, so read the spec carefully. The tests cover things from class but are too long for almost anyone to finish in the allotted time. This class covers fun material but there is a high chance it will hurt your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: CSE 154 is definitely worth taking but if you have Thayer be ready to spend lots of time on homework assignments and studying for tests. The HW is reasonable and sometimes fun but can take hours to complete. The tests will go over what you have been taught but they will definitely not give you enough time to complete everything so write fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He gave really valuable feedback!

Really, really bad instructor who should not even be called as an instructor. Mainly goes over slides in class, which is not interesting. However, the most infuriating thing about this guy is he is not prepared to class! Lots and lots of mistakes in his codes and he doesn't know how to correct it. His TAs are his lifesavers.

Overall, you can tell she's a nice person who truly cares about her students. However, she simply isn't organized. Consistently late, would cancel class at the last minute, and would talk about her political opinions the majority of the time, with only a handful of time dedicated to class content. She's kind, but in all honesty, a bit too much.

I know that comments like these can be personal, but putting personal feelings aside, she is always late. The last minute Zoom meetings we would have, she would be at least 20 minutes late. She doesn't believe in slides and what's worse is that she assigns you to reflect on the lectures...but she just talks about literally whatever during lecture.

She did have really interesting insights on the readings, when we actually got to talking about them. She was late every single day, sometimes 25 minutes late, and then spent an additional 30-60 minutes talking about things that weren't relevant to the course in the slightest.

She is caring...on the surface. Her actions do not show her to truly care at times. She's very knowledgeable, top of her field. However, she's always late, unproductive, makes false promises and doesn't cover actual class material (that was assigned btw). I'm sure she's a wonderful person, but not very true to what she claims to stand for.

Often late to class but incredibly kind, fun, really caring and will make room for you as long as you reach out. She does talk a lot and go on tangents, but she connects them to course material in very interesting ways. Heavily disagree with those saying they aren't course relevant. Assignments are straight forward, readings are very thick.

love love love her...will say she was late a lot but i appreciate how she would incorporate current events into the material!! incredibly fun and engaging, has immense breadth of knowledge and just so fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: She's late to class every single day, even to Zoom ones. She also has a habit of ranting about her political views for at least 20 to 30 minutes per day. Also, contacting her is nearly impossible: she never responds to emails, misses her own rescheduled office hours, and rushes off if you try to talk to her at the end of class. I do not recommend.

She's literally always late, even to online class days. Most of the time, she talks about her political views, then acts surprised when there is no time left in class. Her lectures are mandatory, and we have very long handwritten assignments every week, but they are disorganized. She's a nice person, though, and has good thoughts on the readings.

Late to class every day. Was late to a zoom class. Will talk about random stuff that isn't related to the course materials for 10-30 minutes a day, eating up a good quarter of the class. Secondary reading that were impossible to read as there were incorrect page numbers with little to no instruction. No feedback on writing at all. Fine lecturer.

I have no idea why everyone is rating her so low. I had her for class over the summer and I've never felt so supported and encouraged by a faculty member. She LOVED having conversations in class and made participation inviting and fun. She's a pretty easy grader, as long as you're doing the work and trying. Lots of reading but it's 100% worth it!

FOR ENGL 440: She is passionate, kind and accommodating. Communicating with her and building that student/teacher relationship is something I recommend. She usually goes off topic and can be disorganized, but genuinely such a great teacher. She is one of the best professors I've had. She really cares for her students. Can't recommend enough.

Sweet professor but very disorganized. She would forget to send reading information until the morning it was due in class. She had a lot going on in life, but it stuck with me. Graded on participation (10%), a daily (whenever class was) journal entry (45%), and a final group project (45%). Very approachable and passionate.

Late to every class (at least 10 mins each time, sometimes more), several classes either moved to zoom or cancelled. Assigned a lot of reading, only covered a fraction of it in class. Teacher is thoughtful and knowledgeable, but also seemed disorganized and unprepared, and lectures often lacked direction and consisted of unrelated tangents.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: shes super nice but was kind of M.I.A. as a professor. Late to every. single. class. and canceled/Zoom-ed around 5? Only graded by one BIG assignment you work on over the quarter and a final essay, and you dont get feedback until the last week. There was also a lot of reading, some we did not even cover. Also goes on tangents alot in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Workload consisted of probably about 100 pages of reading prior to every. single. class. Twice a week! TOO MUCH. We had to keep a journal for our readings - 300 words min before every class plus a 400 word reflection on fridays. 1000 words a week seems a lot, compared to other classes I've taken. Would not take again, unrealistic amount of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
Never have I had a professor that loved the sound of their own voice more.

I didn't just come online to be mean to professors. I'm currently sitting in her class, though, and had to complain to someone. ALL SHE DOES IS TALK. For two hours, twice a week, I sit and disassociate to her (albeit soothing) voice. 

She smart tho.

F*** I wanna go home.

My initial impression of Mrs. Norako was good. She was passionate about the class and had an incredible depth of knowledge on the subject matters taught in ENGL210. That being said, she grades very late, which I found to be pretty detrimental. Expect feedback on homework and such around a month or more late.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Did not give feedback or grades till the last week, the class was not as engaging as I hoped for.

She is very passionate about what she teaches, and absolutely loves to share with her class! This does lead to her going on some very random tangents so lectures aren't always useful. I do love that she is so understanding of student struggles. As long as you communicate with her, she will work with you if you are falling behind on deadlines.

While ENGL322 needed a lot of workshopping, I think Prof Norako had good intentions and graded very generously. She was constantly extending deadlines and reducing the workload for students who couldn't handle it. However, the class was disorganized and expectations were constantly changing. Group project was fun, though. Essays straightforward.

Homework consisted of readings that were always 100+ pages. 4 "micro essays" that were to be written in single spaced stretched out over a page and a half. Ridiculous final project with no rubric. Spent majority of class time ranting about unrelated topics.

Norako is passionate, but the workload/organization was unacceptable. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof. Norako was nice but extremely disorganized throughout the course. She barely kept up with what she assigned. There were four essays, reader reports, a final group project, and hundreds of pages of reading weekly to top it off. Her grading criteria is very vague so it's either a hit or miss. The lectures were tangents. Complete waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Does not grade or put grades into grade book until the quarter is almost over.  No explanation of how papers are graded.  Avoid! Avoid!

Professor Norako is the gem of this department. She brings a very unique energy to the class, has a good sense of humor, and really cares about all students' learning. She really motivates you to think outside the box and be comfortable with your own opinions and beliefs. This is a true uni level lit professor.

Wonderful teacher and person! She was clear about her expectations and a wonderful discussion leader. If you go into office hours, she will bend over backwards to help you on work. Very kind person who genuinely cares about what she's doing. Quickly responds to emails. Really a gem.

One of my favorite classes at UW. Syllabus was laid out very well. Readings (all available online and not e-reserves) were not hard, but still very interesting. Leila is a very kind person and very understanding when it comes to assignments and deadlines. She's got a really quirky sense of humor and one of the cutest laughs I've ever heard too.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Norako is the best professor I've ever had at UW. She's super helpful and gives great feedback, and her classes themselves are just super fascinating. She'll make you work, and get ready to read, but it's all worth it and really rewarding. I've taken 3 classes with her now and they've all been amazing, would definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: amazing person! lots of readings! dont
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Leila is amazing. She brings energy and passion into her lectures and discussions and is very knowledgable on medieval literature. However, she expected a ridiculous amount of reading and assignments and papers/projects. This class was so much work and took up a ton of time, but was also very enjoyable. Beware: she had us do an 18 line recitation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Norako is very knowledgeable and passionate about medieval literature and it clearly shows in her teaching. I do not really enjoy this topic and it was at times boring, but for the most part, I did learn a lot about the characteristics/nuances of Chaucer & medieval lit. Class requires 2 essays, a recitation, and quite a bit of reading
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very passionate about what she teaches. Knowledgeable and approachable. She is very invested in her students and assignments are easy. Not too much reading, but be prepared for discussions. Writing notebook is straightforward, two formal papers. Go to office hours! She is the "help me, help you" kind of person. loved her.

Negatives: Talks political opinions a lot, can be unclear on assignment requirements. Positives: Very enthusiastic, well-informed lecturer. Tends to grade easy if you make sure of what she wants beforehand. She makes herself available for office hours, and you should go and discuss projects BEFORE submitting them.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Little is very nice, kind and happy to help, which are great traits for a professor. Expect that she is very bad at teaching. I disagree with reviews saying "stats is hard but Laura makes it easy" because for me stats is easy and Laura makes it hard. Her exams are also super confusingly ambigously worded. Prepare to self teach if u have her.

Prof. Little is amazing! She truly wants you to understand and she is always open to questions. Its clear she cares about all her students succeeding and is open to talking in and out of her office hours. She also holds zoom reviews the night before the exam and has no time cut off so she makes sure everyones questions get answered.

She is very fair, she once made a test question that was too difficult so she made it extra credit instead because she decided it was just a bad question. She holds review sessions and office hours so she is available if you have any questions. The content is hard, but the teacher is good. Also, all tests are open-book, open-note so that's awesome.

She is knowledgeable and is fair in her expectations, but she's bad at professing. She is not efficient. Lectures and other resources are slow, wordy, and lack organization. I wished she took extra care to make her lectures and online material more concise and easy to navigate. I mostly learned the material from outside sources.

Dr. Little was great. Stats isnt the easiest class but she genuinely wants you to succeed. Always accessible outside of class, gives review sessions for exams, and explains things thoroughly so you actually understand the material. Doesn't hesitate to answer questions and offer like 1/2 extra credit opportunities.

She's awesome. You can tell that she really loves her job and she always tries to help us out <3 This class is a hybrid. You can attend in person or watch panopto recordings. Quiz sections are not recorded but they don't take attendance. She's pretty knowledgable on the subject too.

Honestly, after taking her class for two quarters, I can say that Professor Little has to be one of my favorite professors. She is very caring, passionate, and only wants you to be successful. As long as you do the readings, the practice test, and ask questions, you will definitely be satisfied with your grades. *Keep in mind, this was online*

Dr. Little is the best. Of all my professors this quarter, she has by far been the most caring, flexible, and understanding of students' needs during these weird times. You can tell that she and the teaching team put a lot of effort into making the course accessible, and that they really want students to do well.

Professor Little is a really attentive and caring professor. I feel like the harsh comments have to do with how hard the coursework is. Attending office hours and putting in more work in your own time will be what you have to do to get high grades in any statistics class. She's an amazing professor! Don't miss the chance on not having her teach you
Great professor. You can tell she really cares about her students and what she teaches. She is very approachable and helpful outside of class. I would highly recommend taking a class from her.

Laura is one of the sweetest professors I've had, and she genuinely cares about her students as individuals. Statistics is hard, but if I had to take it with anyone it would be her. Offers lots of help outside class and on discussion boards. Lectures can be a bit scattered, but she makes sure to give you what you need for the tests. Love her!

Tests are open book/notes. Lab worksheets cover exactly whats on the test and is almost a step by step instruction. That said the tests won't be easy if you don't study. Lastly, she and her TA's offer A TON of help. I enjoyed this class and would GLADLY take any class Dr. Little offers. This class is only hard if you don't put in a little effort.

Shes super nice but her lectures are practically of no help (watch YouTube videos to learn anything) and her tests have confusing words and often tests things not covered during lecture or even covered properly in readings. The exams are also 85% and while theres extra credit they only count towards the 15% assignment grade
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Terrible lecturer, often gets lost in words and scribbles. Watching YouTube videos is the only way to learn. She has managed to scam the entire school by being super nice. Often goes into side discussions about why do this or that in statistics when we are just trying to learn the basics. Exams and homework often have confusing wording to trick you

Laura is,  bar none, the most compassionate professor I've ever had. Her genuine care for each and every one of her students is incredible. I would absolutely recommend her for psyc 317 and 318. There are lots of tests, but I never felt ill prepared to take them. Sections were very helpful, sometimes more so than lectures.

Laura is one of the kindest people I've met. She is (literally) always there for her students and always willing to help. That being said, her lectures aren't as clear-cut as they could be, and her exams are very conceptual. You definitely have to put in the work for a good grade.

Laura's tests are too long, and it's VERY hard to finish them in the time allowed. I feel like no matter how hard I studied, it's impossible to solve her HIGHLY conceptual problems on the spot while being so pressed for time. Yes, she's a nice person, but it's WAY too much work for a 300-level undergraduate-level class.

She's indeed a REALLY REALLY NICE person. She's always on discussion board and makes time for extra office hours. But she can be really confusing sometimes :( You must put a lot more extra work in order to succeed in her class.

Rep is for being nice, not for teaching ability. Tests don't reflect course content but your personal problem solving ability. If not already statistically literate, avoid her class. While nice, she's unclear and distracted, and she demands more than most. You must be excellent at teaching yourself if you are to succeed. Skip lecture. Not worth it.

A group of us struggled in Laura's class. It's too bad she didn't spend more time focused on the material, and that she didn't make sure the tests related to the study outlines/practice materials and not go beyond it. I like statistics, but this was too much too fast, and it was impossible to keep up without neglecting work in my other classes.

Laura is a great person. However, she can be fairly scatterbrained and lose track of where she's headed. She is always there to help, whenever you need her, but my TA has truly saved my quarter. For an unwanted degree requirement, this class hasn't been bad.

Laura Little is by-far the best professor I have had here at UW! She is not only smart, and respectable, she also takes time to get to know her students!! She provides practice exams and is always available on the class discussion board! Also, she uses an open source textbook- which is free!! Overall, Laura is wonderful and I recommend her class!
Teaching this course for so long but still doesn't know how to type mathematical expressions clearly. Thus very hard to understand her notes. Wordings are confusing.

She is probably one of the best professor's I have had at UW. She truly cares whether or not you have learnt the material and she practically lives on the discussion board. She has an endearing sense of humor, although she may go off on tangents. Tests truly test how well you understand the concepts, although they are open notesbook.
