To be honest, I really hate statistics, but Dr. Little makes everything so much easier. Class is difficult, but she's always there for you. Go to her office hour, ask questions on the discussion board, you'll do great!

Just took this class last quarter and I feel that she is learning from her mistakes from past quarters. There are some negative reviews about her particularly on the exam questions, but she is actually trying to improve because she did point out confusing exam questions and clarify them as clear as possible in my quarter. Recommended

Laura is one of the nicest and kindest professors I have ever met. That being said, she is a bit unclear and difficult to understand at times but she is willing to help if you ask! Definitely not the easiest class in the world but you do learn a lot of new things. If you have a chance to take statistics with her, I'd do it!

Laura is so passionate about teaching and making sure her students understand statistics. She genuinely cares about your understanding of the material and will go out of her way to make sure you're comfortable. She is a wonderful person who puts her students first--I will miss her!

Laura's the best.She's clear,passionate and so caring she'll make time from her crazy schedule to work through problems with you.Unless you get a head trauma there's no way to flunk this class-you get an amazing teaching team of awesome grad TA's and undergrad TA's.She also has this cute,self-effacing sense of humor - you just have to love her.

She's a really kind person. But her tests test harder than you would think despite her in-class examples and homework. The reason why you get mixed feedback on her is because although the exams are open book and open note, she lectures in a way that isn't organized, so you don't know how to go about solving the problem because she goes on tangents.

Thought 317 was going to be easy...Dr. Little is amazingly kind and helpful (go to office hours and e-mail her about extra appointments) but this class was very difficult. My lowest grade so far at the UW. 5 tests...never sure what to expect. It has been very hard to navigate how to study. The TAs are sometimes a bit unclear as well.

Laura seems nice at the beginning of quarter- lays out the syllabus, talks about what we will do. Then, she asks multiple choice questions that even her TAs don't understand (not because they're hard, because they make no sense) and changes the syllabus arbitrarily. She is horribly unclear and frustrating, especially if you have a stats background.

Really difficult class, in my opinion. Lots of homework assignments and five exams total. Everything felt very rushed and unclear. Little is a nice person, I'm sure, but not a very good professor. She goes off on tangents frequently and spends entire lectures teaching the wrong thing. Absolutely hated the class, dreading taking 318 next quarter.

Laura is amazing! She's been teaching stats for 15 years now and knows exactly what she's doing. She's clear, engaging, and always ready to help. It seems like she practically lives on the help forums online. you can run your homework answers by her and she'll tell you if you're right or not. The homework is easy, and the textbook is clear.

318 was much harder than 317, and as usual her final was brutal! But she is an amazing prof and so incredibly helpful - both in person and on the GoPost board. I can't say enough good things about her! If you have to take stats SHE is the one you want to have teaching it.

Amazing prof! Very clear, very accessible for extra help, and very reasonable on homework and tests. I thought the exams were easy (they are open-book): I got 100% on 2 of them, but I love math. Even if you don't like stats you'll like this class. Seriously, Laura Little is the best! (I wish she could teach all my other classes, too!)
Had her for 317/318.  The finals are difficult but Laura is probably the best professor at UW.

Laura has been one of my favorite teachers so far despite how much I dislike stats. It's true that her tests can be very hard, though. But I think she honestly means the best for all her students and I've never experienced such a passion for teaching. She will take time out of any day to sit down and help you.
go to office hours. she really wants you to understand the material and truly cares about her students.

She's extremely kind and accepting of all her students, and she makes stats bearable (because it is a dull subject). However, I found 317 & 318 the hardest classes in college. She is unorganized and her tests are difficult. My GPA dropped a lot after taking these two classes. Even though tests are open book, the class is hard and so is her grading.
She's approachable and wants you to understand the material. Her tests are tricky but they're open notes and book so you don't have to worry about memorizing anything.

While Laura is a funny person who does want you to succeed, she writes the hardest tests. She tends to go off on tangents in class and her lectures jump around a lot. I feel as though I got more out of office hours than any lecture. Her grading scale is also really weird. This class made my life extremely stressful for two quarters.

Amazing professor.  One of the best I've had at UW.  Really cares about teaching and wants all of her students to succeed.  Gives handouts and explains concepts well to make stats more easily understood.  If you can take any class with her, take it!

Laura Little is one of the best (if not THE best) professor I have ever had. I was so nervous about taking statistics but it is great with her! I am going to take an additional quarter to just have her as a teacher again. You have to take Laura's class.

I've taken both PSYCH 317 & 318 with Laura Little, and she is truly one of the most incredible professors and people that I have ever met. If she feels like she didn't explain something well, she loses sleep over it and apologizes & explains later.She knows what she's doing, but she's humble about it and has a cute sense of humor. See for yourself!

Professor Little is one of the most genuine people I've ever met, which makes her one of the best professors.  She will do whatever she can to help students learn.  Doing all the work, paying attention, and knowing when to ask for help will ensure a good grade.  I hated stats before, but she made it interesting.

If you're doing a BS, you will be taking two quarters in a row with Prof. Little. This makes her a popular choice for letters of recommendation. She is very open to this, although you'll get a better letter if asking her for it isn't the first interaction you've had. In terms of teaching, she does a good job making a boring subject tolerable.

Awesome stats (317/318) teacher! I wasn't interested in stats at all and then I took her class. Now I love stats! She really cares about her students and goes out of her way to help you learn. She wants you to do well and to understand that stats is a living field with controversy.  There is a reason she won the distinguished teaching award!
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
She really wants you to learn and will help you out whenever you need it. Saying that, it's not an easy class. Statistics sucks, but she helps you get by.
No Comments

I took him for Math 111 and 112. He's a super kind and funny teacher. He always says random stories in class so we have time to process what's happening. He's quizes and tests are easy, and he actually cares about people getting good grades rather than trying to be difficult. Highly recommend him.

I really love Professor Larry's class. He explains everything very clearly. He is also genuinely funny, and I always enjoy his jokes. I'm the kind of student who gets distracted pretty easily, but in Professor Larry's class, it's actually hard for me to zone out. That probably says a lot about how interesting and well-taught his class is.
Larry is the kindest and most understanding human ever.

He's a really good professor overall. Three lectures a week and they are interactive. He makes an active effort to get to know his students and encourages them to ask questions. He will often call on other students to work through the problems in lecture. You can pass if you want. He goes off topic sometimes, but it helps other notetakers catch up.
Sometimes rambles off-topic in lectures but great teacher and makes the class as accessible as possible. Low stress class.

super chill guy, i watched every single class on panopto and still got an A on every test. very easy exams and teaches the material well. expect that if you are going to attend in-person class that you will be called on and joked with like you're at a math comedy show instead of a class
Really good would take again
I would rate a six if I could
He's very caring and clear with what he wants, and the class is easy.

Great prof, is very clear on what you will be tested on which is so so important esp in math classes. Gives very good explanations for example problems during lectures as well and just overall tries to help the class understand the material as well as possible.
Great help if you needed it, and his lectures were easy to follow. Overall, great vibes all around. He was always in a good mood
Larry is so silly goose, be ready for him to memorize your name all quarter and ask for your help. The practice quizzes given by TA's are helpful for exams, and the class overall is very great!
Great at explaining things and not making students feel slow. Great homework, great tests, great final. Loved this class and loved to have Larry as a professor for my first quarter at the UW.

He treats his classes a little bit like a crowd work comedy show, and if you sit in the front three rows, you WILL be spoken to or complimented. Overall he's a great guy and he explains concepts very clearly for those prone to falling behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easiest class ever. Weekly homework and quizzes every other week but they're very manageable. There's a lot of help from TA's and professor pierce. Attendance isn't mandatory so you only have to show up on quiz days. Very caring Professor and I definitely recommend.

larry is a wonderful wonderful professor. he really cares about all of his students and works really hard to make sure everyone understands the content. he explains things very clearly and checks in with the class to make sure everyone's caught up. one of the best professors i have ever had
Nice fella

I love Larry. I took him in my first quarter at UW, and his teaching is perfect. He is very helpful, and so are his TAs. His teaching style is perfect, and the practice exams were very helpful and well-prepared. me for the exams. this is one of those classes where you get how much effort you put in, so don't fall behind on work and lectures.

Professor never rushes and conveys the material in a very simplified and unhurried manner, making it very easy to understand.
Professor checks in with all students in the lecture very often to make sure everyone understands.
Professor has a sense of humor and is humble.
The professor is fun and makes the class fun regardless of the course itself.

The one redeeming quality about Prof Pierce is that he definitely cares about his students. Office hours can be great. HOWEVER. Lectures are an absolute waste of time. You will learn more about his family than you will about Stoke's and Green's theorems combined. He also likes to cold call on students.

If you work through the past exams and make sure you understand everything in the textbook, you'll do really well and get a nearly perfect score. Larry is very willing to answer your questions and friendly. The final grade cutoff ended up being high, but that was because the exams were easy and the awful median 3.0 policy.

You can talk to Dr. Pierce about anything you want! You want Dr. Pierce to be your MATH lecturer, very highly-sought after.

He will hold your attention the entirety of lecture, he will make you willing to participate and speak out! Very effective pedagogy.

The UW MATH Department has a grade policy that the median grade shall be a 3.0.

Disorganized lectures, horrible examples/explanations and was weeks behind schedule. Practice exams weren't helpful, you're better off using extra Cengage questions. Made pretty easy exams but then set a ridiculous curve (96% - 4.0, 87% - 3.0) so any minor mistake tanks your GPA. Multiple accidentally unsolvable exam questions messed up the curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Larry wanted to tell personal stories instead of lectures, which made us weeks behind previous years, meaning the old practice exams (he didn't provide his own) were basically useless. He also wrote multiple questions incorrectly and he loves making "0" an actual answer, so don't be fooled. He also didn't really use the textbook he was supposed to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Truly awful, unfair curve. Did not properly adjust the difficulty of the class so he set his curve ridiculously high. You may think the class is easy, but be warned: any small mistake will have a huge consequence on your GPA.

He is a nice person, a joy to chat with, and he is passionate about the subject. However, his use of class time was terrible as he often got sidetracked with joking around with students instead of focusing on the content. Every lecture felt rushed at the end and we were constantly behind. Youtube will be your friend. Would not take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took the hybrid section of this course. Larry is a friendly guy, so about half the lecture is him interacting with the in-person students. That makes the recordings a little inconvenient. Overall, the content is explained well. He gives a lot of partial credit on exams. He's upfront about what will be on exams and any mistakes he makes.

Larry is a fun guy that really cares about his students, but his use of class time is poor. He spends a lot of time talking to us like his friends, which made class fun but caused us to rush through content in the end, so I spent lots of time outside of class learning it on my own. Thankfully, he told us exactly what content would be on the final.

He definitely cares but is easily distracted. The class is not hard and only about 10 minutes of lectures are even semi useful.... I really think that his problem is that the content can be taught in about 5-10 minutes but he is given the full 50 minutes, which means he has 50 minutes to just talk about anything and everything...

I took Larry for math125 and math224, and quality of lectures severely dropped between the two. For intro calculus, he went at a relatively good pace but for 224 went excruciatingly slow and left people feeling woefully unprepared for exams. He often gets sidetracked by comments from students, and struggled to explain concepts in depth.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Larry is a rare blend of educator and entertainer. His lectures are engaging, filled with humor, and effortlessly keep students hooked. He turns complex topics into lively discussions, making learning fun and accessible. Beyond the jokes, he's passionate, insightful, and genuinely cares about student success.

Get ready to teach yourself the entire course. Has a weird and unexplained hatred for the textbook and does not have any practice tests. Tests were fraught with errors, leading to an entire restructuring of the grading policy mid-quarter. Wastes the majority of lecture time on personal anecdotes and weird ramblings.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's so nice! He cares about all the students and makes an effort to talk to the class. The content was easy to learn and tests were a breeze to get through, and it's really easy to get a 4.0.

The class was not super hard, but he does not gives rubrics or any feedback on homework or exams.  It pretty much ends up being a teach-yourself kind of class — which isn't great, especially considering how much we're paying. I'd avoid it if you actually want to learn the material.
Loved this guy, please take him.

I pay 4 dollars and 44 cents a minute to take a class at this school (I did the math). Larry pierce spends half of his lectures talking about himself and his life. If I were to time it, Pierce would spend the first 20 minutes talking about his weekend, 10 on work, then a mix of the two for the next 20-30. A waste of time and money. Stay home.
Take his class if you like to teach yourself everything and get a grade that based completely on his own preferences.
AVOID! Doesn't teach, minimum help, grades harsh.

Grading criteria was unclear, all homework assignments were recycled from the previous instructor, and the lectures were more focused on personal anecdotes than the course material itself. Also bipolar, your project grade depends more on his mood than its merit.

Reuses all course materials from a previous professor without updating Canvas but grades inconsistently. Announced the 3.0 median only on the last few hours of finals week—completely unexpected. Lectures are unhelpful since he spends too much time on student names. I have no idea how he qualifies as a professor. Would not recommend.

Larry is by far the best math prof I've had at UW. 208 is a very conceptual class and he does a good job of providing the geometric intuition for what you learn rather than just throwing the theorems at you. His tests are relatively straightforward compared to the conceptual homework and he makes them this way intentionally.
Larry is the best professor I've ever had! He cares about his students a lot!

He's funny in class and makes a genuine effort to connect with his students, which is nice. Attendance isn't mandatory at all. Quizzes are every other week, but they're easy if you do the weekly homework. My only thing is that it took over three weeks to get one quiz score back, and the other grades haven't come out yet.
Larry Pierce is the goat of Mathematics.

Larry's a fun professor, always trying to connect with the class and engaging in the material. All his lectures were recorded, and he emphasized that you did NOT have to show up lol. Weekly assignments on Webassign and a quiz every other week. Exams and quizzes were so easy. Cool professor who was also accessible with great office hours sessions!!

Larry was one of the best math professors I've had, he truly makes an effort to get to know his class and manages to cover all the material while telling stories here and there and overall making the class very enjoyable.
Love Dr. Pierce (he prefers to be called Larry). Very knowledgeable and funny. Manages to cover everything he wants while yapping about his life, which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Larry was the best college math professor I could have ever had. He was a great teacher and person over all he was very helpful and encouraging. You can tell he truly wants his students to succeed.

I would 100% recommend this class, easiest math class I've taken and I was able to 4.0 by doing homework and paying attention to lecture. Really good professor and truly attempts to get to know his class!!!
Larry is the absolute best! He is genuinely so caring about his students and really prepares you for the tests well. 10/10 would take his class again.
Larry is such a king. he made every lecture fun and interesting and I really appreciated how hard he tried!! he always made me laugh miss you king
He's fantastic. Explains things in ways that are relatable.
Literally the best professor

Good and fun person. Highly interactive with students. The test and super easy and straightforward. The only con would be that he talks a lot and only gets through a couple of problems in class so if you want to do lots of problems he's tough.

Great prof. and very understanding. There's biweekly quizzes/final but no midterm and he reviews questions that will be in them in class. Most final samples he gives are harder than the actual final (formatted similar to his quizzes). If you miss a quiz, it's possible to do it in office hours. HW can be tricky but fair amount-wise. Great calves.

I'm glad I took Larry's class. My biggest piece of advice I wish I had done earlier in the quarter is going to office hours. Quiz section can only help so much outside of homework. I thought I would pass this class with a 1.0, and instead, I got a 4.0.

Literally- the only way to fail this class is putting in 0 effort.
genuinely such a caring professor about his students. Be prepared to be engaged with in class! I also enjoyed how he connected a lot of the math to the real world and all of his stories.

Larry is a very chill guy, lowkey makes fun of everyone, 90% of the class is him yapping about God knows what and then the last 15 min we'll actually do work. But I like him although hes slightly unfunny

As a sophomore, Larry is the best professor I've ever met at UW. Perfect lecture and easy-to-understand instruction. And also has low workload compares to other Math class. Besides, final instruction is nice and patient. Includes all necessary files for download.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is the goat!!!

Larry is my favorite professor I've ever had at UW. His lectures are optional but I still attended every one because he makes class engaging and funny, and he's truly kind & wants his students to succeed. Quizzes are really easy if you're up to date with the material. Lectures are recorded and there are lots of office hours. 10/10 thank you Larry!

Larry explains material very well and uses real life scenarios that makes sense. He is a major yapper but in a good way. His class made me like math and I hate math. Explains the textbook in his own words which makes it more understanding. 10/10 recommend !!
D1 yapper for real

Larry makes math fun, and I hate math. Larry is the best professor I've ever had. Even though attendance was optional I attended every lecture because he made the material clear and entertaining. He always ties the material to real life examples and makes it engaging, he's very funny too. I hope to get him again in the future. 10/10 no complaints.

Larry's lectures are clear, easy to understand, and recorded for convenience. You typically have 1-3 homework assignments per week with about a week to complete them, and he always covers any questions about the homework during class. The quizzes are every other week, about 5 questions each, and very straightforward.

Larry is an amazing professor because the way he lectured was very easy to follow and comprehend. The only downside is the TAs during the quiz section were a bit condescending if you did not understand the material. I witnessed a couple of people receiving help from certain TAs who were a bit rude and still had a hard time getting help.

Larry is so kind to his students. He wants everyone to succeed. He is hilarious and his lectures are such a good time. You can tell how much he wants you to succeed, and he is always there to answer questions and offer support. I cannot express how great he is. He has been the most supportive and the kindest teacher I have had thus far at UW!!!!!!
HIM. The goat.

I actually had Larry Pierce for MATH207 (which wasn't an option so I just put 208) but he was one of the best professors I've ever had. Super interesting and cared a lot about his students. His class was unlike any I've had at UW and the class felt like a small community rather than a class.

Larry is a wonderful person and a great teacher! 125 is a difficult class but having Larry as my teacher made it worth it. His use of examples is really helpful in lectures, and his positive attitude and humor is infectious.
Super funny, makes math fun but had some difficult exams.

I definitely agree with what a lot of the reviews said, but I felt like he wasn't the best lecturer, as it was too early for him and me, and I wasn't able to take good notes or sometimes even understand what he was teaching, and had to spend a lot of time self-learning the topic instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Despite the section being held at 8:30 in the morning, Larry's enthusiasm and passion for teaching ensured that I was always awake and present in this class throughout the whole quarter. He wants you to succeed, and if you can get used to his occasionally scatterbrained nature, Larry is a great instructor to get you through any UW math.

Great professor! Kind, great at explaining things in multiple ways, and more concerned about student success than anything else. He was happy to go out of his way to help students, and on a couple occasions I invited friends to his lectures. The friends also felt that he was a super great teacher. I will be looking to take classes with him again!

Truly cares about student success; was willing to push back a lot of the homework due dates. Math dept is stifling him. Truly a nice human being and a great teacher, if only he was given more power to do what he wanted with the lecture time. He tried to make the midterms as easy as possible lol.

Larry is so great! Definitely one of the best professors I've met. He can explain things in a very logic and clear way. His class is super amazing as well ! The lecture is organized very clearly and highly-structured. Very Friendly for note-takers. Highly Recommended ! I would definitely take it his classes again !

Larry is honestly the best math professor I have ever had. He truly cares about whether or not students succeed. He never acts like a question is stupid and always responds with enthusiasm. He's also very funny. He cares about students learning applications and connections, which really makes the material feel relevant. He made me like math again!
PLEASE take this professor if you need an A&H, DIV, or both. Very easy class.
Awesome professor. Worth your time.

The professor is very passionate about what she teaches and she's also very open-minded. She cares a lot about people's personal interpretations of things, so you don't really have to worry about being wrong. The class itself is well structured and the grading is lenient. The only thing she cares about is whether or not you're engaged/interested.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This was an interesting class that she made engaging. She is very clear on assignments, grading, and is generous with make up. The quizzes were very easy and had extra credit occasionally. She gives you all the resources to succeed and if you watch the movies, you will do very well.

An interesting class with a mixture of film and camera analysis. The Friday session was a waste of time, except for the graded quiz. The TA would say the same things that were said during the Wednesday class.

Wow. This professor was so good I made an account just to rate her. If you get the chance, TAKE HER CLASS. She is a fantastic professor that creates a stress-free yet engaging lectures. Very little work to be done, just watching movies or reading short things. You'd have to try to get a bad grade. She cares genuinely about her students.

one of my fav profs at UW! i was scared about taking a french course online for the first time bc of the pandemic, but she made the course flexible and manageable amidst the chaos. she's such a caring person!<3 loved the variety of the reading/lecture topics and how it's all taught in french. i had a very pleasant experience in this course!!

really interesting discussions, professor respects students opinions and responds to your online discussions . Kind of a lot of reading but it's okay if you don't get it all done every time. Some weeks had a lot more reading than others  and it would have been good to have it more balanced. Still this ended up being one of my favorite uw classes.

Wasn't really much about FranceFrench cinema, mostly about the "idea of Europe." Many of the films were French, but we didn't discuss their placement in film history or technique much beyond the 3rd week. Lectures were long & she seemed to frequently reach pretty far for her interpretations of scenes. Clear expectations & easy grader tho.

This was my favorite class of all times! Learning about the idea of Europe through film was fun. Each week an assignment about the film is due, 3 quizzes throughout quarter, 5 random in-class participation questionnaires (drops 1 if you missed class), and occasional easy write-ups for quiz sec. Her British accent is awesome too! Highly recommended

She is super nice and you can tell she really cares about frencheuropean cinema. You don't really have to go to class because she posts the slides online however she does have participation so you should go to class. Make sure however you do go to quiz section because thats were a lot of work is done. The TA's are super nice but are tough graders!
She was a very good Instructor  :)

This class changed how I view everything in the world- I've become a much more aware person. Prof Mackenie is the best prof I have had the pleasure of taking at UW, and I hope to take classes from her in the future(even though French isn't my major). She's just great.
Absolutely wonderful teacher. Very nice, very well taught, very engaging, and quite lenient and patient with students. By far the best professor I have encountered in UW.

Definately agree that this class felt easy, but you also learn a lot kind of without realizing that you are learning. The prof did a great job introducing intersting ideas (the other, bare life) and I know a lot more about Europe now, also watch movies differently! highly recommend.
this was a fun and easy class. quizes/assignments were a breeze and the films were all interesting. just do all the little assignments and watch the films and you'll be fine.

Mackenzie is head and shoulders above the rest of the French profs at the UW. She's way more prepared for class, she really cares about your learning, and if you take the time to go to office hours etc. you will find that she will totally go the extra mile for you and you will have a strong ally when you apply for jobs. Her French is perfect, too.

If you have an opportunity  to take a class or work with this professor, do not ever think of passing it up. She is always engaging and her joie de vivre and love of teaching radiates through all that she does.

One of the best French teachers I've had at the UW. She is authentically engaged in the subjects and you get engaged as a result. She's also a very helpful and understanding teacher, and fairly easy grader. She's very knowledgeable about everything she teaches. I look forward to taking more classes with her.

Having Yulenni as a TA really helped me improve as a writer. Essays are usually the hardest part for me, so this class was definitely challenging, but I found her feedback to be super helpful. If you're able to take the time & really apply her advice you'll see a lot of growth

The grading was extremely harsh and felt excessive for an undergraduate class, with expectations that didn't always seem clearly explained or consistent. If you're considering this course, be prepared for very strict grading and unclear expectations. It may work better for students who are comfortable figuring things out independently.
Yulenni is really funny and caring. She engages the entire section, and is really helpful during office hours. She also gives great feedback on assignments.

Yulenni is a great TA! I was having a hard time but she helped me a lot in office hours. If you care about your grade and want to understand the material, just go to office hours and don't be afraid to ask questions! She's a fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor for this class and lecture were great but Yuleni was the worst part. She's tries way too hard to be funny and doesn't know what she's talking about. The only good thing about having her be the TA for this class is there wasn't section.

Yulenni is literally the best TA ever. Idk what vendetta the other comment has but she's 100% been the TA I respect, trust, and felt I can learn from the most. She's very intelligent, cares about what she does, and cares about student voices. She isn't TAing after this quarter but if you can have her as a professor, DO ITTTTTT she slays
Cares more about her outfits than teaching
Very easy class. Makes her 8:30 worth going to. Midterm and final are easy, group project can be difficult if you get assigned a bad group. Would recommend starting that ASAP.

Louise is a fantastic professor. Highly recommend. Her lectures are very entertaining, and the classroom activities relate to the curriculum. There is a textbook which I rented BUT you don't need it. Her lectures provide more than enough information. Would take any of her classes!
A wonderful professor who is passionate about what she teaches. Loves to use in class exercises to make sense of the topics at hand and it works. She is very straight forward and accommodating.

Best option for MGMT300 if you can get her. Very knowledgeable about the industry, but also very knowledgeable about how to have an engaging and interesting class at 8:30 in the morning. Highly recommend if you have the chance.

Louise is fantastic. She is extremely organized, quick to respond to emails, and kind. Structure is a lecture with one pretty chill team exercise per class. Participation matters - she'll call on you or your team to share. Tests are SUPER easy if you have the textbook - remote, it's open-note and open book. Overall, it's a really chill class

Louise is EASILY one of the best profs I've ever had. She GENUINELY cares about your well-being and success. She gives great tips and tricks for your professional life. Her class is so unique and she makes it so much fun. I swear, my 8:30 class didn't feel like it... You learn the content but in a practical way. Love her!!! (also a super easy 4.0)

Great Teacher, one of my favorites Ive had in Foster, however she will assign points for in class participation assignments that will end up being a huge determinant of your grade in the end. I wish I could only say good things about Louise but her horrible grading scale for in class participation left me with a very bad taste in my mouth.

JL is dope.  Took all of his classes after 204 (which made me become a polisci major). He treats everyone the same and with respect -- this class (unlike many others except in Econ) made me feel like I was being treated like an adult. If he teaches the elections class in fall 2026 should definitely take.

I'm honestly surprised that he managed to receive such high ratings from some students. Professor Long seems to enjoy making his classes unnecessarily difficult. He speaks fast on purpose and each slide is full of paragraphs, making it difficult to take notes and keep up. He also tends to have a condescending attitude towards students
Took 204, 220, 362, and 371 with him. Hands down best prof at UW.

readings interesting but tedious; Long is well versed on the subject matter... It's the way he lectures I could not get past. He frequently pauses for effect in the middle of saying the most basic concept. He could be telling me my own name and still reveal each letter like I've never seen the alphabet before. Tone of condescending self-importance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment:
He's kind of intimidating but the lectures are great and the readings are all really interesting except for the Rose Ackerman textbook which is pretty dull. This class is a lot of work (about 100-200 pages of reading a week) but I learned a lot so it felt worth it. 

30% midterm, 40% final, 10% short response, 10% short response, 10% participation
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Assigns an unreasonable amount of reading. One week we had 195 pages from a pdf and a textbook combined. impossible to manage on top of readings from other classes. other than that hes a pretty good lecturer and I genuinely liked the course structure.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He knows what he's talking about, but he has the speaking cadence and condescending tone of a redditor. I can vividly imagine him telling me to name three Nirvana songs.
Love Dr. Long. He knows what he is talking about. This is a great class if you are ok with getting lectured to for a long time. He also talks pretty fast.

Professor Long is very good at directing a focused and reading-intensive class on an amazing subject. He leaves little room for disagreement, but his knowledgeability and straightforward grading practices reward knowledge and clear thinking above all else. I look forward to taking his course on corruption.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
POL S 220 How To Steal An Election will be offered Fall'25 and Fall'EvenNumberYears.

Reading required before lecture to make sense of slides and lecture, passionate about his research in democratic election integrity, both U.S. and internationally. Only downside is it's not easy to make a personal-academic connection with him during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is based off of 2 books, I found the audio book versions instead and played it in the background while going along my day. You can also just look at the slides instead of attending lecture. Got nearly 100% on the final, midterm, and on the class overall. Just make sure to participate in quiz section and study when it counts
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very clear on expectations, if you go to lectures, participate, and study you should be good.

This is my second class with Professor Long, and I can't wait to take him again. His lectures are genuinely some of the best at this school. Beyond engaging, it keeps things very real. He has lots of cool stories about his research as well!

I've taken two classes now with Prof. Long and he's the best professor I've had at UW. He can be a little egotistical at times but lectures are super interesting and I feel like I learned a lot from each one (he doesn't record so you should show up to them!). His classes always have one final, one midterm, and two homework assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took pols 220 with him and wow this dude assigns too much reading. Each week is like 100-150 pages, way more than any other 200 I've taken. On day one of lecture he also saw someone on their phone and gave a long winded rant about how phones disrupt the classroom environment. He also makes you turn in assignments on paper for no reason.

Menu wouldn't let me pick POLS220 (How to Steal an Election) -- class is so interesting. I'm an CS&E major and took this cuz I needed the credit and it sounded interesting. I guess this is Long's first year teaching it (coinciding with election) and it's totally fun, not that hard, and appealing for non-polisci majors. Full of fun (& true) stories!

Professor Long loves what he studies and really wants to share his knowledge if you're willing to listen. If you engage with the work and study hard you will get something out of this class. Grading is very dependent on midterm and final but they are not impossible and if you study well you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Long's a very good lecturer, and the material in 371 is fascinating. The reading is a lot, but if you focus on the case studies and just skim the textbook, you'll be fine. Grading is mainly a bluebook midterm (defining/explaining terms) and final (two essays). Familiarity with basic econ and game theory helps, although you can get by without it.
Crime & Corruption was my favorite class at UW, Prof. Long's lectures are fun as are the readings -- definitely go to quiz section to discuss the cases as he doesn't always go in depth on those.

371 was a really interesting class, however, the slides were confusing and long. The readings were interesting but incredibly time-consuming (~80 pages for one class) and the book for the final felt shoe-horned in. The exams were open-ended which made studying for them difficult. If you go to lecture and interact with the class you will do fine.

This class is really interesting and has great information that applies to various aspects of the world. Doing the readings in my experience was very important to understand his dense lectures. I suggest checking the main focus of units before lectures, so you know how his lectures connect to the overall class, assignments and tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Clear prof is knowledgable and cares about the course content. Course information interesting but lectures sometimes drag a bit. Readings important, textbooks required- one can be found online. Graded only by midterm and final blue book exams.

I started this course thinking I would fail but actually did alright. Graded on a midterm, final, assignments (2 of which are dropped). Tests are mini essays with broad questions about the material that have no strict right answer, which I appreciated. Talks very fast during lecture but posts slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took 204 and now in 371 and 362 and have loved all the classes (although all 3 very different, even though his style and assignments more or less the same in each). He does hold students to a very high standard, but gives you everything you need to meet that standard -- have also had good TAs in general for his classes (and polisci generally).

Prof. Long isn't necessarily a bad professor, however the lectures feel longer than necessary which I feel enables people to just skip the class and take the notes off the slides (which are put on canvas anyways). Make sure to study the course material, majority of your grade relies on the midterm and final.

I tried to give Prof Long the benefit of the doubt because the class material is just boring to me. But he was so frustrating. He would frequently answer questions with a question or just not be helpful. 70% of the grade is exams, which he gives very little guidance for and the grading was confusing. He also did not allow TAs to do final review.
Good lecturer and engages students well. As long as you complete the readings and attend lectures, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easily the best professor I have had at UW. Very engaging lecturer and beyond smart. Hope to take his classes again soon.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Long is spectacularly intelligent and knowledgeable.

I loved this class and the way Professor Long lectures. He has very clear expectations and chooses reliable TAs that help you out a lot. This class is graded by only a few assignments and reading is necessary, but its really interesting and lectures are fairly engaging/entertaining
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Entertaining lecturer.

I warmed up to Professor Long over the duration of the quarter, but I was skeptical at first. He talks very quickly and commonly goes off on (admittedly interesting) tangents. You have to be willing to engage as you've never engaged before to get through this class. That said, I appreciate that Professor Long takes his students seriously.

Intro to Comparative Politics was my favorite class this year. Lectures are fun and funny, and the class is super organized and expectations clear which i appreciate since I'm neurodivergent and most UW profs are totally unorganized!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor long's lectures are useless, he reads off of the slides and then just rambles for the rest. He is  condescending when students ask questions. The class is interesting but the way it's presented has made me dread it. Graded on a scale where a 77 is a 2.0, one midterm, one final, and section assignments. Pray your TA is an easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: An amazing professor who's lectures genuinely captured the attention of me and everyone in the class. He is so knowledgeable and easy to listen to. Made learning comparative politics easy to understand with the amount of real world examples he provides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Long is truly the best in UW's Poli Sci/JSIS departments. He truly cares so much about his lesons and wants every student to learn. I took both his Africa and Corruption class, and had to do a decent maount of reading for both. He can come across as a little rough in regards to how he answers questions, but generally is pushing your thoughts

Took Global Crime & Corruption and it was my favorite class at UW. You learn about everything from ISIS to the Nazi Party to drug cartels. Lots of pop culture references too -- Prof. Long knows movies, books, and tv shows, lol.

Best intro class in polisci sequence; basically global view of politics where you study different regions and countries (some historical stuff but mostly recent cases). Textbook is helpful -- definitely go to lectures. Long cares about his students and wants them to do well, so listen to the advice he gives at beginning of quarter and follow it.

He will accommodate your disabilities, he just wants you to go through DRS first bc they know how to handle it better than he does. He can be rude and he doesn't have a huge drive to learn more about outside subjects, but he knows his stuff and is a good lecturer. A bit of a snob but he won't waste your time and the class is very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved this class, and word is his version of Intro to Comparative Politics (204) is better than others. Textbook is useful and provides good background (make sure to read the case studies as he doesn't always focus on these depending on the week), but lectures were super interesting and helpful.

I took 3 classes with Long in the political economy option. He takes learning very seriously and wants his students to do well -- hence he doesn't just agree with every question or point made. Def. go to lectures but don't worry about the slides as much -- he posts those on Canvas. African politics/data science class was my favorite.

I took his class over two years ago, and I still find myself thinking about him. He was the worst professor I have ever had, and I have some wild ones. He makes you feel so dumb when you ask questions. Each of his slides are the length of doctoral dissertations, and he keeps them on the screen for no more than 5 seconds.

Took both Crime & Corruption and the Africa data science class and loved both. Definitely lots of reading, and for Corruption, attending quiz section (which I typically find tedious) helped understand aspects of lecture and readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I found his lectures to be somewhat arrogant and obnoxious. He doesn't have great command of the written word - often his exam prompts were unnecessarily confusing. He was not the worst professor, but I did not feel overly welcome and did not enjoy my time in class.
Crime and Corruption was dope class, want to take the Africa classes next.
In Crime and Corruption right now and it's really fun. Took 204 last year and also pretty interesting, but 371 class on Corruption is definitely best I've taken at UW (I'm LSJ and JSIS).
This class is very very interesting. The content is digestible and I found that you can scrape by pretty okay without doing most of the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Long's class. You can tell he really cares about CP, and lectures are engaging. His class made me want to pursue the major. Don't have your phone out where he can see it and don't make extraneous noise. There is a sizable amount of reading, but you can get by fine without doing all of it. Grades depend on the TA you get
204 (Comparative Politics) convinced me to apply for the major -- loved this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Crime and Corruption was the best remote class I took at UW (just graduated). Cool mix of econ, polisci, history, and lots of stuff from current events. The podcast series helped as they don't require reading or looking at a screen, and lots of their guests were really interesting.

Taken online due to Covid. Lots of reading and assigns podcasts every week of him talking with other professors. Posts slides but you wont understand context unless you go to lecture. Talks really fast and hard to understand content. Graded on two discussion questions, midterm, and final. Interesting topic but easy to fall behind in class.

Just turned my last final at UW and excited to graduate! 371 was a high note to go out on despite Zoom this year. Lectures were fun and the reading interesting -- definitely worthwhile to attend quiz section as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class itself is easy, but Prof. Long is so narcissistic... He primarily assigns HIS own podcasts for course materials, creating a huge lack of diverse views on core topics. His approach is also VERY ethnocentric- for example, promoting Narcos Mexico as accurate to Mexican culture, with this being one of the only mentions of the region in class.
Crime and Corruption was dope class, also took 204 with him when I first got to UW, really fun lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The Q&A part of class was best given remote learning -- he actually respects students and takes their questions seriously, unlike many profs who don't bother.
POLS204 made me want to apply for the polisci major.

I do not know how it's possible that this many students have had such great experiences with him. He is seriously rude to students. Ask the wrong questions in class and you'll pay for it. He will shame you if you don't understand things. Moves way too quickly through the slides and he knows it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: First polisci class and this is Introduction to Comparative Politics but it's all about "democracy in the modern world" (and a lot about how democracy ain't working in lots of places) -- lots of current events but also cool stuff from history as well as examples from many regions/countries .

Took his African Political Development seminar and it was my favorite class in college. A lot of reading (most of it good/interesting) and completely discussion-based seminar. Class ended with unit on Afrofuturism that was really cool, including watching Black Panther. Really fun class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Loved POLS204 and 371 (on corruption).

As a Nuero-Diverse student, I need to be in frequent contact with my professors about medical issues. Day 1 in Lecture Dr Long said he is not a Doctor do not talk to him about medical stuff. I dropped that day. Do not take him if you have stuff that may come up and you may need to talk to your professor.

I wasn't sure what comparative politics even was before taking this class but now I'm thinking of adding Polisci as a minor. Professor Long's lectures were great, even during Covid. Learned a lot about all sorts of countries.
371/crime and corruption was hands down the best class I took in college.

Okay, so i'm not sure why Long gets such great reviews. His ego is overtly inflated and he's rude to students. He's condescending when questions are asked. Furthermore, he goes off on tangents and his whole 371 syllabus appeared disorganized. He made really out-there connections with no substance. It wasn't rooted in content but his own hypotheses.
Had him for both 204 and 371 and he was awesome!

Totally cool end to a quarter learning about crime and corruption that he wants students to apply today in the world. Lots of international focus on the course material, but a good deal on US (founding fathers but also Trump and impeachment). Final exam was actually interesting and topical, mentioned George Floyd (and Martin Luther!).
Wow, just heard his last lecture for Crime and Corruption. It was a barn-burner for sure! Best lecturer at UW.

Online learning sucks, but he did a much better job than any of my other profs. Fun lectures and good convos in quiz section. Also, lots of discussion of current events to go along with historical cases studies, which made this class feel more relevant than most other polisci ones.

Maybe it was just because this class was offered online for the first time but I did not feel like Long was as good as other reviews suggest. His lectures were confusing, he didn't seem super engaged in what he was teaching, and I felt that the class did not follow any clear plan or course. The final is also 40% of your grade, the midterm is 30%.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture and reading heavy like other POLS courses, but lectures were very packed and we were bombarded with so much information. Did no absorb many slides because he goes so fast and their are so much on them. TA's grading was very lenient. Graded by weekly discussion questions (easy), midterm and final which was a paper. Overall not too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are super fun and the readings really interesting and topical. The review below this one is dumb -- I'm in the class now and that's not what he said. He posts the lecture slides before class so he said not to worry about writing everything down from the slides because you get the slides anyways. Lectures are fun to listen to!

Longs lecture slides are small essays that he skims over in maybe 10 seconds, giving you little to no time to write it all down. He even admitted before a class, I know my slides are content packed, I wouldnt even be able to write it all down in the first try, so be sure rewatch the lecture. The lecture is an hour and a half long.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I had POL S 204 with Professor Long online because of the pandemic, and yet he was still able to keep me engaged and inspire about comparative politics. It was the first POL S class I took at UW, and I liked it so much that I'm gonna take some more over the next few years. Not an easy A, but I quite enjoyed the class. Easy workload.

Crime and Corruption was a really cool class. You delve into a lot of interesting material from tons of different cases and history. Lectures were great, but definitely do the reading (most of which is fun and kinda quirky).

I greatly enjoyed this class, the lectures were very well structured and the professor knew what he was talking about. The only annoying thing was no technology in class or in quiz section but I'm not sure if he is going to stick with that b/c my class was the first to try it out. He has really good explanations but it's a reading heavy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I didn't love this professor just because his lectures we're really fast, and theres no technology allowed in class. But in the long run I feel like I learned a lot and his tests were reasonable, and I would take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great class, really interesting and fun lectures.
Absolutely best professor at UW, have taken three classes with him and really enjoyed them all!

The best professor that I have had at UW. I specifically took this class because I enjoyed JSIS B 371 with him so much. He has done incredible work around the world and is an amazing lecturer with clear explanations and grading. It was incredible learning from a leading expert on Africa and hearing him speak about his research. TAKE THIS CLASS!!

Best class ever -- especially for intro level. Loved the material and best lecturer I've had at UW. Clearly cares about his students and I've never seen someone so energetic about political science. Can't wait to take more courses with him!

He tried to fit so many things into lecture that the last 10 minutes were chaotic and caused confusion over topics. If you show up late, get ready to feel his wrath because for some godforsaken reason it's his Achilles Heel. Basically you're either gonna like him or you're gonna want to transfer out.

Yells at students for dropping water, sneezing, coming in 5 minutes late. Super condescending and goes by lectures too fast. Also his lectures are much too broad and he tries to connect things that don't work. I wouldn't reccommend taking any of his classes to anyone, and most people I know in the class would say the same.

Amazing lectures, really explains topics well and thoroughly. Pretty important to go to lecture. The readings are all very relevant and make the topic more understandable without being a waste of time. They are all also very readable and interesting. One of the best classes I've taken at UW, super interesting topic with a great professor.

One of the best professors that I have had at UW. The grade is based on quiz section short paper each week and a midterm and final. The tests are similar to the study guide and clearly graded. He is so interesting and engaging, everyone should take his class!

Great professor with really good lectures, but you will need to work hard. Challenging grader and there is SO much complicated reading that he does test on, but really interesting material and overall good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is one of the best professors I ever had. His lectures are engaging and actually teach something. Definitely recommend him. I am very picky when it comes to professors but he got my respect!

I've taken Pol S 204 and Pol S 335 with Professor Long. He is without a doubt the best professor I have ever had, and 335 is the most excited I've been about a course. Any opportunity to learn from him simply cannot be passed up. Interesting and highly applicable readings, amazingly cohesive lectures, and a sarcastic sense of humor.
Amazing lecturer, and thinker. Keeps students engaged and is kinda hot

One of my favorite professors at UW. You'll want to go to his lectures because he's so engaging and knows so much about what he's teaching. Almost disappointed every time lecture ended because he had me so interested in what he was saying.

This man cares about democracy more than I've ever cared about anything in my entire life.  I was in his autumn 204 lecture and I thoroughly enjoyed hearing from someone who has so passionately dedicated himself to his field. Nothing but respect from me.

From his 204 class, and he's probably my favorite lecturer I've had as of yet here. His lectures are entertaining and engaging with interesting material. The readings can be a bit tedious but he explains them well enough. Overall great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: African Politics was probably my favorite class I took at UW. Professor Long knows his stuff and is passionate, which makes his class both interesting and easy to be engaged in.  Expect to be held accountable for your readings and to participate in class, but i'm happy I did because I feel as though I really took something away from this class!

The class was nearly all discussions, but he made sure that the material we read and the topics covered were interesting. A paper every few weeks and participation in class based on the readings was all that was needed. He's really funny and interesting to talk to, and the class was one of my favorites.
Awesome!  I learned a ton about African Politics.  Professor Long really knows his stuff -- definitely take this class.

Professor Long is a really great lecturer. He sometimes lectures on his own research and based on this you can tell he is very passionate about his work. He gives out a pretty accurate study guide for the test, which makes the exams pretty decent in terms of difficulty. To succeed however you should definetely know the material on the study guide.

Your grade in the class is based off the mid-term and the final.  They aren't too hard but make sure you know the content pretty well.  He gives you good study guides for the tests too.  His lectures are funny and entertaining and you can tell he's passionate about his work.

Professor Long is a great lecturer, he presents information in a clear and effective manners and his lectures are always fun to go to. As with any political science class there was a good amount of readings, but not much more beyond 2 tests. Very nice guy, enthusiastic about his work. (I am glad he includes his own work in the lectures)
Great class -- his 447 African Politics class is also great!
great prof
Great class!
knows his stuff, knows how to teach.  Wish I could take another class with him.

Great professor. No weekly assignments, only reading, which was all online. 30% of the grade was participation, the rest was one midterm (very easy, I got 99%) and one final (a bit less easy but still easy). Class was quite interesting if you like politics and he presented a bit of his own research too.

Passionate and knows a lot about math. Talks very fast during lecture so I recommend going over slides before class. Homework is difficult but exams are not bad at all and he usually gives practice exam problems similar to the real exam. Tends to go on math tangents that won't be tested just for fun, which can be a bit confusing. Overall cool prof!

Math 506 with Monty was by far the hardest class I have ever taken. His homework is tough and interesting. The lectures are almost impossible to follow if you don't thoroughly read the material before class, but fascinating and entertaining if you did. Final was brutally difficult and not generously curved. I learned a ton and would do it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. He is really passionate about math and humourous. He is ready to help and caring his students. Very accessible outside the class through email (as long as you seek help). The only bad thing about him is that he speaks too fast and is hard to follow during lectures, so be prepared to read the material before the class.

Monty McGovern is an amazing professor and lecturer, he knows his stuff extremely well, but he is also an extremely fast talker. Would recommend you read his ppt before the lecture to get a general idea of what he is going to lecture on. Overall he is one of the best professors in the department.
He is very patient and explains the concepts clearly during the lecture!

Professor McGovern is very passionate about Math and what he is teaching. His lectures are on the drier side and you need to pay attention to understand. They are big text blocks with few examples that are laid out mathematically and are instead explained in words.

Monty is a good prof, explaining things in detail and being super accessible by email. His hand writing is a little messy on the chalkboard, but he uploads lecture slides ahead of time so you can look over them in advance. Exams are straightforward. Also has a dry sense of humor which is refreshing

Monty is a really lovely professor; he will give many vivid examples to help you learn concepts. If you don't know the concept, you could make an appointment and go to his office hour, he is really willing to help you! At the same time, he was a very conscientious professor. I like his teaching style this quarter.

Great professor, extremely knowledgeable and approachable with questions! He definitely moves quite quickly and is old-school, so you should always show up to class. He often drops hints about exams that are quite helpful for those who show up! Expect to see some problems on exams that are derived from class examples. Overall great professor!

Monty is a lovely man. He is a very old-school professor, so don't expect much technology to be used in the classroom. His online lecture notes are poor but he truly cares about the content he teaches and puts his all into showing his passion for math.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Monty is a super fast lecturer, it's difficult to keep up with hum. He also goes off-book sometimes, which is interesting but you need to show up or read through his notes. His class is tough but he gives you everything you need to succeed if you're willing to work through the lectures and HW with rigor. Weekly homework, two midterms and a final.

The class is so disorganized and his slides teach nothing. Follow the textbook and you'll be fine. And he takes off points on his exam if you get the right answer but compute it using another way he did. He awards points completely arbitrarily and makes no sense in his grading. Awful professor.

Quite confused by the high ratings, especially the tag "Amazing Lecturer". Lectures are non-stop with little to no examples, no pauses for questions, and the notes are presented as giant text blocks with no organization. He is a nice enough professor but there is no way I will be prepared for 403 and seriously regret taking this course.

The way he teaches online classes is by reading slides for 15-20 minutes (for a 50-minute class). Extremely hard to follow. I playback at 0.75 speed in order to "listen"(not understanding) to what he is saying(compare to the 1.5 and 2.0 speed I use for other Profs). He gave high grades, thus a high rating. But not recommended if you want to learn.

If you care about your grade but not the learning, this is your man. His lectures are incredibly quick and difficult to follow (I can count on 1 hand how many times he lectured for more than 20 minutes). Despite my 3.4 in the class I don't think I learned anything. I will likely fail MATH 404.

Lectures are super fast paced; on average 17 minutes. Homeworks are short; about 4 to 5 questions per week. Very responsive on emails and great during office hours. Very lenient professor who in fact cares about his students. Be prepared to teach yourself a lot but make sure to attend/watch all his lectures because he drops massive hints in them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Monty is awesome. His lectures are super dense and he provides a lot extra materials not in the textbook. It is difficult but it is a 400 level class, you should expect to work hard for it. He is really generous with partial credits. Just a lovely man.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Genuinely confused by high ratings. He lectures for only 15 min then leaves. His lectures consist of reading his notes aloud; even when they are about geometry, he provides no visual examples (or further explanation of any kind). Only assigned hw and practice problems from book but half the class was based on other material. Grading isn't too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His lectures are super fast-paced, expect to read the textbook for homeworks and tests. Tests are not difficult as long as you read the textbook and know key theorems and properties. Grades heavily depend on your final exam score. The curve is not harsh, I got few points above average, still managed to get an A.

Great professor who really cares about his students and is dedicated to educating his students math. While his lectures are very thorough, they weren't always useful and are often very complicated with little intuitive sense how he reached certain steps. But if you understood the lectures, his lectures are amazing!
Guys a sweethearted legend. I will never forget his teddy bear cheering me on as I get my butt kicked by his clever tests.
Very easy grader. He talks super fast during lectures and has sloppy handwriting, but he's more than glad to stop and explain in more detail at any time. Awesome guy!

I don't think the tests or the homework or whatever graded assignments we do are the purpose of the class --- if you do the practice problems and make a notesheet, you'll be fine. However, Monty's lectures are profound and very interesting --- sometimes you'll spend weeks trying to actually get it, but when you get them, it's fantastic. Lecture!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Had him as my two week lecturer in a math camp over the summer at UW (I'm a high school student). Although he was challenging from time to time, he would help if anyone needed it. Moreover, he is such a kind, genuine and caring person. You will not regret taking his class. I promise
One of the best professors in the math department. Take him if you can

McGovern is the reason I want to study algebra more.  He will give you the best undergraduate experience when it comes to this subject.  To be honest, there could be more homework, so if you are struggling, try and do more problems out of the textbook (Artin - for which there are hundreds).  Don't skip class, or you'll miss material not in the book

The hype is well deserved. He took a difficult class and made it engaging and accessible. Lectures much more helpful than the book. Readily available if you require help. Designed the tests to be on par with the skill level of the class. Reasonable work load. Generous grading. So far, my favorite professor

Best maths professor at UW, easily.  Pros: Clear, focused, organized lectures. Doesn't stray far from the book. You know exactly what to expect on the tests if you go to his review day. The theoremsdef's he hammers home is only what he tests on. Easy grader Cons: He speaks very quickly and tends to stand in front of his writing. TAKE HIS CLASS!
Boss
By far the best professor I've ever had in UW. An absolute genius with an extremely welcoming attitude towards his student. Very helpful both in and out of class. Great sense of humor. Recommend++!
the nicest, most genuine mathematics professor at the University of Washington

Had him for 309 and 324 which are both very hard classes. He is an excellent teacher: old school, very relaxed, super nice and approachable, willing to help in after hours. His tests are hard, but he's a really easy grader. He has a quirky and funny sense of humor and is very anti materialistic. One of my math favorite teachers.

Lectures and explanations are very well organized. He definitely cares about his students, and you will highly benefit from going to his office hours. I would highly recommend him for any math class you take.
He is a great professor! Go to office hours and you will learn a lot!!!!

Awesome professor and very nice. Assigns only 5 problems a week for homework. He knows every single thing you ask him (about math), and is very helpful and patient. You can also ask him things completely unrelated to the class, and will give you very helpful advice (I asked him for advice about being an actuary). Overall a good prof and nice person
He is very helpful and explains homework problems and in-class material very well.Take his class and definitely go to his office hour!!!

Though he moves at a fast pace, he's clear and concise and very amenable to clarification. His assigns five problems a week from the book and allows notes on his tests, which are weighted equally with homework, making them less stressful. Over all, the classwork isn't very difficult, and if you attend class you should learn a lot and do quite well.
One of the nicest, most genuine professors I've had at the UW. Really knows his stuff, and takes a real interest in his students.

He is one of the best math prof I have ever seen! Talented, know his stuff well and really knows how to teach them to students! He is nice and easy to approach, smart and willing to listen to you!A little bit shy sometimes, but very clear when answering your questions!

One of the best math prof I have ever had,  His lectures are easy to follow, he has easy to read handwritting when he writes on the board (this is very rare for math profs) Whenever anyone has a question he always takes the time to answer it and he seems to always know the answer to everything.  I think he is one of the best math profs around!

A thorough, intelligent, and understanding professor, but not very personable... a bit brusque. He seems to be a very nice guy, but you won't know that unless you go talk to him in person. Homework is difficult but weighted evenly with the tests, so bad test-takers will have a chance to shine. Just be aware that he moves at a very fast pace!

Class about proofs: how to perform them with a variety of techniques in a variety of situations.  Completely new subject matter as far as I was concerned and completely fascinating.  Presentation of ideas and concepts was very clear, and given in quite a number of examples to give an idea of the breadth and scope of how they could be used.

I took Monty for 310 and really liked the class a lot. It was fairly challenging at times, but the homeworks and tests were hard enough to push you without making you overly frustrated. I would recommend taking a class with him. He is a really nice guy and always very helpful to his students.
He is kind of quirky, but  he is an excellent teacher.

Lectures were very informative, and great for giving future context, and making us interested in further pursuing math. He did a great job of tying linear algebra, differentiation, and derivatives together, and giving us better ways to do math than the book always did. He was very helpful in answering questions. Fair grader, fair system.

Professor McGovern is awesome!  He can be intimidating, but he's actually nice, open to suggestion, and a very fair grader.  His TA (who grades HW) was a tougher grader than Professor McGovern (who grades exams).  HW was difficult but exams were very fair and weighted quite evenly with HW.
His lectures, tests, the book, and homework were not well coordinated.
He has a good sense of how material now will be applied later, and thus always gives context.  Great lecturer.

Honors class--extremely tough competition.  Tests never seemed to relate to the homework; several people who got perfect homework scores and who thought they understood the material would fail the tests.  Got more abstract and "out there" with t
An excellent professor; lectures are interesting, tests are usually fair.  His quirky sense of humor makes Calculus survivable.
Really dives into the works covered in class and the context behind them. Highly recommend!

I would suggest only taking one of Marek's classes if you're really interested in the topic. The lectures are not very engaging so it's easy to get lost and lose track of what or who he's talking about. The multiple choice on the exam was also very wordy and hard to understand. I did learn a lot in this class but more from the textbook than him

AH 272, too much reading and  lack of organization and rational outline, but hard grading for all homework, even weekly discussions average ranges is only around 7/10. TA Jade Ichimura puts on a face higher than the professor's position. Don't take their courses.

if you're a history major you would love this class, but if you're not DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. There are too many readings and the lectures are really boring. You will have to memorize a lot of things for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A ton of homework and readings, almost 70 pages of dense academic readings along with usually 90 minutes of pre-lecture recordings. This class was generally boring, and the organization was terrible with tons of unclear deadlines and an unnavigable canvas page.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't get fooled by the title of the course, we do not talk much about Lady Gaga. This class isn't an easy A, theres so much readings to do and prerecorded lectures to watch before lecture and there will be quizzes about the readings. The lectures are very long and boring. I wouldn't take this class if you need an A&H credit.

This class is HORRIBLE, if you are interested in art history then it might not be that bad but he assigns SO MUCH readings it's insane. Quizzes aren't too bad, they;re all online and only 2 exams he assigns and all multiple choice but definitely boring in my taste and kept falling asleep especially since it is in a dark room and it's a 2 hr class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take this class unless you are very passionate about the topic. Most of your grade is based on quarter long project with a randomly assignment group. Group presentations and long reading analysis every week. Prof clearly cares about the topic but doesn't usually extend this care to students or how they are doing in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Probably one of the worst classes I've taken, The professor was so unorganized, one of the weeks an assignment was created the day it was due.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This professor assigns an assignment due friday, sunday and Monday every week that includes long readings, research and a presentation. It is an extremely heavy workload in which you are teaching yourself all of the material. lectures are incredibly boring and repetitive, and canvas instructions are consistently unclear.
could not skate in class. Fricked up. would not take again.
