Don't take this course. He talks about nothing for like two hours and the material is not explained well. No one knows what is going on and he is sassy when you ask questions. Take a different art history course cause you won't learn anything from this one.

I took this class thinking that it would be interesting and fun to try out. There are pre-recorded lectures every week. The material that you have to learn for the final exam is ridiculous.Not being an art history major, I was not taught how to properly write art history papers, which in turn was hard to get good grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is an excellent professor to take upper level Art History classes from. To excel in his course you need to work, and if you are willing to deep dive into the subject he is an incredible guide and supportive teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I will say, this is a very reading-heavy class. There are single question quizzes every week that you can easily get a good grade on if you do the readings, but he goes over parts of them in class during lecture. You don't get new information out of lectures which causes them to be boring. Due to this, I wouldn't take a class with him again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved this class. Really liked him, he was so passionate and good at explaining it made me choose art history as my major

Never took an ARTH class but ended with a 4.0. Read the material and don't procrastinate and you will do ok. If you have never taken ARTH before meet him after the first day of class introduce yourself and mention you are new to ARTH and are excited to learn, he will understand and grade you more leniently throughout the quarter. Marek is awesome!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: i feel like no matter how hard i worked in this class it didn't even matter because how well you do on quizzes is just random. no assessment of how well you actually understand the material. got a 100% on ever major assignment and it still wasn't enough to end with a 4.0 because of the daily quizzes every class period.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Is very opinionated and instead of wanting to hear about our own interpretations of whatever, he would rather hear what he thinks repeated instead. He has us read many pages before class, as well as sometimes two full lectures before we even show up to class. Quizzes every Tuesday and Thursday, lectures before class about what he repeats in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: During the lectures, prior to every lecture you have to memorize multiple different pictures, plus the info that goes with it. On top of that he will assign multiple long readings that are like 50+ pages long. I don't recommend taking this class, and I wish I read the reviews before taking this course.

As an art history major, this is the worst class I've ever taken. Instead of teaching you how to analyze art, marek teaches u to think what he thinks (or u basically fail the class). Quizzes every class which isn't productive to learning. U basically memorize all the content, take a quiz, and immediately forget it all after. Don't take this class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Marek's teaching does not seem to come from a true inspiration to engage with students, but it instead acts as an outlet for his ego. He is unwaveringly opinionated and often oblivious to the world around him. I felt valued at a very surface level value, and was constantly frustrated by both the lecture content and assigned material.

Lecture was so boring + quiz every class. Sometimes I'd get 100% on a quiz, other times I'd get less than 50% even though I read and understood the material. I hated all the reading and how we were expected to memorize/prioritize written interpretations on pieces instead of encouragd to make our own.

He cares about the content, but it's very opinion-heavy. He has a huge ego and this class has turned into a history of Catholic/western art rather than a feminist perspective of art history. I was really hoping that he would highlight female artists more as advertised, but I really hate this class due to the heavy and useless homework and boredom
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had the worst experience in art and climate change. Professor is both full of himself and hypocritical, and thinks that going to an eco-village for three months is a valid replacement for having a course plan. Demanded 100% effort for what was effectively 15% of a class, and I have too many frustrations to list in 350 characters.

Like the other review said, do NOT take Art and Climate Change. Unless you want to do GROUP presentations for majority of the quarter. Long readings. Short deadlines. Unclear expectations and vague yet super long instructions. More like a commentary class on different perspectives regarding climate change. Barely discussed art at all.

DON'T TAKE CLIMATE CHANGE & ART- I haven't talked to a single person in class who thinks the class is well organized. Assignment directions change minutes before they're due (& occasionally after which is always a fun surprise), pages worth of directions for assignments (nobody knows what info is actually important), & curriculum feels uneducated

Great lecturer, but not a good instructor. Lectures are interesting and heavy. Homework is assigned one day before the due date (on weekends). Group projects are the core of the class so good luck on being assigned to one group the whole quarter. Nevertheless, it's an easy class if you have all the time in the world.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took Art History in my Freshman year with Prof. Wieczorek and it's been my favorite class so far. Lectures are super interesting even though so much of the focus on the course is on Picasso. LOTS of reading and quizzes can throw you for a loop. We had to write 2 analysis papers and take an exam at the end that requires a lot of memorization.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Marek is a great person and obviously knows his stuff, but this class was taught as if everyone was an Art H major. LOTS of lectures on video and in person and the papers written did not relate to what we were learning about in class. Quizzes EVERY Tuesday and Thursday are a huge chunk of your grade. Meet people and discuss the dense readings!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Non-art majors beware, this is a really reading-heavy course. Prof would post a lecture for the week in addition to the two lectures in person, and assign multiple (sometimes 50+ pages each) readings for each of the 3 lectures. If you take it with the W credit, the writing doesn't have to do with lecture material, so even more reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class has quizzes every Tuesday and Thursday where you have to memorize around 12 paintings, title, painter, year, and medium and the essays never have a solid prompt. Also there are additional hour and a half lectures you have to watch every week on top of the 4 hour total week lectures.

Professor Wieczorek is deeply committed to students. He is flexible and cares about your learning, so be up front and proactive if you need to miss class and he will usually adjust to your needs. He is super jazzed about Cézanne, so even if the art isn't your most favorite thing, his enthusiasm is infectious.
First prof at UW, and was the most intelligent and considerate person ever. I don't have enough nice things to say about him. Understanding and is clear that he views his students as actual people

Marek was very engaging, well versed, and extremely considerate of his students. All he asks is you raise your hand at least once. Weekly reading quizzes, two exams, mostly easy. Course content and in depth analysis during lecture made for a high quality elective. Dont take if you dont have an appreciation for art lol.

Professor Wieczorek is a great professor. Short quizzes are typically given every lecture day. These make up most of your grade and are considered participation. He does not take attendance, but if you miss class, these quizzes can not be made up. There are two papers and two exams. He gives excellent feedback and is clear with his expectations.

He was my first professor at UW. Hes so passionate about what he teaches and is genuinely so kind and sincere. Hes understanding if you miss class and uploads recordings of every class. Most of your grade is a single question multiple choice quiz about the reading, which arent very long or hard. Amazing prof
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Marek is a great professor, and I really enjoyed the structure of this class. There are prerecorded lectures and readings and then class is devoted to discussion with Marek and other students. He is clearly very knowledgeable and passionate and challenges his students to become better art historians. Easy if you like discussions and readings.

Professor Marek is a knowledgeable person. However, he expects his students to be in similar level with him. It's his intent in creating difficult environment for students to learn more, but it is rather harsh when this isn't the only class people are taking. If you are serious in learning, his class is fantastic. If not, reconsider!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Maybe Prof. Weiczorek just doesn't translate well on Zoom, but his class has been incredibly dull and painful. Short quizzes almost every class that makeup pretty much your entire grade. They aren't too difficult if you do the reading, but there is so much dense material and supplemental lectures despite the lack of papers. Wouldn't take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Marek was a pretty good professor, but it was very test heavy every week. At least 2 small quizzes every week and regular midterm/final. This class is lecture heavy as well, so you'll need to watch the videos he provides and/or read the very long readings. I got a 4.0 but it wasn't easy, as it was a lot of readings and tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I am not an art history major, but took this course to fullfill a general requirement. Marek is a passionate and engaging lecturer. Heavy on the pre-recorded lectures/readings, but this got better with student feedback helping fit the class to an online format. Easy quizzes, and two short essays. Two normal tests. Good for exploring/absorbing art!

Dr Marek is your average art professor, however he is not compassionate or understanding towards his students. The year has brought hardship for many of us, but he fails to check on the well being of students in his class- as I tried reaching out to him about my current situation and received no reply.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I am not an art history major and just took this class to fill a general requirement. I ended up LOVING this class. It is a lot of work, but it is worth it. There are daily readings and mini-quizzes (which are very easy), and 2 exams. Professor Marek is passionate about art, and that comes through in his lectures. 100% would take recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Marek was such a great professor and really cared about how the class did as a whole on tests and quizzes. Super easy tests if you do the reading and homework. He is so funny and kind and I loved his lectures.

This was one of the first classes I took at UW and it opened my eyes to a side of art that I didn't know existed. Although the lectures are a bit long, and the material is initially esoteric, your effort will pay off. What looked like pleasantly assorted planes and lines on the first day of class will come alive on the last. Amazing professor.

I've taken several classes with this professor and each class is more and more interesting. He is incredibly knowledgeable but makes very dense material understandable. He genuinely wants to see you succeed so he tends to be lenient on grading as long as you show up, participate, and genuinely attempt to understand material.

This class was geared towards art and design majors, which I found disappointing for its introductory level. The amount of memorization of specific works of art was gargantuan, especially compared to the minuscule amount of conceptual material on the tests. I felt I learned nothing of value about art. Daily quizzes are 40% of your grade so show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Marek is a great professor. His class content is just very difficult. There are daily quizzes on the reading and the midterm and final are TOUGH. I would not recommend this class if you are not an art his major. But if you are, this is a class that you want to take. But you're definitely going to have to work for your grade
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Although this is was not my easiest art history course, I absolutely loved it! So interesting and loved coming to class. Grades hard but gives you an outline of what he wants & is very clear. Do the readings and go to class and it's a piece of cake. Definitely going to try to take more of his classes.

the best art history professor I ever know, he does have required readings but they are short, and he annotate most of the readings for you, the paper assignments are not difficult to write as long as you have been listening to his classes and go to the museum to see the artwork you're writing about. overall he's a great professor!
Great teacher who cares about how students are doing in the class and is obviously passionate about the subject he teaches.  Very understanding with different difficulties students had with the class

Marek is great. The ideas he taught are powerful, readings are intense for 200level class and all pdf files, but relevant to modern art issues and beautifully selected. If you have the ability of abstract thinking, you will find this class gradually turns itself into a ladder that allows you to climb on and reach the sublime beyond your presence.

I found from Athena to Lady Gaga class to be extra boring, especially bothering at the end with Abramovic stuff. However, because Marek is so professional, he made every single session interesting and would engage students which made me connected to the class. Expect daily quizzes and lots of reading. He is very inspirational and knowledgeable.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Knows his stuff for sure, but sometimes his lectures can be a bit repetitive or dry if you aren't indulged/interested in the work. Be prepared for ALOT of daily readings and quizzes on it, and the tests are basically just 85% memorization of dates/artists of work. Overall though a great prof and would recommend the class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Marek is what every art professor should strive to be. He makes art relatable to his students without compromising its formality and complexity. Participation points are how he integrates learning, so show up everyday for the in class quizzes. I would take his classes again in a heartbeat, even as a non-art major.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Expect a couple essays, short daily quizzes on the readings (about 5-20 pages/night), learning catalytics every friday (mostly graded for showing up, a midterm and final. Tests are the hardest part because you must memorize exact dates for all pieces (not multiple choice; date when piece started/ended) as well as the artist name, material, meanings
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Awesome lecturer, knows so much! I learned a ton in this class and now want to major in AH.

Marek was a great professor. I took a class by him about Picasso and although I was skeptical at first, I really grew to love the class and looked forward to going. Despite my relative lack of interest in Picasso specifically (to be honest I didn't read the description that closely), he was great! Enjoyable, knowledgeable, and pretty funny.

Marek is the best professor I've ever had. He's extremely knowledgeable and well-spoken. I took several of Marek's classes, and I always found them to be the most interesting, yet also most challenging. Under Marek's guidance, I improved both as a student & as a writer, and much of what I learned from him sticks with me today.

A really knowledgable, interesting professor who presents the class with new perspectives and interpretations on the class material. Can get a bit disorganized sometimes. Concepts can become a bit confusing and overly academic and wordy at times, hard to follow. I recommend this class-not your typical art history course! Marek is great!

Best professor in the department.  Marek is so passionate about his material and will challenge you a lot to help you to share his passion and understanding.  At times it may seem harsh, but he believes in his students and is an incredible teacher.  Wouldn't be the same student without him!  Take his class!

Very nice and helpful but not very effective at teach the material. He tends to stumble through some images and there is A LOT of reading. His tests ask specifics that you wouldn't think to study (because he has you study every single image you cover when only about 15-20 appear on the test). Very difficult class to do well in.

Marek is a fantastic lecturer - clearly passionate, and totally knows his stuff. He delves deeply into the material, and encourages his class to do the same. I felt very fulfilled from his class. Challenging and very illuminating. Don't take him if you aren't totally in love with art and interested in being challenged. If you are, he's amazing.
Marek is brilliant,  passionate, and amazing at lecturing. I never missed a class!

The curriculum is challenging. The professor knows his stuff and expects his students to attend class and learn from it. I enjoyed the challenge presented! He is a good teacher caught in a challenging class. Modern Art is not always the easiest subject but a very relevant subject nonetheless. I learned lots!

His tests were too hard to begin with, although he was pretty accessible when needed. He sometimes just mumbles the names of paintings and artists, which doesn't really help much with understanding what he expects students to know. I would not recomend anyone to take this class.

I beg to differ from the other comments. I certainly would not recommend this teacher. First of all he is extremely boring with his monotone voice. His grading is incredibly hard, even though, his test might not seem like it. There are just other art history professor that actually make art history more interesting and not a pain in the ass.
Absolutely Great! Take his class!
I adore this prof. He knows his stuff and holds your interest. Makes you work, but you learn a lot. I will take as many classes from him as I can before I garduate!

I adore Marek! Best Prof in the AH department. He expects a lot but if you work at it you'll do great. Very approachable and passionate about what he teaches. Coming to class is important, lots of images to learn, and the book is used thoroughly (But get it at the library). If you can take him. Oh and he's super cute.
Great professor, Incredibly kind and Caring. Lectures are okay and typical of what you will find in the 12x physics courses. She always does her best to explain things when you ask questions.
Lectures were not helpful  but count for 10% if your grade. Tests were pretty fair, though.

Lectures are dull and unhelpful compared to reading the textbook, professor always flops demonstrations. Labs are unhelpful to concepts taught in lecture yet tested on in exams. She cares more about seeming smart than actually teaching the class and fails in both.

Olmstead is quite nice but sometimes boring, sometimes interesting. Lecture participation is 10% of the course grade. I supplemented with an edition of Halliday & Resnick from my mom and had some prior experience with the material so can't accurately judge the difficulty of the class. Exams are on the more difficult side.

The lectures are useless. You barely have time to work on the examples she gives out since by the time you've finished writing the question down, she's already onto the next thing. Also incredibly monotone and only reads off the lecture slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: please for the love of god just use khan academy for phys 121--lecture is insanely useless and they expect you to teach yourself the material first and then see lecture as a review to stregthen your skills (which is bs for this expensive-ass school)

Your better off just watching a youtube video or sticking straight to the textbook, because her lectures don't add anything of substance. What's the point of a class where the professor just reads her slides, no further explanations, no thought processes explained.

There was a lack of clear explanations in classes, and no distinct effort to make the material more digestible for students. Lectures were simply read off of powerpoints, and you will be better reading from a completely different textbook than the one used by the course. Exams were made way too long, on purpose, which did not feel great.
eh was not a fan did not learn anything in 294

121 is a hard class, but Olmstead makes it kinda fun. Lots of demos, lots of going off on tangents about higher-level physics, and lots of math. Her worked examples are great prep for the exams if you see the underlying themes of the problems instead of expecting that exact problem on the tests. She is a significant part of why I got a 4.0.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Olmstead is a fantastic professor. She did the best job she could have possibly done with the material. The class has a lot of homework so beware, but the tests are fairly easy. A key tip for this class is to learn EVERYTHING by yourself. Do not get behind on the readings or else it will pile up and the class may become difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: PHYS 121 is a mess, it's designed to fail you with a huge workload and brutal exams. Unfortunately, the lectures are simply too short, leaving a ton of self-teaching to the student, this is extra difficult if you've never taken a physics class before. The work needed to do well is too high for an intro 5cr course, take it at a Community college.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class can easily be described as a cluster f*ck. The labs have absolutely no relation to the material learned in class. They are also run by TAs who have no communication with your lecture professor. This professor was fine, she made do with the little time given for lectures. 50 minutes three days a week. Tutorials aren't given enough time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class focused on topics that werent covered on the test. The demos were nice but were wasteful. The lecture videos from last quarter are reposted and are usually 2 hours long. The level of effort to succeed is way to high considering its an intro class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class I took with her was in Autumn 2020 so it was suitably coronafied and hence remote. The way It worked was that she would hold open office hours twice a week, and a private session on Fridays (with appointment). The class seemed really robotic and it was more like I was teaching myself through recorded lectures and the book.

It's necessary to assess what skills are tested by exams. The most difficult part of the exams in this class are the time limit. With only 3 minutes per question, problem-solving must be minimal in favor of a developed intuition. I don't think that's healthy for an introductory course. The professor was unsympathetic to my complaint.

I taught myself the whole quarter straight from the textbook. I couldn't learn anything from her that actually applied to the homework or tests, and it didn't help that I had never taken physics in high school. She very very rarely did practice problems and wasted a lot of time on demos.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The physics 12X series at UW is one of the hardest there is. Olmstead was a pretty good teacher and gave helpful demos during class. Not including the awful organization of the course, she did a good job.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She has an amazing capability to make even the most simple physics concepts confusing, even if they are things you already know. She also loves to throw in completely useless information about the world of complex physics and does lots of useless demos that take a lot of time.

Prof. Olmstead is pretty average as far as physics teachers go. Some days you can totally follow along with her, and other days you're staring at 3 equation-filled chalkboards with no idea what the what is going on. She tends to focus on math/formulas instead of providing examples, which can make applying concepts in tests difficult. Read!! Study!!
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Theres no doubt Prof. Olmstead knows her stuff, but it feels like she expects you to know everything she does. She is very organized, in the wrong way. Information overload in some lectures, often times she will not finish the lecture and have to skip material. Expects you to read textbook before classes, which is fair. At least she is friendly.

It's refreshing to have a teacher who loves what she does.  Made learning E&M fun.  Lectures can be confusing at times, lots of demos,but tutorial and lab do not match up at all due to a disorganized dept. Great teacher, funny, hard exams.  Recommend her!

Dry lectures, the real help was from the prelectures before the class otherwise i would have been lost. If you go to her in office hours she can be helpful. Demos are pretty good, but the lecture and notes on the board can be confusing. She does not post her notes online.

This lady lights up the room with her enthusiasm, even if her lecture content is a little dry. Her lectures followed the book pretty well, clarifying and enforcing the text. GREAT demos.  Pleasant demeanor.
She is really helpful when you go to her office hours.

Well it seems that she is getting a really bad rep so I am going to stick up for her! Yes, she does spend a little too much time doing demos and not enough time solving problems, but I think that she explains the concepts really well. She is not nearly as bad as people say that she is and this class is not nearly as hard as people say it is!
This teacher is terrible. Her lectures are more or less pointless. Very clumsy when explaining concepts. She often explained something, and then contradicted it ten minutes later.

Bad teacher... Simple. Very confusing lectures,and seriously way too many useless demonstrations that don't help at all. She needs to spend more time on quantitative physics instead of just showing what happens when I do this, we need to know why and how to calculate it. Very clumsy too, constantly messing up demonstrations and wasting time.
Horrible experience. Exam questions are very confusing.

Prof. Olmstead knows her physics, but the problem is that she is not very good at explaining to those who aren't so good at physics. She places a large emphasis on the lecture, and the questions she writes for the exams tend to be confusing. Also, her explanations are not always clear so don't feel bad about forcing her to clarify over and over.

Frankly, the freshman from the 1xx classes are whining. This is Physics. Get over it and get to work! On the whole, P. Olmstead gives a difficult class and doesn't hide the fact that she expects you to put in the time and learn the material - she wants you to and will help you, though her answers to ?'s for help are often incredibly obfuscated.
Was very behind the syllabus all the time so that I we were behind all the other classes learning for homework and labs.
People like her should not be able to be a professor. There should be no place for her at UW. Most awful experience I have ever had.
No Comments
No Comments

Dr. Schivell is such an amazing professor, she was great at explaining concepts and left a lot of room for students to ask questions. Her public exams were extremely helpful as well, I'm so grateful to have had her!

Dr.Schivell is honestly amazing. Her lectures are easy to grasp and she's good at explaining hard topics well. Her public exams are a lifesaver and definitely helped me study well. The only gripe I have is that the exams can be very tough despite the public exams, but there are enough outside opportunities to compensate.Take her section if you can!

Dr. Schivell is very enthusiastic and explains topics in a very digestible way. She has "public exams" which help you prepare for the actual exams very well. Doing the daily activities and other assignments will reinforce your grade and she also has a generous drop system.

She made everything easy to understand and is very kind and receptive to questions. You can tell she wants you to learn and succeed. However, lectures were not a great use of time, especially for a class you have every day of the week. POGILS were not helpful at all, Public exam was a lifesaver though

Kindest, sweetest professor I have had at UW. She publishes her exams before you take them, removing test anxiety. The only things I don't like is that she uses POGILS, they waste class time and are very unhelpful, and that her lecture slides are hard to study from because they're basically incoherent. otherwise good!

Releases exams beforehand with redacted values to reduce test anxiety. If you work to understand the content these are basically godsent and will get you the grade you want. You can drop 1 of four exams including the final, so I got to prioritize my other finals. Challenging content, but fairly good explanations and very sweet person overall.
She's kind and makes her exams easier to study for with public exams but her lectures are full of content and sometimes unengaging.

Dr. Mandy does a great job explaining all of the content, however, her slides are very disorganized and she often doesn't post the annotated versions of her slides after class. Labs are very helpful to reinforce content and the TAs are great! The public exams were the best part about this class, they help teach you how to study honestly

Dr. Mandy is a fun and caring professor, and the material was very interesting, so I had a great experience. Grading is mostly based on open-note weekly quizzes and brief presentations on figures, so it was manageable. Dr. Mandy is also the most approachable prof I've had at UW, so I would recommend her to anyone.
Highly recommend her for BIOL 200, public exams make the class very easy

While Mandy does come to class excited and tries her best to be a good lecturer, I personally found her slides a bit disorganized. And when she is teaching, it tends to get very messy with her drawings and descriptions. However, I believe this is just a matter of personal preference, as everyone else I know has liked her a lot. She was consistent.

Professor Schivell is an excellent instructor! Her lectures are very clear and easy to understand, and it is obvious she wants us to succeed by posting public exams. The labs are also super helpful at reinforcing content and everyone is super enthusiastic and encouraging!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took this class Summer 2025. Asking questions was encouraged and the labs were helpful in reinforcing the content. Overall, her lectures and slides made it easy to learn and understand the content. Lots of practice problems provided and room to converse about test questions and get points back.

Her exams were very reasonable and matched the lecture material very well. Participation is very encouraged during class. She would ask a lot of questions for student engagement. However, her lectures were structured and well put-together!

MCD is a very difficult concept, but Dr. Schivell does an excellent job in making it digestible for students. Provides a preview of exam questions before and gives lengthy practice packets that make the exams a lot easier. She's also receptive to feedback and extremely kind, highly recommend taking 200 with her!
recommended

Professor Schivell's class can be challenging, but her public practice exams are a lifesaver. Using Unstuck study and the textbook alongside her lectures helped me stay on top of the material and earn a solid grade.

Dr. Schivell is a great professor. She is very kind, and is also an excellent teacher. Her lecture notes are well organized and relevant. I also liked how she posted the exams before the fact with parts of the questions missing, which I feel helped prepare me.

Curved the class down so that only 5% of students could receive a 4.0. Dreaded lecture, it was mandatory through PollEv and it typically did not relate to the textbook, both her slides and lecture notes were incredibly unhelpful. Would have done much worse in the class if not for the public exams

I really enjoyed BIOL200 with Mandy, she is very caring and wants students to succeed. Lectures are engaging, she explains how what we are learning applies to everyday life. She has "Public Exams" (versions of the exams posted prior to the real exam with redacted information) so you get a good idea of the topics that you will be tested on.

She was a pretty good lecturer but if you did the readings the lecture was pretty repetitive. She had public exams which were great and helped you know what to study beforehand, as well as lots of good practice problems. I've had better profs but she was nice, work load was reasonable, and she seemed to care about students.

Worst teacher I've ever had. Sloppy lectures with hand scribbled notes. Most of the course grade is weighted for exams, if you struggle with test anxiety, get ready to be absolutely shafted by her ability to throw random concepts  at you that aren't on the practice exams, that you went over maybe once in lecture, and maybe read about once. TERRIBLE

She was a unique way of teaching that I deemed helpful but other classmates would disagree. In class work referred to as POGILs help you understand the expectations that would are to uphold on exams. She is very nice and willing to meet with you if you are struggling. Attend her office hours, she offers great information for exams and success.

Mandy Schivell's practice exams are completely idiotic. Because of this system, instead of spending time learning content, you waste 4 hours dissecting her grammatical choices to figure out what has been redacted. Because of this, averages are incredibly high and your grade becomes dependent on tiny differences in points. DO NOT TAKE IT WITH HER!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love Mandy. Her public exams really help you going through all the concepts before exams and easy to get a nice score.

the amount of work this professor gives is crazy. she gave us so much work to do in the first week of class. on top of that, we had a dumpster fire lab where everyone was confused on how to label drawings without any examples given. i was looking forward to invert zoology but this is way too much work and stress! if you enjoy the topic don't take.
I loved her. She is such a good professor.

She is fantastic! I hated bio180 and she single-handedly made me love bio again. Her lectures are engaging, easy to understand and connect to everyday life. She wants every single person to understand the content and ask questions. Be ready for the single roll call in class tho

One of the best professors I have ever had at UW! I have taken both BIOL 434 and BIOL 466 with her and had great experiences in both courses. Dr. Mandy cares a great deal about her students. She is flexible with deadlines, receptive to questions, and encourages curiosity among science topics. I would highly recommend her courses!

Dr. Schivell is the best intro BIOL professor at UW. She is very organized and made the transition from online to in person mid-quarter seamless. Her TAs are also wonderful just like her. This is a tough course, but her caring nature and detailed lectures made this class a much nicer experience than BIOL 180 and BIOL 220.

Professor Schivell is one of the best professors I've had at uw and I highly recommend her for bill 200 especially since its a weed out class. She makes her lectures super easy to understand and most of the questions on the test usually do come from what we learn in lecture. the pogil worksheets are very beneficial. Amazing class and teaching team!
Amazing professor!

The lectures were very disorganized and the format made it hard to take notes unless you have an iPad to download and annotate the slides. Many of the exam questions were very difficult and involved topics that were beyond the scope of intro biology.

Prof Schivell really knows her subject material. I learned so much in her class and she is a kind, approachable person. Her class was also so organized, I never stressed out or felt unprepared for any exams. I learned so much and had a really inspiring quarter. She does a good job of keeping people engaged during class. Love this prof!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Schivell is amazing. Her lectures are clear and relate extremely well to the exams. The exams themselves are not too overwhelming and are a good mix of free-response and multiple-choice questions. She is extremely helpful and willing to answer your questions. Highly recommended.

Professor Schivell has to be one of my favorites professors so far at UW! She is very knowledgeable and open to all types of questions. Her lectures were informative and helpful in terms of exam prep. She held awesome office hours every Friday and had tons of practice problems. Definitely a class to take!
Very good bio prof. The exams would actually test your knowledge of the content. She really knows what she is doing to.
Great lecturer, genuinely cares about students and wants them to succeed and will provide the help to do so. Awesome teaching staff, great course format and overall a great experience!

She is definitely one of the best biology professors out there! The whole teaching team is caring and very nice all around. The grading will be similar to BIOL 180 so there is still a weed out culture in the class. I love Dr. Schivell's lectures and they were very engaging. As long as you can get everything nailed down, you should be fine.

Dr. Schivell is an extremely caring professor with easy to follow lectures and fair testing and grading. The teaching team involved with BIOL200 also are superb! Especially Liz Warfield's diligence as a course coordinator! I will always recommend Dr. Schivell for BIOL200
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Schivell is your best choice for BIOL200. She truly cares about her students and answers every question terrifically.

This class was really fun and interesting! Lots of group work/talking. You have quizzes every week (no exams) and they can be difficult but you can discuss the questions with others in the class including Dr. Mandy and the TA. Highly recommend taking a class with Dr. Mandy, she's great!

I had her for biol 200 & 466. Biol 200 wasnt the best, but its not her fault and she is probably your best choice for 200. But for biol 466, absolutely amazing. No exams, just weekly quizzes where you can discuss with anyone, including herself and the TA. Super understanding and nice. Class itself is an easy A and very interesting

Had her for 200 spring quarter and it was my favorite class! Although the material can be tough at times her lectures were very clear and contained most of what you need to know for tests (other than labs, assignments, etc.) POGILs were kind of a pain but actually did end up helping me. Lots of practice problems that are just like the test material
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Did everything in the syllabus and yet it wasn't enough
I must say Mandy is my favorite professor in uw biology.

Dr. Mandy is a super sweet and caring professor. She made her lectures fun and interactive and it was clear how much she loves biology and wants to share that with others. Lectures were thorough and covered everything you needed to know for the tests. She always made sure to be accessible to students and was always willing to answer questions.
great lecturer, truly cares for students' well-being

I took 200 with Sieverman+Schivell, and Dr. Schivell is super sweet. Online lectures with her were a bit more interactive than her counterpart, Sieverman. She uses POGILs but I honestly didn't mind because they reinforce the more test-heavy concepts. Her cat is super adorable too.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I feel like she makes me love biology. I tool Biol200 with Mandy and Katie, I could always feel their passion to biology and love to students in there class. What is more, they are really nice and all the contents they taught are so clear and learnable , which means you will not feel like not understanding what the said in lecture. Take their class

Dr. Mandy is one of the best professors I've ever had. She's definitely a very experienced teacher so she's not only knowledgeable about biology but also about how students learn best. Like Dr. Katie Sieverman, she makes herself very available for outside help and really genuinely cares about student learning and always meets you where you are.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this course vs 180. I think her lectures were much more clear and did a good job breaking down the difficult concepts we had to learn. To me, she was very approachable and was happy to answer questions or re-explain during lecture. This class is concept heavy and you need to have a good handle on the processes to do well on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took Bio 200 with Dr. Schivell and Dr. Sieverman (duel lecturers). The tone and language of the lectures are patronizing and explanations of the material are oversimplified. This class was my worst experience by far at UW. The labs are good, but the lectures are almost unbearable. They also had a very limited knowledge of chemistry.

I loved taking cell bio with Mandy, she said the course used to have exams but she doesn't do them anymore so its all about the research on the molecular insulin response pathway. Weekly research papers and BQMOC assignments for them as well as "method cartoons" but overall all not a labor intensive or heavy memorization class and I enjoyed it :).
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Do not recommend taking this course. It is all based off of reading and summarizing research papers based on insulin response but she does not give you any background on the papers in class (only explains them after you have submitted the assignment). The grading is very unforgiving and you will get docked points unavoidably.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is absolutely the best class I've taken here! She cares a lot about students, and gives SO many opportunities for help (Friday lectures are office hours and you can ask her questions directly, it's awesome). I highly recommend taking a class with Dr. Schivell, she was so enthusiastic that I never wanted to miss class. Also, POGILS are helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very unclear with what she expects students to know and teaches material in a very surface-level way but the tests cover it on a deeper level with information we never discussed or read about. Didn't learn much from lecture and had to teach myself a lot from the text book, even though she claimed we wouldn't even need the textbook.

Love this class! Lectures are great. She gives really awesome test previews and a lot of practice problems that help a lot for the exams. Reading before lecture is really import if you actually want to understanding lecture.

BIOL 240 Intensive Introductory Biology: Human Health Emphasis It is 15 credits and all of intro biology in ONE 10 WEEK SUMMER QUARTER! It is not easy but doable. Schivell was one of three profs. Her lectures were clear and test questions were ok, she needs to work on making test questions clear about what she is asking which she self admits.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took this class to boost my grade however I was wrong. I ended the class with one of my worst grades ever. The reason is of the grading. If you have been getting A's on papers, homeworks, and tests in other class well you are wrong because the grader which is usually not her grades like no one I have ever experienced before.

Schivell explained concepts very well, but when tests came around, they were much more difficult than what was mentioned in lectures and in practice problems. I really recommend doing all practice problems and going to class everyday. Go to TA office hours with questions!

She's obviously really sweet and cares about her students, but her exams are pretty damn hard compared to the level of understanding she leads to you believe you need during lecture. She seriously underemphasizes memorization of topics (instead focusing on general understanding of processes) but you definitely need it for exams, so watch out!

Amanda is the worse professor I've ever had. She is nice, but is a terrible professor. Her exams are not fair & are ridiculously hard. I learned a lot and invested to much time and effort, and despite all of it, I did terrible in the class (even though I did very well in Bio180). Bio200 is the worse grade I've had at UW & I'm a junior. Save ur GPA!

This is such a weed out class, it's ridiculous. Schivell is actually an amazing teacher and you will learn tons, but that doesn't mean you will do well in the class. Tests cover ALL hypotheticals like mutations and such that are never covered in class. After a reasonable 1st quiz they purposely made all tests extremely hard to have less high scores
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: She is hands down the BEST PROFESSOR i've ever worked with at UW. I've taken many biology classes, and this class wasn't even in my field of interest per se, but WOW. she is SO compassionate, caring, funny, inspirational, just an amazing person and a teacher. She isn't just another professor. She will leave impact in your college career. TAKE HER!

Despite getting a 3.8 in 180, I left knowing nothing. I dreaded 200, but to my surprise Dr. Schivell's lectures were really engaging and organized. She has very clear expectations for what you do and don't need to know for exams. There's a lot of reading, but that's true for all bio classes. Overall, I loved this class! I wish she taught 220 :/
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Honestly one of the best professors I've ever had.  She knows her stuff.  She doesn't give you any more information than you'll need to know and she'll stop you if you're trying to understand something that's not necessary for the test.  She's enthusiastic and was a large part of the success in that class

I'm not sure why so many people dislike Dr. Mandy. I thought her class was awesome! The class definitely requires a decent amount of studying and reading but it's totally doable. I found her lectures to be very helpful (just a bit messy) and re-watching via Panopto is helpful when studying/reviewing. Dr. Many is also super smart and nice!

I should have waited next quarter to take this class with another professor. This class was very hard to keep up with especially because her notes are very messy and difficult to read. Also, her voice gets to be annoying after a while. However, she is very knowledgable about biology and is certainly passionate to teach it.

Dr. Schivell knows what she is doing. Her class is one of my favorite of the bio series because of how well she covers the topics. She also helps you prepare for the midterms and finals by releasing a "preview" of some of the material that will be on the test like pictures or graphs. Very good professor.

I loved taking this class with Mandy! She is a really clear lecturer and her classes were engaging. She wrote on her slides in class, which is slightly annoying because her handwriting is kind of messy, but it is easy to follow along. Clicker questions were really easy. Labs were really fun also.

Horrible lecturer. Super hard to follow and is boring on top of it. Went from a 3.6 in 180 to a 2.0 in 200 and then back up to a 3.5 in 220. MCD is even my major now and I feel like she did not set me up for success in my harder molecular/cellular classes.

I love Mandy, she is an awesome person and professor and I feel lucky that I was able to take so many classes with her. She is always there to help when you need it and genuinely cares about her students. Her classes are pretty engaging, I like I her teaching style and her exams are easy as long as you pay attention in class.
An uninspiring professor. Overall a terrible lecturer and drags students down. If I had to take this class again, I would try and do everything to not take it with her.

Really fun Biology class! Lectures keep you engaged the whole way through, so time flies :) I personally preferred the material over Biol 180, and Professor Schivell provides an excellent introduction to key biology concepts in this class. You can really feel that the UW Biology department is invested in good teachers.

She's a bad lecturer. Doesn't pre-make her slides, she has to write everything down as she says it, makes it tough to write notes, especially if there's no screen space and she crams stuff in. Clicker questions and reading quizzes are filled with trick questions. Lectures don't match the reading. Doesn't set you up for success. Had a 3.8 in BIOL180

So funny and cheerful! She clearly loves teaching biology and she makes every effort to help students learn, which is a rare thing amongst UW STEM professors. Note that you should come to lecture as often as you can, since she usually does clicker questions.

She's still getting used to notes on her iPad, but I enjoyed how interactive she was with the class and how hard she worked to make sure that people understood the material. Tests and quizzes were challenging, but if you are passionate about the subject then you should be fine.

I believe Dr. Schivell was an excellent teacher. She does ask questions that sometimes seem far-fetched but usually they are only clicker questions so that you can learn from them. She really seemed to genuinely care that all her students learned and always has a positive uplifting nature to her.

THE MOST AWFUL TEACHER FOR THE BIOL 200 CLASS. SERIOUSLY IF YOU HAVE A CHANCE, PICK ANOTHER TEACHER!!!! IM SERIOUS I AM NOT OVERREACTING I AM A NORMAL STUDENT LET ME HELP YOU OUT. DONT TAKE THIS TEACHER AT ALL. SHE IS AWFUL!!

Terrible lecture notes, useless inclass worksheets, doesn't give enough time for clicker questions. You have to BUY her lecture notes (even though you're paying tuition to take her class) SAVE YOURSELF
Pretty easy class. All memorization. Class became a little disorganized after the first midterm. The way she phrases questions is sometimes confusing. Other than that, it's a good class.

One of the best teachers and classes I have had. It was fun to have a break from heavily science concentrated classes and look at biological/tech advances from another lens. Mandy was passionate and organized, class was fun (didn't look at the clock!), and expectations were very clear. Just do the work and enjoy!

The instructor normally teaches invertebrate biology, but created the Biomedical Advances and Society class as a side project.  It's not a hard core biology class, but she is great at applying medical concepts to topics such as advertising, lawmaking and marketing.  The instructor is very personable and pleasant, and an engaging lecturer.

This class was a retake for me. Mandy is the best person to take with. She uses a notebook for lectures. She ALWAYS gives you direct info that is on tests. Best advice for a good grade: go to class, FORM A STUDY GROUP, do practice exams/weekly questions (best prep for exams!) and seek help if you need it. Follow these and you'll do great!

Dr. Schivell, to be honest, was an alright teacher. One of the best bio teachers compared to others. Lectures were good except some of the material presented never really showed up on the midterms/final. Of course, I liked how she would present a scenario on the exam ahead of time to prepare. POGIL's were not helpful so just read the textbook.

I enjoyed her enthusiasm for the class, but her tests were not consistent with the way she lectured. Her POGILs(basically in class worksheets) were useless ! I don't think I learned a ton from her course unfortunately. If you take her class, just know that her tests and quizzes are very unorthodox and nothing like her lectures.

"discuss it with your classmates to get to the right answer" -sometimes helpful, not ALL the time! Lecture notes are messy, doesn't bother to adapt newer technology. She doesn't test you on learned material, only 'what if' questions to trick you. Explanations boil down to 'that's how the cookie crumbles' regardless if it's about a grade or biology.

Dr. Schivell is an alright teacher. Invertebrates was annoying because she made the students give the lectures and then expect you to know slightly obscure correlations than what was presented. I could've done better overall in the class if I had studied harder but overall I would say to not take invertebrates with Dr. Schivell, it's tough.

Lecture notes on overhead drawings are very hard to follow and notecard questions during class were just a waste of time. Material was interesting but first time teaching made it very confusing and overemphasized some topics that were perhaps less important. Not as helpful with questions as other people have said.

Great professor, really nice to have a lecture booklet option. Her tests were strange and asked me to recall information in a strange manner, but overall a much more doable class than 180. Some super cool labs!

This was Mandy's first time teaching this class, somewhat disorganized but still did a good job teaching. Difficult to understand all concepts and exam material because Mandy was not entirely sure of certain info as she was herself learning about the course. Good amount of work and only one midterm and one final. Provided feedback on assignments.

Very enthusiastic professor. You can tell that she really enjoys teaching this class. However, it is a definite weed out class and the tests are written sometimes in a confusing manner. The POGIL (in class worksheets) were not helpful and made it more confusing, hopefully she doesn't continue to use them.

She was pretty funny. However, I didnt like her tests (very ambiguous) & wasnt a fan of "pogils", they didnt help at all. Class was ok, there were just a few aspects that clashed with my learning style. Get her lecture packet, there are diagrams and drawings you will miss out on otherwise. And I didn't find the book to be helpful at all.

Dr. Mandy was a fabulous professor - very engaging lectures with plenty of humor sprinkled in. Love the way she does her notes although it does make attending class mandatory. Proposed a lot of various scenario questions in her tests so make sure to study those. She loves biology and it's very evident in her lectures. Great prof!

She is an extremely engaging teacher. Lecture is more bearable purely on the fact that she is very lively. She is also clearer than most. A good percentage of her test question involve "Imagine a scenario in which..." type questions, so there is not much regurgitation of facts.

I was lucky enough to have Mandy for both 200 and 355. She is one of my best teachers I have had at uw. She is great at making complex confusing topics seem more clear. If you can take a class with her as the teacher  I would highly recommended it!

I really enjoyed the way she taught and integrated real world examples. Make sure to get the lecture notes, she draws a lot and most tests are based on the notes. The exams are somewhat tricky and require a lot of logic, so make sure you understand the concepts!

Test questions appear to come out of nowhere at times. Studying the notes is important but she won't often directly test you on it. She prefers to have students try to decipher new material on tests based on what they have learned.

She made what could've been a boring molecular biology class very interesting.  She is approachable, knowledgeable, effortlessly funny, and she likes to answer questions. In lecture she writes and draws as she explains so you don't miss anything.  Her tests are straightforward. She rules!

Best teacher I've had at the UW. Mandy is extremely interested in the subject she teaches, and manages to engage her students during lecture (even with 500 students in class at once). Although her tests are difficult, you remember the subjects long after her class is over. I always enjoyed going to her class.

Good prof, hard exams, really loves her students. and make sure you go to Ben's Office hours as well, he is really helpful. GO TO LECTURE, make sure you understand everything said there and you will be solid.

Decent lecturer, but not quite my style.  Tests are very tricky (which completely screwed me over) but really do test your knowledge.  Pay attention to what she says in lecture.  She doesn't write down everything you need to know. With effort, you can get a decent grade.

Very engaging lectures! Her lecture notes only contain pictures so there will be labeling, but it helps a lot visually. Her tests are challenging, but she puts up a practice exam about a week before each test, and the practices emulate the test format. Homework contains hard conceptual questions that will help you with the rest of the course.

Definitely take Bio 200 from her if you can - she is a terrific teacher, energetic, enthusiastic and knowledgeable. Her lectures are very clear, but you MUST attend every lecture and take great notes to do well in class. Exams are challenging and tricky, but really test your understanding of the material. I'm lucky I got to take 200 from her.
wonderful energetic teacher who is also very approachable. i learned so much from her.
She is AWESOME.  Super enthusiastic, always willing to help students, entertaining lecturer.  Really wonderful teacher.

Energetic and really cares about her students. Her lectures are definitely worth going to. Ended up studying from her course pack and ignored the textbook. Her tests can be tricky, so make sure you do the practice problems and glance over the labs.

Energetic professor with a bubbly personality.  Very good at explaining the material.  Her lecture packet might be all you need for her class.  Exams are tricky and like to tie in several topics in the quarter together.  Class average came out to a 2.6 which screwed my grade over.  Biweekly quizzes keep you on your toes.
Great teacher, very energetic. Loves what she does and is extremely knowledgeable. Her notes were very clear, easy to understand, and useful.

As said before, she is very energetic and makes the class interesting. She is also adept at clearly explaining what she is lecturing on.  The only problem here is the tests.  Often times questions are asked that almost seem out of the scope of the lectures, and can be written in a unnecessarily confusing manner. Be forewarned.
Great, friendly teacher who enjoys teaching. I highly recommend taking any class with her.
Very fair; approachable; cares whether or not students learn
She is such a good professor! Highly recommend! Midterm and final came from her lecture and the homework skill.

Good teacher, but work load is high. I send more time on this class than the other three that are more credits! A good TA counts too because without one the quiz sections just confuse you more. This class should give a writing credit because of the long papers that are due every week. Attendance is mandatory!

I love mandy!!! she is such a great professor, and a great person. She is always willing to help you out no matter what. I love her course packet! they are wonderful :) i loved her class so much that i'm taking another one of her classes! exams are tough, but drives the curve down...

Love her. Her lecture packet is amazingly convenient. She makes going to class fun. She is extremely outgoing and welcomes any student's questions. You will learn a great amount with this professor, and have fun while doing it. Take this course if Mandy's teaching - you will love it!

She was a great professor, explains things very well. Always ready and willing to help you out. Exams however, are very tough. You can never study enough for them. There will always be something you missed.

She is incredible!  One of the best professors I have ever had.  She is really great at taking a complex topic, breaking it down, and making it make sense.  Her passion kept the class very interesting.
great prof. same as all other comments
class was retarded for anyone who actually likes science. but shes a good teacher and cares about students learning. interesting but not the easy a i thought a 4 credit class would be
Excellent professor. Topics were presented in a very clear and organized manner. Also, she is very willing to spend time outside of class to answer questions.

She presented the material well... however her tests need more extrapolation than her lectures suggest.  In short, it is DEFINITELY not enough to simply know the material.  And reading the book is pointless
Very good professor. I love her teaching techniques. The packet and overheads were useful.

She is a very good lecturer and speaker, and she makes the topics very interesting. The lectures never seem like they are 2+ hrs long. Although, knowing the material perfectly doesn't mean that you will do good on her tests.

Easily one of the best professors I've ever had. Her teaching style is a bit different, but is extremely effective. Even if your grade is not good, you will come out of this class feeling like you really learned your molecular biology.
her nerdy humor got old but she always had very complete information and explained it well
She is one of the best professors I've had at UW. She totally cares about your learning, and is very humorous/enthusiastic in class. Excellent teacher.
This class was amazing and is what got me going in genetics and research and developmental biology. Incredible professor who makes learning fun and easy!
Great enthusiastic teacher. Work load wasn't horrible.
Excellent professor.  Made the subject very interesting.
Everything stated above is true.  She was a GREAT professor.
She's nice and REALLY energetic...however sometimes she makes me feel like I'm in high school again....and the way she words her questions on tests is hard to comprehend at times.
very intellegent and energetic.  she talks very clearly, answers all questions and cares that you learn...she is willing to help all the time..i totally recommend her.

HOT! She's the reason I attend every class...
Very energetic professor who wants you to get excited about bio even if you have no interest in it.  Tries to learn all the students' names ina 250-people class.
Very authentic and easy to follow. Lectures are engaging and interactive!

Very easy and fun class. Homework could be completed quickly, 500 word reflection due each week, and open book exams. She also gives extra credit for writing a reflection on her newsletter and the people in it. Her class is so much fun, its very welcoming and eye opening. She talks about a lot of different subjects that people see as taboo. 10/10

Easiest class I have ever taken. One 500-word reflection due every Sunday on lecture topics, plus 1–2 weekly readings with questions, most of which can be answered with basic logic. TAs are slow at grading but very lenient. Three online exams that are also mostly logic-based. Online is much better than IRL in my opinion.

reviews.comment: Loved her so much. If you need a DIV, strongly recommend. Class is very manageable and lectures are interesting. Learned a lot and will miss the class very much.
Great Class, I took it online. She's very engaged with the class. There are many speakers that come to talk about personal experiences.

Nicole is well-known and incredibly respected in the industry. She was a good lecturer and knew how to elaborate. The class itself was easy and chill, definitely a good way to get a DIV credit. Truly just a good person all around, and I'd recommend taking!

reviews.comment: She's a very knowledgable professor and cares a lot about her students learning the curriculum and applying it. Great class and professor if this is your first time receiving formal sex education, though.

reviews.comment: She's a very caring, amazing professor. You can tell she's very passionate about her class and about teaching. Her lectures are very engaging and so are the guest speakers. Attendance is taken before and after class and exams are open notes!

Amazing professor I took this course in person back in 2023. This class is very interesting and I have learned a lot. Imi glad this kind of course is offered at UW. There are tophat textbook readings with questionaries along the reading. Canvas multiple choice exams. Attendance was required by putting in a code mid break in class.

There is a reason her class is so loved. Wonderful teacher, and willing to help if you go up to talk to her after the lecture. Incredibly easy class, as all the exams and the final are open note+textbook. Lectures can start to get boring later on, though, so take async if you expect to have a heavier course load. Overall, great teacher!
goated professor, every UW student should take one of her classes

Attendance & in-class questions required for in-person. Take async if you can. The main highlight of her classes are probably the guest speakers. When her lectures are good, they're really good. When they're not-so-good, she's lost and fumbling all over her words. Also, the TA Luke is an absolute icon, his presentations were very entertaining.

Professor McNichols was a really great professor. The homework reviewed the reading and lecture so it was easy to do in class. LOVE THIS QUEEN WHO STOOD UP TO A YATZEE
A queen who stands up for what's right.
So amazing!!!
Best ever!
Absolute icon. Love her. Serves face. 10/10

One of the best professors I have had in my life! She is simply amazing! Her lectures are engaging and her textbook is well-written and easy to engage with! By far one of the most memorable courses I have taken.
She's genuinely both an amazing professor and amazing person. The content is easy to digest and she tries to add humor to the class.
Genuinely best professor one could ask for.

I took psych 210 online and Professor McNichols was great! Her lectures were very engaging. For homework, you need to read the interactive textbook, then do weekly reflections. It is easy to work ahead if you want to. If you are in the in-person class, attendance is taken and is part of your grade. Overall, great class!

Easy asynchronous. Despite MyUW saying we don't need to buy a textbook for the course, we end up buying her book for $104 (assuming you don't receive the rebate). Good lecturer but some of the guest speakers she invited were a little too repetitive or went on long tangents. Wish she moderated that a little more.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: lectures at first were super funny but in the middle of the quarter got sort of repetitive. minimal work and sometimes interesting.

One of the best classes I have ever taken! She makes the lectures very entertaining and the class is well organized. The exams were pretty straightforward and you have to write a reflection each week which was also easy.

I personally loved her. She was engaging, funny, considerate, and the content seemed relevant and useful. The only thing is the textbook is really graphic, costs $100, and is mandatory for the homework and class engagement. Overall, it was a fun, easy class that you don't have to think much about outside of lecture and assignments.

Professor McNichols is a great lecturer and keeps the class very engaging. At some point, however, the content does get repetitive, and the $100 textbook seems like a waste of money. If you take this class, I recommend taking the asynchronous version as attendance is not mandatory. 
It's an easy 4.0 as long as you do the work and pay attention.

Her "anonymous" comments are not so anonymous. She revealed a classmates name when she felt insulted by his respose then publicly shamed him in a 400+ person lecture. Truly unprofessional and a huge turnoff to a class that was otherwise cool. Also ridiculous that she makes us buy her expensive textbook that just goes into her pocket.
Dr. Nicole is the sweetest professor who always gives interesting and engaging lectures. She conveys the material super well!

Psych 210 is a great class to take if you just need to fill some diversity credits. Its very informative and interesting and the lectures are always a lot of fun. Theres a lot of homework but its all online if you really dont care. Pretty easy class all things considered.
Class is informative without being difficult, definitely a good elective to take and Dr. McNichols makes it 100x better

She was honestly such a great professor. The TA's are super nice and PSYCH 210 really opened my eyes about a lot of things. You can tell how passionate she is about her career. The only small difficulty is the way the exams are worded. Another issue was how most of the class it was just her talking. I wish it would've been a bit more interactive.

Professor McNichols is so sweet and really cares about her curriculum. Its a little annoying that we have to do seemingly pointless weekly assignments, but its really not bad. You do have to go to lectures because she takes attendance, but you can always have a friend do it for you if you need to miss a couple. P.S dont try and do the hw in public.
Spice it up with a toy

She's okay! It was fun in the start of the quarter but the class slowly gets boring. We have to pay for a textbook (which I don't really do normally but then it's mandatory since she wrote the book herself). I enjoyed her class. Fun extra-credit.

I took Nicole again my junior year after taking psych 210. It is a smaller class and follows the same structure each week with 2 readings/podcast before class on Tuesday and then an after class reflection for participation credit twice a week. Her exams are usually 3 lengthy questions and must be around 500 word reflection for each question.

Really sweet professor and chill class. If you've chosen 2-3 STEM courses and want to find a refreshing and relaxing class, just take Psych 210. She is passionate about the course. If students have questions about or are interested in the content, they are encouraged to approach her during the Q&A sessions in class or attend her office hours.

she Forced students to purchase a $100 textbook，which not be very pleasant. Lots of extra credit opportunities to get an easy 4.0. Although the professor never responds to emails, TAs are very helpful.

Didn't think I'd learn much but I learned a lot and it was interesting. One 500-word reflection a week, two interactive readings a week (take about 45 minutes each), and three open note exams. I went in person for the fun lectures, too. The mandatory textbook was about $94. TAs take a long time to grade but they are not harsh graders.

prof. mcnichols is a wonderful professor! she is so beyond educated about sexual education and has such a genuine love for this profession. i really enjoyed her class as i found it very interesting and informative. i chose to take this for diversity cred and i dont regret it! for work there's just readings w/ work and weekly reflections :) also ec!

Professor McNichols is a absolute GEM! She is so funny and her lectures are really engaging. You have to purchase a TopHat subscription ~$94. Everything is graded by TAs, only three "midterms", 40 MCQ in 60 min. Pay attention, take notes and you'll be fine! The guest lectures were my fav. Her lectures are a bit rushed, but everything is recorded.

I really liked this class and I highly recommend. 

Make sure you're double checking you put the attendance code in in the beginning, and the end. IF SHE FORGETS REMIND HER. It's your grade. I got docked a couple days because she forgot, or I missed the code. Take notes during lectures, and do the readings. Honestly, every detail is important.

You can really tell she loves teaching psychology. The content is mostly on TopHat (a little expensive) and comes in modules and readings. Gives a lot of extra credit for surveys and her newsletter. Great lectures, especially guest speakers. Only bad thing would be that she constantly promotes her social media and TikTok almost every class.

Nicole's PSYCH210 is an enjoyable course, though the pricey textbook can be an issue. Lectures move quickly, so staying engaged is key. For an easy A, just keep up with homework and submit short weekly assignments. unstuck ai was a lifesaver for studying!
She is awesome take psych 210

This class was okay. I hated how the tests were timed. Sometimes felt like questions on the test weren't covered in class. Still finished with a 4.0. Never once spoke to the professor, only TAs which can be annoying.

Nicole is a good professor and taking Psych 210 was an enjoyable class, the problems some have with the class are usually related to the homework/textbook behind a $90 paywall. Additionally, she can go over many concepts quickly, making it hard to keep up when taking notes. Overall I would recommend taking this class, just be aware of these things.

Overall Prof.McNichols was an untouchable lecturer. A face for a class where the grading, any questions, etc. was all T.A. run. Felt like she genuinely cared about the content and was good at teaching it and very inclusive. But on the downside having a prof with a social media presence led to lots of self promotion and influencer vibes.

i took this course online. the lectures are entertaining and the professor is funny. exams are easy and workload is very manageable. overall, an easy A. however, the TAs are very slow to respond and post lectures online. i understand this class has over 1k students, so maybe more TAs are needed. it was a bit frustrating.

Easy 4.0. 0.2 GPA boost extra credit offered at the end of quarter. Attendance is long and required, but a short break in the middle. Keep up with guided homework assignments, go to lectures, and submit a short writing assignment at the end of each week for an easy A! This class is educational and progressive in so many ways so just enjoy listening

An easy class and easy 4.0, there's a 0.2 GPA boost offered for writing a reflection. Not a bad class but the lectures are either easy to space out during or over the top and awkward to watch (example: role playing with a dominatrix). Overall its really easy but she's kind of weird

This class is genuinely a joke. It was very easy, but completely pointless. You have to pay over $100 for the online textbook that is not user friendly, Dr McNichols hardly showed up to lecture even before she was injured (luckily I did the online version), and she uses outdated terms and is generally weird when discussing LGBT+ topics. Huge waste
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is my god. A feminist psychology icon.

2H lectures, she goes off topic often. Book is never related to most topics discussed. She will prioritize social media influence over general learning. Exams go over topics that are marked "optional." $109 textbook that you have to buy to be in the class (mandatory attendance codes, workbook). Class of ~600, hard to learn when everyone talks.

Prof McNichols is pretty cool as a person and her lectures are engaging and interesting. She's a funny person to listen to and knows how to engage her audience. However, paying around 100 dollars for TopHat sucks. Majority of the guest lecturers were not engaging and some were just rambling. If you take this in person there is an attendance code :(

This class was really interesting and broadened my perspectives on a lot of different aspects of human sexuality. Nicole seems very sweet and open-minded. My biggest gripe was that she made us pay $110 for an interactive textbook on TopHat, which was really annoying to use. The Friday films were such a bore, but at least the exams were very easy.
Super easy and fun class. If you do the work you will do great in the class!

Very easy course. Outside of lecture, probably spent 2 hours/week on hw. She's entertaining but can get really rude w class. She never showed up to Friday lecture and made TAs run everything where they were confused 75% of the time. Expensive textbook that you have to buy. Feels like she cares more about her social media presence than teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was pretty easy, mostly just reading homework and the tests are all open note/book.
