She makes a mistake every single lecture and relies on the class to correct her. Both of her pages of content that would be on the midterm had multiple typos of equations, and her answer keys have wrong answers. None of this gets fixed unless a student points it out. Students lose points because they were given the wrong equations.
She really does care about her students doing well and thoroughly explains all topics. Definitely recommend!
Best math class I've taken at UW

Professor Naehrig is caring and passionate. She welcomes questions and wants her students to succeed.

I found the class very manageable, considering it's multivariable calculus. The content can be hard, but I felt prepared for the midterms and final. They were like the review material :)

I'd love to take another class with her!

Would ask us how we feel about topics. Communicates with her class. Went up to her after lecture handful of times, and she always seemed to care and helped out. As always, the math classes are rigorous, but appreciated her as prof.
Great professor.

Professor Naehrig is excellent. She carefully prepared videos before class to ensure that students learned the material. The lectures were very accessible outside of class time. She meticulously ensured that everyone could watch the lecture. You can earn extra credit if you actively participate. Midterm were easy, final can be a little challenging.

One of the better professors in the math department. Cares about students, and exams are generally easier/test only on fundamental concepts taught in class. Homework is generally light, lots of examples given during class.

As a mathematics major I would say I wanted to learn more about the math side of the content i.e. more proofs, while Prof. Naehrig hardly explains proofs of those theorems. But she is generally a very caring teacher, you will succeed in her class as long as you put in effort. The flipped class also makes much sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Genuinely amazing teacher and teaching style!

Midterm medians were 90, 95% respectively. Professor naehrig is extremely caring. I would place her exams on the easier side, but if you do away with the desire for grades or a curve, you walk out of class actually having learned. Low homework weight, high emphasis on being active and engaging with the material.

Her class model won't work for everyone but most of us this quarter greatly appreciated it. It was shockingly easy given the advanced content of the course, and I definitely had an easier time grasping concepts than in any of my past math classes. If you can take a math class with her I'd highly recommend it.

Naehrig was an excellent prof for 224. It was a reversed classroom style, so we worked on homework problems in class. Attendance wasn't required, but it definitely helps, and she gives extra credit for doing the poll everywhere. Two midterms and a final with a cheat sheet. Midterms went amazingly. Naehrig is super understanding and a fun lecturer!

The content covered in class are basically just how to use formula and theorems to do calculations, and exams are much too easy. However, I want to learn more through a more challenging class. What she did was not enough. She is a very nice and responsible person though.

She was amazing in multivariable calculus. Don't listen to other people telling you she's bad. She does make mistakes here and there, but she corrects them really fast, and she responds quickly on Edstem as well. Just pay attention, and you will succeed 100%.
Very good lecture style with pre-lecture videos and time to do homework in lecture.

She is very caring obviously, as evidenced by her generous grading policy. Algebra is a very abstract subject, but she does a good job of explaining it in a simple enough manner. This course is not easy, and it does require a lot of work, but at the same time it does feel rewarding. Its actually also pretty fun-i liked algebra better than analysis.
she's so nice!

She is so bad at teaching and literally gets confused by her own questions and makes the class hard with the overbearing amount of homework that she gives out separately. For someone who is completely new to calculus, I found it difficult.
Prof. Naehrig's classes will ask you to engage in the material, but provides a fruitful and simple path to a 4.0 if you do.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: lectures teach nothing, she makes you do problems in class. i'd rather be taught and learn later than on the spot, especially when it's really difficult to understand where she's at. like why are we using polls for attendance and to solve within 3 minutes... i took professor pierce for math 112, it was perfect... this class, not so much.

Dr. Naehrig is an amazing prof who truly cares about student learning & success. I had her for Math 124 Au22 and loved her then. It was great to take another class with her now. She is a great lecturer and is easy to reach outside of class for extra help. She made it possible for anyone to get a 4.0 if they were dedicated enough.

Good lecturer. She used a system with four relatively easy quizzes instead of exams, which I appreciated. She employed a contract grading system - which was somewhat confusing, but allowed for any dedicated student to get a 4.0 by putting in the effort and retaking quizzes. There was an annoying amount of busywork assigned. Easily reachable on Ed.

Professor Naehrig is a very kind person and her pre-lecture videos were very helpful. The poll everywhere was graded on accuracy every class, so that was a downside, and she tended to make a lot of mistakes during the pre-lecture videos and lectures, which detracted from learning. Overall the class was good.

Professor Naehrig provided easy to follow lectures and was always available for help after class. The homework assignments were harder than the exams. The exams were pretty easy. She provided weekly extra credit assignments and had more EC at the end of the quarter.

Natalie tried her best to make sure you get the score you want once you work hard; there are all kinds of extra credits and retake for exams. she sometimes forgot the proof she's gonna write in lecture; but it's no big deal. To take her course, be prepared to do more before and after class, but you wouldn't feel stressed out preparing for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She's nice as a lecturer but lowkey her lectures didn't help much. I just do the homework. Was her first quarter in Math 120 when I took it so she got notes from another professor for us to use for review LOL. Very nice of her.

She's a good lecturer! It's sort of flipped classroom but like not really, maybe 15 mins of prep work needed for each class lol. Easy quizzes (10 "example" questions, 2 easy proofs), reasonable homeworks with opportunity for EC, so not a heavy workload. What a queennnn

Wonderful professor! She has the class structured to be very clear, efficient, and easy for students to succeed. She is very nice and makes class (and math) interesting and fun. She cares a lot about students' success, providing many extra credit and learning opportunities. If you put any effort into this class you will get a good grade.
Good professor! Explains material clearly and with excitement keeping students engaged.

I took Pre-calc in high school before, but I had to retake it again. Having her class was an amazing opportunity because she leads the lecture pretty well and understandable. The HW is a bit harder to understand however the midterm and the final were the easiest questions given to us. I praise her so much and my grade. She's a great professor.

Natalie is a caring professor who makes a tough math course approachable. With consistent homework and quizzes, the class is challenging but manageable. Unstuck study was a lifesaver for quick calculus practice and exam prep.

She assigns a lengthy amount of homework and half of the time, none of the content will be on the test. From the perspective of someone who did very little calculus in high school, you need to do the practice exams she gives out as they are tailored to the actual test.

Professor Naehrig's class is good, she explains concepts and questions clearly, and teaches us German words for every start of the class, I would take it again. But the assignment is a bit difficult, exams are not as hard.

Professor Naehrig genuinely cares about her students, and has a really fun class environment. She encourages student participation, lectures are engaging, and she really works with the class. There's quite a lot of homework through WebAssign, but she doesn't create the problems and has helpful homework videos in case you get lost. She's lovely. :)

In the beginning Professor Naehrig made it clear that she didn't assign the homework, and it was automatically assigned through Webassign. That said, I struggled in the beginning because I wasn't used to how the course was taught. But she gives a ton of extra credit throughout the quarter to remediate your grade. The midterms are also pretty easy.

Prof. Naehrig is so sweet and enthusiastic - she genuinely wants her students to succeed. She also provides tons of extra credit opportunities! However, she's a little scatterbrained in her lectures and they're difficult to follow. The exam review worksheets she provides are identical to the actual exams, so just do those and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Naehrig isnt the greatest professor since there is a ton of webassign hw that doesnt even help you on exams since the midterm archives will. She is extremely nice in her office hours and is much more helpful in a one on one setting. But should stick to upper level math courses and not the intro series.
good teaching, good answers, lots of participation in lectures

Fast paced and she breezes through each chapter without much explanation. Her lectures feel like she's talking at you instead of being engaging, therefore it feels like she's teaching her students as if they already know everything. Take advantage of extra credit & tutoring centers bc the professor herself isn't great at teaching.

Math 124 is an awful class. Between WebAssign and the bell curve, it's time consuming and hard to excel. But she's a good teacher and does her best to teach the content effectively. Lectures are recorded, there's homework drops, and no formal quizzes. She has an accent (German?). If you have to take this class, it's better to take it with her.

She is very nice and approachable. Sometimes she is hard to understand as she has an accent (I believe she's German). She has built in PollEv drops, HW drops, and you can retake the quizzes if you fail. Lectures are always recorded and posted. She really wants you to learn the content and succeed.
She doesn't teach, she rather talk to herself while doing the problems during the lectures. Also she just jumps steps and it's hard to understand. Gives too much homework and a little hard to keep up
Gives a 66 point homework on the same day as the mid term, Homeworks are 10 times harder than the problems in class. Almost no instruction and impossibly hard.

She's a good lecturer. She rarely went too fast or too slow, and her explanations were usually pretty helpful in understanding the material. Her tests were very reasonable, especially for the math department. She also had lots of relevant prep material, and released pretty detailed lecture notes.

Don't listen to anybody here that's shaming Professor Natalie. She is a sweetheart who actually cares about her students and teaches the concepts very well. She's also quite lenient w/ work. I'd never thought she'd teach calc 1 in a way where I would understand it. Props to her. She is a solid MATH 124 professor. I highly recommend taking her!

A good amount of homework and a few quizzes, but there is a lot of grace given to get problems wrong on the homework, and you can make your own formula sheet for quizzes. Class time is spent on problems, but the videos outside of class are clear and make sense. The quiz section was also useful, as it was optional dop-in time for help on anything.

Naehrig actually helped me understand calculus more than I thought I could, she cares about her students and gives them opportunities to improve their grades outside of homework. She does a good job of making the difficult material approachable. The TA's were kind of useless but not her fault.
cares about her students, does what she can to make the difficult curriculum less intensive
made way too many mistakes and would just throw information at you rather than actually teaching it.

Naehrig used all of professor Taggart's old videos and exam archives so I treated the course like an online one and only came in for exams. Her practice exams are EXACTLY like her actual test, don't waste time in the archive, just do the practice sheet she gives you. I understood the math but listening to her lecture she makes it too confusing.

she expects you to know everything that she didn't even teach The TAs are horrible as well. Lots of hw If you think the quiz or the homework are gonna save you after doing badly on an exam, you thought wrong. Let's say your grade was 56.01the hw and the quiz will only make it go up by 56.02 it's just too much if u wanna fail take this class!!!

Professor Naehrig is a great person to be around, but her teaching style leaves something to be desired. In particular, the way she lectures does not make the students more interested in the subject but rather actively turns student's attention away from the matter. That being said, it is hard to drum up interest in a subject such as calculus.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Approachable, though very contradictory in lecture. Her midterms & final are very, very similar to the practice ones she provides--so in that sense the tests are not hard. But a lot of the time in lecture and in the homework videos her explanations are confusing and upright incorrect.

Although Natalie probably isn't one of the worst profs, she very much expects you to know a lot of things before taking the class and should have a decent idea of how to do every topic that is going to come up in the class. She also is not very good at explaining and I spent a lot of time just teaching myself.
I had a hard time following her lectures and this is overall not a good class to take if you want a refresher on precalc. Tons of Web Assign HW, weekly quizzes and two midterms. Did not do well.

Ended up dropping this class because she was not teaching and I felt like she was throwing the material at me. The amount of homework is overwhelming and sometimes she stacks them up for a single day, expect to commit the majority of your day to figuring out the homework and living in the tutoring centers.

This class was really challenging which wasn't her fault, all the 12X math classes are, and she was actually very sweet and approachable. However, she wasn't the best at explaining complicated topics and sometimes made mistakes in problems that led to a lot of confusion. Lots of HW but again, true of all the classes and profs.

Professor Naehrig assigned lots of homework, but it generally felt like it had a purpose. She clearly wanted her students to do well and understand material and did a good job walking the class through practice problems. If I ever had to take a math class again that she was teaching, I definitely would!

office hours are held once a week. daily graded poll ev, webassign homework, her midterms are easier than the other math 124 profs but the final is written by the entire department so keep that in mind. she's a caring and nice prof but it's easy to get behind if you don't understand the lectures. weekly quizzes in quiz section has 3 retakes lol

Lots of HW and it takes a while but she gives a generous drop at the end so you dont have to do it all. Lots of quizzes but they arent too hard. Shes very nice and seems to actually care about the students but isn't the best at actually teaching the material; if you don't have prior knowledge from high school then her teaching might be too fast.

Natalie is very good at lecturing and teaching, and she's very nice and approachable. Her midterms are easy, but the final is co-written by the entire 124 instructional team, so the final is significantly harder for her students. I got perfect scores on both midterms, but did really bad on the final. Great teacher, brutal curve.

Amazing professor, I had Professor Naehrig for math 124, and the lectures were amazing and the pre-class work although it can get annoying sometimes if you forget to do it until last minute but it is 100% beneficial towards the learning experience. If you are able to get her as a professor I would highly recommend taking the class

Professor Naehrig is an amazing instructor for the UW math department. I had her for 124 and 126, and both times I appreciated her flipped classroom model and weekly quizzes as they generally prepared me well for midterms and finals. 
If you are comfortable with constant work, Natalie does a great job if you put in continuous effort.

I took Naehrig last year during Winter '21. She is one of the most understanding and friendliest professors in the math department. She gives a lot of assignments, but are great practice for her exams. She also had extra credit. Her quizzes are worth alot. Her exams are doable and easy-ish, pay attention to lecture and practice exams on the archive
This professor was amazing!! As long as you keep up with the preclass and homework assignments, the class is a breeze. She is great at explaining the concepts and is extremely kind and approachable.

Definitely one of the better Math 12x professors! Her lectures are very easy to understand, and she is very generous with homework and quiz grading. She clearly wants her students to succeed, and her pre-class videos are extremely helpful! Consider yourself lucky if you get her for 124!

The Math 12x series in general is unkind but Naehrig does her best to make things encouraging for her students. She really cares about students' learning and she always offers ways to prove yourself (lots of quiz retake opportunities, extra credit, only grades you on 75% of HW) and also has lots of extra help (HW videos).

Professor Naehrig actually wants her classes to succeed as opposed to a lot of other weed-out classes I've taken. She walks us through problems step by step in class and provides a variety of examples for each type of problem so we know exactly what to do on quizzes and midterms. Ask for help! She is so helpful if you're confused with the material.

Probably the best Calculus professor at UW. She is more lenient when it comes to grading and the spread is pretty nice since half your grade is dependent on 2 midterms/final. She allows retakes on quizzes which average out and bumps your grade while dropping 25% of the hw grade. Her midterms are much more manageable compared to other professors.
Overall, I really liked this class and thought it was taught well by this professor. It wasn't too hard as long as you attend lectures and do the homework! Probably one of the best math professors!

This class requires a lot of dedication to succeed, considering the fact that Prof. Naehrig is not the only one creating the final exam. Although she is very sweet and willing to support her students, the class can be rigorous and challenging, especially when all the math assignments are not written by her. Having a supportive T.A is very helpful.

Naehrig is the saving grace of the intro calculus meat grinder. She is young, caring, and effective. If you miss her great in-person lectures, the prerecorded stuff is still well-thought-out and easy to follow. This site is full of overreactions and emotional takes - but Naehrig genuinely deserves a 5/5. Be grateful if you pull her for 12x.
Professor Natalie genuinely cares about her students and her class is well designed.

Natalie is wonderful professor, though she did rely on Loveless for her worksheets. She made it very clear what was expected of you. There were no nasty surprises. Naehrig took the time to lecture while also having us do practice problems with each other. She was always ready to help, and encouraged question asking and class participation.

Professor Naehrig sets up her class with a very clear structure. Watch all the pre class videos, stay on top of quizzes, and go to her office hours. Professor Naehrig really cares about her students and will work with you to succeed.

She is an amazing teacher. She gives a lot of opportunities to retake quizzes and has pre-lecture videos that are actually helpful. She cares about students and I can see that she wants us to succeed. The final exam is difficult but you should do fine if you understand the materials. Overall a great professor

Overall, if you can keep up with assignments and preclass videos, you're set. She has two ways to bring up your end GPA by 0.1 each so take advantage of that. I didn't do a single reading and ended right smack in the middle of the curve. However, she sets the median to a 2.7 sometimes so be cautious of that. Her lectures are also fast, so keep up!

She's not the best at teaching the material and actually preparing us for the exams, especially the final exam. I feel like I had to teach myself a lot of the time. However, she is the best 124 teacher out of all the teachers at UW. So I would take her again.

Professor Naehrig clearly cares about her students and wants to see them succeed in the class. Her pre-class videos are extremely helpful and prepare you well for in-person lectures, which I found fast-paced and difficult to keep up with at times.

Prof. Naehrig is super nice and genuinely cares about her students. Though I ended up not doing great in this class, I still feel like I learned a lot. Probably the best MATH124 professor at UW. Wish I could have her for 125!

Naehrig is the best math professor at UW. She is caring, understanding, and her lectures are very clear. Her passion for teaching is far better than other professors at UW which makes the class even more engaging for students. Midterms are almost exactly like her practice midterms, cheat sheet allowed which makes it fairly easy. Would recommend!
She’s very kind and explains her lessons thoroughly. Her examples were helpful and I felt she cared about our learning and well-being. I wish I could have her for Math 125.

Puts effort into lectures, designs the course in a way that actually helps you learn. One of the most accommodating professors I have ever had, will work with you to get you to do as well as you can. She seems to be a professor who wants you to pass, which is not what I expected for MATH 124. Learned way more than in MATH 120 even though I struggle

I'm honestly surprised by the low ratings on here. I took her in person during autumn quarter 2021 and she was great. Gives lots of practice problems and exam guides. and her quizzes were easy for the most part. Although the curve screwed me somewhat that wasn't really her fault. Just study and practice and you'll pass.

Worst professor I have ever had. She is a terribly fast lecturer and gives examples in class that are considered easy. Quizzes and midterms are worth 85% of your grade and she does not give you the resources to pass. On these tests, some of the hardest problems I have ever seen arise. There are no problems like them in any practice material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She may be better in person, however, online classes with this professor made me lose sanity. She gives quick lectures that do absolutely nothing to help you solve the problems she assigns. The reading and assigned videos share the same uselessness. You can learn about limits one day and the next day be expected to solve constants for limits.

She is very nice and sweet. However, this class is not easy at all. I spent abt 3hrs on hw every week. Weekly quizzes are not that hard and you can retake during office hours and grades will be averaged. Midterms are not that bad if you pay attention and do the work. The final was extremely hard. There are extra credits for notes and hw completion.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Pros  Caring & Accommodating  All lectures recorded  Good extension policy Cons  LOTS of busy work  Not many examples given in class As much as I wanted to have a good experience with this prof, I personally did not because I learn very heavily on examples. She focused more on the theory behind the problems. Can be great for others!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The weekly quizzes and 2 midterms were reasonable. However, the problems designed in webassign were expected you to retain complete inner tranquility to untangle the most relentless calculations and end with the nastiest exact answers you will find. If this was inadequate, the grading criteria is also lethal for GPA. 2.9 set to the median for B+...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The grading components and scale are too difficult to get a 4.0. When I took the class, getting an overall percentage of 87% just got you a 3.1 GPA. I had a 92% but a GPA of only 3.4, even though I had a 92 on my final and a 90 on my midterm. How this class is graded goes way over my head.

Does problems in class and kind of just assumes that you know the in between steps. My TA was mediocre at best. By far the worst part about this class is the grading system. They set the median grade to a 2.9. It doesn't sound bad until your class median is an 87 and all of the sudden a B+ is a 2.9. Take any other prof, they have easier medians.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Naehrig is extremely caring. She is very nice and genuinely wants all of her students to do well. She has all of her lectures and more study materials available to us which made studying much easier. She does give a lot of homework but it's doable. The course is well organized and overall, I think this was a good way to start the calc series

Professor Naehrig is a really caring professor. Her lectures are organized and she explains the concepts well. She also gives extra credit opportunities to help you succeed in class. There is quite a lot of homework and it can be challenging but the quizzes and midterms are reasonable.

Professor Naehrig is a very nice professor and genuinely wants all her students to succeed. There are weekly quizzes but they're really easy if you have a basic understanding of the material and you can retake them as many times as you want. The midterms are within reasonable difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I liked Professor Naerig. She is caring and wants her students to succeed. There are weekly quizzes, 2 midterms and one final. The quizzes are pretty easy and graded generously, so it is doable to get perfect scores on them. The midterms are fair and similar to the study resources she posts- so make sure to use those! Overall recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I LOVED Professor Naehrig. She explained things in a step by step way, and her lectures were super easy to follow. Homeworks can be difficult, but her quizzes and midterms are easy. She genuinely cares about her students, and passing is easy if you put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Naehrig is very detailed and experienced. She highlights important concepts and is aware of common mistakes students make. Her teaching style makes it possible for those who like a step-by-step approach. The course is very well organized but sometimes worksheets are slightly ahead of lecture material. Great way to start the calc series!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: She honestly cares and although there are a lot of assignments, they are easy and are very useful.

People complain because she gives a lot of assignments, but the assignments are very easy and help pad our grades for the midterms and finals. Her tests are very straightforward and she really seems like she wants to help us do our best.

Dr. Naehrig gave us tons of opportunities to get extra points and credit to help pad our grade. Her tests were reasonable, and she is overall a very caring person and swell professor to have. This recent spring, she dropped 20% of our HW assignments as well as 2 out of 5 midterms. I would strongly recommend!

Worst professor I've ever had and that says a lot. She assigns so much homework as busy work which do not help one bit with the tests. She acts annoyed when she has to help her students with things and was very unaccommodating to our entire class. Many of us are in danger of not even passing her class this quarter. This is a very hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Naehrig's past lecture video is pretty good and easy to follow, but sometimes there's a mix between understanding the topic and confusing concept at the same time. Many loads of web assign hw, weekly concept maps, and five midterms seems a bit too much during the middle of the covid pandemic, but managed to score average on each midterm.

Too much homework. They have nothing to do with the midterm or the lectures or the small video lessons. Nothing correlates to each other. Midterms are timed. 50 mins for work and -0 minutes to take pictures of ur work and upload. She has like 3 homework assignments a week even if u had a midterm that week. About 9 midterms & final. More work!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: For precalc, this class is unnecessarily confusing. Lectures cover basic algebra while homework covers full calc. Somehow neither is on the exam. In addition, I have a quote from after the campus had a power outage to show her generosity: "No alien invasion, no Tsunami, no Covid21, no nothing, will make me give any more extensions from now on."

Most unaccommodating teacher, I think she forgot that we are still in a pandemic and have jobs and other commitments. She gives you too much homework ( doesn't even help with the exams), doesn't teach the content well, and will accuse you of cheating if you solve an exam question similarly to someone else. Simply, this prof sucks, don't take her.

Makes way too many mistakes during lectures for a professor at the UW. Gives out too much homework that will take you at least 8 hours to complete. And is worth 10% overall. You spend more time on homework than prepping for the exam. The homework is not helpful at all- which is why it is absurd. Pre-calc? Nope- more like Calculus. Save yourself.

Her grading was pretty fair but there's A LOT of hw to do which was much harder than her lecture content. Besides, there are too many small errors in either her lecture or quiz (errors are acceptable cuz human make mistakes and that's fine, but TOO MUCH errors in MATH CLASS can be annoying and confusing for students.)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I just dropped this class after 3 weeks so keep that in mind with this review. This prof is extremely unaccommodating. When my Aunt passed I asked for a week extension and she said she wasn't taking extension requests. She gives tons of homework through WebAssign that I easily spent 7+ hours on for each chapter (there were 2-3 assigned every week)

Not good, unless you have strong math basics, don't take hers. So much homework, mandatory attendance even for remote learning which could be inconvenient for international students. Exams and homework are difficult. Lectures are vague and fail to explain the issue. Poor teaching quality and difficult course.

Calc is a very hard and time consuming class, but Dr. Naehrig is great to take it with. There is A LOT of hw, as with any calc class, but its pretty doable to get 100% on everything (except ofc the tests that make up a majority of the grade). She grades pretty fair and gives partial credit with shown work. Be ready to study, the tests are hard!

Professor Naehrig cares about her students, but expect to put in a lot of work. Overall, it was a very challenging course and professor Naehrig put in the extra effort to help her students through. She works very hard and is truly dedicated to her students understanding and success!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Naehrig knows her stuff and cares about her subject and her students. My class was TOTALLY VIRTUAL and I found the homework to be rediculously hard, sometimes assignment would take 6+ hours to complete (I'm decent at calc). There were unnecessary quiz/discussion section that are virtually useless online. tests were very tough but overall ok.
Poor lecturer. Nothing felt even remotely rigorous. Textbook was good though! It was her first time teaching 126 so maybe that's all.

You get a good grade if you put in the effort. Easy ways to increase your grade but takes a lot of time. She also dropped 10% for each criteria except midterms and finals. Her midterms were fair, and she gave us a lot of resources which helped. The final isn't made by her, so it can be hard. We had the highest average compared to other sections.

most annoying class ever, and I am not even one day in. why cant we turn in our work in one place? is it really necessary to use gradescope, canvas AND webassign to turn in homework? is it? I honestly want to copy paste the syllabus to show you how much requirements there are like i am tbh speechless, if you love your life, just dont take it, srsl

Why many bad ratings? This prof had a good lesson plan with short lecture videos/ many assignments meant to help your grade. Most profs don't give those opportunities. 124 isn't meant to be easy, get ready to work for your grade.
YIKES!! This prof. is very theory based. Get ready to cry if you're not good at math and need for credit.

Naehrig really makes you work for your grade!! Many components in the grading, but I found that as an opportunity to help my grade. Lectures are good, has great handwriting. The final was ridiculously hard and the average was low, but that was made by the department and they should have gone easier on us.
so bad!! she really gave an easy lecture but hard exam and grade scale !

She's nice! Just not the best for 124. Her explanations are sometimes confusing, long HW assignments. Tests are harder than content learned in class. Notes and answer keys have quite a few little mistakes. I've learned this content before but I still think I bombed the final. Seems she's a better professor for higher level courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Naehrig is kind but that's where it ends for me. Wording of lecture quizzes/pollev questions is confusing, so it is easy to lose points on stuff like participation, which is frustrating. I understood lectures well, but all of the web-assigns and midterms were not reflected in lecture at all. I got an A in AP Calc and I have a C in this class.

Professir Naehring is a good option for math 124. She did a really good job at adapting to online but cutting lectures into pieces. Homework can be a lot with two worksheets a week that often feel disconnected from what is being taught. Easy to get in contact with. Midterms were tough, but straightforward. Definitely harder options out there
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Homework every single day in different forms EVERY weekday, attendance is REQUIRED if you wan to pass, little new content on lectures, new contents are mostly prerecorded. She drops a portion of bad grades so it is okay if you miss one or two classes or homework. Tests are more difficult that taught. Median GPA is controlled at around 3.0

Changed the syllabus several times during the class is going, which made the grade calculation really hard. The syllabus changing is also tending to grade deflation. Lastly, the exam question for this section is harder than the practice.

I'm writing this during week 10. Prof is willing to help and wants students to pass. Lecture videos are easy to understand. Many opportunities to raise grade with in class polls, mind maps, quizzes. If you practice many old exams, then you're good. I hope I can have her again because I heard she is even better for the higher level math courses.

A caring person but way too much busywork. Many students I know had As in her class until the first midterm, which covered very little of what we'd learned to date, so their grades dropped dramatically. She was not sympathetic and instead wrote somewhat nasty emails about students needing to respect her when they seek help or needed a break.

Her lectures can sometimes be a little confusing, but she always takes her time to answer questions and clear up any confusion. She's super kind, accessible, and always open to help or accommodate. The homework can be long sometimes but they're not too difficult and midterms are fine as long as you study enough.

This class- so much HW. We have 3 webassigns every week that are hard-. Her lectures are kind of confusing but provides a lot of examples- you have to do a short quiz after every lecture(They're not bad). Out of the 124 profs, she's the best- very understanding and caring but tough grader. The tests are fair if you do the practice midterms.

Prof Naehrig's video lectures were all really clear, organized, and easy to follow especially compared to the horror stories I heard from students in the other Math 124 class. The webassign homework was always really hard, but that's not specific to Naehrig's class. Overall she's a good teacher and a nice person.

The professor is fine overall and warm-hearted to students. She is accessible through piazza. I also think that her lectures are mostly understandable and useful. Her homework is not very difficult but every time it took me quite a while to finish. The calculation steps are quite complex. Also a strict grader, in my opinion at least.

I took Prof Naehrig for MATH124 on zoom and although she was a very good professor, I don't recommend taking her until in-person is back. Her lectures were very good but there is A LOT of busywork that can both help and hurt you. VERY harsh grader, but overall she was very accessible and had countless resources that you could use if confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: lectures were organized and included many practice problems. She really tried to explain tough concepts in simple ways, sometimes it could be confusing but we got the point. If you could do the study guide & quiz worksheets you're set for the midterms, which are very similar & aren't tricky. Participation matters, she calls on people ALOT in class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: No tests. Instead, there were weekly quizzes (a day to complete) and a final problem set that we had two days to do (yes, people used Chegg). We had to turn in typed notes called "weekly summaries" that she graded with no clear criteria, and weekly HW. Everyone had a high percentage grade, so curved GPA was based primarily on notes (4.0 cutoff: 97)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. Worst professor I've had at UW. Unclear communication and passive-aggressive comments towards students seeking help. There were 5 tests, changed the format of the exams during week 5. Does not round up your grade. Forget asking for help--she will shame you for not understanding it the first time. Better off with Loveless 0/10

I believe this was her first time teaching MATH120. She was pleasant, answered questions thoughtfully, and made herself available. I didn't do very well on a midterm and she spoke with me privately to see what was up. She provides study guides very similar to the exams and is a very fair grader. Only issue is sometimes hw didn't match lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Do not reccomend. Lectures were always super abstract and I never learned anything during them, plus there was random calls in a huge lecture class that you were graded on. The lectures also did not connect to the webassign well

Natalie genuinely cares about her students for sure. She does her best to explain any questions asked in class and was helpful when I went to office hours. Be warned that her lectures can get a bit convoluted, but aren't overtly difficult to follow. Midterms were easy, 46/50 and 51/52 points, just beware of the final since all 126 profs write it.

Honestly, she wasnt my favorite. All of the topics covered in the class were review for me, yet I still couldnt follow her explanations. It also seemed like all of her material came from another professor. Her tests are easy though and shes a nice person.

This was Prof Naehrig's first time teaching math 126 and she was great overall. She changed parts of the class she realized was not beneficial to our learning (video quizzes). Her midterms were very easy; she links practice problems that were almost the same as the midterm. She said the final would be hard but I ended up getting a 97. Easy 4.0

Natalie is a very charming, nice little lady. Her German accent took some getting used to, but by the end of the quarter I grew to love it. This class was not too challenging for me, because I had already learned a lot of the material in high school through physics. Towards the end, it felt like lessons covering complex material were rushed through
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a very nice person, however, I would not recommend. She's not great at articulating the problems. The first part of math 126 was not bad because it was review, but second part was more challenging. Her exams are not that hard though
Do yourself a favor and try to avoid her. Nice person but her lectures are iffy at best and her exams don't really correspond with what we've done in class.

Dr. Naehrig is an excellent choice for MATH 300. She is happy to help you and go over homework questions during her office hours, and explanations of the concepts are thorough and easy to understand. The tests are very difficult, so be sure to do as many practice problems as you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She isn't good instructor for 424. She is organized, but lectures aren't really helpful in improving your understanding in mathematical concepts.

She is very knowledgeable and caring towards her students. However, I found that she was very unorganized and unclear at times, especially when it came to assignments. However, the class overall should be pretty easy for most people.

I'm retaking her for math307 because my last 307 professor was awful and would give exams that were so much harder than the hw or what he taught because he wanted to challenge our knowledge?? Natalie explains every concept very clearly, the fact that I am learning new things every lecture even though I already took the class just shows.

Her lectures can sometimes be weak, as in she tends to rely heavily on the lecture notes anyways to go through the material. However,  she is really good at answering questions and follow-ups. The more active you are during class the easier the learning will be. Grading is reasonable too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Sometimes she seems a little scattered, but she's clear in terms of explaining the material. Notes are all posted online. No curve in this class so no need to try to beat other student's exam scores.

Uploads lecture notes to Piazza, so attendance isn't mandatory, but helps clear things up. Moves super slowly at first, but it helped hammer the essentials into my brain for the more complicated stuff.  Quizzes every Friday, drops the two lowest quiz scores, offers extra credit on midterm, final, AND homework. Definitely recommend taking her!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Heard such great things about her so I took her class. I can honestly say she's not that great. During lectures she would mess up so much that even she wouldn't know what was right & what was wrong. I felt like going to class was pointless since I learned nothing during lectures. More of a self teaching class but the material isn't that bad
Best math teacher at our university take her class if you can.

Natalie is one of the best math professors that I have had at UW. Her lectures are easy to understand and she does plenty of example problems. There are a couple quizzes, one midterm, and a final, but they are all very reasonable, as long as you have been coming to class and doing your homework you will do great.

Ms. Naehrig is an extremely nice teacher.  Take her class, she wants you to learn and wants you to succeed.  She gives multiple opportunities for extra credit, including a sizeable amount on the midterm AND final.  She is amazing, she also gives you long extensions on webassign if you want it and she has frequent office hours after class.

She does not curve your score but will offer many bonus points, as long as you have an overall grades over 90%, it's a 4.0. And as long as you learn what she teaches, it will be easy for you to get a 4.0. Best math teacher ever.
Have notes online, tests are not hard if you know and understand the material well. She used Piazza which was very helpful during my quarter.

There are pop quizzes but they are short and open notes. She doesn't use the book but the HW is based off it. Her lectures go by fast and its the same material as her online notes, except with more thorough examples. I'd recommend going to class to understand the material better because notes alone sometimes aren't clear.

Professor Naehrig is one of the best math professors I've ever had. Usually classes move too fast and the textbook is a terrible way to try to learn on your own, but she has actually rewritten the textbook and uses it as her lecture notes. This way if you miss class, you can easily catch up. Her tests tend to run long, but are very straightforward.

Very funny and caring guy. Always has a ton of office hours you can attend if you are confused and does his best to make sure everyone gets their questions answered. Lectures are typical for the 12X physics courses but he makes them a bit more fun. He is always incredibly helpful and will try to explain things in several different ways.
He was very nice and very open to any questions. Make sure you keep up with the readings and go to lecture or else you will fall behind quickly. Final was all multiple choice.

Professor Tolich is great at explaining difficult concepts and answering questions. He's also very friendly and overall a great prof. The course is very hard. Exams had low averages, and attendance counts for a lot of your grade.
Amazing lectures that explain the content well. Very accommodating and you can tell that he definitely cares about his students

He's honestly a GOAT, one of the best physics professors at UW. His lectures are clear and informative. I recommend reading the textbook beforehand, since lectures mostly reinforce key concepts. He's also very kind and genuinely wants his students to succeed.
Great lecturer, very clear and understood content thoroughly. Office hours were also very helpful. Tolich is amazing at explaining concepts, he doesn't make discouraged.

Dr. Tolich was an excellent professor! I recommend always attending lecture, he does a great job at explaining concepts and presenting practice problems. Some topics were tough and the exams were difficult. Tolich provides a lot of practice problems and exams to help his students succeed.

Very kind guy and obviously cares about his students success. The lectures were tough just due to the difficulty of the class but he did a good job explaining things, and always encouraged students to go to office hours if they were confused. Tough tests - all had low averages.

Tolich is one of the good ones- he's very down to Earth and it's clear that he cares a lot about his students' learning. The canvas page is well organized and the flipped classroom model works out quite well. Only complaint is the course pacing- we fell behind before midterm 2 and it felt like a mad dash at the end to plow through circuits.

Because of the horrible flipped classroom model, which Tolich seems to support, the course could be run by a TA familiar with the course and w/ decent grading. Tolich is brilliant but it didn't show in lecture. Lecture demos :( and notes were rushed in favor of long discussions. His OH explanations were helpful but long. Disappointed in UW physics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor!!!! Really patient with students and explain everything clearly and in multiple ways
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He's a great lecturer but limited by the odd structure of the PHYS 12X series. The labs and tutorials in 123 were repetitive and didn't add much value. I didn't rely on the textbook—it's helpful for boosting your grade but not essential. The best way to do well is to master lecture content and go through as many practice exams as you can.

Professor Tolich is able to convey the topic clearly and use many different examples to explain the physics concepts being taught in class. I personally found the examples and analogies really helpful, and he is also eager to answer all questions that arise from students during lecture and does so in a very constructive and informative way.

I had Nikolai for 122 and 123. He's definitely a great lecturer but is somewhat limited by the department's strange structure for the intro courses. The labs and tutorials in 123 were pointless and repetitive. The material is a little easier than 122, but harder than 121. If you're ECE, probably take Math 224 instead.

If it weren't for Tolich, I wouldn't have taken 123 and, instead, taken another science class. His presence, lectures, and support made everything crystal clear to me, even the most difficult stuff. He held extra office hours before exams, unlike many other profs. Tolich is amazing and was my motivation to finish a very difficult quarter.

Nikolai is extremely passionate and amazing at teaching the subject; questions asked in lecture are broken down in a very digestible way. Flipped-classroom model, so expect to put in work outside of class to actually read the textbook. Seriously, read the textbook.
love him so much hes goated and i would not trade him for a diff physics prof. 10/10 love him and his voice

the phys 12x series is the hardest intro series (perhaps only beaten out by calc) at UW. Tolich somehow managed to get me to enjoy the pain. Bro held 4 hours of OH before the final. Bro responds on Ed discussion like it's the huzz. Kazumi (his wife) is also incredible and they both are excellent teachers. UW peaked the day they hired the Tolichs.

Nikolai is the GOAT of the basic physics sequence. He's a great lecturer with very helpful office hours, and his explanations and answers to questions are phenomenal - he also does lots of cool demos in class. He tends to write difficult exams, so be prepared to study hard beforehand, but know that he'll help if you let him.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nikolai is a wonderful professor! He cares so much about his students and always makes himself available when someone is struggling and needs extra help. He is extremely understanding and patient, and he does his best to make sure everyone can keep up. Physics 122 and 123 are very challenging classes, but he makes them digestible.

Took this after taking PHYS121 with Kazumi, very similar structure. ~40% of the grade is low hanging fruit if you participate, exams are forgiving since they let you drop one if needed, and your score is bumped up if the class average is too low. Explanations were clear, lectures were well structured and easy to follow with lots of demonstrations.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The pace of this class is like me flipping paper

One of my favorite professors! He is so enthusiastic about every lecture with cool experiments in almost all of them. His office hours are helpful and he's such a sweet guy. Reading the textbook for the reading quizzes is important. Course expectations are clear. A difficult class (regardless of what professor) but his grading policies are great.

Professor Tolich does a great job going through all the example problems brought up in the lecture as well as any additional questions from the lecture room. He also does his best to use examples that students can more easily picture, and is quite active on the online discussion board.

His explanations were very clear. He always explained how to get the answers and why it was that particular value. Like PHYS 121, the tests and homework were extremely difficult; it is easy to flunk the class if you don't study. However, Tolich's office hours and extra availability towards exams really helped me study. Highly recommend him.

Nikolai Tolich teaches very well, he uses slides in class and explains obscure physics content in a clear and understandable way. He is willing to answer questions. The exams he gives are a bit difficult. Not a good experience taking introductory physics at the UW with a variety of homework and pre-class reading problems. The class load was severe.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Intro physics at UW is absolute hell. Tolich is a great professor, who goes in depth with all the stuff that'll be on the exams. If he's an option for 122, definitely choose him as it's the hardest one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 12X at UW is terrible but he is a great professor. Make sure to show up to class and participate as the live quizzes are worth 10% of your grade which makes a difference. Stay on top of the content and ask lots of questions in tutorial/lab. The tests are hard but you can get a good grade even if you do poorly because they grade so many assignments.

Would recommend based on how good his lectures are-- he makes them interesting and has little demos but theyre also super concise and prep you really well for the tests. He's really helpful in office hours too and just generally cares a lot about the class.
He is very kind and great at explaining concepts. He will always make time to help you on his own time if you need it.
handsome and charming
Very Knowledgable in the content:)

Personally, I felt like Nikolai wasn't extremely friendly. But rating him objectively, and judging him purely based on his abilities to teach, he was fantastic. He did an excellent job of explaining complicated topics in ways for each student to comprehend.

Tolich has very clear lectures. Had office hours twice a week. Cared about students improving and show this by being available to advise on study strategies when exams came around. He also really does try to make the exams fair. If you have to choose between him or another professor, Tolich is almost certainly the better option.
I personally dont like physics but i loved tolich as a prof, he made lectures very enjoyable and ensured his students understood the content.

The PHYS 12x series is UW's version of hell. Tolich was a pretty good professor; his lectures are informative but in general, you'll have to learn everything on your own. Print out the final exam equation sheet they give you and learn how to use it throughout the quarter. Try to grind out as many practice problems as possible and prepare yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Despite the terrible 12x physics curriculum Tolich became one of my favorite professors at UW. Not many office hours but willing to schedule one-on-one meetings with students. He's not only knowledgeable but very good at explaining topics, alongside being approachable. Lectures go fast and I would recommend at least skimming the reading.
Hes a pretty great professor and explains things well, but like the rest of the series, the professor doesn't really play a big role in the class.
A very good lecturer simplifies concepts to make them accessible to the general class.

Tolich is the best physics professor at UW hands down. The physics series will always be a tougher series, but he has good explanations during lectures, and is very easy to reach outside of class, especially on Ed Discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Brilliant lecturer, does mostly problems in class which is super helpful. Always responds to every Ed discussion question before exams and overall very nice. Physics is difficult no matter what but he helped a lot

Really amazing professor and even better human being. Extremely considerate and understanding towards students. Amazing lectures and explanations. If you pay attention in class you will easily understand at least half the material. Very helpful and can be easily accessed outside the classroom. The best physics prof. Dont hesitate to take his class.

Professor Tolich is a great teacher, he is so caring and clear in his lectures, and really goes out of his way to help you during office hours. The class has a lot of difficult materials that it goes over, but he makes it possible to understand it all with all the resources he offers. Overall a great experience for a hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Tolich is very caring and good at his job. He genuinely cares about his students knowing the material and can explain difficult concepts in a way that's much clearer than other physics profs' explanations. He always welcomes questions. This class is still very difficult. I recommend doing a lot of extra practice for exams.

After the first week of sitting in both lectures, I decided to join his lecture section instead of showing up to the one I'm actually registered for. He explains physics in the simplest form possible without any of the other tangents that plague other physics teachers. Would recommend.

He showed up to my lab section on the first day of class - teaches around 300 students. Super caring prof that makes sure you know the material. Tolich wants you to succeed in the very brutal physics series. Has just as much hw as the previous 2 classes but with a teacher that makes the class interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nikolai (not to be confused w/ his wife Kazumi Tolich) is the best phys professor I've had. He explains stuff well and really cares about student success. I loved in-person lectures because you get the chance to work w/ your classmates on the in-class lecture quizzes. Phys has never been my strong suit but I ended w/ a pretty good grade in 123.

Absolutely stellar professor. Very knowledgeable, funny, and engaging. The introductory physics sequence is hard in its own right, but Prof. Tolich made 123 a lot of fun. Ask him about his previous projects! Make sure you show up for class and study for exams.

Lectures are very detailed. Course is hard, moves fast but that is bc of the admin as physics series are a ton of work. !!!Edit: You MUST use practice problems outside of class w/ solutions manuals. Study groups/discords help + share these. I learned well after this series. Felt dumb. Academic record kinda nuked due to not knowing beforehand :(!!!
Seemed to really care about his students learning, even online. First physics professor I had that made me like physics.

Professor Tolich knows how to lecture. The PHYS 12X series is pretty challenging, and he was the best professor I had. He teaches you how to relate equations to physics concepts which is very useful for exams. Practice midterms provided were helpful study tools for the exam. Do the homework and review textbook questions before the exam! Good luck!
Prof. Tolichs class was well-organized and well-run. Online lectures were clear and useful, and he was very accessible outside of class. Made PHYS 123 tolerable.

Best organization of all the 12X classes I've taken. Expectations were clear, and Prof went above and beyond to help me succeed. I emailed about struggling to meet the deadlines, and he met with me over ZOOM and gave me permission to turn work in late for full credit! Course was still very demanding and moved really fast, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: The physics intro sequence in general is tough, but I think taking the course with Tolich could help a lot. He gives pretty good explanations to questions and cares about your learning. I feel like he's really passionate about physics and it definitely shows in his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I'll be honest, the physics series is rough, but Tolich made it better. He knows what he's talking about and wants us to learn. The exams are tough but he posts several practice ones and draws from them sometimes. If Tolich is an option, take him (I took him for 122, 123)! I would 10/10 recommend. He's known to be the best prof for the intro series

Tolich is the best intro-stem professor I've had yet. I actually enjoyed being at his lectures and I felt like most of the material presented to us, was formatted on the test in a way that we all felt prepared for it. His practice midterms are really helpful and he even put a few on there. Study and show up !

I really hate physics, but I really like Tolich. He is a great professor and does his best to make EM easier. The content is really rough, but you're way better off with him than most other professors.

I had Tolich in PHYS 122 and PHYS 224 In a sea of science professors and math professors that don't care Tolich is an absolute gem. His lectures are informative and his test prep material is always well set up. Does his section of PHYS 12X very well and also does well in teaching PHYS 224. Best professor I've had in any "weed out" class.

Nikolai is the Man! I had the privilege to have him for both 122 and 123. 122 being my best. However, 123 was still great with Nikolai, but the material was less interesting. Nikolai does a great job explaning concepts. PLZZ go to his office hours. He will test stuff he explained well in class. HE IS THE REASON I GOT INTO ELECTRICAL ENGINERRING.

The professor is good, the class is not. UW physics is a weed out class for eng. majors. So the class averages are very low, but the curve gets to a grade. You will have to teach yourself physics because the lectures are just example problems. Which is a good and bad thing. If you dont understand be prepared to spend A LOT of time at officer hours.

Tolich isn't the most exciting guy, but that's not what you need from your physics professor. Lectures are clear and informative. He's accessible outside of class and seems to genuinely care about students. Was really helpful when I missed a midterm due to illness. Solid choice for sure.

Great lecturer for a difficult subject (don't worry, it's way better than PHYS122). The demos are super important to pay attention to and you should definitely at least skim through the textbook before lectures.

I took Physics 121 and 123 with Nikolai and he's solid. Any class in the physics 12X series is run very similarly aside from lecture style. Nikolai sticks to powerpoints and is fairly learning catalytics heavy (in class participation system). His explanations are great and easy to understand. Study lecture homework questions LC for easy midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: excellent professor, share recording and prepare lecture slides. patient for students' question and can well explain all the question, he makes this difficult class less stressful! i really like this professor!!! i love his European accent!
insightful lecture; would definitely take again if he teaches phys123.
Tolich is the man

Really great professor! He makes physics sound interesting. His lectures are super clear and he always goes over each problem patiently, even if most people get it right. He cares about students. Im really sad he wont be teaching 123 next quarter, I wish I could take it with him

Nikolai lectures very well and even though he does random cold calls he makes you feel like whatever you say has value. He only provides one practice exam per midterm and final so it is up to you to study from the book.
Lectures are not the most informative, so be sure to supplement them with the textbook. His in class polling is great for understanding concepts better. Solid dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Only issue is that he covers material very very quickly. Besides that, the polling questions are very helpful in understanding what's going on, the demonstrations are fun, and he's just a good dude. Very unintentionally funny. Made me love physics.
Great lectures, office hours are even better, does a great job of explaining physics in a clear, precise manner. Exams are very fair :)

His lectures are fairly weak, but the poll questions are really helpful since he walks through the reasoning/process of each one. His tests are fairly difficult and long, so portion your time wisely - the multiple choice section draws from the Mastering homework and post-labs (no partial credit), and the tutorial section draws from the tutorial hw.

Tolich is hands down the best professor I've had at UW so far. The physics course material is extremely difficult, but he manages to teach the core concepts in a clear/intelligible manner. Going to lectures, office hours, study center etc. will help you understand the topics covered. If you have the choice, I would highly recommend taking his class
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I had Tolich for the entire physics series. He's one of the best physics professors, I've heard negative comments about Pedigo and the other profs, but Tolich is the best. He does interesting demos. Make sure to study lecture slides, often he'll take material straight from slides and use them on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Physics is the hardest sequence at UW, it cannot be escaped. The professor doesn't even matter, the material is hard no matter who teaches it. Tolich is a caring guy and obviously knows his stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I took Daryl Pedigo for 121 and Tolich is much better. HIs lectures are better and he is a lot better at explaining concepts. 122 is a hard class in general and it moves quickly but Tolich does a fairly decent job teaching a hard subject
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Had Tolich for 121 and 122. He's really great and his tests are very clear and not overly difficult. Make sure you understand the labs and are doing the hw problems on your own not looking them up or anything. Reading the textbook is also crucial.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor. Really does care about student learning. He will go step by step on paper to show you how to solve certain problems. He will mostly explain till a question is resolved. Still read your textbook very well. Use the Practice textbook, since HW is out of there. Show up for in class questions.
Tolich is one of the best professor in the Physics department. Grab his class before its closed!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor. Does some cool work and has a gift of distilling physics lectures into something generally interesting and entertaining, while still deftly demonstrating the mathematical meat of it all. Pretty visible in the physics study center downstairs and around campus.

He is a fine Professor. Very friendly though he looks super busy. His main problem is that his classes often have abnormally high curves. His exams have three parts: multiple choice, tutorial and lab section. These are often recycled from lab manual, tutorial and slides. Good luck!

Professor Tolich delivers clear lecture. Lots of in-class quizzes and guiding-through examples. Based on my experience, while targeting 4.0, stay above 2 standard deviation over average on each exam and make sure getting nearly full points on all other things, you'll get what you want. Exams are based on homework and what you learnt in class.

Not sure why people like him so much, his powerpoints/lectures this quarter seem shallow and I don't learn  much from them, this could be a result of the new book we are using this quarter. He is a very nice guy though, hes always willing to help and answer questions.
He is really nice, but he goes through lecture material really quickly and briefly. His explanations are good, and he's good at answering questions.
Honestly one of the best professors I've ever had.
One of the best professors I have had at the University of Washington. Hands down. Takes the time to help students with physics

Best physics lecturer I had at UW. Gives a good mix of theory and example problems in lecture and the homework challenges you enough to prepare you for tests.  Between lecture notes, tutorial, lab, and online prelecture, I did not need to use textbook much

Nikolai is a great professor.  He comes off as incredibly intelligent in lecture but manages never to belittle students for questions he considers obvious.  He makes the occasional joke in class and his demonstrations are always worth the watch.  His class is very fair.  It is tough, but he tells you exactly what you need to know for exams.
Awesome Professor!! Humble, knowledgeable, and has a deep understanding of physics principles and are ready to explain to his students in simple words. He always writes fair exams.

Tolich gets a little overhyped because all the other physics professors really suck. Anyways, tolich is great because he's VERY straightforward about his expectations. Study the practice midterms he gives, because he's doesn't go off tangent from those. In his class, you can expect the expected.
One of the best professors in the department
Tolich was great - straightforward, very polite and helpful. He did a good job of slowing down where he needed to, and also keeping lectures interesting.
Always there to clarify, the class moves fast and is challenging, but if your willing to put in the work, he will help.

He is the best physics prof I've had. Super great power points, which he also posts. His test questions are clear and easy to understand, and actually ask about what he teaches in class. Highly recommend.
awesome teacher, clear lectures, easy exams. One of the best physics teacher in the department.

He is very approachable and not condescending when asked questions about the material. If you give enough time to Smart  Physics before lecture and at least try the smart physics homework, you will stay on top of things and probably do pretty well in the class.

Awesome professor, our section was always better than others in terms of performance on midterms. The professor made a difference. Tough course in general, especially for someone like me who hasn't taken AP physics.

Difficult class in general. I got through it by going to the study center every other day. The TAs definitely help and nikolai also helped out a lot  during his office hours. He really cares about you learning the material and won't look down on you if you have difficult time understanding the concepts. Final was easy compared to the previous exams
THE BEST. THAT IS IT. TAKE HIS CLASS.
He was a nice guy, I didn't see him as an exceptional teacher, but he definitely cared if students understood the material.

Can you say coolest accent ever??? Really though I didn't learn much from his lectures, just a lot of fun demonstrations and reading off power point slides. UW physics department is more at fault of the poor organization of the class than Tolich is.
An excellent professor, tough class. Makes lots of available time to help students out during office hours.

An awesome, dedicated teacher. He clearly cares about the class and made me way more motivated than when I was first coming in. If you don't prepare thoroughly for lectures, though, it's a hard as hell class. If you put in the hours, you can get a good grade though. He is always up for answering questions and will talk until you understand.
Hardest class I have taken and hard to follow the examples because he moves through them so quickly.
Very clear and organized, examples are a bit fast. Excellent lecturer
Great teacher, very helpful. Impecable color coordination.
The best professor in the physics department. Very approachable and always willing to help. Very funny and smart, does cool research also.
Great teacher!

Awesome teacher.  The class is difficult but his tests are challenging but fair.  His lectures are clear and he gives good examples.  Also, he is very easy to approach and makes himself available to answer any questions students have during office hours.  He is really good about answering emails too.  Couldn't recommend more.
One of the best teachers i've ever had, he has very good examples and explanations even though material is difficult. You don't really have to read the book if you go to lecture

He explains things very well, and though it may seem weird that he uses (Keynote?) slides as opposed to the blackboard like most profs, I think it was a good call.  He didn't waste class time deriving formulas that are already in the book, and kept everything as pain-free as possible for a difficult class. Tests were very fair, just do the hw!!
He gives very good, clear explanations on all subject material. Occasionally he will crack a good joke too. A very good professor overall. (And he has a cool accent)

Very clear and concise in his lectures. Has good slides that he puts online for review in addition to his clicker questions. Good lecturer with clear speaking tone. Has only a few examples per lecture which is good because he reviews the concepts mostly. Very intellligent and demos are always interesting/entertaining.He only wears argyle sweaters.
Prof Novick is a wonderful instructor and her lectures are both inspiring and thought-provoking.

Don't take her Ancient Chinese Philosophy class if you are not interested in analytical philosophy. She is understanding about late work and she is easy to communicate with outside of class (in that she is accessible, she is not particularly warm or approachable). Lectures were very boring and the concepts were hard to engage with because of that.

The lectures are really not interesting and I wish I had chosen another class for W credit. The readings are not long at all but you do get quized on them in sections. The TA gives the first 5 minutes of class for the quiz and if you are late you don't get extra time. I just wouldn't take this again, it is not that hard it is just so boring.

Phil 100 is a great class which, I think, can never go wrong. Professor Novick's lectures were kind of dead but 8:30s (when I took it) can do that to a class. Overall the content was super amazing and sections were always tons of fun discussing the material. Great intro to Philosophy / Class is what you make of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very kind and accommodating, Professor Novick will probably be one of the nicest professors you'll work with. Her lectures are a bit brain-numbing after a bit but the way she organizes the material makes it easier to absorb.

The lecture and readings were boring and also required boring and unnecessary group discussion. Although there is no hard deadline for homework papers, the grading criteria is unclear and tough. Never take it again!!!!!

Professor is very understanding and has a very lenient policy regarding late work which is much appreciated. She truly wants to see students succeed and is very good at communicating back during office hours or via email. Unfortunately, lectures are not recorded and can be difficult to follow. Grading is harsh, it is difficult to get full points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very intelligent, but grades as if you were a grad student. Best to go to office hours to get your work reviewed before you turn it in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are very boring and the homework is lots of reading but honestly the readings were decently interesting and when you go to drill section to discuss them it's never like a quiz. It's just talking among friends about weather you liked and agreed with it or not while making sure that you know what's going on and what the core arguments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took him for PO141 at Boston U, lectures were very long but informative. some of the material seems like it's common sense, but the readings might make it sound more complicated than it is. to study just reread through the lectures and know the 2-3 most important readings, most readings are summarized in the lecture anyways.

POLS270 is a very intuitive and inspiring course for those interested in economics and politics. However, the problem is that I have always received no feedback regarding point deductions from the grader (I don't know if the grader is Nicolas or someone else), which provides less emotional support to students.
