I loved Pol 270 with Nicolas as my TA! Teaches concepts incredibly well and knows how to expand on teacher lectures. Very responsive to emails and questions. Office hours were always entertaining and constructive :). If Nicolas is a TA option for your class, choose him!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: For sure recommend. Really good TA - one of the best at UW in polisci
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I'm sure once upon a time Prof. Wacker was a great teacher but age and cognitive decline have gotten to him for all intensive purposes his assistant taught the class and he sat there staring off into the abyss. His assistant did all the lecturing, talking, and had to remind him where he was.

Good person, but hindered cognitively so his wife essentially teaches the class. Could tell he was interested in content, but he just couldn't convey it verbally. The course was 3 essays, 1 poster project, annotations, in class activities. Fairly chill grader, especially if you go in person to classes, lenient on extensions, pairs well w/ bio 200.

prof has health issue. he slowly reads, shakes, and sits quietly. wife runs the class. It was not hard, but an odd structure given the prof.
Class was discussion posts, random calls, and annotations. hw was often short notice and essays were under-explained. repetitive assignments were unhelpful to my overall education. no main idea for the course
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class was weird. The weirdest part of this class was that Norman does not know what is going on whatsoever. He reads what his wife laser points on the slide to read which is usually just the agenda and then sits there for the rest of the class blankly staring while his wife teaches the class. I think the only reason he is a teacher is tenure

Typical class day:
1 bro stands right in the middle of the projector screen, facing it, reading each word at a snail's pace and making 2 mistakes per sentence
2 we consume some text
3 everyone reads their discussion post word for word
4 we get an annotation for homework
Felt like elder abuse, wife (whose first language isnt english) ran everything
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Wacker is older and it shows, mainly in the way that he speaks slower and has to reread some parts of his lecture slides. However, Wacker was very kind and gave meaningful advice for all four of our 2-3 page essays. He encourages creativity in your analysis and does have solid materials. Lots of reading, generous grading. Net positive imo
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Wacker is really kind and gives helpful feedback for all papers. I found his grading generous, and discussions are just graded on participation. The only problem was that there weren't clear guidelines on how to write our major essays for the class, but the prompts ended up being pretty flexible so it wasn't a problem.

Norman is a very kind and caring teacher. However, for English 197 his wife taught the whole class. She made the presentations, led the class, and graded our papers. That would be fine but she isn't an English professor so she seemed unqualified. Every class had one to two discussions which we shared out loud. There are 4 essays with no prompts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: I

Professor really cares about his students and the course! Everything was very straightforward and I feel like I learned a lot while also getting a good grade! Definitely recommend this class for anyone interested in taking an English class and doesn't mind reading books/comics! I took this in summer so not sure about attendance in person.

handed in so many assignments late, but still got full credit. I also put in minimal effort and still got extra credit for one assignment and ended up with s 100.21 in the class. honestly a great professor.

If you're someone who likes instructions of any kind Norman is not the teacher for you. I have never been so confused with what exactly it is he wants in his assignments but with that being said I've still got a 100% on everything I've turned in so idk how much I can complain.

Norman is a good prof! Class was interesting. We approached graphic novels and comics in a new way, where we analyzed their applications to historical politics and modern culture. We had weekly discussion posts and essays (fast-paced but doable). Norman reads and comments on your work so you are set for the final drafts. Clear expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Wacker is easily the best professor I've ever had. I turned in most of my assignments late, but he was super accommodating about it and made me feel comfortable about just getting what I needed to do done. He's such a caring guy and the assignments walk you through what you need to do for each major project.
Honestly one of the easiest classes that I've taken, I'm not the best writer and I got 100% on every paper.

Norman was the best! Super accommodating and understanding to students who might not be the best at English, and has also done a great job making the course adaptable to be asynchronous. Quality guy, definitely take him.

Such a nice man!! You are only graded on 3 short essays and participation. He is very flexible when it comes to grading and really good about accepting different perspectives/points of view. Easy W credit.

I took an online class with Dr. Wacker and you can tell by the way he comments on every discussion and essay submission he really cares about his students. I got full points for every assignment. Submitted and so got an easy 4.0. Overall he is a great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Wacker really cares about his students and gives out good feedbacks for essays. His 281 is basically 299/297 that you read scientific papers and analyze them. I've just received 4.0 but I didn't get 4.0 for every assignment so I guess he is an easy grader:)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I took his engl 281 class, you actually dont really do much in class. Its usually silent while people find research papers through google scholar and such to use as evidence for 2 papers and a poster (which is an online template). He is really nice though, and is always willing to help. You dont really learn much besides the first week of class.

I took his ENGL 299 class (Intermediate Interdisciplinary Writing - Natural Sciences) and thoroughly enjoyed it. Dr. Wacker is very approachable and reasonable when it comes to other classes getting in the way. If you miss class, be sure to ask a friend what you missed, because there is no Panopto recording.

Along with the other comments, I love Norman's clear compassion for his students! It is true that organization is not his strength, but overall class with him is fun, and I think he has a lot of great feedback to offer. He is known for his tangents, but I always like hearing what's on his mind!

He is pretty scattered and you won't always know what's going on, but he is genuine and passionate which makes up for it. Plus he is very lenient and accepts late assignments. He once interrupted his own sentence to tell us about some cool trees he saw in Nevada. It was easy, I improved my writing skills and picked up a few good life lessons.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Norman is very easy going and has a good sense of humor about him. I didn't learn a lot during lecture, I learned mostly from his feedback on my papers. He is good at rambling and you have to be in class to get good grades on the stuff that counts.

Pros: is extremely accessible, always answers questions in a prompt manner, very polite Cons: can ramble during lecture, is a little scattered, but this is made up for by his desire to answer any question and provide lots of feedback.

Amazing teacher who genuinely cares about students. Such a great person to talk to. Please ask for clarification at any chance you get. If you don't reach out whenever you get confused, you definitely won't pass. Honestly amazing.

Dr. Wacker is wild. He is such a genuine person which makes him hard to dislike; he really is passionate about the coursework and literature. That being said, he probably gives the worst directions of any professor I've ever had. This man will talk for 20 mins & after minute 2 you will have no idea what he's talking about. However, easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Tests? Not many--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Seems like a good guy and cares about his students, but the course was a waste of time.  Directions are confusing and he doesn't give due dates in advance.  Group work for almost every class meeting.  The few lectures we had were rambling.  He does give thoughtful comments on papers but ultimately doesn't provide a lot of insight

He's a nice guy, but extremely hard to understand what he wants you to do. He rambles on and on, and any point he tries to make it lost in translation. Writing essays for him was a bit of a shot in the dark, since i was confused about what he was saying constantly. If you have specific questions you can ask him 1-on-1 he is pretty helpful
Norm is an awesome teacher and obviously very invested in students' learning. He can be hard to understand sometimes, but is always willing to clarify and help out!

He is probably the nicest person ever, but also sort of a pushover.  It is hard to get  a straight answer out of him, and any question you ask usually gets an answer at least 15 minutes long.  He's great if you're looking for someone to easily grade your essays.

I took a linked Engl class w/ C LIT from Norman. He can be difficult to understand, but is very nice and willing to clarify. He will push you to improve your writing by expanding your thinking. He is not a hard prof but you will learn a lot. He would probably be harder to understand in a non-engl/lit linked course. I would take him again though!

He's very nice and smiley, tends to ramble (but it's okay so long as you don't have another class to go to immediately). He is a self-admitted poor direction giver, so you might be confused about assignments at first, but this can be remedied by asking for clarification 1+ times. :)

I did a study abroad with Norm.  He's a stand-up guy--enthusiastic, friendly, funny and very approachable.  Norm always has time for students, and if his in-class explanation is confusing, he'll always clarify matters for you after school.  He bent over backwards to make sure his students were well-cared for in Prague; extremely intelligent.

Very, very nice man, not a good teacher.  Not focused on course objective in linked course; he is very committed to teaching and has enourmous enthusiasm for the material, but explanations and assignments were rambling and ufocused.

He's a good teacher who is engaging and interested in his students.  In his self- profile on the internet he describes himself as someone who has been loving Shakespeare in public for many years.  That's enough for me.  I'm straight, so the hot/not hot rating is empty.
Norman is great!  He loves literature and cultural studies.  I started to really love school after first taking his modern lit. class.
He's decently smart enough to run a discussion among freshman without thinking.  And most of the time it feels that way.

GREAT! Very enthusiastic about subject matter and no condescension. Explanations frequently a little scattered/unclear, but professor obviously coming from a well-developed knowledge base of subject matter allthesame. Puts solid energy into teaching.
Contemporary American Lit.  Great!  Recommended.  Not arrogant like many of the other UW English faculty.
No Comments
Great instructor and very interesting class! Very knowledgeable and passionate about content, would absolutely recommend this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Love her!! Aside from being a very nice person, she is also clearly very knowledgeable in the content she talks about making her lectures very interesting and enjoyable. Had a great time in this class, not to mention it was also very easy to pass! Currently looking forward to being able to take another class with her in the future.
super Woke!!! super democratic party hack,,. not balanced,  lacks historical sophistication. worthless for those woh really want to understand

Overall, really interesting class. Assignments were very straight-forward and not time-intensive. Easy A. Every once in a while she would show up to lecture not prepared, but besides that the lectures were great. She clearly knows what she's talking about.
Professor O'Mara is awesome! I absolutely loved this class and it was a breeze. As long as you show up to class 50% of the time and do all the assigned work, you will easily pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class wasn't hard, content was interesting, and she is very knowledgeable about what she teaches. However, lectures were hard to follow along, and she would go off on long tangents talking about her own life/career. She's a big admirer of Jobs, Bezos, and Gates, which made some lectures feel like US military and tech company propaganda.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No required textbook, but plenty of required online readings that are provided over Canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: There's a good bit of reading in this class but you don't actually have to do most of it, as long as you properly skim and understand what's going on you should be fine. This class was really great and wasn't too difficult, it was my first history class at UW and I was pleasantly surprised!

Prof O'Mara is great, she's extremely knowledgeable about the content and her lectures are interesting and engaging. She does a great job of presenting nuanced information and emphasizing the importance of studying history. A good amount of reading every week, but nothing too crazy and it is all relevant and interesting (do them).

Her writing prompts are very vague and try to make sure you fail the first time you write in response to them. She knows exactly what she wants but she keeps her prompts vague so that it is not possible to write what she wants and have to re write. Word of advice, do essays early because you are gonna have to rewrite due to her lack of guidance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Margaret is incredibly knowledgeable and put together an insightful and entertaining class. However, the course grader made it the hardest class I have ever taken at UW. I must have spent 10+ hours a week on writing and rewriting the essays and will probably get a 3.0. I'm an English major and this course made me seriously doubt my writing skills.

Insanely smart regarding her subject matter. Also, way more organized than most professors I've had in terms of assignments, grading and criteria. Lectures are very entertaining and informative. Graded on weekly discussions, one group video project and four essays with the option to rewrite for a higher grade. Amazing professor.
I love this woman. Her lectures were fun and fascinating and I thought she gave very helpful feedback. I recommend asking her about Bill Clinton during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof O'Mara is the best!! She is a walking encyclopedia when it comes to US history and really knows how to make her lectures interesting. There is quite a bit of writing and reading, and attending lecture is important, but she is a very fair grader. Put in effort and you'll get a good grade.

Margaret is extremely knowledgable and passionate on the topic, and made lectures so interesting and enjoyable that I never wanted to miss one. She posts outlines of the lectures on canvas but the actual class material is much more in depth so if you skip you probably won't pass. My only complaint is the mountains of reading each week! Great prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor O'Mara is a phenomenal professor when it comes to conveying information. There are reading responses for every book but they are not hard to get full credit on. The grading on the midterm, final, and paper were tough but the TA was a hard grader. This is the lowest history grade I have had and I generally 4.0 300 level courses.

Prof. O'Mara is an encyclopedia on the topic; she knows the answer to any question you have. She is great in office hours. She commands respect in class and I highly encourage taking a seminar with her. Her assignments are easy and honestly fun (look at old issues of the editorials in Suz and analyze them). She is also a lowkey easy grader.

If you want an easy 4.0, do not take professor Omara. Shes a nice professor with interesting lecture but she gives so many readings. She also gives an project youre suppose to work on all quarter with two take home exams. And she goes bananas if you connect to wifi on your laptop of touch ur cell.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: O'Mara is one of the best profs I've ever had. She is super knowledgeable about American History especially modern elections (she worked for the Clinton Campaign). We read her book as one of the assigned readings and it was one of more interesting books I've had to read for a history class.

Class was structured around lectures, book reviews, and take home exams. If your cup of tea is an easier history class, go for it. No huge leaps and jumps are made within lecture and the books you review are god-awful. But, her technology focus as a professor provides some neat insights into American history.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This was one of the more interesting classes I have taken at UW. No tests or quizzes. You're graded on participation and a research project. The research project centered around the University District. Lectures are really boring unless you like urban history. Honestly didn't care about urban history at all. Overall, the research project was fine.

I took her class three years ago and I really enjoyed it. I never did the readings and never talked in discussion session, but still managed to pull off a 3.7. Not sure how that happened. You will learn a lot of American History, though. The outlines that she provided at the beginning of each class were helpful. Study hard for the final.
Awesome prof.

Prof Omara is really interested in what she is teaching and an animated lecturer. However, the material isn't as interesting as I had hoped from the course description. My favorite part of the class was the reading list and discussion section, but some of the lectures were interesting. The test was surprisingly tough and there was a lot of reading.

Passionate about her subject but probably more used to working with graduate students than to lecturing. An absurdly condescending late-work policy: "one tenth of a grade point for every five minutes late."

O’Mara is a great professor. The City was my favorite class of the quarter. She focuses less on dates and facts and more of creative understanding of how cities evolved over time. There is a lot of homework required to succeed in the class, but it is worth it if you are interested in urban history. I highly recommend this professor and the class.

If you're considering taking this class, you should. Jeffrey is so knowledgable on everything related to Seattle architecture and the class itself is really fascinating. He's also a great guy and pretty funny too. The class isn't easy, but you'll do well if you come to lectures and put forth your best effort. Grading can be tough.

First time writing on here, never felt the need to before but Jeffrey changed my mind. He is passionate on the topics he speaks about, his passion is so genuine that every lecture I am always so invested. Im not an architect major nor interested in architecture, yet this class was fun! Pay attention and study for assignments, and you will do great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: So knowledgable, and cares a lot when the students care. He'll put in work when you do. His essay critiques and redlines are the most helpful I've ever had. Absolute resource

I would try your best to avoid this professor. Grading scale and feedback is based on if he personally likes you and your writing style. Rambling surface-level lectures. Talks down to students and argues with other professors in an incredibly unprofessional manner. Think of the most annoying tenured professor and you have Jeffery Ochsner.

Taking Ochsner for 352 after 351 with Huppert was definitely a change in pace. He seemed to perform slightly worse with the online format than other professors in the 350 series. asynch lectures, 4 quizzes, and 2 essays, so not too heavy on the work, but quizzes were MUCH more textbook-based than Huppert.
Best professor I've had in the 350 arch series. He is very passionate, inspirational and know the material very well.

It's an urban design studio's supplemental class. If you want to cover all of the urban design and history preserv. theories, just go for it. He is very friendly and very clarified in what he says. The works might be a little bit overwhelming, but it is very worth to learn. At the end of the day, you'll realize you've already memorized them.

Too many key works compare to ARCH 350 and 351. Have two 10 mins quizzes that quiz about the concepts. A lot of little and unclear information that need to be memorized. I don't really enjoy this class overall.
He is very passionate about his lectures. Definitely knows the material inside and out. Midterms are not easy so make sure you study throughout the quarter.
Don't take for an easy class.  While it's 3 credits, it was the hardest class I've ever taken.  That being said, learned SO MUCH and he is an incredible lecturer.

Roughly 60 key works on the mid term. The final was going to be 100 and he brought it down to 80. Study throughout the quarter. Tests will take up the full class period so be strategic. Ochsner is a pretty energetic guy and it is easy to listen to him. A few of the questions on the quizzes are about the book. You don't need to read for the tests.

Do not take for an easy class, this class is very difficult and requires a TON of content to be memorized.  That being said, if you love architecture it's great.  Jeffery is SO enthusiastic and gets you excited about architecture! Great as a pre-rec, was pretty difficult, but learned a ton!!!
never had such an exciting history class. He's knowledgable and passionate about architecture and teaching architecture.

Prof Ochsner is extremely enthusiastic about the subject, but he talks really fast and goes through way too many key works in one lecture. The GSAs were slow and uneven in grading, and manifested their assumption that every student wanted to cheat. But aside from the unpleasant GSAs, the class was ok, just need to study a lot! Memorize early on!

Class was so/so.  He's at least excited about the subject, which made the lectures more interesting.  Kind of pompous, though.  Gave every lecture with his eyes closed and says "quote, closed quote" in every single lecture.  Kind of a quote-dork-closed quote. Tons of memorization. Memorize key works as you go along, not just before the test!
Pretty easy class, you need to at least kind of read the book for the two quizzes , no surprises but ARCH 350/351 are definitely recommended
She's learning! Some test questions were a little out there. You could tell she was nervous and figuring out how to teach. She is super caring and will prob be really good in a few years.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
This is for BIOC 405, but it isn't an option to choose on RMP. 
She doesn't really teach, just reads off the slides. She also makes mistakes often, especially on tests. Her tests are way harder than the practice exams. Our class average was a 50 for the first test and 60 for the others. Usually, the BIOC 405 average is 70...

Way better than Hurley as a lecturer and explains the material clearly.
The EXAM section was poorly structured, most of the class could not even finished the first two exam, and last two took a complete different style.

Hurley was the real problem with 440, he is too old to teach. O'Neill gives you ALL the information very clearly and although it's a lot, it helps to know everything. Exams had several puzzle like questions that were not explained very well in class and the final was brutally difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Shaosong is a very engaging lecturer when the sessions are synchronous, but when they're asynchronous he tended to not be the clearest. Grading criteria was also unnecessarily harsh at times.

Really fun professor to get classes from. He made an online class engaging for me, especially for a course far outside my degree. Assignments were pretty tricky, but his explanations and tutorials were solid.

For an online class, I found his lectures engaging and clear. Grades are based off of assignments, attendance, and discussion boards. Some assignments may take a couple hours, but aren't too hard. There is an one exam at the end, but it is combined with the finance section which is taught by another professor.

IS305: Shaosong is excited and wants people to learn. Assignments wouldn't be bad IF grading wasn't extremely harsh, specific, and unspecified. Maybe it's the TA, but points are taken off for minor things NOT listed on rubrics which matters A LOT for Foster grading. Prep to email for points back for mistakes which are not your fault or listed...
His midterm was easy and the final was unexpectedly harder. It was back to back with a group project too and I had to carry that on top of studying for an exam. Would not recommend.
If 67 was a professor

Shaosong is an entertaining and engaging professor. His lectures were the only ones where I had no urge to go on my phone or space out. He is very funny and keeps up with pop culture and technology trends, so nothing he says is outdated. Very enjoyable!

He is great at getting people engaged during both in person and online classes, and assigning projects that will genuinely benefit you down the road. I would consider it to be a fun class despite the grading techniques being arbitrary and frustrating.
Talks fast. Unreasonable and very inconsiderate about extensions and issues with grades.
I do not recommend, very hard to reach and extremely hard grader

Shaosong's class is a mixed bag - lectures can be hit or miss, but the content is applicable if you're interested in IT. unstuck AI was a lifesaver for exam prep alongside the textbook. Overall, it's a challenging course, but manageable if you stay engaged.

An engaging lecturer and provides many helpful real life examples. Exams slightly on difficult side, but  apply yourself and pay attention, its manageable. To study for the tests, honestly, make sure to review everything! Slides, in class workshops, lectures. Beware: U learn code and IS systems in ONE lession and are expected to know for exams.

The only redeeming quality is that he is genuinely a nice guy. Unfortunately, the class itself was a nightmare. The lecture content was extremely dry and the labs did little to prepare you for the exams. Last week of class consisted of a group presentation and an extremely difficult final that was very unreasonable.

Listening to Shaosong's lectures is like watching Tim Cook unveil the latest iPhone. Dude's just got a youthful aura.

His tests are ridiculously hard, but very applicable if you plan on pursuing I S. 

I wouldn't recommend taking this class with him if you're taking 4 classes and working a part time job.

Shaosong is honestly one of the best professors at UW Foster. I highly advise everyone to take his class if possible. He's funny and very passionate about the material, and he does a great job of connecting with his students on a personal level.

Sadly Shaosong dissapointed me in the end. He gave us a presentation and lab due right before the final exam. He also said the computer 2nd part of exam would be open note, to quote his own words "if you are using your laptops theres no way I can make it closed book." But day of he went back on his word and only allowed us to use canva and excel.

Shaosong is a very entertaining and funny lecturer. All of the info on exams comes from what he talks about on the lecture slides. The labs and projects require a good understanding of the program used so they can be difficult. The class is pretty difficult, but if you review definitions, formulas, and lecture videos before exams, you can do well.

Shaosong's class is not good because his lectures don't explain everything. He just focuses on one thing and then some of the slides he completely skips the information without explaining. You're supposed to know everything, but he briefly talks about things with little depth. He creates participation assignments without notice
The TA did all the teaching and graduing. All shaosong did was use tiktok and bereal during class.

My least favorite class ever. He's an engaging lecturer and funny, but his quizzes were impossible with the time limit. He expected us to have specific lines of code memorized as beginners who had only used the language once. The labs and group project were manageable. MEMORIZE EVERYTHING IN THE SLIDES - they will be tested in the final.

Shaosong wasn't quite as bad as I had heard, but he was close. I stopped going to lectures pretty early on because they were mostly useless, and it seems like the rest of the class did too. Don't bother going to lab either, just read the tutorial and have chatgpt explain things to you, it's a much better teacher than Shaosong. Yue was cool tho.

Assignments are graded on random things that dont accurately show your knowledge of the content and his lectures are interesting at times and completely useless at other times (most the time) He also plays major favorites. Some content (mostly labs) super interesting but final and quizzes are mostly on the random unimportant stuff we learn in lectu

He makes jokes throughout class to distract you from the fact that he's a terrible professor. His lectures are incredibly dry. I'll look around the class and see everyone dozing off and falling asleep. He expects you to remember 10 weeks of material for the final and expects you to remember how to do a problem that you did once in class 3 weeks ago
Wow, 7 thumbsup in a day, IS 300 did teach buying click farming on Alibaba, didn't it.
This good/bad polarized debate is meaningless. Hope this is the last comment for a while and this course will be better for everyone.
This forum is such chaos: several people (maybe including the prof himself) arguing with each other.
I like Shaosong. Reachable and personable.
Sweet and responsive, especially the TAs

I really enjoyed Shaosong's classes, I also loved his adorable and sweet TA Yue. He is a cool professor with good jokes and lots of knowledge. I appreciate how he stays up to date to trends. Yes, the workload is heavy and exam is extremely difficult, so starting all assignments, labs, and project early is a must. That saved me this quarter.

Great professor. Kind, full of jokes, engaging even tho material is boring. The bad thing (and the reason for bad winter q reviews) is that the final was WAY too long. Nobody finished. Literally NOBODY. He's very intelligent, so I have no doubt he will change the final for next q. With that assumption, he's awesome. Don't be afraid of his class.

I am not sure where all the bash comes from for Shaosong. He is a sweet guy and always inspirational. IS 300 can be a bit boring, but it is not challenging.

Look at the dates of all the negative reviews for Winter 2023; it is very unusual.

Seriously, Shaosong is probably not the best teacher as Foster, but he is well above par.
Fun in lectures but does not help with questions. Final was absolutely absurd
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Get ready to struggle. The final is impossible. Not one person finished the final before time was up out of the hundred+ students in his IS300 classes.
If you're reading this Shaosong just know your jokes aren't funny. Don't take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's very impatient. If we ask him something from the class, he will never repeat or clarify for a second time. And we are not allowed to use recordings to review for the quiz. He just wants to give students hard time and refuses to help.

Shaosong is by far one of the worst professor's I have had at UW to date. He is a wolf in sheep's clothing, as said by many of his previous students. His jokes are not funny, and they are a way to con you into thinking he has a pure heart. He finds happiness/pride when people don't complete the HW. Take Tayfun instead-- avoid Shaosong at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class with Shaosong is so hard. I spend way too much time doing the assignments for this class its so frustrating. It actually is horrible, if you are not an IS major or good with technology. Save us all.

You don't really do much in the class except weekly lab assignments (like excel or other computer language task). Actual lectures aren't very helpful and I didn't really pay attention to them. Grade is made up of 2 lecture assignments, 10 lab assignments, group project, and the final. Final is really hard but I don't think your supposed to finish

This class was really interesting and Shaosoung was a entertaining and solid lecturer. There are weekly quizzes that come from the lecture that can be difficult, but I would say they are fair. You can tell he is passionate about the field and cares about his students. I would take him again as he was entertaining and made it fun. Final was tough.

I think his rating is a little lower on this site because of how hard the assignments and final can be. He's a great guy, a very concise teacher, and doesn't get boring to listen to. Just start the group project early and be prepared to put in time for the assignments. If you can, take this class with 1-2 easier classes. One of my favorite profs!
He tries his best to make the class enjoyable while also helping you learn. The assignments and quizzes are very straightforward. Professors don't often get as good as this, in my opinion.

Amazing professor. Every class was engaging and had something new to learn. The assignments were tough at times but enjoyable. Small quiz once a week. His personality is wonderful. If he's available be sure you take his class, you won't regret it. Grading isn't tough, make sure you do all your work and turn it in on time. 10/10 class overall
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Shaosong is my favorite professor Ive had at Foster! He is very funny, an engaging lecturer, and very accessible in terms of help outside of class. I havent seen another professor put in the effort he has to create a dynamic online learning environment; it was refreshing. It is a tough class for sure, but I cant recommend Shaosong enough.

Shaosong likes to keep up with the current trends! Like the "fellow kids" type. The content isn't hard, but the expectations for lab assignments are inconsistent across different sections (b/c different TAs). Some of the assignments involve a little thinking outside the box. Work together with other people! It helps a lot.

No clear instructions over lab and lecture assignments. He is very enthusiastic but at the same time appears to be low-key mean when you ask for clarification. Quizzes are not hard but make sure to re-watch the recording lectures. He didnt cover tons of materials so make sure to ask your friends who have taken his class before the final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I feel like everyone is being a bit too hard on him here, you definitely need to put in work on the lab assignments, but not too time consuming. The tutorials didn't help at all tho so I just stopped going to them and skimmed thru the replays. His classes are interesting and the only real issue here is how much the content bounces around randomly.

Be prepared for tough assignments that require significant effort. Make sure you're in class, participate, have your camera on, and at least look excited to be in class. He will haze the class left and right with odd requests or other weird activities... Additionally, he is biased toward Asian students.

Shaosong's lectures are great. He is energetic, kind, and funny. However, this class was extremely difficult as the workload is excessive and assignments are unclear. The level of work expected does not compare to the level at which material is taught. If you want clear instruction and assignments that are on par with the course, avoid this class.

I can see Shaosong tried his best to make his lectures fun, and his lectures are pretty good. However, the labs don't have clear guidance and expect probably too much from students. The final project also has very vague guidance and no grading rubric. I would avoid him if you want clear guidance and rubric.

Classes are long and uninteresting. Spends a lot of time talking about unrelated stuff, literally wasting time. The content feels random, you don't actually learn anything useful besides some Excel and SQL. The the final tests you on stuff he didn't spend much time on. If you're looking for technical skills, you're better off learning by urself

Aight, shaosong is funny I guess? Kind of cringey funny. I don't really understand all these reviews saying he is great. His exams and projects are way too difficult and the labs are terribly run and taught. He is kinda funny, does NOT make him a good prof.
Shaosong is one of the best teachers in Foster! His class isn't the easiest but IS 300 is hard no matter who you take, Shaosong is very understanding and makes class fun. 100% take him if you can

I was unsure if I was fit for IS but after taking IS 300 with Shaosong, I knew I was going to continue on my path. There are challenges, but he will be their to meet with you, and will reply to emails almost instantly. He cares so much about his students, and if you want to succeed in this class he will make sure you do. One of my favorite teachers

Don't take IS300 if it's not with Shaosong. This guy is absolutely amazing in lecture and in general. He cares about his students and makes the class interesting. He walks through the content and does his best to make sure everyone is caught up. (also king of comedy!! never a dull moment in this class)

Shaosong is one of the best professors I've had at UW! He is passionate about the lecture materials. His lectures are always so engaging. The lecture contents are also very relevant and useful. He is very organized (which helps so much in remote learning). He gave lots of help on the second hw which made it less challenging than it seemed at first.

Reading the other reviews- Sure, he cracks a few jokes every now and then, but who really cares? Shaosong is a wolf in sheeps clothing. Avoid at all cost. Expects way too much for a 300 level course. 2nd assignment was ridiculous, as was the final. STAY AWAY
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: By far the best professor I've had in all of college. He really cares about his students' learning and participation, and is constantly making jokes to keep everyone engaged. He is always willing to help and make the lecture material very clear.

Shaosong! One of my fav professors at UW and made learning IS a really enjoyable experience. He's always willing to help and explain concepts outside of class and really wants his students to succeed. He has a really unique background and is highly educated. Ask him about his study abroad teaching experiences and his love for futbol!

Shaosong is quite the character. He's a funny guy and its obvious he loves what he teaches which makes the class easy to get through. The exams are pretty hard and I really suggest heavily studying the material. He teaches you valuable skills, especially in Excel and just like all Foster courses, there is a group project in his class too.

Shaosong is super funny and easily my second favorite teacher at Foster! You will definitely enjoy his lectures because of his unique sense of humor. I literally attend his class just for his jokes. Other than that, this class was fairly easy and mostly memorization work for exams.

Shao Song is, and will always be, the funniest professor on campus. Sometimes I find myself falling backwards but he would never let my grades fall. And I'll tell ya, Winter quarter was a slippery slope.

He is a great lecturer and extremely knowledgable guy. It is frustrating because he tests on small details from lecture to make sure you pay attention. Also his midterms and finals are literally meant to trick you even though he says otherwise. I feel like I had to work hard for my average grade in this class, but I respect him for his expertise
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class was pretty straight forward. The 2nd lab assignment was pretty challenging and the final was way more difficult than the midterm. Get good grades on the quizzes, labs, assignments & have a good group for the group project and you should be fine. Reading the text helps with the exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Hilarious

reviews.comment: As others mentioned, I have mixed feelings about him. He's a funny guy when lecturing but outside, he seems to be standoffish. Labs are fine, but some take a lot of time. Exams are based on random information given in class, be prepared to study small details about everything. Good luck on the 2nd lecture assignment using excel, it's difficult.

Shaosong is hilarious and engaging. Most of the grading distribution is made on the midterm and the final (which often feel like trivia with shaosong). I remember the first midterm had like 8 points on auctions, which was mostly from a 15 minute aside in one of the lectures. The curriculum is essentially whatever interests shaosong-- great class.

Shaosong is a great professor for the intro Information System class. He is funny and inspirational. Attend his class, and you will be good for the exam. His exams are based on his powerpoints and his examples provided in class. The lab section is easy. Great professor.

Most reviews below are spot-on. I have very mixed feelings, as he is a fun and engaging professor, but is difficult to get a read on. The course is filled with a bunch of random material, and he tests on the random topics that he finds interesting. Best advice is pay attention to everything and assume everything is testable.

There's a lot of material in this class, lots of memorization of small details, and a lot of the information isn't super practical. That said, Shaosong is super funny, easy to learn from if you care, and pretty clear with expectations and tests. Take Shaosong! But it's not a shoe-in.

For a lower level business course, the workload is unbelievable. The class is entirely tailored to juniors -- avoid waiting until you're a senior to take this course. The content is mostly useless except for the excel portion. Avoid if you have a heavy quarter, as you will spend most your time doing useless homework assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: At first you might think: hes funny and seems level headed... Until u get to the project, exams, and assignments. Such vague expectations and then expects a lot. He admits that very few people get full points for 2nd assignment bc he doesnt teach us how to do it. One of the worst foster profs Ive encountered

Mixed feelings on Shaosong. He's a talented, engaging lecturer and a smart guy but his tests are odd. They don't really test your IS knowledge as much as your ability to memorize useless knowledge. He can be very unclear about his expectations for assignments, the labs are poorly written especially. You do learn a good amount in this class, though.

Very mixed feeling for Shaosong. He is funny in lectures but the exams are not. If you memorize the textbook then that will get you a 4.0. Take this class with someone else and avoid this guy. Also, bonus points for labs don't count for anything and he doesn't tell you until the last day of class. How does this guy still have a job

Very difficult class, I should have taken this class with a different instructor. He doesn't offer good exam prep and his technical problems are very difficult. Worst professor that I have ever taken.
Very good lectures but he needs to work on his notes. Slides lack details and he tests on things we didnt learn in class. His tests are very hard

Good teacher but his test are very hard he doesn't want people to above average. Makes concept seem easy in class but makes them way harder on test with out going over it in class. Do not take him expecting an easy A

Shaosong is a very smart guy and you can tell hes really into what hes talking about. His tests can be difficult and vague in some spots, so make sure you have the lab stuff and concepts down and are able to apply them. Hes kinda funny but tbh he says some suspect stuff sometimes that can make people uncomfortable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very hard to tell what's important or not, his slides are not well organized and sometimes they don't contain enough information to get the point of it. He's final was very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Great teacher, wants you to do well and learn! He always offers extra help if needed. The class can be challenging if you don't go to lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: You will be tested on information which is not in the text and is not lectured on in class. In addition, there will be pop quizzes, difficult exams, team projects, and rigorous take-home projects. The hardest part of the class is the technical aspects. There is no way to practice because you aren't given practice problems. 4.0 was over 98%.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Lecture slides don't include half of what he says, so go to class. Choose the company that presents on the second day. Study for exams verbatim of what he lectures and lab material and you'll do fine on both the midterm and final. The bonus points from labs aren't extra credit, he just does it for "fun" to see which students will do them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Really smart guy, but uses lecture time inefficiently. Tests are much harder than the material presented in class. Extremely vague about concepts that are important to the class. Jokes can be funny/inappropriate depending on your sense of humor. Enjoys randomly calling on people in class. Make sure you understand and can apply lab concepts (Excel).
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He likes to trick his students. His pop quizzes on topics that we haven't learned and he writes really hard and tricky tests. It's unfair when teachers trick students like that, this is not how you learn. You NEED to go to class because he purposely doesn't include everything in this slides. Only like him because he's funny. Not an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Shaosong is the most arrogrant professor I have ever had. He makes over-the-top jokes all the time that are borderline profane. There are pop quizzes, labs, mini-assignments, a midterm, and a final. It's just insane the amount of work for a core class. This should be illegal. TLDR: he's smart, but rude and crude.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Never a dull lecture. Some thought his jokes were over the top but I personally loved them because they kept things engaging. TAKE HIM!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Lecture is full of nonsense jokes. Didn't learn much from this prof and he grades tough on class assignments and exams. Take it in the summer quarter or with some other prof cuz from what I have heard it was midterm optional for the other sections.

Shaosong is an engaging lecturer who opens every class with a joke. The exams and pop quizzes are written entirely from the lectures, lab assignments and supplemental reading (not from textbook), so take good notes. There's a big group project due at the end of the quarter. The textbook is unnecessary (save $ and use library copy, if needed).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Very mixed feeling for Shaosong. He is funny in lectures but the exams are not. If you memorize the textbook then that will get you a 4.0. Pure memorization is not the goal of education, and this class is also poorly structured. Take this class at a study abroad or something and avoid this guy. Do yourself a favor!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's just amazing, you will learn so much stuff ! He's also funny and make jokes all the time.

IS 300 required lots of studying the lecture slides and reviewing the labs through youtube and outside learning. Knowledgeable teacher. Some lectures weren't as useful for the tests. Didn't care too much for the jokes, he knows what will be offensive and continues to say what he wants. Didn't feel extra help was super available. Decent class.

I feel really complicated about him. I don't like him because he always tries to tease his students and in another hand trying to please them using his awkward jokes. On the other hand, he is indeed a knowledgeable and smart guy. Beware of pop quizzes.

Shaosong loves to crack jokes and even though they are often painful, it makes the class interesting and fun. Tests were harder than expected, but not awful. Group project w/ 5 page report was alright, just try to be innovative with your idea. Lab can easily be skipped w/ no impact on grade as long as you do the lab assignments (put on canvas).

He has a great sense of humor; he loves you especially if you're blonde. One thing to note: hope that your team has your group project on the 2nd day versus the 1st. He doesn't make teams turn in their projects in on a due date, because of this many groups change their presentations to anticipate his questions/gauge how to to suck up.

His lectures are pretty entertaining, but not always relative to what is tested. His tests are pretty hard, so you really need to know the material. He loves cold calling and giving pop quizzes, which sucks.

Shaosong has an incredibly inappropriate and hilarious sense of humor and makes class more upbeat and exciting. He knows IS inside and out and is extremely good at teaching it, especially to someone who knows nothing about computers or tech. There were a couple pop quizzes but even his tests are quite straight forward. Just do the homework!

He knows his stuff. He is concise, but doesn't make topics as clear as they could be.  The first half of the quarter is mostly memorization, the second half is excel/binary and more conceptual. You'll likely have to do some Internet browsing to fully understand concepts. But DON'T SKIP LECTURE. He keeps it entertaining and he genuinely cares.

Hilarious teacher who really knows his stuff about IT. The class can be challenging at times, but overall it is not bad as everything is based off the book and slides. Labs are fair, make sure to start on assignments early.

Generally a disorganized class. Be sure to attend class or it will be difficult to do well on the examstests are based on lecture slides. Pretty much all memorization. Professor is okay though. He's funny, but the class ain't. Don't buy the textbook.

This class was tougher than I thought, especially the midterm and final. You really have to put in effort to do well. Materials are kind of all over the place and not really focused on anything specifically.

Pretty good professor overall. Nothing incredible, but definitely presents material well. You don't need to buy the book, but definitely memorize all of the lecture slides and understand the labs and cases. His humor can be over the top sometimes, but he keeps you entertained which is nice. Hard class, but doable if you put in the effort.
Don't buy textbook. Just check it out from library course reserves if you must, because it's really not necessary. Exams are memorization more or less.

Shaosong is one of the funniest and most entertaining profs I've ever had. His lectures will keep you focused, but sometimes it feels like his stories overshadow actual content. On the assignments he is not always clear about what he wants or his grading criteria, and there was poor communication with the lab. Tests were not incredibly difficult.

Shaosong is great in that he is somehow able to be a boring subject like IS hilarious and entertaining. However, don't be fooled by the lighthearted and fun nature of his class, because some of the excel assignments and the final were very difficult in my opinion, and took me by surprise.

Funny but really, really, REALLY awkward guy. Does not require textbook, although it does help out. First half of the quarter is spent learning about technology in businesses, second half gets really technical into exactly how technology works (binary, electromagnetic waves, etc). Would definitely recommend!

OK class. He's funny, class isn't boring but there's only so much new things to learn. Exams can be surprisingly tough, so make sure you jot down everything he says on lectures. Other than that, Shaosong is solid.

Shaosong opens every lecture with border-line jokes I personally found entertaining. His exams require strict memorization of the slides; He has two pop quizzes testing you on material 1-2 weeks prior to midterm and final. The final is a little harder but manageable. He could shorten his lecture to about 45 minutes if he cut out the non-sense

Shaosong may have been the most entertaining professor I've had.  He makes a lot of jokes (some a little crude) and it keeps you entertained and at least a little bit focused. The material was dry at times, but he tried to keep everyone involved.  I felt like the class was very difficult during, but after the curve I found myself with a 3.9!

Be prepared for 5 minutes of attempted stand up comedy before class. Sounds nice, until falling behind by an entire lecture, and the info is rushed the class before the midterm or final. Overall fairly easy if you memorize slides. Some of his multiple choice test questions are vague, making them hard to answer. Did not clearly answer any of my ?s
He is funny and full of passion for what he does.  You will learn and do it with a smile.  Great instructor.

Useless class, made even more useless by the professor. You feel like he doesn't take teaching seriously. If you know anything about the tech world, you'll learn ~20% of the time. Tests are multiple choice/T or F/some essay, but overall completely memorization based -> no critical thinking required. Projects/papers graded very arbitrarily.
The class itself was quite boring, but he was really interesting and entertaining. Since you have to take this class anyway, make sure you take it with him! Also, you don't need the textbook.
Funny professor, but didn't learn anything. unclear about what needed to know.
Cool guy but not really a great professor. didn't really learn much from the class

Shaosong is easily one of the most entertaining instructors at the university. Not only that, but he knows his stuff and you'll learn a lot. Overall, the class is manageable and the exams aren't too tough. The hardest part is the group presentation, so make sure you pair up with competent people, and prepare diligently. This class is a lot of fun!

Ridiculously easy. If you are in any way competent with technology, you will be fine. Not all that helpful, but really entertaining. Just really focus on doing well on the group project; since the class is so easy, it will make or break your grade.

DO NOT BUY THE BOOK. It is a waste of money. But Shaosong is fun and funny! This class has the potential to be BORING, but he is awesome. Choose an early date for your group presentation and just get it out of the way.
Shaosong is pretty cool and pretty funny. His lectures were not awful, you learn a lot of very useful information and many practical applications, the lab section is good too.

Shaosong is a great professor. He makes the subject material very interesting! I didn't know anything about IS prior to taking his class, and now I'm considering taking many more IS classes. He is entertaining, which make the two hour class go by faster than my other 2 hour classes. As for exams, memorize every slide he tells you to memorize!

Pretty funny guy, but his tests are harder than you think. They require a lot of memorization. He will tell you which slides to study for tests. Make sure you memorize EVERYTHING on those  slides and I mean everything, even the most obscure things are game for the test. Overall, lectures can be a little dry at times, but his jokes are pretty funny.
Shaosong is a wonderful professor. He makes learning about IS/IT easy and exciting. I can?t imagine taking this class with anyone else. Strongly recommended

Best professor! The tests are multiple choice, T/F and short answer, and the average is usually about 80%, but easy to get well above. Labs are easy and take only an hour at most.  The group project is hard, so I suggest talking to him about your topic and get a lot of feedback. Shaosong is also super funny and keeps the class interesting.

Very very funny.  Makes lectures very interesting.  A lot of memorization for tests. The presentation can be a lot of work so pick a good team. Make sure you attend lecture because participation in class is graded.

such a funny professor! makes the 2 hour class go by so fast! Now that I've taken his class, I'm seriously interesting in focusing in IS. Plus, the load is not bad at all...Plus, he's very eager to help you learn.

Very funny guy, but the jokes eventually get a little repetitive (It's so hot that...).  Take the presentation very seriously, and study for the test (ALL the slides are fair game, so even learn the obscure ones...).

Getting a good grade in this class is dependent on the presentation and the midterms. He will not help you with what might be on the midterms or the final, will not give you study guides but it is possible to get a good grade if you study everything. Definitely a  good prof and a class worth taking.

he is so freaking funny and down for a lot of things..especially business school events haha which shall not be mentioned. however...you will be surprised w/ ur grade in this class. HIGHLY dependent on the quality of your presentation.
Very interesting prof, BUT difficult to study for his tests and you lose points on exams without explanation. Be prepared to laugh in lecture and then stop laughing when you see your grades...

Great Prof.  A lot of memorizing, but not too difficult.  He really does make class very interesting, and entertaining. Study the slides from class, and don't your waste money on the book. You don't need it.

He always says that his class is  gonna be the best IS class that you ever take, but wow, it really is. His teaching techniques are really sparks interest for student as he periodically tell jokes to keep us awake during the class period. He grades not so easy though. Seriously he should teach another IS classes in the future, HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

I'm strongly considering becoming an IS major after taking his class. He's hilarious  ! Seriously, he would do amazingly well as a stand up comedian. You still learn a ton about IS from him though. My most memorable class would have to be the one where he spent 30 minutes in lecture playing SecondLife and showing us his virtual girlfriend. Haha.

He's a really funny guy! I come to class everyday just to hear his stories.. and of course.. to learn about info. sys. =) Going to his lectures actually made me become an IS major.. HE's a really nice guy but he grades pretty hard.. kinda picky on the exams.. but attend class and you'll do well.. there's no reason NOT to attend!
He's really funny and knowledgeable. He doesn't grade exams and assignments easy, but if you pay attention in class and study for exams, you'll do great.
Pretty boring, not graded on much.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Hard class. Idk why the bad reviews. U can tell how smart he is from how he speaks, good lecturer, tho sometimes it can get boring (but like that's lots of classes). He is nice, answers questions, is responsive. Going to class is important but no req. attendance.

Late grader, hard to review his notes though ngl, - why going to class is important
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Definitely underrated compared to what other reviews say. If you're taking one of the intro econ classes, he is a significantly better lecturer than the other professor. His class has exceedingly reasonable standards for time spent outside of class for tests and exams. Lectures are a bit dry though.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just an overall boring class. Not very hard, and not too much homework, but class materials were very uninteresting and the lectures were not very helpful for tests or class assignments, and very unengaging with random examples. But again, study a good amount and the tests aren't bad.

The lectures are dry and hard to focus on, especially once you've zoned out for the nth time. You have to read about 20–30 pages for each class, but the TA sections are pretty helpful. The practice quizzes are only somewhat similar to the actual tests. Overall, the class is still manageable and not as difficult as some others at UW.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Use the office hours and use your TA!! Mine was super helpful, especially because O'Dea's lectures were often not clear. He is very passionate, but the tests were pretty hard. He wasn't very easy to talk to either.

The professor's lectures were a bit all over the place and sometimes didn't relate to the actual exam content. I learned more through the TA quiz sections and would highly recommend attending their office hours for answers to practice exams and for more practice problems.
Grades highly based on curve.

The lectures can be dry and unfocused, but the TA sessions are very helpful for exam prep. Utilizing resources like unstuck ai alongside the textbook and practice exams is key to success in this course.

I'm actually taking his online Econ400 this summer 2024. Honestly, Dennis is the worst professor I've ever met at UW. I can see how professional he is in academics, but he's just too bad as an instructor. His lecture notes are just scratching paper for calculations; he always put wrong deadlines on canvas; he gives wrong data in HW and exams...

My condolences to any future students who have to take this class. Dennis might just take the crown for the worst teacher I've ever had, and it seems I'm not the only one to think so. He teaches by going along the bare minimum so he won't get fired, with lectures full of ramblings and tangents, making sure to hit a few key points here and there.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dennis Odea is not as bad as most people said. His lecture is lowkey useful to understanding the concepts or theory in the topic we learned, though it can be boring. However, to be success in this course, TA is the most useful resource because they will review the past exams as this course is test heavy (80%).

Dennis is not a great teacher. He goes on irrelevant tangents during class, not paying attention to what is actually on the slides he's presenting. He skips through them, scribbling off to the side in his horrible handwriting. The most helpful thing about this class are the quiz sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course lectures are irrelevant from the course materials and the level of support provided by him is insufficient for student success in this course. He even posted keys to the practice exams after we took the exam.
The course lectures are irrelevant from the course materials and the level of support provided by him is insufficient for student success in this course.

O'Dea was a pretty average professor, he is definitely not as bad as most say. 80% of your grade is based on exams so you need to study hard for those. His tests are 100% based on lectures I got a 4.0 and all I did was rewatch the lectures, you do not need to read the textbook. He does give practice exams and when I took the course he gave keys.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Boring class boing homeworks boring lessons. Exams are hard.

Often goes off on these very long seemingly irrelevant tangents during lectures and had a lot of confusing material/annotations on his slides. TA sections were more helpful than lectures. Besides weekly reading quizzes that are nothing like tests, there is no hw and limited resources to practice for exams, making it very difficult to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrendous. Don't take if you can.

Not sure why Prof. O'Dea has these ratings. His lectures can be long but have plenty of real-world examples and are as good as the book. TAs were helpful, reviewing course content and walking us through Macro problems. Worksheet and homework content difficulty is similar to the exams, so pay attention when doing those. Overall, a good professor.

Dennis was a great dude, but didn't teach the class well. Every lecture was spent laughing at him yapping about some random econ thing. Don't take a class with Dennis if you want to enjoy your classes

Probably the worst professor I've ever had. Lectures are horribly unengaging; he rambles the entire time and doesn't even reference his massive lecture slides, he just scribbles off to the side. Provides pretty much zero resources for test prep and is overall an extremely bad professor, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.
should have stayed at his other university
His practice tests are nothing like his exams. He requires to read the textbook, when the content does not match with his exams. WHAT IS GOING ON?

Terrible. Doesn't provide a single resource for you to succeed. Does not release answers to practice worksheets/exams so you don't know if you're even doing anything correctly. Rambles. Lectures are pointless. Quiz section is your only friend if any.

Doesn't seem malicious, however, he's disorganized, flip-flops around the slides during lectures and goes on tangents. The two midterms and the final are the majority of your grade. Not a lot of work involved. The content isn't challenging but doesn't provide many resources for studying - doesn't return tests so can't see what you're doing wrong.

Um not my favorite, lectures can be hard to follow. Final is hard, but midterm is fine. Not a ton of work but I feel like you learn more in the TA sections than lecture. Also doesn't really lecture while following slides. Also doesn't release answers to practice tests.

It feels like O'Dea wants his students to not succeed in the course. Your grade in the course is mainly determined by 2 midterms, both worth 40%. However, attending his lectures (consisting of FRED graphs), and practicing the few midterms that he posts (no answer key released) is not enough to succeed in the course. He never reviews for exams too.

Dennis was very unfocused in his lectures, often rambling about hypothetical topics unrelated to the direct course material. When asked questions after class, he would respond impatiently as though we were a bother to him and try to escape as soon as possible. His overall attitude was very much not conducive to a positive learning environment.

His lectures do not help at all when it comes to the exams. He does not help students out when necessary. He is condescending and undermines his students when they do ask questions. His role is to be a professor so that means he should be open and available to his students whenever they need assistance, and he does a terrible job.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are so pointless and hard to follow. he doesn't prepare you well for exams because what he explains in lecture is not similar to what is on the tests. ive had to teach myself all the content this whole quarter and he doesn't offer much support outside of class. take this class at a CC if possible.
Literally he is no help in the class at all. Rambles about theories instead of actually teaching the content on the midterms.

O'Dea's lectures are pretty fast-paced, but he takes the time to make sure that the content is clear during lectures like answering questions and using relatable examples. I agree that his handwriting is a bit messy, but taking basic notes for lectures can help with that and for review. Be prepared to put in a little extra effort to do well.

O'Dea has pretty fast-paced lectures, but he made sure that people understood the content by answering questions that came up with relatable examples. I agree that his handwriting was difficult to read, but taking basic notes can help a lot when it comes to reviewing. You have to put in quite a bit of effort to do well in this class.

The worst professor I have had at UW. Ineligible handwriting, tough grading, and super dry lectures. Makes you question why you're paying for your education. Avoid. Take with a different prof instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Perhaps because it was online, but everything about this class was a mess. The lectures were extremely dry and disconnected from class content and the TAs were useless. Avoid if possible.

Dr. O'Dea is one of the best professor at uw, idk why so many people are hating on him. He always make class material clear as possible, I could understand everything he talked about during class. However, gradings are kinda strict, and his pace of lecture is extremely fast, if you missed one class, its hard to recover from that. Very heavy test.
No a good professor for me
Never reply to emails, bad handwriting notes, and exam keys. No class slides, seems like everything he is doing is keeping you away from getting higher scores.

No hate, but this man's handwriting is illegible, I literally could never read anything he was writing on the lecture slides NOR the practice exam solutions which sucked. This class is definitely relied on teaching yourself. Probably the worst class I have ever taken and performed in.

Dude, this class is kicking my ASS. I have never been in a harder class and I have not understood one concept. Tests were hard and quiz section made me even more confused. Our whole grade is based off of 2 tests (70% of your grade) and the rest is HW and article responses.

Class was not sufficient to teach the material and they refused to give keys for the practice exams so there wasn't really any way to effectively learn the material. Lectures extremely dry and unhelpful. TA absolutely useless, just read off slides.

Dennis is bombastic; he won't give keys for practice exams, as he says that there are multiple correct answers, but when you argue your perspective on the midterm, he refuses to accept any answer other than his own, even when I legit found economic academic journals that supported what I said. Got an A, but the avg. grade for my class was a fail.

reviews.comment: Went into this class scared because of his low ratings but now genuinely dont understand why hes rated so low. But quiz sections helped the most with preparing for test questions so hope for a good TA
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He'd never finish the content planned for the lecture. And he wouldn't continue from where he left off last time - he'd start from the new chapter, and leave the rest for TAs to cover. Interesting guy, but if you may found his class confusing without a good TA.

Lecture content was presented in a disorganized manner, hard to pay attention and take away info. Your experience depends entirely on your TA as the textbook wasn't great either. I would watch the recordings of other sections because each taught differently info. None of the worksheets related to content on the exams. this was a tough class.

Lectures were pretty useless, I just read the textbook and went to TA sections and I was fine. Way too much unnecessary information in the lectures that don't help. Also doesn't respond to emails very quickly, if at all. Take this teacher if you can learn on your own and are willing to read a lot.
Does not really teach. You need to rely on your TA. TA is the guide to a good grade

Odea is not bad if you are smart about how you study. His lectures are long and unhelpful, but TA sessions and worksheets are very important. The tests look exactly like the worksheets and practice.
