reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dennis's lectures were fine. They weren't super engaging or interesting, but they weren't bad. I always had just enough time on the tests. Overall, it was an average class; not bad, but not amazing either.

Actually really informative, and obviously a huge econ geek. His virtual lecture style is dry and hard to stay engaged. Another thing; his hand writing is so bad that students had to repeatedly ask what he was writing in the lecture notes. But, he definitely helped me learn about macro

I don't really know why Odea has such bad reviews on here. I think he is a really good lecturer, with good world examples that make the concepts easier to understand. The workload is reasonable and it is a pretty straightforward class. The only downside I think is that the grading standards for tests are really hard, but other than that good class!

His lectures are engaging and he uses a lot of real world examples. You definitely need the textbook, but you really only need to skim the chapters and they all have summaries at the end. His tests are also exactly like the past examples so you know what you're getting into. All around solid guy, would absolutely take another class from him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lectures given by O'Dea are not very useful in terms of tests. As long as you read your textbooks and get a good TA you'll probably be fine. But, the tests are very unfair as in you are expected provide things that weren't asked for and some tests require outside knowledge that weren't taught in class. Also, O'Dea does not respond to most emails.

I do not understand these negative reviews. I have O'Dea right now and I love the material we're learning in class. O'Dea makes sure to answer majority of questions in chat and will record lectures. He also provided a decent amount of practice quizzes and exams. Overall very solid professor and deserves a better rating than the overall
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: O'Dea is fine at best. He is probably one of the better Economics teachers at UW. The class itself is just hard in itself, so be prepared to put in a lot of time and effort. The homework is pretty easy, but the quizzes and exams can be difficult if you aren't on top of it. The TA also really matters, as they each have their own grading criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Would not take his class again. He doesn't reply to emails and questioned students when they needed help.

If youre an independent learner, having odea as a professor is not the worst thing in the world. If you read the textbook and go to discussion sections, youll be fine. Lectures are definitely boring and hard to focus especially over zoom. Just make sure to do the homework and the worksheets that your TAs give to you.

Disorganized and unapologetic about it. Wont answer questions over email or Canvas. No office hours. Lectures are fairly useless, all info is in quiz sections so review those slides. Got grades out a week late. No clarity or ability to project grades. All tests and quizzes are similar to worksheets. You will end up teaching yourself. Stay away.

His lectures are not that interesting, and the contents are hardly focused on things that should get emphasized for this class. Showing up on his lectures or not does not make any senses to oneself. His TAs are pretty nice and helpful. Professor is used to procrastinate materials and email-back to students. His attitude truly makes me disappointed.

Graphs and handwriting in lectures are almost unreadable, so I'd rather listen to my TA teaching, I guess that would be much more efficient. Tough grader, No extra credit at all, does not tolerate or drop any of the mistakes in homework. Easy quizzes every two weeks and homework once a week. Explanations are unclear so prepare to teach yourself.

He is the worst professor I've ever taken up to date. The lectures are so dry and bad I stop going after the 2nd week of class. His exams are like the worksheets he gives out but it's more tricky. Like what other people said, the TAs are better at explaining/teaching. Overall, just don't take this guy if you want a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are SO bad & NOT helpful. TAs in quiz section have more coherent lessons than he does. He doesn't post any practice or real quiz/exam solutions so you can't check your work and practice. Assignments are useless busywork. He also doesn't accommodate any personal/technical problems that you may have during this pandemic! He's the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I wish I could give him a good review because he does seem very knowledgeable, but I just can't. His lectures are very dry and he doesn't really go over any example questions. You're better off focusing on the quiz sections because the TAs are more helpful with the actual course content. He seems like a nice guy, just not a good teacher.

Wasted first two weeks of class bc he refused to switch from panopto to zoom (eventhough panopto was glitching). no practice problems in class, talks at u the whole time. seems knowledgeable but not very good at explaining things: during class it seems like he is talking to himself, not teaching

Lectures are the worst I've had (I've taken calc and chem series, this lecture is worse), is dry, very fast over significant formulas, spends most of time on insignificant/ hard to understand graphs. Examsstraightforward, as long as u do the practice worksheets. Did most of learning through TA and textbook. Posts recorded lectures VERY late

I found I did the right thing in choosing him. He actually encourages students to ask any questions during his office hours. Some might say, he often includes unnecessary topics in class. But personally, I think what he provides for us gives us a broad view of what macro would be like and whether it's your type if you choose to major in Econ.

Heavy lectures. He also covered too much things in each lecture. What I dont like most is that we take quizzes quite often. But generally his lectures are easy to understand and relevant to quizzes and homework.

This is my 3rd year of college and by far he is the worst professor Ive ever had. The lectures are rushed and most of the material covered in the lecture is not going to be on a quiz or midterm. You are expected to learn everything from the homework and the textbook and if you have questions its expected to go to CLUE (the on campus tutoring).

reviews.comment: arrogant, stuck up, and unaccomadating . AND the hw is due before we learn topics in class, get ready to teach urself

Taking online because of the pandemic. He is not lenient at all even with a global pandemic affecting many families. Lectures are terrible. He mainly focuses on graphs and when there is text on slides, it is most likely going to be skipped within 15 seconds to further explain another graph. Wouldn't take this professor.

5 midterms. They are exactly like the past midterms and worksheets he posts. Study those and you should get a good grade. Like the quiz sections are more important as the TA goes over the worksheets and past exams.

He has five midterms and no final. I received very low grades for 2 tests without knowing what I have answered wrong. He deducts points without reasons and says things that would not appear in tests during lectures. Tests are exactly the same type of questions with the worksheets. You get one questions wrong, you are away from 4.0. Don't take.

The quintessential example of a person who is given the littlest bit of power and gains a superiority complex. Draconian policies and is rigid for no reason, even throughout a pandemic which directly affected us. Dull. Tests are unnecessarily irrelevant to coursework. I don't understand the other reviews for this quarter. Professor O'dea was really flexible and nice. His lectures are clear + includes all info from the textbook. I will never take his class again. His lecture is not enriched, and clear enough. And he is not flexible. If you guys have substitution, don't hesitate.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This man is literally showing no mercy on his students during this global pandemic. What kind of professor encourages his TAs to assign so much last minute work towards finals? All these comments make him sound like a monster lol. He's literally fine. Explains the concepts pretty well. Just doesn't give out answer keys to practice tests. But if you study and keep up with the minimal work you're chillin.

Lectures are really unclear and dull. No practice problems for concepts taught and the slides are formatted weirdly. Goes really fast through slides, TAs are meh (hopefully you get a good one.) I'm sure Macro is super interesting, but not when he bases it heavily on lectures. Would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is actually pretty interesting, and wouldn't be too hard if his lectures weren't dull and unclear. The textbook is your only hope!
Class focuses on lectures which are boring and monotonous
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: O'Dea is a very good professor. For his "article response" assignments, he gives advice on content to do your report on, and even suggests what chapters are easiest to pull content from. His tests are fairly straightforward, and if you do the practice exams you will most likely pass. Read the textbook, as it makes the lectures much more clear.

posts different slides online than the ones used in lecture if he posts them at all. gives old midterms but no answer keys. uses textbook for background info but different formulas than textbook. purposefully puts trick questions on tests and brags about having a low average/class passing rate. honestly take this class from a TA instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

He zooms past important info that could be on the test and spends way too long on stuff that doesn't matter. Read the book if you want to actually learn anything. reviews.comment: His presentation style leaves a lot to be desired. Hell spend a lot of time on graphs that dont matter and then a few seconds on the actually important slides. Avoid. reviews.comment: I know a lot of people don't like Dennis, but I thought he was solid. He's very well-spoken and he always ties all of the concepts of real-world examples, especially historical ones. reviews.comment: Lecture was always very boring and couldn't focus. All of the material is directly from the book. Tests always felt like too many questions and not enough time. The lectures in this class are so boring and most of it is just graphs. He tends to skip back and forth through slides which makes it hard to take notes. However, the lectures are pretty much the same information as what's in the textbook so if you read and take notes from the textbook there's really no need to pay attention in class.

The lectures are dull to the extent that no one can pay attention for longer than 40 minutes of the hour and a half lecture. His practice tests are so similar to his actual tests that everyone will do well. When you're in a class that is graded on a curve you can get a quality grade and still get screwed. Enjoy the online shopping in class.

Chances are, you will run out of time when answering the last few questions on his test. You will rush and it will hurt your grade. ODea also stands right in front of his lectures, so if you sit in the front, good luck. He also skips through important slides, making it hard to take notes. You gotta study like 50-90 slides each lecture. Avoid.

Econ 201 is basically material you can sort of learn in like 3 days of just intensive studying but somehow O'dea makes it feel like the hardest thing in the world. 2/3 of his lectures are all unnecessary graphs and he skips through the important slides making it impossible to take notes. Review the worksheets and exams to actually learn.

Prof. O'Dea has an incredible gift - he can make even the most interesting concepts mind-numbingly boring. Problem is, you have to show up because he uses clickers (yes, the old-fashioned kind!). reviews.comment: There are lots of mixed feelings about Dennis. He clearly knows his stuff, but the way he lectures sounds kind of boring if you sit anywhere besides the front. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dennis's lectures are relatively boring, and the clicker questions were expensive and frustrating. His worksheets and old exams are virtually the same as exams, so if you study those and do the reading, you should do fine.

reviews.comment: His lectures are extremely boring, it just drags on, hopefully you will have a good TA which is unlikely. Clicker questions are annoying and expensive, but hey he is the better option compared to taking a TA taught lecture

Dennis is a guy who is super tough on grading-he only cares about percentage not the average conditions. He never realized that the average score should be adjusted. Get ready to receive a lower expected gpa when you are taking this course. Super super bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Here's the thing; he's a really nice guy but his lectures are repetitive and dry. But for lectures he provides lots of examples in class and is very knowledgable. Eh.

Lectures are extremely dry, however you have to go to them because he still uses those outdated clickers. Definitely go over the practice tests he provides online because the real test is fairly similar.

Odea is really boring. The class is conceptually simple, but made difficult by never really providing a straight up explanation of a topic. Much of his lectures are extraneous and vague. Spent the majority of my studying trying to figure out what was true in the first place, leaving little time to actually apply the concepts to problems. Just meh.

He makes easy concepts hard because of his confusing lecturing style so be attentive during lecture and try to piece together what he's saying. Sometimes he'll post the powerpoint before lecture so pull that up to see the poll questions ahead of time. Tests are identical to the practice ones given, so study those a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor O'dea offers students a great chance to fall asleep in his course if they did not get enough the night before. Although the lectures are organized, tests are strictly free response and majority of the lectures do not relate to the exams. He throws random things on the exams, but just study how to use graphs and you'll do fine.

Tests were pretty easy (based off lectures), and there is little hw. There is a 10 page paper due at the end of the quarter, but it was actually very manageable and he gives lots of feedback on the rough draft. The material can be hard to grasp but it was a solid class overall. Loved his lectures, and he's always ready to help.

This is by far the worst lecture class I have ever had to sit through. I cannot stress enough how badly I wish I was in another section. reviews.comment: he's tests are pretty hard mainly because he did not provide answers to the practice exam and doesn't do examples in class. There are lots of material covered in class, if you don't go to class, be ready to fail.

Lectures are pretty dry but they are online so you can see them again and take notes after class. lectures are pretty boring, but he really makes concepts easily to be understand.

Go to quiz sections they are often super helpful. Also become friends with people in frats or sororities that have old tests because he uses the same questions every quarter.

I really have mixed feeling about his lecture. On one hand, they are very dry and long, but if you can stay awake and follow his lecture you will do well in the class. He covers everything in his lecture and I barely even read the textbook. He sometimes says some funny stuffs, but he never smiles. The class materials are actually very interesting.

BEST professor I have ever had! His lectures can be long and dry, but they are so full of information and his explanations/examples are incredible. His midterms were easy, final was a little harder, but different TAs prepare you differently. If you care about econ as a subject, you will succeed! reviews.comment: Incredible professor! Long lessons, but the information was valuable and helpful. His examples were relevant and conveyed concepts really well. Lecture slides are insanely redundant, dry, and long. Every once in awhile throws in clicker questions without allowing enough time to discuss answers with others. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dennis did not seem ver personable and his voice just put me right to sleep. I had a hard time paying attention to him- he just doesn't teach with much enthusiasm. reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I think for an intro class like econ201, the lecture hall is so big that it really depends on you to figure out what you dont understand. I literally sat in the front everyday and never stopped taking notes. If you can focus in lecture, I 'd say you are good.

Not the worst, but certainly hold very sleep-inducing lectures. His lectures are the regurgitation of the textbook, which is helpful when you're preparing for exams. One of the worst professors at UW. Incredibly dry and boring lectures and they all count for points in attendance. You can't keep track of his lectures because he moves INCREDIBLY fast. His grading seemed inconsistent most of the times and unclear as to what he wants to see in the answers. I feel strongly this way, b/c he doesn't post answers to the HW nor practice exams. His grading seemed inconsistent most of the times and unclear as to what he wants to see in the answers. I feel strongly this way, b/c he doesn't post answers to the HW nor practice exams. he's actually the worst. He made the class harder cause people were doing well and most of my friends barely passed this quarter since Winter his class has gotten way harder. His TAs are awful and barely speak english. If you go to his office hours he plays video games and pays almost no attention to you.
Most boring professor and his tests are decently rigorous
I dread going to his lectures. They are very long and he goes through his slides very fast. Taking notes is impossible. Lectures are long and boring because of his monotone voice.

This was probably one of the worst lecturers I have ever had! On average he has over 80 slides and goes through all of them in a 80 minute class, hence no notes can be taken since he skips through the slides so quick. He teaches as if everybody knows what he is talking about. He cares very little about student learning and gives us long exams!

Overall, a great professor. Really knows what he's talking about and was pretty clear during lectures. However, get ready to study! The (three!) exams are not easy and will require a lot of work if you want an A or B in the class. If you are an econ major or genuinely interested in economic works, you will do fine. Just get ready to work.

His lectures are very clear and organized however, homeworks and tests are really hard. He gives homewroks ahead of his material and collects them before teaching them, so you have to do them on your own. It means that you have to do a lot of self-studying. Also, you will not even use textbook which costs like 200$. Don't buy them!
You should go to class since there are clicker questions. Exams are not that tough. Textbook is just optional. If you read his lecture slide, you'll be totally fine.

Dennis is very knowledgeable and a fair grader. however i feel his grading scale is extremely unfair. Exams are only worth 62% of your grade so even if you do well on these your grade is constituted by 38% busy work. While this is beneficial to some it hurts those that find their strengths in tests such as myself

O'Dea is like the Economic Father figure that I never asked for. His lectures can be long, but if you stick to reviewing old exams, you're sure to do very well in this class. The TA that you get can also greatly change your experience in his class, I had an excellent TA and our quiz sections average on tests ended up being really high.

I'm pretty surprised to see so many bad gradings here. Odea is a pretty reasonable professor for intro-level economics. Yes his lecture is kinda long and boring, but he gives really easy tests that are so similar to old tests. Just work through the old exam problems and you will be fine. I would take his class again.

Lectures were pretty jumbled and hard to follow. Unless you are on top of your reading or really interested in Econ it was hard to make sense of lectures. Your grade in this class also largely depends on the fate of your TA as they are the ones actually teaching you how to solve problems for tests. Find a friend to study with.

Odea is such a nerd. He's clearly really into Econ but that doesn't mean that anyone else is. The lectures are a snooze fest but if you start studying early you should do pretty well on the tests. Homework is a joke

The homework program was not helpful at all. The exams are also very unclear and I found myself unsure what they wanted. The TAs were very people were saying after the final that one of of TA leaked the final to her section before the date of the final

It's a really hard class if you aren't good at economics to begin with. Homework was multiple choice based, which is completely different from the actual exams. The actual exams require a great understanding of the material and critical thinking. He's okay as a professor but for a 200 level class it's pretty hard.

Dennis is a nice professor but sometimes the material can be dry. I would suggest reading the chapter before class and get ready for clicker questions. The hw is super easy and the article responses are easy too. There's 2 midterms and a final which are really similar to previous ones.
the lecture is unclear
Not informative at all.

I took this class as a freshman, and it was such a mistake. He uses clickers, and there are two midterms and a final. It gives me so much stress that was unnecessary this last quarter. None of the TA's speak english very well, which makes the class even more frustrating. Be prepared for weekly homework and actually reading the textbook.

Taking his class is awful overall, he has lots of homework but helpless for the course and exam. The midterm looks like disgress from the subject and even don't have any multiple choice questions, so if you want to take econ 201 please be better find another professor or take alternative course.

Lectures are good if you know the material. Otherwise, it's hard to stay tuned in. He really knows his stuff and comes off as an upper-division professor. He's pretty stoic and a bit sarcastic, so going to OH can be a bit intimidatingawkward. But his tests are straightforward and hw is helpful though long (it's worth a midterm, so do it w friends)

O'dea was pretty run-of-the-mill. His lectures are kind of boring and can seem to drag on, but his examples are clear and the class was very organized. I didn't like the way he graded online homework. The quizzes were kind of difficult but all in all, the testing was fair. Good class.
Dennis is a great lecturer, his lectures are clear and interesting. All his slides goes online, but you have to go to lectures because he uses clickers.

Dennis teaches Macro strictly through lectures. All he does is talk for 80 minutes. Personally, I love it since he is extremely knowledgable- I learned most of the material through going to lecture. In fact, book reading was not essential if you attended class regularly. He has clickers, so you better go. Explanations are clear. Would recommend.

Very informative and knowledgable about the subject.  His lectures can get a little long and dry, but if you can past that, he is a very good professor.  The midterm and final are very similar to the practice exams he gives.  Overall a great class and great teacher.

Take this class with a different professor if you can. His lectures are so dry that you can only absorb information the first hour. Test averages were fairly high which made it harder to get a good grade. You'll learn more from the book than from him

Dennis is awesome; he is an excellent lecturer and has a strange charm though he is serious all the time. I admit he is not that helpful so make sure you get a nice TA. The past exams are super important because the real midterm and final usually just copy some of the questions in the past exams.

If you look at practice exams, some questions re-appear on the practice while other ones are very similar. If you show up to class and take notes, you don't need to really read the book, however the book better clarifies why an event happens in economics. Good class in general and makes sense if you take the time to understand it.
Mr. O'Dea is awesome.

Tests are much more in depth that criteria taught, Odea is a lecture only teacher and won't respond to anything else. Content and expectations are clear though. Get a good TA, and try and stay awake in his lectures

I ran into him in Red Square and said hi and he had no idea who I was (not like I expected him to) but he was really happy I acknowledged him nonetheless and is super nice in person. Really clear lecturer, too.

O'Dea is a very smart professor, however, his lectures can sometimes be really boring. He passes by very fast, so it is important to pay attention. TA plays the most important role, so make sure to take a good one! I had an awesome TA and got a high grade.
I went to all his lectures and barely ever felt the need to read the textbook. He explains things quite well, but is a little bit boring, so staying awake in his classes can sometimes be a huge feat.

If you go to class and take good notes you don't really have to do the readings except for supplemental use and additional explanations. As for him, he is useless outside of class and doesn't make an effort to assist you or bother to answer any emails so what you get from class all he has to offer.

He is a cute guy actually. Super easy 4.0; I didn't go to lecture 4 times and miss 4 clickers. Do the homework and a little bit review before the exam and you are good to go. Much easier compared to physics course and CSE.

Class was definitely doable; it was not difficult. However, lack of clarity was an issue; economics needs to be extremely clear for it to work! Sometimes his tests are not clear and quite vague. Tests also have many typos, so beware! Make sure you get a competent TA since he/she grades it and I ran into some disagreements with the grading.

Professor O'dea really knows his economics. His lectures are incredibly clear and informative. He never smiles, but is still a pretty nice guy and very helpful in his office hours. A tough class, but very doable. I recommend using the CLUE economics tutoring to do the homework to make sure that you don't drop any of the easier points.
Boring and unhelpful teacher. He will never smile during the course of your class (just a warning). I had an awful TA, just make sure you get an english speaking one.
Easy class with very clear instructions.
Buy the textbook and the online homework access will come with it. Must go to class to get clicker grades. Fairly easy homeworks and tests. Recommended.
Im currently taking his ECON 201 and i simply love him. Very smart and knows what hes teaching. Easy A class. Take his class if possible!
easy hw (you get 3 tries, 11% of your grade), easy article response (9% of your grade),clickers(5%),3 exams(25% each) overall good class.
Lectures very straight forward and so thus the exams. If you study, you will get somewhat guarnteed good grdes.
O'dea was pretty rude, ignored my emails, and had boring lectures. Tests were ok. All in all, the class is definitely doable, but i didnt like the structure, the graded clickers, or O'dea.

Doesn't require you to get the latest edition textbook, so don't listen to the course website! Wait for the 1st week of class first. Though the HW (not mandatory) is from the latest book, there are equivilants in the older editions. Good professor, love how he can crack a joke but have no change in facial expressions.
MEMORIZE THE OLD TESTS. O'Dea tends to ask really specific questions about a few concepts, and his tests never cover all of the material. Go to class, read the textbook, and pray. Hard class.

Only went to class 10 times. Had a friend click in for me. Got a 3.0 on two midterms without studying, and got a horrible grade on a third one. Came out with a 2.6. Go to class. Read the book everyday and study for at least 15 hours per midterm. Know ALL of the concepts by heart otherwise you're screwed.

Professor O'Dea does not seem to like to use the internet/email considering he is a fairly young professor. This means that emails from him and updates on the website may be few and unclear. That being said, I felt his lectures were much harder than his test, so I would suggest you attend lecture just to know what's going on in terms of homework.

Initially, he seems cold b/c he doesn't smile, but if you go to office hrs. he's very helpful. Very clear & if you read the book/do the practice exams it's fairly easy to get a good grade. Attendance is mandatory for clickers. He also says funny things like, "if you pay taxes in Greece you're a sucker," & "you can't eat money..."

Very clear lectures but really fast paced. Struggled with HW on aplia because you only get one chance to submit and it's hard to get 100% read the books, did HW, all practice problems behind each chapter. Scored around the low 90s in the first 2 exams not sure of finals but ended with a 3.9. Way way better than expected! Recommend!

He's not very approachable and is quite snooty. But other than that he is a good lecturer with concise explanations but he's super fast paced. His powerpoints are annoying because he doesn't know how to use his clicker. Really understand the concepts to do well on the exams because they are really difficult if you don't.

1. never smiles 2. poorly written tests full of spelling errors and mistakes 3. very clear in his lectures, follows the book very closely and is very fast paced. 4. 25% exams, 15% hw, 5% attendance, 5% article responses make up your grade.

Straightforward guy, knows what he's talking about. The pace is very fast, so I suggest you read the textbook prior the lecture. He's very helpful on his office hours. Exams are moderately easy as long as you read and understand the concepts written in the textbook. Do the HW to do well. And, oh! He's pretty good looking.

overall, his class is not bad at all. Very concise and straightforward. Attendance are mandatory for clicker points. Go to his office hours, read the textbook and lecture slides, and you should be fine.

Very interesting class, enjoyed the topics and lectures were very straightforward, albeit very fast paced. He flips through slides really quickly and it can be annoying if you're a slow writer/typer. Read the book, do the online Aplia assignments, go to class, and attend your quiz section, and this class will be a piece of cake. Good luck!

I took the lecture and the lab section of FSH 200 and really loved it. The lectures are packed with information that's necessary for the midterm/final, but the slides are text heavy if you can't make it to lecture. There are attendance points that help boost your grade. Lab section is really interesting if you have the credit space.

Julian is a good (hot) professor and the material in the class is interesting. I took the 3 credit lecture no lab section and It is a lot of work for it being a 3 credit class. Weekly summary sheets are long and midterms are long and graded harshly. Labs definitely give you extra points but not worth it. Grade was much lower than expected

Good professor and very enthusiastic about the content. Was very particular about certain things and the weekly summary sheets seemed like a lot of work for the payoff of them. Tests were long, very handwritten and long. Interesting class though

great professor! took the 5 credit (lecture & lab) was very passionate about lectures, and what he was teaching. included his own stories in lectures, and made it really fun. took this class for my bio credit, and would take again! midterm and final were doable, no outside reading, but weekly quizzes and summary sheets!

Tough grader, lots of trick questions, and not very forgiving if you miss class. Class structure changes each year he teaches the class. Lectures this time were almost exclusively verbal, so digital course materials weren't very useful. If you get on his bad side, you'll know. Interesting course otherwise.

This class was super unstructured and very confusing. Lectures were all posted online afterwards and were totally read off of during the class so there was no real need to go. Tests are on the most small and random facts, so hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: For FISH 423 (Invasive Species Ecology) i thought he did a very good job. content is straightforward and intuitive if you know anything about invasive species. He is tough on tests because they require a lot of writing but just for "short" answers. Requires to remember a great deal of examples on tests
This class was really simple and interesting. A little scattered but you get to learn about a wide variety of information. Olden's lectures where very enthusiastic and entertaining.

Really nice guy, his lectures were more engaging than Schindler. Class would have been better if it was a lot more narrow and just taught by him, like just on invasive species. As it were FISH101 was hard, boring, broad, and disappointing.

It's way too much for the 100 level class. If you're looking for an elective class, do not take this because it's not worth it! The professor is way too hard and he expects from the students too much. Although the class doesn't require a textbook, which is nice, I still think the materials on the class's website is too much for you to handle. >"<

He does not care if you learn or not- he refuses to listen to student feedback, the class is horribly disorganized, even the TAs are often confused as to what is required. I did well in this class, but it was not easy or clear, and he was not helpful. At all. Ever. Be prepared for more work than a 100-level class should ever have.
Great professor!

This class was nothing like I expected, Grading was rough, lots of coding homework & 3 quizzes (it says 5 questions each but it's actually like 20 sections). He also had a thick accent and moved too fast for me to retain anything. I need to take 371 next but I think he's the only professor..
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Ott obviously knows the material but gives incomplete explanations or trails off his sentences. Two quizzes, four large homework assignments, and four labs that are too big to be completed in class. He just doesn't require some of the questions.

There are three textbooks for the class, all of which he provides for free. Two of them he wrote.

It is a very strange class. The professor tried hard to teach, but he had a strong accent. The first midterm exam was incredibly difficult. The second midterm exam was a direct copy of the practice exam, which was baffling. The weekly assignments consisted of at least dozens of problems, which were very time-consuming. He could organized it better.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He made the course material easy to follow and understand. The lectures were very helpful, and the homework was never too difficult. The provided textbook was great too. He always gave us time in class to work on homework and was available for questions.
Good teacher. Class is well structured with an easy to follow textbook. Quizzes can be challenging, but aren't too hard if you prepare using the textbook.
Weird class. Boring lectures, you won't learn anything and he'll take quizzes harder than cse 12X series. Honestly, the TA William Wang was the main problem but a really bad experience.
He's great at teaching.

Ott is a great professor and always answers questions quickly. However, the lectures are a bit boring. The lab and homework were reasonable. I heard that this class would be easy, but thanks to the lead TA, William Wang, we now have two tests worth a lot. The first one was incredibly difficult, and there isn't a curve for the second test.

Ott is a good professor and gives relatively good lectures, but the course organization is wack. There's a good bit of homework each week, and the assignments are extremely long and often contain confusing/conflicting information. When asking the TAs, it feels like they don't even know. I coded more for this class than for my CSE123 class.

A professor actually resorted to such a despicable trick—inserting invisible hints into assignments to confuse the AI. I have no idea what his intentions were. This kind of thing should be discussed openly, not done through such underhanded tactics.

He speaks with a heavy accent, making him difficult to understand most of the time. There's always a lot of homework. The course organization also has some issues; he introduced exams for the first time, and the exams were incredibly difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ott is a great lecturer and genuinely kind. But if your TA is William Wang, run. He swapped the project-based format for two big “quizzes” and forced hand-written code (in 2025!), spiking workload and penalizing tiny syntax slips. Content fine; delivery not. Avoid that TA or another section.
This guy is fricking awesome. Very easy to follow lectures and, through discord, super accessible and always available to help with questions. I love this guy!
Genuinely awful class, he didn't explain concepts clearly and he outright skipped going over Git and the TAs did not help students at all.

Great class for new or experienced programmers. The problem sets are a little tedious, so try not to procrastinate them. Consider doing the extra credit for the earlier assignments while the class is easier compared to later ones. I really enjoyed this class and found Ott as a great professor.

5 stars for Ott!!! Took this course for analytics requirement for Real Estate - LOVED it. Great format, finals week was nice. There's weekly problem sets, labs where you work in a team, and then the final is a group project. Ott is FUN and I learned a lot.

It's a pretty easy, chill class. Sometimes lectures can feel a little slow, but Ott really wants to make sure every student understands what's going on. There's only one Problem Set a week, and several labs are optional. He's also very accessible on Discord for questions.

I loved Ott! The lectures can be boring but he is always willing to help during his office hours and through Discord. Weekly assignments that takes up a few hours to complete if you're new to coding but it's doable and the amount of work is fair.  There's group work for the final project but it's easy if you have a good group.

I didn't have any coding experience before entering this class and feel like I gained a lot through taking INFO 201. Ott has a playful sense of humor and makes the long lectures enjoyable. This is a solid intro class.

The class was interesting and I did learn a lot about R and data analysis. But when I had a lab question Ott was extremely unhelpful in office hours and made me feel like I wasn't intelligent for not understanding the problem. I only figured it out when another classmate came in and we worked together instead. Didn't try office hours after that.

professor ott is a good professor - he and his ta's are easily accessible on campus and online. the only thing is there is a lot of work that he assigns (both problem sets + lab sets) which feels really overwhelming.. it just feels extremely fast-paced and of course its different for everyone but for me, it is a very difficult intro class imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ott is great! Although a 2-hour lecture isn't really justifiable, I really enjoy his structure and material. There is about 3 reading quiz (online), 6 programming assignments and couple of lab assignments and group project. Ott try his best to answer any question 24/7 on discord. Overall, I really enjoy this class and learning R!
Very easy
Professor Toomet is so nice love him definitely would take his class again.

Pretty easy class whether you have prior coding experience or not. Starts super slow, but does start ramping up a bit (content is still very accessible and self-learnable though). 
Textbook and assignments are sometimes a little unclear, but grading is quite lenient. There are no real tests; you'll just have a few problem sets and a final project.

For those with no coding xp, this class is not easy. W the class being redone, Ott had to rewrite all of the assignments, so there were sometimes unclear instructions. Assignments are long, but Ott and his TAs are very accessible outside of class via the Discord at almost every time of the day, even late at night. Hard class, but helpful professor.

Such a nice and caring professor and his team of TA is just as good! its extremely nice that he is accessible outside through discord and is active to help students with code issues. I would def take a class with him again. The HW is once a week due, but can be time consuming, but if u can plan it out youll be fine

Course is being re-done, sadly assignments had confusing, ambiguous questions. Assignments take time to complete but are interesting. Ott welcomes feedback, helps students on Discord with questions constantly. Easy class (with 6 years coding experience), but can be time-consuming. Thankfully, TAs don't grade on code efficiency.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: INFO 371 is more difficult than 370, and has more complex homework. However, Ott does a great job of explaining concepts and is very accessible in office hours. This class allows group work on some projects, which is helpful for the last problem sets. Take this class with Ott!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ott was great at demonstrating concepts in his lecture demos and was pretty funny at times. Problem sets were challenging but he is always on the discord answering student questions along with the TAs. Class got me interested in data and data programming, I would recommend!

Prof. Ott is awesome, and I definitely recommend him for the 370-371 INFO series. His lectures are very informative, and he only gives one small quiz a quarter. Your grade comes from 7-8 assignments, and they are directly related to the lectures. As long as you pay attention in class you'll get an easy A. One of my favorite professors in iSchool.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The best professor I've ever had within my 3 years of college (I am a junior).

Ott is amazing and gives fast and helpful feedback outside class. His lecture is organized and goes in a slow pace. He explains things carefully. Homework load is ok and not hard. Homeworks comes with instructions and it is a good way to learn. Textbooks and other resources are all free.

Ott was super nice and enthusiastic. The labs were chill and directly applied to what was taught in class. Group projects were similar to labs and very manageable. Ott and the TAs provided tons of office hours and help through Discord. I'm not familiar with coding (or really anything tech-related) but had plenty of resources to succeed!
Class was super easy but Ott was still enthusiastic about it. pretty easy projects and he was more than happy to help with them through discord.
You can feel that he cares about students are really learning, not just grading stuff. I will totally take his class!

I took the info 180 class (not info 201). His lectures were incredibly dry. He repeats too much and his pacing is ridiculous. You can tell he cares about his students, but those 2 hours felt like an eternity. His assignments are very easy though. Group work, bi-weekly labs, and 2 tests (no midterms or finals). Easy class, but mind-numbing lectures.

Ott is a great professor. He was willing to change due dates if a lot of the class was falling behind, and was quick to respond to students on Teams. Just ask if you need anything, and he'll help if he can. He was also funny in lectures, so they weren't boring. He does have a bit of an accent, but I was able to understand him just fine.
Can we please improve Ott's rating? His classes are honestly my favorite at UW. Compassionate, patient, and intelligent!

Awesome professor for INFO 370/371. Easily approachable and very amiable! Ott's lecture notes and textbook offer rich contexts to complete assignments and replies questions in a timely manner. He genuinely cares for his students and wants them to get the most out of his courses!

Amazing professor for INFO 370/371. Very knowledgeable and approachable. Ott really cares about his students and he genuinely wants us to learn. His lecture notes/python notes are super helpful, and he is also extremely supportive during office hours or outside of class as he would always provide thorough explanations to students’ questions.

Ott is one of the nicest proffesors you will ever meet. Really cares that students do well in his course and is always incredible helpful in office hours. His lectures are slow, but it's perfect for difficult, programming oriented courses like the data science series.

Ott is an amazing professor who truly cares about his student. He goes pretty slow on the lectures so you can understand the content well. You oftentimes can find him answering students' questions on Teams at 10pm. The rate my professor score does not reflect his course at all, in a way, students might be biased against his accent.

Ott genuinely wants you to pass his class. He joined the discord server to answer all our questions even during the middle of the night. Not just give you the answer, but will make sure you are understanding the concepts. Homework can be a little challenging but doable if you watch lectures since he does similar problems during lecture. Helpful OH.

Took this class with no coding background and 4.0'd. Ott did a great job answering questions and being thorough with lots of examples since TAs were not helpful. I went to the lectures but no quiz section. HW was challenging but doable if you took the time to understand the lecture. The final project was hard but the grading was lenient.

Professor Toomet is one of those professors who genuinely wants his students to learn and succeed. Joined us all on Discord and would regularly answer questions anybody had (even students who had the other prof). Ive literally messaged this guy in the middle of the night and she still answered and helped me on my homework :).

I have never had a professor as caring as Ott. He has many times been up til 11PM helping any student that needs help, so if you're stuck, you know you can just message him and he will quickly reply. He won't just give you answers, but walk you through the kind of thinking you need to do in order to understand the concepts. Great lecture style too!

Amazing professor for INFO 370. People say his lectures are a bit slow, but his pacing is perfect when covering difficult material. He gives very clear explanations and is incredibly helpful in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Students asked many basic questions, but Ott patiently and thoroughly answered all of them. He was also very accommodating and extended deadlines and provided extra credit. Ott really cares about the success of his students. I learned a ton in his class. I went from knowing nothing about R to being quite proficient.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Seems like a lot of people here didn't do well in INFO201 and thus a 1/5 doxx. Ott does NOT deserve this low of a score. His lecture style is exactly how I learn best, and he is one of the sweetest profs I've ever had. Took 370 last quarter and am taking 371 with him right now. Even if I feel too tired to attend class I go for him!

It's the ambiguity in his assignments that takes off points, nothing with difficulty. One example is a R assignment where we examined a simple linear regression for 5 variables, one at a time. Then it asked for a multi-linear-regression using "all variables". This isn't the 5 used previously at once but all variables in the dataset. Happens often.

Ott is an amazing professor and extremely knowledgeable in the realm of data science. His lectures can be dry sometimes hence many don't get to learn a lot, but he is extremely helpful during office hours. Ott will make sure you have understood the concept completely and help you with your homework. Overall, okayish professor, amazing resource

Ott has quite a few bad reviews and while I personally had an okay time in his class I do understand where the complaints are coming from. That said I don't believe he deserves as low of a score as he has on here and is actually quite helpful in providing help to students that ask for it. Overall a tough but fair teacher.

People don't like Ott because of his accent and sometimes dry lectures, but if there is a teacher at this university that cares about your learning more than the grade, it's Ott. He repeatedly will give opportunities to raise grades as long as you put in effort to learn the content. On top of that, he's always available and loves to help.

He regularly allows students to ask questions and clarify their doubts, often repeating himself numerous times. There are also always many TAs ready to help! Most people just don't show up for lecture and that's why they are confused!
The course content is all inside the book. Just forget about going to lecture and ask everything on Slack & read the FREE online textbook which is really detailed and you should do fine.

Ott is nice, but his lectures can be pretty boring sometimes. They are basically demo sessions of the knowledge in the course book. Mostly projects, you can do well by reading the book and using Google. I do recommend going to his office hours, he can give you a more concise answer than in lecture, and he teaches you some useful tricks also.
His lecture is poor structured, it's very hard to follow. The homework specification is poor worded, sometimes i don't even know what i should do. He is good guy but not a great instructor.

This class is supposed to be easy, except if you take it with Ott. Nice guy but if you cant take it with Ross or Freeman dont take it at all. This class was harder for me than CSE142 just because of the way it was taught. I was miserable all quarter and got a grade way lower than I wouldve gotten anyway. If you are reading this run, run far away

I have never been more confused in a class. The material should be easy and do able but you are not taught anything and have to spend the entire class Googling how to do everything. Take this class with somebody else unless you want to make your life way harder than it needs to be.
Too heavy on statistics. Professor assumes students to know all the concepts. Not for all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Ott wants you to know how things work as he tells you how to do things from a terminal (whereas many people just tap on a button). He does not cover all the slides and his examples are somehow different, so you'd better take notes of both. And please, install Linux for his class (at least in a VM), because his demo doesn't always work on Windows.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Nice teacher but hard course
this class is horrible dont take it if u dont have to. worse than any cs coding class ive even taken at UW. Ott is just not a good prof. hard to understand and follow in the lecture
NO SPECIFIC GUIDELINE FOR HOMEWORK
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The homework takes a really long time. The lectures are somewhat related to the homework, but not quite, which sucks because the majority of your grade is from the homework. You have to see help and do a lot of Googling to get the homework done. The online textbooks kinda help, but you really on your own.

Lots of HW but it's due one every week. Lecture heavy. Online textbook THAT'S FREE. Miss a lecture and you'll get lost if you're new to programming anything. Kind and wants to help but you have to seek it yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Learned very little in class. She set expectations that weren't communicated, and most assignments that I missed points on were because directions were unclear. Ton of reading and pointless assignments. Also didn't put many grades into canvas, so I'm unsure how I really did in the class. Nice person and good with data, but don't recommend the class

If you take archaeological theory with her then you're basically teaching yourself, there's so many readings that it's impossible to keep up. She doesn't lecture at all herself so I do mean it that you are on your own, bizarrely despite not lecturing you're still required to attend class.
Don't take her class, no joke, you will not happy with your grade. If you care about your GPA, avoid her FR.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: VERY tough grader, and TONS of readings (like we're talking 3 long articles every two days). Lectures are nonexistent, notes don't help, and if you get a few points off the few assignments, say goodbye to a 4.0 (98%+). She's a great person and fun as a professor, so I'm taking another class of hers, but I got points off for using "too many quotes."
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most disappointing class so far. Despite the summary, class isn't a "2 hour lecture". It is teaching yourself then having group projects about it every class. Yes, EVERY CLASS. She did not actually teach anything she was just a guide on how to do the group work basically. I was excited to learn about Archy of Americas, but ended up learning nothing

2-hour lectures, but does not teach AT ALL. Up to 90 pgs mandatory reading every other day. Midterm/final are creative projects (but no directions/rubric and graded harshly). 98% or higher for a 4.0, and if you miss more than 5 total points on the midterm and final, you can't get an A. No excused absences at all... Learned nothing and lost my 4.0
Passionate about his subject and willing to listen to student feedback. Heavy emphasis on research and what he says in lectures (which are recorded)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I think Dr. Parrish is a great professor that truly cares about his students. He is super passionate in the subjects he teaches and you can tell he wants the students to understand. The class was graded mostly on weekly quizzes and there was not a lot of assignments. Overall a great class!

Prof. Parrish isn't the best or worst professor. He explains concepts well but I think he expects you to get everything right off the bat. He tries to grade thoroughly so that students get as many points as possible but he has high expectations. Don't expect it to be an easy A, but just investing the time to review material makes the difference.

Prof. Parrish was alright as a teacher. He explains concepts well, but I think he expects students to be on the same page of thinking as him, even if the content hasn't resonated. The first exam was rough but he realized that he made it too difficult after seeing the grades, so he does make an effort to adjust after hearing feedback.
Dr. Parrish is overall a good professor, good at teaching, and treats students kindly. The first midterm was super hard but he made some changes to the other two exams and also to the grading scale.
Genuinely cares about his students. One of the best profs at UW by far

This was supposed to be an easy class, but the way he taught the topics were not organized and unclear. He gave key concepts to study for exams but they're hard. He is very nice and knowledgeable about Cell Biology for sure, but I felt like because he's teaching a graduate class, he did not put more effort into teaching this class as I had hoped.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is actually an easy class, but he makes everything disorganized! He seems to be so preoccupied with research that he don't commit 100% to this course. Study guides and practices are always posted late; Grading criteria is not clear; Split one lecture content into two sessions; Overall, good contents, but a really disappointing teaching style!

Good Prof. that cares about you learning the right topics in molecular biology. We read only 1 paper a week that is about 2-3 pages long, and we present on a single figure in the paper for mainly participation. The exams are based solely on recorded lectures (4 tests), you don't need to even attend lecture, just quiz section.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I sent emails with no response and there were 4 exams that are EXTREMELY HARD. The lecture material is not well-organized. We have pre-lecture videos for 40+ minutes and lecture material and paper need to read each week with one GRADED presentation. AVOID AVOID AVOID taking this class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: his lectures are all over the place and useless, he does not care about how his students are doing in this class and even when you reach out. He expects you to watch a 30min long video before EVERY class, somebody please remind him that it's a 3 credit class.

The most interactive BIOL 400 level class taken. Class is set up where you conduct and present your lab projects. Parrish is a great instructor and he doesn't believe in busy work unless you count the lab projects which do require time and care. Participation is a must, and be prepared to come in on your own time to get projects done.

This is not a difficult class if you do the readings and at minimum attend lecture when in-class work is scheduled. Tests aren't made to be difficult or tricky; you'll do fine if you read the assigned texts+articles and make sure you understand lecture topics (look up the concepts he covers in lecture that aren't in the readings).

I enjoyed this class and recommend it to those that are interested in genetics, developmental biology, or neuroscience. Jay is an extremely intelligent professor and he recognizes students who show interest in the course work. The class is not easy but as long as you put in the time and ask questions when clarification is needed you can succeed.

Jay is a very good teacher for upper division classes. If you are interested in the field he is awesome; he really helps you to learn and discover on your own. Unfortunately, he has very little time for people who don't care much about the subject and want things spoon fed to them. He teaches a difficult class that is worth it if you like biology.

WOW. Hands down the WORST teacher I have EVER had. He will drown you in busywork and reading that barely even correlates with lecture (which he POORLY teaches anyways). Mind you, this isn't the only class we take so there is no reason to keep us THAT busy.

Hands down the worst teacher ever. He wants you to read 20 pages of the thick textbook per-class, before lecture. He tests into details. 1 in class paper write, 1 reading quiz, one discussion quiz on top of exams. Two paper due. Someone please tell him it's a 3 credit class. He knows his stuff...but can't teach. DO NOT TAKE!

Jay is a new teacher and it shows. He puts up his power points late and they're slightly useless in terms of content. You REALLY need to take good in-class notes because none of the key info is written on the slides. And when he talks he doesn't make a conclusion, he talks up a subject then just kind of stops. Probably take biol 354 from some1 else

Easily the best physics class I have taken. Intensely good at lecturing and obviously enraptured by the material as much as, if not more than, we were. Students would ask questions and launch her into tangents that would take more of the lecture than I would have liked; leading to leaner lectures later on.

I took this class in Autumn because of Professor Heron's strong reviews, and I agree with them. She's a great lecturer who clearly cares about the material and her students. However, keeping up sometimes required staying ahead of the lectures and content, which can be time-consuming and occasionally made the learning feel a bit disjointed.

Took the entire 14x series with her. I only know to appreciate what I had now, because she made a difficult weedout intro science course really accessible without compromising the complex ideas behind it, and she's a very kind and funny person. The exams are difficult but doable. Not an absurd amount of homework which is nice.
Great in-class experiments!

I quite liked taking the honors sequence with Prof Heron. She's kind, and explains things well. Honestly, I didn't think of the class as especially difficult. Her office hours are great - she put up with a lot of physics tangents and answered complicated questions in a way accessible to first year physics undergrads.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Deeply cares about physics and her students. The class is tough, but her lectures make it easier and explains content thoroughly. Office hours are very helpful and she is very accessible to meet with students. Very knowledgeable as well.

Took whole 14x with her. She's really nice and cares about helping you understand. Good office hours. Interactive class w/ many clicker questions (very fun!), lecture explanations are clear, generally fair tests though that's up to the dept as much as it's up to her. Overall good experience. :)
Couldn't ask for a better intro physics professor

Professor Heron is clearly competent and caring, and does an excellent job making difficult physics concepts more approachable. It is, however, impossible for me to give her a positive review when she is hindered so drastically by the abysmal course structure, logistics, and grading policies.
She is very smart and respectable. The class is hard but it's physics so what would you expect. Answers questions very well and provides good resources.

I think Paula was great, if I was to take this class again I would definitely do more reading and take better notes in class, and if I stuck to it I would do well. Also make sure to use her given equation sheet instead of making your own, as I felt it had a lot more stuff written down that I wouldn't have written for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Heron is a great professor and lecturer! I really loved her demos and her clicker questions helped me a lot in understanding the content. She's also really nice and cares about her students :)

Lectures were moderately large, but it was still possible to ask questions. The lectures had demonstrations and were relatively engaging. Class coordination between the lectures, quiz sections, and labs was lacking, and keeping track of the different assignments was needlessly complicated. Still, I blame the department, not Prof. Heron.

This is the second class I've taken with Paula and I genuinely appreciate her teaching style. Her handwritten notes are the reason she tends to fall behind on material but it helps me learn better personally. She's also just a really kind professor. I took this class during the COVID crisis and she was really forgiving with grading and expectations

Personally, I really liked how organized, professional, and thorough Professor Herons teaching style was. She always did her best to address questions thoughtfully. The textbook is definitely a necessity in PHYS 121, and her lectures can be a bit dry, but her snarky comments and good humor is appreciated. Id take her class again in a heartbeat!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A good professor who made an effort to clearly explain the course material to the students who had questions in class. We fell behind on some of the course material in the lectures so she cut that part out of the final. Definitely one of the better professors in the physics department, but still a lot of work from the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Paula is a great lecture. She writes and draws on an iPad which I thought worked very well. She posts her slides later as well. Poll questions were also helpful and exams often had similar questions to these. Homework sets were less helpful, however. Overall, Paula Heron very professional, organized, and prepared thermal physics professor.

Paula was a good professor, and I like that her notes were handwritten. She was prepared to answer class questions well. Only issue with her class is we never really went through all the material in class because she'd get behind in her notes. She's better than many other Physics professors as I hear.

She's alright but really overrated. No recordings or ppt for students after class to review whether they missed any notes in class( she's too fast and handwriting is too vague most of the time). The exam is completely different from what she offered as practices. To be honest, she is arrogant sometimes and some people may find it funny, Idk.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honors 12x physics series, very lecture heavy, textbook readings are helpful but not strictly required. Lots of assignments to keep track of between sections. Good lecturer, doesn't just read off slides. Encourages questions but can get sidetracked by unnecessarily deep theoretical questions. Good demonstrations to show physics principles.
The lectures were sub-par compared to other physics professors. Not a whole lot of structure compared to what I had in 121 and 122.

she refuse to use lecture recording reason is students won't come if that's available. Refuse to use powerpoint so all she did it's writing notes. it's really hard for student who prefer review instead of preview. in midterm, there's a huge mistake on question, she didn't mention, draw all students crazy then she said we should let her know...

She is so nice that she answers every question you asked carefully. Definitely one of the best and responsible professor I met in UW. Her lectures are great which explains concepts and formulas carefully with strong logic. If you understand the material well, you can pass the exams.
I like how she writes out her notes. She does a good job of answering everyone's questions, no matter how bizarre or high-key pretentious they are

Absolutely love Prof. Heron! Her lectures are easy to follow and she is welcome to questions. I love how she writes the notes as she lectures instead of using slides.  She really cares about whether or not you understand the material. Unfortunately, when I was in honors 122 we fell quite behind in the material. 10/10 would recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She teaches like a veteran when it comes to the simple things that seems to eat up time for other professors like clicker questions and grabbing the class' attention.  She can be helpful outside of class but generally stick to office hours for consistent help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The worst teacher I have ever seen. The course was a waste of time. Never take courses with Paula, especially if you are a Physics major.

She's very good at covering the topics of entropy and enthalpy and explains things numerous times in various ways. There are clicker questions so she knows how the class as a whole is understanding and she focuses on the parts that seem to get people in the class a little baffled.

you can learn all the content of the class from the prelectures on smartphysics; don't even need to go to lecture. she just goes over the same ideas in class and works a few examples and demonstrations, so it's not even necessary to go to lecture except for clicker points.
She's really really smart, you can tell that just from talking to her but sometimes that can interfere with her trying to teach 122. Overall, good quality, there are definitely worse out there.

Clear speaker, well organized and presented lectures. Understands the material superbly, and walks students through the reasoning of more complicated ideas and (especially!) applications. One of the best lecturers at UW.

Great teacher, explains things very well both in class and during office hours, prepares you as well as she can for the tests, answers emails. Wish I could have had her for 121 and 123. Definitely take her if you can, whether its in the 12x series or 224 class.
She makes it easy, asking lots of questions during class and lots of discussion. Had her for 4 consecutive quarters for various classes, and she was very good.
Great lecturer thats open to questions and uses good demonstrations to reinforce the material. Hardness of exams and lack of good practice exams makes this class difficult.

Excellent professor and lecturer. Effective integration of demos, class discussion, and clicker questions to facilitate learning. Great at both lecturing and explaining to students, and uses student participation to enhance learning. However, tests are hard, with few useful resources available. Tests do  not correlate well to HW and in-class stuff.

She is a good teacher, clear in her explanations and cares that her students do well in the class, I suggest not taking this if you didn't take AP Physics before. The homework isn't too bad and reading helps but the teacher lectures well enough that you don't necessarily HAVE to read. Note: This review is about the honors section of PHYS 121

She is a good teacher, very clear in her explanations and definitely cares that her students do well in the class, I suggest not taking this if you didn't take AP Physics before. The homework isn't too bad and reading helps but the teacher lectures well enough that you don't necessarily HAVE to read. Note: This review is about the honors section

Very average. Not the greatest professor, but not bad. requires some coffee to get through a lecture, but provided you're awake and paying attention, explains material well. Writes pretty good tests, and makes a lot more sense than the textbook.
Highly recommended. She does a great job explaining concepts in class. Her clicker questions are what you can expect for the multiple choice on midterms. Easy to contact when you need help.
No Comments
A nice friendly Canadian

Perkins's lectures aren't great--he always goes on tangents and gets distracted, which limits how much content he gets through and makes stuff difficult to follow. His tests are really easy, and he's pretty fly for an old guy and imparts nuggets of knowledge from time to time, but I don't think he's suited for a large lecture hall.

Perkins is a really funny and approachable professor. However, his lectures, especially near the end of the quarter, felt less and less helpful for undertsanding the material. You're definetly gunna be relying on other resources if you want a good grade. On the bright side though, he writes really fair exams.
Very funny and engaging professor who made lecture really interesting. Was also easy to reach outside of class and regularly responded to discussion board.

His lectures are very hard to follow and he takes confusing handwritten notes. He barely explains the concepts but expects you to know them pretty well on exams. He does allow a note sheet and calculator for exams though. If you have to take him don't waste your time in lecture and just watch Thomas Carr and go to the math lab for hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Barely takes any notes and when he does, it is in the worst handwriting. Goes on tangents about random things that aren't related to class and skips over content. You will need outside videos to keep up.
His lectures were easy to listen to, he would put jokes in to keep us awake. It was good to read the textbook before, he would mostly go over practice problems.
Old school professor. Barely has notes for the class and the notes he shares are handwritten and barely legible. Better off learning through youtube and not showing up to class.
Has very fun stories to tell which can make him go off track sometimes but overall very entertaining. Doesnt record lectures but his exams are fair.
really funny guy

He's genuinely the best prof I've had. Lectures are actually hilarious and keeps me awake. He also clarifies any questions you have and you can always come to office hours with questions. I've def make sure to keep ahead of the webassign work though because they can add up, but otherwise great guy

Lectures not structured and handwriting difficult to read, more so goes with the flow...but tests are easier and he is funny (lol). Available outside of class. I would sit in on another professor, but come to his office hours for clarification and come for exams. Also, extensions not readily granted like other professors.

He talks more about himself and his experiences than he actually teaches in the lectures. The concepts also feel unnecessarily complicated when he explains them and I had to rely on youtube videos to learn. The midterms he made were significantly easier with super high averages than the final which is cumulatively made by all the profs.
Super smart guy who can teach math efficiently and crack jokes at the same time. As a matter of fact, I signed up for rate my professor just to give him a 5. Take his class you won't regret it.
best math prof ever!

He is one of the best professors I have had at uw. I took 208,407,408 with him, he was always hilarious and answered your questions patiently. I saw previous comments on his “messy handwritten”, believe me, you have to go to his class and then you will understand concepts and his notes throughly. love his class and office hours.

His lectures are messy and hard to follow, often gets distracted and goes on tangents about random math related fun facts. While he can be funny and crack good jokes, more often than not it is just distracting. His lectures are him just writing down his thoughts (no structure) and often unnecessary proofs that just confuse students.
This professor has very messy lectures. NO point in showing up. Better off watching YouTube videos. Perkins is a great person, but not a very great teacher.

Unorganized, unprepared, gets off topic often His notes are just him writing down buzz words with no structure. He has no structure, no organization, and he just sucks. I will give him the fact that he's funny, a little, but if want to actually succeed in calc 126 and your major depends on you getting a good grade, don't take perk.

Patrick is a great professor; make sure you attend his lecture in person since his lecture notes was just a scratch for him; His first few weeks might be abstract and tough, but don't worry that much, it was just his strategy to frighten those who heard this is a easy course. So attend lecture and ask question in office hour, you'll succeed

Lectures are a bit hard to follow because because he'll start a topic and pick up not quite where he left off but a bit before so the material overlaps and you need to parse out the through line. His handwriting also really sucks and he makes a lot of mistakes in lecture. Has really generous office hours and easy tests though!
His voice is nice, but the lectures are horrible with notes that are hard to understand. The structure are poor, and he goes too fast when explaning theorems. Also, the grading is very tough.

Liked his style of notes of using paper, but had bad handwriting. Would go off topic alot which was sometimes funny, but took time out of lecture especially when we needed it. Had easy midterms but made final harder than what was used too. Would not take his class again but he has a charisma that others liked.

Perkins was okay. He gave easy midterms, but that ruined me for the final. He was pretty funny but the handwriting was hard to read sometimes and he will stop in the middle of an example because we can "figure it out from there."
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Perkins was a decent professor, his lectures were confusing at times so I'd recommend reviewing the homework and textbook before coming to lecture so you have a better idea of what he's talking about. Midterms were easier compared to other professors, so the final was more difficult, so watch out for that. I'd take this class again.

Professor Perkins brings humor to the lectures, but his handwriting can be tricky to follow. Rely on additional study resources like unstuckstudy and YouTube to solidify the concepts. Exams are reasonable with a focus on improvement.

Disorganized lectures, with the prof writing one concept then completely forgetting it and going on a tangent for quite some time. Also, no lecture notes are provided and students are expected to cope up with his whims in the lectures. To worsen things, the class is not even recorded which makes it hard to catch up, Overall disappointing  class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Seems like he genuinely enjoys teaching and cracks a few good jokes here and there. Grading was not terribly harsh, but was not easy either. Overall, a good guy that even curved the overall class average up above the math department's median. Beware lectures not recorded, handwriting is kind of sloppy, and lecture notes are extremely sporadic.
