I loved Phil. I never missed one of his lectures last year. By far my favorite class so far. The material in lecture is straightforward and easy to take notes on. Material is reviewed again in quiz section which is nice to really get the concepts down. Tons of practice exams to prepare for midterms and final. I recommend going to every class.
Phil is the best professor I have ever had at UW. Use the previous tests to study for exams and you will do great.

Very funny and engaging professor. Sometimes lectures covered too much new content at once, but the homework and extra practice problems made concepts click. Professor really cared about students and wanted us to succeed.

Best professor I've had. The textbook is technically part of the class but never needed to read any of it. All material was covered twice (main lecture and quiz section). Homework and studying took about 2hrs/week on avg.

He is an excellent professor and really funny during class. I'd highly recommend him to anyone who's going to take Accounting225. The content is really difficult so be prepared to study over 10+ hours a week on this class alone.

Absolutely best professor I have had at UW. Lectures are interesting and helpful to learn the content. Phil as a professor is extremely caring, funny, engaging, and helpful. He posts all his past midterms, finals, and quizzes on canvas to practice (which is very nice). Strongly recommend taking ACCTG225 with him!

Accounting is just a tough class to me so I definitely did not have the best experience, especially since it was online, but Professor Quinn does his best to make sure you understand the lecture material and he is accessible for help (use all your resources and get help!!!). He is pretty funny and has that dad humor going on!

Phil is a great guy and teacher. He has managed to make one of my most tedious subjects bearable and has done his best to accommodate students needs during online classes. The class is tough but he does all in his power to make it easier. I will truly miss him and his ability to brighten up days in the darkest of times

Phil makes ACCT 225 so much more fun than the subject itself. He's super caring about his students, AS LONG AS THEY DON'T CHEAT. Do not attempt to cheat in his class or else he will definitely find you and you will get equivalent consequences. If you ever need help, he will be there for you, no matter what it takes. 100% would take again.

Took ACCTG 225 with him online during covid-19. He adjusted really well, and made the course feel as normal as possible. Made complicated topics easy to follow and articulates information very well. Super reasonable workload. He somehow made online accounting engaging in the middle of a pandemic. Great prof.

Phil is the GOAT. I had him for ACCTG 225 during Spring 2020 when COVID-19 was happening. The man adjusted to Zoom lectures instantly and adapted the course way more effectively than any of my other professors. The guy really cares about his students and believes in them. The man VOLUNTEERED HIS TIME and CAME TO CAMPUS TO PERSONALLY TUTOR STUDENTS.

Phil has been one of my favorite lecturers so far at UW- second only to Izzy Weber. His slides were absolutely hilarious and made managerial at least semi-entertaining. He helped me with my major outside of class and is super approachable- he really cares about all of us. Get a chegg subscription for the homework- trust me. Love you Phil!

Phil was one of the funniest professors Ive ever had. His lectures were AMAZING and I always looked forward to them even though they stressed me out to the max. You really have to pay attention during lecture, theres no panopticon The homework is incredibly stupid and time consuming, but its not Phils fault. 10/10 recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Hilarious, great prof made even managerial accounting moderately interesting with his jokes. This class itself however is much harder than 215, homeworks routinely take 3+ hours (215 hws took me 30 min tops) and the material is much less intuitive. That said, take it with Phil, he was an excellent prof. Tests follow practice tests very closely.

Phil is a great professor, I was worried about taking 225 because I hadn't heard anything good about those who taught it, after the first day I knew I would be fine. His lectures are great and he is crazy funny, he makes really boring material easier to learn and class was always interesting. Definitely take him if you can, its worth an early class

Phil is arguably one of the best accounting profs at UW. He turns a generally tricky subject into something fun and enjoyable. This does not mean it doesnt require hard work though, as it is a college level course. He is accessible outside of class, and he is very caring and wants the best for all students.
Phil's class was one of the best classes I've taken at UW. He makes what could easily be a dry subject interesting.

I took Phil's class last quarter and I actually miss it. He is an excellent lecturer, truly a "man of the people", and does his best to help us learn. The concepts are hard and I would recommend doing at least one practice problem a day (15min max) the whole quarter. You wont be able to cram it all before the test. I wish I had studied earlier.

Awesome professor who makes hard things easy compare to my ACCTG 215 professor Stephan Sefcik who makes easy things hard. He basically provides all materials you need for getting a 4.0. All in all, if you are gonna take ACCTG 225, I strongly recommend you to take with him! He is probably the best prof. in Foster School, so please cherish him!!!!!

Phil is one of the best professors i've ever had!! He alleviates so much stress from the class by playing music, cracking jokes, etc. This is a difficult class, but he does everything he can to help you succeed. He deserves an endless amount of Chipotle.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Phil is an awesome professor. He cracks typical dad jokes in class, plays music before class, and includes pop culture in his lectures. He explains only what you need and not anything unnecessary. His tests are not unreasonably hard, and the practice tests are the same as the real test. Lots of homework, but it's not terribly hard.
Best professor at UW

Phil is one of the best professors I've had at UW and easily the best 225 professor. He makes his lectures engaging with his humor and pop culture references, I actually enjoyed going to class. Material is difficult, and tests can be hard (especially the final) but Phil provides practice tests and is really accessible. Amazing Professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: This man deserves all the burritos. Fav professor at UW so far. Young, funny, experienced/knowledgable, and one of the most genuinely caring professors you'll meet. He makes an effort to make sure students have what they need to succeed, or meet with him if they need help. I enjoyed going to class!

I actually enjoy spending 70 minutes in accounting when Phil is teaching. He is hilarious and clearly very smart. He loves a good pop-culture reference and will likely be blasting JT when you walk in. The class, of course, is hard. Do the homework until you get 100%. Take the practice tests seriously, with a timer, more than once. Talk to Phil.

Phil is an overall great teacher. He starts off his lectures with pop songs that relate to the material of that lecture and really wants to get to know his students. The class is difficult but he constantly offers his support to students and makes himself available. Highly recommend taking 225 with Phil (He only teaches winter quarter).

Phil is one of the greatest lecturers I have had at the University of Washington. He makes a relatively dull subject come to life with his "dad joke" and pop-culture based lecture slides. The class is hard, three difficult exams that make up 70% of the grade, but if you have to take this class I absolutely recommend taking it with Phil.

Phil was an outstanding lecturer.  His jokes are actually funny and he really tries to create a less "Seattle-Freeze" feel in a large UW class.  The tests are difficult however he posts all of his old exams and goes over them in optional review sessions.  The material is hard to grasp, but if you put the time in you'll be rewarded.

Phil is probably one of THE most hilarious teachers I've come by. He puts effort into making his lectures entertaining for sure. He literally has 24/7 office hours, which was nice. Not the best at explaining things, but he's clear. It's a hard class, but he curves it to a 3.1, weights your best test score the heaviest, and drops a quiz score.
Good lectures, should have read more. Overall the class could have been worse. Glad I took it with Phil.
Willing to meet with students at any time. Very informative lectures. It's very helpful to go to class, but still highly recommended.

He's not the best at explaining material and mostly teaches through having you do practice problems in lecture. But he's really funny and makes the lectures interesting at least. He also offers lots of opportunities for help and genuinely wants you to do well.

Phil does a great job at teaching Managerial Accounting. Exams are hard and are meant to be hard to weed out the class. Quizzes are also hard but primary multiple choice. Best advise would be to go to class, do all assignments at least  once, and study hard for the exams so you don't have to wait time thinking during them. Over all good professor.

Acctg 225 isn't the easiest but I really enjoy having Phil as a professor! He's a pretty cool guy and he provides old exams and extra study material which is awesome. There's definitely help if you need it. The only thing I didn't like about his class is that he expects you to read before lectures. Not a huge deal, but it gets a little confusing.

Im so frustrated with this professor. He doesn't do a very good job at all explaining the material and in lecture makes more jokes then he does explaining where his answers are coming from. Not to mention his answers are just jumbles of numbers. DO NOT take acctg 225 with him! I got a 4.0 in 215 and am struggling with his teaching structure...

He's a nice guy and he really tired to make sure his students understand what is going on. He gives too much time on in-lecture problems so sometimes you just sit there for 10 minutes doing nothing. His lectures would be a lot better if he condensed them into 50 minutes. Otherwise, just pay attention to his old exams he gives you and you'll be fine

Accounting 225 is definitely a hard class, and he definitely won't let you just skate along, but Phil is an awesome professor and tries to make the material relatable by using pop culture references, and he's hilarious.

Lectures are confusing because he expects you to come to class prepared for the material he is going to teach (wants you to read the textbook beforehand). His lectures are interesting because he is young and funny.  Tries to keep accounting as fun and interesting as it can be.
Lectures are confusing.

This course (complex analysis) lacked structure. The homework was like trying to build a skyscraper on a bad foundation. The problems selected were not only unhelpful to my learning of the material, but were so difficult that I devoted all of my time to them, rather than actually learning complex analysis. I hope professor fixes course structure.
If MY girl and Hadrian Quan were both DROWNING, you can catch me at my girl's funeral discussing the BEST differential operator and the GOAT's accomplishments and contributions to analysis.

Dr. Quan is super nice and helpful, his lectures are a bit wonky but they get the job done. I had to do of youtube because his lecture style was not my style but others seemed to do well with it. He is always willing to help you understand. His exams are not difficult nor tricky. I would take him again if he taught another course I needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Fu has a somewhat heavy accent, but once you're accustomed to his intonation on words he's an excellent lecturer (always takes time to explain concepts until everyone gets it). His assignments are difficult, but he is very available for extra help if necessary. Super sweet guy, wish he taught more undergrad courses.

Love Fu! He is so knowledgeable and inspirational about radiation. He must have switched up his lecture style because he does lots of examples in class. Flexible with grade due-dates if people are overloaded by other classes.  Also, just a really kind and cool guy with sweet arm motioning during lecture. He does have a thick accent but just listen.

Prof Fu is very passionate about the material. Material is  interesting, & I recommend taking the class bc it is an eye-opener about how clouds, trees, ocean, wind, etc. all play a role in our climate. Be warned that his accent is very thick, & his lectures are straight from the textbook that you have to buyread. There are pop quizzes in lecture.
He's a good guy. Great researcher. As a professor? no. He really needs to use examples in class rather than just use formulas. The hw is impossible to do unless he shows examples.

Definitely passionate about what he teaches (atmospheric radiation), but gives very few physical examples. Prefers to teach with LOTS of formulas! Nice guy, but wish he could teach the concepts better.
Good proffessor overall, hes just hard to understand at times, However hes always willing to clarify if you need it and hes very helpful.

Prof Fu, not as easy to understand with his accent, but highly engaging since he is so passionate about what he teaches. Nice guy, go to class for slides, can't remember if there was a book. Sections/TAs are extremely helpful.  Great class, easy if you enjoy the subject.  Poster presentation at end of quarter. Keep up to get a good grade!

Her grading system makes no sense. She allows other members of the group to rate your success. If 2 members rated me a 10/10 and 2 rated me 7/10, then my grade would decrease based on those biased polls?? One example, but for an op management teacher, you would think Shawn would have some idea in how to lead an organization such as a classroom.

There is a clear superiority complex with her that makes her think that it is necessary to attend class to understand anything from the lecture. It's operations management not nuclear physics. 93% on both the midterm and final, but ended the class with an 86. Final grade relies on 1 group project and participation which is based on opinions.

This is by far the worst class I have ever taken at the University of Washington. Firstly, the teacher (Shawn) is a joke. Her grading system makes no sense. 20% of your entire grade is based on participation. For it to have the same weight as a a final or midterm makes no sense. She sits there and takes attendance at each lecture, who does that?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Shawn was a delightful professor. She was very knowledgable during her lectures and always did her best whenever we had feedback or questions. I'd say that she is more of a tough grader, but she doesn't grade down. It is more difficult to get a perfect score on an assignment than it is to fail this class. Just be sure to be detailed in assignments.

While having a good attitude her class was the biggest waste of time I have come up against at this school. Her final project guidelines are unclear and vague and she doesn't appear confident in own subject matter. Class is not hard because everything is kinda made up or common sense though. Skeptical if she will earn her PhD given performance.

Professor Quinn was great to have for marketing research! Her lectures were easy to follow, and had many relevant examples and real-world connections. She also takes the time to chat with her students before class or during breaks just about life or even pop culture and what's going on in the world which I liked. Would definitely recommend!

Term long group project is the most difficult part of the course.  Material is not too difficult but meticulous grader (will take points off for small things).  Hope for a good group for the project and you'll do fine.  Exams and HW are easy just review lecture slides

I loved Katie! Katie did a great job of going through the topics and programs very clearly. Participate and pay attention you will do just fine on the projects and exams. She is a fair grader, the textbook is free online, and she is very accessible outside of class. Emailed her several times and always got a response, even after the quarter ended.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Katie is a fine professor. She is very knowledgeable on the material she teaches and has good examples and anecdotes to back up her lectures. Though her content can get a bit boring and repetitive (especially if you've taken PSYCH 101), the group projects in the class make up for it. The class is based half on exams and half on group work.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I have really enjoyed this class. I did spend 50 hours awake straight but honestly would do it again. Fostered great studio culture and the assignment are very hefty but if you are passionate, it will pay off. I had good feedback that really pushed my thinking and loved getting desk crits. I will say that Rhino was poorly taught.

Prof Rasti is very passionate about architecture and teaching. She can be direct but it's not out of disrespect. I appreciated the honest feedback - I came to learn and my growth in her class was exponential. Her classes are rewarding but not for the faint of heart. 10/10 rec. if you want a prof who brings energy and wants everyone to succeed.

Second time taking a class with this professor, don't regret it but definitely wouldn't do it again. Instructions are usually verbal (in class) and extremely vague, miro boards are helpful for understanding what anyone is supposed to be doing. Engaging and interesting class because of guest lecturers, but overall disorganized, lacks structure
Class was incredibly hectic. Glad it's over. Will not be taken this professor again.

Assignments are difficult to understand. Constant technical issues at the start of classes. Leads a confrontational classroom with her students. Just overall a bad professor. Try your best to get through it and lie low in her class. She had a tendency to pick on certain students.

She belittles students but acts as though she's being funny. It's incredibly disheartening to have a professor treat her students so poorly. She's incredibly disorganized and every assignment is a guessing game as to what we should turn in. I really wanted to enjoy the course but she really treats her students poorly.

When I'm the one making assignment details for the professor and I'm the one telling the studio teacher what the assignment is... I think there may a slight issue with the way she teaches.

Don't take this course unless you must. It is a good intro to what architecture students go through. Very exhausting but you'll get through it. Good luck

Zahra is probably the worst professor i've ever had. going to lectures is pretty much pointless because you can never understand a word she says. she's really mean and degrading. if you're one minute late to class she'll call you out in front of everyone. no instructions for assignments, she expects you to know through sparse canvas announcements.
All the students in her studio I've talked to have pulled all nighters. Her lack of communication makes this class very difficult. She responds to questions in a very derogatory manner.

Her instructions are confusing. She says she's holding you by the hand and will give you the least amount of clarification possible. The studio teachers make the work so much easier, but if you have her studio, good luck. She's very blunt. Lastly, she uses AI to summarize Canvas posts.

Did not communicate assignment expectations well, and treated students badly, usually as if they weren't intelligent. Lectures were stressful to attend, but some small attempts were made to make events fun and strengthen class morale.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Overall she was difficult to work with, valued her own personal projects over her job, provided little to no insight as expected of a studio professor, and did not conduct herself in a manner befitting of her position.
She would show up late or not show up at all with no warning and would leave early even if she was not finished with crits.

Zahra is mean and hard to understand, but I'm personally a big fan of that. She'll call on random students/lecturers during lecture and make them answer questions.Every assignment had one or two announcements that you would have to cross reference with the original assignment to understand exactly what the deliverables were.

Absolutely beyond disrespectful. Shows up 2hours late, leaves 2 hours early, leaving time for maybe 5-10desk crits, which is only given to whoever she likes because giving everyone equal opportunity for feedback is "boring". Will undermine the other instructors and has a temper. Easily frustrated and will pubilicly humiliate you to make an example.

Zahra is a one of a kind professor that will push you to think beyond the ordinary. Sure sometimes it's difficult, or unclear, but it's apart of the learning. The skills and thinking I have learned form her will carry on with me past college into my career. It is very clear that she loves and cares for her students.

I've never had a professor that made me genuinely want to drop out. She was extremely disorganized as head instructor for both ARCH 200 and 201, but as a section instructor she wasn't as bad. Additionally, she would leave up to half of an hour before class ended without clear instructions of what was assigned for that day.

Rasti has been pivotal in my understanding of basic architectural techniques. She challenges her students a lot, especially considering this class is just a prerequisite for the architecture program. Still, she seems to genuinely care about her students their success, and her teaching style prepares them for the heavy workload in architecture.

I haven't felt like a professor was working against my education until this class. Rasti would often skip lecture without warning, and would change assignments after students began working. People began pulling all-nighters early in the quarter, I would often work forty hours a week on assignments. Students would bond over how they didn't like her.

In the Arch 200 series's first lecture, Zahra, tells you "You'll be a family by the end," she means trauma bonded. Zahra is hilarious when she isn't pointing her unapologetically blunt critique at you, like when she yelled across a room that she would "kill David" (our TA) for approving designs she disliked. However, out of class, she's very sweet.

Professor Zahra Rasti has given me with the worst class in college yet, pioneering the depths and heights of unprofessionalism, inorganization and workload. In this class deadlines are vague and your grade depends on your professor more than your work. And boy is there a lot of work, for a five-credit class, arch 201 delivers 10 credits of work.

This is a class you want to pursue a careers as an architect, but I cannot recommend this class for anyone who want to take it for fun or is curious. For one, the work load is heavy that makes taking other classes difficult, this is not the class for those with tight budgets and this is not the class to take it your someone who get stressed easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ARCH 200 and 201 are so unorganized that it drives students away from architecture. Project requirements, lessons, and assignments  differed depending on your section instructor. 201 rarely felt like a class bc section turned out to be work time. No assignments, due dates, or tutorials. Everything I learned about Rhino in 201 I taught myself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She assigns a large amount of work and does so in a way that is less structured than what many students seem to like. However, if you embrace this teaching style and are willing to put in effort, you will end up learning more and become a better designer who can actually think for themselves. It's tough love with professor Rasti, not poor teaching.

If you need hand holding this class isn't for you. It's architecture, coming into this you have to know that creatively you will be in charge and that you have to put in copious amounts of hours to succeed. Her critiques though harsh, are exactly what you need and in future studios you will want them again.

Extremely unorganized class. Most students/ TA's had no idea what was going on, and there were mixed expectations that caused a lot of stress and confusion. Deadlines were unrealistic. Lost years of my life. All that being said she is very passionate.

Zahra overall wasn't the best. She was disorganized the entire quarter and wasn't able to be contacted easily. Her class wasn't very hard but the information wasn't given in detail and when needed clarification she proceeded to lose her patience with the class and yell about the requirements. She wasn't the worst professor to exist, but like...
Most of the learning is done through provided videos. The professor is nice.

Prof. Ruth used the flipped classroom approach, and while she reviewed the practice problems for our Linux course in the following class, I felt that her explanations could have been more detailed. Especially towards the end, when I got lost, I would have loved for the lectures to include more practice. Overall, seems like a nice person.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really harsh grading, unfair, not good coding class
how is her rating the same at Kevin Zatloukal's?
Dr. Anderson is a riot. She is so sweet and genuinely cares about her students. Very in-depth understanding of python and its use cases. Would absolutely take another class under her.
Worst coding class
she has "good looking slides" but she wasn't able to explain things clearly.
Talks at a snails pace, 50 minute lectures have about 25 minutes of information. Unhelpful and rude if you have any questions, better try your luck with one of the TAs instead.

The class itself was easy, so the professor made sure to spend more time answering students' questions and asking students to apply the pre-lecture content in discussions and demos. The professor made sure the class felt comfortable and not stressful to take.
Ruth is my hero. If I could have all my classes with Ruth, I would.
Best professor I've had. Ruth is smart, gives amazing lectures and is very empathetic. Reachable outside of class and pretty hilarious in class.

I have had Ruth for two classes. If I had to describe her in one word, it would be consistent. The way she approaches teaching a topic and the way she frames her class structure is very consistent. 

If you get used to her structure and ask for help when needed, her classes are very manageable. She also says "D'oh!" like Homer Simpson which I enjoy

She used good visuals, which helped me understand the calculations. Unfortunately, the homework assignments frequently confused me since they were out of sync with lectures or worded strangely. I did not understand the objective and difficulty of many lab synthesis questions. Ruth is nice, but must support us more in memorization (crucial for 351).

Avoid this professor at all costs for this class. This is the first class I've taken with her and honestly, I don't know if the class is just content heavy or she's unable to finish lectures ever. Most of the time she's rushing lecture and dismissive towards students. And after five years of having an online final she makes it in person.
Sure, after 5 years of take-home exams, switch back to cumulative in-person final exams for no reason.

Wasn't a very good nor bad professor. Explained concepts pretty decently but didn't prepare us for the non-coding homework assignments, which dropped my GPA substantially. She was very unforgiving on both the midterm and final. Some questions on the midterm were dumb.

Ruth provides really good illustrations on the slides during class, although often things might be a little rushed towards the end of class. Took this class winter quarter so we have 10 weeks of instruction but also 13 exercises due in total (9 coding, 4 written). Written homeworks weren't too bad. Amount learned from section depends on your TA.

I was expecting a lot more from Ruth. Most lectures could have been condensed into 5-10 minute videos. TA office hours were very inaccessible; she was dismissive of questions in her personal office hours. The average grade on the midterm was 40% and they didn't curve it. Lots of unclear specifications on both exams & projects, and awful grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was really excited to take a class with Ruth; all of my interactions with her prior were positive. That said, I've never seen a professor so disconnected from the rest of the class. She did her lecture and then that was it. Going to her office hours was a mistake-- she was very dismissive of most questions. Ultimately, I was very disappointed.

Prof. Anderson is great! She really walked you through the code, and would check-in during lecture to make sure the class understood what was going on. Lots of homework, often pretty complicated so START EARLY. Also midterm and final, they're timed but they're take home and you can do them over several days. Easy to contact outside of class! 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ruth did solid lecturing and illustrating on the slides. There was a TON of work and seemed to be no breathing room between assignments but that's just how it is in 332. 2nd project was the most challenging and the write up took a lot of time. Since the 1st 4 weeks were online she dropped lowest exercise grade and exams were take-home + in a group.

Professor Anderson is super kind and caring. Her lectures tend to be wordy slides, works for reviewing/catching up. Tough but interesting projects. Course was quite forgiving, mainly w/ exams. I wish the projects required less of the report writing experimented with. For algos like sorting, it is helpful to watch explanations and animations online.
I loved her lectures and the group projects were fun. The final and midterms were fair. Would definitely take a class with her again :).
Excellent lectures! Great explanations! Interesting Projects! Take this class with her!

A really good lecturer. The projects were challenging but beneficial. But this is one of those classes where you read the instructions and have no idea what to do or you understand the instructions but the code provided is very complicated and requires research (i.e., lots of generics). Tests are hard and P2 might be the worst time of your life.
Amazing lecturer. lots of graded exercises but they are relatively easy

Professor Anderson is pretty laid back and passionate about what she teaches. I took CSE160 with absolutely no prior programming experience and with the guided transition into harder concepts I was able to really keep up and understand Python by the end. The homework assignments aren't too bad, just start early and use office hours.

This class consists of biweekly labs, which range from somewhat to very challenging. However, there are always a lot of resources for students who get stuck, which means you definitely learn a lot in this class. Overall, the material for this class can be pretty dense at times, but Ruth consistently explains things pretty well.

Ruth was awesome. Super caring. She even reached out to students who were having a hard time to check if they were alright and asked if there was anything she could do to help. She uses lots of examples in class and uses markers and drawing tools a lot. Great instructor overall.

Great teacher I think she explains thing really well. The class itself was pretty easy but that's probably because it was online so we didn't have any midterms of major tests. Most of the coding projects aren't laboriously long and I found them very enjoyable in hindsight

This quarter was different (online classes due to COVID) but Professor Anderson's lectures were straightforward and concepts were reasonably explained. That being said, you had to spend a decent amount of time on the homework and labs because they are tougher and very different to your 142 and 143 coding homeworks.

Maybe its a product of 332, but this class was one of those that suffered from the "unclear specification, but we'll grade you harshly anyways" bug that plagues our department. Ruth was complicit to this. Additionally, her lectures were super dry, and she spent most of them stepping through alogirthms you could just read the pseudocode for.

Super approachable, insanely smart, and a great lecturer. Class is a little boring first half, but definitely picks up once you hit graphs and parallelism. Tests are very predictable: results in high averages. Course made by adam blank, so there's a lot of thought put into the curriculum. Stand-out professor, feel really bad I missed the last day.

The best professor to take any class with. She really cares about the students. She does not make the class super easy but at the same time she does not make it super hard either. Everything is perfectly balanced!!!!!!!

A really great lecturer. i had her for both 391 and 332. I think her lectures have lots of examples and explanations and she's great at answering questions. She really cares if students learn and was super accessible outside of class and reasonable when I had concerns or needed to reschedule something.

I thought Ruth was a solid choice for CSE332. Not great, not bad. The homework assignments and group projects were challenging but definitely doable. I really enjoyed the material. The class is pretty lecture heavy, but they're all Panoptoed. The tests are a classic CS time scramble
Good lectures
Absolutely phenomenally super cute, but second to only Adam Blank. Lectures aren't the most exciting in the world, but you learn a lot from them. Extremely approachable and grades fairly.
second only to Adam Blank
Ruth's instruction was very straightforward and she was definitely one of the nicest professors I've had. Her lectures can be somewhat dull but she knows what she's talking about.
Not exciting, not boring. Kind of in the middle. She's pretty decent overall. Her exams aren't super difficult and are similar to the ones from her previous quarters.
Most of the CS-Engineering professors I've had at the UW are bad. Ruth is one exception she is good I would recommend that you take as many classes as you can from her.

Ruth went over tons of things in lecture but the homeworks have some of those components and usually have you go above and beyond to figure some things out. It wasn't that bad, so I felt like I learned a lot. She's a great lecturer and gives TONS of feedback about your personal assignment and the assignment in general. She really cares about you.

Ruth is a wonderful, dedicated professor who clearly loves learning and cares about her students. I'm really glad I had the opportunity to learn from her, and I hope I can take another course with her again some time! There is a moderate amount of work in this class, so stay on top of assignments and you'll be fine. Don't try to do them in a day!

The thing I really appreciate about Ruth is how clear she is with expectations, and always wanting students feedback to become better at teaching the material. She's not the most exciting teacher but that being said, I really loved having her as one just because I knew she was super open to students and wouldn't try and hide any expectations.

Great professor, really clear in lectures and energetic. Very approachable and open to students asking questions, but much better at answering questions in 1 on 1 rather than in lecture. 332: Weekly homeworks (easy) and three large projects (hard), make sure to stay on top of the projects as it's incredibly hard to do them well at the last minute!

One of the best professors at UW (both in and out of the CSE major). Was very clear about the material, went through a lot (but not too many) examples and homework was extremely relevant to the tests, unlike some other classes. Very helpful and enthusiastic, would definitely take another class with her again.

Ruth is amazingly approachable and a really great lecturer. Talks about tradeoffs really well and has a nice way of asking and answering questions. Also helpful during office hours and seems pretty overall cool!
Man she was great! Really clear, and easy to follow lectures.

One of the best professors in the UW CSE department. You can really tell that the students like her. Even for a class with terribly boring material, she does a great job of explaining and her enthusiasm definitely shows. Not many professors that care about their students as much as Ruth.
Just not good at lecturing. Don't like her style at all.

Can take time to warm up to. She responds to emails. Has practice midterms/finals. They're similar to real things, but there are curve balls. Homework is very reasonable. The course had a lot of structure and you had time to complete assignments. The book was terrible. I would recommend this instructor for CSE 373.
I'm also surprised to see her rated low. She's been very good -- not stellar or hugely exciting, but consistently clear, good homework assignments, easy exams.
Surprised she has such a low rating! I found her to be very clear and sometimes a little funny, and I definitely learned a lot from this class. I would take a class from her again!

She sucks big time. Really boring, i fell asleep with a latte in my hand in one of her lectures. Very unorganized and irrelevant lectures. Assumes you already know the programming style that she wants. One time she gave us a  practice midterm with questions that even our TAs couldn't do. Really terrible, stay away from her!
Had her for Data Structures. Its hard to keep track of what she's saying, and seems to go off topic at times, or you won't have a large perspective of why she's saying what she's saying.
The worst CSE teacher I have met. Spends a lot of class time talking about uesless things. you never know what's her point.Never,Never,take her class

Dr. Robinson is one of the better profs at UW. OCHEM is supposed to be hard and she says that, but she is a great teacher and has a good sense of how students learn. She is also one of the only profs that I think wants all of her students to do well and wants what is best for them. The best of all of the option if you need to take OCHEM.
She lied to us about test content, told us certain things would NOT be on the final, but were. Not particularly trustworthy but a decent professor.

Her lectures did rush a bit towards the end. I felt the midterms were relatively fair and she gave good practice, only provides one practice test though and no practice test for the final. The final was very difficult so try your hardest on the midterms, there are 3, lowest is dropped. She made organic chemistry fun for at least the first test

I wouldn't recommend taking if you're not ready to teach yourself a lot of the content. The flipped lecture style makes it so she rushes through the slides that only really contain summaries. Concept videos, discussion worksheets, and youtube were most helpful to learn. She def knows her chem so exams are tricky and long, partial credit is hard.

She's an enthusiastic lecturer who genuinely wants students to understand the material. Very caring, answers questions encouragingly, and keeps the class well-organized (everything you need is really easy to find on Canvas). Honestly confused by the negative reviews; I thought she was a great professor.

She had normally good lectures, only struggle was answering too many questions which led her to rush her last few slides. Her class structure had clear expectations each week (2 readings,1 hw). Sometimes she over or under explains confusing concepts. Ochem is hard no matter the professor, but I believe she was good! Final exam however? devastating.

The class is difficult but Dr. R is just trying to prepare us for CHEM 258, which I heard is WAY worse. She loves to trip you up in her MCQ's so just remember to read them thoroughly. Midterms were fair, but the final was hellish. She is really kind though and accessible outside of class. Really just practice the mechanisms and study up!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Exams are hard but not impossible. She gives a lot of very accurate practice exams. Expects you to understand the content read before class then follow along in lectures. The lectures are helpful but get to be rushed at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: I'm not sure why she gets a bad rep. She's accessible and supportive. Ochem isn't easy, but Dr. R explains material clearly, reinforcing readings and aligning with exams. She does sometimes run out of time and rushes at the end of lectures. Exams were fair overall, though the final was harder. I would personally recommend taking her.

She's nice and her slides are easy to understand. However sometimes she spends too much time on one topic and runs out of time for the rest, rushes through remaining slides barely giving us time to read them and expects us to know them for the exam. Her midterms were fine, but her final was very difficult. Class had low averages so a good curve.

I have never felt the need to leave a review on a teacher, but the final exam for this class was absolutely ridiculous. I studied so much and it wouldn't have mattered. The test was ten times harder than any problems she covered or practice exams and I don't think I would've been prepared if I studied for a month.

If you are taking her class, be prepared to read the textbook before lectures. Her practice exams are much easier than the actual exams. I liked her lectures, although her style of teaching might not be for everyone. If you are coming into this with no background in ochem then good luck, you might find her lectures unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I think she only has a low rating due to the students who didn't put in the time or effort to do well in the class and are instead looking for someone to blame. Professor Robinson had good lectures, accessible office hours, and was friendly and fun to talk to. She is very smart and answers questions well. Do all of the readings, homework, and labs!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. R is one of the main reasons why I'm leaving the biochem major. I did well in genchem, but I cannot deal with her Ochem classes. If you take this class, READ THE TEXTBOOK AND DO THE PRACTICE QUESTIONS. Even then, you might not pass as the exams are way harder than her practice ones and not like the homework. Basically u teach urself and pray.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: No real teaching at all. You have to do everything by yourself. She even missed chapters and go over everything like you already know all of the concepts pretty well. The homework and what she teaches is never the same thing in exam. The exam is totally different and much harder！
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Make sure you read the textbook before going to class because she will race through a topic and then give a poll (credit for participation) on it so if you don't have a decent understanding you will quickly get behind in the lecture. There is so much info in the lecture but she doesn't effectively explain it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Make sure to read the textbook and do all the practice problems she suggests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Don't take her unless you have to. Her way of explaining topics is very confusing and she rushes through slides really quickly, giving you almost no time to take in what you learned. Her tests are alright. The study guides she provides are helpful but there are a few trick questions so be careful. I wouldn't recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Robinson isn't the best lecturer, but her midterms are, for the most part, straightforward. That being said, the final was unreasonably hard. This is coming from someone who scored 100% on two midterms. My grade dropped a little more than 10% after the final. She didn't teach half of the things on it. Study hard, but good luck getting a 4.0.

This class is difficult, and Dr. Robinson's teaching is good for some but can be confusing. She is personally friendly, but gives info-dump lectures that are rarely intuitive. She refuses to give accommodations for many things, which can be difficult in some cases. She is very helpful durng her office hours.

If you miss a word in the lecture, you might as well go home. She explains things in a much harder to understand way than necessary. Incredibly tough grader. Midterm/final averages between 40-50% should say something about her teaching style. You need a tutor multiple times a week to even think about passing.

The professor is nice, knowledgeable, and is easy to meet with. She has resources on her canvas for students. That said, exams are ~75% of your total course grade so if you're not a good test-taker, I wouldn't recommend. You have to get pretty deep into the ungraded practice questions for some of the problems. Lots of reading, but it's manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Robinson was a great lecturer and I believe her classes are very helpful. She goes at a good pace and explains things thoughtfully. I would say her tests are more difficult than expected based on lectures/reading/homework but honestly fair. I would definitely attend class and study more than you think you'd need.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: robinson was definitely a tough grader, but i felt like her midterms were fair and reflective of the practice we had done. she's a great lecturer, and her slides definitely felt more helpful than reading the textbook because of how simple she made everything seem. be prepared to do lots of flashcards if you want to do well on tests!

Samantha is okay. Lectures are dense with information, but she either drags or rushes specific lectures. We spent too long reviewing gen chem topics and too little time on difficult topics like reactions. Her midterms are chill. Mostly multiple-choice questions (partial-credit is almost impossible) and minimal "explain this..." style questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr.Robinson is very kind and some problems are out of her control (lecture being at 8:30, median grade policy, information to cover) so don't panic with reviews. Fair tests, but labs difficult to get full points & lots of errors in grading - prepare to advocate for yourself A LOT. Go to lecture in person even w/ panopto: you will do so much better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class was test-heavy and required a lot of outside effort. It felt more like a flipped classroom, so you need to spend a lot of time teaching yourself the material. She rushes through lectures and does not give much partial credit on exams. The final impacts your grade a lot, and it's pretty difficult. She's nice tho, and def knows her chem.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is heavily reliant on the textbook, so most of your learning will be done through reading. If you take her class, beware that her lectures are very fast paced and will feel rushed.

I'm honestly very shocked at all the bad reviews. I thought Dr. Robinson was a great professor and I enjoyed her chem class very much! She had great lectures that were very good at explaining the concepts! Supplemented with the textbook, this course is not bad at all! Wish I could take the whole chem series with her!!!

She isn't a great lecturer as she often takes easy concepts and presents them in a confusing manner. She takes too long to teach certain concepts and then rushes others, but she does a great job at answering questions. Midterms aren't difficult with averages around 70 to 75, but the final is unlike any previous exams, which will ruin your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Personally, I really enjoyed her class. Exams are very straightforward, with very few open-ended conceptual questions. It's an ochem class... obviously it'll be hard. Learn how to study, go to office hours, and read the textbook, and you'll pass. I have no idea why her ratings are so low. She answers all questions and replies to emails fast!!

genuinely probably one of the worst professors i've ever had. she was terrible at lectures, so even if i attended the lectures, i didn't learn anything. most of what i've learned from this class has been from the textbook or the organic chemistry tutor. TA is also useless, doesn't know how to teach, give proper explanations, or the right answers.
She's nice, but not very accommodating to students. About 18hr of work a week because she doesn't really teach anything that will be on exams, you will have to prioritize this class to do even decent

This professor was very nice, but super hard to learn from. She explains things in a very strange way that makes it hard to understand. Her test questions are also not very clear. I highly suggest office hours and chem tutoring in Mary Gates Hall. You will need to prioritize this class to succeed.

This class was made way harder than it should have been. The midterms are ridiculously hard and not at all of what is taught in class. You have to spend hours outside of class teaching yourself almost everything, and random things never discussed will pop up on the exams, no matter how prepared you are. Class averages are ridiculously low.

Lectures were not high quality. Basically the type of lecture where you are expected to know everything beforehand. She goes over everything really fast and she says "ooh" and "um" a lot. Kind of useless in my opinion. Pretty much all my learning was done outside of class, but you have to go if you want the attendance credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: FAV PROF! I made this account just because it upset me to see her lowly rated. All the resources you need to succeed are given to you and if you do what she advises, you will do well. She is also insanely accommodating and if you reach out to her, I guarantee she will help you out. Don't be scared by the other reviews.

15-18h work/week but tests are 70% and labs 29% and 1% is for EVERYTHING else (A LOT). so much time every week ov useless busywork thats 1% of your grade. graded harshly too and she doesn't seem to care the average is like in the 60%s. everyone confused in quiz section every week, even the TAs struggle w the amt of work ur suppposed to be doing.bad
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture not organised; presented easy concept in complicated way. Expect midterm after 5 lectures, exams come out weirdly. If you don't ANALYSE the content n wording of past papers (she only provides one for each exam), no way of getting high marks. Homework is overloaded compared to the other prof (5 vs 25 question??). Exams are marked strictly.

Dr. Robinson was amazing to have for this course, she is super friendly in office hours and her practice exams are very helpful when studying for midterms/final. It's shocking that she has many bad reviews online when irl people actually say nice things about her. Lectures are well detailed and organized which makes review more easier.

I'm honestly shocked by all the bad reviews--Dr. Robinson was the SWEETEST professor I've ever had, her office hours were so helpful, she's great at breaking complex topics down, and patient with all questions, even "simple" ones. OChem is horrendous so maybe people are using the prof as a scapegoat. Wish I could've taken the whole series with her
Very nice and understanding. A bit strict with grading nomenclature, make sure you know how to spell. Overall lectures were easy to understand and the exams were relatively fair.

She was nice and good at lecturing. The structure of the class really helped me learn (practicing and studying on my own). The exams were straight forward but she was stingy on partial credit and practice problems that actually looked/sounded like the ones she gave us on the exam; most of the practice she gave us was from the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I believe that Prof. Robinson is an amazing lecturer and a great professor, and CHEM220 is much better than the alternative Chem pathway. However, exams are weighted heavily, 70% of your total grade, and averages are in the 50's. It is rough on your GPA and rough on the ego. Outside of the ruthless structure of the course, Robinson is great.

Chem 237 runs through many topics, so it's a hard class in itself, but Prof Robinson made it very enjoyable and gave good explanations of all the topics. Her lectures are concise and clear to follow. The exams are exactly like the practices, and she corrects errors on the answer key promptly. Quiz section worksheets are good and TAs help a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: She was lazy when it came to posting the key answers for all of the worksheets given online. Sometimes she would provide the wrong answer and not even point it out. She ends the lectures early sometimes and tells us to figure out the rest of the slide on our own time. She expects us to know certain material even though she hasn't taught it yet
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A lot of the lower ratings are because OChem is notoriously hard and when people don't do as well as they hope, they get mad. Genuinely Dr R, is a great teacher and super friendly. As long as you do the textbook readings, go to lectures, go to office hours, practice, etc. You will probably do fine.
Very pleasant and covered the material effectively. If you're willing to attend or watch lectures, you should do pretty well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: i really hated this class. chem 110 should not be this difficult. aleks taught me everything + the grading policies / homework load were super rough. would never take again - i wish id just gone to 120 or 142 first. didn't feel like the teacher caredthat average was ~70%. barely passed as stem major

Professor Robinson was amazing! This was just a beginner chem class, which is probably why it wasn't so hard, but she did really well. Homework was decent and if you just pay attention and do everything on time you should do fine. She was easy to access and clearly cared about the class and what we learned. A good intro to chemistry course.
Chemistry is hard, so it will be tough but she genuinely cares about the students which is nice
Great at explaining the concepts, but this class requires a lot of outside practice. Tests are hard but a good grade is definitely achievable. Overhated

Her ratings are awful so I kept expecting her to get bad but it never happened. She is an excellent lecturer, cares a lot and writes reasonable exams. Might actually the best prof Ive had. People really let having to wake up at 7 ruin a class for them. Go to lecture and take notes and you will do well easily. End the Samantha Slander she is my goat

Her lectures are really good and understandable, lots of active learning. But they also nitpick every little tiny thing on exams and other submissions. You'll get 0 points if you accidentally misspell something, or apply the wrong filter to you PDF scan. It's honestly infuriating. You do great on an exam, but get 60% from all the nitpicks

Lectures are pretty good as she reviews textbook sections and allows for questions, but often goes overtime and rushes the end slides. Tests have complicated wording and multiple choice options, and often nitpick at obscure concepts. She expects you to understand the concepts on a deeper level.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were organized and summarize the textbook. She answers questions, but often goes overtime then rushes concepts. Tests often have complicated multiple choice questions or wording, so she expects you to deeply understand the concepts on your own. They're also nitpicky on obscure concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you participate and pay attention, you will do well in the class. The two main gripes I have with the way she taught 237 is that the final had a couple of questions we weren't prepared for and I don't feel she prepared me for 238 or 241. She glazed over a lot of the specifics of topics and didn't go into the detail I'm expected to know now.

dr robinson was okay... she used a flipped classroom style (which is tricky for an ochem class). the homework she assigned was mostly helpful, but there wasn't much exam prep or practise (no variety either, pretty much copy/past questions). she would often go overtime, and exams were worded much differently than practise/lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: A LOT of reading - but well organized. Having to pay for Achieve to access MY HOMEWORK was insane, but I can't really put that on the professor. Midterms were tough, the final was crazy - but the lectures and worksheets were very helpful. HIGHLY recommend doing the textbook problems she picks out. She wants to help, so don't hesitate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nice person but her exams give essentially zero partial credit and add concepts that weren't in lecture. You must work a lot outside of class and have to go above what she provides in class to do well. The final exam is 60% multiple choice + very difficult. She easily has the lowest averages out of the other 237 professors, around 63% per midterm
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: It's like all the other reviews say. She is really nice and her lectures are engaging but the tests are ridiculous. No partial credit, no clear gpa scale, class exam averages of 60% (most people scoring less). My overall grade dropped 10% after the final was graded. Still don't know what my gpa is though 🤷‍♀️ I should have listened to everyone

Exams, especially the cumulative final were ridiculously difficult. Not much partial credit is given and exam questions are often outside of the scope of what we practiced in class and on homework. You have to really study hard and understand every little detail to do well.

This course meets twice a week, so the weekly readings are very heavy. This also means that Professor Robinson doesn't always have the time to explain every concept. You have to be very disciplined taking this course and do lots of practice problems to prepare for exams. You don't have to attend lectures, just thoroughly understand the textbook.

Exams are unnecessarily tricky (covering content not taught in lectures), and grading is also questionable. Not sure if grading is done mostly by Prof Robinson or TAs, but either way, avoid taking this class with this Prof if you have other options.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Homework heavy and test heavy

Professor Robinson's lectures are engaging, and she's great at answering questions. However, the exams are extremely challenging, with questions covering concepts not thoroughly addressed in class. Definitely use unstuckstudy ai and the textbook to supplement your prep.

Good at teaching during lectures and answering questions. However, her exams are very challenging, in length and concepts. There were detailed questions on the exams that she never talked about during lecture or quiz section. No way to anticipate exam difficulty and outcome.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She teaches very well, her lectures are engaging, and she's accessible for questions. However, class is very very test heavy, and tests are very difficult and too long for the time. Final exam tends to have way more difficult questions than her practice exams and is way out of range from what we've learned. Expect out-of-syllabus test questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The chem content in this class is not really applicable or interesting. So much memorization and not enough reaction mechanics and concepts. Prof crams info for exams only a couple days before. Stressful class and labs and class averages were in the 50's. I would recommend taking 142 series
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I honestly don't know why she has low reviews, I personally loved taking chem 237 with her this quarter. Good lectures, all material covered on the final, very kind and approachable, answers questions well. This class is just really tough, heavily weighted on the exams, and the HW was very annoying. I'd say read the textbook and youll be fine.

She's a nice and organized person, you can tell that she cares about her students' learning. But she doesn't teach well given the short time you get to learn 8 chapters or so of material. She spends too much time on some topics and not nearly enough time on other topics. Exams are difficult but if you make time to study well you'll do fine.
Prof Robinson made o chem easy for me. I can tell she really cares about learning, and she explains things clearly. This is the only class at UW where I've gone to office hours.

She was a nice person and seemed to care, but she was awful at teaching. Lectures were confusing so you had to rely on the textbook/HW to learn. She overcomplicates things and spends too much time on random topics and ?s so there isn't enough time left for the more challenging topics. The tests were very hard and didn't align with practice tests.

way too much work for a 3 credit class, she sets it up like a weed out class. the averages for midterms were always incredibly low and she crammed in one right before finals which was absolutely evil. she was an incredibly kind person though. i literally failed the final and somehow ended up on the median.

Poorly set up labs, when called out she often blames students. Difficult to prepare for exams. Class average for exams should not be anywhere near what it is. I really recommend taking a different series. No extra credit.

I'd recommend taking the Chem 142 series instead. This series is ok, but there isn't enough practice for the content we're learning, and our learning is really packed in/rushed at times. We're given learning objectives, but they change the day before exams. Practice tests are nothing like the exams; occasionally tested on what you haven't learned.

I've had Robinson for 3 chem classes now and you can just tell she cares about her students and wants them to succeed. My biggest positive is that her lectures are amazing and organized to follow and she tries to connect with her students when she can. My biggest negative is that the practice tests are nothing like the exams, exams are challenging.

237 is tough no matter who you take, but Prof Robinson was organized, had a great TA team, and wanted us to succeed. Though she lectured kinda fast and some test questions were tough, she was always willing to explain things in a different way. Office hours and quiz sections also really helped clarify lecture. Study via mock exams and worksheets.

Dr.R is so kind and really wants students to do well.She's easy to find outside of class and gives practice qs that prepare you for both the exams and actually knowing the material. Orgo is difficult and takes effort; obviously you have to put in extra to succeed,but she does the best she can to help you do so. Best chem prof. I've had in college
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Just save yourself the stress and take this class with another professor.  Looked over exams given by the other ochem professors, and they were much more comprehensible than her tests. Unless you are already good at chemistry, this class will be difficult for you. Shes a nice person though, but her teaching style wasn't the best way to learn from.

Dr. Robinson is a great person; you can tell she cares about her students on a personal level. However, if you don't attend class regularly, you likely won't pass. The course was a challenging one, though ochem is notorious for that, so I don't blame her too much. The work load itself was fine, but it was very test heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Although Dr. R. wants you to succeed on a personal level, her coursework and the amount required does not make that easy or even doable if you have equally strenuous classes. Would not recommend taking her if you have other course with a bunch of work. Nice person, horrifically demanding professor.

Generally a pretty difficult class with 3 midterms plus a final. There is a lot of assigned reading you need to do to  in order to succeed, and the exams can be challenging. However, Dr. R is great and always answers questions in a clarifying manner that makes a lot of sense. If you are willing to put the work in, you will do fine in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I was nervous about taking ochem becuase I struggled in gen chem. I think this class is generally pretty fair. Organic chemistry is just a hard class. But her tests can be a slight bit confusing. They are written to really make sure you understand core concepts. So, do all her practice problems, take the practice exams and go to office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely frustrating class, my peers and I can confirm her teaching style doesn't really work for anyone. Super hard to grasp what she teaches, I continuously had to spend hours after almost every class reteaching myself the material.
Lots of homework, lectures are a must, a lot of reading and practicing work problems

I wasn't a big fan of Robinson. She was not great at explaining concepts and would cover way too much content in one lecture. All content was briefly explained then appeared on the test as an absurd question.

I love Prof Robinson she's so sweet and genuinely cares about her students. She has lower ratings because Ochem is a hard class regardless, but she makes lecture fun and is great at explaining content. She wants to help you and is so available for that. Def recommend her for Ochem series

PART 1 (lol, didn't realize we had a constaint for characters until the very end. so since i already wrote everything, might as well..)
Okay, I genuinely don't understand where these bad reviews are coming from! This was by far the best chem prof I had. Took her for ochem, & given the rep associated with the subject in general I was honestly scared

Robinson is the best chem professor I've had! I have had 4 different chem professors at UW and she was significantly better than all of them. She was very passionate about chem, making it more entertaining and easier to learn. keep slaying girl, ignore the haters.
Prof Robinson was terrible. If you can, try and take Chem 142 instead of 120, as she fails to cram multiple quarters worth of Gen chem into 2 months.

Took her for Chem 120 and Chem 220. Her exams are very hard, sometimes some questions on the midterms were not taught over in lecture. Had to study really hard for the grade and spend roughly around 10 hours or more for this class.

I took this professor for CHEM 120 and CHEM 220, she was a kind person and seemed like she wanted the best for all of the students. The course is very organized which I loved because it was easy to find everything. Exams are very hard though, some questions were harder than things that we learned in lecture. Labs were not too bad, Study a lot!

I had her for 120 and 220, and what can I say? We have no choice but to take her, so my advice would be to do the practice problems and think outside the box caz the lecture and the midterms are not alike at all, so basically teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Dr. R having such a low rate my prof really feels like slander. She was such a great teacher. Everything she does, she does for a reason that she is more than willing to share.
Her class is legitimately hard to fail if you come to class, pay attention and do all of your assignments, which aren't that extensive or overwhelming.

She didn't give out any pretests for the exam, which would have helped, but the exam she wrote was quite similar to the homework, quizzes, and examples in class. With the exam she included a useful information sheet with all the hard to memorize equations.

Dr. Robinson has a good heart, but her teaching is all over the place. Her powerpoints are hard to comprehend. There are 4 exams and a final which are worth 40% of the overall grade. If you want a passing grade, you have to work for it. Also, it's like she expects her students to have the same level of expertise as her, which is ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Don't take this class with her! Seriously! Her test is hard. Also, she forces you to use her way to solve problems. I got all answers right but she still subtracted my points because of "incorrect setup". Also, this class is really test heavy (4 tests), lab heavy(6 labs, 3 hrs each). Don't take it!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amazing, fun and easy to understand lectures. He speaks clearly and is entertaining, and is clearly very knowledgable about programming languages. His homework is a little challenging but mostly fun and rewarding. Test this quarter was pretty hard though
Stay away - this man will do anything to see you fail

Stuart is one of the best professors I've had. His stories and tangents about cs history might be annoying to some, but I enjoyed it. He really explains why the creators of C++ made the decisions they did rather than just going over syntax.
Nothing he says is useful. Avoid at all costs.

Stuart is the goat. Absolutely show up to his lectures. Project grading is harsh but I can see where the style requirements are coming from. They really make you think about how to write the most polished code.

The flow of this course is very good. The beginning is easier than 123, with intros to ocmal and recursion, the homework has complete instructions and requirements and is not boring. The homework content is interesting on the case of applying the topics in class and can inspire ideas as a result of the restrictions in language

CSE 390C is basically CSE 143X in C++.

Great Intro to C++ for non-majors, considering most come out of the Java series. Only concern is lectures does not engage you and can sometimes be a snooze fest, but he does catch your attention at keyly critical important details at times, those are when you want to tune in, then refer to lecture notes.

Stuart Reges is not your ordinary instructor, one whose style would afford or encourage sleeping in class.  Instead, Instead, he is one who --- and I write this of a topic that is neither historical nor sociological --- will make the subject "come to life", as it were.  Deprive yourself of his instruction at your loss.  But be prepared to work.

Homework's were generally interesting and not too dificult. Style points will be the bane of your existence. Even though I scored 30% above the median on both exams, I ended the quarter with a 3.7 because I lost like 30+ percent on all my homework from style issues.

Reges gets a bad rap, but he's undoubtedly good at what he does. His lectures are highly engaging and informative, and his assignments and tests are interesting and push your understanding of the material. The grading/curve is definitely harsh, but you get a lot from the course in return. Just don't navigate to his personal website . . .

Reges is a very good professor, though style issues are annoying. His lectures and sections prepare students well. 
Occasionally he feels the need to use pseudo-political tangents. Did not discuss his personal views, which was what made it (somewhat) funny.
To ace the class, you need good problem solving skills, not just familiarity with concepts.
professor kind of weird (political views) but he chill

Reges is a passionate professor who makes lectures engaging, though his grading can be harsh. Using unstuckstudy ai and the free textbook helped me prep effectively for exams. Overall, an intense but worthwhile class.

Reges was a very good professor, he has perfected the art of teaching introductory programming. All of his lectures were easy to understand and digestible. He would always post notes after class, so you would never have to worry about taking them. The grading was very annoying for homework, it's like playing whack-a-mole with new style issues.

Weird political views. Lectures are okay but not THAT helpful. Homework assignments are heavy and difficult, but a good TA (shoutout Darel) will make the class much easier. Homework grading criteria were confusing and you will inevitably lose a ton of "style" points which are very poorly defined/outlined. He has a textbook but it's useless.

Great, interactive lectures make you really understand the material and prepares you great for the homeworks. Overall great lecturer, obviously knows his stuff and has passion for it, which makes the lectures engaging and worthwhile. Homework assignments, while hard, felt meaningful and engaging. Style points on homeworks were harsh though
Vague response for questions. Exams are not responsible

Clearly passionate about the course, he developed it himself and has taught it for a long time. Don't ask about his personal opinions and he probably won't talk about them outside of the first day of class. The class is designed to "weed" people out and it does that effectively, the 12x series is much more laid back and your GPA will be higher.
This professor was not caring. Grading did not have a clear rubric. TA session was not so helpful.

The lectures focused on showing mistakes before the right answer which was very confusing. The grading criteria was never explained in class even though its an intro course. You will without a doubt lose points on homework due to bad comments or the efficiency of your code. This class felt more like a weekly test than a learning experience.

Took the course when I was a freshman. Totally a nightmare for me. Teaching and homework are like two different worlds. Neither the TA nor the professor cares about how students doing. They are more like selecting top students rather than teaching.

Reges is a wonderful and essential professor to have to start off your quarter at UW, at least for me. It is no wonder that he received the Distinguished Teaching Award for UW, an achievement that should not be overlooked. His teaching style is unique; introducing concepts is easy to follow, and his enthusiasm every lecture is super enjoyable!

Head-scratching teaching style where he shows you ten different ways to do something wrong before showing you how something should actually be done. At best it hinders learning, at worst it's simply belittling, and one look at his website would certainly back up the latter. You're much better off not going to lecture and just learning on your own.
Teaching was mediocre. Wasted class time on political tangents.

You get the sense that he is a victim of the YouTube algorithm and fantasizes over becoming some sort of pariah through some epic lawsuit that he wins with his epic smarts. It's not really his fault, but I'd rather just not have to deal with someone like that -- also makes it hard to receive whatever good he does have to teach.
Enjoyed his class!

Stuart is a great lecturer and is clearly very knowledgeable about CS/Java. Definitely worth going to lecture (also recorded on Panopto). The problems on the HW themselves are clearly outlined, but you will inevitably lose style points no matter how hard you try. Recommend practicing for midterms/finals with the old question banks. Great class.
The professor was an incredible lecturer and has a strong command of the subject matter. Highly recommend taking Stuart if you can.
Very good lecturer, has a very clear and effective teaching style. He constantly provides examples and slips in review of previous material to keep you up to date.

Controversial opinions, but the only professor at UW who made me want to watch his lectures. Breaks down complex topics in an understandable manner and truly cares about students' success in the class and beyond.

Aside all the controversy surrounding him, Reges is a great teacher for intro CS. He has lots of energy and is very expressive in lecture, which make them easier to listen to. Homework is weekly, but he/the TA's only release feedback the day the NEXT homework is due, so you get around 12 hours to learn from your mistakes from the previous week.

Over-hated professor in my opinion. Regardless of his views, he's a great lecturer. Has energy and enthusiasm for content being taught. There are assignments every week. Grading on assignments is a pain because a large portion of the grade comes from style. Exams aren't too bad.
DONT TAKE THIS CLASS HE SUCKS

An absolute butchery of curiosity. The course outline is overly concerned with insignificant details that prevent you from seeing the big picture. The homework is so scoped down it leaves no room for creativity.
