This course barely has anything to do with real programming - don't be discouraged from the industry bc you don't like this class
Says he doesn't want to talk about politics in a professional setting and spends the next hour giving an incoherent rant
Stuart is an amazing professor. I think the classes that he degisned are well organized and well cared.

Other than bringing his non-computer science-related views into the classroom, (which I found offensive and inhibited my ability to respect his ideas) his teaching was mediocre and uninspiring.

Will not take again.

If you can take the class with another professor, do so. He's traditional but a respected teacher, and knows what he's doing. However, his personality, class design, and overall vibes in his class will absolutely crush any love you have for CS. UW has better teachers for 14x/12x that will foster a love for coding. The cons outweigh the pros.
Staurt is such an amazing professor. I thought I would be struggling in cse14x but his lectures and textbook saved me. Love his class!

Stuart seems like a nice and chill guy, but the lectures can be a little confusing. The assignments themselves are long, but not too hard, they are challenging at times, but style points are complete B.S. There is absolutely zero reason to show up to the lectures. The sections and TA's are really helpful, and if you need help, go to the IPL.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Stuart may be a genuinely nice guy outside of class, but 142 was nothing short of hell for someone with no programming experience. It seemed everyone around me had coded in high school or had prior experience, and the class is partially graded on a curve. The environment was pretty toxic. Loved my TA though, section was helpful.

143X is basically a 10 credit hour class, so prepare for big workload; 
Stuart is a great professor, if you want to be software eng ready, you should take his class.
Stuart is an amazing professor!

Reges is a very good lecturer, and he gives actual exams so the curve is nice. He is one of the few amazing teachers that doesn't read a powerpoint. Instead he either codes in front of the class or handwrites notes on a document camera, and it's pretty easy to follow along. My advice: handwrite your notes and go to section.

Stuart's lectures was very fun, often looking for student responses during class (which was helped by 143X's smaller class size). He explained concepts very well, often giving clear examples to study when working on assignments. Just be sure to re-read your code 5-6 times over before submitting. I always lost like 3 points to style every assignment
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Reges was such a good lecturer. Concepts were pretty easily understandable for me at least and his clear examples during lectures are why. CSE 143 is a weedout class so although it was hard, Reges does well with teaching the students the content for exams/projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took 143X with Reges and it was one of the single greatest programming experiences of my life. It was incredibly difficult, and sure was a weedout class, but I worked with my TA and classmates and studied hard, and I got the grade I wanted. Reges might not be for everyone, but if you're determined enough and truly love CS, take the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Amazing explanation but the pace is super fast for novice. Lesson is don't take 143X unless you are experienced

Dr. Reges is a really good lecturer. The class was very fast-paced, but he was always able to explain things clearly while still injecting funny anecdotes and insightful analogies. Grading was pretty rigorous, but point deductions were explained extensively on the course website.

CSE 390 was a Seminar where we read a book chapter and then discussed whatever was on Reges' mind that day. I loved it. Truly one of the highlights of my Thursdays. (Former National Chair of the Libertarian party) Professor Reges brought much humor and insight to our class discussions, making them so engaging. Take this class if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great lecturer. Makes concept easy to understand. But... this is a weed-out class and you will most likely not come out of it unscathed. The professor and his method of teaching is 10/10. But the resources there that are available to help you with the homework assignments are limited at best.

He preaches the concept of "you either got it or you don't" and elitism in CSE. "Some" may be able to practice it. Not inspiring words for a student. Also had him fix my Finals score on a problem I actually got right. He fixed it then randomly marked down something else, just so he wouldn't have to go thru the process of correcting my grade. Poor.

Ik me and everyone else here is coming to whine about style points but it's absolutely true. Horrible grading system. Prioritizes stupid formatting stuff over having WORKING code. and to top it all off, the requirements for the style points are super unclear. they're spread out across 4 different documents, some of which are really long :(
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His lecture is really good. He explains well, but his assignment is so hard, and it grades so tough. ;(
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst weedout I've attempted at UW so far. Grading was super picky, I lost so many points because my commenting style wasn't what they were looking for and it was very frustrating

Honestly, I was terrified of this class at first, I took a CS class in high school and I was pretty lost. Professor Reges does an excellent job making sure you understand the material and the structure to his class is very organized. It is a tough and meticulous class, so get ready to rewatch lectures and ask questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Weed-out class. Lectures had hundreds of students. Quiz sections were taught by undergrads with a few quarters coding experience. Assignments were graded extremely harshly. Prof. Reges was kind, knowledgeable, and did his best, but the class was a nightmare. Worst class I took at UW.

CSE390 turned out to be a weekly 2-hour meeting where twenty or so of us sat at a conference table and talked about morality. Prof. Reges really is a character! He was a great storyteller about things like how he got fired from Stanford. Class was entertaining and meaningful, even if it had little to do with computer science.
He explains concepts clearly, and the homework are interesting to do. He never makes you feel bored! If you are a beginner with some interest in Java, then take his class. Recommended!

Ive never taken a programming class before and Stuart really did a good job of explaining concepts that might be hard to understand to beginners. I found his lectures incredibly helpful for the homework like you dont really need to read as long as you watch those and go to lab / section.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Be warned: the grading in this class sucks. Perfectly functional and optimized code is only half of the points on any assignment. The rest comes from subjective, inane and not useful outside of this class "style points". If you are quick to adapt to this you will do fine, but this is time wasted learning something not useful. Good lectures though.

Took this class remotely so there weren't any tests as such. Stuart is an incredible professor & gives amazing examples & explanations. The grading system is honestly so janky and they dock off points for the silliest of things in hw assignments, but I guess that's the case for all weedout classes in UW irrespective of the professor.
very good professor, explain things clearly and very experienced. I am more interested in cs now. an advice: always start hw early! The deduction of points is clearly listed on his hw website.

Practice, practice, practice! Do the lab if you can. And start homework EARLY. Out of all of the coding classes I have taken (Now at UWB doing CS), Stuart was my favorite professor and these classes (14x) taught me the most in the shortest time. Regardless of your grate, you will learn a LOT. It is very challenging though.

Gave great work problems during lectures and hw was fun to work on. Although challenging, the homework was always realistic and if you pay attention in lec they're chill. Ppl complain about point deduction... but tbh you just gotta follow the criteria and be meticulous and careful and they're gonna be okay.

Stuart is literally the worst professor I have ever had in my life. His class doesn't have a grading scale or grading distributions at all! Even the TA in the class doesn't know about how the grades are distributed. If he likes you, you get a 4.0, if he doesn't like you, you are done. RIDICULOUS ! smh
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: wonderful professor, love

Reges was an awesome professor. He used really clear analogies to explain concepts and made sure to answer everybody's questions. The class has an excellent structure and exams are straightforward. Homework is graded very strictly, however.
The class is easy, but that's why he is extremely strict about points. The TAs will deduct your points anyway. If you get 80% of points, you can only get 2.0 for this class. That's ridiculous!

This class was very interesting, but also a lot of work. This class was very hard and requires a lot of discipline and focus to succeed in. Grading on hw is alot more nit-picky than 142 and much harder to wrap your head around. Lectures were always pretty engaging and helpful, and he provides lecture notes, code and supplemental readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I was scared about 143 being taught by him because of what I heard about him. After taking his class and listening to his lectures he is one of the best professors at UW. He will explain complex topics to you so that you fully understand and is very driven to help the student succeed. I really enjoyed his class and having him as a professor
The class is accelerated, and the professor didn't want to waste time explaining things. Skips way too much. This class only works for people who started coding real early.
If he confuses you look up Myers Briggs Typology Indicator. He introduced it to class in one of his CSE 142 lectures that he (stuart reges) is INFP. Truly inspirational.

One of the best professors the University of Washington could offer. I never thought of majoring in CS/CE but I seriously considered it after taking the class. His lectures are very fun, polished, and informational.

Stuart is a veteran in cs, but he is the common student's professor. Makes computer science accessible even if you don't have any previous experience. Lectures are enjoyable, as you don't really need to take notes and he has a good sense of humor. CS 142 is a tough class, but easily manageable if you stay up to speed with lectures.

I would recommend using the book to do practice problems. I did lots of practice it (UW online java practice programming problems) and honestly even though it helps I only got a 3.4 because I honestly wrote messy code in the two exams, and lost points on the hard programming question for both exams. I would advise use the textbook.

I've really enjoyed Reges, he's funny, but most importantly very good at explaining the concepts we are learning. Even though CSE 143X is a fast course, he has made it possible to keep up by being very decisive in his lectures. He also tells you all the important things you need for the tests and homework. I haven't really had to read the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Reges is a very inspiring professor to learn from. Admittedly, I had him for a seminar class and not a 14x course, but he consistently blew our minds with new concepts. He's also a great guy to talk to overall as he's very down to earth despite his legendary status. Take the 143 honors seminar if you can - it will change your life.

Not to hard to get 3.5+ as you do a lot practiceit problems everyday that are related to whats gonna be on the test. Also make sure to practice every single type of question on the test and that you know how to do them. Tests aren't bad as long as you practice ALOT for everything. As for homework just make sure you read the specs carefully.

Getting a good grade is not too hard in this class. His tests are very straightforward and he often recycles a big portion of the questions that are on the test. One nice thing, when I took the class, 50 percent of the final points were questions from his archive. But if you want to do well in his class, you need to study everything on this tests

Reges' lectures were hands down the best lectures I took all my education career (and I'm currently a doctoral student so I had quite a bit) I'm glad he was the one who laid down my programming fundamentals. Very tough grader so my GPA did indeed took a hit but I never would have changed his course for anything else.
I know he is a famous professor and has a good reputation. But his lecture is not as good. A lot of distracting unnecessary analogies. Even Whitaker is better than him. Nice guy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Goes on lots of tangents. You will learn way more from your TA quiz sections than you will with Reges.
Extremely difficult class, grading is also very unforgiving, but actual lectures are high quality, if you pay attention you will understand the content. Textbook is totally not needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Basically, if your not going for CS or a major that requires CSE 142/3, don't take these classes cause they kill your GPA so fast. Reges was fine as a lecturer, he wrote the textbook so he knows his stuff, but to do well u need to ace hw and exams. To ace the exams I recommend practicing over and over again, it helped me get in the 90s every time.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Almost all the code Ive written for the hw works correctly but I keep losing style points. If I have a question regarding style, I just have to guess because the tas arent allowed to answer it. Stuart is a good lecturer but the way the class is organized is unfair and penalizes the student for style even though we cant get help for it
He is pretty pretentious, but he knows what he's talking about for sure.
Excellent lectures. Difficult to talk to outside of class. Only ever attended the first lecture. Panopto is awesome.

Stuart is a great lecturer and makes CS enjoyable, but his grading is very heavily style-based. He's also quite rude and intimidating in person which hindered me from asking questions personally. Exams are reasonable, and as long as you study the material thoroughly you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: very strict message board policy. cannot post too many, cannot ask concepts in textbooks/lectures, cannot ask general questions. my messages been deleted many times and received emails from Stuart several times. so be prepared to go to ipl.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Decent lecturer but a bit overrated in my opinion. Pretty rude and not very accessible too. Grading is mostly based on a series of arbitrary style deductions including things such as use of advanced concept as point deductions. I got a pretty good grade but truly believe the 14x series is poorly designed.
Was a very difficult prof even though I had taken previous java classes at a community college. And I thought the teachers at community college were bad until I met this guy and barely passed...
Great teacher and super based guy - in fact he used to be director of the libertarian party. If you're trying to get into CS you really need to get a high grade in this class. (142/143)

DO NOT SKIP THE DISCUSSION SESSION! That is where you will learn the most and if you don't go, don't expect to get a good grade in the class. Homework is purposefully confusing and if you need help, ask your TA in person (they aren't allowed to say much at the IPL). Stuart is rude and not very helpful. Tests and homework are A LOT harder than 142.

This is a HARD class. Stuart didn't fail to deliver in teaching the class; he's a funny and very interesting person which made lecture enjoyable. I think a few things about the course itself (which Stuart made) could be revamped though. For example, binary trees need to be introduced way earlier for any chance on getting good a final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I've taken a lot of class at Uni but CSE 142 and 143 were the hardest of the bunch. Stuart doesn't want students to succeed as much as he wants them to fail and lose points. Even if your code works perfectly, you are going to lose around 4-5 points just for commenting and the so called "style".
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: The intro CS classes are meant to be weed out classes, so not easy, but definitely a class where effort correlates with grade.  He is one of the best lecturers I have had at UW, but not one of the most approachable.  Style points on the homeworks are a huge grade killer.  I received a decent grade because I did a ton of Practice-It before exams.

I had Stuart for 142, 143, and the 143 honor's discussion. He is an awesome and incredibly knowledgable prof, and funny too. He doesn't put up with nonsense but I really enjoyed all of his classes. Take his honor's section if you can because it was crazy cool getting to know him on a personal level outside of lecture. Great prof would take again

He is the mastermind of CSE 14X is the best lecturer in the series. His lectures are amazing and usually come straight out of the textbook, which make the textbook optional, but a great choice to review his material for homework. Stuart is a love him/hate him professor and most people love him!

If you feel like you are smart take his class, Stuart's lectures are confusing compared to Zorah's. He's consciously trying to confuse you. But tbh, his way of teaching does filter out smart ones. So if you are not that smart but still want to do cse, I won't recommend him, vise versa.

Extremely rude. Knowledgeable, but unapproachable. His class is designed to weed people out and he is an impatient and inconsiderate person. He teaches content well and can keep lectures entertaining, but if you ever have a problem, he is not the person to go to. If you don't understand something right away and need clarification, he's not your guy

I found Reges a tad intimidating which meant I haven't been to a single office hour however his lectures are amazing and easy to follow. His use of Panopto means that if you can't attend the lectures there is no need to fret, just watch it online after. With CSE143, the difficulty is the homework which is graded even more strictly than for 142!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Stuart is a great lecturer, and the homework assignments are actually fun projects. Be prepared to lose a lot of style points. It's a really challenging course but it's worth it. The exams are very predictable and he's very upfront about what to expect if you do old exams.

This is my second class by Stuart and I enjoyed it even more than the first. The homework was brilliant, it breaks you down for a couple over hours before the "aha!" moment when you understand a subject. Stuart is also funny and lets the TAs sneak in little jokes in assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Stuart is an amazing professor who is genuinely unique. He may be more difficult than other professors if you're just starting off with CS, but he has such a unique way of explaining concepts.
Interesting lectures. Exams seem to be not very hard. You only need to practice for a little while then u should be fine. But homework assignments can be tricky. Be careful.

Stuart is the bomb. The class is NOT easy, it's like a weed wacker for the absurd amount of students aiming for Computer Science here.   Stuart's lectures are funny, he adds references to shows I like (wubalubadubdub!) and there is a ton of practice material for the exams.   Get ready to lose some style points in this class, and for good reason!

The lectures are clear although they can stagnate a little due to the thorough explanations and attention to fine details. The tests and homework are difficult to get high marks ensuring that students have to study. Unfortunately, Prof. Reges can be a little intimidating but be certain that his explanations are exactly what will appear on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Stuart is an entertaining guy-- his lectures are interesting enough to keep you awake and he does a good job at introducing hard Java topics to complete beginners. The only issue was the grading system used for the homework which sometimes seems rather ridiculous. Overall, I learned a lot in Stuart's class and really recommend taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's great with "showing" the lecture material, but other than that he waste too much time with jokes and lacks professionalism. On the other hand, the grading criteria and homework polices need to be revised because those aspects just made the 142 course too tedious and irritating. If you really need to take CSE142 the. get a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Reges himself is really funny. He can waste time from time to time talking about facts irrelevant to the course, but it can be interesting to some people. The problem is the TA selection and the ambiguity in the grading. The grading is really harsh on homework, but on the exams it's really fair. The TAs are undergrads so they can be incompetent.

Professor Reges is a great professor! His lecture is always interesting and the knowledge is showed extremely clear. He often said analogies and jokes in lecture. And after lecture he will answer students' questions if you come to ask him.

Let me be clear on this: I think Stuart is a good teacher. My main issue is really with how the course is designed.  I think that having 50% of your homework grade based on arbitrary "style" points is ridiculous and seems to be an excuse to create grade deflation because of how competitive UW's computer science department is.

Professor Stuart Reges is a very knowledged and humorous lecturer, who puts lots of effort into his lectures. What would better it is if he chose better TAs. Several times now, I have been return mis-graded homework, which is only corrected after many communication attempts. It is unfortunate that my fate is in the hand of a TA that doesn't care.
Stuart is hilarious! Definitely one of my favorite professors. You'll do fine if you go to lecture and do the work. My only complaint is that most of his analogies are about fridges.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He tries to be funny in a very elementary way and it doesn't really work for him. A lot of times, he spends unnecessary time explaining things that irrelevant to the course, then rushes toward the end of the lecture. Other than that, he's a pretty great teacher as far as introductory java goes.

Best lecturer I've ever had. If you go to class and pay attention, he explains things so clearly that you won't even need to read the textbook. If you understand it, the homework doesn't take too long but is graded pretty strictly. He's pretty good about taking questions but the class is so big that going to the IPL for help is a better bet.

very clear in every details, especially in CSE142 pay attention to each homework from the beginning to the end, every parts are equally significant for doing well in this course do practise-it (an website for online practising) before exams, or you will fail good luck

Lectures are pretty decent; never need the textbook if you attend. Grade is penalized hard for basic mistakes, especially in 143. Sometimes, homework "style" points seem arbitrary, and you don't learn about them until you already lost points. Homework assignments aren't the worst but also don't help much; Practice-It is essential.
Best CS lecturer at uw

Homework is graded on correctness and "style points," which are a set of undocumented rules you learn only through losing points. TAs are not permitted to help you determine what is and is not good style, so don't bother asking. These rules often contradict real-world usage. Expect to lose at least 10% of your homework grade to this arbitrary bull.
Lectures are fun! Best professor
Although he's a nice guy, he refuses to agree with what other students have to say. it's his way or the highway.

Hated his class. Just got a really bad vibe off of this guy. Got an A+, but that was just because I knew all the stuff beforehand and did a lot of reading into the subject. He was pretty rude to me a couple of times during office hours - stopped going to him for questions after that.

He teaches the intro level the way it should be taught. As someone who didn't have any prior programming experience I felt comfortable with the difficulty and expectations of the course. Everyone should definitely go to lectures because he gives hints for tests.

Make sure you sign up for the labs (CSE 190). Do Practice-It problems, probably every day. Do at least a few programming questions/week from past exams/practice exam handouts. Do this by replacing in the CSE142 website _CURRENTYEAR_CURRENTSEASON_ with 15au, 14au, 15wi, 13wi, etc. Also do the future homework assignments while doing the current one
Really interesting teacher

DO NOT, I repeat, DO NOT take this class for fun. He says this class is designed for students who have never done coding before, but this class is VERY hard. Hardest class I've ever taken and I don't recommend it to anybody. The curve is HORRIBLE. If you want to kill your GPA, go ahead and take this class! TONS of work for only 4 credits.

The best way to excel in this class is by practicing minimum 5 problems of Practice it everyday. I did not do great on the midterm but started practicing everyday for the final and did really well on it. Other than that he is a great lecturer. He has a tendency of doing tough concepts right at the end though.

Hwk gets time consuming as the quarter goes on, so make time for it!  It was  my first time programming and I was very confused at the beginning which is why I got a bad grade on the midterm and an average grade over all. Quiz section taught me more than Stuart for sure. Wasn't that interested in the subject at first but now I love it!

Glad I signed up for the lab (1-credit CSE 190). You can lose very easy points for the homework because of "style points". Stuart Reges uses analogies so you should read the book and do practice-it problems BEFORE attending the lecture. Also you should go to Autumn 2015's CSE 142 website to do the homework 1 and 2 BEFORE day 1 of class. Hard exams.

Stuart is a great guy. Just expect to spend a lot of time with hw. You will stress out about hw if you care about your grade because you can not fck up simple things or it will hurt you like a mthrfckr. Also, there is no curve at least for my quarter. I recommend that you prepare to take two easy courses along this course especially4 1st qrter

I loved Reges and his class. You don't really interact with him, but with the TA's. Regardless, Reges has a passion for code and he brings it to lecture. He tries to make you love CS just as much as he does, and it so shows. His assignments are difficult, but fascinating, and the structure of the class is excellent. Highly recommended!

This class has some students with java experience,  "hares". Make sure you do practice-it problems before each lecture, as the metaphors may help - or not. Quiz sections depend on your TA, some are good some are more useless. Sign up for the CSE 190  lab- handy when you need help with some conceptual questions. Lectures recorded in CSE 142 website.
He's a funny guy. Google him ;p

He's really cold and when you're in for office hours, it feels like he wants you to leave.  Lectures were okay, pretty basic stuff. Not much to say really; he just gives lectures and leaves. His analogies are a hit or miss. Oh and he sometimes makes inappropriate jokes or just passes comments that are rude.

Dr. Reges is pretty fantastic. CSE 142 is designed for people who have never touched computer programming before, and he does an amazing job of teaching from the ground up. He usually stays a while after lecture to answer any questions. His lectures are essentially quoted from the textbook, or vice versa, so both are great ways to learn.

Great lecturer overall. Before taking 142, I had no idea about how to program but I felt that Stuart walked me through the basics of Java very well. His cookies are very good so good that I think that he bakes them with weed ;)

Lectures are good. Lecture slides provided online are extremely helpful, especially if you miss a day. There were weekly homework assignment, moderately hard for people new to coding. Class was fun and challenging. Even if you're not a computer science major, I recommend trying this class. Textbooks are useful, but not necessary.
The best lecturer ever in my whole life!

He is a GREAT professor! Lectures are clear and interesting. But coding is more of your own work. You need a lot of practice to get a high grade on this course. Attendance are not mandatory but you need to go to them to have a better understanding. Overall it's great but it is really hard for an intro-level course. Have to put in lots of efforts.
Awesome professor. Do the work, study for his tests, and you can definitely get a good grade.

Reges is hands down the best professor I've taken a class with at the UW. I had no programming experience before taking 142 but by attending lecture and doing homework I got an A in the course. Reges has great analogies that really helped me understand a lot of the topics covered (wish I could say the same for my 143 prof). If you take CS, Reges!
Great teacher you'll love the class. Assignments  aren't too hard it's mainly style that counts.
Best 14x professor out there.

I never took a CSE class in high school so the material was entirely new to me.  I had to do a lot of reading and practice problems to keep up with everyone else and the pace of the class.  However, during lecture Reges is AMAZING!  He's very clear, has a sense of humor, and is passionate about the topic.  Learn to debug your programs.

Reges is a veteran prof and one of the best in the field. He designed pretty much the whole CS curriculum and he is the best prof you can have for 142143. His lectures are absolutely amazing and helpful for both tests and homework. 142 is a weedout class so grading is artificially hard, pay attention to style. Go to IPL and talk to TAs
Great professor, loves his jobs and shows in lectures. Get a head start on the homework, don't wait until two days prior to start.

Awesome lecturer, he is clearly passionate about teaching this course and has excellent explanations. The grading is very specific and unbending, double check all your assignments, do practice-it (the textbooks online practice website) and you'll do fine. Highly recommend the class.

Stuart is an amazing prof. He is really excited about CS and uses amazing non-technical analogies to explain techie concepts. He really sets you up for success in hw during lecture, so go to class! The textbook is essentially the same, & if you want to do well on tests, start early, do Practice-it the entire quarter & take lots of practices tests.

Great class! It's not too hard if you put a little effort into learning the subject matter. Homework can be frustrating because if you do not do it their way, you'll lose points, but you can ultimately understand why they grade it that way.

I never learned anything from going to lectures that my TA's didn't explain more clearly in section. And his use of metaphors was ridiculous and some of them made no sense. He lectured more on the metaphors than the actual subject.

This class with Reges was amazing! Everything was explained very clearly and the lectures always captured my attention. You can tell that he is passionate about his field and I've never felt more interested in majoring in CS than after this class.I really enjoyed taking this class, although some of the grading on the assignments was kind of harsh.
Absolutely hilarious lecturer. Good at explaining concepts in a funny way. Really helpful. I enjoyed his lectures.

Professor Reges is very funny in class and keeps the topics interesting so that the class won't get too technical to a point that is boring. He gives metaphor that makes programming really easy to understand(though some of them are cheesy). Some say he is a harsh grader, but if you pay attention in lecture and go to quiz sections,easy A.

Decent teacher and helpful lecture. However... he has horrible clarity with assignments and is a cold, sarcastic (fill in lots of derogatory adjectives here) person. Not a nice human being and a egotistical (more bad words).

Stuart is great! He really likes what he is doing and that really shows. His assignments are just amazingly fun puzzles to do every week. I really appreciated his non-technical examples. For CSE majors, pay attention to the complexity stuff because I regret not listening as much. Go to the IPL and do the honors 14x section if you can!!

A very good professor. He explains everything clearly. One very good tip to study for midterm and final: go over ALL old midterms and finals that he provide and understand them, because there's a high chance that they will appear on your test (8 of 10 questions were reused for Winter 2014 final exams)

Stuart's teaching style is unparalleled to any other teacher I have taken, but like what most have said, his grading is HARSH. It's hard enough to interpret what exactly he is asking in his homework, but he barely ever tells you any efficiency necessities to keep in mind. Overall though, I liked the class, each week was like solving a new puzzle.
Very interesting and fun class.

Class material is pretty easy, especially if you have learned programming before BUT the standards for grading are riducously high!! This is a weed out class, only a small percent will make good grades. Stuart's a great lecturer but not very helpful outside of class, kind of cold personality. Nonetheless don't be discouraged fight for your grades!!

He's a great lecturer and teaches the material with passion and clarity. However, he tries to weed out too hard, often in bad ways. You *will* lose points on homework for style and his tests are structured like so: 70% of it is easy and the last 30% is meant to make most people fail. Note: he reuses most of his material from past quarters.
Stuart does a great job explaining how to do the homework and how to prepare for the tests. The only difficult part is not losing style points on the homework, which can be challenging at times.

Stuart is a great professor! He's enthusiastic and makes the interesting material even more fun to learn. The homework isn't  bad at all, I usually finished in 1-2 hours. Easily my favorite professor and course at UW!

Stuart was a very good professor. In section X we moved very quickly through the material, but I think Stuart did a very nice job, overall, of getting the information across. My biggest piece of advice for this course is to put a good amount of effort into the homework, because it will help your grade at the end if you are not a great test-taker.

Overall, I thought the class was easy and well-paced for those who know little or nothing of coding.  He uses non-technical analogies to help with tough concepts and his in-class examples are VERY helpful (esp for the homework and exams).  If you miss class, read the book; they pretty much go hand-in-hand.  The message board is useless though.
Best professor I've had! His class never gets dull!!
Great professor. I loved going to lecture. Material was interesting and well paced for a student who had never been exposed to programming before.
Great intro lecturer, coming in with no experience he's great at explaining exactly what you need to know. Don't miss lecture though otherwise you will have to work to make up points

For this class, each HW will consume about 3 - 5 hours and he'll give you a week long. Exams are straight forward with questions similar to quiz sections. Book is useless since everything you need will need will be posted online. He is very clear in explaining the lecture and what he is expecting you to do. Good professor, recommended.
Excellent Professor

I am taking Stuart's class right now. If you have never programmed before, it's going to take you way out of your comfort zone. CSE is whole new level of thinking. But that doesn't mean you shouldn't take the class. Stuart loves teaching and he's funny as well. He tries to be as clear as possible. Homework took me about 3-4 days to complete btw.

No advantage to go to lectures; can't control class, often goes on long, irrelevant tangents, etc.  All of his material is recycled from past years, which makes studying easier, but his effort and enthusiasm was really disappointing.

Seriously, the class is easy. That being said, you get a pretty clear vibe that he doesn't care about the class very much. Test questions are reused, and it feels like the entire class is ran by the head TA. His lectures are pretty clear, but I feel that he goes a bit slow.

Best professor I have had yet at the University of Washington. I'm never bored in class, never have to read the textbook because of his great lessons and explanations, and he always has a good joke or two

I LOVE Stuart Reges!! He is honestly the most enthusiastic professor that I have ever had and he makes me want to go to class more often than not. I have never felt this way about any course I have taken in the past and I am so unbelievably glad that I have gotten the chance to be taught by this man. Twice, even! CSE 142 & CSE 143! Thank You!!
Genius of analogy
I hope I fail this class so I can take it again and again
One of my favourite professors so far. His lectures basically give you everything you need to know and has a great sense of humor.
I hated programming before taking this class.  I am now pursuing computer science.  Enough said.

Super clear, explain things very well. Love his analogies. Class is engaging. Wants the students to think the same way as he do, which is sometimes not very good. Usually reuse worksheet problems on the exam. Overall, Great professor.

I'll put it this way, CSE 142 was the hardest class I've ever taken at UW. Other math and science classes went reasonably well for me. There is a catch, if you find your brain is wired to code, this will be a very fun class. If not, it will be brutal. Unfortunately, as far as the class went, I was one of the few who didn't quite ever get it.

Stuart was a great professor, one of my favorites so far. He isn't easy, but no CS class truly is. What he does bring to the table is his wonderful talent for providing clarity in his explanations of concepts in class. Don't skip.  The lectures are definitely worth attending for his good use of examples and occasional witty moments.

Reges was my first CS teacher, and after finishing the 2 introductory class from him I became a CS major. He is clear and gets occasional laughs from the class. The workload is not too heavy, and no prior programming language is required for 142. Recommend.

This is a hard class. I took AP Computer Science in high school but opted for a swimming class after the first semester. Computer science is a difficult subject. However, Reges is very clear when he explains things and this makes the class much easier than it could be otherwise. Highly recommended.

Great professor who's very passionate about CSE. He's pretty amusing and keeps you awake. You don't technically have to be "naturally born with talent", you just need to able to work independently and spend time to understand what you learned and how to apply it.

Awesome lecturer, shows great interest in subject and excellent use of analogies and examples make is possible for anyone to understand. I don't buy the "if you're not naturally gifted at CS you'll do bad," crap. To succeed in this kind of class, you have to put in a lot of time outside of class.

AWESOME PROFESSOR! Interesting, clear, concise, gives excellent analogies and explanations. Posts clear lecture notes and practice exams online. Class is curved so easiness has nothing to do with professor, so its hard to get a high grade. TA-led quiz sections and out-of-class practice crucial to success. Really anal on how homework is graded.

Yes, the class is hard and he is a genius. Yes, he's arrogant but he deserves it (totally). Yes, he's involved with MDA or whatsoever. I mean... Who cares. If u always expect a perfect teacher who is humble, gives reasonable exams, n have no controversy, u're living in the never land or u're a twilight fan...

This class is pretty hard if you're a nonmajor and don't think like a computer scientist, though through no fault of Stuart's. The guy is nothing short of a genius and teaches very well. I just found the content very difficult while many of my peers breezed through the class.
Extremely precise and engaging; exactly what a CSE professor should be

Reges is awesome!!  He cares about what he's teaching, and he loves teaching.  There is more than ample practice and advise offered, all you have to do is make use of the resources and you should do fine. I loved the programming assignments, even if at times they could be frustrating.  Both cse 142 & 43 were great w/ Reges.

A great professor! Reges is a genius and he is well aware of that, so I see why some people might mistake geniusness for arrogance. He is strict with grading, however if you attend lectures and sections do homework you have nothing to worry about! Also, his lectures are usually very interesting and he is very passionate about teaching!
Probably my favorite professor at UW so far. Not an easy class, the tests were pretty hard, but I learned so much, and Regis had an entertaining way of teaching! I loved this class!

He is an amazingly talented professor and pure genius. He knows what he is talking about. Sadly he is most of the time not very helpful to students. I have numerous occasions where he acted arrogant. He also expects everyone to be as smart as he is so the classes are hard. Take this class if you have natural talent.

The GOOD: entertaining lectures, good explanations, and he starts on-time and won't waste you're time in class. The BAD: Even if you are generally a good student, the tests are stupid hard. As in HARD. It's not enough to read the book, read lecture notes, and do the homework--you need natural talent. Welcome to UW.

Stuart is a boss, I highly recommend him whether you have prior CS experience or not. I took the class originally to fulfill a prereq but grew to the love the subject. The material can be tricky, but if you put sufficient effort and attend lectures/sections you can get a good grade, even if you've never wrote a line of code in your life.

the teacher is very good however if you arent for programming then you have to work very hard... i took cse the second time and i didnt do that good. I think im just not for programming... i spend like 2-3 days to finish the hw.. the exam is pretty clear.. he lets you know the format of the exam.. i recommend to take reges class

I find this class hard. It's incredibly time consuming if you can't write codes in your sleep. This is the kind of class that either your brain is wired for it or it's not. If you have time or like writing codes, go for it
I had never programmed before, so I really appreciated his clarity and straightforwardness. He's also really funny in an awkward way =] I highly recommend this class.
Good teacher for those who had never even attempted to program before.

Crystal clear, articulate, and approachable to discuss concepts. His exams are always fair - though they will test you under high time pressure. He has a good knack of explaining why a theory or operation is relevant and where it fits into larger perspective - which really helps you think. Be prepared to work a bit in his class, though.

I had Reges for 142 and 143.  His lectures were pretty laid back but very useful.  If you attend his lectures, you don't need to read the book much (although it's def still a good idea, esp. complexity and some other chapters).  Some exams have a lot of time pressure, though, depending on your ability to think on your feet, so beware.

One of the best lecturers I've had; he's hilarious, interesting, and great at providing analogies of difficult concepts. Very nit picky on homework though, especially in intro classes, and even for silly things like comments. Tests are tough, but follow a predictable format. Ensure you are proficient with exam type questions. Final = 40% of grade.

I've had him for 143 and 341.  Best professor I've ever had.  Clear, articulate, prepared; he types up his class notes for you, and goes into special topics to keep it interesting.  It's hard work, but worthwhile.  Note that in his intro courses the syllabus he gives you shows the *minimum* percentage to get a grade; often 85% gets a 3.5.

Generally agreeable guy in person and a pretty good lecturer. I had him for 143 and Stepp for 142, I prefer Reges. Assignments are hard, but if you go to lecture, there's nothing in them that you shouldn't get.
Stuart is a nice guy! :-) :-0 ;-)

Interesting in lecture, absolute jerk in person. Don't even bother going to his office hours. His grading is very tough and though I am an excellent student, he expects prior knowledge/you know what you're doing. His assignments are tough, but TAs help. If you can get Marty Stepp, take this class from him. Awful teacher and person. Good luck.

Very clear lecturer and a very understandable textbook. This class is effing hard though. You have assignments every week that take forever and the midterm and final are very hard. Of course I may just be retarded, but I thought this was one of the hardest classes I've taken. I guess it just depends on whether you get programming or not.

Reges is good with language.  His lectures and textbook are both very good.  You don't need prior programming experience, Stuart assumes you know nothing and explains everything.  I didn't have programming experience and did better than many who did.  Grading is easy if you adhere to assignment guidelines and do at least 3 practice midterms/finals.
very hard class. the assignments are difficult. you must score above a 90% on everything in order to get an A. Confusing material. not recommended unless you need it for credit
You need to pay attention and know what the hells going on otherwise the last 40-45 minutes of class are going to be useless.

Awesome professor - very clear and engaging. However, must warn students about the difficulty of the class. You pretty much have to score 92%+ consistently on all homework/midterms/etc. in order to even be close to an A.

I totally wish I had him as a teacher back in AP Computer Science in high school...Stuart is a wonderful teacher and his textbook Back to Basics is probably the best Java textbook EVER. Lecture is very engaging with plenty of interesting tidbits to keep you interested (Asciimation Star Wars, Knuthian hexidecimal dollar etc). MUST TAKE.

The assignments will challenge you weekly, mainly with the picky little details, but they're very doable if you attend quiz sections and glance through your book. The class is east to get a B in, but difficult to get an A in. Stuart is very clear in lectures and is a clever, entertaining speaker.
Class was well structured and covered necessary material in a clear fashion. Class was enjoyable to attend.
back to basics rocks.

Especially good at explaining the homeworks, which is good because they are pretty hard.  Very good at describing concepts, though I sometimes feel fuzzy on the details.  Has an annoyingly good ear - he often shushes the class when the noise level is fairly quiet for a hall with 200+ people in it.

Stuart is a wonderful. He already knows that ~10% of the class already knows the material, so he much of  his time lecturing to us students who are new to this. It is apparent when he covers a new topic; rather than breezing through material in an hour, he usually spends an entire week to ensure that the class understands the underlying idea. <3

He is great at teaching the material...unfortunately that is not enough to get you through the class. The assignments are difficult as well as the exams. Help is very limited, since asking for help is generally discouraged (and depending on the type of help, prohibited) due to his strict policies. Lowest grade I've received in any course.
great teacher, just look out for the TA's.

His lectures were very informative and interesting. I never needed the book(in fact I didn't buy one). The homework assignments sometimes take a while, be prepared. For the midterm, time was the primary issue. The grading is a bit on the harsh side. Do as many of the practice exams as possible. Enjoyable class, great professor. Highly recommended.
Does a really good job teaching.  Always attend his lecture if you want to do well!
Great teacher, really knows his subject.
Midterm was ridiculously graded harshly.  The homework assignments you can almost guarantee you will get below a B if you don't spend over 24+ total hours on it.

Hard class, if you are new to Java programming this class is difficult. Stuart really knows what he teaches but he knows it too well that sometimes he leaves students behind while catering to students who can write code in their sleep. He didn't seem to mind that over 1/2 the class failed the midterm. Midterm is a killer, final is not too bad.
hard

An excellent teacher, at least for those with an interest in the field (and quite possibly for those without one; I couldn't say). Not only is he very interested in whether or not the students learn, but he's excellent at helping them to do so.

Lectures are very interesting and well thought out, his advice and tips are great, homework is also interesting and fun.  His midterms are difficult because of time mainly (beware).  Reges really knows his stuff also.  =)  Overall, his class is pretty laid back and just fun!
Awesome guy.

Very clear, very fun, hard grader, VERY hard to get a great grade, but easy to get a "pretty good" grade. Many hate him, many like him. One thing's for sure, however.. He WILL keep your interest in class and I believe he has influenced a lot of people to become CSE majors. He needs to be more approachable outside of class, however.
Good man

Amazing lecturer. I'd recommend him in a heartbeat. I especially recommend his honors section, should he offer it-- its an entertaining group discussion on topics ranging from Qubic to the Halting problem to RSA Encryption. His lectures are entertaining, his assignments are presented well, though for help outside of class, TAs have more time.
great instructor, lectures always entertaining
No Comments
absolutely horrible teacher!!
He does not communicate well. Do not go to him for help, you will have better luck with your TA.

Reges is one of the best lecturers out there.  He can explain complex topics in such a way that they seem intuitive (and he uses liberal amounts of humor to lighten the mood).  Unlike some others here, I found him to be easy to talk to outside of lecture, so long as you don't ask questions that are designed to agitate or second guess him.

Very good lecturer and funny in the classroom. A total jerk outside the classroom. He was downright rude to me when I asked an honest question during office hours. The class was too easy and not challenging in any way. [yawn]
Absolutley rediculous. listen in class and it's easy. And his metaphors are hilarious, though not intended to be so.
total **** outside of class help. funny in class.

This class was frustratingly easy, because the teacher gave away all of the hard parts of the homework in class, stopping us from having to think about it ourselves.  Since it was graded on a curve, this evened out the grade across the class and stopped the smarter students from coming to the top of the class.  Good for people who get bad grades.
Good teacher in class, but never ask him for help outside of class because he is a complete ass and is extremely arrogant.
HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE!!!!!!

This man is without a shadow of a doubt one of the best professors I've ever had! He had a good sense of humor and made learning fun. He had these analogies that made our assignments easier to approach. He is the man!!
Knows the material very well, very interested and enthused about it. Very clear teacher. The class is not easy, but he is a very good professor.
i <3 the star trek jokes! :D

He was too helpful and too clear. He told us step by step how to do each hw, giving away the "challenging" parts so we didn't get a chance to think about it for ourselves. That unfairly evened out the grade. It was more of a high school class than a college class.
Lots of Star Trek jokes. Funny guy, very smart and enthusiastic.
If you have any prior CS knowledge, this prof will be extremely easy. He's very clear, though, and very knowledgable. Definately recommended
Interesting to listen to and all in all a good teacher.

This man drove me nuts the whole time that i was taking the class.  i had never taken a computer class before so he didn't make things easier because he lectured like we all knew what we were doing... and then there is that sad excuse for a textbook that we have... terrible.

One of the UW's best professors.  He's taken a course (CSE 142) that is renowned as being difficult and turned it into an enjoyable class that anyone can take and do well in without killing themselves in the process.  Students should fight to have him as a professor (rather than have someone else).

He's a cool professor that would talk non-stop from the beginning to the end.  His sense of humor keeps most of us up during the 9:30 am class.  The lecture are mostly interesting and easily understood.

Extremely engaging, always keeps the class interested. Explains material so well that a 4-year-old could understand it, but without dumbing it down. Best teacher I've had so far (in 2 years). Had him for CS 245 (Intro to Discrete Math) at U of Arizona.
Hey is a really nice (from what I can tell) and funny guy. He is a real geek at heart and makes lots of references to Star Trek.

He is extremely helpful and always excited to talk to students.  At least this quarter the midterm and final are open book and open notes, and he does not make them extremely difficult.  I personally have had no prior programming experience and am understanding what he is teaching.

Professor Reges is new to UW as of this quarter (Autumn 04), but has been great so far. He is humorous, gives out some interesting homework problems, and I can tell he is quite good at communicating to non-technical people, much better than me for sure. His midterms can be tricky, watch out.

He is supposed to be the reorginizer of intro cs classes and is doing a decent job in cse 142.  I does not teach theory and vocab, just programming basics.  Becuase of the wide range of experience of the people in the class, it is hard to say if it is easy or not.  Just depends on the person.

Very funny individual, just not the greatest teacher. Podcasts are irrelevant to watch other than the first week or two. The TA teaches better than the professor. Midterms are both easy, but everybody struggles on them. Final is much harder.

I recommend not taking his class unless you are ready to learn everything by yourself. I did that because I didn't understand anything taught in lectures or podcasts. Quiz sections were helpful but really really understanding every single problem on practice exams and quizzes was the most helpful by far because they're very similar to the actuals.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took in spring 2024. Cold calls, very un-welcoming. Can be rude and disrespectful to students

not the worst, but his style of teaching is fast-paced. he's funny and will help you out, but exams were really tough. pay attention to the lectures and in-class worksheets, and i highly recommend utilizing the worksheets in particular when studying. if accounting is not your strong suit, i would not recommend taking this professor.

Flipped classroom model is time-consuming and results in dry lectures (sometimes feels like he's just reading numbers off an answer key). Tests are sometimes similar to practice exams but involve a lot of "mental gymnastics" designed to trip you up, despite the content itself being somewhat manageable. Daily pop quizzes are doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You'll learn more from studying for the exams.
Alot of out of class note taking required to succeed

Currently studying for his final right now. I ggenuinely thinkif I had any other proffessor i would not be so lost. This guy expects you to know all the material before you walk into class! So then what is the point of the lecture?? I hope he reads these to know how hes impactinc his students in a bad way. This guy has passed his expiration date.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He just reads off slides. Doesn't explain concepts. Expects to learn everything in the 1hr podcasts before class. dont take with this professor if you want foster admission

he is super lecture heavy and it feels like a flipped classroom where you watch podcasts at home where he goes over the basics of each problem and in class he just works through problems. Honestly didnt really go to lectures bc hes a boring lecturer (attendance is mandatory). extremly test heavy with some very difficult problems.
very lecture heavy.
All he does is read off the slides. DO NOT take him if you want a good grade!! Genuinely the worst experience with a teacher at UW. Khoth ya aire

If you want to get into foster DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. he dosent know how to teach and all he does is read answers off the screen. also, he expects you to watch a 2 hour long lecture/podcast before you come to class and you you have a pop quiz at the start and end of each class that impacts your grade. He is genuinly not good. DO NOT TAKE HIM.

Over time, I actually could bear Professor Suneel; however, if you don't study and put in the effort outside of class, you will not pass. He's a tough professor because he doesn't lecture and instead works through problems with you to help you understand the concepts. The grading on exams is extremely harsh. Attendance is required.
Worst accounting professor I've had.
Class structure is so unorganized. Cold calls, and adds pop quizzes in the middle of the quarter. Gives minimal prep for the exam.
DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS (esp if you're trying to get a good grade)

If you work hard enough, you can get an excellent grade in this class. The professor is very professional and enthusiastic about his lectures. The cold calling can be tough but it really does make you focus. His class was truly my favourite uw class so far.

Makes u do the lecture before class in vids, which r basically reading off his completed worksheets (he gives u the worksheet but incomplete??). Class is j problems but instead of explaining he reads off answer key. 2 pop quizzes each class, attendance mandatory; basically self-studied. DON'T TAKE IF U CARE ABT GPA - esp. foster prospectives, RUN !

I took ACCTG 215 and 225 with this professor and had a great experience. The exams and quizes are challenging and grading is strict, but he values student progress and effort and might give extra credit for that. Attendance are graded by pop quizzes. He's engaging, funny, and I learned a lot. Highly recommend if you're ready to be challenged.

First class required watching his podcast, then he rushed into problems with no intro. Pace was so fast and note-taking discouraged, he kept going even if we were lost. Final exam was suddenly switched in-person 1.5 weeks before, unrelated to mock, because he thinks AI gives better answers. Honestly, AI explains concepts more clearly than he did.

Prof Suneel was very good at explaining concepts and all the learning is done in class. As long as you focus you will get a good grade. Can be tough because he cold calls on people. If you watched the podcast and go to every lecture class is not that challenging.

Prof Suneel's teaching style was doing practice problems in class that are likely to be similar to the exam. I found this helpful for studying especially. If you do the work studying the right material, you will do well. He is so funny during lectures and really breaks things down for students to understand.

He was such an entertaining professor and I enjoyed going to class even though the content was hard. A lot of the lectures are spent working through practice problems rather than only concepts. I would recommend Suneel!

Suneel was a great professor and lecturer. He talks like he cares about the class, will help with exam grades if you show improvement, and is helpful with the course material overall. Watch the podcasts and do the homework. Only downside is that lectures are example-heavy, so if you don't watch the podcast beforehand you'll be lost on the content.

Being a 3.88 GPA student, this was the WORSE professor I've ever had. He doesn't teach. He just points at numbers on an answer key and just says "add this + then you get this". He doesn't explain where numbers come from and he talks slower than Flash from Zootopia. Only benefit is quizzes/tests are similar to practice ones. Basically self taught.

Graded homework on effort. 2 exams, gave a bonus for improvement, very similar to in-class problems/HW. Pre-class "podcasts" to watch before lectures. Pretty approachable. Presented content well IMO, class is mostly solving questions together. Does cold call if no volunteers. No 10-minute break

Professor Upda is an interesting professor. He has a considerable amount of industry experience, and is funny in class, but often singles students out. Attendance is mandatory, and he will stop lecture to scold students for being late or not paying attention, and frequently cold calls. Exams are unrelated to lecture material and speed based.

had prof Suneel for 225 and now taking 311 with him, and the only reason why I decided to take 311 with him was because of how funny he is. Got a 4.0 in 225 and now doing a lot worse in 311 :( but I could go on forever talking about how wonderful he is. Tests are doable, but unnecessarily long (for both classes). 10/10 would definitely recommend.

She's good at explaining concepts, but don't just rely on the lecture or even the problem sets to do well on the tests, they're definitely a little bit trickier. But there aren't a lot of surprises and it's super straight forward for the most part. It's also one of the easier Econ classes, so overall can't do too bad even if you don't like her.

lecture slides posted, no attendance, no recordings. Very little HW, and graded on completion. midterm+final is basically ur grade. Midterm not similar to practice test, moderately hard. Those complaining about her accent, it is fine if you've talked to anyone who isn't white in the last 20 yrs of ur life. Nice prof, study hard for exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awful oral English. Really hard to understand what she's trying to say. Poor expression and wordy exam questions. Yet the class contents are clear.
The class is hard, but she is a pretty good professor.
She is very patient. Her explanations are good and she always posts slides which helps since the lectures are packed with information. Overall a great class and a great professor.
She teaches 1+12 in class, and tests you derivatives of function...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Chinese Prof  Tough Exam. Lecture notes are not hard, but exam questions are much much much harder!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: hard to understand her english
lots of reading for me atleast but his lectures never bored me, great teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Basically just copies his lectures from the textbook and adds a few personal stories. I don't feel like I learned anything in the class, just learned how to skim the textbook for important things to add to my cheat sheet.
Great dude!
Tayfun is so amazing. He make every concept very easy to understand. I learned so much in this class. Best professor in UW, no question.
Love the classes and his stories. They are very interactive and engaging, truly learned a lot about project management and the final project wraps everything up very perfectly!

He is a great professor and kind person. Strong IT background and interesting life stories. Strict with deadlines. Content is technical, but that's normal for IT class. I graduated years ago, he still help me with job and found me a mentor. He really care. I feel lucky.
This professor is on point. Class material is fresh and keeps us engaged. Grading is clear and consistent. When you email, they respond with respect. A real one.

Tayfun is chill - this class is more like a PM class more then it is technical. Class is case base, a final and a group project. I overall enjoy his lectures, a bit of a comedian himself. Also pretty knowledgeable as he worked in tech / pm industry.

Good teacher/ guy. Haven't talked to anyone with bad things to say. He warns you but he's right, do some reading even though exams are open note. Half our class didn't finish the first exam in time. Labs get increasingly and suddenly harder. First few are misleadingly easy. Wish he taught more classes because I'd love to take him again.
Tayfun make class very easy to understand, final not cumulative, and he teach many useful things

Tayfun is THE professor you want at UW Foster, no question. His teaching is on point, and he really cares about his students. He'll go the extra mile to help you out. If you can take IS300 with him, don't even think twice. Just do it!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tayfun is really one of the kindest professor I know. He reply email so fast, even midnight! Class start very easy but become hard later, so don't relax too much. Exam is tough but open book, so time management very important. Good intro to Information Systems. I highly recommend him!

Everything is open note, so no one really studies for quizzes and exams. The only grade differentiator is the group presentation at the end. Curve is high bc everything is easy. He's a funny guy, but so boring. That's probably because the content isn't very interesting. Everything in this class felt like busy work.

He was so nice and funny! I took his IS 300 class and the quizzes, midterm, and final were all open book open note. I hated the lab assignments we had in this class every week, they were the worst part of the class. Since everything was open-book I would zone out during class a lot.

Tayfun is a solid professor. He provides clear grading criteria, and his assignment schedule is designed to reduce finals week stress. The group project can be tedious, but Tayfun has you do it throughout the quarter to reduce cramming. The curve is VERY HIGH due to the average grade being above 90%. Go to office hours and get to know him, fun guy!
Easy course as long as you listen to lectures and do the homework. It would be very hard to fail this course with all the chances he gives you to improve.

Super simple class (very similar to biostats). Prof Sandh is caring, funny, and has plenty of opportunities to raise your grade. Homework and lecture quizzes are optional but I recommend doing them for practice and extra credit, they are also like exam questions. Tends to go at a slower pace so lectures can be kinda boring.
He really cares about your learning.Take him as a professor if you get a chance!
Incredible lecturer, very good at explaining and teaching epidemiology concepts. I wish more professors had the talent that Dr. Sandh has with teaching.
Clear expectations, fair grading, tests only on material covered, plenty of practice, and so many chances for improvement.
I wish he taught more of the public health classes! There is so much practice and so many opportunities to ask questions that he actually answers (even if they are basic).
Funny, friendly, and passionate about epi. Gives lots of chances for significant extra credit, and is very fair and clear on assignments and tests. No tricks. Nice guy, would take this class again.

Simon is the GOAT, if all of my profs were like him college would be so much better. Provides lots of extra credit opportunities, and is a great lecturer overall. You can really tell he cares about your learning, and he prioritizes exams way less. Exams were very fair, testing only on the things that you've spent weeks practicing.

Just call him a gymnast because he will bend over backwards to help you understand something. If you're confused on something from earlier in the quarter, he never judges you, even if it was “supposed” to be known weeks ago. He will explain it again patiently until it clicks. Super supportive and zero shame energy.
Chronically online professor.

I don't like speaking up in class, but Dr. Sandh has a QR code on every slide where you can submit questions anonymously. He reads them off his iPad and answers them. Made class feel way less intimidating. Ask your dumb questions, you have no reason not to!

Dr. Sandh actually teaches, not just tests. The brain dump extra credit points is a lifesaver and really helps if you mess up on a test. He wants you to learn, not fail. Fair exams, clear expectations, and lots of support from him and the TAs.

Dr. Sandh is one of the best professors I've had at UW. He makes epi actually understandable, not scary, and his lectures are engaging and super clear. He genuinely cares about students, is very approachable, and wants you to succeed. Fair grading, great vibes. Take his class.

Love love love Prof. Sandh, he's so sweet and funny and made lectures entertaining. I personally found the content easy, there's lot's of practice, you get a notesheet for exams, and there's extra credit opportunity. Unless you love epi it's a little boring, but a great class to multitask in since content is pretty simple to follow along with

You can feel the entire teaching teams want you to do well. I really liked the practice review sessions that the TAs had and the quiz sections gave me time to ask questions. The professor is so nice and you can tell he really wants to be there. He gets so excited over certain things in the class and it even made me excited for those things too.
I loved this class! It was really nice to have someone who understands academic struggles teach this class. Life saver.
Great professor. I didn't do good in the class but he always tried to support me with extra practice I just never had time to complete anything.
Not a public health major but because of this class, I might actually switch my major. Great crash course into epi!

We were able to pick if we wanted homework to count towards our grade. I have a job and no time to spare to do homework so it really helped me a lot. I didn't do the homework and so most of my grade was just based on exams.
Dr. Sandh made epi really understandable and this is coming from someone who hates numbers. Take him if you have the chance to.
Show up to class, raise you hand, ask questions, go to quiz section, and you're all set. This class is easy as long as you do what's expected.

The lectures are fun, he's really nice, approachable, and the TAs want you to do well. Homework and brain dumps being optional really helped me. I didn't do them and so not having them count boosted my grade.

Students from last quarter told me horror stories and after taking this class, I'm pretty sure they weren't putting in any effort. Simon was really nice, funny, and humble. He took time to make sure everyone was following along in lectures and answered questions clearly. Showing up to class and paying attention really goes a long way in the class.

Was pretty worried about taking this class since I heard about it from other people around me, but the grading is fair and the lectures are really great! homework and participation is optional, but you can get extra credit from it.

This class is honestly what you make it. Simon keeps it real and sets you up pretty well for the quizzes and exams, but he's not gonna hold your hand. He lays everything out super clearly. If you pay attention and put in effort, a good grade is totally doable. The only way to flop is if you just don't care.
Pay attention to practice problem, the exams are really similar to them. No curve balls, sets you up for success.
He pushed me to realize that even though epi was a new class for me that I already knew most of the concepts. He connected examples to things we already know/do so it was really helpful for studying.
Class was good and he was nice but still very fair in grading. Also provides great advice on how to remember things

Epi isn't easy, but Simon helps you succeed if you put in the work. The corrections were a huge plus for me. Sometimes it was hard to stay motivated when students around me wouldn't shut up during lecture. Even though I didn't get a 4.0, the class was my favorite last quarter
Made me really interested in epidemiology so much. Might get my masters in it.

This was a weird class, Dr. Sandh did a great job but during group work students in my group would hate on him because he had the most basic expectations like coming to class and doing work? It was weird to hear that because when we did the group work it was the same students that didn't know the answer to a single question

Office hours are a big help. I only started using them at the end of quarter and learned so much. Wish I had used them at the start of the quarter. Make sure you stay on top of it all at the start of the quarter so you'll be lost.
Looked at my final grade and yup just as much of an easy A as I thought. He makes it easy to get high scores in class

Prof is chill but actually cares if you learn. No surprises with grades, super clear and he gave us an Excel sheet to calculate our final grade if we wanted to drop homework. Lectures were solid, exams were fair, and he added fun bonus questions. Easily one of my favorite classes.

He wants you to get good grades and incentives your success. I ended up getting 7 extra points on the final because I did all the brain dumps and because my group had the highest scores for a few weeks. That was the easiest 7 points I've ever gotten on an exam.
Listens to students and concerns ans tries to accommodate. Let's us not count homework in our final grade if we don't want to. I didn't do the homework so it really helped my grade
He's funny and helped me a lot during office hours. I had a lot of stuff going so i didnt focus on the class but he always tried to help and encourage me

Easy to get an A, just do the work. Everything you need is laid out for you and if you can't get an A in this class, it's probably because you're not paying attention. Lectures are dumbed down so even the slowest people can follow along and the group work has corrections which let you learn from your mistakes. If you're fumbling, thats on you

Prof Sandh is super chill and makes lectures engaging without being boring. He's approachable andcares about his students. Workload is super easy, barely any take home work/projects. Just stay on top of your work and he doesn't overload you with pointless busywork. Highly recommend.
Keeps lectures engaging even when the content is dry. No issues.
Really easy to approach and ask questions. Literally has a brat pouch and speaks brain rot. I need all my professors to take lessons from him.

He's honestly one of the best professors I've had! He tries to keep class engaging and explains things in ways that actually makes sense. He really cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. He's super knowledgeable but also down-to-earth, which makes learning from him really fun. If you get the chance to take his class, do it!

Not a difficult subject by any means and anyone can get through this class with a little bit of focus and study. If I'm being honest though Simon could be better. Learning environment was kinda toxic and the time was used poorly. This class could have been a fun, interactive, and interesting course with a professor who wants that for their students

A fair professor and you'll get the grade you deserve. Class was fine but sometimes made me want to scream because students would ask questions that he had just answered. I liked that the powerpoints on canvas weren't filled in fully. It kept me focused in class but didn't feel rushed because I could get whatever I didn't copy from the recording

an excellent instructor and does his best to support everyone and his teaching style makes the class worthwhile. He's available for help and encourages questions, which made a difference when I struggled with the material. The TA wasn't as helpful but overall no complaints.

This class was tough, but he made it manageable. He's supportive and TAs were decent, but not always very knowledgeable. Group work and homework helped with exam preparation. The corrections system was great but some students didn't care and were dead weight in group work, leaving the workload to others. It was frustrating but thats a student issue

Professor Sandh is a great teacher. The course was challenging, but he wants you to succeed. He has regular office hours you should use, and my TA was helpful with homework. The corrections system was a lifesaver; I could redo things and get credit for improvement.
