Pretty easy class if you just pay attention in class. Hit or miss on how much you absorb during class because sometimes the students in your area end up being really distracting so I suggest sitting near the front where students actually want to learn.

He is a good person and really knows the topic well. His class set up was very tough as we had group work worth 30%, along with extra lectures and the midterm was veryyy long, to the point where halfway through the quarter he had to change a few things and even gave us the option of how to grade the midterm. Taught well though, but attendance requ
Super accommodating! I missed some classes due to person issues and he worked really hard to ensure I was able to make up work.
Was waiting to review until I took the final. This is one of the few classes where the exams are actually things that we learn. Most of the final was just easier versions of the group work.
Show up to class, actually pay attention, and do the work. Simple. You'll do great!
The only class this quarter where I actually learned anything.

The class was fine and he kept it pretty straightforward. There is group work though and that's the worst part because you get random groups and half the students in the class clearly haven't even paid like 2 minutes of attention. They'll ask questions during group and he'll hand feed them an answer and they still won't get it. Like COME ON.
Loved his class so much I'm signing up for his 330 class too. Can't wait to see him next quarter.
Simply the best professor ever. Just put in an honest effort and you'll be good.

I don't usually leave ratings, but this class left me no choice. Genuinely, it's tough not because of the content, but because of the professor. If you have no religion, start searching for one, because you will indeed need it to survive this class.
Run. RUN AND NEVER LOOK BACK. For those who are taking this class I pray we pass this serious matter, and those who are not in yet just don't and pray for those who are in at the moment.
BABBYYYY DONT WALK BUT RUNNNN DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IM CRYING WHILE TYPING U DO NOT WANNA BE ME RN. DO UR SELF FAVOR DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

i feel a little bad about the reviews. his format is very strict and group work is a struggle since grade is based on ur group and not individually, but he is actually a very genuine and kind professor. i think if it wasn't for the group work weighing 30% of our grade, a lot of ppl would like him.

Just took the midterm. It was the most unorganized exam I had ever taken. He took our class time to move desks around so that they could be facing him. I understand why he would want to do that but it wastes 10 minutes which could've been used to answer the 3 problems I didn't get to. The length is a bit too long.

Waited to write a review till after the midterm… just took it, and I swear this guy is getting revenge on us for past quarters. The length was straight-up ridiculous. Can't believe nothing's been done about this class with how many people have shared their frustration
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: not trying to hate but if the professor is reading this pls CHILLL like im dyingggg. ARE WE EVEN PASSING THIS CLASS? try change this formatting is so unfair and crazy. you were once in our shoes please be understandable at least

if you haven't attended his office hours or spoken with him, please don't leave a review. He's genuinely kind and willing to help! Yes, the material can be confusing, but have you actually asked for help? Probably not.

Group work can be frustrating, but it helps you see what you do and don't understand. 

 Be fair and kind!
By far the worst professor I've ever had. The lack of awareness is astounding, and a significant portion of the class is unlikely to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice.

I don't like him! Lectures are long. He takes 30 minutes of our group work lecturing and expects us to know. Group work sucks, we can't even choose our group and no technology is allowed so you have to depend on your group member. It is worth 30% of our grade. He makes his grading that you must attend every lecture and quiz section.
Should be an easy class but your grade depends on how your group work goes.

Him and his team are so unreasonable and grade us on group work. don't know how that's helpful considering he makes us split up the work and we get graded on our classmates abilities not our own. they are insane for a 4 credit class. he needs to leave or fix his formatting because it's extremely unfitting with the uw and phgh major

Professor, and teaching team, has made multiple students cry (including myself). He's not accommodating or understanding of different circumstances and his teaching style/attitude do not fit the UW Public Health teaching style. Painfully condescending as well. I cannot fit all that I want to say within the word count. So much unnecessary stress.

He grades us on group work that is usually split up because we don't have enough time to do it together. He spends the first 40 minutes of lecture yapping then lets us do group work. He teaches the material the day before we have to go and work on it. avoid him if u can. he is so unreasonable
Terrible organization and class structure. He is also a VERY condescending and rude professor. I could say so much more but just read the other reviews. DO NOT TAKE SIMON.
Unfortunately Rate My Professors has a word limit. That's all I'm gonna say

Unorganzing yet uncompromising?? Super strict attendance policy, no drops. Grade is based on "group work" which is basically weekly group quizzes. So frustrating everytime, grade is based on other people's knowledge.  Unclear expectations. Boring AF lectures. Worst crime of all, he is painfully millennial and SO unfunny.

The grading scale is 70% exams—20% midterm, 20% final, and 30% “group work,” which is really just weekly exams. There's not enough time to actually work as a group, so everyone just splits it up, making it pointless. Feels like he was a researcher with no teaching experience or background in education.

Sandh's class is a disappointment for the School of Public Health. His no-tolerance attendance policy and lack of equity contradict the mission statement, making it difficult for students to prioritize their health. I urge others to report concerns to UW PH-GH anonymously (to dcinfo email), as others have already done. The more reports, the better.

Concepts are easy, but the class is terribly designed. Group work worth more than final is every week. These timed group tests are created for concepts learnt the same day. Grade is dependent on other people's abilities rather than your own. Requires lectures outside schedule. Many, many calculation mistakes. Being sick not allowed.

Professor Sandh doesn't teach to help his students and has little to no respect for his student's time. He does a flipped classroom layout for Wednesdays, so we have to complete the recorded lecture beforehand (which is monitored), and then complete groupwork in class. The professor is very condescending and petty when you ask for any guidance.

His teaching style doesn't fit the PH-GH major. Strict attendance rules (no room for emergencies), uses old pre-recorded lectures, and tells instead of teaches. Despite meeting three times a week (4 CRs), he adds an extra lecture and monitors to ensure you don't skip a second of the online video which results in no credit if you do. Petty w/ ego.

I tried HARD to like him and his class. But he is awful! No wiggle room to miss anything yet he himself is so unorganized. Instructions are very unclear and he is condensing when you ask. I wish I took this class earlier DO NOT TAKE SANDH

He was mad cus nobody showed up to his class last quarter so he's taking it out on the new students this quarter. His lectures are so long and boring and dense tbh. Be careful approaching him he's sassy and condescending and doesn't really care about student health... 😭😭

i don't know what he's on this quarter but he has made his 4 credit class harder than my stem 5 credit ones lol. he makes us watch a lecture BEFORE class and during class we do group work. a waste of time considering we could do the lecture in class and group work during quiz section. he is also very childish tbh and the lectures r boringgg

Professor Sandh was great at explaining epi concepts, though material was dense at times. Graded by quizzes mainly and one open ended creative group project that was pretty easy. I can see why his personality might rub people the wrong way but I thought he was funny. I recommend overall, I did well with minimal/moderate studying

All he does is talk about himself. During the first week of the quarter he spent 30 minutes of the lecture talking about himself. Dude has a big ego. Not to mention he's a grown man that acts like a child, overall very unprofessional.

Very condescending and sassy, he doesn't seem like he wants to help the students. Boring, disorganized lectures which go on way too long. Around 3 hours of lecture every week where all the material gets covered in about 45 minutes in the quiz section. The class isn't hard but it's not fun.

Petty, condescending, and disorganized. Overall, the class isn't difficult, especially compared to other STEM classes at UW. The lectures are heavy and often not finished in class. Sandh seems to enjoy that his class is difficult for students. The group project can be fun but the expectations and instructions are unclear/confusing.

I had Professor Sandh for both EPI 320 and EPI 330 and he is one of my favorite professors at UW. His lectures are clear and understandable and he really cares about students learning the course material. Assessments are also fair and accurately reflect what is taught in class.

Amazing and engaging professor. Lectures can be dense and full of content but Professor Sandh manages to keep students still engaged. Going to class/watching recordings is key to doing well in the class. Make sure to write down relevant material on study guides and the tests can take you up to the last minute.

This professor is extremely rude and condescending. When you need help with something he acts like he is inconvenienced and does not provide clear directions. The way he speaks to students is totally inappropriate and I have no idea why this man is on a power trip. If you want to be treated like an adult do not take any of his classes.
Covers 20 lectures of material in 3 lectures! Avoid missing class if you can
Covers 3 lectures of material in 20 lectures. Avoid going to class if you can

Protect this man and his bow ties at all cost. He's so thoughtful and caring and also understanding! I was away from school for a week and he was the only professor that didn't give me a hard time about making up work and he even checked in to make sure I was okay. Epi seems intimidating with all the math but he makes it fun, just pay attention.

Professor Simon is one of the best ones I have eve had in my life. His explanations, examples are so good that he turns complicated subjects into easy, digestible ones. He is so much fun too!! He is fantaaaaaastic. Just be there in all his lectures, that is more than enough!!

I struggled with the class but that's on me because he did all he could to help. He would keep my spirits up and help me review homework step by step during office hours. I had a really rough quarter and he was the only professor that cared enough to make sure I kept with it. My grades were disappointing but he made me proud of my improvements.

Simon is a great professor. He is able to effectively and clearly explain confusing topics and follows the textbook word for word. You can really tell how much he cares about his students learning. I would take another class of his if possible!
Straight forward. Do the homework, do the worksheet, do the project and you will get good scores on the exam. Done.
Bless this man! I barely survived biostats and this class not only taught me epi but also taught me all the stuff I couldn't wrap my head around in biostats.

It was a big class but you know the prof is good when he tries to learn your name. It made the class feel so much more personal. He had to ask for my name almost 10 different times and he eventually got it but it just made me feel all warm inside to see him put such an effort to know students. Only if my bio profs would do the same thing.
I struggled so much in this class but he was literal perfection! Recommend.

Just took the final and he's a great professor. He's knowledge and passionate about teaching. He's also really patient, approachable, and willing to help you understand hard concepts. But my TA was terrible and he was really condescending. My TA quiz section confused me even more and I had to go to the professors to understand the material

Very mixed feelings. Pros: Note sheet on tests, easy hw, gives you candy, has a sense of humor. Cons: Many things worded badly yet graded harshly, zero attendance flexibility, often condescending, super easy to tune out (can be a pro too). Overall easy to get away with the bare minimum. If epi itself weren't so interesting, I'd rate him lower.

Epi is HARD but taking Dr. Sandh made it so much easier. It was one of the best academic experiences I have ever had. He's knowledgeable and informative and his compassion towards each and every student was unparalleled. He's funny, truly cared about our success and went above and beyond to ensure we understood the material.

Prof. Sandh is an excellent professor. He always takes the time to answer questions and explain concepts clearly. He also encourages class participation and is very encouraging of his students. He is passionate about public health and provides a stimulating environment in the classroom. Highly recommended! The TAs though are a whole different story
don't come to this class if you love yourself
He is very hard to approach and dismissive. Half of his students are scared to talk to him because of how condescending. Why be a professor if you hate helping your students??????

I was a little worried about this class because I'm terrible at math but he made everything really easy to understand and made sure I wasn't afraid of the class. He really cares about his students and I would definitely take again.

Professor Sandh is a breath of fresh air at UW. He is very thorough in teaching, has fair exams, and is understanding during any difficulty. He is also very relatable and has amazing TAs as well. Honestly best STEM class I have taken in my 3 years at UW.

Literally a mess, can't make or follow timelines or deadlines. Gives poor instructions or instructions day of project due dates. Ridiculous tests with weird time periods, wastes class time just talking or coming in late. Literally just a mess of a class, so sorry to anyone who has him.

Great professor and class. Really enjoyed getting to hear in lecture and tell stories in TA sections. Very chill course- attending each lecture is very helpful but not necessary. There aren't any surprise quizzes or exams.

Chris and Roger are very nice and personable people. There is a decent amount of reading required, but it's all stories. You're not graded on much, the writing is easy, but twice you have to tell a story from memory in front of a medium sized group. Lectures are not recorded, so I recommend you attended. It can get boring with the long lectures.

Course on indigenous storytelling--super unique and impactful material that's fun and pretty low effort. Very little homework: readings and a weekly 250 word discussion post. Two storytelling opportunities that seemed scary but were easy. Course was a little disorganized with several miscommunications. Don't buy the print books get the ebooks.

AIS 305. Not 375, 305 just wasn't an option to select. I can't believe anyone didn't give him a 5/5. Took an indigenous storytelling class with him, it was fantastic. Just come to class, do the readings, and meaningfully engage with the material and you will get a 4.0. He wants his students to care deeply about the material, just like he does.

Teuton is very clearly passionate about Indigenous literature and it shows in his lectures making them much more enjoyable. The class requires a lot of reading but you dissect it as a class with Teuton's help and it's very informative and eye-opening. There is weekly writeups and a few essays. I would recommend this class and Teuton

His lectures are really fast paced. You cant take notes and listen to lecture at the same time. He doesnt upload the ppts before class so youre just going to have to wing it which doesnt help because his exams are lecture heavy. His weekly discussions are hard bc he requires a question answer and examples just in 250 words and cant go over it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Teuton is very passionate about getting others to learn and engage in the Indigenous culture and history. There is a good amount of reading, stay caught up on it so it's easier to follow along in lecture. Lectures are not recorded. There are multiple guest lectures through the quarter. Two exams, and weekly reading response.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: He doesnt know how to teach. He piles you with information he EXPECTS you to remember and understand. 5-6 pointless articles that are 20-35 page.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Really caring professor who wants a lot of class participation. If you don't like speaking up in class, this probably isn't the place for you. Also, the readings are really important because you have weekly online discussions about them.

Teuton is an amazing professor, but his voice is soothing and the room is warm, so it's easy to fall asleep. There's been several guest presentations, and they always add interesting new viewpoints and topics to the class. And you HAVE to do the readings-- he brings them up in class often. The midterm was pretty much copied from the study guide tho
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: really really really monotone. just read the books and you're chillin. So boring I am doing this during lecture but he's still pretty chill I guess idk.

This professor doesn't seem to care much about students and often changes the syllabus whenever he desires, even right before finals just because he wants to grade the final project differently. The class is very lecture heavy, so you can't miss any lectures. His grading is vague, and it's almost impossible to get a 100 after the first week.

Very unclear with grading expectations on all assignments and midterms. Will not give you a 100% almost ever, even if you redo assignments. He tries to get class interaction and participation but often asks extremely confusing questions and gets visibly upset when the class doesn't answer. Uses AI to make his lectures for him. Veryyy philosophical.

Good Speaker, but expectations were mostly unclear. Class was interesting at points but also got pretty niche and outside the realm of sports and global affairs. Do not expect a good participation grade if you do not raise your hand multiple times per class. Taso seems like a really nice guy, however the class itself was far from perfect.

Does not want to give you an 100%. There is no work outside of the class and the work is easy, but it is almost impossible to get a 100%. Lets you redo assignments but still won't give you a good grade, only gives you a few more points. Overall, his grading is just really unclear and tests are lots of writing but overall material is simple stuff.
Seems fun until your grade drops my 5% on the last day of class

Taso is a great teacher and understands what it means to be a university lecturer. You are not in high school. You are invited to learn to think and create your arguments rather than regurgitate what you read in a textbook or hear in class. If you are intrested and passionate about the subject choice you will do well with relative ease.

Taso is unclear about grading expectations, you must mention every point he personally believes in order to get an OKAY grade. Few assignments use points for grading which makes it very very easy to get a low grade. Participated more than most people in class and received a mid participation score. Rarely received full points. Lectures weren't bad

Horrible professor. Refuses to use Canvas, only email submissions but then complains that he is bombarded with messages. For a 100 level class, his expectations for in class group assignments are incredibly high. His feedback often doesn't reflect the content of submissions. A zoom call with him is a participation grade and he was 30min late.
Unclear criteria on participation grades. Will not get full marks on participation by just attending class and completing assignments

This professor was extremely unprofessional. Guidelines for the course were confusing and I felt he switched up his expectations very often. It was nearly impossible to do well in this class due to his arbitrary grading. I also felt he was extremely judgmental and close-minded. Would not take if you want me succeed. Skip and take another professor.

The Professor has a great sense of humor and provides an active learning environment.
However, his grading is unclear! His grading is based on his personal impressions&assumptions. Received a low  participation grade after contributing in assignments and projects greatly. Quite sarcastic with feedback once he dislikes you. Sad

Although this class was small and only 1 credit, Taso was still a great professor! He cared about each of us and was not a hard grader! Definitely worth the credit, and I would highly consider taking another class taught by him!

Taso is wonderful! A great teacher as well as a great person in general; it's clear he respects his students. He genuinely cares for his class and wants everyone to do well. Very knowledgeable and insightful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Taso is an amazing professor as he makes contribution to his course content and reflects on his own preparation. The class is informative and has productive discussions. You can learn a lot both from the professor and classmates. Also, the professor is humerous and easy to reach out. Reasonable workload but there is no paper. Highly recommended.

I took Professor Lagos class because i heard so many great things about him and his teaching but its not a teaching method for all. class time is chaotic and you're not sure the direction you are going. last minute assignments are common and the questions are extremely elementary and even still you wont get a 4.0. I recommend but beware of chaos.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Lagos is a very engaging lecturer and a very interesting character (in a good way). I thoroughly enjoy any class I take with him, and I love the interesting talks that I have when I go to his Listening Hours (He doesn't like to call them Office Hours).  He has a great sense of humour!

Taso is awesome. He understands his subject and really wants to help students understand the material. His passion for his work, his family, his career and his country of origin (Greece) and his adopted country (US) is obvious. His class isn't a pushover as you will have put in some time, however, if you show up and care, you should get an A.
2 hour lectures were often boring and slow, but his use of class time for small group discussions was very helpful

Taso is pretty cool. As the assistant to this course, he added a lot. I really appreciated his thoughtful written comments on assignments. There was kind of a "you won't know if you don't ask" effect on grades, which resulted in some lost points. More than a few students grumbled about that. However, he was willing to discuss grades w an open mind.
Taso is a very dedicated professor who cares about what he is trying to teach and his students. His occasional ambiguity is worth his heart. He truly made a difference in my life.
Really easy. Class was super confusing but if you can construct a good argument you'll get an A
Make sure to pay attention during lecture...except during one of his tangents. Also, if you have any questions whatsoever ask them early in the quarter, read the handbook...CAREFULLY!

Taso is a fairly effective speaker and I give him credit for attempting some jokes. However, his teaching is incredibly confusing and it is impossible to get a high grade unless you devote a TON of time and never miss a class. I took two of his classes and still question what I actually learned.

i am also concerned about the grading for this class. I was sure my grade would be higher!? What the heck happened? i don't want to raise a stink as i have taken a class with him before and he was great. maybe he was having an off quarter. the t.a. may explain it but still he should have some control.

Unbelievable. The amount of effort required for this class is not worth it. Your grade will not reflect it. Required two addt. days outside of class time. This is not considered. His "TA" does the grading. Best to kiss her ass considering that grades based solely on favoritism. What a joke. An insult to my intelligence.

I felt like this class was totally off topic.  I used to think that Taso was ok, but in this class, he rambled about off topic subjects.  I felt like he was often trying to be funny, but instead was offensive or insulting to college-level intelligence.  Do not take from him if you are interested in learning relavent material.
Honestly, I don't know what happened to Taso, he used to be great...he seems to have "lost" something. The class was in disarray, unorganized, off topic and often times just completely worthless.
Taso Lagos is a pretty good teacher. He talks a lot, but the class is very interesting. His class clearly maintains you motivated. Also the class is pretty easy.
Yikes. Easily the worst class at the UW, I'm sure Dr. Lagos is a decent man but his class is elementary at best with impossible to nail down expectations. No bueno.

I don't know how anyone can't enjoy this class.  He is a good speaker, especially in dealing with so many individuals.  He is genial and lighthearted, and he uses powerpoint/movies to great effect in lecture.  He excels in every way that a teacher should, and I can't wait to take another of his classes soon.
Didn't like him. Not hard, but not a good prof. LONG classes, he didn't make sense. Bad jokes.
Interesting lectures, and movie clips. The professor is very passionate about the subject matter.

He's pretty funny and provides power points for easy notetaking. Going to class is a must though because he adds a lot of things in lecture that aren't the book. I did enjoy the class overall. He's very passionate about the subject unlike a lot of other profs.

One of the worst classes I've had at UW. It's easy, so if you're a slacker you might like it, but it adds nothing to your education. Taso is an interesting guy and the lectures aren't boring, but this hardly feels like a college course (certainly not a 300 level at least)

Most of the class was about himself.  We kept beating the drum on and on about 4 different terms: localite, cosmopolite, framing and priming.  The rest of the class was autobiographical.  Plus, he lets those hard headed students always speak in class -- the same ones over and over again who always waste the class' time with their irrelevant questio

Taso Lagos can be a very strange character but he is funny and he keeps the students in the edge of their sits. He clearly talks a lot about random stuff, but at the same time it makes the class more enjoyable. The problem that I see with this class is that it is too long, and having Taso for that many hours can get exhausting.

He often talks about his life and goes off on tangents.  I was sort of confused as to what direction the class was taking - wasn't sure what to study for the exams, and most of the lectures didn't match the readings at all.  It focused on the "Cutlure War," although the material seemed kind of fluffy.  Also, he often seems to be too dramatic.

This class is a lot of work: 5 books to read, 2 papers to write, 7 quizzes and 2 exams. However, the material is interesting and useful and Taso is a great guy. Personally, I like the class but, unfortunately, do not have enough time to do all what's required. If you want to learn and have enough free time, do take him. Also, he's a generous grader
He writes the most difficult test questions. I completely understood the course material, but was not able to figure out what his questions were asking or what the multiple choice answers meant.

Taso's a good lecturer but tries too hard to be entertaining. His self-depricating sense of humor can wear thin and intrude on an otherwise interesting and relevant anecdote. His tests are a sore point: too often multiple choice answers are too similar, and I fared poorly on the two main exams despite knowing the material very well.
He is an interesting teacher...but his tests are hard.
terrible.

Taso's exams are not very good, a majority of the class scored very low and I know that I knew the material well and studied and only got a C!The good thing about him is that he is definitely not boring because he is passionate about what he teaches. I'm not sure I would want to take another class from him though.
Taso is one of the most passionate profs I've had. He Has fun and if you have any interest in the topic you will too.

Grading procedures for final papers are extremely arbitrary. Tests are poorly written and test your comprehension of the question rather than your comprehension of the course material. Frequently adjusts assignment requirements outside the syllabus description through non-traditional channels, e.g. Yahoo group lists.
Don't take anything from him!

He did a good job with the most awful material ever! He is honest and straight up tells you what is on the test. You have to admire his determination but a culture difference can possibly hinder certain communication
No Comments

I've had him for 201 and 382, and I have to say that he does a good job with crappy material...those crazy stories about Greece, combined with his penchant for swearing a lot, made those classes a whole lot more interesting than they would have been.

He upbeat personality is just about the only thing that kept this class alive. He has random pop summaries to make sure that you always attend class. If you miss a day of class with a pop summary your grade is greatly affected.

He is the worst professor I've ever had! He is not clear when trying to explain something and then in midterms he leaves out important information that can effect you answer and then tells you after it has been graded.

I had him when he was a TA for a quiz section. I felt like he was forcing his opinion on us and would interrogate the student until he/she agreed with his point of view. He is enthusiastic, but not so much in the right direction... and I wouldn't know about his grading as a professor.
I agree with the last post.  His test questions are unclear and personally so are his lectures and expectations for papers.  I don't like his grading policy either.
Taso has great enthusiasm. His class was hard, but I learned a lot :)

This instructor had a difficult time teaching the material.  I can appreciate how difficult his job is.  The plus side is that if you understand his lectures the first time, you can skip the next couple.

VERY VAGUE TEST QUESTIONS AND UNCLEAR DIRECTIONS FOR PAPERS.  HE THINKS ITS CHALLENGING BUT YOU'LL FIND IT UNNECESSARILY FRUSTRATING.  TAKE HIS CLASSES ONLY IF YOU WANT HAVE YOUR GRADE POINT AVERAGE GO DOWN.

He's a nice guy and you can tell he has tons of experience. That being said- his lectures are full of tangents and you never really know what to write down. A lot of the class is common sense but still not worth it. His TA was lit though.

I just could not stay engaged with his lectures at all. Technical difficulties took up 20 minutes every class, and while it's clear he has lots of experience from his past, class usually ends up as a long ramble. There doesn't feel like preparation beforehand on his part. Not a hard class, but it was mentally draining. S/O his TA, she's great.

He is a sweet man, don't get me wrong, but he would go on long tangents and a lack of visuals due to his problems with modern tech, which would frequently delay the class by twenty minutes. He didn't post his syllabus until a week later, and doesn't respond to emails! Please rely on the TA! Easy grade (common sense) but a waste of time!

Doug just sits at the front of class and talks at you for 1.5+ hours. Chronically mentions absurd topics such as drugs, political associations, etc. Kind of entertaining but not worth tuition dollars. Clearly has great experience and thoughts surrounding his materials but gets off on a lot of tangents. Easy pass, but painful to sit through.

Nice, caring guy, but bad professor. Rambles on for two hours and often goes off topic. I have no idea what is going on, no matter how hard I try to listen. Smart man, but his teaching methods are so unengaging and unhelpful. When he lectures, I have NO idea what he is talking about. Easy class, but I really wanted to learn about media ethics.

Doug is fantastic. I took his narrative journalism class, WQ, and it was the highlight of the term for me. He is caring and makes an effort to get to know everyone who shows up. His lectures can get a little boring, and he can veer off topic, but an easy class with a lot of creative freedom. His comments on assignments were also very insightful.

He loves to talk the entire class with no slides, he turns on the projector so the screen lights up blue and thats it. Try to avoid taking a class with him you really don't learn much. It's a very low maintenance 5 credit class but his teaching style is very out of date and unrealistic, this is a visual learners nightmare.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very caring, however, he needs a new teaching style. It is very hard to sit through his lectures and to see connections between what he is really trying to say. There are only a few assignments but the final exam is so insane. If you're into philosophy and want to be tested on it, this class is for you. Philosophy heavy so be ready. 1/10 fr.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very caring about his students and will always lend an ear to listen. Unfortunately, his teaching style is very outdated and he struggles to engage with his students in an interactive way. The reviewer below me feels bad for the professor, like ok, but that doesn't change the fact that this class is super boring. :shrug:

Although not necessary to attend for the completion of assignments, of which there are few, Doug's lectures can be interesting as he brings up relevant ethical dilemmas from real-world examples and tries to engage with the class. Students rarely speak up, but I appreciate his effort in engaging the classroom despite students' apathy.

Writing this as I'm sitting in a runaway train lecture. I've never been compelled to write anything on this site until now. He doesn't use slides, is extremely disorganized, uncommunicative, and rambles on about unrelated topics. Everyone in this lecture is uncomfortable. I have no idea what the point of this class is. Tenure should NOT exist.

Literally the most boring professor I've ever had in my 4 years at UW. Lectures for 2 hours WITHOUT SLIDES, so we can't even take notes on anything. He talks about random stuff at times, and it throws focus off. I can lit hear gossip from students about how it's hard for them not to fall asleep during lecture. Prof seems nice, but that's about it.

Professor Underwood is sweet and he really cares about his students. His lectures are heavy sometimes, but he knows a lot and is passionate about what he teaches. He is also very flexible and understanding. The readings can get heavy, but he always tries to get students engaged with small group activities which also help with assignments.

Not sure why all of these people are so negative, Prof Underwood is such a gem. He is so kind and really cares for his students. Although there aren't lecture slides, he does his best to engage students with his plentiful knowledge and good charisma. He's also reeally understanding too, a king, we stan.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I feel bad leaving such a negative review because he seems like a sweet guy, but jesus, I learned absolutely nothing from this class. There was no feedback given the entire quarter, and no grades put in until after the final. At least I'll get the credits and a good grade, but I wish I had learned something too.
Doug was a bit of a boring professor however, he is SO smart! it is great to talk to him on eon one, he knows so much right off the dome. Would take it again.
Yes, his lectures are not engaging and can be pretty boring BUT he is a wealth of knowledge and it is so interesting to talk to him one on one
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Zzz... A very knowledgeable guy in the sense that he stands in front of the room with no visual aids(no slides or anything) and just TALKS for practically whole 2 hours. I wish there was more organization. Was not difficult for a good grade though, so if there are no other easy A options I guess you can do 468. Be warned, it is so boring it hurts
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: If this class is part of your major, avoid it at all costs. Lectures are disorganized & he goes on tangents so you never really know what you're learning. People don't show up to class and one time I counted 4 students out of 95 in class. Doug is a really nice guy & a wealth of knowledge but the disorganization and lack of structure is unacceptable

Great professor! Really know his stuff, has written several books and incorporates a wealth of knowledge into his class (does occasionally stray from topic material). I would recommend going into his office hours and getting to know him. He's very eager to help and advise.

Doug is a very sweet man and really cares about students and deeply for journalism. The class was not taken serious by many people. It is a TON of reading and I mean a TON along with essays and note driven. It was okay. I did not enjoy it much because it was painfully boring. I got a 3.4 in the class. That's the average, although many did better!

I am really glad I took during Fall Quarter COM 468. Professor Underwood taught me how to chose the right action also in my personal life. His class goes beyond accuracy and ethics in journalism. His readings are about real life experiences and can empower you to promote values and social justice. It has helped me to think clearly in many areas.

FALL 2016 I was pretty disappointed with the organization and overall content of this class. Book and group projects focused on specific case studies  ok but class is awful because his lectures are about off-topic religious principles and the tests don't correlate with the majority of class discussion. they are just about philosophy and religion

Narrative Journalism COM 469 has been one of the best classes I've taken at UW. He is very supportive and makes you feel confident with your work progress. I absolutely loved this class! He uses a practical humanistic type of communication. I was lucky to take this class!  It has open new doors in the written, spoken and teaching world.

Grading is based on a midterm, an hour-long group presentation, participation in a mock panel in front of the class, and a 5-pg analysis essay on a journalistic scandal, with some participation points sprinkled in for the quiz sections. The midterm grades were low, but the class curve was EXTREMELY generous. There is also a good amount of EC.

The class itself isn't too hard but you're going to have to suffer through it. Especially during lectures when he's just talking for two hours straight about things that aren't really relevant to what you need to learn from the class. It was hard to get myself to show up. Underwood himself seems nice enough, though.
easy 4.0

DO NOT take this class, SUPER BORING, UNORGANIZED. You have to buy his book for the class reading. TONS of readings required, you can never finish reading them. This class: boring, too much readings, 25 pages paper. He talks what he likes instead of what we need to know.

Great professor. He used personal experience and clear interest level in the material to enhance quality of the class. Although he is not tech-savy, that isn't necessary for classes of this type. I would take Professor Underwood again in a heartbeat.
Worst class I've ever taken as well. It was boring, unstructured and unorganized. Not a tech-savvy guy despite teaching a class on mass media and politics?? Do not take this class!

Hands-down the worst professor I have ever had. I love the topic, but he is disorganized, rambles about his own career endlessly, and seems to have only a vague sense of what he wants to teach in class. The entire grade is made up of two assignments which are due the last week. I wouldn't wish this guy on my worst enemy. Avoid at all cost.
5 minutes late to class everyday. lecture about self too much, doesnt respond to email. 1 paper and 1 final for the whole grade. dont recommend
Great class. He really digs deep behind the lives of famous authors and influences from journalism. He is pretty laid back and easy to talk to.
Interesting, experience, nice. Stay awake=4.0.

He was a nice guy with good intentions, but I literally almost fell asleep during his lectures. Most boring class I've ever taken and the textbook was hardly used. He talked a lot about religion and philosophy, and himself. I had higher expectations.

One of the worst "professors" I have ever had. Talks on and on about his own personal life, then crams in the material at the end of the course. Textbooks were never used, wasted money on those. All in all a large waste of time and money. I regret taking the class. For the most part, Doug is a well intentioned man with very poor delivery.

I took 468 in Aut 2010 and it was a tragedy the way that man handles his classroom. The only saving grace of that class was the TA, who was wonderful (even though this was not her background, she did her very best and it showed). Underwood's lectures are BORING. Where were the current ties into today's ethical dilemmas? NOT RECOMMENDED.

He utilizes personal experience to highlight material covered.  Can present a seemingly unequal perspective on material.  If you listen and come with an open mind there is interesting information presented.

to say he's out of touch would be an egregious understatement. He uses transparencies on the overhead of the handout he gives to class. Someone should tell him the 80's are over. Obsessed with Reagan (he's unapologetically liberal in his ranting lectures), and a chore to listen to. That said, I did very little to get a great grade!

NO NO NO NO NO NO!  I wrote a letter to the COM department complaining about Professor Underwood.  Worst professor I've ever had at UW.  Not worth your time.  No class structure.  No additional help available--he doesn't even respond to emails.  Boring.  NO NO NO! Don't take a class with him.

Does not use PowerPoint like most professors, does not cater to most undergrads interested in doing the minimum.  Most students spent their time sending text messages, using Facebook, and skipping.  The subject was interesting.  The instructor did well despite the total lack of participation and interest from students.

Worst teacher in the Comm department. I really don't understand how people this bad get tenure. I'm sure he was a great writer and journalist, but people this out of touch with his students should not be teaching. DO NO TAKE A CLASS WITH HIM WASTE OF TIME AND MONEY!

The absolute worst teacher at the university of washington. Never take his class. He doesn't care about the teaching at all, rambles on about nothing, horrible organizational skills, no class website with information, DO NOT TAKE A CLASS FROM HIM!

He is the horrible. Absolutely terrible. He rants about politics that have nothing to do with the class. He does not care if we understand or have questions. The class feels like death. absolutely awful. I was interested in this class but he ruined the topic for me
He is great, will talk the whole time, understanding about attendance and totally laid back!
can be a little dry, but he isn't teaching to hold your hand like so many undergrads want. He wants you to think and challenge him.

I really liked Prof. Underwood.  Though his lectures could be a little dry, the class grading was very fair and the projects allowed us to actually apply our knowledge.  All in all, he's also an extremely nice man.

He is THE worst professor ever in my years at the UW. I have never experienced a professor who lost his students after the first five minutes. This class was used as a great way to catch up on some sleep. You should see his office, it is a complete mess with things sprayed all over the floor and his desk. Worst professor ever.

Underwood has ten year so he can say pretty much whatever he wants - he's VERY liberal and is not afraid to let you know that.  He lets his TA do much of the work (like grade our entire final project). he talks A LOT about random stuff. but overall the class was interesting and i would take another one of his classes again if i had the chance!

Worst teacher I have ever had at UW. Not only were the lectures boring, they seemed to have no relevant point! He just rambled on about nothing and even on his overheads he would just write questions and never answer them. I will never take a class with him again, he even made me consider dropping the COM major altogether.

I have never taken a Com class that has made me want to gauge my eyes out before! The guy refuses to get a cell phone and obviously hates blogs which are both a major part of new media structure. Wants people to ask questions and rambles on and never answers them. Doesn't know how to use power point or make copies w/out his secretary...bad news!!!

Worst prof I have had in 3 years at UW.  He is beyond boring and just rambles on about nothing.  He is extremely unhelpful, and on top of all that, the class is hard!  If you are even thinking about taking a class from him, DONT!

He just rambles about nothing.  I was bored everyday out of my mind and had to fight to stay awake.  He grades super easy though, on tests and essays/ projects (I never read and got a 3.8)... even given the ease I would never take another course with him-- just do to the boredom of hearing him say the same stuff about newspapers everday.

He is scatter-brained and unhelpful.  He rambles on all lecture and barely talks about anything that is useful for the exam or the paper.  He doesn't field questions well from students and doesn't clarify anything.  I would avoid taking any classes from him.

Underwood is great! I had him for COM 445 last Summer. It was a small class and we discussed literature and journalism on the lawn in front of Denny with a guy with ridiculous credentials. He was the lead political writer for the Seattle Times for a long time as well as USA Today. When I talk about UW, I always mention his class as why UW is great.

i took american press and politics from him over the summer and thought the class was great. we just had discussions all the time but i found them really enlightening. made me think about the world and expanded my interest in communications and politics. i didn't do most of the reading and still did pretty well in the class too, but i still learned a lot, somehow.
Makes you buy his own book which sucked and had nothing to do with anything!

I don't think I've woken up yet from all those days I slept in this class. On the bright side, he's a very easy grader on papers. But I can't say anything more because he expects you to remember 2000 terms and people for the test and doesn't even know the names of the 2 people who took up the entire "class" discussion."
he's not very good.  nope.  easy though.  if you like to fall asleep in class his longwindedness will at least give you a good cop out
snoozefest
I think that this is the perfect class if you are looking for a good grade.  Lectures are boring but his expectations are as easy as can be.  I will definately take more of his classes.
No Comments
No Comments
Blathers endlessly without bothering to get to know his students at all. Repetitive, redundant, dull lectures. Will have you read his own book, which, in his case, is not a good thing.
She def has favs. She has a bit of an ego issue

The most awful professor I have ever taken in all my years at UW. Please stay far away. The course itself could have been so amazing but I found myself hating it. She is condescending, emotionless, intense. She thinks she's always right and that the student is wrong.

The class itself is not super complicated if you pay attention. with that being said, this class was so mind numbingly boring at times so paying attention was hard. This class did not feel real, I would take the class again but not her. The exams are not hard if you really study the slides and vocab words from the readings.

I'm surprised to see the negative reviews. I enjoyed her class and found her lectures entertaining. The content was really easy and I got a decent grade considering the effort I put in. Midterms are easy and occasional homework usually takes 10 minutes.

Arguable the worst professor I've had. Could have been an interesting class, but taught in a terrible fashion. Grading criteria was very ambiguous and the professor would just insult you if you asked questions surrounding lecture or the rubric.

Prof was really solid - a lot of the reviews here are a bit misjudged. When a dumb question gets asked she usually gives a dumb answer - I found this pretty entertaining. She is really respectful and understanding of things people are going through and is a really solid professor. take these reviews with a grain of salt, there are worse professors.

She's nice but somewhat intense at the same time. She likes people who speak up and participate. Her system for midterms and the final was annoying because you had to bring your Husky ID and they went around checking everyone's which took a long time.

This class overall sucked. Most of the projects are graded by the TA who doesn't really follow the rubric. Prof. Uduehi seemed like a nice person but overall spoke condescendingly to everyone. Lectures were long, boring and useless. Only went cuz of the pollev. Guest speakers were good tho and tests were easy.

First off, I actually think she's a decent professor. Lectures were generic but engaging. I do understand the students who might receive condescending comments but I have yet to see a real bad one. My main issue with her is that her TA grades the projects and doesn't even follow her own rubric.. thus it's hard to know what she actually wants.

One word that summarizes this class is engaging 

From the class discussions and competitions, the pop culture references, to the occasional Office reference, Esther does a tactful job keeping her students intrigued. Far from being condescending, she's just a walking brochure for Oxford and Wharton, loved hearing about her academic adventures.

Condescending, unreachable, and boring. 

Pros: guest speakers were fantastic & I appreciated the clear graded requirements - 3 projects and 3 tests and 5 HW. 

Cons: teacher answers questions with questions and is condescending when answering. Lessons are drawn out. Material is tired and overall boring.

Regularly talks down to students in a very condescending way. Arbitrary grading systems where she will grade you down on things that you did fine. Was actually rude during our final presentations by how she addressed the students.

She's a nice person, just not a great professor. Around the final exam, she would snap at people who asked her clarifying questions, telling them to "check what the slides say." Honestly a big part of why I decided not to pursue marketing as a major option at Foster.

Her instructions for group projects were unclear and broad. She can be expecting something completely different than asked. If you try double checking she sometimes gets defensive and says to read the grading rubrics. She also replies back in a condescending manner at times. Exams were based heavily on memorization and no notes allowed.

She's a nice person, just very disorganized. Participation is important, but she makes it difficult to do so. She picks on people, speaks condescendingly, and gets defensive when she doesn't know the material. When students ask clarifying questions, she mocks them, and then shuts them down. I guess it's a step up from name-calling.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I thoroughly enjoyed mktg 301 with Prof Uduehi. Lectures were fantatstic. She made sure to incorporate real-life examples and encouraged participants to make the class more interesting.
Pros: She cares about your learning and encourages questions
Cons: Grades a bit harshly on group projects. I think it's so there is a curve

Definitely made the lectures interesting. I liked listening to her points, as she had great enthusiasm for the class. She also has a great sense of humor. The information she teaches is easy to understand and relevant to life. However, her tests are very specific. She also knew every name in the classroom by the end of the quarter.

Professor Uduehi is a great person and lecturer but I feel that the grading was strict and feedback was generally unhelpful (docking ten points with only "confusing proposition" as reason) . The course was also disorganized, particularly for the group project (separate grading documents scattered throughout canvas that had differing information)

I respect how Uduehi puts in effort to get to know her students. The lectures & content was honestly average, but it was fun to go to interactive lectures. Be aware that she'll call on random people in-class & press people to explain their answers, just have fun with it & don't take it as a personal insult. She's not trying to make you look dumb!

It seems like Prof. Uduehi is coming into her own as a newer teacher, and a lots of those negative bits of feedback don't hold true anymore although I see where they came from. Lectures translate directly to tests, she is a bit rude in class but it's usually fun/teasing, and her rambling is relevant to the material and makes it more memorable.

Professor Uduehi's slides were fun and engaging, she really emphasized using real life examples to help students make connects. Midterms were fairly easy if you attended and actively participated in class to understand the concepts. Could get by in the class without reading the textbook in my opinion. Only accessible through office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Where to begin.. Esther attended pompous universities and it shows. Well-versed in marketing theory but never worked in industry. Won't open exams afterwards. Unclear grading. Skims slides of material that end up on exams. Open book, but this hardly helps. Got an A by filtering every class PPT and cataloguing information to CTRL-F. 233 KEY TERMS...

She is a nice person. However, she is not a good professor. Unclear grading criteria and she ended up with multiple revisions posted to Canvas. She forgets what she put on her rubrics when you ask questions. She rambles on about random topics that were honestly annoying to me. Her Canvas is never updated, it's still not and grades are posted. Bad.

This was her 1st year as a professor and we could tell. Assignments were very unclear, lectures were dry, and she struggled to clearly answer questions. She often gave condescending responses to questions that she considered "obvious". In a few years, she should be a good professor but she has some work to do. Nice person though.

Esther is a great person but one of the worst professors I have had at UW. She is a horrible lecturer. The slides are messy and you never know what exactly you need to study for. In lecture, she starts discussing random irrelevant subjects. She also is very condescending in the way she teaches and makes you sound dumb when you ask questions.
easy class and goated ta
Really nice and genuinely cares if you understand material or not. Explains concepts in the best way for your understanding. 10/10 would take again.
Great professor, inspirational, helpful, great at explaining concepts, and goes above and beyond to help his students
Professor Upsal is a great person and this course is not hard at all. But beware of those weekly quizzes, they are not hard but the grading is a little bit tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class itself is straightforward as can be. There were weekly quizzes on the previous week's material, so after doing homework and some of the in-class problems, it was pretty chill. Homework can take up quite a bit of time if you're not comfortable with programming, but they're not hard by any means.

Its less about Jeremy's ability to teach but rather the fact that the class (AMATH 301) itself is setup really poorly. Despite being called an intro class you require a strong understanding of fundamentals and the quizzes require a truly strong and deep understanding of the material that the homework and in-class work mediocrely prepares you for.

He isn't the worst, but the content really ramps up after week 3 and this isn't reflected well in the teaching. Since concepts are really difficult it can be hard to follow along. I'm sure utilizing office hours is probably helpful, but quizzes/homework are hard (and half your grade). No practice quizzes which is a bit messed up but ig ai can help.
Others say his lectures are confusing, but I found that the online modules he created were enough on their own to understand all the concepts well, and the weekly homeworks were engaging.

sigh... i love the content and there is so much potential. but i wish that he would teach the topics well too. it's clear that he's passionate about amath, but passion isnt enough to be a good teacher. his explanations are really confusing and when you ask him questions he just reiterates instead of actually addressing your confusion directly.

Nice guy, tries to be fair, but his class is not set up for fairness. His study guides for weekly quizzes are confusing and mostly just make u memorize syntax, and then the quizzes are extremely nitpicky and ask for a strong command over the material. Each question on quiz worth ~10% of it. This can bring your grade down quick. if taking, good luck

This class does not feel like a beginner coding class, If you don't have previous knowledge of coding you will struggle. There are weekly quizzes with trick questions and do not pertain to the lectures. Weekly homeworks have nothing to do with what we learned, and take 6-8 hrs to complete. Lectures are unhelpful and prof doesn't explain anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor is nice, but the workload is extremely heavy for an introductory coding course. Expect to spend 8+ hours weekly on assignments. I found a significant disconnect between the lecture content and the homework requirements, which made it MUCH more difficult than anticipated. Would not recommend for those with a heavy STEM courseload!

Lowkey the only reason I'm rating a 1/5 is because there's no options for 0/5. Upsal is a nice guy for sure, but definitely not a good instructor. 2/3 of the lecture hall is empty by the end of the quarter, that said a lot.  I'm sorry Upsal, I don't mean it, but you really messed up this quarter. And I'm not the only person who says this, sorry man
The class is a little unorganized. I get that he's trying to restructure it and make it better and all that (not working, btw), but the final's in a week and he still hasnt posted the topics list

The flipped format is flawed; rushed lectures just repeat the PREP readings. HW load is wildly unpredictable—some take 2 hrs, others an entire night (HW9 was brutal!). Weekly quizzes mean constant cramming. The first 3 weeks of basic coding were great, but Data Science got crammed into the last 2 weeks and felt super rushed. Start your HW early!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 4 credit class? more like 8 credit class. i spend more time on this class than my other two stem classes combined!
thought his rating was too high... helping bring it down 😭. i have no words

there are so many typos. on the hw, on quizzes, everything. it's fine once or twice but it's consistent. it increases the stress levels of an already very stressful class. like ok the hw is hard, dont make it worse by writing wrong stuff. ok the quizzes are sneaky, dont make typos! like please! we already have limited time!

he lowered the median from 3.9 to 3.4 because it was "too easy to get a 4.0". he tried to justify it. no one is happy obviously. if we need a 97 for a 4.0 with the median at 89-90, teach at that standard too please

Quizzes: unnecessarily weird, which is annoying since you have to take them weekly after finishing the weekly unnecessarily weird homework. 
Study guides: vague, so are his answers to questions about them. 
Lectures: him scrolling thru code
Avoid if you can, though that may be tough bc he's the only one teaching the class for the rest of the year!
Lectures are confusing. Homeworks are long and difficult and weekly quizzes are even more stressful. Nice guy but would not recommend.

Weekly quizzes worth 30% of your grade. It's too easy to lose a lot of points, partial credit is a myth. This guy not knowing what he's doing does not help. He keeps skipping over parts of the lecture because he's "out of time" or "wants to move on", and then wonders why we're having trouble on homework and why the quiz median dropped so much.

He makes the assignments and quizzes super challenging. The lectures are ineffectual since they have nothing to do with the quizzes or insanely long homework assignments. No intro class should ever be this rigorous and demanding. Nice guy I guess but really should not be teaching the intro coding/applied math courses.

Upsal has the challenge of teaching a large class of students who do not have the background necessary for the class (coding, lin alg, diffy-q). Although there were flaws in his teaching techniques at the beginning, he is very receptive to feedback and implemented suggestions immediately. Very caring though it may not always seem like it.

Many folks spent over 30 hours on one of the last assignments. That said, he has a deep passion for the subject and eagerness to explain things as practically as possible. He's a deeply caring and responsive person. He's definitely a great person to teach this course, but just bank on it being nearly a full time job for at least a few weeks.

Professor Upsal's teaching can be difficult to follow, especially at the beginning if you have no prior coding experience, and his homework can be difficult and taxing, but he will help if you come to him or the TAs and he does listen to feedback. His exams are reasonable and come with practice exams. Overall not bad but can be difficult at first.

Upsal gets a lot of unwarranted hate, as someone who had no prior knowledge in Matlab/Python I had no issue understanding the topics discussed in class. His midterm is fair but his style of grading is bad he shows the grade as pts/ 4xx so its really disheartening when you miss 1 pt on a quiz and know you only have 5 more until your grade drops.
I think while the professor is caring and passonate, he needs work on his teaching techniques.

Do not take any class from Jeremy! He does'nt know how to teach, and just loosely reads through the notes in lecture. He made the hardest midterm ever, with some questions never covered in class. I had a terrible experience with him.He puts completely ambiguous questions in the test and when you discuss with him, he says with a smirk, "I am sorry."

Dr. Upsal is an out-of-box thinker. "I do not know. Every student should get a 4.0." That's how he responds to how many students gets a 4.0. He provides only two practice exams, which do not prepare you for what's coming in the real exam. Most frustrating is that questions can be in a grey area where they test you on details never covered in class.

The professor is not good at explaining course content for people to understand, rushes lectures, and is rude. The class material itself is informative, useful, & clear, but the professor makes it more difficult.

Jeremy did a great job teaching this class. What stood out to me is how much he cares about students' success in the class. He noticed when the class was struggling on a certian topic or assignment and adapted to help (e.g. explaining commonly missed quiz topics or extending a hw due date). He is a very kind person and easy to talk to in general.

Jeremy is a fantastic instructor. There were some wrinkles but most of those was proactively ironed out. He put in great effort to help his students with lecture and homework questions. He is also understanding of student's struggles and is generally very approachable and accessible. You can succeed in this class if you put in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Worst professor ever! He does not know how to make a useful lecture, and the way he grade the homework is unreasonable. Most of my work is exactly same as the example he gave, but I got no credit. And the lecture helps nothing for his quiz and for my understanding. He made this course feel like I am wasting my money and time to study here.

Jeremy didn't know how to run this class. Lectures had nothing to do with homework. Communication was poor. Mastery based grading was poor. He made little effort to change things. Office hours was the only way to get through homeworks but they were packed. I didn't learn anything from this class. If you have to take this class, I'm sorry.
Not recommended at all. his lecture is unclear, and the materials are confusing. For grading, he doesn't follow his rubric. By the way, he changed his syllabus many times. Avoid him in AMATH481/581.

Doubt the course notes, doubt the lectures, doubt the assignments - there are many small typos and a few fundamental errors. Generally not very details-oriented, so make sure to get everything in writing and check back several times. Don't start working on assignments too early - there will be "clarifications"; it's a mutual learning experience.

Jeremy Upsal has some of the most disorganized and uninteresting lectures that I have ever attended as a university student. For a class focused on learning MATLABs, we spent a much longer time learning about the conceptual and theoretical parts of linear algebra and diff eqs, which were not pre-requisites to this class. Avoid Professor Upsal.

Jeremy is a fantastic teacher,  he clearly cares about his students and I would take any other class he offers. The class wasn't particularly difficult, the homework took some time but there was only one assignment and one easy quiz per week. There was lots of resources outside of class too. I learned a ton from him!

Dr. Upsal has a laid-back, straight forward teaching style. He is very easy to talk to and cares about his students. He is also very understanding and open to critique, giving us weekly check-ins about our personal progress and thoughts on the class. Overall, I really respect his approach to teaching and highly reccomend his classes.

High workload compared to others lecturing the same class. HW focuses on the application while the test focuses on the concept heavily, be ready to spend some time on this course. He also falsely accused many students in my class of academic misconduct which was hilarious (i.e. the plagiarism detection algorithm he uses is pretty much broken).
Terrible!!!
explains everything so clearly, one of the best amath profs i have ever had
Kind of a deep lecture, but you will definitely learn things with him. Accessible and helpful in OHs, and he might arrange extra OHs for exams, which I am so grateful for and extremely helpful.
Lot's of homework and exams are super difficult
The workload is a lot. I like the lectures and organization - and the subject is very interesting - but I am so burnt out by the weekly homework that often takes 15+ hours to complete.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: A tough class but worth taking it. Instructor Jeremy is very caring about his students, and he is willing to give feedback about HWs and even personal development after the class is over. You should take it but beware of heavy workloads and kinda hard exams.

Stay away. Excessive workload to the point that it distances you from actually learning. Furthermore, after bringing problems to his attention he is too rigid/unwilling to change. So, if you have a legitimate concern about his methods expect it to fall on deaf ears. Additionally, his lectures are very weak. Expect to be underprepared for exams & HW

Great course! With almost no prior coding experience, AMATH 301 taught me how to use python. Jeremy was extremely responsive on piazza, gave solid explanations, and is an all around solid dude . Homework was reasonable and helpful. With mathematical knowledge up to linear algebra and vector calculus, this course was not conceptually difficult.
I liked his class a lot. It wasnt too hard to do well, but it does take a bit of time and effort. The lectures were super useful on the assignments and quizzes. Overall a good prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Cool guy; very responsive on Piazza. Changed course schedule to help people w/ coding. Canvas organized w/ weekly modules. 1 hw, quiz, reflection, and activity a week. I wish he wouldn't edit the hw halfway through the week though. Hw was using stuff from lectures/activity. I've taken math and cs up to 126 and 143 and had no problems (no 307/8).

He gives immediate and detailed feedback anytime on piazza. You can even post your code for HW privately, and he will point out or hint where you are wrong. He also cares about students' grades, and he's not stubborn on the policies. But he really gives hard, and heavy HWs, harder than what you might learn from classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The course is tough and chill at the same time. The workload is extremely very very big and hard. Self-quiz and activity every week. He grades on student's effort. I once made one homework terribly wrong, but he gives me nice marks. The bad thing is homework is always not clear. Each week, he modified homework up to 5 versions. Some are on the due
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Someone said you should take math 308 before this, it's absolutely not necessary. I'd say taking math 126 before is a good idea (even though technically only 125 is a prereq), just so you know, like, what a vector is and stuff like that. I haven't taken 308 and it's fine, you don't do any matrix algebra by hand at all past what you learn in 126.
This professor is so awful that can not imagine before taking this class. He does nothing besides give a lot of homework.

Totally loved his teaching style - spontaneous and easy to grasp. He is passionate about teaching and delivers lectures pretty well. Assignments and tests were reasonable. He is easily approchable outside the classroom and happy to help with conceptual doubts.

I'll give him credit for putting effort to make lectures for MATLAB & python, but how he sets up his class is so confusing. Like when we submit hw, he did not specify a certain way how until after the hw was due, and due to that I lose 10% of my grade for that hw. He even told me I should've read the instructions when I did but there was nothing!

Jeremy's alright. The homework assignments were really long and lectures did not help that much. Definitely recommend taking math 308 before this class. It would make it a lot easier. A rude group of TA's also don't help. Exams were not that bad, only a couple of coding problems. Make sure to study the material from the "quiz section" day.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is so open to feedback and improving his teaching which I really appreciated. A tiny bit frazzled, but it doesn't detract from his teaching.
IDK why this guy got such bad reviews. I liked his style of teaching and found the tests and homeworks to be reasonable. Pretty chill guy, unfortunate to have a psycho TA.

After about two weeks of going to lecture I stopped and never went back. He teaches too slowly, and it was more helpful to watch back double speed later on Panopto. The activities were useful in understanding but the TA breathing down your neck for even having a phone out was terrible. The threat of losing credit completely was also not helpful
Lots of homework, be prepared to ask lots of questions. Exams are difficult. No answer for the practice exam.
Jeremy was OK... But the course was poorly structured. Be prepared to be unprepared for homework and belittled by pizza responses by snobbish TAs.

I found upsall's lectures virutally never be clear or coincide with the homework that he assigned. Material on homework was thus a lot harder, as it was covering material that was poorly covered in lecture. Average of 2-3 of additional hour long lecture videos to watch that we were quizzed on. These were honestly much more helpful than actual lectu

This class presents itself as an "intro" class to coding/MATLAB but the TA's and professor often act like its not -- help is vague and tests are hard to prepare for. I felt completely lost all quarter and any time I asked a TA for help the answer was condescending. Things you needed to complete HW often aren't taught before its due. Don't recommend

The contents in class is not enough for homework, you should post a lot of questions in piazza and get some 'hint' to finish your hw. There's only one practice exam for each test, and they won't give you the answer for both practice exam and tests. The activity must be done in group, otherwise you'll get 50% grade off. Exams are very detailed.

Took L ARCH 210, a class I was not sure that I wanted to stick with before attending, and after her first couple of lectures I felt super inspired and interested! No midterms and finals in this class, which is a total blessing as instead we completed 3 projects throughout the quarter. Great at engaging the class and answering questions!

Had her for LARCH210. Environmental Design+Sustainability and she was amazing.She knows how to use technology and it never got boring with her lectures as compared to other professors that have a big class.She gave out extra credit and she made us think out of the box for our assignments.I would definitely take her again in the future.

One of the best architecture studio professors I have had during my time at UW. Gives amazing crits, actually cares about the students success, gives resources to assist with studio... program of studio will be super useful for future courses as well. take her class if you have the opportunity!!

Professor Kim is one of the most caring and amazing professors ever. He is truly passionate about teaching and looking after his students. All the class expectations are clear and grading is very fair. Everyone should get to experience taking his class during their time at UW.

He cares a lot about his students, and is always trying to help. Lenient grader, and has great energy. I wish he was more thorough w/ what he was teaching, as most things are skims of important historical events & film techniques (albeit I took an intro class). Would recom. if you need the credits and want fun, not if you want to critically think.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Mr. Kim is hands down the most caring and personable instructor I've ever had. He cares deeply about the course and his students. He always strived to improve his lectures and make the course manageable for all. Seriously, he is such a gem of a human-being and I would take any class he teaches. 

(Korean pop culture is actually Korean cinema fyi)
Really sweet and understanding guy. It's also a fun class

Ungsan is a guy who definitely cares about his students, but he can be a little condescending and narrow minded at times. He teaches things very well, grades very fairly, and takes effort into consideration. He is different from other 111 professors in that he gives quizzes, but they're relatively straightforward, and he curves your grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Ungsan was an awesome TA! He was more than helpful during his sections. Although our class met once a week, he was more than willing to meet outside of class. He really engaged the class in discussion and overall made the classroom an intellectual and friendly environment. Most importantly, he is extremely nice and cares about every student.

Ungsan was a great TA.  He was really friendly and put in extra effort to help his students.  Essays he grades have comprehensive and very helpful feedback.  When students started struggling on quizzes, he reached out and put extra effort to help us succeed.  I had him for C LIT 272 (Martial Arts Film).
Definitely good if you're a little interested in the subject but don't want to put a crazy amount of work in.

English 111 with Ungsan was by far my easiest class at UW. If you participate in class discussions and ask him to read your essays before the portfolios are due, you'll get a very high grade in his class

Professor Kim loves to engage his students in class and often leads interestingthoughtful group discussions. Just make sure you pay close attention in class and contribute to conversations actively if you want to get a good grade from him or if you just want to make class more enjoyable.
Professor Elizabeth Umphress demotivates students to attend her class due to the excessive assignments she assigns without providing meaningful feedback or taking them seriously.

Took Elizabeth's MGMT 402 class--a lot of fun.
