The cases are relatively interesting (each case is a different topic) and the in-class are negotiations are a lot less intimidating than you would think. She grades specific to a rubric and there's pretty much no leniency. Participation matters and read the textbook! "Final" is a paper.
You can't skip class, but you won't want to anyways.

Caring, sweet and funny professor. This class is every day and participation is very very required, so get ready to be disciplined in your French studies especially if you're a beginner. She's very understanding and will let you turn in some things late if you ask. Overall I'd take a class with her again.

It was really wonderful to watch how much everyone in the class improved.  The class was over zoom which she handled very well.  She taught 90%+ in French which meant I didn't understand some of the instructions and the results on some assignments were hilarious.  She deals well with those kinds of absurdities.  I would take any class she taught.

Hélène genuinely cares about her students and it is obvious that she wants them to succeed. She requires participation and there is quite a bit of busy-work, but she's very understanding about deadlines. She is pretty scattered, but in my experience that hasn't inhibited my learning in any real way, and she's very apologetic about it.

I like her anyway. She is full of wisdom and she is interesting. She also encourages me to show myself more in class cuz I'm shy.I feel at home in her class. I don't care whether her class is organised or not, I feel good to learn a language in this way without much pressure Due to the time and distance I cannot take her class often that's pity.

She is very unorganized: -she will comment on you about your hw when she doesn't mark your hw for 2 weeks and doesn't tell you the correction she wants on time while telling you that she is taking marks off because you were not listening -she just posted a final complete essay due 4 hours before the deadline, nothing was mentioned weeks before
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was totally unprofessional for the 2020Au FR203 online class. She didn't teach anything, had us put a part of our homework during class in the chat, and corrected them ONE BY ONE until there are only 10 minutes left in class. Then she will go on to talk about other things that are not relatable and thus taking you extra 10 minutes after class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors ever! Hélène is so kind, thoughtful, and attentive to her students' needs. Class time was used really well and homework assignments and compositions were definitely helpful in improving my French. Tests and quizzes are at a reasonable level. Would definitely take a course from her again!

Basically you get a 100 for every homework you submit. Helene is a nice person, but she is also the most disorganized professor I have seen. She doesn't give feedback at all, but you don't need them for good grades because everyone gets A+s. She would forget about class and she gives the most unclear instructions. Again, she is very kind though.

She is a really caring and passionate french teacher however she assigns a lot of homework and is unreasonable and unclear about her expectations with her students and expects you to learn quickly or you will not do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Is very unclear about the homework, so unclear about what she expects and what receives what grade. Also the grade is highly effected by homework.

She is such a sweet professor! Class was always fun and upbeat. You will be required to participate every class, but it isnt anything intimidating! My French lab homework, but she gives you plenty of time to complete it. Tests are very similar to review and straightforward. Overall super fun class and I learned so much!

Helene is fantastic. She sets aside time to work individually with everyone in the class on our pronunciation (something no other french teacher I've had has done). I once had to take a test in her office and she popped in and said she was making coffee and brought me some. If you can take her class, you won't regret it.

She is one of the kindest teachers I've met! She gets to know all of her students and remembers really detailed things about them. Her class is not hard, there is homework due every class but it's fairly doable. The work was sometimes really frustrating but it felt rewarding and wasn't especially hard to get in the 3.8-4.0 range at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Helene is sweet and knowledgable. Class is relatively disorganized but I think that's a "French" thing. She's a hard test and essay grader, so be ready to put in work. She's nice and not judgmental so always try your best and you'll be on her good side. Go to class!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Helene is a wonderful teacher, but be prepared to have lots of papers floating around. My folder is overflowing with work, but I think she just really likes giving out a lot of papers to help our French skills. In any case, she was very pleasant and lively, not too many boring moments in the class.

Helene is a wonderful person and professor. I learned so much because she made sure that each class was super engaging and got us talking a lot. Her quizzes are difficult but she provides extra credit and will work very personally with you if you need extra help. Her class was also very grammar-heavy but that's common in the French department.

Helene is INCREDIBLE. She was the lead for my quarter-long study abroad in France and was the best professor/tour guide/surrogate mom we could ask for! She is incredibly knowledgable, warm, caring, funny, and helpful. She helped me work out some tricky grade conversions, the right path for my major, and a few hiccups during the study abroad

She's so sweet!! She WILL push you to do your best, but through this your French will improve so much! She's also a native French person, so she brings very interesting perspectives to class. She's got a fabulous sense of humor too. I'm usually super shy in class, but Helene is so wonderful I was able to break out of my shell!

I love Helene, she's like my school mom. If you are willing to put in the work she will do anything to help you be better and do better than you thought you could. She is very clear with her expectations and the work load in the 300 level courses. And although she is a tough grader, she writes all the french exams so there aren't any surprises.
This is the worst.
She expects a lot, but it's nothing that anyone can't handle. Also, her knowledge of French language, culture, and history is so impressive and makes the class engaging.

Helene is so wonderful both as a professor and a person in general. She is one of the best professors I have ever had--she is like a walking encyclopedia of French history and she makes it really interesting! Her classes are well-organized and her expectations are clear.  Take a class with her if you can-I work my schedule around taking her classes

I love Valeria so much she is so Amazing and Wonderful and Beautiful. She is so knowledgeable about the subjects she teaches and constantly had recommendations for other books (fiction and nonfiction), movies, and just resources in general. Again, wonderful wonderful woman, a gift to Seattle and Washington state.

Taking Professor Valeria for Classical Archeology 447 was an amazing experience. She's highly knowledgeable about the class and lectures were interesting. Grading for this class was super easy, there were 4 assignments worth 25% of your grade each. This class was basically a free 3 credit course.

Such an amazing lecture, clearly knows her stuff, and can tell great stories. It is a big lecture hall which is kinda sad (to the group of guys yapping their life away over the prof. in the back of the hall as if nobody could hear you-bane of my existence, I hope your shoe laces never stay tied even if double knotted) ANYWAYS highly suggest!!

Valeria is clearly passionate about Greek and Roman myth, I found myself looking forward to her lectures

reviews.comment: Vince is extremely knowledgeable with ARCGIS and Excel. He keeps class entertaining with his sense of humor and wants his students to get good grades and will stay late after class to help.
Vince the goat

Vince is easily one of my favorite professors in college. I had him for both 397 and 497 and despite not loving the content of the classes I still enjoyed the classes because of Vince. He cares a lot for his students and is always willing to help. He goes over everything in class so the only way you will struggle is if you don't show up. Great guy.

Honestly, one of the most chill professors I've ever met. The class is basically just excel 101. it gets really complicated towards the end but it's easy if you have excel experience. class is boring but he records lectures. You do one long project throughout the quarter. final is tough, but the rest of the class is a piece of cake. Take him!

Prof Wang is an amazing professor since he genuinely wants his students to succeed in his class! He will walk through all the practices and upload lecture recordings on Canvas. All 4 assignments will be mainly covered in weekly lab sessions and all practices and first 3 assignments accept re-submission throughout the quarter.

This is one of the best classes I've taken at UW. Either attend lecture or watch the lecture videos and he shows you how to do every single assignment and all quiz sections guide you through the projects. Very easy and I've had little work to do outside of class hours.

Very great professor, answers all questions patiently and responds to email quickly, one of the best professors at UW. Give clear instructions in class, as long as you attend class and follow along, you will succeed.

The best professor I have had at UW. Class is set up as one big group project with module quiz every week. Show up to class and follow directions and you will pass. Easy to talk to if you ever need help and is one of the only professors I have interacted with that genuinely cares about you as a person.
super kind and flexible
Such a wonderful professor! He really cares about his students' success and allows for lots of creativity. Would highly recommend!!!
Eric was great teaching this class, His grading is very flexible which is wonderful I wish more professors at UW would be like that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: (Drama 101) Fun, enthusiastic, and engaging, Prof. Villiers's class was what you made of it. The work was incredibly easy and only attendance in quiz section was required, so it's possible to do the bare minimum and get a 4.0. However, you can also learn a lot from Villiers and the course content if drama truly interests you.

This is a fairly straightforward class. If you do the work it's pretty simple and professor Villiers is great! The quiz sections are a bit pointless though, considering its the exact same thing we would do in lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall a good accounting professor and you'll be in good hands for ACCTG 301. Don't underestimate the difficulty of the midterm and study hard for the exams. For me, my grade improved significantly when I took the final because I solely focused on practice tests and reviewing slides, rather than other study strategies she suggested.

Its just a hard class in general, so prepare to be confused a lot. HW is only two trials, and you can't see what you got wrong the first time. she thinks it helps us, it doesn't. Exams are hard, but Kendall's outfits are harder 🔥. She's nice overall & fair. Just ask for lots of help, study ahead of time plzzz. Open up your 215 notes fr.

Kendall is nice and caring to her students. Her class was a little challenging, but she was able to make it fun and enjoyable. She really care about her students and is passionate about teaching accounting. Amazing professor, highly recommend!

Kendall's a great professor. She's got a good sense of humor & attempts to make each class as enjoyable as possible through various examples. Her tests are hard, but she provides many practice tests/examples & is very reachable with extra office hours. She hasn't published our final grade, though (and it's after the deadline...). TLDR, take w/her!

Cares about her students learning and is very approachable, but this class is hard. 1 midterm, 1 final (cumulative). Exams can be tricky but she provides a lot of practice + allows a note sheet! 4 not too bad group assignments. If you have a basic understanding of intro (acctg215) you will be fine!

highly knowledgeable and kind, takes time to explain every problem and is very eager to help out in office hours. grading philosophy made sense but was very harsh, often awarding 1/10 or 5/10 points. her TAs were goated and helped out a lot in review sessions. also had a lot of exam study materials, so it's up to you how you make use of resources.

One of the best professors I have had. She teaches you not only the course content but also through the conceptual problems you learn how to better write proofs. Finally, the exams are also very similar to HW so if you do that nicely there should be no problem. Also lets students know about many math opportunities outside the classroom like WDRP.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She cannot teach, after 2 weeks of attending lectures I gave up. I had to teach myself the class with the use of thomas carr and the textbook, she reuses majority of the exams and does not provide answer keys to practice exams. I was paying for myself to teach then to come in and take her exams would NOT recommend.

if you can do 1/3 of the exam you will get a 2.0, if you can do 2/3 of the exam you will get a 3.0, and if you can do a little over 90% of the exam you will 4.0. the exams are similar to the practice exams and she gives you a lot of her old material to practice. her lectures are hit or miss and often require extensive textbook or thomas carr help.

reviews.comment: Viray is passionate about math, friendly, and puts a lot of effort into the class.  There are ample resources to prepare for tests, homework, and you do learn a lot.  However it's very difficult to get a high grade, 80% of the class is tests which have 24 questions combined, you can't miss more than 1 of those if you want a 4.0
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams were worth 80% of the total grade, so as long as you study hard you should be fine. She makes the exams very similar to her homework as well as previous exams she wrote. Flipped classroom structure was alright, I only went to lecture if I felt that I still didn't have a solid understanding from the readings. She's good at explaining concepts!

This was my objectively a really hard class but if you put in the extra effort to go to office hours and ask questions it's not that bad. She's really nice and good at answering questions and giving multiple ways to solve problems.

She's not quite as bad as some people suggest. This class requires lots of capacity for mathematical reasoning which is just hard regardless. The conceptual problems can be confusing since there are no answer keys. The exams are one of the easiest parts of the class. If you can't stand flipped classroom don't take this class unless you have to.

very intelligent prof who is good at explaining in office hours, but doesnt post answer keys or respond to discussion board. her class is flipped classroom, so if you dont prepare before lecture you will be lost. you either get a 0, 1, 5, 9, or 10 out of 10 on every exam question, but they are similar to her past ones and not too hard. proof heavy

People on here need to give her a break. Yes, it's frustrating that there are no answer keys, but the entire class relies on being able to write an effective proof which is nowhere near one-sided and are generally easy to reason through with the theorems in the book. The class is entirely fair just understand the theorems and you will be fine.

No transparency in grading expectations, including the lack of answer keys for exam preparation. She's one of those teachers who is so convinced she's teaching students the "right" way that she refuses to listen to the students themselves. As is obvious from this rate my professor page, she's gotten this same feedback year after year.

Bad lecturer, horrible grading system. You need to know the esoteric textbook inside out.

The ONE good thing is that her exams are decently fair and just like the homework, which is not true of some other 208 professors at UW. So depending on the quarter she might actually be your best option. RIP to any young innocent pre-208 students. Godspeed.

The grading scale and her style of teaching are intimidating at first, but into the quarter, it comes together. Her explanations can be lacking at times, so it's important to either reach out or go to math lab. She's responsive and gives a lot of practice that is exactly like her exams. The only downside is that there are no answer keys.

Her grading method is weird and intimidating at first, but I think it really helped me focus on my understanding. Her homework is extremely relevant to the exams, so you're never blindsided by the tests. Lectures are informative, textbook is absolutely mandatory. Don't be intimidated by the grading system and just focus on doing better each time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: i have not been to lecture since week 3 bc she make the material so much harder than it needs to be. her lectures do not cover the complexity of exams and her grading scale doesn't make sense. if you have to take her class, watch thomas carr on youtube. she has a lot of practice material so if you study them you can def pass her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the first class I have ever taken where going to lecture makes the class more confusing. She doesn't actually teach any of the material, she has you read a confusing textbook and then expects you to be an expert in lecture the next day. Tests aren't super hard if you study though. Watch Thomas Carr videos and ask TA's questions instead.

The flipped-class approach she uses is ineffective. She expects students to learn material on their own before class. The lectures aren't terrible, but they don't prepare you for the tests. Readings and homework are excessive and time-consuming. This course is far more work than it should be—choose another professor if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Viray is an amazing professor, made me love linear algebra. Great class

if you want some of the worst explainations for some of the most basic topics take this professor. She provides next to nothing to check your understanding or work about the concepts in class. She also has a terrible way of grading where you basically get full, half, or no credit. 10/10 would not recomend

She doesn't provide answer keys for the practice exams, and never provides feedback unless you ask in person at the office hours. Lectures are confusing and hard to follow since she jumps around and adds a lot of math side tangents and exceptions. Get ready to teach yourself the material.

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She expects you to read the textbook + do HW before the lecture on the topic, aka flipped classroom, which is horrible for math. Lectures don't solidify concepts, so were useless, but her review sections before tests were good. Test questions are all fair game, but she never uploads answer keys so you're left wondering what you did wrong.
NEVER TAKE HER CLASS

Lots of questions are proof based, but the worst thing is she never shows what kind of proof is a good proof, which can give you credit. I often get 1/10 points is a problem because I use a conclusion or a theorem outside a textbook, or their is omitted steps in my proof, even if I get the correct answer.

lectures are useless, I need to learn it on YouTube. However, the thing is I used a conclusion I learn in YouTube in the Final exam, and I only get 1/10 points. And the comment is: We have never learned that in lecture.

Lectures weren't very engaging, it was just a lot of her doodling away on her Ipad and not really emphasizing the important stuff. Grading policies are quite frustrating, she will give you half credit or even less for answering problems correctly but giving a valid-ish explanation that she (or TAs, as instructed) slightly disagreed with. I'd avoid.
Avoid this professor if you want a good gpa in this class.

The way she structures this class is actually insane. Homeworks are due before the subject is taught, and nothing is graded until the last week. The content of the exams is easy but they're graded on whether you reference a specific theorem from the textbook, so you can get 1/10 pts for a correct answer. Take this class with literally anyone else.

Don't take this professor. I was willing to over look her awful lectures and tough grading scale (0 1 5 9 10) becuase the midterms were very easy. The final was by no means hard but getting a problem completley right and getting a 1 is frustrating! If you want a good grade and to actually learn the content of linear algebra choose another teacher.

Not good do not take. Avoid at all costs. You will regret.

She made Lin Alg excessively difficult and I'm disappointed.

Horrendous lecturing and grading criteria. I've never had a math professor like this before. I don't understand anything she says in class (what the hell is “walks like a duck quacks like a duck theorem”). One of the most ambiguous math grading I've seen.
avoid this teacher if you can

Lin Alg is a hard class to teach, but she makes it harder than it should be. The whole class is proof-based, so get ready for that. Honestly, all of my learning is done on YouTube. Imo, her tests aren't that hard once you study them, but her grading system is dumb. Not the worst, but also definitely not the best.

Using the flipped classroom model for a completely new branch of math to many people with a dense and strangely arranged textbook is flawed. On problems out of ten, she will only use 0,1,5,9,10. That is an actual policy. Makes no sense. Class is largely based on proofs. Which also makes no sense. Makes this much harder than it should be.

Pretty chill as a person but her grading system is designed to screw you over. Her TAs grade your assignments like they hate you and seldom leave written feedback. Ambiguous rubric/ no release of rubric to hold leverage over your grade.

reviews.comment: If you see this professor for your math class, RUN! She provides no support in class and rarely explains what she's doing. She also spends extremely long writing on her ipad, which only wastes lecture time.

reviews.comment: She teaches her class in a flip teaching format, where the reading assignments are due right before the lecture. Her teaching is horrendous with A LOT of analogies which just doesn't make sense, and which merely harm to our understanding.

The worst teacher I have ever had. I would strongly recommend taking a different class if she is your only option. She is very subjective and unclear on her grading scheme, there are too many small assignments that take up time, the homework is always due before class so there is no point of going. Highly recommend not taking any of her classes.

Work through problems in class.  Most of the time you have to learn the concepts on your own time with the textbook and other resources. Homework was 3 conceptual problems and some practice sets. A 3 credit class... not really

0/10

Worst math professor since primary school She does not know how to teach

The worst professor I met in UW. Sending emails for questions a few times and the first one got no responses, the second one got responses after two weeks, very irresponsible. Putting the double amount of homework at the final weekend, extra pressure on students. Still got no response after sending regrade requests three weeks before. Avoid her.

reviews.comment: Her class is such that you need to teach the material to yourself. Lecture is for asking questions. her explanations for questions are often not enough or are incomprehensible. Before each class theres preassignment which helps to understand the topic sometimes, but you still had to research topics on your own. Quizzes are terrible

Teaches the course in a flipped format meaning that lectures are mostly further explanations of the material/working on harder homework problems and you read the textbook beforehand. The online format had weekly quizzes with 3 midterm like problems each that had problems of increasing difficulty. Overall it's a tough class but she prepares you well

This professor is great, if you don't care about grades. Honestly, she really encourages her students to utilize the internet as a resource, like she will literally link down which keywords to search for and 3blue1brown videos. I will in admit that in class lecture was not as helpful, but I went to office hour and I loved it! Great prof and caring.

She seems like a nice professor but has a really hard time explaining concepts in a way that makes sense algebraically. She isn't gracious about handing out partial credit for work at all
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class in Fall 2020 can be rebranded as a DIY class. Lectures are used as "clarification" for the reading and we're assigned weekly quizzes worth 80% of our grade and has 3 questions each (2 which are very hard). The ONLY way you are learning is from the online textbook, and if you don't like reading technical math jargon you're out of luck :/

Professor Viray's class was a great experience. The way the class is designed, the homework you do will give you some intuition about the concepts that will be presented in the next lecture. Homework assignments are only two problems, but are given after every lecture. She is caring, and her class is very informative.

Very fair grader and spends the time to make sure that those of us who actually attend lecture fully understand the material. She asks a lot of critical questions that really help further your understanding. One of the best professors I've had.
Expect to learn by yourself. This is a nontraditional class where I learned more from one quiz section than 3 days of lectures.

Worst professor I have gotten, do not take her if you expect to learn in lecture. She expects you to teach yourself with the textbook. She does not lecture, instead, she makes us go over one to three problems and discuss them with people around us. This class might as well have been an online class if it's going to be self-taught. Hard exams too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Viray's final exam is more organized than the practice tests. There are definitely no T/F questions so you need to really understand and explain things well. Discussion problems and the second midterm are more abstract and more difficult than the first midterm so you must spend some time studying for them.

A solid choice for Abstract Algebra. She expects a lot from her students, but considering it is a senior level class, that is appropriate. Read before class, do notes from the book. Her lectures are not a carbon copy of the book, in fact the usually only touch on the book's material. Instead they broaden your understanding of the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is very knowledgable but it doesn't mean that she is good in explaining. The proofs she gives are interesting but not necessarily relevant. Even if you have prior calculus background from high school, be prepared for plenty of self-studying because her tests are very difficult and nothing like the homework and lectures.
She's helpful but not the best at explaining things. Having already taken calculus before and already understanding a lot, she kind of made it more confusing.

Professor Viray gives very challenging conceptual tests that require a much deeper understanding of the material than the homework does. If you attend every lecture, take good notes, and study the textbook before exams, you'll be fine. A lot of work for a 3 credit class!

Tests were very conceptual and required much deeper knowledge than I felt we learned and needed for homework. Grading was harsh and there was little partial credit offered. I definitely feel she became a better teacher as the class progressed, and wish I attended more office hours as they are more helpful than the somewhat disorganized lectures.

I would recommend taking another professor. Her lectures sound as if she's reading them directly from the book. She has unreasonable expectations on tests. It felt as though we were writing proofs to theorems that we would learn in the next math class in the series. If you haven't been accepting into your dept, steer clear.
This class quickly turned into a disaster because instead of testing on the mathematics involved with 308 the midterms tested very abstract parts of the class.

Professor Viray knows math very good and for some reason expects students to be on the same level. She gives 5 pages of extremely difficult problems on tests and expect them to be solved in 50 minutes. She doesn't go over any similar problems and doesn't give any test practice sheets. Be prepared to often look for outside help.
If you think a math class should be more about calculations and numbers, don't take this class from her.  If you like proofs and a wordy math class, go for it.
insane amount of reading, difficult to keep up with. the grading system is ridiculous, you can't see your grade until the end of the quarter.

Vince is a nice guy, but his class structure isn't really effective: If you skip class twice, you could lose credit for class. Baseline grade of B+, need to complete lots of EC for a 4.0. SO MANY READINGS, and he basically recaps them in 2hrs. Daily reflection assignments. Everything marked either incomplete/complete. Easy for 300 but also dry :(
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is built upon discussions about the readings that were assigned, so it was difficult to understand what the Professor was talking if I didn't do the readings the previous day. His grading is labor-based grading which was difficult to understand at first, but if you just do all of the assignments on time it shouldn't be difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Vince was extremely accommodating this quarter. We utilized discussion boards on canvas to reflect and talk in small groups, and mostly used the chat function on zoom to discuss with our section. You're graded on your diary, 4 letter assignments (4th one was optional), and participation but he gives out some extra credit opportunities.

Someone who truly cares about his students and it shows. He was very understanding if things came up once or twice and very kind. He really knows the subject well and I learned a lot from each class as a result as well as enjoying each class.

Really nice guy who cares for his students. He is very understanding and is happy to give extensions if needed. Very heavy on the readings though, so be prepared to keep up with them. Simple group participation is a big part of grade. Easy A if you're on track.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: His expectations of us were very unclear. He is very passionate about the subject but his disorganization made it hard for me to feel that same passion. The class itself was not too difficult but it was frustrating at the same time.

The professor gives a meaningful lecture about issei and nisei Americans. The only downside is that the class have to do a lot of readings and online discussion. Other than that, the course is excellent, and I would retake the professor for a different course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: SO MANY READINGS! We had anywhere from 2-5 readings every week and weekly discussion posts about them. You have to buy 4 books and class time is discussion and lecture based. Reading journal on every reading is due with final. Vincent is a super nice guy that will help you out when needed, but super disorganized and unclear of course expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: really nice guy but is extremely unorganized. He will mention an assignment once and barely give any specifics about it, then expect us to know exactly what to do. Grading criteria is very unclear. Class itself is pretty easy though. I showed up about 50% of the time and still got a good grade. Lots of reading but you can get by doing barely any

Very lecture heavy. He is a great person with good intentions, but he is very unorganized and unclear. Many students were confused about midterms, journal and final because he was never clear. So unorganized. The history was rich and beautiful, but the way it was presented was poor. Did the very bare minimum and passed with a great GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Vince really cares about the material that he is teaching. Readings can be heavy some days so do as much as you can but make sure you show up to class. Coming to class really ties things together, fills holes, and would in the end help with your papers and reading journal. Vince is understanding with student stress but make sure you do your part!

Very knowledgeable of the class material and is interested in the subject. Very understanding about students work load and any other issues. Lots of reading, but he provides useful skills for students to skim well in order to still get the information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Knows a lot about the meterían and is really invested in what hes talking about.  Is very understanding about issues of any sort and is available to talk outside of class. Is also very understanding about the load that students have per quarter. LOTS of reading, but he does provide good ways to skim in order to still absorb the information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I took the class cause it seemed interesting and easy. Instead there are tons of readings that are trivial and mostly boring. Somehow he makes an interesting subject a nightmare. I always dread going to class for fear of being lectured to death. Its finals week and we havent received a single grade all year. If youre reading this its too late.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Was looking forward to my class topic, but was very disappointed. The lectures felt endless, class was mostly listening to him go on about multiple diff subjects, only a few of which would seem connected. Outside of class was a ton of reading. The assignments werent difficult, but I definitely dont look forward to class. Would not recommend.

He structures the class as a typical lit class. Expect lots of reading, sitting through two hours of him lecturing, and two papers that show that you "get" the material. It's honestly pretty easy to zone out bc he's monotonous and doesn't engage students well, but he's very open to office hours if you need any help. Show up for daily participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Explained topics well
Good at teaching but lectures are quite boring. He was more engaging in CSE123.

Had him for 123 and really liked him but the content of this course is so boring and difficult to be interested in. I could also tell James enjoyed teaching 123 more, but I don't really blame him. Class was pretty chill but I wouldn't be able to tell you what I learned.
Was interesting and explained topics well.
Great class, attendance is a little bit wonky as they might mark you absent sometimes, which is worth 10% of your grade.

Probably the best CS professor at UW. His lectures are amazing he actually explains in depth with quality examples and doesn't just read off the slides. He gives on-the-job examples which are super useful. Overall a great professor. 100% recommend.

James is very engaging with his concepts and explains the topics in a way that is easy to understand, allowed me to fully grasp the content just soley by listening during lectures. James's lectures are not boring but indeed very interesting and almost like a story, it gets super intresting and made me love the class so much
The class is just boring. Fell asleep multiple times.
Reads off slides like a bedtime story.
He is just reading off the slides for the whole lecture like a speech (without any expression or engagement).

Sits in front and reads off slides. No value in attending lecture. Material is 99% pointless and consists of made up math that doesn't hold any value (if you love math, you'll hate this). Will not use anything learned in this class in any other context.
The class is very boring. I think he is just reading off slides and literally 0 engagement with students. It made learning difficult in this class.

He simply reads off of slides, and doesn't make any effort to engage students. I am not finding any value by attending lectures, and it's evident the rest of the class doesn't either, as less than half of the class attends lecture.
Tbh class is kinda boring, and I have fallen asleep in class before
He is a great teacher. Lots of good visual examples and answers questions thoroughly. Projects are graded harshly on insufficient comments.
james also teaches 344!

I echo the sentiment of the previous reviews. You don't have to attend the lectures to do well in the class, but they're def useful for stuff that you don't really learn in high school. The grading's tough cause of the TAs, but if you use your resubs wisely then it shouldn't be much of a problem. Overall good intro course and James is a great prof.
His lectures are very helpful and engaging. He draws lots of pictures which is nice.

Funny and engaging professor especially during lecture. They aren't required but very worthwhile attending since he's great at breaking down concepts. My least favorite part about this class was that TAs are very particular about grading and often nitpick over code quality instead of the actually concepts.
James is a funny and engaging lecturer! This class truly equips you with all the tools you need to succeed-- every TA is also amazing. Great experience, learned a lot.

Wilcox is a good programmer and professor and his lectures were interesting despite me having previous experience with most concepts. I did find that project grading (by TAs) was quite specific and highly focused on code quality; it was a bit annoying. You can see past assignments online on the course website.

Lectures were great. He does a great job at explaining concepts and giving the right mental models for digesting the course material. Absolutely go to them. Grading can be tough at times, but that's more of a departmental issue rather than the professors themselves.

Clear lectures, homework is pretty strictly graded for commenting, quality, etc. A lot of kids in 123 have knowledge beyond the scope of the course, but will still need to lock in on the homework due to these standards.

Entertaining and engaging teacher during lectures! Although homework is graded extremely strictly (and I mean extremely), resubmissions are allowed once per week for assignments. This works well because there is typically only one assignment per week, so you can ace all the assignments if you get them right within at least one resubmission.

James is a great lecturer and he makes lectures very interesting, and he has a good sense of humor. His teaching style is very organized and structured, easy to follow along even if you miss a day. Highly recommend participating and following along in lectures since he goes over content that is very relevant to the quizzes.

Great lecturer and one of the best professors I've had. He knows how to effectively explain any topic. His lectures are fun and very informational. He does a lot of in class coding rather than going over too many slides which has proven to be a very effective method of teaching.

He is a great lecturer and is good at breaking complicated topics and explaining where they fail and succeed. He has significantly changed my understanding of how Java works. Homework is reasonable but get started early! You always know what to expect because everything is planned out at the beginning of the quarter, and rubrics are explained.
really average class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lecture-wise, he's great. Unlike most OS profs, his class has a final. Details about the final were vague and replies on ed were slow. We weren't given practice finals and were told to review past problem sets and lab questions, most of them didn't get graded until a day before the final which made it difficult to prepare in advance.

For CSE 344 (not 341). Lectures were fun and he clearly cared a lot about databases. Homework was very simple and easy (except for the last two), as well as the tests. Answers questions on Ed very  quickly and with lots of insight.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Highly recommend taking with James! His lectures were really interesting and you could tell he cares about not just explaining content but also why it is important. Homework was all things that were covered in class, and exams were completely reasonable. He's also active on Ed and could easily be asked questions outside of class. Great quarter :)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is for CSE 344, not 341 (344 wasn't an option). The only reason why I took this class this quarter is just so I could have James as a professor for the third time. The class was incredibly fun, and the final project was challenging but rewarding. Overall one of my favorite profs.

CSE 344, NOT 341 - didn't have the option to pick. He clearly cares a lot about teaching but he's also super funny so he doesn't take things too seriously. Lectures were absolutely necessary, but they were recorded so I did them from home. Weekly hw assignments weren't hard. Tests were reasonable! Overall one of the best UW CS profs imo

Phenomenal lecturer and explains important tools and concepts very clearly with connections to helpful examples. Grading in the 12x series can be very strict (almost exceedingly) but he was very generous with opportunities to resubmit assignments.
good professor and i got a 4.0 but not very approachable

The lectures made concepts easy to understand and covers the basics, but I do feel really lost when doing the programming assignments. I was at the IPL every week trying to get help to make myself understand what's going wrong with my code. It could be a struggle for commuters but quizzes and final were surprisingly easier than coding projects.

James was a fine professor. Lectures could be boring, but he did have important explanations that were crucial to understanding the material. There's one project a week for the class. They aren't really hard, but they still take time. Most of the learning will come from section, the projects, and your own effort and practice with programming.

I can tell he cares but the grading criteria is extremely unrealistic and his lectures are hard to follow as the class progresses because he rushes through topics and oversimplifies them (which we later faced the consequences for during project completion). The grading for the projects is absurd as resubs can hurt your grade even for minor errors.

I was going to give him a 5. But he came up with a super difficult FINAL that contained a lot of very detailed points that he hadn't covered in class. He has a great sense of humor in his classes and is very easy to talk to. However, his lectures is very fast and often time switches windows and he cuts away before I have a chance to read the code.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really made me want to give up CS all together.
lectures were a waste of my time. The TA's are great.

Overall a good professor. However the lectures weren't super helpful as they were mostly just simiplified explanations of the topic. The best way to learn was in the quiz sections and just through other students.
He offers a R-James resub opportunity!
Nice guy, good at lecturing. Nothing against him in particular, the 12X series just sucks, but he's a great guy.
I wish to have James teach me again in my UW CSE Career.
What a guy. Well deserved rating on here.
just a bad person
James is an amazing professor and really cares about his students. Very good at explaining things and debugging! Would highly recommend taking his classes!!
Professor Wilcox is a joy to have as a lecturer.

James is very funny and very engaged when lecturing, and you can see the passion that he has of what he's teaching because he really likes computer science! Sometimes can have a little bit of trouble speaking up and telling the class to quiet down though. Overall good professor!
really engaging and funny
Very good at explaining concepts and setting you up for success in assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the best lecturers in CSE

I have to give James some love. I took both his 452 class and Web browser class and they were both amazing. He's a really funny guy and the grading criteria is concise (you can get a 4.0 if you put in the work). I would be super down to take another class with him.

Really excellent professor. I had him and Zachary Tatlock for CSE 505 and both made the class really fun. James is quick on the spot and often has examples on-hand to answer even the most tangential student questions. The grading policy is super transparent, which is helpful because the homework in 505 is pretty tough. Awesome course and class!

Tough assignments but he's very accessible and will talk about programming languages for hours. Overall a really cool guy who cares more about the fact that his students learn than the grade they recieve.

It was a hard course, but I really enjoyed taking it with James. I thought he spent lots of time prepping for his lectures. His classes tend to use a pretty compassionate points system, so you can choose what you want to do and still get a 4.0, which comes pretty handy towards the end of the quarter when I'm seriously running out of energy.

He hardly prepared for the lecture and just read the PPT. Some examples of codes that he wanted to show in the lectures didn't work. Finally, only about 20% of the students attended the class. Grading was always delayed so they affected the next assignments and exams. Rubric, weighted points, and reasons for deductions were not properly registered.
Very enthusiastic and caring professor; the best I've ever had in the CSE department so far. I loved his class!!

Josh is awesome, if you have a chance you should definitively take his class. He teaches with such clarity and is extremely easy to understand. He really cares about you as a student and wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: hardest class i have ever taken, but incredibly kind professor who took time to help me finish the quarter strong when i reached out. would definitely recommend

Josh is so funny as he likes to blow stuff up, and he's very dedicated to teaching. But he sometimes went over unnecessary stuff in lecture and filled slides with long equations. The hw and Python do take a while, so utilize his office hours. The quizzes were pretty hard, but not impossible, but you def need some calculus knowledge for this class.

This class was probably my favorite in the honors series. Vaughan is really funny and obviously cares a lot about his students. This class is advertised as "if you put in the work, you will get a good grade," and I do really think that holds true. It's more work than the regular series of course, but if you stay diligent it will pay off.

Professor Vaughan is very passionate about teaching and chemistry in general. I personally loved his teaching style as he goes at a quick pace, but also goes in depth and is always open for questions. His grading is incredibly transparent, but this is still a hard class as python assignments and fast paced quizzes will challenge you. 10/5 class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He made things so unreasonably difficult. All practice problems given were much easier than tests. Although you didn't need coding experience, coding assignments were very difficult and little to no help was given, was told to google how to do it. Spent full lectures discussing his research then told us to learn topics on the exam via google.
Very smart and caring professor. Always willing to answer questions and help.

SO much work!will mention that 1st lab was disaster but class gets better(lots dropped after)partial credit on exams will save ur LIFE/GRADE.he was great lecturer tho he was not particularly helpful for the last units but whatever/i would say read the txtbook prequiz+look@slides/class was fun!he always tried to entertain us!curve was incredible!

midway through chem145 and josh is crazy. he's up past 12 am responding to students on canvas and he helps me out even when i make simple mistakes with python. on that note be ready to have a weekly schedule consisting of lab/lab report, quiz/quiz prep, textbook homework, and python. but he blows stuff up and wears awesome chemistry pun shirts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Josh is awesome. Extremely caring guy and funny. The material is super difficult, however he makes it clear that he is aware of it and sets up his lectures and grading methods accordingly. His tests were very hard though, some of the most challenging I have taken. But they were fair, and never deviated from what he taught. I would take him again!

I liked Prof Vaughan. He had a fun personality, and he had a way of making challenging problems seem less challenging in lecture. He also supplied us with helpful resources. Of course, he still threw curveballs on exams. Redo homework problems constantly, and do all of the practice tests. I personally didn't use the textbook or online notes.
I would lay down my life for this man
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Josh is nice person and great professor! 
The class is hard, and he acknowledges that. It was a LOT of work, but his lectures were funny and useful, his office hours were always helpful, and he was often available on the canvas discussion board outside of work hours. Too much python imo, but don't let that stop you from taking the course.

Great lectures and in-class demos, but assignments (homework and Python) were very long and keys were not uncommonly incorrect. Definitely a very smart dude that loves what he does, but not for people who don't want Chem to occupy every moment of their existence like it does for him.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Incredible guy. You can really tell he cares about the subject matter and his students and wants them to succeed. That said, you won't do well unless you put in the effort. He's willing to meet you where you are and will genuinely be up at 3 am answering emails and checking the Canvas discussion board. Also his in-class demos are great.
very funny and inspirational professor with average level of difficulty exams

Lectures are information heavy and move fast. Luckily, the slideshow and lecture recordings are available. While attendance is not mandatory, his classes often have interesting demonstrations and are worth attending. Quizzes are hard but your lowest score is dropped, and he curves the average up to 3.5. 11/10, would recommend to chemistry lovers.

As a professor, he is really kind and very attentive on the discussion board, but his exams are quite challenging. Also, the equation sheet provided for the exams is not that helpful as a lot of equations you actually need are not there. :( but he does a lot of fun demonstration and gives you candies.

Homework was manageable, lectures were great. Complicated concepts were simply explained and he didn't mince words. Always willing to answer questions and exams never had surprises. His online notes are rightfully his magnum opus. I liked Prof. Vaughan a lot, and would absolutely recommend his class! Pchem isn't so scary with him as a prof :)

BEST PROF I've ever had, a rare occasion when prof puts more work into the course than students; ie. sleeps less than you. Explains everything as clearly as possible, always stops for questions. Makes hard but very doable quizzes/assignments, pushes us to APPLY knowledge. Extremely caring and approachable. Prepares you well for 155, 165

wasn't a huge fan of the lectures, but the amount of outside help and support he provided was impeccable. try to read the textbook or you will be playing maze runner. quizzes were a time crunch, but managable with a reasonable amount of studying (3 hrs). idk i just rly liked him. he emailed me at 4 am after i emailed him at 3 am. why is he awake.
This professor replies to discussion posts 3am at night and generally respond to emails within hours. His lectures can almost count as an entertainment.

The lectures - while fast - were very well taught and insightful. I recommend reading the textbook beforehand so you don't get too lost. He also cares a lot about his students. He'll reply to questions at 2 AM, stay after class, etc. A great prof. Just be aware of the LARGE amount of homework. It was about 25 hours per week, with Python tears.

Genuinely one of the most insightful and enjoyable classes I have ever taken. Josh is super caring for his students and an excellent teacher as well. He was teaching a new curriculum this quarter but his familiarity with the material was unquestionable and it was clear how much effort he put in for his students. Hard, but worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Although Professor Vaughan is a really nice and charismatic guy, he failed many students this quarter when it came to educating. I was a part of his first 145 course with the new curriculum, and as he stated, we were his guinea pigs. He gave us assignments he knew we didn't know how to complete and his goals on tests were for half of us to fail.

(taken Au19) Prof. Vaughan gives interesting lectures with fair mix of concepts, example problems, and do it your self. He also gives super interesting in class demos. He values feedback a lot. He is caring to students. 145 is concept and quantatative reasoning heavy, so be prepared for the amazing ride!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: (online during covid) I can't stand chem, but Josh put more effort into the switch to online learning of any professor I've had or heard of. The amount that he cares about his students is astonishing and he will respond at 2am to questions. The class was very difficult, and the profs are a package deal--be warned that Prof Ginger, for 155, is evil.

Vaughan was my favorite professor my first quarter. Very thoughtful, well-planned lectures and adapted to the online format well. The class was fairly difficult but that is to be expected in an honors chem class. Overall, great professor, awesome office hours and will respond to emails at 2 AM.

Vaughan is truly the best. He's a genius, and the content of this class will blow your mind even if you have a AP Chem background. By far the nicest professor, he's so reasonable and accomodating. He is truly the best.

Prof Vaughan is so amazing!! He was very patient with all my questions, and he really goes out of his way to be accommodating and help students learn. His lectures were always engaging (even with the online format), and I was able to just use his lecture notes instead of the textbook, which saved me hours of useless, confusing textbook reading.

Professor Vaughan was an amazing start to chemistry. His well planned lectures allowed him to effectively teach the class material. The class was not exceptionally hard, but you have to work for your grade. Plus, Vaughan is a very friendly and caring teacher, that really wants you to succeed. He will set the bar high for other professors.

Josh is Awesome. He has a really good sense of how challenging he can make the class without making it unreasonable. If you like chemistry you will love 145 with Josh. He really cares about his students and gives fun engaging lectures. Plus the curve really reduces stress. Word to the wise though, do your research on all the 1x5 profs not just josh

Vaughan was an amazing teacher to have as my first professor at the UW. Just this year he was nominated for a UW Distinguished Teaching Award. I had his class in Fall 2020 (online due to COVID); he fully revamped the curriculum to adjust for the course being online. He cares a lot about his students and is very available. Class is very hard though
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Vaughan spends tremendous effort to bond with his students. He's extremely down to earth and will always surprise you with his goofy demos.

Tests are pretty big. Homework is basically graded on accuracy, but averages are lower for those than you'd think so don't fret too much. Labs aren't graded on accuracy but you give yourself an ample amount of time to work on them, cause if you don't get them it can get frustrating. Lecture notes are AMAZING - use them for memorizing derivations.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was a really tough class but it is very rewarding. Dr. Vaughan is very helpful.

Taking this class is hard but rewarding. He makes it clear that if you put in the effort, you will be rewarded, as the curve is set high. Vaughan is a greater lecturer, explaining things in detail and checking to make sure the class understands each part.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Best Chem professor I've seen. First quarter honors chem wasn't that bad because of his riveting lectures. I enjoyed every class and the tests honestly weren't that bad as long as you knew what was going on in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is an Honors class, and going into it first quarter at UW is tough. If you are 100% dedicated to doing only school work I say go for it. But if you want to dip your toes into the college social life, I would suggest 142, definately a doable 3.5, this class takes atleast 3-5 hours outside of lecture. 3.0 is doable but it takes work.

Honestly, he is the best professor that I have ever had here at UW. He is super funny and makes lecture engaging. He doesn't record his lectures, so attending class is a must. He posts detail lecture notes which is really nice. His exams are super tough but fair. Averages are around 50% which I really appreciate since students can beat the curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The tests were fair and covered content that was covered in both the lecture and the homework. His lectures were interesting enough and the demos were pretty fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor. Cares a lot about the student's learning.

He gives EXCELLENT lecture notes so attending class isn't mandatory. He really cares a lot and almost no one fails. The homework is a bit challenging but going to tutorial and office hours really is so valuable. He is also really forgiving and drops your lowest 25% so like a midterm, the homework or even half your final. He gives really hard exams.

Professor Vaughan was fantastic, & I truly felt like I learned a ton. Obviously, being an honors class means it was very tough and your peers will be SMART, but I never once felt like the content was beyond my capabilities if I got extra help/worked harder. Labs were a bit dull, quiz sections were hugely helpful, lectures were thorough/math heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: good teacher, but hard class

This guy is an amazing lecturer. His class is challenging, but you get a lot out of it if you put a lot in. He is very approachable and very helpful, and he does the coolest demos in class. Go to office hours and don't skip class, but would highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor! It's a tough class, but his lectures are interesting and engaging, his office hours are very helpful, and he grades fairly. It can be difficult to prepare for tests because there are limited practice problems, but this will get better with time because he uses old exams as practice tests. He also has some really great demos.

Josh made me actually like chemistry, which was weird for me because high school chem caused me more stress and anxiety than anything in my life. He's a great professor, is hilarious, and genuinely cares about his students, especially if you reach out to him outside of class. I definitely recommend him!
Great teacher for being such a young guy. He can be unclear sometimes and can get mixed up in his own thoughts, so be sure to go to office hours, where he will definitely help sort stuff out.

It was a hard class, but its honors so that is to be expected. The lectures were ok, but he mainly just did problems then walked around and then solved the problem. No real lecturing, exams were ok just very mathy and not a lot of chemistry for say, if you know how to use a formula, no real concepts. overall an ok class, you are smart don't worry!

Dr. Vaughan is friendly, approachable, and does fun demos. The class is difficult and its essential to do your homework and be comfortable with math/physics to keep up with the average in the class (it's honors- people are really smart). His lecture notes are helpful and clear but he is often algebra-heavy with solving problems.

His lectures are very fun and entertaining, and he loves to do demos which can be really fun. It's not an easy class, so you will need to put a lot of work in to understand some of the topics. Overall he is a great professor who is willing to help you understand the material, and even learns everyone's name by the end of the year.

Lectures are sometimes confusing where he will skip steps when doing calculations. He cares about his students a lot and will help you if you ask for help. A kind professor. Tests are very hard as it's pchem.

One of the hardest class I've ever taken. He sometimes rushes through multiple steps when doing calculations but he gets the general idea through. He occasionally makes mistakes in his lectures. He really cares about students and holds his own review session and learns almost everyone's name in class. He's a fair grader also.

I love this man! Chemistry teachers are always my favorite. He is very entertaining during lectures and he really tries to get to know his students. He is really smart and he wants us to succeed. However the class was really hard material and you have to work really hard to do well.

Dr. Vaughan is my favorite teacher ever. Lectures were engaging, interesting and entertaining. He literally cares so much for his students and helped us to understand the course material. Dr. Vaughan stimulated my interest of learning chemistry.  His class was a lot of fun and noteworthy . definitely must take class

One of the best professors I have had. Really cares about his students learning and it shows. Lectures are interesting, entertaining, and make tough concepts totally understandable. Of course the material is hard, it's Pchem, but you'll learn a ton in his class.

One of the best professors at UW. :) Professor Vaughan is a great lecturer; his lecture is always interesting and engaging. He also posts detailed lecture notes after each lecture for students to study.  He remembers everyone by name and genuinely cares about us. Not an easy class, but it was a lot of fun!
Simply an amazing Professor.

Dr. Vaughan is probably the best P-chem professor you can have. Goes the extra distance to make sure you understand the material by posting A LOT on the forums, and is there for you during office hours. Lecture notes had minor mistakes but is quite negligible. Good demos (esp. the hydrogen balloon), and is overall a great teacher. Good luck on exam
Dr. Vaughan will help you if you seek his assistance. Chem 145 was the most challenging class I've taken in college.

Professor Vaughan is one of the best teachers I've had in my life. He gave our class hard material, but he was always available to help us through it, and was very good at explaining and connecting the concepts in the class. He also learned every one of our names, and really seemed to know and care about us individually.  Great teacher; kind man.

Good job lecturing. Granted, this is honors chemistry, so the material and the content is HARD. You have to work hard to understand the material (at least I did and many others) The first test average was roughly 66100.  He does however, make a lot of errors while lecturing, and sometimes even on tests, which is more annoying than anything

Josh was great! He was helpful and understanding. He always makes a genuine effort at being extremely approachable, and it often works! One of the (if not the) best professor iv had at the UW. Also, he was cute :P Chilly peppers all around.

Dr. Vaughan genuinely cares about his students and shows it. From providing super detailed lecture notes, to answering discussion board posts late at night, to even holding an exam review session over a weekend, there was no doubt that he was willing to do anything he could to help his students succeed. I definitely recommend this professor!

An incredible professor/person! Really went out of his way for us students and responded to our feedback. He was open to correction and always approachable! Very engaging and genuinely wanted all of us to learn the material. The class is difficult but he was more than fair in his grading! His notes have all the info you need. Definitely recommend!

This was the professor's first time teaching this course, which may explain some of the errors on his notes, but their extent and detail was impressive. There was no need for the textbook. His enthusiasm was evident in every lecture he gave. You'll have to work hard for an A, but a passing grade is attainable. His grading is more than fair.

By far one of my favorite professors at UW. He had great notes and was an easy lecturer to follow along with. He also put an enormous amount of effort into making sure everyone understood the material. The tests were pretty difficult, but it's pchem so you wouldn't expect anything less. I definitely recommend him!

This professor was wonderful. The amount of work he put in on students' behalf is actually kind of frightening. This is p chem, so yes, it is rather difficult until you learn a few tricks. Make sure to go to class and pay more attention to lecture notes than the textbook, which is a complete mess with numerous solution errors.

He is easily the most enthusiastic physical chemistry professor you'll find. It's a hard class but you'll learn a lot. The homework really isn't that bad and builds on the lectures very well. YOU NEED TO GO TO CLASS. He really does provide enough resources for anybody to at least pass the class if they make use of them.

Great teacher, I appreciated his willingness to admit when he didn't know an answer or when he made a mistake. The amount of effort/time he put into the class was really great. He was definitely a dedicated prof!

This was incredibly difficult subject matter, taught out of a terribly written book. If you took all of your math and physics pre-req's your freshman year be prepared for a world of hurt. Vaughan's HW problems are MUCH better than the book and will help you learn the subject matter faster. (if you could learn it at all solo).Great teacher,bad cours

Not as bad as previous comments say- it's his first time teaching the class. He was good at replying on discussion board posts and was open to students questions/corrections (he does make mistakes). His notes are really helpful to study with - he does skip steps, but it's usually basic algebra. Tests were difficult, but he's a fair grader.

Please avoid...contents i believe are not too hard to understand but this professor makes them extremely hard. Especially his notes. He skips multiple steps at once so you get stuck very frequently. And when you find out what trick he used, you will feel very frustrated how easy it was but it is very hard to realize at the first place.

very bad Professor. Too many typos on homework and Lecture notes, does not teach within the scope of the homework problems which makes it very very frustrating to do his assignments. This professor simply cannot teach, plain and simple.

This professor makes up his own homework problems that are 15% of the grade.  They are constantly with lots of typos and errors, which he later corrects. They are not found in book for reference so if you are an independent learner, you will feel stuck.

I knew no Chinese going in to this class so I was very nervous, but Ma laoshi is SO sweet and soft spoken, she was not scary at all! And she's very understanding, like if you have to turn in something late. It's a pretty fast paced class (I think all language classes are tho) but you will get used to it and it will get easier!!!

She's very sweet and cares a lot about whether you learn. It is sometimes easy to get lost during lecture, but she creates assignments that help you to preview everything that will be covered, so as long as you put in the effort, this class will treat ya well.

马老师 is one of the best professors I have had at UW. She has a professional attitude while maintaining a kind heart and helpful nature. Her lessons are concise and I think she has mastered the pacing of an introductory Chinese class. She is a generous and fair grader. I am lucky to again have her for CHIN 102, and I think very highly of her.
Ma laoshi the goat. She's really caring, helpful, and supportive! Encouraged us to not be afraid of making mistakes especially when speaking. Highly rec going to office hours.

Xi Ma is one of the best professors I've ever had the opportunity to study under. I took the series of Chinese 101-103 with her and it has probably been the only class I will never regret taking student loans for. If you are at all interested in learning Chinese, I urge you to give her a chance.

She is nice with grading on oral exams and on quizzes that are given 2-3 a week. Bit of studying required but it builds up as you go so things can get easier. Don't memorize pinyin for exams, characters are better in long run as it helps reduce chances of losing points due to wrong tone marks. She's very understanding about personal circumstances.
Really great teacher! She is probably one of my favorite Professors.

As long as you pay attention to the lectures, you will have no issues with this class. She explains everything very clearly and is always willing to answer questions. High key the goat, would take again, am taking again.

She's really good at answering question and giving us opportunities to practice speaking in class without feeling overwhelmed or put on the spot. She doesn't make you feel embarrassed or stupid for getting something wrong and is a relatively easy grader.
She is the platonic ideal of a professor. Kind, knowledgeable, detailed. Xi Ma went above and beyond. I cannot overstate how lovely my learning experience was.
She is the best Chinese teacher ever. She is SUPER kind, and have a very clear answer for every question you have. DEFINITELY RECOMMEND.

Ma laoshi made Chinese feel easy. She's a very lenient grader, but there are a lot of things you are graded on. Low-stakes quizzes every day based on memorization, but exactly what you're expected to memorize is stated clearly & you are graded very nicely. Same with bigger exams, expectations are clear and she is clearly very passionate and caring.
She was great. Her lectures were super interesting! Her exams were pretty easy, the group project counts for a lot of your grade, but she was always happy to help.

She's energetic, but talks for the whole class. 40% of your grade is exams where it covers all the previous content for it, but curveballs are thrown at you for the questions. Other 40% group projects for a final presentation, where you can only do it outside of class time. Marks you for the littlest of things. I would rather take other professors
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great prof well educated. Lectures are actually interesting. There are some clicker questions so you need to be in class or have a friend that will send u the link. One final presentation but not that hard. Just listen during the lectures and you'll be good.

I took her during her first year teaching, she was very passionate about what she was teaching but didn't have the best class structure yet. Midterm and final were online, timed, with multiple choice and free responses. The grading criteria was unclear and easy to loose points. She likes to grade to the hundredth of a decimal like 19.87/20.
Nice professor, young, energetic, humorous. Love her.

She knows the content but struggles to convey the key concepts. Her frequent grammar errors make lectures even harder to follow. Slides cover a lot of content but unorganized. Homework instructions are unclear, and workload is excessive, seemingly ignoring that students have other responsibilities. I learned better from online resources.
Very good professor. Sets a demanding pace. Sometimes the assignments include pretty tedious technical components around data ingestion and output, but I suppose that's good to have to do.

Professor Xia is clearly very intelligent. However, I feel she has a hard time explaining concepts in lectures. For example- my class was very new to machine learning. Rather than framing the domain- we launched full long into a term long project, with little guidance. The same approach happened with each lecture (push forward regardless).
very good lecturer.  Learnt a lot from her class and I'm using the algorithms I learnt from her class in my job now!
she is a great instructor who really knows the domain inside and out.

Hard to understand in lecture. Her work is easy to follow but her explanations didn't make that much sense sometimes. Her TAs were really slow and didnt grade things until the very end. Class is heavily weighted on exams, only 10 percent homework.

She lectures using her own notes, not textbooks, which leaves you with no extra reading or practice questions. She's also late to classes (even exams). Her panopto recordings are of poor quality, often with no image or sound. The final exam is bizarre, covering almost nothing from the first half of the course. Grading is also vague. Not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely did better after I stopped going to her lectures. Tests are your entire grade (90%) and are WAY harder than the lecture and homework examples. Use Thomas Carr on UW and never attend her class.

Xiaowen's lectures are good and examples in class make sense based on what is taught. Tests are NOT easy. In fact, they are quite difficult and nothing like the tests in the math department archive because she teaches based off of a pirated textbook. Good luck, do your best, unfortunately there is only so much you can do to prepare for the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There has been multiple times she has been late to lecture, and at one point our midterm. She is a nice and funny professor, however her exams are completely different from other professors, and her lectures don't adequately help her students prepare for exams, as she provides very little prep material.

Her lectures were alright, tests much harder than any homework or lecture problem. She often forgot to charge her computer and did a large chunk of our lectures on the whiteboard. This wasn't ideal since she has the handwriting of a right-handed pharmacist using their left. If you have experience with ODEs the class should be a breeze. I did not :(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures were okay the only thing is her handwriting was sort of hard to understand. The homework was not bad at all, but the tests were quite difficult. It felt like there were little resources to prepare for her exams and she said all we needed were her lecture notes but then the test would just be everything on another level.

I had an ok experience in this class. I felt that the professer had clear lectures that really helped me understand the concepts. However, for exams, there was very little practice material given (only provided one practice exam that was not similar to the actual exam at all) and the exams were VERY difficult. She does give a lot of partial credit.
Average lectures, really hard tests
Has very difficult exams, make sure to study off of the lecture slides and be ready for edge cases you haven't seen before in class.

Explanations/notes/answer keys are unorganized, hard to understand-- she often skips/simplifies steps-- and sometimes incorrect. Exams are entirely pulled from lecture notes, only much trickier. Homework is long and hard, and does not align with test content. Great person though. Gracious grader, considering 60-70% exam average scores.
