She's pretty funny in lectures, but overall class structure is unorganized and grades take 2+ weeks. Grades are heavily based off of tests, which she doesn't give much study material for and are more difficult than other professors'. Exams are heavily based off of her lecture notes, so you'll probably do ok if you understand them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Xiaowen displayed gross incompetence as an instructor, copying both midterms exactly from past quarters, giving people who knew someone who took it the previous term an unfair advantage. Doesn't follow the rest of the department's lesson plans, has harder exams, and routinely arrived late to her own lectures. Finding a different prof recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: HIGHLY emphasizes using lecture notes & examples to practice for exams over doing homework problems or the past exams provided by the math department. Took 2 weeks to grade the 1st midterm, and 3 weeks for the second with only a few days left till the final. Her notes can be messy, so its best to take your own during lecture.

Gives a lot of examples in her lecture notes, but her writing can be messy so sit in the front of class. Homework is light. Took the second midterm almost 3 weeks ago and it still hasn't been graded and our final less than a week away. It's hard to prepare for exams cuz she's stingy with providing past exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, a super clear and effective lecturer, I really enjoyed her teaching style and the examples helped a lot on the exams. The first exam was honestly really difficult, but I think 207 is the type of class where you really have to understand the topics to succeed. I highly recommend :)

Good professor overall, I like her lecture style and she does a ton of examples which makes a huge difference in understanding material. Only bad thing is that it takes 2-3 weeks for the exams to be graded. SO FRUSTRATING. The final is in 6 days and we still haven't gotten midterm 2 back (took 18 days ago). She needs to get on the TA's.

This professor is pretty ok. Her lectures are good and she does a lot of examples. But for the first exam she only provided us with one practice exam and no answer key. Second exam we got one practice exam which included the answers, so there's very little practice u can do before exams.

Gave only one practice test with no answer key for midterms, wasn't even going to provide that until she realized some students had found it online already. Extremely test heavy and the actual tests are 1000x harder than her practice midterms. Stopped going to lecture and supplemented with Thomas Carr on youtube instead. Wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was pleasantly surprised by Xiaowen's teaching style and care for her class. If audio gets messed up on Panopto recordings, she re-records and publishes it. She is quick at responding to Canvas messages if you have questions about the weekly homework. Tests are difficult when it comes to grading, but that's more of a math department problem.

Xiaowen was super knowledgeable and most of this class was a breeze for me (with the exception of the final). Really enjoyed her deadpan sense of humor and her lectures were very instructive and concise. She made ODEs feel super painless and intuitive!

Easy midterm, will see how final is. Long but good assignments, one every 2 weeks. Posted good lecture notes. Not always the best explanations for me so I often supplemented with the textbook. Not a bad prof, not my favorite
The grading is fairly lenient and the tests are a good difficulty but aren't too hard. I really liked this class

She is so great! She does all the work on the whiteboard, so try to sit at the front. The tests are very fair and when people did better than she anticipated, she curved the class differently to reward our hard work.

Professor Zhu is a great professor. Lectures are clear and give good examples of what to expect on the test. Zhu is very patient and nice. The worst parts about the course (test heavy, aggressive curve, ect.) are due to the math department, not Professor Zhu herself.

Xiaowen is a great lecturer! She knows and explains the course materials very well! She always provides a lot of examples to explain the concept, which works very well for me. Some problems in her exams can be a bit hard but all exam problems are from her lecture notes. So it's easy to prepare for the exam as long as you pay attention in her class.

Xiaowen's schedule is completely different from all the other sections for 207 and for no good reason. Poor class resources, subpar desired, midterm 1 had a question that she had not taught us how to solve because "you guys seem smart enough to figure it out.", both midterms were identical to last year so the curve sucked.Thomas Carr on YT saved me

Amazing professor. She did a great job of defining the different kinds of problems you will be faced with, and then outlining how to solve each kind. Super comprehensive. I wish I could have her for every math class!

The professor talks clearly and thoroughly. When I have questions, I go to the office hour to ask until I understand. The professor has great patience. I'm always amazed by how she can make complex topics feel so approachable and understandable. The way you explain concepts makes learning feel enjoyable and less intimidating.

Professor Xiaowen Zhu at the University of Washington is an exceptional educator who demonstrates a profound passion for teaching and mentoring students. Their deep knowledge and expertise in their field are evident in the clarity and depth of their lectures.

Go to lectures and pay attention to lectures. The exams are hard but they are for the most part fair, the final was something else though. Gives loads of partial credit so as long as you are studying her lecture slides and practice problems, you can pass. Her lecture style is made up of all examples which worked well for me.

Prof Zhu is so awesome!!! Currently tied for my favorite math prof at UW. Super funny and gives really good explanations. She gives step-by-step strategies for solving problems that are easy to follow. She spends most of class going over example problems that are very similar to what's on homework and exams. So so great! Would highly recommend!!

One of the two best profs I've had in my entire life! Inspiring and super funny, she was kind and interested in student success. While she'd cover proofs and definitions a little, she mostly spent class time doing practice problems. You'd never see something on homework or exams that hadn't been covered in some way in class. She's so amazing!

I loved MATH207 with Professor Zhu! She didn't follow a textbook; all content was taught via very information-dense, fast-paced lectures instead. Her tests (except the final) were pretty straightforward and similar to lectures. She seemed to genuinely care about us and was super nice and understanding, not to mention hilarious too, recommend!

Doesn't know the material, once said "I don't know, this is too hard" on a practice problem and then that exact problem was on an exam. Relies heavily on practice problems in lecture which isn't bad but explanations can be lackluster. Had to teach myself a lot of the concepts in this class.
Try out the final in Winter 2024, and you will know everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She relies solely on doing examples in class and just assumes everyone has the knowledge she does. She never slows down, making sure people get it.If you get lost then you're screwed. Her notes are super hard to follow, and her grading scale is even harder to follow. 90% of your grade is between 3 tests so if you struggle with test then good luck.

Honestly, she's really good. Her teaching style revolves around example proofs then explaining the relevant topic. It works super well, at least for me. Her lectures go very fast towards the end and there's a lot of content. She sometimes doesn't notice when people have their hands raised so if you have questions you should be vocal about it.

Xiaowen might be one of the smartest people at UW. She knows the material inside and out. All questions asked in-class were answered quickly and in a helpful manner. She is also helpful outside of class, has a fun sense of humor, and presents the material well (she relies solely on the whiteboard, so sit towards the front). I recommend this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Zhu is one of the best Math professors at UW. She is an amazing lecturer and has a good sense of humor. Her exam is very fair if you practice and do her assigned homework. When you have any confusion about any material, the professor and the TA are always available to help you resolve that confusion. Overall, Prof. Zhu is awesome!

One of the best professor I've met in uw, she is so passionate in the class, and tries to make the lecture as clear as possible. Each of her lecture has a brief summary and some practice questions at the end. She'll also provide revision lecture before midterm and final, and also give some very helpful practice question. Only 4 very easy HW!

I believe this was Xu's first time teaching at Foster. She is very knowledgeable, but a lot of solo work is necessary to grasp the concepts of the class. Lectures were confusing and lacked interaction. Xu was very nice and I'm sure her classes will quickly improve.
Professors should have to take an exam or something to prove they can teach. If they did have one, Xu would not pass.
Take literally any other finance elective. Do not put yourself through this. Lectures are unstructured and confusing.
Just don't take her.

If you have a choice, do not take her. Prone to emotional outbursts, goes incredibly fast with minimal explanation, slurs words, heavy accent. 2 midterms worth 20% of grade each and final worth 35% so 75% of your grade is 3 quizzes. She is lenient with late work and seems to care about teaching, but shes just not good at it.

She gets confused at herself a lot. She gave three pop quizzes which were okay. Some of the questions on the midterm were like the ones she provided but there was at least one question that we never went into depth about. If you are okay with learning Calculus 3 on your own you will be fine. I would not rely on her. She is not sympathetic either.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Meng's lectures are in-depth but often struggle to actually impart any information on the students. There are quizzes on recent materials without notes or critical formulas provided. If you struggle with quick memorization it is very easy to fall behind in her tempo. Her accent (length as lens, etc) makes it tricky to follow unfamiliar topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wouldn't recommend her. Her strong accent makes lectures hard to follow, and students must learn most material on their own. She may also put students on the spot if they don't know the answer, which can feel discouraging. This approach can make it harder to build a solid foundation in math.
for the love of God, avoid her for any class. her lecture is a waste of time

This was her first time teaching Section A of summer - she did a really good job communicating to the class but had a hard time organizing the class content (it was a lot to cover, afterall) and overall the class had a hard time keeping up. The class had a rough start and overall was a rocky ride. They are very smart but the class was difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't have enough space for the praise I want to give this class! Prof Xiao makes orgo/inorgo super digestible and teaches in a way that makes her passion for the material evident. There are no trick questions on her quizzes, the TAs are amazing, she's an effective lecturer, and the assignments challenge you but are graded reasonably. 10/10 :)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Xiao had great lectures that were engaging and easy to follow along with. The class and the quizzes are hard but the content is really enjoyable! Attending her office hours is great to get more help with the material/ask questions. The only issue was that the 2024 quizzes were a lot harder than practice quizzes from previous years.

I am seriously not sure why she has such high reviews for chem 312. She is such a passive aggressive lecturer and her quizzes are so difficult. She loves to have quiz questions that are not at all similar to the ones for her practice quizzes and picks out topics not discussed during class. The TAs were not very helpful either and very arrogant.

One of the nicest professors I have ever met and is super helpful and gives clear lectures. She made even confusing material understandable and I felt the exams were fairly graded and reflective of lectures and homework
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 165 was worth the terrors of 145 and 155. Xiao made the curriculum digestable and enjoyable. I did not dread going to chem as I did in the past. The changes to the homework and quizzes lowers the stress of this class. I would absolutely reccomend everyone in the chemistry department to take a Professor Xiao class; she is awesome!

One of my favorite chem profs ive had. I wasn't a fan of quizzes before, but her lectures were really easy to follow, and she provided a lot of practice quizzes. Some of her lectures went off topic, but she really likes what she does, and made inorganic my favorite chem subject at UW. I would strongly recommend her to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I appreciated how organized Xiao was with the course content and actually reads the mid-quarter class evaluation. She is very intelligent and humble professor, but not that great when it comes to answering questions. One of things to watch out for this class is how strict the TAs are when it comes to grading labs.

Prof. Xiao is a great lecturer-- answers questions very thoughtfully, organizes her slides neatly, and gives a lot of practice material. However, the exams are much more difficult than the practice, and this is very frustrating come quiz time. Art project was super fun, and this felt like a typical UW Honors class: basically a graded seminar.
Super nice and organized!!

Dianne Xiao was a great professor for CHEM 165. Her lectures were extremely informative and organized. The class covers a wide range of topics, but Professor Xiao does a great job of teaching it all. I think the class was slightly too easy for an honors level class, but I still learned a lot.

Professor Xiao is very accommodating to student feedback. Her lecture is very clear, and she knows the content well. She provides clear lecture notes that are very valuable for reviewing and studying. Exams are reasonable. 165 is a mix of ochem, inorganic, and materials, so content is rich, but explanations are clear! (taken Sp20)

Dr. Xiao is a real gem. Humble, generous, and scholarly, she structures her lectures very well and always informs you what to expect on exams. She gives speedy and quality response when you reach for help outside of class. No pop quizzes whatsoever and tests are designed to make you pass. She does move fast in class, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her tests are reflective of what you would expect based on lecture examples and the problem set, which is more like a weekly checklist to see if you understand the lectures. No pop quiz/clicker question at all. The lectures were easy-to-follow discussions, with little to no class participation necessary.

Lectures, homework, and practice tests did not correlate to the final exam at all. Midterm wasn't too bad, but the final was extremely difficult and incredibly difficult to study for since we were not given the proper materials.

Prof is very enthusiastic about Econ but not the best at teaching it. Going to lectures definitely matters; all notes and some practice are posted to Canvas so there is content to study-- however, the final did not reflect this content well and was really hard. Overall course content wasn't too difficult but somehow the class was hard anyways.

Lectures were long and dragged on while never actually showing how concepts came up in problems. There was no way to practice concepts outside of practice exams and HW which were nothing like any test. Overall it was real sad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Midnight's lectures were meh + prof has a grating voice. Textbook is written like an opinion article not an actual textbook. Way things were taught varied from book to lecture to section to homework to exam.
Previous exams vary greatly from what is put on these exams.
Not impossible to get a good grade but its a poorly designed course overall.

worst class i've ever taken. lectures are boring and my ta had no idea what was going on either. the first midterm wasn't too bad, but the final was absolutely nothing like any of the practice problems we were given
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't even bother studying for the final because nothing you study will ever appear on the exam. Pray you get a helpful TA (I did not) Avoid this class if possible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was pretty difficult and a lot of learning needs to be done on your own time. Professor Midnight tends to ramble during lectures but she is enthusiastic about econ. Homework level is reasonable but the final was pretty tough compared to the past finals on canvas. Overall the class was fine but nothing extraordinary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The first half of the course was well curated and easy to understand when work was put in, but the final was very hard and full of things we did not learn in class. I studied 15-20 hours preparing for the final and none of the questions correlated to the practice tests or the lectures. Do not take this class if you do not have to.

Teaches basic concepts in lecture that are easy to understand, but puts things you've never done in your life on the exams. Studied more than I ever have for the final, and none of the problems were anything we had ever gone over in class or TA section. Provided us with 13 practice tests yet none of them looked like the final. Absolutely unfair.
Worst professor I've ever had. Teaches you nothing and no matter how hard you study you won't do well.
Rambles about nonsense and then complains about being behind. Easy lectures but then hard material on tests from textbooks.

You can get by without going to lecture because everything is posted on slides, however you should go to office hours to get the concepts explained and to work through the problems. Homework is a fair bit difficult and tests even more so. Your TA will be your saving grace so make sure to attend all office hours you can.

The lectures actually weren't bad, just make sure to keep up with the textbooks as well. Just make sure to do the assignments and pay attention during class the tests don't seem as hard. There were minimal assignments that do not take long.
Midterms and Finals will kill your grade. I was blessed to have a really good TA, shout out to Austin but genuinely if you can avoid don't take this class.
Genuinely the worst professor I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really appreciated how clear and fair the midterm and final were the exams felt straightforward and matched what I practiced, which made studying much less stressful. I also appreciated the generous curve and it made a big difference in my grade was 95.5%

Professor does not record lectures. I attended every lecture and TA section. The midterm was not the worst, but the final was difficult for no reason and did not match up with the practice exams. Did every practice exam to review and the exam did not match up. Average on the final was a 53%, I mostly had to self teach myself, good luck.

I attended majority of the lectures and every TA section. I loved my TA, absolutely amazing but the teaching during the lectures wasn't my style. I did great on the midterm but the final? Absolutely not. Econ 200 was one of my favorite classes and I thought it wouldn't be so bad but I was wrong. Median on final was 53%. Good luck

This is not a well-organized course. The content from the textbook, lecturers, and exams feel disconnected. Theories are taught in isolation from each other, making this a mere game of remembering. Prof. Midnight explains ideas with good examples and quite clearly, but with a tiny bit of prior knowledge in econ the lectures can be boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Final paper was exceptionally hard and just written poorly. The lectures and TA sections were fine but they just teach the basics of each topic and how to approach questions instead of pinpointing what leads to such topics and knowledge points, making the overall course a bit boring as it disconnects a bit from the real world.

Not a horrible person, but creates insanely hard tests that feel very different from the lecture material. Did all the practice exams since 2020 and walked out of the exam feeling lost. Study hard and make sure you understand every concept thoroughly.

Yoav is a great professor. He's really knowledgable on the conflict and weaves the narratives in a holistic way that help you understand the full scope of the situation. He speaks fast so get ready to lock in and take notes, but if you put the work in and care about the subject, you should do well. Highly recommend.
Really enjoyed my class. Super intelligent, good lecturer, constantly offered help and support and office hours. Lecture heavy class and taking notes on lectures to complete assignments was key.

This is the 3rd class I've taken from Yoav. He's incredible & I recommend to everyone (polisci major or not)!! Work load is 1 discussion post and 1 quiz a week w/ 2 additional papers. Very interesting and enjoyable lectures and tends to be a lenient grader. Definitely cares about his students understanding and succeeding above all else :)
His lectures are really really interesting and enjoyable, hes a lenient grader.

He's an amazing professor and he's so funny and knowledgeable, he definitely makes class hella entertaining! Readings aren't too bad and you don't have to do all of them to succeed. Required a textbook but I don't think I opened it more than once… Lots of information covered in lecture but super fascinating and presented easy to understand

Professor Duman is great. Really interesting lectures, and he is always available and willing to help during office hours. You can tell he really cares about students ACTUALLY succeeding. Just make sure to stay updated on the readings! Go to lecture and quiz section and try to participate during discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: TALKS EXTREMELY FAST. Make sure you attend lectures!!! A lot of different ways to get credit, so it takes a lot of pressure off. Not a super tough grader. Make sure you do your reading and prepare before the midterms. He posts an extensive study guide so it is pretty easy!

Yoav has been my favorite professor this quarter and quite possibly this year. He shows genuine care and interest while offering many extra resources for learning on specific topics. Lectures were always very interesting and he is funny, though always moving. The course requires a lot of reading but if you love politics, it won't feel like it.

Not a difficult class at all, if you need the credit I would recommend it, as long as you're ready to study for midterms/finals. Instructions were always very clear, and Yoav is a funny guy, but sometimes his lectures stray off course a bit. He was very open on feedback about what students would change about his class too.

Professor Duman has all the great qualities you'd hope for in a professor. He is one of the most, if not the most, passionate teachers I've ever had. His tests are somewhat difficult, but he gives a very helpful study guide. Lots of readings will be on tests.TAs were hard graders but very helpful and kind.

Professor Duman was amazing.  His lectures were the best!!  He is passionate about political science and his lectures were so interesting and well put together. He was always available to answer questions online and was quick to grade assignments.  I would love to take him gain.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Duman was great!! His class was manageable and he was very accessible outside of class. the content wasn't fairly difficult and exams are easy if you study. he is seriously so accommodating and kind i really cannot recommend him enough. DO TAKE!! your gpa will thank you lol

Yoav is everything you want in a prof - engaging, caring, helpful, and clearly loves his job. I was continually impressed by his efforts to lower students' stress. As a STEM student, this class made me want to take more humanities courses. Readings are a lot but very manageable. Go by the study guides rather than worrying about every detail.

I took yoav online and he was so accommodating and quick to reply all quarter! He is very clear and accurate with his guidance and recommendations. he provided study guides and all of the exam material was straight forward with choice. definitely recommend him!!

Professor Duman is very passionate about politics based on the depth of his lectures. Many long lectures and readings, but the weekly assignments are well organized and the grading metric is fair. He also extended deadlines for assignments and tried to lower, not increase the stress taking the class. Would recommend! Understanding and passionate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class was my absolute favorite that I have taken at UW. I absolutely LOVED the lectures, they felt more like a story and were easy to follow and the information was organized really well. Yoav is a very nice and accommodating professor. He is always available to help and responds quickly to messages. He is also an easy grader.

One of my favorite professors ever, his class is my favorite class in my entire life. Great Lectures, amazing teacher! The weekly work could be done within two days, it is a 200 level class so it is very in depth but also easy for beginners on the subject. learned a lot. Can't say enough good in 350 words.TAKE THE CLASS. Took ONLINE

Yoav is the best! Very passionate and knowledgeable on the Arab/Israeli conflict. Don't just watch the PowerPoints, take notes from the lectures, they're great! Dense material, lots of reading! But if this subject interests you, hands down one of my favorite classes ever taken. Do the work. Easy grader.

Yoav is an amazing person who truly cares about his students. There is a lot of material to go through, but Yoav actually makes the content interesting and listens to feedback. Not an easy class, but you will succeed if you put in the work. Definitely one of the better classes I've taken!

Probably one of the more difficult classes I've taken, due to the amount of time required to understand so much dense material. Lots of reading! Long detailed lectures. If you take good notes from them, you'll be fine. You can't just get by on the Power Point slides. Use the notes! Hard work but I Loved this class! Great content. Great Professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This guy has synthesized a world of information and conveys it in an almost captivating way.

Yoav is amazingly unbiased and passionate about his subject. He made complex course material very interesting and was very engaging with the class and hilarious. He cares a lot about learning and is not a hard grader and will always be willing to help you out. As long as you participate with the class, you can do well!

I took an American Government class at Green River College and it was very interesting. The most important thing was showing up to class and engaging in the material. Not particularly difficult if you do the work. Instructor is interesting and understanding.
He is my little any angel

This professor is the most boring lecturer ever, it is the longest monotone monologue you could imagine. I am a poli sci major, I LOVE politics, and I barely make myself go and definitely don't pay attention when I do.

It was hard to tell whether it was the course material or P. Duman himself that made the class dull. Either way, I found myself oftentimes bored. There's a lot of reading assigned, and a weekly discussion assignment that I found more annoying than useful. Overall, not terrible, but not exceptional either.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I liked him. His teaching was very straightforward. Basically, if you attend lectures and your quiz sections, you're all set. Reading was covered by him in lectures so it wasn't really necessary to finish the readings. Just take notes, and start studying two days before the exam. paper? he's a very easy grader. and i mean it. very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Took this class, Winter 2016, 2 response papers, 1 narrative analysis (easy), 1 midterm, 1 final. Exams are extremely straight forward and manageable if studied for a couple days prior to test-day. You basically don't have to read if you go to section (I'm Serious). Lectures are definitely not mandatory but are always interesting.
Terrible at leading class discussions. Two hours of rambling chaos every time.

Yoav was an amazing lecturer.  He is amazingly unbiased and presents material in a very organized manner.  Going to lecture and doing the readings are critical to success in this class.  He inspired me to major in Political Science.  I highly recommend Comparative Politics.

Amazing professor. He is from Israel himself and teaches the class in a surprisingly unbiased way. Presents all sides, always focuses on pros and cons. Exams are fine if studied for! Keep up with readings.
Yoav was a great professor. He was a pretty lenient grader for the two short papers and midterm. Study hard for the final.

THE absolute best lecturer I've ever had, very very organized, really passionate about the subject (Arab Israeli conflict). He is thorough and clear, he organizes the class material chronologically so it all makes sense, and he explains cause effect relationships very well. no confusion at all as to what happened, when, and why it happened

He genuinely cares about the topic he's teaching. He is very knowledgeable, and easy to approach if you have any questions. The class was almost like a history class LOTS of background information. Textbook is not necessary, just do the article readings, he'll explain everything else in lecture. Follow the study guide & you'll do well in the class.
Professor Duman is awesome. Always very helpful, it's obvious he really cares about the class (students and subject). I recommend taking him!

Not the greatest teacher I've had but I didn't really attend lectures. He has a strong accent and really bad handwriting so it is hard to understand what he is actually getting at in class. His tests are pretty straightforward although I failed the final so. he isn't great at explaining concepts or answering questions so wouldn't recommend.
Disorganized, super fast unclear lectures. Almost feels like he's reading off a script. Heavy accent too.

Not the worst lecturer but he focuses way too much on computation and uses A LOT of math jargon.

He also put eigenvectors on a midterm before we learned them.
Prof. Liu was pretty good. I had him for Modern Algebra (MATH 402) about a year ago. He gave good examples in class and spoke very clearly. Overall, decent professor!
Good luck trying to understand what he's saying. He also never explains anything and moves through examples very quickly so it is incredible hard to keep up with what he's saying.

lowkey this professor isn't that bad, his first midterm was based off of what we talked about in class. wish he would slow down during lecture but I just go back to the recorded lectures. 2 hw assignments per week including skills problems that are on completion, and conceptual problems are half correctness/completion. also has a heavy accent.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very messy and disorganized hand writing, doesn't really explain what is going on and doesn't explain the true geometric understandings behind every concept. Extremely thick accent which makes it even harder to understand on top of his bad handwriting. I would say he is better than Koblitz but ideally avoid this professor if you struggle with math.
boom boom okay les star
Quite hard to understand what he is saying a lot of times...
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not be deceived by the good ratings on this guy. I had Professor Hoffman the quarter before for math 207, and I thought he was bad since everyone complained about his every day even though I good a good grade in his class. But Yutao made that dude look like an angel. 100% the good reviews are fake; this is the worst professor I have ever had.

Probably the worst professor I have ever had. If you already have some linear algebra experience, this class shouldn't be that bad. Otherwise do whatever it takes to avoid Yutao Liu. Very strong accent, rambles on certain topics, doesn't explain things well. Makes up examples while teaching so sometimes the example problems can't even be solved.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good professor. The lectures are fairly dense and he can be a bit fast at times but he explains the concepts very well. Exam grades take up a majority of the total grade, which cover the material covered in the lecture and homework. Midterms are pretty easy and the final was a bit harder. Homework is long but manageable. Amazing fits as well.

Absolute icon. He lacks experience compared to older professors, but he really cares about the students and makes sure that we understand the materials well. A lot of potential. His adidas tracksuit is the most stable thing in the universe. Very competent and passionate, 5/5 would take again.

Midterms were easy, but final was more challenging. He had solid lectures and explained the material very well. Very efficient during lecture and definitely knows his stuff. Overall, amazing professor.

He was a really nice professor. He writes fast and his accent is a bit hard to understand sometimes, but he seems to genuinely care about his students. Make sure to read the textbook though because it supplements his lectures really well. Also, his midterms aren't unreasonable if you study and do the homework.

A really great professor with a good grasp of the course concepts. HW is challenging but makes you really think and learn. Exams cover the topics covered in the lecture. Really fun and has great fashion sense.
great notes, great exams. idk bout the lectures cus i didnt go

I think he was a fine prof. Accent not hard to understand at all imo. Has a great understanding of the course content, works through examples in lecture to help. Conceptual problems homework were difficult but often rewarding (except the purely computational ones). Midterms/Final difficulty was fine, not too hard or easy. Good class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures are incredibly dense but all the exams are based on what is covered in lecture. His midterms are pretty fair as they are more on the application side rather than the conceptual side. Overall, great professor and fair class. His organization of the canvas does need work but no real complaints.
This the goat right here, unbelievable aura got me quaking in my boots.

His accent is very difficult to understand. Not very good at explaining concepts. Rushes through practice problems. Conceptual problems are harder than the problems shown in class and are graded on accuracy.

Standard math class. Conceptual problems are long but interesting and intellectually stimulating (except for the computational ones). The lectures are fast, but I found that I could get most of it down, especially with help from the textbook. He also allows note sheets on exams. Just write down the theorems, and you'll do fine.

Lectures are very fast, hard to write it all down let alone understand what is happening and why. Conceptual problems are long and wacky, but I think all 208 profs have them. Gave good exam review session, seemed like a nice guy who cares and tries to help/explain things, thick accent. Meh

prof. liu is nice but i thought his lectures were difficult to follow. he was very fast while writing and left no room to think about the problems (imo). he also does have an accent as ppl said. the weekly textbook assignments were nice but the conceptual problems given were absurd (difficult & time consuming). i'd agree exam problems took too long

He is such a kind professor, and his explanations were awesome. If you didn't understand his explanation, he'd explain in a new way that was also super helpful. The grading was pretty nice on exams, and the class is based mostly on exam grades (80%). He does exam review before exams. He does have a heavy accent, but he writes out what he's teaching
thanks for da midterm my goat 🙏🙏🙏

Very strong accent, impossible to follow lectures. Had to teach myself all concepts.
Exams were too long, not easy to complete on time. Homework was graded extremely unfairly and written problems were low quality (very few, unnecessarily long and challenging problems) and didn't give good practice.

Just a normal linear algebra course. Conceptual assignments may take awhile, webassign HW are easy. Lecture pace is fast & he had a bit of accent, but he explained each concept in detail and clearly. Tests are moderate, most are problems not going beyond the scope of HW & lectures, but can be calculation heavy at times. Good teacher overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Li's CHEM142 class has a fair grading structure, with multiple-choice exams and a helpful ALEKS homework system. While lectures can be hit-or-miss, Unstuck AI proved a valuable study tool to supplement the course material.

No guidance for research and he pick up favorite students and gives them support especially Chinese. 
He can destroy your future. So passive, judgmental, not easy to work with.

Took this class online and lectures were awful. Could not read professors notes, professor did not provide satisfactory alternate learning methods. Excelled in all other science courses at UW and in IB and this one I nearly failed. DO NOT take this course.
In week 3 he told me "If you don't understand my content I recommend dropping my class." I did. He's terrible and this was my only withdrawal ever. Take chem with anyone else.

This class tackles some of the hardest topics during the first weeks before that first midterm so be prepared. After that first midterm, the class gets easier as it is mostly about topics that are easier. Read your textbooks before every lecture as Professor Li only reviews it in class. Do ALEKS in advance, it is an easy grade to earn.
Taught class like it was a review rather than an introduction.

I found his class structure and grade distribution to be fair. His exams are all multiple choice and he gives you a detailed info sheet for the exam and allows you to bring your own. There is a lot of ALEKS each week but it was a good supplement to his lectures and buffer for my grade.

Professor Li is a great guy; he has a good sense of humor and is very kind. However, I rarely found his lectures helpful in any way. ALEKS felt like my teacher - and there was a lot of ALEKS. The nice thing about his class is that the tests are multiple choice. I enjoyed his in-class demos as well.

Li was a good chemistry lecturer! He was engaging and going to lecture actually helped my understanding, but unfortunately his pace for lecture was slightly behind the  homework at so some of the things he had to say you already had learned on your own. I would absolutely take Li again. His grading was fair and expectations were clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is definitely a weed out but Li's humor in class makes it worth it. The labs are probably the hardest part- they're graded pretty harshly. I would recommend going to the study center for your labs and getting help from the TAs. He provides practice midterms which is nice. The hw is ALEKS which SUCKS but it's easy points.

Mr Li is a pretty good choice. He's funny and seems to care that you pass. I barely read the textbook and took minimal notes, but I still managed to get a B. Just study and practice the practice exams he posts a lot and do the worksheets and you should be fine. Also do the aleks work and lab stuff. That's easy points.

Take this class with Professor Li! He's a real gem and the lecture demos are super fun! Do the work, put in the effort, and you'll be fine! His lectures and practice material are really helpful for the midterms and final. There is a lot of ALEKS but it's honestly helpful for practice. Use the textbook for help!

A decent professor. He occasionally glosses over topics but those topics are also usually not covered on the exams. The class does have a lot of homework, and ALEKS will leave you traumatized by the end of the quarter - its an extremely punishing HW system time-wise (not grade-wise) but does provide an infinite source of practice
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Li is a solid chemistry professor. His lectures draw directly from the textbook and his multiple-choice exams do a fair job at reflecting what is taught in class. The online homework program, ALEKS, may be a bit much at times but manageable with time management. Lastly, Professor Li does skim over content he deems "AP Chemistry" content.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: great professor to take if you are planning to take chem 142. Test are somewhat easy if you can do practice exam and PoV question. I never read the textbook but if you want a 4.0 i would recommend you to read it. Overall one of the best prof. from chem department

Prof Li is a funny guy and very straightforward on what are on his tests. I did well in this class because I practiced the exact points he mentioned would be on the tests. Demos are cool and he's a nice professors. Can't access him much because there are so many students so rely on your TAs for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have the chance to take a class with professor Li, DO IT! He is a great lecturer you have to come to class, do the ALEKS ( do not procrastinate), and do practice exams to do well in the class but its very feasible. I personally had a great TA as well which I know is a hit or miss but I would definitely recommend taking advantage of the chem
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: prof li was a super entertaining lecturer, but im ngl the class is test heavy and if you dont show up to lecture/read the textbook the class will be hard. however, if you show up to lecture you'll be completely fine
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Li's class was pretty straightforward: go to lecture, take notes, do aleks, repeat. His lectures are not super engaging in my opinion and you'll get about 20 aleks modules per week to do on average. There is also only 2 midterms in terms of exams so good luck if you're not a good test taker.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: For me personally, I didn't really pay too much attention during lecture. I just took notes from ALEKS (the homework website) and I knew what was going on during lecture and on tests. Didn't read anything from the book.

Prof. Li is not super loving or sweet, but he was pretty funny and if you actually put in work, the tests arent terrible, especially with the curves. Hes also pretty clear during lecture, and if you dont understand something the textbook can help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Li is a solid professor to go with. The way his course was laid out meant that tests were a large part of your grade, so make sure to do solid/average on those. His lectures are easy to understand and he is approachable for questions. If you have the choice to go with a Professor like Keller or Craig, I would recommend checking them out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Xiaosong Li is one UW professor who is truly a matter of taste. I personally enjoyed his style. It helps that he is very upfront about your grade projection after each exam. The exams are hard if you do not study. Choosing to take the exam without doing the practice exam is a suicide mission. Do the ALEKS, be engaged, and you will get a 4.0. Enjoy.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Miss him if possible! Li isn't available outside of class for help and can be extremely passive aggressive in emails. He glosses over topics and expects you to just "know them". His exam questions are not very straight forward and purposely trick you . At one point about half the people started skipping class because his lectures were no help.

Li is a skilled lecturer, tests are reasonable if you go to class and do the practice tests, and there is a lot of ALEKS homework but that's unavoidable. The class isn't easy but it's not supposed to be. There are lots of resources provided, so make sure you find the ones that work for you and use them.

An okay instructor. Often glosses over certain topics, so ensure you have a solid background in HS chem. Exams are fair; they only cover content he covers in lect. Clicker questions and practice exams are a good representation of the exams, redo them until you feel confident. Lab and ALEKS make a difference for your learning and grade, so do them!

Li was a solid choice for Chem 142. I liked that his exams were very similar and even some questions were identical to the practice exams. Be sure to nail down every question of the practice exam and understand the clicker sessions and the exams will be pretty easy to do well on. Do not forget to do well on ALEKS and labs. It will help your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures were eh but the demonstrations were fun to watch. If you can't make lectures there are some online so it's not a big deal. Make sure to review the practice tests and the clicker questions like a thousand times before midterms/finals and you'll do great. Overall wasn't too difficult and the professor gives you room to do well.

very straightforward and good lecturer, tho he fairly often skipped stuff he claims students should know from high school chem. the tests are hard bc u have very little time for each question, but there's almost no surprises on exams. Li is a pretty cool dude and makes jokes at times, would definitely recommend for 142!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Li was overall a great professor. He kept lectures fairly interesting, although it did get a little bit repetitive with slideshows. Luckily, this also meant that the course content was easily accessible from Canvas if you missed lecture. His study guides were very representative of the tests and he was generally clear about what would be on tests.

Prof Li is a good guy but it doesn't seem like he wants to be a teacher at all. He doesn't hold office hours, doesn't take homework questions after class and doesn't make his classes engaging. His exam questions are very conceptual and tries to trick you and are not very straightforward. He is a fair grader but isn't a good teacher.

He was a pretty decent lecturer but attending lectures were not crucial to understanding concepts (at least for me). I did most of my learning from ALEKS, textbook readings, and the practice worksheets. The practice midterms/final were very similar to the actual tests so make sure to do them!
He was a fair grader. I really appreciated how his practice midterms were almost identical to the ones one the actual midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Li is not the most amazing teacher, but he is a fair professor when it comes to such a difficult class. The exams are worth a lot, but as long as you do lots of practice problems you will be fine. Basically, you just have to work really hard in chem 142 to get a good grade. Don't procrastinate ALEKS because it can boost your grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Clear grading criteria--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I love professor Li. Obviously the class is hard, but his humor at 8:30 in the morning makes it a lot better. I would take his class in a heartbeat again, easily my best teacher this quarter. ALEKS sucks and labs are graded extremely hard but honestly, if you know basic chemistry youll be more than fine
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Went through slides rather quickly with minimal explanations expecting us to already know what he's talking about, tons of ALEKS objectives, and only around 15 to 20 questions on tests. Don't take this class if you don't already have a strong background in chemistry or if you value your mental health. Nice person but not a good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Li is a fine professor - not spectacular but definitely not terrible either. His average on the exams is always a 70 and he rewards the class if they do better by increasing the median. All are multiple choice, no quizzes, and clear course structure. There is a fair amount of ALEKS hmwk due each week though it is very helpful.

I loved this class and by far was my favorite class of first quarter. Professor Li is so fun and he makes jokes that are funny throughout the course and in his demos. He is very realistic about your chances of passing and I found the workload to be entirely manageable and the content to be fairly simple. I did AP, organic, and enriched chem though.

Seriously, do NOT procrastinate. I recommend doing the ALEKS work way in advance, because it will help you understand the lectures. Professor Li is nice, but he doesnt explain everything in a clear way. Take advantage of the TA in the quiz and lab sections if you have questions!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Admittedly, Professor LI has a vey cold persona and would make you feel insignificant at times. However, when it comes to assignments, Professor Li is very fair on the topics that he gives on the tests. His clicker questions are directly related to the multiple choice questions that you get and the aleks is only slightly computational.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Teaches the content as if we already know and learned it recently which wasn't effective for many people. Lots of homework every week and the content is very hard. One of those infamous STEM weed-out classes from UW. Don't expect a stellar grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Li sometimes glosses over topics during prerecorded lectures. Usually, I found it best to read the chapter from the textbook before watching his lectures. In addition, to do well in the class, it is crucial to attend the live tutorial sessions. In these, Professor Li goes over clicker questions that are similar to the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Li, like all of us, was still adjusting to completely virtual class and chemistry may be one of the more difficult online classes to teach so there's my disclaimer. Overall, the class was not too bad although Professor Li's lectures were very fast paced and at times hard to follow. Not very engaging online. Didn't feel very supported.

Good professor with clear outline of course expectations and material. Since it was online, he was only accessible through his tutorial sections, or by a scheduled meeting. His recorded lectures were easy to understand, but if you read the book and take notes well, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Took this class my first semester at UW and hadn't taken chem since sophomore year in HS. Was really worried but I read the textbook and finished Aleks before quizzes so it was not too bad! Lecturing is a bit boring and demos don't really help so you have to do your own work. His quizzes/exams are math-heavy too but easy once you get the hang of it
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Li is disrespectful and lazy. If you email him with a question/concern don't expect more than a blatantly dismissive one liner. He makes it extremely clear he has no time for his students and no interest in their success. He only cares about his demos which are pretty dumb. Only good thing is he grades pretty easy. Do not take this class!

There was a lot of work to do and at least in my case I had to spend a lot of time studying. Class wasn't mandatory but definitely recommend, I would also advise you to do the Aleks homework assignments as soon as you can as well as the reading. Then use the recorded lectures as review. There are also no midterms just weekly quizzes and a final.

Li's teaching style is fast so if you don't have a basic understanding of chemistry, it can be hard. As long as you finish ALEX, do good on lab reports, and get average scores on 5/7 quizzes, you can get a 3.0 in this class. The 24min. weekly quizzes can be difficult, some weeks are easier than others.

This class was honestly fine, though interaction with the professor is limited given how many people are in the class. Lectures are a bit dull and he does ramble on occasionally, but the information is clear. There are weekly quizzes and a final, all are multiple choice and heavily math based. Overall, workload is pretty heavy, but manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The Prof only seemed to care about the grades and curve rather than helping the actual students. He was always booked and ignored my emails. The quizzes are way harder than you would expect and( they are meant to set you back.) For this class studying the lectures and textbook isn't enough. The weekly quizzes were something I dreaded!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 8 Question Quizzes every week that are 24-26 minutes long and half of your grade. Does not respond to emails. Lecture style is a bit rambly, expect to do a lot of reading and ALEKS work.

Li was an OK prof for Chem 142. His lectures were pretty good, but his coverage from topic to topic wasn't very consistent, and I had to go to tutoring to fully understand concepts because his explanations can be confusing. The amount of work each week is a lot, but that's to be expected in a class like this.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I've heard Li is definitely one of the better professors for this class. I think a lot of the ratings are because the class itself is really difficult, especially for intro freshman. His lectures are clear but the tutorial sessions are what relate back to whats on quizzes. So many kids in this class, I used my TA a lot more than Li.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Personally didn't like his lecturing style-- felt he rambled a lot and was hard to understand the main points. Also found him discouraging. Quiz material barely matched what we learned about in lecture-- clicker Q's, tutorials, ALEKS really helped me. But the way he curves grades makes sense and he tries to help his students as much as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Li is an amazing person. That being said this course was a full time job. Lectures, weekly quizzes and hefty amounts of homework on ALEKS. You really must be dedicated and organized if you want to do well in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There are quizzes every Friday that make up 50% of your grade. These are about 24 minutes and 8 questions each but all the questions are math heavy. There is also a lot of homework and reading.

My advice is be wary if you don't have experience with chemistry or a solid background. Since this is taught at a higher level, Li tends to skip over details and speeds through information with the assumption that you've already learned it. Not many opportunities for help so you're on your own. His lectures didn't reflect what was on quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Li speeds through problems during lectures and spends most of the time showing demos. His clicker questions barely relate to the quiz questions. You have 24-26 minutes to solve 8 questions. Office hours are scheduled by emails, which he does not respond to. I would not recommend this class if you are terrible or even average in chemistry.

Professor Li is really kind and shows that he wants his students to do well. The majority of your grade is based on weekly quizzes that as long as you pay attention in lectures and tutorials and study enough you'll do fine. There's a lot of homework on ALEKS, but its doable. He teaches really well and is helpful when you ask questions.

50% of your grade will be based off of weekly quizzes totally 8 points and coming to 42 point for the quarter. If you mess up on this you are screwed on your grade. He is also incredibly strict and will not give exceptions for anything and will constantly tell you that what you learned in highschool is pointless.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Li is the best man on the UW campus. During his weekly tutorials, he goes through example problems for the weekly quizzes that are extremely helpful. He is also the sweetest and funniest professor I've had and really cares about his students. Please take this mans class!

Prof. Li taught the first chem class I took at UW. That being said, his quizzes are definitely an adjustment from high school. They are purely mathematical instead of conceptual, you have to be proficient and quick in the subjects before you take the quiz. They are a large part of your grade too. Li is a nice person and wants students to succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Li taught the first ever STEM class I took at UW. I'm not sure if his teaching is different in person than it is online, but online, his teaching is terrible. He loves pre-recorded demos more than he likes to teach. Speeds through lectures and is very condescending if you do not understand certain "pre-requisites". Textbook is very useful.

I took this class online during COVID. The best advice I can give is to stay on top of the lectures, and do as many practice problems as you can. Very math-oriented questions on exams. Textbook is good for problems!! I got a 4.0 in this class by staying really organized with material and ALEKS objectives. Really nice guy, but very dense lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's an okay guy but out of touch and a bad professor. Had weekly online quizzesdidn't give us enough time. Cares more about speed than quality. Made many rude comments about if you can't solve problems fast you're a bad student. Cares more about the curve than comprehension. Lectures are confusing, you need to teach yourself. AVOID if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had to take this class online and by far is one of the worst class experiences I had at UW. Pro. Li doesn't teach the materials well and he expects you to know them from high school. I basically had to read the textbook my self and used Khan academy for extra help. HW load is a lot and didn't help to prepare for the exams.

I had him for online spring and his weekly timed quizzes are awful. They aren't hard, but it's really hard to solve everything within his time limits (that aren't even nice numbers, they're all like 22, 18, etc minutes). He might be a better prof to have outside of online learning but the way he taught online was not my pace.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This has been a terrible experience, from the past reviews prof Li seems to be a good & caring professor in person. But with the current circumstances of online classes he has been one of the least involved professors Ive had. Chemistry is a subject that should be practiced in repetition to master. With weekly timed quizzes learning is impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is funny and does interesting demos in class.

He doesn't really seem to care much about his teaching and is obviously here for his research, but his exams are very easy and CHEM 142 is the only 4.0 I've gotten at UW so far haha. If you're choosing between him and Craig I'd choose Craig but otherwise his class was awesome considering how uninterested he appears in teaching it (he's funny too).

Professor Li tends to rush things in lecture and when going through example questions, he tends to not fully explain and instead goes through general points. In order to be successful, you need to study A LOT. He's a funny guy but his lectures tend to be very uninteresting and not very helpful, try avoiding this one when taking CHEM 142
Quite easy class. Exams are basic mutiple choices. He's really a chinese-style professer.
He was a great professor and his lectures were very good. Compared to other chem professors he is by far the best. I would recommend this class. He curved my class to 3.0

If you do the readings before class and complete the ALEKS hw, it should be an easy class. His midterms were easy the averages were really high, but the final was nothing like the midterms (do the book problems for the final).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Li is one of the best chem profs at UW. His lectures are fine and he'll crack a joke here and there. Make sure to show up to the lecture before the exams because there will be helpful review sessions. Also, the curve my quarter was set to a 3.0 which was great.

Li was a great guy and seemed to really care about if his students did well. He moved the curve up so the median was a 3.0, so we didn't get punished for being a smart class-I really appreciated this. Some people complain about his demos, but I thought they were always fun and interesting, and you could tell he put effort into planning them.
He did a good job!

First class I ever took at UW was his chem class. Overall, he's a solid choice- sometimes he rushes through some of the tricky math in lectures, so be ready to review it more later until you fully understand it. Otherwise, he's super approachable and the demos were great.

All CHEM 142 classes are set to a curve of 2.6, so of course this was a difficult, competitive class, but Li got us through it. He had many engaging demos, he answered questions, and he even raised our entire class' curve. Honestly, CHEM 142 is going to be hard no matter what, but you can make it through this class if you study hard and show up.

Very hard to understand. Demos in lectures take away time and do not contribute to learning. Avoid this class if possible. ALEKS is annoying but is the best way to learn material. Grade is determined by 2 tests and a final.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Demo's are okay but don't really help most people understand. He goes through lecture fast and ALEKS is a pain.

Professor Li was not that bad of a teacher. His tests were multiple choice and fairly straightforward. If you study a bit, you can easily finish them within the given amount of time. Great thing about Li is that if your class exceeds his expectations for a test, he bumps up the curve. For my class, the curve was set from a 2.7 to a 3.0.

This course in general covers similar material to high school chem (I didn't take AP), with a couple more math-y lessons. In my opinion, he went over very little of the difficult problems and too much of the easy problems. He does lots of demos and I recommend doing practice problems in order to do well on the test! Btw, his accent really isn't bad

The tests are a time crunch but if you practice a fair amount you'll likely be fine. There are times when he goes fast through lecture or doesn't explain an example super well but he still covers content in lecture well. I would definitely still read the textbook though. Fun demos every class!

He is a great guy, and it is obvious that he loves to teach chem. The class is very difficult so be prepared to work outside of class. The tests have a lot of trick questions and they are a time crunch. The class is heavy on tests,so to get a good grade you have to do better than everyone else.

Professor Li is honestly a pretty great professor. So long as you read the textbook along with the lectures, you ought to be pretty well off in the class! Li himself provides fun in lecture demonstrations and is very well versed in what he is teaching. Be careful though, as he does go over concepts pretty fast if that poses a problem for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Cared that his students learned the material and gave great demos.

Dr. Li was a super fun teacher with a great sense of humor. He is a researcher but has an excellent ability to communicate the material to his students. He has an accent but if you have a very good grip on English it isn't too bad. Some of his test questions are sneaky hard but we beat his expectations so the class wasn't that hard. I'd take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a pretty good professor even though he has a bit of an accent. Would take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Li doesn't get enough credit. He genuinely cares that his students do well. He gave 15% of my class 4.0s and his love for demos made every class enjoyable. Yes, you have to study outside of class to do well but it's not so bad. Compared to other Chem teachers, Li gave out the least amount of work and the highest grades. He also bumped up our curve
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Funny demo experiments, clear materials from powerpoint. If you have taken chemistry before, take a class with him! He is approachable, clear, and dont forget to go to class when there is pollEverywhere(trust me, it's really helpful! most of the questions in the exam are sometimes similar to them)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is very intelligent, and he knows what he's doing, but he doesn't seem that interested in teaching well. He changes mid-thought quite often and skips basic chemistry concepts, and almost never works through example problems, which is unfortunate considering this is the first in the gen chem series. I had to learn everything outside of class.
Just not good at conveying the information!
Absolutely great professor. Funny demo experiments!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great lectures that covered all the material efficiently by being vague when need be to provoke thought and thorough on harder concepts. Mentions exactly everything that will be tested on so go to lectures to hear what will be on the exams. Practice midterms are extremely helpful and mirror the exam. Problems in the book look like what is on exams.

I liked Li as a professor, he had clear grading and lectures. All of his notes are on canvas and if you prefer to learn on your own you could only show up on clicker session days (which he always announces in advance). I didn't use the textbook at all, I just did the Aleks hw and practice exams to study for tests and did fine.

Prof. Li is great! I found his lectures pretty informative, and he's not hard to follow (his accent is really not a big deal). He loves helping out students and his test review is basically the test - examples on his slideshows are really helpful too. I will warn you that the exams are tightly timed scantron exams and you need to be ready for them.

Second time taking Chem 142 and wow what a difference a professor makes. Professor Li is very accessible outside of class and really cares if you understand material or not. It may not seem like it in lecture but MAKE THE EFFORT TO GO TO OFFICE HOURS! That's what he is trying to tell his students.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Did not lay a good gen chem foundation for me. Went by content too fast, expecting us to figure out the rest on our own. What was worst was as a freshman, learning how to study was hard. He didn't seem interested in assisting us with that. Accent made it hard to follow, don't remember getting supplementary material. Tests were fair.

Heavy accent which makes listening to lectures very difficult. Known as the harder of all the chemistry professors. Speeds through problems on the board without working through the problems (to show you how to do them). Curve is set to 2.6 GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I struggled quite a bit at the beginning of the course and did badly on my first midterm, but he was really approachable, was eager to talk over my exams with me, and was just overall really helpful and accessible and actually appeared invested in helping me understand the course material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Li's class was enjoyable, but the tests were hard. Make sure to come prepared for the tests if you want to score above median. Pay attention to lecture, as he usually focuses on topics that he is gonna put on the test. I'd say practice tests and problems in the back of the chapter were most helpful for tests. My TA was also really helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Li is so funny and genuine. He makes his lectures fun, although he tends to skip through the "easy" material really fast. His tests are different than his practice tests that he posts online, pay attention to clicker sessions because those questions will be on there! Labs were easy and TA was a lot of help.

I think Professor Li is a solid choice for Chem142 especially if you have some chemistry background (he skips the easy parts). His tests were straight from his lectures and if you pay attention in class, you can definitely ace it. He puts a lot of focus on the tests, and he does demos a lot. His sense of humor is amazing. The TA (J) was cool too!!
Pretty good professor and really care about his student

Sometimes it's hard to follow along during lecture and that he messes up occasionally when explaining practice problems but overall his lectures were enjoyable. When he messed up he laughed it off and his sense of humor made the lectures bearable. The midterms were doable but I found the final to be more difficult so be prepared for that.

Great Professor. I Was very nervous going into Chem 142 but this class was much easier than I thought it was going to be. Lectures were fine and covered all of the information that was going to be on the test. He is very generous with his grades, if you score above one standard deviation on the tests and do ok on the labs expect a 4.0.

He is pretty reachable and actually replies to your email. Very easy to see him during his office hour. His tests are not too easy but are very similar to the practice tests he gives out. Occasionally adds some humor in class, which is nice. From what I heard, I thinks he is the easiest chem 142 teacher this quarter.

Professor Li is adorable! While the class and the material was hard to follow at times because of his accent, he really does try his best to make lectures fun and enjoyable! Expect to do lots of outside reading and homework problems if you even want an average grade in this class.

I was scared for this class, but professor Li made it a lot easier. Just make sure to attend class and go over his lecture slides at home (I usually went over the lecture slides ahead of time so I can listen during lectures). Exams are just like the practice tests he gives out.

He is really hard to understand and doesn't explain practice problems he does in class. His tests are hard and his practice tests aren't similar to the actual tests. He hardly gives you any resources to study with, I would recommend looking for a different teacher if you have him.

His teaching has too many gaps, his lectures are hard to follow and he's too confident in his English and speaks quickly but really it is hard to understand him when he goes off on long lectures about a topic. But he's easier than other professors.

Li is awesome. I came into 142 thinking I wouldn't stand a chance, but he made everything extremely to understand in the lectures, even though they can be fast paced. However, he posts all of his slides online, and his practice midterms are exactly like the tests. I wish he was teaching 152, because I would definitely take another class by him.
awesome!!!!!!
While some of the information covered in lecture was pretty boring, Professor Li's sense of humor made the class fairly enjoyable. The tests were very reasonable and involved a lot of calculations.

TESTS ARE EASY!!!! I got 95 on my first exam, 100 on my second exam and 95 on my final exam. And I got 4.0 !!!!! When I come to his office, and he can remember all my scores just after I told him my name!!!!  this teacher is amazing!!!! His exam is very easy, all you need to do is listening to the lecture carefully and you can get 4.0 easily!!
I liked the class but the exams are tough. Felt really ill prepared for the final exam, the level of difficulty was above what he actually prepared us for.
He is a really tough grader. His tests are never easy, think CAREFULLY before taking the classes.

He's super kind, encouraging and funny. Very engaged during lecture, especially with demos. Encourages students to work hard and do well in the course. Has a heavy Chinese accent but fairly easy to understand. I don't think you would pas this class without going to lecture. His examples are not great, just go to the chem study center.
xiaosong LI is really an amazing teacher!!!!! love him!!!!!!
He has a nice sense of humor and tries to make lectures very clear. Cool guy- really into the seahawks, makes fun of himself when he makes mistakes. I would take another class from him.
A true legend. The best chemistry professor I have ever had at UW. #lizardsquad

This was Professor Li's first time teaching 142 and it definitely showed. Lectures were sometimes confusing and tests were difficult, but I didn't find that he tried to use trick questions or test us on something he hasn't at least mentioned. He has a fun, light personality, but he's probably a better teacher for higher level chemistry classes.

Dr. Li was a very nice guy. Does a good job of trying to motivate his students and has a positive attitude about everything. 142 with him was easy, I'm glad I had him. One of his tests was exactly the same as a worksheet he gave us. Just study the practice tests he gives you and do problems from the book and you'll be fine!

Worst science class ever. Chem 142 would have been a lot better if he was actually prepared for lecture. I would come out of every lecture really confused. I was really disappointed about the overall quality of the class...

This was his first time teaching Chem 142 and he had a bit of a difficult time explaining easy and general concepts. I didn't use the book at all since his material was more computations than anything.

He's a nice guy, but his class was really confusing and I could never understand him. I would study really hard for his tests, and they felt impossible. The average grade was around a 60%. Not to mention ALEKS, quite possibly the worst homework site ever invented. Would not recommend this class to anyone.

I failed this class, but I wouldn't say that it was Professor Li's fault. He's a really nice guy, likes making jokes, and tries to motivate his students. The topics were difficult for me, but I think the majority of the class thought that it was fine compared to what they heard about other teachers. There were no surprises on tests, just study!
He was very nice and tried his hardest to help but I couldn't get past his terrible handwriting and obscure accent. I am so excited to be done with his class.
