He's so adorable. You can barely understand him but he sends out all the power-points and reviews/keys to reviews. He's so nice and understanding. Very easy class. But he's a fantastic teacher and always willing to help!
Awesome professor! Take his 455 and 456 if you can. I regret I didn't take 455 with him, because he knows how to teach! I got 4.0 in 456. Very very nice guy!

Best professor ive had at UW hands down. Funny and a genius. PChem had a notoriously bad rep when I went into it but Li turned all that around. Super interesting, well organized. The guy literally tells you problems that will be on the tests if you go to lecture. Its hard work and a bit math heavy but so very worth it. TAKE IT WITH HIM IF YOU CAN!

This guy moved a little too fast for me, but he repeated everything over and over, so there's that. Honestly, I thought his TA was more helpful making things easier to understand. Expectations were pretty clear and homework was reasonable, although tests can be tough.
He is one of the best Chem Profs that I have ever had. I took Chem 455 and chem 465 from him. TAKE BOTH!!!!
His class requires a lot of work if you want to keep up with lectures. But he is a funny guy and you'll enjoy listening to him lecturing p-chem stuff...
Very straightforward class and very helpful teacher. In class test reviews were also very helpful. Midterms and finals are very similar to the practice tests he gives.
Dr. Li consistently showed that he cared about our learning.

Best Chemistry professor I've had so far. Very organized and teaches material in a very logical order. Breaks down material as best he could (quantum is hard to teach!), which 99% of the time he is successful. Good sense of humor. Lays out expectations very clearly.

His lectures are organized, and it's helpful that he provides those slides at the class website. He does his best to explain really really difficult concepts , and a lot of the time succeeds. He's also great at giving extra help outside of class. Be prepared to brush up on those integration skills.
He acutally made pchem fun and interesting! Great class.
Great lectures, enjoyed seeing real world application and examples. Tests make up a significant portion of your grade but practice materials are sufficient.
Best professor at Foster, amazing lectures, highly recommend.

Yang is an engaging & funny lecturer that does an excellent job explaining the content. He is also happy to answer questions and truly cares that his students leave this class with practical knowledge. My only gripe is that 85% of your final grade is based on the midterm/final. Overall, he is a great professor and I would highly recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the best professors I have ever had. While participation was not mandatory, I recall that nearly everyone participated in a meaningful way because he made it interesting and engaging. Unfortunately, I have not encountered many other professors like him, so take his class if possible.
Professor's teaching style was very engaging. He is an incredible lecturer, effectively communicating complex and difficult ideas and formulas.

The class is incredibly easy. Three assignments and two tests. The tests are practically given to you, so curve is insane.

Prof. Song is a good teacher; however, he has a lackadaisical approach to learning.

Put simply, 460 is a little nuanced version of 350. If you don't have to take it, I would say take something more interesting.
Legend, loved him

Yang is absolutely hilarious, it is a joy to listen to every one of his lectures. His lectures are filled with stories, examples, etc- plenty to learn difficult Finance concepts. There are a few easy homework assignments spread out across the quarter, and the exams aren't too challenging either. Absolutely take this class if you are able!

Yang is an amazing lecturer. His slides are super easy to understand, and he makes many difficult finance concepts easy to understand. His tests are hard, so doing the examples in class with him will significantly help. This class's curve is relatively high, so be prepared to study for those few extra points if you score a 3.5+.

This was genuinely the best class I've ever taken. The way the class is structured, the content, everything was fantastic. I learned so much, and yang is so knowledgeable that it felt like he was just scratching the surface of what he could teach you, I could ask this dude finance questions for days, he's awesome.
My best finance professor so far

Professor Song cares a lot about his students and his class was very straightforward. Four assignments, 10% participation, and two exams. Class median is very high until the final. The final (40%) was unreasonably difficult and tested a lot of niche material that ignored the core of what we learned, which prevents him from being a 5/5 professor.

Throughout the course, the content was very easy and straightforward. Professor Song was decent in the beginning but focused on discussing things that were not relevant at all to the exams and we spent a lot of time doing useless calculations. The final was unbelievably hard and we were absolutely not prepared by the professor. Very unfortunate.

Extremely clear on what will be on the midterm and final. He wants students to learn a lot while having very little stress in doing so. You get one sheet of paper as a cheat sheet on all exams, so you don't have to do too much studying. However, pretty much everyone does well in the class, so having a 93% still equated to a 3.0 :/

Yang is extremely passionate about this class, you will never get bored in lecture. Not only is he engaging, but he also teaches the course in a way that can easily be understood. He cares a lot about his students - patient, offers extra office hours, homework help, and will ask for your feedback about pace and difficulty before or after lectures.

He is so awesome and makes it very clear what you are learning. He obviously wants everyone to do very good and learn the important topics. Gives you guideline of what tests will be on (just midterm and final) and answers any questions you have well. Also picking highest median grade possible which is very nice.
Super clear about what is and what is not going to be on test. Wants all students to succeed and does a good job presenting clear information. Great professor would highly recommend.

So awesome! Clearly knows what he is teaching and is very helpful in preparing for midterm. Material is hard but manageable with how well he teaches. Highly recommend. There are pop quizzes for participation only then a couple hws and midterm and final. Not bad at all and great guy

Dr Song is one of the best Finance professors you could find in foster. His lecture and classes are very well organized and he will not trick you during the exams, and he'll offer tons of practice during class to make sure you really understand the concepts. if you take FIN 460 pls make sure to take his class
Such a great teacher everything is very reasonable but interesting and important if you are going into a career in finance.

Very clear logic that makes lectures very easy to follow, unlike some other professors that just talk and talk and talk but it's hard to grasp their point. Professor Song makes it clear what is expected and when do you need to do what. Course load is just right to get you to know the material well. Great experience overall.

Turkish is a hard language, but Melike hoca explains it in easy to understand terms! Very easy grader as long as you try your best. There is a lot of homework but she's very generous with giving extensions. Attendance isn't required but it is a language course so it is fast moving and you fall behind easy if you miss too much. Very caring teacher!

all of her assignments have no clear expectations, which sounds like a decent thing until u realize she doesn't have any clear instructions of the rubric (has no rubric at all) and she seems to grade based on how she feels - literally a lottery. she doesn't even tell u why u got the grade u did. no office hours,avoid if u can and take w better prof
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Melike hoca is an amazing professor! she is so caring and she cares about her students. Her class is fun, she gives lots of extensions, and her grading is not harsh at all. You learn a lot from her! Definitely take one of her classes if you like learning about the Turkish language and Turkey

DO. NOT. TAKE. HER. Her lecture notes are borrowed straight from the textbook, are confusing, and she spends more time rambling than anything else. Quiz sections are amazing, but only because of the TA. Lectures do not align with the textbook, and I'm convinced she used ai on both her Midterms + the final. She does not care about teaching, AT ALL.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed this course and Dr. Huang's teaching. I had a limited CS background prior, so this class really opened my eyes to a new world within engineering. The format (hw, hands-on, lecture, office hours) kept me engaged and interested, so I learned a lot. Awesome professor and subject, definitely take her classes if you can!

Dr. Huang was a top-notch professor. She is VERY knowledgeable in both MSE and big data/ML, providing relevant perspectives and avenues for pursuing this subject in academia and/or a future career. You can see that she cares for her students and their success, making herself available to help/guide them. I highly recommend her and this course!
Luna seems closed off at first, but she really cares about her students! She tells you what you need to hear, and believes in student growth.

Her lectures did not make much sense as she pretty much read over each slide on her power point she got from the textbook. In order to succeed in this class, you actually have to read the textbook. Also, the homework assigned were not really relevant to what she was teaching in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Truly, utterly, completely abysmal. The worst academic experience of my life.

The movies were pretty interesting, the pre-recorded lectures were long but had interesting concepts in them, and the creative exercises were fun to do but it requires you to have many people help you.

He is a bit cautious about AI use but it is a film class so I think thats a fair paranoia to have. If you want an easy class, you can try this out
I cannot say what I want here because RateMyProfessor would remove it
So happy this class is over. What a complete horror. Avoid any class with this guy at all costs. Every review so far isn't even scratching the surface. Run!!!

This professor is oblivious to the fact that students only take this class for the A&H credit. He is so paranoid of AI, that he progressively makes assignments obnoxiously tedious each week, with the most unnecessary requirements like timestamps strictly from the Panopto recordings and refusing to post the in-class assignment question for students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the assignments straight up required us to edit a movie. Like we had to edit out the sound from a scene and replace it with sound from another part of the movie. He did not each us how to do that. There are other similarly absurd assignments. Do not take this class unless you actually have a background in video editing and photography.
too much homework for a cms class. the professor locks all the assignments too so you can't work ahead and speedrun the assignments. definitely avoid
Professor got his PhD in something irrelevant so he has a superiority complex

the creative assignments are ridiculous, I took a 0 on one of them because I legit didn't have enough friends to do it. Professor also told off a dude who was older than him just bc his phone went off, he needs to chillax

Although an "easy 4.0", this class has been nothing short of miserable. Mandatory lectures that basically regurgitates information introduced in the mandatory several hour pre-recorded lectures. Weekly creative assignments that are tedious. Just a ridiculous set of standards; don't waste your time.

Not a super hard class, but insanely tedious. Lots of lectures, lots of assignments, and the professor seems to believe that this is the only class students should care about. Way too much work for a 200 level class, but the only actual hard things are the creative assignments cuz he assumes you have access to editing software (and friends).
not worth the effort unless you really care about chinese movies. prof is full of himself too
Absolute joke lol stay as far away as possible. Talk about a guy with a huge ego who needs a reality check.
way too much for a 200-level film class, flipped classroom. pls avoid.
this teacher is so bad,with bad explanationt and too much homework

I cannot express how ridiculous this class is within RMP's 350 letter count, but all I can say is while it is an "easy A," there is a LOT of tedious work. 2 hour lectures could easily be condensed to 45 minutes, and there are additional 2+ hour online lectures to watch in order to complete homework assignments. AI will be your friend for this class

This class is a complete joke. There is an obscene amount of work.  The lecture is 2 hours, which doesn't seem so bad until you realize that you just had to spend 2-3 hours watching the pre recorded lectures and writing about them. You'll also receive class wide emails about how you are a bad citizen for using AI because it kills the environment.

An unbelievable amount of pointless work. Before attending the near 2 hour long lecture, an additional 2-3 hours of pre recorded lectures must be watched beforehand. Professor clearly cares about the subject material, though I find this is often translated into pretentiousness and an annoyance with the amount of irrelevant canvas messages sent out.

Do not take this class. Changed how the class is. Long assignments, all of which are completely pointless. You have to do "creative assignments" and make videos and photos relating to the movies. Flipped class, so you have to watch hours of lectures to then go hear the exact same stuff in class. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is a mess. Way too much work. Not only are we told to go outside to capture content but expected to read around 50 pages of texts and provide 300 word explanations for each class (2x a week). We also have 3 creative assignments which requires us to write 1,000 words. Takes more effort than all my other classes combined
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Braester is very knowledgeable and passionate about the material he teaches; his lectures are detailed, informative, and thought provoking. The films chosen for the coursework are varied and intriguing. The assignment prompts are well thought out and he is always available for questions or encouragement. Beware group projects!

The lectures were boring, but I enjoyed the quiz sections so much. The course is mainly about watching Chinese films and later writing a paragraph that was self-graded. If you need an easy A&H class take CMS&271

class is self graded so easy A! i recommend going to class though because he's very sweet and tries very hard to get students engaged. lots of movies to watch but they were honestly entertaining af and i loved them. easy class but lecture heavy so be warned ! sometimes i'd have two hour lecture in class and two hours to watch for homework lol
It's insanely lecture-heavy, and I think you just have to be incredibly passionate about/interested in the specific topic to enjoy the class, even if you're interested in film.

There was one specific film that I was particularly eager to see, which was not included in the syllabus. Upon sharing my interest with Yomi, he kindly provided me access to the film so that I could watch it. Class was largely lecture-based but engaging due to his passion. Assignments were relatively brief and enjoyable to complete.
He is the best prof at UW. I took three of his courses. He always gave us honest feedback and suggestions. His classes were engaging and very interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Yomi possesses an impressive depth of knowledge, particularly in the realm of world cinema. Although the weekly readings can be challenging, his patience and willingness to assist students make the learning experience enjoyable. I thoroughly appreciated the class!

Professor Braester is a kind and caring person who is very passionate about his work. His lectures can be slow, but the course load is very manageable, and we had no exams. This is a good class to take if you want to balance out your schedule.

Yomi is so gentle and kind, and very passionate about genre films. The class is extremely lecture/film/essay heavy, and has 3 group projects per quarter. But it's very easy, and you don't really need to watch the movies to answer prompts, just be prepared for 6-7 hours a week of lecture alone, not to mention the 2 weekly films. Can afford to skip.

His course work is not difficult but takes a little time. We need to complete both the pre-recorded lecture and the offline lecture. He respects the culture and the classroom, and the film clips and cases he shows are interesting. He started using the non-grading system, let the students control their own grades. I would recommend taking his class.

Frighteningly slow lectures. Even at 2x, a snail coming home from a funeral would have more energy than him. The entirety of his 2 hour gathering could be explained in approximately 3 slides on a PowerPoint which he enjoys dragging out, and is oblivious to how he behaves. Quiz sections could be condensed to 1 slide and TAs still drag it out. YAWN!!

I really enjoyed Professor Braester's class, which he taught collaboratively with Prof. Chris Hamm. They had organized presentations and engaged students. At the end of the quarter, they brought in the director and producer of one of the films we'd watched. A really great experience if you are looking to dive into CMS.

The overall class and writing assignments are easy, but the grading rubric is stupid. Clarity? Adherence to Prompt? Depending on the TA, it's hard to get full points because of his subjective grading rubric. My TA always nitpicked and took off points. This is how he maintains a stupid 3.3 median. With artificial difficulty in a film studies class.

Yomi is absolutely a wealth of knowledge on Chinese cinema. If you have a chance to take his class online (and watch him speak on 2x on video), do so - he speaks very slowly. You will be exposed to a trove of great cinematic analysis, cultural commentary, and a very bright mind. One of the best classes I've taken at the UW.

Coming from a non-major. No attendance. No live lectures. No exams. Don't have to do the readings or even watch the lectures to complete most of the assignments. Two weekly 250 word essays. Surprisingly tough grading, picky TA. BS essay prompts where you have to stretch and find deep meanings in surface level stuff, busy work. Overall easy tho.

This class was okay. I enjoyed the content and felt like the films we watched were quite interesting but at some times, the classes dragged on. He talks a lot and quite slowly but overall is not a hard grader. If you show up to class and put in the work, it won't be hard to do well.

Yomi gets somewhat of a bad rep from non Cinema Studies students at UW, but the guy has changed my life for the better. After my 3rd CMS class with Yomi, I realized what an unbelievable wealth of knowledge he is. Never a bad question with him, and my guy always adds insights. Be prepared to work, yet know that Yomi is a worldwide legend.

The entire class was based off of papers on movies and readings that were done outside of class and the papers were always around 500 words so only like a page and a half. Not bad at all, and you really never had to go to class and could do great. I skipped at least once a week and just did the assignments and always got 100% on them.

Yomi is super passionate, and while he can get on a tangent easily and spend a whole class on it, he loves teaching and is very accessible and easy to talk to and understanding. He knows a ton about film
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: the class material is fun and easy, but he made it very hard to understand, he always stuck in a question and keep asking student to answer. he never reply email or any question posted online. worst thing is he fail to open the video he want to show in class every time for the whole quarter. and he always takes more than 5 mins to fix that...

This Professor drags lecture material that could fit in a 50 min class into a 2 hour lecture. The material is boring and useless, he doesn't approach the material in a exciting matter but in lifeless one. Don't take this class for an easy grade, you will regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I think because of the class I took I had a positive experience with Yomi. He didn't seem annoying to me, he even used memes in his lectures. MEMES. He tried to crack jokes? But the class was also jointly taught with Chris Hamm. He is quite hard to follow, and does go in a circle of rants but it came off more as passionate to me than arrogant.
He's arrogant, but without a reason to be. He's like the poster boy for those attacking academia as elitist and useless-- he's almost a perfect caricature in this respect.

Prof. Braester is an very strange person, but not "elitist" as others say. If he behaved the way he does AND was at Harvard AND had Harvard-level intellect, then he'd be elitist. No, he just seems to have an inferiority complex where he needs to prove how smart he thinks he is & put others down to pump himself up.

He's a nice professor that knows his material well. He tries hard to make sure the students take part by pointing at students and asking them questions, which is sometimes scary if you don't know the answer. He has that philosophical attitude, wanting to dive deeper even though its a simple concept. He hates students using their phone in class.

His lectures are super slow and annoying because it takes him an hour to explain a 10 minute concept. Can't space out during class either because he and his TA's like to randomly pick on people in class so I would do the readings and skip lecture. The whole class is on one Chinese director, which means a lot of subtitles and hard names.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: As a film major I found this class to be incredibly easy and sometimes boring, but I did learn a couple things about global cinema and watched many new movies. Lectures can feel long but the final assignments are all very easy! I really enjoyed the SIFF aspect of the course, it was a good excuse to go to many films at the festival.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Decent professor, interesting material. Gets upset when people use their phones in class though, but oh well.

I really enjoyed this class! It was a lot of fun to talk about films in intricate detail with Yomi and the other dedicated students. For this class you'll get weekly readings, movies to watch, and quickly answer a couple questions plus 3 main essays. A pleasure taking his class and work is doable and worth it!

He is a thoughtful intelligent professor who knows his stuff and gives good feedback. Sometimes he got criticized for not being that clear with essay expectations, but he really tries to clarify. In the end, everything came together and worked.
confusing,  condescending

Yomi is interesting to listen to and his class is an easy high 3.0/4.0 as long as you attend the lectures and screenings.  Grade consists of 3 essays (500, 1000, and 1500 word), attendance in quiz section, and scores on post lecture quizzes(fairly easy).
Yomi is a good professor! The class contents are interesting as well. There are many movies to watch. If you want to get VLPA, this class is a good choice to go.

Most of the films are interesting, but he shows some very boring&slow ones too. Lectures are hard to understand and extremely boring because his analyses/interpretations are so deep and longwinded. But the workload for this class is also manageable
He is a nice guy who is crazy about Zhang Yi Mou. If you are into Chinese cinema, you should take C LIT 271 or 272 with him. Weekly quizzes and a final paper.

He is pretty awesome, and he presents really interesting topics and interpretations that make otherwise terribly boring films worth watching again...I dont have much of an interest in Chinese film but after him, i'd be down to watch the in class screenings again just see his interpretations and views. He's very talky but interesting with enough cof
Yomi is a very intelligent guy but extremely boring.  The movies that we watched were almost all horrible.  Do not take this class

He definitely knows his stuff..  Lectures aren't too bad, but he has the WEIRDEST way of wording things.  I had to re-read his lectures notes at least twice to know what he's really trying to say.  The movies that he shows, however, gets progressively worse...  But he's pretty easy and a reasonable guy.  I actually recommend him.

Yomi was a great professor.  There were daily quizzes, but all open note (final was open note too).  He knows what he is talking about and makes it very easy to get a good grade in the class.  I highly recommend him!
Most boring professor i have had so far in my college career and probably wont top him. He knows his chinese films but picks the worst movies to watch.     P.S. dont take this class

The guy really knows his chinese films and is a decent lecturer, but is somewhat boring. However, he seems to pick the WORST films to watch possible. If you are taking the class so you can watch movies, this is a mistake. Most of the Chinese movies we've watched are awful and incredibly dull. Skip the class if possible.

He knows his stuff but that isn't enough to qualify him as a good professor. Insanely boring lectures! Like half the class sleeping or on facebook boring. Also far too full of himself which holds him back from being likeable.

interesting accent from Israel, however, lectures are boring... don't get me wrong, the guy knows his stuff, studied at the top university in Israel, got his masters at Yale, and his P.H.D. at Berkley but... he acts like an elite prick sometimes and its hard to understand his termanology. Also he makes you take daily tests...
Professor Braester is hilarious.  His film analysis was visually very interesting and you could tell he really cared about the subject.

His israeli accent makes his dialogue very interesting to listen to.  His slideshows are very professionally made and his lectures are quite intriguing.  However, the concept of the information is a bit difficult to grasp.  All in all, a great professor.

Really smart teacher, but acts kind of elitist. He'll use his own translations of literature in class if he deems the published translation is not good enough. YOU MUST READ A LOT IN THIS CLASS, OR YOU WILL FAIL. Daily graded writing, so attendance is a must. Not a class for the lazy or weak-hearted.
No Comments

Good class however Yomi said some of the most pointless things ever.Obvious he knew his stuff-but a sense of elitism surrounded his lessons making them a dread to listen to.Also a really tough grader and is known for curving DOWN to keep courses from being
this guy was wicked sweet. and he really knew his stuff. i'd definitely reccommend him. my friends & i tried to break down his accent all quarter. good stuff.
This class made me HATE martial arts films.  Which is hard to do.  Yomi made me want to gouge my eyes out everytime he spoke.

Testimony and Allegory class.  This class is hard.  If your'e stupid or lazy do not take this class.  Yomi is brilliant, check out his CV if you have doubts.  Take it, you'll get an Ivy league course for state prices, (I'm at Columbia now, this class was good prep.)
He's obviously extremely intelligent, and very passionate about what he teaches.  I think he's definitely underappreciated by most students.
No Comments
He's not the best teacher ever but he means well and film is always worth taking.
No Comments
Beware The Opium Wars.  I think this class COULD have been interesting, it just. . . wasn't.
Teaches the most boring Chinese film class in the history of mankind.

He gave fair quizzes and good study guides. Homework was manageable. Sometimes hard to understand in lecture but he is happy to answer questions. He also explains how course material is used in his research which was nice.

Messy notetaking that was hard to follow in class and fully uninterpretable when not combined with verbal explanation. Which was made worse by his lack of recordings. Canvas resources consistently late and disappeared right after finals. 
Very harsh grading, including a 12% deduction for an arithmetic error on the final that never got regraded.

This was my second time taking a class with Prof. Zhang, and he's much improved. His lectures are clearer, the homework aligns well with the material, gives in-class extra credit quizzes, and his pre-exam guides are accurate and helpful. I wouldn't hesitate to take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The scoring requirements are too strict. It is completely different from the difficulty of the past exam.

Zhang can be tough to understand, leading to me not attending the lectures often. He references the textbook in lecture so I ended up just reading from the book most of the time. When I took the class, there were only 3 take-home quizzes and a take-home final. I will say he's great one-on-one / in office hours.

I found that the take-home exams don't always pertain to the content covered in class. Additionally, my TA is extremely harsh on HW grading. The class has a challenging grading system. While it is relaxed depending on the classes' overall performance at the end of the quarter, the most challenging scale is a 98.3% for a 4.0 and an 88% as a 3.0.
He's passionate about lectures and very caring. All the tests, including final exam, are take-home, which is excellent.

Prof goes over ppt in class and is willing to answer questions all the time. Drop this class if TA is Laura Thomas. TA is a tough grader. Your points are deducted randomly, though your answers are correct. You should wait for weeks to receive your assignment and quiz grades.

I think Shiheng is awesome. Contrary to the other reviews, I am taking AMATH352 right now and it doesn't feel like that much work at all. The homeworks are a breeze, I would say far less work than the other math classes I have taken. He is extremely kind and caring and passionate during lectures.

Zhang is a kind professor, but assumes deep knowledge of non-course material. He's a harsh and inconsistent grader, with vastly different rubrics on the midterm and final. He also assigns an incredible amount of homework, with 3 assignments/week. A combination and his unclear, difficult lectures landed me with the lowest grade I've ever gotten.

poorly structured lectures, unbearable amounts of homework, extremely slow grading, and very bad pronunciation. His lectures are straight up him reading the textbook to us, often uses weird approach to Calculus and techniques used in this class is sometimes out of scope of prerequisites. He is often inaccessible during the afternoon.

Zhang knows his stuff and is very caring 1-on-1, but he goes quickly through slides and his lessons are very similar to the textbook. Also his accent can be hard to understand sometimes. Make sure to go to class and ask questions, and he will be helpful!
Good at teaching but doesn't record lectures. Also doesn't use a tablet and instead writes physically which makes it difficult to see. He tells you what's going to be on the exam which is helpful.
Doesn't use canvas at all

Professor Zhang demonstrated a gentle, uncompromising devotion for the math that he showed in class. Admittedly, however, his lectures require some labor to understand - if you struggle in math classes, do not forgo the readings. He is also markedly old-school: he often opts to not use the microphone and diagrams everything by hand.

Thought he was a solid professor. Did not like how lectures were not recorded nor were the notes digital. Notes were also written in a sometimes faint light blue pen. Lectures were straightforward and appreciated that he told us what the midterm topics would be about. Put work in and you will do well in his class. Final was unpredictable.
grading was unclear. doesnt explain anything well. doesnt use a mic so it is hard to hear. hard to see the projected work.

Prof is a very funny guy, courseload is manageable. Go to lecture because no notes/recordings are available! He gives a heads up as to what to expect on midterms however this is a double-edged sword because it makes the averages higher so you may be deceived about your expected GPA going into the final. No heads-up about final which was not easy.

No Panopto recordings or slides from lecture so you have to be in lecture. Some might not like that but I prefer that to pre-lecture videos and it also forced me to go to lectures. Manageable class, just do Webassigns and you will be fine. Jolly guy, always smiling, put a smile to my face. Wasn't smiling when the final was excessively hard though.

Prof Zhang, while a nice person, is not a good lecturer. He writes and projects while teaching which is extremely difficult to see even in the front rows of class, he is hard to understand, and clearly doesn't care much about the class. He has very few resources posted online and what he has is not up to date. His lectures are also not recorded.

The lectures were pointless and exams unnecessarily difficult. The exams given did not match the teaching. out of 3 classes for math 126 the quarter I took this he had the LOWEST averages by a large margin, after telling us he would curve the exam to his class since the averages were so different then didn't. I took BC in HS, this was ridiculous

Great professor! He explains everything very clearly, and his exam preparation sessions are extremely useful and helpful. In addition, his exams mainly consist of exercises similar to those in the textbook, which makes studying very focused and effective.

Professor Zhang is a little more "old school". He likes writing on papers that are projected onto a screen, has a minimal canvas page, and didn't have his lectures recorded (so show up to class). But, he is well prepared and has a topic list that we consistently get through in each lecture. He was also very detailed in what he expected out of us.

His lectures were decent, however you had to attend as lectures weren't recorded. He told what each question would be for the midterms, so if you study final exams you will do very well. He had no resources on Canvas, so I had to seek out Dr. Loveless notes for review. As a teacher, he is average and his midterms are very reasonable.

Professor Zhang is a nice, caring guy. Lectures are not recorded though. Lectures are ok, but I always understood the material better after lecture than reading the textbook. Examples are either very basic or confusing, but follow his advice and do old exam problems. He also gives a good idea of what will be on the exams.

Super enthusiastic during lecture, does go over very simple examples though so homework can be a little hard sometimes. Gave us a good idea on what would be on the midterms and quizzes. No online material or recorded lectures so you have to go to class.

Prof cannot lecture: just redoes textbook ex.s and his explanations/defn.s don't make sense. Learned more from quiz section, textbook, & Loveless' notes.
For 3D stuff, he has a tiny popsicle stick model & a sheet of paper, or the actual cords of the doc camera or HIS MICROPHONE for 3D curves. Topped with chuckles to himself, it's so bad it's funny.

Professor Zhang's MATH126 class is no easy feat, but with the right approach, you can succeed. His lectures are engaging, though attendance is mandatory. Unstuck study and the course textbook proved invaluable for preparing for the challenging exams. Overall, a rewarding experience.

Lectures got really hard to follow towards the end, especially since he doesn't come with pre-prepared lecture notes and just writes them down on pen and paper on a projector. Spends much more time computing than teaching the methodology and problem-solving patterns. He is subtly hilarious though.

Graded based on homework, 2 quizzes, 2 midterms, and one final exam. Zhang is a good, caring lecturer; the lectures are not recorded and are done on paper, so attendance is mandatory. Going to quiz section is key for this class, the worksheets and problems are very useful for homeworks, midterms, and quizzes. The final was very difficult though.

Zero online resources provided. No canvas, no outside sources to help you succeed. Didn't even know what my grade was in the class until after I took the final. His lectures are helpful, but are not recorded and are all taken on paper, so attendance is mandatory and it would be wise to make some friends in the class if you ever plan on being gone.

A very difficult class but Professor Zhang does not make it any more difficult than it needs to be. He is very helpful leading up to exams and really seems to care about how his students do. Some of his TAs are much better than others though.

Prof. Zhang is a funny and happy guy. He tries to make jokes in lectures. His lectures are fair, not great but not bad either. He doesn't post his old exams online so its kinda hard to know how he writes exams but doing WebAssign homework is definitely helpful. I wouldn't be too worried if you REALLY need to take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's pretty funny and you can really tell he cares about Math and teaching. His class takes some time to get into the rhythm to, but there's usually only 2-4 homeworks per week, and two midterms and two quizzes per quarter. He's not very available outside of class, but his TAs (broski Cody Tipton is the best) help a lot.
So funny and engaging. Tests are really difficult.

Prof. Zhang is always happy. His lecture notes are well structured and clear to understand; ATTEND LECTURES and you won't have to do the readings. WebAssign homework can be tricky but usually straightforward ("Watch It" button is always helpful). Discussion sections with TAs are like study halls, so bring homework questions.
Sooooo nice and kind

He's generally a pretty good professor. If you attend all the lectures and put an effort into understanding the content outside of just the homework or class time you will likely succeed. However, there are no recorded lectures and a LOT of your grade will depend on your TA as they teach and grade most of the content. Challenging, but doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are not recorded, and Zhang uses Canvas/other digital tools almost not at all. However, lectures are informative, clear, and Zhang is super cheerful and enthusiastic. The topics can be tricky, but Zhang makes them very accessible and he obviously cares about students' learning and engagement.

I don't do these reviews often. But he is by far the worst professor I've had at UW. He just copies the textbook word for word in lecture but his tests are HARSH. No examples. No questions answered. No review/study guide. The only reason I didn't get destroyed by his class is because I watched my friends professors lecture recordings. RUNNNN

This dude puts in no effort. No canvas page, a bare bones website buried in the depths of the math department, no lecture notes. Each lecture he just repeated the textbook word for word but the textbook itself is garbage. Nowhere near enough to prepare for the difficulty of his exams. Hell I stopped going and watched my friends lecture recordings.

Professor Zhang is a professor that evidently cares. His lectures tend to be straight forward and cover most of what is needed to complete the online homeworks. His midterms are difficult but reasonable. Overall, a solid choice.

We started the year off going online, but his lecture recordings were always super blurry and oversaturate making it tough to see what he actually wrote. Once we got back in person, it was slightly better. Also compared to the examples he does in class to the HW and the Exams, the exams were much harder and tougher so watch out.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took his class while covid began so this is unlikely to be a recurrent issue, but I think it shows him being suboptimal professor. He cancelled our 40% of grade final which I was planning to be my saving grace. Not only did he give no options to replace it, he was rude about it. Hurt my gpa for sure.

Overall an awesome professor. I went to most of his office hours to ask for questions and he explained everything to me very well. His online lecture quality isn't very good when I took his class so it was a bit difficult to see what he wrote on the whiteboard sometimes. Overall a solid class to take!

If you want to learn 126 through YouTube by yourself, go ahead and take his class. Taking his online class in horrible, the lecture videos resolution is very low and overexposed for most of the time. His teaching has no difference from reading the book by yourself. I borrowed my friend's account and watched Loveless's, that's how I got through it.

Grades are based on two things- homework and 5 quizzes (each worth 1/6 of total). Missing a point on a quiz drops your overall grade by 2%. Miss 3 points per quiz (7/10) and prepare to retake the class. For reference, the quiz average of our class was 70% while the other class (taught by a different professor) was 83%. Make of that what you will.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed MATH 126 with professor Zhang. His lectures are clear and tie right into the homework and quizzes. The bulk of your grade is based on five quizzes spaced out throughout the quarter, but as long as you watch the lectures and stay caught up on homework, you should do well on the quizzes and in this class. Overall, great professor.

Grading system is horrific. Quizzes which are each 16% of your grade are made up of 3 or 4 questions, so a dumb mistake crushes your grade, and getting partial credit for mistakes is beyond rare. Follow that up with the only way to boost your grade being homework at 16% and lectures that cover maybe 50% of what is on the homework. Avoid if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Zhang is a nice person, but his lectures are not in-depth enough for the content covered in the quizzes. So basically its the text book or 3Blue1Brown for your grade. Also, the each quiz has 3 questions, and each are 16% of your overall grade, so there is a huge chance of losing a lot of points for stupid mistakes.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Zhang didn't teach this course this Fall; he just reused his lecture videos from the Spring. Grades were based on just 5 10pt quizzes worth 80% of the final grade! There was a lot of HW, which is good practice, but only worth 20% of the grade!!! Quiz questions sometimes were different from the hw. No retakes, midterm, or final to boost grades
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class was asynchronous, which made the material harder to learn since we couldn't ask questions live. He gives good explanations, but he did not go in-depth at all, and the video quality of the lectures was poor. The tests weren't too bad if you did many practice problems, but he didn't provide any - I had to find them from Dr. Loveless's site.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a really friendly and funny prof who knows a lot about his field. Lectures are pretty easy to understand though they were not recorded (I took the class this winter). The review sheets that he gave to us before the exams is great as it tells you what you need to know and what to expect for the test.
Really nice, funny guy but doesn't really care if you actually understand the concepts fully. Memorization is one of his goto recommendations for students.

Zhang is hilarious. He jokingly 'kicks you out of class' if you have previously learned what he's about to teach but he's all serious when it comes to math. He gives really good feedback and he's so passionate in math. He designs his test questions in a way that the calculations are horrific but always lead to a simple answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hes not a very good lecturer, often confuses the students more with explanations, and relies too much on the textbook. Also he had his exam a week earlier than the rest of the math 126 classes and he doesnt post any of his old exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nice guy, friendly and wants students to learn, lectures are very clear and have a good balance between theory and examples. Has good jokes and tests aren't too hard.

Zhang is a really nice guy and a good teacher if you just want to learn formulas, not the why behind the math. His tests were easy in comparison to other teachers'(but by comparison the final was pretty hard). Can be hard to understand if you have trouble with understanding accented speech. He is super nice tho, always willing to answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: This was the hardest class I've taken at UW so far. His lectures are really hard to comprehend and most of the time it seemed like he was just writing formulas on the board. His exams are unreasonably hard which doesn't make sense because he never goes over examples in class. He is a nice, goofy person though but not a great teacher.

Don't take this professor. His lectures are the same as the textbook and he does not answer questions well. His tests are made overly complicated by difficult algebra and he gives little to no partial credit for simple algebra mistakes even when it is clear there is a conceptual understanding.

Worst Math professor I've had at UW by far. He is hard to understand and his lectures are repeats of examples in the book with little to no explanation. I would recommend switching classes or solely relying on reading the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Was hard to understand in lecture, TA was also hard to understand, does not use Canvas at all, gives study guides with no answer keys

He is a pretty nice guy, although I wish we got more resources to use outside of lecture and the textbook. He tests require lots of tedious computations that make it hard to finish on time even if you understand the concepts. There was also harsh penalties for simple algebraic mistakes (which are easy to make given the nature of his exams)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I really liked Zhang , he had very easy going lectures where he would write out notes and example problems for us, and if you have a question you can just ask it. The class is hard purely because of the material, but he does a good job of going at a moderate pace and reviewing exactly what will be on the midterms. Only con is how he does the curve

He gives weekly quizzes which are a pain but they are not that hard. His tests are very hard though, but as long as you're above the average you should be fine. I overall did not like his lecture style and it is hard to read the notes he writes and understand him sometimes. You must work hard in this class. Plus he has no old midterms posted.

Professor Zhang is very easy going, goofy, and really cares about his students. His tests are difficult but he is very transparent about test content/difficulty and how to succeed in his class. Definitely would recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Zhang is a great lecturer -- I enjoyed going to his class. He is eager to help and answer questions when possible. However, his grading system is based on class rank and not standard deviation, so you absolutely cannot mess up on any midterms or finals. He does not use panopto or canvas so it is absolutely essential that you go to lecture.

That is the most disgusting professor I have ever had!He hardly mention the key point in the class only repeat all the formulas in the textbook. He even refused to answer my question in his office hour!His tests are also awful. The calculations are huge and the questions all focus on the calculations but the theories that we learn. DON'TTAKEHISCLAS

Doesn't use Panopto and there are no online notes. You can't find any of his past exams online and they are 10x harder than other professors'. If you're lucky and get a good TA, you'll be safe but land a terrible TA and you're done for. He also doesn't add a little leeway to your hw grade like some other professors do.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: A very calm guy who is knowledgeable in maths. He'll try to help if you ask for it. He also teaches at a faster pace than his fellow colleagues so beware of that if you do not enjoy running through the syllabus.

Professor James is a lecturer that makes sure his students understand how the equations are derived and how to tackle some difficult questions. He often tries to cheer up the class by making silly jokes and some of them were kinda good. I always relied on his notes in class instead of the textbook and I can say I got above average on both midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Zhang's lectures often covered very little of the textbook material and his explanations were not thorough, especially when answering questions from the class. Expect to rely heavily on the textbook and online resources for the homework (Loveless' notes are great). His midterms are fairly easy, but be prepared for a much harder final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Must go to class!!!! Relies heavily on the textbook. Quiz sections are optional, usually not very helpful unless you have a stellar TA. Very tough when choosing the average GPA so screws people's GPAs up even if they are fairly above average.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: As math teachers go, professor Zhang is not the worst one you could get. He makes sure to provide at least 2 or 3 examples when introducing new concepts and is very clear about the material that will be covered on tests/quizzes. However, to do well on the midterms and final exam, it's important to fully understand concepts rather than just formulas
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He teaches well. He avoids proofs and spends most of each class giving examples. Lectures are never too fast.  Before each midterm and before the final, he gives out review sheets that tell you exactly what topic each question is on and gives you several very similar example problems for you to practice.   He cares if you understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you enjoy laughing at nothing for 50 minutes during lecture and being told before every test that you're probably going to fail then this dude is perfect for you. If, on the other hand, you want to succeed and do well in math 126 then drop this class instantly and find another teacher. In all honesty he puts equations up with no explanation.

Going to make it short and sweet, do not take him, switch to Loveless who actually helps students and is understandable. Learned more from Loveless's website alone 3 days before the final than an entire quarter of Zhang.
Do not take his class, weired, never go over examples, so it is pretty hard to understand materials. OH is very useful though

He seems to be a decent professor at the beginning of the quarter. But midway through, it fell apart for him. He crammed multiple lessons into one because he had to be gone many times throughout the quarter without planning for a sub, so it ended up with him giving us equations without really explaining what the equations do and how to use them.

Did not understanding much during his lectures. I'd have to go online and look for calculus notes to better understand the material. While during homework, my friends and I would always say, "Wait, when did we learn this stuff?". Turns out a lot of stuff on the midterm or the homework was not touched upon in class.

Good teacher. Tests and quizzes were pretty easy compared to some other professors but don't necessarily prepare you for the final all that well. A little hard to understand in lecture because he has an accent, but you get used to it and he's very good at explaining the material. Also, make sure to ask questions because he's very good at clarifying

Dr. Zhang has a slight accent, but I found It wasn't a problem after the first lecture. He has a very bubbly sense of humor, and clearly wants all of his students to succeed - He always makes sure students are comfortable with the material before going on. His first midterm was incredibly easy for my class too.
A nice and interesting professor. His lectures are fairly clear.

Dr. Zhang is clearly knowledgable, which is great. He even left town a couple times because he was asked to speak at conferences. His lecture style is pretty good. He tends to work through examples versus giving formulae. He's really friendly, but strict at times.
The professor is fine, but the midterms are very hard.

I didn't take 124 at UW so perhaps I was a bit unprepared for this class. Zhang while enthusiastic and humorous can be a bit hard to follow at times. He tends to skip steps assuming we know what to do . . At the same time though, it's math, open up your textbook and you'll find what you need to know. The final was a beast from hell.
He tries really hard to be funny during lectures. Very friendly guy, always smiling. Math 125 is just hard in general, so I would say he's pretty good.

He's a great person, not a great teacher. Things you need to know: 1)He is not easy to understand, you lose focus while he speaks especially 126 is different. 2)Exams are hard(different from students). 3)Quizzes are hard. 4)just doing homework not paying attention in class will not work. 5)although he's 3.9 now, do look for other prof for 126..

His first midterm was extremely easy, the mode was 100%, the second midterm was definitely harder, but he does give hints on what's on the tests if you go to lectures. I really enjoyed and will miss his enthusiasm and bubbly personality.
His test are extremely weird and had a lot of T/F questions. The midterms are no where near the practice ones.
His lectures were well planned. He had a good sense of humor. His first mid term was easy his second was a bit harder, but wasn't that bad.
The class was moderately good - not great. I felt bored multiple days I came in and the lectures didn't really prepare me for the final.
He is a nice guy, but he does not clarify, skips a lot of steps, and rushes through a lot.
Really good.
Nice guy, midterms are pretty reasonable.
Excellent Professor. Best lecturer I have had at UW. Take his class!

Zhang prepares you for his midterms, but  not very well for the final. He had grad students with poor lecture structures teach some of the most important topics and wrote test questions specifically on those missed lectures. Zhang usually lectures clearly, but also rushes his notes at times and uses unneeded proofs instead of explaining topics.

Exmaples that he does in class were too easy so you might have problems when you are doing your hw. Once I sent emailed n hope he would explain on of the hw question, but he jus gave me the right answer (which does not help cuz webassign marked me down), no explanation at all. The second time I emailed for help, he just told me to ask my TA.
Explains wonderfully. Accent not too pronounced.
He's really nice, and is pretty funny. He's not great at explaining though. The first midterm's easy, but the second one's hard. Overall, he's not bad, but not great.

Though I know many students struggled with Zhang, I found his teaching to be very clear and straightforward. He also has a goofy sense of humor that can lighten up the otherwise dense class. If you are taking MATH 126, I'd suggest Zhang.

Zhang was a quality professor. I struggled in the class, but his teaching style was straightforward and effective. He tends to focus more on general proofs and conceptual understandings, so it can be hard to make the transition of practical application on tests. Grading was fair and lectures were overall quite helpful.

His lectures are put together very well and he explains the concepts really well. Examples are not extremely prevalent, however there is not as much need as you have a good understanding without them and then you can use the book. First test is easy. Second test average was a low 60. Overall very helpful and good class.

First midterm was easier than second midterm. He was trying his best to teach, and is not hard get an A if you do all the homework and practice more. He tried to encourage us by promised to give anyone who get 100 in finals a 4.0. That motivated me to work harder for his finals. I did not get a 4.0 though, but was motivated by him. =)
He didn't explain things well at all, but he was a really nice guy. He has trouble with English, so often times questions were misunderstood and went unanswered.

James Zhang is a really good professor. His lectures are very organized however, the illustration of examples is pretty low. He approaches more to a proof or general formulas which are difficult to understand without examples. Overall, very good. You will not regret for taking his class if you study on time:)

James is a nice guy, but that has little to do with being an effective teacher. He does not do a good job lecturing and relates concepts to the class very poorly. His first exam was a cake walk, and his second was completely impossible (top score in 300 students was an 80%, mean 46%). Like I said, nice guy, bad lecturer.

His exams were easy. It is REALLY similar to his practice exam problems. However, he doesn't explain things very well. And his tests were so easy, it made the curves so high (mean was a 86), that it was very hard to get a decent grade.
Very clear, easy to understand.
Zhang is a very good professor! He has a cute sense of humor and class is always fun! He's really cool, i recommend him!

I don't really like Math, so I think the whole course was hard, but he seems extremely easy to appoarch. Review cover most(70%) of the material on the test. Study hard! Final is not made up by him only, so it might be harder than the usual test that he give out.
He is really nice and really helpful. I heard he teaches right out of the book but I haven't even looked at my book other than for homework. His quizzes are pretty easy as well.

Seriously amazing. I hate math and everything to do with math but somehow I still wanted to work hard in his class. He's very funny and is ALWAYS open for suggestions to make the class better. He's got a really cute sense of humor and is always happy to see his students in office hours.
Very fun, entertaining, and tries to be as helpful as possible.  Tests and quiz material was reviewed and outlined very well.

funny prof. cuts out lots of excess hwk--makes it easier. midterms are fair, did very well on both, but final is the killer. probably got less than 50% on it..messed my grade up so put LOTS of time into studying for it, they make it extra hard--if u have choice of teachers take him!
Zhang is the man!
Very fun teacher.  He really likes to cut out how much homework, your are supposed to get according to the deparmental standards.

Extremely good professor. Teaches very well and makes calculus interesting. He is cute (in terms of actions), and he's always asking for student's opinion/suggestions to make the class better. He's willing to teach you in office hours too.
Very good professor, wants to help you learn, knows his stuff very well, very open to questions.  Highly recommend
Best Math Prof I have had so far. Great Lecturer, explained concepts very well, and he goes step by step. He has a great sense of humor too.

Professor Zhang is the best instructor I've had in UW so far... he's funny and extremely helpful... he laughs a lot, which makes the class fun and not serious at all... his behaviors are kinda adorable sometimes... :P
Couldn't understand him very well- seems like a nice guy, but didn't get much from his teaching.

Great professor. Makes sure you understand the material- always asks for suggestions on how to improve the class. Actually made exam 2 harder due to(someone! grr) asking for it to be so. Only complaint is that his pace is very slow- I have done very well on all exams and skipped class many times. Never opened my textbook except for homework.
He teaches really well. Only problem I've had with him was sometimes I couldn't understand him clearly.

Prof Zhang is a great teacher. He's funny and puts a lot of effort into his lectures. He is extremely helpful in/out of class, and somehow makes the textbook understandable! His tests are pretty hard, but if you study your notes and asks him questions, he's very open to helping you.
goodddd....

He made an otherwise confusing textbook understandable.  Explains things clearly, even if he does tend to go through material rather quickly - willing to slow down if requested.  Wants his students to do well.
Great guy.  Very enthusiastic, but often misunderstands questions and explains something completely different.
His teaching style is great.
Zhang rocks. Hes funny, if a little difficult to understand. I got the sense that he really cared and put alot into his teaching.
somewhat difficult to understand in a large lecture hall. but still, that only took a small part away from the overall lecture. take him if you can.

By far the best math professor I've had during my undergraduate years at the UW.  His step-by-step approach to problems helped me to understand the materials better.  HW and exams are fair in terms of number of problems and difficulty.  If he's teaching Math 307 and/or 309, take either one or both.
He taught really well and cared whether we learned or not. He also didn't waste time and used each minute effectively because he prepared each lecture well.

Professor Zhang is always cheery in class and usually explains the material very thoroughly.  On our last midterm, the average was a 39/50 which is very good for a class of 100+ students.  I highly recommend taking Math 126 from Prof. Zhang.

Teaching style is very fast-paced with little to no check-ins on student understanding. Lectures often are one sided. More structured delivery and periodic comprehension checks would greatly improve the experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Doesn't provide grades throughout the quarter on Canvas. Never answers questions directly and can't teach any of the primary sources in his own language and regurgitates quotes throughout the lecture without any clarification.

Top notch instructor with a class perfectly tailored to graduate work. He respects your time and intelligence and provides a well-structured challenge. I took him a few years ago and still feel the benefits from his class.
The class is well organized and engaging, the readings are relevant, and the coursework is instructive.

If you're in TC, Mark's class is the type of experience that called you to grad school. He edits one a premiere journal of our field, and his knowledge shines. He gives freely of his time within and beyond office hours.  When you're done, you will likely recreate your understanding of the TC field. Expect to spend 30-40 hours a week on TC 501.

Dr. Su is absolutely amazing! She cares that you are exploring the content, so grading is very kind, especially for a 400-level math course. She entertains questions, her slides are accessible and great, and the work is very reasonable. One of the best math profs I have had.

Professor Su's lectures can get heavy and overwhelming so you may need to do some self learning. But the exams were fair and HW reasonable. Prof Su also clearly cares about the students and their learning.

the goat! professor su has well written exams + reasonable hw assignments. lectures are a little slow but very thorough. she's also really funny and great in office hours, cares that her students are actually learning. super active on ed (discussion forum) and has office hours 3x a week. take 207 w/ her! she makes it easy to do well

Dr. Su was awesome!! She clearly cares a lot about if students learn and knows a ton about this subject. She's incredibly interesting to listen to (and funny!) and very much wants students to succeed. If you show up and do your work, you will do well in this class. Definitely one of my favorite professors I've had at UW!

Very caring and encouraging professor she really cares about you are doing in the class and goes over difficult topics again. Lectures can be fast but she revises the notes after and is clear. The homework and lectures align with the exams perfectly and her exams are very doable just practice and attend class. Best prof I've taken for math so far.
Her lectures are so confusing and the speed that she goes through everything is so counter productive. She is kind and does try to answer questions but her answers are not clear

She is just the sweetest and best! She truly cares about whether her students understand the material, and not necessarily the grade you earn. 2.0 was a 50% while a 4.0 was 95%, so you will pass if you get any grade in between, so don't stress about grades. Take her! She is worth it

she is a good lecturer, very reasonable and straightforward professor. class expectations are clear. she does a good job of explaining (difficult) concepts and tying lectures together and responds quickly to ed discussion. she cares about her students and their understanding of the content.

I love Professor Su!!! MATH 444-445 were difficult for me, but asking questions really helped me. Su cares about her students, so if you need extra support/time just ask! She also brought in snacks for presentations (torus = donut/bagel haha). There were days when I'd go to office hours just to chat, and Prof Su has had really cool experiences too!
I just love her. she's so nice

Su is a pretty decent professor. I think math 444 has a lot of super abstract concepts and the class itself is very difficult. She is very kind and offers lots of help through office hours! I would recommend her and warn of the difficulty of the class. I hate presenting but the group project/final was fun and she brought donuts and bagels!

Really good Professor. Enjoyed her class and she was very nice. Gave us extra credit. If you put in the work you'll do great. Exams are kind of like the practice problems she gives but I'd suggest doing multiple different scenario practice problems as it's not always the same exact question on exams.

Clearly a very knowledgeable professor, Su has great lectures and is very straight to the point in her explanations of important concepts. Expect significant difficulty, but also a lot of support from Su and her TAs.

amazing teacher. she taught math 120 in the spring and she constantly showed that she was trying to help the students succeed. she made midterm guides, posted lecture recordings, and posted solutions to past exams for us. super consistent and friendly.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Su for 126 was amazing! I thoroughly enjoyed the math we learned in this class because Dr. Su made it approachable and easy to apply. Exams are extremely fair game and her grading provides generous partial credit for really trying! Lecture notes are easily accessible and easy to follow, and Dr. Su provides lots of support outside of class.

Dr. Su was a great professor to have for 126. She makes online guided notes for lectures (easy to review) and posts the completed notes after every lecture. Su is open to questions and receptive to feedback. Tests are very reasonable (Loveless videos help too).
After midterm 1 the pace picks up. At least skim the chapter section before lecture!

Iconic! Her online notes are well formatted and easy to understand. Lectures go by quick, but there's a lot of content to cover. Extremely generous with partial credit. Exams are very difficult compared to some other professors, but not unreasonable and her old exams will prepare you well. Would def recommend Su for this class!

Ms. Su is the best professor I've taken at UW. Her lectures are very clear (not just for me, but for many of my classmates as well). Her approach to solving problems is easy to follow and well-structured. She's also very nice during office hours! Taking her class would be a great experience for anyone!
She's great at explaining things, cares for her students, and is funny. I'd recommend taking her class for anyone with the option.
Super nice and thorough lecturer and person. She cares a lot about students and the content she is teaching
Such a good teacher and she's really sweet and she's kinda funny. She goes a bit fast but that's bc the classes are 50 min. Highly recommend.

Incredible lecturer. Teaches concepts extremely clearly and answers questions very well. Outside of class she answers questions pretty fast and is always ready to help out on homework. Her tests are very reasonable and cover almost exactly what she lectures.

Very challenging prof, exams/teaching style took a while to get used to. Lecture notes matter a LOT, use those for revision and review her practice exams carefully. Tests were extremely hard, but not unfair. Helpful in office hours and active on the discussion board. Take this prof if you want to really understand the material.
Su is absolutely a great professor! Her digital lecture notes are clear and easy to follow. She would be very patient during office hours and guide you through problems. Love her so much!

She makes the math easy to understand. Makes a worksheet before each class and fills it in with us instead of writing on a whiteboard, very clear and organized. She posts recordings of all lectures. I practiced with prev exams of other profs and hers were easier and more straightforward. Around 2 problem sets a week, very doable.
Su was a great teacher - really liked her lectures and she gave out a lot of practice. Her exams had a few difficult problems, but she prepares you really well for the exams.

Su is a fantastic professor with super clear lectures and great visuals. She takes notes live and posts them after class which are great to review. She has all of her past midterms available to practice with. She has regular office hours in which she's super clear - albeit slightly intimidating - and works with you. Tough class, great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Su has great visualizations during her lectures, her midterms from the past few years have had the very similar format so they aren't that bad.
Stellar professor, extremely accommodating to outside circumstances, the material make sense if you do all of the homework and the practice exams.

She's a great lecturer and great teacher overall. She's super accessible on Ed Discussion since she responds quickly and frequently. Her lectures are a bit fast-paced though so I definitely recommend skimming the textbook before each lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I didn't do well in the class but that was not of Dr. Su's teaching this was because of her behavior towards me during my time in her class. When asking for help she initially seemed very caring and helpful but in meeting with her she was very condescending and rude. She belittled my abilities as a student and made me feel incapable of learning.

Great Canvas organization and lectures. Print or use PDF's of lecture notes, study them heavily for exams. Released midterms and worksheets provided are your best study material over homework/additional practice. Professor Su was witty and her care for the subject and students was very evident. Final was much harder than midterms given.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Best math professor, love from China

This was my first math class at UW, and I'm so glad I picked Dr. Su as my professor. The course material was challenging, but Dr. Su explained it well. I definitely would not recommend taking this class autumn quarter because most people in this class already know the material and are try hards, causing the curve to be horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, her lectures are really clear. If you have questions, go to her office hour and she'll help you out.
Very good professor, class lecture note is very good, very experienced!

Her notes were all online and super clear and easy to read since her handwriting is also nice and detailed. She is a great math teacher where I actually understood what was going on if i paid attention. Her midterms were not bad, people overall did well. The only con is that she kind of speaks fast but it didn't bother me that much

Hard class but great prof. Posted detailed notes from lectures and was super accessible through ED discussion board. She answered all my questions within an hour. I actually think her midterms were easier than other profs.
Good class and lecture, but the midterms are demons. Also graded on a curve.

I've listened all the three cal3 (126) professors' lecture in uw and I'm glad I'm in Su's class. Her lecture is really clear and she gives very detailed notes after lecture. Definitely recommend her class

It was intimidating taking my first math class at UW, that too Calculus 3. My first UW class ever was a 9:30 math class in Kane Hall and I was super nervous seeing so many students around me. However, the professor made me feel relaxed and welcomed. She explains the concepts beautifully. I don't know who wouldn't take her for Math 163.
Prof. is a super clear explainer and goes into much of the intuition behind the concepts that really help. Lecture notes are always pristine and tests aren't too difficult.
Lectures are very informative and professor tries her best to explain everything

Lectures and lecture notes are great and nice to follow along with, but those midterms are skewed, not normal. The curve is pretty harsh on the average math student who is not a super crazy pro who already knows all of Calc III and making it hard for normal people to survive the class. It's pretty hard to be more pro than the pros.

Prof. Su was incredibly knowledgeable about the course material. Lecture pacing was great and she was to-the-point without being dull or boring. Course material was challenging but you can do well if you put in the effort.

Dr. Su was one of the best professors I've had. She puts students success first, you can tell by the way she gives lectures. Although this course is very difficult, her lectures and explanations were very clear. If you have the chose to take this course with Dr. Su, I definitely recommend!

Taking Professor Su will be one of the highlights here, especially if you take her in Autumn. Lectures just fantastically organized, super clear notes, very helpful office hours, and overall just a wonderful human being who is passionate about math. Really inspiring work. Tests are difficult and more conceptual than computation, which I liked

Very friendly, easy to talk to. I liked the class structure she had 10% taken off the final hw score and worst midterm worth 20% and best midterm worth 30%. The exams are harder than the hw, but curved so it's not bad really.

Su's explanation were extremely clear and to the point. Detailed lecture notes with both pre-class and post-class versions that contained additions made during lecture. You could skip lecture and read the lecture notes and have a very clear idea on what went on, though Su's explanations in lecture were top notch anyway so attending class was useful

Fantastic math professor. Granted, the course is still very difficult (and my grade tanked), but her lectures go over the content very, very clearly. Expectations for grades and exams were made clear and she felt like a very responsible professor. Take the intro math sequence with her if you can.

Professor Su is awesome! She doesn't drone in lectures and her 3D drawings are really good. The tests can be tough but she gives you a lot of resources to succeed and will answer your questions quickly and clearly.

Su is serious and organized & lecture notes are circumstantial and lucid, with challenging assignment problems discussed. Efficient office hour, clear-sighted and astute with explications of concepts and responsible for students' learning. unimpeachable overall. Why difficulty 5.0? Final is out-and-out condign for the seat of reservation.
Try the 2022 Autumn Final and you will know everything.
I love Dr. Su! She's always very open to questions and explains class content very well. She's quick and efficient.

Her lectures are extremely fast and can sometimes be hard to follow but she is thorough in what she teaches. She gives A LOT of WebAssign but it is a good way to learn. Be aware that her grading curve is ROUGH. I got a D on the first midterm and my approx GPA was 3.1, then a B on the second midterm and my approx GPA dropped to 3.0.
Although her Webassign is much more than other professors, she gives amazing lectures and easy-to-read lecture notes. I would definitely take her class again.

Her lectures are super clear and easy to understand. Math 126 is mostly 3D surfaces so her organized diagrams really helped a lot. The problems assigned on Webassign are relevant to lecture material.
