Her exams are clear and correspond to what we learned in lectures. We also used Ed Discussion to ask questions and she responds really fast and clear
She is the best professor I have met, she made difficult material very easy for students to understand.

Professor Su is nice and always willing to help. However, I found it difficult to keep up during lectures. Some lectures were too fast which made it hard to keep up. I recommend reviewing the material before every lecture just so you have an idea of the content going into class.

She was the professor of my first math class at UW! She is very serious and responsible, and it can be seen from the daily teaching that she has been teaching for a long time and is an experienced professor! After taking her MATH126, I took MATH208 this semester. These two courses should be completed together.

I was really lucky to take Dr. Su's class in person! Her teaching can be relatively fast-paced, but her lecture notes are the most descriptive I've ever come across. I will say that the curves for exams can be brutal at timeshowever, there's nothing on the tests that she doesn't cover beforehand. By far my favorite math professor at UW!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: TOUGH grading curve, but her lectures are clear and you know what to expect on exams. you can tell she cares about students and loves to take time to answer questions
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Su is awesome! If you're going to take 126 with anyone, she's the only person you should consider. She's very considerate as well. You definitely want to show up to class and make sure you do all the required work. Tests aren't necessarily challenging but you will want to work fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Su is an amazing lecturer and I wish I could have her for my other math classes. Her lectures are well organized and her use of one note drawings helped solidify the visual concepts in Math 126. It's obvious that she cares about her students and she is very clear about what problems will show up on tests.

Dr. Su is an amazing professor. Her lectures were incredibly clear. She does move pretty fast, so try to pay attention throughout the lecture, but she prepared us really well for the exams and she's a very understanding and relatively lenient professor. She provides you with notes that are really concise and thorough.

Professor Su is amazing! Her lectures are clear and she posts all her notes and resources on Canvas. Her exams are quite straightforward and it's clear what topics she expects us to review/focus on. She's very accessible outside of class i.e. office hours, email, Canvas. Do her practice exams, do the homework, ask questions, and best of luck!

Su is an amazing professor! Though fast at times, her lectures are clear and comprehensive, and I found myself rarely having to refer to the textbook. Su is very compassionate and cares about the success of her students- moving HW deadlines, quick responses to emails, detailed practice exams, etc. The only annoyance is the required class curve.

Dr. Su is absolutely a great professor, but the class overall is very hard, especially when you have to do better than half of the class to get a 3.0+. Make sure to start the practice exam early and go to her officer hour. She is very encouraging and always willing to answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Su is an amazing teacher i wish i had her for all my calc classes. Make sure you do the homework and practice exams and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I have never enjoyed math, but Professor Su has really helped me develop admiration and interest in the subject. The course is hard but she puts a lot of work into the course to make it manageable, from detailed lectures to posting recordings and notes after. The midterms are manageable (she posts practice exams), but the final is hard.

Su was great, I enjoyed her lectures and liked going to class. The class is on a curve and I found it to be very competitive. Even still, Su helped me understand the material very well and with the competitiveness, I was still able to do very well in this class.

One of the best professors, 10/10 would recommend. Lectures were super easy to understand and she was always willing to stay after class to for questions. Exams are fair, just do a lot of the exams in the archive. It's still math tho so it's a difficult class and is super competitive.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Mrs. Su is great. The class is very well organized and extremely straightforward. There is no ambiguity about when assignments are do or what will be on the tests. You can also tell she really cares about the students.
Good professor in all. Reasonable and organized lectures. The only problem is she is really talking fast you should have confidence to catch up her speed.

Perfect professor!! Best professor in UW! Little homework, easy quiz, and no need for participation. Gives solutions to all students' questions posted in piazza. An easy 4.0 if you listen to her recordings. She cares students a lot. She meant to let you understand math. I love Su, and she is my beloved Don't miss her class if you have the chance!!
Very good teacher

Dr. Su is the best math professor I've ever had! Math126 has some pretty challenging concepts that involve a lot of visualizing and she helps us understand it all with such ease. Her lectures are very orgainized and clear. She's extremely resonable with everything. I usually tolerate math but this class helped me develop a real appreciation for it.
Great even in an online setting

AMAZING professor. Knows the material in and out and is great at explaining concepts. Extremely dedicated to the course. Very responsive to emails and questions on Piazza. Clear geometric drawings and uses OneNote like a pro. Approachable and answers every single question asked. Lecture Vids are a bit slow, but 1.25x speed works perfectly :)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The course is good for those who have hard times learning math. Her online lectures are slow and boring because he explains everything calmly and deeply. Her drawing skill is very excellent well fit with the class she teaches. The quizzes are unique unlike those in past exams but she posts similar practices before the exams. 30 HW on Webassign.

The class is about coding a video game from scratch: should be amazing, right? WRONG. The professor somehow takes all the joy out of it, publicly reprimanding students who do not adhere to his requirements that he does not state. Take literally any other capstone, avoid this one at all costs.
Constantly showed up to lectures late, didn't seem like he cared or wanted to teach. Good luck trying to get ahold of him. Would avoid him.

Quite literally the worst professor I've ever had at UW. He encouraged the use of AI to build games, emphasizing quantity over quality, and then would proceed to mock students for random bugs in their generated games. Ridiculed games for being uninventive, but didn't bother to invest any time into teach us how to make inventive games. Don't take.
Just avoid.

I want to preface by saying that Popovic is clearly very knowledgeable in and passionate about his field.

However, he does not seem to be very interested in teaching. He will get to class late and leave as soon as it is finished, and has no patience for "incorrect" answers/questions in class. I mostly learned from the TAs and external textbooks.

In case someone needs to hear this, it's not the worst thing to take a class with Zoran. If you're interested in the subject, you will enjoy the project content and appreciate some of his tangents in lecture. If you don't have the bandwidth to deal with Zoran being late or leading unorganized, questionably relevant lectures, then avoid.
Never reply to students questions on Edstem.

This course offers 0 additional resources. His lectures are disorganized and he relies on 5 minute youtube videos to teach. Besides those little videos, the rest of lecture is just disorganized and random whiteboard notes. There's no text to read or further help you can get. I had to drop this class because of how inaccessible and ableist it was.

It is currently 8 days past grades due for quarter, he has not done them and only earlier today the TAs finally got any response from him. The only info they are able to relay to students at this time is "He will probably do the grades soon". During the quarter we had to use slides from prev quarters because his were incomplete and uploaded late.

He never even bothered to post the lectures online. He was constantly late to lecture. Still haven't received a grade for the course despite the fact that all the assignments were graded over a week ago and final grades were due a couple of days ago. TL;DR: Zoran Popovic fails to do even the bare minimum.

Easily the worst professor I have ever had. Zoran gives rude, inane advice and comments while everyone looks at him with tired eyes and annoyed breaths. One example of this was telling another group that they had the worst data that he has ever seen. He was also one month late to give us grades, giving us zero communication during this. Avoid.
Great experience
Kind and responsive

So far, I have had an amazing experience in BIO A 101: Human Biological Diversity: Sports, Movement, and Activity! This class teaches you so much about the human body and why we function the way that we do. Abigail is extremely helpful and passionate about the topic. If you take this class with Professor Kramer, take Abigail's quiz section.

One of the most interesting classes I've taken at Washington. she clearly knows her material-- if you ask her a question she will give extremely detailed and helpful responses. There is a book for the class, but you can get by without it. She very clearly WANTS her students to pass, so if you're struggling, ask for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Swann is a wonderful professor. She truly cares about her students and is clearly very knowledgeable about what she teaches. I'm an English major, so I struggled a bit initially, and she was so helpful and patient. I highly recommend going to her office hours; I found them to be very beneficial, especially for the problem sets.

Professor Swann was an awesome teacher. I took her ATM. S. 111 class and loved all of it! Her exams are very straight forward and as long as you study the slides, go to lecture, and pay attention in class, you'll be fine. The only thing that I didn't like was that homework was worth %25 of your grade, so that brought my grade down a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This course is pretty easy, but she asks way too many clicker-type questions that are worth whopping 20% of your grade. Then again, intro classes seem to cater to those who at least showed upShe gives about 20 seconds to answer for some questions and passes onto the next one, indicating some of them aren't even thought-provoking/discussion-worthy.

I only leave a review to counter the bad one. This class is super easy, the textbook was a waste of money for me (I only read about 5 chapters), and Dr. Swann is excellent at replying to questions and clarifying during lecture. If you're looking for an easy and clear NW credit with interesting information, I recommend this class.

Overall, it's a good class and Abby is clearly knowledgeable. Wasn't too stressful as long as you're okay at writing essays on time and did the homework. The HW is pretty easy, and any mistakes can basically be erased with extra credit. Lots of extra credit if you go to class.
Really passionate lectures and clear instructions. Her slide is easy to understand and got extra credit opportunities. (Although I took ECON 435 but did not find in "select course code"

Abby is a great teacher! Her slides are easy to understand and she moves at an easy-to-understand pace. Amount of work is totally reasonable. I went to all the lectures and only studied for a few hours before the midterms and was able to do well. Her fun personality makes lectures more engaging, especially for an econ class.

Abby is so sweet and quirky! She genuinely wants everyone to succeed. Attendance was mandatory but her lectures arent the worst and she had us do activities. Way easier than the large lecture version imo. She only had us write one paper and do simple homework like four times. Make sure you study, and her office hours are super helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment:
The greatest art professor at UW if you really want to improve. Many art professors feel a need to say something kind about each piece and skirt around real criticism. Zhi does not do this. However, by not doing this, you truly understand what you need to do to improve your drawing skills.

Work outside of class hours is needed to finish projects.

Zhi Lin is a great knowledgeable instructor. He is a little tough in his advice and criticism but I can tell it is tough love (I have experience). His teaching is what made me move faster with my drawing process. Heavily recommend his class if you want to seriously improve your drawing skills. The main bad thing is that he is "appointment only".

This professor is very tough; he's hard on participation, and you have to put a lot of effort into class. It's a bit stressful, and he can be very critical. However, he is extremely skilled and a great teacher, and he can also be extremely funny and thoughtful. If you give him your absolute best, you'll come out of the class learning a lot!

He is very direct and harsh in his feedback, but if you can handle it then his classes are super helpful. He really cares about his students and their success, and when grading he factors in improvement over time. He isn't critiquing *you* just your art, and if that kind of tough love works for you then Zhi is perfect, I've learned a lot from him.

If you want to be pushed to improve your art skills, I highly recommend Zhi's classes! He can be abrasive, but he cares a lot about your success. As long as you make an effort to incorporate his critiques and ask clarifying questions if his feedback is confusing, he'll recognize that effort. Definitely not a walk in the park, but so worth it!

Zhi focuses on hands on learning. The lectures and demos are short. His critiques of your work can sometimes be frustrating, but it's clear that he's just being honest and is pushing you to improve. Zhi cracks jokes and is overall easygoing and caring. He's challenging but fun, and you will improve your drawing skills significantly.
Need to work very hard in order to get good grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Lin appears quite hardcore but he genuinely cares about how much you learn. I still remember him saying something like "Learning is painful" lol don't be intimidated! There are lots of homework, but by the end of the quarter, you'll have a large portfolio (which is great for an art student). He's very professional, devoted, and funny!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Bad experience. He brags, is rude and abrasive, heavy on criticism and light on advice with the advice given being very cryptic. Due dates are unpredictable, irregular and at times unannounced. He says that he's a rebel. I learned these drawing concepts at SCC for half the price. I'm not learning anything at UW, which is the most upsetting.

TOOK DURING EFS i think the ratings are low because he can be blunt about your work and sometimes makes jokes at your expense (i promise, he means no harm). it can be pretty difficult but you're allowed to re-turn in everything at the end for a better score and it's important to show improvement. lectures are boring but attend for critiques!!

Zhi doesn't try to spare your feelings during critiques and is intimidating until you get to know him but your work will grow hugely in his class. He's also very supportive and funny outside of the classroom, and will go out of his way to help you and grow your art if you ask for it. He expects you to work hard and seriously in his classes.

Seeing Zhi's relatively low rating on here was discouraging at first, but I realized pretty quickly that he doesn't deserve it. Yes, he's a bit blunt and intense sometimes, but you'll learn a lot from him and if you work hard he'll respect you. He really cares about his students and is really fun to talk with once you get to know him.
Consistently goes like 15-25 minutes over class time every single day
super disrespectful to students :/

People are super harsh on the ratings. He is very strict but he genuinely cares about both the work and you as a student. Can be frustrating at first but if you stick with it and listen to the content of his critiques you'll see serious improvement. Can't wait to work with him again.

Very confusing, disorganized, and disrespectful. He is verbally abusive to his students and gives awful feedback that is often very confusing. Also extremely sexist towards the women in the class. Lots of work to earn a semi-decent grade. Says he's tough for a reason but there's a line - and he crossed it. Didn't hand out course evaluations either.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Lin provides nothing but pernicious, shallow "critiques." He makes fun of students' artwork and says it isn't good enough without properly providing feedback on how to move forward and improve. Don't take this class if you are just looking for VLPA credit. I'd recommend a different professor if you are in the major.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Probably the hardest professor in the art department. He is intimidating, strict, harsh, and blunt, but also hilarious at times and truly wants you to do your best at art. He'll make you work harder than you ever have in your life and will push you to your limit, but you will improve so drastically and will reward your hard work in your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Student's attitude toward the course matters the most. If you want to learn, to improve yourself and reach your potential, then this porfessor's course is absolutely worth taken-you will learn a lot by the end of the quarter as you follow his instruction. On the other hand, if you want merely VLPA credit, this might not be the best choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Inspiring artist, great teacher, makes you work for it. You'll get better if you show up and work hard.
he gives very useful critique, and you will learn a lot in his class!

Malicious, verbally abusive, no worthy art educator conducts themselves in such a manner. Do not take his class, you will learn some concepts just like you would any art class where the teacher puts effort, but it's not worth it and there are much better resources and classes out there

He is a great artist, but not a great professor because he  is racist. I don't understand why he is so rude to Chinese students but he is also a Chinese! He would be a lot nicer to native students. I understand that he might have personal issues with racism, but having prejudice against students shouldn't allow him to be a teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Tough grader, high expectations, learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Zhi is awesome. He definitely makes you work for your grade but helps you significantly along the way. He may come off as blunt, even rude, but he is genuinely a very kind man who wants you to succeed and become a better artist. Try to look past the intimidating exterior and take in his advice/critiques. He will certainly make you a better artist.

Zhi is one of the best art professions I've ever encountered. He is very strict so don't expect to lay back in his class. He will make you work hard and harder for a better level of art production. The progress after one quarter is significant. He is the only professor teaching figure painting. You are lucky to have him. I promise!
DO NOT EVER TAKE HIS CLASS!!! He was very strict and has discrimination on colored nations!!!
Really good professor, very funny during lecture and tries his best to help you.

If you are able to take critiques and know how to not be affected by words, you will like this class. Deeply, Zhi is a very nice person. He is very experienced in this field. Be sure to work really hard. Three hours per assignment is considered not lot of time. It can be from 4-15 hours.
I enjoyed this class, homework load was not too extreme, spent around an hour a day. I thougth Zhi was pretty funny with his sassy humor and what not.

Should not be teaching basically. However, if you decide to take this class, make friends fast. Don't miss any days. Seriously. He will change things on purpose for the skippers. Don't expect him to email you back for anything period.

To take advantage of what this fantastic teacher has to offer you'll need take your work very seriously yet be able to laugh at yourself at the same time. This professor rewards hard work but continues to push you further, simple as that. I came in with very limited skills and improved greatly under his tutelage. Highly recommended.

If you are prepared, you would learn a lot in this class. To be honest I didn't enjoyed this class, the teacher is harsh and has his own way of doing things. But he did teach a lot of stuff that is very useful.
Take him with the sense of humor and work very hard and you will improve significantly.

If you can't deal with this teacher, consider dropping out of art school. Did you decide to be an art major because you thought it would be easy?? He pushes you to do your very best work, and good luck for your boring life if you think doing anything less than that will cut it. Give me a break!!

Fun class for those who like strict guidelines to art.He critiques brutal and mean until you draw/paint what he wants, but then grades easy if he likes it.A good class for those who think they might want to major in art, but not for those just looking for some VLPA credits. Be prepared to spend $300+ on art supplies (he says it'll only be 100 max)

Although he is a good artist, go to his art work on the web, and a lot to offer, he takes the opportunity to be arrogant and verbally abusive to a captive audience, the students.  A real chip on his shoulder.  The language barrier in an acoustically poor room doesn't help.  He shouldn't be teaching.
Do not take this class unless you want to listen to pointless lectures, spend hours working and redoing assignments, and spend a TON of money on supplies like several hundred dollars.

I wasn't a fan. His lectures seem aimless and contradict themselves, the personal 'help' he provides is even more baffling and contradictory ("don't draw a square!! a square is like a shark in a cup of ramen!! do it like this:" *draws a square*), and he will openly laugh at a student who's asking for guidance. AVOID.

Go to class, don't get offended and talk to the TA's and other students and you'll be alright. He has high expectations and brutal critiques, but his grading is more lenient than he lets on. His english is very difficult to understand and his suggestions for improvement are vague and unhelpful. He's brutal, but truly wants you to learn and improve.
One word: AVOID

He is too strict. If you don't want to be miserable, then DON"T take his class EVER!! Like, I would spend about 5 hours a day on my artwork, and then next day, he would tell a lot of students to re-do all the work. It took me so much time, and it was taking over my time away from other class so I had to drop out.

He is really demanding and critical of his students.  But this is only because he takes his role as a teacher very seriously, and he wants everyone to improve.  He is not afraid to point out your weak areas or to embarrass you.  He doesn't play favorites, and if you put a lot of work into something, he'll notice.

Prepare to get your self-esteem destroyed because this teacher doesn't hold back. He will let you know everything that is wrong with your art and you must fix it or else. But the flip side is you will improve greatly. He is a great teacher. Has a hardcore belief on art foundations. He knows what he is talking about and he wants to see you improve.
Harsh personality, super picky, encouraged exact replication of techniques, discouraged experimentation. Learned in this class, but didn't enjoy it. Clearly made nude models uncomfortable.

I found Zhi to be an amazing professor and I learned a lot!  He helped me make it through my senior exhibition class and had a great sense of humor.  He is critical but wants to help you.  You have to have a tough skin and have some fun while you take these classes.  I appreciate everything he taught me and would recommend him to all art students!

Oh you thought you could draw? Well this class will****you. And afterwards you will be better because of it. Its all about tough love. Youll hate him, hell hate you, but good things will be produced and youll notice it when you are done. Highly advised.
Excellent professor, very able to teach you how to draw technically well. He can be very critical but you WILL learn so much
His class is a lot of hard work and tough critiques but everyone in the class made a lot of improvement. He's hard to understand sometimes but the TA's were very helpful.
great teacher, harsh at times. weird sense of humor too.   if you can't take criticism, you shouldn't be an art major. take zhi's class if you can.

Awesome class!  Zhi's critiquing style combines extreme seriousness with a fantastic sense of humor.  He shows his students by example how to be self critical and critical of society.  On a technical level, Zhi is good at presenting anatomy.  All of the students in the class experienced rapid growth in their observational drawing skills.

Sometimes Zhi is just plain cruel! I can't say I didn't learn anything from him, but I dreaded showing up to class everyday. I wanted to cry on several occasions because of his mean teaching style, which consists of ridiculing and insulting your work. I LOVE art, but Zhi made me hate drawing. DON'T take a class from this teacher!

Yes Zhi is critical, but what's the use of taking a class if the teacher tells you you're great all the time and never tries to help you learn? Mediocrity is too often encouraged in the art world and Zhi is not someone who encourages mediocrity. Take his class! The most useful (if at times painful) painting class I've ever taken.

Even though out of all the professors it seems he cares the most whether or not you learn, but the way he makes sure you're improving can have the opposite result a lot of times because he can make many hours of work sound worthless!  shouldn't diligence count as a merit when you're in an academic class?  he's known for having made students cry so just don't take what he says toooooo personally :(
Mean!!!  Don't take him if you don't have to.  He'll straight up tell you your no good and heck... if I was "that" good, I wouldn't have to take his class.  I'll be teaching him instead!!!
one of the hardest art teachers, but one of the most amazing artists in the world.  if you can survive the first week of class, you can learn amazing things from this man.  have a thick skin.
a dogmatic jerk with only one way of doing things--his way

Worth the challenge. Definitely the best prof I have taken in my moderately lengthy college career.  The instructor was very knowledgeable, fair, took great interest in whether the students learned or not, and gave very honest and educated responses.
Unclear grading and classes filled with irrelevant topics.
Unclear grading and classes filled with irrelevant topics

Still hasn't given final grades (class ended 7/23) and lectures are barely correlated with the cases. Make sure you have a good team and don't expect him to give much support
Attendance matters and active participatiok is required

Take his own advice and don't take this class with him. He has interesting insights but he genuinely takes this class so unnecessarily seriously. He never even released grades. I think teaching undergrads is not his calling and don't let this class be the last of your undergrad career because it'll leave a very bitter taste in your mouth.

Such a disappointment. I truly believe that Gupta does not enjoy teaching students. He relies solely on peer evaluations to grade so dont expect any helpful feedback. Grading policies are obscure and he is incredibly rude when you express any sort of concern. He will kill your drive to learn and make you regret signing up for this class.

Lectures are limited (1-2 hours a week max) and really ineffective. Course is very "quantity over quality" with unreasonable grading expectations. Professor has a passive aggressive attitude - course starting off each lecture with what we are doing wrong as students rather than accepting feedback for his ineffective teaching. Last&Worst class at UW

I also created an account just to state that Gupta's been my worst experience at Foster. This site has usually been good for telling if a prof is bad, so I felt blindsided by how much this class has sucked. Loads of time-consuming busy work combined with horrible grading policies. Hopefully more negative reviews come in to actively reflect reality.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've had. Spotty coverage of complex topics. Extraordinary work load/minimal time allotment. Grading has been a disaster. Policy says "good" grade is 2/4 or 2/3 and grades aren't curved. So a "good" performance gets a D or F? Says wont know grade until posted on MyUW at end of quarter. I created this account just to rate Gupta.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Avoid if you want quality, fair, and rational instructor. Professor Gupta appeared like a nice guy initially but soon demonstrated his inability and incompetency of being an instructor. Directly told students that he has no time to grade their work during peer reviews. Instructed students to avoid giving high scores which encouraged grade wrecking.

Overall a great human being, but not a good professor. His lectures are extremely boring, and he has a horrible time management skill. Gupta will spend more than four hours on a 2h50min class. He told us that we need to care about our time management and be in the classroom on time, which is hilarious, that he never did his time management well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The toughest part of capstone was that everyone was competing to get called on for their participation points. This made it intimidating to speak up at times. Besides that, Gupta really makes you think about how you can apply your previous coursework/knowledge to real corporate problems. He was also very friendly and helpful during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Worst professor in Foster. Doesn't care about students, harsh grader. He will wreck your grade for the case competition. Gives out two individual cases and you get 24 hours to analyze for each and expects 4000 words on it. Doesn't upload grades, lazy professor. I have warned you. DO NOT TAKE GUPTA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Instead of the stack-ranked CapSim, you do a group project that, albeit being a lot of work, prepares you better for the case comp. Gupta pushes students to think for themselves, so even if the first few days seem scary bc you're not used to participating in class, know that it's all for the best. The workload is manageable, but get a good team!!!

Capstone wasn't the nightmare I thought it would be and I think it's because I took it with Gupta. The guides he gives you for cases and projects are a little unclear but the work was manageable. For me, the most stress I encountered were from my teammates. PICK VERY WISELY.

Class time is discussion based 75%+ of the time on a reading from the coursepack (typically 12 pages). Aside from in class time, there are 2 individual case analysis assignments and 2 group projects. Be weary of finding a good group. Group projects are 50% of your final grade. No quizzes or exams, but there are 2 presentations and a few papers.

One of my favorite professors at Foster. Prof Gupta is engaging, funny, incredibly smart and personable. His class is discussion based, so participation is required but you can miss 4 classes and still get full credit. HIGHLY recommend him as you don't have to do the Capstone simulation and there is no busy work. I actually looked forward to class.

The professor made the projects accessible for everyone including students with no experience, some of the assignments early in the semester were too easy, but it got better. The lectures really open my mind and made me appreciate art and understand it better
Be ready to have to teach everything yourself! I never really felt respected during my time with Abed.

Cool guy, bad teacher. There were multiple projects in which students were told to "look up a youtube tutorial". He's generally understanding if you don't have any prior art experience, but it is clear that he favors experienced student's work more. Absences and tardiness affects your grade. 3 absences is an auto fail.

This class was quite easy. You're required to do at least 18 hours of volunteer work for the entire quarter. The class had interesting elements to it but I didn't feel engaged. Some of the work in class is quite repetitive but easy to understand. Edmundo is a great and funny person but I didn't feel like I learned much when taking this course.

He tended to go on tangents that didn't make much sense for most of his lecture time. There were a lot of assignments that were all essentially asking the same thing, and I don't feel like I learned much.
took 280 this quarter, he had an amazing TA and brought a lot of interesting views and communities to light.

Was passionate about the topic, had great lecture guests that were also featured in the class content. Flexible with attendance but it's better to go in person. Option to do two credits for an extra project that wasn't too difficult.

Eddie is super kind and caring, you could tell he is in teaching for the right reasons. That being said the lectures always felt all over the place and a little awkward. I didn't really feel like I learned anything from being in class. Lots of writing assignments, which all were easy but felt never ending.

Took for EDUC 280. He is very kind and seems to be engaging, but a lot of his lectures were all over the place and he never seemed to finish in time. Lots of guest speakers. Spent most of my time on homework and volunteering
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr.Aguilar pretends like he cares about his students but he ignores them when they reach out for real help

The course content often seemed to lack engagement and was unorganized. Additionally, the professor appears to be late for class constantly. There may be opportunities to foster a warmer and more supportive classroom environment.

Professor Edmundo is by far my favorite professor! He doesn't believe in exams and believes in creativity and finding your own voice. He truly inspires his class to speak up and not be afraid to do so. Overall a professor that I recommend!

3 assignments: 2 essays and one PDF of a summary of each reading and lecture for every class. Don't know how much they are worth for the total grade. Lectures were interesting, but also hard to remain engaged. Prof knows a lot, but lecture can come across as rambling. Don't take if you aren't disciplined to pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is my second class from Mr. Abrams, and both experiences were excellent! Lectures are engaging and insightful. Graded based on two essays and a set of lecture summaries (1.5 pages per lecture). Abrams is very caring and fun to talk with after class. A few "rants" in class, but nothing that subtracted meaningfully from the class. Overall great!

Bruh, he loves to go on tangents so his lectures can be hard to follow. He has too high expectations for papers and has taken off points if he doesn't agree with your argument. Weirdly liked to mention my ethnicity a lot.

He loves to ramble and while sometimes his stories make you chuckle, his rants make it difficult to follow; he likes to drone on and on. A bit creepy ngl ... I overheard him mentioning how he looked up a student outside of class. He's passionate and well versed in what he does though. I wouldn't take him again if I had the choice. He's a bit boring
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor wants every student to to succeed. He's really passionate about the subject matter and it shows in his lectures. If you fall behind, he will help you catch up if you talk to him. The class was based on a long essay assignment (with drafts) and a final exam. This was ideal for me to space out homework and studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really liked this class. It wasn't the most exciting when it was taught online but Prof. Abrams is super knowledgable and is clearly very passionate about the subject. If you like reading, then I would recommend this class.

If you get the chance to take an American Lit class with Prof. Abrams, DO IT. His insight into the texts is thought-provoking and makes so much sense, and he's supportive of and excited by new ideas from students. He was incredibly lenient with the online class (recorded everything and extended essay due dates). Very knowledgeable and a fair grader

Class time is all lecture with a small group lecture after. He can be hard to follow and I couldn't really tell when his sentences started and stopped, but the lectures are recorded. Two essays and an open book final for work. Strongly suggest reading the texts carefully because some are pretty dense but important for the papers. Chill guy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took his class WI' 20. Class format is a lecture for 1 hour, 10 min. break, then discussion for remaining class time. Solid lectures/course material, but a bit hard to listen to his long lectures straight. He did record them & allow for a lot of flexibility in assignment deadlines. Grades were decided by two papers and an exam. Overall solid guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Abrams was absolutely the highlight of Zoom class. He's super old school but clearly an expert in his field and great lecturer. Truly cares for his students and super easy to talk to. Syllabus and assignments were extremely accommodating. A wholesome, bushy-bearded, east-coast accented joy to talk Melville with. Unexpected gem of my time at UW!

I took Abrams 352 class. One of the best teachers I've ever had. It was over zoom too and he still managed to make me connect with him and want to work hard for his class. Above all, professor Abrams is a truly kind soul and he really does care about his students. At the end of the day, you can't ask for much more from a teacher.
The English 281 online class was 6 total essays including the final. The reading is helpful but not needed. Great feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He knows so much about American Lit, and it's easy to understand and learn from his lectures. He's also pretty funny and understanding. I've recommended him to other English majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Intelligent and passionate professor, fair grader, funny, and an original thinker. Highly recommend.

He is obviously well versed in American Literature, but the class in almost entirely lecture based and offers little room for student engagement If you like discussion based learning (as I do) stay as far away from this course as possible... He lectures and you listen The only benefit: he is a fair grader and will take time to listen to essay ideas
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very passionate and intelligent professor.  An original thinker and a genuine person.  It is not a hard class as long as you put in the normal effort.  He cares about his students and you'll learn a lot from his lectures.

Took him for a grad seminar years ago. Terrible. Just terrible. Self-absorbed, arrogant, completely unhelpful. Dropped the seminar just before the deadline, thankfully. I use the experience now as a cautionary tale of how not to teach and/or interact with my own students.

Fantastic professor.  Definitely not easy, but really seems to care about the students and spends a lot of time explaining the material if you put forth the effort to ask questions and listen to his advice.

Very smart and well educated in his field and it's obvious he cares as to whether or not his students are learning. As long as you go to class and pay attention and follow the readings, his classes are challenging but very doable and enriching. Talking and commenting on readings is very beneficial! Really enjoyed his class!
One of the best teachers I've ever had. Genuine, funny, ties things together in weird ways. His tangents are actually relevant to the course material. Positive-minded and cares about his students

This Professor has a very set idea on what he likes and what is correct. On a few occasions, he even interrupted a student mid sentence b/cuz he did not agree and although attendance is not mandatory, he is very aware of who comes to class and who doesn't --gives death glares often. Smart guy but I would never take lectures from him again. NEVER!

Very genuine person, cares about his student's writing. Lectures offer great insight to write a successful paper, which he is more than fair in grading. Overall, a passionate prof, I def recommend for anyone. Non-english majors should not hesitate to take higher level English classes.

Big marxist/feminist/critical theorist/afram atudies/anthropology approach to American lit. Great sense of humor, and was always very nice to me, but less patient with those who chose to do no reading all quarter. Highly recommended - very inspiring.

Best professor I have had at UW. Abrams knows the material and enjoys his work. His lectures are a balanced and critical analysis the literature, not about himself and not espousements of personal political or other viewpoints like some other professors. Easy to get an A if you show up, are genuinely interested, and put some effort into the work.
He's facinating and insightful. Got me into the English major even though I only read 2 of the, like, 7 novels we had to read.
He went off on so many tangents it was hard to focus on material.
Really intelligent and interesting teacher.  I enjoyed nearly all of the reading even when I though I wouldn't. Sometimes strange, definitely, but never in a negative sort of way... I recommend him.

I agree with the third comment about Prof. Abrams being the unusually good about handling divergence viewpoints.  He is funny, a great lecturer, and infuses his subject matter with a lot of passion and relevancy.  One of the very best professors I've known.
Nice guy.  He's a little weird, though.

I took his english intermediate expository writing class online and loved it. I found it interesting and nicely paced. I did not find the work load overwhelming at all and I found his comments very helpful for improving my writing. I would highly recommend him.
best professor at UW; handles diverse opinions with dexterity and expertise
No Comments
He's ornery, but great.  He knows his stuff and gives entertaining lectures.
Frequently complains about his job and the institution.
No Comments

Nidhi was an approachable, energetic, and kind professor. Attendance is "mandatory" because you do activities in class for participation, but it is up to you if you care about those single-point assignments. The only other assignments were group project-based, so that was the bulk of the work. Tests were based on the lecture slides.

she's really nice but her lectures can get boring sometimes. however, go to class to get all the class participation/assignment points. one thing is that her instructions (esp on the group proj) can be vague and unclear so make sure to ask her. would def rec taking w Martha instead.

She's incredibly nice and genuinely cares about her students' well-being. Every class, we had a worksheet that served as our participation grade, which was always done in groups. No midterm and final, instead we had two concept checks throughout the term and it was all mcq, fairly easy.

She was such a sweet professor! Every class had an easy participation element but a lot of it was groupwork where only 1 person in the group had to turn the assignment in. Make sure you have a good group for this class because you have group conversations a lot! But this class was easy, all multiple choice midterm and final.

She's super sweet and bubbly and cares that her students are engaged and learning. Group project instructions can be confusing at times due to ambiguity, recommend talking in person for help. Overall an easy class if you come to lecture and study the slides.

Nidhi is a very kind professor but not necessarily the best. Lectures felt super boring and useless and her exams were fairly difficult because of all the concepts and many of them sound or are worded similarly. We also did a group project for the class where we're consultants for a local company that I felt unprepared for. No final and got a 3.0.

Nidhi is super nice and really caring. But holy moly did she make the class boring. It was just 2 hours of lecture every class and I did not learn a single thing. Just memorized some stuff and passed. If you want an easy A, take her class, if you actually want to learn stuff... find someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nidhi is probably the kindest woman I have ever met. She is such a great professor and LOVES her students. I had her during online classes due to covid and she was always super understanding and willing to extend deadlines if needed. Class is primarily based on fairly easy discussion posts and a group project, midterm and final weren't bad either
Very knowledgeable and seems like a nice guy, lectures can be difficult to stay focused on however

While the class content was pretty interesting, Prof Agol's unenthused voice made it difficult to stay awake sometimes. The work is generally very straightforward. I used a lot of quizlets online to study, and barely used the textbook at all except when the online homework directly cited when it would be useful.

Professor Agol is nice, if a little shy. He will help students who reach out to him. Lectures are mostly clear, but also kind of boring (it doesn't help that class is 80 minutes long), but you don't really need to go to them because he posts slides w his markings online. I hardly felt the need to use the textbook, I wish I'd just torrented a copy.
The class is pretty straight forward; I'd recommend studying for testsquizzes, but they're not impossibly hard. Eric is a great guy, but his lectures are very dry.
difficult to stay awake during lecture. but he is super nice and flexible.
Boring lecture. Don't take when this guy's teaching Astr323.
Fun class with awesome materials. Nice person, but grading (in absolute scale, not curve) makes this class very difficult. Take astr323 when Gelco(Zeljko) is teaching.
Nice guy and incredibly flexible. He seems kind of shy but he is really willing to help students out of his own time. I really enjoyed his class.
Funny guy, I recall he included some 'Periodic table of dessert' for an intro to astronomy class once. Still don't recall how it's relevant but A for humor
Great professor. Very knowledgeable, but sometimes too knowledgeable that his explanation could make you even more confused.

Has a quirky sense of humor that is great in the middle of a lecture. Just an all-around awesome guy!! Class is simple, and still really cool. Simple math skills for the exams, otherwise, not much effort required and his slides are the reason to go to lecture, if you don't find astronomy interesting, that is. (Im a CSE major)
Great teacher!  Very understanding and wants everyone to learn.

Jameel Saab is an amazing teacher. I've never learned a language so quick as I did Urdu. His guidance makes the difficult concepts easy to learn without being overwhelming. Through this class I developed a love and interest for Urdu. Truly a wonderful class and Professor.

Best professor at UW. I love Jameel Saab and hope everyone interested in Urdu takes it with him!

He is compassionate and calm and most importantly very good at teaching Urdu. His knowledge and passion in the subject is extremely admirable, he truly cares about Urdu. He is also available outside of class and is flexible if things come up.

Probably my favorite teacher here at UW. Incorporated history into his lectures which I deeply appreciate and made learning a new language an exciting experience. This is coming from someone who couldn't read or write Urdu script at all and spoke it like a plebian. Very wholesome and caring, overall 11/10 experience.
Jameel sahab is my favorite professor at UW. He makes classes fun, interesting, and low key. I wish I could take his classes forever.
Participate the class and finish the homework carefully, then you get a good grade. If not, vice versa.

He is really good at teaching. I felt the course was very light for a 5 credit class. Readings, essays, short stories, all very easy as long as you follow what they want. Don't hesitate to him questions too.
Jameel Saab is fantastic! He's an easy grader as well. If you want a GPA booster... take this class. Very fun!

I love prof. Khalid so much, I'm in 102 right now and already dreading moving onto the 200 level without him. He is so funny and jolly and going to Arabic is easily the best part of my day. Khalid is very accessible through email and office hours and if you put in effort into his class, he's more than willing to help you succeed.

He makes Arabic feel simple. So kind, funny, and believes in all of our abilities. He made me laugh at 9am pretty much every lecture. Daily homework but takes no longer than 15-30 min. Most quizzes/tests are online, and he preps you so well you won't feel too challenged. Put in the hours outside of class to really master the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Starting a new language is intimidating, but Prof Ahmed is so fun and a really good educator. There's definitely a lot of assignments and work that goes into this class but it's manageable. He's always willing to help and does his best to make things clear and stress-free. Assignments come with feedback and you can resubmit for full credit.

In the begging he was nice. However, he began to be rude and petty with some students and even hard to communicate with, in and outside of class. I am happy to never take his classes ever again. He lets his emotions get in the way of teaching this class professionally and honestly. 0/10. Other than the professor, I learned a lot and was fairly easy

This man is a literal angel. I took 101-3 with him and have never loved a prof more. I was having a really rough year, and he was the reason I was guaranteed to smile at least once daily. I could not imagine learning Arabic without him, and am sad that I'll have to go on doing so. Do yourself a favor and take anything he teaches!!!

Khalid is the absolute best end of discussion. He's such a jolly man and genuinely made Arabic fun at 9:30 in the morning every day. Love him and miss him to this day. Hope nothing ever bad ever happens to him ever!

Khalid genuinely cares about your progression through the Arabic language when you are willing to participate. He is more than willing to provide extra help and makes the lessons easily digestible. I went through the entire 100 level series with him, all it takes for a good grade is attendance in lecture and effort. He is the best ever.

Khalid is a great Professor, currently taking him right now and he's very thorough, knows what he's talking about, and gives feedback. The other reviews on him I read did not match what I saw in class. The only thing is attendance is apart of grades but it is language class so makes sense. Overall a great professor

I took Arabic 101, 102, and 103  series with Khalid, he is a nice professor who cares about the students and what he is teaching and is very passionate. I would have him as a professor again. Participation matters a lot in the class FYI be prepared for that, he is very accommodating as long as you communicate beforehand. 10/10 Class and Professor.

This class was so refreshing to show up to. Khalid is a joy to be around. He just wants to share his knowledge and make students as enthusiastic about Arabic and Arab culture as he is. No tests and very few assignments that it seemed like you automatically get 100% on for turning in.

he's a really nice prof and makes the class fun and engaging. learning a new langauge is difficult but if you put in the effort and keep up with class, ull get a 4.0. highly recommend for the whole series!
HE IS TH EBEST PROFESSOR I TOOK THIS YEAR IM TELLING YOU TAKE HIM WHILE YOUR EYES ARE SHUT NO DOUBT! TM WALLAH

I took this class for credit and let me just say this man is horrible. I don't even consider him a professor because of the LACK of care he has for his students. He seemed nice at first but once he shows his true colors throughout the year he is rude. He teaches the class terribly and will make you feel so bad about any life struggles. JUST DONT.

Taking Arabic with Khalid has been so much fun-- he is very funny, approachable and makes learning a new language feel not so overwhelming. He does assign quite a bit of homework, but most of it is graded on completion or not graded at all. It's obvious that he wants his students to succeed and is always happy to help.

Take this class if you want to put in the effort. A lot depends on how willing you are to work in groups for practice. Can be a lot of homework at times but its manageable. grades a lot on effort. Khalid is an incredible teacher who genuinely cares about his students. Makes jokes, is always smiling and telling us to take care, drink water, etc.

Khalid gives around 5 quizzes and 3 tests. Homework is due everyday and he never gives feedback so don't expect to know what you're doing wrong. He knowns his stuff, but doesn't teach it well. wish the near east dept would replace this prof...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Khalid doesn't seem to care much about his students and personally took the fun out of arabic for me. If I didn't need his class to get my minor, I wouldn't be interested in continuing. I'm disappointed that he took something I loved and made it into a chore...

Khalid is an amazing Arabic professor. He teaches you the patterns and underlying structure of Arabic, rather than just emphasizing memorization. I would say the class is not too difficult, but you need to have an actual interest in the language to succeed--otherwise it will really show in your grade! Take his class if you want to learn a lot!

The best Arabic teacher ever! If you follow classes and do your homeworks, you will learn a lot and get a good grade. He is very helpful. The class is very well structured, grading criteria is super clear.

Khalid is an awesome teacher. I've had him for two consecutive years now, and the improvement in my Arabic has been incredible. Be warned- Arabic is an extremely difficult language for a non-native speaker to learn, particularly native English speakers, so if you're looking to get a good grade without genuinely caring about the language, you won't.

Hard lectures, tough grader and dosn't seem to care much about his students. Lots of work and preparation. We started as a big class, but many students dropped, including myself . I really wanted to declare Arabic as my minor but after one quarter with Khalid, I decided to drop it. It's hard not to be motivated.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Khalid's an excellent teacher, however be prepared for a very work intensive class. Participation is 10-15% of your grade so showing up to class is a must.

hes a great teacher, his lectures are very clear. makes jokes in class here and there. i wouldn't consider the class hard if you attend class and ask questions you don't understand and he'll  take the time to go over it step by step. tests aren't that hard if you do homework and readings, which aren't bad.

Khalid is the best Arabic professor I have ever had. He is so nice and really wants his students to do well. Second year Arabic is way easier than first year. If you do the homework and go to class you will be fine.

Gives decent lectures and explains concepts well, but his lecture slides aren't great and the canvas page is terribly organized. The grading weighting is also not great, like an in-class canvas quiz got the same percentage as a final project that we were given weeks on. All in all, not bad for 424.

About one quiz per week, two tests, three field projects, and two software labs were present. Each field project had a few labs. Eight homework assignments were due throughout the quarter. The deadlines for the quizzes were before the end of the lectures. I recommend opening the quizzes before the lectures start, so you can start them quickly.

Content of this course isn't hard but the prof makes it as hard as he can. All lectures are is him reading off badly-made slides that are a struggle to understand/sit through. No actual exam review material given. All content is reused every year, test answers are locked so you never know what you did wrong. No guidance at all for GIS/AutoCAD labs.
doesn't explain how to use any software/programs so you just have to mess around with stuff or look it up in order to do half the homeworks. nothing is explained clearly. nice guy though

He reads off old slides and reviewing the slides outside of class is difficult, so pay attention in lecture! He doesn't give us any information about what will be on the exam until the day before, so there is little to no time to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kamal has a great way of implimenting required attendance with quizzes but also making it enjoyable.  His lectures are fun and thoughtful.

Kamal is super funny and makes the lectures lively. He also is understanding and helpful.  If you are someone who attends lectures and wants to work hard while acquiring skills this is your professor!

Professor Kamal is a great professor. If you are attentive, go to lectures, and focus on the material you will succeed. He is very quick to respond to emails and has excellent availability for office hours. I have taken Kamal for two classes and both have been great. I highly recommend Kamal!

Puts no effort into lectures, has little patience, acts like he's never at fault despite the (sometimes prevelant) errors he makes. The course is easy, he makes it hard. I've taken many classes with harder material but a competent and hard-working professor can often breach this gap; making for a better learning experience. Kamal is a contradiction

Kamal is lowkey hilarious. He has taught this class for like 20 years and is a little stuck in his ways, loves a good PowerPoint transition animation. He asks constantly for feedback, although I'm not sure how much he actually listens to it. He always talks like he is really strict, but when asked he will extend deadlines and be nice.

This professor's job is to teach, and not to educate. He gives tests to students but don't tell them what they got wrong because he wants to reuse them next quarter. He also has been using his slides for years and there are still abundance of errors. Also he likes to ask questions on the slide and don't post the answers anywhere. Overall a nightmar

Generally a very interesting and experienced professor. There's a huge emphasis on group work that makes the class really fun. The only negative was that his class was generally kind of disorganized and the lectures could get really dull by the end of the year.
Lost a lot of weight this quarter!

I am and always have been a horrible tester but he is very clear on what will be on his exams which is helpful. Exam questions are very similar to homework problems, so if you do well on homework and actually understand what you are doing, you will do just fine in his classes. Great professor for both Geosurveying and construction engineering.
Great guy, very helpful, very clear, stellar all-around teacher.
Great teacher! Funny and nice. Don't by textbook for his class... his package is good enough
Very good teacher.  Would recommend to anyone who can take his class. and yes he is a straight BOSS.
Had him for surveying and construction. Great guy with really good explanations. Very helpful and approachable. Also, he is a huge boss.
Good teacher, but curriculum was a bit dry at times.  Still, his courses offered plenty of hands-on experience, which wasn't available in many other courses.
No Comments
No Comments

Pretty good prof, makes jokes, gives one minute breaks when he feels like people are falling asleep (which happens a few times a week).  HW completely managable, tests kind of tricky only because you have to remember a lot of specific info.  Has great course packs w/ all the lecture slides.
I shouldn't have favorites but professor Sama is the best professor I've ever had.

Although this was Sama's first quarter teaching the course, his deep passion for teaching is evident during class. Lectures feel more like conversations between him and the students, and he makes an effort to learn your name if you participate by showing up and raising your hand. I highly recommend him for any of his courses, especially Psych 300.

While he is super engaging and hilarious in his lectures, he's not very accommodating if you have any disabilities or hardships. He is difficult to reach outside of class and lectures are not recorded. The syllabus is not clear either, the course is very quiz reliant, and he doesn't really communicate what weeks will have a quiz or not.

The best! Super discussion heavy lectures where participation is very much encouraged, but Sama creates a very warm and welcoming environment where talking in class feels easy. Super kind and easy but thoughtful class where insightful learning is more important that quizzes.

Great human being, one of if not the most engaging course that I've ever been apart of. Professor Ahmed finds every way to make the course as engaging as possible. He completely designed our class based around what we wanted and made the content incredibly interesting. Highly recommend!

Professor Mal is so enthusiastic and encouraging. I always enjoy their lectures. They are very knowledgeable and passionate; they really seem to want their students to understand and succeed. I struggle with understanding a lot of the content in Mal's classes, but I take them anyways because their teaching makes it so enjoyable. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was very confusing for me, but Professor Ahern kept me invested in the coursework! I could tell that they were very passionate about the subject matter and were available to answer questions in person or online at all times. She explained things thoughtfully and thoroughly, taking extra consideration and respect for her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Easy enough class and Mal is super entertaining. Workload isn't too heavy, and you don't need to do the readings to do well. Quizzes are weekly but she tells you exactly what to study and they're pretty easy. Final and midterm the questions are posted beforehand too so it's also easy to prepare.

Lectures can be a bit boring sometimes, but they are informative for quizzes and tests. Try not to skip the class too much, as the lecture slides she provides would be useless without the context of the lecture. She is a really nice professor, but grading and email reply times can be frustrating. Be ready to take notes and review them before class.

I took this class for A&H credits as it was open for all majors. This class requires a lot of time commitment however, which feels very taxing as a commuter especially since it was a morning class. Weekly memorization quizzes in person first thing in the morning, along with a handwritten multiparagraph essay for both midterm and final was tedious.

In the middle of the quarter I was taking this class in, I got into a car crash and ended up losing my mother and Professor Ahern was so incredibly kind and empathetic. She made sure it was clear that my health and grief was a much higher priority than her class. She checked in on me multiple times and i'll forever appreciate and recommend her!

Weekly in-person quizzes, a midterm, AND a final for arts and humanities credit. The professor is incredibly unorganized, and you are required to memorize specific years of events that aren't related to the topic (like years of the Civil War and the railway construction) and be tested on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Easy weekly quizzes, uses presentation slides for lectures. She's nice too. Unfortunately, she sounds like she has no idea what she's teaching about. She spent lots of time teaching us about the nervous system and wars in a CMS class. Incredibly unorganized in her lectures and slides. Very frustrating. She tries to make class fun though.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mal is a very nice, engaging, funny, and overall good professor. She really explains her lectures in great detail and makes them more interesting to learn. Would recommend it if you see her teaching a class.

This was such a fun class! Mal really works to make sure her lectures are engaging, and it shows. She really cares about the class material and how her students interact/learn from it. One of the most interesting, fun, and creatively-challenging classes I've ever taken.
I use the knowledge of this class all the time. I want to talk to Mal all the time.

Mal teaches with a lot of passion, wit, and humor. Her lectures are very well-organized and leave you reflecting on the content afterwards. She often highlights exemplary student writing responses to promote discussion. The assignments in the class were really fun, and the grading was very reasonable! I couldn't recommend her more :)

Mal is really passionate and informed about what she teaches. So nice and supportive. The class is set up in a organized way that makes the assignments easy to understand. If you do what you need to do, you will do fine in the class but it helps if you're actually interested in the topic. It will be a great class if you are. I recommend this prof!
Focused on your learning.
Very knowledgeable and cares about his students learning. Goes over topics well and is invested into what he teaches.

Ashfaq cares about student success without a doubt. He is extremely accommodating and will make sure grades aren't a worry. But his execution of section can be poorly paced sometimes and convoluted at its worst. His sections would certainly benefit from more structure and a more concerted effort to gauge student interests and questions.

Incredibly kind and open to all student's opinions (very patient). Extremely knowledgeable and is always open to questions, and always provides a detailed explanation when answering students. Sometimes it's difficult to follow what he's saying, but if you pay attention you'll learn a lot.

Great lecturer who tries hard to accommodate questions. Uses real-world examples from India and surrounding regions often while discussing topics, especially on populism. Super crazy looking blackboard notes, think red string map. Depending on the class's engagement, quiz section can be a delight. I look forward to them, but I do participate often.

Ashfaq was a really great TA. He went deeper into the topics from the book and lectures and he is a great source of deeper insight into important ideas. He is a very good person and he genuinely cares about his students and their success. Don't be afraid to go to him for help. He is super smart and I feel lucky to have had him to enlighten me.

Ashfaq was a very kind and passionate teacher. He expanded on concepts in multiple different ways to help students who were confused. He was very excited about student questions and ideas and incorporated them into the lectures. I felt confident in his knowledge. I would take a class with him again and would recommend!

Ashfaq is extremely knowledgeable and he is very helpful when talk with him about specific questions after class. Come prepared to his classes with the readings completed and ready for discussion. Participating actively in discussions is how you make the most out of his classes.

Ashfaq is one of the most understanding TAs I've had during my time at UW. He is incredibly helpful in guiding students through course readings and texts, offering insights that clearly connect the course topics with the required textbooks. As long as you attend the discussion sections and actively participate, you should do well in this class.
I advise no one to take any course from him. No coherence in teaching. I didn't learn anything. Utter waste of time.

Ahn is the best!!! If you actually show that you're trying and that design is a passion of yours, he will help you and support you. Try and make connections with him, he will help/give you tips on how to get internships and jobs. He is such a caring professor, hard to find ones like him here at UW.

Prof Ahn is an incredible instructor. While communication can occasionally be a challenge, his expertise in drawing, CAD, and ID is truly unmatched. His passion shows through in every lecture and critique. Before graduating from UW ID, I highly recommend taking at least 1 of his classes, I promise-you won't find a professor who is as knowledgeable.

Incredible instructor. Was hesitant to take his class after reading reviews, but I'm glad I did. He's an exceptionally talented designer, and I am privileged to have learned from him. While the class was definitely intense/challenging, it taught me a lot abt design and the professional field. Prof. Ahn is not only funny but also genuinely caring.

Awful grader, an awful teacher, simply did not teach the class. It's required for the major so you have to take it, so prepare to not enjoy ten weeks with him. You learn maybe one or two things about drawing and the rest if not helpful. If you are already good at drawing you will be fine. Everyone else I wish the best of luck.

Worst professor I've ever had. Could've learned the same amount from a YouTube video. Consistently weeks behind on grading but also gives ZERO feedback on any assignments. Assignments are long and tedious and final (50% of your grade) uses none of the skills learned in class. If you're reading this you probably have to take him. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ahn's funny and cares about students but has high expectations. The amount of work makes you improve because you're always drawing but it pushes you over the edge along with other classes. Try to build a relationship with him, so he knows you care. Naturally talented drawings are the ones who succeed in the class, not the ones who improve the most.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

ahn is a dedicated and talented professor but has a different approach to teaching which can sometimes be frustrating. he was supportive and dedicated to his students but communication was difficult, and his expectations and requirements were unclear, and very high.

It can be tricky to communicate, but you get the hang of it. He is otherwise a great teacher and excellent designer. He has been been at the building after midnight on a Friday night to help students from our class. He cares as long as you do. BTW, who wants an easy design class or professor?
Ahn is hard to understand at first, but he grows on you. He genuinely cares about students success and preparing them to actually get a job when they graduate. He is great.

Ahn is really difficult to understand despite his 13 or so years in the States now. question is...

Hours worth of lectures to watch with often 2 discussions and 2 quizzes to complete every week. Way too much work for a 3 credit class, I spent more time on this course than any of my 5 credit courses this quarter. Wouldn't recommend taking unless you're minoring or majoring in RE

Not a hard class for 480 if you have Shannon. Get the homework done once a week and you'll be fine. It is pretty easy and will set you up to apply for jobs. I recommend doing it sophomore or junior year if you're looking for an internship.

Shannon is one of my favorite professors at UW, caring towards his students. 480 was set up with only 1 assignment a week; a 500 word essay due every Sunday night. The class was insightful and I feel like I learned a lot from Shannon that will help me in my career.

super easy class. Every week, read the chapter, do hw/sb, and discussion which are all easy. Midterms and final take questions directly from the HW. Shannon is a-mazing!! Sometimes we would start our Zooms by jamming out to his fav songs. He had a mid-quarter survey and he actually listened to students and made the workload a little less. Don't freaking understand her English!��

reviews.comment: The class wasnt an easy A per se, but its definitely possible to get a high grade if you put in a fair effort. Lectures are kind of dense and its super obvious they are reading off of a script. Some of the assignments felt like busywork but overall the class wasnt bad.
Super nice teacher, easy to get an A if you genuinely try but you cant breeze by very easily, have to pay attention to detail

The online class was structured really well with asynchronous learning, and all the class modules were really easy to navigate. Lectures were super important for the quizzes, and readings not so much.

midterms are super hard and i cannot understand her at all. heavily accented. would not recommend taking her class unless you like writing pages and pages of stuff that was way harder than what was done in class on your midterms and finals

The professor should take a survey about the knowledge level of the students. She teaches like everyone knows everything. No methodology. No proper flow. 
No sense about topic selection.

People who know the subject, should opt for this professor , just to revise and practice. else if you want to learn, then NO!!

As a student in Mashhadi's class, I was disappointed with her teaching approach. While lectures are dry and can be avoided by just reading the slides (unless you've got questions to ask), I always found Afra to be helpful when I had any issues. No extra credit opportunity, Teaches like a robot, doesn't have passion for teaching at all, lectures are boring, feels like she doesn't know subject herself, copies from the book, surprise final exams which are taken straight from leetcode .

Afra Mashhadi is a TERRIBLE teacher if you can even call what she does teaching! She doesn't teach anything related to her assignments. reviews.comment: Light assigned reading every week, consistently interesting lectures, some more light assigned reading, straightforward test expectations with good study guides, even more light assigned reading, the occasional short and easy essay, and some optional supplemental reading. Lectures pretty much based on reading materials and it's such a heavy reading for a 3 credit 200 level class. Take her class if you want to see what below a 2.5 on your transcript looks like without having to take a STEM class.

Afra Mashhadi is the worst instructor I have had in my entire life. For her class, if you want to score high it really depends on luck. Pray to god if you are taking her class

3 homework assignments, over 300 pages of reading, 2 midterms and 1 final. Test grades average around 60 / 100. The test questions are made by TAs who pride themselves on difficult questions. Nice, but her class was hard to understand as far as grading and expectations.
