Found this class relatively easy. His lectures made me sleepy. Concepts are fairly easy so you can learn from textbook and hw. The 2 midterms are reasonable and easy if you do the hw and study a bit. Make sure to get 100% on the quizzes as there is no partial credit for the problems. HW was mostly from textbook. Lab depends on your group and TA.

Homework and midterms are moderately difficult, professor just goes over the textbook examples. My TA was terrible, so that didn't help either. I worked so hard in this class only to be killed by the final which was mostly on material that we very briefly covered in the last lecture...  Okay professor, difficult final exam.

Class size was around 20 people so his teaching style might change during the regular school year. He was a pretty good, never was confused on material went over in lecture, tests are alright. One of those professors that like to put a "thinking" problem on each test that messes a lot of people up. Homeworks mildly difficult. Study for his class.

Class is relatively easy other than the fact that lectures are 2 hours +. Prof is really passionate about the subject and knowledgeable about the topics. Class uses textbook that is on Canvas so it's free, there are three exams but one gets dropped. Overall, really good class that was fun, but it's a history class so it's long.

Genuinely one of the best professors I've had so far, super easy grader, and is passionate about the subject. There are 2 tests, and he drops the lowest grade for one of your tests. a lot of the credit is based on in-class video watching worksheets, so participation matters

He brought pizza, salad, and cookies for the last class too!

Very thorough lectures, you can tell that Barry is extremely experienced and puts time and effort into his teaching. Open note tests and clear grading. If you show up and participate you’re golden. He’s pretty funny and entertaining too.
Great class long lectures and then film every class. Really cool down to earth guy. Open book tests multiple choice.
hard test

Barry is a solid professor. He provides the entire class with all of the notes you could possibly need, which you can just copy down. He encourages textbook, worksheet, and note use during all exams. intro to construction management.. yet taught like its a level 500 class. the grading scale makes it impossible to 4.0. Barry writes the hardest test questions and doesn't even review or make study guides for his ambiguous exams. Probably the worst professor at UW. STAY AWAY.

Class was great in professor's Aamezcua's class. She tries to make everyone participate in class and generally cares about the students. Passionate and engaging. A professor you can not help but listen too.

Someone who's truly meant to teach. Participation/attendance is counted, but I found myself wanting to come to class each time because his lectures are interesting and his passion for the material is contagious. Will totally be taking more classes with him in the future if I can.

Dr. Wirsing is truly a god among men. I'm 4 years into my degree and he's the best professor I've ever had. Friendly, available, perfect Canvas layout, recorded lectures, balanced workload, clear rubrics. His experiences in research are both educational and incredibly inspiring. Also his vocabulary is massive, bring a dictionary to lecture.

Aaron is a great professor, and he's got so many cool ecology examples he's worked on to talk about during lectures! It's hard to be bored in lectures, and discussion sections will really depend on how talkative your classmates are.

Aaron is a great teacher! He has basically done everything ever and has a vast wealth of knowledge. You'll benefit from speaking up in class. Tests are straightforward, based almost completely on the lecture slides. Just come to class and you'll do well!

Lectures run long or into multiple days, labs are more lecture with little student input. Tests are 75% of the grade and 25% is attendance labeled as "participation". Waste of time unless you need a class to nap through. Discussions are an extra 90 minutes of him lecturing without any useful information. Lectures offer little other than review from 100/200 level courses. Shares his opinion and rambles on with stories that aren't useful and wastes your time.

Good luck ever getting him to reply or meet with you.

reviews.comment: Amazing prof and I love how engaging the lectures are! Loved hearing his personal experiences and many stories. I enjoyed how passionate he is about his work and if I have the opportunity I would love to take another class with him.
Engaging lecturer; not much new material from a college-level bio, but an enjoyable class regardless. Has me considering a wildlife biology ESRM concentration

Hands down the easiest class at UW. Have been thinking about majoring in ESRM after taking this. Lectures can be a bit repetitive, but he had good examples to explain everything and showed videos and whatnot. His enthusiasm for his field and research is awesome. Section and section work was easy and interesting, too.

Dr. Wirsing is my favorite professor I've had! Wildlife isn't even my focus, but I continue taking his classes as his clear communication, approachable nature, and deep knowledge and enthusiasm for wildlife biology/ecology have kept me coming back. He is well-articulated and great at answering questions. Has done super interesting research as well!

Good professor and I enjoyed his lectures. Did both 350 and 450 and 350 is mainly a review of stuff learned in biology classes, but 450 is where new topics start to pop up. Make sure to review lecture slides, especially any graphs or figures that appear.

Make sure to study lecture slides and watch the recorded lectures because they will come up on tests. I wasn't a huge fan of Professor Wirsing's lectures (sorry). I found them to be mostly review of concepts I had already learned in intro bio classes and other ESRM courses.

Very knowledgeable and has a lot of interesting field experience!
Took attendance through writing questions on notecards every day. He's very enthusiastic and answers questions well. 
Definitely study the lecture slides, there's a few tests that aren't hard if you understand the concepts

Prof is the best teacher I've had at UW. His concepts on wildlife and the systems and environments involved are so insightful and fascinating. Lectures are easy to understand. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are fun. There are discussion boards & short readings to do every week. A couple of other assignments too, but theyre easy & not time consuming. reviews.comment: Before taking the class I read all of the previous reviews and they were all positive but also led me to believe the class would be an easy A. Work hard on the big group project, it will be worth it to get full pts

reviews.comment: Tests are worth a lot in this class, and they can be challenging so be prepared. But Professor Wirsing is so passionate and knowledgeable about the class content. He has incredible stories and connections from working in the field. Very engaging in lecture, and he really values questions and student input.

Professor Wirsing is the best professor I have had at UW. He is knowledgeable and enthusiastic and really sparks an interest in wildlife and wildlife ecology. I wish he taught more classes! ESRM 350 and 450 were interesting every single day, and I looked forward to going to class. Definitely take a class with him if you get the chance!

Aaron's great.  There's no textbook so you have to show up because all exams are based entirely off of lecture.  But if you take half way decent notes then you shouldn't have a problem.  Will be taking ESRM 450 with him because his teaching style is so great.

Great professor! The material is interesting and he's a very engaging and enthusiastic lecturer, and is always responsive to student questions/feedback. Definitely a must if you are interested in wildlife! Assigned work is very reasonable- reading and discussing a paper every week, then writing one at the end of the quarter. Not hard to do well.

This class isn't super easy, but it isn't terribly difficult either if you go to class, pay attention and stay ahead on the final paper. He grades fairly, knows his wildlife and has tons of case studies to explain the core concepts.

Easy 1 NW credit. He invited a lot of researchers around the world to show you their researches every monday through the seminar. Most topics are pretty interesting and easy-to-follow even if you don't know anything about environmental science. I'll recommend this course if you want a NW credit.
really easy professor
Great professor! Easy non-cumulative tests. Very happy with his enthusiasm and he is always willing to clarify himself and help students out.

never encountered such a abysmal professor in all my 14+ years of education experience. Flint is pretty chill and has a really good sense of humor. I learned a lot from this class, mainly from the assigned readings.
Flint is awesome!!! I really like his personality. The class is super chill!

He cares a lot about each student and just wants everyone to succeed! Always excited to teach and very down to Earth!

reviews.comment: He is very nice and friendly professor. I recommended coming to class every day because it will help you to write your paper.

ENGL 200 with him was a super interesting class, and it was pretty clear on what to do to get a 4.0. Essay extensions were always easy to get, and he graded easier than my high school english teachers. No tests, 3 major papers, extra credit at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is by far the most work I have ever had to do for an english class. On the first day aaron said he "rarely gives out 4.0" which is the understatement of the year. You have to put so much effort into his class to get an okay grade because he is a very tough grader. I actually think he's jealous of people succeeding in this class
Very easy grader as long as you show up to class and do the readings. Also always gives extensions. All you have to do is ask.
Ottinger was a sweetheart, was easy to connect with as he worked to connect with us. Amazing teaching style and 10/10 the best professor I've had.
Aaron was a great professor. He helped us understand the material learned, helped us with our writing, and was a fair grader. Every class plan was made to make sure we were doing well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

He's an expert in 18-19th century poems. Consider this before taking ENGL 111 class with him. Papers are very challenging and going to UW's CLUE Writing Center can help a lot.

His heart is in the right place, but his class was tedious and largely a waste of time. The topics weren't very good as a whole. For a portfolio that represents 70% of the grade, there was far too little feedback on the assignments.

Aaron is the best professor ive had at uw so far. He is funny and obviously knowledgeable about the subject he teaches. His specialty is british literature, so expect a bit of discussion on that even if it isnt your assigned text. Very forward thinker, tries to get students involved.
Aaron is one of the quirkiest professors I've ever had. His sense of humor is really dry but his lectures are interesting and he gives good feedback.

Really cool guy. I think he did a pretty good job teaching the fundamentals of college writing. He likes to connect other academic disciplines with English, such as philosophy and biology. He is a good instructor, a bit awkward, but nonetheless, he is very knowledgable concerning the his subject. He raise up very interesting questions and make amusing analysis.

This class was awesome. The topic my class received were interesting, abstract..but interesting. He is thoughtful, helpful and approachable.

Would not take another class with him simply because his topics were boring and very uninteresting in comparison to what my other friends were writing about.

Class/essay topics were not very interesting. Professor made the class worth while. He was really chill and down to earth and kind of funny. He talked about things that he did over the weekend on Mondays. Participation is 30% of your grade but you just have to say something once a week for the weeks points. I would take another class with him.
Very knowledgeable about subject matter.

I would say the above comment made was spot on. Prof Acikmese has a lot of experience. Lectures were full of useful and practical information, but the consistency in the notes and the varying math notation definitely made the class harder to follow. He does include reminders and (on occasion) summaries which are really nice.

Bechet seems to mean well and the topic was interesting, but aside from that his course was disorganized.  Lectures contained inconsistent notation and were error-prone.  Did not stick to one book but bounced around several sporadically and diverged from book notation.  On occasion tried to bring the point home.  Very few examples. Stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is very passionate and enthusiastic about medical anthropology. She tries to engage the class with materials learned in lecture or readings by doing different activities such as free-writes, small group discussion, and large group discussion. She genuinely cares about what students have to say about the course content/readings. Shes organized!

This teacher's teaching style is good but she expects a lot from students. You will learn a lot in class if you are serious, but if you think you can just pass without really trying and expect a good grade. You wont get it. She has high expectations and if you work hard you will do well and learn a ton about writing. being there is required.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I have taken this course and there is no denying it is kind of challenging because there is a lot of writing and she is a pretty tough grader, but i felt I am def. a stronger writer. I learned writing styles and how to analyze and research in Acquanda's class that I didn't in others.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I highly recommend NEVER taking this course with Acquanda. Her writing assignments rarely make any sense and she is an unreasonably tough grader. I had a terrible experience with this instructor and know a number of other students who felt the same way. If I could give a 0 I would.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She does not give clear idea of expectations, grades extremely poorly, and spends no in class time relating course content to the assignments. Do not take her class!

Papers have little to no direction and you must follow her writing style or points will be deducted. Overall one of the worst english classes I have taken at UW. She's more worried about making sure the students know she is a feminist and breast feeding activist than teaching how to properly write an essay. Unless you have to, do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is not very helpful at all in class. Assignments don't instruct very well at all. Will get on you for talking too loud with a classmate when doing a peer review with that person. Also knowing that she said its okay to talk. Overall just not a great professor with bad communication skills with her students. Also teds to miss class a lot.

Chethana's class is well-structured and has appropriate course load. You can get an A if you pay attention in class and follow guidelines. She has an intelligent+dry sense of humor that I found engaging in class. There is a lot of group work, but she is very liberal with grading those.

One of the best teachers I've had at UW. Lectures are very straight-forward and easy to follow, and she gives good explanations/examples of concepts. Very easy grader, and tests are extremely fair, with no dumb or confusing trick/"gotcha" questions. Also does efficient in-class review before exams. I didn't even buy the textbook and I was fine
She is articulate and a good teacher. Is accessible outside class and helps understand course materials.
Unorganized, assumed class was about environment, it was about atmosphere. if you like science and are an introvert hes your guy, otherwise beware
He's really nice and really fun and really good at explaining stuff.  class was awesome and interesting.

Ackerman is an awesome guy. May be a little intimidating at first, but really a good guy all around. Go to the extra credit he offers, it will really boost your grade. Overall, class was easy but you need to put in a little effort.

Not very concerned about students, but a pretty interesting speaker most of the time. The class wasn't terribley difficult for me, and I really hate the sciences, but you definately need to study.  No mult choice tests so you have to know your stuff and explain it fully.

Professor Aaraund is a great teacher. I really enjoyed this class! We did some fun class projects. The only downside is there was so much reading. Two small response papers, one 4-5 page essay, and art project final. Not a difficult class if you keep up with reading.

She was soooooooo amazing!! She isn't just a teacher, she's like a mother or even a best friend! Great instructions & great teacher! Would love to see her around more often, very busy lady since she goes to both campuses (UWB & UWS) but great feedback! :)
She is seriously one of the best professors I've had. You can tell what she teaches is something that actually interests her. Its not a lot of work but the work you do, do is totally worth it!

Rebecca Aanerud is one of the most wise and fabulous teachers I have ever had.  She is inspiring and I took every class I could from her.  I learned so much from her and her classes have forever changed me for the better.  She has a powerful and quiet way of bringing everyone into the dialog and a patience with learning and a desire to reach you.

I lament having to give Dr. Aanerud a good rating, because the content of her course was absolute drivel. She was quite dry and steered the course in the direction of her own research, in that she made a class on philosophy all about women's takes on spirituality. I'd say don't take GWSS 206 unless you want it to be staggeringly boring and easy.

Dr Aanerud was a great professor. She makes the class very interesting whether or not you have a prior interest in GWSS. She's very helpful, the class is definitely an easy class. I never studied for the midterm or the final and got a 96% on the midterm and a 100% on the final. Just go to class and you'll be set.
Her lectures are very helpful, but a bit boring. You need to read the textbooks to do well on the quizzes, though not so much on the tests. She doesn't grade on a curve.

Prof. Aanerud is one of the most engaging professors I've had at UW. She makes lecture so fun and you can tell she's passionate about what she teaches. Prof. Aanerud really cares about whether her students are learning or not. The textbook really only comes in handy for sections, in which there are weekly quizzes on reading.

Becky is a wonderful teacher, who makes all of her classes fun and interesting. You can tell that she really loves what she does, and wants everyone to learn and be excited about the material. Looking forward to taking more classes with her!

Wonderful teacher, extremely helpful and encourages true and critical learning. Women's studies really changes your life. Learned so much in this course, loved talking to her everyday & loved the questions she raised in class. Highly recommended!!

Dr. Aanerud is awesome. Her lectures are interesting and worth going to. My only complaint about the class was my TA. The Friday sections are mandatory, making it hard to avoid wasting that time. The exams are easy, however the written assignments are graded on a "how you improved" scale which was rather ambiguous. But overall a great class!

The books are expensive for how often I used them. I didn't open my textbooks once for the last half of the quarter (after the midterm) and I didn't read the novel and I passed the final with a ninety. If you go to lecture she goes over the ideas behind the reading anyways. She shares personal stories that relate to material which was helpful.
One of the sweetest ladies I have ever met. Extremely helpful and fun! Tests are easy and if you attend lecture, youll get a good grade.

I have taken two classes (intro to women studies and phil of fem) from Aanerud and she is always helpful and wants the students to gain something from the course load. She is super friendly and approachable.

I had her my first quarter at UW. She has been my best teacher and I am about to graduate so I have taken my fair share of classes. She really cares about her students and is an excellent teacher. I was not looking forward to the class but I really enjoyed it! I would take it with her again without hesitation.
Pretty good teacher. I'd take a class with her again if I was interested in women's studies.
Aanerud was a wonderful professor to have because she really got me interested in the topics she was teaching. She was also funny, passionate, and helpful.

She assigned the textbooks that she was the author of (which were very expensive at $45 and $75 a piece for relatively thin paperback books) and then changed the edition right after the quarter was over. Seems to me like a convenient way to gouge her students because we had no choice but to buy the books.
Wasn't even that interested in the topic of Women Studies when I first took the class but was really blown away by her passion and knowledge about the subject matter!

Highly recommend this class! She was very passionate about the topic and clearly cared about how much the students were learning. I talked to her once outside of lecture and she's just an amazing person. It was a huge class but I was never bored and I never felt removed from what she was talking about.

She is a great professor! Lectures are never boring, sections are interesting and the tests are very manageable. She relates a lot of the topics to her own life, which made her really down to earth. I would recommend taking any of her classes
no comment

She is one of the most amazing professors I've ever had! She made this class amazimg. And she does everything she can to make sure you pass. Just go to class, do the work, participate, and you have an easy A and a class that will change the way you look at everything.
She's just great!
Nice professor. She goes a little bit too fast with the powerpoint, but overall, interesting class.
Very excellent teacher!

Prof Aanerud is very helpful and interesting.  Go to lectures because they will help a lot on the exams.  This class will make you take another look at the world around you seeing how different factors (ex. gender) plays in role.  Great class

Easy class, though the grading system is a little ambiguous.  Lots of reading, and lots of pretty dense texts, but the lectures cover a lot of what is needed for the quizzes. Dr. Aanerud really tried to make everyone in class happy, which I thought actually might have hurt the class a little, because it wasn't structured enough, but a good class!
She really knows her stuff!  I learned a lot.  It was a little weird how she tried to tailor the class to make everyone happy.  I expected her to be a little more hard nosed.
I basically want to be Rebecca when I grow up.  Class is pretty hard and reading heavy, but you will actually want to try.

prof. Aanerud is such an amazing profesor. Her lecture is well organized and teaching style is effective. Her senior level course is very well structured and all the readings assigned really make me think deeper on intersectionality of race, gender, class, sexual orientation,etc. I am super sad this quarter has ended because i admire her so much!
great teacher and really easy too! dont really need to attend class but it was a very interesting lecture

At first I took this class for credit but I started to enjoy it. I learned a lot of interesting things, some of which infuriated me (learning about how unequal the world actually is). Dr. Aanerud is a really good teacher, and always answers emails promptly. Her T.A.s however, in my opinion, need more practice learning how to grade.
Really interesting materials, great films, awesome lectures, but she did talk quickly, and note-taking was difficult and frustrating.

Professor Aanerud is an awesome professor! Her enthusiasm in the subject really showed when she taught the class, and it is because of all that she has experienced that she is able to teach the way she does. Her tests are really not that hard, just attend lecture and she'll basically tell you what's on the exams (1 midterm, 1 final). Life changing!
Great prof, very nice and understanding...do the readings, and take good notes and you'll be fine. She has been my favorite prof at UW so far, and I only wish I could find more classes like this one!

skipped half of the lectures, but still ended with a 3.8. class was very easy and enjoyable. i've learned the most out of this class then i have out of any of my other classes at UW. this class gave me life lessons, no lie. this is coming from a dude.
She recently won a teaching award!  She is great, interesting, and very caring.  Recommended!

She is amazing--this class has a wide range of topics, but each unit was packed with interesting information. She is an amazing lecturer, and reminds students to relate course topics to real life, which is especially important within this department.
Great teacher.  Really nice and caring.  Very interesting class and she has good lectures.  Recommended!!!!

She was an awesome teacher. She knew what she was doing, she's funny, and makes sure everyone understands. If you go to her office hours, she will put in double the effort to make sure you get the test score you want.  If shes teaching, then u should definately take the class!!!!

The class has an obvious liberal-slant but even speaking as man, the class was enjoyable as I learned about race and gender through a different perspective. The class is pretty easy, you probably can afford to miss a few lectures and not do all the assigned readings and still get a high grade (above a 3.5).
She is awesome. She really knows what she is talking about and she makes the class really interesting.
LOVED THIS CLASS. highly recommand! very interesting. you come out with new perspectives!
Great teacher, easy class, tests were easy, final was not accumulative. Interesting, would recommend to anyone looking for an easy, entertaining class.
Clear and concise. Makes the class interesting. Not you typical women's class: discussing issues focused on gender, sexuality, race, and class.

A word of caution before taking this class: be prepared for a large amount of course reading. While course text is generally not visited during lecture, you should definately do the reading. This course comes with the option of service learning or a larger amount of paper writting. Service learning, while rewarding, is a large time commitment.

A word of caution before taking this class: be prepared for a large amount of course reading. While course text is generally not visited during lecture, you should definately do the reading. This course comes with the option of service learning or a larger amount of paper writting. Service learning, while rewarding, is a large time commitment.

WOMEN 200 is a great class. Interesting and easy to understand. If you at least skim the readings and go to class/have notes from class always, you will be fine. Couple of essays, but they were easy and graded easy too. Perfect class to take with ENGL 198 for W/C credit!!!! Do both!

Becky is by far the best teacher I have ever had. She is a perfect role model and has a fantastic sense of humor. Not only has this class taught me about how women have struggled in the past and still do now, but I also learned a lot about myself in the process. This is one of the most useful classes I have ever taken, thanks especially to Becky.

Engaging. Wonderful. There is so much to say about this class. It changed my perspectives and Aanerud is definitely dedicated to the source material, she really cares about what she is teaching. However, most of all she cares about the students. <3

The class was very interesting.  I took it because no other classes fit into my schedule but it ended up being my favorite.  She does a wonderful job at incorparating aspects of race and class into studying gender.
GOOD

while women 200 is a big lecture, i had the pleasure of speaking with becky one on one in a quiz section and she is very dedicated and conerned with her students and their progress in her course.  i enjoyed this class and would definitely take another from her given the opportunity. be sure to do the reading for midterms.
I loved her and her class. I wish I could take it all the time.
Very cool
great teacher, really welcoming and assuring of her students, my class of 170 felt like 15.

Good basic introduction, but substandard lectures. Fact checking would be handy. And in a social science course given foundation by statistics, some viable ones would improve her credibility drastically.
shes the best! I really enjoyed her class and lectures, and she really makes class enjoyable and interesting.

He isn't a bad professor, just don't think this is an easy class. It's a lot of content to memorize and apply. There's no homework so the only things that count are quiz sections and tests. The tests can be hard, not a lot of practice material for the exams. Overall I didn't expect the class to be that much.

The class is alright if you make sure to show up to lectures and quiz sections. His practice exams are mostly irrelevant because he switches up the contents of the class often. He is nice but a not personable.
Pretty enjoyable class if you watch the lectures and pay attention. He is nice and accommodating to students, and very knowledgable.
Review lecture notes and concepts, then it's easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Leaché's lectures were straightforward. Anything on the lecture powerpoint is fair game, including tables. Class is boring at times, but memorize the lecture slides and pay some attention in class and you'll get a good grade. Quiz sections don't require much effort either. I would recommend BIOL354, specifically with Leaché.

He's a really good lecturer and has a good sense of humor. Be sure to be on top of your reading because he does random call-outs and you want to be prepared. The tests are tough, you HAVE to know your stuff inside and out because the grading is really strict and you have to get everything exactly right in order to get a good score.

He's very passionate about biology, which is really refreshing to see. Nice guy overall, makes a lot of jokes. Tests are difficult; rote memorization will sink you if you don't comprehend the concept. Clicker questions can be tricky, but he is pretty fair overall. Awesome lecturer, and I will take him again if I get the opportunity

Fast talker, but clear in expectations and good at giving specific examples in class. Go to class! Has clicker questions and calls on people, even in a 600+ lecture. Test questions are pretty tough because he requires you to understand, not memorize. Great for a 180 teacher.

Leache was an awesome professor. He was very clear and often a little funny, which is hard to do in such a (boring?) class. He also checked in for understanding. Even though the tests and clicker questions were difficult, he was a good professor.

A great professor who explained things very well and did a good job organizing the class. He had a great sense of humor and really loved what he was lecturing about. Would recommend his class to anyone looking at biology.
Adam is a fantastic lecturer who will keep you engaged and awake in a large lecture hall. His tests were long but made sure students were thorough in learning the material.

Leache was a very effective professor. His passion and love for Biology was evident through his teaching and his lectures were always engaging and descriptive. His tests were difficult, but fair and he inspired students to learn. I would recommend him to anyone taking Biology at the UW.

He reads from his slides a lot, but his lectures were fairly interesting (especially compared Dr. Janneke Lambert who taught the 2nd part of the quarter). He seemed to care about whether the students learned. The only thing that really irked me was that he posted his notes 1 hr before class, so I'd have to run to Ode to print them between classes.
He's really enthusiastic about his teachings. His tests were a little too long, which made them difficult. Overall, though, I really liked him - going to office hours is super helpful!

Excellent professor! His lectures were very clear and lecture notes were very helpful. He is super enthusiastic about evolution and phylogenies, which helps keep the class interesting. Definitely try to take a class from you if you can!
I loved his lectures!!! He made the concepts so much easier and interesting. However, I do have to agree his tests were long for the time given.

Because of him, I was inspired to keep pursuing biol. His tests may be hard, but he's an absolute incredible professor, who wants the best for you. Although it may be hard, his enthusiasm for biol makes you want to learn. I think he's the best professor I've ever had at UW. His slides were clear & understandable, his method of teaching is amazing.
He's a pretty good professor, he has a good sense of humor, but his tests were a bit long. Overall I liked him.
He is a good professor that genuinely cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures are very clear, and his grading criteria are not strict.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Honestly, you'll start loving python. He actually tells you how to code. He will solve problems for you in-class and help you understand the basics of coding really well. He actually cares about students, will answer every doubt of yours.

For a program that markets itself as career-focused, this course missed the mark entirely. The quizzes and tests deliberately obscure and inaccessible, making it nearly impossible to demonstrate understanding as a bilingual student. This quarter has made me seriously reconsider staying enrolled in the MSIM program entirely. Such a waste of money.

This course provided zero value to my degree or career. The material was completely irrelevant to my career. The exams were deliberately obscure and inaccessible, making it nearly impossible to demonstrate actual understanding. This quarter has made me seriously reconsider staying enrolled in the MSIM program entirely.
Online summer class. Totally chill asynchronous, everything was set up ahead of time, so you could work at your own speed.
Super fun class!
Great class, too bad it was all online.
Fun class!  Too bad it was all online.
Solid all the was around.  Well built class, not overworked, and provided lots of feedback.
Best class I've had as an MSIM student
This was IMT 550 Don't know how to create a new class. Fun class, but required.  Lots of reading and cases and case write ups. Overall, pretty good time.
Fun class and professor.  The TA Carol was great as well.  Read, go to class, stop by office hours.  fairly easy class.  Moore has no agenda does not shove politics at you all day.
Required class, but easy. Just do the readings and show up to class. Prof. Moore knows info ethics. Not your typical prog lib prof.  Easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Study for the quizzes by looking over the ppts.  Read what is assigned and you will do fine.
Required but fun class.  More like a philosophy class than the typical info offering.  Cool dude
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Took Prof Moore last winter. It was a good class he is super funny at times.  Did not start the class with pronoun disclosures happy for that
Moore is funny. Lots of humorous stories and cases.  The obscure TV and movie references were the best.
Overall, great class and professor. Ethics?  I thought I would hate it but it ended up being fun.  Study the ppts.

A required ethics class for INFO majors?  In the end, it was good actually.  Prof. Moore is funny and he makes the material relevant to tech majors.  Use the ppts to study for the quizzes.  Loved the insane psychosurgery case.  Moore loves weird cases, but they made the class fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Adam's cool. Quizzes aren't bad, but I would recommend studying. Lectures were kind of boring but to be fair my experience with him was on Zoom last quarter due to UW failing to assign us a room.
He is probably one of the smartest professors I have had, he is very knowledgable in what he talks about, and i respect him a lot. the class is challenging at times but not awful

The class was a special topics class about the philosophical perspective on ethics related to "Technology, Freedom, and Justice." Dr. Moore is really knowledgeable and explained things well, but the quizzes and final were challenging. You can earn up to 5 bonus pts (the class is 100 pts) from quizzes. Very interesting class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great class and great professor. I am a tech Student and this was an ethics class. Nevertheless, it was good for steve and we had great discussions.
Very boring lecture and terrible slides. Quizzes are worth half of your overall score, and those quizzes are superrrr hard!!

Pretty interesting and sometimes funny lectures. Quizzes are all open book, open note, but can sometimes be tough. Term paper isn't that bad as long as you choose an article that you're interested in. Section is partly a debate class, though your debate ends up being pretty chill as long as you know what you're talking about.

Prof Moore is definitely a smart professor. Much of the quiz info can be found on his slides so reading isn't necessary, but some of the articles are really interesting and make you want to read them anyway.  The only "hard" part is the term paper, but even that is not so bad if you choose an article you're interested in.
Interesting Topics. 1 Page film diary each week. 4 test that are easy to pass if you study.
Moore is one of the smartest profs I have had here at UW
Prof. Moore was interesting and funny.  He made going to class fun.  We did too much in class group work.

He would always give some pretty interesting examples of philosophy with regards to how it can be applied. Class wasn't too bad, you end up studying off lecture notes instead of doing the reading. Exams were kinda tricky where, "all the answers were false and you get worried." Oh and the class wasn't curved so you have to work hard to that regard.

Interesting guy to listen to, the readings assigned are dry but luckily they aren't really necessary to read. Show up to lecture and sections and they do a great job of explaining the material. Good class

Prof Moore was funny and made the material easy to understand.  The readings -- posted on ecourse reserves -- were hard....but between the TAs and Prof Moore's pots/lectures it was not so bad.  I didn't think I would like philosophy and now I am thinking of taking more philosophy classes.

Class on the philosophical foundations of libertarianism.  Best class I have had at this university by far.  Finally a philosophy class where Rawls was not assumed to be the 'one true view.'  Prof Moore is the best

By far one of the best classes I have taken! Professor Moore is extremely helpful and interesting. The lectures are long but certainly go by because he knows what he is talking about and wants everyone else to enjoy it just as much!

This was a small class covering topics in information ethics.  This is Moore's area and it shows.  The class, lectures, cases, and discussion were all first rate.  Easily one of the best classes I have had at any university.
info ethics...lots of fun...great cases
info ethics class...great class.  I finally graduated...
nice class, clear lecture, great ppts...best of all...does not spin everything to a liberal view...
Great class and prof...the lectures were clear and interesting.  The TA's were Ok...  Can't wait to take another class with him.

He teaches with powerpoint presentations and posts them all on the class webpage, so going to class isn't crucial, but it still helps. His tests are fair, but be warned that he LOVES to use "none of the above" as answers to multiple choice questions. Overall, great professor.

"Well...uh...I uh...don't uh...really know what to write here....uh....and...uh..." Welcome to lecture with this man, painfully dry, never going anywhere, and infantile tests. When in doubt, answer "none of the above" and you'll do great. Great TA's though

Very easy and straightforward. All the powerpoints are published online, so you really don't have to go to class. The tests are mostly MC with a few short answers, and they're taken straight from the powerpoints. Subject matter is pretty interesting as well.

Really easy. you can get a 93% and still get a 3.9. His tests are straight from the power point slides so as long as you study those well, you'll do alright. Section  helped me a lot in terms of comprehension, his lectures can be a bit rushed and some of his examples don't quite make sense, but overall a decent professor.
Hes very clear and for the most part an interesting lecturer.
great class
Very interesting.
funny guy
Great teacher! Very nice and understanding!
Intersting and informative...
Great lecturer, but the class as a whole didn't go very deep into the philosophy.  Only skimmed through topics.
no complaints
Great prof!
One of the best professors I have had at UW.
Great Prof. -- great class

The class was hard because the readings were difficult but also because it challenged a lot of my thinking. I thought I understood queerness pretty well before but the class sort of exploded my ideas about it, which I actually liked. It wasn't hard to pass, and assignments were fun- final was a card game- but it really made me think.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Adeyemi's really funny, smart, and nice, but by her own admission we were reading graduate level texts by the third week of INTRO to queer studies. The class is way too advanced for an intro class, which led to a superficial understanding of complex topics and made me feel like I was trying to catch up constantly even though I wasn't behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I actually took her for GWSS274 but it won't give me that option.
She is amazing!! Her lectures were super engaging, she always answered questions thoughtfully, and her assignments were creative and intellectually stimulating. Would totally take a class from her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I'm not a GWSS major but they are my favorite professor. I lowkey had a crush on them too. They are so funny and charming and the class is so interesting despite having no interest in GWSS before

This professor understand students. She relates and understands how important mental health. 2 hour lectures are tough but you do get a short break in between. Kemi is open to question. The readings can be a little long but doing them helps you follow along in the lecture. Attendance was optional, but the lecture really is important for passing.

Very fun and interesting lectures. Barely any assignments, ones that you do get are interesting and not hard. The lectures aren't recorded but you don't need to go to them, although they are very good lectures and the time goes by quickly.
I loved Kemi, she is very wise and her lectures are amazing. The assignments we had to were very easy as well. Definitely recommend taking her especially in person.

GWSS 200 with Professor Adeyemi set the bar high during my first quarter at UW. She's sharp, passionate, and has a great (deadpan) sense of humor. She always was thoughtful when answering students' questions. Passing this class isn't hard, but investing in it will prove incredibly valuable.

I absolutely loved this class, mostly because of how amazing and engaging Professor Adeyemi was. I would recommend absolutely anything she teaches. No traditional exams and assignments mostly graded on completion meant that the class was easy, but you can get so much out of reading and participating in discussions with classmates-I learned so much!

Kemi is an incredible professor. This was the first ever GWSS class I took, and it was so good I decided to minor in it. There was quite a bit of reading, pretty dense but incredibly interesting. She's a wonderful lecturer, very passionate, kept me engaged for the full hour 50. Many small group discussions, too, cool to learn from my classmates.

An inspiration lecturer who is extremely passionate about what she is talking about, and is able to explain nuanced concepts of gender studies in digestible and funny ways. Assignments were graded on completion, and the final project was very simple. 4.0 class as long as you show up to lecture and section.

I loved this class! We had quite a few readings, but they aren't hard to read and they're enjoyable! The professor and TAs were all very good at teaching in my opinion. Professor Adeyemi was a funny and great lecturer! (btw the guest speaker came to destigmatize sex work, not to say what the other person claimed).

Professor Adyeyemi gives amazing lectures, and each TA gives about a week of lectures as well. However, the TAs are extremely knowledgable and experienced with lecturing. Each time I left class, I walked away knowing I genuinely learned something valuable. There is little homework and minimal effort required but you get what you put into the class.

Professor Adeyemi will be the most caring professor you will have at UW. She, along with all of her TA's, are incredibly respectful and encouraging. They allow for discussion on every topic and the lectures and quiz sections are worth attending.

Professor Adeyemi is one of the best professors Ive had at UW. Ive taken 3 of her classes and every single one has been amazing. There is a lot of reading but the readings are so worth it. She is extremely caring and passionate about the subject, which translates into her lectures. I would 100% recommend this class and professor to anyone.

Professor Adeyemi has been one of the most laid-back professors I have ever had. I don't know if its the nature of the class or that's what they're like in every class they teach but they had a couple assigned readings per week (but you only HAVE to read like two the whole quarter), and as long as you did the assignment you got full credit.

Dr. Adeyemi is phenomenal. There is no better class to practice close reading theories/concepts. Dont come to class (or even register for the class) if youre not prepared or plan to be present - itd be a shame if you were to skim over the course material because everything is thought out so intentionally that the class, itself, is an art piece.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I will always recommend to take Adeyemi if you really want to learn concepts and think. She is a tougher prof than other GWSS profs but you will learn so much! She is a reasonable grader but expects you to put in work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Adeyemi is probably one of the smartest prods I've dad the pleasure of having. She tries her best to help you understand something that doesn't make sense, but also relies on the class a lot for their opinions, as this was a seminar/discussion style class. She keeps it real and is passionate about what she's teaching. I would definitely rec!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: the best.

Dr. Adam is a very specific person; he is adorable and very knowledgeable. The course is a little disorganized but very interesting. His lectures can feel very long, but if you are willing to collaborate during class, it makes them much better. He is a little slow with technology but really tries his best for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Ok so the class wasn't that challenging, but it became harder because professor Drewnowski lectured for almost 2 hours in the most slow, tiresome and dull tone. He's so kind, but I couldn't even sit in class or attend lecture after the first week because I couldn't pay attention. The class was interesting itself, but the teaching was not good.
Good professor, fun class, learned a lot 👍

he's so funny???loved this nice old man

gave 6 "white paper" assignments with bullet points, double spaced, 12 pt. font, where you just answer questions relating to lecture without any citations or anything. says "don't overthink it", plus an extra credit paper!

the most work is in the group presentation, but follow the rubric and you'll be fine!

Adam is a great prof that knows everything about nutrition around the world. His lectures are long and can be boring, but are full of info, and bases his exams on them a lot. Papers require you to do research on a country, so be ready to spend a little time on them. 
Assignments: 1 group paper, 1 final paper, 1 mid-term, and 1 final exam.
Best professor I have had yet! His work and lectures are amazing, he is very intelligent and has a lot of wisdom to offer. I learned so much and would definitely suggest taking a class with Adam!

Class wasn't too easy or difficult. Assignments I did get high grades but what weighed down my grade were the quizzes and final exam. The questions were confusing and are on specific points of readings. Other than that I did learned a lot from this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He specifically designs his classes to be easy and with a reasonable workload! He's incredibly reasonable in the amount of workload and grading for the course. Definitely take him. Funny and reasonable (hard to get both in UW).

Interesting class materials. He also invites a lot of people to give fun guest lectures. Only 8 small quizzes given unannounced in class, so attendance is pretty important.  There are 4 writing assignment in total, and his TAs gives really good grades on them. I almost got all hundreds on them. Recommended!

Good lecturer, but I found his assignment requirements to be very confusing at times. However, it was a good class and I learned a lot! His pop quizzes are the 'minute quizzes' which are two questions long and quiz you on readings. There were 4 assignments overall, which were graded pretty easily.

NUTR classes with this guy are incredibly chill. You pretty much get 4 homework assignments (for the whole quarter!), 10 minute quizzes (which is usually 1-2 straightforward questions on lecture or reading. He's a funny, wise old owl type of professor. Highly recommend! Incredibly reasonable too which you don't see much at UW. You won't regret!
Fun credit/no credit seminar!

NUTR 411 didn't have any exams :0 ! Relatively easy short writing assignments and making infographics (use a website :P).  And easy like paragraph answer type short answers at the end of class.  He is a very good professor, knows his stuff and is pretty funny in a way ( I found him hilarious though). He doesn't try to be tricky at all etc.

There is so much leniency when it comes to attendance, assignments, extra credits, and exams. No question on the exam is unexpected. It is so hard to get a bad grade in this class unless you truly make an effort to fail.
Very entertaining lecturer that gives very reasonable amounts of work. I found the exams to be very easy if you show up and take notes during lecture and read the textbook.

Loved the professor; he was clear, and you could tell he really understood what he was teaching. The class itself was very note-heavy, not a fluff class. You'll want to actually read and take notes on the textbook and the lectures. Quizzes allowed one note card, but even then, you really had to understand the material. Regardless, I loved the class

He is absolutely amazing and you can tell he loves what he does and cares about his students. The content of his classes is very daunting and can be difficult, he explains things great. This class can be tough and require a lot, but he drops a lot of assignments. The biggest assignments are multiple-choice exams, but he gives detailed study guides.

Overall easy class and fair grading structure. However, the attendance aspect where he says he'll try to catch you out doing PollEv at home rubbed me the wrong way. Very blunt and abrasive as well, especially during exams or when asking questions during class. Obviously cares for cognitive psych, but not sure if that extends to his students.

If you are a traditional student, you'll be fine. But it's not very accommodating or easy for anyone with extenuating circumstances which makes the dude a little classicist. He's a nice dude but clearly come from privilege.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great teacher, kept classes fun, very clear on what your grade was on, transparent on grade logistics, exams are vocab-heavy, but as long as you study them there won't be any surprises. Overall a very nice and informative class! Also drops the lowest test grade (and for other categories), and there was a lot of wiggle room for your grade.

Dr. Andelin manages to simplify complex content in a way that anyone can understand, something very important for complex topics like neural communication. He is an incredibly engaging lecturer and prepares students extremely well for the exams. Couldn't recommend him more, he really made my Biopsych experience special!

Dr. Andelin's PSYCH 202 course was certainly more difficult than his PSYCH 101 class, but nonetheless, he was effective in connecting lecture concepts to the textbook readings. In every lecture, you could just tell he was passionate about what he was teaching and confident in students' retaining knowledge. Overall, a great person, and great teacher

Although this class is completely outside of my major, the way he taught it made it fun. The textbook and lectures were clear and had supplementary graphics. He also would show a lot of pictures of his dog, which was really cute. Lectures are fast paced, but he also has a decent amount of extra credit opportunities. Overall a good guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: PSYCH 101 is a very easy class (note sheet permitted so no need to memorize), but Dr. Andelin still makes it very fun and enjoyable

He's very knowledgeable about the coursework, and his lectures are engaging. He's very kind and would show us pictures of his dog at the beginning of class everyday which was adorable. Very good teacher who I highly reccomend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Your grade in this class is mainly decided by four exams, but he drops the lowest one and allows notecard use, so barely anyone takes the final. It is much easier to do the class like this. The textbook we used was lovely and his lectures were very good, but fast-paced. I would recommend him for sure. Very, very interesting material.

Professor Andelin is an amazing professor!! I was very nervous about taking Psych 202 because i'm not the biggest fan of bio, but I really enjoyed his class. Very upbeat, easy to talk to, loves his dog! He shows a pic of his dog at the start of the lecture everyday. 3 exams and the final is optional. Allowed a notecard on exams. Such a good guy.

Professor Andelin is for sure one of my favorite professor's I've ever had. Psych 202 was amazing! He gives very informative lectures and as long as you stay on top of the readings and assignments you're almost guaranteed to get a 4.0. He's super funny and so kind during office hours. Make sure to meet his dog Bodhi on the last day of class!
Such an enthusiastic lecturer! His dog Bode is so cute and lectures are interesting but move fast. Extra credit is chill and helps a lot. Lets you drop lowest exam grade!

Dr. Andelin is an amazing Psychology professor. His workload may be gigantic, but I believe it's all part of learning introductory psychology. His lectures are meaningful and complement the textbook, and are overall informative and worth it. Would 100% take his classes again, and his dog, Bodhi, is adorable.

One of the best professors I've had. He has a good choice of TA's who grade fast and good feedback. He explains really well and genuinely cares about his students. If you really pay attention, the class is easy and it's so interesting too as a psychology major. I'm really happy I went down this path, especially with Adrian Andelin
Great!  I am really enjoying the course!

I took Adrian for bio psych and he wasn't my favorite professor but this class made me love him as a teacher. Just keep up with the readings and go to class and take notes and you'll do good. Drops lowest exam scores

This course was super interesting and was one of the easiest psych classes I've taken at UW. There are a lot of terms and memorization for the exams but he allows you to make a notecard (front and back) to help with that. Dr. Andelin also provided an extra credit essay assignment for those wanting to boost their grade towards the end of the qtr.

Dr. Andelin is well organized and has clear grading criteria. I really enjoyed the flow of this class. I recommend doing the textbook reading prior to the lecture, as it makes more sense. He goes somewhat fast which I like, but without doing the readings before lecture it can be harder to absorb more in-depth info. No complaints, loved this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Andelin was an amazing lecturer and kept the class extremely engaged. His midterms were extremely easy, as long as you studied the content and took notes in quiz section. Also, the reviews before the midterm were very helpful. Overall, I highly recommend taking his courses.
Andelin is one of the best psychology professors I've had at UW. I'm about to graduate, but he's someone I'll truly miss. If you're unsure whose class to take, just choose his!

Basically as long as you read the text book and go to lecture you'll do great. I like his grading style of dropping your lowest grades from each section of your grade. Poll everywhere is for credit, but he often reissues questions from poll everywhere on exams so getting these questions is really helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: content can be difficult but andelin is a great teacher and made lectures engaging and understandable. you will need to do the reading but he makes good study guides for tests, your lowest test score gets dropped. pollev questions for attendance but there are drops and ways to make up the points
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This is my second course with Dr. Andelin. He is super helpful and genuinely cares for his students. This course is a little more challenging than 202, the workload is manageable. I recommend go to his office hour if you are confused about course contents. Exams are not difficult as long as you understand the lecture and reading contents.

I always looked forward to attending the lectures because the Professor's lectures are enjoyable and he always shares pictures of his dog! The class in general wasn't as difficult as I anticipated, and I learned a lot. There's a clear grading criteria that he states on the syllabus and his exams were all multiple choice.

Goated prof with goated dog. If you want entertaining lectures with a cute dog named Bodhi, 10/10 class for you. 4 exams, one of them you can drop. Lots of extra credit opportunity. To do well in this class, minimal effort is just paying attention in class and reading the textbook with flashcards. Good luck.

one of the best professors I've had! I will definitely take other classes that he teach!
Just stay on top of your studying and you'll do great, especially that everything is graded fairly!

Prof Andelin is a great lecturer that keeps class interesting. He made the content easy to understand. I would say that the way quiz/exam questions were phrased sometimes were a bit confusing, but you should still do well if you keep up with lecture and textbook readings. Bohdi (his dog) is really cute, you'll get to hear a lot about him.

One of the best professors I had here. I highly recommend taking his class. I found it super entertaining and he's just a great guy. If I could I'd take his class again just for fun. He knows so much information and make the class very intriguing.
Had a blast
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Although this class can be hard at some points, Professor Andelin makes it a welcoming environment. 4 tests, one of which can be dropped, and most of the text information you can get from the PowerPoints. Study guides provided. Really funny and has a great dog. Side note, I think the organ of Corti should be called the organ of Bodhi.

Dr. Andelin is goated fr. Love his dog. 4 tests, one of which is dropped (including the final, so you can get away with not taking it). One thing in each grading category is dropped. I hate lectures but his were entertaining and soothing.

His teaching was so lucid & I could clearly see his passion in neurobiology. Content-wise, this is one of the toughest class in psychology with many arcane biology details to master. 3 open exams, 2-3 polls/class, weekly quizzes & scholarly journal presentation and summaries to polish your critical analysis skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: do the readings early and you'll be fine. Dr. Andelin is a super amiable and nice guy, don't be afraid to go up and ask questions if you're confused about anything and its an easy A.

Many people don't like him for 355, but for 202 which I feared because of what people were saying, he made it so easy. It was almost difficult to not do well. Just go to the lectures (which are fun af), read the textbook (which is actually engaging for once), and do the work.

Fantastic professor who teaches at a good pace!

This by far is my favorite class and professor I have had at UW so far. The class is hard but if you read the textbook and go to lecture, you will be fine. I wish I could take this class again. Its amazing.

I frickin love this man and his dog. Be prepared to read a lot and attend/watch all lectures. If you do, you will need to study minimally since it's just lots of memorization. Superrr knowledgeable and hilarious. 4 midterms, weekly quizzes and graded class participation. But he drops the lowest score from all categories! Fav class i've ever taken.

Very engaging lecturer but exams and quiz questions are poorly worded in my opinion. Also grades attendance every day with poll everywhere which is problematic. Otherwise, he's nice and you can tell he cares about students, just not my favorite teaching style or class structure. I can see how it might work well for a different type of learner

A genuinely wonderful professor across the board. He cares for his students, wants them to succeed, and has the cutest dog in the world (I love you Bodhi). Make sure to do the textbook readings and go to lectures to fully understand content. He drops lowest grade from every assignment category, including exams, and is ultimately one of the best.

I don't intend to subject to any halo effects. His teaching style is overall phenomenal but has the potential for information overload. Concepts are highly specific and exams had ambiguous and complex wordings that can mess you up. His dog was interesting but I found him went too fast in lectures & occasionally did not address my questions clearly

Very passionate about the subject. You do need to study for this class, but it's not too bad. As long as you pay attention and attend lectures, you'll get an A. He's just a really nice funny guy, who makes the material fun to learn. Would definitely recommend.

Great lecturer and super nice! We were graded on many different things, but the exams were brutal. So much material and the study guides were super broad. He's bad with communicating sometimes too, especially with canceling class. That being said, he's probably the most entertaining professor I've had at UW and I would definitely recommend him.
Andelin is super entertaining, understanding, and informative. The class was great and not hard to follow at all!

I would recommend this class because Dr. Andelin does a great job at explaining things in an interesting way. He relates things we learn to real life scenarios, which makes things easier to comprehend. He also talks about his dog a lot, it's so sweet. This class has a lot of busy work and requires a lot of memorization, but it's all very doable.

This class would be unbearable if it were any other prof. This course has a lot of information and homework. The tests are DENSE. You must read the book and attend class to succeed. This is the only time I have read the entire book for a class and genuinely enjoyed and understood it. His teaching style is very effective. Nearly perfect professor.
He has really entertaining lectures, and he brings his dog on the last day of class.
Dr. Andelin is a kind person! His exam will not be difficult if he takes notes carefully, and will provide a lot of extra credits.

I've had Dr. Andelin before and he's great! Sometimes a little cocky, but aside from that he's passionate about psychology and you can tell he loves what he does. Class is overall pretty easy, tests are closed note so be sure to study, but as long as you do the work on time and well, you will do great in his class. A LOT of info though for sure.

This Professor is really good. He answers student questions well, his lectures are interesting, his criteria is clear, he holds office hours, and he's really kind. One time I forgot to write my name on the exam; rather than throwing my exam in the trash, he graded it and I got my score. Best of all, he drops the lowest assignment for every category
I took this back in Jan 2022, so it was partially online. Concepts were super easy. The dog is adorable. Easy 4.0

1. A lot of homeworks. But if you complete them carefully, your grades will be good.
2. 4 Exams. 3 Midterms and 1 Final. The lowest Midterm will be dropped. 
3. Textbook readings are recommended but not required. I fell like if you attend class everyday, it is fine to not read the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved his class. His lectures were super funny and the only thing that was actually making me get out of bed for the 8am class time. It was mainly memorization, and if you just review the study guide it'll be super easy and fun.

Like many students in the class, I only took biopsych because it's a prerequisite for the psych major. Professor Andelin is very friendly and charismatic, but he struggles to answer questions well and his study guides for exams are unhelpful. He often curves exams which is nice. I like him as a person, but I don't think he's an effective teacher.
He is an amazing professor who if you study the study guide well will do fine in the class. He is caring and really has a passion for teaching I recommend him to everyone

His lectures are engaging. He loves his dog a lot. He will extend 1 thing for you per quarter maybe more if he likes you, but he did not like me. This is my 2nd time taking this course. I had to retake because I had a medical issue and missed the final and he would not extend it even though I had doctors and ER notes. So... dont get hurt.
This class was super easy, basically all memorization. Dr. Andelin is a great lecturer and very funny as well. Highly recommend taking it for an easy elective.
Dr Andelin is very knowledgeable and has a great sense of humor. He make learning fun and relatable. Love his jokes and his dog. 12/10.

The class is easy and concepts are clear. Lectures were unnecessary-- he took nearly everything on his slides from the book-- I only went to lectures and didn't read the book and got a 4.0. The issue with Dr. Andelin is that he is disrespectful to students and TAs. He constantly misgendered a TA and is not understanding in difficult circumstances.

Dr. Andelin was a great teacher for Psych 101! I enjoyed how up he was with the times. Lectures are not necessary, but can have specific questions on tests. The every other day in-person lectures were okay, although I prefer in person. Can show annoyance if certain questions are asked though, so pay attention to not miss things! Loved this class!

There are four exams, a quiz about every week, review questions every week, one discussion post a week, and poll everywhere questions for extra credit, with the lowest score in each category is dropped. The material itself isnt difficult, but some of the exam question are long and make you think, so if you can manage your time well, youll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This professor has an engaging lecture style with a sense of humor and vibrant tone. He clearly loves this subject and wants us to learn all about it. He also talks a lot about his dog (Bodhi) and includes a pic in every lecture, which, hello!!All lectures are recorded but class is more fun. Grading is really fair across many assignments.

Professor Andelin was great. It is clear from his lectures that he is passionate about teaching psychology. He cares about his students doing well and trys to make lectures fun and engaging. He wants you to do well and the class is easy to succeed in.

I really like how he teach he always make the lecture fun and not boring lol if you love dog I guess you would get along with him. This class requires a lot of reading but don’t worry quiz and test are easy just make sure to read the textbook and listen to his lecture and you will be solid :)

Look, he's a fairly good lecturer which is what most of the class will be and tho there is a fair amount of hw its all easy. I just don't like the pop culture references on exam questions and (crucify me idc) I just don't care about the dog.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you go to class everyday, you can get 2 extra points to your grade. Lectures are a little boring as its just the presentation of info. 4 exams, first 3 you can drop your lowest and final is mandatory. Read the textbook, go to class, ask questions, study; youll do great!

Dr. Andelin has been a wonderful professor because he puts effort into teaching and making sure students understand the material being taught! Not only is he great at teaching, but he's also an educational and professional comedian! I would 100% take his class again because I actually learned a lot without even wanting to try. Great job, professor!

Professor Andelin is a fun professor and he is definitely knowledgeable. But his style of teaching is not that reassuring and responsible for his students. There was a blank picture in exam and he just sent us an email and pretend there is the picture. As we open it, it was his dog Bohdi (Bohdi is cute but you wont feel happy when that happen

This class is absolutely great! I had this prof for PSYCH 101 and it was just amazing. The content from 101 and 202 will overlap, so its a bit easier to understand concepts. His participation is not mando, but will offer extra credit if you do show up and answer his Poll everywhere questions. Pay attention and you'll get a minimum 3.5, easy A.

This teacher is literally amazing. He cares so much about his students and works really hard to make lectures interesting and engaging (like watching the office clips). There are 3 noncumulative midterms and 1 cumulative final, but he drops one. Weekly quiz/discussion, 2 papers, and extra credit polleverywhere for attending class. Best teacher ever

Dr. Andelin is amazing! He makes the class engaging (online) with pics of Bodhi. He always tries to answer all questions raised in class and is an overall very helpful and enthusiastic professor. The class overall isn't very hard if you keep up with readings or lectures. 4 midterms (tests), 1 final. Easy grading.

I really enjoyed this class. His lectures cover a lot of information in a decently concise manner, and his assignments are manageable. There are quite a few of them, including papers, article summaries, and quizzes, but they aren't too difficult if you do the readings and attend lecture. There are lots of extra credit opportunities as well!

He is a nice, friendly, and approachable professor. Yet, too much homework: 2 papers (3-4 pages) through quarter, online quizzes every week, reading the textbook 40-60 pages a week, reading assignments (around 1-2) every week, asking question on Packback 1 question and answer 2 others questions a week,4 midterm every 2 week, and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I need more professors like Dr. Andelin. The class is a lot to take in, but I live for his dog and all the pictures of Bodhi scattered throughout his presentations. Andelin care a lot about his students and is an awesome person to talk to during office hours.

The best professor I have taken at UW! I really enjoyed his lectures and hw assignments. Try your best at reading the book/notes and learning the concepts as it will help you to get an easy A on exams. P.S. his dog is awesome!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: This was one of my favorite classes at UW so far. 3 midterms, weekly quizzes and reading assignments, but the worst of all 3 categories is dropped. Final cant be dropped but tests are super easy if you ready and study. Prof Andelin is super funny and makes the class very enjoyable. Poll everywhere each class that counts as extra credit too!

Dr. Andelin is a cut above the rest. Cares about students and is truly knowledgeable. Learning about Cognitive Psych was a joy. Read the book before class to really get the most out of class. For Covid era online class this was great, lectures were fun and fresh just like being in the classroom. Classwork aided learning and exams were fair.

Dr. Andelin is by far my favorite professor in the Psychology department. He makes every lecture fun and interactive, and if you do all the polls you get 3% added to your overall grade. The tests aren't hard and the homework is usually just readings. 11/10 would recommend

Truthfully, had two classes with Dr. Andelin. He respects students, asks for a lot of feedback to his teaching. Most grades are depended on quizzes, which are not very difficult if you spent time reading the textbook and reviewing his lecture slides. He also offers a lot of outside class help. You will learn a lot with him if you spend some effort.

This class was online during COVID, but that didn't stop Dr. Andelin from giving amazing zoom lectures! He reviews previous lectures almost daily and drops your lowest exam. His dog is so cute!! The exams were more than fair, but then again they were open-book. I read almost all the assigned reading but probably don't need to. I recommend!!!

The exams aren't too difficult if you did your readings and review the study guide. Pollev points were 5 extra credit points but he did have some trick questions to catch the people at home (they wouldn't get any ec for the rest of the quarter). Easy material and quiz sections weren't mandatory unless there's a project!! He also loves his dog a lot

This class was very difficult. Get ready to read the whole textbook or you will not do well. Was very confused most of the quarter as what he taught in the slides did not match up with what was in the exams (all from the textbook).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: attendance is not mandatory, but it counts for up to 5% extra credit which is generous. study guides are super useful for whats going to be on the exam, and the exams are not too difficult although he through in 1-3 questions that are a wild card. about 45 multiple choice questions per exam. overall would recommend him for this class.

At some point, you will realize that he doesn't know what he's talking about. In class, he seems to be knowledgable, funny and approachable, but towards the end of the quarter, you'll know what I'm talking about. He doesn't accept alternate answer even though his answer is DEFINITELY wrong and if you don't see him reply to your email -> rejected

Incredibly nice guy with a clear grading criteria and he's knowledgeable. Grade relies heavily on in-class polling but he has panapto. Exams are 25-40 questions all multiple choice but the questions can be very specific and long. You have to know the material well - go to most lectures, take notes, read the book, review panaptos to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Adrian was super nice, however it was obvious how desperate he was to be liked. His lectures were interesting but it was obvious he read the book last night and was just going off of that. Sometimes, I felt as though he didnt really understand the experiments he was explaining to us. Also, he never shuts up about his dog.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Hes a good guy and definitely accessible outside of class. I like him and I like his straightforward lecturing but he is annoying in a few ways. His test policy is that ANYTHING in the 400 page textbook or lectures is fair game. He asks about tiny microscopic details and writes way too lengthy questions. You cant miss class, polls will kill you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy
