reviews.comment: Dr Andelin cares about his students, that is evident. However, this is his second quarter being an lecturer at UW. His teaching style and grading methods are still being ironed out. A 2.5 in his class is an 80% which is pretty rigorous. his test questions are too verbose and even though exams are 70% of your grade, they are only 25 questions!
You can tell that Dr. Andelin cares about what he's teaching and wants you to love the material as much as he does.

If you go to class and ask questions he was great at helping and responding, however if you don't feel comfortable asking questions it is very hard to learn anything. If he is teaching and it is flipped class, at least for me (and many others), it is very hard to learn anything.

this class lowkey sets you up to fail. his lectures are on youtube (which are 7 years old by the way), and that is his primary source of teaching. to compensate for that, he assigns a LOT of homework (individual, group, and quizzes before the start of the week) and readings. overall: difficult to understand and does not put enough effort to teach.

His class set up is not designed for student learning, it's designed for his laziness. The video lectures are very hard to watch as they are so boring and hard to learn anything from. He can explain things well when asked so I'm sure he would give awesome lectures but instead class is essentially mandatory office hours.

Instructed hybrid-like "flipped" classroom and got prissy when students didn't attend to work on HW. Doesn't answer questions effectively. Claims video lectures "benefit student's learning" over real lectures - they're 7yrs old. Class organization does not make sense - quizzes are due before HW covering topics. Isn't in touch w/student needs.

This class was genuinely a waste of my tuition. The entirety of the content class was based on monetized youtube videos the professor made 7 years ago that are not useful when it comes to the exams. The exams are also worth 75% of your grade and he fails to post ANY practice problems or even a list of what the exam covers.

Absolutely awful at asking questions on his homework, will withhold information to make things more difficult and confusing, and will be anything but straightforward. Not good at teaching the subject outside of a few tangents, he went on, overall not great.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very helpful!

His classes are difficult no doubt. Yet, you learn a lot because he is really passionate about teaching and really puts efforts in letting you learn. After taking his class I TA his class and I can say that he really cares his students, you can tell by him hosting two 2-hour long office hours each week.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Adler is great. While his lectures and HW can be hard to understand, he does everything in his power to help you succeed. He has a lot of office hours and is always willing to answer questions. His exams are fair and his exam system is really nice. Overall great prof and gives you a great chance to succeed in his class.

Despite the negative reviews of this professor (which I personally disagree), I still think Prof. Adler is a very good professor in terms of teaching and caring students. His lectures give examples after each concept; He holds 4 hours of OH each week, and he teaches with passion. Yes there are lots of hw and reading, but they are all useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Flipped classroom approach: comprehensive and clearly articulated video lectures supplement reading assignments and give you everything you need to solve weekly problem sets. Exams count for most of your grade but are straight forward and well represented by problem sets. Very responsive to questions. Great environment for learning the material!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Tests are worth 80% but he's been my favorite instructor in ChemE.

His self-described "Socratic" method of teaching just means his lectures are SO boring. With his soft quiet voice, I know for a fact it wasn't just me that would fall asleep during his lectures. Homework and tests were tough, but not impossible. He couldn't make me care about the subject, even though thermo is really interesting on its own.

Beware! Stuart Adler exams are incredibly difficult and you may or may not have enough time to completely figure them out in 50 minutes.   They are so tricky and unlike the textbook, it is not even worth studying for them in the traditional way (like "practicing problems")... BUT you better hope you understand the concepts.
He made it clear that "my hw philosophy is to make you suffer" too bad his exam makes you suffer more
homework? crazy! exam? extremely crazy!
Worst Chem-E professor

Before I took this class I had a cactus and a girlfriend. I spent so much time doing HW that my girlfriend left me for an art student and my cactus died from neglect. I'm more neglectful than a desert.
Great explainer. Gets a bit too busy with other stuff.
Homework is crazy in this class.  I am probably spending more time for this 4 credit class on HW then I have the two years COMBINED in all my other classes...

Just don't. The 3 and a half hour lecture should've already steered you away from even thinking about the class. Not an engaging lecturer, and the homework is pointless. It's an easy A but at the cost of extreme boredom. Kinda surprised the university even lets him keep teaching this course? Also  got marked down sometimes for stupid things so...

My favorite class until I lost 8 points on homework due to a Canvas issue and went from an A to a B. I reached out to Adam, who replied rudely, accusing me of lying. I showed him canvas grading and grade calculations done by hand, showing how 8 points tanked my GPA. He then ignored my emails for the rest of the class. Ridiculous grading

I am shocked by the bad reviews. He is really enthusiastic, his homework did not take long at all as long as you took notes in class and the grading is so damn fair.  This class was the lightest class of my whole STEM career.

This review is for KAYLA HALL, who has been teaching Adam Summer's classes this year. Kayla is the worst lecturer Ive ever had in all 4 years, has cancelled office hours every week because she "might not feel well" even though no one understands the content and she doesn't take notes in a MATH FOCUSED COURSE. wish I could formally complain to UW

This class consisted of scicomm assignments and math assignments, which 100% determine your grade. But they take hours, and its extremely difficult to ace the scicomm assignments. Grading is also ambiguous, because one of the graders is more lenient and the other one is strict. I dont recommend this class online, it might be better in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: not really accessible outside the class. have many poll eve questions nonrelevant to class materials. be prepared to take a four-hour class with five minutes break. he has tons of calculation questions. and no feedback for homework. does not have a grade scale in this class, so be ready to feel confused when you are anxious about low graded dues.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Math problem set: you get to work on tons of questions, definitely time consuming. Writing assignments: unclear grading criteria. Besides, he used a standard grading scale for this class, which means sometimes a 1% difference in total grade could make you lose up to 0.4 when converted to 4.0 scale. Make sure to pay attention to your grade?

Summers is very knowledgable and an overall nice guy. HOWEVER, each weekly homework/essay writing assignment will take you 5+ hours to complete and the only feedback you will get is a number. No comments at all. Then when you email them to ask why you got that grade you'll never get a response. Class is interesting but the logistics need work.

He is very knowledgeable and well respected in the science community. I don't appreciate that he would always randomly call on students. I also felt that the grading criteria on assignments was not clear or consistent. There were no tests, homework would take HOURS to complete (no joke--5 hours min.). Definitely beneficial to have a study group.

One of my favorite professors of all time at the UW. His class was tough and you had to attend as he doesn't post notes, but works problems and ideas through with the class on the whiteboard.  Very approachable, friendly, and interested in you actually learning.  If you can take this class with him, I highly recommend it.

Prettt much worst professor. He has a PhD in engineering and biology so he expects his students to be geniuses. His grading standards are too high and often does not give answers or explanations as to why points were docked. Assignments also take countless hours to complete.
It was a quarter-long yawn.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: she's a joke lol

no. just no. unclear materials harsh grader bad feedback and boringgggggg lectures. if you are not interested in art, do not take it or else you will be so bored. only graded by a few things so if you do bad then sucks for you. also tas don't really help much

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROF SHE IS AWFUL!! She is SUPER boring and this class feels like an eternity despite being only an hour and 20 mins. She doesn't let us use electronics and expects us to hand write all our notes. I dread coming to lecture and quiz section every week, overall would NOT recommend taking her.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Incredibly lackluster.
Great coverage of cross-national comparative content.

The professor is completely uninterested in anything but her own opinions, but worse, the course is soooo boring. It's as if she doesn't even want to be teaching this material to anyone but those who already agree with her.
Confusing and quiet. I am an AH major and STILL felt this class was amateurish 2/10

Very clear expectations! Two papers for the quarter. Loved discussing art with other students. She did a good job of showing a variety of pieces from different movements and allowing open discussion. We covered heavy topics, be careful if you are worried about trigger warnings.

I am assuming negative reviews are from people who have never taken an art history class. I personally really enjoyed this class and found it to be engaging and really well organized. The workload was super reasonable. Professor rounthwaite is very knowledgable and very clearly cares a lot about her work. Would absolutely reccomend.

Ugh. Just ugh. Do art majors love this pretentious crap or what's the deal? Also it's a writing course, but she doesn't so any teaching about that and the TAs also don't do much, even though its most of your grade. Ugh.

This class ended up being one of my all time favorites because of Rounthwaite and the TAs, even though it required a fair amount of work. Rounthwaite addressed subject matter with respect. She was open to student feedback and made herself accessible outside of classes. Willing to give extensions if you provide her a reason ex. covid
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I'm not sure why Rounthwaite has such bad ratings! Maybe not from art majors? I thought the class was super interesting and the tests were not that bad, I've had art history professors who are way worse. She is very clear on her expectations. It is lecture heavy and can make you sleepy, but overall a good choice to get an art history credit.

I did not like this class. While shes brilliant and very well versed in her area of study, I dont think I have taken a more pretentious class in my life. I would not recommend this class or her as a professor, I lowkey dread it most days.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She knew the content but never really cared about her students felt. When I asked her about quiz questions, I was met with presumptive responses like "you should listen harder in lecture". Her lectures sometimes had images of extreme body modification and self-harm which we were never warned about and triggered my panic attacks.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Rounthwaite had amazing lectures and always had interesting points to make about the work she was presenting but the class itself is frustrating. Quizzes had picky answers, participation matters and there was too little time spent on writing skills even though this is a W credit. Overall, if you're not into art, take a different course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is a good lecturer for the subject (ART H 209), but this class was awful. It was a writing credit, and our two essays take up the bulk of our grade accordingly. Unfortunately, she never teaches writing in class. The only thing that matters in lecture is content for weekly quizzes which are a small portion of your grade. Grades papers too hard.

Engaging and challenging professor - she seems to be analyzing the texts and works alongside you, but doing so in an incredibly complex and impressive way. Intensely philosophical content and difficult readings, but if you get engaged it is extremely rewarding intellectually.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Ailion loves what he does and it shows. He really cares about the material and wants you to think like a scientist (a lot of test questions are highly hypothetical). Watch the video lectures - they are very engaging. Lower exam averages but the questions are genuinely interesting imo.

Partner professor was not the best lecturer this quarter. However, I wouldn't just blame the partner Professor. I think Professor Ailion could have stepped in and helped make the course better. Taking this class after BIOC 405 was upsetting.

It is a 400 level course so i totally understand why this course is hard. What made it even harder is the lectures. I felt like I wasn't getting enough information, and the exams were a lot more difficult than the lecture content.

Chill dude. Unfortunate that Daina ruined the class for him before hand. You can tell he's trying really hard to get students excited again for biochem after his sorry teaching partner. Tests are super hard but it is a 400 level class so its understandable. I like him. Keep it up.

Hilarious guy, interesting lecturer, just writes pretty difficult exams. He writes very conceptual questions, so you can't get away with only memorizing content - you need to memorize AND understand it thoroughly. BIOC 406 is a tough class, but very doable to succeed if you study hard, and Ailion is a fun professor. Love the meme contest!!

His exams are ridiculous, lectures are semi-interesting. His exam questions are difficult for no reason. Rather than test on the actual material, you are forced to think of an answer to a random hypothetical about a molecule that was on one slide of the lecture material and he only mentioned it once in prelecture recording. Use anki and pray.
I don't like him. The exams are too hard.

Biochem 406 is super hard and very based on memorization. He is a nice guy, but his lectures in zoom are pointless. Watch the lectures and study hard to get a good grade. Overall a decent teacher, the material is just very hard and there are 3 midterms and one final. Tests are very time-crunched which makes them hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's funny. He sounds like a decent guy. He seriously needs to work on his presentation. I don't doubt his knowledge but most of his slides are just empty. No clear explanation of what's going on. Whatever comes out of his mouth doesn't really help much either. Exams were ridiculous. Considering how much he teaches you in class, he expects a lot

Dr. Ailion's slides are probably the most confusing out of all in the biochemistry series. You need to read the textbook because sometimes what Dr. Ailion is saying makes no sense. His tests are a lot of hypothetical questions which have vague answers and I found his tests to be the hardest.
He's a good guy. Idk why people complain about this class - spend time memorizing those lecture slides and you will get an A. COME ON!

Michael Ailion is not a clear lecturer; get ready to compare your notes with other students because you will most definitely be confused. His exam content is the easiest, but because of his flawed lecture style, you will struggle to grasp the concepts.

I found his test questions to be the hardest in the biochem series. He really emphasizes conceptual and math questions, but also requires heavy memorization like all the other professors. However, he is extremely encouraging and wants all of his students to do well. I contacted him with questions and he was always extremely kind and helpful.

Ailion was awesome. Biochemistry can be a drag, but he really made sitting through the lectures worth it. His tests follow the same format as previous exams, so study from those heavily - he likes to recycle questions and change them slightly. Use the discussion board frequently (or at the very least, browse them).
He teaches the second half of the course and is way more engaging than Brzovic. also he throws candy around.

He made the second half of class. He has a sense of humor, is passionate about biochemistry, and has the knowledge to back it all up. During office hours he is very attentive to students questions and is willing to help until you understand. He is a great professor who expects a lot from students and therefore writes hard (but fair) exams.
really funny guy, great professor. tests are tricky but nothing different than bio 405 or the other bio 406 professor's.

Ailion is such a cool guy- his lectures are fun, he's just ridiculously nice and funny, and he doesn't focus so much on rote memorization(but expect some- it is biochem after all). He explains things well, tells great jokes, and always has candy to throw around. Tests are fair and the final was easy. Take biochem with him if you can!!
Really, really smart professor, and genuinely wants you to learn. Highly recommend for anyone who wants to learn R!
Talk too fast and doesn't change her tone at all... Materials are way too easy than my expectation which makes taking this class a waste of time.

Professor Ainsley values her students learning and chooses to structure her curriculum in such a way that prioritizes active discussion over heavy coursework. That being said, this class really depends on your group involvement; you are split into breakout rooms every class and those groups go on to work on research projects. Highly recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very organized. Professor Ainsley did an amazing job of getting students to interact & collaborate via zoom with a very well-designed structure for lectures and class discussions. She is extremely knowledgeable and intelligent but genuinely interested in your learning, so the work is challenging, but she is supportive and encouraging!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Caitlin goes above and beyond to craft engaging lectures that convey complex subject matter in a digestible way. The examples she uses are extremely useful and easy to remember, and her lecture slides are the best I've ever seen - posted online with links to each subheading making them easy to return to when exams come around. Absolutely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Ainsley is able to take a difficult concept and make it accessible for students to learn. Although there is quite a bit of reading, this allows for the concepts in class to be better understood. She is easy to talk to and also is accessible outside of class through her office hours or an appointment. I recommend her to all Pol S majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Caitlin is a phenominal instructor. She gives clear and effectice lectures with both conceptual abstract and hands on approached to teaching. She is extremely accessible and lots of fun. I highly recommend taking any class you can with her.

Professor Ainsley took a topic that is complex and not intuitive, and made it accessible and fun to learn. Going to class is essential because she clears up any confusion on the topics, and the assigned readings make the topics more understandable due to their accessibility. She is a great professor and I would recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: She is really nice. However, her lectures are long and boring. She grades EXTREMELY hard. She is super nit picky. I havent had a french teacher grade so hard. Ive done extremely well in the past and this is the first french class where I havent. I will never take her again. Shes organized and cool but her grading makes the class miserable.

She is a very kind and easy professor. She might be a bit opinionated sometimes, but that's forgivable. One thing I do not like about her class is the lack of discipline and sometimes lack of organization. However she is very nice and teaches well. I really have learnt a lot during this course.

Aimie is a solid choice for learning French.  She will cover all the things you need to know for a test and the things you should know if you're traveling to French speaking countries.  She also provides handouts with a quick run down of new terms/ grammar / etc.  She's a very organized and thorough teacher.

Took her class  back in 2014 at UW Bothell. It was BIS 390 Special Topics - Francophone. Anyway, she was fairly new then and didn't have a rate my professor yet. She made the class fun, though the writing and tests were brutal especially if you did not read the book. There were class discussions about the book too. So make sure you read guys!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Yassss gurl shes the bomb shes just an awesome french teacher. shes got a little attitude to her sometimes but it's not bad just don't be one of those retarded students who is annoying. She's Canadian and talks about it a lot it seemed like. She says "about" funny. But she's pretty gucci overall would rate 10/10. Hate the book and online work.

Shes aweeeeeesome! She explains everything throughout and always makes sure you're on track. She's never rude (maybe because she's Canadian). And she pretty much makes the class as fun as possible with as much information as possible. She will cold call on you so be prepared, if you don't like to participate in front of the class, skip this prof.
Tests are generally not difficult. The pace can be a little fast but all the online homework is due on the day of the test so you can plan ahead. Overall a very good class.

Aimie Shaw is an amazing professor! It is always a struggle to get a French teacher that has a good accent, is patient, and covers all of the course material well--and Mme Shaw met all of that criteria! I feel like she genuinely cares that her students learn and enjoy the class. There was homework assigned almost every night, but it was easy.

Excellent instructor. I recommend doing readings prior to the associated lectures because she covers material extremely quickly and expects you to keep up. 80 minutes is a long time to focus and I suggest that you never come to class tired, but if you do the work and keep up it'll be worth it. She's very passionate about the material.

While she is a good lecturer she is not the best with organization or with the reasonableness of her expectations. She is often vague with what is wanted for assignments and tests and expects her students to value her class above all others. Also she sends all class materials by email to be printed, often times late at night.

She's very passionate and no nonsense.  Her classes are well organized but move quite quickly.  If you don't have a decent grasp of the material to begin with, you'll have to work very hard to keep pace.  On the other hand her explanations are good and she's quite patient outside of class.
She's demanding at times, but passionate and clear. She is highly available to her students and actually wants them to succeed.
I think she's wonderful!!!
She is very tightly wound, but a great teaher and she is really really passionate about what she does. She is also one of the top Schoenberg scholars in the world.
Passionate and great professor. Really don't understand those who give him 1 point.
He's a really nice guy

Majority of the class complained about the prof during the Mid-course evaluation. Imagine learning calculus but the professor never shows you how to evaluate a integral. This is pretty much what it was like. I don't know how anyone could do the questions on the homework based on the lectures. One of the worst classes I have taken at UW honestly.

This man should not be allowed to teach. HW was so hard because he taught close to nothing in class. Shows you a bunch of random equations and expects you to apply it somehow on the HW. Class is easy to pass but don't expect a high grade whatsoever. I would avoid him if possible.

Professor just reads off slides most of the time. Example problems were rarely done by hand and instead were put on power point with some of the steps skipped.  Lectures felt like a complete waste of time.
Really nice guy and accommodating but his lectures were almost impossible to follow. Tests and HW were pretty hard since the lectures were hard to interpret so expect to look online for help
Very difficult to follow the lecture. Both labs and lectures are difficult. Tests cover homework materials that are due three weeks from the exam date.

Akio is the best art prof I've had at the UW - am taking him again for intermediate ceramics. He is kind and encouraging, but also helpful and honest about your work and ideas. He isn't overbearing and is a great person to simply talk about art with. Is also pretty funny in his own subtle way.

Great prof!He's really funny as well.He's very humble and kind. I highly recommend the class. It's creative and fairly easy although it's a little time consuming but other than that it's one of the best classes I've taken so far.
Great guy! Awesome teacher..all around.
Akio you're the greatest!!!

Akio is my favorite professor ever. He is truly interested in helping his students learn and improve. He is humble despite his achievements as an artist. He will take time with students and actually teach techniques.
Akio is wacky-packy! He has lots of interesting things to say and he's funny. During critique, though, I definitely get more nervous with Akio than with the other two.

Fun fun fun!!  He teaches you the basics and then lets you use your imagination.  He's picky about cups (since he had to do hundreds of them a day when hew as in Japan), but he's fun and a great person to learn from.
No Comments
The most intimidating of the three in Ceramics, IMO, but a really smart, funny guy with great ideas.

I had her for Japan 301, not 201. She was an amazing teacher and really cares about her students learning. She seems a little intimidating but she is always willing to work with you and get you to succeed. I found this level challenging because it was all in Japanese but she encourages all her students to try and make mistakes so they learn.
She really cares for her students and their wellbeing. She is very easy to reach and is very open to answering questions and helping students when they don't understand something. So kind :)
I just realized that I submitted it twice

Definitely the best professor I have ever seen in my academic career. She was very reachable, flexible, and she had asked us if we were doing OK when we missed the deadline. 

She CARES about her students so please never hesitate to ask for help from her. 

I hope I can be a professor like her one day.
The class was very well structured and grading was extremely quick and efficient, but Iwata Sensei can be strict and get upset over things such as turning in work late or leaving class early.

Iwata sensi has the perfect demeanor and style to keep you interested in Japanese while also supplying the discipline needed to keep up with the painstaking work of progressing in a language that is very difficult.

Iwata Sensei is a fantastic professor. She's very perceptive and is sure to use words and grammar that students are familiar with. She also has a great sense of humor ^-^ As long as you turn everything in and pay attention, you'll do great.

Her class was pretty chill. Not too hard and she is willing to slow down a lot for you to understand. The exams weren't too bad and so were the HW (except moodle, yuck). She makes effort to get to know students and make small talk, which is nice. But she is hesitant to help over email, so go to office hours if you have questions.

Very rapid class - right when you are finally starting to understand one thing it's time for 10 more things. Homework every single day including weekends and holidays. Focus on the midterm and final - these will absolutely destroy your grade, even if you do pretty well, just because they are weighted so heavily. Practice speaking at home!!

Really enjoyable course! Iwata sensei can be a bit strict with deadlines and grading, but is accessible for students and is generally very engaged with the class. There is a decent amount of homework but it is doable with a bit of planning ahead. Would recommend this course to everyone, the immersion aspect was great to progress language skill.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Iwata Sensei is a good lecturer. She teaches the concept clearly.

Late policy is a bit strict, but that's overshadowed by how enjoyable the class was. Discussion was always engaging & she always gave feedback to students (both on hw and quizzes). Also students were able to shape/guide their own learning because there was a mix of skills levels in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is a brilliant university professor who makes a lot of engaging activities and fun projects for us to do. On top of that, her personality is pin-point!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Iwata-sensei was very kind and accommodating. I learned a lot with her class despite the fact that it was online. She really puts forth the effort to make the class interesting and relevant to current events in Japan. It was not just a language class it is a Japan Culture Class as well. I am grateful to have taken her class.

I have Iwata Sensei for the whole 2nd year JPN. She is helpful and kind. Her classes are informative and specific and really helpful if you are interested in linguistic and special uses of grammar. Prepare to spend a bit of time after class to reveiw vocabs and grammars though. SPEAK JPNESE IN CLASS & AVOID AMERICAN TAs. Defo recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is a great and caring professor. Very accommodating as well! Although there is a lot of homework and they are very hard, it was graded mostly on participation. As long as you attend class and do the homework you will get a pretty decent grade.

I did First Year at CC and Iwata sensei's HW is incredibly hard. Be ready to have your points taken away if your handwriting isn't perfect. She's a nice person, but an extremely tough grader. Online learning isn't very affected by this class. Prepare to memorize words for quizzes that are also heavy.
I didn't have Iwata Sensei for my quiz section, but her lectures were very clear and understandable, as she makes to speak in both Japanese and English.

Iwata Sensei is very sweet and can be funny at times. She does all of her quiz sections and part of her lectures in Japanese which can make it difficult to understand sometimes. She is very fast with returning grades and graded material. Participation definitely matters so make sure you come to class every day.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I had Iwata Sensei for two quarters already, and she was very very nice. I felt no barrier between teacher and students. Also she is a light grader. She would tell you how she grade. She would list all the grading stuff to you before you do your project. I would like to keep taking her courses in the future.

Iwata is definitely a responsible and nice prof. Yes she is strict and her tests were hard. But I really learnt a lot from her lectures. Presentations and interviews were relatively easy because she let you prepare beforehand. She is also a nice person to talk to. Office hours were useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Iwata sensei is strict but in a good way. You can learn more due to her strictness. Exams are kinda hard and sometimes tricky but you will be fine if you go to class and listen to her lectures. Overall she is fine
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of my favorite teachers. I always try to get the sections that Iwata teachers, she is the best. Yes, she is strict but you will learn a lot of you put in the proper effort and are excited about Japanese. Easiest class with moderate homework, always a fun class. Definitely recommend.

I just transferred from BC and took Iwata Sensei for Japanese V. She is kind, and helpful if you ask her for help. However, I had more homework in her class than in my other two classes combined. You will be expected to remember how to write kanji from the previous chapter, on the current chapter's test. This class will hurt your GPA.

Really strict on handwriting, deducts a lot of points if she feel your handwriting is not right. Lectures are not exactly interesting but very specific and clear. Her quiz sections are fine, everyone gets called on at least once to answer something in every class. She is really nice teacher though.

Great teacher! Very kind and willing to help you with any questions you might have. Her lectures are organized and clear. I had her for lecture and section and would absolutely take her class again. She does penalize messy handwriting after the first few weeks, but only after she gives feedback about what needs to be changed. Very fair grader.

Worst instructor I have ever had in my career at the University. Too grade conscious, is superficial about student achievement, and is not consistent about what she says during class. If you speak English to her, she will judge you. Cannot describe in enough detail about coming to class and being so uncomfortable listening to her speak. AVOID.

Initially, I hated Iwata Sensei, but looking back on it, she made me the student I am today. 90 percent of her lectures are in Japanese, which means you have to learn how to understand and speak it no matter what. On top of that she's an insanely tough grader. However, if you take her class seriously, you develop some really good study habits.

I had Iwata for lectures, but never for section. I thought she was a really good lecturer and was surprised by these ratings. The curriculum follows the textbook and she uses slides to go over it in detail, with added picsvideos. Friendly, strict, won't call you out if you're unprepared. My friend preferred her for section leader even.

I have no idea why the rate here for her is so low. I took the whole forth year Japanese with her and she is very approachable and helpful. If you take this class seriously as a 5 credit class, there should't be any problem of learning.
Grades very harshly, will mark off if she thinks you have bad handwriting. Be careful.

I did not find her teaching style effective at all. I felt that she emphasized on things that were not really important so that we can really learn and enjoy the Japanese language. Too grade conscious.

She's a decent professor, but the course is very fast paced and strictly follows the textbook. Very difficult if you started Japanese in HS/another school with a different textbook (she uses Genki series).Grammar, handwriting, workbooks/tests are graded especially rigorously. Almost too Japanese; don't expect any leniency.
Grades very strictly and teaches to the book. Very hard to transfer to this class from another institute because of the unfamiliar style of the textbook, which is the main focus of the class.

This class was painful to sit through everyday for an hour due to Iwata-sensei's teaching style and attitude.  Class was often dull and, most of all, it felt as though she underestimated our intelligence and treated us like little kids. Also felt like too many things were trying to be covered at the same time. Overall, not recommended.

She's a great teacher. The class doesn't have a textbook and you will be using materials she finds on the web. She's willing to give a day or two for you to understand a difficult grammar structure and such. The grading sometimes can be harsh but if you put in the time, you should be able to do well.
One of the sweetest professors! You can tell she really enjoys what she teaches and she always comes to class with a really positive attitude!

This class was tough but the professor was amazing. She's so passionate about the subject, it's inspiring. Definitely use the study guides even though it's online. The tests are tough. Overall, I would reccomend the class. It was super interesting and Professor was genuinely such a great teacher who actually cares.
Anne is a great professor. During lecture, she is always sweet and she cares about all the student during lecture. I recommend taking this class and this class is easy.

probably one of the most passionate and caring profs I've ever had. I loved listening to her talk. she was so engaging, patient, and took time to get to know us. would have her as my prof 100 times over. loved it!

By far the nicest and most caring professor out there. She deeply cares about each student's well-being. You should attend class because there is a group assignment each time but they are very fun and straight forward. She is always very positive and wants each student to succeed! perfect intro to the nursing major!!

One of the sweetest professors I've had. She taught this class with Eunjung Kim. No homework, just small group assignments after each lecture so attendance was important, and exams were open-note. Highly recommend this course!

Dr. Kalkbrenner is one of the best people I have ever met. She clearly cares for her students, fellow staff, and patients. She gives feedback without point deduction if you happened to miss something and is always so cheerful and polite. Definitely the best professor I have ever had.

Anne seems to always be super happy and teaches her content well too. She and Dr. Eunjung Kim taught the course together for me and they both are pretty similar in that they are extremely nice, into what they are teaching, and have plenty of experience to share. The class is quite easy if you just complete your work. Tests were open book.

I loved Dr. Kalkbrenner! She is so sweet and caring and shows she cares about situations you may be going through. Tests are open note and the lectures are interesting! I cannot stress enough how much I loved this class and the teaching team. Even if you are not a nursing student I recommend this class 110%!

Hands down one of the best instructors Ive ever had. Shes so sweet and you can tell she really cares about her students. Her class is not overwhelming at all and I definitely recommend taking her class !

Very sweet and super smily professor :) she is passionate about nursing and it shows! Attendance not mandatory but there is a group assignment after every lecture. 3 exams total going over chapters covered on pearson ebook. Virtual life simulation assignment was interesting and there were small assignments to answer 3 questions. Overall easy.

Professor Kalkbrenner is such a nice and caring professor. She is really passionate about nursing and it shows. She good at lecturing and answers any questions you might have. She has a great smile and gives good feedback.

10/10 PROF! She is the sweetest, most caring professor ever. Lectures are quite long but help clarify concepts within the book. She makes the effort to call everyone by names and I'm sure she knows all 150+ student names. You have group work at the end of every class which is fairly easy if each member contributes. TAKE THIS COURSE!!! I loved it :)

She was very energetic and ready to teach about life development! She made sure everyone understood the material and tok breaks here and there throughout lecture. Truly amazing class and it was also a nice class to take while online due to COVID. Attendance is not stated as mandatory, but you should attend to take part in the group activity after.

Even though attendance is not mandatory, it is crucial you take part in group activities that start right after the lecture. Anne is truly an amazing professor who is passionate about nursing. The lectures are your standard powerpoints but she really goes in-depth about topics and readily answers any questions you may have.

Professor Kroll is such a sweet guy and you can really tell that he wants his students to succeed! He is always willing to answer questions and clarify anything that you're stuck on. There is quite a bit of homework in the course but it really does help you build an understanding of the course material.

Professor Kroll is a great professor. He cares about his students, and his teaching style (making it fun) really aligned with how I like to learn. His tests were REALLY hard though, and they required a lot of studying. Overall he is a wonderful professor, and I would highly recommend him.

I thought Kroll was better at explaining 152 topics than 142 topics but he was great at explaining both. His exams weren'tthat difficult and by far the best way to study for them is by doing quiz section worksheets. The only thing that bothers me is his grading scale since there is no curve in this class. Other than that he's great!

His course for 110 is hard. Exams are extremely difficult no matter how much you study, I've always averaged 50% on his exams. Numerous amounts of students are failing his class despite it being an intro course.
Good teacher that made chem actually bearable. Knew most of the content from high school but his lectures were very well paced and easy to understand. Kind and easy to ask questions to.

You will have a lot of ALEKS to do, thus leaving you no time to focus on study materials. He never fully answers questions, often going on tangents that never actually give you a straight up answer. Does not curve, even when class median is a 60%. This class is truly memorization contrary to what he may tell you.

Kroll is a very caring professor, and has great lectures, but his tests are super hard! Even with background chemistry knowledge, I struggled a lot on his exams, as they only give you 45 minutes for 5-10+ minute problems. Great lecturer, but the majority of the grade in this class is exams, and they are super difficult.

The way he taught did not mesh well with my learning style. His tests had questions on it that I had not seen before. Otherwise, he was a very average professor. He's very kind and caring but he wasn't a good teacher for me. He also used AI images on slides which did not sit right with me.
worth reorganizing you're entire schedule to have him- made chem super easy, doesn't expect you to have any previous knowledge!!
Easy to understand. Didn't need to study much beyond the set homework each week.
Very straight forward, understood the material very well. Best exams and exam preparation. Very funny and kind guy. Amazing explanations during office hours.

Cannot recommend Dr. Kroll enough! His slides and explanations were informative and gave all the information we needed to know. The content itself is not easy, but he clearly and reasonably states all the topics you need to know for testing. I have testing extra time, and he was easy to work with on that front. Have him again for 152, so excited!!

Especially right out of high school, Dr. Kroll was an amazing professor. His lectures are engaging and informative, and he makes every effort to make sure his students are aware of due dates and what they should be working on. Sometimes the ALEKS homework doesn't exactly line up with the material in class, but it's not a huge issue.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Kroll is really enthusiastic about teaching chemistry and is really helpful at answering questions, especially in office hours. The only thing to watch out for is the midterms as those can be really challenging if you only do Aleks and not do any discussion worksheets independently or do some textbook problems.

Do the readings the before lecture and it will be much easier to understand what's going on. His lectures are amazing and fast paced so this helped me keep up and do well on the "concept tests". Prof Kroll really cares a lot about his students and works hard to make his expectations and deadlines clear.
Alec Kroll is the goat!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The teacher is really good, he is funny makes jokes and loves chemistry and teaches from his heart, the problem is the tests are lowky hard. I studied for the midterm 2 weeks prior and still got a bad grade, the teacher is great but the tests are hard and YOU HAVE TO STUDY HARD TO PASS THE CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Krolls a good guy and a good lecturer. My only complaints are that the class isn't graded on a curve so even if everyone does bad, you're not going to get a grade boost. Our averages for the first midterm and final were in the 60's and no curve. I also didn't think the reading quizzes were helpful. Other than that he's good.

He was an excellent prof! Out of all the core sciences, chemistry is by far my least favorite, but this class made it tolerable. He is very accessible outside of class and updates and adjusts proactively. His lectures were entertaining, and expectations were clear.  Not a really cram-suited class, so don't procrastinate (oops)

Professor Kroll is a very kind, approachable and endearing man who teaches the content very well and gives lots of opportunity for practice. The issues I had were that leading up to the test it is very hard to tell what will be covered within the exams and the level at which everything should be known. Make sure you study A LOT and you'll be fine.

One of the best chemistry professors. Gave us one exam drop, which was extremely helpful and took the pressure off of exams. Lectures were straight forward and easy to understand, I barely read the textbook. Very receptive to student feedback and is constantly looking to improve as a professor. Overall, if given the choice, take his class!
meowwwwwwwwwwww
Professor Kroll is a really nice professor, I highly recommend taking this specific professor for the chem series you will not regret it!!! if you don't take him, you will regret it!!!

YOU GUYS NEEDA STOP GIVE HIM HIGH RATINGS CUZ I LITERALLY CAN'T GET INTO HIS CLASS. God bless me my registration is tomorrow morning hope I get into chem 152 with him. I took chem 142 with him and he was kind and the lecture was clear, tests were not too bad.

i fell in love with this man. he is sooo sweet and teaches so well. i did sooo bad in 142 then i took 152/162 with him and BOOOOM goes my gradeee. genuinely if he needed a kidney i would give it to him.

KROLL IS THE BEST PROF I'VE HAD AT UW. The friendliest man on earth, go to office hours, it's a fun time, and you can tell he cares about his students. I learned a lot because his lectures are bite sized and conversational. He knows what to say to make the info stick. He's so passionate and has inspired me a lot, I'm now considering a chem minor.

BEST CHEM PROF AT UW BY FAR! Tests were fair, grading was fair, discussion worksheets were always harder than the exams, exam practice material was accurate. Dr Kroll is so sweet and easy to talk to after class. Explains topics so well. He is lenient with polleverywhere by giving you 6 excuses absences with no penalty. Best prof at UW lowkey

Took Kroll for all three gen chem courses (142, 152, 162), and he was my first STEM professor. He's a great professor, teaches well, and actually cares about his job and his students, which isn't too common for weed out courses like this one. Tests aren't too bad if you study, and he doesn't curve the course so no one else's score impacts yours.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took Kroll for Chem 142, 152, and now 162. I don't read the textbook because it's much easier to digest the information in his lectures. To do well on the exam, review lectures & do the practice questions, concept tests, and quiz section worksheets. Although I didn't meet him outside of class, he seems like a good person and cares about you.

I think Kroll is a great professor, he makes things very understandable and knows what it's like to be a chemistry student. His pacing was sometimes either too slow or too fast in my opinion but he was still able to get through all the content of the class pretty well.

I had Kroll for 152 and 162 and he was great! Naturally, chem is difficult, but Kroll teaches the content in a digestible way and is very clear in what he expects of student on exams. He also quickly responds to student questions on his Ed Discussion page. If you have the opportunity to take the intro chem series with him, I'd highly recommend it!
Professor Kroll was an amazing teacher and grader. Loved his class overall, would take again.

he lets u drop one exam which is huge. he goes fast but overall, he's a good lecturer and theyre recorded. i honestly have no issues with kroll. his exams are pretty fair. its definitely possible to succeed in his classes. also hes super approachable

Has kroll for 152/162 and he's the best! So kind and explains things in a way that make sense. Very consistent in the way he teaches during lecture and assigns practice questions and questions on tests. Def take him if you can
Dr. Kroll is amazing! His lectures are awesome and he does a great job explaining concepts/answering questions.

Kroll made me love and succeed in chemistry after taking AP Chem in high school and struggling A LOT. Had him for the entire gen chem sequence at UW, and during the whole year he had consistently clear and engaging lectures, relatively easy exams, and a very good homework model with ALEKS (though this may be an unpopular opinion🙃). Best prof ever.

I've taken Kroll for 152/162 and I can say that his lectures are way easier to understand than reading the textbook. I gave up on reading and only attend his lectures now, and it's made my life so much better. His tests aren't super hard but not easy at the same time. He will totally answer your questions, so ask!

I had him for both 142 and 152. He is the sweetest professor on the entire planet. His teaching is really good. He also listens to his students' feedback a lot. He makes sure to show representation in STEM, and he also makes us feel like we're more than just our grades (which is rare in a weed out class). Have him as your professor if you can!!

Had Kroll for 142, 152, & now 162. Lots of examples and goes through lectures quickly, so I've had to rewatch in my own time, but his explanations are clear and easy to understand. Genuinely wants his students to succeed, loves the subject, and is excited to teach! Grading guidelines and learning expectations are clear.

Lectures are fun. He makes sense, and actually answers questions. Takes time to explain new concepts. Does take attendance. Available outside of class, and will work with you if you have questions during office hours. Acknowledges Chem is hard, and wants all students to pass. Checks in to see where students are at in content.
New to UW so the occasional typo or iffy due date but no big deal. Class is easy if you study the practice problems and review problems. Light tests but come pretty prepared to the labs.
i would take every class with him if i could, he is fun and clearly cares

He is overall just a super nice and respectable guy. The tests were relatively easy compared to others and they related well to the lectures. The lectures werent my favorite compared to professor Craig but they were still helpful, I just felt they were a bit example heavy at times and lacking the conceptual aspects, but overall he's an awesome guy

Professor Kroll was one of the best professors I've ever had. His lectures were interesting and engaging. His exams are really fair, you wouldn't be surprised by something difficult. He has some demos, and makes the lectures funny in a way!!

Lectures are very helpful, though make sure to set time aside to redo examples bc he goes thru them fast. ALEKS & generally practicing problems is important for tests (& ALEKS is part of your grade). I took him for both Chem142 & Chem152 & got
Fantastic lecturer but DRS student be warned

Prof. Kroll is a fantastic professor. He is funny, engaging, and has clear lectures. He provides good exam practice and is accessible outside of class for questions. With studying and keeping up with the course material, getting good exam scores is definitely possible - his exams are very fair and there were never any surprises.
love kroll! so kind and encouraging and actually made me felt like an understanding of chemistry was attainable. not hard to do well in his class if you put in the work!
Professor Kroll was amazing. His lectures were very interesting and engaging. Probably the best Chem professor at UW.

Kroll is a great lecturer! He sort of teaches like you are in elementary school but not in like a "you're dumb" way, more like a thorough way that makes so much more sense than some other professors' teaching. The class is tricky but you are more likely to succeed in his class than in a lot of other professors' classes.

I LOVE PROF KROLL!!!! He's so chill and his drip is spot on. He does just read off of his slides but his office hours are great and he's so passionate. He told me I wasn't a weed to be weeded out and that inspired me.

Kroll is a really kind professor, and he cares so much about chemistry that his excitement really carries through into his lectures. He explains things really well and he gives a lot of examples in his lectures. His tests are really fair, too. At the end of the last lecture for CHEM 152 the class burst into spontaneous applause for him.

Lectures are always clear, concise, and engaging. fair grader and takes the time to ensure students understand the material. homework heavy but its a reasonable amount of work if you want a good grade
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A really great professor who clearly cares about his students, and it is easy to get a good grade if you work hard. Only problem that I had with his course was that if you had the earlier chem lecture, he would often have a lot of mistakes in his slides that would get really confusing if he had to keep correcting himself.

Amazing professor! Best one I've had at UW so far. You can tell he genuinely loves teaching and cares about the students and gets so excited talking about chemistry which makes the lectures super engaging. He's a fair grader and gives lots of practice and review material. If you study, it's easy to get good marks on his exams.

Alec Kroll is an amazing professor, very passionate about teaching and about chemistry. Answers a lot of questions in class, makes sure everyone understands the material. Very reasonable grader, really cares about his students. I had him for 142 and 152 and will for 162 in the spring, has been my favorite professor so far.

I actually had him for 152 but I don't think the course is on here yet because it's his first time teaching it.  He is much considerate of his students and reasonable. He is also adorable and a good lecturer, although he does move fast. He also makes an effort to answer all questions and interact with most students in lecture which I appreciate.

Very good lecturer, the class is not a weed out class at all and over all not very hard compared to the chem lecturers. Really cares about the subject and the students understanding of material. Answers questions with no judgement and honestly. Attendance is required through poll everywhere, but lectures are recorded.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: SO kind, genuinely cares about his students. Tests easy if you pay attention and he gives very clear explanations in class.
Definitely cares about his students. If you pay attention in lectures tests are relatively easy. Lectures are engaging and go quickly!

Dr. Kroll's lectures, for the most part, were awesome. His classes were interactive, and he explained concepts extremely well. Used easy-to-understand language, while simultaneously highlighting important keywords students should use in their answers. Exams and quizzes were very reasonable. Overall sweet, great guy, with  fun sense of humor!

Okay, don't judge me on my grade but he wasn't a bad lecturer. I took him my first quarter so that might've been why. I will say that he is quick paced when showing how to solve step-by-step equations but always clarifies when asked. I often attended his office hours and was always the sweetest. He never hesitated to answer other's questions!

Loved Dr. Kroll. So enthusiastic about Chemistry and seems like such a nice person. His lectures were also fantastic at distilling the textbook into manageable and understandable chunks. Would recommend to anyone unfortunate enough to have to take the Chem 1X2 series at UW.

Loved this prof! Had him for Chem142 and am currently enrolled in his Chem152 course. Excited to be there and teach, genuinely wants us to learn the material. Expectations were clear & materials were easy to access. He's always acknowledging feedback so he knows what does and doesn't work for our learning. Very flexible in the pacing of the course.

Amazing professor, I'm purposefully taking him again for Chem152. There is no curve, however, I think his grading is very clearly laid out and very fair. His lectures are very engaging and you can tell he loves chemistry and loves teaching it. The 2-3 reading assignments a week are very short, but leave time for ALEKS modules as they can be longer.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Kroll is an amazing professor that teaches really well. I feel like I was able to really understand and learn topics rather than just memorizing them. The class is hard, but if you put in work you can definitely succeed. The grading system is also not curved which is a plus.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Alec Kroll is an amazing professor who really cares about your wellbeing and success as a student. He consistently comforts and reminds his students to get help if you do not understand topics and provides office hours and other help for all topics covered in the course.

I give Kroll props, as the Chemistry Department at UW is horrible.
Engaging and fun lectures. Clearly dedicated to teaching his students and has a love for chemistry!

Absolutely great professor. Clearly cares about his students and is willing to make time to help you. Very engaging lectures that do a really good job of explaining material. Clearly shows how the course is graded. Lots of work involved but was well distributed

He was a great professor! Super enthusiastic and helpful-- made me actually like chemistry lol. The homeworks were all very helpful and the lectures were focused and engaging. Would definitely recommend this class!
He has so much enthusiasm teaching the class and is always in a cheery mood. He cares so much about his students and makes the lectures fun and engaging sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor! You can tell how much he cares about chemistry and his students. Gets very busy in office hours but tries to help everyone. His enthusiasm made the class very engaging and I learned a ton. Lots of textbook readings and ALEKS modules but they ended up helping me at the end of the day.

Professor Kroll did a great job teaching the course and provided many opportunities for students. Although chemistry is not the most interesting topic to me, he did a great job keeping the lecture engaging and explaining the topics clearly. I learned a lot from him, and I am hoping to take his higher-level Chem classes in the future.

Kroll is very nice and you can tell he cares about his students. Lectures are engaging and he has office hours where you can ask for help. Chem is hard in general but he is good at explaining the topics. If you're stuck I recommend the chem study center on the 3rd floor of Bagley. He uses poll ev so you have to go to class to get points for it.

Spent the quarter being talked down to, not taught. The class was run through a disorganized Excel system, instructions rarely made sense, and he seemed more focused on praising AI and acting like an expert despite little industry experience. He also argued with TAs, and grading felt inconsistent and mood-based.

This is the most disorganized and confusing professor I have ever had. None of his "lectures" were structured and were mostly either irrelevant rambling or taught by TA's. He claims to want feedback but dismisses real objective criticism. His grading system is absolutely ridiculous and assignments in his class are objectively just busywork.

This course is essentially the professor stroking his own ego with irrelevant anecdotes and hyping up chatgpt. For a technical writing course, there is zero critical thinking as AI is both encouraged and worshipped. Extremely confusing google sheets system for course organization and subjective “XP points” that count for 24% of the grade.

Although I couldn't understand anything the professor said in class, but he added a touch of fun to my otherwise boring life. I always wanted to laugh whenever he spends half the lecture argue with his TAs. I can't imagine what he would look like in person walking into the IEB. He speaks like an ancient god and his headphones are his true identity.

This class often left me speechless, laughing in disbelief, and learning more from nyt games than anything the professor ever taught us. I have never met anyone who worships chatGPT more than this man which would have been funny if he weren't a communications professor. I called this class Rage Bait 101, and it lived up to that name all quarter.

prof Mamishev is a genius who is constrained by the bureaucracy of a university system. His spreadsheets are impossibly dense but communicate that he has forbidden knowledge that he has yet to share. Take his class if you seek a greater understanding and technological enlightenment.
Professor Mamishev is Awesome. Very clear course guidelines and an easy to follow structure.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Poor communication skill, written, and oral. Over-organization and have poor grasp of his own organized materials. Subjective xp point (24% of grade) credit giver (mood-based). Lack industry knowledge yet arrogantly give his takes. Loves AI quality work.Complains solvable personal mess alot. If someone rates 5, I would belive that they are bribed.

First day talks about how useless this class is, and only required because of IEEE auditing. ~250 page document with instructions so detailed and specific they are impossible to sort through all of the useless information. Homework on a google spreadsheet shared with class. Super easy though, and a nice guy. Terribly organized.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I genuinely think the positive ratings on here are a PSYOP. Went to lecture for 5 weeks, just listened to him complain about his lazy TA's that wouldn't fix all the problems he created. In terms of the work, it is incredibly easy once you understand his terrible class design. Take it with friends so you can work together in the group projects.

Genuinely the worst professor I've ever had. Didn't learn anything about writing, only how to click on a bunch of links are follow his super specific super confusing instructions. Would get offended if anyone asked questions or suggested his instructions were unclear. Seriously don't take.
Solid.

Professor Mamishev has a unique way of teaching and organizing his class which may throw off some students - but ignoring that, he is a fantastic teacher. Cares deeply about technical writing and teaching students properly. Grades fairly, good at communicating, and very accessible outside of class (on Slack/email or through TAs).
For a class about technical communications, he certainly did a horrible job communicating about class assignments and logistics. It is offensive that the UW requires EE students to take this garbage.

He is good, at least for technical writing, i think i learnt some useful stuff from him. and he is also a good person. he treats students well and respect students. although he has accents sometimes i can not get him. but overall i think he is good

DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM!! Falls way behind schedule and moves super slow through lectures, every assignment has major typos or are just plain wrong, and exams don't cover what we learned in class. In fact, he added a question of stuff we never learned to "vary the exam scores". Worst professor I've ever had.

The whole course revolves around him indoctrinating you on his Stream tools handbook (which of course he authored and profits from). Most of your grade revolves around your ability to memorize and use these tools. Very little time spent learning actual technical writing skills. Pretty easy to get a 4.0 or close, though, so there is that.
Just Avoid taking class with him! You wont learn any thing. His tests are tough.
Great Prof. Intelligent, helpful, and funny.
Awesome professor!!!

Teaches entirely off power point slides.  Very unhelpful.  Tests were difficult with sometimes oddball questions.  Frustrating.. although it brings everyone's grade down and then he curves back up.  Could just give easier tests or actually do some problems on the board so people were prepared.. or not.  Funny guy but wouldn't recommend him
avoid
This professor isn't exactly horrible, but I don't have anything great to say about him. He seems to not have a great interest in this particular class (EE 351). He probably shouldn't be teaching it.
One crazy crazy Russian
Awesome instructor
Good class but takes alot of your time if you take the second course in the winter.
good class, not technically hard

Ali is very communicative of his expectations and the content of his exams are never surprising if you study. He is passionate in lecture, as well as clearly knowledgeable about his subject. Would recommend!

first module of the class was very easy, second and third modules were quick-paced and much more difficult. his lectures were confusing, but the textbooks helped. class was not the worst if you made sure to keep up, but exams can be harsh as they're not worth many points. did a good amount of self-studying because my TA was not super helpful

Nice guy, taught all the material well. Participation not required, but recommended as it counts for 5% of your grade (polleverywhere). 3 main non-cumulative tests that are pretty hard and only have one practice test each. I didnt read the textbook, not necessary. I recommend going to lecture, quiz, and watching the videos for a good grade.

As long as you attend the lectures and do the work, you'll do well. Each class has questions you must answer for participation credit. The class is divided into three sections so there are three midterms (all non-cumulative). For each midterm there is a quiz and problem set (that you must do by hand) that goes for each one.

Lectures move quickly but content is somewhat manageable after rewatching and self-studying. Tests are only out of 24 points each so every small mistake is costly, but quizzes are straightforward and asynchronous. Problem sets are usually confusing, time-consuming, and don't completely align with core course content.

Not a great lecturer, hard to understand, and tends to go through his slides far too quickly. The problem sets take forever, and many of his questions tend to be worded strangely. TA was great and taught me far more than the professor. Only posts 1 practice exam per test, watch the pre-lecture recordings for the key concepts. Tests are pretty hard.

He's an amazing professor! He provided free textbook excerpts for the material covered, which made the class more accessible. His teaching style and resources show how much he cares about students' success. He helped me regain confidence in economics. Stay on top of assignments, watch the pre-lecture videos, and use the resources to do well! 😊
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class and found Ali to be a fantastic professor. You can tell he genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. The tests are difficult, however if you watch his pre-class videos, go to lecture, and do the problem sets you should be fine! I would recommend this class to anyone interested in macro.

Class was flipped learning, so video lectures for homework. Alright as a lecturer, but sometimes was a little confusing. My TA was not that good, so a lot of it was self study. Concepts can be harder to grasp, but exams weren't as bad as people say if you actually did everything he asked and studied before hand. Problem sets took a while tho.

Ali was a great professor for this class, especially because he was good at explaining the content in detail without brushing over important parts. Attendance was mandatory through poll everywhere, but there were some you could get dropped. The tests were difficult for some people, but I found that if I studied ahead of time they weren't that bad.

Want to experience wasting your life while fully conscious? Take him. He just reads blurry 2010 PowerPoints. Ask a question? He'll say "it's common sense" or tell you to read a book he hasn't mastered. Exams and lectures are in parallel universes. Unless you want to self-teach, STAY AWAY.

My experience of Econ 201:

I personally didn't like his lecture style, he speaks extremely slowly making it difficult to focus and I couldn't (and didn't) pay attention to any lecture. It's clear that he's a nice guy accessible for help, and provides plenty of resources (videos, homeworks, practice problems) to be successful anyway!

He does everything he can to help you succeed and grades on a curve. It is a very tough class because the concepts are very challenging. However, he goes above and beyond to provide information to help you succeed. There are readings, videos (max of 10 minutes), in depth lectures, and the power points are super thoughtfully crafted.

Class is graded on a huge curve at the end of the quarter because the class struggles on exams. MUST watch the videos before class, attend lectures, and go through the slides after class and that will set you up for success. Teacher has a great personality, just hard concepts for some students to understands.

Ali was a fantastic professor. He was passionate about the material and did his best to connect what we covered with real-world events. He was also very accessible outside of class.  However, his exams were difficult, and there wasn't as much prep material as I would've liked. Make sure to focus on drilling homework problems and asking questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a good professor and cares about his student's grades. His exams are pretty tough with averages being around 58% with tough and harsh grading. A fair amount of homework and the problem sets take A LOT of time. His lectures were informative but the chapters were very back and forth making it tough the follow.

he really does care about his student's learning and how to push us with the material. It definitely wasn't a super easy class, but I thought that it was intellectually stimulating and challenging in a good way. He seems to be very thoughtful and puts a lot of effort in our assignments and lectures to best serve the students

Professor Ali is very nice, however this course is a bit challenging, stress inducing, and takes up a lot of time. Maybe it's just a me problem, but I do watch all the assigned videos (average video is about 5-6 minutes, longest one so far is 11), take notes, and attend every lecture, yet I still struggle occasionally on problem sets and tests.

Half of the stuff on the exams the professor doesn't even talk about in class. Yet the class is still somehow so lecture heavy. I found it very hard to study for exams as the professor only uploads one practice exam for BOTH the midterms in this class. The professor is a cool guy don't get me wrong but this class is definitely my least favorite.

I am never the type of person to write something negative about a professor, but truly, Ali was not the professor for me. He jumps from topic to topic with no correlation and then comes back to a topic that isn't even relevant. He struggles getting his point across sometimes, but there are times when his lectures are ok.

Professor Ali is an excellent instructor. His lectures are clear, smooth, and humorous, making class engaging and enjoyable. He often encourages us to connect current events with course concepts, which deepens our understanding. The exams are a bit tough, but they truly push us to learn.

This is a super easy class. There are two Modern Focus videos per week that have short discussion and quiz that go along with it. Aside from that, there are three midterms that are pretty simple, all information is in the Canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Arch 150 is really awesome, I recommend it to anyone needing A&H credit.
Super easy class you don't even have to do all the discussion posts and quizzes. There is a textbook but you really don't need it at all. Some busy work but it's pretty easy.

It's two discussion posts a week. Two homework assignments the entire quarter that are maybe an hour each. The videos are actually interesting and like 5 minutes long. I got literally full points in this class without the textbook but it's technically there. Tests are all open note and online sooooo
Super chill class, great professor
I took this class online and it took maybe 30 minutes a week. Super easy A and an A&H credit. Just have a few small assignments per week and 3 tests total.

This class consists of discussions, super easy quizzes with unlimited tries, readings, a few assignments, and a few tests. You can get extra credit by doing more than the required amount of discussions. Personally, I thought this course was quite interesting, but it is very history and architectural design elements heavy, which may not be for all.

Arch 150 was really chill class. You just do the discussions and modern focus quizzes on canvas for homework. Take notes on canvas lessons consistently because they can stack up and that wasn't pleasant. There's textbook but it's useless. Study buildings on study guide before tests. Overall, 100% manageable.

Do not take this class unless you are actually interested in the boring history of buildings and civilizations. I regret taking this class. The only way you know what to take notes of is by going to the end of the section, looking at the test study guide, and taking notes every time you hear that vocabulary term or building (he wont tell you).
You don't really need the textbook. Just do the assignments, which are easy, and make sure you know what the buildings and landmarks in the study guide look like.

This class was great! Everything is done via learning modules and recorded lectures. The lectures are short but engaging. There are discussions every week, 3 tests and 2 assignments. Everything was pretty straightforward. I took this as an elective, so I didn't have much time to dedicate but it was managable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Gives great lectures and easy to reach. The class is easy to get 4.0 and contents are interesting.

This class was genuinely the most boring class I have ever taken at this school. While Prof. Anderson was just fine, I saw very little of him. The vast majority of the class was just reading and reading and more reading about very specific architectural details that I did not care for. Not a hard class, but not fun by any means.
I took that in SP 24. It was an easy A+ class if u submit all assignment on time. He offered few extra credit ( ~ 1.5 ish? ) which could raise +0.1 for your final grade.
Lectures were interesting and insightful.
A+ professor. Class was chill and laid back. Lectures were recorded and that helped a lot. Just need to keep up with lectures and you should get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love love love. It's a big class, but most students didn't attend after the first few weeks and either watched the lecture recordings or winged it. He's super engaging and funny!!
Interesting class to learn about architecture
He is one of the nicest professors at UW. I liked his lecture and the way he interacted with student. I recommend you to take this class offered offered with him if you need A&H credit.

I took this  because I thought it's an easy 4.0 but that's not true because the tests ended up being hard so you have to put in effort. There are no surprises so if you go to lecture you should be ok. Can't just read lecture slides because they have no info so you actually have to listen. As for Anderson himself, he is very kind and accommodating.
