I cannot think of a single bad thing to say about Amelia. The fact that her ratings are stellar on a website where people come to complain is very telling. She is caring, honest, and so understanding. Every single lecture was engaging and the material was fascinating. She is eager to help students and wants every student to succeed. Thanks Amelia!!

An extremely kind professor, Amelia cares about all of her students. She is very aware of how busy people are, and as a result makes sure that she is being reasonable with her workload. She gives very thorough feedback on writing assignments, and is very transparent about how she grades. 4.0 is easily attainable if you turn in all assignments.

Ms. Lehosit made the class very fun and interesting. She made it easy by grading using a grading contract, meaning that as long as you turn work in, then you would be guaranteed a 3.0 and then you can do extra stuff for a better grade. Ms. Lehosit also gave really great feedback that truly helped to improve my writing. I highly recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amelia is a great person and very passionate about English which makes class enjoyable. She's easily reachable and gives great feedback. Grading is completion-based to get a 3.0 and then you can do extra stuff to increase your grade which is nice. Assignments were reasonable and well explained.

Really great class and pretty easy too. Everything you need to do is clearly stated for each assignment and you're graded on a grading contract which means its easy to do well if you put in the work. Feedback on essays were really helpful.

The sweetest, most caring professor I've ever had. She leaves extensive comments on your papers and schedules short conferences to talk about your experience in the class. The class is graded with a guaranteed 3.0 and she adds to your GPA based on your attendance and your completion of every assignment.

Al-Wahish is very nice. She loves demos, and will occasionally spend most of demonstrating basic principles before rushing through much more complicated material. She assigns homework through the e-textbook which is frequently harder than either what is taught in class or what is on the tests. In-class questions are mandatory, completion based
Incredibly caring, passionate about what she's teaching, and wants you to succeed. Thought I didn't like physics until I took her class. Go to lecture and use the practice exams to study.

PHYS 114: passionate but horrible lecturer who can't bridge her knowledge to entry level. Attendance is mandatory but lecture is just doing practice problems, yet she expects you to have learned the subject AND completed the problems on lecture slides by the start of class. Homework website is held together by two lines of code and a prayer
Really good lectures and did a good job of breaking down concepts

Tests not bad if you studied and reasonable workload but I hated her lectures. I never asked questions bc whenever someone did she would embarrass them in front of the class/ make them sound dumb. Mandatory attendance questions were super annoying and lecture was not very helpful. I think she wanted us to learn but was too intense for intro physics

I went into physics not really caring about it, but Dr. al Wahish did a great job at inspiring her students because you can tell that she genuinely cares about their success. She is strict when it comes to talking in class, but I appreciate that because it leads to less distractions and helped me to focus. Overall, it was a good class to be in.

Wahish is the most passionate, caring, and inspiring professor I've ever taken. The lectures pass by so fast because they are genuinely so fun! The grading seemed intimidating at first, but she truly wants everyone to succeed, we we're usually curved up and given chances to recover points, and she offers so many opportunities to receive more help.

I really struggle with math courses, but Wahish was great! She's genuinely a great person and puts a lot of effort into making lectures enjoyable. The style of the class didn't really work for me (flipped classroom-ish) but I refuse to dock her points because I liked her that much. Definitely should do the optional practice problems though

I found her lecture to be enjoyable, with clear explanations of physics concepts and plenty of demonstrations. Despite having studied physics in high school, I still learned a lot from her. When I visited her during office hours, she provided thorough explanations for each problem.

She really cares a lot about her students and the lectures are fun to attend. The exams are pretty hard but watching her exam review and making sure that you know how to do all the problems from there really helps. There was also 4 pts extra credit for each final if you did corrections.

A wonderful and compassionate professor, she not only taught the lectures but also led the tutorials for Phys 115. The content she taught in tutorials often appearing on exams. Her caring and accommodating nature made the learning experience enjoyable and accessible for all students. Highly recommended to attend her exam review and office hours.

Had Al-Wahish for tutorial and she is a tough lady. Beware of quick cold-calling as well as her voice ringing her your ears for months. She is very book and calculation based for exams. Her way of teaching is also aggressive and confusing in my opinion.

At UW, she stands out as the most caring professor I met, consistently providing exceptional exam reviews. Never skip her lectures or office hours, recognizing the paramount importance of her exam overviews. Over 80% of her questions are reflections from materials covered in class, practice exams, and review sessions.

Over 80 percent of the questions on her exams from reflection prompts featured in her in-class quizzes, review sessions, and practice exams. I strongly advise attending her classes, working on her in-class quizzes,  and making use of her office hours to ensure you're well-prepared.

I enrolled in Phys 116 a while back, and it was an incredibly enriching experience. Recently, I revisited the lecture notes from that course to aid my understanding of my current classes. The quality of her lectures is outstanding, and she is a wonderful and caring professor. I highly recommended to attend her office hours.

She delivers outstanding lectures. She consistently inspires her students, employing both slides and the blackboard in her class. Attending her office hours proves advantageous, as she devotes a considerable amount of time explaining a variety of questions.

Wahish is the kind of professor who maintains high standards but provides all the resources necessary for success in the course. Despite the inherent difficulty of quantum mechanics, she refrained from adding unnecessary complexity. Her organization was impeccable, with well-structured lecture slides, and the assigned homework.

She stands out as the most compassionate professor. Having graduated, I made the decision to return to medical school. I reached out to all my former professors, requesting letters of recommendation. Out of everyone I contacted, she was the only one who responded to my email, offering encouragement and motivating me to pursue my dreams further.

She is the kindest professor I have encountered, exceptionally helpful with excellent lectures. Professor Wahish provides pre-lecture notes in advance and schedules all in-class quizzes at least a week beforehand. The quizzes are graded based on 0.8 participation and 0.2 accuracy, with a final quarter-end scaling of 1.25, ensuring full credit.

I would not recommend this teacher to anyone. This professor is very hard to understand, yells at students and randomly calls on students to answer questions during lecture. Also, there are in-class polls that are graded by accuracy, and the window to answer the questions is so small that there were many times I couldnt answer or just guessed.

I'm delighted that I enrolled in Phys 114 with Prof. Wahish. I'm currently enrolled in her Phys 115 class. She is not only kind but also helpful. I attended most of her office hours. I was disappointed of first exam score. However, after discussing it with her, she provided guidance on how to study more effectively. Thanks to her advice, I got A!

Professor Wahish is genuinely enthusiastic about physics. Her love for physics is contagious, creating an engaging and dynamic learning environment. Whether discussing classical mechanics or delving into the intricacies of quantum physics, she has a remarkable ability to ignite curiosity and foster a love for learning in her students.

I was dealing with personal issues that were affecting my focus on school, but Amal was a true lifesaver. She proactively reach out to me, offering support and guidance to help me regain my footing. Amal suggested various student resources at UW, and following her advice, I reached out to DRS for assistance with my anxiety. She's an excellent Prof

In times of adversity, I turned to her for guidance, and she played a crucial role in helping me navigate through the challenges. She is an outstanding professor, exemplifying the kind of support students require in today's world. She provided several examples from her research that were relevant to the lecture!

A wonderful and supportive professor. I visited her during office hours, and she generously assisted me after my DRS officer recommended it . I enrolled in Phys 114 with her, and I eagerly waited a whole year to take Phys 115 with her. I'm delighted that she is my professor again this year.

I enrolled in Prof.alWahish PHYS114 class during the summer and followed up with her Phys115 class in the fall. She has consistently ranked among my top professors here at UW, and she is genuinely altered my outlook on the student-teacher dynamic. She is an excellent Professor.
She is a great professor. I took her for 121 and 122. Love her engaging lectures, I actually looked forward to class. So, I took Phys225 and got major in Physics. Do your best and you'll be fine.

I had Amal for PHYS 114. She is incredibly helpful and kind. Her exams are tough, and the exercises explained in class are not clear proofs of what you will find in the exam. Go to office hours, she is so happy to help students!! study with practice exams. The grading criteria is on your favor, study hard and you will succeed

Took her class for phys 114. Sometimes she is difficult to understand. Class moves very fast so it is difficult to do well on exams. Maybe physics just isn't my thing, but I found the class very difficult to keep up with.

The most amazing professor at UW. She is smart professional teacher. She always helps her students. Very kind professor. People rate her down because they do not do well on her exams. If you study, attend her classes, and participate in the discussion, you will do very well in her class. I like when she gives real life examples in the class.
Awful teacher. Unless you want to hate yourself your life and hw forever do not take this. Yeah

She is one of the best profs in physics. Very good lectures, clear expectations, and unbelievably nice. Has many office hours where you can get lots of help on lecture and homework. It's really clear she wants you to succeed and you totally can if you put in the time. Go to class, ask her for help, and put time in to get the HW and you'll do great.

Professor al Wahish cares a lot about her students learning! I took her class the first quarter after covid hit and she really went put in the effort to do what she can to help. The class content is very difficult and I found that lecture material often didn't click until I went to office hours to fill in the gaps in comprehension.

Amal Al-Wahish did a fantastic job in teaching 122 and I end up with a 4.0. She made it a lot easier for people who went to her OFFICE HOUR! Lectures are recorded, but office hours matter. Participation is not mandatory but I strongly recommend bring questions to her office hours; it matters especially during exam weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: In all fairness physics 122 is a very hard class. But she does not make it any easier whatsoever.
Good professor, interesting content, lots of reading
Clarification - not JSIS 478, MELC 396

This is for JSIS 478. I loved the class! There was a reasonable amount of reading to do before classes, but it really contextualized the material covered in lectures. Field trips made the class super engaging too, I got to see Seattle from a different perspective and had fun applying it to the Middle East! I'd recommend the course and professor.
Great professor and interesting and interactive lectures!
The classes were very interesting, and Prof Shai does a great job of making all the students feel part of a community and bring them together. Classes were also very interactive.

Very rude and condescending, he shows no respect towards students. He will also point out criteria that you've somehow missed in assignments, even though he never clarified in the assignment guidelines that he was looking for it. Not worth taking the class with him even though the content is interesting.
The coursework was Instructure and not made easy for undergrad coursework. Wouldn't recommend

Very smart, nice professor, but not great at teaching beginners. 4 cases, 6 quizzes, and a group project. Cases required lecture material to complete. The lectures were confusing but after applying them to the cases, I understood better. Group project guidelines were broad, so we had to consult him and the TA for more clarity. Quizzes were easy.

Amandeep genuinely tries to teach this class at a level of technicality not found in the IS major. This class is VERY code-heavy, and if you treat this class like a coding boot camp, you'll 2x your python skillset. He's not great at making information easy for non-coders and is more of a graduate-level lecturer stuck with undergrads.

He's clearly a smart, nice guy but also seems very inexperienced in teaching beginner-level students. I was able to self-study to get by but I often felt like I wasn't making connections and understanding the material in class, to the point I wasn't even sure what questions to ask. Grading was generous. Don't get the book, it's not very technical.

I would not recommend anyone w/o experience in data analytics take this course. It was very unorganized, required a $125 book we didn't use & he had us use ChatGPT to write our code. There was very little instruction specifying the why and how of the code & attending class was a waste of time. Tests & assignments did not match the lecture material.
Professor was really nice and covered a lot of material that helped me get a job in analytics. I would definitely recommend taking the course.
This professor is too funny and her optimism is contagious
This professor has the right experience of work and in college. Brought a lot of experience to class. Also has a funny sense of humor!
Class was extremely stimulating and definitely stretched my thinking. It was very challenging and required a great amount of time.
The two cases study definitely helped us to comprehend the topics. Homework and quizzes are also very effective ways to learn in class.

Although somewhat time-consuming, I do think discussions before the lectures help with understanding the chapter better. The group project also helps summarize everything we learned into one final assignment.
This class was wonderful I feel I learned a lot and although the class periods were very long the instructor's effectiveness in keeping the class engaged was very high.

IF THIS PROFESSOR IS YOUR ONLY OPTION, YOU ARE BETTER OFF WAITING TO TAKE THE CLASS NEXT QUATER WITH SOMEONE ELSE THAN TAKING IT WITH HER. She just reads off slides, and god forbid you have a question. She will be so passive-aggressive and belittling you that it caused two students to leave the class and drop it.

Creates a very negative environment with her students. All of her quizzes and assignments are accessible online. Interrupts students while talking and doesn't give her students freedom to bounce ideas and talk with students properly. Reads off of slides and doesn't explain properly. All of her tests/quizzes are textbook heavy.

Apurva is uninteresting and the least engaging professor I have had throughout being at UW.  Luckily I have already taken a similar course so I did not struggle with the tests and quizzes but if it were the first time I was learning the material, it would be impossible.  The powerpoints are messy and the math is not clear (despite being easy).

i wouldn't wish him on my worst enemy. he said to the class before the last exam that if a few of us got similar grades he would select certain students to get certain grades based on who he likes as students better.
I used to really enjoy operations and supply chain management until I took his class. His lectures are somehow both confusing and boring.

I used to be super passionate about SCM...that is until I took Apurva's class. He made the content sound uninteresting, so I had to reevaluate what I wanted to do after graduating. He did not even grade our midterm, final, or group assignments and was passive-aggressive at times. He ranted so much, that there was nothing to study for for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very understanding and kind. He does not explain things very well and would always say, " You already know this" but he never taught it, he just expects you to know from other classes.

Apruva fails to convey basic instructions for students during lectures. 
His slides are completely awful, and confuses the students even more when he tries to explain the concepts. This is the definition of a tenured professor that should be reviewed for effectiveness of teaching.

Complete waste of time for MBA courses.

Professor Jain is passionate about the subject of SCM and Operations but is not the greatest teacher. Often his lectures are very hard to follow and require a lot of follow-ups to fully grasp concepts. His assignments are hard to understand and require a lot of background and time to complete. Luckily, the number of assignments is low.

His lectures could be hard to follow, but he has a lot of supplementary materials on Canvas that is easy to follow. Homework is collaborative, which could be heaven or hell depending on your partners. Very accessible outside class, and passionate about the material.

Homework problems arent explained in lectures, and wording was always super confusing. He would spend literally 30 minutes going on a tangent about one slide, and then after say that we dont need to know that info. The lectures were just super boring with all of the useless talking.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: We only covered a third of the material that we should have for the quarter, and I really didn't actually learn anything. I did well because I was willing to teach myself the concepts outside of class, but his lectures were confusing and all over the place. I wouldn't recommend taking him unless you're willing to teach yourself the material.
Professor Apurva is nice and friendly, his accent might be hard to understand at times.

Really cares about his students, super nice guy but very confusing lectures. No textbook required, prints out all material which is nice. Was very hard to follow and homework was mostly self-taught. Should go over more examples in class. Spends too much time on concepts not enough application. would not recommend this class

Professor Jain is probably one of the best professors in the OPMGT major. He is helpful, kind, and always willing to help. His homework and tests are clear, concise and he even records excel video tutorials to help you. He is awesome! I highly recommend him. Midterm/Final are open note/book.

I don't know who you are. I don't know what you want. If you are looking for ransom, I can tell you I don't have money. But what I do have are a very particular set of skills, skills I have acquired over a very long career. I will find you, and I will teach you.    - Apurva Jain

I wouldn't recommend Apurva in my wildest dreams. But, he's the only one who teaches this class! He spends the most time blabbering about the big picture but no one pays attention because it won't be tested. He has 2 simulation games which again teaches you nothing. He never tells you any grade stats for the class. I learned a whole lot of nothing.

Possibly the greatest Operations Teacher in the Foster School of Business. He designs his class in such a way that you really learn about all aspects of Supply-Chain Management and have a great time while doing so. He genuinely cares about each and every student. He let me reschedule my mid-term to attend the Seahawks Parade! AWESOME

Pretty solid class, very straight forward and you learn a lot of stuff applicable to real life businesses.  Apurva uses no textbook for his class (only print out slides).  Tests are fairly easy and straightforward, just make sure you leave two or three days to study.  Like most classes, you get what you put in.
Apruva is a great teacher. He uses a lot of great examples to illustrate concepts. Class isn't too hard. However, he does have a thick accent which can be hard to listen to at times.
Very energetic about the subject. Also uses many informative/comedic real world examples.

Great professor! Really cares about his students and is very accessible. No textbook, he prints all the slides out for you, tests and homework are very straightforward and you're allowed to use a cheat sheet on the exams. Replies to email questions within an HOUR. Class is very relaxed, and he's funny!

Apurva is really pleasant in lecture, however, I don't think he's a very engaged professor. My biggest problem with him is his lack of clarity. For example, he'll ask a question on a prob set, and the answer he's looking for is not what he asked (I went back and compared the questions with his answer sheet).

i agree with with the person below. He is a nice guy and has the best intentions, but he really is not the best teacher. he teaching methods are confusing and tests are not really related to to the practice exams and homework. tests are woth 70% of grade. he was just not very helpful

He is a nice person, but he cannot teach. I hated all his lectures because all he does is asking you questions instead of TEACHING you. When studying for your tests, it's frustrating because he is so not consistent. I feel that the materials of Opt Mgmt are interesting, but he just makes them not. But, I got to say this tho. He is a good person.

BEST TEACHER EVER! His class was extrememly laid back and fun. He is really clear with what he want. He gives you 3 Hw assignments over the quarter that help prepare you for his tests which are not hard if you did the hw. Overall he wants you to succeed and do well. Friendly, Great Guy. The class was always exciting. Take Him!! you learn a lot.
His class was very clear, interesting and engaging.  He seemed very much to care about his students, and was a pretty funny little man.
The class was not hard but she just gave a lot of work for students to do. She sometimes grade students unfairly. Overall do not recommend her online class at all.

Good prof. very helpful but she demands a lot out of her students, projects, group work, homework, participation in class. Her tests are extremely hard, be aware! Some of the hardest tests I've taken in my college career.
All around a solid prof.  Nothing spectacular that will blow you away but effective.  Exams a little tougher than everything else but not too bad.  Good teacher, nice person.

Overall, her class was ok.  She tries to make the class interesting by doing class activities.  She gives out a lot of assignments, some which are a bit high-school, but she's pretty lenient on those.  Her exams are pretty hard though.
Overall, I liked her class. She definetely gives out hard exams, but she grades other assignments preatty easy. She also gives out a lot of assignments, and topics can be boring.

Poorly done intro class. She is obsessed with MKTG research. The is a ton of work to do in this class, multiple HW, case studies, group project. She grades all those really easy. Her tests are very hard and she grades them really hard, too!

Her lectures were short but they were well delivered and pretty fun. She has a lot of knowledge about journalism and if you talk to her in office hours, she is really an amazing person. In this crazy covid times she was very understanding and gave everyone a pass that they could use for regrading. It was an easy class but I learnt a lot.

Had 10min lectures each week. No direction. Didnt grade all quarter. Then gave a few harsh grades with no feedback. Barely any assignments but weighted heavily. I was excited for this class and learned nothing.

I dont really know what happened in this class. We didnt have lectures for the last 2 weeks before our final paper was due. We didnt have much direction with our work, but she graded easily. Participation will get you a 4.0, but its hard to learn a lot in this class.

She doesn't sugar coat things, but everything she tells you is constructive. Her experience as a journalist and her educational background give her really good insight on storytelling, and data mining.
Aparna is a TA for a lot of com classes and she gives good feedback! She is very experienced and provides good advice and supplemental materials so we can learn
I had Aparna as a TA for COM360 and COM362. She has lots of great advice and truly cares about the well-being of her students. Would recommend again.
Love Aparna, she keeps it real and cares about our learning

She was my TA for COM 360. Always gave thoughtful feedback and was available for additional help. Gave great advice and reviewed journalism internships / resumes / cover letters. A really funny and genuinely amazing TA.

Prof. Craig is super kind and passionate about the subject matter. Overall this class was pretty easy with minimal work. I found most of the topics covered in class interesting. She also hosts great guest lectures. I really recommend this class as an elective or for someone who is potentially interested in studying wildlife.

Extremely easy class. Just review the slides and take some rough notes, do the quizzes after class, and you'll definitely pass. I bombed the final because I had to prioritize other classes and didn't study at all (24/50) and still ended with a 3.8 from other work I did. Final & paper constitutes most of your grade but relatively easy.

Lectures are pretty boring but Apryle seems to be excited by the content. Worst part of the class was the day she dedicated to talk about plagiarism and academic integrity, cool I've heard it 50 times. Every class had a lecture quiz following it that was pretty easy if you just look at the slides but some were more tricky.

she is really sweet and cares about what she is teaching. there are discussion posts & quizzes every week, two (cumulative, open-note) tests, and one paper. it's a pretty easy class online but there is a lot of information shoved in your face every week. kind of boring, but there is some important information you can carry with you from this class

She seems really nice in person, but when she can hide behind a keyboard is a bit mean. On one occasion she discriminated against me because of my race and gender. She would randomly cancel class several times a semester without an explanation. She is enthusiastic about the topic, but the way she presents it is a mess. The readings are outdated.

Great teacher, difficult midterm and final exam but if you pay attention in class, show up to the lectures, read the material, and participate you should be fine. Not may grades other than the weekly discussion questions. Do well on exams and the presentation or you won't do well at all in the class.
I received a lower score than I would have liked

I took this class in a small seminar-like setting in the evening. She is always very smartly dressed. Lectures go over most of the reading (which are from online links, not a textbook), so they're not that necessary to read thoroughly, just skim. She is always very impassioned about the subjects and I really enjoyed the class.

She understands the topic, but doesn't teach it in a way for students to understand. "Textbook" is a compilation of various articles, many that are outdated & hard reads. Exams are essay style. Would help if she posted her slides before class so you can take notes on them. Barely got a C, regularly an A student. Whole class struggled. GPA buster.
A lot of things to do. She appreciated what you did but gave you a very low grade. She hided in the syllabus how she was going to grade you. I calculated myself: 85%=2.5... 95%=3.5  Very harsh.

Very nice lady, good at explaining concepts. However, her tests and quizzes can be tricky. You may know how to do the exercises but in exams they may be presented differently. The final was ridiculous, she didn't even show the statistics unlike the previous tests.

She's a great and lovable person, but... when explaining examples she moved extremely fast. I would definitely like more organized and systematic explanations. More often than not it was hard for me to follow her. Also I feel there was a lack of clear connection between the chapters.

I've talked to a lot of my friends prior to taking Math 308 and they said that it is a very abstract and confusing class. However, Prof. Camili makes these abstract concepts understandable and her lectures are very clear. She is a pretty enthusiastic teacher and she is very helpful during office hours. Take a math class with her if you can!

Makes an abstract subject like linear algebra understandable.  Clear explanations and she's quite enthusiastic about teaching math which is always a plus!  One little downside is that she speaks kind of fast so for a slow note taker like me, it's sometimes hard to keep up.
Great instructor and super hot!
I learned so much from this class. Very easy concepts. She made math 307 easier to understand.
Lectures can be confusing.  I learned more from reading the book and looking at examples.
Lectures are extremely confusing and hard to understand.

One of the harshest grade scales I've seen. Professor Banerjee had no desire to teach this class and it showed. Almost everything I learned was from the textbook and I felt better off on the tests by just teaching myself. Very boring lectures with no enthusiasm. The course content was not difficult but the professor made it hard to get a grade.
Lectures were boring and monotone, harsh grading in comparison to dawg path, try to take a different prof

The class material wasn't too bad and the practice exams prepared you really well for the exams. He definitely knows his content. However, lectures were all over the place rambling, difficult to follow, generally irrelevant. You're better off just teaching yourself. Tight scale 98% 4.0, then every percent after that was 0.1GPA less
it was a forgettable experience. So boring, can put a dead man to sleep

He is a bit monotone, but he clearly knows his material very well. I think his quizzes are challenging but fair. I would take again, I liked him and the class. They should shorten the class for the non tour days for sure. Consider it a pretty easy grade, and a good intro to the major.
This class was extremely boring. Lectures were dry and unengaging. I didn't feel like I learned much and ended up teaching myself most of the material.

If I'm a sophomore or junior taking his 337 class I'd just quit the major honestly, his class was so boring and the fact that he was forced to teach this make me so sad. He's made to do great research, not for lecturing 3.33 hours in IEB where almost everyone is on their phone or laptop. 3 factory tours only? The previous class got 5 tours! Robbed!

Most boring class I have ever take in UW. The course content is so important that the lectures shouldn't be presented by professor like this. He's just look at a single slides talk about whatever he thought about, and test it in the quiz
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Waste of time. Never had a class that had so much hype that delivered so little. Truly one of the most boring classes in this University as even interesting concepts that are crucial to the major are made horrifically stale. Equivalent to stale bread. Not a single person doesn't watch youtube and you are expected to take notes when you can't.

Banerjee's lecture style is awful; he rambles constantly, asks questions, and looks at the class with a blank stare. The class is very unorganized, and the content you are tested on or write about has minimal to do with in-class lectures. The class isn't challenging, but it is tough to engage with, and the lectures feel like a waste of time.

Lectures were poorly executed, and Prof. Banerjee fails to emphasize important topics and communicating his expectations. The quizzes and homework felt irrelevant to his lectures. Be prepared to be tested on niche topics that he does not make clear in lectures.
Super lecture dense, the quizzes are way harder than the material. He said that some stuff wasn't going to be on the quiz and it was. Grading rubrics are very vague.

Unclear and arbitrary grading criteria. Answers will be graded wrong for not using the desired phrasing, even if the idea is the exact same. 
Tests and homework are not related.

Lectures were incredibly dense and meandering. Prof would lag for 10 minutes on one slide only to speed through others. Homework and test questions were sometimes on a) material not covered in lecture b) material Prof said ONCE in lecture and is inaccessible anywhere else. Thankfully, he barely touched shop time, the sole saving grace of this class

Lectures were vague and also rarely gave helpful, detailed answers if people had questions. Questions on the test were too specific, making them nearly impossible to solve given the sheer amount of material covered, as well as the vague examples given in class.

Despite asking for further clarification, his homework assignments were still extremely vague and the grading policy regarding what correct answers would actually garner credit was extremely unclear. This was compounded by his poor performance as a lecturer that made answering homework questions even more difficult in the first place.
Really bad at teaching and explaining. Not intuitive and boring class I ever taken

Nearly impossible to stay engaged. Lots of rambling and very little information in lecture slides. TA graded every assignment leniently, but come group project time, Prof Banerjee decided to grade non-transparently without any rubric made public to anyone. Told no one he would grade on a curve, then made 0.1 GPA increments decided by 0.75%

Lectures are basically useless ramblings. The most frustrating part of this class (I took mfg processes online) was the vagueness of grading criterion. He will ask you to explain why X happens, then mark you down for not A) hitting EVERY detail when you hit most, and for B) not including 4 examples when the question doesnt specify you include any

The best advice I can give you is to read the book. Professor Banerjees lectures are useless. He doesn't go in to detail about anything but will expect you to know in depth material for the test. You're better off not even going to class and just teaching yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: His lectures are eloquent and rehearsed, I'll give him that. However I don't know how someone can say so much in a lecture yet have all of it be completely useless information. Be prepared to prove equations in order to learn the different manufacturing processes (no, you didn't misread that).

The class was on manufacturing processes, but exams have absolutely nothing to do with manufacturing. Get ready to derive pointless equations that you'll never use in your career. Oh all within a 50-minute time period. You will need to find a solutions manual and scour through the book in order to get some understanding.

Good class overall. The course is very lecture-heavy, and attending class regularly is important to do well. The professor made the material engaging, clear, and easy to understand. The textbook was not necessary, as all exam material came directly from the lecture slides. Exams were straightforward and closely reflected what was covered in class.

Professor Cansunar was actually very good! She is very excited, friendly and has a lot of knowledge. She has a unique way to give her lectures, bringing many examples and trying her best to make us understand the topic. It's not a class with many assignments, so really study for midterm and final, otherwise your grade will drop easily.

Lectures are informative and engaging! You don't really need to do the readings; the lecture slides cover everything you need to know. The midterm and final are the same format: 2-3 long answer questions with multiple parts. Be sure to include examples with your responses, as just explaining the concepts the question asks about is not enough.

I loved this class and Prof. Cansunar. Never did any of the readings as everything you need to know is in the lecture/slides. Lectures are engaging but can be information heavy so make sure to review them. Prof. and TAs were very caring and tried their best to make sure students were succeeding. Overall just a great intro polisci class!

She was a great professor and explained very well. You don't need to do the reading to pass but if you want an A i would recommend as she likes clear explanations for the tests. Most of the content needed to memorize is on the slides which she posts!

She's SO funny I love her, lectures were always so engaging and you can tell how passionate she is about the subject matter. Grading CAN be strict but she always wants her students to succeed, I got a 70% on my midterm and the entire class did bad so she offered a 5% extra credit boost to our overall grade in the class to help us out. Got that 4.0!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A solid intro POL S class. Very nice professor and goes in-depth in lectures. The discussion questions and country report aren't too bad. The midterm was graded pretty harshly and the average was low, but extra credit offered. Don't bother with the textbook readings just focus on the lectures.

Asil Cansunar is a really nice and funny prof. She goes pretty in-depth into the topics. Never did the readings because she goes over them in lecture. Exam was graded very hard though, class average was a C and the main reason given was that we did not write enough even though TA's told us to not write that much.......kinda contradicting

Asli is a great professor who is very knowledgable on the subject matter. Her slides are clear and straightforward, and as long as you understand them, you'll do perfectly fine on the midterms. My TA was wonderful as well, overall a solid pol s intro course.

Prof. Cansunar is great! Super helpful and passionate about the subject matter. Lectures aren't recorded but if you read the slides you'll be ok. Def don't need to do the readings but the ones that aren't from the textbook are pretty good.

Prof Cansunar is passionate, knowledgeable, and entertaining. Don't do the textbook readings, she covers what the textbook covers in a chapter in the first few minutes of lecture, and in a much more engaging way. She is skilled at showing how multifaceted a lot of these topics are. Always willing to answer questions and clearly an expert in POL S.

Lectures and content from Cansunar were rarely dry and were often entertaining. The professor herself is a good person and cares about the content she teaches, as well as her students. Only complaint I have is my TA. The political science TAs at the UW tend to have favorites, which is reflected in the grading. Get on the good side of your TA!
Very kind and knowledgeable professor, put in effort and you will easily succeed in this class

Prof Cansunar is really sweet and super smart about many issues and does a great job quickly explaining historical scenarios. She also does take student feedback and even retaught slides when the TAs communicated that most of the students found it confusing. Her lectures kept me pretty well engaged for the 2ish hour slot, which is always nice.

She is a good professor, clearly knows her stuff, and her lectures are pretty engaging. However, the class feels pretty disorganized, the grading criteria is not clear and you are graded by a few things (Midterm, final and an essay). The readings are pretty long, although not necessary if you attend lectures since she pretty much covers everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures can be broad and boring, but the information is pertinent to many other political science classes. It's easy to succeed even without doing readings and viewing online lecture slides. She is a caring and inspirational teacher, although TAs, especially Yusri can make the class more confusing and grades somewhat harsh/without clear criteria!
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I think that Dr. Cansunar is the most inspiring professor at the University of Washington. I was honored to be in her class. It is clear in her lecturing that she is extraordinarily knowledgeable about comparative politics and comparative political economy. Furthermore, she is very helpful during office hours.

Professor Cansunar is an amazing lecturer who puts lots of care and personality into every meeting in class. However, beware of harsh TA graders! Section did not prepare anyone in class at all for the midterm, and has been defacto useless. There are no clear rubrics for grading. Avoid this class if Yusri Supiyan is your TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures are very boring and this class is structered around very broad material, but the class was very easy overall! She posts all the lecture slides online (which is great if you choose to skip class), and only has 2 midterms and an easy country paper/presentation. She is a very kind professor that wants you to succeed in her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Prof Cansunar is great! Thanks to her engaging explanations, the in-class content is incredibly clear. The grading on the exams was fair, especially thanks to a review prior to the final. All info came from slides. Discussion-based quiz sections were a highlight and Nela made it very accessible to participate! Def recommend for a POL S intro class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Cansunar is one of the best professors I have had. She makes the lectures fun and you can tell she really cares about her students and our success. The substance of the class is so interesting and the assignments/exams are quite straightforward due to how she lectures. I had a TA named Nela who was a huge help in section. 10/10 course.

2 non-cumulative online midterms, country presentation & report (very easy), and section participation. Cansunar is a great lecturer and is the sweetest prof I've had. Her slides are easy to follow and the content is so interesting (also available on canvas!). Nela is an excellent TA and makes section super helpful! One of my favorite classes!

Professor Cansunar is great during her lectures. I would say grading on the exam is very unclear. I have knocked off points for something that wasn't even in the question. I also tested positive for covid 10 minutes before the exam and emailed my TA and didn't hear back until I send a third email. Professors are great but beware of crappy TAs

Prof Cansunar provides great slides for her lectures, is passionate about the lessons, and her lectures are detailed, but easy to understand. She doesn't record her class but posts her 40-page powerpoints. Great sections/TAs, but definitely do the reading, as the quiz sections are based primarily on the reading. Exams were only a midterm and final.

Taking PHIL 320. She's the type of person that takes herself too seriously. Her grading is atrociously difficult, and I have no idea why she keeps calling in-class quizzes/exams as "assignments". They're not. The only good thing is her lectures, but other philosophy professors are good at those too. Don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Extremely harsh grader with not enough support given on assignments for students to understand how to get a better grade. Weekly pop quizzes on readings, and often two in-class testing assignments a week. Does not allow any technology whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Not even strictness it's just full on unfair grading, being ok with the majority of the class doing awful on essays because that's just 'how it goes'.It would give us more to strive for if the harsh grading wasn't as intense but it truly feels like spite even sending out passive aggressive announcements to students that feel completely unnecessary.

Currently taking PHIL 320. Good lectures. EXTREMELY HARSH GRADING. Almost impossible even for Phil majors to get a perfect score on ANY of the 5 IN-CLASS Argument Reconstruction & 4 Passage Analysis assignments, even with 2 scores dropped. Don't recommend. Love the content, but this class will cause enormous anxiety that's not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I was honestly a little intimidated taking one of her classes based on the previous feedback here, but now I can't recommend her enough! She is a thoughtful grader who does not tolerate laziness in her class. Stay on top of the readings, come to class, and rely on her previous feedback for assignments and you'll do great! :)

Professor Assaturian is easily one of the best I have had at UW. While she is a tough grader and doesn't tolerate laziness you will learn and grow in her class if you choose to take a class with her. She is committed to excellence and that encompasses her style of teaching and the expectations she has for her students. Take her class!

She could be considered a tough grader for some, especially if you don't follow the rubric for the writing analysis. If you're one of these, I would suggest going to office hours, so you can understand what you're doing wrong. Gives great feedback though. Quizzes are easy as long as you read, which is cool. Other than that straightforward class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She was really wonderful! If you show up to EVERY CLASS and engage with both her and the material, you will do really well. She is very knowledgeable about the Republic and Plato in general. She does not care at ALL about your personal take on the content, but rather your grasp of Plato's claims. Really great class, can't recommend enough.

Sosseh is a tough grader in comparison to other professors who tacitly operate on a completion-based criteria. Yes, there is a lot of reading. But for a history of philosophy class that is to be expected. Maybe I just loved the Republic but I can honestly say this class and her contributions to it made me contemplate the form of Pedagogy.

Either everyone in these reviews is pulling my leg or I am GOATED, either way this class is not a 5 in difficulty. Really interesting lectures and made the Republic very easy to follow. Would for sure take one of her classes again
She considers a 7/10 to be above the class average. Very hard grader. Going to class is enough, must go to office hours for better understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Though professor as you may experience very high standards from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The topic sounds very intimidating; but Prof. Ashleigh made it super interesting and undergrad-friendly. No exams; grade is determined by a reasonable spread of paper, reviews, design projects, and assignments. Definitely recommend for STEM majors that want an introduction to bioengineering/contemporary research :)

Prof. Theberge utilizes whiteboard lectures more than lecture slides, which makes the material much easier to digest. She knows a lot about the subject and is able to explain things in detail, and is very accessible outside of class. The labs are very time consuming, but apply to the course content very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Theberge is one of my favorite chem professors at UW. She’s willing to help students and shes passionate about her work/research which is super cool!
Coolest class I've taken!
Great lectures and clearly passionate about topics, lots of reading and some difficult assignments
Really enthusiastic and knowledgeable about the subject. The class is manageable as long as you're diligent about the reading.

She is very energetic and enthusiastic about classics. At first, her enthusiasm was a little hard to get use to but, trust me, by the middle of the quarter, you really appreciate it because she makes the class more bearable. There is a ton of reading so be careful when putting together you schedule.

Ashli is an awesome teacher! Super high energy and happy. Really easy to talk to and ask questions. I would DEFINITELY recommend her highly if you get a chance. the class is not difficult but very interesting!
excellent teacher, learned a lot, really easy class
She is amazing... very articulate, funny, and cheerful. It's actually a useful class too!
Amazing professor. Great lectures and thoughtful class discussions. This is what the university experience is supposed to be like.

His small classes are almost exclusively discussion based. A good assignment structure- a few short response papers based on class readings and offers good feedback and direction on what thoughts might be particularly fun to discuss as a whole class. Assigned a final paper with a broad prompt. He practices what he preaches. Very cool guy overall.

Prakash is awesome. The best professor I have ever had at UW. Always encourages respectful debate in an academic environment that is often hostile to independent thought. The lectures are long, but he is a very engaging instructor.
Professor Prakash was great. He challenges the way you think and promotes great discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is nice. If you show up you'll do well.

Aseem was one of my favorite professors at UW. Class is discussion-based on the readings. There are 6 one-page papers, 3 two-page papers, a research paper, and a presentation. He is intelligent, cares about student opinions, and is so funny. He offers rebuttals to your opinions to get you to think deeper but not insultingly. I 100% recommend him!

Professor Prakash is super nice and he really loves the show Yellowstone. His goal is to challenge the way we think, and he does a good job without making you feel stupid or attacked. The lectures are long but worth it, and the paper prompts are well-considered and easy to write to (in my opinion). The readings are short and fit the lectures well.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prakash is super passionate about the topic and really pushed students to engage. His TA is also a great resource. The course load is fair, just make sure to attend class. Only critique I have is the essays had little to do with information covered in class. If you do not already have a grasp of world politics, you will need to put in extra work.

Professor Prakash is awesome! Hes a bit intimidating at first, but is caring, wants you to succeed, and will give you extensions and let you do make-up work if you communicate. Hell push you to defend your opinions, so be ready to explain your thoughts. Hes always open to feedback and will take it to heart. He also emails back very quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Overall, pretty interesting class! The hardest part about this course was participation, even more so than homework. Prof. Prakash says that he likes to push his students, so come to class prepared to state and defend your opinion. He is also very responsive to feedback and modified the workload based on the results of a midterm course evaluation.
Wow. Just wow! Probably one of the greatest professor that I've had in the Political Science and JSIS department. I would highly recommend taking his course if you have an opportunity to do so.

Hands down the best prof. I've ever had. He pushed people to be able to develop multiple skills in his class, and challenges you to defend your ideas without being a jerk. He's extremely intelligent but wants everyone to share their intelligence as well. He is funny, smart, and genuinely seems to care about your ability to grow during his class.

Prof. Prakash, at a school with a humanities department that wants to push their opinions on you at every second, is a wonderful anomaly at UW. The lectures were genuinely amazing, he pushes everyone to analyze their own opinions and see other sides. He's extremely intelligent, caring, and subtly very funny. Class discussions were the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: best prof in uw. really good discussions. he will challenge you.

Prakash was the best professor I've had so far. Lectures are engaging and the structure of the class was great. Grading is based on pop quizzes, two papers and a group project. No exams & no textbooks. Don't skip class and do all the readings, just assume there will be a pop quiz every day. The quizzes usually just ask your opinion on the readings
Great professor! Pretty funny. Interesting topics discussed in class

Prakash by far is my favorite professor here at UW, he engages, listens, and is never polarizing in his lectures. He encourages students to think and critically analyze every aspect/contributor  to a situation. I've taken two classes taught by him, and would love to take another.
I took his environmental politics class last quarter. amazing class. changed the way i think about environmental issues, very good professor. great discussions. makes you read a lot

He is definitely the best professor I have had at the U. He is so engaging, and while the class can be demanding with weekly readings and article memos, there was never a day I didn't step out of class in awe. Trying DESPERATELY to change my work schedule to take his class this quarter! Very rewarding!
Very engaging, fosters discussion better than any professor I've had, no tests outside of pop quizzes that are pass/fail (there were 6-8), and two essays that were reasonably graded.
Really good discussions. The professor knows a lot. There are not mid term or end term exams. He has class quizzes which are quite easy. I like the presentations. Guest speakers were great.

Really interesting class. Best thing about it - NO TESTS. There were written pop quizzes at the end of some classes, ensuring attendance, but they were pass/fail only (I totally BSed one and got credit). If you put some effort into the three papers and the presentation, you should do great. Also there is a lot of interesting class discussion.

this is the best course i have taken at UW. the professor has a unique perspective on NGOs and knows a lot. It has made me think about NGOs in a new way. There is a lot a reading and the professor makes us write weekly article memos.
smart professor. Lots of class participation.
really good and funny. knows a lot. don't like the quizes
clear and funny
Outstanding instructor. Knows a lot. I love hearing him lecture.

He is one of the most influential professors I've had at UW. Incredibly knowledgable, and greatly respected in the Political Science community. If you put in the effort, you will do well in his class. He really wants his students to succeed.

I took American foreign policy with aseem and he is probably the most awesome teachers to sit there and listen to assuming you really enjoy political science. He has had a cool career and interesting life and seems endlessly knowledgable about everything he discusses. Papers are easy cause the don't pertain to lectures, just go to class for popquiz

This was one of the worst classes I have taken. It should be listed as a 200 level history class. The professor just rambles in lecture, there is little, if any, structure to his course and it has little to nothing to say about how American Foreign Policy is made. I'm a Jackson School senior and I took it for track requirements, I regret it.

Prakash's lecture was more of a indoctrination into his realist paradigm. His lectures provided no alternative view points, but only his slanted ideology.   He had random pop quizzes on the readings, sometimes the quizzes were given the day a paper was due.  The grading is also ridicules. To get a 4.0  you would have to have between 99% to 100%.

Prakash really enjoys class discussions and encourages everyone to participate. There is a lot of reading, but the pop quizzes are fairly simple. There are no midterms/final, just essays and a class presentation. This class helps you to develop a perspective on American foreign policy; extensive notetaking is not necessary

The "US Foreign Policy Class" I took was nothing more than a weak history lesson with his own speculations inserted. Not an academic class. No logical structure or organization of concepts or theories. I went every day because of the pop quizes and got nothing at all from this class. Complete waste of time.

His propensity for critical thought is amazing. In my 2 years at UW, he's the only teacher that I could just go on listening to: I never want him to shut up. He makes everything relevant and important to you. Clarify papers with him, though, prompts can be very misleading. Don't miss lecture - you won't get much from slides, and he has pop quizzes.

He used to be a theater major so he is very enthusiastic about accounting and his exams are a big chunk of his grading scale but hoping to bully him into lowering the weight of them. Buy him stock in Joe's Chocolate for extra credit!
He teaches the subject well and is very approachable however this class is so unreasonably difficult

I struggled pretty hard in this class. The lectures were at 8:30am and were boring. Going to the quiz sections led by the TAs helped a lot. Two midterms, one final, and a few quizzes. They drop the lowest quiz score and offer a couple extra credit opportunities. Overall I recommend staying on top of lectures/hw, and find people to study with.

Generous in grading cases and giving partial credit on exams. Very approachable and helpful in answering questions but generally sticks to the content. Got out of class early on occasion (what a treat!). The class is only as difficult as the content. 3 exams, noncumulative, the second one is the hardest IMO. My favorite of the intermediate profs.

Ash is a great professor. He is approachable and is willing to help with what you struggle in class. He lectures can be engaging or a little slow at times depending time of day. Hw is due 1-2 times a week which is manageable but what takes the most time is studying for the quizzes and exams which take up a huge portion of the grades. Mostly exams.

This class was okay. It made be realize that business just isn't for me but overall he is a decent professor. He is very passionate about what he teaches which helps the lectures to be slightly more interesting.

I think that he does a good job teaching the material. He answers emails quickly and isn't difficult to reach outside of class. However, he focuses a lot on journal entries in the course, but the quiz and exams are more comprehensive than what he lectures on. I recommend reading the textbook as well.

Ashwin was my TA for INFO 201. Learning was a little difficult due to lecture being online, but ashwin tried bridging this gap as best as he could during section. He was very responsive even at off-hours and helped debug code during meetings even around midnight. Would definitely recommend taking INFO 201 with him.

Very good TA and allowed students to ask many questions throughout lab sections. He was always prompt when showing up to class and lab which allowed students to get the most out of him. Definitely a cool guy to be around. He helped me with my networks issue in an internship outside of the University and really explained the issues we had.

TA Subbaraman is an amazing TA. He would always help me understand the whole network and answered all my follow up questions. He would stay after the scheduled time in order to help students and was always happy to help. He is very good at explaining tough concepts to students and I found him to be very helpful when it came to homework assignments!

Professor Subbaraman was a wonderful professor/TA and honestly made this class so much easier. His explanations were very thorough throughout the quarter and he gave us many chances to ask questions for further guidance. He was always showing up to class with a smile on his face and excited to teach us. I love Subbaraman and recommend him!

Throughout my entire academic career, I have not encountered a more passionate and genuinely inspirational professor. Every class brings something exciting and you end up wanting to do more than necessary just because of how engaging Arar makes the class. The lectures and assignments are so fun and interactive, you apply everything you learn.

Prof Arar is amazing!! She gets to know her students and cares, adjusting the class schedule if something works better/worse. She's very energetic in lecture and looks for participation and good writing. Expectations for the class are balanced and she gives great feedback with freedom for creativity, I literally wrote my midterm on Minecraft lol
Very helpful and wanted to see all her students succeed. Provided lots of extra credit opportunities and kept us engaged during lectures.

Professor Arar is by far one of the most impactful professors I've had here at UW. The readings are really interesting and she tried to cater to our schedules which is basically unheard of, but much appreciated by the class. Arar is an incredible human being alongside being an incredible professor.

Professor Arar cares. A lot. From the first day of course, she was constantly adapting class structure, which, at times, made it feel disorganized, but meant we'd always be doing something new. Prof. Arar's energy was infectious! Class participation is a clear value of hers, so participate and it will pay off. She wants to get to know everyone!

Professor Arar is quite literally the best professor I have ever had at UW. She is genuinely so kind and incredibly passionate about the content she teaches. Her seminar class has a lot of reading but all of the readings are incredibly interesting so there's incentive to do them. I highly highly highly recommend taking her class!

I loved taking the LSJ immigration course from Rawan! She is incredibly caring and loves her students, and as long as you are trying she is happy to chat with you. She was very accommodating during COVID, lots of reading but she makes it fun. I would take another course from her in a heartbeat!

Professor Arar is very kind and approachable. She certainly exhibits what it means to be a compassionate professor and gives great advice. This class really helped expand my thinking on topics surrounding immigration and rights. All the readings and assignments we did were interesting. By far one of my top favorite classes in the LSJ department.

She's very nice and accommodating. She puts a lot of effort into her lectures and goes above and beyond answering students' questions. Some stuff may be review if you've taken many LSJ classes. If you actively participate and do the readings, you will get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Arar is very sweet and genuinely loves teaching. Her projects and group activities can feel disorganized, but she really tries to make class fun. Lots of good info and readings. Everyone should take this class if they want an idea of how immigration works in the real world.

He is disorganized and does not take his teaching seriously. He often makes unnecessary jokes and spends class time talking about his personal life and activist concerns rather than focusing on the course material. I would not recommend taking his class if you are looking for a structured and academically rigorous learning experience.

Unorganized most of the time. Lectures often felt like his personal show rather than a class. He makes constant jokes about himself, which he may think are relatable, but they become distracting and uncomfortable. Instead of teaching, he focuses on his “activism,” which feels insincere and more like self-promotion than real engagement.
Very antisemitic and even anti-Islam. You can find everything in his class except knowledge. I would never take a class with him again.

I would prefer not to take another class with this professor. The course often felt unorganized, with frequent joking in place of structured instruction and no clear rubrics or expectations for each session. This experience highlights some of the ongoing issues within the Persian program at UW.

Aria's class was one of the few that not only imparts knowledge but also teaches critical thinking and the ability to question issues. He is super caring, kind, and flexible with deadlines:) . The class was fun and insightful at the same time. As long as you do the homework assignments, and respect the class you'll do fine.
Professor Fani is easy to communicate. He's clear on instructions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Aria is one of my favorite professors at UW! He really cares about his students and the content he is teaching. His class content is really powerful.
I love Aria! He's such a great professor and kindhearted person. I can tell that he really cares for his students, the content he teaches, and current world events.

Professor Aria was definitely my favorite professor I've ever had. He was always willing to help when needed, and was available through email always. He's very funny and genuinely cares about your education and what's happening in your life. He gave a clear schedule of the weeks and I highly highly recommend any class taught by him

Prof. Aria is an amazing professor! He spends the first half of class with a brief lecture but the students really lead the discussion. He's very understanding and easy on grades but class is so much more interesting when you actually do the reading. For homework we got to do actual translations as well which was really fun. I definitely recommend!
Prof. Fani is a gem. If you want to take a class where you enjoy the experience, have fun, and learn valuable lessons, he is your professor.

Not sure what the other guy is talking about. The course is not recorded or live streamed and there are in-class activities, the professor is a great lecturer with tons of interesting case studies and details - so if you don't attend class how are you going to learn anything? Really enjoyed this class, very different from other EE courses.

Unprofessional. Changed the syllabus 5 weeks into the quarter and made attendance mandatory although I put more than 100% effort into the work that's given for a “light work” class. Never taking again.

Took EE299 for Early Fall Start. Great guy, but lectures got boring towards the end. We had two big group projects and we put a lot of work and effort into them only for everyone to get a 100. I wish I had known everyone would be getting a 100 because then I would've spent more time studying for the final.

I wasn't super interested in the class because it was really focused on energy calculations. The lectures were dry and I found it difficult to pay attention to them. The two group projects are pretty involved, but they're graded on completion. You basically just need to do well on the quizzes and final because participation isn't graded
Exceptional Prof. He taught us in good detail, enough to understand what is important. His homework was real-life examples. It was a great experience.
Goes into depth more into the math and engineering side of sustainable energy, so if you are looking for a class for more of the policy/environmental side, I would recommend finding another class.

I took this class for EFS and professor Arabshahi is a good professor who is interested in the subject and helped me get acquainted with university classes. The class itself, however, is focused more on the math side of energy matters rather than policy and theory. The math itself isn't super difficult, but requires a lot of supposition.

I took EE299 as an Early Fall Start class. It was pretty easy. The projects seemed to be graded for completion. That being said, "complete" for the projects is a heavy amount of research and writing. There were also quizzes, but they were pretty straightforward in my opinion. Also, there was some light math to learn for this class and the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he's a funny dude and lectures are super interesting. a lot of work for a 1 credit class (weekly readings & papers + interview + one 5 page research paper) but he grades very generously (pretty much gives 100 if you do the assignment). he's usually fair but he assigned our final paper super late, overall great prof tho

The class was part of Early Fall Start, as my first class. The quizzes are easy as long as you study, and he tells you what you should study, and the work load is minimal except the final project. Plan to put in some time for the final project. Very approachable, lectures are fine, and communicating with the professor is smooth and easy.n
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The class was pretty okay and the knowledge of this professor is  considerably good given the many examples he presented his class. He also likes to relate the lectures with his personal work and I found that really interesting. There is always something new to learn in every class session.

Took Professor Payman for my Early fall start class as a freshman. This was the first college class I've ever taken and it was a great experience. He was very knowledgeable about the topic and he made teaching interesting. He is also a funny guy and one of the more chill teachers
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Great personality and teaching skills.
Tough and very time consuming final project, open-ended and took forever, but ultimately we did it. Other projects OK. Good class for communications track.

Intense and challenging class with a lot of work, a midterm project and a final project. I really worked hard; payoff was fair overall. Professor was very helpful in and out of class. Motivated me to go to engineering school.
Cool guy, great teacher takes FOREVER to grade.

Great professor,very resourceful and actually has a sense of humor.  The class was quite intense, so be prepared to work hard.  The class is what you make it to be.  I would highly recommend anyone (any background) to take this class!
Very nice person!Very easy course!I get my first 4.0 from his class.
Workload light. Professor very approachable and sometimes funny. Easy to get good grades.

Professor Arai was a super nice, kind lady, and she is really knowledgeable about the topic. Taking this course really pushed my knowledge, super engaging during the lecture, and I've learned SOOOOO many new information about how I could view the world differently. Going to lectures is important but not mandatory, heavy readings and paper writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Make sure you show up to class. She has so much experience in the field and a lot of connections to the authors. She's also willing to sit down with you and talk about the material, so take her up on it when things are unclear! Extremely kind. However, don't expect to know your grade in the class until the end.

Poor lecturer; Readings were too wordy and the class as a whole felt unorganized and too wishy-washy; no grades or even an estimate until long after final. Do not take class unless you really really love the subject matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although, professor is very knowledgeable about the subject, she was extremely disorganized and would interrupt students when she asked them questions. She does not use powerpoint, instead, she would write down on a whiteboard, which was extremely difficult to understand and overall confusing lectures. If you can, do not take her classes.

The good and the bad reviews are all true, but at the end of the day prof. Arai will always make sure you know what you need to know and is very, very knowledgeable about the topics she has us study. Yea, she will show up late sometimes, go on tangents, and interrupt students when they're responding to her questions, but I still respect her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: It's all really confused...

The content was the redeeming part of this class. Overall, I never knew how well I was doing in this class. I got my first grade on week 8. Expectations for grading criteria on all assignments including discussion posts, exams, and the final group project were always vague. Had student "discussion leaders" that she would constantly interrupt.

It's obvious that she knows a lot about her field, I don't want to discount that. However, her classes are incredibly hard to follow. She shows up late every day, and uses up all the class time going on tangents. When someone does have the chance to participate in a discussion, she will interrupt and not let them finish. It all feels disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I thought Arai was pretty understanding and a good teacher. The class was dense, and there was a lot of reading, but the workload wasn't impossible. The content was interesting, even for non-majors.

Surprised by low ratings. Lots of reading but Prof. Arai wants to make sure students comprehend the material & the topics were interesting. She reviews during lecture (even provided notes/summaries for us) and was very available for those with extra questions. Clear about expectations and did not grade hard. Read the assignments and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Arai's class is definitely hard but informational. Be active and ask her about what you don't understand, she is not a harsh grader and is very accessible and helpful outside class. She provides lots of help, don't hesitate to take her class! Read and keep up with the class you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor seemed cool at first but she wasted every second of class. She does not know how to teach and I (along with my classmates I've talked to) essentially learned nothing from her class. Her grading system is unclear and she will not get back to you if you email her asking about your final grade (she never even gave us our final paper grades)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is very passive aggressive and takes the opportunity to use class time towards useless conversation on topics that do not apply towards the final projects. Gives very little time or direction for final projects, and exams. Overall, I learned nothing, and felt as if my background on mixed race effected my grade and her investment in my learning.

Although it is a heavy reading course, if you don't procrastinate and take notes while you read, it should be fine. Arai goes over the readings and discusses with the class about the readings so TAKE NOTES! Follow the study guides she gives you for the exams, read over your notes (especially on what she talks about), and attend the study sessions!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: The lectures were long and very repetitive. She expects you to analyze each and every word of the reading. Arai takes attendance, and is not accommodating to students. She assigns movies to watch, but expects you to watch them on the weekend with no access online. Only to be viewed in the library.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Arai is one of the smartest people you'll meet at UW. However, that information requires you go to class daily, ask a lot of questions, and participate nonstop. She also requires a lot of reading and thinking compared to other classes, but what you can get out of this class and and this professor in terms of knowledge is truly great.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took Prof. Arai's joint Anthro/JSIS class on Japan. The class itself was fairly interesting and thought-provoking. Lots of class discussion and Arai can tend to ramble at times. Her grading is strict, but she does provide feedback which is helpful. Overall, I'd recommend her, especially if you are comfortable speaking up in class.

The lectures were an opportunity to hear her review  the previous lectures. The actual content that was chosen to read and watch was excellent, but the use of class time was atrocious and disappointing at best. All in all, she was extremely patronizing and disregarded any opportunities to discuss the material as if we were in a college classroom.

Andrea Arai is very knowledgeable about the Anthropology of Japan and intricacies of Japanese culture. I would suggest her courses to anyone with even an inkling of interest in Japan. It is important to read the content and show up and participate in the courses to receive a good great. She is very friendly and a wonderful resource.

She is very interesting and don't bother fighting with her. However, READ the material and show up. She likes it if you talk. Constantly ask what she wants from assignments though, because she can be unclear what she exactly wants.
