Unpleasant to deal with on the cruise and had an insane power trip. Very enthusiastic but also unaware of the fact that she is not liked by a decent portion of the student body.

I felt this class was on the harder side for a 3 credit class. The main issue wasn't the material, but rather there were tons of inconsistencies in the info between the professor and TAs. Further, the professor does the lecture with overheads rather than ppt, which makes challenges on what was said (vs. TA) hard. Class is on a curve.

She's a good teacher and her class is pretty easy. As long as you go to lecture you'll be fine. Homeworks and tests are the same difficulty, not hard. She's very energetic and is helpful. Always takes questions and very easy to talk to.
good teacher. make sure you go to class and take notes. her homework and tests follow her lectures exactly. I recommend taking her class

I gotta tell you, I can learn more from wikipedia than attending this extremely boring n useless class...she is incomprehensible no practice exams or quizzes, and exams are 2 orders of magnitude harder than exams...she barely scratch the surface of the materials and expects us to answer really difficult questions...j

This class is extremely boring, too much work for a 3 credit class. Lectures are boring, and very dull. Overload in information, and grading scale is bad. THIS IS NOT AN EASY 3 credit class. LOTS OF HW! DO NOT TAKE IF LOOKING FOR A EASY 3 CREDIT CLASS
Incredibly well spoken and charismatic lecturer. Fantastic course, would take again.

Assignments had unclear grading criteria. There was an assignment where around half the class interpreted it one way, and the other another, and she decided that because most people got it that she would mark the rest wrong even though we still answered the question. It probably depends on which TA you get, though. A great person and lecturer.

Denied my request to record lectures like most other profs do (right after lecturing on disability rights lol). I think she j didn't want ppl to sell her lectures.. ig she cares more ab profit > student needs (more irony lol). So I couldn't access her lectures at all but I still got a 4.0, showing how useless they were anyways (j do the readings).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Respected

reviews.comment: I had the privilege of being taught by Professor Arzoo and can confidently attest to her incredible knowledge. Personally, I gained a lot from her teachings and appreciate her sense of humor. She also makes sure that students do not get too stressed and challenges any statements made in class. Overall, she is an exceptional educator.

Prof. Osanloo knows she's a queen. I loved this class for its content, structure, and how material and guidelines were conveyed. You can tell she designed the course curriculum. Considering the complex, global scope of human rights as a topic, Osanloo does a great job condensing it into a cohesive course. Readings were tough so go to quiz sections!

So intelligent, so charismatic, lectures felt like watching a stand-up comedian in the best way possible. I learned a lot from this class and could tell that Arzoo put thought into the assignment structure. Lectures sometimes felt like a lot of info but as long as you do the readings and show up to quiz section you'll be totally fine.

I absolutely loved this professor! Lectures were super engaging, and they would always go by so quickly. There aren't any tests in the class and 50% of our grade was based on weekly essays which was a little tiresome, especially with all the readings you had to do, but I preferred that to having to take a test. Overall, this class was so much fun!

i dont understand any neg reviews. lecture was so fun. section was easy. skimmed through the readings / barely gave effort and got  3.9. Just a discussion post every week + bare minimum participation + final paper that was graded SO easily
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I am so inspired by Prof. Osanloo and could listen to her talk about her career and research for hours. Her lectures can feel long, but they really are full of interesting information and occasional fun side tangents. Was respectful of student opinions but also was able to challenge them to broaden discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of my favorite profs ever. Very accommodating and cares about her students. Facilitates great discussions, has great insights, obviously knows what she is talking about. She's also hilarious, and makes things due at 9pm "so you are asleep by midnight and not working on the assignment anymore."

Osanloo was extremely accomodating this quarter due to COVID. There were no required sessions, and the weekly assignment was a 500-word post about the readings. Readings and lectures were extremely interesting; I would totally recommend this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Osanloo was the best you could have hoped for during covid quarter. Very accessible and accommodating of all student needs, lenient grading, lots of support. Not a ton of reading - 100 pages or less per week. Weekly assignment was a 500 word discussion post, mainly graded on participation. Take her class! Subject has never been more relevant
I have loved LSJ 426. Professor Osanloo cares so much about what she teaches and boy does she know a lot. I would highly recommend this class and her as a professor for sure.

Professor Osanloo is amazing as a seminar teacher! She loves to hear from everyone but won't make you speak if you don't want to. She truly cares about what she teaches and her students - offered lots of extra help outside class. She is amazing! The class had a lot of reading, 2 sizeable papers and weekly blog posts, no exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I really loved her class! I took LSJ 321 expecting to not enjoy it but she made it really interesting. Professor Osanloo was really helpful in office hours and you could tell she really cared about what she was teaching and her students. She gave me great advice on going to law school as well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: A lot of these comments are outdated and quite inaccurate. You should give this professor a chance! The enthusiasm and knowledge the professor provides makes you engaged. In other human rights classes the instructor can be very robotic and mono toned leading to inattentive and disengaged students, but professor Osanloo is quite the opposite.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor, the class was fantastic but the content was a little disorganized. The grading is pretty straightforward for the three essays, and overall course load was decent.

Arzoo is a fantastic professor. Very passionate about the topic, which makes for delightful, engaging class time. I found her to be a very fair grader, and always helpful with her students during office hours, through email or after class. Highly recommended.

Although the topics and readings are quite interesting, lectures can be fairly disorganized and frequently don't connect to readings. Grades are based off three papers; each covers several different aspects of human rights, international law, etc. which can be challenging to fit into 5-7 pgs. Section very helpful for clarifying confusing points.

Took her seminar on Refugee Law - highly recommended. Leads discussion very well (always respectful and generally insightful with responses) and her few lecture-ish interludes were useful. Surprisingly funny after a few weeks, very helpful in office hours. Grade comes from discussion and papers - which were easily managed. Office hours help a lot.

Absolutely horrible! Disorganized, rambles and goes off on useless tangents, clearly doesn't care about her students. My level of interest in the subject of human rights was far greater before I took the class than after.

I was really excited for this class because it looked very interesting but her lectures were very hard to follow. The TA I had was also awful. She was 10+ minutes late every section. I think this says a lot on the ability Osanloo had to pick an effective TA. Also Osanloo was gone for a week. Very disappointing.
Stay away unless you like incoherent rambling about her trips to Cairo or Iran

She rambles on about everything except what is important to the class. I learned nothing more than what I knew going into the class. I do not agree with her style of teaching. If you take this class, make sure you address issues beforehand because quote Osanloo, "after this quarter, you guys are not my priority so if you need something, oh well".
Human Rights class. Entertaining and exciting lectures, quiz section dependent on TA. Overall, it was a great class that made me start thinking about Human Rights in a different way.

AMAZING! Prof Osanloo is a thoughtful, knowledgeable, and personable instructor. She encourages real learning in her classroom and the work she assigns is always purposeful and never unnecessary. She is very open to student questions and extremely cool and approachable!

TERRIBLE! I don't know what class everyone below me took. She is passionate, but so unorganized. Lectures were just her rambling and reading quotes. Also, a 700 page course pack + online readings is not a normal amount of work. Could have been so interesting, but I felt like I learned absolutely nothing.

She teaches with passion and expertise. She does not try to exhaust the topics of genocide, ethnic cleansing, etc,(as mentioned below), but rather offers an introduction to these topics and examines how they have been used to label different events around the world. The case studies are challenging but very doable and dare I say a little fun!

An authentic academic who is not only a leading authority in her field, but also an excellent teacher. Her experience as a lawyer came through in the class. She was very helpful in office hours and didn't mind spending extra time to make sure that i understood the theories and concepts.  By far one of the most inspiring teachers i've had at UW.

Prof. Osanloo's classes are all absolutely fantastic.  The material is engaging and relevant to current issues.  You take what you make from her classes- either you can sit there and breeze by superficially, or you can use it as a launching pad to explore issues deeper. If you approach her she will gladly help you expand your knowledge on any topic

Arzoo wants you to cover about 5 different subjects in each memo she assigns...in depth and comprehensively.  I did this superficially for a good grade.  However, in a more substantive class, 7 pages covering genocide, humanitarian intervention, labor laws, indigenous peoples rights and methods of enforcement,  is a disgrace to these topics.
Excellent teaching ability

This class made me want to be a human rights minor.  The material is difficult at times, but well worth the reading.  Osanloo is very enthusiastic and the guest speakers were inspiring to say the least.
Organized and enthusiastic, It was always fun to come to class to see her.  A fair grader and extremely knowledgeable.  I HIGHLY recommend this professor.

This was one of the last classes I took before I graduated.  I'm glad that I chose a topic that was so important to the global perspective, and from a professor who really knows her material.  I learned so much in this class, and it encouraged me to read further into the subject and seek out my own material.  I would recommend her to any Anthro major or Political Science major who is looking for an interesting class.  It does require a lot of work, but it's well worth the effort.

I learned so much from this class.  It's great for those that have no prior knowledge of the topic.  Lots of writing and analyzing.  You're expected to participate alot becuase of the level of course, not a bad thing though
great class. learned alot. you have to work to do well but it's worth it
Great class, learned a lot, good texts, clear and concise teacher who cares deeply about the topic
Extremely knowledgeable, insightful, respectful, and transparent about her own biases. I thought she was an excellent lecturer.

Great professor, and certainly deserves the good reviews. This class does make you work, but as long as you show up and study for the exams you will be just fine! This is a names/dates class, but you will know exactly which dates you should be remembering! She is very receptive to questions and definitely rewards critical thinking and discussion.

Fantastic lectures, clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject. A bit of mandatory reading for section each week, and consulting textbook is helpful for papers / take home exams. Very reasonable deadlines / workload, 10/10 would recommend.
I really enjoyed her lectures, and learned a lot from them. There's plenty of opportunities to ask questions. Also, her requirements for quizzes and essays were extremely clear and concise. Loved it.
One of my favorite professors I have ever had. Very engaging lecturer, makes it easy and enjoyable to get the information you need to pass. Highly recommended

One of my favorite classes I've ever taken and one of the most interesting profs I've ever had.

Do you want to be challenged? To expand your mind on the historical paradigm, and underscore the value of an education on the Middle East? How about receiving feedback that will embellish your own writing?  Take Dr. Bet-Shlimon's courses on the modern Middle East.

I never missed a single lecture because I knew that I would be missing out on a wave of information, and an interesting lecture!

Dr. Bet-Shlimon is clearly passionate about what she teaches. Her lectures are dense & engaging. You are encouraged to ask questions & she leaves plenty of time to allow for this. If you are going to refute her, be prepared to back it up with scholarly sources (no, blog posts don't count). Previous knowledge on the ME is helpful for this class.

Professor Bet-Shlimon is not only an amazing professor but an incredibly inspiration individual.  I looked forward to coming to each and every lecture, despite them being two hours long.  Her work ethic is awe-inspiring and the course content is impeccably chosen.  Grading was extremely fair and represents the work a student puts in.

Arbella is nice teacher but her lectures are really long. She talks very fast which is not helpful when trying to take notes. There's a lot of reading, participation in quiz section, a map quiz, 2 lecture quizzes, primary source essay, 1 midterm and final. Elective classes are supposed to be fun, this wasn't. Only take if can't find other div class
She was an amazing teacher overall and made the lectures interesting. The course content was already interesting in itself and she just made it even better.

I had Dr. Dudon for STMATH 208. She is a nice person and treats you with respect but, she's just an average professor. Linear algebra is a very conceptual subject with a lot of terminology and concepts linking to one another. She fails to teach us how to connect the dots between ideas. solid teacher, I took her for ST Math 208, and she genuinely does care about ur learning, has frequent office hours. Reason im giving 3 is cause I like the reverse class where you would watch vid and come to class, and the in person lectures sometimes id get lost in the material lol.

Ended up liking Prof Dundon more than I thought. The course is def tough and attendance is mandatory, so many papers and so much prep before and after classes but that is to be expected since the course is hard. But professor is really nice and they do post all the answer keys, the midterms and quizzes are similar to what you've already done before

reviews.comment: Amazing professor who answered all my questions. Typical flipped-classroom instruction, weekly quizzes with a partner, and 2 midterms. Lectures and HW assignments on MWF, doesn't take too long. Calc 2 was much easier and enjoyable with her.

Dr. Dundon is a wonderful professor who takes time out of her day to support her students. Axiomatic Geometry has been one of the best classes I have taken at UWB because Dr. Dundon is such a good professor. If you have questions about a problem you can send her an email and she will respond within a day with a detailed answer. Highly recommend.

The materials aren't hard, but there is a lot of stuff to memorize. I found the materials pretty interesting, but repetitive. There are three exams, and the class averages were about 63. There is a quiz every week, and they are worth 10%. You're expected to sit in class for 2 hours to do your homework if you want full participation, which is 5%

I took 493 combinatorics and also stmath 330 with professor dundon during the 21-22SY. I truly will say she is really unclear in her expectations of students, and her lecture notes exceed 20 pages weekly with paragraph blocks of writing. I am disappointed and have had an easier time in real analysis than I did in her class.

Online cause of covid. She has pretty decent lectures. There's a quiz every week. Quizzes can be difficult. Great math teacher, totally knows what she's doing. Easy going, overall great!

Professor Dundon is a very good professor, it did take time for me to get use to her. But i eventually got used to it. Sometimes she tends to talk a little fast, but not fast enough for me not to understand her. She's a great professor and I felt very confident in her understanding in mathematics since she taught fluently in her teaching.

Dr. Dundon is probably my favorite teacher I've ever had during my 3 years at UW. After having previous Calculus experience in high school, I got a 3.6 in the class while only spending maybe 2-3 hours per week on homework. Very fair and sweet and is understanding about any problems you have. Do the homework and you'll be good. I didn't buy the book

Professor Dundon is a clearly a math lover.  She is passionate about what she does and seems to love spreading her knowledge.  Participation of students during lectures isn't as great as it could be.  Her voice is very clear.  It will be a great help to review algebra before taking this course with her.

Well she's nice and pretty, and also has a fun ascent.  Not very good at explaining things and usually prefers to do things manually, or the hard way, then showing the easy way after a week in or so.  No graphing calculators or notes allowed, unless it's the final.  She curved our final because of the low averages.

She lectures way too fast and doesn't slow down. She talks very quickly and writes on the board way too fast. Your hand will be cramped up by the end of the class. It's hard to keep up. The explanations are good though and help a lot when doing homework. The homework is easy. The quizzes and exams are not. They are ridiculously hard.
Pay attention in class, mostly to the examples and you'll be fine. She knows her stuff.

Dr. Audrey is one of my favorite professors at UW! Take her classes, especially the plant classes.

Just overall a great lecturer, really enjoyed the way she taught and there wasn't too much homework, just a problem set every week and lecture activities done in class.

A great professor. Proof that school doesn't need to be stressful and difficult if you want to learn. Things I learned in this class helped me with other immunology courses (especially ones that had terrible lecturers) would take another one of her classes.

Self study needed.

Uses outdated slides, doesn't explain anything, somehow makes concepts MORE confusing than they are. I was utterly lost until I started skipping all classes and self studying, then I finally began learning. If you have the unfortunate fate of taking him, do linear algebra first, know series, rely on the god tier TAs. You can survive this! (maybe)

He comments frequently on how no one is asking questions and then berates students who ask questions. Even one of the TAs told me that skipping class to self-study would be a better use of my time.

Easily the worst professor I've had the displeasure of encountering. Cruel and demeaning toward students. Makes it obvious he doesn't care about students learning. All grades were based off tests which were majority copied verbatim. Final exam was nothing like practice or content covered and the final grade was screwed up. The TAs were amazing.

This class was pretty terrible solely because of how heavily weighted the final exam was. It was worth 50% of our grade and covered content that was poorly taught and not on any of the practice exams. Avoid Bulgac if you can! Not worth risking the GPA hit to get the requirement out of the way.

Bulgac's lectures are meaningless. All quizzes, lectures, midterms and practice exams were not made by Dr. Bulgac but rather he uses other professors materials. Final was far harder then other exams and had little content covered on practice exams. Learned far more from our TA then by going to lectures. Need to read and review textbook often.

Belligerent toward students, first few weeks of lecture were useless and his slides are unhelpful. If you need to take a course from him be prepared for self study and read the book. If you're comfortable with the 200 level math sequences at UW specifically math224 and 208 you should have no issues with his phys227 content wise.

Writing this review purely for the TA's, they were excellent. Truly saved the class from complete destruction under the reign of Bulgac. Bulgac is a poor lecturer, slides were convoluted and not helpful at all. Just stay home and read the textbook, seriously. Final was also extremely difficult and had questions that no one had ever seen before.
Aurel Bulgac is hands-down the worst professor at UW and the worst thing resembling a teacher I've ever seen. Avoid at all costs, even if you must take an extra year of undergrad.

Bulgac is a funny and nice guy under the gruff exterior, but he is not a good lecturer. Slides are so convoluted. No homework, grade is entirely in-class quizzes and exams. He is known to reuse old exams and quizzes almost exactly, so it's an easy class to do well in. The textbook is great though, you're better off reading that instead of lecture.

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's the most unhelpful professor you will ever encounter. If you are here because you need to take his class please consider taking it another quarter. You're better off self learning material from the textbook than go to his lectures. He will be aggressive if you ask him any questions.

Extremely confusing; lectures are not helpful at all. He makes a lot of references to terrorism, quotes Reagan, tells problematic jokes, uses strange analogies about a dull knife in his office. Seems upset when asked questions, and even more upset he asks a question and a student's answer isn't exactly what he wanted. I relied entirely on the TA.

I was in phys 121, but there was no option for that. Bulgac was rude to students with questions, flippant with teaching the lecture material, and generally hard to understand due to his mumbling and trailing off midsentence. Avoid him in entry level classes because he doesn't seem to care. He responded to emails promptly though.
Really poor teaching of the material. He's a funny guy, but he complicates simple concepts. I went to lecture to get the participation credit but  read the textbook to understand the material.

Definitely a cool guy with a subtle sense of humor, but his lectures aren't always the clearest and his exams had a lot of content that weren't covered directly in-class. Average class grades were always 50%, which felt pretty rough. Overall he's not horrible, but he's far from the most helpful professor I've had.

The first half of the class (relativity) is ok but the second half (particles) is incredibly dense and Bulgac does not teach it effectively. He interrupts when you're asking questions, is blatantly rude, and expects you to have knowledge of classes that are not pre-reqs. Exams are much easier than HW but the MT and final constitute 70% of grade...

Worst professor I've ever had at UW. Mumbles through explanations or skips over lecture slides. If you try to ask a question, he'll interrupt you halfway through and not answer your actual question or will insult you and say you should have been paying more attention. His lecture slides and homework look like they are organized by a 4-year old.

Dr. Bulgac knows a lot, but it seemed he didn't understand where his students stood. Some lectures he beat a dead horse with his reviews, which muddied the waters more than anything. However, with new topics, he went way too fast and spoke too little. Homework helped a lot; exams were easy; not a super efficient online class. I was often confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bulgac is a smart guy and he cares about his students, but his lectures are not the most helpful. He can sometimes be difficult to hear and his handwriting is often confusing, but he generally teaches to the textbook, so make sure to bring it with to follow along and don't be afraid to ask questions. His digressions can sometimes be funny, too!

He's definitely an acquired taste. -Direct sense of humor, doesn't beat around the bush. -Won't hold your hand. You can skip the lectures except for the weekly quizzes, but you need to read the textbook and understand 80% of what you read. -He has a heart of gold under a tough shell. -Low test grades but high high high curves. MeanGPA 3.0-3.3

The worst professor I have had so far. Like many others say, he mumbles with a thick accent and his handwriting is almost impossible to read. His lectures are not organized well, especially for students who are learning the material for the first time. He either disregards questions or yells at the students for asking them.

Worst professor I have had so far at UW. In addition to having a relatively thick accent, he has hands down the worst handwriting of any professor I have ever seen. Was gone for the whole week of the 2nd midterm without any notice. You will learn more reading the book than going to lecture (clearly everyone agrees as 30/200 people actually come)

Worst professor I have ever had. He doesn't even have end of the quarter course evaluations. Avoid at all costs, his hand writing is illegible and his lectures are convoluted. Also avoid office hours unless you want to be talked down to.

reviews.comment: He's class is really hard. I cannot read his lecture notes because of his terrible hand writing.

reviews.comment: His class was somewhat difficult because his handwriting can be extremely hard to read, making it so if you miss a lecture, it's hard to learn from his notes. His final exam was difficult (100/240 average). He also didn't make enough tests for the final, so we waited an additional half hour to start the final exam. Would avoid him if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Horrible at teaching. Lectures are unclear, he has a thick accent and mumbles quietly through explanations, and gets pissy when students ask him to reiterate or to clarify what he just said as if we were "insulting" his intelligence. Clicker questions and exams are horribly formatted. Avoid him if you can, seriously.

For being a crazily intelligent man teaching a simplified version of the subject he knows and loves, Aurel Bulgac is one patient dude. With his grim visage, Romanian accent, and infectious sense of humor, it's hard not to love him. He's got as much passion for the history of physics as physics itself, which made for very enjoyable digressions.

Aurel Bulgac is a horrible teacher. He mumbles when he speaks and his accent is so thick you won't understand anything he says. He leaves out important course information and doesn't know how to use his own technology. He leaves for Italy without telling anyone and leaves the TA by himself. Avoid this teacher at all costs! You will regret it.

He's an awful teacher. Tests are near to impossible. Even if he goes through how to do the questions after the exam, majority of people still don't understand. Last test: 12 mc questions top score was 8. how sad. Many people got zeros on that test. and Average was 4/12. on a MC test. avoid.

He mumbles so I can barely understand what he is saying. His lectures are kind of useless. I learned more from reading the book than I did attending lectures. He gives us practice problems that don't correlate at all to actual problems on the test. He was horrible. But most physics professors are UW aren't that good, so choose your poison.
Worst physics lecturer I've ever had. Just reads off the lecture slides and gives us practice problems that are completely different from his actual test questions. Avoid if you can.

fantastic professor. He is not mean, he has a very abrupt sense of humor. On top of that, he has said some of the wisest statements. an un-exact quote: "you must know all details the material in the book. If you went to Italy and a pretty lady said something in italian, but you forgot what it ment, YOU LOOSE!!"

I am both terrified and enamored with this dude. He's impatient, condescending and sometimes outright MEAN but he's one sharp cookie. Rumor has it he owns 5 cats and a dog. This juicy little tidbit makes me think that underneath his gruff exterior he's got a heart two size too big.

Bulgac is my favorite professor at UW so far. He does have high expectations on students and I'd say that it's probably hard to make friend with him. However, if you have real interest in the subject and do some work before his classes, his lecturing style will make you feel very smart. It is NOT impossible to get full mark in the quizzes or exams.
hard but has an interesting in your learning. I can see how he can come off as rude when you say something wrong but I never really found it that offensive.

The rumors are true, Bulgac is very hard prof. He is reluctant to give partial credit, so even a very small mistake can cost you big points. But overall, he is a very good teacher, and you can tell he cares a lot about teaching.

Fantastically difficult professor. Everything written above is true, but remember that 114 is a physics for non-physics majors class, and is designed to be easy for medical student and the like. In real physics classes he's very difficult and gets angry and verbal with the class when people fail quizzes. Average grade on the final 6.5/38

Very hard prof. He has very high expectations of people to keep up with the material, and remember every little detail. Harsh grader. Can also be cruel if you get something wrong in lecture, however wants everyone to keep asking questions to be sure they are learning it. He also cracks a lot of jokes. It's very love-hate with him.
Terrible professor. Makes fun of students for asking questions, rarely finishes examples and never contextualizes why we learned what we learned.

Most of my learning came from reading the textbook and attending Tutorial. Lectures were a bore. Exams were pretty difficult and you must read everything carefully since he does not give any diagrams in his exam questions.
I didn't like how the class was set up. I don't do well on multiple choice tests and I didn't think his lectures helped me on the tests at all.

Funny professor! Definitely makes physics interesting. I personally dislike physics but he makes me want to attend lectures everyday. Midterms and final are all MCs, no partial credits but you can guess if you know nothing. Homework and click questions are extra credit! Study hard and definitely read the text and do lots of practice problems.

Very dedicated to teaching physics and has a very funny subtle sense of humor. Grade comes entirely from 4 multiple choice tests (1 of which you may drop). Homework is E.C. There is such thing as a stupid answer in his class so watch out when he asks the class questions.

bulgac is a funny guy. he has a strong accent, and lots of random stories that he somehow pertains to physics. tests are multiple choice, but hard. class average goes about 50%. read the book, study daily. a lot of critical info is condensed. all in all, he's prob one of the better physics teachers
sweetest and most caring professor ever! super fun and interesting lectures
She is nice but one sided.

nice teacher

she's such a great teacher! sooo sweet and understanding=)

Crazy cool! Her lectures are full of energy and she makes it fun to go to class.
She is awesome.
Really enjoyed the course. Went over a lot of provocative and had to determine why is was or wasn't ethically right (in a class where there is no right answer).

Such a good professor! His first semester at the U and he seems to really be connecting with his students! He is funny and engaging and makes the class material exiting and fun. I have never hated missing a philosophy class so much in my life. Lots of writing but thats to be expected with an upper level PHIL class - its nothing cruel or unusual.
Fareed was my TA for Phil 120 with Cass Weller. I can't explain how much he helped me through that class. Highly recommended.
Class was too hard for 110. way too demanding for this level.
Fareed!! You are the man. So intelligent, helpful, and witty.
Fareed rules!
Recommended, very smart and helpful.
Ewww.
Great TA, really helpful, and cute!

The modules are clear and easy to follow, and while the workload is manageable, it can be time-consuming and challenging if you have little experience with art. He gives plenty of time to turn in assignments and always provides positive feedback.

Axel is a very knowledgeable professor. I went in with no design experience and I felt supported by him and the TAs. Feedback was helpful and you're given many opportunities to improve before submitting. Great intro to Adobe Illustrator. Grading is subjective and lectures were a bit dull/ repetitive at times but still a good class.

reviews.comment: Very caring and able to explain a lot of design concepts. A lot of movies watching though, don't know if that was because it was online. A really good beginning design class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Axel is great. The class is very entertaining and Axel is a great teacher to learn from. He did a good job adapting to online classes. This class is a great intro to design.

This class is excellent, the prof. is organized, fun, and very engaging. Lectures are well presented and not dull. Few homework assignments (they become harder) and feedback sessions with TA's are great and helpful. Not a stressful class by any means. Would recommend a basic knowledge of Adobe Illustrator for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easy class, generally easy grader, but design is arbitrary and there's no clear grading criteria, and you don't get feedback for your projects. He sometimes reviews student work in classes, and keep in mind he likes MINIMALISM. No textbook, just spend a few hours doing the projects and you're good. Most days I don't even think about this class.

Axel is incredibly passionate and it shows during his lectures, although he does ramble sometimes. As someone who knew nothing about design, I've learned a lot. The projects were really fun but grading can be subjective and tough. Overall, this class is a great intro to design/the design major and I feel more prepared for Design 166!

Professor Roesler is a really cool guy. His lectures are somewhat long and he can drone on in class, but overall presents really useful information about Design. If you're interested in the Des major, I recommend taking this easy intro DES 150 class as a foot in the window before DES 166.
Axel is a great professor. He knows a lot about the subject and is always willing to help. If you're curious about a topic, go talk to him about it. He's like a human Wikipedia.

Axel is insanely passionate and had a great sense of humor. Lectures were a little long, but always interesting. TA Coreen was super nice and gives great feedback, though her office hours were sporadic. Fairly organized class for it being the first time its offered! Even non-design majors should take this class. Makes me excited to pursue design!

He is funny but he has a German accent so make sure you listen. The final had nothing to do with what we did all quarter but it was definitely a fun class. All hands on designing. His TA Coreen Callister was kind as well. Graded slowly for only 97 students.
Engaging, passionate and hilarious!
axel is brilliant. plus he's a babe.

Axel was great but to get a good grade in his class you're gonna have to work your butt off. Make sure to take advantage of office hours. I know everyone says that but this time actually DO IT, the personal help is priceless. Also, you can redo projects at the end of the quarter so don't stress too hard if you get a bad grade on one.

Definitely passionate about design, which makes the lectures more interesting than they would be otherwise.  Rambles a bit but fun to listen to. Helpful in discussion section.  However--this isn't a good class to take if you're really uptight about your gpa and are not all that great at design--grading is quite competitive. Fun projects though :)

Worth taking! He (as well as Prof. Thurtle) did an outstanding job. The work load is college level, but the information that I learned was terrificly interesting as well as random and fun! I'm pumped to take Art 166 with him!
No Comments

She's a nice person, but a horrible professor. She usually went on tangents during her lectures, which resulted in a lack of clarity and in the class not finishing the final two chapters listed on the syllabus. I learned everything from the book, not from her. Rarely replied to emails, even when reminded. 60% of grade from midterm + final.
She is really cool. She's funny in class and really chillax. If she sees that you are trying she does her best to help you. She tells you what is on the test and is very clear and straight forward.

reviews.comment: Aurora was great. ECON200 with her was straightforward and clearly defined as to what you needed to know. Exams were also pretty straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Aurora is a great teacher who cares about every one of her students. I was able to overload into her class the first week & she let me in without hesitation. The tests had no surprises. Office hours are very helpful. Her lectures were engaging and casual. It was easy to ask questions. 10 points of participation E.C available that go towards final!

Aurora is the best instructor I've ever had! I also took Econ 300 with her and enjoyed every minute of her class. Econ 400 is meant to be a hard course, but her lectures were so clear and concise. She also gives great examples to help us understand some abstract ideas. Moreover, she is very helpful during office hours. Choose her class if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I liked this class a lot compared to other econ classes. She is very friendly but a tough grader, but will reconsider if you ask her for extra points

Learned a lot, great class. Exams are hard, you really have to know the concepts really well. She is more concerned with the concepts than the math. She gives problem sets, class activity worksheets, and she gives practice exams. She also held extra office hours on the day of the exams, super helpful just to get any lingering questions answered.
I really did not enjoy her class. She was not approachable, difficult to understand, and rude to students. I'm not sure it it is because she is an international student or if she just doesn't care.
She is very clear in classes and very helpful in consult time. Read before the quizzes and you'll be ok
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: very dry lectures, runs a few minutes late frequently (even on the days of the exams, with no additional time to make up for her tardiness), minimal feedback... avoid

I really enjoyed her class her sense of humor is strange though. I got an A by showing up to class and reading before quizzes. She gives ungraded problem sets but they are optional. Oh and she likes it when you ask stuff in class
EXAMS ARE TOUGH AS HECK! ONE QUIZ/ WEEK. SHE WILL AND CAN WRECK YOUR GRADE. AVOID HER!!!!!!
Shes ok. I had her for micro and exams are difficult but classes are fun and she is very patient
Did not learn anything from this class

Macroeconomics was a difficult course for me at the beginning. I was frustrated by the topics I couldn't wrap my brain around but this teacher opened her office hours up to me as often as I needed to understand the concepts. Aurora Stephany is an outstanding teacher with a very genuine passion for economics that for me has been contagious.
the worst teacher I have ever had
definitely avoid
She's definitely very eccentric! Hard class to follow, speaks fast with a heavy accent! Grades fair but exams were hard!
She is very clear in classes and very helpful in consult time
avoid...
Classes are very hard but you'll be fine if you go to office hours, she's very nice
She is great and her classes are a lot of fun. Participation is optional but she gives extra credit for it so I asked a lot of questions in class
The subject is tough and much harder than 200 and 201 but she's very helpful and gives many examples in class. I would take another class with her no doubt
Hard to kinda understand. Definitely very eccentric.
Aurora is the best. Take a class with her if you can! She knows what she's doing and she is an amazing and fun person!!!
Absolutely love her! She really got me interested in the subject and kept the lectures interesting. Definitely one of my favorite profs at UW!
Great teacher! Explains well, and is very laid bacleasy going. Learned a lot and had fun!

He's incredibly passionate about the subject matter, but very harsh grader. Only things we are graded on is 3 exams which he does not provide study guides for. Writes the exams the day before giving them so his answer to when asked what to study is "everything." Wants very specific info on tests, only feedback is "no" "irrelevant" so not helpful

No homework except he expects you to read twice a week which isn't bad. Nothing is graded except for 2 midterms and 1 final. Really funny, keeps the class entertaining, Actually got me interested in Japanese classical literature now- I would take another one of his classes but my previous grades were too low to enroll in his other class womp womp.

reviews.comment: Professor Atkins is awesome--he seriously knows his stuff and is a joy to listen to lecture. JAPAN471 could be a fairly difficult class if you slack, but if you show up to lectures (which you won't want to miss anyway) and keep up with the totally reasonable weekly 6 hours of prep time Atkins asks of you, it's a very doable and enjoyable challenge.

reviews.comment: Atkins lectured for 2 hours straight, directly from the slides. He only has 3 exams in grades. So if you fail one, you're screwed. This is not a discussion class only history.

reviews.comment: Only get graded in 3 exams, he said that he'd gonna use old style way to give feedback to everyone. Bunch of notes need to take for exam, however he never pointed which part and what was the improtant for exam.
COLD

I gained an appreciation for Japanese literature after taking this class. Prof. Atkins' enthusiasm was contagious and really demonstrated his love for what he taught. As long as you come to class and participate in discussion, you will do fine. Highly recommend!

As soon as the quarter started it quickly became my favorite class period. Atkins is a fabulous teacher and really knowledgeable. He's also pretty funny.  He does not appreciate late or absent students, as he called attendance nearly everyday this quarter. So show up and read the book. Read it once and you'll be fine. Then light review for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Amazing guy. If you can take his class or even just get to know him, do it. He's an incredible wealth of knowledge if you're actually interested in the subjects. He's clear about everything he knows and identifies what he doesn't. He encourages discussion and you can tell he loves what he teaches. The homework was moderate reading and analyzing.

Atkins is very knowledgable but he is a self-admitted medievalist. You can tell his expertise in certain areas of the very broad swath of Japanese literature from around 600-1850, is hazier than others. His specialty is from around 1300-1580. Is very nice but does seem to want to be taken seriously even though the class isn't very difficult .

Professor Atkins is a great teacher! His lectures are engaging and his PowerPoints are very clear. This quickly became my favorite class of the term! Your grade is mostly made up of three or four exams(with study guides) and participationattendance.  If you read the text and review before the exams, you will do fine. Would take his class again!
you have to memorize every passage of a text and know every single terminology to have a hope of passing

The readings were required, and if you at least read everything once it was not bad at all. He goes over the readings and more in lectures and does a very good job of doing so. Very clear, understandable, funny at time. Don't be late to class though, it pisses him off.

Good course which gives a holistic view in the security realm. Gives homework regularly which is good to keep in touch with the course and makes preparing for mid terms and finals much easier. Mid Terms and Finals have logical questions for which having a clear concept on the topics is necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very helpful and good teaching methods to make every student understand important concepts.

Good Prof

Nice guy, eh professor. Lectures were difficult to follow, and he often went on tangents. Midterms were pretty easy/reflective of the quiz section, but the final was not like the midterms at all. It was insanely difficult and tanked my grade.
Had to teach myself everything, unorganized lectures, and final did not reflect midterms

Lectures covered only the basics of material. They were sometimes boring, and occasionally he'd start talking about something irrelevant for a while. His typed lecture notes were clear but his handwriting can be bad. Had to search for online videos to learn other material, even after reading textbook. He was very cheerful and his tests were easy.
Just an ok professor

His lectures could be hard to follow without reading the textbook beforehand. However, he always paused for questions and answered them thoroughly. His midterms were easier than most, which made the final feel more challenging. Overall, he's engaging and genuinely cares about his students. I recommend taking his class
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Jayadev was THE BEST professor I had this quarter! He taught content in a way that was easy to understand as well as giving other students an extra push to think about material in a more difficult way. He gives many practice exams and homework problems leading up to the midterms and exam to ensure you are prepared. TAKE THIS CLASS WITH JAYADEV!!

The professor is very knowledgeable and skilled at math, a good speaker, and probably one of the better professors in this course but he does go at a faster pace. The lectures cover the general topics, but the homework is where you will face intricate problems. I recommend being familiar with calculus before this course as it moves very fast.

reviews.comment: I found his lectures confusing and not very helpful. He's passionate and entertaining but not super helpful in understanding coursework. Challenging and I had taken calc before.

Professor Jaydev is an amazing teacher and an even better person, who truly cares about his students. His lectures are clear, organized, and enjoyable. Exams and grading are very fair. His office hours are helpful and encouraging, and he explains concepts patiently. Overall a great professor I highly recommend taking his class!

Okay so he is incredibly smart and passionate about math which is an admirable thing, good and entertaining lecturer but not the best because he can go a little too fast most of the times. reviews.comment: Professor Athreya likes to pretend he loves math, but he is actually very impatience and makes a lot of errors when doing example questions during lecture. The difficulty level of homework does not match what he teaches in class.

Professor Athreya cares deeply about mathematics and the concepts within, however he is not the best at actually teaching them. Lectures are boring at best, with up to half of the time spent reviewing material from the previous lecture. Grading, although, is quite good, with no surprises and clear expectations set from the beginning.

Very nice man, considerate of personal issues. His lectures tend to get boring and he can talk and write very fast without giving any problems for the class to figure out, handwriting it also quite hard to understand sometimes. The exams are not hard if you know the material, there are no trick questions, he is just testing your ability to do math.

Very gracious grader and all you need is to show up to lectures to know how to do the HW. No final, just a proof portfolio at the end of the quarter. reviews.comment: Prof. Athreya might give the deceptive impression that he is passionate about mathematics and cares about the students. In actuality, I think he's very insincere and impatient.

I really enjoyed having Professor Athreya for MATH 126. His lectures were very engaging and made good use of outside resources. Prof. Athreya is clearly very passionate about mathematics and interested in student success.y only complaints are that his writing is nearly illegible and he makes a lot of small errors. Also, exams were perhaps too easy.

Jayadev is a great professor and person! You can tell he's passionate about the material and his advice comes from the heart. I like how there weren't any exams and that we have lots of time to do the homework. He could be a little impatient with people who wouldn't quickly get material or get out of their chair to work on the whiteboard though.

reviews.comment: I really liked the way he taught and enjoyed his lecture, however he does NOT know how to write exams. Curves are extremely high (80-90) so getting a good grade means not messing up rather than actually understanding material. Save your GPA, I would recommend not taking this professor solely to avoid his exams.

Honestly, very average as an instructor. He explains fairly well, but makes frequent silly mistakes which mkes you work harder to follow along in lecture. reviews.comment: Overall, a very nice professor, but unorganized and often very cocky. He skipped around and was too focused on the concepts themselves rather than their application. He tried to incorporate humor into his lectures, but often came across as trying too hard. His grading was very harsh and he did not seem to care about student success.

reviews.comment: DONT TAKE HIS CLASS EVER it will ruin your gpa. He is the kind of person who said one thing, but did something opposite. His TAs teach everything basically. To be honest, I do not even know why he is having the lecture.

This teacher is not a good one, he was not patient for student, and often change what he said during the class, even after class will change office time after you got there. My advise is don't take serious of what he said
Best math professor I've ever had. Hands down.

Kuya is super funny and relatable. He gives homework for your benefit but does not grade it so you can learn from your mistakes. He treats all his students like family (if you respect him) and above all else, he wants you to learn.

Kuya is very encouraging. Your grade depends on attendance so don't take the morning class if you're a nightowl like me. No Tagalog experience required, show up, have fun and 4.0 this class! Speaking practices are fun if your partner is fun (mine barely smiled and talked to me). Final is a group video project (again, find a fun group for this).
Kuya Richard is awesome! He made Tagalog very easy to learn! Just come to class and do homework! Also, no textbook needed.

His class is SO  much fun! you get to learn tagalog which is an uncommon language. and you get the vlpa credit. he's really super nice and friendly. it's an easy A class; you just need to try and come to class. otherwise there's no problem. it's a super fun class. the only univ in WA that teaches Tagalog! no textbook he posts power point slides.

There is no textbook, which is nice. Attendance is important (obviously) since you need to be in class to practice speaking. Kuya Richard has a great sense of humor, is very encouraging (I never felt afraid of making a mistake), and provides other helpful materials - download of lecture slides, access to Quizlet for more practice.

I loved his class. Really fun and easy to learn. :) No regrets in taking this class, no textbook just powerpoints. Just review the vocab in powepoints and quizlet super helpful. Visiting his office hours work, even though I never did.

Kuya Richard is an amazing teacher! I took Tagalog on a whim (having no Filipino background) and I have loved the class. Kuya is a super enthusiastic, funny, and kind prof who prefers not to use a textbook. You must come to class though! It is pretty much all speaking-based, no homework essays or anything. Great class!!! Take it. :)

Kuya Richard is the best Tagalog Professor! His very energetic and its always fun attending his class. Since this is a language class, attendance is mandatory. He is very engaging on the things he teaches and explains the things you don't understand clearly. Fun class to have and I recommend you taking this class!

Kuya Richard is a super fun and nice guy. He genuinely cares for all of the students in his class and if you are having trouble he really encourages office hours. As long as you come to class, participate and regularly practice, you should easily get a 4.0.

Kuya Richard was a great professor! He reaches his student's needs and gives good explanations. Attendance is mandatory because its a language class. A lot of speaking practice in class. Participation is a must! Overall, really nice and understanding.

Really enjoyed this class last Spring quarter (2025). Really structured and clear what we needed to do to succeed and it was taught clearly. I like the cute comics he had to keep me engaged throughout lectures. Will miss his class now that I have graduated!

Best and Funniest teacher at Foster. He is very knowledgeable and willing to help. He makes simple market structure concepts such as futures arbitrage seem like the most interesting thing in the world.

Professor Kamara is a very wholesome and organized professor. He structured all his courses with the appropriate resources to learn everything. His lectures were also neatly organized with lots of opportunities for questions. I also appreciate the cute comic strips he includes.
Lecture notes are heavy and hw before each class but you will learn a lot and it is interesting stuff. He does a great job of explaining and always welcomes questions

Lectures are dull and not recorded. Lecture notes are too dense with over 80-100 pages of content. Look for other options for an engaging learning experience, unless you have a strong understanding of the material.

Lots of respect goes to Avi for his ability to explain complicated concepts in simple analogies/examples. Be ready to spend time thinking about problems. Lecture notes although dense (80 pages), but they will teach you everything and how derivatives work in the real world. You will come to love him in the end of the quarter!

Professor Kamara's class is very straightforward and you won't be surprised by anything on the exams. The lecture material is dry but he's very effective at teaching it. He can seem a little abrasive at first but he's an extremely nice guy and you'll come to love him. Lots of homework, so be prepared for that. Exams aren't bad at all.

Pros: 
Provides 0.4 extra GPA points for participation, provides a generous amount of extra credit for homework, and everything in the tests was actually taught and practiced in the homework.

Cons:
Does not record lectures, notes are extremely; difficult to study from.

Summary: Don't take this class if you don't plan to go AND participate.

The lectures are pointless as he skims through slides far too quickly to read anything. All learning will be done on your own, outside of class by reading extremely dense lecture notes he provides for each session, ranging from 20-80 pages long, with a homework due each class. Brutal, not worth taking. Fin460 is the vastly superior option.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took this class 20 years ago.. Among all the finance classes I took, this is one class that I would say was useful in my work (I worked in Treasury as Derivatives Sales). This is the one class that I still remember in my heart. He was very approachable and explains very well. The key is you have to be interested to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: the true test to this class is actually the homework, not the midterm or final. You'll have homework due before the start of each class, which will be extremely difficult. But if you're able to get pass that, you'll do fine cus the exams are basically structured around the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: PARTICIPATE IN CLASS. Avi gives up to 10% extra credit for "valuable in-class contributions." Very easy to get 100% on the homework as there is a lot of extra credit. I got a 37/40 on both the midterm and final and got a 4.0 because of my participation. My friend got a 39 and 38 but only got a 3.8 because he didn't participate so didnt get any EC.

Listen, if your in school to simply to get the credits and take the easy way out of everything- maybe this class isn't for you. However, if you actually want to learn something and aren't afraid of learning something thats difficult yet rewarding to learn, take this class with Avi. The material is tough in that its new, however its rather intuitive
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was pretty bad. The material is pretty tough and Avi races through everything. Never really felt like I learned anything in the class. The midterm is based off the homework questions, but theres a ton of homework, so be ware. Overall would not recommend this class. Take 460 and be done with it.

Super easy class. Midterm based on HW problems, some of them exactly identical. You need the course pack as the material is directly and strictly from it. Good professor, and will help if you need it.

May be suitable as a beginning level instructor, but his calculus lectures lack direction and confused myself and those around me. The book isn't utilized and instead powerpoint presentations that lack relevance to current material are emphasized. I would avoid this guy simply because he does not know the material well enough.By the way I got an A-
Awesome, inspired guy
Failed first two tests, made a bet to base my grade on the final and received a 3.7 for the quarter

I watched him literally scream at students who he thought were not paying attention and throw a hissy fit once or twice. He also kicked one kid out of class for reading The Daily and told him to never come back.
Very supportive for me personally and had great office hour availabilty- very likable and has a great sense of humor, a truly great professor and hilarious individual!
No Comments

His tests and quizzes are fairly easy and straight forward. You learn the basics and for a class like 111 he did a very good job. I think, however, if you have him for 120 or above his lectures might be too simple and you might not be prepared for more advanced math. Overall great guy. Recommended!
really great guy. took 120 with him about 6 years ago and he still remembers me. very cool and a big van hallen fan

Definitely entertaining!  Kept things very interesting and you get to use your homework on quizzes!  If you're looking for a good grade in math, take this one.  But, if you want to learn the material really well, go with someone else
He wants the student to learn.
Great at keeping your attention in class.  Oversimplifies materials.  If you really want to learn the material, take from someone else.  If you want the easy, watered down version, he's your man.
He likes the simpsons...but it is still math
Awesome professor.  Make the class fun!
great teacher if you need help staying awake in lecture.
One of the best teachers I have ever had in my life.
visit office hours alot. he'll remember you/maybe boost your grade in the end.
No Comments
Tries to be funny at least
Really cares about the student. As long as you get your work in on time you will get 4.0
If you take ENGL 131 take it with him, nothing more needs to be said.

Andres is hands down one of the best professors they have at UW, he is caring, passionate and encourages his students to do well and understand the concepts. . 4.0 guarenteed if you turn in the 8 assignments and show up.

Super easy class with a super cool guy. He does labor-based grading but still gives helpful feedback for improvement and is very, very encouraging. The material we learn is surprisingly engaging because of how invested he is and you can tell he cares. Attendance is mandatory, but you're guaranteed a 4.0 if you show up and turn in everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Andres is so adorable and a real chad. If you have the chance to take one of his classes, definitely go for it!! He's very sweet and his ENGL 131 classes are graded based on whether you attempted the assignments or not (essentially participation-based), so everyone is pretty much guaranteed an A.
Barely any feedback for a WRITING CLASS, no constructive feedback, condescending, discourages multiple viewpoints

The comments here that say you get no feedback are true. I don't understand how you can become a teacher and feel like students' don't deserve any engagement with their work. We are all convinced she never actually read a thing we wrote.

I didn't learn anything in her class. Just read three readings and then write about them. Need to write about 700 words a week but she doesn't read or give feedback. She asks for an A grade to complete additional assignments but doesn't tell us why it's only a 3.5. can this kind of person be a teacher? She can finish a class with a random grade!

avoid her if possible. professor bou ayash was condescending on more than one occasion, and and claimed to do contract grading, but marked me down to a 3.5 at the end, which was unexpected because she gave no feedback or grade projection thruout. one positive is that the required reading selection was wonderful, but the way she taught it sucked.

My goodness, Nancy was just terrible. And I mean truly awful. She needs to change, something, anything! The class provided literally, and I mean literally, nothing towards my education. It was utterly useless and she was no help. She was condescending and provided no feedback through the whole quarter. AVOID AVOID AVOID! And Nancy, please change.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Bou Ayash is so flexible and patient with students. I learned a lot from her and enjoyed her class. The class is well organized. I loved the thought-provoking questions she raised for the class to think and write about.

Her projects have very vague descriptions and grading policies. Lectures are totally unrelated to the assignments, but you are asked to attend the lectures. Writing is not a big deal in her version of Engl 131, because there are two major graded oral presentations! In a writing class!

One of the worst profs I've ever had. She "didn't want to read the same paper 40 times," so she made up vague projects and didn't explain her expectations. There was barely any content; I could have skipped 5 weeks and known the same amount. She picks favorite students and only listens to them, but everyone who shows up gets a 4.0. Waste of time.

Personally found Nancy to be a great professor who really wants you to learn. The whole class was discussion-based and content wasn't too difficult. She is very patient, especially with some of the more difficult students. Found many discussions enlightening, which is saying something since I usually don't say much in discussion-based classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Nancy is a nice person, but that doesn't always translate to her role as a professor. Her assignments are vaguely worded and she clearly has favorites in class. If you participate, she will like you and grade you better overall. She is friendly and helpful in office hours however, attend those if you can. There are better 131 teachers out there.

It seems like she forms an opinion about you in the first few days of class and judges you by that for the rest of the term.  This is bad for class morale because you know she will always hold that negative view of you.  She is very judgmental and doesn't allow her students to voice their ideas.  Avoid this class if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I love Professor Aylor she was amazing for poetry. The zoom class was very entertaining and she is very engaging. I would love to take her classes again! There is reading to do but that is expected for a poetry class and she uses great examples to help for understanding on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: best english professor I have ever had
Most understanding teacher ever. Take her for English 131, provides really good feedback and genuinely cares about the students.
Super caring and always willing to help!
Emma is the best! Super caring.
Best professor for an English Comp class you'll have! Super sweet, understanding, and really cares that you understand the material.
Take her class if you plan to take 131!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Emma was such a great teacher for ENGL 131. She was super nice and was understanding on the assignments. Do all the assignments because you will need them for the final portfolio (that determines your end grade). She gives really good feedback on all the assignments you do and is available to help if you're stuck! Would totally recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Emre is a GREAT professor -- he really knows the material well. He is so helpful and is a great teacher. This class requires a lot of work, but he's more than willing to help you. He made an 8:30AM class a joy to come to. Great econ lecturer, take him if you can!
quizzes and exam  are super relevant with the practice one. but some questions might be tricky. overall very good!

Lectures are clear, tests are very relevant to practice tests and homework. Quizzes can be slightly tricky on theory questions, so spend some time to read the book after class. His office hour is extremely helpful. Go there, tell him the question you're confused about, and he'll walk you through every step.

At first, I only  took this class because it was pre-req for my major; however, I love Econ after taking this class. Emre is a very nice guy. He will give you addcode if you attend his first lecture. His lecture is very clear and easy to take note. Use textbook only for practice problems (very important).   Easy to approach and will answer all ur Q
SUPER COOL

Emre is such a nice guy. He has a thick accent but he is easy to understand and is good at simplifying the otherwise complicated economic concepts. Quizzes were relatively easy but for some reason I didn't do very well on them--medians were around 70%. Final was easy--I think the median was like 90 or something crazy like that on that.

Mia is extremely sweet and openminded when it comes to students' individual styles of writing poetry. She personally helps you with your own writing during conferences (two), and the peer groups help as well. If you're interested in poetry, take this course. It isn't hard as long as you commit to actually writing poetry. Loved this course.

I absolutely loved this class.  Mia was incredibly thorough and helpful with her examples and lessons.  I've been writing poetry for years, but I feel like everything finally clicked when I took the course; My improvement as well as my classmate's improvement over just 10 weeks time was amazing. I plan on taking 383 with her next, she's awesome.

Awesome teacher! She was very helpful and thorough. Class objectives were clear. Do the readings, attend class (for participation grade), and do the assignments... you're guaranteed a decent grade if you show the effort.
amazing teacher!!!
Made a required english class informative and engaging. Very accessible and helpful when I had writing questions.
She is such a great instructor.

Does not allow notesheets on tests... Not really interested in whether students learn or not. No one's perfect, but he didn't really seem prepared for lectures and kept on making careless mistakes, which made notetaking difficult. Tends to talk to the board/himself, so it was kind of hard to hear.

Nice guy with a cool accent, however he doesn't seem to invested in his teaching. Classes consist mainly of New Theorem -> Proof -> Repeat. No homework though so that was a plus, just quizzes and exams. Be ready to write proofs on the exams.
Jonas is the man! Helpful and knows his stuff. He's a new teacher and you can tell, but he's a great guy and very willing to help his students

Professor Nijssen required an online textbook. A homework assignment, consisting of problems from the online textbook and on Canvas, was about once per week. A lab was about once every other week, with the lab report due on the day of the next lab. The first and last labs did not require lab reports. Two midterms and a final were present.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Highkey did not go to class. Not a bad guy or professor otherwise.

Bart clearly cares about the content he is teaching. However, that does not translate well to actually teaching the class. Homework grading was changed multiple times, each time making the homework harder. This class was taken in 2022 as a hybrid model, switching to in person half way, which did not help, but meant midterms were online.

lots of unnecessary derivation in lecture that he barely tests us on. Lectures are all over the place and hard to follow when you get lost. He's very personable but he desperately needs feedback on his class to make it better. Compared to all the other civil classes I'm taking this quarter, he is severely lagging behind in quality.

One of the most organized and well-prepared lecturers I've ever had. He definitely made a difficult subject easier through his teaching skills. The homework and tests were hard but very manageable. if you go to lecture and study.

Professor Nijssen is a great professor! His lectures are extremely organized and clear. He is also very helpful in office hours and always willing to answer questions in class. On top of this, he is hilarious! All in all, fluids was a great class. I would highly recommend taking any class from Professor Nijssen.

So many holidays and cancelled classes. Very genuine guy outside of class— visit him in office hours— but as a professor, hm. Canvas was disorganized and his directions were barebones. Kind of dependent on your classmates doing the readings and having something real to say; mine didn't, for the most part, so we spent a lot of time reading in class.

Pretty chill, attendance is taken and a lot of class is him presenting and us discussing the readings. Three books, two movies. Weekly discussion posts online are graded on completion, one group presentation, one creative rewrite essay, and one group podcast project due at the end of the quarter. Didn't grade till last weeks. Overall pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Class itself is really boring, most students were there because attendance is mandatory, and he checks it at the beginning. Other than reading it's not much work except two big group assignments that are a majority of your grade and he doesn't have ANY GRADING RUBRIC which is really difficult & he puts in grades the last week of the semester..

Very flexible prof! Decent workload but lots of extensions, EC opportunities, dropped assignments. Always willing to work with and encourage you. Just do the HW and come to class and you will learn a lot and get a high grade. 4 essays throughout quarter along with weekly smaller assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I honestly think the ratings given for Prof. Bacon are unfair. She is an extremely caring teacher, although many of the lectures get very technical and a bit hard-to-follow at times. As long as you show up to class and participate (even in small groups, you don't have to raise your hand), you will be good. Ample retakes given, clear instructions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Don't take this class she grades extremely hard dropped within the first week. likes to call out students and docks you based on if you talk enough in discussions or not so if you're naturally more quiet you already have a disadvantage in this class. :/

she's a extremely tough grader she grades based on if you raise your hand in class and if u don't talk enough. Got docked because I took my phone out to take a picture of the slides because she views it as 'not paying attention'.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Harsh grader. Lots of homework and writing assignments, feels very overwhelming. No other composition courses requires this much work, especially since this is a 100 level introductory course. Take ENGL 182 from another professor.

I won't lie, I spent less than a week in this class before dropping, as did a dozen others (Maybe she should think a little about why this is). The amount of homework required is completely insane. No other composition class requires that much work, there is no additional gain from taking this one, so there is no good reason to take this one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This professor was horrible, she was a harsh grader. She would not provide feedback on my assignment and just give me the lowest grade possible. My friends who got a 4.0 in this class even helped me with the assignments and still she gave me a low grade.

Would never take a class with this professor again. Gives a ton of homework and an extremely harsh grader. I resubmitted assignments after talking to her and she gave the same grade with a "did not pay attention to feedback" comment. Biased against certain students and gives them a very bad grade. Goes to the extent of calling them out in class.

Do not take a class with this professor. She expects so much from her students and it's not fair. She assigned so much homework and papers every single week, I spend almost all of my time doing homework for her class. It wasn't worth it anyway because she would grade so hard that no matter how much time I spent working on my I always got bad grades

The workload in this class was insane considering that other 131 professors assigned less essays and homework and overall were less tough.

One of my classmates was hospitalized and the teacher did not provide accommodations for my classmate, and even criticized their email professionalism while they were in pain in the hospital.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Cares very deeply about his subject and students and wants to make sure everyone understands the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: For ENGL471: anis is an extremely understanding and knowledgeable professor. this class has a lot of dense reading and multifaceted discussion, but anis makes everything accessible to students, offers really good feedback, and is lenient with deadlines. he's extremely kind and caring, cannot recommend him enough.

Anis really doesn't have any flaws as a teacher. He is extremely knowledgable about the subject, he provides excellent feedback and support to every student, and the work builds upon previous work in the class, providing a good flow. Would definitely take another class from this professor.

First time this class was offered, but you could tell him and Tony (the other professor) really enjoyed teaching the content. He loved hearing from the students and would always bring up interesting concepts for the class. Class itself was very lax, no real syllabus since it was the first time it was offered.  Lots of reading for canvas discussions

I actually took CHID 100. He is so caring. Really connects with students and cares about how you're doing, notices you as an individual and your effort in class. Great lecturer too, very engaging! Please take him if you can.
If you attend lecture you will do great. His lectures are ver thought-provoking and he clearly cares about the students' opinion
Nic is one of the kindest and most engaging professors I've had. The course materials and readings were also very interesting and well curated. Wish I could take this class again!

One of my fav profs at UW. Hes caring and you can tell hes passionate about what he teaches. 2 readings weekly, discussion posts for attendance, 3 essays including the final essay. Im in stem, but I learned a lot in this class and got me interested in the topics that we discussed. I HIGHLY suggest taking this class, its interesting and not hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Barr is one of the most caring and accommodating teachers I've ever had.
