There is a natural 3/4 day grace period for turning in assignments in late for full credit which makes the class way less stressful. Lectures are long and can get a bit boring at times but he is very passionate about the subject and he def knows what he is talking about.

One of the most empathetic people I've ever met. I feel like this class really helped me get better at looking at complex issues and thinking critically. His lectures are fantastic, and hold attention for the full 2 hours quite well. He's very understanding and truly cares about all his students.

Nick is, without a doubt, the best professor I've had in college and one of the best educators I've had in my life. He grades your work comprehensively and makes valuable notes that help you improve as a student. His assignments provoke critical thinking on a whole new level. He is compassionate and an amazing person. 100/10, would take again.

One of the sweetest people you will ever meet. Took his study abroad class and it was an absolute blast. He is very knowledgeable and understanding when it comes to his students. Would take a class with him again 100% if I had room in my schedule.

If I could give Professor Barr a 6/5, I would. He is one of the most caring, passionate, and accommodating professors I have ever had the pleasure of sharing class with. The course presented lots of challenging themes, but Professor Barr was consistently respectful and articulate in guiding student discussions. Fantastic experience.

An amazing professor! He cares a lot about both his subject and his students. Very lenient about due dates. Attendance was not mandatory, but I had to miss a couple weeks and felt like I'd missed out a bit. There were several essays throughout this course, all based on very interesting reading material, and he gave excellent feedback every time.

Nick is great! Super understanding through the challenge of the pandemic (lenient due dates, accessible thru email). I struggled getting stuff in on time but he reached out and helped me through it. Super interesting lectures and readings as well! Truly an awesome professor.

Prof Barr is a wonderful teacher. He is so understanding and caring towards his students and tries his best to be optimistic about school work and the virus. He has a lenient policy when it comes to due dates which is very much appreciated especially when you're taking other difficult classes. His assignments aren't too hard as well. 11/10

Nick is a true gem. You need to take him if you get the chance. Learning from him is a very indulgent experience. He has a lot of information to share, but all of it is meaningful to the subject. As long as you pay attention, he makes difficult concepts very easy to understand. (He is also very handsome)

Amazing prof! Really cares sooo much about his students and the class itself is so well thought out and relevant! There's definitely a good amount of reading, but it's all super interesting. Don't know if it's possible to get a 4.0, but if you truly care about the material and put effort into your work, 3.5+ is very possible.

One of the best professors at UW. Clearly cares about his students and always willing to help, I have never had a professor as helpful as him and cannot recommend highly enough. In class he provides clear expectations and helps to stimulate excellent discussion.

Nick is great professor and solid human being. He invests in his students. He is intelligent and thoughtful and lectures in a way that includes his students in the conversation. The class covers very relevant readings and his lectures are engaging. I love this guy!

This was his 1st time for 207 and hes still adjusting, but overall he's a great teacher. He's really passionate about the material and even though its pretty heady, he's good at breaking it down. The class has two large papers and three smaller book summaries, grading is straightforward and not at all hard to get a 3.3+, but impossible to 4.0

Awesome lectures and really cares whether the students learn the content. She makes every question feel welcomed and you can tell she wants the students to not only understand but make it as accessible as possible for success. By far one of my favorite professors and the structure of her lessons are awesome. 10/10.

Amazing prof. Took a super late class, and she structured it in a way that worked for all students. Wants to make sure you understand the content and all of the content is available at all times. It is a lot of information, but expectations are clear of what you should know.

I only used 2 weeks to study mgmt200. One week before midterm and one week before final. I got a 3.5 but her class is the most time efficient one I've ever taken. The homework are 19 quizzes but only count 10. They are all due a few days before final. I recommend taking quizzes before exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thoroughly enjoyed Bebe's class and she is clearly incredibly well-versed in her field. Lectures were easy to follow and she always gave the class good idea of what exams would look like. Although she does not provide practice exams, concept check questions were always very similar to the actual exam and I did not have a hard time studying.

Bebe was rlly chill. The class was pretty straightforward and she only tests off her lecture content, so I would recommend reviewing the slides instead of the textbook for exams. She talks pretty fast and there's A LOT of content so make sure to frequently review. Graded based on midterm, final, and 3 short canvas quizzes + textbook chapter quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super fast and dense lectures with almost no notes on his slides. I honestly think he writes his lectures beforehand and reads them like a script. That said, he's funny enough that I genuinely didn't care about that. He's also willing to answer any questions that you might have. Exams are pretty easy too.

Very, very intelligent and accessible.  The class was lecture-heavy, but asking questions was heavily encouraged.  Graded on very few meaty assignments, but prep was easy to do.  Cares a lot about learning and current affairs, definitely a class to take if you can.

His lectures are very clear, they do tend to have a lot of content at a fast pace, but he always encourages questions from students. Homework is super managable only brief readings each week, with weekly quizzes on lecture/reading content. Professor really cares for each student. One of the most intelligent professors I've had at UW. I RECOMMEND!!

Easy grader, but he talks really fast, doesn't use slides, and if you don't take notes you will struggle. Make note of overarching concepts and events but don't worry about the details of the events, just note what caused them and their overall impact. Do the readings and take notes on them, referencing them boosts your exam grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bessner is excellent. He is incredibly knowledgeable about social science and foreign policy. This course is very content-heavy, but you generally split into groups, do a presentation and group paper, and engage in great discussions with the rest of the class. Participation matters more to your grade than anything else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Bessner was very nice, always quick to get back to your emails. There were only four assignments throughout the quarter, not very difficult. The main problem for me was that we didnt have much material to work with besides his audio lectures, which made things a little more difficult for me since Im not familiar with foreign policy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Bessner has SO much knowledge in his field, it seems like there isn't anything he doesn't know. There is a lot of reading for this class, but the class consists of only group projects/papers which presents it's own challenge, but honors kids are pretty reliable. He is approachable, kind, and wants everyone to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Take his class. Just do it.

Bessner is such an amazing professor. His class was my favorite class at UW. The class was discussion based, and every discussion was incredibly intellectually engaging without being too difficult to understand. His lectures were also super interesting, and I really appreciated hearing his perspective on a lot of current events. Take his class!!

Professor Bessner is a respected professor. He gives you extra credits if you go to his talks. The extra credit is worth it since you only have a midterm and a final. Talk to him about anything, he knows the subject well.

Extremely intelligent and successful; it is an honor that he teaches here. Students without a background in history may struggle with his fast-paced lectures; I think he should integrate them more with discussion. However, he is always on your side, especially for questions related to your real life and he grades kindly (average class grade 97.20).

Do you like getting good grades? Legit I got a 97/100 on the midterm and a 98/100 on the final and tons of people got 100% on both. Daniel is legit the best teacher I have ever had in college and gives the most amazing lectures.  He is so smart, soooo smart and honestly I would vote for him if he ever ran for any gov. position.  He not ugly either

Daniel is a great lecturer, be prepared to take a lot of notes and focus on history. His class is in depth and you should know that, he is a historian after all. His open discusses and friendly demeanor is another reason Professor Bessner gets a gold star in my book. Plus for the course no book, all online. What a champ!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Incredibly smart and engaging professor. If you have the opportunity take one of his classes! He clearly tells you what he expects and is a reasonable grader. He is also very open to discussion beyond the class' material such as current events.

Truly engaging lectures from a knowledgeable respected professor. It can be a bit exhausting to take notes for 2 hours straight, but I would listen to the lectures for fun on my own because I like history and it's presented in an interesting way. Prof Bessner is also really not out to get you. He seems to care much more about effort than polish.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Take him if you can! Professor Bessner is an amazing teacher. He is one of the most intelligent professors I have had, and facilitates great discussions while at the same time he genuinely cares that his students learn. If you have a chance to take one of his classes, attend a talk/seminar of his, or stop by his office--do it!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Bessner clearly knows his stuff and is passionate about his field.  He gave relevant, important information that I regularly find connections with in my other classes.  Almost every class is completely lecture, that he reads nearly verbatim from his notes.  More interactiondiscussion would make this class a GREAT class.

You cannot help but respect how passionate he is about his field. He genuinely cares about students learning. He makes seemingly dry topics really interesting. His lectures can be dense sometimes, but they are always engaging . He also likes to point out interesting information and fun facts about the material. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

TAKE ANY OF HIS CLASSES! Brilliant professor, engaging, witty, attentive and very easy to talk to. Discussions are challenging, but very well designed and the readings are AMAZING. Tests and papers are hard, but reasonable, based on your critical analysis of class concepts. Overall, a great professor who pushes you and makes subject come alive.

Extremely demanding class that requires you to be constantly paying attention and remembering every little thing she says in lecture and in quiz section. 
She does give a little extra credit but the expectations for the tests and presentation are so unclear and yet very specific where you will always score lower than what you think. Don't take....

I enjoyed this class with Dr. B! She incorporates a lot of small group work into lecture, so participation is important. She's also funny and approachable and often brings snacks. The material can be hard but is manageable if you attend lecture and discussion section.

I missed a quiz section at the beginning of the quarter by accident, and it seems like she has had it out for me since then. Completely unaccommodating, doesn't want to work with you, and won't help you with questions if she doesn't like you. She reads from her lecture notes, which disconnect from her talking, I doubt her knowledge of the material.

I took this class 2025 Fall and loved it! It was taught by Dr. B and Dr. Gilbert. Although there was an exam every other week, you got one drop and were all multiple choice. Slides are posted and clear to read. I never read the textbook, just rewatched the lectures and review the slides. Do go to PF sessions and office hours if you have time.

The lectures are A LOT of information but she does a good job explaining it all. Some people, like I did, might have to rewatch parts of the lecture to fully understand the content. Her office hours and PF sessions on test weeks are really helpful.

The class was taught by two professors, Dr. B and another, who alternated each unit who taught the material. Despite putting in the same amount of work all quarter, I did significantly worse on the exams where Dr B. was teaching because her lectures were so confusing and hard to follow

The content is a lot and it is hard, but Dr. B does her best to make a conducive, welcoming, and supportive learning environment. There are lots of practice exams and questions (from her and from the PF workshops) and plenty of extra office hours to get you help if you need it. The classes do revolve on participation and active learning.

Overall, a pretty good professor. You can tell that she really cares about the content and is passionate about the content. Beware, she does grade poll everywhere in class and so that makes attendance mandatory. However her grade drop policy is generous so you can miss a few classes before it affects your grade. She also has an exam drop too.

Currently taking this class right now, the readings might as well not be worth it since we gloss over everything in class quickly. Promotes active learning environment but wastes time with calling teams and using whiteboards. I never went to a PF session but studied with exam reviews and extra PF resource sessions, but somehow it's never enough

I'm currently taking BIOL 118 with this professor. The fact this class is an exam heavy-weighted class has a lot to say. She gives out exams every other week, once you're done with one exam, guess what? You have to start studying for another. The readings are hefty so you might as well not have a social life at all.

Amazing Professor who really cares about her students success. There are daily pollev's but you can drop a certain amount of missed polls. Her exams were straight forward if you studied and paid attention in lecture.

Hour long lectures everyday that you need to show up for in order to receive credit. She also spends way too much time calling on teams and then complains when we start to pack up a minute before lecture ends because she didn't finish her lecture slides. Exams every other week so be ready to study a lot. Way too hard for an intro class.

The class is test heavy; however her expectations are clear, and she cares for her students. She always leaves room for questions in class and its very interactive as it's an active learning environment. She is super nice when it comes to questions and her tests are very correlated to her slides and lectures. Overall, a great professor

Great professor who clearly knows what she's talking about and cares about getting her students to understand the material. Lots of opportunities for extra work if you are confused and some opportunities for extra credit. As long as you show up to lecture and pay attention, you'll do fine. Don't really need the textbook.

Her class is very interactive but i honestly liked it. She explains things detail during lecture. I dont even go to the PF meetings but i have a good grade. I really like her class tbh. It is a test heavy class and attendance is mandatory but honestly it is not too bad. Use the slides as your reviewer and use resources such as peer facilitators.
I kindly sent her an email, but she replied in a very impolite tone. She's being extremely rude to her students, and I'm quite sure I won't take her class again in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Grade is mostly determined by exams, there is one every other week. It's a lot of work, but if you study the material and stay on top of things you should be fine. There is a textbook, but you don't really need to read it. You get credit for attending lecture. She is a good professor, and you can tell she is really passionate about Biology!!!

she has a lot of information to teach but she always adjusts based on what she gets through and what she doesn't. theres an exam every other week, and attendance is pretty mandatory. in each unit she connects to a health equity issue and relates all info to real life scenarios. i feel like i learned a lot but def hard work

She switches up her exam style throughout the quarter. If you ask her to clarify what she was talking about in class she doesn't know what she meant by what said half the time. This is a physiology class and she barely ever tested us on mechanisms but rather transport proteins. She is awful, UW needs to fire her, NEVER take her class!!

I loved her lectures but make sure to look at the book too. Show up to class for participation questions/points. Had one group project at the end which sucked but can be done with minimal effort. Also GO TO OFFICE HOURS nobody ever went but she will answer anything if you do go and its super helpful. We had 5 exams, equal weight and drop lowest 2.

Professor Meredith is a fine professor. Not the best I have had and definitely not the worst. She teaches endocrinology well but is not the best at answering questions. Her exams focus on topics we did not focus on in lecture. The true only saving grace of my grade were the amazing TA and peer facilitators.

Worst professor I have ever had at UW (as a senior bio major). You can tell she has not taught this course before because she could not teach the material. Expected us to know so many details in such little time-Midterms were very two weeks. When I emailed her out of class, was not nice or helpful over email. Avoid taking her classes at all cost!!!

This class really grew on me as the quarter went by. Professor Bachman deserves all the praise. He is extremely knowledgeable and able to make connections across various topics through his PowerPoint presentations. I highly recommend this as an introductory course to IS.

150-200 pages of reading per week on content that is never covered in lecture. Slides probably haven't been updated since he got tenure in the 40s. Dull lecturer but he knows the content very well. I enjoyed the content, but the readings really brought this class down.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bachman is a very dull lecturer but is very knowledgable about the content. Despite it being a smaller class there was virtually no discussion unless folks had questions. The reading selection was generally good and prompts for exams reflected the readings + lecture topics well and were published in advance. Take if you are interested in the topic.

Bachman is nice but dull (though he sounds better at 2x speed on Panopto!). The workload is heavy but doable; just skim/skip the reading and focus on the final (defining/explaining terms + an essay) and the research paper. Not a lot of fun, but if you need to take the class, it's certainly not the end of the world, especially with a decent TA.

This class overviews relevant topics for anyone studying/interested in IR. It is the most demanding course I've taken at UW, so get ready to put in the work. Lectures are recorded/non-mandatory, you really only have to attend section to do well (I had a great TA). I liked the content and learned so much - I would only really take it if you like IR
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: He monotones in his lectures so it makes it difficult to want to go to class. Also the final has an absurd amount of possible choices, and half of them we barely covered. Other then the appx 200pgs of reading per week, the workload is not bad, as we mainly had one essay that was like 35% of our grade but was easy if you're good with essay writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: JSIS 201 should be renamed The Making of the American 21st Century because we talked about everything from a US perspective. Bachman's nice but lectures are monotone, and by the last week barely anyone showed up. Readings are long (150 pgs per week) and have nothing to do with the lectures, and even my TA was confused about Bachman's expectations

Final exams (yes EXAMS) are the bane of the class. One includes two parts, where you remember 86 terms because you will be tested on 10 of them randomly. To also order it in chronological order, while explaining the 10 (3-4sentences each). Then followed by essay (1 of many RANDOM prompts). NO NOTES. Good luck staying in this for IntStudies major.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures were dull and he moves through the text-heavy slides so quickly you can't even type it all. You're forced to read multiple chapters from multiple books each week. At the end you have an essay, a presentation, AND a final exam, and the exam is INSANE. 86 terms to memorize, a full timeline, and 12 potential essay prompts... good luck...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible, skippable lectures - reading from slides, lacking any nuance/analysis. Archaic course format with hardcopy submissions, pop quizzes, disorganized canvas/syllabus, and most graded work due in final 1/4. Tanks GPA by curve grading for no apparent reason. Pray for a good TA. This prof is an example of the bad consequences of tenure.

First few lectures already tell it will be a long quarter. He talks extremely slow and monotone=hard to not fall asleep. It is recorded, but it would be even harder to watch. 7 different articles to read on first week, followed by needing to buy 4 required other different books. Have fun sitting and watching him read directly off slides for 50 min.

Lectures are recorded. Readings are long and lack connection to lectures. Everything graded is due in the last 2 weeks of class. Professor Bachman is kind but the class is dull and focuses on an American-centric history of the Cold War through a lens of political economy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is super knowledgable and knows what he is talking about but his lectures are extremely monotone and will bore you very easily. Also this class requires a LOT of work so be prepared to write lots.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This course material is actually super interesting which is why I was super disappointed by Bachman. There is a outstanding amount of reading with monotone lectures that do not coincide with one another. Bachman never released rubrics until the last minute and our TA never knew the answers to any of our questions. Made this class more difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class has the opportunity to be really fascinating but is so hard to pay attention. The format is unbelievably dry. Lecture does not relate well to the readings and feels as though the readings & lectures are parallel and never intersect . Would not recommend. Prof Bachman seems as though he has done this 1,000x over and would rather not be
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you are interested in international relations and history, the readings are inspirational guidebooks to grasp the basic methodology and ideas of international studies. Dr. Bachman is sufficiently humorous. I wished this smart guy was my granddad. Love you, David.

His lectures are really boring so I never went after the first day but attendance isn't really mandatory so. My effort level for this class was close to zero but I still did fine as long as you know what's going on in the news and participate in quiz sect. It really depends on your TA though because mine was lenient with grading and participation.

Bachman's lecture presentation style is standard. He reads the slides and then gives further explanations. If you don't want to go to lecture, you can watch Panopto and read lecture slides. As for the difficulty of the class, I barely read the texts and still got a good grade. Tips: stay updated w/ news & know basic post-WW2 history for an A

i was planning on majoring in international studies but after this class, nope. there's too much reading & sometimes we don't even discuss it, classes are so dry (but as a person bachmans nice) & there's panapto so u don't even have to go to lecture, ta's expect too much out of you for the 10% participation that its worth so def go to quiz section.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: terrible class. Lectures were dry, and we hardly went over discussion questions for 100+ page readings assigned every week. He also stopped putting out discussion questions after week 5 so it was hard to know just what he wanted you to get out of the readings. Super harsh grader and your grade depends on three assignments. Would not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Glad the class is over. Professor Bachman's lectures did not relate/contribute anything to help us prepare for our paper assignments or exams. Finals are SUPER hard! It's the hardest final exam that I've ever done and I'm not sure how I did on it. However, my only hope is that I can pass this class because I DO NOT want to have to retake it again.
super boring lectures and tons of tricky points to prepare for the final exam. It was too late when I realized I have to drop this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Bachman is a great Professor, yet comes off as a bit dry when teaching JSIS 201. However, he is a wealth of knowledge and is well respected in the Jackson School. In regards to JSIS 201, it's the weed out class for the JSIS major. It's certainly a tough one. Would NOT recommend taking this class for fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: While the subject of the class itself is very interesting, Professor Bachman's lectures are extremely boring, and very minimal in terms of being useful for the final and four other papers you must write. You MUST do the readings to pass this class, as that is where you learn most. It is a hard class, and don't expect it to be easy at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Hardest class ever!!! You are basically forced to take this class if you are in the UW Jackson School, so I don't recommend taking it for fun. I was an Asian Studies major and even I found it so hard taking this class. The finals will be closed note/book and you have a lot of terms to know/remember as well as written essays and the New York Times.

UGH!!!! Dr  Bachman's  lecture is so boring and unenthusiastic. I only take his  class as a requirement for my major to graduate. His class is one of the hardest class that I've ever taken. You are basically busy every week with response papers, research papers, readings, etc. TA grades you hard and study guides for his finals are long and tricky .
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Dr. Bachman's Rise of Asia was slightly boring, but overall a typical lecture based class. The subject was interesting, especially when Bachman discusses more abstract, modern concepts as opposed to just the history of Asia. The reading was very heavy and I often found myself getting behind, but it's possible if you can organize your time well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Bachman is real nice guy, with a lot of knowledge on Asia. When it comes to teaching 201 though, he's not the most passionate. In general the lectures are just a historical review and if you're doing the readings you can probably skip. His voice also is kind of soothing which can be hard to handle in the afternoon.

Bachman is a very knowledgeable professor who is passionate about his expertise in Asian relations. However, his lectures are very boring. His voice is monotone, and he has a tendency to ramble on about bullet points on his slides. There is a 6-8 page research paper; it is not too bad though. Lots of reading, for sure!

He gives long lectures in a somewhat monotonous tone but he's a really bright guy and it's a privilege to get to listen to him, particularly regarding China (which is likely what he'll be teaching). Class is not extremely difficult but not easy per se.

Prof. Bachmann's lectures can be boring and monotonous; however, he is extremely knowledgeable (specifically about US-China Relations and East Asia subjects) and great to talk to about IR during Office Hours. Not a super overtly enthusiastic lecturer, but I think he really does care about his students (need to make an effort interact w/him)

I really enjoyed Dr. Bachman's class. He's clearly an expert in his field, and it really shows through in his lectures. If you are going to learn about history with an Asian focus, or especially US-China relations, I highly recommend his class. Also, take advantage of his office hours! He has good things to say.

Extremely knowledgeable about US-China relations. Lectures are a bit monotonous but occasional discussions are quite insightful. Prof. Bachman won't really show his views until the end of the quarter, and challenges, but does not judge, people's opinions. He seems intimidating at first, but you'll find that he genuinely wants his students to learn.

Very knowledgeable professor. However, his lectures can be extremely boring because of his mono-toned voice. Make sure to read the books because they will come back in the midterm and especially the essays! Though the main things that are tested is through his power points.

Definitely read the books because they like to see you use them on the final.This class is a lot of work, but if you're interested in international studies its really fascinating.Bachman really knows what he's talking about and gives great insight.  If you don't go to class, be sure to watch the screencast b/c lecture info is very important.

Bachman is probably the best if not one of the best China studies professor at the UW. He's a hard but fair grader and won't try to impose his views on you. For papers, as long as you have a strong argument backed by evidence, you'll be fine. Anyone doing a China studies focus MUST ABSOLUTELY take a class by Bachman.

Bachman ran our "Task force" group and I have to say he didn't seem to enjoy doing that. He hardly ever said a word and he struck me as just a  professor who clearly wasn't very good at hiding the fact that he didn't actually want to teach students. Probably he enjoyed the pay and lifestyle of being a prof. but he just seemed pretty burned out.

Bachman is incredibly intelligent. Everything he says is important, which makes note-taking hard. If you are struggling go & meet with him! He is so helpful one-on-one. unless you are interested in IS, don't do it. The TAs are REALLY hard but REALLY helpful. They want u to learn & gain skills & engage. Meet with them one-on-one too! Really helpful!

Professor Bachman is extremely knowledgeable when it comes to China. He knows just about every single event down to the exact date and specific details. This class has a lot of reading that requires a lot of time. It's a bit tough, but definitely worth it, especially for those interested in China and US-China relations!
Very nice professor!!

I learned a lot from Bachman! He is really intelligent and knows what he is talking about. If you have any questions he will help you. Everything you need to know for the course is provided in your notes. Reading the books is helpful but attending class is more important! Loved this class and got a good grade :)! Amazing professor!

Bachman is incredibly intelligent. Loved the class. Maintaining interest in the class is really up to the student, not the professor, so if people say he is boring that is their fault for not caring enough about what Bachman had to say.

I would agree with the one who said his style was a mix of academic disdain and disinterest. I also witnessed him making a mocking statement about a graduate student who he did not seem to like or agree with politically. Before this student presented, he told the rest of the class to come back after the break to "hear his performance."

Bachman is extremely knowledgeable and very thorough in his lectures. However, he does not use lecture slides, but rather a word document with a few key points. This, coupled with he monotonous voice and occasional mumbling (although he was generally eloquent) can make it difficult and boring to follow lectures. This is the hardest class I've taken

Hard class due to the sheer amount of reading that must be done. You don't have to do all the reading, but it obviously helps you out on all the papers you'll be writing and the final. It's a weed out for the Jackson School, so I don't recommend taking it for fun.

I really loved both SIS 201 and Professor Bachman! I think the comments here are misleading.  His lectures are interesting and well-organized even though he isn't very animated, he really cares about what he is teaching and whether you learn. He makes some really funny deadpan jokes and he is a really genuine, kind man and good professor.

My opinion... I REALLY disliked that class. His monotone voice put me to sleep each time. I always had to refocus my attention from daydreaming! The textbooks are interesting (except for Keylor). His TAs are hard asses! Smallest thing and you are graded down for it. On a brighter note... It is an interesting class. I definitely learned a lot.

Professor Bachman was surprisingly one of my favorite professors that I have had so far. His lectures helped clarify the required readings and put them into a bigger context. He is very intelligent and a genuinely nice person. . However, if you aren't interested in international studies, you probably shouldn't take this class, it's a lot of work.

This may have been a result of the course format (giant lecture), because he's obviously an intelligent man, but gosh I have hated taking SIS201 from Prof. Bachman.  His lectures are bearable, but the way he structures the course (assignment schedule, grading) makes me feel like I'm in high school again. Ugh.

His class is fairly easy if you pay attention to the materials that he's teaching. I got a 3.7. However, he does speak in a monotone voice & gives out a quiz once a week based on the readings and news article(s). Nonetheless, he gives a lot of extra credit and grades fairly. I learned a lot of interesting facts about Asia in this class. :]

Gosh he's mumbling in class. It's hard to understand him even WITH the mic. Lecture notes are sent to students, but they're kinda messy. TAs are very strict at grading. Reading assignment is super long, I gave up at the middle of the books. The good thing about this class is the extra cred and the fact that you got to update Asia's news every week

He's a good prof.a little bit boring that makes u wanna sleep, a lot of writting and readings,but i never read the book and got a A so it was not that bad. 2 long papers to write but not difficult, and his grading is fairly easy, very knowlegeble on the subject and a nice person.
very dull. monotone voice. sounds like he's having a boring conversation with himself. imagine watching c-span in person. that is his lecture.
Great professor!

Course material was interesting, but Prof. Bachman made it really difficult to enjoy. Lectures were extremely dry and full of lots of historical facts and information. He speaks with a monotone voice, barely raising his voice so you have trouble hearing him. Lots of reading and writing in this class, but take SIS 201 with Prof. Migdal if you can.

Very knowledged on his subject matter and very clear in presentation, but lectures tend to be just him talking with no interaction with the students (doesn't ask questions to the students, have activities/warm-ups/etc).  Would advise a hefty dose of caffine before any of his classes.
He presented the the class in a very linear and easy-to-understand manner.  He obviously knows his stuff.
His lectures are very informative and interesting.  He is obviously very knowledgable about the subject matter.

I entirely disagree with the negative comments.  Prof Bachman's introverted personality can make him come off as slightly hostile, but he's not.  He's actually friendly and helpful if you talk to him.  He's very knowledgable and gives good/informative lectures, but does require a lot of work so be ready to put in the effort.  Very good prof overall

Prof. Bachman is really bright and knows a huge amount about China. He's pretty helpful and draws a lot on the readings. His organization is strong and I really liked getting the notes emailed to me after the class.

Monotone voice, no sense of humor, and a hybrid of sincere disinterest and academic disdain characterize his dry, factual, repetitive lectures. Tip: he rarely mentions or refers to assigned readings, and you need not do more than read the conclusions for his tests, in my experience.

Excellent lecturer, truly knows his stuff! Homework's and Final were fairly difficult but graded very leniently. Very interesting material presented in an effective way where often you will prove parts of results shown in lecture.

His lectures were great, just a little long. He answers questions well and is very helpful during office hours. The class is also difficult, but he does a really good job teaching, so it's not impossible. Also, the final was a take-home, so do with that information what you will.

Fantastic professor, class content is diabolically hard but very possible to succeed in. I don't really do STEM which is probably why I struggled, but I still scored highly consistently. Just make sure you turn everything in on time!! Feintzeig is actually the goat though, incredibly intelligent and really easy to work with outside of class.

I have so much to say about Professor Feintzieg. Not only is he incredibly knowledgeable, but is also incredibly accommodating -- his class was difficult, but difficult in the way that you leave the course with a completely changed mind and as much passion as him. I absolutely recommend him for PHIL470 (and honestly for anything else) :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prepare for dense readings. It is very possible to do well, although some of the subject material can be boring and complex. Prof and TAs are very helpful and accessible. The back-to-back papers are pretty demanding. Otherwise, a pretty manageable class considering the topics. I wouldn't want anyone other than Feintzeig teaching this.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Respected

reviews.comment: Really interesting guy but terrible class. Did for psych major but instead ended up doing a philosophy of the history of science course and struggled. If you attend office hours, do the readings, and pay attention during class, you have a great shot. 4 papers plus final essay and take-home exam are not bad when you get the hang of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lectures were extremely boring, and he always assigned a crazy amount of reading to be done before every class (which you were also quizzed on). Never talks about anything interesting really, and there never seems to be a "point". Four papers assigned and due back to back, in addition to a final essay AND written response final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is a great person and enthusiastic about the subject. However, participation was graded based on accuracy, which I didn't like (PollEv). The papers were graded harshly by the TAs. Don't take this if you're looking for an easy elective. You will have to put a lot of effort in to get a 3.5+. Very interesting course material though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Feintzeig was very caring and considerate of student questions and issues. It is easy to tell that he is passionate about philosophy. He calls on students randomly but he calls by name, so you will probably only get called on twice throughout the quarter. You can pass when he asks you, but you have to answer the next question.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Benjamin is such an amazing lecturer. The way he develops a topic and engages you makes the class so enjoyable. My advice, when doing the essay assignments go to your TA's o/h and have them guide you through the writing process. Especially for your last essay. Losing a point here and there early on makes getting a 4.0 at the end much harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you haven't written a philosophy paper before get ready to put in a lot of work. Lot of reading and Is a morning person.

Great philosophy teacher.  His class is very reading and lecture heavy, but it is clear that he honestly cares about the material and his students' comprehension.  The class was tough, and was graded heavily on only 3 papers, but the grading was fair and he is happy to work with you to help you succeed.  No tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Feintzeig is a new professor and we were very much his guinee pig class. As a result, we had work that was not always clear and A LOT of students were upset. Lectures were interesting but you had no idea what was relevant to the course. Still a good course, but expect a good bit of work. Also expect it to improve by next year's course.

I think this was his first time teaching the class, which may have contributed to the complete disaster that it was. The lectures were extremely boring and moved too fast to take good notes. The assignments were hard and they were graded even harder. Wouldn't recommend taking this class with him anytime soon.

Great professor; great at explaining complicated topics in a way that inspires you to want to read more in your free time. Reading responses are graded very generously, but the lectures are so interesting that he makes you want to read closely anyway. I learned a lot about philosophy of science in this course and was pushed to think for myself.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment:
Best class ive ever taken and amazing professor, her lectures were great and the readings were extremely interesting. 
Two essay-based exams and about 5-6 quizzes, you can take the quizzes 3 times each. In class assignments are easy and given about once a week. Discussions with other students are encouraged in class.
Professor Katherine is amazing!
Indoctrination type class--hard socialist. Typical rants, dogma, dogma dogma. You get the point.

Professor Beckett is great, this class does have 4-5 weekly readings that can range from 10-50 pages, but if you are interested in the LSJ dept. or social justice in general, the readings are anything but a burden. The lectures are awesome and interactive, she really knows her stuff and how to convey it to students.

Professor Beckett is incredibly knowledgeable. As for the class, there was weekly reading responses that varied from 10-50 pages, so it wasn't the easiest but definitely manageable. 2 papers, 3/5 pages. 2 hour final, short answer/essay. Definitely recommend the class for anyone interested in hot button legal issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Beckett's lectures were fascinating and incredibly informative! The class is pretty reading-heavy, but tbh, I think that's normal for LSJ, and there wasn't a single piece of material that wasn't worth the time. Two papers, worth 20% of our grade EACH - which, ow, but honestly, the class is worth it. Took this in connection with ENGL 298.

Overall, do not take this class if you do not plan on minoring or majoring in LSJ. While Katherine and the TAs are all great, the class content is very repetitive. The reading responses/assignments honestly feel like busywork. All in all, I feel like way too much work is asked for from a 200 class. This class made me stray away from the LSJ dept.

She is a really nice prof, and the RA I had was amazing as well. I had a family emergency partway through the quarter and they were very accommodating. Your grade is based on 2 essays, the final and then reading assignments/participation in quiz sections 2 times a week. Overall the lectures were super interesting and can be rewatched if needed
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: She is amazing! Her lectures are very insightful and easy to follow. They are recorded, so attendance isn't mandatory (but discussion section is). The course consists of weekly readings that come with a set of 6 questions to answer for 1-2 of them per week. There are 2 papers and 1 final exam (5 short answer & 2 essay). She is very understanding.

Professor Beckett is a wonderful professor. She is super knowledgeable and clearly loves teaching. The class is also well-organized. There is a lot of dense reading, but if you go to TA office hours, they will help explain the main concepts. Overall, a great professor and course.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Really nice professor. Really well-organized classes, very kind and patient, and she keeps trying to make sure that she and her TAs are teaching consistently. Highly recommend her LSJ 200 because she is experienced in teaching this course and she knows how to make her students understand every concept well. Also very caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: prof beckett is the best i've had at uw. her lectures are super informative and not boring and all the readings are so interesting they don't feel like homework. two tests and a paper plus small quiz section assignments but ultimately if you have a passion for lsj you will pass easily

Prof. Beckett is incredible; she's a fantastic lecturer and super woke. Readings can be hard but are explained well in quiz section. Lectures are participation heavy, so students should show up and contribute to get the most from her class. Slides are posted on canvas but they don't get close to what's said in lecture (AKA, show up!!)

Prof. Beckett is amazing! Concepts taught in class were very interesting. Lectures are interactive and there are plenty of opportunities to participate. There are a lot of readings assigned, but don't let that stop you. They are engaging, ties into the course very well, and expands on ideas from lecture. Definitely will take a class with her again!

Beckett is an amazing professor! First-ever class I took with her and I loved her! Her lectures are super interesting and she's inspirational. Although her classes are huge, she really tries to engage with her students. She also brings guest speakers in and they are actually relevant to the class/interesting.

Although lecture slides are posted online with all the key information, actually attending class will make the information clearer. Professor Beckett gives a lot of examples and clarifies any questions about curiosity or concepts discussed in class. There will be a lot of reading, but I found the class to be really interesting so it was worth it.

Definitely the best professor I've ever had at the UW. Her lectures are pretty intense and the slides that she posts online does not cover enough of what she tests you on so this is a class where you definitely cannot skip if you want to pass. Reading responses are helpful for the tests and her TAs definitely grade hard but fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Involved in class, difficult testing

Prof. Beckett covers a lot of interesting topics in depth. The midterm, final, and papers are HARD, but not impossible! I definitely suggest seeing her in office hours and meeting with your TA and taking good lecture notes. She makes you work for your grade, but the amount you get out of this course is worth.

I love Professor Beckett! She's incredibly knowledgeable about the subject matter of her class and her lectures are discussion-based and engaging. There were 2 tests and one major paper when I took her class, but from what I understand that tends to vary from quarter to quarter. There are quite a few readings for each class but they can be skimmed.

This class has heavy reading (lots of articles with reading guide that has to be typed and printed) which can be time consuming. Don't take this class of you are a conservative because listening to the libs talk for a quarter can make you go crazy. I learned a lot and really enjoyed reading "Just Mercy" (required book to read)

AMAZING PROFESSOR. My favorite who made me de ide to major in LSJ. A difficult class with lots of reading, but WORTH IT and that is coming from a stoner. Interesting concepts of war on drugs and criminalization of the minority. Super relevant to today and its common knowledge that she is a tough class so don't let that think that affects too much
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I LOVE Prof Beckett! LSJ 200 was an amazing class and made me want to major in LSJ. Beckett is well-spoken, articulate, caring, and passionate. She engages students in discussion, which is interesting in a large lecture hall, but I enjoyed it. The class is organized well into 3 major units, with either a test or paper at the end of each. Take it!

Katherine is a very intelligent prof and this class made me want to take more LSJ courses. However, she spends a lot of time calling on students for examples which can be frustrating, but you don't need to show up to lecture. Exams are straight-forward and you get a study guide.
Never went to her office hours but her lectures were on point. Just make sure to take good notes
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Beckett is smart and passionate about her classes. It's tough to have a discussion-style atmosphere in a 300-person class, yet she does her best to engage students rather than lecture at them. I appreciate the extra effort. She has great TAs, and between Prof Beckett and your TA, you will work hard; however, it will be worth it. Great class!
Beckett is great. Her lectures are very clear and she is so knowledgeable. She makes the lecture into a discussion which is very interesting and rewarding. I would highly recommend her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Prof. Beckett's lectures. She was really knowledgable and straight forward. The tests are definitely very long. You NEED to know what you're doing so while going to lecture isnt mandatory, you most def should! I genuinely enjoyed the class but it was graded a little hard. Would take her again though, for sure.
GREAT INSTRUCTOR!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best, if not the best, professors I have had. Extremely clear, intelligent, and helpful. Lectures are never boring and the expectations of the class are never unknown. 10/10 would recommend, not an easy A though

Beckett is awesome. She's very clear in lecture and engages with all students. Many people didn't like how she held a discussion in a large lecture class, but I thought it was fine. Gives exam possible prompts out in advance and is very straight forward with grading. I plan to take another one of her classes! Definitely take her.
While her lectures were discussion based, she did a pretty good job of making sure her points came across in lecture. 2 essay midterms and a take home essay for a final, with a lot of fun material!
Make sure to read ll the articles or you won't learn anything. Don;t be afraid to participate in lecture! It gives you a better experience.

She is a great professor to have! She is very clear, very professional, and makes seemingly boring material very interesting. Her class really expanded my mind in ways I couldn't imagine and made me want to minor in LSJ.

Beckett is a wonderful teacher; extremely respectful of the students. Everyone's input is valid. I never thought of her class as discussion based... that's what the quiz sections are for. She invokes active learning by asking for examples. She is very eloquent and concise. The midterms are easy, just pay attention to the prompt. Have fun!

This class was all discussion and no lecture which is a completely inappropriate way to teach a lecture with 300 students. I really don't care about other people's opinions...I come to lecture to learn the actual material! The expectations for the final essay were also not clear and the exam essays were graded really hard despite having the topics
Great Prof. enthusiastic about what she teaches. Exams are written but she hands out the prompts well in advance.

I really enjoyed Beckett's class. She's clearly intelligent and is very good at explaining concepts. Lectures are straight forward as she has an outline for each one. You don't *have* to do the readings in their entirety, but you should at least skim (most of the content can be had from quiz section discussion). Definitely recommend her.

Puts forth an honest effort to know and recognize every student.  She could be a bit clearer about what she wants from her essays.  While she puts her outlines on Catalyst sometimes, they are hard to understand if you don't go to lecture.  Good class and reasonable workload if you are okay with essay midterms/finals.

She goes through material off an outline really fast and rarely points out where she is.  class is discussion based so be prepared to hear a lot of examples from classmates. she gives the essay exam questions in advance. she gave the prompts for the essay early on to.  no surprises.  read, go to class, take thorough notes and you'll be fine!
Intelligent and clear!  Reading is interesting and reasonable.  The lecture is quite different as it's held in a conversational manner, interesting, nonetheless.
She doesn't finish her sentences, which makes answering her questions difficult than it should be.

I found this professor to be a bit of a joke. She ran the 200 student lecture in a manner not fit for that many students. Also, her presentations tended to ramble and some of her information was questionable. She also interjects too much political opinion into her lectures.
She dresses well. Harder class if you hate writing essays.

Katherine Beckett was the best professor I've had so far at UW. I learned way more than I had expected to. She is extremely intelligent, but isn't smug about it. She tries to include everyone in the lecture, and always has good responses to people's questions. Also check out some of her outside research--pretty impressive.

Class material is very interesting and she is really smart but runs her lectures complelety wrong.  tries to have class discussions in a 200 person class and people just end up shouting out useless opinions.

I hated her lecture. I felt like she taught it like a high school class. She tries to hold class discussions with 300 people. She spoke probably 30 minutes of a 90 minute class period. The rest was students talking and giving their opinions. I don't feel that I learned anything from taking her class.

It's not completely easy, but the extra credit gave me a 3.7 for the class. It was a fun class, and Beckett is one of the best lecturers. She is clear and not boring. Can't wait to take her in the fall again!

intro to law. class format: 3 essays (2-3 pages each; each worth 10% of final grade), a midterm (very easy, class average was 88%; worth 20% of your final grade) a final (10 page essay; worth 30% of final grade) and sections grade (based on small quizes and participation in discussions; worth 20% of final grade. class focused on immigration law.

She's so nice! Very clear. Only one midterm (definitions and essay) and one final paper. Relatively easy. Also three mini essays. She doesn't make the topics difficult. Grading depends mainly on your TA. No class website and she doesn't email any lecture notes. Makes the class interesting. Will always helps when needed.

Great, clear teacher. Enthusiastic. You have to attend her lectures since she doesn't post them. How your grade in that class is partially how well you write (it's worth 90% of your grade) and how your TA is. If you TA is rough, then you're going to have a rough time. My TA was cool, but pretty rough. Not sure why she was removed from RMP earlier.

Great professor--friendly, helpful, and very interested in her students and the subject matter.  Class isn't too easy or too difficult--two essay exams, one essay, and pop quizzes...it's all very fair.  Highly recommended course!  You'll love this professor!
Best class EVER!
One of the best prof's I ever had
No Comments
No Comments
Best class at UW!
Hot soc teacher, a great intro to deviance course
She is the GOAT. She genuinely cares about her students and their learning. The lectures can drag on a bit, but she is an amazing lecturer. The coursework is really easy and everything is open note.

Professor Kirk is super caring, respectful, and passionate. She really cares about what she is teaching and is super flexible and easy-going when it comes to grading of assignments, quizzes, and tests. The class was not very high in intensity or effort, but did require reading, participation, and attendance.

Her lectures are great but can get repetitive and boring if you read the textbook ahead. She's very passionate in what she covers about in class so it's very easy to stay engaged. Class was easy as long as you did the work and paid attention. I would recommend this class to anyone for an easy A (assuming you take good notes).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very human environment. Class was very easy.

only 50% of attendance is needed for full participation credit. exams are online and open-note. the only "homework" is doing a 10 question quiz with your learning group in quiz section which you can ask other ppl for answers or just look back at the slides. amazing professor and TA's!!
Kirk was super nice but lectures were ridiculously boring. I would find myself struggling to stay conscious.

Took this class as a first year and switched to the nutrition major after taking NUTR200. Content is interesting and useful. Exams are open book and reflect material accurately. Large class but Dr Kirk is happy to talk one on one with you after class. I would recommend this class to anyone looking for science credit.
She's extremely kind, understanding, and accepting of everyone. Truly one of the best professors! Super empathetic when covering sensitive topics. Def take any class with Dr. Kirk if you can!

Dr. Kirk is a wonderful professor. Before the lecture, she always waving everyone for saying hi and a lot of students gets to say hi to their neighbors. She's very sweet, nice, she cares about everyone. She was very friendly to everyone. She gave us two extra credit if we fill out the course evaluation for the lecture and discussion section.
I really enjoyed the class and professor kirk is very knowledgeable and kind, I would recommend, the class isn't stressful and only 50% of attendance is needed
Great professor, Dr. Kirk is very fair and a fun person to talk to outside of class. class is always fun, love it.

Super incredible professor, one of my fav

Didn't read "required" txtbk
but focused solely lectures
(I learned what I wanted, i.e. diseases, how 2b nutrition healthy, etc. -> you get what you want out of the class)

lectures -> cover 85% of tests
Ez Quizzes & Exams (>=1/wk) = 60% of grade i.e. bulk of the class (excluding attendance 40%)

Had Dr. Kirk for nutr 200 before and loved her! She answers questions well, you can tell she's passionate about what she does, and she's good about posting slides and recording lecture. Definitely don't skip out on the readings because that's where a majority of questions are from, but if you're worried about attendance you only have to go to 50%

Great class and great lecture because it's really the closest thing you can get at UW to a sports medicine class. Dr. Kirk is very well-organized, passionate, and uses her lecture time very well. Exams are online, and open note. Submit assignments on time, keep up with provided notes, and attend at least 50% of lectures for a good A. Learned a lot!

Useful lectures about nutrition; talks about diets, chemical composition, and nutrition labels. Contact by Canvas mail only. 3 lectures + 1 quiz section a week. Quiz section is a short lecture by TA and short Canvas quiz. Attendance is graded. Doing 50%+ of PollEv in lecture gives participation credit. Encourages all to do survey for extra credit.
She's genuinely kind and cares about you learning the course material. Learn how to use your resources before going into the class, and you will be completely fine!

Prof Kirk is fantastic! Really knowledgeable and the lectures are great, as well as making daily recordings of the lectures and posting them. Follows the free textbook but not much reading is necessary. 10/10 would love to take more classes with Professor Kirk!

Wonderful at teaching the intro nutrition class. VERY heavily uses the textbook. All of the quizzes/exams are 99% based on the textbook. It is a very interesting class. Assignments and exams are online. Some extra credit opportunities are offered!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Kirk is amazing! She's a great lecturer and genuinely cares about your success and learning. There is so much valuable information from her class. Would definitely recommend taking a class with her.
Great professor, clear explanation, and overall a great person.

She's also super understanding and does a great job of demonstrating hard topics with diagrams and visuals. Her exams are super doable and she loves watching her students succeed which is very refreshing. She offers very generous extra credit for doing the course evals so most people end up super pleased with their grade in this class.

Dr. Kirk is really caring for her students and is very lenient when it comes to graded assignments. For nutr200 there are weekly quizzes & four 45-50 MC Qs exams BUT everything is very easy to find online. For exams I suggest taking them with a friend but its an easy 4.0 if you use your recourses ;)

Dr. Kirk is amazing! She genuinely cares for her students and loves to make jokes during lectures to keep everyone engaged. This class was super interesting and not too hard at all. The 4 exams were online and open note, so not too hard. Would recommend!

Great professor! Such a sweet person and really cares about the needs of her students. Easy A, tests are online, and she assigns barely any homework. Lectures and discussion sections were super interesting, I learned a ton from her class in a very low stress environment. Would definitely recommend!

All tests were online, open note, and not too difficult. Professor Kirk is one of my favorite professors! She is kind and lectures were usually easy to follow. All lectures were online when I took it. There were also review sessions before the exams which were very helpful. I thought this class was really interesting!

Kirk is a great professor who clearly cares about her students. Lectures are not mediatory but are recommended in order to understand material. Exams are open book and assignments are done with ease. If youre looking for a GPA boost or to learn about nutrition Kirk is your best option, she is the best!

Kirk is by far one of the best professors I have had. She genuinely cares for her student's wellbeing and is amazing at teaching. All tests were open book, and I could do well on them with just my lecture notes. The textbook is included with a website you purchase a subscription for, but I never really had to read it

Prof is very knowledgeable and passionate about topic but is a bit difficult to pay attention to during lecture for me personally. Also i felt like she went through the slides too fast sometimes and the font was very small on the slides, so i just watched the online postings of lecture to take notes instead.

The content of this class was pretty standard and was similar to things I learned in middle school health. The tests however had some tricky questions that made it a little difficult to get a 4.0 but all exams/quizzes/homework were completely online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Kirk is a flexible prof - she takes time to review & regrade questions that were weird/confusing on quizzes. Not the MOST enthusiastic, but you can tell she's very interested in sports nutrition. Provides notes guides for lectures and exams are pretty easy. Readings are more detailed than what she expects students to know, so skimming is best.
I would not take her class anymore. Because I think there is not link between her lecture and exam. her exam questions make me confuse: have I ever learn this????

It was such an easy A. We were graded on four exams, launchpad assignments, weekly content quizzes on the lecture (3pts max, super easy), and weekly discussion section quizzes (participation is not required and both lectures and sections are recorded. As a non-STEM major, this is an easy 3.8-4.0.

TAKE THIS CLASS WITH FRIENDS. Lecture heavy, she goes fast and gives a bunch of info. at one time, but it's one of the easiest 4.0s at UW if you take with friends. All tests are completed online and they get harder with each test but just use your notes and you'll be good.
All exams are online and are open note so it is easy to do well! Pretty chill professor and lectures are interesting

Exams are all online, so you can use quizlets or your notes to take them and they are pretty easy. Her lectures aren't necessary, but then you'd need to read the textbook. Online assignments are just based on completion, but I enjoyed her lectures and personality. She does polls and they are graded based on getting the correct answer, however.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Heres what you need to know if you take Nutr 200, I took it with Melissa Edwards To get a 4.0 1. Have resources quizlet 2. Take with a friend poll everywhere is tricky 3. Be fast at control f finding answers to test questions 4 exams all online Hw and quiz section easy points guarenteed
Sports nutrition is really fun! Dr. Kirk is one of the best professors Ive had & always makes each class fun.

Not a crazy hard class, but definitely pay attention to textbook readings and lectures, because the exams can be thorough. She's a good lecturer. Super sweet, makes corny jokes and interesting real-life connections. She'll share relevant stories and connections worth coming to lecture. Do the work and you should be fine. It's an interesting course!

Dr. Kirk really cares for her students. She doesn't give a lot of work--just 10 super easy online assignments (drops lowest 2). No midterms/final, just 4 online exams. Go to class not just because of pollev (2.4% of grade, still important because a 4.0 is 98+) but because you can actually learn so much. Take notes & exams will be fine w/ quizlet :)

Kirk was super helpful when responding to emails and helping everyone outside of class. You have to show up to lecture because they have in class questions they ask nearly every time. The tests are all online and are easy if you pay attention to lecture and do the assigned readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Kirk is awesome! One of the few professors I've had that actually cares about the material and her students. Caring women, and an awesome group of TA's. Polleverywhere questions are counted for credit which makes participation pretty much mandatory. All exams are online and open note. Awesome class.
Best professor ever!!! She's so gooooooood! You can learn so many useful things and easily get an A!
She is so cute and funny! loves to laugh at her own jokes. She really cares about the topics she's teaching and loves her students. tests are online and uses pollev!
Informatic and funny, got me interested in public health and nutrition. Strongly recommend!

Love her! Love this class. Totally recommend. Subject really interesting, and she is really nice and cares that her students learn and pay attention to good nutrition in their lives! Go to class - you get 2-5 points each day by answering questions in lecture. You have to pay attention & take TONS of notes, but I always looked forward to it!

I took her Nutr 200 in the fall because I wanted to study nutrition. And it turned out to be the exact way I thought it was. She was passionate and knew what she was talking about! Her class definitely impacted my food choices in the future. And the exams are not so hard if you read the textbook and pay attention to the lecture! Would recommend it

I took it in the fall and didn't find it to be too stressful-exams online, she gave some extra credit with polleverywhere, and the homework was manageable in the class. Pulled off a 3.8 with minimal effort so I'm sure it's not hard to get a 4.0. Kirk's attitude is great and you can tell she loves nutr!! Has also helped me make smarter food choices
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Kirk for NUTR 200 in the fall and took her again in the winter for 406. Exams are online and if you read the textbook and take notes then the answers are almost always in your notes. Kirk is a great lecturer and really cares about students learning and utilizing knowledge for outside of class. Very interesting if you care about nutrition.

She uses Pollseverywhere for most lectures so show up for the participation grade, all the exams are online (still need to study though because it's timed and you don't have enough time to flip through notes/textbook on every question). Sometimes she goes kind of fast on lecture slides but she does Panopto recordings so just look back on those.

Prof. Kirk is super knowledgeable and her lectures are very well-paced and informative. Tests are online and open note. I typed notes in class so when I took tests I could "control F" and search through my notes super fast. I never had to read the book. Her supp du jour quizzes are super easy, she gets her questions straight from the text.
get ready to spend $80 for an "easy" class cause of the hw
She is a really good professor.
I did not attend class one time and got a 3.8. All of the tests and homework assignments are online and the participation points could be done from home.

Dr. Kirk is amazing in that her lectures are very interesting, but only if you're interested in nutrition. I really enjoyed the class: tests are online (4 total), two nutritional assignments, and quiz section grades. This course was called NUTR300 so look at those reviews as well. Overall, I highly recommend!

While it is easy not to show up to lecture, make sure to participate in PollEverywhere questions because it helps to get a small grade boost at the end. It is a very easy class with exams online and only two small projects.

4 Online Exams. 50 questions in 50 minutes. Love it. Clickers are only 2% of your grade but you can get extra credit. One of the few subjects that are interesting even for the worst students (the students who get bored easily and probably should leave UW). To get a 4.0 you need a 98%. Also some of the answers to some test questions are online.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Go to the lectures and take notes like you should do in all classes. Have poll everywhere questions which are easy and gives extra credit by them. Exams are online so just go to the lectures and you ll be fine.

Professor Kirk is well-spoken and cuts clear to the point. Her slides are straight-forward and follow the text. As long as you attend lectures, you'll pass the exams. You don't need to purchase the text because it is available on reserve, but be sure to to stay on top of any assigned readings.

I had Elizabeth freshmen year and I enjoyed the class. I learned lots about nutrition and about healthy eating which really helped me out to take smart food choices. Really appreciate the professor the class overall.
Kirk has very interesting lectures and keeps it interesting for the whole hour. It is a easy A class as long as you keep up with all the lectures. There is absolutely no homework, which is a plus.
Lectures can be a but dry at time, but exams are super easy as long as you study some the night before. Overall a very good professor.
Clicker points, but other than that, not much class participation. Clear lectures and she is able to share life stories that enhance the material.

Dr. Kirk's lectures are awesome! She was always available after class to talk or answer questions and all her exams were online this quarter. Some of her questions were tricky, but if you studied the material beforehand, you will be fine! I definitely recommend her. She does have clickers for participation so attend class.

Easy 4.0. 4 online exams that are all worth the same (46%). You just have to show up to quiz section because its basically participation(33%).  Two small projects that take like 30 mins (19%) and the clickers are worth 2%.  And on top of that Dr. Kirk is super kind and sweet and shes pretty awesome.  Classes are also on recorded on panopto.

Dr. Kirk is such a sweet lady. Although lectures can be a little boring, students really can't complain about this class. No homework, 4 ONLINE tests and the final isn't cumulative. She tries her best to keep us entertained and the subject matter can be really interesting if you put effort into paying attention.

Her lectures are dry but I admire that she tries to be humorous throughout it. Tests are online and super easy. You will need to the textbook if you wanna do well on tests. Classes are semi-mandatory as she has clicker points but they're worth 2% of your grade and she has panopto recordings.

Tests are based on lecture material but the questions can be very specific, so try to not skim over sections while studying. Make sure to go over in-class clicker Qs and the practice exam Qs - she will reuse some. She ended up giving an EC assignment to help boost some grades, which was really nice! No final and easy HW questions on Canvas weekly.

Similar structure to NUTR300 except that tests are not online and there were additional assignments. There are 4 exams (no final!), 2 assignments, clickers, and mini reading assignment "quizzes" done online. As long as you study the notes (study practice exams because she recycles some questions!) you should do well.

She's a pretty laid back professor and likes throw in a few jokes here and there.  There are clickers, so you should probably go to class everyday if you want easy points, though I know some people never did and still ended up with a good grade. Tests were online, so you could use notesinternet, but the questions themselves were tricky at times.
The class was somewhat interesting and wasn't that difficult. The exams were timed and online. Professor Kirk never answered any of my emails and reaching her at office hours was hard...
Online exams for my quarter. Pretty interesting lectures. Go to class and you will pass.
Professor Kirk tells you exactly what you need to know for the tests. So just pay attention and do the study guide questions before the test.

Dr. Kirk's class was really interesting! Her lectures are recorded but there are clickers that count for participation points. However, her clicker points were only worth about 2-3% of your overall grade. I thought this class had a fair amount of assignments and the tests were easy if you attended lectures and did the assignments!
Great Prof. Online exams were mostly straightforward if you paid attention in lecture. Very helpful one on one as well

Never went to class, never watched the screencasts even though she did have 5 points total for clicker questions. I pulled 3 all nighters for her 3 exams and just studied the notes provided and got a 3.5 in the class. Very nice teacher, boring content- study for the exams and you'll do well

Helpful professor who worked hard to make the class accessible to all students.  Exams were easy as long as you attended lecture and paid attention.  Minimal studying outside class. A background in chem/bio helps along with a general interest in the topic.

This was a very easy and interesting class. Lectures are posted online so attending class is not necessary. Textbook is not needed at all. Dr. Kirk is a great teacher who engages the class. She gives very personal examples that captivate everyone in the room.

Most work for any 3 credit class I've ever had. Lectures so boring they're hard to sit through. She screencasts everything online, but basically there was no correlation between lecture and tests. I took for an interesting NW, don't recommend.
