Super easy class if you have test files. I rarely attended class and managed to get a 4.0. Her lectures are very boring and full of unnecessary information that don't pertain to the exams. There are 6 small assignments and 2 diet reports that take at most 20 minutes.
I really enjoyed this class, it was pretty easy and the majority of grades are assignments.  She's a really nice lady and really cares that students learn.
super easy class.  Lectures are boring but everything is screencast, outlines are posted, and the book does a really good job at explaining.

i easily got a 4.0 in this class after memorizing all her lecture outlines for the midterms. she said she wouldn't give extra credit, but she did. it really helps to boost your grade. you barely need the textbook to study off of.. just need it for the online multiple choice questions. her lectures are all screencast so you dont have to attend

I really like how she just wants you to understand and doesn't try to trick you. Her expectations are extremely clear too. Just do your best because you can only miss 4 pts in order to get a 4.0. Nutrition is also very interesting as it pertains to everybody :)

I loved this class! I found it more interesting than NUTR 300 just because it wasn't largely "science-based" (i.e. we didn't really focus on the GI tract and digestion), and we went into more depth on how the food was produced. Super easy to do well, just do the exam reviews and review your notes. I recommend this class to everyone!

The professor was very clear on every topic we learned in class. The exams were pretty easy especially because she post example questions for us to study off of. I liked the topics we learned in this class a lot and I recommend taking this class! One of my favorite classes I took at UW.

If you get a hold of her past exams and memorize the answers, you could literally never show up to class and get a 4.0. There are six online assigments througout the quaerter that you need the textbook for but other than that, it's a waste of money to buy..just check it out at ode. She's a great professor if you're interested in nutrition.

MEMORIZE ANSWERS FROM OLD TESTS!! you only need to read the book for the assignments..class is a waste of time..i fcked up because i didn't go to class or read the book, but i memorized the answers from old finals and got a 100 on the final! Should be an easy 4.0
Easy Class. Exams are easy if you can get the old exams from someone who took the class before because Professor Kirk recycle the question from the old exam.
Pretty easy class, especially if you get the past exams from someone (I counted maybe 4 different questions between the 2009 final & 2010 final). Lots more biology than I expected.

Easy class! Prof. Kirk is great. Highly recommend her. Note that this class is more about the biology and processing of food rather than food itself. Quite a bit of information to memorize for just three credits, but not hard. I barely did anything for this class and got a 3.9.

I feel so lucky to have had her as a proffessor! she was wonderful and funny. She made me very interested in the topic. Reading isn't too neccessary if you attend her lectures. Test are also very straight forward

Very straightforward material,however, MUCH more biology than expected.  Tests are based pretty much entirely on lectures, textbook is only used for the diagrams she shows in lecture pretty.  Nice 3 credit NW class.  CLUE sessions were extremely helpful for me.  Relevant, interesting material.  Kirk is super friendly and funny!

Kirk was a nice professor whom may be a little boring sometimes. I found the book to be useless if midterms and finals are all you consider, but the book does have a lot of interesting readings and details. Kirk has neat lecture handouts and they were super useful for the exams and her exams were straight forward and many were common sense.

Very easy course just know that it is about more than just food, we discussed the biological aspect of food and eating too. If you can get your hands on past exams you will ace the class she is very consistant when making tests!

For the first exam, I had read every recommended section and went to classes, and got a 98. For the second exam, I only took notes from her lectures, and got a 98. Her tests are very straightforward - she doesn't try to trick you.
Great professor. She will tell you the 1st day that if you take notes you will not need the book. the tests are from her notes. She is funny and very helpful.

Kirk is approachable and very clear in her lectures. Slides are printed for you and she basically lectures exactly in conjunction with the textbook. Not solely focused on food nutrition, though. Has many elements of biology that may be harder than expected. Class was overall very organized

Information is way too specific for a nutrition class. Goes into strong detail of human biology -which is not what I expected. Boring lectures and does not make things clear. TA's are not much help either (some of them didn't even know the answers to students' questions!)

We had 2 group projects, 2 reading responses, and one open notes final which is open for one week so in terms of workload this class was manageable. You often discuss with your group and sometimes will do fun activities depending on the lecture. 2 professors and 2 ta's we had and all of them were chill and understanding. Not a stressful class.

This professor and my TA, Youssef, made racist and classist comments. When students told the TA that they had problems with their microphone or camera, he told them, "to just go and fix it". The professor also felt that there was no issue referring to enslaved people as slaves. And yet, this is a class on improving population health? What a joke.

Stephen was one of my favorite professors at UW. This class was so interesting and you can tell hes very passionate about his work. Theres a lot of group work and its not hard at all. Theres two tests but they basically tell you what to study.

Very clear requirements to get a good grade in the class. Make sure you understand the key ideas that is being repeated throughout the lectures. Don't skip too many lectures as it's a part of the grade. Are able to be creative in how you do projects, and tests are very easy, no studying required if you show up to class and listen.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Bezucka is very knowledgable and passionate about the subject matter! The course setup was active learning and thus based on small group discussions. The course itself was not busy work at all - you can easily earn a good grade (3.8+) if you put in the effort. High recommended!

I loved this class! This class is really interesting and teaches a lot of skills that I use in everyday life. This class is really easy you just have to follow the grading criteria. You basically get graded on one group project that you present at the end of the quarter. There aren't any tests either which is great!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Bezruchka makes his class very interesting. My perception on public health has changed and learned a lot from this class that I can apply to my life outside of school. He actually cares more about you learning than the assignments you do. In quiz sections you deliberate a lot about the topics. Would recommend for diversity credit.

Dr. Bezruchka's classes are very hands-on, but you won't be doing busy work. HSERV 476 did have some readings, but you could get a good grade without doing most of them. Your grade is based on a few moderately-sized, but fun assignments. No participation points but still worth going to clarify assignments and get help. Lots of time to work in class

Coursework is manageable however grading was unclear and most assignments had little to no feedback. Instruction and expectations extremely vague especially with the final. Class participation is essential every class.

The class was super easy and requirements were clear. But she had multiple non emergency class cancelations and didn't seem to care at all about the class. Small group discussions were nice but the way she responded back to peoples opinions seemed very passive aggressive and blase.

Professor Bhowmik runs a very solid discussion-based class. JAPAN 435 leaned heavily on theoretical texts, which were harder to discuss than literature, but the central ideas and themes were very interesting. I also enjoyed seeing her research interests incorporated into the class, as well as her openness to learning from us as well as vice versa.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Found the class very interesting and professor Bhowmik very nice and kind. I did not enjoy that she did not once give a grade or feedback on any of the work that was being done. I had not even received a grade or any feedback for my midterm by the time we received our final grade.

Took her Okinawa in the Japanese Literary Imagination class. She is well versed in this subject but sometimes can get repetitive. It is a great class though. She is a pretty easy grader but make sure youre participating in class especially discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Took her course "Okinawa in the Japanese Literary Imagination". She is very understanding as a teacher and genuinely wants her students to learn and succeed. Class is very participation based, so its important to do the readings and show up, but aside from that she can be quite lenient on grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Do the readings and participate as much as possible and you'll do fine. Something I really love about Prof. Bhowmik is that she's not biased and actually likes when people play the devil's advocate. She's also very accommodating if you need to take your final early for studying abroad which was awesome.

I'm pretty sure last quarter was Bhowmik's first quarter teaching the intro to Japanese film course, but I absolutely loved that class and her teaching style. Very straightforward content, lots of small group discussions and she's always open to listen to everyone's ideas and interpretations of things. I highly recommend taking any of her classes

Dr. Bhowmik is easily one of my favorite professors at UW. She brings an exceptional variety of literature to her classes, and gives clear, thoughtful feedback on papers. She's also quick to respond to questions outside of class. I would recommend her colonial lit course to anyone who wants a rounded view of Japan and enjoys reading short stories.

Dr. Bhowmik gives clear guidelines and has some amazing insight into colonial Japanese literature. I learned a lot, and as long as you show up and study along with her test outlines the class is easy to ace.
Davinder is a pretty good teacher, but the class was extremely boring. As long as you do the readings, the class is cake. Only 2 tests, with study guides given. However, it is a REALLY boring class.

She expect you to know themes & significant aspects of a story as well as present it clearly in a 1-2 page essay(s). Also, she will mainly talk about the authors more than the story itself during LC, but during the exam, it will mainly focus on the stories, so dates, plots, characters & themes are important to remember. Exams are not that bad.
In a class where we should be discussing the books we read, 5% of the time is dedicated to that and 95% goes to lecturing about the authors, which is a subject we never study, test or write on.
Best global health class I've ever taken!!!!
Alisha was very dedicated to preparing us for real-world practice and making sure our time in class was spent on the most high-yield information.

this professor initially proclaimed her interest in mentoring and supporting students, however she would often show up to class late, didn't provide feedback for assignments until the end of the quarter, spent the class on her phone, threatened to fail students, and often did not know the answer to questions and would direct students to look it up
Just simply amazing. Try to take a class with Siddharth if you have the choice.

This was such a fun class to take and I really enjoyed having Siddharth as my professor because he was so nice and accommodating and just generally made the class super easy to stay engaged with. 10/10 would recommend taking 131 with him if given the chance :)

What a guy! He's such a character, and I love to hear about his life stories as they make me believe that it will all work out. His assignments were relatively clear, and I enjoyed his one-on-one feedback. A great prof to have for a mandatory class.

I am a stem major and took ENGL 131 because I had to and was planning on putting in the bare minimum effort. However, Siddharth made me want to show up and put in effort because he is a really interesting person and an engaging speaker. I always looked forward to this class and was never stressed about it because he is so chill and understanding.
Writes way too fast on the board - gives 10 seconds to complete class problems. Not very clear to comprehend material. Assumes that you have strong Math 126 knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Arunima is a fantastic instructor! Loved this class.
Honestly, the best math prof I have had at uw!

Literally cannot understand half of what she is saying because she goes so fast, she will erase stuff off the chalk board after letting you look at it for a total of 4 seconds, hard tests, will not respond to your emails, just overall rude and unapproachable. Would not recommend, avoid her class if possible.
Long papers, heavy load of readings!!! Not an easy 4.0 class

Very intelligent and young so she cares a little more than older profs. However, she will spend 30 minutes of each class going over where you left off from last class so be prepared to hear the same material a lot. Gives great feedback on papers.

It was my first political science class, and I took it based off of her ratings.  And she's great!  By far the best professor I've ever had.  I dragged my friends to her lectures to see her present.  Fantastic public speaker, incredibly engaging, intriguing.  Could not recommend her more. And yeah, she's also pretty hot.
Best professor I've had so far at UW! so enthusiastic and clear in  class! you don't even really need to read all of the material. you can pass by on mainly lectures

Deepa was one of the best, if not the best professor I ever had in my time at UW! She's amazingly smart, knows political theory inside and out, and is very sociable and easy to talk to. I would definitely recommend Deepa to everyone! It's an easy 4.0 if you do the work.

Deepa is a great instructor. You leave the classroom feeling the energy of the many political theorists. The class was not easy, but manageable. The essays are graded harder than your standard 200 level class. I highly recommend you talk to Deepa outside of lecture, she will clarify questions and greatly add to your overall success.
She's a great professor, I really love her class. Really nice, incredibly helpful. Also she is super hot.

Deepa is the smartest and hottest professor I have ever met throughout my entire college life. If you have the privilege to take her classes, you should be glad because you are going to engage in classroom discussions everyday and you will learn the most important part of Liberal Art studies, how to "trouble" the world with your knowledge.

The short version: she got me hooked on political theory. The longer version is that she provides excellent explanation of very complex and abstract concepts. Brilliant, helpful, kind, but she doesn't pull punches when it counts and will really help your writing. Highly recommended.
She's young, makes sure to explain things crystal clear and she is really passionate about what she's talking about. I loved her. She's SO smart. Lecture slides are online.

Deepa was a great teacher! She was engaging, knows what she's talking about, and very helpful because she has much experience in her subject. I had her for Eng 198 joined with Poly Sci 201 and she helped SO MUCH in understanding that lecture as well as how the Poly Sci TAs would grade. Great person and really helpful essay feedback!!

She's amazingly helpful and will help you in anyway that she can. I took her class linked with poli sci 201 but thanks to her I understood it all. Great teacher, very cool too, brought us donuts and coffee once lol.

Deepa is a great professor! She is very helpful in discussion and clarifies everything in lecture.  Deepa is incredibly engaging and intelligent and it's very refreshing to have a discussion leader that is very aware of her students and the information she is presenting.  I hope I can have her in the future!

Deepa is first and foremost a great teacher.  She's able to explain things that the prof is not clear about in lecture and able to pinpoint what exactly to take from readings.  She's also very candid and has an amazing ability to engage with difficult students.  Plus, she's insanely hot.

Amy is a very helful and knowledgeable instructor. She shows genuine care for the understanding and education of her students. She also does a great job mixing up the class so it is not all lectures. She has small, interesting class assignments and also does a great job striking interest in students for fun class discussions.

Amy is a very helful and knowledgeable instructor. She shows genuine care for the understanding and education of her students. She also does a great job mixing up the class so it is not all lectures. She has small, interesting class assignments and also does a great job striking interest in students for fun class discussions.
Amy is always prepared and willing to help.  She is a great professor.
Amy is an engaging TA who takes a sincere interesting in her students.  She is a very professional teacher who is incredibly knowlegable about her field.

Prof. Bilmes definitely cared about the subject matter and loves teaching. In-class quizzes are ridiculously difficult - 20 minutes for 25 questions that are select all that apply (so 1/31 chance) and no partial credit. Also recorded extra lectures that were mandatory 5/10 weeks, outside of class. Homework was difficult. Learned a lot but 20hrs/wk

Bilmes is the best professor I've had. EE 514 covers dense material like entropy, Huffman coding, and Gaussian channels, but his intuition-first approach makes it click. He remembered my exact confusion from two weeks prior at office hours. Problem sets prepare you perfectly. 10/10, do not miss this class.

Professor is kind and learned, but the lecture itself is extremely hard. He tries to cover roughly twice the amount of material that normally take in ten weeks, and his monotonous teaching style makes it even worse to follow. All those assignments will cost you half of every week, especially the shockingly difficult in-class quizzes.

The topics are too wide. The lectures are too long and boring. Professor never repond to students email, he also sneared at in class questions  "Do you really understand this topic?" ,"Ok, I think you should read the material again", it's a problem of tenure.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is hard to get in touch with. Never respond to students' email or discord. He wants to teach 16 weeks contents in 10 weeks. If you are not ready to spend 20+ hours a week on his course, then consider carefully before taking his courses.

The professor, while very knowledgeable about the subject, fails to bring it down to a level understandable by those that haven't spent years in machine learning. The homework is extremely hard and his class sessions do nothing to help you get it done. Expect to do a lot of google searching in order to complete your homework. Frustrating & tiring.

Lucid and detailed instructor that gives a comprehensive treatment of the material. Very accessible and provides detailed answers to student questions. Best machine learning class I have ever taken - really gives Andrew Ng a run for his money!

Great guy with a lot of knowledge on the subject. However, the class was poorly managed by the TAs. You have to ask many questions and spend dozens of hours on assignments that are posted late and revised several times just before the due date. I felt cheated by the unprofessional environment. Lectures are 4 hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great professor, great class!
youtube videos are a great addition
Lecture is like reading the handout material.

Excellent class and excellent instructor. Prof Bilmes went all out to help us learn and his use of videos of class lectures was very helpful. Bilmes is probably one of the most underrated instructors.
amazing class topic and instructor
Superb!
was great

the class was really hard, prof Bilmes is obviously brilliantly smart, he really knows his stuff, and he seemed to care about learning (his office hours were great, maybe where i learned the most). The class material stretched my mind though, I'm gladd I took it.  the book wasnt so great, a little too theoretical.
Good luck if you want to take his course!

Not very easy to follow his lectures.  He speaks very quietly and lectures entirely off slides that are not all that well designed.  Student questions often are not answered very clearly.  Nice guy but not the greatest teacher.  If you take him plan on finding some way to learn the material on your own.  The textbook barely used.  Terrible Jokes.
the original linguist family anti soviet to usa gift human family

This was the first time she was teaching this class and the usual time allotment was basically cut in half so she did very good with what she had. Lectures were interesting, engaging, and thought-provoking, and the final project was very fun and free-range. Highly rec for an extra few credits. Dense reading but easy to skim and still participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Memorization is key in this class. Make sure you show up to lecture, as she often says things that are explicitly on the exam. Take notes!!! Talking to her outside of class is easy, and you also have helpful TAs in case she isn't available. She's very sweet, but don't take that to mean she's a pushover. Had a wonderful time overall. :)

Very engaging prof, even when I thought the subject matter was super boring. Lectures are live-streamed and recorded. Decent amount of reading assigned each week, but not really necessary to do if you attend and take notes during lectures. Midterm and final have a lot of super detailed questions and can really sway your grade, so studying is a must
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You'll do well if you pay attention in lectures and at least skim the readings. She's very funny and relatable, and the content is very interesting. Few things are graded, so it's important to do well in the quizzes (open-note) and attend discussion sections. Overall, I didn't have that much work for this class, and I would highly recommend it. :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Understandable Prof, gives feedback, available after & out of class. Many Soph took this class and I recommend if you need just one Anth class. We did have quite a bit of readings but was manageable. Has decent make up assignment if missed class. Assignments sounded heavy but were interesting and turned out better than expected. Ended off good!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's the best professor I've had so far at UW! Very kind and accommodating and genuinely wants everyone to succeed. Mix of lectures and class discussion that led to a very chill environment. Really appreciated her knowledge and point of view. Provides make up work for absences.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's fun and very insightful, lectures are easy to follow and interesting. I liked hearing her perspective of what's happened to Ukraine since the conflict started. All lectures are streamed live too, which is super convenient.

Professor Bilaniuk is very passionate and knowledgeable about her subject, which helps her teach effectively. The class was very interesting, just sometimes tedious as they were 2 hour lectures. I really enjoyed the class and found the workload manageable, with only one big paper, the midterm, and a multiple choice final.

While the materials that we covered were interesting and the workload was very doable; she often struggled to answer students questions about the material and a lot of material that she assigned were out of date. Some materials she assigned for reading were 20+ years old and the academic consensus on this issue has changed drastically in that time.

Professor Bilaniuk is fantastic! She clearly cares about the subject she teaches. The class material is relatively easy to understand if you attend lectures. She will give you a list of all the terms you need to know for the midterm/final and she will not trick you and put random stuff on there. Overall a great way to take care of art credits!

The major paper was super fun and applied what we learned in the course. Lectures were long, but often engaging. Posted lecture slides were helpful for catching up if you missed class. Quizzes were chill. The midterm and final exam were clearly written and questions were covered in class. Laada was also super nice and helpful!

I think overall she was a good teacher. 
If you don't like 2 hour lectures where you just listen to the prof. talking all the time, this class isn't for you. 
If you want to learn about Ukraine and Eastern European linguistics, this class is for you.
Major paper, 2 tests&quizzes.
Tests are hard, but questions are fair game (just phrasing it hard).

I really loved Professor Bilaniuk's class, she is really knowledgeable about language politics and identity and brought in some really fascinating and relevant points about Ukraine and the current war. Her lectures were really insightful, and she was always asking students for their opinions, which I found really nice. She's great!

I absolutely LOVED her Anthropological Linguistics class! I was already interested in the topic, but I think anyone can succeed in this course if they take notes and stay engaged. There is a fair bit of terminology but nothing crazy, and she's an excellent lecturer. The workload is fine (not many grades), I learned a ton and recommend her courses!!

Professor Laada was such a gem! She was clearly very passionate about what she is teaching and the tests had no surprises - everything she discussed in lectures. I did not do the readings and still got a A+. If you ever have any concerns you can always meet with her outside of class and if not, she replies extremely quick to emails. Would retake.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Bilaniuk is clearly passionate about the subject and it shows in her lectures. The quizzes can be confusing and I definitely had to put in a lot of work to memorize all the terms. All in all, I'm glad I took this class and found it very engaging.

Took this class as my easy A class and it ended up being way harder than I expected. The midterm seriously plummeted my grade and the final is cumulative!! Over like a million things. Def not an easy A.

Professor Laada is a great professor she really knows what she is talking about and her lectures are well put together. Class participation matters and it is important to always get to class on time. She gives great feedback on assignments and always willing to set time to talk 1 on 1 if needed. She is enthusiastic and cares about her students.

Love hate relationship with her. She is very smart and proactive in her assignments, she really cares about her classes. But she also comes across very judgmental during lectures and talking to her 1 on 1 . Some of her readings are difficult, graduate-level type readings. You will learn a lot in this class, but it's not the best experience.

Prof Laada is pretty understanding and lenient with due dates (online learning). The focus of this class leaned more towards linguistics, but she incorporated her anthro work in Ukraine for the last chapter which was interesting! Keep on top of asynchronous and synchronous lectures, quizzes, the readings she attaches and you'll do fine.

I took this class online (covid) & I struggled at times. First part of class (1 hr) is Asynchronous (watch videos) Second part of class is live lecture video (1 hr.) Shes nice & funny but the material isnt the best. The quizzes were difficult & a lot of individuals struggled. hard class, need to stay up to date & fully participate. uses pollev
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Laada is responsive and listens to her students' opinions. I can tell that she cares about the subject and whether her students are understanding the material. The format of this class is organized and flexible. I also appreciate the various forms of outside sources for us to analyze rather than just relying on the book.

I got a 4.0, but I had to work for it. Some students struggled in this class (when we got our midterm grade, I heard one guy say to two friends "I can't believe we all got a D), but if you apply yourself and focus, you'll do well. Good feedback, too. My paper was headed in the wrong direction, and she talked me through some alternate ideas.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class at first seems fine at first. However, my specific TA was not very helpful and graded hardly and never told us why he took off points. The final was ridiculous, she asked questions that could have had multiple answers. She did not give us any idea on how the final would be, and overall many students felt unprepared for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Laada is a very engaging prof, her lectures are easy to follow. She does polling and has trick questions if you aren't there so you gotta show up. There is one midterm, final and a 6-page paper at the end of the quarter but it's not too bad. Not that tough of a grader as long as youre close you get the credit and she really does want you to do well

There was a lot of hope for this class as enthusiasm and personal attachment to the subject was evident however there was a clear lack of guidelines in the class. She consistently graded us on a strict grading scale, though her lectures/course content were incredibly ambiguous and course outcomes were close to non-evident. Shows favoritism too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: A good professor. She is enthusiastic in class. Students will love her.

Professor Bilaniuk is an amazing professor. She knows her material and is willing to help her students at anytime. Participation and attendance matters. Only one test a final exam and one 6-8 page paper. There is a presentation based on your research project and a lot of in class assignments for attendanceparticipation grade. She is a fair grader.

Very fun class, learned a lot. Participation is a must for most of the quarter. Very fun research project. Felt very slow and slightly boring at times, but the class overall was good. Really good teacher, very helpful, and cares about her students. There were lots of interesting discussions.

Professor Laada is really nice and always ready to help. She really loves what she teaches, and her interpretation really made me became interested in Anthropology. Textbook really unnecessary, because everything is on powerpoint and she records every class. Clicker questions are used to check attendance, but do not cheat or you will die.
She's so enthusiastic and it makes going to lecture really fun. Workload is so manageable and she makes the material interesting

Although her lectures tend to be a little boring, she is a great teacher. This class was a breeze and I learned a lot (which is how I think school should be). All you have to do is take good notes (which is basically just copying from the slides) and study the list of terms before each exam. I never even had to pick up the textbook. Great class!

Laada is a great and fearless educator, which is rare these days. You will leave her class knowing so much more about yourself and the world. Her class is perfectly well-structured, so no surprises. She grades more than fairly and is available for extra help. She is a very nice person, too.

Laada is funny, nice, and knowledgable. Very interesting, makes material light-hearted with silly examples. Loved this class, especially since she posts slides and had course-recording available, making studying a breeze. TA's were good as well, if you were into the material. Overall great intro and covered interesting topics.

I loved Laada and her Linguistic Anthropology class. She is super interesting, engaging and clear. Her lectures are also recorded and posted online in case you miss a day but don't skip too much because there are clicker questions. She keeps things relevant with Youtube videos and movies. Not too hard and she really wants everyone to do well.

Maybe this would have been interesting if I was an anthropology major (I'm biology, fulfilling prereqs). She's certainly a fun woman, who is clearly enthusiastic and passionate about her work. She's entertaining to watch/listen to. However, the material felt unorganized and scattered, with no clear linar course. All in all a snooze.

Laada is a kind and intelligent woman. The class is great for people who have never taken any ANT b4, super easy. Moves slow, really an intro course. Easy A if you show up and do the work. Didn't have to read the text, just Language shock, everything was in lecture. Exams were easy, final multiple choice. She gives it her all and does a great job.

Laada is brilliant. As an anthropology major, I was blown away by her knowledge and passion towards what she teaches. She may seem unorganized, but she's extremely nice and approachable.  As for those who think you need to "suck up" to do well, it is a class based largely on discussion - i.e. speak up, don't just sit and stare.

Much of your grade depends on how well you kiss up to your TA and how well they like you.  That said, Laada is a dull lecturer in a subject that could potentially be interesting.  She takes WAY too much time accommodating every loudmouth's quest for the floor.  Tests were tricky so study the terms well.  Better yet, take a different class.

Pretty, nice. She uses the word "gender" when meaning "sex" as in male or female. That drove me nuts. Much of this class is about "meaning" which means a lot of opinion rather than facts. I would take her for another class but the type of material that passes for a class these days in the dept is about "meaning" ie opinion, rather than hard facts.

She was nice and told interesting stories.  The tests were appropriate for the material learned -- not too easy, not too hard.  It's tough to do a lecture with 100 people, but I thought she did a good job of keeping it interesting.  The paper was a lot of fun to do.  She tried to help everyone and included everyone's voices in the class.

laada was an OK professor. shes nice but lectures were so boring. i dreaded going ot them. and she doesnt have very good manners either..she would always interrupt people in the middle of asking a question to answer it, but wouldnt even answer the question because she wouldnt wait to hear the whole thing

She might be good if she wasn't so wishy washy (which is a bad trait for lecturing). Repeats herself, and doesn't organize lecture very well. The TAs didn't quite have their stuff together, I think that's mainly 'cause Laada doesn't have her stuff together. She encourages questions: doesn't work in 150 person class.
Terrible class.  Boring and learned nothing.  What a waste of $ and time.
Laada is an aweful teacher.  I will neither take a class from her again or refer her to anyone else.  Though her class is very easy, it's not worth  sitting through her freakishly unhelpful lectures.
Laada is an incredible teacher. Her lectures were both fun and informative. You will learn a lot from this teach and I'm sure that if you ever need help, Laada will help you.
Repeats herself a lot and rather uneffective as a teacher. Nice though.

One of the best lecturers, professors, and people I have met. Flipped classroom with long-ish YouTube videos, so be aware of that, but it's worth the watch. Her communication skills are out of the world and she knows so much. You ask her ANYTHING and she will be able to keep up. Changed my perspective on biology forever. TAKE HER CLASS. FAIR EXAMS!

I was scared seeing the RMP, but Dr Brunton is one of the best professors I've taken! Flipped classroom, but absolutely amazing, engaging lecturer who is very passionate about the subject. There was one midterm, which was pretty difficult, but final was just a 500 word paper on a subject of your choice! Plus we had some really fun debates in class!

Her class is flipped with long lecture videos and hard quizzes, all in-class polls are graded on correctness no completion, and her midterm was bad. There was no grading scale on the syllabus, and assignment grades weren't posted until the end of the quarter. Assignments were posted last minute. I've never taken a more unorganized course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would rather rip the hair out of my head strand by strand than take a class with this woman again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No structure to the class, would tell you something to your face (like your answer was correct) and then grade you opposite. Nothing was ever graded in a timely manner, when I asked her about it she was extremely hostile. I'm hoping to be able to work with administration as this is never how I've had interactions at UW

She seemed so great in the beggining, I had a few medical issues and was very communicative all quarter. I was told I would receive an extension, and then at the end of the quarter she docked everything 50%. There was no structure to the class, we wouldn't even as far as 2 days in advance when something was due.

I would like to speak up to warn others looking for a PI for grad school programs. Administration has confirmed that Bing's behavior is unacceptable and not reflective of the values of the school. All students in her lab have confessed to crying at least once due to an interaction with her. It is common for students to leave her lab.
I learned so much in this class.

She should stick to research because she doesn't seem to be interested in teaching. She does not hold office hours or offer advice aside from "search Stack Overflow". Be prepared to spend 20+ hours on homework if you've never coded before. You could learn just as much for free using Stack Overflow and other online resources.
Wonderful lectures

Was not the best professor. Shes a tough grader not giving you proper feedback and she can be quite condescending if you dont understand a concept. She is not helpful either. Avoid this prof if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Felt more like a seminar than a lecture; heads up if you hate reading/discussion. The course description can sound philosophical, but the readings were thought-provoking and (mostly) enjoyable even for a technical person. The best part was writing my own paper -- lots of flexibility and room to explore. Reasonable workload/grading if that matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Bill is super sweet and cares a lot about his students. The TAs are also great and helpful. In terms of grades, there is a lot of opportunity for extra credit and to improve your grade. Sometimes he can be chaotic or disorganized, but if you put in some extra time outside of class, you can definitely learn a lot and succeed.

Bill Howe is a professor who means well. However, he tends to ramble during lectures, which can leave less time to focus on the coding. I stopped attending class after week 4 because I felt I could learn the course individually, but I was wrong. He wants his students to succeed, but his teaching methods don't work for everyone (it works for me).

Seemingly doesn't know the course materials and there is always some kind of error on his part with the problems we do in-class. He is also not equipped to train TAs (as they are equally as unhelpful) and to work with students with any kind of accommodations. 99% of the course is spent on teaching yourself the content.
Professor does not explain questions about material in an easy way for students to understand. Often feels like going around in circles. Is not very clear about grading criteria.
Great intro database course, definitely learned a lot.  Bill is knowledgeable, supportive, and open to feedback.

Bill's teaching style at UW is a mess. He's late, barely audible, and his lectures are a jumble of confusion. His speaking volume is so low that it's challenging to hear him even in a quiet classroom. Rather than offering clear explanations, he often seems confused himself, which adds to our confusion when seeking clarification. AVOID  
 HIM!!!!!!!

Dude has no idea what he's talking about, he can't even explain his own examples. Lab for this quarter is also being taught by a different professor and there is no communication between the two, so Lectures & Exams don't align with Labs. He's nice tho and seems like he wants to help, I just have little faith in his knowledge on this topic...

He is unconfident in the materials he is trying to teach. Gives us problems to do but can't explain how to do it or won't give us a clear explanation. Tries to do the problem on the board, pause, erase, and tell us he messed up the problem. Teaches new information in the lecture before our midterm and expects us to know it for the midterm.

As a Vietnamese person who speaks broken viet at home taking this class, taking this class was pretty easy; the same can be said if you were non-vietnamese, as those who barely show up were still able to get the lessons. Her assignments were pretty easy to do. She also provides good context about Vietnamese culture and dialect.

Cares about her students and flexible with students who communicate with her. Makes learning Vietnamese enjoyable and engaging. She enforces fair expectations and grading. The signed student projects that are presented in class are surprisingly very educational. The professor is kind and funny. Will happily take 1 year of Viet courses from her.

I took this class to get a better understanding of my Vietnamese heritage and so glad I did. I was hesitant at first because it is a 400 level course but thanks to professor Turner, I did learn a lot about Vietnam's literary history, society and culture. The reading assignments, class discussions and movies are quite interesting and enlightening.

This is not an easy class for me as a freshmen, but Professor Turner made it really fun and interesting to learn. There's a lot of work but it's worth it. You learn a lot about modern Vietnam. Grading is reasonable, and the professor really loves what she teaches, cares about the students she works with. Take her Viet classes, you won't regret.

Great Viet Professor. She really wants her student to succeed so just go to her office hours if you are struggling. Straight forward class, do the work and show up on time and you'll pass with a high grade.

I took all three levels 113, 211 then 311 with co Bich. I could speak some Vietnamese before the class and just needed to work on writing, reading. Co Bich was so kind and helpful. She let me upgrade one level after each class I took, which was nice to get the credits I needed. I am grateful to be able to talk to/write mom and grandparents now.

Just lots of vocab, she doesn't teach proper sentence structure too much. If you already know Vietnamese, Viet111 will be a breeze but if you dont, be prepared to be overwhelmed. You get 5 free attendance passes, after that she starts taking off points. There's 3 tests and 3 hw assignments, and has extra credit too. Try not to mess up too much. GL
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Had minimal knowledge. The class was fun, and interactive. She is very, very, very helpful in office hours. She is clear on what's on tests.

She gives points for attendance. During class she will call on various students. You barely have to read the textbook, just look over the vocab. Homework is daily. The tests aren't tough but be careful of trick questions. The final papers are very short. I wouldn't stress. Even people with minimal knowledge can get a 3.9 in this class.
Very good Professor. Really nice, understanding, and funny. Willing to help students if you ask. Has daily hw, but its not hard. Extra Credit.

I took the whole first year sequence with Cô Bich (she's super nice!): There are 3 tests total and a final. Participation isn't mandatory but she does have a participation portion in the grading. There is homework every day (except weekends) but they are easy Also, She gives out easy extra credits! Worth 10 pts - the whole class is 100 pts.
SHE EVILLLLLLLLL

The professor is very condescending and inconsiderate of her students. Gets frustrated when students don't know what is going on or what to expect grading wise despite having nothing explicitly stated in syllabus, and only gives verbal instructions for most things. Lectures are in no coherent chronological order and feel very random.

Worst prof I have ever taken at UW. Unclear grading structure, lectures are just pictures taken from the textbook & she just gives very vague descriptions of each slide w/ no teaching outline. Tested on random facts mentioned once in lect. Ignores students' feedbacks/concerns. Avoid taking, she is very condescending & is only teaching for funding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely hated this class. Overall grade outline sucks. Treats this class as an ego boost because she had us watch biology videos she was in and mentioned a lot how she has 20 years of teaching experience but you can tell she absolutely hates teaching. I was excited about the material beforehand but she made this class unbearable.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: lol never met a prof who really - LIKE OBVIOUSLY REALLY - didn't like their students. We were second lecture in and she was already so annoyed by us. I hope she doesn't think she's a good prof, cuz she's actually the worst. Try to avoid. But if you can't, don't bother going to class. Just read the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very frustrating. "Lectures" were just copies of figures from the textbook, and she did a poor job explaining them. I had no idea what was expected of me; the midterm had obscure matching people's names to their research, along with random phylogenies, while the final was incredibly basic. Despite getting an A, I learned very little in her class.

Really poor experience. Professor seemed much more interested in having a mid-lecture conversation with the class's overqualified students instead of making the material accessible for everyone else. Tests were fair but lecture presentations were among the worst I've seen. For the first time in my life, I had no motivation to succeed in a class.
Her biology lab is an interesting class especially if you don't know alot about evolution and it is pretty easy to get a good grade too!
Her bio412 class is easy. She is extremely helpful and willing to answer any question. You will do very well in her class as long as you follow her assignment guidelines and participate in class.
She's super mean.
Billie Swalla is one of those professors who can motivate her students and pass on a lot of useful knowledge.  I had fun in her biology classes, and I am looking forward to taking more from her.
No Comments

This class is NOT easy and you will have to work for a good grade. Despite that, Tim is one of the best professors I've ever had. He is a genius in the environmental field and his passion shines in lectures and the field. The exams (1 midterm, 1 final) are partially based on plant and bird identification, so be prepared to memorize a lot!

Honestly one of my favorite classes, however, the main discussions were not enviro education but enviro justice and racism. There are a couple opportunities to teach kids through outside organizations (amazing experience) and classes are student led discussions. Tim is awesome and makes an effort to learn names. Research paper is graded harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: *301 not 315. Surprised by the # of good reviews. Many readings were so out of date they were a waste of time and there's so much busy work. Tim seemed nice from afar but was not pleasant one on one. Midterm was poorly written which resulted in bad grades for most. Not very understanding in general. Weird vibes, took a picture of us w/o permission
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Tim is a great person and teacher! I just wan't impressed by the readings and lecture topics he chose, the class was supposed to be on environmental education and we mainly talked about racial issues within environmental education. Very important topic, just was repetitive and unexpected. A lot of our discussion questions were the same every week.

The man, the myth, the legend. I love Tim Billo. One time he even sang to us in class. I loved my quiz section too, but it depends if you get a good TA (Chris I love you). He did announce a final that we originally weren't going to have a few weeks prior because of a cheating issue, and exams are hard.

Tim Billo is by the far one of the best professors in the POE! He is so kind, caring, and approachable and you can tell he just loves what he's talking about. Lots of outdoor time and great field trips! There is a lot of work, but it shouldn't be a problem if you enjoy what you're doing.

Environment 100 is the perfect Autumn quarter class for a freshman. Assignment wise, this class is difficult but a good class should be appropriately difficult. You will have to work hard for the 4.0. Content wise, this class is extremely relevant and has amazing information on Climate and Social Justice. Lastly, Tim is amazing, smart, thoughtful.

YOU WILL BE OUTSIDE FOR 1/2 OF CLASS. I was unaware of this and wouldn't have taken this class during the fall. LOTS of memorization of plants and birds (latin names, identifying from pictures, bird noises). Easy class but not what I was expecting. Tim is great though!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Tim is a great professor, and this class was incredibly easy. It was taught with Prof. Weng, and in comparison to her his readings were much more lengthy and dense. I got by without reading most of them (due to time conflicts), but just a heads up. Overall would take the class and professor again!

Grading was too difficult 95% for an A is absurd, especially since they made the Final in-person, it definitely made it more difficult for most students, and no accommodations were offered in exchange for that.

I love Tim, I think he's so enthusiastic and generally loves to teach his topics. He's a little frazzled at times but this is my second class with him and I think he's a communicative teacher who cares about your learning. He also helped my group personally when we asked and set aside time for us!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: He was nice and obviously passionate, but I think this class was poorly organized. Tests seem to have random questions that have nothing to do with lecture most times. He assigned ridiculously long and dense readings for a 100 level class. Quiz section was also annoying because it was 2hrs long and mandatory while being unhelpful for class & tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Billo read directly from his slides a little bit too much during lecture and there was wayyy too much reading assigned each week, especially towards the end of the quarter. Also tests didn't have enough time and were a bit confusing. Overall it was still a fun class and not hard to get a 4.0 as long as you do the work and a bit of EC.

the class is great, tim just spends way too much time on other things rather than the information we need, rarely gets through slides on time. Class is graded on weekly quizzes and discussions which are easy. Lectures are recorded. Midterm/final more difficult, but open note. Overall pretty easy A and enjoyable class

He struggles to teach intro classes, we wasted a lot of class time on "discussions" (in a 300-person class) and rarely got through all the content we needed to learn for exams. Full of interesting information & he's very caring, but good luck getting through the content

Tim is a nice guy and is very passionate, this is however the most disorganized class I have ever taken. Expectations were not clearly communicated, guidelines for assignments would be updated the day they were due, and the course Canvas was seriously outdated. Lots of work and really high expectations. This class was VERY frustrating at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Tim is very nice, but I would not recommend. He has high expectations, yet doesn't communicate them. He was often late to class and would keep you after because he rambles on for 10 minutes just thinking out loud. His assignments are confusing and he is unprepared most of the time, and he assigns way too much homework that's worded unnecessarily.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I've heard great things about Tim's classes. Even though I did not enjoy this class AT ALL I do think I got some skills from it like working on original research projects and reading scientific papers. However, I don't think Tim's instruction crossed over well to online. The course was unaltered from pre-pandemic times which made it difficult.

I have taken ENVIR100 and 250 with Tim. He is an amazing instructor. Some students do not appreciate his style of lecturing and talking because he is quite pensive. But I really appreciate his careful thought and feedback. If you talk to him outside of class, he is full of interesting information. Highly recommend! No textbooks, but readings import
He is just sort of a slow lecturer. Not very interesting. He can get information across effectively, but it was not really a fun class when he taught.

Tim is a caring guy who takes sincere interest in his students' work. Although he's very passionate, I didn't feel like I got a whole lot from his class. The course included relatively basic and dry lectures, a quarter long group project, lenient grading/testing, and clear, worthwhile labs (Excel labs were actually a highlight). Overall, easy A.

In my opinion, Tim is nice enough but very disorganized. His lectures are hard to follow and kind of just random pictures. He cant keep track of time either so getting away from off-campus lecture spots can be difficult

Most unique class I've taken. It provides experiences like camping, hiking, birdwatching, plant identification. Plus, slowing down and appreciating nature outside the classroom (class was usually outside) is an important skill. However, unexpectedly hard tests. Make sure you study for them.
Tim is a great guy, the class is fun and hands on. The field trips are dope and you'll be able to identify the plants around you constantly
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: This class was by far the best class I've taken at UW. Anyone who loves being outside and really learning and understanding about the nature around them will fall in love with this class, and with Tim. We went on multiple field trips that were really educational and fun, very chill. But this isn't an easy class at all!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great professor, knows alot about birds, and cares about his students! I've known Tim Billo for two years now, and he's one of the best professors i've had. Take this class even if you aren't an Enviro Sci major, it can come in handy no matter what you do.

Environment 200 is a weird class. Tim is pretty cool. His wife had a baby during the time I took this class so he would occasionally pop in and teach. The tests were way too long for the amount of time given and the lectures did not match up with the tests. He goes on tangents a lot.
The best class taught be the greatest professor in UW! Make sure you take this class before you graduate from UW.

No textbook needed, all readings are online. His clicker questions were tough. As a person, I really liked Tim. However, the class itself was a mess. It was insanely disorganized and tougher than it should've been for a 100 level course.

Tim is the best professor I've ever met. He had the power to make every student care about the nature. ENVIR 280 is an awesome class where you go on a lot of field trips. After taking a class with him, you will wanna be out on the field all the time!
The best class you will ever take at UW. If you ever get to go bird watching with Tim, you are a blessed soul.

If you don't already know, Tim Billo literally has a cult following at UW. Seriously, search #timbillo on Instagram. By the end of the quarter (ENVIR 280) you'll literally want to BE him, and know everything he knows. He geeks out, has a great sense of humor, and is not intimidating by any means. You will be lucky just to be in his presence!
You don't use a textbook in this class. It's all readings online. His clicker questions are IMPOSSIBLE.

I took English 131 with Mr. Binh Tang and I am so glad I got him as my teacher for the quarter. Binh took a class that has terrible layout, tons of busy work and makes writing and composition enjoyable to everyone. Binh is an amazing person who made class very engaging. He doesn't have a rubric but gives so much feedback. 10/10 class, 10/10 teacher
Very encouraging of finding your own voice and incorporating it in your writing! He always gives good feedback and genuinely wants students to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: His teaching takes a while to get used to because at first, there is no clear structure and instructions for essay are vague. This is done on purpose to enable students to be creative and grading is lenient with lots of good feedback. I love Binh Tang
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Binh Tang is a predoctoral professor and it really shows. There are no rubrics to his essays, just general requirements that can use very strange and sometimes confusing wording. If you truly care about writing, his different perspectives could be useful, but in a STEM focused school like UW his assignments feel like a gigantic waste of time.

This discussion-based class is graded on only a few things, making it difficult to know what the professor expects on exams, especially for both short/long answer questions. Class time is mostly spent sharing opinions, which rarely help with the exams. Assignments are not uploaded consistently and often appear at the last minute. She is kind though
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Learned so much in this course. She is very smart and knows the material inside and out, often cultivating interesting class discussions.Tests are often and can be stressful, but she prepares you well for them if you come to class and do the readings. Write everything down because tests are open note. If you listen, you will learn so much!

I loved taking her course. She's a great lecturer and I loved the class curriculum. However, the grading felt a bit arbitrary at times and sometimes I did not receive a lot of feedback on assignments. After receiving a grade I was unsure of how I lost points because the rubric is very subjective.

She is nice but extremely difficult to please. Grading feels arbitrary and based on her personal beliefs rather than the actual prompt. Be prepared to lose points for "unwritten rules" not found in the syllabus, and don't expect flexibility or the chance to redo work. If you have an analytical learning style, getting a 100% is nearly impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
A great class to take as an underclassmen before you declare a major. Very good intro to moral philosophy. Not a lot of homework outside of reading which was nice.

Tests are short-answer responses to lecture content. If you study adequately, you should have little issue.

This is a good and interesting schedule-filler / major class. I recommend!

Professor Blake was an awesome professor and taught the material especially well. The only note I really have is that there was minimal guidance on what would be on the exams and how to study for them. The quiz sections also didn't feel useful/productive for class material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very interesting class, Dr. Blake does really engaging lectures, they were the highlight of my week, the quiz sections felt unnecessary but otherwise a really great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I'm honestly just impressed by how he presents the lectures, really had me engaged. Great class, manageable workload. Professor Blake is very understanding as well.

Stereotypically verbose and excited philosophy professor--he is a GREAT lecturer and I'm so grateful he was my first philosophy class experience at the UW. But we had very few assignments so when I missed less than 5 points on an assignment my grade dropped significantly. Very easy to distract him with questions.

Fantastic professor he knows what he's talking about. TA's are SOO hit or miss. Since your graded on only FOUR things the entire class you need a decent TA. I got lucky with my TA so they were fair on lots of grading but I had a friend who said the class was a nightmare with a bad TA. Harsh grading overall don't take if your looking for an easy A!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Funny lecturer and chill guy. He explained concepts in ways that made them interesting. Maybe not the easiest to access or most organized.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: the chillest professor for an intro philosophy class is absolutely hilarious. he lectures so well and answers so many student questions and explains things in various ways so that you actually understand it. the TAs are hit or miss tho and only they grade the FOUR ASSIGNMENTS so actually put in effort for them.

Professor Blake was very knowledgeable about the topics discussed in class. However, his TAs were harsh graders and gave little wiggle room in answers on tests and papers. The class is comprised of two papers and two tests that are heavily weighted. The exams are not based on the study guides. For a 100-level class, the grading is too extreme.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Blake has very entertaining and informative lectures, and the course content is pretty easy for an intro-level student. The grading is largely done by TAs, who you will generally interact with a lot more. Sometimes there would be some confusion on logistical things, but the TAs sorted it out pretty quickly every time.

very funny guy, and is always willing to take questions (sometimes almost too much, and we sometimes went on tangents because of plenty of student questions. but i guess that comes with taking every question). keeps lectures engaging and interesting. be wary that there's only like 4 graded assignments that will make up all of your grade.
HE THE GOAT FR
PHIL 102 is a really fun course when led by Professor Blake. Would 100% take his class again.

Absolutely loved professor Blake's class! He makes lectures incredibly entertaining and is very approachable. He's very knowledgable about what he's passionate about, and offers terrific insight about the topics. If you're interested in philosophy, or are looking to get out of your comfort zone academically, I would highly suggest his class.

He records himself at a side view talking to the ceiling in his chair. Professor Blake likes to make controversial claims and then proceeds to say, "I don't know anything, I don't endorse anything, I'm just leaving this out for you on the table". Odd dude. Oh yeah, he's obsessed with the word "penetrate" for some reason.
One of the best profs I've had at UW. If you like to think you'll actually enjoy lecture. He gave every side a fair representation which is more than I can say for many profs around his field
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Blake is one of the best professors I've had at the university. He gives amazing, entertaining lectures and makes complicated concepts seem really simple through the use of funny and clear concrete examples. I definitely recommend taking Phil 102 if you're at all interested in philosophy. Grading depends a lot on your TA, but the workload is light.

The majority of the work comes in the form of discussion forums. The topics posed for each discussion forum are quite interesting and really have you take a personal approach to each week's material. There are also two papers, a midterm, and the final was broken into two parts. He's a tough grader, but he provides feedback on everything you do.

Blake was a really good lecturer and a funny guy. But don't take this as an easy VLPA.  The class in my opinion was graded to strictly for a 100 level class. Also, the course description did not fit the actual class. We covered all of the ethics stuff in the last like 3 weeks and spent most of the time on actual philosophers.

Do not take this class for an easy VLPA it will screw you over. I put in work, went to 2 different philosophy writing center tutors and still ended with a 2.9 and my cumulative is a 3.7 so im not dumb. I loved the material but they make it ridiculously hard.

I took this class online and really enjoyed it.  His presentations were clear and fun to listen to.  Part of the final was a 20 minute - 20 question multiple choice exam.  When several of the students commented that this was a very short time given for a class that you're supposed to slow down and think about he worked with us.  Great guy.

His lectures were interesting and very interactive which was cool. He is very casual with his students and will take time to have interesting conversations with his students; very personable. The material is not easily grasped, but with the added interaction make it's easier to grasp. There is a lot of deep thinking needed for this class too.

Michael is a great professor. He is engaging and knows what he is talking about. The grade that you get in the course depends on which TA you get. The concepts are easy to get but it is a lot of information to remember. The course had two papers and one final exam.
Blake is amazing! He really engages many of the moral problems that society faces and breaks it down so that everything is understandable. I definitely recommend!
Amazing lecturer and professor, wonderful !

LOVE HIM! Honestly the most interesting class I have ever taken, I really enjoyed class and was sad when it ended. Midterm was surprisingly easy and if you follow the grading rubric it's easy to do well on essays too. This was my favorite class at UW, he is an amazing lecture, makes class so interesting and he's super funny! EVERYONE SHOULD TAKE IT

I definitely recommend this class! Prof. Blake is an incredible teacher- I've never rated a prof before but I feel like he is worth rating-- he is extremely well spoken and he keeps lecture interesting, fun to go to. Interesting topics and papers, Tests are pretty fair. Definitely worth taking a class with him!
Best professor I've ever had. Class isn't mandatory, but I honestly went for fun.

Only time you'll need to read the textbook is to write papers. Other than that, lectures & quiz sections will be more than enough for the tests. A lot of questions and debates goes on during lecture so Blake had to cut down the amount covered from 9 topics to 3.

Love this class! I think his teaching methods have changed since some of the other reviews because he uses a Powerpoint and the lectures are very interesting and easy to follow! He does let people participate freely in lecture so we are REALLY far behind now, but I think that's way better than rushing through. DEF take this class!
This man is such an amazing man! He is so smart and educated! Definitely take a class with him.

i took this class for an easy, interesting VLPA requirement. the class itself wasn't hard to follow but the papers and finals were impossible to get a decent grade on. the professor set his means before even looking at papers at low grades like 2.7 or 2.8 in a 100 level class. Do not take this if you plan on having an easy 4.0 to help out your gpa.
Took for an easy VLPA credit, but was not that easy.  Lectures are miserable, not orgainized at all.

Michael Blake is a very impressive individual. His resume speaks for itself. It's not that hard to get at least a 3.0 in this class. Two papers and a final. Blake however does not use power point and his notes are scattered. Very good class to fufill a VLPA credit, better then a traditional art class IMO.

Blake is a G...one of the absolute best professors I have had in my college experience. He enjoys his subject, is extremely articulate, loves the class to join in debates, and never once said anything remotely condescending. Attendance isn't mandatory,but highly recommended as you wont need to read anything if  you just show up and take good notes.

Blake is an excellent orator - However, I think since there are only two papers and a final, a lot of your grade will be decided by these three. The value of the class is pretty good, as he talks a lot about moral theory. Should anyone take this class w/Blake, I suggest you to look at the SEP. (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy-it's on his page.)

he speaks very well and tries to make you laugh, but his notes are all over the place. i think you either make bank or go broke depending on your TA. he/she is the one who's going to be grading your two essays that make up half of your grade.  nevertheless, it's a relatively easy VLPA and having no homework is nice too.

Professor Blake is an absolute GENIUS. He knows everything about his field, and can take/answer any question directed at him. His lectures are very fun and easy to listen to, but the content wasn't necessarily in line with the course title. Don't expect to learn about a great deal of "contemporary moral issues," mainly just morals in general.

Genius. He's very smart and entertaining. It was very challenging but I was one of the only freshmen in it. If you have Olsen as a T.A., drop it. Trust me. Other than that, it is a very good class and it really makes you think. A plus is that there aren't quizzes every week and the section is just a review.
He is VERY interesting!! and knows alot! He is funny, and isnt boring at all! I REALLY liked this class and sections were sometimes heated decussions! GREAT CLASS TO TAKE!! and Blake rocks!
this guy is a genius! lectures are interesting and informative. his sense of humor and breadth of knowledge in the field made the hour and a half literally fly by. highly recommended!

There are professors that teach the same courses and their midterms are generally much easier. But, I think that she is a good teacher, and if you attend her lectures, you will do well. You have to listen and follow what she is doing, I don't know what more you need.

She is not easy! There are professors that teach the same courses and their midterms are generally much easier. However, I think that she is a good teacher, and if you attend her lectures, you will do well.

Bekyel was openly vocal about how she did not want people to pass her class and ''if we didn't have at least a b in the class we don't belong here''. The homework and quizzes are barely related to the tests. She likes to throw curve balls. Midterm 2 was the hardest in my opinion. She doesn't record lectures so you have to go to all of them
Her midterms are harder than the other professors, her style of teaching also genuinely sucks.
Never take this teacher.

Her lectures are easy to follow and she gives good notes to work with. The exams are average difficulty, but she gives a lot of her old exams, which end up being similar to the real exam. She tells you what questions will be on the quiz, so those are no problem at all. I learned a good amount from her in this class and she's very nice and caring.
If you attend the lectures and take notes, she is very helpful and everything is pretty managable. The final Autumn 2025 was pretty hard, but on the other hand the midterms were pretty easy.

Her lectures went quickly, and I felt like she assumed prior knowledge of new material. Online homework took a long time. Weekly quizzes were mostly easy, but the 15-minute limit was tough on one. The midterms felt unnecessarily difficult compared to other 124 teacher midterms. The 124 department final was extremely hard to get a good grade on.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The first midterm SO hard. I got a C, B for midterm 2, and A on the final. Studying efficiently is important, and having this prof will prepare you for the final. She cares a lot and has high quality lectures, always enjoys answering questions. Take with this prof if your goal is to learn. Take with others if you just need the credit.
Good luck taking this class without having taken AP Calc.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a very good lecturer. If you go to class and take notes you will do well. Her tests are very similar to the many old ones she provides. The poor reviews are probably from students who either don't go to class or major in communications. The plus side is that they are lowering the average and therefore raising my grade, so I'll take that.

For better or worse, you will end this course intimately familiar with its content. Dr. Bekyel is an adequate lecturer (if a bit fast and prone to skipping steps and assuming you can fill in the blanks), but her lectures are very basic. Most of your learning will come from the sheer volume of homework, and difficulty and tedium of her exams.
RUN. Her tests are so much harder than other professors' tests........she did provide past exams and study guide for us to review but her tests are so hard....
DO NOT TAKE.

It's clear she enjoys what she teaches and she's very sweet but she, and I quote, expects you to 'learn on the homework.' Luckily, for each homework question you get 5 attempts to get the right answer but doing that for 8-20 questions adds up. The TAs are a hit or miss. Textbook is also expensive for never using it (it's required to access the HW.)

Took Ebru's MATH 124 a long while ago, when its the start of COVID. She does an okay job going through the slides, and I can understand the concept with a bit help from my friend in Math major. Exams are not very hard, and similar to previous years. But again, that's my first quarter in uni and its a very chaotic time on zoom.

if you go to class and pay attention you will be fine. she's pretty funny and the lectures are pretty straight forward and her practice exams are pretty similar to her actual midterms. her OH are very useful and she's overall a pretty good professor. don't listen to the negative reviews.

Had Dr. Bekyel for 126 and 300. She is incredibly engaging when explaining proofs, always finding the simplest entry and guide through the reasoning from students' perspective. Exams aren't easy, but provides review materials to help prepare. Though there are no recordings, you'll want to attend the classes of such a dedicated and gentle professor.

the first midterm was so hard that the class average was like a 14% and then she said to the class "if you got a low grade on the midterm, you shouldn't be here." she didn't want students to learn. she didn't prepare us for math 124. for an introductory class she made everything impossible. overall worst experience at uw was taking her class.

This is by far the worst professor I have ever had. She is rude and unprofessional. She rushes through lectures and teaches in the most convoluted way. She assigns unreasonable amounts of homework. If you have to take her, plan to go to the IC or MSC daily if possible. Also, most learning will be done in section so pray that you get a good TA.

Lectures aren't recorded, so find people to exchange notes with. Works through the content quickly, but accessible office hours to explain things. Answers questions in class, but doesn't always understand the questions asked, so be clear. When using the math study center, make sure the clarify that you needs something solved with the class content

This class is one of the worst classes that I have taken so far. She is an extremely tough grader. She doesn't post notes, or lecture videos and never posted even a syllabus. Everyone failed both midterms and probably the final as well. 120 is not for her

I don't think Dr Bekyel is always a bad teacher, she's passionate about math, but I don't think teaching Math 120 is for her. The lack of lecture recording and of posting of her notes made this class harder than it needed to be. The midterm averages for both midterms were poor. If you take her class, go to your TA's office hours it helps so so much

Prof. Bekyel is really smart and knowledgeable about Precalc/calc and is very qualified, but she couldn't slow down enough to really explain everything during this course.
