The average test scores were below 50%, and she was rude and blamed students for this instead of adjusting her teaching style. I would recommend her at a high level, not Math120.
The contents of the tests did not match up to the types of problems recommended for review, so you end up studying the wrong things.

Dr. Bekyel is extremely qualified, but can be shockingly unkind, uncaring and unhelpful. 
Throws away notes after class, forcing students to wait up to 25 min. in a crowd of students after class to take a photo, or suffer. 
If you have DRS accommodations or need help at all, expect contempt. Ask Loveless for an add code & use those materials.

Average on the first midterm was 42%, she said some of us need to consider changing career paths. She went fast and wouldn't finish problems in class. Lecture wasn't recorded and filled in notes weren't posted so don't skip. Homework assignments were nothing like what we did in lecture. She was nice, but be ready to WORK and visit office hours.
Best professor ever! Highly recommended 11/10! Don't listen to other reviews, they are wrong ❌. The class is basically high school math review, easy peasy lemon squizzy 🍋

Lots of hate here, but I thought she was fine. Took Math 126 with her during my first quarter of freshman year. The lectures were not recorded, but catching up is easy with youtube. She enjoys the subject, making lecture less of a slog to sit through. The curve is difficult, but ample studying outside of class will get you a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: First midterm and more than 89% of the class failing.She does give example on what to study for quiz so that's a pro but the midterm is difficult, she doesn't seem to listen to the TAs to adjust the quiz, "If you can't do number 3 on mt you either study really hard or consider changing your major"I don't want to put negative review but just don't .

She's a nice professor overall, holding clear and amazing lectures, giving questions with different difficulty to practice. But the workload for her class is relatively high, and it's hard to get a good grade. But choosing her as your professor will definitely influence your ideas towards math!

She doesn't post ANY lecture recordings or lecture notes, so if you miss a day you get automatically put behind. The content of this course isn't that difficult but she moves so fast that if you don't understand one topic, you likely will just continue to struggle. The tests are weighted so heavy that homework doesn't boost your grade. She is bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor's disorganized teaching style, lack of recorded lectures, and failure to provide promised worksheets make it difficult for students to keep up. Slowing down, providing structured notes, and ensuring materials are uploaded would greatly improve the learning experience.
Keeps lectures engaging, she has a strong focus on building intuition and good grades are in reach with a reasonable amount of effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Despite the reviews listed here, Dr. Bekyel is very engaging and a fantastic professor. She is quite the charismatic professor who cares about her students success. If you want to succeed, study outside class is absolutely necessary in addition to the homework, notes are important as her lectures aren't recorded but overall, a great professor.
lectures do help, homework and tests were okay, but the grading scale was so bad.

MATH 134 with Dr. Bekyel is a very relevant class for students intending to do math. Covers proof writing which shows up in many STEM fields, covers some analysis in calculus which makes Real Analysis more familiar later on, etc. The class is time consuming and your gpa will probably drop, but it will prepare you very well for the future.

This was an incredibly difficult entrance to college level mathematics, but Dr. Bekyel was consistently willing and able to help understand assignments and course content. Lectures weren't always the most beneficial, but provided useful context for some textbook concepts. Homework and tests were graded very harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Grades are heavily curved down, and lectures and notes are not recorded anywhere, meaning you must attend class or learn the material through your own resources. Nearly weekly quizzes/midterms. Do not get sick! There are no make-ups, and due to the curve you have no opportunity to get your grade up (not even with 99% on the final).

Dr. Bekyel's lectures are clear and helpful, clarifying the essence of things. Quizzes and exams are difficult but very related to what she has taught in class. You prepare well as long as you are actively engaged in classes. She is friendly and patient when you ask her math questions, and gave inspiring encouragement to my thank-you email (⌯'▾'⌯)♡
Heavy tests yet good lectures. She clarifies everything and is even more effective during OH. I got a 4.0 by just paying attention and doing past exams.

Other calc 126 classes has their 4.0 grade at ~94. Ours required a 98 for a 4.0, even though midterm difficulties were similar on average and final exams were the same. Very tough curve from this professor specifically.
No prelecture, no panopto recording, the notes were written by hand and never uploaded on canvas, though she is a smart professor.

Bekyel's lectures are clear and straightforward. She's funny and engaging in class (saddles became a meme iykyk). Quizzes are easy as she tells you exactly what's on the quiz ahead of time. The midterms and finals aren't bad and similar to past exams and HW, but highly affect your grade, so make sure to study. I don't think she deserves the hate.

She is absolutely terrible. She negative curved our class because we were doing well (not because of her by the way). I learned every ounce of material from the textbook, no help from her AT ALL. 

TERRIBLE teacher. A 91 was a 3.1 😭

reviews.comment: She has a fast pace during the lectures which makes it difficult to follow along sometimes. Also the real exams often had completely different questions than the practice and previous ones she gives you to help you practice.

- lectures confusing
- not recorded despite room having recording equipment
- had to learn everything from quiz section :(
if taking this prof you MUST pay attention to the lectures
idk why people are hating just pay attention ong
Intensely Confusing

Bekyel teaches very in-depth and explains things clearly. Very willing to answer questions especially during office hours. Quizzes aren't too difficult; basically just cover homework problems. Overall a very great and kind professor.

Only downside is she doesn't record lectures, but it's good motivation to pay attention.

Professor Bekyel is an excellent professor. It is clear that she has been teaching the 13x sequence for a while. The most important thing when taking her classes is to attend Office Hours. However, her grading is quite strict and to an extent nit-picky. But on a plus side, this will leave you extremely well prepared for any higher level classes.

Dr. Bekyel is not particularly helpful if you are struggling in math. The 134 course itself was difficult, but her being the teacher only made it worse. Her methods of mathematical proofs are unconventional and she does not sufficiently justify why it is so different. She grades your homework on the basis of her weird and unconventional proof style

Tough math class, but Professor Bekyel is a great teacher. Lectures are engaging, and the textbook is really helpful. Make sure to go to office hours and use resources like unstuckstudy AI alongside the coursework. It's a challenge, but doable if you put in the work.

Had Prof Bekyel for the entire 13x series, it's a tough one but very rewarding. Not only with credits but just the students are amazing, lectures are interesting, textbooks and homework problems are great, and just highly recommend. Not an easy class but it gets easier throughout the year, 134 is 100% the hardest class. Go to office hours!

Personally, I felt the calculus & diffeq portions were taught well, but the linear algebra portion was difficult to follow w/o extensive outside reading. Tests and homeworks are graded very strictly (hardly any true 100s from anybody on anything). Overall, enthusiastic and fun teacher, just put the honors in honors math lol...GO TO OFFICE HOURS. gl
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her lectures make less sense than reading the textbook. She also does not provide enough solutions to really know what will get you a good score. Really smart professor, but expects her students are as smart as her from the start. She does not post lectures notes or solutions to review problems. Also moved midterm 2 days early last minute.
if you miss the class, you will fail.

Math 13x is very tough, but if you're a diehard math nerd looking to dive in, it's the way to go. Introduces proofs and honestly every math class you take afterwards will be a breeze. Bekyel teaches the course perfectly, tough but fair. She's also just a nice person and gives good lectures.

Im currently taking Math 208 at the uw but my professor's teaching style is pretty chaotic. However, I stumbled upon a set of video recordings by Professor Ebru Bekyel and it has been a lifesaver for me. She explains every single concept in a clear and concise way, which has been extremely helpful. I really appreciate her!

Lectures are fast and can be confusing, and the font size on the lecture notes is tiny so having the notes on a tablet or something is very helpful. The quizzes are pretty easy and will boost your grade. Doing just the homework isn't enough.
(MATH 135) A lot harder than 134 in my opinion since all the topics are new. You won't do well if you only do the homework. Also, make sure you study for the final or else you'll fail badly.

Does not record lectures and goes insanely fast. So hard to keep up with what she is doing. Timed quizzes in quiz section are impossible to correctly complete in time. She is also very unapproachable if you have a question.

Bekyel was an incredible professor. Lecture style is clear and she doesn't use technical language. TAs are all very well prepared and helpful. Syllabus is short, so there's no confusion about grading.
Exams are difficult - usually 1-2 curveballs, and the weekly quizzes can also be hard. But partial credit is very generous.

Bekyel is very passive-aggressive towards students, especially when asking for questions relating to the content. Bekyel is also difficult to understand due to her lectures being conveyed on paper, as well as having a strong accent. Overall, would not recommend taking her sections, especially with her content being heavily influenced by lectures.

-Please only take this class if you're already comfortable with calculus. Otherwise you will struggle.
-Be careful on the midterms/final, as they are a large part of your grade (and don't make silly mistakes).
-Go to office hours.
-Don't start studying a day before the exam.
-Don't start the homework an hour before it's due

Bekyel is a kind and intelligent professor. Lectures were dry. Homework was quite difficult and time consuming. Tests were mostly straightforward, but always had some tricky questions. In general, don't take this class unless you're extremely comfortable with calculus and aren't doing other rigorous coursework. Go to office hours!

This is my impression of her after taking Math 134. First, she's a very tough grader, it's never unfair grading, but she doesn't let small mistakes slide, which can be frustrating at times. Besides for that, she is a pretty good lecturer and I did learn a lot in her class. Most of the difficulty comes from the course content itself, not her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Absolutely awful experience that I wouldn't wish on anyone.Take math 124 with anybody else, especially if it's online!

The 13x series is interesting and very time consuming. The amount of questions on homework will decrease as time goes on, but each will likely take more than hours to solve. Don't be afraid to ask questions (get clarification when needed). Her office hours helps greatly. Strongly recommend if you are interested in learning the "how" and "why"

Do NOT take her in an online section. Insanely low test averages, M1 was a 45% average and M2 was a 39% average. Lectures are long and hard to get through but they do help, make sure to have a study buddy or a group because it will make your life a lot easier in this class.

This class sucks. I retook the online version 3 times. 0.6 the first time, 1.8 the second, and I'm about to finish with a 3.1. U know what changed? the 3rd time i watched every lecture. They're hard to sit thru sometimes, but prof bekyel is very thorough with her explanations and covers all the weird algebra tricks you need (if ur paying attention)

A good lecturer but a bit old fashioned (doesn't record lectures, doesn't have a lot of online resorces). Also I thought all the midterms were pretty fairly written but the final was a bit overly difficult.

For Math 13x in particular, she is a pretty good teacher. Relatively effective at introducing and explaining new topics, but you've got to be constantly paying complete attention or you're done for. She can be a fairly hard grader, but once you get the hang of it, it isn't too bad. She loves to throw in tricky questions on tests, which is annoying.

Dr. Bekyel is simply not a good professor. She does not record lectures nor does she post notes that students can follow along with. Her lectures are incredibly fast-paced and she is absolutely awful at responding to emails. Her tests are incredibly difficult and contain material irrelevant to class. She is quite intimidating too.

Creates very difficult tests that aren't even close to difficultiy of homework and lecture problems. Even students who had taken previous calculus classes found her class to be extremely hard and toughly graded.

I don't want to just show up and drag a professor, but honestly the worst form of instruction I've ever seen. Recycled course material from the prior semester, put zero effort into actually teaching. Just seems like they're there to collect a paycheck. Does easy examples for online "lectures" then assigns things never discussed before.

Don't be afraid of her reviews.124 is a hard course no matter who you have. If you show up to office hours and make use of her resources Bekyel is a good and straightforward professor. I got a 4.0 in the class because she answered all of my questions. Issue - she does not record lectures. 

Do practice tests and go to her office hours to succeed!

reviews.comment: carelessness

reviews.comment: After finishing my degree this quarter, I can officially say she was the worst Professor I ever had. BY FAR.

Tough grader and has a lot of homework (get ready for some 10+ hours hw assignments). However, Prof. Bekyel herself is approachable and is a good lecturer. Proofs done in class are hard, but don't hesitate to ask questions and ask Prof. Bekyle to reexplain the confusing parts, she'll be happy to help :) She is very patient when answering questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
She gives way too much homework, and the course is weighted too heavily on exams.
However, Dr. Bekyel and her TA are very accessible, cool, and helpful.

The lectures are pretty dry. Solutions to homework/exam review problem sets are never posted.

Dr. Bekyel is a very cool person and accomplished professor, but not a good instructor in my opinion.

She is not nearly as mean as other people here say, but she isn't very personable (I didn't talk to her once). The midterms and finals can be really rough, even if you're comfortable with the material, so make sure to study as much as you can for those. Overall, a fine class that if you take it seriously, is pretty low stress until finals.

I wouldn't say she's takes joy in failing students, but she's definitely very strict and not very approachable. If you have to take her class, make very good friends with your TA (shoutout to Marvyn!), make use of the tools WebAssign gives to practice stuff you did bad on, and do as many practice tests as you can before exams.

Probably the most work I've ever done in a class. Take Math 134 if you want to spend most of your time doing work for it. On the other hand, the lectures are very engaging, and the content/level of learning is worth it. If you like math or want to like math take this course.

DIFFICULT! does not give extensions of assignments even if you're really sick. her exams are specific and expects you to remember concepts learned in freshman geometry. she does not record lectures so if you're sick, you're screwed. her tests have an average of 50-60% while other professors have them in their 80's.

The professor does not care for your success, the professor is not understanding in the slightest. Encountering professors with the same mindset as Dr. Bekyel's tests my dedication to my education. I would never recommend this professor, if I could switch out, I would. Beware future students.

Bekyel is a menace to a hilarious degree. Everyone comes into 12x with nightmares of getting a teacher like her - she is the personification of UW's weed-out system. She takes joy in thinning the herd of incoming STEM kids. If you're not already strong in calc, stay away. If you are (and love schadenfreude) sit far back and enjoy the show.

Dr. Bekyel is a fantastic professor. She cares about her students and the math, but she grades harshly and her tests and homework are difficult. The class and 13X series requires a lot of work, but is rewarding and there are lot of resources from Bekyel if you need help.

I don't know how the UW could hire a person like this. Teachers like this are what make the math department low quality in terms of student satisfaction and success. It almost seems like her goal in the class is to fail as many students as she can. This is the type of teacher who makes college unenjoyable, Do not Recommend at all.
Shows you the easiest version possible of a problem and tests you on a problem way harder than you could have guessed possible while not explaining any of the topics.

reviews.comment: not a good teacher at all. ruined my passion for math. test questions were much harder than the lectures/practice, and it she does not do a good job of explaining in her lectures. not many study resources available. average on midterms was a 45% which is ridiculous for calc 1.

reviews.comment: Extremely unaccommodating and no empathy for students who have 2-3 other classes. Horrible at explaining things in lecture and expects way too much of students. Calculus should not be this hard, but she makes it hard. Even TA said that her exams were way too hard for the short amount of time we're given.

Avoid by all means necessary. This lady is straight-up evil making sure midterm questions are on the subjects the students know the least about. 60% of your grade is the 2 midterms+final. The average score for my class on the midterms was <45%. Take this class at a CC and transfer it in if you have to. You couldn't pay me $50k to take this class.

Hardest class I've ever taken, but Bekyel was generally helpful. Best piece of advice: go to office hours. She's very good there. (Regarding the honors calc series itself, don't take it unless you're already comfortable with calculus.)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The other reviews are right, really unaccommodating, lots of homework. Don't find out the hard way.

Horrendous professor. Honestly believe the course would have been easier if UW instead gave me a Khan Academy link and a prayer. Lectures are incomprehensible, will solve half a problem and say "you guys do the rest." Rude, curt, and unhelpful with student questions. Everything else on here is true. Only take if you enjoy math, masochism, or both.

reviews.comment: Everyone I spoke to agrees that lectures are incredibly hard to follow and overall useless. Extremely unaccommodating. don't recommend :///
Tough but fair. The class goes really fast. Just be prepared to look at a problem and not understand for a few hours. The tests are straight forward. If you enjoy math this is your class.

This is a very hard class and your best resource will be TA's and additional help outside class. I had background calculus knowledge and still struggled a lot to get an acceptable grade. Test questions are miles harder than lectures so really try to understand practice tests and problems.

Had Dr. Bekyel for Honors Calculus 1 so my experience is different than most. She seems to work best with more advanced students who enjoy mathematics. A LOT of homework and difficult exams. Only take honors calc if you love mathematics. She is a decent lecturer, sometimes quite helpful sometimes unclear. Very helpful during office hours, so go!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: seriously dont take this class with her. everyone i know in the class hated her and she was extremely unaccommodating. she wouldnt allow a quiz retake even with a doctors note from being in the hospital. is such a hardass on grading--even worksheets that were graded on completion.

Prof Bekyel throws in some witty remarks every now and then, but she does go pretty quickly through the lectures. Be prepared to spend plenty of time studying on your own to understand concepts, she only really introduces them and shortcuts that you can take after you understand concepts. She does provide fairly good review material though.

reviews.comment: Please for the love of all things good, do not take Prof. Bekyel if you value your mental health, especially if you're not naturally good at math. She never explains things clearly, and goes way too fast over examples and explanations. The workload is unrelenting, and she's rather unkind too. Avoid at all costs.

Terrible, she made a mistake grading my test and deducted a few extra points from it, but when i corrected her and she saw she messed up, she said she could give me points back here but then deduct points from somewhere else because of some long made up excuse that my answer was not sufficient although i got full points for it initially.

This class was just asynchronous videos where you didn't even see her, it was just her writing and SO BORING. Homework was manageable and tests weren't too hard. There are semi-weekly-ish quizzes which aren't hard either. I didn't put a ton of effort into the class and didn't do particularly well on tests or anything but ended up with a 3.8 somehow

Super disorganized. Wasn't respectful of students in other time zones. Didn't take into account the current pandemic. Lectures sucked and looked like they were made on a 2008 flip phone. Unclear expectations. Super unfair grading. Just a horrible professor all around. If you can switch to a different Prof, DO IT!!!! I have no clue why she has a job

Take this class with another prof. The only thing keeping me from dropping this class is that S/NS for this quarter is okay for prereqs. Tests do not look like homework or lectures at all.
