So if you want to score high in this class pay attention to every detail! But if you want a more theoretical approach then this would be disappointing.

Professor Bekyel is the one of the best professors i've had at uw so far. She has a great accent, is funny, and her lectures are clear and to the point. She records all her lectures and puts them on her website too which is a plus, so attendance isn't mandatory. I heard her midterms are easier than other classes as well.
She goes fast and isn't always clear about where she is going. If you pay attention, you'll get it. Office hours were also a must for me.

Worst math instructor I've met at UW. Hard and extremely time-consuming homework. Unreasonably strict on both homework and tests. My friend got 2 points deducted for a spelling mistake in test. She expected us to memorize more than 70 definitions and theorems and utilize them well during test. i.e NO cheat sheet at all! Do NOT take class w/ her!!!
If you want to have math125class at uw. You must choose her class!!!! Her lecture is very clear to me and I got 4.0 this quarter.

Lectures are boring but essential. Shes cute in a little old Turkish mom kind of way. Weekly quizzes, but she tells you exactly what's on them. Midterms are fair, challenging but not at all horrible. Gives you the website that has all of her old tests. Records her lectures and posts notes online. Homework is hard but its easy to get outside help

Love Professor Bekyel! She color codes all her notes and is the clearest, neatest math professor I've ever had (A rarity, I may add). She is incredibly intelligent and explains things very well. Wish she was teaching 126 next quarter!

Bekyel is the worst math professor I have ever had, Perkins class was the same quarter and his students averages were amazing compared to our class. She over complicates everything and makes you leave class feeling stupid, and her tests are extremely hard, way different from the review! This class caused me a lot of stress and anxiety, avoid her!!

Boring lectures. 2 midterms. Hard homeworks. Few help provided online(except that she did post lecture note). Information about tests was so little(she didn't even send out any info about our 2nd midterm, which my friend and I were so speechless about.... ). Do not recommend!

She's a very nice person, but her method of teaching focused on giving light weight examples and then dishing out massive complex homework assignments that were due within days of each other. It would require lots of reaching out for help to pass a class with her as a professor.

I honestly liked her a lot! She wrote the notes up in front of the class and did her best to help explain. She also reviewed before the Midterms and Final, if you spoke up she'd go over any problem you asked. The only problem was her tests were very difficult, but she always cared about how you did and asked about it next lecture.

Ebru did an okay job teaching MATH120. I would say she could rely less on the textbook for guidance of her lectures (would literally write pieces of chapters word-for-word). Doesn't utilize the given technology - writes lectures on projector. Made lots of mistakes.  Pretty careless in her teaching. Didn't seem like she cared if we succeeded.

Terrible teacher. First day of class she said no one would come out of her class with a GPA higher than a 2.4. I believe she accomplished that. Her teaching style is set to prepare someone for Math 125.

Lecture is literally useless. She makes mistakes while teaching and gives easy examples that are nothing like the homework. If you go to office hours she can be mildly helpful. Homework is the hardest I have ever had to do, and I received an A in AP Calc AB in high-school. I made it out with a B, but I had to work pretty hard.
Has good intentions but she truly is a poor teacher.  Makes a lot of mistakes during lecture and makes the tests really difficult.
Spent hours doing homework and spending money on a tutor to find that I ended up failing the class. Would not recommend Ebru at all! she will ruin your life.

Expect to do a lot of homework and have to reach out for help to pass. Using on campus resources such as CLUE and the Math Study Center are highly recommended. Since when you sign up for math it doesn't display the professor at UW, just hope that you get someone else. It was very difficult but I did get a grade good enough to go on to 124.

She's the worst instructor I've ever had. Lectures are basically useless, homework is almost unrelated to lectures, and tests are much harder than expected. Expect to self-teach most of the material if you want to have a shot at passing! Avoid her class if you can!
TEST ARE HORRIBLE! Lectures don't match the homework, and the exams she gives are harder than all other professors.  If you go to office hours you'll have a chance though.

Her lectures are in no way indicative of what you can expect from WebAssign. IF her lectures are easy to understand, then it's not what the homework will look like. Tests are extremely difficult. Only real help I got was from the Math Study Center.
Literally decided to rate her in the middle for studying my exam. I already know I'm going to fail. Had to ask my high school math teacher for help the entire quarter.

This professor is awful by far the worst math professor I have had. She gets simple math wrong all the time in class and doest care at all. The tests and HW are hard and she doesn't teach them in class. She frequently leaves out information that is necessary to do homework. The tests are not at all like the HW but similar to practice midterms.

Fall2015 Math 120, Homework: is usually one chapter due every tues and thurs. One time there was three chapters due where there would usually be one. that was the tues before a thurs. midterm.  Her lectures most usually have to do with the hmk. She tells you what kind of problems to expect on the midterm.

I think I was very lucky to have her as my Math 328 teacher because math 328 is a very hard class. The topic itself is already bloody hell difficult but she tried her best to make student understand everything. The most important thing is that her office hour is very very useful and she is very patient. As long as you try your best you will succeed

Worst math professor at UW. She does not teach you at all. Her lectures do not make any sense and do not match the webassign homework. She sometimes gives out 3 chapters of homework out at once all due on the same day while other professors do 1 chapter due at a time. A lot better off learning the material on your own. She messes up way too much.
She is the least helpful math teacher I have ever had. I learn more in quiz section then I do going to lecture.

She skips steps and messes up often when working through problems during lecture. The WebAssign homework is lengthy and 20x more difficult than what she teaches in lecture. Expect a majority of your time to be spent on WebAssign homework. Class average on the 1st midterm was an F (20/50), as well as a majority of the weekly quizzes so far.
She is the worst math teacher I have come across. She messes up frequently during her lectures and her homework assignments are ridiculously hard.

Is passionate about the content but does not always come across clearly. Works very quickly during instruction and questions are answered with repeats of prior instructions. Overall the TA was more clear than the professor for the course.

I had Ebru for 111 & 112 & dreaded both classes. I'm good at math so I had no difficulty w the class, but if it's not your strong suit, you will need help. She also was stubborn. Lecture got behind the HW & she wouldn't listen to us, so we got graded on assignments we hadn't learned how to do yet. If you have a choice of profs, don't take her.

Lectures and homework were straightforward. She told us the first midterm would be extremely similar to last year's midterm but it was MUCH harder. Second midterm was okay, but final was also hard. As someone who did well in AP Calc in HS, I thought this class was going to be easy, but it was much harder than it should've. Avoid her if you can!!

I had to teach myself and work very hard in her class to end up still not doing well. I had never struggled in math before, but she made everything very difficult. Hard to understand her in lecture and very rude towards students. Would certainly never take a class from her again.

Ebru got her PhD from Brown; she is smart. However, she is not the best professor. She goes super fast in class, so you just copy down notes without absorbing anything she's saying. She makes lots of small mathematical errors on in class examples and on answer keys as well. Her tests are LONG and hard, and she has no sympathynever gives pts back.

HW & Lectures helped most. Tends to be rude at genuine (ez) questions frm students (expects you to know already). Makes many mistakes during lecture (a lot). M1 hard - misled every1. M2 ez - straight to pt. Overall, I understood most of the stuff. Wouldn't recommend if you have a hard time with math already (fast pace). Good luck
Test prep doesn't cover the actual test material. Can't understand half of what she says in lecture.

She is really passionate about mathematics and business calculus. MATH 112 is required for business school at UW. Compared to MATH 124, it is more like applied calculus.  Material is not that hard, just calculus I stuff. Eburu is great lecturer and she always give clear explanations. 4-5 quizzes and 3 midterms. One midterm is harder but do-able.

Bombed her midterm (Most of the students did) Her class examples and homework are super easy compared to her tests & quizzes. I went to talk to her about my grade and she was very rude and said there was no way I could pass her class. It seemed like she was out to get us giving us 2 page quizzes and only 10 min. I would NEVER take her again.

Bekyel is clear in her examples during lecture. Her quizzes and HW, which seem to be the same regardless of the professor you choose, are easy. However, that's where the pros of taking a class with her end. Her first midterm during Winter 2014 was not similar to last year's midterm, which she told us to use to study. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASSES.

DO NOT TAKE CLASSES FROM HER! The examples she gives in class and  on homework assignments(which by the way are excessively long) are super easy but then her tests are extremely difficult with super hard questions and you don't even have the time to finish. Again, AVOID HER AT ALL COSTS.

I don't recommend taking her class for math112. Her lectures are easy to understand but judging from the first midterm we took today, it's significantly more difficult and had problems that don't resemble questions from previous exams. No Bueno

I thought her math 112 class was easier than her 111 class. Quizzes are always very easy, homework is hard and time consuming, and midterms and final were really hard and tricky. Do as many practice problems as you can in preparation for the tests. class was curved so even with a Midterm score of 50% I got above average

Professor Ebru is very friendly and helpful. Although sometimes she can be a little ambiguous, mostly she is pretty clear throughout the lecture. This class was hard as hell though. Don't take it unless you're going to major in mathematics.

Took her class during Autumn 2013. Her first time teaching MATH 111, and she teaches the simplest examples in lecture and gives easy quizzes. Midterms are extremely hard and her final was hard. She never finishes her examples from lecture. My overall percentage was in the 60s and I still had above a 2.0. Overall, she's okay.
She makes this class much more difficult than it needs to be and the tests are ridiculously hard. Avoid taking it with her at all costs and try to get with another proffessor.

The second midterm was ridiculously hard because the problems were extremely different than the examples she gave in class. The curve is not helpful either. I would take it with another prof if I could unless you're willing to accept an average grade of 3.0-3.3.

This professor is hard to understand during lecture. She goes over fairly easy examples during class, and then puts extremely hard ones on the exam. She does not prepare the class well for exams, and when the mean score for a midterm was a D, she did not curve it. Overall unfair compared to other math professors.
Great, friendly professor.

Good instructor, very clear. Uses dual overheads, which upsets me as someone who likes having computerized notes to print and write on. Getting down all the notes requires a lot of focus in lecture. Unless you like asking questions, I wouldn't bother going to non-exam quiz sections, your time is probably better spent practicing out of the book.

Only took two calculus classes at UW, but was the better one I had. Explains material well most of the time and posts gobs of supplementary on her website. Tests are extremely difficult, but are very generous with partial credit.

Wonderful lady! She is so sweet and has a way of being so funny and entertaining during lectures. Yes, her midterms are more difficult than many of the other profs but she gives you access to all her previous midterms so if you are willing to put in the effort you will do well. I would love to take another class with her!

If you've taken math up to Algebra 2 in the past, the concepts should be mainly review. After making it to the first couple weeks of class, I really only went whenever I wanted a refresher. She gives many examples but the homework is extremely time consuming. Her second midterm was also unreasonably hard for the material covered.

I adore this professor. She is enthusiastic with a mild yet engaging sense of humor, and she's always so cute about it! She shows care for her students and gives clear, concrete examples to explain concepts. Her tests were always challenging, but certainly not unreasonable. I like that she has high expectations without being intimidating or mean.

Great professor. The class itself is really easy and Ebru just takes everything a step further and dumbs it down for you. Im not the smartest kid and I got a 4.0. Midterms were super easy, you just got put forth the effort and study. Final was pretty hard, don't underestimate it.
She is honestly really awful. The language barrier is enough that she doesn't really understand what you are asking. She doesn't go over sections and then puts them on the test.

Horrible professor. Had a 4.0 in class all the way up until the final (based off of me teaching the concepts to myself) and Ebru wrote an extremely terrible final exam that was way off topic. She excluded huge concepts we spent weeks on, and tested over half the test questions on minuscule details. AVOID AT ALL COSTS

GREAT professor! I didn't have to read the textbook once through out the quarter because she was very detailed and clear in her lectures. The only down side is that her tests are incredibly difficult (which doesn't matter much since it shows in the curve). Highly recommended!!

Really great teacher! She makes sure you are prepared for your exams. She is easy to follow and really nice. The only negative thing is that she tends to write down EVERYTHING that comes to her mind, but she does take really good notes!

her notes is really IMPORTANT!!! read and review all her notes are helpful for midterms and final!! Although her writes lots of "extra" words, when you get review, it is really useful for thinking! I really like her class! She is nice too~

Her explanations are clear, and the grading policy is fair. Also she drops out the lowest grade for the quizzes, worksheets, and hw. I've got much better grade for this class than for Math 124, which I took with other professor. Attend the lectures, do the hw, do practice exams, and you should be good. Good luck!

Absolutely sweet professor, but not the best at teaching math. I wish I took another professor. Avoid her if you can, especially if you're new to the course. Her lectures are confusing and you're better off asking the TA/self studying the material rather than going to lectures.

Her explanations step-by-step are super clear and detailed! She loves and understands math, so it is interesting for me to listen to her! Also, math in general requires a lot of self-study and patience, and it is important to get her "simple examples" (as some other comments say) to move to harder ones.
I would not recommend her. Confusing lectures, hard tests, hard quizzes. None of her examples come up on the tests. She is great person to talk to though. She should rather be a counselor.

Bekyel tries to explain concepts through examples, but her examples are sometimes confusing. Go to her lectures, practice all types of problems that she demonstrated then you can easily ace this class like me!

Great teacher but bad lecturer. One on one conversations with her are great, but lectures are almost useless. Examples are slowly performed and sometimes uncompleted. And her quiz sections are unorganized. But she is a very nice professor, highly experienced and knows what she is talking about. Overall, she seems to have a better class than others.

Sure, she's a nice person, but that is not a qualification for a job as a professor. She makes everything unnecessarily difficult by solving problems in the most roundabout way and not even explaining why. Her tests are more difficult than anything she does in class. She should not be teaching.

Bekyel's lectures makes concepts more confusing than it should be. Her midterms are unreasonably hard, even if you understand the material, she will put  curveballs in the midterm that you've never seen/practiced before. Most professor's makes the midterm easier than the hw, but she makes it harder.  Do not recommend her AT ALL.
She is a pleasure to be around. Very helpful if you go to her office hours. Class is not easy, but she makes the most of it with examples and a (dry) sense of humor.

Bekyel will teach you all the material that needs to be taught. She will also give you a lot of basic examples so you understand. Homework is more difficult than her examples, and her tests are harder than her examples and the homework. Can be ditsy. You have to do a lot of self study and make study buddies if you want to succeed with her.

Such a great Math professor!!! Absolutely enjoyed her class. She has the cutest way of explaining abstract things and her explanations do stick with you. Midterms are not easy but definitely resonable. Work hard and you will succeed!!

Pretty good. She is pretty clear about every step she takes when she does examples. However, some lectures she neglected to mention at the start what she would be covering, so it was a bit difficult following. Tests are kind of difficult, but you get a cheat sheet so no complaints there. The grading is ok. Not too harsh or too lenient.
She is really nice and seems to know a lot about her topics. Lectures are not all that bad but I will say her midterms are very difficult and I don't think she cares much about student success rates.

If you do the work and study for the tests, the class is very doable- the professor is helpful and the expectations on exams are well established. Be careful not to fall behind on the material. Took this class straight out of high school using AP credit, and had no trouble.
She is very clear and concerned about explaining things well in her lectures.

Exams are definitely harder than other 126 profs. Lectures were not the best, sometimes hard to follow and never finished the examples she says she will. Much more helpful in office hours than in lecture. I found this class harder than 124/125
NOT RECOMMEND. Her lectures are not clear, and very careless with her students. She doesn't post all the answers of homework. If u want challenging, this is her.

This class, for me, was MUCH harder than 124 and 125. Her examples aren't that great and quiz sections were not very helpful either. I was never really able to wrap my head around the concepts covered in this class and barely passed.
If you like math, her lecture is your choice.

if you try to review her metrial after class, you will find many notes are useless and hard to follow. It is said that her 124 and 125 is easy, but I got to say that her 126 is hard to get a very high score. She try to control the average, therefore in her midterms you will always bump into some hard problems. Recommend Alexandra Nichifor's lectur

I had her class for Math 124 and 125. She never finished her examples. If you learn through examples like me, try to get a different teacher. She is nice and I know she was trying but she is not helpful with learning this material. Teach yourself through the textbook.

Ebru was wonderful! I hate math, especially Calculus, and have difficulties with it. She helped a ton, and though English is not her first language, her lectures were very clear. The homework was WAAYYY harder than the lectures, but I'm not sure if that was her fault. She's incredibly nice, I would HIGHLY recommend her!

Bekyel is an awesome teacher. I had her for 124 and thought it was great for a math class. She's a lenient grader (will give you points even if you make mistakes) and her midterms aren't too bad. Study her past tests, attend lecture and you should be fine.
Enthusiastic about the material. Very enjoyable lectures. Would take her again.
Ebru's teaching method involved making up problems she could not solve and repeating useless information. She seemed to have a thin grasp on the concepts she was teaching. I stopped going to class.
Abosultely a great teacher. She definitely explain everything clear and effectively. The test will be very easy if u attend every class of her

Bekyel did a good job explaining things in class and using a variety of examples. I thought Math 125 presented a lot of challenging material but if you go to class, take notes, and make the effort to do the homework you will do well. Her exams are not graded that hard (very small deductions for minor mistakes) and you will learn a lot.

I hate math. I hardly took any in HS, but I needed 124 for my major. The homework was long and tedious. Quizzes were fairly easy. Midterms were okay if you studied. I liked Ebru - she made a painful class tolerable. Plus, her tests are apparently not as hard as other Math profs. Bottom line: I recommend this professor.

It was an okay class...you don't need to buy the textbook (all homework assignments are through webassign). The tests are difficult and she doesn't really care if you learn or not. She's probably one of the nicer math professors at the UW but isn't terrific...

After not having taken calculus in H.S, I was worried I would be lost and do badly, since many people in the class had taken it before. However I found the tests to be quite easy, and the examples she did in lecture were very helpful; she has a slight accent but it does not in any way impair understanding. Would recommend.

She is not a good teacher. She doesn't care if you learn, and takes no interest in you at all. I once emailed her friday afternoon with a math question. Then on monday I asked if she had seen my email. She responded by saying "I have a life I dont respond to emails on the weekend." Overall not a good teacher. I needed the book to understand anythin
teaching is not clear. I took calculus in high school and all she's doing is confusing me even more.
Avoid. Does not know her information. Gave the wrong equations during lecture, even said she did not know how to explain a problem in class.

Ebru Bekyel is clear and organized, but an excessively difficult and terribly demotivating teacher. She responds scornfully to students' questions during class, so I never visited her during office hours. Maybe she's okay in person, but I doubt it. Her quizzes are timed so that you can barely finish them and her tests are very difficult.
She's very clear... she's one of the nicest professors I've ever had!!! she explains materials until students understand those...I love her =)

I've been in Ebru's class twice (for Math 125 & 126). Her examples in class are thorough and clear, but I found that it was equally helpful to just look at the same examples in the textbook since her explanations were rarely more in depth. Her exams struck me as unnecessarily tricky and she was reluctant to answer any of my questions outside class.

Having taken Bekyel two times, I speak from experience. I always thought she was a great teacher in MATH 125, but I took APcalc in high school, so I think I falsely attributed my good performance to her teaching. In MATH 126, I realized she was poor at explaining, and that you had to do very extensive studying on top of her lecture notes to get a B

Ebru is a good proffessor - her notes are very clear, she seems to highlight the main points well. Go to class and you will understand everything you need to know. Her midterms also seemed a little easier than other professors teaching the same course.

She explains everything clearly, and if you don't understand, she will help you understand individually. As long as you do the homework, go to classes and study hard, passing quizzes is easy, but watch out for the midterms and final.

I had a better understanding of calculus before taking this class. My high school teacher taught the same material much more clearly. Also, learning calculus without a calculator... useful when? Certainly not in engineering.

Prof Bekyel taught my M307 class. The textbook is HORRIBLE to read on its own - go to class, pay attention! Bekyel is coherent despite accent, and her teaching style is OK, but her notes are often wrong or hard to follow. I will only recommend this class to those who will truly enjoy the material. I got a lot out of it, but not the best experience.

Poor profesor when it comes to Diff Eq. Her accent ins't a problem and she was amazing when she subbed for my 126 class but is terrible at 307. She makes frequent mistakes, teaches WRONG stuff. Most of my notes are worthless because she gave us the wrong equations.

Excellent teacher. Her explanations were very good and it's definitely worth it to go to lecture. Exams were tricky but fair - best way to prepare is to do her past exams and put effort into the homework assignments.
Worth math teacher I've ever had. Avoid, if possible.

Prof Bekyel taught Math 126 very well. The material was difficult but she tried her best to teach it. She is fast-paced which keeps the class going and she will help you if you are stuck on a problem. Be prepared for her midterms and tests. They're a bit harder than you would expect so pay attention in class. Go to lecture.
Not very clear example
Good prof. She really makes the effort to make sure her students understand the material. Tests are reasonable as well.
Wonderful
LOVE HER HOW SHE GOES OVER THE MAIN POINTS IN THE IN EACH CHAPTER. SHE IS EASY TO FALLOW AND UNDERSTAND. SHE ALWAYS HAVE A SMILE ON HER FACE.
Ebru rocks!

Really good professor. Taught the material in a very nice and straightforward way that was easy to understand. Tests aren't that hard if you just study the sort of problems she does in class and be sure to do the homework.
Very easy class. Prof was very nice and is funny.
Good at explaining concepts, long office hours. If you go to lecture, you'll understand how to do hw problems without having to read the book. Enthusiastic about what she does. Funny.
good professor with clear explanations. go to lecture and you'll get through without reading the book at all.  but her homework is kind of challenging.
Ebru is funny and personable.  She is good at explaining and will reiterate topic if you don't understand it.  Just make sure you stay on top of the homework. Quizzes are based on it.
Fun professor. Very Helpful. Long office hours. Nice accent. Good looking!

She is an awesome professor. Her tests are much easier than my tests from 124 were (with Devinatz) so the transition has been awesome. She is helpful and reasonable. If you talk to her she will agree to not have you turn in homework after midterms etc, she is real chill.
Tests are fair: she states exactly what is going to be on the quizzes and midterms. Her office hours help are very helpful.
She was really boring, lectures put me to sleep. But her tests were fair, if you go to tutorial and do the homeowork you can do well.

Professor Bekyel has a corky sense of humor-she always keeps me entertained in class with her comments. She is good at explaining the concepts; however, the tests are not all concepts-there's a lot of arithmetic involved, so don't mess up on the algebra! It's ok if you do though, cuz the right answer is only 1 point, and working is 9.
Tests are depressing
I found her lectures to be rather dull and boring, which didn't help when it came to the tests.

Bekyel's lectures are ok, some of the earlier lectures seem to be a bit confusing by just diving right into the material without introducing what it is, but the later lectures were better. Her tests are very hard, but they do prepare you for the final. Just make sure to score above the avg on both midterms

If you're good at math, take her class so you can do well on the tests and be above the curve. If not, I'd suggests that you take the class from another prof and sit in on her lecture; she's amazing at explaining concepts, but her tests are definitely on the tricky side.

Taking calculus for a first time, i thought the material wasn't too bad... until you get to the end of chapter 3 and beginning of 4 (related rates and optimization problems! ugh!) however, the prof... i suggest not take her unless you really want to fail math! her midterms are crazy hard! she was chuckling when we all failed the first one!
She's a good teacher. The midterms are pretty difficult though.. but everyone does bad so it's OK. She's really nice but her midterms are really mean.
very hard if you havent taken any calculus prior. very sassy [probably because of pregnancy]. doesnt explain steps taken to arrive at final answer.

She would go through really difficult proofs to explain a concept and would then only do one practical example that was way easier than any homework problem we had or any question she would put on a test so that we would have no idea how to actually do it.

Lectures are really dry; She tends to give midterms that have questions that are harder than the problems practiced in class and in the h/w; Didn't find her midterm reviews helpful at all; avrg on first midterm was around 55%; avrg on 2nd midterm was 21/40 points [tends to give 4 problems on the midterm, ea. being 10 pts]
clear lectures, not too much homework, want students to understand material, tests aren't easy but not too hard, overall good teacher

Overall a good professor that obviously understands the material. At first didn't seem too great but improved throughout the quarter. Although the class was pretty hard, she curved it nicely at the end. Main complaint is the easiness of her examples compared to the difficulty of the homework problems.
Amazingly helpful. She spent a ridiculous amount of time helping me outside of class in her office. I'm 100% certain I wouldn't have passed the class without her willingness to do this.
The exams were reasonable, so was her grading but I do not enjoy the lectures - her notes were long and she writes pretty fast. I did not find the lectures very useful.
She's alright

She is really good at explaining complex ideas in an understandable fashion. The only complaint I have is that the example problems in class are never as hard as the homework problems, and so you end up relying on the book a lot more than the notes. I recommend her as a teacher, though.

The best math prof I've had in my life (and I'm a math major). She explains hard concepts better than any other prof-and she is very smart, very nice, and more than fair on tests. If you're looking for a math prof look no further, she is INARGUABLY the best math prof ever. Explains hard concepts better than you can explain addition.

One of the best math lecturers I've come across-- she goes through problems step-by-step in a clear, organized manner that's very easy to follow. Her tests are reasonable, and she's very approachable outside of class.

She is a good prof, and she does explain the material well.  i dont like how she writes down a lot of wordy things, like 'there is a small problem with...' because i dont like to write down a lot of words in my math notes.  but thats just a small complaint i have.

Awesome instructor.  Lectures were decent and orderly.  Homework was a little long and tricky, but exams were very reasonable and she did a terrific job of preparing you for them.  Not the least bit intimidating, and ALWAYS helpful should you have a question.
Clear lectures, very helpful outside of class
Extremely clear and gives good explanations in lecture. Lecture style is very organized and always willing to answer questions. Overall, great professor! I would highly recommend her.
She was nice since BU. Happiness for her.
Extremely good lectures. Very clear explanations and examples. The material itself is not easy, but she makes everything clear. She does have an accent, but it is understandable without extra effort.

All of the questions on the midterms/final exam are on the study guides, but knowing the terms is crucial as there are lots of close multiple choice answers/matching that requires you to know the definition. His lectures are very engaging and educational. Make sure you put in effort on your group projects because they end up being worth a bit

Lecture style is great. Slides do not have much information on these so attendance is required for an actual understanding. There is lots of reading which aren't all necessary but helped me. Group projects are essays.

Lecture style was cool, but slides are set up with limited information so attendance is necessary for full understanding. Lots of reading which isn't required but definitely helped me. The group projects are essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I was super excited to take this class but it turned out to be not very challenging at all. 3 tests are super easy and you could go get an A without reading what he assigned all quarter. Pretty annoying when he answers all the questions people have in class...like cmon use office hours please but that does mean he is very approachable and kind.

90% of the time, are just chatting and talking about the readings that we assigned. The reading was not easy, and if u want to be engaged, you have to be super "smart." he just thinks so deeply about the readings. His class was great, the work was not hard at all, just some writing,easy A. Love the teacher, But not take it again.

Richard knows a lot about the topics covered in the course which were interesting. I would NOT take a class with him. What was expected wasnt clear and he often went off course. He goes on a lot of tangents and is disrespectful at times. 2 people dropped the class because of him. He isnt sympathetic to students struggling with mental illness.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Block could not have been a worse teacher. Going to class meant listening to him complain about anything and everything. He doesn't know how to use modern technology and genuinely might be too old to be teaching. The only reason why I dropped this class was because of him.
Took him for German 120. Interesting to say the least. Sometimes he graded easy, sometimes he graded more difficult. He talked a lot and rambled. Overall not too difficult
A good course with many interesting readings.  Block is very open to student ideas as long as you have evidence from the text to support your ideas.  A very good learning experience.

Professor Block is incredibly understanding and caring. The main component to succeeding in his classes is in-class participation. If you show that you are giving the assignments and the class your best effort he will work with you to help you succeed in the class. He is a big fan of open-ended, lengthy discussions so come to class with opinions.
He really helps you develop your ideas and figure out how to present them in essays
Fair and fun and you learn a lot, a whole lot
Much more interesting and challenging than I thought--one of my favorite courses
happy to hear other's ideas. yes, you need to participate in class, but he gives very positive feedback.
The class was the best at the university
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Pros: good writing feedback, no harsh deadlines, lets you rewrite as many times as you want for a better grade, cares about important current events Cons: unorganized, talks about other peoples grades in front of the whole class, and you must repeat exactly what he says on essays (no room for own interpretation)

Participation and attendance matter, you get graded on how much you speak up in class. For the essays, he wants you to reiterate exactly what he says and doesn't leave room for your own interpretation. However he allows makeup essays. Lectures aren't very clear or organized. Unless this is a required class I would try to find another.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I didn't know what to expect., but we had the most interesting and thought-provoking discussions almost the entire quarter. The professor used the material to help us think about immigration today. One of my three favorite courses so far.

He does a wonderful job of relating the historical material to current events. He is opinionated, but he is as open as any professor I've had to student's comments and criticisms. Also, a great course to take at this time

Worst professor I have ever had at UW. I had very high expectations for the class yet am incredibly disappointed. His class has no organization and he is impossible to follow along with. His only opinions are correct and he often invalidates student's opinions. In personal interactions, I found him rude and not caring.

Class lectures were mostly the professor talking about his political beliefs and had nothing to do with the readings or class content. If you don't hold the same beliefs as or analyze texts in THE EXACT SAME WAY as the professor, prepare to get a bad grade (as was my case).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is very accessible and care a lot.

His class was disorganized and unrefined. His heart doesn't seem into it and he showed up to class with 0 preparation. Despite being a class that begs for original critical thinking skills, he expects you to parrot and repeat his ideas. "Discussion" is illusory and used as a catalyst for him to lecture. Least favorite prof I've had in 3 yrs @ UW
Really taught me new ways to think and watch movies. Not a lot of pressure and the atmosphere is very friendly. Open to opposing points of view as well
Very open-minded and always lets you rewrite to improve.
I don't get to take a lot of these kinds of courses, so they have to be good.  This exceeded my expectations.
great class  plain and simple
the best experience in the UW classroom .  only complaint:  he gives students too much time to explain ideas that really aren't relevant.
Always willing to give you a second chance and really cares.

Took European Jewish Literature from him and adored the readings. He is baffling at times and seems a little buried in theory (Marx and Freud occupied us for weeks) but there is deep emotion and desire to connect with his students, and if you aren't precisely sure if you connect to the reading the same way he does, he still listens
He has a way of simplifying very difficult ideas and helping you work with the text to start figuring it out.  Sometimes, it is a bit above me head, but he always has patience.

I found his explanations to be very clear. He emphasizes certain things so definitely show up to class and take notes. IMO doing the readings aren't super important, just be sure to listen to what he will say about them. The bi-weekly quizzes are easy if you review. Usually there are only 4-5 short answer questions. He also makes funny comments.
The most thought provoking course to date. the discussions were awesome.
the only professor I have had who really helped me with my writing.  He really worked with us to get us thinking critically.

I didn't really know what to expect from this class, I took it randomly. It turned out that I actually kinda liked it. Lectures were always really interesting. Not much homework really. You listen to the interesting things Professor Block has to say, watch films about the Holocaust and talk about them in class, the books we read pretty good too.

Took Holocaust and Film with him. Be prepared to make your case if you want to share your opinion with him. He is open to opinions, but if you want a good grade, then write whatever he says and his opinions. Not much work is asked of you, but exams are difficult. Interesting discussions of the films and topics though.
very interesting discussions, best so far.

When I signed up for Environmental Literature, I expected a class that discussed... environmental literature. His class was boring and focused on literary devices and stuff like that... Not the course I was wanting. It was his first time, so I'll cut some slack, and the grading was easy. But I did not enjoy the class.

Took a queer theory/german lit class. Gave very interesting analyses, but makes unsubstantiated logical jumps and is slightly egotistical. Easy grader by repeating his ideas in your papers. Overall, fun enough class.
Good lecturer. Quizes easy. Smoking hot TA
smart and kind. one of my favorite classes of all time.

Took a lit/germanic studies class from him. Very knowledgable but if you don't think the exact way he does, it is very difficult to succeed in this class. He tries to help but is sometimes unclear in his suggestions. He often makes harsh political jokes during lecture, which are distracting and irrelevant to the class.
great prof!
awesome!

Hands down: favorite professor.  Block is exceedingly intelligent, funny, sarcastic, & keeps lectures interesting. When he sees you make an honest effort, he WILL make sure your grade reflects it.  Had him twice and loved both classes. Teaches large lectures but encourages participation, loves to get feedback, and loves debate. Highly recommend.
best class so far!

Cool professor and class. Participation points for attendance. Had in depth analysis for each film. Essays were you reiterating/expanding on his analysis (not creating your own analysis) and you got a good grade if you did so. Was laid back and responsive to student feedback. I would take another class by Block.

I feel very conflicted when it comes to Prof. Block. On the one hand, he is very interesting to listen to and is obviously extremely intelligent. On the other hand, he can come off as arrogant and uninterested, often making fun of students or calling their work "crap." :/
Great sense of humor, very interesting lectures
one of the best at the u.  difficult topics but you are rewarded for thinking critically.
the best and fairest prof. i have had.
great sense of humor.  very intelligent and nice

Amazing lecturer. He has the ability to keep several different threads of conversation going and tie them all neatly up at the end. Attendance definitely mandatory--he uses the texts as jumping off points, but there's no way to do well on essays or quizzes without knowing lecture material. Great prof, hope to have him again sometime.
good sense of humor.  generous grader
No Comments
I really enjoyed his class!
No Comments
Very disorganized and bad at communicated expectations clearly. Lectures aren't helpful and expects students to watch long pre-lecture videos.
Disorganized class, Lecture is basically from the past quarter. He forgets to announce things. For example, he posted midterm specifications 3 days before test day.

Very disorganized class, writes lab specs the week that they're meant to be released, so when they're actually released they're full of mistakes/tasks that we can't do simply because they're not possible. Lab specs change as we work on them so the requirements are always changing. His lectures are the same, he learns as he goes leaving us confused.
Not a very hard course. Grades are good for most students.

He's rude, not reasonable. If you debate with him about grading and even if you have good reasonings, he will just pay defensive and be like "well, I guess we have a disagreement." He's the worst jackass professor you will ever see in UW

Be prepared to be on your own during the whole 10 credit course. The professor probably knows a lot but since there are no lectures being conducted (only sporadic checkins and milestone presentations), you won't get much knowledge from this kind of teaching. When asking tough questions, you'll get redirects and no answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Hannaford teaches 447 without a lab which I think made the class a lot less interesting. Most of the stuff we learned didn't have too much application in my opinion and the Sci-lab stuff was just absolutely ridiculous. In the end the average grade in the class was a 3.7-3.8 and he had to curve down because too many people would have gotten 4.0s.
One of the greatest teachers at UW!!!

Professor Hannaford is a great instructor. His examples were fascinating and came from years of experience in the field. His coverage of the extremely diverse materials in Robotics was rigorous despite the high volume of information. The book we used aside from Craig filled in all the gaps Craig leaves out. I got much more than my money's worth.
He is the greatest EE professor ever. He is really good at teaching. Also, he's hot!

I took his Financial Accounting class at Oregon State University. He's a really fun & funny guy who you can tell is a good lecturer. there's a fair amount of homework but there's 2 midterms and 1 final which are very difficult. But, if you do better on the final, he will replace your midterm(s) grades with it which is nice.
Hardest class I took at UW. I wish he went at a slower pace, but I learned a lot. One of my favorite profs, he really cares about his students.
Good guy
LOVED this class. He relates everything you do back to the stock market or investment decisions, which is a bit different than other accounting profs. He is one of the best!
Terry was great. He really cares about his students. Even long after the course was over he found time to mentor me. Definitely take 301 with him!

Great professor. Goes off topic sometimes, but lectures are interesting (for accounting) and he really cares about his students. If you don't come ready to work, you will be miserable. If you show up and put in the effort he bends over backwards to help you.
Blackburnes awesome. Im a finance major, and almost switched to accounting because of this course. If youre a finance major, take Blackburne!
He is not clear at explaining concepts. Most of the time I was confused during the class. Final exam was too hard.

Blackburne has potential. He seems like he is doing his best. However, he doesn't seem confident in his knowledge or his ability to teach. He rushes through slides. Spends more time talking about accounting principles (which he seems to know more of) than teaching actual problems. He doesn't answer questions fully in class. Expect to teach yourself
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: You're going to have to work hard, but I probably learned more in this class than any other I've taken at Foster. I didn't appreciate all the work he made us do at the time, but you'll leave his class with a solid foundation. Blackburne really cares if you learn the material and will you remember you long after the course is over.
Terrence is a good lecturer. I learned a lot. You do need to spend considerable time at home doing problems to succeed. Pre-read the chapters and do all of the suggested problems to get a 4.0.

Midterm, two group cases, one writing assignment, and final exam. Go to class! You don't need to read the textbook because his lectures are enough for what you need to know to prepare for the midterm and final. Do ALL the suggested hw problems because his exam questions are very similar to the hw questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Blackburne is one of my favorite professors that I have had at UW. He is very knowledgeable and super approachable outside of the classroom, always eager to talk about real-world accounting. The class may be one of the more difficult, as it is a "weed out" class; however, if you put in the time to read and engage in the work, Terry is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Blackburne did a great job navigating through the material. My only regret was not going to office hours earlier in the quarter. Although the course is difficult, he is very helpful and enthusiastic about teaching. Make sure to do all the suggested homework problems THROUGHOUT the quarter. Also purchase the hard copy book and coursepack!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This was my first UW professor after transferring from CC and could not believe the drop in teaching ability and quality - very disappointing. Multiple lessons were spent fixing mistakes of prior lessons. "I'm not an accountant" was used dozens of times. Office hours? Right.  Switched majors after this course and thank god every night for it.

He was a pretty average professor. When a student asked a question and he did not know the answer, he would make the excuse that he is "not an accountant, I'm a financial economist" which was annoying. He is a newer professor and his class was very disorganized. He isn't the worst teacher, but he definitely doesn't deserve such a high rating

Good professor. Lectures are interesting (for accounting), and Blackburne seems to take a genuine interest in his students. Even though the class was a bit disorganized he's relatively new. I think he'll only get better over time. Overall I'd highly recommend this class.

Amazing professor! Super energized and funny, and really likes accounting! Also, very helpful and generous for partial credit. Exams are tough, but that's because accounting is just hard. Definitely take 301 with Terrence!

Terrence is one of my favorite professors at the UW! He was very engaged in his teaching and guides you through problems. He is more then happy to help you if you need extra help, and he really appreciates class participation. Whatever you do, make sure you participate in his class!

Professor Blackburne is extremely cocky and quite arrogant. He talks about his white house job and how he quit to learn accounting. His lectures are quite dull, requiring you to bring printouts every class. He doesn't upload a single assignment grade online, so it's difficult to gauge how you're doing in the class. If possible, avoid this prof!

Professor Blackburne is an amazing professor! He really does care if you learn and is eager to give more examples if you don't understand. His office hours are helpful, and his lectures are informative enough that reading isn't entirely necessary.

Easygoing and approachable. His lectures were clear and discussions were fun. No group project when I took the class. While exams were somewhat challenging (no surprise given it's Foster) , he is VERY generous with his grading. Only complaint is that he never got our assignments back to us, so I had no idea how I was doing. Otherwise good class.

Professor Blinov did a perfectly fine job with physics 324. I'm pretty sure its standard protocol for professors teaching 321-325 to lecture straight from Griffith's textbooks. I have found reading the text during lectures to be useful. Homework was fair and Mathematica made them a piece of cake. Take home tests were also fairly easy.

Truly the worst class that I have had to take online during the pandemic. Blinov gets a single point from me due to him being funny and I'm sure an enjoyable person to talk to, but his lectures were actual garbage. If you want to laugh every now and then while gaining any deeper insight to the material, Blinov is the man for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Blinov is a funny guy and a decent lecturer. The curriculum for the class left much to be desired though. Little to no overlap between tutorial/lecture content (same deal for tutorial sessions/HW and lecture sessions/HW). Exams were graded very harshly and partial credit was very scarce. Definitely seek out extra help for this class if needed!
Simply the best physics professor at UW. Fair papers and grading criteria. If you're reading this Boris, you're a god-sent.

The students grading him poorly seem to dislike the physics sequence, not this prof. He was fine. He explained concepts well and was great in office hours. There isn't enough lecture time to fully explain the 'equation' side of Physics. To get a full understanding, you have to read the book before and solidify your understanding in lecture.

Blinov only covers the concepts, and barely touches the surface. He covered the concepts of LRC circuits in the last lecture of the quarter and there were 5 LRC questions on the final. I suggest you watch Khan Academy and MIT open courses to study ahead of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Can't answer student questions typically, especially ones relating to math. Teaches concepts, but not how to actually do problems, even though the exams focus primarily on math. Nice guy, horrible teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Boring lecturer, just regurgitates the textbook in the form of slides in a way that no one actually learns anything from his slides. Tries to make stupid jokes about java updates, which are soo awk. Always says "this is quantitative" or "this is quantitative." He makes you go crazy, and then when another prof makes the tests, you're screwed.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Boris focuses primarily on physics concepts, rather than math, and teaches straight from the textbook. Unfortunately, his style of teaching is often confusing for the average student, and the tests do include the math that he does not teach. Be prepared to do quite a bit of outside studying if you have him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: The only saving grace of Boris' teaching style is that he has a good sense of humor. Otherwise, he teaches directly from the textbook so be prepared to enlist in external sources for help or you will regret taking physics with him. He is unprepared for review sessions as he only decided to do "easy" problems from the review material.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I'm not usually one to write rave reviews of my professors, but Blinov is of a caliber that makes him an exception. He is an incredibly talented teacher and focuses mainly on the conceptual side of physics than the algebraic side, and is always there for help. If you are reading this and considering his class, close the page and go sign up.

Like all classes, come to class prepared. Look over examples in the textbook, do some practice problems, do all HW, and make sure you understand the topic by the end of the day. I didn't do any of the things I mentioned consistently and my grade didn't turn out great, but that doesn't mean he wasn't a good teacher.

He's a laid back professor with a sense of humor. I barely read the book. If you do the online homework and practice exam questions, you'll do just fine on the exams since he recycles a lot of the same questions. He curves the class average to a 3.2, which is high for UW. I passed with a decent grade and I don't even know anything about physics!

Boris is great, physics 123, not so much. I think Boris did a really good job of explaining simple concepts, however he worked very few examples in class. His tests were also really hard. I think the best way to succeed in this class is to make sure you understand the homework and take good notes in class. Good luck!

He might be a good human but teaches crap. He takes summer quarter too lightly as far as teaching is concerned but his mid-term was unfair and gave something that was not spoken about in class or in homework. Overall he is horrible!

Prior to taking this class with Boris I was dreading physics, but it quickly became one of my favorite classes. To anyone who needs to take it I highly recommend Boris, his MC questions are very fair, and he curves the class to around  3.2! Also is just an all around nice guy. Worst part is that going to 115 is gonna be a real drag now

Professor Blinov is engaging, intelligent, and totally charming. I expected to hate this class, but he made the material easy to understand and kept lectures interesting with real world applications of the concepts and plenty of demos.  Made me wish I had majored in physics!!
Great professor. Fair tests. Study the practice problems he gives. People scared me going into physics saying it was hard at UW but with boris its not bad at all. Highly recommend him.

If you dno'tunderstand physics, take Boris. I do not understand physics AT ALL and I got a 3.9. Show up to class (he basically teaches out of the book, so if you're confused do book problems) because it's great clarification. Do the practice problems!! Our final had 75% of the exact questions from the practice exam. Put in effort and you'll do well

Best physics prof ever! He was a little boring sometimes, and I honestly found the book more helpful, but he's a nice guy. Curved class grade really high, which helped me big time. Never thought physics could be a GPA booster. Also, exam questions were mainly conceptual and easy to follow.

His lectures are pretty useless, I only went to 9 lectures all quarter because I realize the book is way better. BUT he is super nice, super easy on exams, thus it is easy to get a good grade, because for some odd reason he curved the class to a 3.2? o hw, do practice problems and the exams will be a breeze.

Blinov is not a bad professor, I just hate physics, so it didn't come easy to me. My favorite days are when he did demos, he honestly is the funniest guy! Lectures were boring sometimes, but he tried to make the tests easier and easier each time! Curved the section to a 3.2, he really wants us to do well in his class! I'll miss this guy

Really engaging professor. He asked the class after every exam what he could do to help us learn better. Do the homework, do the practice problems you should do well in the class. Sometimes he puts problems he goes over in class on the exam, verbatim. He curved my section to a 3.2. Good guy.
He knows the material well, but he isn't very good at teaching. He will vaguely introduce the concepts in class and breeze through a few examples without any explanations.

Boris is a solid professor, definitely recommend him. He offers clear explanations, has engaging presentations, and does not rely too heavily on a textbook. His workload is just right, even with the long term paper. Cool Russian accent to boot.

This class was the worst I have ever taken and this was because of Blinov.  If you want to attend the most boring class that should be taught to 5th graders do not sign up.  I dreaded going to class but the clicker questions made it so you had to go. I got a very good grade in this class but I hated every second of every class that I went to.

Most of you will be very familiar with the material that's covered in this. Because it's not much new information, you still need to go to class for clicker points. The lengthy research paper due at the end is very time consuming but doable. Plenty of chances for extra credit offered for the paper.

This class was a cakewalk compared to most classes at UW! I got a 4.0 and I barely put forth any effort, but at the same time I enjoyed going to class because it was still interesting!  Blinov cares more about the material than the grades! I highly recommend this class if you are looking for a NW credit that is relatively stress free!

This class was very easy, however, I can't say it was all that interesting. I suppose it would be more fascinating to someone who had absolutely no physics background, but I already knew about most of the topics and only showed up for clicker questions. Take this class if you know nothing about physics, or if you just want an easy A.

Prof. Blinov's "Physics for Liberal arts majors" is pretty much just a non-mathematical version of the year long physics series at the UW. You will get students criticizing you for taking "physics for poets," but the class overall has some interesting topics,and Blinov covers them fine. Can get a little boring at times, but show up for clicker Q's

For some reason "for liberal arts majors" translates to "as boring and impersonal a class as we can possibly create." Blinov was fine, but the material was sandpaper dry. Very easy A - I stopped showing up to class, finished with a 35% clicker grade, and somehow managed a 3.8. But I'm still trying to find an INTERESTING science class for non-majors

Fun and funny teacher! Excellent course if you're looking to get a general overview on Physics, which I was. IMO it was an easy A since he drops your worst pop quiz scores and takes the best 1 out of 2 midterm scores. The hardest part was the final paper, which was 5-10 pages on whatever you feel like within the physics realm, which wasn't hard.

He seemed pretty bored with the class - I don't blame him - but was overall a decent professor. Very funny, doesn't take the class too seriously, makes fun of his own accent. I had some trouble getting help from him when I needed it, but he eventually came through. Also: pretty foxy.

Probably the best professor in UW physics department. The best thing about Blinov is that he actually sets the average GPA pretty high (3.0 for me, compared to 2.6~2.7 from other professor) that actually makes a huge difference in your GPA! His tests can be easy since it is concept based. Just do all your work, and you should be more than okay.

Great professors. Didn't expect my grade to be so high.Cares more about concepts than about plugging numbers into equations. Also tells pretty funny jokes! A plus in the physics series which is otherwise pretty boring.

He is the best professor I've had at UW so far. Physics isn't all that interesting to me, but he made me genuinely want to learn. He's hilarious and doesn't take his class too seriously, but still manages to teach incredibly well. I had to use my book everyday in 121; with Boris, I only needed it for the handy list of equations.

Took both 121 and 122 from blinov, he gives extra credit on exams just for making an equation sheet. If you make a real good one you could get 8 to 10 points, even only 5 pnts is an extra 5% on the test, which can be the difference between a 3 and a 3.5 on a test. 14% percent of both classes got 4.0 (instead of the normal 8%).

Blinov, put simply, was the one saving grace of the 12x series, which otherwise was horribly disorganized and terribly coordinated. He's enthusiastic without being excessive - the demos are quite engaging, and he's got a quirky sense of humor (long live the Russian Banana Potato!). Exams are difficult, but relatively straightforward.

Took Pedigo for 121 and Blinov for 122. Trust me, Blinov is wayy easier than Pedigo!! His tests are more conceptual and with easier calculations. Some problems can be solved only by plugging into the equations. His lectures in 122, though, are sometimes unclear. But I still suggest to take his class especially if physics isn't your forte

Good teacher. Personally I hated physics before I took this class but Blinov made it very interesting. Lecture is worth going to, even if only to see the teacher. The tests are all pretty standard  tests and the homework is out of the book.  Great class.

One of the most difficult classes I've ever taken, but mostly because of the WebAssign homework. The class was difficult to follow at first, but the lecture became increasingly interesting, clear, and amusing. Blinov's demonstrations are especially engaging.
Good teacher, Really nice guy, and pretty straight foreword tests. I would recommend taking him,just keep up with the assigned reading and start the homework well before it's due.
I really like this professor. His tests are straightforward- there aren't any "trick" questions and he does a good job of explaining things during class (lectures are actually interesting, too).

Not a bad class at all, grades on a curve, the mean is 2.7, so if you are in a smart section, the curve might actually hurt you.  Lots of practice material provided, and attend class, since most of what is important will be covered in class. There are also clicker questions almost every class period. Read the book too, cuz that certainly helped.
Best prof I've had in the Physics series; no BS just does his job. Exams are straightforward and he gives plenty of practice exam material. Lectures are concise and relevant to material.

I took MATH 525 with Bobby in spring 2025. MATH 524 (with Bube) was perfectly fine but Bobby made the series impossible to take. He is very smart but not a great lecturer, he is bad at explaining and his handwriting is illegible. Tests are unreasonably hard. Me and 2 other friends all ended up dropping the class.

Lectures are from the textbook verbatim, homework is often unrelated to lecture material and seem to be testing how well you understand things rather than helping students gain understanding. Strangely, midterms were much easier, though how well we did on said midterm remains a mystery due to grades still not being out by the final week of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Wilson is an insanely intelligent mathematician and a poor teacher. He has such a clear familiarity with the material that he forgets that students don't. Lectures are recited from the book, homework is never motivated and frequently on concepts from the book he hasn't taught. Tests are at least simple enough. It's a frustrating experience.
unapproachable, just recites the textbook verbatim, no test materials whatsoever. Difficult class made more difficult for no reason.

Bobby Wilson is a very good professor who actually cares about the content of the class. He does not provide test prep material, but the homeworks and lectures are engaging, and if you pay attention in class the tests are much easier than the homeworks. Overall would take again.

He is the worst prof I have ever had. Don't take him. He:
-Blatantly lied to us that a topic wouldn't be on the midterm (I asked twice, it was 25% of the test)
-Refuses to give study material for tests
-Gives test questions that do not resemble homework/lecture
-Is awful at explaining things
-Homework is so hard, the TA couldn't do it
-SO much more

Took Wilson Autumn Q 2023. He assumes the class has a background in calculus from HS, so he flies through examples. His lectures are fast paced/confusing/bad, my TA was better at explaining the concepts. If you need to take the Calc series just take it at Everett CC. The profs care more & are better teachers. 2.3ed 124 at UW & 4.0 125 at Everett.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I was good at IB HL Math in high school but barely passed this class. Lectures are so awful he rushed through content. No extensions at all, unlike every other 124 professor. Such long assignments, sometimes 3 due on the same day. Worst professor I've ever had, TA was pretty unhelpful too. We had to do the quizzes before learning content on there
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Wilson is easy on grading and his tests were not difficult at all. But will only recommend him if you have taken AP Calc in high school because he doesn't have the best lectures.

Prof gives a lot of homework, makes it difficult to keep pace in class. The teaching itself is decent, but not particularly engaging. The ta's are often more helpful, would highly recommend approaching them instead. Overall, decent prof, but not my best experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He definitely is a smart guy but not great at teaching. Way too much homework that never aligns with the lessons (way harder than the midterms too so not helpful). Classes were unengaging and did not explain anything at all. I even took calc in high school and I feel bad for anyone who didn't. Quizzes were usually easy.

He goes over very basic concepts in lectures and the homework in much harder. I took calc in high school before this and that was the only way I understood. Would not recommend for people new to calc. TAs are useful in explaining the confusing homework problems. There is also a big curve- I ended with an 81 but GPA was 3.4 (median has to be 3.0).

Seems nice but lectures were dull (mostly proofs ans textbook readings) and he didn't do as much as other profs in terms of supplemental materials and review. He often didn't finish lectures because he spent time writing the proofs, so if you like examples you'll have to find other resources not included in the class.

Very difficult to follow unless you have taken calculus before. Professor does not know how to teach new topics without heavily relying on theories and proofs, and didn't teach a lot of skill applications. The homework is significantly more difficult than the materials used during lecture. Quizzes and tests are simpler than the homework though.

He rushes through lectures and doesn't give you much time to learn the material. He also assigns a lot of homework specifically on WebAssign, which doesn't tell you why your answers are wrong or give any feedback on how to do it right. My TA did all of the teaching in this class and it was generally poorly structured and guided.

reviews.comment: Wilson is very unapproachable and not nice. He is not a good lecturer either. At OH, he has this disconnected bored attitude with you. During lectures, he just recites the textbook, never adds anything new or insightful to the concepts. I've asked several questions during class and OH, and he'd return recitations of the textbook, had to self-teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Decent professor. Won't blow your mind with intuitive and mainstreamed methods to learn and digest Calculus super easily, however he did teach decently well. As long as you pay attention in lecture, read the book, do hw regularly, and do a couple book practice problems, you can expect a grade >B+

Prof. Wilson is a great guy! The only complaints I had were that he was too pedantic and slow in his live lectures, but always answered every question that popped up in the zoom chat. He is clear about deadlines, tests and homework and is a very approachable and friendly person.

Professor Wilson is a great professor. He is very professional. His exams are not that tough and if you attend his lectures and study from his lecture notes you'll be fine. However if you're taking the class remotely, be mindful that the final exam will be lengthy. Don't expect him to be super friendly, but overall he is a really good professor.

Do not take this class if you haven't taken calculus before. I got an A in AP Calc in high school and this class was WAY harder. The homework , quizzes, and exams were much more difficult than the lectures/worksheets. I basically had to rely on my high school notes and teach myself.

Lectures can be hard to understand but the overall grade is made up of a lot of things meaning that the midterms + final aren't going to determine entirely you're grade. Tests are easier to understand and get through than what he teaches in class/has on WebAssign which is really nice, and the structure of the class is really straightforward
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I dropped this class because we had webassign quizzes every week - not like other 124 classes. His lectures are all over the place and it was hard to grasp concepts. This class is VERY test heavy with lots of HW that are WAY harder than the stuff he teaches in class. Would not recommend if you have not taken calculus before.

Professor Wilson is probably one of the better professors in the Math (calculus specifically) department. His lectures are straight-forward, but he does not go into much explanation. If you have trouble with math, you might want to do extra learning like reading the textbook, Khan Academy, or go to tutoring. Choosing a good TA really makes it too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I really like Professor Wilson, he is super real and a great guy. Sometimes his style of lecturing is a little confusing and it can be easy to get lost, but the tests and grading style always feels very fair. Would recommend!
His lectures are very clear and he hits all the information that you'll need. If you go to lecture and read along in the textbook there's no reason not to do well.
I mean hes okay. You can tell hes newer to being a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is an incredible lecturer, only did examples on the whiteboard which can be a positive or a negative depending on your learning style. One of the most real professors at UW.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Bad at teaching, moves through material very quickly, does not wait for questions, explains nothing. Avoid.

Ivana takes much effort in preparing the course and it was very helpful. The content is a bit too much (~ 2 to 3 times of a common course), and she didn't provide clear guides for the final, so it was really struggling during the final week. We were allowed to bring a cheat sheet but it was not helpful at all! The grading is nice though.

Professor Bozic was super enjoyable for stochastics. The class is well positioned to give an intro to measure theoretic probability, while still keeping the material grounded in application. The lectures were clear, the grading criteria was incredibly straight forward, and she was incredibly kind!

Course started out pretty straightforward, got gradually more difficult. Based on 3 books, especially on Matt Lorig's course notes. Lectures were mostly just her reading off slides - which were taken straight from the book - and writing up some proofs and formulas. She's friendly. TA office hours were helpful for HW questions, her OH not so much
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This course was straightforward. Powerpoint lectures. Homework was mostly straightforward and short (4 questions, the majority of which were pure computation). Prof. Bozic seems very nice, although I didn't go to her OH at any point. We did get to watch a few videos in class towards the end of the quarter, which made the material seem more fun.

Overall I was incredibly disappointed in this class because it felt disorganized and did not effectively address techniques for solving differential equations nor implement Matlab. The homework was overly rigorous and the process for submitting was ridiculous. Also, the tests were too long for class and written as though for a weed-out class.

reviews.comment: 50% Homework and 50% test. Class is categorized as AMATH but have not touched MATLAB once. After finishing all of MATH 307 material (Diff eq) moved onto non 307 related topics.

reviews.comment: Very hard class. Homework isn't that bad, but tests are incredibly difficult. Also, going to class is next to pointless because she just copies notes onto the board.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Doesn't post notes or homework solutions, grades homework too harshly, tests are too long to finish. No organization, I have no idea what she is going to lecture about before I get to class, and she doesn't post notes, so I am left trying to speed write her notes, but unfortunately she stands in font of the board while she is writing.

Ridiculous amount of homework and content for a three credit class. Not flexible at all for late work despite giving a ton of work. Additionally, she grades the homework very harshly and doesn't care about the student. Dont take this class with her
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ridiculous amount of work. Class is supposed to be Applied Mathematics as the name implies but didn't touch MATLAB once. Lectures are very monotone and content is rushed.

reviews.comment: Lectures by reading off of a script and writing formulas without explaining them. No late work accepted, not even for extreme reasons. Homework is ridiculously difficult compared to examples in class, and the material is so rushed that you're going to have to learn on your own. Does not respect students, or allow many questions during lecture.
