reviews.comment: my goat tbh

Fave class i've taken at UW. Every class followed a similar structure so you always know what to expect, but despite that, you get a chance to explore a wide range of materials and topics. It really lends itself to getting to learn what you want to learn, within the context of the class ofc. Prof Belic is a fun and informative lecturer. Easy 4.0

This class was awesome! I loved Bojan because he cared about everyone in the class. This class was super fun and somewhat easy, just get ready to memorize a bunch of material. The final was worth 30%, but you just explain what you learned in the class. Quizzes(40%), Participation(10%), and Report(easy 20%). Overall, an amazing class and person!

Hes the funniest professor & shows up with jokes everytime. Hes super lively & his class was the highlight of my day everytime I went. He would even call us out if we didnt wave when he walked in lol. There are quizzes to take every class, but theyre easy & short. They all have a pattern, so youll know what to expect. Fun lectures. Easy A!

Bojan is a hilarious professor! There are daily quizzes and daily reports that make up a significant chunk of your grade, but once you realize the pattern for the quizzes/reports they're super easy. Lectures are long but informative. 10/10 class!
Bojan's class is never boring. Probably one of the most passionate professors I've ever encountered
Bojan is truly one of a kind. Hilarious lectures and genuinely interesting content. If you need an easy and fun class to take I would strongly recommend Slavic 101!

Bojan is an amazing person. He plans out his PowerPoint and times the animations LOL. He is super funny and you can joke with him all class. The lectures are 2 hours so sometimes I get a little sleepy but that is a personal problem. If you pay attention in class and realize the pattern for mini-quizzes it isn't hard at all. I definitely recommend!!

This class was very easy, easy 4.0. Bojan is super fun and engaging though his lectures drag on a little bit. Homework is very easy and kind of fun. I'd love to take a class with him again. Make sure to engage in class and he'll joke around with you!

jointly offered with SLAVIC370/570, LING 480, CHID498C. 2 take home projects (100pts each), 1 final (exam or paper depending on which credit you're taking it for, 100pts). definitely a class where you get as much as you put in. Prof will not go out of his way to offer extra guidance even though his instructions are minimal at best. but easy grader!

- gives poor feedback x1000000 - unclear grading criteria - funny/snarky, likes to joke - easy points through canvas (graded on completion) - easy grader, but again, poor feedback (literally "? -1" is how he grades papers) - this class is foreign language heavy so if that's gonna throw you off I don't recommend. he translates ofc.

Great professor, really passionate about what he teaches. He has a big personality and really takes the time to be a good lecturer and to actually discuss topics in class with the students. I got to know him on a name to name basis because his classes are very small. It was my favorite class, cant wait to take another he teaches.
Easy class, as long as you show up and pay attention you'll do great. Prof was 10/10, lots of banter and he is the dunkmaster ��

homework assigned everyday. 3 midterms and final including oral exams. the teacher is nice but will lose his mind if you take out your phone. likes to make jokes throughout quarter, but is a good teacher. would reccomend for Russian 101
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amazing lectures to be a part of. He's easily one of my favorite professors! He was enthusiastic about his students and the material. Made the class super fun with his sarcastic and sassy attitude. Just be ready to banter with the teacher - he loves to throw jokes around! Overall great (and easy) class - just study a tiny bit for tests and its good

Bojan is a really nice guy. I took all of his class in Freshmen year, including Slavic 101, 110 and 370. Those three courses are really different, but Bojan is so nice that I found all courses are fun and comprehensive. He is the best professor I have never had. Go take his course, he is so fun to learn from.

Really funny teacher. He will yell in Russian throughout the entire lecture (he usually doesn't speak English in class), which helped me remember the words and pronunciation. Although, sometimes it would have been nice if he explained things in English so the class as a whole was able to get a more thorough understanding of the material.
Don't take this class. If you want VLPA credits, you're better off taking communications, drama or art. This class is a complete waste of time and it decreases your GPA no matter how much you study.

He is an amazing teacher full of passion! He uses good and vivid lectures for students to memorize vocab in class. And he tells jokes in class. Super interesting and inspirational!! I would definitely take it again. And just study and do the homework everyday, it will be easy to get a 4.0.

Bojan is one of the best profs I have had at UW.  He knows what he is talking about and is a good language professor with an awesome sense of humor.  If you are taking a language try your hardest to get him because he doesn't teach lower level classes that often.  But beware- he HATES when people are late and will call you out.

I had limited knowledge of the Balkans and linguistics prior to attending Bojan Belic's class. Thankfully Bojan jokes throughout the lecture making the class very entertaining, while still addressing the main topics. Grading was very fair throughout the course. If you do the readings and attend class you will succeed. I highly recommend!

Bojan is absolutely one of the best language teachers out there. He's extremely helpful and thorough, but works hard to make class entertaining, humorous, and clear. For a language as challenging as BCS, this is essential! Can't recommend enough. Just make sure you're on time - the one thing there's no joke about is punctuality!

Bojan is passionate and engaging with a quirky sense of humour.The class was mostly in Russian yet it was easy to understand him because he's so good at getting ideas across.He can be very kind and patient,but there're class rules that you shouldn't even think about breaking.Also very helpful if you ever have questions/problems.Not to be missed!

Best language instructor I've ever had. I don't agree with the other raters who said he's difficult. The languages are difficult, but Bojan makes them very approachable and is a relatively easy grader. Probably the most efficient use of classroom time I've ever seen from any instructor I've seen across disciplines.
kinda quirky, but reasonable, just don't argue with or accuse him of anything, cause you can't win. recommended
He's pretty hot.

Bojan is an excellent teacher. He's engaging and hilarious, and at the same time he's serious and professional. He's easy to talk to, encourages everybody in class to participate, and makes my mornings a wonderful experience.
Bojan is such a character!  My day is much improved after I attend his class...HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!!

The class was pretty funny at the beginning. 2 weeks into it, I started hating the class. He's too psm-y. Take a midol dude. He yelled at the class for not understanding concepts and made a big deal out of little things. He has a vein on his forehead that bulges every time he gets mad... He'll go off on you for no reason.
Bojan was very entertaining, but still managed to teach us very well.

Dynamic, charismatic, passionate & committed, great sense of humor.  Great at teaching difficult concepts with clear explanations.  Gives us sufficient work to learn the concept, but not "busy work."  Tests very challenging but push us to use everything we have learned.

Dr.Zhao is very passionate about GIS. I took 360 with him, and as someone who usually shies away from any data/software-heavy classes, I felt like the material was very approachable and interesting. The one thing I will say, sometimes the lectures can be droll and you can use the slides on your own if you don't have the attention span.
I was praying to jesus that he was a good professor, he made me lose faith in the lord.

Bo's a very organized teacher who lays out a clear structure for the class and maintains it. The assignments are easy enough if you go to lecture. Overall, probably my favorite teacher in the geography department due to being such a kind and caring guy. Try to get to know him.

Really enjoyed this class. I had some HTML/CSS/JavaScript experience beforehand but this class doesn't require too much previous web design knowledge - the focus is more on leveraging web design tools to answer geographical questions. Would recommend taking the class with Prof. Zhao whenever it's offered, he did a great job and is very passionate.
Lecture matches the textbook pretty well, and the lectures are clear and helpful, sometimes providing additional content not in the textbook. Overall, it was a great experience and good intro course.

Class is just hard but not necessary his fault, but the lectures are not really helpful, and uses Pearson to conduct all his homework which is never good as it is impersonal and contrary to what it claims does not help in learning at all. He's overall fine but just bad class structure to teach hard concepts.

The professor seems nice but there is a discontinuity between the difficulty of class problems and those on hw, labs, and tests. He teaches concepts on a shallow level and then will test you on your ability to do advanced problems. Unreasonable expectations, boring lectures, and overall just not a good experience. He was decent in office hours.
Respected

Karl is definitely attempts to make sure lectures are informative, but they fail to be adequate enough for the class. The tests were unreasonably difficult for no reason. Homework is also on Pearson which is just a bad platform to host assignments on. There was a difficulty mismatch between the problems taught in lecture and in hw, lab, and tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, gives several examples of concepts during lecture, and is very available for questions. Exams are difficult but doable, and grading is pretty generous. Also just a very kind and caring teacher who wants the best for his students! Would highly recommend.

His lectures are good and he's also really really nice. The exams are hard but that's not really his fault. My only issue is that on the mylab/mastering homework you lose 10% of the question points every time you miss an attempt. I think this is really stupid b/c you're obviously gonna make mistakes as you're learning new content.

class was online at times but moved back to in person. He is an okay lecturer but his lectures are very fast and not descriptive. He will just put numbers on the screen and not go into how we get them sometimes. Skips steps a lot. Also likes to have labs be done the same week as midterm while assigning heavy homework on top of that.
One of the better professors if you actually want to learn and are not just looking to earn an easy grade.
Lectures are clear and concise, and lab help solidify concepts. He really cares about his students. Couldn't have asked for a better professor.

Lecture are excellent compared with most other. Slides give a clear outline of the material, which his commentary enhances. The class gives a comprehensive overview of MEMS processing. Four difficult homeworks, 1 midterm, and a final project (MEMS device design). He speaks with a german accent but is very easy to understand unlike many engr profs

Really good solid professor. Has informative lecture slides and teaches very straightforward and clear so that you can understand. His class was the only one that I never missed. He puts up all his past tests for practice and his homework is hard but if you do the homework well as well as the labs then it'll be good.
Awesome teacher, knows his stuff, and cares about his students.
Challenging homework requires some serious preparation and studying. But then, one also learn a lot from the class and from further investigation! Highly recommended for those who like to learn.

This professor seems to be a nice person, but is a horrible teacher. His lectures cover some of the most basic examples of a concept, yet the labs and homework are much more advanced. In many cases there are no examples to be found in the book or from lecture that come close to his assignments. He doesn't seem to put effort into teaching at all
Really good professor, although really busy.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
good lab
Prof. Bounds is incredibly nice and respectful of her students. There is a lot of busywork, but it's pretty straightforward.

This class is heavier on the reading but it goes by pretty quick. The class is really a play analysis class and can feel more like an english class with a theatre focus. I enjoyed it but do not take it if you do not like reading plays. Mackenzie is good and teaches well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: You def read a lot, but she warns you about that at the beginning of class. The plays are not boring, they are actually interesting & you learn a lot in a few weeks. she clearly cares about students & seems passionate which is always nice..I like that she is straight-up about expectations but also accommodating when stuff happens.
Attendance required field trip not listed anywhere on the syllabus, no mention until a week before... -_-

What does he even do? Has no office hours for help on homework, doesn't do lectures, and student posts on EdStem for help have 0 replies after weeks. The only teaching is through weekly 5-minute videos by a random Youtuber, paying thousands to attend here btw. Unfortunate since the class is interesting in concept.
Very average as a lecturer: sometimes interesting, sometimes not. Mostly this class felt like a retread of what I've learned in other natural resources classes. Meh overall.

How I wanted to like this class. I don't think it's his fault, Trevor has a brilliant way of explaining economic concepts in relatable and interesting ways. However, it's still economics taught for people predominantly interested in conservation. Rough start, but pretty good by the end. Study well for the exams, don't let multiple choice fool you.

Professor Branch was great. I had him for QSCI 482 which I was pretty worried about, but he made it interesting and easy to learn the material. I barely used the text book and mainly relied on his lecture notes for learning/studying. I would go out of my way to take a class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: McCoy is very nice and caring, but her lectures can be quite confusing. The HW and lab reports take forever to complete, and she is very strict on grading, but the Python isn't that bad. Beware that the midterms are extremely challenging (60% average, much harder than 145), but the content itself isn't as difficult. Utilize TAs and office hours.

MUCH harder than 145. Was told they get progressively easier and did find 65 to be the easiest but 55 HAUNTS me. Structured diff than 45/65 (MTs vs quizzes - but no python (!!!!)). It's obvious Prof McCoy cares a lot about chem, just found this class to be torture compared to 45/65. grade was not that diff bc crazy curve like 45 (4.0 vs 3.7)

Professor McCoy is deeply passionate about chemistry, and it's clear that she loves teaching chem 155. Her lectures are useful, but sometimes border on overly pedantic and confusing. The class is difficult, but there are resources provided to help.

I found this a little bit easier than 145, although I still got the same grade.

Long homework assignments, tedious labs, but McCoy's lectures made up for all of it. She gives just enough detail to get into the complexities of different topics, but not too much to the point that it feel irrelevant. Plenty of out-of-class help and decent clarity of expectations. Would recommend!

Great class to take if you hate yourself. Every single homework set I actively took mental damage from the content - she writes the most ontologically evil trick question problems ever and also doesn't show her work on the answer keys so if you don't know how to solve something you just have to scrounge and suffer like a worm upon scorched earth.

Couldn't understand her explanations in office hours most of the time. First few homework assignments were endlessly difficult and the exams felt like they were intentionally trying to throw me off. TAs were fun people though

Professor Mccoy explains things very clearly. Problem sets are hard and sometimes irrelevant to the exams, but they help with understanding the concepts. Labs are kind of boring. Exam difficulties are acceptable. I rarely get in-class poll questions correct, but thankfully they are not graded on accuracy.

McCoy is a friendly instructor, but the class was so problematic. Lectures felt very rushed and consisted of slides of dense theory with very few worked examples. Nearly every problem set had one or more errors. Lab rubrics were frustratingly vague. Exams contained trick questions and curveballs, and no partial credit was given. Glad to be done.

I thought CHEM 145 was terrible this year, but CHEM 155 was even worse. McCoy's exams/homework keys always had errors. The TAs didn't know what they were doing half the time. Lectures were never helpful. The homework took HOURS to complete. She always threw in curve balls or trick questions on midterms which messed up a lot of people.

Content itself is actually relatively straightforward. However, the grading is tough on lab reports, PowerPoints and lectures are both fast in terms of switching slides, but slow in terms of how quickly we move through material. It’s hard to get her to answer questions during class, and you will need to go to office hours to get them answered.

Insufferable. No resources, incorrect answer keys, defensive answering questions, unreadable powerpoints, completely useless lectures/office hours/quiz sections, class took more time than it was worth with labs and hw that didn't align with what was being "taught" in class. Never worked examples (likes theory/hates math). Inspired me to hate chem.

Dr. McCoy is a very caring professor who seems to really enjoy the content that she teaches and loves giving cool demos. Lectures are clear and understandable and she's always open to questions. Tests were very similar to the practice exams so as long as you did those you were good to go.

Although I felt her lectures were a bit confusing at times, she was happy to answer questions during office hours. I loved the many demos she prepared during lecture and she was always enthusiastic in my chem 153 class. The tests were fair and she was quite generous with the partial credit on short answer questions.
She's nice. I hate chem but she makes it fun sometimes with demos. Listen and practice and work a lot and you can pass :)

Dr. McCoy is such a passionate and amazing professor! She is super helpful and really cares about her students. Shes also accessible outside class and answers questions well. She likes to do cool demos, too. Overall, a great professor and class.

I had a pretty good experience in this class. Prof. McCoy was very accessible outside class and provided practice exams before every test. Her lectures were very comprehensive and included many demonstrations that were relevant to the material. Although the material was difficult, Prof. McCoy put in a lot of effort to help us understand it.

I had the 153 class with Professor McCoy. It combined the end of 152 and all of 162. At least for our class, she seemed to enjoy lecturing and positive all round. She is available outside of class and gave us practice exams for every exam. For the exams, make sure to do the practice and study the areas that are in red in her power points online.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had Dr. McCoy for Chem 153, which covers the second half of 152 and all of 162. It's a challenging class, but McCoy is very organized and her lectures are informative. It's also on Panopto so you don't have to attend class (although there is PollEverywhere). Go to office hours, that's the key to doing well - seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: It's as if she purposely makes her lectures esoteric. Us students are left scratching our heads and using KhanAcademy as a substitute. Her grading system is capricious and arbitrary as she set the grade lines at random numbers without statistical basis. Spent 20 minutes using confusing calculus to derive an equation, then said we don't  need it.

Lectures are very confusing with lots of errors and unnecessary demonstrations/information. She's also very unorganized and repeatedly posted grades incorrectly or very late and made lots of mistakes when writing exams.

Her focus on derivations in lecture is especially confusing when seeing material for the first time, so reading the text before lecture is necessary. Tests can be difficult.  She can be very helpful in office hours, though I attended few. Discussion worksheets are well designed and helpful. Do the suggested problems! Love her humor and laugh.

Lecture slides are disorganized and make it hard to take clear notes. Learning objectives are often unclear, clouded by unnecessary demos and information that is not useful to know for tests. Tests had low averages. Prepare for tests by doing challenging practice problems. It is most helpful to read the textbook and use lectures as a supplement.

Lectures aren't great, but office hours are amazing. Answers all questions and gives huge hints as to what are on the tests. Tests are highly conceptual, and are much easier than book problems. Get ready to read as they do help explain the more difficult concepts. She's very nice and funny and loves to help students. HW, not much. Would take again
Tests are difficult and she doesn't prepare you very well for them. Much more difficult than the practice worksheets she assigns in quiz section. Lectures are a must with clicker questions everyday.
Love her class, first midterm is pretty hard cuz I did nt prepare for it. But second midterms and final are incredably easy (got an A-) or something. Work hard, practice matter a lot in her class
Her tests were extremely hard and she wasn't the best at explaining concepts. She is very excited about the topics but things didn't come across very clear. Clicker questions every day!

Avoid. Got an easy 4.0 in Chem 142, but this was a completely different story. There were not very many questions on each midterm, so missing one question brought you down 0.2 gpa points, which is ridiculous. Take with someone else. Also there were so many typos on everything including the exams which made a tough class even harder.

Her tests were difficult, mostly because she was new this year and had no past exams to study from. The book problems didn't help because her questions were so different. Got progressively worse at lecturing as the quarter went on, she just took the book and condensed it. Her office hours were helpful and she was kinda sassy which I liked.

Lecture is extremely difficult to follow. There are constantly mistakes on her tests and lecture slides. I spent a good amount of time on her last midterm trying to figure out what the questions were  even asking. Do not recommend.

Her lectures are AWFUL. Although you have to go to get the participation points, she is terrible at explaining. In addition, her wording on tests is done in to try to trick you. The concepts in this class are hard enough without the smoke and mirrors act. Her class average dropped by almost 20% between the two midterms. Take with someone else.

The way she teaches is terrible. Also, her tests are ridiculously hard compared to the material given in the class and the quiz sections. If you take her be ready to put in a tremendous amount of effort. If you can take a different teacher!
If you want to hate chemistry, attend one of McCoy's classes.

She has clicker questions every class, and participation points for that, so go to class. She explains theory way more than she need sto and just confuses people. Go to her office hours, those are good. She makes tests way harder than she needs to, but it is all multiple choice.

Honestly, she's bad at explaining questions and problems, and she can't explain concepts well. Chem 152 is already a hard class, and she makes it harder than it needs to be. She likes being trick on the exam and her slides are confusing. My TA left in the middle of the quarter so my lab grades were inconsistent.

You never understand what she's talking about; it's not ENGLISH. Her slides are horrible, I really want to know who did them, extremely confusing and you don't know what she's trying to say. The TAs don't understand what's going on, and they admit it!

McCoy is much better than the professor that I had for CHEM142, but I wouldn't consider her to be "great". The tests are difficult and the review packets are nothing like the exams. pretty good

Super nice person with a passion for the subject, I recommend!
He was so chill and engaging during lectures!! He makes learning about env. science interesting and entertaining for non-stem majors.

Professor Harvey is very nice and excited about the material. All the coursework is easily accessible and grading criteria are clear and fair. He makes sure his student's opinions are considered and really encourages participation. Definitely recommend for a fun class!

His lectures are fantastic, and his wording and teaching style makes everything very easy to understand. Hard class for sure, but it could have been a lot worse without him teaching it. Professor Bretland is a really caring and thoughtful professor.

Amazing teacher when I had him last spring quarter. He explained things in depth and understood where the students were coming from since he took the same class at UW when he was an undergrad. The class was quite difficult and I wasn't a huge fan of the flipped classroom method but Prof Bretland himself was pretty good. His explanations were clear and he answered questions pretty well, also he was nice and approachable

The physics GOAT.

good teacher

Nethan really cares about his students and his teaching style is really effective !!! Would highly recommend !

Nathan is a kind person and cares about his students. His lecture is very clear and can prepare you well for the exam.

Straight up just good at teaching. Exams were fair, lectures were captivating, everything she was responsible for was set up nicely to make me confident in electromagnetism, a class I was worried for. Would highly recommend her if you have a choice between her and another professor.

Course when I took it focused around blackness and Afro-pessimism; reading and theory heavy. Heavy historical/political focus, if you're an international student you might struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gust is an interesting character, but classes are very relaxed usually. He randomly roasts people which was funny. Wears the same jeans and chukka boots to class every day. Just turn in everything on time and put a little effort into the portfolio.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He is really really really helpful and understanding. Gave more homework initially but was the best afterwards.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Gust Burns is a very fun teacher. I'm not quite sure why his other reviews are so low, but I thoroughly enjoy his class. He has funny jokes and low key roasts people which is hilarious. The only downside of this class is his feedback/teaching can be a bit vague sometimes.

Gust is a great professor.  He is a funny guy and he makes me laugh.  His feedback is very clear and he tells you what to do to improve.  I would recommend him.  I am being serious.  Not sure why he got negative reviews. I think he's great.  His class is a lot of fun.

He's not the worst teacher in the world or anything, but he's definitely up there. I will mention that this is his first year however, so who knows maybe he'll get better. All I can say however, is that he is very difficult to understand, and too abstract. In other words, don't expect anything out of going to class other than participation credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: "Do not think of me as an obstacle to success" is what he writes in the syllabus, but I assure you, he is most definitely an obstacle. He just doesn't know what he's doing! His feedback is terrible, it's literally just him saying "redo this and that, oh and this is wrong". Period. No context, no explanation behind why, absolutely nothing.

Great lecturer who explains concepts clearly but doesn't finish slides during class. Pacing can feel uneven at times, with more time spent on introductory topics and less on complex ones. Be prepared to practice independently, though there are plenty of problems provided. Grading can be strict, which is typical for this intro series.

His lectures were engaging, and the quizzes he gave were mostly easy. The programming assignments increased in difficulty and time required by quite a bit, but because you could redo many of them using resubmission forms, it was easy to achieve the maximum score. Issue: The final was longer and harder than a basic coding final should have been.

I took his ethics class which is diff from 12X most students take with him. He's a great prof and he engages his students during discussion very well. You might get the sense the he's totally against AI but he encourages you to form your own opinion. The reading isn't a big deal, have a sense of what the chapter is about and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor and well-organized class but just difficult in general. The grading scale is makes it hard to determine your GPA during the quarter which is frustrating. They don't give Es generously so make sure to take lots of time on weekly assignments to build a cushion for the 3 quizzes. The final was much harder than the practice material.

Brett explained concepts well. He gave us many opportunities to ask questions and used thoughtful analogies to explain things. But, important grading criteria was unclear, so TAs graded assignments very inconsistently. This does not reflect well on Brett, regardless of who implemented this policy, because of the stress on us. Overall, he's ok.
Very good lecturers and excellent at explaining CS concepts. He was co-lecturing with Matt Wang and I felt like his explanation was a bit more understandable (Matt was also a great prof though).

Professor Wortzman had everything you'd want out of a CS professor; his lectures were engaging and well-planned, he was available outside of class, and assignments and tests were for the most part at an appropriate difficulty level. Quiz difficulty did vary quite a bit though, and the grading structure was very unclear.

Amazing Professor, CSE 123 is a challenging course, but every time I went to lecture I feel like I learned something new and interesting. Wortzman is very likable, and explains concepts well, and if you pay attention in class and attend quiz section, you are gonna do well.

Quite clear (and loud, maybe due to the microphone in the room) during lectures. Is really enthusiastic about the subject being taught and is willing to answer any and all questions from the lecture room clearly to the best of his ability.
CSE intro series in general has vague grading criteria. Homework and quizzes are much more difficult than class content. But he's a decent lecturer - engaging + good explanations.

This guy will maintain your attention span the entirety of lecture. Go to office hours, you can talk to him about anything you want, he will spew out a lot of great stuff. Talk about UW, UW CSE, or Academia & Industry, he will talk! Greatest UW CSE professor, designed the Intro to CS: CSE 12X sequence for greatest accessibility and learnability.

The class was challenging but the professor was helpful. Attend lectures, do lots of practice, and check out tools like Unstuck study - it really helped me prepare. Overall, a tough but worthwhile course.

He's a great lecturer in terms of how he explains concepts and you can tell he cares about the material, but I personally didn't like his teaching style. The class itself is set up so that you can succeed with things like resubs on assignments, but it's very hard to determine what your GPA will be throughout the quarter bc of the grading scale.
Brett is a good professor, making course content easy to understand while also keeping it entertaining.
Good lecturer, very inspirational during lectures. I also heard that he is the designer of the 12X series. These courses are enjoyable and meaningful.
CSE123 was not easy but the professor was nice
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's a good prof. It was a tough class for me though, but you just need to do loads of practice if you aren't naturally adept at CS and want a good grade. I kinda goofed and never went to lecture in-person, just watched the recordings, but Brett seemed like a good guy and decent prof.

Brett is pretty cool! He definitely knew his stuff and you can tell he has a background in education the way he treats his students with so much respect and is always happy to answer questions! He loves fostering discussions in classes, but most of the time the classes were pretty boring and most things can be learned through pre-lecture / section.

Brett is a ridiculously overrated professor.  His explanations are good but he treats university students as elementary school kids.  He spends way too much time on everything and once spent 40 mins during the 3rd lecture talking about syllabus stuff.  Painful to listen to, and grading is very very harsh, and you can't argue against it.
really engaging and funny

Took CSE 121 in Autumn 2022. Wortzman was a great lecturer and clearly cared a lot about the students in the class. Clearly cares a lot about the subject that he teaches as well. Lectures are recorded (like all of the CSE 12X series) if you ever miss class.
Great teacher for the CSE 12X series, lectures are recorded if you ever miss class.
arrogant. offical speech,  useless lecture. Wonderful Harvard student. consistent with my impression to them. (personal opinion, is incorrect if you disagree with)
Great, funny guy - not very personable though, sometimes responds dryly to questions and comments.

He seems pretty intimidating but is actually very organized and nice. I came in with a lot of previous knowledge, so it might have been a bit easier for me than for others. I absolutely loved the projects, they were all super fun!

It's clear that Brett is passionate about education. The 12X series is hard, but you have plenty of resources and support to succeed. Brett is flexible and receptive to feedback, and constantly changes the courses based on what works and what doesn't. He and his TAs go above and beyond to accommodate students. Super awesome series! I will miss it.
Best CS Professor I've ever had. I'm envious of how much energy he has and his passion for his field.

Good lectures; makes sure students grasp content and cares about our success, also teaches clearly (same cannot be said about his co-teacher Kohlbrenner). Generally a pretty relatable guy. Sometimes comes off as condescending but only to students that actually didn't read directions, etc. Grading is very very nitpicky for "code style"
Brett gives great lectures! He tries to keep things fun and interesting and it feels like he has students' best interest at heart.
I had Brett the first time that 121 was taught at UW. Overall, very good! Code quality was graded very harshly, but it generally felt like the course staff wanted you to succeed.
Great Intro series professor.

He's a really nice professor and a good guy. Make sure not to fall behind on the lectures because every week you learn skills that build off the skills you learned the previous week, so if you didn't understand what you learned the week before, you'll get confused really easily and fall behind. Go to IPL office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Compared to Elba who co-taught in the fall of '22, Brett was a saint. He was enthusiastic about the material and really did try to put the student's best interest forward. He took responsibility for mishaps in the course structure unlike his counterpart, and the TA's overall were pretty nice. I would gladly take another class with him.
very enthusiastic!

I think Professor Brett did an amazing job introducing me to CS. I appreciate the clear format and schedule the course had. Grading can be a bit weird with multiple TA's giving feedback but the course is very manageable and forgiving if you put in the effort to learn. 
Overall, Brett is a really good instructor for CSE.
He is such an amazing professor!!!

As a non-major, the class was very forgiving. Compared to my chem and bio classes, CSE 121 always made adjustments so everyone can do well in the class. They were fair with deadlines (even changed a few due dates so students had MORE time), had a lot of opportunities to retake quizzes and resubmit projects, and had a lot of practice material.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Brett really cares about every student's success. He teaches the material in a way that makes sense, and although the class is sometimes difficult, the instructors and TAs do everything in their power to help you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Brett is a clear and straightforward lecturer, making the concepts easy to understand and is helpful outside of class as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I like this easy going and straight forward professor!

Brett himself is a great guy and instructor, but the class has like 500 students, so don't expect him to know you by name. He's not accessible outside of class, but again, that's not really his fault. I ended up dropping the class for other reasons, but I would definitely recommend Brett if you don't mind 500-person lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really liked him, he's funny and kind and makes boring coding lectures actually entertaining and interesting. The class overall is pretty easy, I didn't do much and I got an A. And if you have Brett as a prof, it makes everything so much easier and more fun because he is a funny dude with lots of energy. Definitely would recommend!

One of the best professors I've had at UW. He taught my CSE 142 lecture alongside Kasey who was also excellent. The course is very beginner friendly, but I think it prepared me quite well for my future CS classes.

CSE 142 was probably the best class I've taken so far and it's largely because of the way the course is structured. Highly recommend this course and professor. Kasey and Brett are absolutely amazing lecturers and I actually felt like I was learning in every class.
best prof to have in an intro to cs class. miss you king x
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: 142 is extremely beginner friendly. 4.0 is a joke.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Brett was an amazing lecturer and has to be one of my favorite professors. He made the content easy to understand and engaging. He also gave plenty of opportunities to fix old assignments and turn in work past its due date. He legitimately cares about if you understand the content and made an awesome teaching combo with the other professor Kasey.
A very nice teacher that was always willing to help.

Brett's lectures are super engaging (but sometimes a but too much energy for me). I personally am not the best the cs material but I'd say if you have the proper interest in the topic he's an amazing professor. Weekly workload includes a weekly 'assessment' due Tuesdays and checkpoints on Saturdays. The resubmission cycles are super lenient too.

Brett was always super enthusiastic about lectures and made learning enjoyable. He explained concepts very clearly and the mass amount of TAs + the discussion board made help easily accessible. Only bad thing I can say about him is that he sometimes took 1-2 days to upload recordings of lectures, but not a big deal if you're attending in person.
Really nice guy. Can't ask for a better intro series professor.
I love Brett!! CSE 142 is not hard! You can get a very good score if you treat this course seriously!

He explains every concept really well in lecture and clearly cares and wants everyone to understand everything. In addition he's just a cool, chill guy. I asked to interview him for another class and he was nice and accommodating to schedule it. Also the grading and resubmission policy made this class pretty forgiving and enjoyable to learn from.

Brett really does make his lectures engaging and understandable. For CSE142, we used a standards-based grading scale with resubmissions, so you have opportunities to improve your grade throughout the quarter. Also for Autumn 2021, there was no official midterm or final exam, so that made this class less stressful. Overall not too hard of a class.

Take this class with Brett! Hes very chill and puts in effort to help students. One Weekly checkpoint and assessment throughout the quarter. Being able to resubmit every assessment made it much easier to end with a good grade. Go to the IPL if youre stuck, it helps a lot more than youd expect!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Thanks to Brett for saving my interest in CSE. Real good professor with a efficient TA team. Lecture is concise and clear, with the weekly checkpoint you really have the feeling that you are learning something. Best class I've ever attend.

Both 142 and 143 dragged me through the mud because I'm not great at coding, but Brett and the rest of the staff are fantastic. They're all very professional but still fun, and I have 0 bad things to say about them. Such a huge fan. (i will say do not take this class without coding experience.. don't make my mistake)

Brett is the G.O.A.T of the CS department! A real gem of a person and a great teacher. His lectures were pretty clear and he cleared all my doubts within the lecture itself. Even though this class's material can be complicated, Brett makes it seem very fun and easy. Would highly recommend for both CSE 142 and CSE 143.
Damn, this is one course that I actually enjoyed
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Brett is a great professor! He's very passionate about what he teaches and is always open to questions during lecture. Lecture itself isn't mandatory since it's recorded but you'll need to understand the concepts to do well on the assignments. Final grade is made up of weekly checkpoints and assessments, which usually take a few hours

Lectures had hundreds of students, and quiz sections were taught by undergrads with a quarter or two of coding experience. Weekly assignments were graded extremely harshly with no opportunity to make up points. The lectures were recorded, though. The prof himself had little impact on my experience taking the class.
Great professor overall!

He was a great professor and I agree with the other comments. However, he changed his grading system to ESNU scale which makes it impossible to know what your final grade will be until it's actually released. His grading was harsh and unforgiving because of this scale and MANY students felt their final grade was much lower than expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Brett is an exceptional cs teacher. He explains everything clearly and is enthusiastic about teaching. There are weekly assignments and checkpoints, and two cumulative assessments. Grading for weekly hw could be harsh but there are resubmissions and a bunch of helpful resources to help you succeed.
Very pog professor

This was my first CS class and Brett made it very enjoyable! Lecture recordings are usually available by the end of the day, so you don't necessarily need to be at the live zoom call. Brett always takes the time to answer questions and really works to help his students understand the material. Also very accommodating during the pandemic! 10/10

Brett was a very engaging lecturer and while I was bored at times, it's coding so can't really expect much. I thought the grading criteria was very clear and detailed feedback was given on assignments, and on top of that, we were allowed to resubmit big assignments. This class was very fair and flexible online, and Brett was a great professor.

I didn't really interact directly with the professor, since the class is so large. Textbook use is technically optional, but it goes into detail about stuff that isn't covered in lecture. He leaves time in lectures for people to ask questions, which is nice but detracts lecture time, and people keep asking questions already addressed elsewhere!
The best CSE professor - take him if you have the chance. He really takes the time to make sure that students understand the course content by giving thorough explanations.

I had Brett for CSE142 online and the organization of the course was phenomenal. The lectures were recorded and it was easy to meet the staff through TA hours. His lectures are also easy to understand and fun. The course load is a little difficult but he offers great resources and always tries to clarify. I would definitely take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Even in an online setting, Brett is the best :)
He is the best CSE professor one could find at UW. His method of teaching is wonderful and he is damn hilarious. Also gives amazing examples.

Brett is a super genuine person who cares for his students. On multiple occasions he has listened to feedback from students and adapted his teaching or the course work to best suit student needs. He ALWAYS makes time to answer questions and really goes above and beyond. He is a very fair person and I am looking forward to CSE 143!! Highkey a GOAT

Good professor and lectures are informative, explains very well, and he wants you to pass. The grading can be strict though, I got my program to work but a small indentation error caused my grade to go down
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: It is the coronavirus quarter and everything is online. Unlike all other case classes I took that quarter, he refused to record the section though for many times I emailed the course stuff telling them how that would be really helpful for students like me in a different time zone. In general, he is really non-responsive to many things, not caring.

I had Brett for both 142 and 341, and he was great for both. You can tell he really cares about the material, his lectures are clear and his answers to student questions are clear. On the downside, he does tend to progress through the material a bit slowly, but I found I learned more from him than other profs because of his pacing.
Probably the best lecturer at UW. Highly recommend taking him for a higher level course if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: It is a CS class so the curve is wack but he is funny and wants you to succeed. He definitely cares about his students. One of the best lecturers in the department.

Lectures were interesting and Brett is a very knowledgeable professor. Get ready to learn! 1 homework assignment per week, 1 midterm, and 1 final. The assignments take around 7 hours to complete each week and I was able to do well by going to the IPL Help Center to ask homework questions. Also, sign up for the CSE 190 lab for 1 additional credit!

Great teacher, explains things well. CSE142 is impressively well-coordinated for such a large class (around 800 students for me). Haven't spoken with him in person, but he seems nice. 1 midterm (handwritten), kind of tricky but doable if you study and practice throughout the quarter. Beware that he does go rather fast, but lectures are recorded.

Brett is a responsible, caring, brilliant professor. He's definitely one of the best professor I had ever had. His lectures are clear, and he has the super power to explain difficult things in a way that everyone can be easily understand. Even though I had to spend 6-7 hours per week working on the homework assignments, I really had learned a lot.

Always enjoyed Brett's lectures. His style and presence were captivating and it made the content all the more interesting. The homework load is pretty heavy; while there was only one assignment per week, they took 4-7 hours for me to complete. The book isn't necessary but pay attention in lecture and section. Practice timed tests before final!

Brett was very good at passing all of the elementary java information to everyone. I have yet to meet anyone who didn't find his lectures interesting or didn't like his teaching even though for many people CSE 142 is rather hard. Highly recommended even for those who already know java as he may give you some new perspectives. P.S. don't use jGrasp.

He is a really nice teacher. I have never imagined I could get a 4.0 at the beginning of the quarter. You could get 0.33 extra credit on homework each time if you show up in the exploration one time. At the end of the quarter, there will be 2 extra credit on the creative husky program assignment. Do the previous exams, you will get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Shoutout to Brett! Really amazing lecturer. Every topic was extremely clear and each lecture was entertaining and fast-paced (in a good way)!
He is an amazing teacher. He is very funny in the lecture which helps you absorb new concepts quickly and easily. One of the most enjoyable things to do is taking his course and you do learn a lot.

Although he talks relatively faster than other teachers, Brett Wortzman is great at effectively explaining key java concepts so that even someone without any prior coding experience like myself was able to grasp the concepts. He is kind, relatable and is able to connect well with his students. Go to office hours!

Brett is a great lecturer and explains concepts very well. You can tell how much he loves the subject and hes always in a good mood. Really enjoyed this class. The worst part of the class is the test-taking situation in Kane 130 where you barely have enough room for a 9.5 by 11 size of paper to fit.
Brett is an amazing lecturer, even though the class will have upwards of 500 people in it he will still be able to interact with students and explain concepts clearly. Highly recommend him.
I love him. Great guy and great lecturer. As a student who has never touched CSE before, I'd say he did a great job explaining Java and helping me understand the programming language.
He's a good teacher. He knows what he's doing and he knows how to teach it. Lots of homework assignments in this class and you have to dedicate time to get a good grade.
He is very nice to you and fun to listen to. I can sit in his lectures for hours on end.

Brett has been absolutely amazing so far, I couldn't have asked for a better lecturer. He explains things very intuitively and in a way that is very easy to process and understand. His lectures are very fun and full of enthusiasm, and you can see he genuinely wants you to do good and pass. Overall, I highly recommend his class.
Fantastic! Brett went through this material in a way that people new to CS can understand how everything works and excel. Lectures were engaging and fun.

I had no idea what coding was about coming into this class but ended up doing pretty well. Solid lecturer and concepts were clearly explained, although I would say to learn Java with no background in CSE142 lots and lots and lots of practising and thinking are necessary outside of the classroom despite the fact that lectures are helpful.

Okay it's nothing against Brett but more against the fact that I hate the CSE department at UW with every bone in my body and this is the class that shut the door on my STEM career here forever. Brett in general goes a little fast but he's enthusiastic and genuinely wants you to pass. It's not him that's the issue or you, it's the course.
Brett is so awesome. He is easy to approach, has a loud clear voice, and a great sense of humor. I've only had him for 391 - but if he ever teaches an upper div class I would definitely take it!

Having never taken a CSE course before I was afraid of doing poorly, especially at UW. Wortzman taught high school for many years and really knows how to cater to beginners and experienced students. He was uplifting and stressed that your effort, not your past experience, was how you could get a good grade. Fantastic lectures and clear criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Best lecturer ever! Brett explains things extremely well and is very open to everyone's questions even when he has a class of 720. Do yourself a favor and take his class!!
Attend lectures and you will be fine,
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is solid for 142, and many of his tests can be easy but require you to dump a lot of time into studying for them, and they are graded quite harsh and you won't really see your errors. Class overall is lecture heavy, and if you pay attention you should be fine. One thing that sucks however is the release of homework and the due dates are awkward.

The hardest course I've taken in my first quarter of college. Big amount of workload. It's hard, but if you are willing to spend time on practicing you'll be fine. I actually enjoy the process of learning CSE but it's actually hard to get a high score. BTW I feel sooo sleepy in Kane Hall during his lectures. Every single time.

Brett's a nice guy. I come in blind and learned so much. Attendance isn't mandatory (large class) but I recommend going, as panopto takes time to upload. Be careful w/ hw assignments--check style guide and basically any resource available to you. Doing practiceit before exams rly helps, but start early. The system crashes when everyone's using it.

Is able to take the basic concepts they teach in CSE 142 and make them somewhat interesting. Overall, I dislike CSE 142 --- I think grading is pretty subjective depending on your TA, they make a lot of errors in grading, there are a lot of curveballs on the tests, and it's just generally somewhat stressful. Brett--still great, but the class sucks

Brett is easily the best lecturer I have ever listened to before. Each lecture is extremely clear and well-thought through. He knows the subject like the back of his hand and knows how to engage the class so that they pay attention.
Great great lecturer. Very interactive. Codes in his lectures so we can learn alongside. Knows his stuff. Gives great answers to student questions. Good experience overall.
Brett's awesome. He really knows his stuff and I can tell he really loves what he does. Would love to be able to take more classes with him, he makes it really fun!
Really good!

I came into this class with no prior knowledge, and Brett did a great job of explaining everything so I could easily understand it. Assignments are time consuming but they are fun and we only have one assignment each week. Exams and really difficult, but Brett and TAs tell you exactly what to expect.

The CSE 142/143/143x series at UW is a well oiled machine and Wortzman is no exception. The lectures and homeworks were all pre-written by Reges and Stepp, so Wortzman mainly just regurgitates these materials which is fine since the materials are clear and cater to the individual with no prior programing experience.

Brett is a great professor. You would be lucky to take his class especially when you are new to programming like me. He teaches everything clearly and gives a lot of examples. He posts the programs he used in lectures online for you to review later. Also, he is humorous.

You will have an amazing time if you take CSE142 with Brett. The class is hard especially if you are new to computer programming like I was. Attend lectures and quiz sections and you will do just fine. Plenty of resources to get help from, and most of the TAs are very smart and caring. His lectures are fun and easy to follow.
Amazing lecturer!!! He genuinely cares about his students! He is always so passionate in class. Love him.
Amazing professor! Made the accelerated intro class material super understandable, albeit the departmental grading system made the class as a whole much more difficult. Would recommend him highly.

Need to take CSE 142? Do yourself a favor by taking it with Brett! Not only is he knowledgeable, but he is by far one of the most affable professors you can possibly have at UW. His tests tend to be on the more challenging side, but he is super helpful with answering questions after lecture and during office hours.

All I can say is wow. Mr. Wortzman is one of the best teachers I have ever had. I came in with 0 coding experience and decided to take this class for fun. I'm so happy I did. He does an excellent job of breaking down the hardest java topics into easy-to-understand pieces, loves answering questions, and truly cares about his students. 10/10
One of the best lecturers I've ever had. Engaging, super patient with questions, and is very organized in course material. I barely cracked the textbook open because he explains everything so well!

143X goes over tons of material in a short amount of time, and Brett does a great job of keeping the class on track. Great explanations. Read the book before lectures and ask questions during office hours to solidify your knowledge and make debugging easy. Generous curve so an easy 4.0 if you do well on the final.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He. Is. AWESOME! Super interesting and clear lectures, always open to any types of questions, talks at just the right pace. Tests are challenging but fair. He is extremely helpful if you go to his office hours, I couldn't reccomend using those enough. You can tell this guy knows what he is doing and is very passionate about CS. A+ prof

She's clearly very passionate, but I felt like I didn't learn much. Her midterm was mostly just memorisation of vocab. The TAs were great, grading criteria easy to follow, interesting readings. There are definitely better and definitely worse, as professors go.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super chill professor! You can skip each class and still pass (just do your readings, please.) She posts the slides and (some) TA's give you a vocab "practice" sheet in quiz section, which is basically giving you 30% of the midterm/final exam. She doesn't tend to connect topics covered in class within class, so you'll have to do that individually.
Exams felt more like remembering fun facts than actually showing you understand the concepts/material. She is little intimidating.

I really enjoyed Professor Burstein as a lecturer, and found the readings and the formal analysis very interesting! However, tests (one midterm and a final) make up 70% of the grade for this class (the other 30% is quiz section participation). If you test well, this makes the class easy, but if tests are not your strong suit, it'll be a struggle
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams count for 60% of the grade while also being UNRELATED and fun fact heavy. Grades are not curved despite low average test scores. Avoid if possible.

The midterm/final honestly felt totally unrelated to most skills/knowledge gained in the actual class. She would loose track of what she was saying and go on tangents. Every discussion was dominated by the same students because if anybody else spoke she was sort of rude to them? Def had favorites and wasnt very approachable. TAs were great, though!

Prof. Burstein is a very engaging and passionate professor. She does ramble a bit during lecture but not to the extent that it affects your knowledge or grade. Lots of readings but most felt relevant to the course. I probably wouldn't take another class taught by her but overall a really good professor!

Her lectures are disorganized and full of irrelevant rambling. The readings she has us do, we don't talk about in meaningful ways. The class didn't feel "intellectually stimulating", even from an English nerd. She's not a "horrible" option, but I DON'T recommend her; you will have to really put in effort to get something out of her teaching.

Imo Prof. Burstein is a fine professor but assigned readings, assignments, and exams are too heavy compared to other English classes that are the same credit and level. Exams are very "fun fact". About 3 dozen readings and the exam will randomly present a small excerpt and ask you to name the author and title. Would not take again.

Professor Burstein was excellent, and I would definitely recommend taking 202 with her. She's engaging and funny -- she can ramble a bit sometimes and lecture is mandatory/not recorded, but ultimately, all the important exam stuff is in the slides and her thoughts on the topics are passionate, intellectually valuable, and largely worth your time!

Professor Burstein is a fantastic professor. She is truly passionate about literature, and that is definitely evident throughout her lectures. As has already been mentioned, she is certainly a yapper; however, I found that this made the lectures more engaging, and she never abandoned the topic at hand, so it's never a waste of your time.

great professor, especially if you really enjoy English. she's a yapper but it's perfect for English geeks. exams aren't too bad. small packet you have to buy with the readings & a book ~ $40. readings before each lecture, poems or prose stories. very interesting class that is great for English professors. she is so passionate about her job.

Burstien was overall a great professor, you could tell that she loves what she does. I will say that she is tough. You have to have a thick skin, especially when interacting with her. Come into office hours PREPARED. It probably would've saved me many tears. Her feedback can be tough but it is VERY helpful. Be prepared to have dense readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: 5 essays (3 are graded cumulatively and worth 40%, and last 2 are individually each worth 20%), in-class scribing worth 20%. Interesting lectures, not clear grading criteria for essays. It's very clear to a point that it's not (she doesn't want a thesis but if you don't write one, you won't get a very good grade). 4 novels + additional reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: JB was a terrible professor. She rudely yelled at me in front of the whole class for being a couple minutes late one time… she treated us like children even though we're all adults. Do not take her class if you want to be respected.

Incredibly easy class. The enjoyable things were the readings and new vocab. However, the vocab was brushed over. Burstein was impossible to follow. The tangents taken and answers to questions were completely off-topic, just words they spoke for the sake of speaking. Wasn't able to take a lot away from this course.
Tests are very "fun fact" heavy and require attendance given that most material is not listed in the lecture slides. The professor tends to go on tangents but the material is usually very simple.

Loved loved loved Professor Burstein. The class is difficult, but so rewarding -- I learned so much this quarter. The readings and lectures were very engaging and informative, I can not overstate enough, they are a GREAT lecturer. The tests are difficult, but as long as you spend time studying and engaging with the material you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very unapproachable. exams were unrelated to lectures

Took ENGL242 and overall enjoyed the experience. She has a way with facilitating good class conversations and asking philosophical questions that really make you question your own ideas. Seems to be a fair grader and took class feedback accordingly. Reading was heavy but expected. Overall a good professor that makes you think outside your own box.

For sure a critical grader; come in with thick skin, but be aware that the feedback is useful. Lots of reading. Recommend strongly taking one of their classes if you want to pursue English in any capacity.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you're sensitive about someone giving critical feedback, look elsewhere. But, Burstein is knowledgeable and explains abstract concepts in a unique way which makes them easier to digest. If you would like to learn from an interesting individual who is not afraid to challenge students, you'll be happy.

we read a book in 2 days, the sylabus changed 6x?? the lectures slides included google definitions which I didn't love. it made it feel like we covered surface level critera. TA's were amazing. The class is graded on 2 exams so if you dont do well on them you'll fail the class. would not recommend. prof. is knowlegable but curriculum was a 2/5

Syllabus changed 6 times. Class got canceled four times. Three lectures on a Zoom call but in-person for health reasons. Captivating lectures, but belittling/degrading when asking questions. Burstein is very intimidating and unapproachable which is unfortunate as they are knowledgable in the subject matters discussed: aestheticism, Wilde, Didion

Somewhat condescending. Most of what is discussed during lecture is not on the midterm/final, so the entire interpretational aspect of the class is somewhat redundant. You honestly don't even have to go to lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class is focused on a novel for the first half of the quarter and poetry for the second half. Be sure to read the novel, but other than that you do not need to have the readings completed before class, just show up to lecture. She was a little demeaning when answering questions and the lectures were sporadic but she was overall knowledgable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Seems a little deranged, made us read book in 2 days
The best literature professor one could ask for. Her literary enunciation, humor, and passion are all I could ask for.

The syllabus changed a lot and things were taken off last minute--at the moment it was great since I was juggling other classes--but, more objectively, it had drawbacks since we didn't get to as much material. It was easier to get a good grade than I initially thought. I like her lecture style; it's engaging and refreshingly unusual. Lots of readin

My experience with her was terrible She was rudever answered my questions directly or respectfully Often turned me away with snarky remarks&that I "should already know that" or that I should ask someone else She gave no f*cks for my performance Her lectures were vague&aimless Extreme pessimist grading Unclear rubrics Cited things not on syllabus
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: JB has a wealth of knowledge but very rarely, if ever, does that come through in their lectures. I wouldn't even call them lectures. They just seem to come to class with an idea of what they want to discuss for the day and kind of take it from there. I loved chatting with them one/one, but their class was confusing AND hard to pass.

Ignore any subpar review. Anyone serious about reading or writing who cares about doing it at a high level must challenge themselves by taking JB. Some of the deepest thinking I have done and witnessed. JB could be at an ivy but we have been blessed at UW. Infinite knowledge of modernism, fashion, and culture. If you lean in, your mind will thank u

Take a class with this terrible professor if you want to be graded with check minuses and check pluses in college. God forbid you have a question, she will not be able to even follow it let alone respond in any meaningful form. It seems like she goes into each lecture with absolutely no idea what she's gonna say and improvs it all at 0.2 speed.

I personally enjoyed Professor Burstein's class. It was set up very collaboratively, with small groups as well as whole-class discussion. Workload is very reasonable, papers are graded according to very clearly laid out expectations. Kind and personable professor, and generally interesting material. Would take again!

Overall, this class was kinda off. The teacher is energetic but can be passive-aggressive at times. The lectures went in circles, and when she asked questions, there didn't seem to be a right answer. The readings were interesting, but near the end, the objective of the class was unclear. Work is mostly reading responses so at least skim the plot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Burstein is clearly an expert in her field & passionate. It's a shame that did not translate online. She was scattered/inconsistent, struggled to maintain discussions, never replied to emails, and graded w/o a lot of rhyme/reason. She p much clocked out by the end. Probably awesome in person, but definitely struggling with the pandemic format.

Jessica is brilliant. Her expectations are high, yes. But she gives you the guidelines she grades by and the feedback you need to improve. I admit she can be blunt (and this may discomfort some) but I have always appreciated frankness in a person. Get ready to write (qualitatively speaking).

Professor Burstein is abhorrent. She is mean for absolutely no reason, and her criticism on paper is not professional at all - it's personal. She's an eccentric with a penchant for cruelty. I would not recommend taking her class at all. Nothing is learned and almost everything is miserable.
Jessica is wonderful. Her class is difficult but you will come out of it a better reader and better writer. Worth the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Jessica is wonderful. I have never had anyone stretch my thinking and improve my overall skills as a reader and writer than she has. She pays very close attention when grading papers, reading them not just as answers to a question but as texts in themselves. As a result the feedback she gives is very very good. Also her fashion sense is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Burstein is an awesome lecturer and truly involves the class in discussions of the books read. I got a lot out of each lecturer, so go to them! I had to work hard to do well on responses, but got the hang of it eventually. She gives awesome feedback and a lot of chances to improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof. Burstein is all around an amazing professor! The material taught was very engaging and she did a great job involving the class and getting our opinions. She gave great feedback on the few papers that we had to write and she wasn't that hard of a grader. She is a funny and caring professor and I would absolutely take a class with her again!

Professor Burstein is an interesting character. She checks a lot of boxes on the list of traits common to the "eccentric intellectual" type of professor. I liked the books on the syllabus, and she did a good job of conducting class discussion. She makes clear what she considers good writing; you don't need to guess.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: What a brain! You'll find yourself walking out of her classes using larger words and thinking larger ideas just as an effect of being around her. Assigns interesting texts, leads brilliant discussion, and gives kind grades. Naturally, she's intimidating, but she's very responsive to student ideas, so that'll fade. Brilliant.
Great class discussion
She's a very good lecturer. If you find her use of 'big' words ostentatious,  you shouldn't be majoring in English.

Had her for 301 too-I think she is very engaging and entertaining to listen to, even if you do not participate AT ALL in her smaller classes. Overall she is an interesting professor, but if you can get past the intimidation factor and speak up, she can be very insightful and will expand on your ideas no matter how outrageous they are.

Self-important nonsense. Lectures on the assigned texts generally contained an average ratio of around 3:1 of ostentatious vocab exhibition to actual meaningful commentary. Not horrible, just tiresome.

Prof. Burstein is an intimidating professor because she is so well-learned, but her lectures are very clear and engaging. She provides a lot of information in lectures so skipping is unwise. She is great at providing examples of the terms she uses and the exams, if studied for, aren't bad at all. I enjoyed her snarky sense of humor!

She is hard, in the sense that she is very smart and depends your attention in lecture, if you go to lecture everyday her tests are EASY. I did little studying and got an A :) But i went to class everyday and payed attention to her vocab. Otherwise, shes tough but passible. She also has engaging lecture and a cool wardrobe!
Snarky. (Class renumbered as ENGL 301)

Formidably intelligent, sarcastic and hilarious, Prof. Burstein is a perpetual student. She is always challenging her students, whilst challenging herself to be a better teacher and understand the texts in new ways. By far the best English professor I've had. Dont be intimidated by her. Take good notes, engage with the texts, and you'll do well.

Burstein was funny, knowledgeable, helpful, and fairly easy for me. People say that she's condescending but she wasn't at all in lecture. Tests consist of stuff she says in lecture and VOCAB terms. Make flashcards, study the terms, and know how to use them. Studied about 4 hrs for the midterm and got a 103%. Trust me, it's not as hard as people say

Professor Burstein is sassy, extremely intelligent and completely intimidating. The tests are not impossible but yes, you will have to study your brains out. Overall, really tough. But worth it. Plus who doesn't love her all-black outfits complete with combat boots? Keep an eye out for the rare red scarf or beret.

I'm extremely frustrated by this class. I've never not gotten an A in an English class before. English isn't just my intended major, it's my PASSION, and this teacher is almost making me hate it. She's obscure, uncaring about student problems, and makes me confused about concepts I thought I understood. I have no idea what is expected of me.

I would consider her class to be the "weed-out" class for English Majors. If you want to join the major as your "back-up" or because you think it is going to be easy... this class is NOT for you. Professor Burstein knows what she's doing, and isn't willing to put up with students who think English is "easy."
Hard class. I studied hard and went to every single class and still wound up completely lost at times. I did well but it took a lot of work and I am not lazy, I STILL say AVOID!!!

She is a bit of a nutter, although she is very intelligent. She likes to make that fact very apparent too. She seems to be one of those people who enjoy making others feel inferior, but she is nice if you actually give her a moment to get past showing off her vociferous vocab. She is a formidable gateway into the great world of English at the UW.

I'll never get over her dynamic lectures. Witty & formidable, she's the prof you want if you plan to major in English; her authority on modernism can't be matched. Show up, pay attention, and YOU WILL be ready for 300-level classes. Naysayers are only lazy & unprepared. Warning: she can take down a smart-aleck w/a few words & a withering gaze.
One of my least favorite classes.  Jessica is very intelligent, however her lectures were extremely hard to follow.  Not to mention the whole sucking on the candy during lectures didn't help.

My favorite professor so far. She's brilliant - her lectures are incredibly articulate and intellectually stimulating. A lot of people complain about her exams because you're tested on tiny details mentioned in lecture (often irrelevant to the course), but if you take thorough notes you'll be fine. She's just testing whether you paid attention.

She scared me at first, but she is clever, witty and approachable. Her senior seminar became my favorite class, and she became my all-time favorite professor. Stick with it and put in the effort and you'll be rewarded.

This class was deceiving. She begins with a witty introduction and then leads you into a path of destruction. The ability to comprehend what was required was near impossible. For the midterm we were told to "study what you would need to know at an English Major's cocktail party". This may be the quiz section prof issue, but Jessica was not helpful

The Professor Snape of UW. She's clever(but scary) and about eight weeks into the course you come to appreciate her sense of humor. Burstein really knows her stuff, but the discrepancy between this 202 course and others taught by different professors is unreasonable. The material is incredibly challenging and the exams ask very obscure questions.

She's not easy, but not impossible. She scares off a lot of people the first day of class. Yes, she gives exams in an English class.. But she's witty, sarcastic, and knows her stuff. I have her for quiz section, as well, and I've enjoyed that the most. Don't waltz in expecting and easy A - you need to work for it, but you get more from the class.
Terrible professor. Never take a class from her. She treats the students as inferiors and will not explain herself.
