Singing African American church music is all we do during class. Very enjoyable for me. You only got one opportunity to skip lectures and we do need to attend two mandatory concerts and turn in a paper about African American church music to receive the credit. A little big amount of workload for a 1-credit class.
Most rewarding class I've taken at UW, Professor Byrdwell is a great teacher and really gave us a thorough experience in gospel music. Organized, funny, and extremely personable!

This class is awesome! If you know how to sing/have prior experience then you should definitely take this class! She is strict(ish) but it's not really a problem as long as you have learnt the words - which happens naturally. It's an awesome class!

If you do not know how to sing, then I would strongly advise you to not sign up for this class! Don't let the "no auditions required" subtitle fool you! You will be put on the spot if Phyllis catches you lip-synching or messing up the lyrics of a song. Great class overall, but too much work for a ONE credit class--rehearsals + a paper!

Lots of HW that is posted after each lecture. Some problems are posted Friday and due on the following Monday. He gives many trick questions on multiple choice. He is a good lecturer but his course policies are frustrating.

Great professor! Very kind and approachable, and lectures are actually engaging. Exams and clicker quizzes are well-designed—some questions are pretty clever and even fun. As long as you attend class and keep up, you'll do well. Highly recommend!

Very textbook heavy. He only covers very hard example problems in lecture, not the material itself. Homework sets are assigned every lecture, meaning Friday sets are due Monday night, which isn't ideal. His exams have medians between 35-45%, typically. Also, if you miss more than half of lecture quizzes, he cuts your final grade in half.

Interesting lecturer; covers page-long example problems only rather than content itself. Textbook heavy, the textbook is very dry. Every lecture has a corresponding homework set, and homework sets assigned Friday night are due three days later on Monday night which isn't ideal. Exams are very challenging with medians below 50%, generally.
Very good professor, and he is kind to students, easy to communicate.

Yes his class is difficult. Yes he makes his exams unnecessarily difficult though it is all content relevant to the course (none of that "it wasn't taught in class" stuff), however there is absolutely 0 curve, the class is structured similar to that of a weed-out class but for the flowers that have yet to bloom. Do not take this class

Unfortunately, I am just another engineering student who has to take this class to graduate. Despite all that, he has taught me many things about statistics in the limited amount of time I dedicated to this class. His classwork is not easy, but he tried his best to deliver and gave us opportunities to think. Amazing lecture notes, sometimes funny

This class is almost as much about memorization as it is about statistics. So many symbols and concepts are similar, but importantly not the same thing. Professor Marzban is charismatic and tries to explain things, but there's simply too much content for him to do a good job. You also learn R for your quiz section, and don't use it otherwise.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Requires attendance, the tests are harsh but completely graded on a bell curve. The only complaint would be that the tests are so time constrained that you barely have enough time to find the clever insights needed for some more difficult questions.

Very enthusiastic about the subject, and many complained-about-policies have been changed since past reviews here! Informational lectures, but lecture notes are a bit difficult to follow and lectures are not recorded. Clicker quizzes. Exams are rather difficult compared to homework but there are like 20 practice exams to get familiar with.

He doesn't record lectures and goes fast during lecture. its all conceptual so its ez to feel lost in the class. he has an interesting way of writing his hw and exam questions. there's clicker questions during lecture based on accuracy which is annoying. also he doesnt post blank past exams. but ig hes very passionate abt teaching.

He clearly cares. His grading guidelines are statistically fair. He's an engaging presenter. 
However, the lecture notes are difficult to reread. 
I also took him for 390 and the R labs clearly need some work there.

Generally good professor. He is very enthusiastic about stats and teaching which is what I think made me like the class and subject. Tests are very conceptual and quite difficult but manageable if you understand the concepts well, meaning that you complete all the homework and attend lecture. Labs were also not too difficult but need R knowledge.

The concepts in this class are interesting, but Marzban somehow finds a way to make you despise it. Labs were horrible as you learned everything about R on your own, and lectures were dull and unorganized. Tests were very conceptual, which could be fine if he was not trying to make you choose wrong.

This is me being objective, I've had Marzban for 2 classes. He assigns homework on MWF that are all due the following Monday. The homework he assigns on Fridays(heavy load) where you might be spending all sat/sun working on it also the weekly quizzes suck and homework is obscure and long. I graduated in stats from UW, avoid him if you can.

Marzban's STAT220 class is tough, but with the right prep and tools like Unstuckstudy, you can get through it. Attendance is a must, and the exams require careful studying of the textbook and lecture notes. Overall, the class is doable with dedication.
No record for reviewing and attendence madatory

do NOT take this class if required for your humanities major, as a soc major who despises STEM marzban had me STRESSED! did awful (whole class did) on the midterm and did slightly less awful on the final and ended with a B only bc i did good on every single HW and lab quiz, and went to every class (lecture MWF lab TTH is insane btw)

Professor Marzban is misunderstood, reading these reviews. His Stat220 class is difficult if you do not do the prep work for the tests - the midterm is 30% of the grade and so is the final and thats what makes or breaks your grade. Do the pre tests!
He is very caring though and funny, and he is very passionate when he teaches.I enjoyed his lectures

At first, Prof. Marzban is extremely scary. His homeworks are hefty and exams feel nearly impossible. As a stats professor, however, he knows and cares about his stuff. His teaching isn't fantastic, but once you get what he's saying, his quirky personality makes you intrigued about class each day. The final class curve can save anyone who tries!
DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE! He makes easy concepts complicated.
Exams are worded so weird it's like he's trying to trick us into getting the answers wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Worst Professor Ever! I would rather take Chem and Biology all over again. As a senior with a high gpa I can say this is the toughest class I've taken. You lose points if you miss class, his notes are unreadable and disorganized. I understand the book exercises more than his lectures, but he makes up his own questions and expects you to know R.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Wow, worst professor at UW. Entry level stats required to gratuate and its this hard?! Well, as a senior with a 3.6 gpa student I can tell you the professor is the issue and not the material. He is unclear in his notes and lectures. Learning how to code R?! 
Avoid this class like Covid, unless you want to fail.

Horrible, avoid at all costs. 
The whole grade is based on two exams that's not related to the lectures at all.
HORRIBLE HORRIBLE PROF, if you respect yourself avoid him. If you wanna hate stats he is the perfect dude for that.
Please avoid him at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: bad professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overcomplicates the most basic concepts not even the TAs understand what he's asking for. You know there's something wrong when the averages on his open book, open note, and even open internet exams are around the low 60s. Sick or sleep through his 8:30 lecture? Too bad. He doesn't record them.

I understand why other students may have rated him so low but I personally loved Professor Marzban! I thought he was very funny and I enjoyed being in class. He really encourages asking questions, and I found the course to be really interesting and was able to keep me awake even at 8:30. But test questions are very difficult and a little confusing.

I thought Marzban was great. Lectures were entertaining, even at 8:30am. He did a good job of explaining things clearly, and making sure we understood everything along the way. The tests were obviously harder than the homework, the lab quizzes were easy, and was long as you pay attention in lecture and read the textbook, the class is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: If you have the option to take a class other than STAT 220 for a requirement, do it. This class was more difficult to succeed in than my gen chem class. His test questions are very difficult and feel unfair. He asked for feedback on the class and people took time to reply honestly, and he sent an email rejecting everyone's suggestions.

I wish I dropped the class or listened to his reviews when I had signed up. I didn't like any second of this class. My TA was confused about what Marzban wanted from her so all the students were confused too. Don't take stats with him
OVER explains some of the easiest concepts, lecture notes are way too unorganized and hard to understand..

I thought these reviews were exaggerating but I should've DROPPED this class when I had the chance. He makes the easiest concepts and questions confusing. For quizzes, my TA had to regularly explain what he was asking because no one could understand.

Yes UW STEM is difficult, but when test averages are in the fifties thats a problem with the instructor. Disconnect between lectures, quiz sections and exams when it came to material covered. Is accessible outside of class but won't clearly answer your questions. I would describe him as unnecessarily confusing.

Overall I liked professor Marzban, he's not as bad as people say. I managed to get by without reading much of the textbook since it's very lecture-dependent. If you attend his lectures, preferably in person, and apply yourself you'll be fine.
The main thing I would say is to study HIS notes and hw well since the test questions are abstract & hard.

one of the worst professors i have ever had. He has awful class time usage(with forced attendance), unreadable handwriting, and a policy that can cut your grade in half no matter how well you were doing in the class. 100/10 would rather eat rocks than take another one of his classes again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I think Professor Marzban is ok. For STAT220, like he said, attend lectures, read the books, and I think most people would be fine. R is not hard, however it is taught by TAs which I think they did a good job. I believe the main issue is lack of planning and communication. Information about how tests and are assigned are not released early.

I despise this man. He has been one of the worst teachers I have had at the UW. He is unhelpful when answering questions, and gets defensive if he gets something wrong. The way he grades homework is laughable, randomly chooses 2 or 3 of the problems he assigns and those are the only ones he grades. Lectures are confusing. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Studying hard and Doing exercises in the back of the textbook is meaningless because the test is less related to the exercise question. So just reading the notes, that's all you need to do. Grading is also ridiculous. You will get lower and lower grades unless you get all the quizzes and homework correctly. Don't take his class, trust me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Caren Marzban was the worst professor that I have ever taken. He mutes test answers on canvas and releases test answers through a form of a survey or assignment instead. His class has been really confusing. He doesn't communicate with his TAs on what his grading rubric looks like so even the TAs are confused. NEVER TAKE A CLASS WITH HIM!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I got sick right before the final to where I missed the midterm because of sleep troubles. . He told me I should have told him before I got sick I was going to be sick. Gave me a 1 1/2 chance to take it Saturday morning from 8 to 9:30 before closing that opportunity and told me to drop the class. I woke up at 1 that day. I took his advice.

Super scattered lectures. Doesn't take questions/criticism well. Will tell you things 'dont matter' and to not worry about concepts. Makes up own definitions. Have to learn R? Doesn't believe in study guides. Homework questions are worded super confusing and in turn you lose points for not doing exactly what he meant. Overall, take w/ someone else
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I graduated from UW many years ago. If I have to recommend one class in UW, it would be Marzban's STAT390. It covers all essential knowledge of frequentist inference. He explained regression really well. I appreciate that he taught us to be cautious of using causal words, which is not common in undergrad level class. Super helpful, must take.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I'm a senior and I think this class is really normal for UW. Yes we learn R but he makes it extremely easy. I think that the bad ratings can be attributed to the large amount of freshman take this course. I think if you've ever been apart of the working world you'll like this guy. He doesn't care if you show up online or in person - its not hard

This professor tells his students to read the syllabus carefully, but the syllabus basically says "we're not really sure how it's going to go, but we'll let you know when the time comes" It is week 4 and I don't know how this class is graded. He also told us that only 3 homework questions out of 8 were graded AFTER we turned in the questions.
Get ready to learn by your self
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Be ready to teach yourself how to code using R for a basic statistics class. Quizzes are on material learned 20 min ago and not solidified. Lots of homework where he will take questions from the book and 'modify' it to make you use R, super confusing. I usually pick up things fast, but it seems as he expects you to already know R! So unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Received my lowest grade in this class, 3.3. Marzban is a good lecturer and makes the content interesting. The amount of homework is often way too much and he uses quizzes about R which is self-taught. He takes feedback to act like he cares but will never change anything regarding class structure despite students complaining every quarter.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: We are not even to the first midterm yet. I read all the bad reviews and was willing to give him the benefit of the doubt. He actually seemed not as bad as people say in lecture. But today, he introduced an irrelevant (to stats) brand new concept DURING a time-limited quiz. This is not teaching, it is a deliberate attempt to manipulate students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Takes away points if you give the wrong answer on multiple choice part of test. This along with his terrible course website show how antiquated he is. Homework given Friday night at 5pm is due Monday. If I could do it all over, I would take the STAT 394/395 and STAT 391 series just to avoid this professor. Avoid at all costs.

Mean grade on tests is an F. Course claims to "teach" R. That's a joke. R section is completely self taught and yet you are quizzed over it every week. Introduces coding concepts (for-loops, arrays, indexing) DURING the quiz, even though this class does not have a coding prereq. His handing of the R portion is what brought him from 2 to 1 star IMO
Thanks for making me hate statistics.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Why bother sending out surveys? You don't care about student feedback anyway.

I made this account solely to state how horrible he is. Most time is spent insulting anyone who disagrees with his methods or complaining about past students attitudes. The workload is absurd so unless you treat it like a full time job have fun trying to actually learn the concepts. The R portion is self taught and not covered in lecture. Avoid him

Marzban's key style is to test/quiz you over material that is introduced DURING the test/quiz. The class would be better if the "lab" was actually a lab instead of a weekly quiz over R documentation that was handed out 3 days prior. To say that this class is teaching R is borderline unethical. Read R documentation and you'll be just as well off.

One of the few professors I've met that actually respect students as human beings, with clear grading criteria, thought out lectures and HW. For ex, he once caught himself calling us immature then said that's condescending and changed his wording. I've met some stat professors who outright called us that. It's also obvious he spends time planningHW

Tests and homework are hard, but if you do the homework each time after it is assigned (rather than doing all 3 assignments on the weekend) it is quite manageable. The practice tests are very helpful to study for the exams. Marzban makes the lectures engaging and interesting.

I paid out of pocket, $1300, and found this class *extremely* well worth the price. Marzban works very hard to make sure the students _understand_ the material. I have rarely taken a class and retained so much afterward. The grading was very fair. Though hard at times, I couldn't recommend a course more, under Marzban. A+ teaching, in hard times.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Caren Marzban is one of the most arrogant people Ive ever come across in life. His attitude is epitomized by an exchange in which he asked for an example of a certain dataset, then berated those who gave accurate answers... before trying to gaslight the class (I dont want to confuse you...) when he realized his snap judgement was wrong. Horrid.

He honestly wasn't terrible. His lectures were ok, the course as a whole was well organized, and he was helpful in OH and thru email. My biggest complaints are the confusing tests and the amount of homework. Class tips: 1) get familiar with R before the class, 2) go to the Stat Study Center, 3) go to lecture, 4) read the HW and quiz solutions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Which is the antonym of "right"? (a)wrong,(b)unjust,(c)left,(d)none above. This is not the exact questions he gave us, but the structure was very close. Recommend his past exams and lecture notes. You need them to succeed in this class. Hw took a lot of time but was not counted as much as the game-show question on the tests. A very smart guy tho
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Caren makes every student who asks a question feel like they are stupid by being condescending all the time, unless you are one of 5 students that is extremely smart and befriends him. He goes through lecture extremely fast so that you can barely process the content during class. Homeworks are hard and take forever

Cons Makes you print out code/output for hw Quiz on R that he literally never teaches any of Worst course website ever created Makes you copy paste url extentions to get datasets Quiz every week on R that he never teaches that has the vaguest instructions Average of 5 hw Q's a day What he teaches doesn't align with book HW Pros Passionate
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Marzban's class. Though his 390 gets terrible reviews on here, I thought his class was great. I learned an incredible amount of very useful material over the quarter. His class is by no means easy, but if you listen to every word he says, things will make sense. The daily homework is a lot, but his clear lectures makes them easier

Did not enjoy this class that much. The teacher's lectures started out okay but got confusing and his tests were fairly difficult. Definitely has a tough homework load. Would not recommend taking probability with marzban.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This prof is not teaching you, he is flaunting his toughness. Ambiguous question descriptions on quiz/test, arrogant TAs, and ridiculous grading rubric. each "HW set" with 20+ problems only worth 10 points. And they don't grade it by counting correct answers you have, instead, they deduct points from 10 for wrong ones. So half correct0 points lol

Made a simple subject excruciatingly difficult and dull. Has some weird grading system based on subjectivity and will always make the bottom few students fail. Lecture notes were awfully structured and handwritten. Daily graded quizzes. Insane amount of derivation based homework that covers new topics instead of reinforcing taught ones.

Marzban is NOT the evil professor that many have said he is. Lectures are clear and he does a great job explaining different topics. Every past exam he has ever given is posted, which is useful. Quiz section coding (rstudio labs) isn't tested, but the "morals" are. Homework is long but useful for the exams. Don't need to read the book to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is a polarizing prof, I personally loved this prof but here's the bottom line. Take this course ONLY IF you're prepared to put in a lot of work for this course. This means attending lectures everyday (clicker quizzes), the homework is long, and grading scheme is complex. The pay off is that you will gain a solid foundation for statistics
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The class is entitled "Statistical Methods in Engineering and Science" but the way Marzban teaches, it is clear that he only cares about future statistics majors. He skips the probability chapter and wastes your time with multiple visits to linear regression. If you can, take another stats course for your science/engineering needs (and GPA).

Overly complicated grading system that takes several lectures to explain. Emphasis on definitions and vocab, yet he makes up his own definitions and vocab that are different than the textbook. Lab is worthless, 30 minutes of dead silence (no TA instruction) followed by a quiz that requires previous programming experience. Worst  I've had yet.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Caren is a very special human being. Your grade in the class is determined by an overcomplicated statistical method in which he wastes an entire two class periods explaining. The grading scheme is quite cut-throat and non-negotiable. The homework takes a ridiculously long amount of time. Lab is useless, but required because a quiz is given weekly
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The hw takes forever, you won't have weekend anymore, otherwise either get an A or F. as said below, he has some ego problem: acid, brazen, rude, sort of baseness, hauteur. He makes the students compete to each other, and fail the bottom 10%. My friends talk him for the grade, he said it was not his business, it was all about other students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Instructor Marzban was able to break down complicated concepts of Statistics, so it could be understood by an undergraduate student. I personally am very happy that I had a pleasure to take his class. He really knows his stuff and extremely quick on feet throwing jokes here and there. I recommend him as an important asset to your college experience
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: If you like artificial difficulty in the classroom then you'll love Marzban. One of the worst experiences at UW: useless lab section, lectures that are explicitly aimed at entertainment rather than teaching, and exams that focus on only the most subtle details of the material. Enjoy your single half-sheet of notes for the cumulative final.

I don't think Prof. Marzban was that terrible as everyone makes him out to be. He's a pretty good lecturer, and while his organization is a bit lacking, it's clear enough to see what he expects out of his students. He provides past exams going way back too, although he doesn't really reuse old questions. Overall, I thought his class was fine.
Worst professor I have ever had

Seriously, I don't understand why Prof. M get so much negative reviews here. He's amazing. The fact that his lecture is so easy and clear just means he's a great teacher who can explain hard concept in an understandable way. This is the first stats class I take at UW, and it blew my mind. But you do need to study hard for it. I learned so much.

He comes off as egotistical and paranoid. He refuses to use precise mathematical terms in favor of vague gibberish even on tests, telling us "everything in life is ambiguous, so get used to it" when students get confused by it. He throws tantrums in class if you don't loudly answer his questions like "do you understand."  I would not recommend.

Seems to have little regard for his students. There's just so much ego that a UW auditorium can handle. His lectures were great until the middle of the semester, when it seemed like he was fed up with us. After that, it felt like he was hunting us for sport.

Probably because it was a summer course so the material was kind of squeezed.  But I didn't find that course helpful at all.  The lecture were okay, but all those stuff putted together in the exam was totally awful.  The explanation in lecture was not helpful at all. No extra practice test to practice which sucks.

Awesome lecturer! Gives very clear explanations explaining the math "in English" (interpretations of your calculations). Posts lecture notes and summaries online and I learned just how useful stats is! Warning: hw is long, tests are hard (make sure you get the THEORY down), and labs aren't that useful. Overall though, thumbs up!

Awful teacher and unorganized lecture slides. He is arrogant and his lectures make everything seem simple which is a real wake up call when his test are extremely tricky and difficult. Labs are completely useless and only go to take the quizzes. Awful class.

DO NOT take it UNLESS you OK with a hit on your GPA. I am an A student, but I got B+ even though I put hours into studying and felt like I knew the material. His test questions are tricky and grading system is super weird(he would take 50 min to explain it). He is a great lecturer, you will learn a lot, just prepare to get a hit on your GPA.

Prof. Marzban is one of THE MOST entertaining lecturers at UW! He cares about statistics and wants you to learn. Simple: if you want to do well, expect to work ~8-10 hours/week , otherwise don't complain if you get a bad grade. You must also be a disciplined student in order to benefit from this class. And he really is reasonable!

Arrogant. If you ask stupid questions, he insults you in words.Hate that!!!Straightforward. He gives the direct answer rather than talks around the topic forever. If you survive from his words, you will start to appreciate his pedagogy. At least, he knows what he teaches. Hard class. Grading is fair but terrible. Avoid him if are bad at math/stat.
Hard tests, inane lectures, and useless labs. avoid his class

He is definetly intimidating during lecture. He takes a little too much pleasure out of making people look dumb in class. That being said I think his grading system is fair and his tests honestly should not be too bad if you know the materia. I think he is the only one who teaches STAT 390.

If you can, you're better off spending your time elsewhere- Marzban teaches a terrible class that nobody would take if they didn't have to. There aren't really any good alternatives at the school.. Some of you may be able to get away with taking CSE 312 or IND E 315 or a lower level stat course or QMETH something. If you can, you should.

Extremely arrogant. lectures are quite annoying as he constantly shoots students down for incorrectly answering trick questions. As many people have said here, the labs are completely useless unless maybe you are a stats major. Tests are full of trick questions that lead to bad grades given to students who actually do know the material.

Quite a character. Very good lecturer and a pretty good course & professor. Very strange grading techniques (exam questions worth variable # of points based on his clustering of student responses). Helpful and knowledgeable, but quite arrogant and does not restrain telling students that they're wrong and/or stupid.  Loathes math majors (admits it).

I personally didn't find Marzban's homework too difficult or long - it was his tests that made me angry. They did not correlate well with lectures/the textbook. If you absolutely MUST take 390 (I, of course, recommend that you don't), be prepared to study really hard for the tests and, as someone else said, "for your GPA to take a huge hit".

Professor Marzban really makes sure that you understand the material. He assigns lots of homework problems to make sure that you learn alot. He is readily available, and definitely knows the subject. It was a challenging class, with a lot of work, but it was worth it. Great class, Great teacher!

Despite some of the comments below, I actually kind of enjoyed Prof Marzban's lectures. Very entertaining guy in lectures, and very helpful at the Stat study center. This wasn't an easy class, expect to work hard, but you know what to expect (his test questions all come from the book). Tests are open everything (minus people). Great guy!

After reading the comments here, I dreaded taking this class. Well, I was very pleasantly surprised. Prof. Marzban is an excellent instructor and a really nice guy. His lectures are very clear and delivered in an entertaining style. He's got plenty of enthusiasm for the material. I really can't see what inspired all the negativity I found here.

There is a lot to Stat 390 despite being 4 credits. Homework every week, he assigns a little bit more daily. All of his work is organized online. Weekly lab with a quiz, most of the lab/quiz material is painfully easy. Harder tests, but they are open book, open note, open laptop. Overall a good professor, don't listen to some of the whiners below.

He's a pretty good teachers, and he puts up everything online in a well-organized site. My main complaint is the length of the HW, but I guess that has been a problem forever. With enough prep and study time, anyone can do well on his tests. Just don't eff up on any problem, as the grading scheme is pretty rigid. Oh, and he has a cool hair-do.

As stated, homework and labs (= modifying snippets of code in R) are relatively straightforward and easy. Tests are open book/open note/open laptop (!), though the multiple choice questions are extremely tricky, and a few MC makes a big difference in grade. I ended up with a 3.5. Do as many problems in the book as you can to prepare yourself.

His lectures are solid and despite coming from a physics background, he knows what he's talking about. Homework is easy and so is lab. The big problem is his exams! They are very difficult and contain many trick questions (especially in the M.C). His method of making ?s is to take ?s from the book and tweak them. Also, the grading is a bit unfair.

Worst. Prof/instructor. Ever. This guy just plain sucks. I took this class thinking "oh, nobody likes him, but they're probably all wrong. They say he sucks, but he probably isn't that bad." I was wrong. He's the worst. Tests and HW don't correlate. Exams too long. Material on exams isn't from HW. No time to cover all that he expects from you.

absolutely worthless professor. piles on the homework. tests are hard, yet he scares you away from asking about anything. if you must take STAT 390, i am very very sorry becuase i think he is your only option. just prepare to be discouraged from stats
His exams are always full of surprises as it seems he TRIES to trick you. Textbook rarely helps as a supplement to his lectures. Would not recommend unless your GPA can take a huge hit.
Hard tests, inane lectures, and quite useless labs.

Grading scheme is as follows: group all correct responses into a pile, then he will choose "the best" response.  That one (or possibly two) responses will get full credit, and all the other correct answers will be marked down (as already stated - even if they are correct).  Not a bad lecturer though, just expects A LOT.

He knows his material, but has trouble teaching it to students. He came across as pompous and a little arrogant. The textbook is hard to use, with errors and typos throughout. I'd recommend taking a lower level stat class instead. you'll learn the same material, and it will be easier TO learn.
Tough class, tests are only a few problems long so know everything, doesn't give practice exams

Lectures were rarely illuminating, and the textbook is simplistic and not very helpful. Prof seemed pretty pompous. Quiz sections were probably the most boring I have ever had (and the content was provided by the prof). Lectures posted online, which is nice since you'll never want to waste your time going. Try 394/395 instead, or another teacher!!

Very hard prof, but does very good lecturing and really cares about how much his students learn. If you take this class, be ready to work really really hard. Grading is tough, but you will learn a lot.
Multiple choice tests, and weekly quizes on any topic from the quarter.  If these are what you excel at... great.  If not... you are probably not going to get a very good grade.

The class was challenging but Camacho was a helpful and encouraging professor who was accessible outside the class through office hours and EdDiscussion. He takes and incorporates feedback from students into the class and his teaching style is the reason I passed the class.
awesome professor

Professor Camacho is a wonderful professor. He deeply cares for his students and wants you to succeed. However, one gripe with the class is the WebAssign homework. A couple of questions he assigned took SO long to complete. The tests were reasonably challenging, but expected for a calculus class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Charles brought a lovely attitude to math. He was consistent and always happy to help with questions if someone wasn't understanding. He creates videos to watch before very helpful lectures. While slow to respond to emails, he is about as accessible as a professor as I have had. Getting homework done timely is crucial to understanding content.

He's honestly the GOAT. His pre-lecture videos are super helpful, and he uses class time to go through practice problems, which I thought was a great structure. The exams can be tough, but they're fair and reasonable overall. One of the best intro calc series professors.
the absolute goat. actually cares about students, timely emails, so many review materials. makes everything clear. the best at uw
Very kind professor and great lectures.
Has pre recorded lectures that are very helpful. Is great at explaining things, had amazing and fair tests.
Loved him in 126. He is a great teacher who truly cares.

.Very good professor and he made things very clear while going in depth. His tests were extremely hard compared to some of the other classes midterms and I think that was one of the reasons the final was one of the hardest finals in years.
Great professor.
Great lecturer, goes very in depth and seems to genuinely enjoy teaching. Practice exams are a phenomenal way to study for the exams as the difficulty tends to be rather consistent. Nice guy too.
Great lectures but more difficult midterms than other MATH 126 professors.

Camacho is a very kind and helpful professor. He has pre-lecture videos and goes over the material again in class which really helps! The tests aren't the worst, but they aren't the easiest either. He has a lot of office hours and does exam zoom review sessions. Decent amount of homework but it's good practice overall. I definitely recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Charles gives you all the tools you need to succeed and helps make everything really easy to understand! He's super chill and makes an effort to keep us engaged (sometimes when he says 6 7…I just KNOW it's on purpose), and you can tell he really cares about our success and wellbeing. Love that man!

Camacho is the man. He made my first quarter of uw math enjoyable. Lectures were mostly focused on applying things we learned to practice problems. His pre-lecture videos is where you learn how the math works conceptually. He's a really smart guy, can't go wrong with him.

Good. Just pure goodness. Good teaching, good vibes, good test questions (though I'm pretty sure all 126 classes have the same final exams). Office hours can be quite full though. Please go to enhanced office hours and do the problems--they are usually pretty creative and fun!

Charles is a super sweet and caring guy - he earnestly listens to any problem you have about the class, and takes feedback into consideration seriously. Pre-lecture videos are clear, though some topics that show up on Webassigns etc aren't really introduced at all. Quiz Sections are eh because the TAs can be super clueless. Tough class though.
He's a great lecturer and explains the concepts very well! He's also incredibly understanding and very easy to talk to. The midterm questions are also very fair.

Dr. Camacho was a very nice professor to me. I ended up going to many of his office hours and he was always happy to provide help when needed. If you're stuck on a question he will not only help you get through what you were stuck on but stick with you until you finish entirely. Out of 400+ students he knew me by face too which was very nice. 11/10
Love this guy

Camacho is a caring professor who wants you to succeed. He's very kind and soft spoken. He's great at teaching the material, the class and material itself is just extremely difficult. Would take a class taught by him again!

He's an amazing professor, and easy to talk with. He's interested in student learning, and wants everyone to succeed. Calc, sucks and is hard, but he makes it an experience you'll survive and made me want to attend class.

Camacho is genuinely a good calc professor and he explains things very clearly. The problems many students have are just with how calc at UW is overall. Make sure to go to office hours and genuinely take the homework and quiz sections seriously or you'll fall behind on the fast paced content.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i had Camacho for 125/126 last year and i made this account just to say that he is THE GOAT. great pre-lecture videos and lectures, very friendly and approachable guy, just wants to help students get the material. he is the best math professor i've ever had, maybe even the best professor period -- if you get the chance to take his class, do it!
126 was a conceptually difficult class in my option compared to 124 and 125. This guy made the material make sense and he provides a million resources. 10/10

This teacher is amazing! It is very evident that he cares about our learning and does everything he can to make sure that we get the support we need. He holds lots of office hours, utilizes real midterm problems, and gives ample time to ask questions. Content is hard but he does everything he can to make it better. Good lecturer. Just Webassign HW.
Lowk the goat of math

From the sounds of it, it may have just been the quarter I took this class, but the midterms were terrible. The first one was so difficult I saw people leave crying, and the second was so easy the median was 34/35, which made for an awful course grade curve. That being said, I really liked the pre-lecture videos he made for the course.
I came from prof. Perkins. Night and day difference. Word of advice: skip perkins and come to camacho lectures instead. Thank me ltr

Had Camacho for 125 and he was the absolute best, but the way he described 126 went right over my head. Loveless was a fill in for a lecture and it was clear he has mastered how to convey the geometric portion to students. Curve was super high on most tests so impossible to 4.0. Camacho was great for 125 but definitely take loveless for 126.

He makes lots of prelecture videos which are super helpful and important to watch, but they are really nice for reinforcing concepts. His midterms were pretty easy and all had high averages which gave a nice cushion for the final which is always tricky. He is very nice and understanding and definitely wants his students to succeed.

He is a really poor explainer, he gives examples but doesn't give us any strategies for writing proofs on our own. I got a 76 on the final and that was a 4.0 since the entire class failed because of how bad he is at explaining things. It left me really unprepared for the next proof writing class. To his credit, he is very available at office hours.

Camacho genuinely cares about his students and he makes sure lectures aren't extremely boring. He provides pre-recorded lectures on all the main concepts before class and uses class time to solve example problems. The midterms weren't too bad, but the final was much more difficult.
Super great at explaining things, SPOT ON pre-lectures. Charles makes calculus a breeze.

he was a really great professor, very chill and made lectures interesting. the pre-lecture videos were always super helpful, make sure to watch them!! and do the homework, it'll definitely help. weekly quizzes for participation
Super great teacher, he doesn't know how to make tests though. Lectures help, but his pre-class videos are necessary (and also godsent, they're so good). Super nice dude too.
Created an account on here to write this review if that says anything. Prelecture videos rule. Definitely take advantage of office hours throughout the quarter. Great prof overall

Professor Camacho is an amazing professor and you can tell that he genuinely cares about his students. His pre-lecture videos are so organzied and easy to understand, and he is very attentive and gives one-on-one help during the lectures and during office hours. I highly recommend taking him as a professor.

Great Professor. Releases pre-work videos on Edstem that essentially tell you everything you need to know about the topic, making homework easier and giving you a lot more free time than some other professors would give.

Professor Camacho made me love math. His lectures felt quick and easy, and it made me feel super confident with my calculus abilities. His office hours are super chill, he's a very thoughtful person which made it super easy to get help. Seeing someone so passionate about a topic was extremely inspiring, and I really hope I can take Math 125 w/ him!

Charles Camacho is the best math teacher I've ever had. He does not miss a beat during lectures, and is also very funny at times. Camacho made math 125 easy haha.

Quizzes and worksheets during section are graded on participation not correctness.

He does put out a lot of prelecture vids, about an hour or so every night. I recommend watching them.
Great lecturer and the pre lectures are super helpful.

Class was lecture heavy, but he is around to answer questions after. He is a very nice guy, and passionate about teaching and I enjoyed his class in the fall. His examples are very clear, he goes through where equations come from and then he does multiple examples which is helpful. He has good review days before midterms and exams as well.

He's an amazing instructor who takes the time to make sure his students actually understand the material. His class is difficult, but Calc 2 is a tricky topic and Charles does everything right when it comes to teaching. Make sure to watch his pre-lectures! They're super helpful!!
He's really good at lectures and outs our pre-lecture videos that are great for studying for exams and reviewing as well as preparing you for the classes.

I really liked this professor. He gave a really time constrained midterm I but curved it generously to make up for it. I felt like the tests were very balanced and he is very good at preparing you for them if you read the notes and show up to class.

Really clear lectures. Had a pre lecture that went over the basics before the class itself which is worth watching, actual lectures were mostly for tougher problems. Super organised and understanding of his students.

His exams were not well written(he failed to adjust the difficulties) but curves were nice and his lectures are just amazing. Very well organized and makes sure everyone understands the concept. Also very friendly and caring. He is always kind to students whenever they ask questions.

He offered resources for students in canvas and is very kind and happy to answer questions. His pre-lectures and lectures were confusing and hard to follow due to the way he would explain concepts. In class, we would do examples as well but it would be nothing near how complicated the web-assign would be.
Great class structure, explained things well in prelecture videos. It was his first time teaching 126 so he made the first test too hard and the second too easy, but was overall not bad.
Very great professor and on the come up. It is clear that he wants you to learn and succeed despite the horrendousness of the calc series.

Great lectures, semi-tough class. Homework and quizzes aren't hard but he can write some very hard questions for the midterms. Prelecture videos are better than the lectures for learning the material, actual lecture is just practice problems. His lecture problems are always way easier than the exam and quiz questions though.

Very good professor, his lectures a very well spent. He cares a lot about people's learning and holds lots of office hours for extra help. Beware his tests are super tough, but he grades on a curve. Highly recommend.
Great professor and guy. He genuinely cares about helping everyone succeed and is very organized. Class material was consistently posted early and expectations were made very clear very early on.

Professor Camacho is one of the sweetest men ever. He is very kind, and gives lots of resources to help you learn. The content is tough, but there are pre lecture lessons for all lectures, videos, sometimes a few, ranging from 15-20 minutes. All lectures also recorded. The first test he gave was really difficult for everyone but he rounded it well.

A kind professor. His pre-lecture videos are better than the actual lectures. They go over the entire topic in only about 15-20 minutes (double speed). His explanations sometimes use unconventional thought processes that may or may not click for you. Personally, I disliked his method of explaining concepts, but I know some people who liked it.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The pre-lecture content was really amazing and allowed me to fully understand what was going on in class. Camacho is really receptive to feedback and there are lots of resources in order to do well on the exams. Besides being an experienced teacher, he has a great personality and made the lectures interesting and draws well in 3D.

Camacho was an amazing professor for Math 126. The pre-lecture videos were very helpful and were honestly where I learned a bulk of the content. The lectures themselves were focused on going over examples. There were some issues with test difficulties, but he curved them fairly. I felt that his lectures and prepared me well for the final.

Camacho had fantastic lectures that enhanced my learning of the subject. Only bad thing is that he isn't great at writing tests, first midterm he created way too difficult of an exam, second midterm it was much too easy. Very kind man though!
Extremely friendly and approachable. Quiz and exam problems were much harder than the lecture and homework problems.

Brought great enthusiasm to lectures, pre-lecture videos were incredibly helpful. His exams varied a lot in difficulty, final and midterm 2 were easy, while midterm 1 tanked my grade but its content made sense to me once I actually sat down and studied for the final. Overall, excellent lecturer, moderately difficult, but study and you'll do well.

I think this was one of his first times teaching Math 126 because the first exam was brutal and basically tanked everyone's gpa right from the start. The examples he used in class were often way too simple/easy compared to the homework and exams. He's a really nice and understanding guy who will help you if you ask/go to office hours.

I can say this is the best math professor in UW! He's really careful and warm-heart. I got 4.0 in the end and took lots of work but I can say it worth! If you want to take math 126 then choose Charles!!!!!!!!

This man. Boy oh boy, where do I start? This man has been the best math professor I've ever had, his lectures are things of legend. His midterms cause tears of joy. For reference, the second midterm had a MEDIAN of 34/35. Jokes aside definitely take him if you get the chance. Lectures arent mandatory but are incredibly helpful. He truly cares.
Great professor, pre lecture content was super helpful and he was very gracious with his tests, despite the first midterm being pretty tough
Great professor, pre lecture content was super helpful and he was v

Camacho is a really good teacher. First midterm was hard, and second midterm was easy, but the final was fairly written. The pre-lecture videos are incredibly important to learn the content. Camacho was an outstanding teacher and very clearly explained concepts in lecture as well as office hours. You should take him if given the opportunity.

Overall a very kind and lenient professor and pretty decent at explaining concepts in pre-lecture videos + lectures.

However, he‘s rather poor at writing fair exams. This made the IQR for the course extremely narrow and so the curve was harsh. He also did a poor job in the Taylor series unit, and it seemed most ppl had to self teach.

Lectures were really helpful but he did not always cover everything, so make sure to watch the pre-lectures. There was quite a bit of online HW. The first midterm was significantly more difficult than the second midterm or the final. I think it was his first time teaching 126 but he has a good personality and lectures never got boring.
He's a great lecturer but isn't very good at writing exams. Either extremely difficult or too easy. Pre-lecture videos cover everything in lecture, so there really isn't any point of going.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: fought for my life to get a 3.7. he's really nice and decent at explaining concepts (VERY good at drawing 3D models!), but it's funny how he always says don't email me after releasing a grade💀 also the first midterm sent me spiraling and doubting my entire career like i cried several times

Most complaints on Camacho is probably on the the extremities of his exams. His first midterm had 50% median (curved to 72%) while the second midterm had 97% median. By the time others take his class, this shouldn't be an issue since he will know how to give out better exams.

His lectures are great though and he's a very nice and lenient teacher.

I wish I had him for math 124 & 125! His classroom is very accessible and re-sparked my interest in learning math: well structured class, organized canvas page, in depth pre-lecture vids, & notes on OneNote. Attendance only mandatory for discussion sec. If there wasn't a character limit, I'd write essays on how much I recommend and appreciate him
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a good lecturer and the homework pre-lecture videos are really helpful but I have to downgrade a little for the awful first midterm that went over topics not covered in class and was worded terribly. I do believe that overall though its the the 12X series being the worst and less on the professor.
His pre-lecture videos are helpful.

Not a good test writer… the 1st was too hard and involved question types never practiced in class. The 2nd he told us exactly what the questions would be, making it too easy. The order he teaches topics isn't the most strategic; my hs calc teachers structured their content better. He's also good at disappearing when people are bound to email most.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best math professor so far, the content is hard but it's not his fault, Professor Camacho manages to explain them well, and I start to love math. Go to office hour, he's really nice and basically answers all your questions, and do some practice, then you will be just fine :)

Good for his first time teaching the course.
Tests are the biggest graded part, but some credit for the webassign homework. 
Textbook is a supplement so don't use it to learn topics from scratch (not very good book)
Good at explaining things and practice problems. Go to office hours for help
Skipped lectures and did fine, but skip at your own risk.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is such a sweetheart

Great professor who you can tell really cares about his students. Midterm difficulty was a bit weird (the 1st was super hard and the 2nd was super easy), but he was very accommodating after the 1st midterm and adjusted our grades accordingly. This quarter was his first time teaching the class so if you take him later they should be fairly standard.

Easily one of the best professors I've had at UW. His teaching skills are phenomenal and I always absorb information well with him teaching. Beware, as his midterms and finals are fairly difficult, however you can still succeed with a good amount of studying and practice, attending office hours, and doing practice midterms.

LOVEEEEE!!! Best Math Teacher ever. He gives pre-lectures before each lecture session, which was really helpful. Even though midterm 1 was pretty hard, the curve he gave out for the midterm was sooo good!

Although the midterm is hard(but I think it's not that hard, just more calculations and questions), his curve is soooooooo nice!!! Even if I were a professor, I wouldn't get my students high marks so easily. His lecture and pre-lecture are also clear. Love him so much. If you want to have a math class, Camacho is the best choice.
The midterm is too difficult!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Words cannot express my respect for him. I'll never have such a good teacher again.

Camacho is a skilled lecturer and kind professor. Unfortunately, the material (concepts, examples) in his lectures were not anywhere near the same level of difficulty as the homework assignments, midterms, and especially final exam. He can't necessarily control the assignments and exams, as they are department-wide, but they are brutal nonetheless.

Hands down the greatest math prof and maybe overall best prof I have ever had. His class was, for me at least, extremely difficult (probably not what you want to hear), but I was able to get a 4.0. His exams were, in my opinion much harder than the archived exams, but he makes up for it by being an amazing and caring person who knows his stuff!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think this was his first time teaching Calc 2. I found the class to be pretty difficult but I don't think that was his fault. The math department is just crazy. The tests were fair, but I feel like there were some topics during lecture that just weren't explained clearly. I often had to look to other sources for help.

Camacho's lectures were very easy to follow and understand, but were always the simplest version of problems and then we would encounter significantly harder ones on homework and exams. Often made things seem easier than they were. Very nice guy tho and he wants you to do well. Automatic full credit homework extensions were the best.
As someone who nearly failed calc in high school, his teaching really helped me succeed in college calculus
Can't say enough good things, made math fun.

Very accommodating, can tell he really cares about his students. Early in the quarter he ended up providing all students an automatic 2-day extension on all homework and always seemed very happy to answer questions from students in lecture. Homeworks are a lot but they're department-wide so not his fault. Very kind and understanding. TAKE HIM!
Cared for students and was very lenient with late homework. Lectures did feel useless as they only covered very surface level stuff in comparison to the midterms and homework

Fine teacher, but it did feel like his lectures were useless because they were far easier than any of the homework or tests and he did not explain his work very well. My class consistently scored lower on all tests, including the final, by an average of 10%. Seemed like a nice guy though.

Really good professor and would always overstay to help people at MSC past his office hours. Lectures were great at explaining topics. The workload for 124 (Webassign) is the worst out of the math series, and he allowed automatic 2 day extensions for the rest of the Webassigns of the quarter. Exceptionally nice and explains concepts very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The exam and grades are fair.

This class made me feel like I could learn quickly without being overwhelmed. Office hours were always helpful, lecture notes are accessible, and midterm regrade requests were simple. My one complaint is that we couldn't view our final exam unless it was by appointment the next quarter. Still one of the best professors I've had.

Good teacher and gave us plenty of resources to help us pass the class. The only problem I had with the class was the harsh grading of the tests. He does give the option to ask for a regrade but even after the regrade I still felt like I was being cheated. He does not give regrades on finals and he also turned off his email for a week after it too.

Professor Camacho is a great professor! I struggle with math personally but he really wanted me and everyone to succeed. You can schedule a personal appointment with him if you need it. If you need to take calc and aren't great with math I highly recommend this professor.

Professor Camacho has a great teaching style that is very easy to understand, even though the class is faster-paced. Although the class is designed to push you and possibly make you fail, his lectures are very focused on whether you understand the topic. It is very apparent he wants his students to succeed and grow in mathematics.

Great prof! His lecture notes are very accessible & easy to read. He is sincere, makes class fun, and is very interactive. His office hours are short however,  he helps everyone as much as he can.  I would recommend taking his class as someone who's weak in math. Sweet guy!

Charles is very good in explaining the theories, and always give examples in every sub-topics. I always enjoy going into his lectures, the environment in class is very good, his pace was great. The only cons would probably be his handwriting, but overall, Charles is the goat of Math dept.
Charles is the goat honestly, he puts so much work into making sure his students are successful and explains concepts during lecture in such simple terms.

The grading of this course is really harsh. It is the most nitpicking grading I have ever encountered at uw. You would be punished for absurd reasons like "not enough reader scaffolding". Even cse 143 style grading is easier to follow because there is at least a general style guide.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I really enjoy his class since he really cares and put effort into helping all the student understand the concept.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Carly is amazing! She provides most materials in class which is super helpful, and gives amazing feedback tailored to your personal style. Her feedback allows you to hone your craft and push your comfort zone while also making sure your work stays really true to you. Truly an amazing professor and an amazing class!

Professor Carly is a sweet and caring person! She is very orangized on assignments! The painting 292 was a combination of painting with printmaking. I learn lot from both subjects especially printmaking coz we spend most of time at printshop. I really appreciated her time and the class! It was what I look forward everyday to be there!

Carly was awesome and helped me push myself creatively. She helped me discover my painting style, and I looked forward to going to class every day. She also provided materials for us to use in class, so we didn't need to buy more materials, which I appreciated.
He and his TA are tough graders, and they take forever to grade your assignments. It tooks forever to reply your email. It is hard to track your performence.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Really really really hard grader!!!!!!!!!

He and his TA are heavy graders, and they take forever to grade your assignments. Don't try using AI in his class, they would know easpacily for any data class. I wouldn't recommend ChatGPT; maybe another AI


Absolutely, build a study group where u guys can help each other out. I wouldn't pass this class if it weren't for them.
Links lots of helpful resources online so if you miss lectures its easy to catch up/learn the material in your own time. Updates Canvas very timely/regularly which is convenient

Nice class. Attendance isn't mandatory but lectures aren't recorded so if you go the easier assignments are. Prof talks a lot during lecture but the info is good- he's also approachable & helpful. Tests aren't a huge deal, the important assignments are the bi-weekly ones and the project. Pace is good and you learn a lot of applicable things!

Lots of work throughout the week due on a specific due date, but there is also a 48-hour extension with no penalty, which helps a lot. The class is pretty easy if you don't make it hard for yourself. It's pretty simple; just get the final project done with a good group of 3!! Even if u know you don't want another person, add them; it would help!!.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Honestly, the only Best INFO 201 section is Carson Miller's. Trust me, someone who dropped from
Ott Toomet I can finally understand the criteria; the weekly assignments are not too heavy at all.
Midterms are just corrections; the labs are Chill. Just have a good group for the project, and you'll be fine!

Also make sure to do those lecture quizzes

Fall 25 - Pretty easy class if you've coded before. Even if you didn't make sure, you know someone who has. Honestly, if you don't know anyone there, the class will be so hard for no reason, so make new friends; He will also push that on us!!

- Every lecture he has a quiz where the prompt will be only up for 10 minutes 
- The Ta Are Tough Graders
Super chill professor

Boring lecturer but easy grader. Very flexible, sometimes don't even need to attend lectures. Just do the in-class activities and data assignments. Really understanding and nice guy. Explains things step by step. Really easy/not too much workload class.
Awesome person and really enjoyed the class. Lectures and assignments are very detailed and easy to stay on top of. Definitely enjoyed taking the class a lot.

Tbh he yaps a lot and the lectures actually aren't that great, they're very repetitive. You could honestly just skip the lectures and do the in-class activities by yourself outside of class time, they aren't do but it's good to do cause the instructions are all on the assignments. Grading is very lenient and he makes it really easy to have an A.
Great professor who makes the class very easy and enjoyable. Very lenient in grading and late policy. Take him if you can.

Carrie was great, and it's clear she's very passionate about what she teaches. The only thing I didn't like was that most things took a long time to grade. Everything except for the major projects is graded based on completion.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My favorite professor and class so far and Im not an english major
As long as you do all the work, you'll get a good grade. She's very passionate about what she teaches and genuinely cares that students are learning. If you speak up in class, she'll love you.

Very understandable, this was class is her first online class (if I remember correctly) and she very easy to communicate with. A LOT of reading fiction,if you enjoy reading or be able to read fast then it shouldn't be less of a problem. Homework and exams mostly required reading to answer questions and give thoughts, arguments and replies about it.

Carrie uses a grade contract so as long as you complete the assignments with the given grade you wish to work for, its a very accessible 4.0. Everything is based on completion and turning things in on time (she is very understanding though!). Attendance is required and expected but engl 299 was only 50 mins and very manageable.

Carrie is a great instructor who truly cares about the growth of her students. The workload assigned is more than reasonable, and she will always make accomodations as long as you reach out and are respectful.
Hi everyone. i highly recommend you guys to take her class. I am an international student. it was my first time to learn something completely in English. She is pretty helpful
She is really accessible because of how much office hours she has.

Carrie is a passionate professor who cares about her students and social justice. She does grade contracts, so as long as you do everything you sign up to, you get that grade. For papers you do intense group peer-grading, so you get a lot of valuable feedback. She isn't the most organized, but to make up for forgetting something she brought candy.
Carrie's really nice and kind. However, she assigns WAY TOO MUCH homework for a class that meets twice per week.

deduct points arbitrarily, boring lectures, and nearly 30% of the grade for the final project was docked solely due to formatting issues. Absolutely no consideration given to the students' worry on group projects and gpa

lots of homework, come with tough grader and few non sence taken off points. I was told not participate in class and been taken off up to 4 points, but I attend every class and participate in class activity. I got my p9 feedback after the end of the quarter, which cause me lose points in my p11. group work was harsh.

This professor has given me one of the most insufferable experiences of a class ever. Unfortunately, this was a class that I was excited to learn more about, however, with constant unclear assignment expectations, bad communication, and busy work rather than helpful work, I will not be missing this class at all. Please change something.
not bad but so many works
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: A nice professor who clearly cares and the subject -- if you make sure to set aside time and put in genuine effort you'll get a good grade. Beware assignments take longer than advertised. Moreover assignment requirements were incredibly unclear -- little communication between Cayla and TA over expectations and grading criteria led to confusion.

Very easy to get an A in this class, but not in a "Megan doesn't care about looking into submissions" way - she genuinely looks at the effort and care put into an assignment rather than having right or wrong answers. She also gives amazing and thought provoking feedback. Would take again!

Really great professor that puts in 110% effort in all assignment feedback and comes through as a very caring professor even as our class was asynchronous. ENGL 296 was an engaging, yet laid-back class with a grading contract (putting in effort and turning things in on time gets you a good grade). I highly recommend taking it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Megan was a fantastic professor who provided awesome and supportive feedback on all of the assignments.  There were 3 major projects, and you have a lot of room for creativity. This was one of my favorite English classes I have taken, and it is very easy to get an A as long as you participate and complete assignments on time.

This teacher is rude to people with disability accommodations. Any slight miscommunication and she will immediately switch her tone with you and become extremely passive aggressive. Her email was literally an essay about how she thought I was entitled and misusing accommodations. This class is an easy A otherwise. Proceed with caution.

Megan is personable and has your best interest in mind. She values co-learning and caters to student interests. She grades really easy because she values your learning and discovery more than meeting a certain standard. What you learn in this class is largely unique to you and the more you put in the more you'll get out.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Megan is SO understanding and makes an effort to reassure everyone that she's there for you not only for class assignments, but for emotional support as well. She cares about peer interaction and effort; as long as you put a fair amount of effort into the class, you'll do great! Don't hesitate to reach out to her if you need help (for anything)!!

Dr. Callow cares about student success. She is willing to meet to help you succeed, and she will provide feedback if you go to her and ask for it. (feedback won't come to you, you have to get it). Make sure to engage in lectures, come to class prepared, and be active in your revisions for both yourself and your peer reviews.

A great upper level Biology class. Very interesting class content, no exams, and the teaching staff is very willing to help with weekly exams. She is a very engaging lecturer, and labs are low-stakes!

The class topic was interesting. The problem is that this class is a major 'You should know all this before I even teach you it' vibe and the grading reflects it, and she won't help you on any of it until after she grades it. Not to mention she just says you lost points and don't tell you what is wrong.

Emily is a no nonsense kind of person. I had her for FHL 420, and she did an excellent job of balancing out the rigor of the other courses with a more exploratory, ecology-focused program. She makes you feel like what you think a marine biologist is as a child. Highly recommend taking her class at least once for the fun of it.

Prof. Bitz definitely leans on math in lecture, but it is very clear that she is genuinely interested in making sure everyone understands the course material (and will spend a lot of her own time outside of class helping people out). Super smart and super kind person.

She is the NICEST professor that the UW has EVER had. She has AMAZING connections (having visited many top schools, I know this). With a LOR from her, I got top student fellowships into BOTH UChicago and Brown (and almost Yale) with a 3.18 GPA. Without her, I wouldn't be alive today. My biggest regret in life is that I didn't discover her earlier.

The course content was awesome, and it would've been a super easy class if the information was presented in a more interesting way. If you work well in lectures and classes that are impersonal and uncreative, go for it. If you prefer more stimulating classes that force you think outside the box, stay away. She's a sweetheart, but she's so quiet!

I was not interested in global warming at all but I found this class interesting. There were many extra credit opportunities. Make sure to go to quiz section because there is participation points for that. Not a hard class if you study and read the book.

She's a very nice and accommodating person. There are many extra credit opportunities and you can drop all sorts of lowest scores throughout the quarter. Pretty interesting course material, hard to sit through 2 hour lecture. It's a nice class to take if you have any interest in global warming.

Easy teacher, many grade booster opportunities. Yes there's a lot of "facts", but nothing too hard to remember if u go to class. She puts up summaries every week, even podcasts online if u miss lecture or want to review! Quizzes r tough, but not THAT bad. She curves the grade with other scores so no complaints here. Book = interesting read.

One of the best lecturer at UW! It's 2hrs long, probably why ppl would say it's boring, but I found the material very interesting! Clicker q's help boost grades, gives extra credit on top of that, and many many opportunities to get a good grade. DEFINITELY RECOMMEND for this class and if she taught other ATMS classes, I would take them with her!

shes a good person, very nice lady. She gives a lot of extra credit opportunities, and a lot of dropping opportunities too which is hood. However, her slides are unorganized, too much info is on there, and completing the homework is basically like a Ctrl-F treasure hunt between slides.. Other than the fact that this is not a GPA booster, not bad.

Her voice is so boring.. she doesn't make interesting contents and facts with humor. Her intonation is weird and her voice seems so nervous and people rated 4.0 for easyness and in my opinion, it is overly exaggerated. Her tests are complicated and hard. She doesn't intentionally twist her words, but the question wording is incomprensible sometimes

This class is super boring. She is a very nice teacher, however she doesn't sound confident when she talks. She tries to help the best she can. I didn't like how she didn't have a grading rubric so I guess my grade will be a surprise! 3 MC. Cum. Final. Tests fair, just memorization of facts and numbers. Book was not needed.

THIS CLASS IS PLAIN BORING.There is a lot of information that you have to memorize:( Homework is hard. I heard that ATMS 111 is a good GPA booster class, but IT'S NOT. She and her TAs make midterms way too hard.

Cecilia is the nicest and most amazing professor ever (and I *really* mean it). Unlike most professors, she actually cares about her students, and she's always willing to bend the rules a bit if it means that the students learn more. Thanks to her, I'll probably end up at Chicago or Caltech, rather than end up rejected everywhere I apply.

she's very nice, and definitely knows what she's talking about, but stuff just gets plain boring.  fortunately the online quizzes really help, and all in all she's one of those teachers that really wants her students to do well, so overall, I'd recommend the class, but bring an iPod or something to do on your laptop

One of the best professors at UW in terms of grading clarity and genuine engagement with the class. The structure of each class is roughly the same, but every session is different and focuses on a different speech, and its so clear that the professor understands the material inside and out. Always urges participation in the lecture.

Repetitive, kinda boring. Quiz every lecture, lots of reading. No rubric for papers. Doesn't use slides, writes on whiteboard with bad, sometimes illegible, handwriting. Easy to get a good grade in the class, the process is just annoying. Content isn't worth the time spent.

One of my favorite classes and professors! Leah is super engaged with her students in every lecture and really strives to make it possible to succeed in the class. She offers a huge extra credit assignment and also drops your 4 lowest reading quizzes and in-class writing assignments which allows for absences and mistakes. And no midterm or final!

attendance is mandatory since we have work sheets and quizzes due on the day of class which are timed, the work sheets you cannot do if you did not attend class since she requires you to pull examples that she specifically said in class otherwise doesnt give credit so you have to pay close attention to lectures that are boring speeches

by far the worst class ive taken at uw. boring lecturer. too much reading. difficult tests. and so inflexible when it comes to grading. it makes all the work you do not worth it. i personally will never be taking a class with her again lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ceccarelli is one of those rare teachers who acknowledges that she has as much to learn from students as she has to teach them. She will help you develop an idea and give you a new perspective on your own interests. She wants you to give your honest time and thought to the work. The way she presents rhetoric makes it come alive and is inspiring.

Sweet teacher, but the class is so repetitive and boring... Expect to read 40/+ pages of speeches every Monday and Wednesday. Quizzes before every lecture which can be easy if you look up keywords in the text, but the midterms really require you to know all of the 50/+ vocab words and provide direct examples from the speeches. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy
