reviews.comment: Well, Public Speaking is never easy. But, professor did an OK job of making the class seem a little interesting. The content is hard. 3 speeches cover 75% of your grade. If you have trouble dealing with nervousness, this class does little to help that.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you attend class and take notes you will be fine. There are easy 4 question multiple choice quizzes most days but the midterms and finals are open book so if you have good notes you'll get a good grade. Very minimal work outside of class

Tests are easy if you attend class and take notes. Daily quizzes on the reading, also easy if you read the texts. Lots of reading but not very dense. Grades on 4.0 scale so 3/4 doesn't equal 75% but a 3.0.. Pretty awesome, very enthusiastic about a students understanding

Not the best lecturer she hops around & seriously not good public speaking skills BUT her class wasn't terribly hard. If you came to class & took notes on what was going on you were going to do well in the class because she allows open notes (SO TAKE NOTES) Honestly the class was mostly boring but if you want a good grade it's a good class to take.
Great class! Professor Ceccarelli is very organized and competent about her discipline. The live debates were also a plus. Exams and homework assignments are fair.
Was a great lecturer

Overall pretty easy class, however lectures are extremely boring and hard to sit through. Prof Ceccarelli's lecturing method consists of reading her notes word for word off of her iPad. If you're looking for an easy VLPA class or your exceptionally intrigued by the topic of debate, this would be a fine class to take.

Lectures are very boring.  I had her as a public speaking prof, and she does not conduct herself in a very professional manner, especially for public speaking.  Students tallied the number of times she said "um" and "uh" during a 50 minute lecture, and usually got around 350 times/lecture.  She is pretty boring, but sections are interesting

She is alright, the video clips are a little rediculous at times. I did reasonably well in this class, but I had to work for it. There is alot of stupid busywork, pretty much due every other day. You need to go to class, as pop quizzes will happen the day you skip. real talk.

Very, very easy!!! She gives handouts so you don't have to take notes and the tests are also really easy (mult choice). She uses lots of video examples which is really helpful. Class is somewhat boring, but worth taking, especially for the live debates.
Like every other prof on campus...too liberal! Hated the stupid video clips, she seriously shows 8-10 every lecture.
No Comments

she was a decent lecturer, and showed clips from the daily show and other various tv shows. the powerpoint slides were posted online, which was very helpful, but it made most kids not come to class. didn't care for the 'busy work' but tests weren't difficult and the class topic was interesting enough.

Lectures are boring. There are long essay assignments, quiz, discussion post due almost weekly. You can only miss 5 points out of 400 points to get 4.0 in class. Asked her respectfully if she would consider rounding 0.08 points up so I could get 4.0, and she was passive-aggressive: "I will not respond to a plea." I would've taken no as an answer...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't know why I took another class with Lowe. I regret it now. I took ANTH228 last year and took ANTH 469 recently. It was long, dry and the quizzes were so difficult. Lots of reading and major papers to write. Instructions seemed unclear and the quizzes were on obscure content not major themes or learning objectives.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is the second class I've taken with Prof Lowe, and I've loved both. Clear grading guidelines, good feedback, and fair grading. Would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was one of the most boring classes I have ever taken.

I really enjoyed this class with Prof. Lowe. There is so much reading (150 pages a week) but minimal homework where you get to pick what you are passionate to write about (within the topic). 5, 3 page essay assignments, 5 discussion topics, 5 easy quizzes. Short lectures. Easily reachable via email. I will take another of her classes. Good content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Lowe was extensively knowledgeable on the topics that this course involved. Her ability to articulate the necessary topics was helpful when it came to completing assignments related to the material. This was a full length summer course that was made up of 5 modules.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The worst class I have ever taken. Lowe is uncaring and unkind and lacks the motivation to see her students succeed. Her assignment instructions are unclear and confusing and she is unwilling to explain without a disgusting attitude. You read a very packed online blog this course it seemed which is hard to follow and never-ending. don't take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: It was all just okay? Like it wasn't terrible, but it wasn't great. The amount of reading was sort of ridiculous. Also if you already have a grasp on environmental issues, the whole class becomes even more tedious. There are a lot of papers--however, they aren't long and they are open-ended so that you can write what you're passionate about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof Lowe was a good teacher, but not my favorite. Asynch class was really boring and having a paper due every other week along with a quiz and discussion got boring fast. Be prepared to read full books and write papers that have rather vague descriptions. This class was interesting, as I learned a lot, but not the most fun or engaging one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I'm kicking myself for taking her again (I took JSIS351 too). Like before, assignments have vague descriptions, so it's hard to know what to do. She offers little feedback on assignments. A module assigns 75 pages of textbook reading with no heads up, so then you're scrambling to keep up. Boring professor, not engaging at all. My worst class ever!

4 textbooks, lots of reading! This class is fairly easy, homework is manageable, but Lowe is not very engaging. I liked this material, but video lectures were boring. She frequently spoke of her time in Indonesia and the book she wrote, which isn't really all that impressive. Syllabus lacked clear grading criteria. Still, easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Amazing class. I learned a lot, and I had an amazing experience. The only thing that I didn't like was the grading. It was based on points. A 390/400 is a 3.9, a 380/400 is a 3.8, and if you miss a point, you cant get it back. However, the class wasn't hard as long as you do the required readings and material.
I had a great experience, in fact, taking another class with her for the next quarter. Easy class and easy grader, gives good feedback.

dislike her very much. she doesn't know how to give out clear instructions for the assignments she's giving out and when you email her for clarifications, she responds with a fat attitude. her lectures doesn't make sense, very disorganized while she reads off her paper.

Lowe was very nice, but I did not like her teaching style. She was very lecture heavy, often relying on movies and guest speakers. Directions for assignments were very vague so I wasnt exactly sure what I was supposed to do. Also I feel like most assigned reading wasnt important to the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Old and always so serious. She wouldnt give me a group and was told to work on a research project by myself. You have to be in class to take notes or else youll be cluelessly staring at your computer screen during the quiz every Wednesday.

Took Global Environment online and loved it. I would definitely take Professor Lowe again. The class had 5 lessons for 10 weeks so 1 every two weeks and just one written assignment / quiz per lesson so the work load was very manageable. I thought she was a very reasonable grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She cares a lot about her political views, but she doesn't seem to care much about students.  Lacks charisma to excite students.  Slipshod feedback.  Seems overly reliant on guest speakers, film, and group activities, making it seem as if she doesn't like teaching.  One of the worst teachers I've ever had.

I took Celia's  "Climate Change and Global Health Class." It was horrible. My group was amazing, but they were the only good thing about the class. The lack of information pertaining to our essays and projects made it twice as hard for each student. I never knew what my papers were suppose to be about and had to "wing" it each time.
ehh...
No Comments
No Comments
Her lecture is not down to earth. She does not seem to have any talent in teaching!
She doesn't seem to know her material.

Well her lectures techniques may seem to be a little different, she makes the student pay more attention and learn more material faster.  She is a extremely fair grader and knows the material that she is speaking of.  She is a extremely good teacher.
Great lecturer, very clear explanations, would take again.

Luiz is an excellent professor. CSE 351 has some very fascinating content, which Luiz explored in a way that helped students understand. He used metaphors and analogies effectively to help me get complicated topics. 10/10 would take again.

His lectures are amazing, clear, and precise, and he is enthusiastic. He even recorded an additional lecture for us to help us better understand an especially confusing topic.  He is ready helpful, friendly, and accessible outside of class. If you can't attend his office hours, he will find time for you, even if it means staying late on Friday.

Great French teacher, definitely cares about her students and you will learn a lot. However, if you don't show up for practically every class you won't pass. A bit of a tough grader as well, and won't give you the information you missed if you were absent. That being said, great teacher and she cares.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class was really great. It was really obvious that she wants you to succeed and if you show up the quizzes and tests are not difficult because she reviews what will be on the test with the class throughout the unit. I really enjoyed this class and the other reviewers probably didn't go to class which is why they found it difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Entertaining, tough but fair. really cares about the students which is nice! Some of these other reviews must be from people who didn't show up or try very hard. I really liked this class (and it was an intensive summer class so that's saying alot.) Really knows her stuff

Dantzel was a wonderful teacher. I had a lot of fun in her class and even though the class was mostly review for me, I felt that I actually learned quite a bit. She is very kind, helpful, and her expectations as well as her accent are clear and easy to understand.

Class was easy, but found she couldn't fully answer some grammar questions. It often felt like class time was being wasted and not very useful. She's not a difficult grader at all, but I didn't feel like I got much out of it.

She is very good at what she does. If you ask for help, she's willing to be there, and she makes an effort to interact and connect with students. Sometimes, her grading techniques are a little unfair (on presentations/interviews), but overall, she's very generous with grades. As long as you study and participate, the class is doable.

Easiest class I have ever ever taken. She doesn't teach anything though, only the numerous online assignments do. All the guys think she's hot, so they like her.  To be honest, she's not even that good at french and makes mistakes all the time. She ruined my favorite subject for me

Dr. Celeste is awesome! She is ridiculously intellectual and hilarious. Lots of reading in this class but it is all interesting and fun. I don't usually feel comfortable speaking up in classes but she is so sweet, open, and insirational that I felt totally comfortable raising my hand to answer questions when I knew the answers. Love her!!
Bad and irresponsible Pro.. Avoid her at all cost !!

One of the worst classes I have ever taken at UW. The difficulty level is that of a high school class and her course content is merely a painful repeat of everything you learn in 201 and 202. The busy work is outrageous, her lectures are unorganized and explanations are not clear. No one ever knows what she is looking for. Waste of your time!!

She was really nice and when she actually was teaching she was really good, but a lot of the time she just read off of the slides, and it would get really boring. The tests are really long, and I think kind of hard. There are some really obscure questions about the texts.
Manoucheka has great energy, very clear, and is great to be around.  Her test are a little to long for my taste, but what is on the test is what she covers in class.

Cecilia is a fantastic professor! I had her for 2 quarters; a spring prep seminar then during a summer study abroad. She was incredibly knowledgeable and is clearly passionate about what she teaches. Furthermore, she will do everything she can to ensure that students understand the material. Molto bene!

Cecilia is one of my favorite professors of all time. I was lucky enough to study abroad with her, and would love to learn from her again. She is hilarious, caring, and clearly passionate and knowledgeable. She could be teaching me how to cut a piece of paper in two and I would come away feeling more confident in my abilities. Simply amazing!

I had the pleasure of taking two quarters with Cecilia and going on a study abroad trip with her. She is a great professor, very excited about the material and really wants to make sure you learn. She pushed us in unexpected ways but ultimately taught a lot and in an really enjoyable personable way.

I took two quarters of class studying the intersection of Italian history, literature, and the environment with Cecilia. She cares about her students and offered extra time outside of class for help. Her knowledge on Italian history and current events seemed to be boundless. I've never had a teacher who brought so much enthusiasm to class!

Cecilia is greatly committed to her role as a teacher and works extremely hard to make her courses structured and engaging. She is extremely personable and kind and is open to discussions outside of class. I am so thankful I got the opportunity to have Cecilia as a professor.

I took a spring course with Cecilia, intended as preparation for a summer study abroad, also taught by Cecilia. She is an energetic and charismatic teacher, and it's clear that she cares deeply about the success and well-being of her students. She's also easily the best language professor I've had, lei è una professoressa fantastica!

I took her a few semesters ago, students would run through a brick wall for her, she is incredibly respected and by far the best professor in the Italian&French department at UW. If you not only want to learn a language but also want to learn about Italy and it's culture take her. She's passionate and will do everything she can to get you an A.
Best Italian prof ever!! Take her!!

Cecilia is awesome. She is funny, kind and tells great stories to mix things up. She went out of her way to set up review sessions before every test and she is super helpful if you need it. She teaches to all levels of learners and gives chances for those doing well to move ahead and for those struggling to catch up. Could not recommend more!

Cecilia is passionate and energetic and has a great sense of humor. I loved her classes and I am taking another class with her next quarter. I have learned so much Italian in just two months (Winter quarter is short) and my friends from Italy are so impressed now whenever we talk through Skype. She cares about your learning!! It's a fun class!! :)

Few professors have the ability to capture & maintain the classes respect and attention like she does. What I like most about Cecilia is that she goes great lengths to ensure the success of her students. Not only is she insightful and know the material brilliantly but she is also hilarious (which makes the class fun and enjoyable). Highly recommend
Cecilia Strettoi is a truly caring individual. While I struggled in her class, which was a seminar with a five credit work load, she genuinely cared about the subject. She is passionate and kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I love Cecilia!! She is a phenomenal professor and goes out of her way to make sure you understand the material. She truly cares about her students and keeps class exciting and fun. She's also super helpful and hosts tutoring sessions if you're struggling with the material. È una dei professori più bravi dell'università!

Cecilia is an awesome professor who truly cares about her students.  She is definitely a tougher grader than most, but is constantly giving extra help to any student that needs it.  Her energy made classes enjoyable.  I recommend taking a course with her.
Understands the things that English speakers would have trouble with and really pounds out the lumps.

Cecilia was a wonderful instructor for many reasons. 1.) she is very energetic and passionate about what she teaches, and a very lively person in general. 2.) She cares about her students' learning and is very helpful and will help you if you need it. 3.) you will never get bored or fall asleep in this class if she can help it.

Cecilia is by far the best instructor in the italian department. it is clear that she enjoys coming to class everyday, she talks to students as if they are her colleagues. Not only did I learn a lot, but she takes the time to get to know each student and recognize what their strengths and weaknesses are. you have to do the work though, its hard!

I took this as an 8:30 class and I still really enjoyed it because she's such an amazing professor. She gets to know all of her students and really cares that they understand the language. Overall one of the best professors I've ever had and I wish I could take 102 with her.

Cecilia is great. She really takes an interest in her students. She clearly loves Italy in all regards and genuinely wants you to continue to study, and will gladly help you do that if you choose. She has been a great mentor for me!
Cecilia is amazing! Her passion for the language is contagious. She is strict but her methods really helps you learn the language efficiently.

Cecilia is a wonderful professor. She can be rather difficult, and does push students to pronounce correctly, but it is very helpful to the class. I enjoyed her stories and means of teaching. She is intense but very effective.

Also had 101 with her. She snaps at you, she can be loud, and she will really push students to pronounce well because you sound stupid if you don't later. She's hard but obviously wants EVERYONE to learn. She will probably like you more if you talk to her and try hard...duh. Great professor for those who really want to learn the langauge.
Great!!!  An amazing Italian teacher!

So helpful, very clear, with a very effective teaching style that lacks excessive homework. Her grading style is fair, if not lenient, and she made me more excited to continue my education in Italian.
She is too strict, and noisy. Also rude at times.

Her teaching style has declined in the years shes been here. In my class she chose favorites and made it clear who she did and did not like. I dont think her grading style was very fair towards those she did not like, and I feel like she spoke english too much. Out of class, shes nice, but she made me like italian less.

harshest grader in the department, but not unfair. she seems scary because she's loud and has a strong personality, but i liked her a lot. she's very kind and caring, but she will not take any crap from you.
She's great!
She is amazing. If you're the type of person who doesn't like to speak a lot in class be prepared, you WILL be speaking a lot!  Definitely recommend!
Cecilia is amazing!  She loves what she does and it shows.  Her enthusiasm makes it fun to be in class.  She's in high demand, but take her if you can!

Cecilia is a great teacher, very nice. She's very animated and excitable however and she once screamed at us for waving instead of clapping. Not an angry lady, but an intimidating one. NOT FOR THE FAINT OF HEART.
She is a great teacher! I'm so glad i took this class. Fell in love with Italian and she is great and teaching it. Light homework every night but so intruiging. LOVE HER!
Terrific teacher.  Extremely clear and totally open to help you during office hours.  Very enthusiastic and fun.  Her lessons will stick with you if you plan on taking more Italian!
Take the class if you want to learn about the planets and better if you do this in person, and also take advantage of the office hours as well.

Syllabus did not outline units or due dates. Due dates changed frequently, mismatches homework and units. Scattered unlocking of assignments problematic as a full time worker. Assignments nearly entirely multiple choice, with correct answers never provided. Be prepared to do your own research constantly. Textbook had errors, lacks accessibility.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She really doesn't understand astronomy.  Not the brightest star in the sky.

Cisneros is a very flexible professor & wants her students to succeed. The syllabus  lays out all work for the quarter with due dates. Sometimes assignment explanations can be confusing and in-class discussions are kinda pointless, but the lectures are helpful for the homework. Not really about the planets, moreso a physics class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Super easy class. Good as an intro to the subject if you care, and good for an easy A if you don't. But some assignments are weird and rely on material not taught in the course. Online class so I didn't get to know her, but she seemed nice enough.

I liked the content of this class, but some of the assignments were annoying. A discussion post due every week in which you have to post your own response at least 24 hours before responding to 2 other people, sometimes I would forget since Canvas would show the due date as being on the Friday (when in reality it is a Thursday). Busy but easy work.
The professor assigns so much homework weekly, but is not involved at all. Recorded lectures are years old, and all communication is done through the TA's.

I was given the wrong grade in her course and when I asked for it to be corrected she agreed she made an error then made no change for 3 months, when I asked again she said it was "Not her problem." I saw no change to my grade until I got the Dean involved.
Why would there be at least 24 hrs gap after you post your discussion post to reply to your classmates? Also, she doesn't want to communicate through email. Somehow she is obsessed with office hours.

The class is extremely easy, but Prof. Cisneros' contribution to the class is nonexistent. The answers to quizzes aren't in her lectures, you have to google them, so I eventually stopped watching the lectures. Only the TAs grade, so she adds nothing to the class. It's a shame, because the content is fascinating, but I learned nothing despite a 4.0.

Dr. Cisneros is a quirky, fun, and funny professor who teaches fascinating material in an accessible way. Being in class was interesting every day, workload was minimal with most coming from the textbook and subsequent homework which was never too bad, and there were no high-stakes exams. If you have any interest in astronomy and physics, take her.

Professor Cisneros is quirky but very knowledgeable, and might come off as less qualified because of her silliness. I love her as a Chicano cause she uses Spanish phrases every so often. You will surely be told "échale" for answering a question correctly at some point. I found her very loving and learned a lot. She also brings her dog to lectures.

Cisneros is a really engaging and motivating professor, she wants you to do well and learn as much as possible. there's a lot of work in and out of class but that's to be expected for a 5 credit NSC and RSN. it's nothing unmanageable and it's all doable. going to class is extremely important, don't skip. content is vv interesting. no exams too!

The course was so easy and relaxing since there were no exams or tests in trade for no late work accepted. The TA's are really helpful with each lab. Prof Cisneros is super aware of how complex some of the topics are so she's super understanding and ready to help with questions and allows us to use google for any homework or quizzes.

Taught astronomy in a very interesting manner. Comprehensible for people not attuned to math and astronomy. Many opportunities to earn points on assignments. Wants us to succeed and become good thinkers.

Took her online course and had to say it was pretty easy! There's a lot of work like discussion posts, online HW, lectures + quizzes, lab worksheets. Most of the answers you can find online for the HW and quizzes. There are NO exams, but in exchange, Prof. Cisneros accepts NO late work. I recommend taking the online version if possible!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Day 1 she tells us it doesn't matter if our mom dies or if we have COVID (her examples), she does not give extensions on assignments. She seems to love giving "tough love" to her students and clearly thinks she's very cool. She's just not very nice. Also good luck reaching her outside of class. The class is easy but she just rubbed me the wrong way
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof Cisneros has some great lectures, she keeps it interesting. I took the online class and enjoyed it. There were a few things that made it difficult, like the organization. You'll have to do a LOT of research on your own if you're going to get even close to passing this class. Was also a little reading heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Labs were easy and there are no major exams, but beware of pop quizzes in class (graded on participation mostly). Sometimes lectures could get a little all over the place, but the TA's really held the class together, and even brought us snacks for lab sections:)

The lectures fantastic funny. but she is bad with tech. TA's grade so strictly. about 4 assignments a week. Each one is 10-30 mins. you're going to want a (online)study group. one assignment in each category gets dropped at the end, there is no latework very strict because they drop a week. No final exam or midterm(s). last EC is up to 1%.

She's hilarious and all the work is pretty easy if you took physics and algebra in high school. If you didn't, the TAs explain it really well in section. There are a lot of opportunities for extra credit and no midterm or final, can lectures are really fun because Dr. Cisneros makes them interesting

Overall, easy class because there are no tests, finals, or quizzes, but grading is harsh, and the professor never responds to emails or canvas messages. There are multiple assignments that take a lot of time and require you to go outside. Most quiz answers you can find on Quizlet. Also, grading was unclear in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Cisneros' ASTR150 asynch section was ran well. Clear expectations and nothing was unreasonably hard. The class was however, tedious as there were many assignments in general and some assignments required us to do eccentric things such as go outside and take photos of pinecones.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: very good professor

I was expecting the class to be much harder but professor Citko is very nice and helped a lot during office hours which made the quarter a lot easier to get through. There are some big concepts in syntax but the professor is easy to get along with so I definitely recommend taking this class (even for fun! yes! syntax can be fun!)
Really good professor for a difficult subject. Barbara did a great job this quarter

I loved Prof. Citko! Syntax isn't my strong suit and we sometimes moved through topics quickly, but she did her best to keep the entire class on pace. Grading was super lenient, but the professor and TA gave good feedback, so it didn't feel as if I wasn't learning anything. Played livestreams of puppies during the 10 minute breaks!!!

I very much enjoyed Professor Citko's class. She is very friendly and approachable and does her best to help all her students. The way the class is structured is very forgiving in terms of grading, so it is quite easy to succeed. (All quizzes are open note with unlimited attempts and she drops the lowest quiz and HW score).

Difficult class but Citko is super good at presenting the content clearly. Class is mostly her lecture with a little bit of group work but she provides correct answers/explanations/alternative examples as much as we need. Grading on the weekly homework is really easy as long as it seems like you tried
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Citko is one of the best syntax professors I've ever had. She is extremely clear and has a talent for simplifying complex concepts. The class isn't easy per se, as a lot of reading of dense material is expected.  Concerning the projects, she will be very straight forward with you on their quality and tell you how to improve your work. Very helpful!

She is boring and not good at explaining things. Her classes are confusing and sometimes if feels like she doesn't know what she is talking about. She makes us do presentations and long papers, totally unnecessary.
Citko is very engaging. I like how she always adds something fun in each lesson to keep us interested and understand the material. She is very fair in grading.

One of the best teachers I've ever had. She is an expert in her field, and it shows. Super sweet, helpful, approachable, clear, engaging, has VERY reasonable expectations, and genuinely cares about her students' success.

I had her for both LING 200 and LING 462, and I think she is much more in her element when she has a small class (e.g. she doesn't like to use PowerPoint). In the syntax series, she's a good lecturer, her class moves at a fine pace, and she's very approachable. I highly recommend her there.

I have had Professor Citko for LING 200, 461, and 462. She is indeed in her element with Syntax. She is always pleasant to deal with and takes a GENUINE interest in making sure her students actually grasp the material. If you get to choose a Syntax professor, she is wonderful.
Am I really the only person that enjoyed Citko's class!? She isn't the most enthusiastic about class, but the material is straightforward and she knows what she's talking about.

The people who gave her a bad rating all had her for LING 200, but for LING 461 I thought she was great. Her explanations were good, she was helpful outside class, she had very realistic expectations, and moved at a reasonable pace. Maybe she is just someone who teaches better in her own element (syntax) than introductory level courses.

Avoid taking it with her! She makes linguistics terribly boring and I pretty much learned everything from my TA and the book(not her).She was not at all helpful. Don't even bother going to lecture. It's a waste of time because she gives horrible explanations and drags out unnecessary irrelevant topics. Horrible use of examples. Very bad speaker.

I don't know where to begin with this woman. She is terrible at explaining concepts. She drags out topics and is never clear about what she is trying to teach her students. I regret taking this class because those 10 wks were a waste of my life. If you're considering her class, rethink your decision. I've never had a teacher that was so inadequate!

Pretty easy if you are just looking for some VLPA credit. But don't expect to be super engaged during class. Some topics are pretty interesting, but she just reads off her slides when she could be inspiring enthusiasm! Boring.

The way Professor Citko is teaching is slow. Especially for the subject of linguistics. It would be better if she speed up her talking with the powerpoints but you can basically miss a few lectures and come to sections, without missing much. If you miss lecture, you might have to find out some things in section or carefully reading the book.
She is really boring and kind of annoying. She takes to long to explain things. Going to class isnt really necessary as long as you skim through the book

She is not a very good professor at all. She sits at the front of the class and takes more time than necessary to explain something that could have taken a minute. And then once she has taken too long to explain the easy stuff, she just speeds through everything once the class has ended. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HER!!!!!

Barbara Citko is an excellent professor, with a very broad base knowledge of linguistics and more specifically syntax. Her accent (Polish) can be a little be grating at times, but otherwise she is an excellent teacher and seems to enjoy teaching a lot. I would highly recommend her to anyone interested in Linguistics.
Online Fall 2022 - Cindy is SO nice but I really don't like how she teaches

This class (Community Engagement), seems to be way better for her to teach than the management one. Cindy definitely knows her stuff and is one of the nicest people I've ever met but her grading is...interesting. I like the way she encourages student interaction on Canvas. Class was not hard and had 3 very engaging assignments. I'd recommend her!
Nice person teaching horrible content. Assignments are not useful. Goes off-topic a lot. Appreciate, however, that she is willing to talk about anything and help you with ANYTHING.

Very, VERY nice person who is able to help you if you need anything, but the class content is awful and should not be required in the MLIS program. While management is relatively important to learn, the curriculum itself is outdated and does not take into consideration new developments.

She seems like a perfectly nice person but she's off her rocker as an instructor. Very disorganized and goes on long tangents. We only had around 10-20 minutes of ACTUAL lectures a day in a 2 hour long class, the rest was completely useless. The essays were just busy work that didn't show what we learned at all.

My advice: take this class if you are an INFO major looking for an easy major elective. Assignments are very easy and readings are interesting enough to make you want to do them. Marika is a slow grader and responds slowly to emails, but she is a really friendly person and a good lecturer.
Prof. Cifor had interesting lectures and was very kind. She made going to class fun. Assignments aren't too bad. We did too much in class group work though.

She is super kind, caring, and a wonderful person. The class I had with her was really disorganized, but that was because we were figuring things out as a class. There weren't many assignments and not a lot of work in general, mostly the final project. One of the nicest professors I've experienced in terms of patience and friendliness alike.
Awesome teacher. Very knowledgeable about archival studies, good lectures and interesting assignments/readings. Fair grader. Confusing Canvas page layout.
You will learn a lot in her class. Course content is fascinating and assignments are very useful for people interested in archival work. She is an easy/fair grader.
Not too difficult but a very insightful course. Professor Cifor is AWESOME.

Marika is very nice but often goes on rants that somehow connect back to the class. She is kind of a pushover in that you can modify assignments to give you the most creative and meaningful outcome. I LOVED the book we read, Data Feminism, and the other course readings in this class.

She is very scattered with her lectures and slides. Most topics presented were extremely interesting, especially the readings, however her lectures are hard to follow because of how fast she talks. She does make an honest effort to meet with students and get to know them, especially with group projects. Easy on grading. Interesting class at least.

Among the best classes I have had at the iSchool. Professor Cifor actually knows the material and does not dumb things down by having students teach themselves and do endless busy work or by using a parade of guest lecturers. She really cares about what we get out of her class.

Marika is very kind and a great people person. She was a great lecturer, very clear with her instructions, and gave a lot of feedback on the final. She allows you to express who you are in class as well!

I took Info 402 with Professor Cifor last quarter and I really cannot say enough about how excellent of a professor she is. She teaches a unique curriculum with very light reading but very useful and essential information about DEI. Additionally, she is very calm, kind, and resourceful.

Professor Cifor is probably one of the most well-liked professors in the iSchool. She is so kind and caring that it's hard to hate her. A lot of her assignments and activities are really fun, especially in the second half. The class is very lecture-based, but the content, readings, and (hybrid) structure are very well-thought-out.

Dr. Cifor is amazing. She's so sweet and kind, and she's literally always ready to help you if you need it. This class was online when I took it and for a graduate class was very manageable. Readings were excellent. A must-take for MLIS students interested in archival services/administration. My one criticism is that she responds slowly to emails.

Marika is very kind and one of the best professors in the iSchool as far as her lecturing goes. It didn't really feel like a 400-level class with the content but I did enjoy it thoroughly. She is very accommodating and willing to work and meet with you.

Marika is great. She's super helpful and cares a lot about student success. Only reason why I'm not giving her a 5 is because of some issues I had with this class's hybrid structure. Do the work, attend and participate, and be creative on assignments and you will be MORE than fine. Visit her in her office, she's very approachable in 1-1 settings.
This class was a lot more reading-heavy than test-heavy. Professor Mastrangelo is incredibly understanding and easy to talk to. Just be ready to read and write a ton about the textbooks!

I had INDE with her Spring quarter. I thought lectures were helpful and tests were fair. I didn't love the required quizes but in the end they didn't impact my grade that much. Christina herself is approachable and kind.

Hands down the WORST professor I've had the displeasure of having. Unhelpful teaching style, little materials to prep for exams, and doesn't believe in recording lectures. Genuinely sorry for anyone who decides to take this class with her.

Mastrangelo is by far the worst professor I have ever had. Regularly wrong answers, defensive and doubles down, wasting time and confusing students. Lies that topics will not be on midterms. Required in-class online quizzes despite lectures being a waste of time. No recordings. No exam prep materials. Use GPT to learn.

Examples are hard to follow and useless on exams.  Wraps class very quick with minimal detail to feed her paycheck. It's best to self learn from the textbook  She also lied on whats gotta be on cum final. Couple days, she said only 40-50% on stuff after 2 midterms and rest from beginning of class. But instead 80-90% is from after the 2 midterms

If she is the only option wait and take Patty Buchanan(greatest prof ever).She doesnt upload solved examples in class even though you may have illness or family emergency. She herself gets many of the examples wrong. Her lectures have a negative effect on understanding. She expects a 77 percent to be a 2.3. Best of luck(trust me you will need it).

She is very defensive when instructing and makes many errors in examples during lectures. Skip the lecture and read the book. Her examples are difficult to follow. Her office hours are a day after the homework is due and she does not usually post the next homework until the day after her final office hour.

Professor wasn't able to answer questions very well and got defensive when she didn't know the answer. I have never felt more unprepared going into the next series of this class. Read the book and skip her lectures.
Very respectable professor. Crystal clear explanations of material. I usually asked questions via email and she responds in a timely manner.

Prof. Mastrangelo made it clear our class was her lowest priority. She was often late to class (15mins) and provided very little feedback. She rarely responded to email. Only 4 of our 7 assignments were ever returned. Grading was very unclear. Lectures were disorganized and hard to follow. The only stuff I learned was from the textbook.
This is my second time taking this course. First time with this instructor. She is by far the better instructor. Very good lectures with clear examples and good explanations of concepts.

The class was asynchronous and poorly organized. You get graded on 3 assignments that are graded unclearly and without a rubric making the grading confusing. Teaching is very surface level and she never goes in-depth about topics, teaching doesn't flow and is disjointed between topics. I wanted to love this class but it was very disappointing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would consider restructuring the organization of the class in terms of deadlines and expectations. Get ready to write. Accessible class since lectures were short on canvas. Assignments should be more concise. Leaving things open for students to explore their own interests, sometimes causes expectations and grading to become unclear.

Taken pre covid. Not a fan of her class she just read directly off the slides and was tested based on the slides, She is nice and tries engaging the class but didn't really "teach" and probably learned more from quiz section. The TA's are tough graders and really look for any reason to doc you points off your paper. Lots of reading of old papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Presents material in an effective manner that is easy to understand. Have taken her classes before and my advice is to start early on the research paper as it is time consuming. Have had both harsh and easy grading ta's for Cichowski's classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had Professor Cichowski for Women's Rights and she is amazing. Her lectures were broken up to make paying attention to a bit easier, her slides were straight forward, her explanations were to the point. There are 3 exams which are "short answer" style and one 10-12 page essay. Pay attention to lectures and definitely on the readings.

I've had Cichowski twice (online and in person), and her classes are always very well organized with clear study guides for exams. She's definitely passionate about the subject matter, highly knowledgeable, and accessible to students. Class is better in person, but she did a good job adjusting to COVID. A solid PoliSci professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Great lectures filled with enough information to answer all questions you have. Exams ask a lot of questions so be prepared; do the study guides. The essay takes a lot of research and time so start early. Must attend quiz sections. Would recommend, especially to second year pol s/ lsj students.

I enjoyed having Professor Cichowski this quarter, especially during this tough year. Lectures were pre-recorded, organized, and concise. There's a research paper you have to do but she gives good advice on the research portion and clear instructions on how to write it. She sends us cute dog photos/videos :)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super knowledgeable and gives really interesting lectures! Course was a little reading heavy, but discussions about the readings were super cool. Only one research paper for the quarter, and there are short assignments leading up to it about your research topic, so you've basically written the whole thing already by mid-quarter.

I would recommend this professor to absolutely anyone! She is so smart and genuinely cares about what she is teaching and that the students are understanding it. The research paper was assigned super early and the midterm and final were completely based off the study guide. Took her remotely and all her lectures are pre-recorded. Amazing prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Fantastic. Rachel made quarantine bearable. Quirky, funny, and a great lecturer who really has the online format down. Had personal issues mid-quarter and went out of her way to help/accommodate. Easy grader but you learn a LOT. Expect cute videos of her dog, funny emails, and a truly passionate expert in her field. Cannot recommend enough :)

Noticed a comment by someone complaining about needing to read Girls Like us in a weekend AU18 - I couldn't disagree more, it was easy to read and get the necessary information. Lectures were heavy but study guides for exams were comprehensive so it was so easy to ace this class.

This is my favorite class that Ive taken. At the end of the day, Prof C really just wants to share her passion with us & get us interested in constitutional law & courts! You get plenty of time to work on the research paper, and the study guides prepare you perfectly for the tests. The lectures are well organized & interesting. TAKE THIS CLASS

I absolutely loved Prof Cichowski - she is so kind, funny, and intelligent. She is so available to her students and is great at facilitating productive discussions; it's obvious that she cares a lot! There is a lot of reading, but I got a lot out of it. I can't wait to take more of her courses.

In AU18, the reading load was heavy and required to read the whole book, Girls Like Us in a weekend. Most readings need to read for TA's class. No lecture slide on canvas and the prof tested the slides and readings in both midterm and final as memorizing exams. Professor's lectures were boring, but The research paper and extra credit were fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Cichowski has a fun and witty sense of humor, she definitely knows her stuff and is passionate about it, her lectures are very organized and are at the perfect speed for note taking, her study guides are a huge help for exams. She really wants her students to learn.

Professor C was absolutely amazing! I signed up for this course on a limb to explore law, and was blown out of the water by how well the content was laid out, how helpful, knowledgeable, and kind Professor C was. You have to really study the study guide to do well, but if you do you'll be very successful. ASK FOR HELP FROM HER EARLY FOR UR PAPER!

She is kind and it never feels like you're wasting her time with any question. Her lectures are clear, as are the assignments. The readings aren't necessary to do well on tests. You're graded on 1 midterm, 1 final, 1 10 page research paper, and attendance. Go to lecture, pay attention, and you'll do well. Her study guides are VERY useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She has the potential to be very interesting, but her classes tend to be disorganized, she is a tough grader, and there are very few things to be graded on so if you get one poor grade it really affects your overall grade. I found her class to be very boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures are boring but you need to go because there are writing assignments (summaries of the readings) due every single lecture. A mile wide and an inch deep into the material. Long papers with harsh grades given. No tests. The TAs do the grading, so utilize them BEFORE you turn in an assignment, not after.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Overall, boring. Her lecture slides are very unorganized and often unclear. She does not manage time well (eg. spends a week of lectures talking about what a social norm is). She gives fairly poor examples for the concepts she's trying to explain. There's both too much and too little work. Worst LSJ/Poly prof I've had.

Lots and lots of busy work. Unclear assignments and grading rubrics, and even the clarifications still aren't clear. Very heavy on readings and half of the class is spent doing not useful things. "Short" papers are not five pages.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Prof. Cichowski is an incredible lecturer and really knows what she's talking about. The reading is standard for a POL S/LSJ class, and the homework is very doable. There is one big paper that you are given more than enough time to complete. She prepares you well for tests. This is one of the best classes I've taken at UW.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very great use of class time. Two hour lecture but it gets divided into group work, videos, guest speakers, etc. segments that make time in class go by faster. Subunits are divided nicely. Instructor gives a very fair courseload.
i love her as a professor! very straight forward and up front about her expectations. i loved this class!
I loved the professor. Take this class. It's super fun and easy!

Convoluted lecture with lots of busy work that I didn't feel helped me with learning.  Class was WAY to broad to actually cover topics beyond the most surface level.  It was a two hour class that never felt like it was spent well, usually taking the first HOUR to review the website.  I took this class with 7 friends who all felt the same way.

She is awesome! Definitely one of the better professors in the poli sci department. I really recommend taking her Women's Rights course, its super interesting, not as demanding, and you can tell she's really passionate and knowledgeable in the topics she presents. Homework is easy, so is the grading.
Really sweet and energetic.  She doesn't give many assignments (comparatively) but they're typically meaningful and enjoyable.

Loved going to lecture, kept me interested and her slides were spot on with the readings and the lecture topic. One of my favorite professors at UW, very approachable and knows what she is talking about. I would definitely recommend her! The class challenges your ability but she is not too difficult of a grader if you understand the material.

I loved Cichowski's teaching style. Her lectures are crystal clear and the books are covered in full. It's not the easiest class, a lot of studying is required for the tests. The paper requirements are very specific making a stressful topic easier. Overall great class and teacher!

Most important tips to succeed in this class: go to class and write down the lecture slides, don't procrastinate on the research paper - start at least 2 weeks before and you will feel much better, and completely fill out the midterm and final study guides and then review them. If you do this a 4.0 or at least a good grade will be in reach! :)

Great Professor! Loved that class! Very straight forward, easy to understand, and a very, very interesting! Have learned a lot in that class! I would definitely recommend it! Come to lectures and read the articles/books, most of the readings are actually very interesting!

She's certainly clear and helpful, though a little boring, due partially to the dry class material.  Overall a nice, pretty good prof.  This is a class I would recommend if you're looking for an easy one, the study IS THE TEST.  Really straight forward expectations

LOVED THIS CLASS! I took it and though I struggled with it in the beginning, it was really easy to catch up and redeem myself. She makes it clear what would be tested on and she really makes the effort to help you help yourself. Prof. Cichowski is one of the best professors I have ever had at UW. Take the class, you won't regret that you did.

My favorite soc sci teacher. If I can, I would take another one of her class. Not only do you learn a lot, but she is probably the fairest teacher I've seen. If you do the work, you can get a very good grade. Her #1 quality is that she is EXTREMELY clear of her expectations. If you follow it like a checklist, you're golden.

One of the best poli sci professors out there. Learned so much in her class, it's unbelieveable. Not difficult if you put in the work. The research paper seems like it's a big deal, but just don't procrastinate too much and you'll be fine. Lectures are interesting. Take the class.

She really tries to engage the audience asks us questions. Her lectures are extremely important to attend. There is a research paper she really is there to help out though. I also had a great TA that helped my quiz section a lot.

Pretty easy class, but Cichowski exposes her students to interesting concepts.  She is clearly passionate about law and courts and demonstrates an eclectic mix of coarseness and sophistication.  One of the few professors I've observed who can use the term "half-assed" in class and still sound intelligent.  Would love to take more classes from her.

Professor Clark is one of the best professors that I have ever had. She is so passionate and knowledgeable about what she does and during discussions she is so eager about our own thoughts about class material. Some participation point assignments and one large group project, she gives you all the material but you have to keep yourself on track.

Dr. Clark is very welcoming & engaging. My only issue is that when it comes to the 3 big assignments her instructions can be vague and misleading (this caused issues for people at multiple points) and based on the feedback she doesn't seem to be actually reading the essays and is just spotchecking/skimming, which isn't fair to students.

Really great class! Professor Clark is passionate about what she teaches and I learned a lot in her class. Participation is not mandatory, but she does have random participation assignments throughout the quarter. As long as you go to most of lectures, you should be fine! Plus, she offers extra credit. Highly recommend her and this class.

Most of grade is based on 3 (easy) reflective essays and polls that are taken just for attendance, not for right or wrong answers. She is very kind and funny, and I looked forward to her class everyday. No homework besides reading then writing ungraded discussion questions. No midterm and no final! Easy A w/ effort.  Definitely take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed her class.

Such a sweetheart who is genuinely passionate about teaching. Highly values student feedback, grades by a few short, easy essays and one pop quiz (also easy), and creates ample opportunity for student input and perspectives
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved her. Class was fairly easy but I am a senior who has taken classes thatve already touched on the subject material. Biweekly readings that weren't awful, especially since they were discussed in class and there was a following small group discussion. Respected differing opinion and encouraged discourse unlike some professors I've had in anth

I absolutely loved this class and this professor. Everything we learned about was so eye-opening and relevant, and she does a great job respecting other people's perspectives. There are a lot of discussions but it's always interesting, and there are readings every week, but as far as Anth classes go it was not too much.

If you are debating taking a class with professor clark, take it. She is clearly passionate about what she teaches and clearly cares about whether or not her students are learning. She checks student evals once around midterms and then makes changes if she needs to. Great class, I wish i could take it twice.

I really enjoyed this class, it was kinda boring mostly because I'm an anth major and already knew most of the content. Shes a great person and professor. Kinda weird grading but group tests and 2 essays that actually need a bit of effort but overall you can 4.0 this class. Polls every class.

Dr. Clark is amazing! 10/10 would recommend taking a class with her if you ever get the chance. I took her Introduction to Medical Anthropology 215 course & absolutely loved it! There was a considerable amount of reading weekly, four quizzes, two essays, a mid-term/final & in-class Poll Everywhere participation. Hilarious & loved feedback!

She is a very engaging lecturer and the content is interesting. However, the exams are on obscure details and it was very difficult to know what is important to remember for tests. To her credit, after receiving a lot of negative feedback, she changed aspects of the class to make expectations and important material more clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not a bad lecturer. Interesting material, but course was poorly organized. Tested on very specific things that are glazed over in class. Expectations for learning and assignments are unclear. Grading system is unfair. Not a very flexible professor considering how many times she changed the format of the exams or the course in general. Not a fan.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Heather is amazing. Made me decide to do an anth minor. She is very passionate about what she teaches and wants you to succeed and not be stressed out by her class. Gave a group midterm and final, both were scantron. Two easy essays and a few poll everywheres in class that you could do from home. Take her class! Learn a lot and get an easy A :)

Graded on obscure things such as minute details rather than big concepts, number of power points rather than content, etc. This was also a class with very little to no room to share opposing viewpoints. If you don't agree with what is being taught, I don't recommend this class. What is being taught is also are extreme and impractical viewpoints.

Took linguistic anthropology with her at Cascadia. Amazing teacher who is obviously very passionate about her work. Her lectures are interactive and interesting. Read the textbook (an easy read) and show up and youll be fine. Id love to take another class with her if I got the chance.

The class was really fun and Heather was a pretty good teacher. The final was really really hard though, but I still ended up with a decent grade. Not much homework at all, I got the textbooks and read them just because they were interesting and I think it helps to do so. It was overall a fun and great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Heather is the most enthusiastic teacher I have ever had. She really loves what she teaches and makes it engaging.  This class was LING203 and ANTH203. The only homework was one paper and it was relatively easy. This class was definitely geared toward freshman though. Overall she was a joy to have as a professor and I would love to take her again.

Will need a good ta to understand concepts thoroughly. Lectures are very simplified and difficult to follow (do the readings before lecture to understand). Will test on niche topics that were covered very briefly in class. Nice and funny professor but not very effective, especially for a slower learner. Didn't record lecture or post correct slides

Very funny guy. Lectures were not always super helpful but generally got the job done, just make sure you can do the practice worksheets for the tests. Tests were not that hard and honestly very fair to the material he was teaching.

Tai Chen genuinely cares about his students, but he's definitely lacking as a prof. His final exam had a 21.2% STD— it's clear that he left a large portion of the class behind. For me, I found that most of his explanations were oversimplifications and didn't reflect the difficulty of exams. Find a good TA to make labs bearable if you take 215

Pretty chill professor, gave good lectures with lots of information. Exams were straightforward, and he was very responsive through email and very accessible outside of class. Will take time to speak with you about class outside of office hours.

Wish I could give this guy 6/5 to boost his average rating. Absolutely wonderful man that made sitting in the front row enjoyable and is a good reminder that you can absolutely get a lot out of lectures. He met with me regularly outside of office hours bc of class conflict and could take a concept I was stuck for hours something I could do 10 mins.
Hilarious guy ngl

Tai Chen is a very caring and fair professor, who is very knowledgeable and informative. He's capable of explaining the same concept in multiple ways to ensure you understand the material. Go to his office hours as much as possible, he can teach a concept that would take 2 hours to understand on your own in just 15 minutes.
chinese grandpa vibes, literally so homey

Tai chen was an okay professor and his explanations were fairly good. He did come off as condescending when asked about clarification on topics so that was a bummer. The homework was pretty difficult at times and the exam problems were very similar to the examples during class. The labs were difficult and often didn't correlate with class material.
While the Pearson homework is difficult, Tai does an amazing job with lectures. His intelligent and charismatic lectures prove to be equally entertaining and educational. Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, articulates things well, tests aren't that bad compared to other EE 215 profs, HW can be long though, overall good professor.

He's just another average professor that does not care about his students at all. His teachings are mediocre and his exams are hard for unnecessary reasons. 

I highly recommend to not take his course... I have no clue how he has managed to get a good rating here.
Awesome professor. Really cares about students and fosters a fun and supportive environment during lectures.

Tai Chen is a very eccentric professor, but course organization is almost entirely by TAs and they are ABHORRENT. He has a TA that has written garbage labs that are impossible to do because we haven't learnt the material. Two midterms in two weeks and homework over breaks takes the cake. Heard he was tough but fair, but his TAs are ruining it.

I took 3 classes with this professor (215,233,341). He has reasonable expectations and a curve that rewards the best students without punishing the average ones. Lectures are recorded so if you aren't able to make it to class or want to review material later you can. Tai Chen is very friendly and has a welcoming, approachable demeanor.
Passionate about teaching and EE. His office hours can be a lifesaver.

Okay lectures that sum up information fine and contain helpful examples. Does not cover a lot of material needed to fully understand labs and does not provide nearly enough time to complete the labs, it is expected you meet with your lab group outside of class time to complete them. Schedules homework due on and the day after thanksgiving :(
Dr Chen is a gem of a teacher. Hes considerate and caring. The accent might make it a bit hard to understand him sometimes but he knows the stuff.

Dr. Chen's class takes work, as any STEM class at UW will, but he made the class super doable. In my experience, the homework was very similar to what you are tested on, so if you could do the homework just by reading the textbook, you might not even need to go to lecture. However, his lectures are pretty helpful if you're not a textbook person.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Due to pandemic, class was taught via zoom. The class is graded by labs, hw, quizzes with no exams. Quizzes are fair. You will be fine on quiz if you go to lecture. hw is done weekly with 2-6 problems. Labs are not hard with example code provided. I think you will do good if you follow class along! Highly recommended take it with Chen!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Chen is a good lecturer. He explains the concept well. As long as you follow along his lecture, you will do fine in 332. However, 332 final project is pretty hard. My group didn't get to finish it but it was cancelled due to pandemic and protest. Also, I recommend you take 331 with Chen if you can do it.

Never went to lecture in the entire quarter. Only went to the labs. The professor has a heavy accent so I can tell that going to his lecture might not help much. Just be ready to practice a lot of the problems from the textbook. I did in average an extra 15 problems per chapter. Curves are very high so even a tiny mistake can cost you dearly.
Great Prof, sometimes goes fast in lectures but he's very accessible and will walk through any problems in office hours. Fair class if you put in the work.

I had Dr. Chen for 331/332. When people say he means well, he really does. His office hours are super helpful and he will try his best to make sure you understand the material. For 331, the book is super helpful so review the book and homework before exams. For 332 however, slides are more useful.

Great office hours! Go to those. With questions. Tai rips problems right from the book, so read! It's helpful to be able to go back and see the types of problems that will be on the midterm(s) and final. He's really sweet, and REALLY funny. Just actually put in effort and Tai will respect you. He means well.

Make sure you practice problems from the textbook for each exam because me means it when he says he'll use those examples. He is an intelligent and a well-spoken instructor who makes sure every student succeeds. Homework might sometimes take a long time so make sure to do them ahead of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Chen was a great professor for EE 215: he was clearly very knowledgeable on the course content, he tried hard to make lecture enjoyable. In addition, there were some issues with grading on the first midterm. If you had any issues with the grading, he would personally go back and re-grade anything you felt was unfairly graded.

TCC is a pretty good professor who cares about his students and is funny. I have taken him a few times and found that his lectures get a bit harder to understand as the course goes on, and his tests become harder as well. Do not use practice tests as a basis for the how ready you are, they were never particularly helpful, study homework/textbook.

Study the homework! He's not joking when he says he includes a HW verbatim on the tests. This even applies to the final. He is very welcoming in his office hours and can pick up where you are stuck very quickly. Great teaching style, and SUPER funny. He's also willing to give points back on your exam if you explain why. Tai is a god.

Caring, funny, nice professor. Lectures sometimes go fast though. Has accent, but nothing too heavy. Labs and homeworks don't always match up well. Textbook reading is really helpful. Stricter curve. Tests are textbook-based; nothing too imaginative/over-the-top.
Great Prof, really smart and funny and knows his stuff. Extremely helpful and available in regard to office hours. Really understanding when you're sick or going through issues.
This man got a long standing ovation on the last class. nuff said. 30/10 recommended

Chen is awesome. SUPPER funny, has great lectures, and is extremely respectful. EE 215 is a moderately difficult subject, but I'm glad I took it with him. He does have a strong accent, so at times it can be hard to understand him, but that's the only downside I can think of. If your an ME major, this class is an easy A.
Hauck is Tai in the digital world, Tai is Hauck in the analog world.  If you know what I'm talking about.

If you want to memorize formula without truly understand what's really going on. You should take his class. Had many different professors but his way of lecturing is really too hard to follow. Got high GPA but didn't understand anything.
VERY GOOD PROFESSOR

He's a very energetic and quirky prof. Really enjoyed his class. He has a strict curve, which is really his only downside (avg 3.2), but fortunately it's not that low. I would totally recommend as he is engaging and accessible.  Some people complain about his accent, but it really isn't unclear. I have terrible hearing and I didn't find an issue.

Tai is my favorite professor at UW. I've taken many of his classes and his style is really consistent. Lots of lectures that are clear and organized. His tests are straight from lecture so if you pay attention you're fine. He's one of the professors that actually makes the curriculum so he knows it really well. And he actually CARES about students.

Explanations of material are very clear. He doesn't waste time reviewing older concepts, which could be good or bad depending on how well you keep pace with the class. Very accessible outside of class and is eager to help students. He also has a great sense of humor, especially in smaller class sizes, he likes to joke around a lot with the students

I took him in Summer 2016 and he was pretty great. He was a fun lecturer and would care whether or not students learned. He is very open to questions during and outside of class. He just has a bit tight of a curve but other than that, his class was great!
Awesome instructor! Sticks to the point and has a very very good structure of the lectures. You can go back to powerpoint slides and review the lectures because they are so good!

If you go to his office hours, he is very helpful and interested in getting you to understand the material. I found his lectures clear. Tests closely resemble the homework problems. It's not an easy class and most of the grade is test-based, so you have to really understand the material to do well.
Very decent professor... doesnt compare to the likes of Peckol, but definitely helpful, friendly and teaches extremely well.

The lectures and class as a whole were very well organized. Used lecture slides but would leave some things blank as he filled them in during lecture (somewhat forces you to go to class). Homework is generally pretty easy as he took many problems straight out of Schaumm's outline of Signals and Systems.

You can tell he is interested in teaching the subject but the subject matter was so boring and sometimes very unclear that by the end it got kind of boring. Overall his tests aren't too bad if you do the practice exam but he curves at a 3.2 for this class which is one of the lower cases in the EE department

He is really bad professor I have to say. First, he just intentionally ignore the key points and hard points in the class, OR he DO NOT know what are the key point of the materials. Secondly, his class is really boring and not worth going, usually there are over 50 free space in his class. At last, he gives out high grade but I DID NOT LEARN THINGS
He is terrible at explaining. All you get is 'good? OOkay.'He doesn't even pause in between.

This guy is awesome he makes lectures entertaining. At times it is difficult to understand him. His tests and quizzes are not extremely difficult. As long as you attend class and do the homework you should be fine

The most irritating class , I have ever take. Very boring! He teaches out of his slides. Nothing to do with his exams. He can not Lecture, You need a billion red bulls to stay up in his class. Do not take him unless you have to. He is the worst.

I only have had him once so fare. However by the end of the quarter i realized that he is a pretty ideal instructor. He cares, he is pretty efficient with teaching the course and he has a sense of humor.
I liked his cross-use of computer projection/slide show.  He enjoys interactive students.
Good teacher, always willing to help.

He's a good guy, but only a mediocre teacher. He has a heavy Chinese accent. He does vague examples in class that are much easier than the homework and exams. He pretty much just reads off his lecture slides. His exams are straightforward though, no trick questions. Sometimes he doesn't explain things fully in class.
He is really good, his tests are always similar to the homework problems.

Hands down one of the nicest professors I've had at UW. He has the energy of a goofy high school English teacher, which is incredibly refreshing and makes for a class room environment in which I don't feel nervous at all to speak or share my thoughts. The class itself is easy but very interesting/engaging, especially if you're into classic myth.
Clauss truly cares about his students and making sure his lectures are engaging!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: This professor is definitely the best professor I've had at this school. He truly cares about the well-being of his students and helping them achieve their goals. He's really good at making you think without judgement, and he's very flexible - working with the students. Take at least one of his classes if you can!

Professor James is very easy to talk to. Due to personal circumstances, I missed a large number of his lectures, yet he was willing to work with me to ensure I get the full experience as everyone else. His lectures are engaging and inspiring. He also offered me tremendous support during my graduate school application. Highly recommend!

I was very excited for the course but was disappointed honestly. The professor does not support students' unique perspectives and drones on and on without waiting for student feedback or a response. Easy grading but some essay prompts are hard and essays are numerous in quantity. Prof was weird with sending long emails after class finished for qtr
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class for needed credits and I will be honest in saying that despite his good reviews Professor Clauss is not my favorite. Rather than inspiring free thought he often tells you exactly how to think and rambles on and on assuming everyone agrees with him. Easy class but not my favorite .
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is easy if you attend class and go over his lecture notes. The grading was just based on 4 two-page midterm essays, an eight-page film script, and 5 two-page final essays. If you use the lecture notes on your essays, you'll be fine. He is very caring and reached out to me when I didn't go to class a bit due to outside circumstances.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: such a fun class and he is really fun to listen to. quite a bit of reading, but he is not a difficult grader, and is not looking for only one right answer. honestly loved this class, and the only 4.0 I have gotten here. also he is really knowledgeable.

This class was a great change of pace from a typical college class because instead of focusing on grades, tests, and papers, he wanted us to focus on learning the material, gaining experience, and enjoying the process. V encouraging. Likes to tell jokes. Knows a lot about linguistics. He lent me a book about ProtoIndoEuropean bc he knew I liked it.

Super kind, knowledgable, and encouraging. He wants you to think outside the box of typical classroom learning(ex. memorization vs. self reflection). Provided lots of interesting random facts at no extra cost! I didn't read The Iliad and still got 100% on the midterm, but I read the Odyssey and got 80%, so be thoughtful in your work.

BEST TEACHER EVER. He is such a sweetheart and genuinely loves what he is teaching. You do not really have to do the reading either, just follow along the slides in class. Answer every part on the midterms and you will pass with a 4.0. The class only has two take home midterms and a creative writing take home assignment for the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Clauss is the best lecturer that I've had in college. He is funny, engaging, and very excited about everything I have heard him lecture on.

The most caring professor you will ever have. He is a total goofball and is so passionant about Mythology. I highly recommend his Classics 424- Epic Tradition class. The midterm is very much opinion based and he encourages you to have fun with it. He also sometimes sends out very encouraging, thoughtful, and hilarious emails to hype you up.

Clauss is one of the best educators I have ever had at any level of schooling. His passion towards the subject is second to none and he's one of the few teachers nowadays who actually cares about you learning the material and using it learn something about yourself. I would highly recommend this class and any others he teaches.
My favorite professor so far. Very passionate about teaching and makes the material super interesting. Very caring about his students and does whatever he can to get them to pass.
an absolute cutie, knows his greek and roman mythology for sure.
Definitely one of my favorite professors. Any class with him will be fun and you won't regret it
Very fun class. The prof is helpful if you've missed a class you just go to his office hours and he'll catch you up.
