This guy is awesome.  Just take his class, you won't regret it.  You'll learn a bunch and raise your GPA.
No Comments

Fun fun fun class.  Great prof, he's hilarious, he jokes around, really has fun with the class, which of course makes it more interesting to you.  I'd highly recommend this class to anyone and everyone.

I had him spring 2025, his first quarter teaching. Was a little unstructured bc it was his first quarter teaching, but you could tell he really liked his field and it was interesting hearing about his personal research. Expect to show up for every class with some readings before and talk in small groups over it. Def go and talk to him, W guy

Honestly very kind and genuine teacher that wants you to succeed. He's very good at answering questions and helping you workout thoughts. I think his tests may need some work as they are very reading oriented, like direct thoughts from reading which can be difficult with you know memory and such, but with that they are open note open reading tests.

He was a very nice teacher and accommodating. There wasn't a lot of homework, and was very lenient when grading. Assigned 3-5+ readings with some being up to 20 (or more) pages. Tested on specific things from reading, but all (+final) were open note.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Though it was his first time teaching, he cared about students, the material, and his work. While his lectures could feel a bit monotone, he brought in personal interests that added life to the class. The quizzes were oddly specific at times, but with more experience, he's sure to grow into a stronger and more engaging instructor.

I really enjoy her lectures, she seems like she knows what she's talking about and really engages with the class. She makes you feel like you can ask any questions. There's only 3 tests but the top two are averaged and lowest is dropped, so it's not that bad. I'd take a psych class with her again.

Clara is a very nice person. However, as a professor, the same can't be said. She shows up to class unprepared, her slides are very disorganized and minimal, and she relies too heavily on studies to make sense of concepts. Her exams consist of memorizing various studies as opposed to theories related to social psych. Plus grading scale is tight.

Super easy class with very few assignments. Self-grading accounts for 40% of the total. 
It's definitely better to attend in person, as the class is discussion-based.
Also, she's cool.

This class had the potential to be excellent, and I am sure it would have been better in person. The class is graded on mostly exams with a few assignments graded out of a couple points, so be wary of hitting EVERYTHING on the rubric or your grade will hurt. Lectures were just a past quarters recordings which got really annoying really fast.

The lectures were super engaging and interesting! While they are recorded and the slides are posted online, attendance is pretty much mandatory because 8 random lectures (which you don't know beforehand) will have an assignment worth 1% of your grade. Overall easy and fun class, two open note online tests and one big final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Ellie is great! Her lectures are clear and informative, I was never bored. She's very responsive and helpful. She does give small participation assignments during lectures sometimes. Workload is very reasonable, moderate amount of reading (you can skim), with a research project at the end. Def my favorite class this quarter
Ellie helped make the material easier to understand

Very accessible outside of class. Gives great feedback. Only minor problem I had was the weekly quizzes sometimes had unclear questions with no ability to get clarification. Other than that, awesome professor, loved her class!

The instructor is nice and good with feedback. One discussion post and one short (3-5 question) quiz per week, with midterm and final essays (4 pages minimum so pretty fair). There was some nitpicky grading here and there, but overall I enjoyed this course and was not overwhelmed by the workload.

Claire really helped me progress quickly in French. The class itself moved pretty quickly, but it was easy to catch up. She really emphasizes talking with a partner in French for a good portion of class, which I found challenging at times, especially because the class was every day.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you are wanting to take french take it with Claire. She is really nice and a very light grader, not saying studying is not neccesary because it is but she gives half credit for most questions on the quiz. She is really funny and got my french skills to advance quicker than any other langauge ive taken before.
Considerate and knowledgeable professor, runs a very straightforward and participation heavy approach to learning that helps students pick up languages surprisingly quickly.
Claire is super caring and wants her students to succeed. Her lectures and expectations are very clear and organized. Be sure to go to class and get ready for a lot of group work.

She is very good at teaching beginner French! I like how she does engaging activities that force us to speak in and listen to the language. She is super sweet and wants her students to succeed. I definitely recommend her!
She's super caring, passionate about what she does & is always willing to help students who are struggling!! I would definitely take her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Claire is a solid French prof. She knows what she's talking about and is helpful in continuing your learning. Not too hard. A presentation, a few essays, online tests, etc. I would take it again! She's very kind and a good prof

Claire is very kind and cares about her students. She speaks almost in French which makes the study environment more authentic and you can get used to the French accent. Grading is easy, attendance is counted toward final grades, and exams are online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really great prof overall. Kind, funny, and smart. Lots of hw but it's easy. She only explains and answers questions in french which can be frustrating if it's already complicated, and it was a little thoughtless to assign a quiz, paper, and final all due within a 5-day span during week 10 but for the most part she's great. Would def recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: claire is incredibly sweet and caring for each and every one of her students. the class itself was super straightforward and easy. hadnt learned french since high school (3 years ago) and it was so easy to pick it back up. she explains grammatical structures and important concepts for each test incredibly well. wish all my profs could be like her:(
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Claire is super nice, friendly and always patient with the class. There are a lot of worksheets but they're easy points! She does a great job of answering complex questions about grammar/structure. Sometimes the silence after she asks a question gets a bit awkward, but she's super chill and really cares about students understanding the materials.

Claire is really chill. Flexible, nice. Only complaints are that she sometimes sticks to "only speaking french" during lectures, leaving you a bit confused when she's giving directions, and she doesn't respond as quickly to emails as I'd like. Also online format requires you keep track of FIVE websites. Too much. But overall, recommend.

Claire is great! She's very responsive to emails and answers any questions you have and is always makes class interesting and engaging for us. She lays out clear expectations and deadlines so things are generally easy to follow.

Claire is the best french teacher ever! She is so genuine and kind and really cares about your french education. I honestly didn't like French at all before I had her, she just made the whole class. She answers questions with great clarity and explains sentence structure well! If you need a language to graduate take french and take it with Claire!!

One of the nicest professors I've ever had at UW. She makes a genuine effort to teach the class well, something that's especially difficult during the ongoing pandemic with online classes. She handles student questions well (explaining the complexities of French grammar in detail) and provides clear expectations for what you need to complete. 10/10

Great at explaining concepts in lecture. Course is structured logically, fair difficulty.

Quizzes often based on minor proofs or theorems shown in class, which sometimes verge on memorization, so revise the notes before you come.

In office hours, he is more than happy to go over things you missed or clarify concepts in more depth, so use them.

François is great. He's honestly kinder than he needs to be. Makes difficult tests to encourage students to actually think critically. Scores will be low but the curve makes up for it. One of the most caring and attentive instructors I've had at UW. Highly recommend for a good learning experience.

* extremely knowledgeable prof
* high expectation of students, but this translates to learning
* weekly quizzes with high emphasis on knowing the mathematical definitions/proof mentioned in class and being able to do similar small problems
* use anki to practice core definitions
* could benefit from including numerical answers to exercises in notes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Clement is a brilliant professor with a fairly ruthless grading style. Minimal partial credit is awarded (not zero but much less than average). His weekly quizzes are predictable and fair, focusing more on reciting his work than original thought. Exams are rough, but they are rough for all students. The curve is good.

The class was very hard and annoying because there were quizzes every single week, but I got the sense that he truly understands what it is like to be a student and only does this out of our best interest, forcing us to study the whole quarter, which actually makes the midterm and final much easier.

The curve for the class is decent with a 70% being a 4.0 and I think this speaks volumes to how hard the class is. I thought I was going to fail the class (he doesn't enter anything but the quiz scores and I failed almost all of them) but ended up getting a 3.8. He is SUPER patient in office hours and very helpful. His lectures are very confusing.

This is the worst lecturer I've taken in this school, his hand written is so bad and even for the notes he upload are not well structured. The weight of grading is unreasonable, he puts unproportional weight on tests, and his test is the most difficult test among the all lecturers, he also has weekly quiz. Don't take this guy's course!!!!!!!!!!!!!

I had no idea what the professor wanted from his grading and had no idea what the quartile lines were while taking the class. First math class I took that I didn't know what the professor wanted from me in terms of grading.

Somewhat unclear feedback on exams, quizzes, and the project. Arbitrary 70% 4.0 bar. High expectation for self-study. 

Needs to use gradescope to scan quiz/tests and post answer keys to study resources and practice exams. Concepts are reasonable but the difficulty is the product of an imperfect hands-off structure. Has the potential to be great!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: My biggest gripe is that his written notes are very illegible, so if you miss class theres no way to catch up
no course for 407 here yet; but this professor is one of the harshest at UW. I genuinely believe that there is no such thing as a researcher that knows how to teach well as a professor
Math 407 wasn't an option. Genuinely the worst professor I've ever had. He teaches terribly, and grades incredibly harshly. Condescending in online communication. Do everything you can to avoid.

Annoying, extremely broad and unclear final group project. To do well on exams you have to memorize every single example and proof he did in class and regurgitate it. Not a fan of that but if you're good at it this class will probably be a breeze.
(407). Don't expect to get a 100% grade on anything in this class
This is for 407. (407 code not added). Exam content is terribly structured. Throws trick questions to intentionally throw off students. Never take this professor
Unreadable handwriting during lectures, difficulty of quizzes/exams is unreasonable, simply reads from notes what make little sense unless you already know the content

This is for math 407 instead of 381. 
He is a good lecturer and has an excellent grasp on the material. However, the expectations are so punishing and confusing. He set a 50/63 on the midterm as a 4.0 and did not make the curve clear.

Inconsistent expectations, chaotic group work, and poor grading transparency. Treats undergrads like PhD students. Lectures are just reading materials aloud. Feedback is vague and personal. Changes standards mid-quarter.

Prof excepts math major students to be familiar with code as a CSE major and excepts CSE major students to be good at math as a Math major. Topic itself is not that complex  by he can make it complex. Just like previous comments, 2 exams but no study guide, no practice exam and even no review section.

Agreed with the previous review. 4 Homeworks, 2 Exams, 1 Group Project. Good lectures, nice grading, but the course was just too hard and too fast, especially if you don't already have background knowledge like me. DP done by the 2nd week and Graph in 2-3 weeks. I took CSE 373 simultaneously and this course covered 2x the content in half the time.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof has a very high expectation this 300 level class. Expected us to pick up on algos, graph theory, LP and IP, Flow in a week each. Like it takes Math394 a whole quarter to go from expectation to markov chains but somehow we were taught that in a week. Somehow squezeed in a group project and 2 exams that have no study guides. Nice prof, but 2much
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Claudio is one of the sweetest professors at UW and genuinely cares about the content he is teaching! He does a wonderful job presenting the films in an interesting way yet sometimes he would get onto a tangent and the information would be unhelpful. He also does not provide grades until the very end so I had no idea where I stood.

I liked his lectures a lot and he has a lot of good insight on his subject. He is not easily accessible outside of class and grades are not updated on Canvas, but he is very passionate and wants to engage students in dialogue and make the class fun. If students did their homework and were respectful, it was smooth sailing. He was fantastic!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My only complaint is that the class is graded on a few things, and he can be unclear about expectations for assignments, reflections, etc and can grade very subjectively. Other than that, he is terrific. He gets sad when people don't go to lectures, so please do!!!!!!!! it's so sad when he's sad. HIGHLY recommend him!

I enjoyed taking this course with Claudio. The expectations were pretty manageable, only watching films, a reading of 5-6 pages on each film, and an evaluation of each film. However, my only nitpick was the canvas was not very helpful, assignment grades were not posted on there so I don't know what my grade for the paper, presentation, etc. were.

He does not update your grades on canvas, I had little idea on how I was doing until final grades posted. Unreachable outside of class - did not check his email. He does not teach very well in class. He expects you to memorize your vocab the night before and then he quizzes you during class (with public shaming if you get the answer wrong).

Professor was really friendly, it was clear he's very passionate about the Italian films he teaches. However- it was very hard to track the current standing of my grade, as it wasn't updated on canvas until after the final exam paper. Personally I wouldn't have done well if I wasn't paying attention in class, I didn't dare miss a lecutre.

Claudio warned on the first day of class that the films were meant to be for an Italian spectator, not for entertainment--many people did not listen. Very lecture heavy but towards the end we leaned into class discussions (better style). Two "visual quizzes" (write abt random scenes/stills), one midterm and final paper. Interesting, but not enough.

Claudio is an amazing prof! Lectures are amazing & he gives many opportunities to practice conversation! Possibly the greatest lang. prof I've ever had (&I'm a LING major). He truly cares about u and cares more about u learning the language+culture than he does about "grades." He's goofy+fun+friendly. If u want to speak Italian, take his course rn.

One of the best professors at UW. I'm terrible with languages but now I can actually speak conversational italian (a feat on its own).Though students who switch from different professors in the italian department might struggle because his bar is higher than some other profs. The high bar is good!
He is a great lecturer! Not only will you learn the Italian language, but also learn about the culture and social norms. I highly recommend taking this course!
Course was easy if you put the time in, but lots of and lots of busy work. If you want to learn Italian, take it from another professor. This guy is rude and has some serious issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: The best professor I've had, and would definitely take again. He's so funny, caring and helpful. He only wishes the best for his students. Also, prepare to be roasted, it's out of love.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I really enjoy Prof. Mazzola. Every morning I am greeted at the door; Mazzola is always early, usually by 20 minutes. If you ever need to talk with him, he will make time for you. I do recommend you show up on time. The class is very grammar heavy, which is not my specialty, but we mix in cultural readings, films and skits. Study guides provided!
Claudio is a passionate teacher, and it is easy to tell he genuinely cares about each student's learning. He does a great job of explaining subject matter in ways that are clear to each student.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Being an Italian major, Claudio is one of the best professors in that department. he can go off on tangents and like many foreign language professors the syllabus is never concrete and the course packets have been commonly offered throughout the course. he really wants you to think deep about Italian culture and he is great at explaining things!
He's an engaging instructor who demonstrates a genuine interest in students learning and writing about the material.

Good GPA booster for a VLPA. However, only take this class if you're okay with writing A LOT. the final was a series of essays on the films we watched-it took a lot of work. He is not too harsh of a grader, but not an easy grader either. some films are hard to follow so just pay attention during the class discussions of them.

Excellent professor, he is fun, happy, and likes to incorporate the current cultural issues in Italy today into his lectures. He genuinely cares about his students and their education. Even know, when he sees me, I receive a warm, happy greeting, and he remembers my name. He's amazing.

Claudio is the most amazing professor one could ever ask for. He wants to make sure everyone participates so he calls on everyone in class. Do your homework! He doesn't ask for it to be turned in, but expects you to do it before you come to class. Come prepared. He's funny and serious at the same time.

He is a charming man, but he tries to incorporate too much information into the slides and then simultaneously talks so it's hard to write notes and listen. The midterm/final are long essays but overall the class isn't that hard. There are pop quizzes and so going to class is mandatory seeing that you can't make those up in section.

WOW! What can I say? I signed up for his class just so I could fill up my class schedule for elective credits. I did not think I would like it, but Claudio BLEW MY MIND. He is a film genius and one of the best professors I have had at the UW! His detailed lectures made the essays easy and I left the class with a new love for film and Italy!

Bad professor! Very boring lectures for two hours. Mid term and final does not reflect what he tells you to study for. 51 questions on the final study guide, only 3 of them were relevant to the 20 questions on the final. Horrible at preparing you for his tests!
one of my favorite profs at uw. he's super helpful and funny.

Boring, boring, BORING!  This man's lectures are torturous to sit through!!  He points out things on the screen as if we were all clinically blind.  Master in the art of stretching out the simplest concept into an hour of babble.  Take this class ONLY if required.  That said, Neorealist films prove to be cool.

This professor turns an otherwise interesting subject into fluff.  He assigns articles that prove his point in a lot fewer words and typically develops a circle of favorite students.  Ultimately a good person but a weak professor.
awesome teacher, very entertaining and his class was very interesting... i will never watch a movie the same!! take him if you can
Best professor ever hands down. Funny, caring and incredibly knowledgeable. Cares about his students immensely and has a heart of pure gold. I've never learned more than from him.
Mazzola is awesome. He is a great, down to earth teacher with a heart of gold. Take anything he offers.
No Comments
Prof Marshall makes lectures engaging and personalized, and you can't help but laugh at his quippy jokes.

He had really interesting lectures, and he's funny. He answers questions well, and he's overall very understanding. He does do random call during lectures, but they're all easy questions. You might never even get called at all. The work load isn't bad. There's only one or two readings or videos to watch before lecture. I had fun in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Colin's lectures are very intellectually engaging and well-organized. He's also very accommodating, easy to reach, and has a great attitude. Probably my favorite professor at the philosophy department!

I loved this class!! I took PHIL 118 and it was a great class. The stuff we learned about was really interesting, and I really liked the professor. He taught really well and was super accommodating and I felt really confident about my understanding of the content.

Had Colin for modern philosophy- we watched a lecture video (~30 mins) prior to class, and used class time as discussion. Lectures were great and he does an amazing job at answering questions. He let us out early since we watch the videos prior.

Took Modern Philosophy with him. Was a great class. Lots of discussions which made the class great. He was able to answer all kinds of questions that students threw at him, really knowledgeable. Will be taking another class with him soon. Highly recommend.
Best professor I've ever had. Truly cares about students education and is proud to teach philosophy

Professor Marshall still does pre-recorded lectures and uses in-person class time for "discussion" that frequently turns into a second lecture. He is a knowledgeable professor who cares about student comprehension of relatively difficult philosophical material. He also gives students an online, free version of the textbook.

Colin is a great professor/loves the subject more than his job. I have taken three classes with him, and one thing that slightly gets on my nerves is how much left ideology is infused into the course. Some may think it is whats best, some think its wrong. I think it should be neutral and each person can make up their own mind, thus having free will
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easy class, as long as you keep up with readings and assignments. 3 rlly short and easy-graded essays. Lectures help understand readings (which can be hard), but can afford to skip sometimes. Doesn't record lectures but basically goes off powerpoints anyways. Quiz sections graded. Discussions and class beef are the best part tbh
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Really smart professor and very emotionally intelligent inside of class. Clear, useful lectures that really help with the (fairly difficult) readings. Very tough grader, however, and extremely unforgiving late policy (a paper which is one day late nets you a zero, with no wiggle room).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: More assignments than I expected. Just expect a bunch of weekly long reading assignments and reading responses. Three major papers. Small assignments are due in class, so quiz section is mandatory to attend. What annoyed me was getting randomly selected in class for discussion. Great professor though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Mr. Collins does an absolutely wonderful job of teaching introductory Philosophy. Discussions are fair, respectful, with him always openly and genuinely encouraging different views. Lectures somehow make 8:30 AM classes bearable, and I had no regrets about taking this class. Papers aren't too hard at all, and the feedback given is very helpful.

Colin made class really interesting, and is very clear in his expectations. There is a lot of reading but it's spaced out and not too overwhelming. Was definitely a class I looked forward to in the mornings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great prof, passionate about phil and makes it very easy to follow and very interesting. Lots of reading but material is thought-provoking. Grading on papers can be rough because they're worth so few points, but they are easy and laid out for you. Make sure you get every possible point to get an A, don't forget drafts, worksheets, participation.

Some of the readings assigned are difficult, but his lectures explain the content very well. His lectures are overall pretty engaging and entertaining. There's pretty regular homework but outside of the reading it is not very difficult.

I took this class as my "easy" class for the quarter. While it was a bit more work than I was expecting, it was worth it. Colin gives good lectures, with a lot of credit for small, easy assignments. There are 3 papers, but they are reasonably quick. This is a really good class for those interested in philosophy.

Great lecturer and keeps the whole class engaged. Weekly readings which are pretty tough, but is explained thoroughly during lectures. Definitely not an easy A, but I think this class is well worth the experience. Very interesting topics discussed and would take again!
Nice grading system! Class is not boring if you focus...

Marshall is able to lecture in a very interesting and clear way. He obviously enjoys what he does and wants to share that with the students.  I only have two criticisms: (1)his left-wing politics enter the class more than should be the case. (2) Some topics we discussed would have been better for other classes, eg race, the second amendment.

This is an entry level class and yet the readings that we receive are very tough. Even after we read and go to lecture, I would still struggle trying to understand the concepts he was teaching. Tried to take this as an easy elective, but it was not worth it. A lot of tough reading.
Great lectures and he'll make you read stuff that matters
Good professor

Professor Colin Marshall is a great lecturer and has the ability to engage the whole class in what he is saying. He has a great sense of humour and is very helpful if anyone needs help or has questions about philosophy.
Great Professor

Exams worth 80% of your grade. Course entirely based on lectures he recorded in 2020. Exams have an insane amount of questions, no partial credit, no note sheet, and sections where you can earn negative points for wrong answers. One office hour per week. Answer keys often have sections where he simply didn't feel like writing out the entire answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dave is the best professor I've had at UW. I took 411 and 412 with him, and they have been the most fun math classes I have ever taken. He's a quiet guy, but personable! The content he teaches is really interesting and he is very knowledgeable. I love Dave, take his class!

Class is almost all group work, so if you get stuck with people who don't care you'll be miserable. Dave has no office hours, doesn't answer questions, and even though he claims to post answer keys to everything, they usually skip problems and don't show the work, just the answer. The content of the class is fascinating, but Dave is a poor teacher.

The layout for 412 is the exact same as his 411 class so there's no surprises coming into the class. It was amazing to have a professor as caring and supportive as Collingwood and he redeemed math for me. I now have a new love for proofs and math. If you have the chance to take a class with him, don't pass up the opportunity!

Dr Collingwood's class is a flipped model however his lectures that are recorded are still amazing and easy to follow. The tests were reasonable if you know all the homework and the study guide. He's one of my favorite professors and I'm so glad I got to take a class with him because he made me love math again!

Prof Collingwood explains things like a textbook. This leads to roundabout explanations that aren't very practical but serviceable. The homework does not match up with the difficulty of lecture material at all. Be prepared to not get 100% on all the webassign hw. Thankfully though the midterms were on par with the worksheets which were easier.

He had to leave 2 weeks in advance due to an emergency, but was still generally accessible. Lectures, for me, were not followable. I would leave lecture understanding a concept and then go and watch Ochem Tutor and realize that I in fact did NOT know the concept. If his lectures don't work, don't go, I got a 3.8 w/ ochem tutor. Grading can be dumb.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he had an emergency and was out for 2 weeks, but was still accessible by email! his lectures go by FAST and are sometimes hard to follow, but his midterms are really similar to the in class examples. could have been a lot worse but wasn't the best, i basically taught myself 60% of the concepts.
Collingwood is a good professor so long as you understand the lecture content well and can follow along with his speed. Strong Algebra background recommended for his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hark, ye who value thy mind and sanity beware! A most accursed and treacherous scholar walks among us, a professor in name only, yet truly a bringer of woe and despair. This fiend did abandon his flock but two weeks ere the final trials leaving us to flounder in the abyss of ignorance. No aid. No lead but a gaping void where knowledge should dwell.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I felt like Collingwood didn't want to be there at every lecture I attended. Never did I once go to a lecture that I felt clearly helped my on the assignments and not at all towards the final. The TA I had also was very poor at teaching.
Teaches well but papers are tough

Compared to my other friends in the course, they all had objectively easier teachers who lectured in a more concise manner. Use office hours and study very hard. keep in mind that each MATH124 professor writes their own midterms (2 midterms, 1 final), and the other professors' midterms seemed to be easier.

Prof. Collingwood was a rather traditional but informative professor. His classes were mainly lectures, homework, and tests. Beware: his midterms were way easier than the finals. The finals resemble the tougher HW questions. Otherwise, he was a clear lecturer and can tell you clearly and quickly about derivatives.

His lecture is super heavy and a little boring, with simple powerpoints only and he writes on the screen. He goes really fast that you'd better not being distracted for one minute. Homwork heavy, needs like 8 or 10 hours a week to complete every week. Test is tough as the time is too short of 50 minutes, so prepare well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This man is an amazing lecturer. Clear voice, steady pace, and doesn't leave any move unexplained. I didn't need credit for 124 and just needed to take math 125, but I didn't feel prepared by my high school and the AP curriculum, so I took 124 at UW. So much more clicked with him. Dude's great
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Collingwood's lecturing style was very informative, even explaining why theorems work. And he answered questions in a clear and earnest manner. The homework could be quite difficult, but that's typical at the UW, but was also strangely helpful and guiding. My TA Dora Kassabova was also amazing and an extremely thorough explainer.

This class is very difficult so be prepared. On average my friend and I dedicate about 24 hrs a week to this class. Mr. Collingwood though is a great teacher. He explains the content very well and answers a lot of questions during lecture. He's also very patient and nice and goes over parts for clarity. Overall great teacher and would recommend!

Super good at explaining material for such a hard course. I've never had a teacher who has had such a clear teaching style that's understandable to the students, in my opinion. I took calc in high school which may have helped, but this course taught me more than anything I learned in high school.
Mid

Pretty chill guy. Grade in the class is defined almost entirely by the two midterms and final, but there are a lot of resources available online for those. Your understanding of the material relies heavily on how much work you are willing to do outside class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing proffesor. Took for 411/412 and would highly recommend him. Did a weird structure of lectures online, and then class time for questions and homework. Was nervous about it, but it worked out really well. As long as you show up and try, you should have no problem getting a good grade. He does grade based on attendance though.

There is a lot of information covered in this class, and he goes by very fast. All of the exams were much more difficult than any homework or practice exams we were given (the practice exams were from previous years exams). The class average for each exam was around 50% and he didn't do much curving if any.

He knows his stuff and will explain to you if you need help, just ask. Class itself used a flipped classroom model + participation for doing a worksheet with your group. Homework really isn't too bad once you split it up. Helpful review sheet before every exam, always see him engaging with students in class. Great professor!

Prof Collingwood definitely made math bearable for me. Prepare to keep up because he can be fast paced, but he does know what he's talking about so pay attention to all his examples. He is very clear on his expectations of what you need to learn and is pretty helpful for clarifying questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really like Prof. Collingwood!!!!! He tried to explain the concepts to us as clear as he could and the stuff he taught in lectures is really straightforward. If you watch all lectures and make sure to do archives before exams, you will definitely get a good grade for this class.

This was supposed to be an in-person class. After the first week of online classes, he decided to go online for "just one more week." Instead of doing lectures, he made us watch an hour-long video on our own time and then come to the Zoom class and ask questions. I am not paying a cent for any more online classes.

I actually enjoyed his lectures more than I thought I would. The class is fairly easy if you remember any high school calculus he responds to questions on the homework pretty quickly. Only thing I didn't like about the class was that he makes you watch a recorded lecture of his from like 8 years ago before every in-person lecture.

From what I've heard from my friends, this is the hardest math 124 professor there was during my quarter. He definitely knows what he's talking about but he works fast. You learn more from the pre-lecture videos of him teaching it back in 2013 than going to in-person lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Horrendous professor. Had watch 1-2 poorly recorded lectures before actual lecture, fast paced, and his exams gave me migraines. Note: homework for his course was due sooner (by 1-3 days) than the other profs.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lectures are recorded, we are forced to watch his lectures back in 2013, which is super blurry, pretty sure you can't even read his work. He doesn't care about if his students understand the content or not. Just choose other profs instead of this dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is the most difficult class I have taken in my entire life. He is a horrific professor who gives out a tremendous amount of homework and everyone without at least hs calc is screwed even though it is supposed to be calc 1. This class has been h*ll for me and I have had several mental breakdowns due to this man and his horrible teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class was very challenging and fast paced. Lectures were recorded , long and very dense in material. Professor did not seem to care if students really understood and these concepts are objectively hard and he just kept going. Homeworks were very long and multiple pages long. Your grade was also dependent on very few things.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: one of the worst class I've ever had here. Pro spent lots of time on lecture, but never actually care if anyone know what he's talking about. The abstract algebra series are supposed to start with group theory and then ring theory. He just reversed the order and started with ring theory first, that people could not even find any helpful resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's okay. The class is pretty tough but he does a decent enough job. My one pet peeve is he isn't super responsive with student feedback and emails but the TAs pick up the slack (like in most of the math department). The homework is a little excessive but he puts up lectures and notes online and the tests are reasonable.

He was not understanding at all specifically with what is going on in the world currently (corona and BLM protests). He does not go much into detail and it was just a horrible experience overall i do NOT recommend taking him.

Professor Collingwood's Math 124 class is difficultafter all, it is a weed-out, but he is fair and helpful. His lectures are actually useful and the homework load is reasonable and actually reflects the lecture material (which is surprisingly rare at the UW math department).

411 with Collingwood consisted of group work for each homework assignment. He has a system and if you stick with the system, don't be a bad partner, and do all your homework you will pass. I am not the greatest mathematician. But take it from me, his material is well chosen. He doesn't involve himself much but his class system is top notch.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took Dave for Math 411+412 (Algebra for Teachers) and he was excellent. The concepts were sometimes difficult for me to understand (all proofs/abstract), but he was willing to talk me and walk me through each concept one-on-one until I understood it. He would always take the time to help and do things for/with me!

In my experience, I felt that Collingwood was burnt out, unmotivated, and didn't care about his students' learning. I spent hours on each homework assignment, and there are 2-3 per week. Without a quiz section, it's very difficult to get help. Even when I emailed Collingwood for a private meeting, he brushed me off and suggested other options.
Very good teacher. Makes every detail clear.

I don't think he really cares about his students.  He seems like he's been doing this for long and maybe he's a little jaded?  His Midterms are ridiculous though, the concepts are applicable but he finds new and creative ways to bust you up. Maybe he's better in person but on-line?... Just don't do it.
his midterm was crazy
Cheap textbook, good explanations and accessible lectures. Rushes through examples quickly and leaves out details, lots of quizzes

I took his online class last quarter. It was average hard level, basically for the content of Math 124 isn't that hard. In first week, he informed some important things you should know in pre-calculus, but You need your classmates on Piazza or go to the website such as The Math Page to make more specific. Tests are little bit tough. READ BOOK!

I was good at math in high school. I got an A in calculus, but it didn't count for college credits, so I had to take it here. DO NOT TAKE CALCULUS FROM COLLINGWOOD, ESPECIALLY ONLINE. There is so much homework, the tests are ridiculously hard, the lectures aren't very clear, and basically, I've never felt more dumb in my life.

Taking this class online wouldn't have been much different from taking it in person. The TAs and professor hold office hours and they are very accessible. Online sections also have an online forum where you can get questions answered by peers, TAs, and the professor. Practice tests and homework are much easier than tests so practice hard problems.
This is a difficult class and Collingwood makes you work for your grade. However his explanations are very clear and he has an obvious passion for what he is teaching.

Oh, Dr. Collingwood. From your boring, uninspired lectures to your impossibly difficult tests, I can say with complete certainty that you are my least favorite professor thus far. In lecture, the the problems are manageable, but on tests, they are frustratingly advanced. Wise decision: choose a different professor for 124.
Worst professor at UW this year. Horrible explainer, and goes from 0 to 100 REAL QUICK when it comes to test-question difficulty (enough to have 40% exam averages). Avoid Collingwood like the plague.

Terrible class. Tests include material that have never been mentioned anywhere. Lectures are not clear and when attempting to do homework there is a fair amount of material that you never went over. To add to it all, he does the classic assigning a ton of homework during dead week because he didn't assign it earlier. Avoid if possible.
The tests don't cover what he goes over in lecture. Seems to take pride in making his exams incredibly confusing (to the point where the average is a 40%). Do not take this class if you can help it.

With the class being online and most communication done online you have to stay on top of the work and the emails. Take advantage of the online resources and you will succeed. However, if you have an issue with grades for any reason you won't get much help from David, he tends to be short and if you mess up, well, you mess up.

Took Collingwood's Math 124 online and it was a great decision.  He teaches his material well, and problems on the 2 midterms and homeworks mirror things he covers in lecture.  Definitely take his class if you have the option.  Only difference compared to in person class is no quizzes.
Hard professor who gives challenging exams. I studied every day for 7+ hours, but still failed every single exam he gave.
He's really clear in his explanation, and you're sure to understand the work. However, his exams are pretty hard. Aside from that, he's a great professor.

The class is really hard and he isn't very helpful. His lectures are okay but he goes through things pretty quickly with few examples. He was not helpful at all when I approached him after class. Thank god I had a wonderful TA.

This course is extremely challenging, especially having not taken calculus in high school. He moves very fast, but is very thorough in his examples and explanation. He also videotapes his lectures and puts them online which is helpful if you don't understand something. Just make sure you don't talk during his class or mess around on your phone.
Very nice and helpful professor. Lectures were clear, but boring. Has videotaped lectures, so you don't have to show-up all the time! His tests are fair and he tells you what's on it beforehand.

He's a really nice guy, and his lectures are pretty good. He's willing to answer questions if you have them, and he's definitely helpful. The tests are quite challenging, though, but that's probably the same for all math 124 classes...

Pay attention in lecture. This is necessary for all calculus courses. Unless you've already taken calc, which i have, it is necessary to attend pretty much all lectures and copy down what he writes. As long as you pay attention in class you should do fine. He doesnt give quizzes, so grades are based almost solely on hwk and tests. do well on tests.
He is a good teacher, but he gives hard test!

Collingwood is a good teacher.  Very reasonable in what he expects of you.  Basically tells you exactly what types of problems will be on each test.  Just practice the problems and you should do fine.  Dont bothering buying the text book.  I never used it.
He isn't particularly interesting, but he is reasonable and teaches pretty well. Math 124 with him wasn't bad at all.

At first I had qualms about his class, but he turned out to be pretty good! He goes through different types of problems and approaches, and makes sure you understand. Go to class, copy whatever he writes, do a lot of practice and you'll be fine!
Great math teacher, sometimes he's too thorough, but that's better than not being thorough at all.

He knows what he is teaching, he just doesn't...teach it. he gives you a textbook that is pretty good in explaining it, but it doesn't give students enough practice or usable examples for the material. Great, knowledgeable TAs and very helpful himself. Be sure to do all the problems that the books offers or you won't be prepared for the final.
Perhaps the best professor I've had at UW.

After hearing about all the other math professors he seems very cool and much easier then other ones. He has great TA's and he is always willing to answer questions in class and compromises with his students a lot!!!

Pretty good teacher, seems nice, but he doesn't prepare you for his tests. Almost as if he is setting you up for failure. On a scale of 1-5 1 being easy, he assignes level 1 and 2 questiosn, but tests with 4 and 5 without showing you how to do them. Expects more out of you than he communicates.
Such a great professor ever. I wish I could take his class again! However, midterms are kinda hard in some way.
Good teacher... Did see him wearing spandex at the IMA one day, which was mildly traumatic...
he's a really nice guy.. he does everything he can to teach the class.. so he does a really good job.. but its a really ugly topic especially if u never took calculus before..
He's very effective in teaching.  Gives you many examples to learn from.  If you don't understand, he'll do the solve the problems step by step.
excellent teacher, very aproachable, knows his stuff
he's a great teacher, but the class in general is very difficult. Tests are very hard, but he's a good professor who knows what he's doing.
Pretty boring and dry. Saw him naked in the locker room once.
Collingwood was good at explaining things clearly and though his lectures were boring, they definetly helped me understand the material. Going to lecture everyday really helps.
it's a huge loss to UW that he left. simply GOATED on all accounts. can only wish him the very best.

Good lecturer, clear expectations, has note sheets with everything written, no curveballs, lots of opportunity for extra credit, extremely flexible for late or missing assignments. You have a week to do all homework - plenty of time to get help. Open note tests and more time than necessary - low stress.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: honestly just such a great guy above all else. he's enthusiastic about what he does, and it really shines through in his lectures. class is super well-structured and he's very clear about what you need to do to succeed. lectures are always recorded and homework is directly correlated to what's covered in class.
It's Ryan Creedon!

Ryan is so caring and his classes are sooo organised and clear. He's the kind of professor that lets you breeze through the class and focus on learning the material instead of stressing about grades. Great professor!!!
Prof. Creedon is soooo good at teaching and lecturing. He makes the lectures so much funner!

I think all the other 5/5 ratings speak for themselves. But Dr. Ryan is genuinely THE BEST Math instructor I've ever had in my life. He genuinely made me fall in love with the subject and you can see that he is really passionate about what he's teaching and GOOD at teaching what he's teaching. WE LOVE DR RYAN!!!!
Really good prof! accessible outside of class and always willing to explain things further!
BEST PROF EVER!!!!
Best Instructor Ever!
Dr Ryan is the best teacher I have ever had in my entire life. Dude is so funny nice and caring. Insanely funny and a great teacher! He is the king!!!
awesome
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Utilize Ryan's weekly lecture notes, they really help.
The best professor I had at UW so far! Ryan's lecture is awesome and gives out lots of extra credit.
Really understanding professor and the class was extremely easy.

Great professor for 301 and other amath classes! super considerate and wants to help his students succeed + clear expectations for the class. Well explained and thought out lectures too. Course content was also super interesting and applicable to a variety of fields!

Very caring prof! He knows that there are issues with the accessibility with the topics often covered in math, and is making a HUGE contribution toward the change of that. Easily the best math prof that I've ever had, and will happily chat about topics not covered in the scope of the course :)
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: amazing prof if you can take a class with him absolutely go for it he made me like math more than i already did :)

Great Professor. I always hated coding but with Professor Creedon it is fun! Quizzes are mostly on concepts and not coding, and the lectures were always fun to go to. Before Ryan, I hated Math @ UW, but he has changed my mind! He also offers a lot of extra credit opportunities! If you see him teaching this course make sure to register!!!

Definitely my favorite prof this quarter!  Prof Creedon is excellent at communicating expectations and comes into class with a lot of excitement (esp for an 8:30)!  Seems like a really down to earth guy, talks about his cat a lot which is endearing.  Homework/quizzes are closely related to lectures and grading is generous.  Highly recommend!

Amazing lectures, relatively easy homework if you pay attention in class and overall a really good professor. This class had online quizzes and weekly homework but no tests! Would definitely take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I would go over RMP's limit to try and get out everything I loved about this man. My only complaint is MATLAB only works the way you want it to about 20% of the time, no matter how experienced of a programmer you already are. But that is UW's fault, not Creedon's. Take him and you'll be one of the few UW students who didn't completely hate 301.

Professor Creedon gave great lectures and explained linear algebra concepts in simple terms. He was very caring and receptive to student feedback. The course was not too difficult, especially if you have taken math 208 at UW.

He is the best professor I've ever met in UW. He is an enthusiastic person. The grading criteria is clear and there are extra credit opportunity throughout the quarter. Strongly encourage to take his course.

Arguably the best prof at UW. Ryan's lectures are always easy to follow and his humor keeps me engaged. The HW tends to be long, but the questions are interesting so it didn't feel too bad. No exams or quizzes, only HW assignments every week and a final research project. Very responsive and helpful through email and on Piazza.

He is the ever best Amath professor I have met, I took Amath 383 this term, but it doesn't showed in the course selection. The educational quality and course prepartion is perfect. I would suggest everyone take his course

Homie is great. I had taken linear algebra prior to this class so the concepts were already familiar, but he teaches in a way that is very easy to understand which is good for students new to linear algebra. The HW itself was very closely related to the lectures, so it wasn't too bad.

Ryan is always positive, energetic, and enthusiastic about teaching, which helped keep me interested in the topics. He is clear about how to succeed. He clearly wants the best for his students and cares for everyone. He is passionate about teaching and what he is teaching. I definitely would recommend Ryan to anyone interested in taking AMATH 352!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Jacob Cooper is easily the best professor I have had at UW. The class itself is not too difficult, the quiz grading is pretty specific, though.

My favorite professor at UW. He really cares about making sure students learn, and all the content is really interesting. Professor Cooper's classes have had the best learning to stress ratios out of any I've taken. I'd sign up for any class if I saw he was teaching it.
Great professor overall from over the summer
It's super evident he really cares that students are learning the material. Super fun and nice professor, made the class super enjoyable!

Professor Jake and this class were lots of fun. You really do learn a lot about the content and the class is set up in a way where learning the content is actually enjoyable. But, the class does focus a lot on participation and things like polling and scratchoffs were weighed very heavily and do not leave any room for error.
Nice and funny!

This is by far one of the most engaging professors I have taken at this school. His lectures are genuinely entertaining, and he's a very friendly and fair professor. If you get the chance to take a class of his, take it
My favorite professor ever!! If you get a chance, take a class from him. He's such a quirky guy and he makes learning so interesting and fun.
best sharky prof but bit difficult

An absolute gem of a professor. Cares deeply about his students' learning and about the topics he's teaching. Lectures are super engaging. Exams can be challenging but if you thoroughly understand the material they're doable, especially since he awards the occasional bonus point.

Update: I actually ended up doing fine in his class, but omg it stressed me out so bad. Cooper has really hard tests, & I feel like he didnt accept my alternate explanations until later in the quarter. He is an AMAZING lecturer who makes sure his students have good understanding and feel cared for. Ultimately though, if good grades are hard, I hate
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I went into the class thinking it would be the easiest of the intro series, but it was honestly the hardest. Every exam question felt like a trick question, and I don't think my grade reflected my understanding of the material. That said, I did enjoy the content, but the class structure was not my favorite.

Jacob Cooper's class was one of my favorite classes I've taken at the school. Bio 220 was a requirement for my major, but he made class fun and interesting while simultaneously informative. Homework as a small review before going to class was a very nice approach, and the work load for the class was reasonable.

Cooper's tests are very hard. That said, he's such an incredible professor that it more than makes up for it. Knowledgeable, funny, passionate, cares deeply about his students. Excellent lecturer, and very willing to explain things differently if you don't understand. I wish every college prof were Jacob Cooper, one of my favorites I've had.

Jake is an amazing lecturer, he's charismatic, knowledgeable, and very human. I'd absolutely recommend taking a course with him, he does all that he is able to make the class accessible! He makes concepts digestible. Some exam questions are poorly written truthfully and are nothing like other Biol exams in the series.

Best bio class I've taken and imo much easier than 180 and 200 and I want to say it's because of Cooper. He cares a lot and it enthusiastic without it being over the top or annoying. I really like how exams are graded because if you have the right thought process you get credit, so they are graded pretty leniently. Highly recommend him as a prof.

Dr. Cooper is one of those professors that you take in college once and remember for years after. He's a genuinely caring, bright guy who goes above and beyond in so many little ways. Yes, I was annoyed that his class didn't round on 0.5% like Crowe's Bio 200, but I did really love lecture. He gave everyone shark temporary tattoos on the last day:)
Greatest professor I have ever had or will ever have. Outstanding in every way that a professor can be measured. Anybody who speaks ill of Jacob Cooper in any capacity is an enemy of me personally.

Jacob is my favorite professor in the basic biology series. He has a very strong sense of empathy and a reassuring academic style. His exam leans more towards applying the concept of learning in situations similar to the examples given in class.
He is very friendly and patient. He is a very, very nice person.

Prof. Cooper is very caring and passionate about biology. He has clear grading criteria and is overall a really pleasant and pleasant person who ties in real data from papers and experts in his lecture. The content feels so much richer as a result and his exams and grading criteria are extremely fair. EASILY best bio prof ever.

hall of fame professor. maybe the greatest to ever touch the game. focus on really deep conceptual / systematic understanding instead of pure memorization and you'll do good on his tests. you should know every detail of every system you learned and understand WHY changing each individual variable affects / doesn't affect others. highly recommend.

Honestly I'm not sure why people hype him up. His lectures are pretty bad and he rants too much. I often rewatch lectures to understand material better, each lecture only has 25 minutes of actual content, if attendance wasn't graded I wouldn't go. He doesn't care about technical issues, fully wouldn't give me credit for days I was there.

STELLAR PROFESSOR. He clearly wants students to learn and puts SO MUCH effort into his lectures. He uses lecture slide animations and cool biology studies to engage students and keep bio interesting. And his explanations for everything are IMPRESSIVELY clear. Yes, some test qs can be tricky, but they are fair (similar difficulty to the practice).

He teaches on niche scenarios and doesn't explain broader concepts and then tests on other niche scenarios that have nothing to do with either. You get graded on how well you can read his mind. He puts out four poorly worded practice questions. This class is impossible, and I did well in 180 and 200, I am not fluent in mind reading.

Dr. Cooper is such an amazing professor. You can tell that he loves the subject and genuinely cares for his students. His lectures are incredible engaging. His tests are difficult, yes, but once you get used to his style of questions (mostly applying knowledge rather than memorising things), it's definitely doable. Oh and go to office hours!

Cooper is by far my favorite teacher at UW. He is compassionate, funny, respectful, has great vibes, and excellent at teaching. He is always available to speak with after class and earnestly cares about each student. Some exam Qs were tricky as they applied material to unexpected situations. But overall, he is SO worth it. (And he adores sharks!)

Dr. Cooper is without-a-doubt my favorite teacher at UW. He's fun, compassionate, chill, inspirational, & overall has great vibes and teaches very well. He is always available after class to speak to. Some of his exam questions are tricky as they require applying learned material to various real-world situations. Overall though, he's SO worth it.

Cooper was enthusiastic, but exams always had questions that would be incredibly difficult to answer no matter how much work you put in. This makes it difficult for people who put in lots of work to get a 4.0 - Most people will be stuck right below. I watched every lecture over again to take notes and studied countless hours but ended with a 3.9.

Nice guy & great lecturer but tests were awful. Vague questions with unfairly specific rubric criteria, impossible to get full credit. Tests don't reflect material, feels like solving a riddle & stubborn with regrades. Content is cool but this class made me question my interest in science. Be prepared to study super hard and do mediocre at best.

Super nice guy and fun engaging lectures, but really bad tests. Vague questions and he expects you to be able to fish out what answer he's looking for. It's really difficult to do well on the tests even if you feel very confident in the material.

I had Dr. Cooper for both BIO 220 and 359, and he was an excellent professor! He does a great job at breaking down the material to make it easier to understand. You can tell he is very passionate about what he does and cares about your success. As long as you keep up with the assignments and attend lecture, you will be fine.

Had Jake for 180 which was amazing but 220 felt more harder because of the concepts, had HWs not RQs and we barely had practice problems and if we did they weren't really relevant to content and quite vague this time. Questions were interesting always a fish in the questions rather than humans concept so alot of it is applying to different systems.

Cooper might seem like a nice guy but he is honestly the worst professor I have had at uw. His tests are worth 65% of your grade and he makes up questions that are so weird to the level where you start to rethink your life. He barely provides any practice questions for them too. Honestly recommend waiting and taking the course with someone else.

Dr. Cooper is very likable and engaging but his tests suck. It's very unclear what content from the slides he actually tests you on, there are few practice problems, and he goes very big-picture when talking but is very detail-heavy on tests. Also, his exams have the same issue as other bio series and focus too much on keywords and not concepts.

Lectures are AMAZING, he's a great public speaker. But, I talked to a TA and Cooper decided to remove most of the practice problems available 4 us in his curriculum, so there's only q's he made available. We only end up getting 8-10 practice problems PER exam. Learning is problem solving. There's NO practice for his exams, ydk what to expect at all
I don't know why the ratings are so good. Yea he's a good professor and very sweet but you are set up for failure with those exams with the averages at 60-65 percent you're lucky to 3.0.

I actually enjoy to his lectures because he teaches in an engaging and funny way. Really makes you feel accommodated for and makes everyone feel seen in a big class. Good at helping you understand concepts and I think the test questions are honestly fine,  mostly easy to understand, and he will give back test points sometimes and values effort.

Took Dr. Cooper for 180 & 220--you know how you can just tell that a professor loves *teaching*? That's Dr. Cooper, his lectures are so engaging and hilarious. The exams are frustrating since so many questions are vague and you kind of have to read the exam maker's mind. Other than that, I want to major in biology physiology 'cause of him

Amazing prof for sure. HIS EXAMS omg is vein of my existence. His exams are so much more vague than any other professor. "Suppose I snap my finger and your O2 in lung magically turns into N2" LIKE WDYM?? But I love him cus he is caring and best bio prof for sure. SO hard to get good grade (90-100) due to lack of practice exams.

BEST PROF I'VE EVER HAD!! Dr. Cooper makes lectures extremely engaging to the point where class time flies so quickly. He breaks tough concepts down and simplifies them to make them more understandable. Plus, he connects with students more than most professors. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

Jake is a very understanding professor and enjoys the topics he teaches in this course. Most, if not all, of the material I had never learned before, which made the quizzes challenging, but his practice exams are helpful. There is one project that had a tough grading rubric, but is manageable. Overall, I would recommend this course!
Uses scientific approaches to improve quality of lectures and is always trying to maximize learning over plain memorization. Incredibly caring and approachable, take his class!
Take him. He is amazing. Not only you will enjoy going to the lectures, you will actually learn so much from it. I personally enjoyed it so much that I got really good grade!

Took Him Summer Quarter & was the best decision I made Prof and TA were amazing. They were encouraging and cared about you. Lec was a lot of discussion and poll everywhere but in a good way. If you review lec and do the study questions the exams will be fine nothing to stress about. There are drops so if you feel sick it's okay. Take Him If you can

Dr. Cooper was alright. He did give a good amount of drops for exams/homework/labs/attendance, but his lectures weren't super engaging. I did learn and understand it for the most part, but there were just so many "discuss with your neighbour" stuff that it's hard to follow his lectures, which were sometimes too vague too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: how many letters are there in 'dr. cooper'

Dr. Cooper was by far the best professor I've had at UW so far. The content was still a bit hard, but he broke things down and made the lectures entertaining, plus there were plenty of drops for labs, homework, and one exam drop that included the final. Dr. Cooper makes it clear that he cares about his students and wants us to succeed.

Jake is easily the best professor I've had thus far and I honestly doubt I'll ever have a professor as good as him ever again. He made his lectures incredibly interesting and relatable, and I learned a ton in his class. It's clear how much effort he put into teaching this class and how much he cares about his students. 100/10 would recommend.

Dr. Cooper is the best professor I've had during my 2 years at UW. The lectures were engaging and the tests were graded with generous partial credit. It's clear how passionate they are about their job and how much effort they put into this course. If you have the chance to take a class with Dr. Cooper, do it!!

Amazing professor. May have less practice materials than other professors but he has only been teaching this course for a short amount of time. Pay attention to lecture content (exams were pretty much whatever was covered in lecture). I appreciated Cooper because he kept it within the scope of the class and made sure we didn't need to memorize.

Best biology prof. I ve had so far, amazing lectures with examples, practices, and discussions, which is a lot better compared to most other classes of similar size (physics 1xx, chem 1xx). He also gives easy to understand explanations to complicated topics. Getting a good grade in his class encouraged me to continue in Bio major. 10/10 recommend.

Dr. Cooper is probably the best professor I have had so far. The lectures are mandatory, but they are incredibly helpful and his style of teaching really helped me learn and understand the material. As long as you pay attention in lecture, you should be set. He also grades very fairly and partial credit is given pretty generously.

Best prof I've had in 2 years. He makes lectures interesting and despite this being one of his first quarters teaching BIOL 220, he was flexible and even went through and remade blank versions of slides for people who take notes. The practice exams were short but relevant and useful. You can tell he loves physiology and connecting with students.

Not as easy as BIOL180 but Dr. Cooper has made this quarter so much more bearable. I like his lecture style the most out of all bio classes I have taken. He keeps it interesting but is also so reasonable. Tests are slightly difficult but you get the hang of them and partial credit is forgiving. Dr. Cooper enjoys his job and cares for his students.

By far my favorite biology professor so far. Very excitable and passionate and easy to engage with in lectures. Funny and the tests are graded pretty fairly, not so much like BIOL 180 because there's a little bit more wiggle room and as long as you're able to apply concept logic you can do pretty good. Highly encouraging and positive as a teacher.

Dr. Cooper was so engaging and clearly cared so much about biology and his students. This was his first time teaching this course and he did as much as he could to make it fair, organized, and a reasonable amt of work for us. Test grading was a little questionable/picky sometimes but overall not bad. Just review lecture slides and you'll be set.

Put an incredible amount of effort into lectures and listening to students. Class was enjoyable and I look up to him as a prof. However, the exams were hard to prepare for, difficult, and graded somewhat questionably. Since it's their first time teaching 220, we did not get any practice questions, but future quarters will probably have it easier.

Cooper does really care about Bio, but I don't think he cares as much about his students. It is not that difficult to do well if you put time in, but some test questions are graded very questionably. When I got marked wrong for questions and brought textbook evidence for my answer, I was told it was just wrong. It says it in the textbook so idk.

This was Dr. Cooper's first time teaching Bio 220, so although I wish we had more practice problems, he tried his best. Time went by so quickly in this class because his lectures were always engaging. Also, you can tell that he genuinely cares about his students and tries to grade as fairly as possible. Overall, this was a great class to be in.
Dr. Cooper is such an amazing professor, highly recommend any of their classes!

I took 220 when it was his first quarter teaching. Intellectually, class was easy. However, exam writing and grading were written like he was teaching 180 again. Questions were too open-ended but looking for specific topics/wording/phrases when he did not ask for them. When taking exams, expect to try to read his mind on free response questions.

Absolutely phenomenal professor, I had him for 180 and loved him so much that I took 354 with him as well! He's incredibly engaging and kind, one of the best professors I have had here. I'd take another class taught by him in a heartbeat
One of the best professors I've ever had at UW. Professor Cooper has a great talent for conveying the most important ideas in a very concise and engaging way.

This is one of the best professors you can take at UW. Took bio180 at FHL and he made it such a good experience. Learned a lot, I just suck at bio so didn't do great on the 3 exams throughout the quarter. But he still helped me pass, great human
This is one of the best professors I have ever met.  His classes were great and always kept my focus, I learned a lot.

Jake is awesome. Truly cares about what's being taught and about how well students are doing. The lectures were mainly example-based rather than material, so it was important to do the reading before class or I was lost. As a result, the tests were super similar to lectures in that they were examples or case studies. Love love love jake!

definitely the best prof I have had so far at UW. Exams are not easy or hard. My man is very passionate and super nice. Very clear to understand. Too bad couldn't take him for bio 200. There I got the worst prof so far, which had super boring and confusing lectures.

Genuinely the best teacher I have ever had.. Jake genuinely cares about you, and about you learning. Outside of the class, Jake was always ready to help you learn more. Learning with Jake was a wonderful experience that I will always remember. Jakes Bio Lecture forever. Beef for life.

One of my favorite, if not my favorite professors at UW. I took BIO 180 with him at Friday Harbor Labs so it was pretty different from the giant lectures on main campus. Regardless, Dr. Cooper was super accommodating, engaging, and funny. Take BIO 180 with him and you'll have a great time!!
i love this man
Loved taking Bio 180 with him, his lectures were always well done and you could tell that he cares about every student's learning experience. Would highly recommend, favorite UW professor so far.

Favorite course & teacher so far at UW. Makes everyone feel valued and just radiates joy and passion. He has that cool uncle vibe and a great sense of humor. Class is super interesting and the elegance of the topics kept blowing my mind.

This has been my favorite class at UW so far. Professor Cooper provides numerous studies to help explain the Game Theory concepts, which are very relevant to everyday life. His lectures were super fun and engaging and having everyday group work allowed me to actually meet other people in the class. Would highly recommend taking this Honors course!

Jake is probably the best prof I've ever had. He really emphasizes learning and understanding concepts over just getting a grade, and makes lectures fun and engaging while still being informative. He is also very supportive and accommodating to students needs. Can't say enough good things about him, definitely take him if you can :)

Jake is my fav prof at UW. He is so funny in lecture and has a very interesting and unique teaching style. The exams were on par with your normal biology exams so they were hard but nothing crazy. He is so understanding and accommodating you can tell that he really cares about his students and genuinely loves to teach. Can't say enough good things!
Very caring professor, he made recorded lectures very interesting.

I had an AWESOME experience in Cooper's class. He is a sweet guy who will go to great lengths to make sure students succeed. Online, be ready to advocate for yourself and ask for help if you need it- it could be easy to get lost in an online class. Would definitely recommend Cooper.

I'd give him a 6/5 if I could. He's easily the most supportive, friendly, and understanding prof I've ever had at UW. He regularly goes the extra mile to make sure you understand the topic, always give feedback on assignments and his focus is for you to learn, not to test you. You would make a mistake by not taking him.

I hate chemistry, those hard subjects, etc., but he made biology one of my favorite subjects, he was an awesome professor and makes biology so interesting and easy to understand. He doesn't use unnecessary words, speaks clearly and concisely. Cares more that you learn the material well than do busy work earn "the grade".

Dr. Cooper is hands down the best professor Ive ever had. He teaches with great enthusiasm, which makes the lectures 100x better to sit though. He encouraged open communication and always listened and considered students concerns and suggestions regarding the course structure and workload. All around a remarkable professor.

Prof. Cooper truly wants his students to succeed. I took his online bio course and his lectures were easy to follow and the course was well organized. Would definitely take his class again if I could. Exams were flexible and considerate of students despite being challenging (still realistic).

Dr. Cooper is hands down the best professor I've had at UW. He's funny and kind and goes out of his way to make class enjoyable. It's also clear that he wants all of his students to succeed. Office hours were super helpful and tests required some critical thinking but weren't that hard as long as you studied.

Cooper is ok. He's a decent lecturer, but his instructional team definitely did not know how to run an online class. A lot of his exams were very well written, but there was widespread variance in the grading. Overall, the course could have been organized better, but Cooper wasn't terrible. 180 is a weeder, so online or not, they can't make it easy

took online in summer 2020. There's readings, reading quizzes, pre-recorded lectures & lecture questions. Seems like a lot but once you establish a routine it's not bad. Lectures are short, simple, & easy to understand. Readings go more in depth (helpful). U can earn full credit on every practice exam by reflecting on mistakes. Real exams r tougher

Cooper is satirical and ostentatious. While seemingly caring about his students, he believes himself and his instructor team holds the invariable truth to all questions.
