Inefficient virtual lecturing isn't his fault but I readily learned nothing more than an affectation of common senses spoken in biology jargon in this poorly administered class.

cares about leveling out the playing field as evenly as possible for all students, really tough exams but your best bet is familiarizing yourself with as many potential dilemmas as possible and digging deep into understanding each presented concept

Solid choice. Definitely stands out from other STEM profs because he shows genuine care for his students' success and generally keep lectures interesting. Exams are kind of tough, but that's true for any STEM class. Fun to listen to, never condescending. His class definitely gave me more hope in finding success in science courses at UW.
Professor Cooper really cares about the learning aspect of the course. The lectures are interesting and engaging. If you get the opportunity to have professor Cooper, you definitely should.

Amazing professor in biology. He really motivates students to learn and understand the concepts important to become a scientist. He puts in so much effort in class to make them interesting to think about. Tests were quite challenging, but for the things you learn, it is definitely worth it. Take classes with Dr. Cooper, you won't regret it!!

Easily the funniest and nicest professor I have ever had. His lectures are really interesting and surprisingly funny. The content is really interesting and the expectations for the class and homework load are very reasonable. I STRONGLY recommend taking his class!
Absolute favorite professor at UW, taught in ways which were both traditional as well as innovative, I looked forward to going to lecture.

Cooper cares A LOT about his job. Almost too much. As a result, his class in general is weirdly personal. He makes u spill your hopes, fears, and insecurities in really corny writing homework assignments that I feel like he reads at night before he goes to bed. He answers piazza in like 30 seconds. His exams are pretty difficult like F/D averages

While Dr. Cooper does his best to be engaging, I feel like his lectures could use more structure, as most of lecture time was spent giving us fun facts, and while they related to what we are learning, I know that I would have benefited from teaching more broadly. Also, he doesn't show grade percentages in canvas, so that sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I WISH I COULD TAKE DR. COOPER FOR BIO 200! He is one of the funniest lectures Ive ever had. He always begins new topics with examples which I find is such a great way of learning because he really makes you think! I would take him again if I could because he was the most engaging professor Ive ever had! Study a lot!

Jake Cooper is hands down the best lecturer I've ever had. He's kind, funny, and genuinely cares so much about his students. His lectures are never too fast, nor too slow; he never tries to cram things in the last few minutes of class, and he never gets behind his teaching schedule for the quarter. He is amazing both as a teacher and a person.

Best professor and hardest exam. Love him and hate him. His lectures are so interesting and he really cares about training students to think like a scientist instead of to simply memorize everything. But his exams seem to be subjective (99% short answers) and it's hard to grasp what is "correct". Some reading quizzes don't match readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Cooper's lectures are amazing. In a course that meets once a day for a majority of the week, I've never experience a stale lecture once! You can tell Dr. Cooper is extremely passionate about the course material and is even more passionate about his students learning. The tests are hard not gonna lie but man does he inspire his students.

Dr. Cooper is the best professor you will take at UW and the only reason BIOL 180 is tolerable. He is hilarious, extremely nice, and very good at his job; you'll come away with a quarter of knowledge that you didn't forget at all. His tests are extremely difficult, so be ready for that. Other than that, the class isn't much work.

Prof Cooper is awesome! He is probably the best Bio prof you will ever have at UW. The class is very organized and the course material is relatively easy. They do daily polling, so you really do have to go to class, plus there are daily reading quizzes and weekly exams/practice exams. But overall, this is a great class!

I love this man with my whole being. A fantastic and engaging lecturer, an uplifting and understanding mentor, and a all around wonderful human being. He and the rest of the teaching team handled the end of W20 with grace, even though they were SO stressed (obviously). Take his class. SO MUCH LOVE for Jake Cooper.

Definitely my favorite professor so far at UW. Unlike other professors that do the equivalent of reading PowerPoint slides for lecture, Dr. Cooper takes what we read from the textbook and explains in greater detail with good examples that make you really think. I love his sense of humor and he's a great lecturer, and puts a lot of effort in.

Only time I've written a review before, and I'm not even in his department! Phenomenal lecturer. I agree on some of the other points about tests, they tend to ask questions that I consider unfair: even if you understand the concepts and how to apply them, you're made to decide on and defend a point that is sometimes arbitrary.

Cooper is a cool dude but like any BIOL 180 class, the tests are absolutely insane. His tests tend to be worded in a very ambiguous manner with little clear instruction so regurgitate what he wants or you won't do very well. Lab is simple and gives you free points for the most part. His lectures can be very disorganized with many tangents as well.

Dr. Cooper cares a lot about his students and gives very engaging lectures. In my experience, though, the content and grading of his game theory course is slightly more challenging than other HONORS classes. However, it was still a great experience and I highly recommend taking Dr. Cooper's classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Cooper has been one of my favorite teachers at UW! Hilarious and topical lectures, with fascinating material every time. He is relatable and kind, great grader if you put in the effort. Clearly cares about his students' and their well being, but treats you like an adult. Would HIGHLY recommend! You won't regret it! Fascinating class, great prof

Jake is a really amazing professor. I took his first offering of a game theory class through the Honors Program and it was so great. He constantly checked in with us to make sure everyone had a thorough understanding of the concepts discussed and he was very caring and had a good sense of humor. This was by far my favorite class and favorite prof

Jake Cooper is such a bomb teacher. He really makes each lecture engaging (idk how that's possible) and tries hard to motivate and inspire students. If you have the chance to take his class i'm sure you won't regret it.

To be honest, Jake is a really good professor. He tries to minimize stress in the classroom by grading lots of things (all under 15% each), but if you do poorly on quizzes you're not going to do great. He also is very, VERY, inspirational, to the point where if you ask a question, he says you're doubting yourself... :/

Probably my favourite professor at UW, he's a really nice guy, funny, and great at lecturing. Nothing in this course was worth a very high percent of your grade so it wasn't too stressful either, he has pretty reasonable expectations for the class.

Unpopular opinion: while Jake is a great professor, the way he taught 354 was terrible. It was mostly taught in a group, he graded polling questions on correctness, and his test questions are unbelievably tough. He makes you think like a scientist, which is fine, but sucks when youre being graded for it and have no prior experience of it.

Hilarious wholesome dude, &his lectures reflect that. Hands down best professor I've ever had in my 2yrs at UW! On the class itself, it's difficult but nothing compared to Chem 142 (Take chem first if you haven't already! Less trouble). Do hw! Labs are easy enough, but tests do require that you not only know the material but also how to apply it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Jacob's a great prof, really nice, great sense of humor, and most importantly caring. Won't lie, this class will challenge you, but personally I've enjoyed it so far. As well, Dr. Cooper's grading rubric spaces the grading out; quizzes, labs, poll questions, reading, etc. One bad quiz score or lab write up won't sink your grade. Take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: While I didn't like intro bio (it was mostly review for me), JAKE COOPER IS THE BEST. He's got a bit of a cult following at UW, and for good reason! He is so energetic, fun, caring, and effective at explaining material. He encourages class engagement and tries really hard to listen well to students' questions. I'd absolutely recommend him as a prof
He is the best lecturer!!! He is smart, passionate, fun and he knows how to engage students in class. This is a hard class, but he brings out the interesting part of biology.

Dr Cooper was my favorite UW prof. He gives reading each night and weekly quizzes, which can be annoying, but if you pay attention to them you will 100% pass the tests. His lectures are very important to attend to succeed, but they are VERY fun. He also makes an effort to get to know you, and remembered me a quarter later when I saw him in HCK.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: HE IS THE BEST! If you can move your schedule around to take him then do it! His lectures are extremely interesting. Every time I feel like not being there, but his lectures made me feel glad that I was there. His expectations are very clear and his exams are straightforward nothing really tricky.
Best lecturer in college yet! Engaging, interesting, inspirational. Expectations are very clear. Wish more professors would be like him.

This processor is really awesome, great things is all that I have learned. I took bio after a long time and the material was also really new, but Dr. Cooper is really awesome at explaining and making his lectures the most wonderful lectures out there. The lectures are really engaging and get ready to be wowed and I would take it with him again.

2nd class w/Dr. Cooper, and the fact that many raters here have taken from him before should tell you a lot. The average grades are higher than in bio 180, but  the course is not easier because you can easily spend 3 hours trying to understand the details of primary literature. Enthusiastic & always answers questions. Best prof I've had at UW.

This is my second class with Dr. Cooper and it was the best decision I made. I learned so much from his class. He's a genuinely caring and thoughtful person. Lectures are based on discussion, polling, and fascinating scientific studies. He's inspired me to study evolutionary biology. Best professor ever.

Biol 356 was the second class I've taken with Jake and it was probably the best decision I've made this year. I felt like I learned something new every lecture and the workload was very reasonable (The tests are way easier than 180). Also Jake brought the whole class Macaroons for Passover because he's the best.

Jake's the best, his lectures are engaging and entertaining, he's very approachable and always happy to talk to his students.  Grading on the tests is super tough and even the best students get frustrated but if you pay attention and stay on top  the of the readings the class is designed for success.

Dr. Cooper is the most caring, engaging, and respecting prof at UW yet. Class is mandatory, but fun with discussions, poll questions, and demonstrations. Reading quizzes every night which makes class more involved than other lecture courses. Labs are low stress group activities and short in lab reports that really help understanding.

Loved him! He cares about how his students are feeling and tries to connect them in every way. Lectures are definitely worth going to and his personality is awesome! Exam grading may be tough but the overall concept of this class was super structural and I learned some great stuff! Recommend 100%
An amazing professor! He'll make you work for a good final grade, but he's passionate and willing to help at any time.

Dr. Cooper connects with the students very well and his lectures are super interesting. The class as a whole is extremely challenging because the teacher assistants who grade the exams demand that you are precise and concise. Lots of readings but the Biology textbook by Freeman is fascinating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Cooper is one of the best professors I have had at UW. His lectures are fantastic, engaging and helped tremendously with my learning and understanding of the material. Exams are hard, but look for key words/ understanding of the material rather than just memorization. He is very approachable and I recommend him to anyone, he was great!
Hands down the best professor I've had at UW. He really knows how to explain concepts clearly and connect with students. Expect to do a lot of reading to succeed in this class.

The lectures were very interesting and overall the class was pretty interesting but the material can be pretty difficult to understand. He offered office hours and email for extra help and questions. Was very enthusiastic about the material, and excited to teach everyday.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, his lectures were very engaging, he's a funny guy and made the material interesting and clear to understand. He was very encouraging, and even made effort to learn student names in a lecture hall with hundreds. Tests are pretty difficult, and studying is a must, but if you apply yourself you should be able to get a decent grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great lecturer who cares about his subject and does a great job of making it interesting. Tests are difficult with odd grading criteria, but that is the nature of a 700 person class. Would recommend if you are a science major or you like science a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He was the greatest bio professor I could have asked for. He really makes you think and apply your learning which is hard but worth it when you start seeing the world differently.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Cooper was awesome, his lectures are amazing, he conveys complicated topics with ease, He is a really nice guy, and has a really good voice.

Dr. Cooper is my favorite professor in UW! He is passionate and very caring. I enjoyed his lectures so much. He really knows his stuff and is always prepared to answer any question. It's really surprising that it was his first time teaching! I would definitely take his class again.

I loved Dr. Cooper! He is an amazing teacher. He cares about his students and he tries to involve them in his lectures. He made the content very interesting and fun. I recommend him as a teacher. I personally struggled in this class because of the grading, since the TAs grade. As long as you put in time for office hours, you will do good.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Amazing Prof and knows his stuff! Lectures are amazing and very fun. Even though there are hundreds of people he makes you feel involved. A lot of online homework based off of the textbook reading (which are required if you want to pass). A lot of exams but they can be difficult. Overall, amazing Prof for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Cooper is the best. Fall quarter 2016 is his first time teaching Biol 180 and he rocks. The lectures are  interesting and he's pretty good at answering questions. However tests are hard,so you need to go to classes, because the tests are pretty lecture-based. There's also polling questions in class so participation is important.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Fall 2016 was his first quarter teaching and he is amazing. He really cares about the well being of his students and he remembers them and with more that a thousand kids that is in itself a fantastic skill. The class is very lecture based and the book does not help too much but it is not a bad thing to have. Do not be afraid to ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Loving him. I can't believe this is his first time teaching bio 180. He is doing great and I hope I can take his class again.

I can't believe that Autumn 2016 was Dr. Cooper's first year teaching the class. It feels like he's been doing it forever. He knows the material super well and the class is definitely formatted for your success. He is an excellent speaker, explains material well, and is humorous. He will definitely hold your attention in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Just go to class and do the reading then you will pass. Really fun but needs some commitment.

Dr. Cooper was wonderful. Apparently this quarter (Fall 2016) was his first quarter leading the class, and he did a great job. He was entertaining, the subject matter was interesting, and was well loved by everyone I've spoken too.
This guy was really respectful of students and their time, and was always really entertaining to watch in our required-attendance class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Cooper is an amazing teacher and his lectures were always entertaining and informative. Be careful of test format and really pay attention to what they're asking for in the question. Other than that as long as you pay attention to what Cooper emphasizes you'll be solid.

I can't believe that this was the first time Dr Cooper ever taught a class, he is one of the best lecturers I have ever had! Every single lecture was interesting and engaging, and he did an awesome job of making everyone feel good about themselves. I hope I get to take another class from him in the future.

Cooper is such an amazing professor even though its his first time teaching. His lectures are really engaging and you can tell he really cares about what he's teaching. His office hours are pretty helpful as you have the chance to ask more specific questions. Super down to earth, tests aren't that hard as long as you do the study questions and read
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: eh. He's a great person, don't get me wrong. And he's a great lecturer. But you don't really learn that much in lecture. If you're not naturally good at biology, you prob won't do well in this class. Exams feel like a crapshoot. And this is from someone who average a 3.7 in the gen chem series. It's not really him that's the problem, it's bio 180.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Solid professor. Lectures are extremely interesting. Bio 180 in itself is a tricky course just because the answers they are looking for on tests aren't always straightforward. Definitely do the study questions and stay on top of the readings so that the reading quizzes and polling questions come easily to you. Forming study groups is really helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: DR. COOPER IS THE MOST AMAZING PROFESSOR! He knows his material so well and teaches it in a way that is both fun and engaging. He makes a class of 700 feel like a class of 20. Go to his office hours, they are helpful and entertaining! He is such an inspiring professor and really cares about every student. Tests are killer but 10/10 take this class!

Dr. Cooper is truly an engaging lecturer. He is able to make seemingly boring topics into fun, and up beat lectures. The best part of all,  I learn something new each time. Even though the grading is tough (especially if you don't use key words!), you get to learn  the fundamentals of biology, and on top of that, how to have better study habits,
Cooper was always super engaging and respectful of students. His lecture style is very clear and he makes the class super interesting and fun. TAKE THIS PROFESSOR IF YOU CAN HE ROCKS!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He makes the class really fun and interesting. He's really funny and approachable and he makes participating in class much less stressful. One of my favorite professors of all time!! Take his class!!!

He always creates comfortable atmosphere to ask in class. Keep the class interesting all the time. You learn new things every day in lectures. He will do polling and random call to answer his discussion questions. So reading is necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Seriously such an entertaining lecturer who keeps class interesting. Very approachable and cares about the students doing well (even though it's a huge lecture). Don't be scared to ask questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Jake makes this class very enjoyable even though it's a GPA-killer. He's very passionate and caring for students.

Disorganized, seems to not know what's going on in class. Instructions not clear, written on assignments differ from the verbal ones given in class- also change on the day/person asking. Very little time to do assignments. The Mill can get very busy, when everyone is trying to complete things on time, often staying very late. Content was good tho

Took this class in fall of 2019. Lectures are engaging and fun, takes the time to know every student and remembers them. Ive had three classes with Brock and love his style of teaching! He doesnt believe in memorizing and spitting out info on tests; instead he has quarter long projects that are fun and help you learn hands on! My favorite prof!

This was my third class with Brock and honestly I hate information visualization. Stats, data, and graphs are all boring to me but somehow Brock made lecture interesting and engaging! Learned a lot from this class and Im glad I took it. Brock makes you feel like a friend rather than a teacher talking at you, genuinely wants to help you learn.

Brock is amazing! I took this class in 2019 and his lectures are never boring. He actively asks for student feedback on his teaching methods and immediately implements them. Makes you feel like he genuinely cares about your learning! Highly recommend.

Brock is honestly my favorite professor of my entire academic career, included all the teachers I had before college. He is kind, caring, hilarious, and brilliant. He always puts his students first and makes difficult concepts easy to learn.

Brock's a cool professor who clearly has a lot of knowledge and experience in the field of physical computing. The classwork is understandable and very doable even though I wasn't very familiar with the subject matter. Grading techniques were effective and he allows for people to work together through the class.

Bock is honestly my favorite professor ever.  He is always available to talk, and and welcomes questions and open-mindedness.  His lectures are hilarious, and he gives excellent advice, academic or otherwise.

Juliet is a very fair teacher. Her lectures were interesting and her availability for help is impeccable. Lectures never felt rushed, the class was very engaged asking questions, and she was always happy to answer them. She was able to help me with stuff from outside of class 1:1. You will have to put in time to study, but it's all reasonable.

ESS 212 was a fairly chill class; all of the exams were online and open-note. However, Juliet isn't engaging as a lecturer since she speaks slow, and the first five weeks of the class were basically repeats of the assigned pre-lecture videos. She is more than happy to schedule office hours outside class and was very helpful with the final project.

This class is the most awesome and inspiring class ever in ESS. Topics are interesting and easy to manage if you like geology. Labs are great, fun and easy if you work hard. TA taught extra informations during labs, love it. Tests every 2-3 weeks, but they are all MC questions, not that hard. Best prof + TA ever!!! Recommend if you like geology.

I loved Prof. Crider! Her class led me to the decision to minor in ESS at the UW. She didn't post lectures online so you have to attend class if you don't want to fall behind. She gives great study guides before each test. Really spend time studying them and you'll be fine! Only used textbook for clarifying certain topics, but never read it for hw.
Really good professor who knows her stuff and is very accessible. Not an easy class by any means as there are a lot of things to learn, but pay attention in class and you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: If you're expecting a remotely easy class, look elsewhere. Despite poring over the textbook and studying extensively from the study guides, there isn't much to be done as far as getting a good grade goes. Lectures touch on unrelated topics often, and points are taken off exams at will. Labs are impossible to get full grades on.
study from her review guides, extremely useful. go to her office hours, and you will get much better understanding of geology

Juliet is an awesome prof. Her lectures are interesting, especially for a geology class and she gives out excellent study guides before each test. Class is worth attending as tests are almost entirely based on what she lectures on. Highly recommend!
A really sweet professor, who is encouraging. She was welcoming and made sure everyone had a chance to contribute.

Interesting content, but poor grading. The grade conversion is very strict, and there are few assignments. Losing even 3-4 points in the entire class can drop your grade significantly. There are no rubrics for assignments, so grading is a guessing game. Professor can also deviate from grading scale and assign lower grades.
I love Cristina she is awesome.
the only drawback of this class was the group project. otherwise cristina is so kind, caring, and knowledgeable, and can't recommend her enough.

Really sweet and super nice,
Some group projects and she loves to listen to outside perspectives.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took nutr 415 in winter it was mainly group work reading. I took nutr 406 in au 25 very easy, there's a group project and online multiple choice exams. poll ev in class as participation. She is very nice she reopened an exam since I forgot to take it

Such a sweet prof who's always happy to chat with students and answer questions. Content was interesting and I overall loved the class. There was one project that felt a little disorganized and was graded harshly that I know most people didn't like (pop. diets one) but other then that workload and exams are fair!
Dr. Harris is a great professor who taught me a lot of valuable information. Super great and engaging lectures. I recommended this course to all my friends.

i LOVED dr. harris! her lectures were super welcoming and her course was well organised. there's no hw assignments (only weekly quizzes), and that + exams are online open notes (hard to fail!). she is super friendly. she does use pollev for participation but there are drops! would 100% take again

Easy A+. Was free to talk with after every class and can talk about applicability of certain foods to your own diet that she is happy to explain. Extremely easy course, classes went over readings that took 15-25 minutes. Exams and quizzes are online and open note and textbook.
Really good professor and super easy class. Exams are open note and so are the weekly quizzes. All assignments are basically online except for the required quiz section.

Dr. Harris is a great teacher! The course was pretty easy. Grades based on weekly content quizzes, group projects every monday (monday classes on zoom), 3 writing assignments (easy), and participation. The only thing I didn't like about her class was how early they were since participation mattered. Group projects arent bad at all.

Dr. Harris is an amazing lecturer who really cares about improving community health and challenging misconceptions about health. She is extremely clear about grading and is available for extra help when needed. The class is not too difficult as long as you go to every lecture and start assignments early!

Super kind and very well-versed and enthusiastic of what she teaches. Exams covers exactly what's in the textbook and are also open book and note. Very organized lectures and presentation. Does go a little fast on lectures, but doesn't even matter that much since her lectures mostly goes by the textbook. Had a great time learning from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Harris is a great lecturer who is really passionate about what she does. She's also very mindful of using inclusive terms and language, and is a really approachable person. Lectures are recorded so they can be accessed after class, and the textbook is definitely your best friend. Great class!

Her lectures are interesting and well organized. Not much homework outside of class, just the once a week quiz section assignment which takes around 20 mins. The class lectures are 3x a week at 8:30am which is tough but it's super important to attend bc we do polls throughout class which count as a portion of our grade.

Dr. Harris knows her stuff and she shows she cares about her students. The class itself is a super easy A as long as you do the assignments. No attendance is required and everything is recorded so she keeps the class very flexible for everyone.
So incredibly nice and cared a lot about the students and content

Great prof, very caring and understanding person, lectures are easy to understand. Homework, while sometimes tedious, isn't confusing and is good practice for upcoming exams. There are many opportunities for extra credit so take them while you can.

Dr. Harris is super kind and her lectures are pretty straight forward! There are weekly lecture quizzes and 4 large exams that are all taken online from home. The test questions can be confusing at times, but I skimmed through readings & focused more on lecture content and am projected to get a 4.0. Extra credit opportunities are also offered!

Her class is relatively easy. Quizzes heavy on textbook and lecture. Most of the lectures are pretty interesting and the TAs are also pretty accessible. She is kind enough to make lectures live and in person.
Very easy contents. No need to have any foundation in related fields. No final or mid. Just 4 exams and several extremely easy online homework.

Professor Cristin Harris was amazing. Her lectures are informative and her course layout was brilliant. I was able to learn through group discussions and assignments relative to physical activity. I would love to take this class again knowing it isn't test-based but learning how to engage w/ others and become a effective leader.

Professor Harris seems like she genuinely cares about the material that she's teaching. The class itself is heavily reliant on your understanding of textbook readings. Exam questions are pretty much memorization from the lectures or textbook. Not a hard class just a lot of memorization and work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lots of lectures! But they're all usually around 30-40 minutes, so it's not too bad. Take good notes and you won't even need to read the textbook to study. Harris was organized and energetic during class. She has a lenient grading scale and I never stressed about this class. There was a lot more bio than expected, though, but it was still fun!

Dr. Harris was nice and made herself available outside of class. The class had a lot more biology material than I expected but the tests were open note. I am giving her a 3 instead of a 4 because we had to do what was basically a glorified diet app for the course.

Dr. Harris is an amazing professor, and explains material well. She's very easy to talk with outside of class. There are many things to memorize, but the exams overall were not so bad. She drops a few lowest scores on some assignments.

Prof. Harris gave a really great introduction to the topic of nutrition. I took this class because I needed a science credit, but I ended up really liking it and considering Nutrition & Food Science as a major. If you pay attention, this class isn't too difficult.
I enjoyed professor Harris lecture style a lot and loved her as not just a professor but as a person. NUTR 200 can be tough though so taking good notes is imperative!

Professor Harris is a very caring and nice person. You can feel that when attending her lecture. The class did cover a lot of information. Luckily, the exams were open note and taken online or I would be struggling with memorizing the information. Overall, it is not an easy class for credit as I thought but I still enjoy the class.
Cares about her students, gives good explanations, and is lenient when it comes to grading/taking tests.

Harris is a great person and clearly cares. This class is a lot more than I signed up for - if you're not interested in biology, then you're going to have a tougher time, especially because the way information is structured in this class is less than linear. Thankfully, tests are open-note.

Amazing professor and person. Loves what she does and it is clear she is passionate about her subject and informing her students. Very compassionate and understanding. It is a shame I was not able to take her class in person because I would loved to have gotten to know her better and have been more engaged in her lectures.

Caring and sweet professor. I learned so much taking this class! The grade consists of 4 easy exams online, polling, launchpad assignments, and quiz section! Youll need the textbook just for the assignments. Not a difficult course if you just study all the slides & go to class!

LOVED this class, EASY 4.0 self-graded on assignments and final essay, discussed as a class what should be our syllabus. She is such a sweetheart, very passionate and flexible with your schedule, and would make sure everyone understands the lecture. Very empathetic, BEST professor and class!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Literally the kindest, most accommodating  prof you will have. Gonna be self grading my final essay (worth 40% of my grade mind you) and she allows the class to make decisions about the way it's structured. Easy assignments lowk a lot of reading but you'll be okay. Just truly very kind person and you can feel that she cares about you personally

She really grew on me! Extremely flexible to students needs. Reach out for accommodations and she will meet u with understanding. Genuinely cares about their students which feels very rare at this school

Cricket is the epitome of the word flexible. They really care about creating the best learning environment possible. I highly recommend spending time in office hours with Cricket if you end up taking one of their courses. Listening to them think and speak brought me so much inspiration as an activist and feminist scholar.

She is an amazing teacher and uses techniques and ideals portrayed in the reading and gives the class a chance to implement it, she is really taking a new approach to teaching by avoiding traditional teaching methods and encourages participation that can be done in various ways ex. online discussions instead of speaking in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There is no structure. We read feminist theories and discussed them all day every day. We were told to lead discussions, create "class rules", and even create prompts for our papers. Cricket's a lovely woman but the class was boring and long. We are graded on 2 essays, participation, classwork, and final project (AND ALL ARE WORTH 20% EACH)

She's so kind. The type of person you just want to hug. She doesn't believe in a lot of traditional education things so she tries to make her classroom really inclusive (disability justice). The class was reading-intensive and has in-class activities. Essays and assignments were graded easy. Wants you to succeed, opportunities for extra credit.

Hard to understand and there was no real reason to go to lectures. I only ended up going to get the polls. Reading from the textbook is what helps the best for exams, her lectures make little sense and more importantly are just really slow. I don't really like bad mouthing people but there's little good to say about her.

She doesnt teach content in lectures, you must read textbook. Exam content is traightforward (if you learn from TA or textbook) but rubric makes it difficult to get full credit even if you know the answer. Would not reccomend
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Horrible professor do not take everything everyone is saying is true. Should genuinely be fired and I am appalled there are such gifted people out there who probably cannot get the opportunity to teach because people like Alison Crowe are tenured. The class structure kind of just sucks in general at UW but Alison Crowe makes it horrible.

I believe that people shouldn't be judged by their voice- Crowe is an exception. It's that bad. Didn't read the textbook- just made flashcards. Got an easy 4.0 because I already knew what was going on, not because she did anything right. I could have taught this class far better than she did, I think most people could have. Avoid her If possible.

I learned more from this class in an hour of lab than a week of lecture. Reading the textbook is what gets you the grade rather than lecture. She does not go into detail during class but the details and key buzz words are what is on the exam. It is less of a test-your-understanding and more of a “memorize what she wants you to say”. Cannot teach

I feel like I could have taught this class better than Crowe with no information other than reading the book. Her rubrics on tests are terrible, and I felt like she wanted me to memorize how she would answer questions more than she wanted me to learn. She also gives so much work in the learning reflections.

Lectures are useless, tests are graded quite subjectively with you having to get key buzz words to get credit instead of conveying understanding. Wants to test students on weird analogies instead of actual content. Seriously should not be teaching. The material is super interesting but she manages to make it miserable to learn and she can't teach.

Awful teacher, horrible class structure. Topics covered for each exam have little to no correlation with each other and jump around the textbook a lot. Lectures are useless due to her inability to teach and awful nasally voice. My TA was personally super useless as well and had no idea what was going on. Read textbook instead of going to lecture.

The professor has a terrible style of notes that don't clearly tell you what the material is that you have to know. The lectures also don't cover much of any of the content that you actually need to know. The TA's in this course are the real teachers, they lecture in Lab along with whatever lab was supposed to be done.

Bio 200 is a hard weed-out course, but I would recommend avoiding Crowe at all costs. If you are stuck with her, make sure to kiss your mental health goodbye and lock in. I would recommend reading the textbook and using practice problems to study for the tests. In this class, a 2.0 is a 75, so be prepared to put in high amounts of effort.

shes a nice person truly but her lectures are a waste of time. lots of polls, WORKSHEETS that take up most of lecture, and lectures covered MAYBE 40% of what u needed to know for the exam. but the textbook often went wayy deeper so idk what her expectations were. labs and the textbook were the best resource. exam rubrics were also subjective

She makes bad use of in-class lecture time with polling questions, group call, and worksheets. Extra assignments chew up your time. Go to lecture for attendance points and tune the rest out, take good notes on the textbook chapters and do the practice exam problems. Avoid bio with her if you can.

Professor Crowe is deeply caring and has very good lectures. She explains everything thoroughly and always makes sure to answer questions from students, and her answers are really good. Her classes were the highlight of my quarter, she's great

I hated this class; it RUINED my mental health. Crowe cannot lecture and there is no clear grading criterion. My graduate TA told me not to use the lectures as a study tool and instead to use the textbook. I learned the most through the lab and the textbook. If you can, save yourself a quarter of pain and do NOT take BIOL 200 with Crowe.
She was a bad lecturer and a bad grader. Do not take her class.

She cares about how her students are doing and goes out of her way to help them understand. Her lectures are a little boring and voice at times can be tiring but overall it's a bio class and she does a good job. The concepts are hard but that goes for any teacher teaching this subject. I would take again with her.

Its clear that Professor Crowe is trying to implement a classroom style to encourage active recall rather than memorization, but unfortunately she doesn't do a very good job. There is no information on the slides and endless assigned readings. She is making it genuinely difficult to learn in what SHOULD be an interesting class. Wouldn't recommend.

Leaving this review while currently in the class because wow. I've had my share of tough professors/classes but this is by far the worst. Her lectures are so patchy, she skips around from topic to topic and will put things on the test she has never talked about in class. You NEED to do all the readings and also recommend watching vids ou
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She does not teach. Although she may be nice, everything you learn from the class will either be from the textbook or simbio. I repeat, she does not teach. She expects you to come into class with full knowledge of what she's going to teach. You need to pay attention to the readings because stuff that she's never talked about will be on exams.

Her lectures were really bad paced with introducing many terms at once and handing out useless worksheets that don't seem to supplement her lectures. She very very assumes you have read the textbook so if you don't you are cooked. In class polling is used free response polling so you have to go or you don't get poll credit.

Prof. Crowe is amazing. I had her last quarter for Biol 200 and was able to thrive in her class. She is incredibly nice, has a very endearing personality, and gives a lot of practice problems. Her exams are tough but fair. I love her so much and I really would recommend taking Biol 200 from her if possible, I am unsure why others do not like her.

she never actually taught—just made us talk to partners, so no one knew what was going on. Her nasally voice, awful metaphors, and unreadable handwriting made things worse. We were doomed from day one. Good luck if you take her, but honestly, Bio 200 might just suck no matter the teacher.

Does okay explaining questions in lectures. Really messy handwriting and loud/high pitched voice. Generally a good lecturer if you keep up with the readings and homeworks. Homeworks are based on your summary of the reading and fairly easy.

I knew Biol 200 was going to be tough, but not like this. Crowe is a fitting name because with all due respect she sounded like one. Lectures were painful and the class jumped around material a lot compared to others I've taken. For reference I find organic chemistry much easier than her bio 200 class and have the grades to prove it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: BIOL200 is a weed-out class known to be difficult, I don't believe the structure is something Alison had control over, however even in light of that, her instruction is not great. Her lectures are often hard to follow, and although she is very compassionate and very intelligent, she is not very engaging.

Dr. Crowe for 200 was pretty hit or miss, with (rumored) test averages to be very low while some kids excelled. 

Lots of busywork (ie reflections, RFAs) which reduced availability for office hours, ultimately hurting students. 

Practice exams are likely the best way to prepare for exams with wording being a large part of getting or losing points

Honestly really bad. I wanted to get past the squeaky voice and the bad hand writing, but after the first two exams hearing through the TAs that the average was low 60s and they didn't really care to do anything but blame students she lost my respect. Would avoid 200 with her at all costs.

Exams were extremely difficult compared to the lectures. Do not recommend, her lectures are boring and overly simplified that I would rather skip and read the textbook, but pollev forced me to go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures had no structure or organization and usually weren't helpful for exam content. There were way too many worksheets that detracted from learning opportunities in lecture. Good exam scores are attainable if you do the practice questions to get familiar with picky grading and key words - you will lose points for not including exact phrases.

I mean wow, I don't usually write RMP reviews but this might be the worst STEM professor I've had in my time at UW. She struggles to explain concepts clearly and concisely and instead hands us worksheets, often about concepts we aren't even familiar about yet. You will 100% have a better time learning the concepts by asking TAs and going to CLUE.

Crowe herself seems lovely, but lectures were disorganized and heavy on worksheets. Midterms require a lot of memorization, which I hated less than the constant reflections and learning skills activities. Overall, a deeply frustrating class that felt determined to waste my time, but it barely redeems itself because I did actually learn biology.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Nice person, horrible teacher. Test questions take so much extrapolating; very broad/confusing questions and expects a very specific answer. Get ready to learn everything you need to know on your own time, lab might be the one helpful thing, def not lectures.

The class was fine; a lot of unnecessary in-class worksheets and PollEv and she's more stingy with extra credit than Mo, but the tests are very doable if you use the given vocab sheet on the front page of the exam.

My big takeaway is that one of my friends noticed she sounds like Chris from Family Guy when she lectures and now I can't unhear it.

Dr. Crowe seems like a sweet person, but I didn't enjoy her teaching style; there also was a lack of structure and communication with regards to course expectations and grading. Her exams were always looking for hyperspecific wording, and I know people who lost so many points over the simplest things; get your hands on past exams from her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's a very nice and caring lady but she's got a squeaky voice, bad handwriting, boring lectures, and gives packets that wasted class time. Good study materials, helpful labs and chill review sessions, but most of my learning was done outside of class.

Lectures are unorganized and all over the place. She wastes class time with worksheets instead of actually teaching. How are we supposed to answer questions we've never covered? Exams were EXTREMELY difficult packed with multiple subparts, and focused more on vocabulary than concepts. Grading was harsh; you lose points for not using specific words.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I disliked her teaching style and the choices she made in regard to which concepts were taught in depth. The questions that we did class discussions on were very surface level, and not helpful for exams. I found the "you should be able to" study guide style to be vague and misleading, which made studying for the tests extremely frustrating.
Ppl complain cuz they're lazy. She's a good teacher, just read the textbook and keep up. Very sweet prof

She's very nice but not great at explaining concepts and lectures are mostly for doing worksheets that aren't explained well. Reading the textbook thoroughly and taking detailed notes was really helpful, it's one of the best resources. Make sure to do the practice questions before the exam, exams are similar and ask the TAs any questions you have.

Prof. Crowe tries her best but is not the best lecturer. She has a very shrill voice which can make lectures slightly painful. Exams can be picky about technicalities but if you learn the content thoroughly they're fine. Overall a very kind and knowledgable person, the course is just not designed super well and she can be bad at explaining things.
She gave us a 2nd point of extra credit lets go
Hard to listen to. Assigned readings are unrealistically long and it is unclear what you really need to look at before lectures/understand for exams.

Would not recommend taking 200 with Crowe, the lectures are not at all related to the exam material. Most of the lecture time is spent on worksheets that are not at all explained afterward, leaving students confused. There is also little room for partial credit on exams, answers must be word-for-word identical to the answer key to get any credit.

You actually will have to work in this class. Members of the dissenting party must realize that their own performance is a product of their own effort. I recognize that my inability to get the grade I wanted is my own fault. Dr Crowe is very passionate and knowledgeable in her field and is likely constrained by the limits placed by the dept.

Professor Crow cares about her subject. But her teaching style is so unorganized. The only valuable tool she provides are the practice exam questions. Lectures are usually spent doing a worksheet which are not useful when learning a concept for the first time. If you rely solely on material covered in lecture, you won't pass this class.

I wouldn't recommend taking Biology 200 with Alison Crowe. Course felt very disorganized. Her lecturing felt messy and her choice of wording is not as specific as she would expect from students on her own exams. Asking for practice problems felt like pulling teeth at the start of the quarter. Class activities felt age appropriate for 4th graders.
the grading rubrics are very very specific, but if you do all of the practice questions and understand them, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is a kind person but the test grading rubric is intensely specific, and if you have the all of the right concepts and answers, but are missing a specific order of words, you will easily get a 60% on the exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Crowe's a wonderful caring person. BUT OH MY GOD THE WAY THINGS ARE GRADED. You'll be left splitting hairs over everything. You get 99% of the question and miss one key word? Congrats. No points. In biol 180 you got 1 percentage point extra credit right? SAY GOODBYE TO THAT. You get ONE POINT. Also she inflects every sentence up like a question HLP

Lectures barely touch on important topics and only briefly discuss hard concepts. Spends half of lecture on worksheets instead of lecturing; these worksheets are useful for studying but not when introducing new topics.

Prof. Crowe is undoubtedly a caring person, but that does not translate to this course whatsoever. The lectures and exams are not related in any fashion, nor do the textbook or her endless supply of worksheets help for doing well. Having to rely on the TA's mini-lectures in labs to understand anything is concerning, but that's what's going on.

This class is structure like my grandma's back, nonexistent and problematic. It seems no matter how hard you try, nothing work because its usually the prof's job to teach you the basics and for you to elaborate on your own. Class average on the first exam was around 60% and on the second was 50%... think that says a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This seems to be UW specific but it seems the bio professors tend to be overly-hyper & dumb down material in lecture and then make the tests way more complicated than the material they teach. Crowe's no different. And gives out WAY too many packets to do in class instead of actually lecturing. The thought of doing another POGIL gives me nightmares.

Yk that one meme where a student interrupts his high school teacher by getting up and telling her that she should actually be teaching and connecting with the students face to face instead of just handing them a packet yo

That's this class

You can tell that Professor Crowe is passionate about her subject, but it is unclear if she cares the same level for her students' learning. Professor Crowe reuses the same graphics throughout the entire quarter and her lectures have no structure. Half of the class is just doing group work on POGIL worksheets instead of actual teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She doesn't explain concepts or the grading criteria very well, so even if you self study A LOT you could tank the test because of how specific she wants you to be. Do a TON of other practice through CLUE and worksheets. She also doesn't answer questions properly and always goes on about some roundabout, irrelevant answer.

ONLY TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU'VE DONE AP OR IB BIO! Teaching is so confusing, uses so many unnecessary analogies that nothing makes sense. Textbook readings don't match the lecture. If u must take her use Khan Academy or YT, focus on learning outcomes she gives out, do practice exams (gives a lot), and go to lab, TAs explain things better.
She pronounces "as" like "a**" and it distracted me the whole quarter

She obviously cares and wants students to do well but lectures are infuriating sometimes. They can feel pretty disconnected and/or dumbed down compared to the textbook and exams. she will often spend large portions of class using weird analogies to explain trivial concepts while completely leaving out difficult concepts that need to be covered.

I am really not enjoying this class at all, the pre-readings and lecture content are incredibly disconnected, and even further disconnected from the lab content. Her lectures are dumbed down, but then poll questions and test questions are really complex. I have constantly had to teach myself test concepts that she doesn't cover.

Lectures are extremely surface-level compared to what is expected on exams, the textbook isn't much help either. The exam questions are generally all or nothing, with minimal partial credit. She also consistently blames poor exam scores on a lack of studying and depth of answering questions, yet she never covers what she expects as a test answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Although attendance is mandatory, you're better off spending lecture watching khan academy. She simply dumbs down content and writes her exam with high expectations. After an exam she encouraged the class to learn how to write complete answers, but we never showed us what she expects us to cover in our answers.

Tests are difficult and harshly graded, but expected of a bio series course. The real problem is lectures- I feel like concepts are taught in such a simplified manner, almost dumbed-down, that the big picture gets lost. No transition at all between topics taught. Had to teach myself using Khan academy and textbook, but still managed to do well

She is probably the worst biology teacher I have ever had. The material in this course is not hard to grasp, it is her lectures, constant worksheets, and exams that will give you a headache and tank your GPA. You ever have that one friend that loves Biology and just yaps about it without making any sense? Yeah, she is that friend.

Alison isn't an easy professor, but she's a terrific one - patient, available, present, involved, knowledgeable, and caring. Her course is set up to encourage your best work. I took Biol 400 from her after nearly losing my love for molecular biology. The course content and the way she addressed it helped me reignite my passion for the field.

Dr. Crowe was one of the most supportive and encouraging professors I've ever had! (Not sure what the other students are talking about.) She organized her class incredibly well, and provided ample resources to prepare for exams, engage with the material, etc.; would highly recommend taking a class with her if you have the opportunity.

Dr. Crowe makes sure you know what concepts will be on the exams, and is accessible outside of class to answer questions. I like that she puts questions in the lectures, so it tests our understanding of the concepts. The tests are pretty hard, but if you study the right things than they aren't too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I actually really liked Crowe. She tells you exactly what you should know for the exam and gives a lengthy practice test that if utilized correctly, will set you up for success. Everyone complaining about the exam and grading just obviously havent studied correctly. I think everybody forgets the mol. bio is a hard concept, so exams are hard too.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFF!!! Ignore the highest review on top. expects so much out of her tests but doesn't teach enough during lecture to understand the material. you can't even use the textbook since it doesn't help. DON'T take it online though that's my advice. she is nice and well spoken, but that doesn't help. GPA ruiner and HARD exams.

I found the 2hr exam window that Dr. Crowe enforced very fair (vs. 24hr in 180). Write lengthy responses to demonstrate your understanding and you're set. Unlike other profs, she doesn't grade on key words and is open to alternative answers to exam qs (not on key), which was awesome since bio is open-ended! Equity is her moto. Great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Weekly tokenism, blamed not having group exams on poc, and not accomodating. Her lectures are helpful, but not enough to pass the class. She expects more than she gives. Little to no effort in actually helping students. If you're slightly rude on regrade requests, she won't consider a regrade at all. Terrible educator. Tries to be woke lib, fails

this was a weird class. Prof Crowe is pretty nice but her tests are extremely hard. syllabus tell you to not memorize, concepts are the most important; yet tests are graded on how many key words you managed to squeeze into your answer. Some exam material is barely in the textbook, so you'll have to find your own resources. Very average
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She single-handedly made me hate biology :)
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Tests are the only things that mattered and were graded by a random number generator.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Its intro bio, it will ruin your grade
I enjoyed my time greatly in BIOL200, would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: SOOO HORRIBLE! Dont take this class online. The biology department is terrible. She mentions things on lectures that arent on the exams. Everyone cheats on the online exams and no one is given accountability. Her LFAs are only a little helpful. She doesnt know how to teach and should go to teaching school. WORST CURVES at the UW.

I took Biol 200 with her and Dr. Buchwitz this quarter, and they did an excellent job. Her lectures are interesting and engaging, and in combination with the recommended textbook readings, were good prep for the tests. Midterms were difficult, but the practice problems accurately reflected the level of difficulty to expect and one exam is dropped.
She's so nice and caring! 200 is MCD and so for all you prospective MCD majors you don't want to skip her!

She's a great professor with fair exams. My recommendation for succeeding in this class is DO THE READING BEFORE THE LFA!! I definitely slacked on this and it made the exams harder. She's clear and very nice. She taught this course with Brian who is a sweetheart. Honestly some of the nicest ppl in the bio department.

Awesome professor. Biol 200 is probably one of my favorite and best classes I've ever taken. Prof Crowe gives great lectures and and explains things clearly so you'll understand it. Tests also correspond appropriately to the lectures, so if you understand the material, you'll do well on exams.

Super sweet professor and doesn't hesitate to reach out to help students. Although the lectures can be a little too general in comparison to the exams, the resources that the biology teaching team provides makes up for everything. Would recommend and definitely work hard to get a good grade!

Although at first the lecture style may seem a bit boring, professor Crowe was quite a gem. She explains the content thoroughly and is careful to answer any questions to the best of her ability. She seems to really care about student learning and is enthusiastic about what she is teaching. The class is still not easy but she makes it easier.

Allison Crowe cares about your learning and will make an effort to show it accordingly. Sometimes lectures can get a little confusing, but reading the textbook and asking questions is a good way to clear those things up. Follow the study guides to the bone and you'll be good for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Read the textbook before class and you'll be golden. She's easy to follow in lecture and exams are fair. She likes engaging with students which is rare at UW

She doesn't want you to memorize, she wants you to learn, interpret, and think like a biologist. The material is hard (it's molecular bio!), but she is a great teacher. Her exams are straightforward if you go to class and PARTICIPATE. Super straightforward format + grading criteria. Office hours are really helpful. She is the best!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She tries to let everyone learn and succeed in this class.
Exams were fairly challenging, but lectures were pretty good so overall not a bad professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Her clicker questions were very confusing, but other than that she is great professor. If you ask for help, she is always ready! Also she loved to show up in lab section and talk to students. I really liked her!

Tough course material, so be sure to review the course manual before tests. Lots of writing assignments (5 total, ranges from 1-4 pages), but will improve your paper-reading skills. Professor and TA are helpful and want students to learn.

Wonderful professor. Really cares about students, answers all her emails thoroughly and quickly! Very approachable, polite and respectful. Does as much as she can to enhance student learning. Would highly reccommend, great class.

Awful.  Constantly stammered over her words and wound up confused by her own thoughts.  Could not form cohesive sentences.  Lecture was pointless and disorganized.  She actually detracted from my learning.
She is obviously the best 200 professor. Very intelligible and manageable class

Not a great 200-level professor, but an awesome 400-level one.  She definitely encourages questions and discussion if you put a few thoughts into what you are saying.  Very difficult course load (especially for the number of credits) but you learn quite a bit.

Her lectures were very hard to follow- she constantly switches back and forth between overheads and powerpoint slides. She often expects you to know every minute detail of a process and asks short answer questions that are extremely specific and hard to get right on the exam. I do not recommend taking this class from her.

Her lectures did an excellent job of outlining what sort of material you would need to understand and apply to the test. I preferred her short/long response tests- perhaps unforgiving if you do not understand or care about the material, but if you read and do practice exams it's not difficult to do very well on them. Recommended.

She is very difficult. She isn't very organized and switches back and forth between powerpoint and overhead. She doesn't realize that her students haven't been working in the field of biology as long as her and she expects you to know every little step. Very tough class. Her tests are very scatterbrained. Study, study, study! Wouldn't recommend.

She is very nice and clearly very intelligent. However, I think she fails to realize that her students haven't been working with the material as long as her, and thus don't know every step of every process in the body prior to taking the class. Tough class, but it wouldn't be if she'd just be more thorough. Study her lectures. GO TO OFFICE HOURS!
Too much work for the credits offered. Did not learn anything new. I suggest you to look for other classes! AVOID!
Nice professor, but very disorganized. She is not good at encouraging discussions either. Cares about answering questions but does not show any interest in getting to know students.

I was lucky to have her during the intro bio series.  It was clear early on that she had put some thought into the strucure of her notes and teaching, and I did very well on the tests, despite their difficulty.  I intend to take her more advanced classes later on.  Very good.

She mainly teaches the advance cell bio and cell bio labs. Her teaching style is a bit disorganized and you might feel lost when looking at her in-class notes. Overall, she's very helpful and kind if you approach her for help. Her tests aren't very hard, but they are very conceptual and open ended, so you must read and study from a lot of sources.
Nice lady!

Larry was a FANTASTIC professor, his lectures are incredibly engaging and he obviously very deliberately chooses our class readings. As a hard core STEM student that hasn't taken a liberal arts class in over two years, I appreciated how much feedback he gave, and that he was always available to answer even the stupidest of my questions.

Professor Cushnie took over 318 for the last few weeks of the quarter after our original professor had a family emergency, and he could not have done a more amazing job. He is funny, caring, understanding, and incredibly intelligent. It was obvious he worked incredibly hard to make the transition of professors seamless, and he did a phenomenal job.

I highly recommend Dr. Cushnie's class. His lecture always makes students focused and interested. Be sure to take the course during the regular quarter because the course load will be slightly heavy during the summer A/B term.

Great class, I learned a lot about labor studies, very informative. I love his lectures, he kind of sounds like the Khan Academy person. One thing, he grades kind of tough. Definitely follow the rubric, if anything strays from the rubric, it's usually marked off a few points. Maybe even go above and beyond.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Larry was an amazing teacher. He was not only incredibly entertaining but also insightful and educational. The time and care you put into an assignment to show you care is appreciated and he wants you to succeed. These aren't easy classes but you learn a lot and if you are willing to come at it with some effort and personality, you'll be just fine!
Larry is the best!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
I really loved this class. He was really passionate about his job, and I've learned a lot from him. So I would definitely recommend other people to take this course.

Larry was my professor at Bellevue College as he teaches there once every year. He is a great professor, but his grading criteria is a little unclear. Your grade depends on eight response papers you write throughout the quarter, usually once every week. It is a easy going class, but he grades tough on the response papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Awesome professor! Makes you work for your grade, but in all honesty, his teaching style is well worth the work you will put in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Larry is such an engaging and hilarious lecturer, and if that isn't enough to catch your attention, he is a very attractive guy. He presents information in a way that is easy to understand and fun to listen to. Lots of guest speakers. No midterms, just papers.

Professor Cushnie is a fantastic lecturer. He's hilarious and engaging, but still gives you tons of information in a very digestible manner. Guest speakers were cool, but they were hit or miss. Easy grading, no tests, and you can skip most of the readings if you pay attention during lecture. Super nice guy and would definitely take again!

Larry is a very good professor and I learned a lot from him. However, he is a very hard grader compared to other political science professors here. I should have gotten a 4.0 and ended up with a 3.5. Take the class for the content; don't take it for the grade.

I took labor studies with Cushnie and loved it. He had amazing lectures that were very in depth about the readings (can be dense). He is very inspiring and easy to comprehend. I think everyone should have to take this class because the subject is from such an interesting point of view and he does an amazing job of teaching it. 10/10 would recommend

Awesome teacher.  Manages to make some of the boring texts interesting.  Assigns readings, but they're often not necessary to fully delve into; a skimming and his lectures  good.  Pretty funny in class too.  He gives very indepth page by page feedback on writing assignments.  Discussion, paper draft, presentation, paper, no final, no textbook!
He is really awesome.  The class is really discussion based so don't go with out reading because you will feel like a fool.  Also lets just be real, he is a handsome man.

intro to political theory. this guy should be teaching instead of the jerk thats teaching....the professor was horrible and larry was the best TA a student can ask for. he made sure to help and shed some light on the stuff that the professor never went over LARRY YOU ROCK
Very good intro to political theory TA! Go to class and you'll learn!! Knows his stuff, very helpful if you go to his office hours with any questions.
Went to class just to look, ended up learning too.

Prof Crowder taught this course in a manner that was satisfactory for an introduction to sociology class. He definitely knew most of the class was not Soc majors, and the course content reflects that.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Literally I love prof. Crowder so much. He's super nice and his lectures aren't boring. His tests are lowkey easy if you go to lectures and do the readings. He is so organized it's so amazing!!! DEF recommend him!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Kyle's the best! He's sooooooo humorous and aims to make his lecture attractive. Feel free to fall asleep in his 8:30 class. He's even going to turn off the lights to let you sleep better lmaooooo

Prof. Crowder has very good and thoughtout lectures. Easy to understand and quizzes were all multiple choice and open-notes. Knows his stuff and overall one of the best professors I've ever had. This class made me want to switch to sociology major.
A really nice professor
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. This is the second class I've taken form him and he managed to make STATs interesting. He's a very understanding professor and was accommodating to issues experienced during class. Honestly easy for a STATs class especially in the online format. I'd recommend any class from this professor.

Professor Crowder is a great lecturer and wants to make sure you fully understand course materials. He assigned us bonus lectures but they were very helpful and he gives good examples. I would say beware of the grading scale (97-100% is a 3.9-4.0). Besides that, stats wasnt awful.

He is a really good professor, this class consists of homework and discussion questions once a week and four quizzes throughout the quarter. Attending the lectures is very important to succeeding in this course. The biggest issue with this class is the grading scale (4.0 is 99 & 100%), but with hard work it's definitely possible.

Amazing professor, he designs his class so you can have enough time to soak in everything and still learn what is needed. I enjoyed this class, he gives amazing lectures. He has 4 exams which are relatively easy if you study, then has a discussion question every week, along with a homework. Very good professor. Take him.

Crowder is an awesome dude with a well organized class and great lecture material. He is incredibly funny, and very clear about what you will be quizzed on. He doesn't allow the class to feel rushed because he wants to take his time to hear others' opinions and answer questions. Only thing is the grading scale is steep, so for example a 96% is A-
Engaging lectures over zoom! lectures can get really long but slides are posted to look back at later. 4 quizzes and online discussion board make up majority of your grade but all very manageable

Coming from someone who's not particularly good at math, he made this class very clear and easy to follow. The class was graded on homework, discussions and three quizzes; he's very understanding and fun to learn with, making it obvious that his purpose was to help us learn and not struggle.
Professor Crowder is a great guy. He answers questions in lecture very well and gives clear explanations. He makes a lot of dad jokes, too. Highly recommend taking a class with him!

Lectures are easy to follow, great power-points, super approachable, makes dad jokes, class is well structured, sets clear grading criteria, and willing to make accommodations as the class proceeds. If you can take him I definitely would. Attendance is not mandatory- panopto available. 1 weekly hw assignment & discussion q. 3 non-cumulative quizzes

I never leave reviews but felt inclined to rate prof Crowder. I took him for STAT 221 during the COVID outbreak where classes were online. He structured the class very easy to understand, gave enough time for quizzes (3 total) and his lectures were amazing and to the point. He answers questions very well and genuinely enjoyed having him as a prof.

Lectures are long but he makes them interesting through the material and his enthusiasm. Most of the grade was 4 quizzes which were pretty easy and he had an in class review session right before the quiz which really helped. The material was interesting and the class was pretty easy as long as you went to lecture and reviewed before quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Your whole grade in this class are four quizzes, and a small amount of participation/homework points. Quizzes are all multiple choice and relatively straight forward. He is clear with what you need to know, and in my opinion, lectures were usually generally interesting. He is a really nice guy, I would highly recomment.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: His lectures are funny and easy to understand and engaging. The exam answers are mostly on slides which are simple. Readings are simple and he tells you what's important from them. A few things he either said, or ignored when students said them, seemed tone deaf, but overall he's a great professor I'd highly recommend.

Professor Crowder is one of those tough professors. Will not take any late work. Must do the extra credit and class is highly competitive for grade. He speaks so quickly about complex terms that it was hard for me to understand and apply. Seems to be more concerned with his research than teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Crowder is a mediocre professor compared to other professors in the department. Warning, if you take the class, be sure to do the extra credit. Even though he claims not doing the extra credit won't affect your grade, the final grade percentages are curved to factor in the extra credit, so if you don't do the extra credit you will get a lower GPA.

This is one of the easiest classes I've ever taken, and the prof is SUPER NICE. Absolutely a fun guy, tells funny jokes, gives fair warning on what will be on quizzes. Offered extra credit but I opted out. As long as you do the readings and go to class (online, no textbook) you're set. I barely studied.

Kyle is one of the best professors that I've ever had at UW. His lectures are actually amazing, and interesting. Its like you are listening to a speech. Class had 6 quizzes, finals optional if you do really well on all the quizzes. Need a clicker for the class and overall, recommend him for sociology!

I don't usually write reviews unless I've had an awful or exceptional experience with teachers. I am happy to say, that Crowder is one of the great ones.
