It is rare to find teachers whose number one priority is the learning of the student. He truly wants you to get a lot out of his class and not just a grade. I really appreciated his motivations.

3 quizzes, together they're only 36% of the class grade. Attendance and participation gets you a lot of your grade.  Come to class, do your homework assignments well and you'll do great. Cheat sheet allowed for tests.

Excellent class. Your hard work will definitely pay off. Please please take any class with Crowder if you can! He's so funny and really cares about his students. The grading criteria was clear and makes it easy for students to succeed. The quizzes (no exams) are really easy and you get to bring in a cheat sheet. I get excited coming to class!

Professor Crowder was awesome! His tests are clear and pretty much just based straight off his powerpoint slides. Go to class and you will be fine. Not a tough course, but still have to do the homework and attend. Crowder is funny and makes lectures interesting.
Absolutely LOVED him! I actually learned so much without working that hard. His powerpoints are the main source of test questions. Attend lecture physically and mentally and you'll be fine.

I highly recommend Prof Crowder for Stats, I tried to take Stats with another professor and dropped because of their chaotic teaching methods.   Thankfully, Prof Crowder was clear, concise, and quick to respond to questions-I ended up really liking Statistics, and doing very well in the class!

Kyle was an outstanding professor. His lectures were crystal clear. He has a great personality and is very approachable. Quizzes only make up 36% of your grade, while weekly homework assignments, in-class assignments (really easy to do well on), and participation make up the rest of your grade. This class is social sciences majors-friendly.

Crowder is an awesome professor. He truly wants his students to understand the concepts. Lectures were actually fun/interesting to attend and the work load was not overwhelming. MAKE SURE TO DO THE READINGS! Tests are pretty straightforward if you read and study the lecture notes. I totally recommend this class!

I absolutely loved Prof. Crowder! Really fun, personable and very helpful. He responds to all emails with helpful answers. Lectures are interesting and easy to follow, slides are posted online which really helps with reviews. Exams are really easy if you attend class! So far, my favorite teacher at UW.
really good lecturer, assignments were reasonable and tests were not too bad as long as you go to lecture and study a little, never fell asleep in any of his lectures even though it was at 8:30 am

A fair amount of reading. Not an easy A class. But he's a great professor, very funny, and definitely passionate about what he's teaching. It makes it easier (only a little) to get up every morning and attend an 8:30 lecture. Very interesting class! Entire grade is based on two tests and 3 assignments which made it a tad more difficult to do well
Very boring class, a lot of readings, and did not learn a whole lot. I do not recommend this class.

He's a really good lecturer, and he has no problem with you asking to put up his lecture powerpoints on the course sites if you missed some slides in class. His tests are not that hard as long as you do the reading, which is a moderate amount of reading per week. he does keep track of participation each lecture. overall he is a good teacher
He's a great guy and the best lecturer that I've had ever. Extremely helpful at office hours.

Isn't 1 level class supposed to be an introductory appreciation course? The workload feels like a Harvard graduate seminar. Most students taking this class aren't even dance majors, they're either just casually interested or short on credits, and you still expect academic rigor as if you're the only serious professor in online education

Took this class for VLPA thought I should write a review on why you should not take this class. This is not your usual VLPA class. 2-3 study guides a week which take a long time to complete, hour long videos that can't be sped up with no captions. There is a lot of busy work that will affect your other classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: For an online class, there's a TON of work!!! It's understandable to give a reasonable amount of work, especially for an online class, but you end up doing a ton of work for homework every week. Easy class but a huge load of work!! Take it if you actually know you can finish a 15 pages average homework paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: DAN 101 Dance History online- the study guides take up the most time. Annoying that PDF's are images so you can't copy and paste quotes. Interesting class, easy grader. Be sure to keep good track of deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: One of the most unnecessarily difficult online 100 level classes I have taken. Way too much homework that took a lot of time each week. With that said, as long as you zone out and haul through it, you'll get a really good grade. If you like writing papers, you'll be fine.

This class was easy but had a LOT of work each week. The quiz questions came from the weekly study guides so as long as you did them, it was easy. The midterm and final copied some questions from quizzes and others were easily found on Quizlet. I would suggest taking this with other people to help lessen the load.

This class has a ridiculous amount of work. 6 lessons and a study guide for each lesson, which consist of 9+ pages of questions about readings and hour long videos. There's a quiz or two for each lesson and discussion forums and essays. The exams are open note but tedious as you have to write an essay. An ok grader and 3.8+ is easy if u do the work

As long as you do the work and put some effort into the discussion and assignments the course is an easy 4.0. There is weekly quizzes, papers, and discussions but nothing too hard if you just fill out the study guide that is provided with each lesson.

Take this class only if u've no other choice. This isn't ordinary DANCE 101A Class but more like Dance&History,senior level. Every week you gotta:Read lots readings;Watch many&long videos;Submit study guide wmany QS;Participate in Discussions,3writing papers,quizzes,mid&final exams wessays submissions;Extras.  Very tough if u'r not a dance major!

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. I'm a senior about to graduate with honors, but the time commitment demanded by this class will bring your grades down significantly. HOURS of busy work per day for "study guides" where he wants you to search readings for minute, specific quotes. Don't be fooled by other students' claims that the class is easy - it's not

Best VLPA course I have ever taken at the UW. It's a very interesting course and you will definitely get to explore more about the dance topics and the history of dance. Even though it is a 5 credit course, and requires extra effort, I would definitely recommend if you need a GPA booster. He gives extra credit so it's a benefit.

Such a great class!!! Yes! It is time consuming but the grade is so homework oriented! The two tests are open resources and not difficult at all! The essays are solely based on opinion and as long as you write you'll do fine!! Time consuming but totally worth it! Would highly recommend if you want to boost your GPA!!

He literally hands you every resource needed, and you never have to go outside the links and sources he provides you. Yes it is very, very time consuming, but it is a 5 credit class that isnt hard. the quizzes are easy A's, the study guides are participation only, and the assignments are super easy writings. It's very time consuming but worth it.

Dance American Experience. I think this is a new prof.  Tries to accomplish too much in a short time.  Obviously the prof loves the topic, but by the end you may be burned out on academic dance.  I don't know if this is an example for the dept but I don't want to do a dance minor now. You MUST be on your game with time management.

I'm halfway through the quarter and regret this class.  The workload is really high even for a typical overzealous online class.  I expect to get a B in this class, but if you do not have time for a solid 15 to 20 hours per week on one class I advise you not to take this one.  The topic is amazing, but the approach is overwhelming.

I've never met a professor who cares as deeply as Curtiss does about the success of each and every student both in and out of the classroom. His lectures are amazing and energetic, his exams are fair and well-written, and he will go out of his way to give you every opportunity to succeed. I haven't had a better mathematics instructor!

This class was one of the easiest math classes I've taken at UW thanks to Curtiss. I heard many stories about professors being tough graders, but for this class the homework was very straightforward and exams quite manageable.

Curtiss is a fantastic professor. His lectures are helpful and spaced out well. He is very caring for his students and made an 8:30 class something to look forward to. Coursework is not very hard as long as you space things out. Would highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Curtiss was very passionate about his teaching, therefore always happy to help students further understand the material. He was always happy and upbeat, even though it was 830. He also responded to emails within minutes which is always very helpful. if you have a choice, choose Curtiss, he's great.

Professor Lyman has been the best professor I have ever had. He had coherent lectures, neat handwriting, and would always check with students if they understood the content. On top of his amazing teaching skills, he always brought a bright and happy personality to the classroom. This was the first math class I enjoyed at UW.
Curtiss is awesome and will always try to meet student needs and help you succeed. I recommend spacing out the homework because they can be bulky, but I enjoyed this class a lot.

Curtiss is such a great teacher and person! You could tell he cared about his students and looked forward to teaching us, even if our class was super dead (to no fault of his). He never gave up on trying to communicate with the class and keep us upbeat even during an 8:30. Loved having him as a teacher and I'm going to miss him. Totally recommend!

She is an amazing professor and is very accommodating. Extra credit is offered, and she reminds when the opportunities arise. She warns that 4.0 is a harder grade to receive (she associates it with graduate and professional level work). She responds quickly, and offers help/feedback outside of office hours.  She brings a lot of energy with her.
Do not take this class if you're looking for an easy 4.0. She does not give them out often if it all but it is a fun class to learn about photography.

Rebecca was a really great prof, and I would highly recommend to incoming art students. Sometimes she didn't always give feedback, but she was really receptive and helpful when I reached out to her. She definitely cares about her students, and her assignment outlines were very clear. Lectures were interesting and useful.

Rebecca's a great teacher and really does care about her students. Many of my peers were disappointed by subjective grading and spending time learning about artists. If you just want to take good pictures and have a closed mind Art 140 with Rebecca may not be a good fit.  If you want to learn about and put effort into making art, this class is bomb
Incredible artist, taught me a lot about the basics of great photography

This is a basic photography class but you will not get taught how to use the camera or how to take a picture. Lectures are so pointless, just slideshows of pictures and weird videos, I guess they're considered "art". She's sweetie but a be ry tough grader, doesn't give out 4.0's. She said average grade is 3.4-3.6. Very subjective grading.
Nice lady. Always willing to help and meet up outside of class. Lectures can get boring sometimes. However, studio was a lot of fun!
Awesome class, fun and easy to pass. If you love art, you should take this class.
Easy class. Just follow the criteria of your homework and you will do fine. She is welcoming and always willing to help if you contact her.

So this is supposed to be a basic photography class. This is by no means basic! Rebecca expects you to use a camera professionally, otherwise you're stuck with a horrible grade. Total grade killer, as other people have mentioned, do not take! Thank god i changed my grade to S/NS
WORST CLASS EVER! SOO BORING! What a subjective grading system. Thats why none of us end up as photomedia majors. DO NOT TAKE!

This class is based on a very subjective criteria. Although it's an intro to photography class, you're expected to know how to photograph professionally. I dont recommend taking this class it's not within your major. Also, Rebecca couldn't have a care in the world for her students. The lectures are pointless, I have yet to learn anything...

The lectures of this class are extremely boring. She has no organization whatsoever. It's not a good class to take since everything is based on opinion- I'm surprised rebecca hasnt changed her class structure despite all the negative feedback. The interest level of the class is extremely low. Oh well...

The class is somewhat unorganized but if you ask questions everything gets clarifies.  The projects are easy but the class does take a good portion of your time.  The grading is subjective and not really clear how they get the exact grade but its not hard.  in class questions are turned in for participation credit during lectures.
LECTURE IS BORING. (unless you like to look as slide shows of photos and creepy videos)... She loves art, but does not teach us much about how to take good pictures.
Her class was kind of vague. I found it really hard to learn from lectures. It was much easier to learn in Quiz Sections when we were actually working with cameras.

Nice, but not extremely organized/clear.  Go to office hours and speak up in critiques. She's a teacher who really cares but is sometimes lost in the art world and has difficulty relating to those who don't speak art. I love photography but was a little bored by this class.

This class actually stressed me out because I didn't really know anything about the techniques of a camera. And to have all of the people who do makes it intimidating. Rebecca is an amazing prof; extremely nice! In class you have to critique your peer's work, and vice versa. This is a little nerve-racking too. Overall fun class. Got a 3.4.

He's a Masters in Data teacher. I don't know why he teaching undergrad!!! He cruises through the lectures and answers questions like we're already supposed to know. The material itself doesn't seem that hard but the way he teaches it is hard to understand. The IS kids in the class are going to do well but the finance/accounting kids are screwed.

This class is a lot of work, but Asher makes that very clear. I did not think that I would enjoy this class, but for what it is worth, Asher makes it a lot better. He is very funny and engaging and loves what he teaches. The only thing is that he is a slow grader, so it is hard to gage where your grade is at.

This class was entirely case based. No tests. Each case takes A LOT of time (especially the group cases) so be prepared to spend about ten hours a week just on those. Most cases had very little to do with accounting, more on data analysis. He is a slow grader which can be frustrating since your whole grade is just based on cases and participation.
I wish I could take Dr.Chang again for future lectures, she's super sweet and her lectures go by so fast. Her exams are basically all things from lecture so attend them!! 10/10 prof

Dr. Chang seems like a nice person, but she's very disorganized and a poor lecturer. Her tests aren't hard per se,  but they're very poorly worded. I already knew most of the information due to having taken this course at another university, but if I was coming in blind like most of my classmates, I would have been super confused.

i really liked her as a professor! She was enthusiastic and kind, answered all questions. All the tests were open note, there were 4 different extra credit opportunities and worksheets to boost your grade. The grade is mostly based off test scores though. I suggest going to lectures and doing the readings to get the best grade possible

Plant ecology has been the worst class I have taken at UWB. Treated us like we didn't know anything just because we were all environmental studies/science students rather than bio majors like she normally teaches. This class a burden and I do not feel like there was any educational gain from it. Awful lecturer. NOT approachable.
She is not helpful and does not explain anything in her lectures but wastes everyone's time in class

Dr. Chang experts students to come prepared to class and participate. Assessments have been weekly but we are allowed to redo them all, the same exact questions and gain back 75% of the points we didnt get on the first time. She has office hours and was accessible by email as I worked on the redo assessments. Easy to gain the points back.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: To say that I am overwhelmed is an understatement. She gives us one assessment per week and 3 quizzes. The class average for each assessment has been a 20/50. She said we can retake the exam to get our points back, but she failed to say that we only get 75% of points back. No where in the syllabus does it say 75%. She does not care for her students
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I've taken intro biology before at a different college and the material we learned was the exact same as this class. I did very well in the previous bio class but am seriously struggling in this one. The professor is really nice and charming but doesn't care about your success in the class. The way questions are worded on assessments is horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Chang is nice but she doesn't really care about students' success in class. She's inaccessible outside class and wants students to come to class to learn, which is why she doesn't put up lecture slides after class. The way she teaches the textbook is so blatantly awful that I stopped coming to class and read the textbook only. Still got an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's nice but has very, VERY unclear grading criteria and is inaccessible during office hours. She also talks very fast during lecture and doesn't put up the lecture slides, just Panopoto recordings of the class that are basically bad-quality livestreams. That being said, she's awesome during lab. I feel like she's just an out of place HS teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Dr. Chang's lectures most classes. She's very passionate about her job and you can tell she enjoys teaching Bio. She doesn't seem to be too personable or care about whether or not students are really learning the material and she is hard to reach during her office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures are so confusing and she goes way too fast. Expectations are really unclear for exams and the fact that theres no multiple choice makes it nearly impossible to succeed. Even if you do all of the reading, there will be plenty you dont understand. Take another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: There's a lot of tests, and the class is hard, but she's a nice teacher with good lectures. Didn't need 180 for my major, took it first year to get credits out of the way. Really nice but never there when you need her to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I have taken Bio 180 before and gotten a 4.0, I was barely passing this class after Bothell did not accept my previous course. None of the study guides prepare you for the exams. The exams are all fill in blank and short answer, no multiple choice. I heard from another student she was not in her office during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The wording on exams/lecture is confusing, it feels like shes making it sound complicated than it actually is. GO TO CLASS and write GOOD NOTES, she does not have notes on lecture slides if you skip. Use up all the class time, 2 hours of full-lecture. Practice exams are not like actual exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Just do yourself a favor and take a different professor. Her exams were very confusing, to the point where I'll get frustrated with her wording. Her lectures are very fast paced, and some examples used in lecture are inaccurate. She's a nice person, mostly anyway, but not the best teacher. It feels like she overcomplicates everything

Her class was very confusing. She seemed to care more about if you were actually reading the material than actually teaching it. She does random call and pretty much asks the class questions the whole lecture. It's like we taught ourselves. Exams were extremely confusing.

Very CONFUSING! Simple things that I have learned from other professors she has made it hard to understand. None of the slideshows were helpful for review. Studying for tests was hard because she would use words that made the question confusing. Along with that, her practice exams were nothing close to the actual tests.

She is a hard professor. But if you are taking BIO 180 or any of her biology course, you better be ready for your long route of hard classes anyways. Her Bio course gives a great reflection into how to study in college for your grad school/master... You work hard, participate in her class, she gets to know you. You will do just fine.

Prepare for a quarter of confusion and frustration. Clickers are graded, reading quiz before each lecture. Just do the worksheetsshow up to lab to keep your grade up. Exams are brutal. Class averaged 42% on the first exam, and it didnt get much better after that. Also, dont buy the book! This class asks for 5th ed but you need 4th ed for Bio200
Cynthia is such a great person, she's so enthusiastic and enjoys what she does. She's tough and expects you to learn the material. Basically just go over her lectures thoroughly and read.
She's an OK teacher. If you get the chance you should always choose a different teacher instead of her though.

Not a bad teacher, just that she wasn't super experienced so I don't personally blame her. In the beginning things were rough because her clicker questions and practice exam questions were killer because of the occasionally awkward wording but as the quarter progressed she got a lot better. Plus she's super nice and enthusiastic and approachable!

This was Dr. Chang's first quarter teaching, so it wasn't exactly the best time ever. She is super friendly and tries her best to answer questions, but she doesn't word questions very well (most notably clicker questions and practice exams). Her exams are fair. She's improved much over the quarter. Don't slack off and you'll be fine.
I took CHEM 110, which was an easy class in general. HW was significantly harder than the exams, which meant that succeeding was easy. So the curve was also crazy and you need above 90% to get 4.0.

Professor Stanich was great for Chem 110. Lectures were clear and taught the material well. She also provided practice tests for all the exams (including the finals) which was incredibly helpful. Very approchable and willing to answer questions.

For CHEM 110, I really appreciated how she made practice midterms and a practice final for us to study with. They were very similar to the actual midterms and final! She is a great lecturer and explains things really well; she also stops to answer questions during lecture and made it clear what we needed to know for the exams.

Stanich was fine, theres no chem 110 option but thats what I had her for. Her lectures tend to overcomplicate simple topics and she introduced a curve at the end of the semester that wasnt mentioned before. The final was way harder than the midterms. Stanich is fine no complaints I suppose very middle of the road lecturer
Doesn't teach tbh. Reads off slides and is not helpful. Exams are harder than practice exams.

Note: I'm no Chem-fan. She's inexperienced & a little silly, but she's enthusiastic, and that always helps. Her grading is a little weird, but she's still sort of new to it, and it's not too bad. Do the practice problems in the book & you will do fine.

Cynthia is about as enthusiastic as chemistry profs come. Her tests were easier than the other professors and the curve was high. Make sure to count how many times she wears the "I <3 Lipids" shirt. Overall a great chemistry professor.
She was not a very good professor. Lots of verbal fillers such as "um". Really distracted from my learning

I'm not sure where these other rating are coming from. Stanich certainly wasn't terrible, but was not a quality professor. I found it hard to pay attention in lecture because she would simply read her notes and did not provide strong conceptual explanations. I still went to every lecture and did very well in class, but it was not because the prof.

She's new, so she's not so great at time management/grading scales. The first midterm was SUPER easy, but the second one not so much. Hard to know what to expect. Overall passionate, and her lectures are better than most. A really nice lady but a (somewhat difficult) midterm a week before finals? Probably better than the other professors though!

A great professor! At first I was iffy about the class being taught by a grad student, but she proved to be a really great instructor! Stanich is really passionate about chemistry and she gets really excited about some of the concepts, which is great because when the professor is passionate, it makes the class more enjoyable. Definitely recommend.

I LOVE HER! She's clear and concise. Takes her time explaining the details to you and doesn't just assume you might know something already. She shows a true passion for chemistry is also really nice and dorky but in a GOOD Funny way haha. I Definitely recommend her!

Truly investing effort into her teaching, Cynthia is friendly and helpful to students with any question(s) and is always clear about expectations for homework and tests. Easily the kindest chemistry professor.
One of the better math professors, mostly because most of them suck. She's a good lecturer, the homeworks are pretty reasonable, and the tests aren't too bad. Overall she's a solid choice.
Class was hard but Vinzant did very good lectures, very clear at teaching hard stuff

Vinzant was well organized, which was easy to see in her lectures and tests. The class was by no means easy and definitely needs to be worked for, but I expected that with the calc series. Tracy was also a great TA! Grades always came back very fast for midterms.
Hated this class, it one of the hardest weed out classes there is in UW.

Definitely have heard that Professor Steele is very difficult in her normal classes, but this class is decently easy. I was an okay essay writer in high school, but I found her grading for the two essays we wrote pretty laid back. Lots of reading and work to stay on top of, but as an Early Fall Start experience, I had a great time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Possibly the most dreadful course I've ever taken in my life. You have to read like 3275039284 books (which add up in price), read 45823908 articles, and watch 39082390845 movies and documentaries. She hardly speaks because she makes you discuss the 30000 questions she assigned for you to talk about in groups. So much busy work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Science fiction themed comp lit during early fall start was amazing. She chose really fascinating short stories and movies for us to watch. Fair grading on essays, provided lots of guidance and feedback on them.
Pretty easy and discussion-focused class with not too much writing. This class is a great early fall start class and she is a very sweet professor.

C LIT 251 will be an easy class to pass as long as you do all the readings/movies assigned. In class was boring because all we did was talk to our groups about these assigned readings. She does take attendance but I did skip this class multiple times. Make sure you keep up with all the assignments and you'll for sure get a 4.0! Not a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH HER! She is the most boring professor Ive ever had. For the most part she doesnt teach at all. Our class consisted of reading a long book and watching Narcos: Mexico and a lot of group work. She never taught us anything at all. I never skip classes, but I skipped this one multiple times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great prof. Definitely take her for C Lit 240. Should be easy 4.0. Stay on top of your work. Do all the assignments and show up every day. Do the homework. Very good way to enter university through Early Fall Start. Scale: 95%+  4.0, 85%  3.0, 75%  2.0... But she is an easy lenient grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you're an international student who hasn't done a whole lot of essay writing before, this class is gonna be a major pain. She is not very clear on essay grading rubrics. She claims that she will factor in the lack of experience of international students, but I don't think she does. The class I took required a 100% for a 4.0.

Amazing class, she really is passionate about what she teaches. Most of the class time is spent in group discussions. Good class if you love good books and are happy to talk about them. Grading on essays (most of grade) is also super nice, good feedback too. Was a pleasure to be in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Not great, but has potential. She needs to seriously cut how much writing is done in the class. The readings (we've gone through multiple books) should be enough for weekly homework. The Messent book in the first half of the quarter is absolutely terrible and practically unreadable. The presentations need an actual rubric as well as the essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Interesting topic, horrible professor. She often spoiled movies or did not let you draw your own conclusions from them.  Was never clear as to what needed to be done and when it needed to turn in. The questions she handed out for group discussions always had names of characters mixed up. I would not reccomend her. She will ruin your experience
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Took some interesting books and made them incredibly boring. Doesn't actually teach you anything - class consists of discussion in groups. Technology (i.e. Canvas) seems to be a mystery to her. Assigns a lot of time consuming work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Watch a movie one day and then the other you talk about the assigned films for the week with questions she provides. I don't feel like I learned anything, honestly. Just write about what you read and watch.
Terrible teacher, very disorganized, and boring as all hell. Don't be fooled by the interesting course topics, she is an awful teacher.
Not a good teacher. She doesn't present any new information, doesn't really teach, and is uninteresting. The course concept had potential, but actually attending failed to live up to it at all.

I enjoy films so I wanted to take this class. Professor Steele did choose a good variety of films but textbooks could have been better.  2nd half of quarter is attending SIFF which is very fun!  This is definitely not an easy VLPA, there is a lot of reading & writing and a few quizzes. Be prepared to write many film reviews.

She's a very young professor so I feel she relates to my struggles as a student really well. Very helpful and understanding if you reach out. The class was a bit hard to grasp but definitely eye-opening. The group assignment is reasonable but I had bad members and couldn't choose who I can work with.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: She does not know the material very well. She basically explains the textbook in a much more confusing way.
She is not a very good teacher, doesnt really explain anything. Lectures are a waste of time, just read the book.
Going to lecture is like textbook story time. You might as well just go home and read the text on your own. She is also not very clear with her explanations.
I think the class is useful, but the teacher definitely has a personality deficiency. She seems to have an attitude towards students. As a professor, you gotta treat students nicely.
Probably the worst teacher I have ever had. Overall class was not terrible, but the professor is useless.
very helpful and extremely clear
Immoral, unethical and horrible human being.  Take a look at her past rating before she was kicked out of teaching at CUNY. http://www.ratemyprofessors.com/ShowRatings.jsp?tid=516740
best professor ever!!!! Unfortunately, she's moving to Pennsylvania:(

Awesome teacher. I had her for two classes this quarter and she made each so relevant and engaging. This class is all about law which I had zero interest in prior, but thanks to her teaching style I feel like I learned a lot as well as will be getting a good grade.

The material was interesting, the book wasn't bad, and her tests were straight off the practice tests. The portfolio grading system meant that you were practically guaranteed a 4.0. I was thinking about going to law school and this class convinced me that I should. Definitely take this class.

This class was great. Insanely easy- the tests are about 85% STRAIGHT off the practice tests. The material was interesting, and the book wasn't bad at all. Read the textbook, but the Supreme Conflict book isn't really needed. I didn't mind the name tags and sitting with my section, I got to know people better that way. Moot court was fun too!

The material was taught in a way that did make it easy for students to learn and it was kept somewhat interesting. The only complaints are in the way she handles classroom decorum. She tends to treat her classes like grade-school children, with name tags, assigned seating, standing up and reciting concepts like it was the pledge of allegiance, etc.

Cindy was great, really personable and fun. This was a negotiation class and the material was interesting and useful for every day life. My only complaints were that her lack of organization and strict guidelines was sometimes distracting. She is laid back, but more expectations from here would have been nice. Otherwise, great prof!

I took a special topics class with her (negotiation) and i LOVED it. it was a 4 hour class once a week and she actually made it work! her assignments were totally reasonable (reenacting negotiation scenes! and some writing) and she wasn't picky about turning things in on time. So a great, laid back professor & I learned a lot.
take her classes!

one of hardest and least rewarding class I have ever taken. The workload was well over 30 hours a week, for the 100 level course. Participation at every lecture was mandatory or your grade suffered, reading was over 70 textbook pages a week. And the exams would bring up material not covered in class. do not take if you value your time or sanity.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Montgomery had very engaging and informational lectures and is obviously passionate about the topics discussed. He did move quite fast through slides at times, but as long as you do the readings and corresponding quizzes that isn't much of a problem. Exams are quite difficult and can drop your grade so definitely study.

I think he's really knowledgeable and caring, but he reads pretty fast through the slides and sometimes gets lost in what he's saying. I think that his monotone reading can make lectures feel boring, but he makes side comments which are funny. The busywork and the end of the quarter group project is not very enjoyable.

Not an easy 4.0 if you are looking for an easy class for gen-ed credit. Exams can be tough and drop your grade a lot, lectures are pretty fast-paced, and the grading scale is odd (I have a 93% and that's a 3.5). However, Dave is very intelligent and thought-provoking & there's easy homework. Insightful class just oddly difficult for being 100 lvl.

Dr. Montgomery is a knowledgeable lecturer and he can provide a lot of information on the topic. I took his joint class with Eli Wheat. However, the busywork and the TAs make the class less enjoyable. I think that both Dave and Eli are great people and professors, and the structure of the class would benefit from being changed.

Dr. Montgomery is a great professor and a great author. He knows how to speak science to the general populations in a way that is not diluted but still easy enough to understand. The discussions we had in this class with a small group of people was amazing because everyone can share their views and ask questions.

I loved Davids's lectures in ENVIR 100. They are organized SO well, and he is incredibly passionate and educated. Highly recommend, but be prepared to attend every class. Despite scoring high 90s on exams and assignments, I ended the quarter with a 2.5 due to not attending (seasonal depression killed me this qtr).

Don't recommend this class unless it's your number one passion. Very fast and difficult to keep up, and if you wanted a really good grade you had to devote hours a day to studying. The teacher was nice and a good person, but not my kind of teacher. Tests were incredibly hard and you literally had to memorize everything to get a decent grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

the reading guide is misleading

Don't get me wrong, it was an easy A, but I just don't think Psychology is my cup of tea; at least, not the way Culligan teaches it. She drags ON and ON and makes you despise the content SO MUCH that you get sick of it. I suggest you take it with someone else.

Dr. Culligan is an amazing professor! Her lectures were filled with examples and even guest lecturers to enhance your understanding of the material. Let's you keep exam questions so you can study for the final! :D

I LOVED this woman. I've rarely had a professor that I respected so much. She knows how to teach the material and is super excited to teach it to her students. She is a little over the top, but that just made the lectures interesting and dynamic. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Assigned over 250 pages worth of articles in the last two weeks that were going to be on the final. Doesn't respond to students in regards to grades received. Lectures are virtually obsolete but you get forced to go because of poll questions. Leaves poll questions open for two seconds so be careful on your bathroom breaks
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She's amazing, one of the funniest professor I've met. Her lectures can get a little dry but she tries her best to make it fun and worth while. A lot of reading and midterms, but it's all ok if you study hard.
Lectures always went longer than needed, was dismissive to student questions, and she never gave us an adequate amount of time to finish our poll everywhere questions IN CLASS.
She would miss class contents, whereas the tests would still cover that.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I had Ann every morning at 8 am. She was always scattered in her lectures, and never got through the content that was needed because she'd go on a side-tangent. Her intro to the syllabus was literally 2 days long. Tests tended to include a lot of trick questions. Interesting class, but Ann made it so much less enjoyable.

You can tell that she's really passionate about what she teaches, but because of that she can drag on about certain subjects sometimes. Participation really counts so plan on going to every lecture possible. The class is structured pretty rigidly and there's a lot of assignments so make sure you keep your planner updated.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Hardest course in UW. Exams are not same as the lecture content. 65 MC questions. Lots of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class was exceptionally easy and Dr. Culligan was a great professor! The lectures are recorded online and the reading is minimal. She answers any questions and is kind and funny. There is also no textbook, it's all online, and ample opportunities for extra credit.

Dr. Culligan does a great job of going over the material and elaborating (even if it seems excessive) so that students really remember the material. The lectures were posted online, but don't skip class too often because it really helped to be there.
Dr. Culligan is very interesting and accessible. She is willing to answer questions in class as well as by email or during office hours. I enjoyed her class.

One of the hardest classes I have taken in my 4 years of college. Huge amount of homework and weekly assignments along with 3 exams and one week when you have to do a summary of all of the readings. If you read fast should have no problem. I found this to be difficult material emotionally so, be prepared for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Culligan is amazing and incredibly passionate about what she teaches. The course content is relatively straightforward and sticks pretty close to the textbook. Lots of reading but it's worthwhile material and it's important once the exams come around.

Dr. Culligan's class is difficult to excel in.  One of the hardest classes I have taken in my 4 years of college. Reading is very heavy and exams are multiple choice but, difficult.  Basically, you have to memorize every article that is posted. Her lectures are long and just take a guess on what is going to be on exam.

Very passionate about what she teaches and knowledgeable about the subject. Gives very clear examples for each topic. Always open for questions. Uses PollEverywhere for participation but offers an abundance of xtra credit participation to make up for some days. HW can time-consuming but teaching staff/sections are helpful. Exams are multiple-choice

I was expecting more from the lectures, and was disappointed. The class had a lot of content to cover and I could easily learn everything needed from my textbook, so classes felt rather dull. I also believe she has some learning to do as a teacher, I'm sure she's a fine person, but I found her to be abrasive and at times felt disrespected.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She can be very demeaning and condecending to her students at times. She often tried to force comedy that doesnt always work. She she talks very very fast and will use 2 slides in one hour.

Dr. Culligan is a great individual outside class but that doesn't mean that she is a great professor. There are times that she is funny but most of the time she tries hard to be funny. I am not sure if it is just the class itself that is boring or the way that she is teaching it because you just come to class to get the read the textbook to you.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She's a great professor. It's hard to say otherwise. She's very clear when she's lecturing and is incredibly down to earth. She uses a free mobile app for a clicker and a free online textbook which is awesome. The downsides of the class don't relate to her, we were a guinea pig class for some new content and she was very receptive of our struggles.

Great professor. Don't go on your phones otherwise she will call you out for it. Great energy. Study for the tests well in advance otherwise you will fail. Use the book supplements and go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Ann is a lovely lady. Her lectures were very good but sometimes a bit dry for me. There was basically no homework outside of studying for midterms (of which we had 4 as well as a comprehensive final). There is quite a bit of reading but she uses the old edition of the textbook without the online companion and so it saves you at least $100.

She's a very easy professor. Don't even show up to class, just read the textbook. If you do show up then you can have the textbook read to you. You also get a show as she stumbles over herself trying to stay politically correct. Very easy class. Quiz sections were fun... usually.
As long as you learn the vocabulary and read the textbook, the exams are pretty straightforward and easy. There's also easy extra credit opportunities throughout the quarter.
Study for the tests ahead of time, especially the one with brain anatomy. Do the review problems.

When you start the quarter, you will hate Ann. 100%. But  just suck it up because it gets better. Ann truly cares about her students and wants them to do well. She is willing to talk to students, but the students are not willing to talk to her. Read the textbook. She covers approximately 32% of the exam material in lecture. #lovelife

She's a good lecturer, explains concepts fine but only covers half of the material of the test in lectures, the other half you have to read them on your own. Lectures are quite slow too. This class isn't hard but any means but it takes up a lot of your time. DO NOT treat this class as a GPA booster or a fun class to balance out other hard classes.

Very disorganized lecturer, aggravating to listen to at times because of how slowly she covers material without getting distracted. Lectures are recorded online, and tests are very easy to pass without much studying. Didn't look at the book at all. A good grade booster if you've taken psych before.

There are only four midterms (one dropped at the end) and one final. The professor is really nice and passionate but the things that she talk about get pretty redundant. She records her lectures so I just took notes from ppt and read the book. The tests, all multiple choice, are easy if you study for them. Also a lot of extra credit.

She rambles for days, and maybe averages about 10 minutes per slide, it's so slow I sometimes can't handle it. She figuratively beats seven dead horses per lecture. So you will more than understand the material. Easy class overall, read the lecture slides and the textbook and you're golden. Extra credit is fun too.

I hated my class with her. My friends and I took bets on how few of the slides she would get through, because of her useless, disorganized rambling. I took her class maybe a year ago but decided to post this after hearing a friend who just took her class say that it was so awful, it turned her off of GWSS. Would not recommend.

I took all of the intro to psych courses with Dr. Voorhies and she is phenomenal! It obvious she loves what she does and helps any unsure psych pre-majors fall in love too! Absolutely one of the best profs I have had so far at UW out of any programs! If you ever see her teaching a class... TAKE IT! P.S. her lectures are structured around the book

I really really love Dr. Voorhies' classes. I have taken four classes with her. She is really clear with what she wants us to know and what will be on the exam. And more importantly her lecture is so fun and she is hilarious! I just love her! I will definitely recommend you to try her classes!

Dr. Voorhies was the reason I found That Psychology is my passion.  As for Psych209 i felt like the class content was a little boring ( but easier)compared to Biopsych or Psych101. However, Dr.V are excellent in speaking , which made the class more exciting. EXAMS ARE BASED MOSTLY FROM WHAT SHE SPEAKS IN LECTURE!! w/ 3 EC questions on every exams.

I truly regret taking this class. Exams were hard and instructor is sometimes rude and not approachable. It is unfair that there are a lot of questions in the exam, but the duration of the exams are very short (50 minutes only)! TAs are not helpful too. Grading by TA is very tough. Not recommended.

Ann was great in this Psych 403 (motivation) class. It's a small class setting, which is nice compared to most of UW's classes. Participation weighs heavily on your grade, which was scary for me as someone who doesn't talk much, but I'm 4.0-ing the class without a problem. This class has been my favorite at UW so far, HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

I was excited to take the class then disappointed by the content of the class.  I can see Ann is trying to make the class fun by raising her voice but it's been having the opposite effects.  Her examples are very confusing.  The exams are pretty easy.  class not curved.  But I would try to avoid her.

Dr. Voorhies is the main reason why I decided to major in Psychology! I have had her as a professor for every Psychology Pre-Req. course thus far and she teaches just as well in all. Psychology is interesting in itself, she just makes it more interesting! If you simply pay attention during lecture you can do well on her easy tests and pass.

Dr. Voorhies is the best professor I've had so far. She is very enthusiastic; her classes are super fun and interesting. I learned so much from her classes her own opinions. Her explanation is very clear and easy to understand( sometimes she speaks fast). Her exams are tough. You need to work hard for them. Recommended her for this class!

Professor Voorhies was THE best instructor I have ever had in a college setting. Even though the lectures were screencast online, she made you want to show up because she was so entertaining to listen to. Her exams were very fair. As long as you know what is on the slides, you will do fine. I look forward to taking another one of her classes!!

Professor Voorhies is an excellent lecturer because she always makes sure to clarify when something is uncertain. She cares deeply for her students and is willing to help out anytime, even in the middle of class. The tests are hard though, and she makes you work for a good grade. I definitely recommend taking her class.

Goes on a tangent sometimes. Lecture are very clear and easy to follow. Exam questions can be very specific. Hated the readings; felt like they were useless. Participating in weekly discussions is fun but key for your grade. Very knowledgeable in what she teaches. Her cellphone policy is what I disagree with most. Class should not be labeled psych.

I've never been so excited to learn about the brain until I took this class. She's super intelligent, extremely cheerful and passionate about what she teaches and I recommend her class for anyone interested in learning about the brain and behavior.

Dr. Voorhies is one of the best professor I've had so far. She is very enthusiasm. Her lectures are AMAZING and she explains things really well. She is quite strict and her expectation of students are high. Tests are reasonable if you put time on your reading and review class material regularly. recommend her for psych101!!

I really enjoyed Prof. Voorhies' class; she was contagiously enthusiastic and very knowledgeable about the subject. She answers as many questions as she can and while the textbook is vital to passing the exams, coming to lectures alone will teach you a heck of a lot. Attendance matters because the class involves clicker questions.

This class is difficult, lots of material covered, small details tested on. She's very clear and articulate, but slow class because lots of questions and comments by students. Assignments, tests, and mandatory quiz sec&lecture participation (clickers) extra credit available and some random extra points added on clicker questions so COME TO CLASS

Dr. Voorhies is insanely passionate about psychology, which is refreshing and respectable, but also results in the longest and most boring tangents. She got very behind on the material she needed to cover, yet still tested on what she didn't lecture. Five tests total, one dropped, all very easy. Easy A class but often boring.

I was excited to take this class but was extremely disappointed by the content delivered by Ann. The material was based on her opinions and she would attempt to verify with poor statistical data. She was forceful with her views. On the tests you are expected to answer based on her views. Other students I spoke with also dreaded going to her class.

Ann has taught this class before with better structure, but by far one of the worst classes I have ever taken.  In Autumn 2014, she had students submit five questions every week about the readings, and there were about 30 students in the class. So, for the final and midterm, you had to study over 500 questions to prepare. No validity whatsoever.
Super fun class! Tests are pretty easy if you put in effort (read the book + lectures). Also, try to get the clicker questions right because it will help your grade a lot!

Prof. V is the coolest professor ever! She makes every single class FUN! Her lecture is very clear but you gotta keep up with the reading because there are lots of clicker ques Also, she speaks quite fast so reading will help you better understand what she's talking about. I HIGHLY recommend her. Ps. can't wait to take Biopsych with her nxt quart!!

Ann is a really great teacher. She's very enthusiastic about Psychology and you can tell she loves it - often rambles and spends a lot of time time on one topic, but her examples are great. Tests were mainly info out of the book,  so reading is a must! Would take this class again and as well as other psych classes.

I read the high ratings for this class thinking that this would be a great class to take. Unfortunately, I did not expect the class to be what it ended up to be. The teacher "lost" clicker points when the majority of the class got them right. Tests are challenging, especially when you consider this is a intro class.
She is so kind and knows the topics she is talking about. She is also super passionate about her topics! She's great!
She is very knowledgeable, her lectures are super clear and easy to comprehend. There's a lot of material but her slides are easy to study and lectures are usually screencast.

There's no tests for this class, only 8 short papers and 1 final paper but don't let the amount of reading and writing scare you away from this class. She's one of the best professors that I've ever had and she makes you want to work hard. Plus the content for class is interesting and useful. I highly recommend taking it.
She has her stuff down and doesn't deal with any nonsense. Do your readings, go to lecture, study, and you'll do great.

Made Biopsychology fun--informative and fascinating lectures, challenging but still perfectly reasonable tests. Source material was interesting to me at least, so I found the class a great continuation of Intro Psych.

She is a nice and good professor. You have to attend lecture. She gives clicker questions every lecture and participation is a big part of your grade in this class. The material is very dry in this class. She does her best to "spice it up" but this class is still very boring. Still, Ann Voorhies is a good professor.

Dr. Voorhies is an amazing lecturer. She explains things thoroughly and it makes things better that she is excited about what she teaches. You have to really study for her exams and read the textbook to get As. However, you can get by with just studying lectures. Not hard but still takes the effort. I 100% recommend her for Psych 202

Dr. Voorhies is one of the best professors I've had. Her lectures slides are great tools for studying. Tests are extremely straight forward. She is a phenomenal lecturer. She recognizes that the material in research psych is dry and mundane but she tries to make class engaging. Super enthusiastic about teaching.

She talks very fast but isn't hard to follow. She covers everything you need to know for the tests in lecture and is very clear about where the information is in the textbook and what you need to know on the test. The class is primarily memorization and the tests were MC. If you put in the effort and go to all the lectures you will do well.

Dr. Voorhies is really nice. She is enthusiastic about biopsych, everyone can tell from her lectures. The lecture is organized and fun. But her exams are a little bit hard. She always ask really specific questions. And a portion of final is cumulative, which is REALLY hard for a subject like biopsych.

Great lectures, notes are uploaded online which was really helpful. Exams are very fair, not hard/not easy. Very passionate, can occasionally plug in her opinion heavy-handedly, but the distinction between her opinion and fact is usually pretty clear. Definitely a great professor, very passionate and helpful. Super fast grader, which is also nice.

Dr. Voorhies is one of the best professors I had at the UW. Although everyone says readings are required, I was still able to get 4.0 without actually reading textbook. But you're going to have to study her lectures a lot if you decide not to read textbook. I spent about three hours including lectures everyday to study for this class.

Dr. Voorhies is phenomenal. She lectures with great clarity and answers each question in depth. She approaches each topic with enthusiasm and makes you want to learn just to keep up with her. Although there is quite a bit of reading, the content is not hard to swallow and can be quick. Attendance is mandatory due to clicker questions.
One of the best professors, if not the best, I've had to this day.

Dr. Ann Voorhies was excellent at lecturing, and made it very easy to follow what she was saying.Be prepared to have to memorize a lot though, so utilize your best personal tool for memorizing things.
Dr. Voorhies was awesome! She taught everything really well and was readily available for help. TAs and clue sessions were also awesome. One of the best classes I've taken.

I loved Dr. Voorhies! She explains topics well and is very excited to teach us, which makes the students interested. This course did have TONS of reading, but if you did the reading and attended class you should be good to go!
she's so awesome! I really don't like biology but she makes the class really interesting. Not an easy A, but if you study hard you'll get good grades! Definitely go to class and sections

Ann is such a cool gal. This class is NOT an easy class though so don't expect to get an easy A. I dissected her study guides and still never managed to get higher than 84% on her exams which of course isn't that bad. With that said, be prepared for lots of information thrown at you but Ann is SO nice, funny, and helpful, the class is very doable.

Dr. Voorhies tends to go on in her lecture. She doesn't move from topic to topic quickly and reiterates her points. In a two hour class don't expect to go more than 4 slides. She is very knowledgable, but I found her pace too slow and frustrating. You have to attend lecture and make sure you do the reading.

You can tell Dr. Voorhies knows what she is talking about. However she uses unnecessary big words and is also very repetitive-not about the important things though. She is too wordy and I think she tries to make you connect with the material by making it funny, but it didn't really work for me, I mostly found it annoying.

I adored Prof Voorhies. You could tell she loves teaching psychology. She was very interesting, her lectures were very insightful. There is a lot of reading and her lectures have clicker questions which is counted for participation. I highly recommend her for any student taking psych 101.

Ann is amazing. She can teach the most dull information and still keep you engaged. She's very willing to help and is quite intelligent. I highly recommend her. However, the subject is extremely difficult, so you really have to study. But she is an easy grader for assignments. I got full credit on all of them.

This class was so fun and interesting! Awesome professor, I definitely recommend her and am going to take another class with her in the future! She made Psychology so fun and easy to learn! Definitely take this class with her.

Overall this class can be summed up into two words: interesting and easy. Voorhies teaches you about psychology, but you learn a LOT about yourself along the way. Lots of memorization from the book, but there's extra credit and she drops the lowest exam, so it's pretty easy to get a high grade. Bonus, she gives really good college study habits!

Straight forward, clear, very reasonable exam guidelines. A fairly easy class, but a good introduction to college and it will help those trying to get used to studying. She is also very committed to her students and she is entertaining in lecture. Information is interesting, especially since she is so dedicated to it!

She is the teacher i have met so far in my life who LOVES teaching that much!!! She enjoys her lecture time and you can tell because she always almost dances in the lecture. The punchline of this lecture, according to her, is "no panic!". She is utterly loving and the exam is extremely easy if you know how to memorize! HIGHLY recommend her!

She's really nice and pretty straight foreword about her expectations. No quiz section so a decent amount of outside work in necessary to do well on the tests. Doesn't speak very efficiently in class and often runs out of time on power points.
She is the best professor I know so far. She is so enthusiastic and helpful. For psych101, it is not that difficult. I decided to take psych202 with her, but only with her!

A difficult class for sure, but she is an amazing teacher! Extremely approachable, enthusiastic, easy to understand... she is the best professor I have had to this day. I wish she could teach all of my psych classes. They'd kick my butt but it would be worth it! I learned so much.

Dr Voorhies is an excellent professor.  she made the class so fun.  she talks with such clarity.  i never needed to open the textbook.  there are 3 exams but if you pay attention in class or watch the lectures on screencast you'll do fine.  great fun class!
Great professor. She is very enthusiastic in the subject and one of the best professor I have had so far on UW Seattle campus.

Great professor. Engaging lectures and you can tell she loves the material. Despite morning class, she was able to keep me awake and interested. I learned a lot in her class and she explained things very well. Very friendly and happy to speak with students after class or during her office hours, even if it isn't class related. Highly recommended.
Loved her. She was always engaging at 8:30 and showed how much she cared about her class and if we were learning. Keep up with the reading and GO TO CLASS and you should be fine!

Professor Voorhies is the BEST! She presents the material in a well organized manner and she's very clear on all the concepts. Her exams are tough but there are bonus questions. I learned a lot from this course and I definitely recommend her!

My favorite professor thus far in UW! I've taken 2 (currently doing psych of gender) classes from her and I love it. I hated bio related stuff before biopsych, but now it's my fav, I wish we covered more in that class. I'm definitely taking more psych classes with her.

Great Professor, She cared about helping students and realized that the course load was rather difficult. I also found the course content very interesting. Most of the questions on the exams came from lecture, but a few were from the book. 4 exams (lowest exam score is dropped) and a final that is 1/3 cumulative. Not an easy A, but its doable.

She is the most straightforward teacher I've ever had. Her tone of voice is extremely motivating, no monotone, but not too annoying either. Very down to earth and approachable. Course difficult but she makes it doable

Great professor! She really cares about her students and is passionate about biopsych (oddly lol). She's really helpful and WANTS you to understand. The class is very tough, and you have to put in a lot of effort. But there's many tools to help you through the class. Don't really need the book! Mainly goes off of lectures. Highly recommend!!!!

Definitely the best Professor ever!!!!She is easygoing and funny. I really wish I could take more classes with her, but since I am graduating, no more chance to do so. The class materials are very useful.

Great class, great teacher. She is very helpful and obviously passionate about the subject. However, this class was difficult and by no means an easy A. Lots of work required for an A, but it's pretty easy to get a B.

Not only is Ann a brilliant teacher she is also funny, easy going, and relatable. Even though the class was large she encouraged participation and was available for one on one help as well. I went to every class even though she puts slides up simply because it was enjoyable. Highly recommend anything she teaches.
Very enthusiastic and committed to teaching her students

Great professor. Clear lectures that were posted online. Lowest midterm dropped, final ~33% cumulative only. She really cares about students' success and her lectures are really worth waking up early for! Fair grading, just read the book, do the homework, and study a bit every week.

I love her! Interesting class! there are 4 mid, 2 writings. 1 final. the lowest midterm score is dropped. no clicker. no quiz. you dont need textbook to get 100% on exams. Lecture slides are enough to study. but if you want to know about the topic more, or want to score on extra credit problems, get it.

One of my absolute favorite classes taken at UW! Biopsych is so interesting and you will learn a ton! Voorhies is such an enthusiastic professor she makes the lectures really interesting, plus everything is screencasted so you don't actually need to go to class. Highly recommend!

I had Biopsych with Voorhies, and she is wonderful! She's full of energy, engaging, and funny. She talks extremely quickly, so if you attend class be prepared to take fast notes! However, you don't actually have to be there - everything is screencasted online later. Point of interest: my male friends thought she was hot.

I loved this class & you don't have to attend lectures (all online) which was helpful because it could get confusing. MEMORIZE her lecture notes for the exams and you'll be okay. I only went to class to take the exams and got a 3.6 - super easy if you are truly interested in the material, you will do fine!

Best professor I've ever had at the University of Washington, by far. Even if you can't make it to her lectures, she posts her lecture slides before and screencasts immediately after class. Her lectures are super clear and easy to understand. I wouldn't just study the lectures slides though. The things she says are really supplemental to the exams.
Beautifully precise and concise, awesome workload and clear expectations. you'll really learn a lot.

Excellent professor! She is by far the best prof i've ever taken a class from at the UW. She makes the class very interesting and fun at the same time. She's clear, patient and is always open to questions and comments. She's simply a brilliant professor!!

I honestly thought Biopsych was a very easy class. Just hunker down, do the readings, pay attention. Learn the material. Just do it. Don't get overwhelmed. Just learn n you'll be fine. Dr. Voorhies is a great teacher. I don't think I've ever given a hot rating before since it is irrelevant but you kinda have to. The bonus questions on exams r gr8

Voorhies is an awesome teacher! She really cares about her students and her lectures are interesting. She provides lots of ways for you to get extra help outside of class, (which I would highly recommend because it is a hard class). Stay on top of what's happening by reviewing the lectures and reading the book.

hands down my favorite class and my  favorite professor! there is a lot of memorization in the class but if you take the time to memorize everything and actually understand the material then you will for sure get an A in this class. Professor Voorhies is really awesome and entertaining.

There is a lot of memorization required for this class, so I would say the difficulty lies in the amount of material you need to know. That said, Dr. Voorhies is fabulous - she is enthusiastic, a great help during office hours, and a professor you would rather have for an 8:30 class.

Ann is the best teacher I've ever had!! She's so enthusiastic in class and in office hour. Always happy to answer student's questions. But don't waste too much time in reading the book. The lecture is super super important.

This was the first time Psych of Gender was taught, and she did an amazing job. Tests were easy. The textbook I kind of skimmed, it's the articles you want to read well. Class average was high for tests. 2 MC and Cum. final (mostly focus on later material) she tends to get behind though, students ask questions and takes up too much of class time.
I love Voorhies.  I have taken a number of classes with her.  Biopsych of Women (357) is one of the BEST classes that I have taken at UW.

She is without a doubt one of the most incredible professors I've had.  She is spunky, energetic and is passionate about psychology.  If you can take a class from her, do it!!!! You will NOT regret it.  Just don't be lazy and you'll learn more than ever before and will enjoy it all.
Loved the class and Ann! Would highly recommend taking one of her classes.

I had her for biopsych and i loved her lectures. she's so enthusiastic, she makes it fun. the course content itself is very interesting and very useful to not only psychology but life! she is definitely one of my favorite professors at the uw.

I had Ann for biopsych (PSYCH 202) before this and in both classes she has been by far the best teacher I have ever had at UW. Going to class is necessary, as is asking questions when confused. She is always willing to help and provides plenty of opportunities to help you out.

If you study everything from lecture, you should be fine. This class is basically pure memorization but the material is interesting! Voorhies is an excellent lecture and she makes going to class worthwhile.
Love her class, I always return online to recapture what she'd said in the lecture, and it is really helpful, also if TA have review session you could go, it is helpful too.
The class is really interesting, and listen to her lecture will make you want to study! Lecture is really energetic and fun. Recommended!!!Love this class

This was definitely one of my more enjoyable classes this quarter. Dr. Voorhies DOES talk pretty fast (like a lot of people are saying) but she has screencasts and the discussion board online is very helpful. You have to study to get a good grade, don't expect an easy 4.0. The material is difficult but interesting (esp. if you're a psych major!)

She's very clear in her lectures of what she expects of you... but her material is HARD.  If you want to get a below average score, overall, go ahead and take her class.  You literally would have to study hours every single day to even get close to a 4.0.  No one has time to devote this much time to a class.  The online course is EASY.
Fantastic teacher who is very clear, and does an extraordinary job of  teaching Psych 202. This class is a lot or work but worth it if you willing to put in the effort. Study Early!

Tests were multiple choice and straightforward if you studied. It was very clear what students were expected to know. Dr. Voohries is passionate about the subject and my TA (Yong Sang Jo) gave us great resources to use for studying. I loved the class!
She presents info clearly and logically, but still with enthusiasm. Great class!

Prof. Voorhies was a great professor. She really knows her stuff and you can tell she is really passionate about it as well. Her lectures are clear and informative but reading the textbook is necessary. Overall I would say her tests are hard but fair and there is NO busy work required for the class (just one writing assignment).

Professor Voorhies is engaging and cares that her students learn the material.  I appreciated her enthusiasm for the subject and sincerely enjoyed the class as a whole.  The class covered a lot of material, but overall I felt that the tests were fair.

Voorhies is simply amazing.She is the only prof who can keep me awake at 8.30am.She has this really expressive and musical tone of voice,and casual humor that transforms the goriest of biopsych into fun.She's also super friendly & helpful, encourages us to think critically and takes questions very seriously.Her TAs this quarter have been great too.

Great professor. She enjoys teaching and explained things in a way that makes them interesting and easy to understand. However, her class is definitely a lot of work. But if you do the reading and study early then getting a good grade is definitely doable. Overall a great professor and kept me coming to class at 830.

AMAZING. She is hands down the best professor I've had at UW thus far. She has a great way of explaining complicated subjects and knows what she's talking about. Her screencasts are extremely helpful, as well. Let's just say I used to hate biology, but now I've found a great interest in it. Take her class if you can!

Absolutely one of my favorite professors. She is always well prepared for her. She doesn't merely lecture in the class; it's open for everyone to discuss the content, and it gets very personal. It was an early class, but she always kept it interesting. Work was fair and you could always get help. Would definitely recommend this class with her!
she's sweet and helpful.

best prof I ever had...don't really need the book a ton...just study and know the words on the review sheet...she's really into teacher and makes it fun...work on the written early on...studied hard and got a 4.0

One of my favorite profs! She is energetic, sweet, and enthusiastic. Her lectures are interesting and clear. The class isn't easy, but she is very helpful to students who work hard. I asked her a psych question unrelated to the class, and she sent me articles even in the midst of grading finals. A very sweet lady.
Wonderful teacher.  Great class.  She is always available for extra help and id very knowledgeable and understanding.  Knows the subject like the back of her hand.  Also, very hot.
Great, super confident, loved the class. Do go to section - very helpful.
She's incredible; enthusiastic, extremely knolwedgable,and she's ready and willing to help you with anything. However, she's tough.

One of the more difficult classes I've taken at the UW. She talks really fast during lecture. However she is very enthusiastic and passionate about what she teaches. Get a good TA if you can -- helps a lot to understand the material!

The course itself is all memorization with loads of terminology but Voorhies does a good job covering everything on the test during lecture. Quiz sections are helpful to understand the bigger picture.
really funny professor!

Funny, engaging, very interactive for a lecture class. She is extremely competent and willing to help, and always has time for questions. She makes a potentially very dry and boring class interesting.

She was OKAY.... The first 3 tests were the most hard. There is a lot of terminology (annoying) and her tests questions are multilayered- so when studying you have to know everything for each concept. Study where NT's are projected- those were the hardest for me! Her test outlines were unhelpful bc they literally cover everything. Get a good TA!!!!
Best professor I've had thus far! (and Im @ the end of my jr yr)

Professor Voorhies was extremely enthusiastic and passionate about the topics also very nice and approachable!  This class takes a lot of studying but all from the lectures I didn't use the book at all! Definitely recommend this class especially with Professor Voorhies!

She is an amazing teacher, knows how to explain, very enthusiastic about what she's teaching her students, and although i have never talk to her, she seems like she's extremely approachable and willing to help! The content of the class is very interesting too!

Dr. Voorhies is about the best professor you could hope for with this frustratingly difficult material. She is very clear and organized, friendly and approachable, always willing to help. This class requires constant attention and studying. She certainly doesn't keep track of attendance, but DEFINITELY watch the screencast if you miss lecture.

motivated students a lot, very intelligent and charismatic. Liked coming to class. Is very helpful and clear. Class is fairly hard and covers a lot of information but if you study a lot and know your material well then you'd do fine. Just remembering the information will not help.
She tends to regard her class as 4-years, but the material is well-covered.

Most other comments here have explained how she is a phenomenal teacher. However many fail to mention that Voohries is HOT. Somehow her intellect combines with her physicality to make her just insanely attractive. Look at it this way, she has the same haircut I had when I was 10 (im male fyi) and yet she is still smokin.

Great teacher. I loved her class, her lectures were interesting, engaging and fun. I liked the structure of the class and as long as you attend lectures, read assigned readings and do the work you should do fine. Not that hard of a class I liked it!

I really enjoyed this class, and felt like I actually gained real knowledge. Podcasts are a convenient alternative to going to class, and I felt it worked best for me in terms of this class. I got a 3.7 without buying the book. Probably could've gotten a 4.0 if I didn't get sick and bomb the fourth exam. Excellent teacher, vibrant personality!
