She is very involving in lectures and brings up very interesting examples and is also often quite funny. She also gives you plenty of opportunity to get extra help. While the class is quite difficult, I had a very good experience taking the class from her. Recommended!

Dr. Voorhies is by far the best professor I have had. The course covers a TON of a material, but she presents it in an effective way and provides many avenues for getting help (email, office hours, online discussion). Anyone complaining is just bitter because the class actually required studying.  It's college, duh.
Very interesting class. The tests are very straight forward. As long as you go to lecture, study, and understand the material, a 4.0 is do-able.
Really good with the material, for how much, and how hard it is. Her voice is always so engaging, and she is helpful with studying material. Good teacher for how hard the class is.

Reads straight off the slides so kind of hard to stay engaged in the lecture. I also didn't like the way she talked it was really repetitive and her tone gets super annoying after the first 3 minutes of class. Grading wise its pretty straight forward. Test material is straight forward too.
ann voorhies is absolutely adorable! and shes always so chipper
This professor is really enthusiastic about biopsych

This is an extremely intense class.  We got so much information, and the exams are multiple choice, but are mean't to trick and confuse you.  I listened to podcasts,  took notes, studied intensely and still only got a 76!  You must get an 85 to get a 3.0!  Great teacher, fun class but intensely difficult

She appears to be warm & nice when you first meet her. However, I found her rude & public about grades. She embarrassed her students by correcting them in front of the entire class. She would roll her eyes obnoxiously! She needs to be professional & confidential. The class was only fun b/c everyone fell in love w/ their rats. NO HELP & sarcastic!
Great professor, very clear on what you need to do to get a 4.0. Go to class, study your notes (ALL test questions appeared in the notes!) and get an A!

Easy to 4.0 if you go to class everyday/listen to the podcast everyday.  Review sheets tell you everything that will be on a test.  Sometimes she goes on tangents and answers questions  that don't really matter, but overall, a great professor!
Awesome teacher. Likable and easy to understand.
Awesome prof, notes and podcasts were promptly available online for the days you missed class.  Sometimes spent too much time on questions, but very helpful.

For psych 101, she's not the easiest teacher. Some of her test questions are tricky. I can't say she is the greatest speaker either. She did enough to just keep me awake. However, she is extremely helpful through email and office hours.

The material was basically what you might expect from such an intensive class.  Little things about her and her way of teaching irritated me.  Her random grading scale is completely ridiculous and I also found her very rude to students, even in front of class.  She moves too quickly, and doesn't emphasize what's actually on the tests.

As someone that is taking biopsych for the second time with a different professor, I really miss Professor Voohries. She's very knowledgeable, but her pace is really fast and her lectures are packed with a lot of details and information. Her class is hard because there's so many details, so concentrate on memorization and you should be fine.

If you are not one to pay attention to TINY detail do not take this class. Her tests are so detailed it's impossible to get an A- instead of asking the main points shes VERY focused on what neuron goes where- not what it does. Did not learn anything- just tried very hard to memorize TINY details. Book is only used about 10%. follow the study guide
Must attend ever lecture and do ALL of the readings or you are screwed on the tests.

Reads straight off a powerpoint everyday. Her lectures might be useful if she talked slower but you end up spending most of your class time trying to get all of the info from her slides, rather than listening to her. Her tests are straight from the slides but unfortunately if you miss some of the info on the slides your screwed. She did seem nice.

I have just finished taking her PSYCH202 class for Winter08 at UW.  She is an animated/energetic lecturer, puts complex topics into easy analogies.  Excellent clarity, office hrs extended to accommodate me.  Tests = Easy, moderate, hard, easy, easy (drop 1). Stopped taking notes in class due to pace, but listen to podcast/take notes = getting a 4.0

Very nice and lectures well. She makes going to class worth it, though podcasts are very handy to have. The exams are intensive but not impossible, definitely not as hard as people have been making them out to be here.

worst professor ever! do not take this class from her. she moves way too fast through her notes..yea she posts them online, but theyre incomplete from the ones during lecture. i took her and got a 1.8. i retook it with olavarria and got a 3.7. avoid her at all costs

This class totally shot me down. She gives you so much information so quickly. When it comes down to studying for exams, you can't really sort through it all. The tests are worded so differently than the material she gives. It's unbelievable. Bottom line- Intensely hard class. Don't take it.

I thought she was very nice. Class was incredibly laid back and pretty fun. The paper we had to write was hard, and she sent them to a reader to grade, which sucked because I know she would have graded them much easier. Overall, she's cool!

Went to class everyday, printed off the slides from online to take notes, and the information was still a mystery to me. She talks really quickly and basiclly regurgitates what is on the slides with some extra information (some helpful, but for the majority not). And her TA didn't help the pain either.

Prof. Voorhies seems like an incredibly nice person, but she needs to learn how to manage her class time better.  She rarely gets through her slides and leaves it up to students to finish them on their own time.  Also, there's a comprehensive final, but at least you get to drop a midterm.

Not horrible, but not great. A whole quarter of slides, slides, slides and long textbook and other readings is not my cup of tea.  I dread going to class because she goes through slides so quickly and lets people ask irrelevant questions to which she normally answers "I don't know" in a peppy tone.  She is repetitive and makes tests difficult.

Ann Voorhies totally sucks!! DONT TAKE PSY 202 with her, she is so0oo0o0 crazy!!   Her slides are so incomplete and she move soo0o0o  fast and her test are so hard. Her grading systems sucks as well. She is rude too!!
I enjoyed her class so much. She was so helpful and she wanted to make sure that every students in her class understand the materials. She is so nice!

I know it's nice to get A's, especially when you don't have to spend >15 min for each joke of an assignment and 15 mins in class most days, but that DOES NOT mean the teacher is even remotely competent. I can't believe that someone so clueless has a PhD. I learned absolutely NOTHING useful and this was by far the worst class that I have ever taken.

Let's see here... kay? Really knowledgeable, goes into detail about subject matter enough for students to really understand it. Oh, sorry, I misspoke. She's actually none of that. She's nice and peppy, but in that cheerleader sort of way. Give me an A! That's about how easy her class is. You won't learn much, very limited spectrum of knowledge.

Basically a more attractive textbook. Her mouth says "I have a Ph.D, omg look at it it's so pretty", but her actual knowledge doesn't seem to sretch beyond her powerpoint notes. Don't expect any technical explainations, and don't bring up any other research - she hasn't read it. Either take her class or buy her course book - they're the same thing.

Psychobiology of Women is an incredible class and Dr. Voorhies cares about her students and wants them to do well. The first test is a killer so leave no detail unstudied! The other exams are more reasonable and she is fair in her grading overall. This class is mostly anatomy, physiology, and endocrinology. This class is detailed, but worth it!

Prof. Voorhies ROCKS. She teaches a really dry, difficult subject with an amazing amount of energy and enthusiasm- her lecture style could give Feynman a run for his money. Her engagement with the material is contagious; she makes Biopsychology fascinating and accessible.

Completely incompetent. I have never had a worse teacher and I cannot understand how she is even teaching classes at a good university like UW. If you want an easy grade, then sign up for any of her classes. But if you actually want to learn anything, then by all means, aviod her! She had no idea how to grade a paper or conduct a class.

Very good teacher and very helpful. the only reason i sat in the front row was to take notes for a handicapped dude. Didnt need to go to lecture, cuz the book had all the info. i got a 4.0 just by reading the book. She is a good lecturer tho and she kept me awake in class. Take her classes!
Very helpful, nice, and fair.  Will always reply to emails and is very laid back in class structure.  I would take her again!

Are you kidding? She does not talk too fast, the course is just tough. Listen to the podcasts and if you can't understand, pause or rewind. I never went to class and got an A. And fyi she IS hot. And she is super nice, she never even got annoyed when the same kids kept asking really stupid questions during lecture! I'd totally take her again!
She talks quickly and goes through the slides fast. She's helpful if you go to her personally.

Ann is very nice. However, she moves so fast through the material. Winter 07 was the first time teaching 202. She seemed to want to teach the class EVERYTHING she learned, when getting her PHD, in one introduction class.  Too much material, in a small amount of time.  Also, not enough ways to recieve material, it was all presented the same.
AWESOME TEACHER! SOOO GLAD SHE'S TEACHING. I HIGHLY RECCOMEND HER! AND, SHE'S PRETTY HOT AND YOUNG!

She tends to talk kind of fast and sometimes sounds like she doesn't know what she is talking about, however, she sounds like she genuinely wants you to learn and she goes out of her way to make sure you learn the material.

She reads off slides and you can get all the information out of the book.  It took me a while to even warm up to this professor, because she moves really fast through her slides and does indeed say "okay" at least once per sentence.  However, after the "Reproduction" unit, when she actually started involving the class a bit more, it got better.
always says "sorry i misspoke"  and "kay?" - gets a little frustrating because you feel like she doesn't know what she is talking about.
No Comments

Easy class for requirements since it's mostly discussion posts. I don't know how the TAs were, but I was assigned to her group and the quizzes were easy and doing the art projects can be straightforward if you watch all the lectures. People interested in modern art would really find this interesting. Attending office hours was not mandatory

She doesn't actually teach. Course content is from 5 years ago, and it is a few people (who aren't even involved in the course anymore) just reading off papers. She only interacts with you via grading and the occasional canvas announcement, and my friends and I noticed she would copy and paste the same vague comments on all of our assignments. Lazy

Considering this is a generic gen ed that most do for just the credits, it's quite tedious. TAs grade unnecessarily harshly and mark points down to avoid giving out 100s. In my case, TA docked me 1 point for final assignment for a rather stupid reason just to avoid giving a 4.0. In the end, the class is still pretty straightforward and easy.

I loved this course. Although I did not quite receive the 4.0 I almost got, I still admire the professor and her course. I would recommend everyone to take this course because of its uniqueness in content and how it will inspire you to think curiously and creatively. Thank you, Stephanie Deumer.

Grading was clear and assignments were interesting. Beware of the readings, they are quite complicated. It would be nice if the professor could condense the readings into shorter articles, I would have loved the course more.
Cool course. Was not very passionate lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing assignments. Loved having the ability to make my own ideas and not just a boring prompt or paper.
I wish the lectures were freshly recorded and not just recycled from past years. Overall the course was amazing and I learned a lot, but I wish the lectures were fresher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class is awesome if you do the work. Weekly discussions are great to build on thought. Projects allow for you to use your own imagination. This is a THEORY HEAVY COURSE. Less application and way more THEORY.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing course. Quizzes should be treated like midterms. They have super heavy weight along with the big assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was an amazing course! I loved learning about new media art. Before this course I did not care about art, especially modern art. But now, I love it! This course is marked by weekly discussions, 2 quizzes, and 3 large assignments. I encourage everyone to take this course, because artwork delves into all fields of science and expertise. Awesome!

I loved this professor! The course was inspiring and eye-opening. I didn't know anything about new media art before taking this course and now I feel like I am an expert. This course will challenge your curiosity and writing skills. The three major assignments were my favorite. Writing heavy, but the ability to create my own artwork was fulfilling
LITERALLY SUCH A TOUGH GRADER FOR WHAT

I dont know if its fair to rate this prof because she doesn't really teach. For the class, you watch pre recorded lectures and she just posts reminders of assignments. She wasn't a super tough grader but this is not a great class to take if you are genuinely interested in learning. Quick credit overall.

This is a warning to any art kids that think this class will help them, it wont. Most of the work is discussion posts, no actual practice outside of the 5 assignments which have vague rubrics. It's labeled as a digital arts class but all the art work is conceptual, nothing for those looking for digital illustration/ animation. Don't waste your time

Course was not what I had hoped. Course was taught w lectures recorded by past/other instructors who read directly from the slides. I had little to no engagement with this prof--only interacted with TA. Assignments made you to think outside of the box, but some instructions were not clear enough. Participation in weekly discussions was fine.

Weekly discussion posts that require you to cite and reference readings. There are 2 quizzes which are worth 30% of your grade (based on lectures, readings, and interviews). There are 5 assignments and 1 final project. My only complaint is the grading discrepancy. My advice is go to TA office hours to see what your TA looks for when grading.

Professor Kelly is very kind and caring, but not the best teacher. Her lectures are hard to follow and the quizzes arent very easy. Its clear she really cares about the topic, she just doesn't teach it very well. Assignments are given in each class and due at the end of class. There's extra credit and 3 quizzes.

she was a decent prof, not the best but def not the worst. i took it as an easy A which it was but the tests were like 10-20 questions and simple but if u don't pay attention then it would obvi be bad. participation/credit is taken by writing down 6 facts from the lectures and turning it in at the end of class.

Deb doesn't organize well, but she is very supportive and obviously wants you to succeed. This class was less of a class and more of a weekly check-in meeting, and I would've appreciated more structure with it. What Deb lacked in teaching, she made up for in enthusiasm and caring.

I respect how passionate Kelley is, but I found her lectures very boring and lacking in organization. The concepts are not that hard but the way they are presented makes the quizzes challenging. You have to attend class but honestly you can just do work during it. I appreciate that she offers extra credit.

She seems like a really nice person, but the lectures are painfully boring. She spends a lot of time talking about her past glories in the 1990s which leaves me wondering what new things have happened in the past... 30 years. Attendance was mandatory for Zoom class since you had to submit a word document immediately afterwards about the class.
One of the most boring lecturers at UW, and she constantly talks about her past accomplishments. I just want to learn some stuff...

Really like Deb a lot. She's an incredibly nice person and her passion for the Oceans is very inspirational. That said, I found the subject material pretty boring (but it's probably just me). Lectures are long and sometimes confusing. She does provide detailed study guides for the quizzes. Her TA's are very harsh graders though. Easyish 2 credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I like the professor. She always has the coolest PPT to show to us. But it's a lot of work for just 2 credit class. We have to write 3 abstracts and the TA won't pass you easily. But the tests are not so hard. She gives sample quiz and you know how to review the knowledge learned in class. Further, you gotta participate in every lecture for 6 point

Deb is very inspiring and kind.  She's willing to help explain anything that you are confused on (which ends up being a lot) and cares about the students more than any professor I have ever had. That being said, the class is extremely confusing.  Nothing is clear and I didn't learn much.  Each 3.5 or above with minimal effort. I got a 4.0

I took this class just for the credits but ended up falling in love with oceanography. I changed my major because of this class and it had a lot to do with Deb's passion for the ocean and not just the class.

Deb means well and is a nice person. However,she should not teach this class. Lecture was the most boring part of my week and her TA's graded papers so harshly. Deb does offer a lot of extra credit, but good luck getting help with finding information! Do not take this class, unless you like  torturously boring material. Worst class I've ever taken.
Deb is such a wonderful person. She is so accomplished and down to earth. I really admire her.

"Debs" is a sweet person and professor, is extremely passionate about oceans and shows some beautiful footage of life underwater. Reasonable workload, some interesting guest speakers. Some lectures confusing/moved too fast and impossible to take notes on, which is unfortunate because you need thorough notes to write the 3 required abstracts.

This class was really boring.  Unless you absolutely love deep sea life don't take this class.  It was torture for me to go to class every week.  Grades consist of three quizzes, daily facts, and short written abstracts.  There is no text book which is nice.

Dr. Wu is really good! The exams aren't hard at all. You can use index cards, so as long as you study, you'll be fine. Just be aware that there's a big group project throughout the quarter during quiz section.

Dr. Wu is amazing! She goes really in depth with her explanations which is really nice. I can tell she really cares and wants her students to succeed. She also never really judged students for answering her questions incorrectly, and also made an effort to learn names. I would 1000% take a class with her again!
This class was one of the best courses I have taken at UW. Her approach to teaching the material is in-depth, well-organized, and straightforward. Plus you get notecards in exams!

I LOVE DR. WU. This class has a lot of writing, but it is super interesting, and she is super accommodating of student needs and preferences in the class. She is all around caring, sweet, and knowledgeable on the subjects she teaches. Her answers to your questions are also super good and promote further learning. Love her.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Wu is an amazing professor who made me excited to go to class. PSYCH 448: Close Relationships was such a fantastic and dynamic course overall! This was my first course with Dr. Wu, and I wish I had taken more of her classes before I graduated (I was a senior when I took this).

Dr. Wu's lectures were very informative! It's very clear she is passionate about her work and helping others succeed. There are a few readings every week to help understand lectures. You definitely need to internalize the information given in lecture but with the way the class and lectures are structured, you're pretty much set up for success.

Wonderful and passionate about her work. Multiple opportunities for extra credit. Connects textbook material nicely to lecture content. Canvas and lectures well-organized. Easy to talk to if you have any questions in office hours! Does include a quarter-long group project w/ presentation, but as long as you keep on top of the work you'll be okay!!

Incredible, kind, and passionate. Exams were generally simple, but study the lecture slides and understand the real-world applications of the concepts. The group poster project was the hardest part of the class, so find a good group and put in full effort. Tons of extra credit offered, and ability to retake missed portions of exams. I love her

This class wasn't necessarily difficult, but it takes a lot of effort to succeed. The grade is based on exams (passing certain learning objectives) and a group project. However, there are many extra credit opportunities, like attendance and homework assignments. I wouldn't recommend this class unless you want to be a PSYCH major.
She's such a great teacher, so kind and understanding.

loved Dr. Wu! the class structure is so different from other classes i have taken- so many opportunities to get a 4.0. i literally would've had above a 4.0 if it was possible because of my extra credit. only thing is she used norton inquizitive and i absolutely hated that program + it costs 30 dollars. Dr. Wu was 100% my favorite part of the class.

Psych 101 is graded very transparently and different from the courses I've taken before, you are given a google spread sheet to monitor your own grade throughout the quarter. The lectures are recorded, but I found I retained more by coming to class. Opportunities to make up for lost points, overall informative class. Quizzes are multiple choice.

Probably some of the best lectures I have ever had, formatted with notetaking in mind and very clear what information was most important. She also created an environment where no one was afraid to ask questions and always kept track of time. Probably one of the best professors I've ever had.
She's really nice! Go to her office hours!

Amazing professor, and a FANTASTIC lecturer. Grading scheme was interesting, but if you manage your participation and exam grades then it is not hard to stay on track to get a 4.0. Very accessible outside of class, and cares if students do well in her class. If you have the chance to take a class with Dr. Wu, I would highly recommend it
best professor I've ever had
LOVE

LOVE Dr. Wu. She clearly puts effort in making course content accessible to students and she really wants students to learn. Very approachable but also knowledgeable. Wants her students to get the most out of her class. Weekly homework assignments and lecture quizzes that are undemanding. 3 exams + 1 final with lowest dropped. Lectures are engaging

For being her first year of teaching, Professor Wu is AMAZING. Super easy class, funny professor, and interesting content. Easy to follow lectures. 3 relatively easy tests with chances to earn back half your lost points. Only issue was that grading criteria could be foggy, easily leading to deducted points from TA.

Dr. Wu is by far one of the best professors I've had here at UW. Was always accessible outside of class, and you can tell she really cares about her students. Great communication and attendance for lectures wasn't required, but I ended up going to almost every one anyways because lectures were always upbeat and interesting. Take her!

Fantastic professor!!! Her class is really interactive, and she cares every student in her class! She always try to remember everyone's name. She always ask each student whether they have understood the questions. The lecture pace is a little bit fast, but she is always willing to answer any questions!

Dr. Wu is very entertaining and engaging during lectures. She also makes it known that she cares about her students and wants them to succeed in her class. Overall, the class is not difficult as long as you complete the assignments, read the textbook, and attend lectures. Highly recommend taking a class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: First time teaching the course, was passionate about her lectures, very clear grading criteria, lots of homework, but has 2 grading plans.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Wu was great. Really great personality and really wants the students to succeed. Her lectures are basically everything she had in her tests. Would highly recommend her if you want to learn Psych. The papers were a little difficult, so approach TA's and her office hours for you to succeed.

Professor Porter loves the sound of her own voice. Her lectures are half common sense and half word vomit. There is almost no effort put into the lectures and assignments. All the tests are multiple-choice, but all of the questions are deeply subjective. Assignments are hard to understand, and she is hard to reach with no weekly office hours.

She literally grades so harshly. So hard to keep an A in this class. It's also so hard to understand her complicated language. The content of this class was nice but taught in a terrible manner. Do not take if you want a good GPA - this class will tank your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's amazing. She pushed me but it was worth it, just don't be afraid to ask questions and contact her directly!

Prof. Porter definitely is an eccentric character, it's clear she's passionate about what she does. It is difficult to understand what she is talking about most of the time during lecture. There is a lot of reading, but early-mid quarter reading assignments are relatively easy if you keep up.

She is an amazing woman and really nice to converse but my issue stems from how complicated her lectures get. It's really hard to follow her sometimes and I need to invest extra time to comprehend her language. Grading is really dependent on how explicitly you can connect topics and multiple quizzes for lecture. Overall, a hard yet nice lecturer!

Very unorganized lecture slides and vague rubric. Grading for presentations seem biased as well as her lectures. She expects you to actively listen to all her lectures and remember the information, then gives you five minutes to take a four question quiz. Do not take her.

Prof Porter's class was really eye-opening and special. She'll really spend time dissecting and discussing with you, the more you engage and ask the better it will go. Definitely take advantage of her outside class efforts- she puts a lot into each student, what you're willing to invest you get back 10 fold!

Prof. Porter's lectures are highly subjective and lack clear logic. She seems to promote a perspective that could be interpreted as historical nihilism. She's not a great listener either. Therefore, don't bother trying to discuss anything with her because she'll just shut you down harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Genuinely the worst teacher I've ever had. Other than the fact that she never puts clear guidelines for assignments and then gives harsh grades for not reading her mind, she is unreasonable and uncaring. Has made me cry multiple times, and has never cared about what I'm going through outside of class. If possible do not take any of her classes.

Her slides are very unorganized and hard to pay attention to (every slide is using different fonts and styles). She talks for 85 minutes, then you take a quiz right after that is open for 5 minutes. x/4pts, and one try. There are also 3 specific books you need, and there's presentations on movies. Very biased opinions given in the class.

professor porter is such an amazing professor. i honestly was not the biggest fan of her at the start, but she really grows on you. she gives extremely detailed feedback and will explain the assignment to you until you get it. shes definitely intense and loud but it just shows shes passionate.
Great professor.

Worst class I've taken at UW. Bad grading, poor course organization overall and really unclear expectations for assignments. Does not explain content or expectations well and then talks very derogatorily to students when they are confused. Despite putting lots of effort in, I feel like I learned nothing. Took a toll on my mental health for sure.
Doesn't have a clear guideline or rubric in terms of grading. Assignments and its instructions are very unorganized. Do not take this class.

Lectures were not posted anywhere else and 40% of the grades were based on a four multiple questions quiz right after class with only one attempt. You could only get good grades if you could guess her understanding on Asian culture correctly. She is friendly and responsive, but her lectures were dry.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Porter's class is an anxiety nightmare. The grading weight is 40% for quizzes, 25% for a meme project (yes, that kind of meme) and 35% for a multiple choice final. The quizzes are just a test of whether or not you can regurgitate the professor's personal opinion. Easy A if you can guess her opinion. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. She speaks like she's teaching Merriam Webster and each slide in her lecture is a 5 paragraph essay. Lectures aren't recorded; what she says doesn't match her slides. Directly after every lecture, there is a quiz that is either on what she said or what is on the slides. Good luck figuring out what you should take notes on.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The quizzes are 3 questions long, graded generously. Have to attend lectures to do well on quizzes! She expects you to read the books, but I never read them. They're mainly for the final project where you have to create 3 social media posts and use evidence from the books. I was worried for my grade at first but ended with 4.0. ATTEND EVERY LECTURE
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wanted o drop the class the first day. Whole grade is based off 14 quizzes (3 lowest quizzes get dropped), attending 3 workshop classes, and a final project. Ended the class with a 96% but was worried I'd get a lower grade when I first took the class. Have her look at every project because it'll help you get a good grade
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course description sounded really interesting but the class ended up being NOTHING like expected. I thought we were going to learn about collective trauma after war or terrorism but we ended up learning about how everyone is haunted by a ghost of their grandmas infidelity. The professor is nice but the class is definitely the worst class ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I loved her class. I took it over the summer and got a 3.9. She really knows what she is talking about and it was probably one of the most interesting classes I took at UW. She really works hard to make sure that you learn. All the important notes and information are on her slides so do NOT skip class, ever! And you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you attend her lectures you will know what you need to pass her tests. Her tests are based on her own interpretation of the events and civilizations, so you need to know her lecture material to pass.

The worst professor I have ever encountered. very not clear on what she wants out of the assignments, and grades you down if you don't get her expectations. a very strange setup of her "three sentences" practices and tests. Her tests are hard, long, and answers are usually very subjective. Her subjective grading is very frustrating.

Honestly I regret taking her class. Yes she is very knowledgeable when it comes to Chinese history. But her lack of knowledge and attention on other Asian cultures really bothers me. And keep in mind that She is very, very, very subjective. So wanna pass? Agree with her points. And beware that her tests are hard and she is a really tough grader.

Great class, the online structure is great and very easy to accomplish if you just read the instructions. There is additional Self-Quizzes that help your understanding but are not for credit, I have been taking them for a better grasp of the content for the course. I am worried how your  grade hinges on group project, only thing I'd change.

Unfortunately this class isn't what I expected. We have to watch 7 films, several of which are horror or psychological thrillers (not fun). Additionally she is very unclear and even changes what she wants for an assignment after the fact. She is also too involved in discussion forums. This class is for her interests and I'm finding it frustrating.

The class is all about learning about what the professor wants. It's very objective learning and you don't have room to create your own idea because she shuts you down. It's not fun. If you respect yourself do not take this class.

Don't take this class if you're expecting to learn more about Asian Civilizations--this class is purely of her own view and not the broader perspective. 23 of the quarter was spent practically comparing other countries to China (of which, they were "traumatized" by). The only thing I got out of this class were the texts she had us read.

Very enthusiastic, and interesting subject matter, but rather than cover the material in depth, students are given a cursory lecture on events and academically accepted views, and the rest of the time (80%) is spent trying to get us on board with her psycho-historical hypothesis. Thus, no room for student interpretation outside her fundamental view

This course needs lots of readings and needs to be prepared for each day of class. For Midterm and Final, you need to write almost five pages of the course materials. Very Hard. If you want to learn take this class, otherwise, its pretty tough class.

Deborah Porter is a wonderful teacher and person. Very knowledgable in the subject. She brings a lot of enthusiasm to the class. She has a penchant for comparing everything to China, because this is her area of expertise. However, this doesn't detract from the quality of her class. Speaking to her during office hours was very helpful.

Professor Porter was awesome!! She is so incredibly smart and is very enthusiastic about her research. She expects high quality work and sets her standards high so don't take this class if you don't want to take it seriously.

she is clearly intelligent and knowledgeable in her work. The movies are really fun to watch. The quizzes are pretty easy (you can google summaries and stuff) The first lecture about civilization/oracle bones was pretty interesting - but every lecture after that is BORING AS HELL! So those are the pros and cons :)

I think professor Porter is great. She really cares about being a good professor - making her less susceptible to other people's opinion in a sense; but than again she is a Princeton graduate. She speaks fluent Mandarin Chinese. I did not realize how smart she is untill I started talking to her in Chinese. Grammer construction ability = IQ. Voilà

Prof Porter's great!  Very enthusiastic and helpful!  Like all international studies classes, it will take lots of your own time and efforts to do well in the course, but she is one of the most helpful teachers I've had at the University.  During discussions she tends to go on tangents that can prevent other students from contributing, but it's ok!

Confusing with her requirements for the assignments.  We did watch a lot of great movies, but god only knows how they fit in with the class.  She was clearly reading from her own notes in her lectures which makes it really hard to follow her ideas.  Especially in the Yongjo period of Korea.  I'm still sorting out that dynasty.

This professor is extremely well organized and articulate in her lectures.  She really cares about being a great teacher.  It is also very clear that she is brilliant.  Don’t miss her class if you can help it.

didn't like how all sections are combined for tutorial, makes it hard to ask questions. clearly depies doesnt make the slides so hes lowkey confused/unprepared during tutorial. but hes truly truly a wholesome guy. he has funny (and slightly concerning) life stories that he relates to lecture content. anyways tutorial meh but lectures informative!

Very engaging and fun lectures; gives real-life examples and lots of practice. He actually remembers what it was like being an introductory physics student and actively tries to improve our experience. Go to his office hours! He talks about not just physics, but also just goes on random tangents, and everyone has a great time.
The exams are very fair there is more than enough prep to get you ready for them, lectures were great made physics easy to understand and has a good sense of humor.

Prof Depies was awesome!! I was genuinely excited to go to lecture which is not something i usually say. He was great at explaining concepts and his lectures were super engaging and funny. also super accessible outside of class, go to his office hours and ask questions--he wants you to do well!

Autumn of 2025: one of the best professors I have had at UW. Was very worried about doing well in this course but professor depies explained every concept from ground up, not proceeding until he was aware of everyones understanding, office hours were amazing (recommend) and lectures were perfect! Emphasized understanding over test taking skills

Very kind and funny professor who wants his students to learn and understand. Easy 100% in the 40% category of pre-lectures and clicker questions so mainly graded on the 60% category for exams which can have tricky questions. If you pay attention and practice the concepts, you'll succeed.
Very funny professor, heavy on blackboard lectures and cool demos, exams were straightforward

Professor DePies is extremely kind, caring, and genuine. He is able to explain every introduced concept thoroughly. He also establishes a clear premise of what it takes to succeed in this class and what the exam range would be as tests approach. Course itself is a little challenging and reading heavy, but put in some extra time and you'll be fine.

Unfortunately this professor is not capable of teaching content in a way that lands with students. His explanations only lead to more questions and use the class time is very poor. While the course content itself not very difficult, he manages to make it far more convoluted that it needs to be.

he's so fun and silly!! i don't even know if i'm gonna do well but his enthusiasm for teaching is so infectious. no homework, only exams, if you study you WILL do well; just make sure to use the previous exams on the physics department's official websites, the practice tests he gives are usually harder than the actual test. and do optional homework
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love him soooooo much especially for his new ideas on explaining the theory. Always takes some inspirational stuffs to class and do experiments himself or with a random volunteer. So funny and easy to keep up with. Exams are easier than the practice ones. Curving when the average is lower than 65.

Prof. Depies is one of the best professors I've had. His lectures are enthusiastic, chalk-board heavy and very interactive with students. He is very good at connecting concepts learned in the class so far with current concepts and preparing us for material to come. Homework is tough but graded only on completion and exams/quizzes are much easier

Professor DePies' lectures are incredibly engaging and interesting. He very clearly both cares about and enjoys physics and teaching physics to students. The way he structured the course as a whole was nothing short of exceptional, and despite being quiz/exam-heavy, the expectations were always reasonable and grading was generous.

I seriously thought I was gonna do terrible, I had never taken physics before and when it comes to math I'm historically not the best. But, this prof had engaging and informative lectures and just was a funny guy. While hoping for a 2.5 in this class I ended up with a 3.4! If you want to take physics for the first time, take it with Depies.

Professor Depies is amazing. You can really tell he cares about his students. He makes lectures engaging and makes teaching interesting. He really likes what he teaches. I'm excited to take him again for 225.

Never took physics in high school & was super scared for this class. Dr DePies is one of the best profs i've ever had & made it very clear what it takes to succeed. Great in lecture & easy to get a hold of outside of class. Helped me one on one several times and seemed like he cared about my success. Tests typically easier than practice questions.

Depies is great at lecturing and showing you how to solve certain problems. He doesn't care if the class gets a little behind schedule so it never feels rushed. He's pretty funny and goes on tangents but I found those were nice so that I could finish writing notes or just get a break from the math. Would and will take again!

He's a great person, caring, funny, and keeps the class engaged! However, lectures were unorganized and confusing. Doesn't use lecture slides and teaches via practice on chalkboard. Exams get significantly harder if the class meets the 65% average. I retook this class with another professor and the difference in exam difficulty was significant.

Dr. Depies is a genuinely hilarious dude, so lectures were always entertaining. You will be relying on the textbook, as many days lectures just consisted of him copying stuff straight from it without adding much extra to it. Days where we strayed from the book were the best. Quizzes and Exams were very fair, and he wants to see students do well.

Dr Depies was so great! Every lecture, everyone is quiet and engaged. You can tell he tries to get students interested in the class and does a great job of it! Physics is hard no matter what; the exams are challenging, but Dr Depies definitely makes it a doable class. Come to class 100% ready to listen and be engaged and you will succeed!
No complaints! There's a lot of work, but the way to learn physics is to just work on problems. Really funny in lectures, easy to follow along with, and gives us enough prep for his exams.

Prof. DePies is one of the most entertaining lecturers I've had. He's super funny and keeps class interesting with stories and engaging discussions. Lectures can be hard to follow if you don't come super prepared, but that's more the fault of the class than DePies. Homeworks are pretty tough, but quizzes and tests are manageable and fairly written.

One of my favorite professors at UW. There's a lot of reading, but it's more for preparation for the lecture than for learning. Exam content is challenging, but there's nothing on the exams that he doesn't thoroughly review in class beforehand. Would recommend, he gives funny and extremely helpful lectures.

I want to be completely honest. Physics is an enjoyable subject. The way he writes his tests feels like its only about reading comprehension instead of the actual physics content, which I think is really unfair, and not at all helpful to someone actually trying to learn the material. That could be a UW problem tho but still worth considering.

Great guy! Fun lectures & demonstrations, super caring, chalkboard-style. Not really in-depth during lectures (tbf it is an algebra based physics class lol). Pretty easy id say compared to my other classes, study a bit on your own time and you should be good. Utilise tutorials! 
Will take again, 10/10.

Professor Depies is ABSOLUTELY AMAZING!! I have taken physics before and this is by far the most effective and engaging physics course that I could have ever imagined. He teaches via blackboard and lists all of the topics covered in the lecture, which is very helpful. He is hilarious and takes the time to make sure that you understand the material.

Dr. Depies is very patient and encouraging. Lectures are recorded, but points are given to in-class participation. He uses blackboards so I'd recommend siting near the front. Exams are weighted heavily with little homework. Review sessions and practice exams were provided, but the actual exam is usually easier than the practice.

I am only 1/3 through the quarter, I don't usually rate professors because I don't have memorable experiences with them. But Professor Depies really is above and beyond. He's empathetic and kind. I never had a professor care and be so understanding and accommodating towards me. I really hope he gets everything he wants out of his life and more.

Funny prof during lectures, but not the best at teaching. Didn't really answer discussion board questions & lectures were taught via chalkboard rather than slides like the past two courses in the sequence?? Skipped a lot of practice questions or relevant material and explanations were sometimes confusing/not in depth.
He was very optimistic and supportive. Encouragement and positive reinforcement were always given after an exam. The workload is slightly heavy but the class was fun overall.

My absolute favorite professor I've had. His lectures were perfectly timed for me to learn all I needed to so I could avoid the textbook and just look up yt videos. He was incredibly passionate and had a fun physics experiment nearly every day. It was difficult, but fun since I'm biased for physics and math. Overall Depies was a perfect professor.

This course was very difficult no matter who the professor was. I do not believe our class was ever prepared for the exams, they were very difficult (averaged about 60%). The class is not curved which is a bummer because the majority of students did poorly on the exams and there is a LOT of homework. Prof. DePies is very kind but also disorganized.

Professor Depies is probably the best professor for 121. He cares about the physics and hates the software just as much as the students. He prefers teaching on the chalkboard, which is so much more helpful than just teaching out of the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: DePies sometimes glosses over things, but overall does a great job explaining topics and resolving common misconceptions. PHYS 121 itself is a hard weed-out class, but DePies does his best to make it more manageable and useful.

He made 90 minutes(I took it in summer 2022) of lecture very involving and fun! Will definitely get good grades if you attend to his lectures and write down what he emphasizes. Loved his lectures and I am glad I had him at least for the last physics class. Not sure if he'll ever read this, but just want to thank you so much, professor Depies!

I was really scared to take physics but Dr. DePies is a genuinely caring person who makes lecture entertaining with his funny examples and joking comments. He likes to give pep-talks and really makes sure everyone knows they aren't stupid for not knowing something. He's super approachable.
Do the homework AND as much of the practice as you can.
he's a good lecturer and makes taking physics less painful; def take him if you get the opportunity

Depies made physics enjoyable for me again, lectures were engaging and necessary for understanding content. Exams are fairly easy because he gives a practice that is almost identical to the test. Homeworks are difficult, but gives partial credit for trying. 10/10 great professor, just go to class and do the practice exams.

Physic is hard but depies explains in a good way and is very accessible to students. DONT SKIP CLASS, you will fall behind and every lecture builds on one another. He is very kind and understands that physics is hard. Don’t take any shortcuts in his class and you will do well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: DePies is a funny, intelligent professor who teaches class in a easy-to-follow way. He is very experienced and knows his stuff. He is stern when need be and caring and funny otherwise. He is flexible and understands that physics majors are usually stressed to the max. He genuinely cares for your grade and wellbeing and it shows. Take his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He sometimes cancels class but is very fair in what he puts on the exam. Only problem is that the multiple choice is each worth 5-6.5 points which could plummet your grade easily. Luckily he curves. Overall, this class isnt so bad as long as you go to office hours.

Dr. Depies is a very enthusiastic professor. He is very passionate about physics and making sure everyone understands. He has office hours and is always available to help clarify the material to you when needed. He did cancel class a couple times during the quarter, but if he doesn't get to a topic in class he's not going to ask it on the exam.

Dr. Depies- favorite teacher I've had at UWS and UWB. He cares, he's super helpful, simplifies tough stuff, fair as can be. He makes physics understandable to those who don't understand physics (me). Goes slow, but he wants us to UNDERSTAND. He understands we are not physics majors.

Dr. Depies is hilarious and knows how to connect with his class. Would not recommend taking if you intend on texting during class or show up late because it is easy to get on his bad side if you do that. He grades on a curve so even if you do "bad" on an exam you may not do bad in the class. Every day of class he brings energy and passion!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: An approachable professor that uses sarcastic humor to connect with his students. He makes himself available to students who ask for help. His passion for physics and teaching is evident in his lectures. His exams are based on material covered in class. Attendance is not mandatory, but if you miss a class, he will email you to make sure you are OK.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Overall, he was a good professor. He basically gives you the layout during lectures but it is up to you to practice hw and read. My first physics quarter, I did an average of 75 percent on the exams. This quarter I improved significantly . I just got 90 % on my first exam. I gotten more used to the physics concept and I'm also reading the book.

By far the worst professor I have ever had. Does not care one bit about students succeeding and you can tell that he could care less about teaching. Barely replies to emails, and if you can't make his office hours because of another class, he won't care and might "try" to help you if you can make it while he is at school and not busy.

I left this class knowing just as much physics as when I came in. Everyone was failing his exams (Average was a 60 pretty much the entire quarter) so he gave the best curve I have ever seen (probably to save his own butt). I failed majority of the exams, did homework and ended up with a 3.0. Cant complain for now but need to self teach for MCAT.

Attend lecture (pay attention), do the hw, ask questions, and give thought to what you're asked in class. Dr. DePies is one of the best professors I've had at UW. His lectures are engaging and actually feel like he's talking to you, not at you. His expectations are clear and class is well organized. Use of chalk over tech was much less distracting.

Physics has brought us so many technological advances that it floors me how most physics profs insist on writing with chalk. Depies tends to scribble and talk fast and doesn't utilize screencasts or lecture slides...which makes it very difficult to follow along. That being said, he's still about the best you can get from a physics professor at UW.

The worst prof ever. Does not understand student problems, exams different than HW, if you took physics before might be easy, overall I would not recommend taking him. When you ask him a question, he becomes mad, and does not explain well.

Worst professor I've taken ever. Although he seems very knowledgeable in Physics. He is not organized, clear, & very biased towards certain students. I want to give him the benefit of doubt & say that this is his first Astronomy class he's taught but still... not a very pleasant experience learning or helpful. Won't be taking his class ever again.
He is a funny professor, the class isn't that hard. Showing up to class is important because of the lectures he gives. He makes you feel like you don't know what you're talking about!

He is a really fun person and I love talking to him outside of class, but his lectures are so difficult to follow. He goes over concepts quickly and he gets irritated when no one answers questions he asks to the class. I wish he would go over concepts in class that are useful for the homework or for exams. Find a study group outside of class!!
This is a relatively demanding course, but you couldn't ask for a better professor.

A great teacher. He knows how to teach and knows physics very well. I was not at all looking forward to taking physics but he made me actually like the subject. I recommend studying the book, especially chapter problems, for the exams and for use on the cheat sheet. Ace the homework and you will be fine!
Enthusiastic and knows what he is talking about.  Do the homework and ask questions and you will be fine!  Prof. Depies changed my perspective about physics!
Best Physics teacher I had so far at UW. Very clear lectures and expectations. Exams weren't too hard and was mainly focused  on concepts.

Take advantage of office hours!He's generous with his time,and helpful.His exams are fair, and you know what to expect from him by the end of the series.He's so enthusiastic,it's hard not to like his classes.Ace the homework!Make sure to attend lectures so you don't miss his explanations or clicker pts.Be respectful and you'll all enjoy the class.
Great at giving lectures... Has favorites... Will call you out if you are a distraction

Prof Depies ("Matt") is an AMAZING lecturer, I learned a LOT and he made it painless.  You *have* to go to class though, because he doesn't publish notes or videos online.  All the conceptual questions on exams were straight out of lecture examples.  He's friendly and approachable, but DON'T let him catch you texting, he WILL call you out.

Professor began as friendly and funny. First few weeks were clear and helpful. Towards the middle of the quarter he begins section on relativity and focuses all class time on it (he says most profs don't cover it since it's not useful). He's irritable when students don't understand concepts and stops class to point you out if he hears any noise.

Very good professor, he's especially funny during office hours. He's helpful and cares about his students. The only thing I can complain about is that his lectures don't match with his tests. Some of the questions are just plain stupid. But other than, he's a good lecturer!
awesome lectures, was very clear about content needed to known to succeed in class

Prof. Depies was one of my favorite professors ever at the UW. His lectures were always interesting and he does a really good job of explaining difficult concepts. His tests were pretty easy, so the averages are a little higher than normal. I wish he taught higher physics classes because I'd definitely take another class with him.

He is such a good teacher I never once was uninterested in lecture. He interacts with the class in lecture so you don't fall asleep. His tests are prettysimple except his written part that's always hard. He is also a little condecending bit overall best physics teacher I've had and one of the best teachers in general I've had. Office hours are really helpful.

Had a tough time explaining tough concepts multiple ways. It was strange because he could not understand why someone would have trouble with the topic of relativity. Has issues with respecting great scientists.

He very obviously did not want to teach this class. His manner of teaching those in the liberal arts class is condescending and demeaning. The slightest hint of noise in lecture and he would freak out. His immaturity made me feel like I was back in high school again. Hopefully he's better with normal physics, but he shouldn't teach this class again

Greatest physics professor I've had at UW! Matt's lectures are very interesting, makes everything very clear, and very good at answer clarifying question, also very approachable and helpful when I had homework questions. His tests are very fair (gives lots of hints in lecture, and a lot of partial credit- attend lecture and you will do fine!
Enthusiastic and entertaining!

He is the best prof. I've ever had! He really cares about the well being of his students and makes time when you need to see him. lectures are helpful and exams are easy and relative to material covered in class. do not hesitate to take his class, you wont regret it! [=

Never liked physics, but this professor made it fun. Very approachable and helpful. Exams were very easy (if you go to class before the exam). I think he just received his PhD and he teaches physics in a new, 'modern' way. Take him for sure!

I took physics and calc with matt.  I would have to say that is the funnest teacher i have ever taken. Applying everything to astronomy. I would agree with one of the prior posters, He is way to smart sometimes in his lectures and doesnt realize that the class isnt on the same page
A nice guy, approachable.  He uses many good examples, but you still need to pay attention if you want to understand.

He definitely cares a lot about whether students learn. I think he's so smart though that in lecture he doesn't understand that some things aren't as obvious to us as they are to him. Maybe he is better one on one. A very nice guy.
Matt is the best teacher I've ever met.  He is a smart, articulate person who can construct a triple strand concertina barrier like nobody I've ever seen.
Took him for summer, he's VERY HELPFUL! very clear in explanation, patient in teaching weaker students. Easily one of the best teachers I ever had. got 4.0 in the class. :)
Very personable and is truly interested in the student learning.  He is the only professor I have had so far that knew my name in a class of a hundred students.  Great teacher!!

Attending lectures and doing the practice exams are the keys to success in the class (it got me a 4.0). Clicker points are an easy way to cushion your GPA. He's a nice guy who focuses on understanding concepts and seems to actually care about your success in the class, always encouraging you to visit him in his office if you need help.

He's very fast on teaching the material, tends to prove a lot of the concepts and expects everybody to do the same.  But as long as you attend his lecture, you should be fine on the tests.  Also, he uses clicker a lot, getting 70 percent of the clicker points will add .2 final grade, .1 for pretty much just showing up.  Tests could be a little toug
All in all very good. Uses the clicker too much though which is a disruptive waste of valuable lecture time.
Usually clear about the material, always friendly, seems interested in teaching concepts rather than just what's in the book.

Very good professor. His lectures are interesting and he covers the material well. He is very enthusiastic and cares a lot about his students. The class itself is difficult, but he gave our class a high average.
I love her! She's an amazing professor
she lectures wih a teleprompter and writes things out while explaining them. Very easy to understand and gives you the resources to do suff on your own. One of the best lecturers ive had.
Professor Debbie is the BEST PROFESSOR at UW. I LOVE HER CLASS, wish she could open more classes. MAKE me love stats. SHE IS AWESOME!!!! explains everything so well, so nice and kind
A great approach to teaching statistics, and a reasonable set of expectations, content, and lecture style that helps you use this course as a resource in later work.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I had Debbie for 317 and now 318. She is the best professor I've had at this school and helped me realize that statistics is one of my greatest passions. Go to lecture and quiz section and you will be beyond set for exams.

Debbie is so, so sweet and takes her time making sure that her students understand the content. She handwrites all her lectures so that her class operates at the same pace of someone that is taking notes and has open-note exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I LOVE DEBBIE! She is one of the best professors at UW and you can tell she genuinely cares so much about teaching and her students.The BS seems scary because of stats but Debbie makes it all so much easier to understand! She will always stay after class to answer questions and will literally be awake at 2am answering questions on ed discussions.
teaches material really well and is super nice during office hours or asking for an extension on a homework

Although I was really scared about my grade being 85% exams for this class, it was genuinely a breeze. Debbie is an icon, super funny, and has a unique teaching style that allows you to understand the content and enjoy going to lecture. I can't wait to have her again next quarter for 318!

Debbie Paulsen I am such a huge fan. There are few words to describe how iconic and amazing this woman is. I love Dr. Paulsen, she is a fantastic (and hilarious) lecturer who does a phenomenal job of explaining concepts and preparing students for exams. The structure of the class is easy to follow and I feel like I've actually been learning.

Debbie Paulsen is a wonderful professor. She is thorough and clear in her lectures, writing all of the notes on paper and projecting that. If you copy what she writes and important things she says (she makes clear what is important), exams (open note) are exactly what you expect. (same for psych 317)
genuinely a great teacher

I ABSOLUTELY ADORED DR. PAULSEN!!! I had her for Psych 318, after taking 317 with Laura Little, and my grade and attitude towards stats in general grew so much with Dr. Paulsens teaching. This is my first time leaving a review, but I really just wanted to share what an awesome, caring, and funny teaching she is!!

Loveeee Debbie! I came here to write a review because I forgot to do the course evaluation and want her to get credit for being an awesome teacher. She makes non-intuitive concepts approachable and is humorous, too. I also appreciate that she cares about us actually understanding what is going on in the formulas. Definitely recommend her class!

Great teacher! She was very clear and always willing to help out. She makes sure students really understand the content. I was nervous going into it because I was never good at stats but she made this class a lot easier. Also all lectures are recorded and lowest exam score gets dropped

Debbie is a fantastic and highly approachable professor. She makes her content ever so clear and goes over all the materials in class before each exam so there're no surprises. There are four exams plus a final, so five in total but you can drop the lowest one.

Debbie is literally the angel for stats and is super approachable. She is super helpful and really cares her students. If you have questions about class, go to her. Stuck on questions? Go to her! Problem with homework? Go to her! Definitely attend office hour! She loves what she teaches and can give you tons of examples until you understand.

A true gem. Learned a lot from paired or block designs, factorial ANOVA, Chi-square tests, and multiple comparison procedures. There were five exams and a final about designs identification & all were within reasonable difficulty. TAs were very helpful with HWs. Her lecture pace was easy to follow and prepared us well for the exam, very predictable

This is not a typically challenging course given you had previous exposure to AP level stats courses. Professor wrote detailed notes in lecture via slow yet deliberate fashion. 5 exams consisted of 85% of total grade but were reasonably hard save elusive wording can trick you occasionally. Generally, very accessible & reasonable instructor.

prof. debbie is amazing! she's a very great lecturer. the lecture pace is great (not too slow and not too fast). her teaching team is very attentive too. the exam questions difficulty are reasonable and usually it's from her lecture so pay attention to her lectures.

She's very humorous! 5 exams, no final. Assignments due fridays but sometimes 1 more. Quiz section is vital for learning the application of the knowledge. But lectures are important for foundation, as lectures teach definitions/concepts that are tested in the few mc questions on the exam and her examples that are similar to that of exam questions.

Debbie was one of the most passionate professors Ive ever had at UW. She was good at giving examples and showing you each step to solve a difficult problem. Her practice exams were in the same format as the actual exams, and the difficulty was similar too. Highly recommend taking Psych 318 with her (317 too.)

I learned I wasn't as good at probability as I thought I was. Debbie was a fantastic teacher in 317 and 318; she took the time to explain the theory and not just show examples. She made us laugh at times. She is a caring person who cares about her students. Tough classes though!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Debbie is a good professor. Its pretty difficult to get a 3.5+ in the class since is it so test heavy and every point matters but most of the material is not hard to understand. Had her both in person and online and can say she taught well and cared for her students a lot in both environments.

Debbie is a fantastic professor. Her lectures were comprehensive without being exhaustive, and her grading criteria was clear. She's willing to help with homework during her office hours and is easily accessible outside of class. She's clearly knowledgeable and experienced in her field. She's caring and wants to see her student do well.

For the first time in my life, I understand statistics. I expected this class to be dry and the content to be hard to digest, but Debbie is clear and concise when explaining the concepts. She also writes notes down during the lecture which is wonderful because you are able to keep up with the lecture while taking notes. She's the best!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: LOVE DEBBIE!! One of the best instructor at UW. The course is not particularly easy, but it's not hard either. She tried to make everything straight forward. She's super caring and nice. Very approachable outside of class. Truly care about her students.

Santosh is a great lecturer, he gets a 4 because his notes are pretty poorly organized, but he tries to connect what he's teaching to the real world at all times and all the content in his class seems directly useful. His homeworks and tests are fair, I didn't do very well in them but they were fair

Devasia is a pretty cool guy but his lectures are fairly useless in the context of the class- any understanding I have gained from this course is just from reading and re-reading textbook sections. In addition, homework is poorly connected to the lectures and exams are even further disconnected from the whole class.
Vibrations with Devasia was difficult, but I learned a ton and the topic really resonated with me.

Vinod was adored by a lot of my peers; he clearly cares a lot about student success! He's very accessible outside of class and will give you very detailed explanations even if you email at odd hours. He's a good lecturer and his accent is easy to understand. Office hours are even more helpful! Tests are an okay difficulty and are weighed fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Vinod is excellent at teaching Econ 200 subject matter. If you want an interactive learning environment in a classroom instead of Kane and want to learn the subject matter, you should take his class. He gives individualized feedback on every homework and his lectures are exceptionally organized. He provides you with everything you need to excel.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Vinod is very helpful and accessible. Even though his accents is hard to understand sometimes, he did a good job to clarify(but remember to ask during class so that you can get participation points). I would say his grading is strict but you should be okay as long as you follow the lecture and do the worksheets.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I would say he is one of the greatest teachers in UW! He's really responsible and helpful! Every time I got stuck , he would give fast and efficient feedback! Highly recommend for sure.

Very long lectures aren't his fault, but he can be hard to understand and frustrating to listen to for 2 hours straight. Lots of quizzes with tough grading and while I felt confident going into midterms and the final I still got a bad grade. If possible, just take the big lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Vinod is a good professor, especially for a grad student. His lectures can be confusing as individual practice problems get expanded, but he still teaches the material effectively. His tests are very challenging, as they are all written answer questions (no multiple choice), but he offers lots of office hours and is good at clearing up confusion.

Dr Dhavan gives incredible lectures with a deep historiographical analysis of the subject, including critiques of the assumptions made by the textbook. She has high expectations for her class but is very willing to help her students reach those expectations.

As someone of south asian origin, this class gave me a whole different perspective on my own cultural history. Taking a class with Prof. Dhavan will be invaluable and one of the highlights of your college classes. I cannot recommend her enough. You won't regret it :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Dhavan is a great teacher. She's supportive and gives good feedback. The lectures are long, so be sure to take notes. If you feel like you're falling behind, start going to her office hours. She's accessible outside of class and via email, and a good conversation with her will go a long way in how you structure your essays.

Professor Dhavan is a very knowledgeable, engaging speaker and frames her lectures in a clear sequence. She always made it clear to students that she was available outside of class for help with writing assignments and offered good feedback on your work. Would recommend this course for learning through a nuanced perspective on global history.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Assigns a lot of readings, really critical on paper assignments, requires participation in class. If you blink she'll put you on the spot to answer and she expects that her class is the top priority. The papers don't look difficult on the surface but they require tons of research and she expects you to be very detailed yet concise in submissions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far my favorite professor. Incredibly disciplined, hardworking, compassionate, and articulate. I learned so much during this course and had a blast doing it. Be adventurous with the role-playing game, ask questions, finish your essays early and GET HER FEEDBACK (it's priceless). 10/10

Can't recommend Professor Dhavan enough she is so caring! Class can be fast-paced and a lot of writing but just talk to her she is understanding and helpful. She wants you to succeed which is so rare, also gives detailed feedback if you're looking to improve. I love her lecture style so much I took another class with her the following quarter.

Amazing!! Her lectures were fascinating and the readings tied into the content really well. It's an automatic W credit and you only write 3 papers, which are weighted differently based on the grade you receive. She does take attendance, but participation is self graded. Overall, excellent class and she was a phenomenal lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Dhavan is one of my favorite professors. Her lectures were very interesting and engaging and I really enjoyed them. The readings are long but fully doable. A lot of the work given is in the form of writing assignments, but she gives a lot of support to students during the process. She is very willing to help students outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Hands down the best history course possibly one of the best I've taken across the board, and it's all thanks to Prof. Dhavan. Many people felt she had given the most feedback they had ever received on a paper, and it was all effective and meaningful. Lecture is always engaging. Only had 2 exams, 2 essays, and participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor who really cares about the topics at hand. She is very accommodating in terms of assignment/provides feedback for essays before theyre due. A LOT of complex readings, and the class is quite heavy on historiography (how you study/look at primary sources). As someone who is not used to learning about SA history, quite challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Dhavan is a gem. Any class by her will be a highlight of your academic experience. She expects a lot, but she gives even more in return in the form of thoughtful primary source selection, explanation, and personalized feedback. There is a lot of reading, but never any "busy work". You will use everything you read for class.

Dhavan gave interesting lectures and incredible feedback. She was always available and made sure that you understood the material well and had all of the necessary information to succeed in your class. Not to mention that she was incredibly lenient with deadlines and due dates. She was a fantastic professor, 11/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: First off, I want to say Professor Dhavan is an amazing professor. She cares for her students, and it shows. I had a hard time in 2020, and she was very relaxing with extending deadlines every so often. She gives amazing lectures on South Asian history, responds to emails fast, and overall is an amazing teacher.

(Taken online during COVID) I took her class Spring 2020 and honestly it's been one of the best classes I've taken. Lectures are engaging and she really leads you through the topics. She offers extra feedback for anyone who asks outside of class before final drafts are due. So even as a mediocre writer, I was able to get high grades on every paper.

Prof. Dhavan was great! I took her class in Fall 2019. While the essays seem difficult at first, she gives plenty of feedback at office hours for all of your drafts. She passed out lecture notes at the beginning of every class, which was super helpful for concrete information. Her lectures were very engaging and I felt like I learned a lot.

Disclaimer: This was an online class during COVID This is the first history class I've been truly disappointed by. Purnima's lecture style feels like she's just reciting lists of facts out of a textbook. The grading criteria for the papers is rigid and use of outside sources is discouraged which is ridiculous for a class on such a broad topic.

(Taken online during COVID) There will be a lot of readings in this class from not only the textbook but also from outside articles, journals and excerpts. All of them are really needed for the short papers you write along with lectures/podcasts. If you're looking to take this for W, DIV and I&S, it's an alternative to PSYCH210 but there'll be work

Professor Dhavan's lectures are really good at holding your attention, especially with how animated she will get. If you decide to take notes by hand, it's a lot easier to do it on the lecture notes she hands out so you don't write duplicates (as lecture notes are her slides). There are four major assignments and meeting with her will help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Dhavan knows her stuff, but she is not a good communicator of the knowledge she has. She gives round about responses and has little idea on how to engage an undergraduate audience. Her speech pattern is also both very fast and difficult to understand at times.
