At first I felt that the expectations were too high and the class work was taking a lot of time from me (especially cause I'm not a history major). However, it was doable. I'm actually really glad I took this because it solidified my writing skills and increased my appreciation for history. She definitely has high expectations but she really cares.

This was my first course taken at the UW from community college and it felt like a lot of work (and it is a lot of work for a 200 level class) but she was wonderful at providing extra help when I needed it. Hilarious, upbeat, and whimsical. Her lectures contain a lot of information and she moves quickly so if you write your notes be fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took Dr Dhavan's class for my first quarter at UW last year. She is a good professor and cares about how you did and get out of the class. However, her class is not easy, you will read  a lot of primary sources in her class and have 2 essays as well as a midterm and final. However, you are allowed to use a one page note for both of your exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you send her a paper before it's due, she will give thorough comments on how to improve it, is very clear on what she wants, and even though her lectures are 2 hours, I enjoy them if I'm not exhausted.

The best and most lyrical and energetic lecturer in possibly the whole world. Makes sure students are engaging with recent scholarship and debates about historiography and challenges you to make original historical interventions. Emphasizes class issues, the complexity of religious conflict, gender. Very smart and serious but approachable, kind!

Brutal, covered a lot at top speed (even she admitted it's more like a grad class)--and funny as hell. "Now that the sultan was dead, everyone got along like one big, happy family, yes? Of course not! His successor killed his uncle and blinded his brother," she says, chipper & smiling.  Loved her. All original source readings, hard going.
Great instructor and compassionate individual who truly cares about her students. That being said, her courses are tough and require dedication - in other words, lots of quality work.

She is extremely passionate and actually cares about how you do in her class. But do NOT take unless you are really into South Asian history.  If you need a writing credit this is a good class.  You can write two 7 pg papers (vs the mandatory two 5 pg papers).
nice and energetic professor, but her grading us brutal and strict. the class contains lots of dense and dull reading.

She is a very good teacher.  Of all the teachers at UW, she's the one who actually cares about what you get out of the class, and How you do in the class. I thought she was awesome. She is lenient on grading, and lectures are engaging. I would love to take her again.

Excellent professor!  She knows everything there is to know about south Asian history; her lectures are dense but well-organized, and she is a very engaging speaker.  She has clear expectations, and is always happy to answer questions.  I had very little interest in this region prior to the course, but she manages to make the topic fascinating!
Professor Sanabandu does not give the best lecture but he personally is an easy-going and helpful instructor and the course contents were pretty clear with flexible course pace and rules.
Lecture are well taught and clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
Least enjoyable EE class I have ever taken--probably mostly due to the content, but Sahabandu was not helping. Lectures were poorly paced, his work often had mistakes, and course policies kept changing.

That said, he clearly cares a lot and will try to help you succeed. I have full faith that he'll become a better prof, but he's not there yet IMO.
Really goated professor, always available. Did really bad because of personal matter but can't recommend him more than enough

Bro knows how to teach. He goes at a very good pace knowing that the subject is not easy, connects class principle to how they are used in engineers. Very active on discord, will answer any question you have promptly. Gives a ton of resources to practice for midterms and finals. Holds online review sessions for even more practice and clarification.

Goated first year professor. he cares about the student so much that he does problem reviews for homework and exams outside of class every week. is not a harsh grader. available all ways on discord even lat at night.

He has unclear expectations and high expectations. The class had a lot of work weekly for being a 1 credit pass/fail. Honestly the worst professor I have ever encountered and I strongly recommend you take a class from literally anyone else. He didnt grade anything until 2 days before the quarter ended which makes it hard to know where you stand.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There were many mixed reviews about this professor, so I started the course with an open mind. However, for a course that is completely online and you engage with him maybe twice, he is a strict grader with little to no guidelines on what he wants from his students. Awful communicator. Would not recommend this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very rude professor. Big ego. Do not waste your time.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Proceed this professor with caution.

It's an easy to pass class with minimal effort work, but if you're not ready to deal with conflicting  & confusing messaging of class instructions, having mandatory weekend (Friday night, Saturday morning) meetings, and dealing with a professor who's ego is larger than your tuition...

Don't take this class.

This is a one credit class, yet the amount of required work for the group project is substantial to a 3 credit class. Furthermore, Diggs-Yang's canvas is disorganized. You can only access the pre-lecture materials for the week from an email, because he doesn't update the actual website. Would never take this class if it wasn't required for ELS.

Very picky about how students work in a completely student led class. Complained that we did too much work for our group presentation. Lowered the maximums each time we communicated with him, despite the syllabus stating otherwise. It is absurd how an College of Ed professor doesn't have a clear syllabus and activly discourages student involvment.
Different compared to my other classes, but in a good way. Genuinely cares.

Dr. Diggs was very helpful and caring. He let me join the class late and made sure that I was included in the group. Easy to talk to, felt comfortable talking with him. I totally recommend him, just show up to class it's that easy to get an A.

This class was interesting. We made videos on education topics, and we discussed them on Canvas. It was pretty cool to see how the other groups made their videos. Other than the week we presented the rest of the class was pretty chill. It was different, but I learned a lot. Dr. Diggs-Yang was helpful but sends lots of emails.

Pretty easy class, but he was so rude. Had to do a group meeting with him and my group did not show up so he yelled at me saying it was my fault. I was supposed to know why they were not there. Also, did not grade anything until after the quarter was over. Gave feedback that I should have done more, but never communicated that until afterwards.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sucks that EDUC 280 is required to get into ECO because honestly, Professor Diggs-Yang is pretty tough. He is honestly not as caring as the other EDUC professors around here and is OK at best. He is pretty critical of your work and what you say... You can expect to pass if you do the work but he is a critical grader so it won't be a 4.0.

I don't feel like I learned a single thing all quarter. All of the materials were unorganized and outdated, and assignments were unclear. There was too much written work that felt like it was just assigned to keep us busy. The prof was unhelpful and didn't respond to any of my emails. It's a required ECO class that's the only reason to take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Greg was very disorganized. All of his lecture slides were from quarters past, all assignment due dates on canvas were unclear/also from quarters past, lectures to be watched before class were posted all over the place, and as opposed to most of my discussion-based classes, I feel like I literally learned nothing this quarter. :(
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Diggs is so kind and relatable!! He makes such an effort to get to know his students and to check in on our lives and how we're feeling. Definitely take his class to learn from a thoughtful professor!

I would only take 280 with Diggs-Yang. The updated syllabus was not posted for a majority of the quarter. The grading scale got posted week 10 of the quarter. Hard to get in touch with and overall disorganized.

I dropped this class after three weeks because of the amount of unprofessional encounters I had with him. Went to my advisor as a result of him not being approachable and being defensive when you do bring a concern; now the dean of that college is involved. Didn't teach anything because class was asynch group work DURING A PANDEMIC
He is fine, but somewhat unhelpful and unclear when explaining things.

Had him for EDUC 310 in person last year. He comes off as an understanding guy but when it comes to grading or accommodations he is strict. He definitely had favorites in his class in person. When grading my final for online EDUC 299 the only comment he left was that he didn't like it but gave full points.
I'd recommend him for 280 but not for anything else. There are papers and hes unclear, just follow the rubric. Come to class. It's simple
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Ive never rated a professor before, and at first he seems really cool, but the way he acted when I told him Id have to leave early one day, and then how he continued to tell me the only way hed let me make up partial points, in a way that I told him conflicted with my anxiety, not that he cared, made me drop the class 1.5 weeks in.

Greg is great. Took his EDUC 310 class on Identity Development Theory. He is very passionate and insightful about what he teaches. Will answer questions and is really nice and accommodating! He really cares about the wellbeing and mental health of his students. Also has funny stories. Encourages you to explore identity and how it affects all of us.

TERRIBLE. His syllabus is not up to date, he doesnt even know when things are due! His rubric on canvas is different from what he says in class. His expectations are unclear. He reads off the PowerPoint word for word. This two hour class has no break in the middle. The only plus is that he replies to emails quickly (within a day). Never again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Diggs was truly awful. He is not accommodating at all, and very hard to get in touch with outside of and inside class. Truly not sure why he is a teacher, as he does not care about the students at all. This had the potential to be a great class, the information was very valuable and interesting. However, Diggs ruined it.
Ben is awesome. He's a great professor and knows a lot and does what he does best (which is GIS)

Class mostly graded on labs w/ attendance on poll everywhere & 20% final. Wording/grading on final wasn't the clearest bc it was the only test in class. Most/all grading is by TAs. Dittbrenner mentioned using ChatGPT for a lab guide once when a mistake was found in it but is otherwise a solid lecturer, passionate about beavers, & generally affable

The class time was very valuable. Ben was very good at explaining concepts and processes in a way that everyone could understand and when there were people having problems he was always able to help them work through it, whatever the issue. Ben also did a great job at making ArcGIS exciting.

~60% of required ALEKS homework wasn't taught in class or tested on.  I took HS chem 5 years ago & lectures felt excruciatingly slow – maybe a good pace w/ 0 chem knowledge. Tests are fairly graded & Storfer seems very kind & passionate. 110 is definitely worth taking if you need a chem refresher but can basically be self-taught to little detriment

Exams are ez she gives previous exams that are exactly like the exams she gives. As long as your doing the wkshts she gives out/prac the prev exams you will 4.0 the class. Aleks questions don't show up on the tests so don't waste your time practicing those cause theyre super tedious, material is easy to teach urself if you dont understand lecture

I lowkey feel bad writing this because she is very nice and definitely cares about chem, but her lectures are soooo bad. I got an A in the class, but that's only because I had to teach MYSELF everything. She didn't have clear slides or anything to go over and would basically just yap about chem for an hour and go on hella useless tangents.
explained things in a way I understand

This professor made me love chemistry, which is saying a lot because I am a way more "right brained" person. Her lectures were super clear and I loved how she made everything build on itself throughout the quarter. She made chem feel exciting and accessible for anyone to learn. Take chem 110 with her if you can!!

Professor Storfer is a good person, just a terrible teacher. She as an accent which makes everything so much harder to understand. Despite this, if you are going to take 142, take this class first. Her lectures are useless and the textbook is bad(don't buy it), but make sure you go to each test review lecture. 
Tests are wayway easier than the hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's very very sweet, but her lectures were pointless. I ended up teaching myself the material through the textbooks, and skipped the lecutres all together, as they went painfully slow. Most ALEKS questions didn't even apply to the midterms and tests. Luckily for me personally- the tests/midterms were a breeze.

HW on aleks is completely irrelevant to whats being done in class. Lectures can be somewhat confusing, and you should probably read the textbook or work with your ta in office hours. She does usually do a short review of the previous lectures material though, so thats nice if you miss a day
She made me love chem!!! her teaching style is at a perfect pace.

Prof. Storfer is an extremely kind professor who obviously loves the subject she teaches. However, her lectures are very difficult to understand. You're better off just reading the textbook. The homework is also completely uneccessary, has either nothing to do with the test material or harder than it, and takes hours to complete.

She's a kind person, but very hard to understand and her lectures are very slow. She assigns work in ALEKS that doesn't relate to the class/she never teaches, and sometimes puts trick questions on the exams. She doesn't use slides, so you have to pay attention to every word she says, despite the challenges I mentioned. She doesn't answer questions.

Honestly she's chill, gets a lot of hate from what I've seen in the other ratings. If you show up and are respectful she also is. This was my 2nd ever plant class and it was honestly completely reasonable for a 5 credit class. There is a lot of reading, but this is a 400 level class, so like you know what you're signing up for lol.

Took her for BIOL442, horrible teacher, not accommodating, rude and passive-aggressive towards students. Confusing, disjointed lectures. Quizzes are made to trip you up, with lots of "half-correct" answer options. I came into this class with prior experience with plant biology, but she expects you to know as much as a grad student. Don't take.

I would not wish my worst enemy to take a class taught by distillio. I have sufficient background in plants and evolution and was still constantly in a state of confusion throughout the course. She was condescending, expected graduate level understanding of plant genetics and graded harshly. For the sake of your mental health, do not take this
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is okay. Her lectures are really dense and usually disorganized. She cares a lot about plant biology, though, she tends to forget that most people taking her class have 0 knowledge of plants. That being said, she can seem condescending because she expects a lot out of students.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One word horrible! She messes up on grading and has to fix it afterward. Her canvas course is disorganized as are her lectures. She is not good at explaining the content. Her panapto recordings are muffled and hard to understand. It's a complete nightmare. Do not take this course. This is coming from a student that consistently gets great grades
She did a great job and is very knowledgeable about plat biology and development. Would take again.

Classes are boring, and has quizzes at the end of every lab that have nothing to do with the lab, just your ability to remember something random from a prior lecture. Tests don't test your knowledge of the class because the questions are so specific that if you miss that question your entire test score is doomed
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: she's seriously so smart...... this class was really hard and a lot of work but if you work hard you will get a good grade. two non cumulative tests and clicker quizzes. tests are pretty fair. I learned so much about plant biology

Super easy exams, just be ready for a lot of writing, they're long. Questions come straight from lecture and she asks questions that you wouldn't be able to get from reading the book. Not super helpful during review sessions and not the most interesting professor, but she was alright.
Easiest. Tests. Ever. That are not graded insanely harshly, unlike those of other professors. Just pay attention in lecture. She's very nice, but I do remember falling asleep quite a bit in class.
This class was very difficult. I only got a 2.1 cuz I did not understand the exam format and wasn't studying right. I received my worst grade ever.

Dr.Distilio was a pretty decent professor. Her tests were pretty easy because as long as you remember everything from lecture (which is not that hard) it's not hard to score above an 80, and definately possible to get in the 90's. She was pretty good at teaching, but was a little boring when she would just read off her notes.
As she lectures she looks as bored about her subject as everyone else. Thought she was OK until I saw the comparison with Dr. Kerr and realized how bored I was in lecture with her.
Tests come right out of study questions and lectures. She is not difficult to understand if you actually are paying attention to the lecture, and she does care if her students learn.

I thought Di Stilio was a nice professor, she has an accent, but I rarely had trouble understanding. A lot of people don't like that her lectures are exactly like her powerpoints but I found it helpful in case there was something you didn't understand, she clarified it. Her test was very reasonable

Not the best bio180 teacher, but not the worst either. As long as you do the practice test and study questions its not that bad. Go to class for the clicker questions but don't take anything she says seriously.

This is my second time taking Biol 180 & trust me she is one of the better Biology professors at UW. She has study questions & practice exams, & they're similar to what the midterm looks like. She's extremely helpful during her office hours & she seem to care about the students. Her test was easy compare to the first one I took 2 quarters ago.
Good teacher who is very enthusiastic about the subject... not always the clearest though!

her lectures are directly from the book, yes. but this is a good thing, considering you won't need to read much of the monumental-sized text. she is a bit intimidating, but i liked her. she's very concise and organized. a lot better than the new prof teaching the 2nd half of the qtr... he's a total spaz
Great professor, probably one of my favorites at UW so far.

By far the rudest and worst professor I have come across at UW. It's obvious from the way her class is that she doesn't care about teaching at all and really is only there because she has to be. She's definitely more interested in her research than she is teaching. Why do people like her even have to teach if they are sooo bad at it! AVOID!
oh i had her about 2 years ago. very very very rude, and belittling when you ask her questions. not to mention she lectured straight from the book and failed almost everyone
I hated her. Not to  mention when I came to ask a question after class shed glare or roll her eyes at me.
No Comments

Her accent is a little hard to understand but she did a good job presenting the material in class. She also made herself very available for extra help. Her tests were mostly fair, but with a few questionable parts on the first exam (questions could be taken to mean a few different things). Final was very well written though. Nice lady.
BAD BAD AND BAD.  She is a horrible teacher
By far the worst teacher I have ever had.  She failed so many people.  The mean grade in the class was 30/100.  She rambles and uses those stupid clickers
You have to listen carefully because of her accent, and sometimes she mixes up what she's saying so you need to be sure to have it straight in your own head.  But otherwise a good professor
I concur--all she does is read off the slides. She mumbles too and sometimes talks really fast. Her tests seemed to have very little to do with what was covered in lecture.

Not only does she only read off of her slides in lecture, her slides are directly out of the book. If you have her, don't bother going to lecture, your time is better spent studying the material in the book since every aspect of her course, including the tests, is straight from it.

She reads exactly what is on her lecture slides, which are posted online, so her class can be really boring. She also is not enthusiastic at all and makes the material uninteresting. Her tests were hard too. She tends to ask about material that were not covered in lecture in detail.

Very sweet and very nervous when lecturing in front of students. Knowledgeable when answering questions. His lecture videos were just his slides and him on a separate screen talking at you. Clear, but not as engaging as Neil King's. All test questions are material from the slides, so if you just memorize the slides, you'll ace this class.

Professor DiMaio was a wonderful lecturer and professor, but the exams presented felt a little bit unfair or extremely detailed for something that wasn't covered as excessively as it should've been. However, he's incredibly intelligent and does well in responding to students questions clearly and really does care if we understand the material.

Professor Frank was a really sweet guy who is very energetic about the topic of biochem. Although Biochem may be very boring at times and the lectures project this unfortunately, Frank tries his best to make it easy to follow along. Office hours were very helpful to me. This class also does only focus on exams so make sure that you are prepared.

Cool professor! Maybe his lectures are a bit drier than Neil King's, but his slideshows are really easy to follow (Anki image occlusion enhanced - thank me later). Certainly cares about the topic and is approachable outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is biochem so its going to be hard. I dont mind his lecture videos, but sometimes he says something really important but its not on the slides, so make sure to watch and take good notes. He seems to really care about students and does his best to help them. Grading and whatnot is pretty standard for the bioc dep, so cant blame him for it
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's super energetic and bouncy, looks and talks like John Green. Which for me, was great, it helped me follow along. That isn't everyone's cup of tea though, in the end it's still biochem and still sucks.
SAVE YOURE TIME AND TAKE THIS CLASS WITH SOMEONE ELSE. HE IS BADDDDDDDDD!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Engaging lecturer, clearly cares about students actually learning and understanding the material. Grade is only based on exam grades. Mainly self taught (lectures are meant to be watched prior to actual class).
He is such a cool dude, clearly cares about the subject and about the students learning. Would definitely take again.

Dimaio is amazing! 405 is a memorization-heavy class no matter who you take it with but Dimaio makes it a lot more enjoyable. Beware that the class uses a flipped-classroom model, which I hated at first but it grew on me. Tests are extremely fair and predictable, especially if you know everything on the slides. Take this with Dimaio if possible!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Frank is the best professor I've ever had. He is so silly yet so educational. He also shows up every day in the best outfits I've ever seen a professor wear (Stanley cup in his hands). He is truly a joy to have as a biochem professor. I love him. 100/10

+.1GPA EC for ez hw questions, 1 drop exam, 4(-1) MC (27Q) exams determine grade. Take good notes and study well before the exams, (using old exams is best study method), avoid cramming, start early! No extremely hard or suprising questions, very good lectures. Frank obviously is very passionate about bioc, haven't had a better STEM prof at UW.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: amazing prof, super nice and helpful and makes lectures fun. bioc is hard no matter what so u have to put in the work for any prof. weekly quizzes optional and can boost grade. avg set to 2.8. 4 exams weighted equally and 1 dropped.

Professor Dimaio taught the first half of the course, and his lectures are very helpful for the tests. He covered a lot of the materials in a short amount of time, but he taught it well and clear. It is a test-heavy class, but if you remember everything on the slides you will be fine.

Frank is a gem, truly. The TAs are incredibly active and fantastic and are willing to go the extra mile to help you understand. The class is well organized, and it's on a curve so everything is fair. I love the class, and definitely recommend it!
Great professor, just make sure you know everything before the exam.

researched based professor unwilling to help students in many ways. Research uni--not a good one to go to if you actually want to learn the content. find myself memorizing minuscule details on slides all the time instead of overarching concepts/important biochemical details. horrible exams, anti poc unaccesible quit other classes just study this!!!

The exam problems were worded in such a way--he's just trying to trick students at this point. You put in your 100% effort-- it doesn't pay off. not all of us can afford to take one class without jobs or other time commitments. He makes me not wanna go into research/academia since he's so bad. Also,100% of your grade relies on the exam, good luck

I thought that I was prepared for the exam, knowing all the content from the lectures, doing post lecture problems, pre-lecture, but that was not the case. the professor is really bad. unorganized start to the exam and not enough time given, the proctor stole the sheet from my hands and was so aggressive. terrible class atmosphere.

my friend & I were in the review session for 2+ hours only to get vague + confusing answers. basically this is a research university with faculty unwilling to help, and difficult exams which determine your entire grade. Take this at shoreline or cc and transfer it. chem advisors here are terrible too. wordy prof, repeats things, no explanations!

BIGGEST weed out at the dub! he basically summarized the exam review session by staying studying everything in the 340+ slides, compiled into 27 break or make your grade questions! ridiculous way to run the class. The TAs are super unhelpful too-went to their session and didn't even get any questions answered, waste of 2+ hours. unorganized review.

my son was in class. he deleted old comments. biochemistry is a good subject! not supposed to be made into tricky one. don't send your kids to this school, UW is a weed out school! they don't want anyone to go into phd, md, or anything related! my son wanted to become biochemist phd-  changed his mind after this! beware international students too.

super tough weed out class! The professor is not a good lecturer and repeats things horribly. The content is good but he is not a good professor. he is trying to cram in a bunch of concepts without explaining them properly. every question he asks is a trick question or just complete memorization off slides--this is not biochem!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is a joke.  He speaks so fast without explaining anything.  The tests seem like random facts rather than biochemistry.

I have to tell you that this CLASS is lecture dense and very challenging(at least for me personally). But Dr. Dimaio is a GREAT professor, super nice, and passionate in teaching. Go to his office hour if you need help. Big advice: DO NOT CRAM DO NOT CRAM DO NOT CRAM

He just reads the slides very fast while giving you a headache. You dont learn anything in this class you just have to memorize random facts and hope the facts you memorized will be on the test. What a disappointing joke this school is.

Biochem is naturally challenging given the emphasis on memorization, but Frank was a great lecturer. He was accessible outside of class and held weekly office hours to answer all questions. Everything you need to know for exams is on the slides so no surprises. Don't fall behind and remember that biochem builds on itself. Know the pollevs.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Frank speaks very fast and at times is difficult to understand due to the jargon he uses for this class. I found his part in this course to be the most challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Found myself memorizing patterns of questions and answers provided in previous exams rather than reaching for an understanding of the content itself to get by in class. Really disappointing considering how fascinating biochemistry could be as a subject when taught well.

Online this class would have been the easiest. You cannot command F your brain and that is what is expected. If you like a professor who strings together 15 syllable vocabulary words into run-in sentences nobody could hope to understand this is your man. I would give my left hand to have taken this online. Absolutely stupid amount of memorization.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Another tell-you-what-without-telling-you-why kind of teacher who throws a wide range of general information at you and expects you to memorize the details for the test. Do not take this class unless you have to.

This guy is solid. Lectures can be a little fast, but it was fine online, cause I could go back and rewind in case something was too fast. Somewhat clear expectations for tests, but really better to do the available practice. Still quite difficult, but would take again.

Lectures were very dense and long, but well organized and easy to follow. This class required work than a 3 credit class should, but the material was fun and interesting to learn and he was always enthusiastic about teaching it. Tests were a bit of a time crunch but not super difficult because questions came directly from the lecture slides.

Dr. Dimaio talks really fast, so it makes his lecture not boring but also you can miss things but pre-recorded lectures are well-organized so you can always go back. Because of online class, tests are harder and have more questions with the same allotted time as in person class. You have to memorize everything on the lecture slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is a lot of work for 3 credits, but Prof Dimaio is great. He talks really really fast so it was kinda nice having his prerecorded lectures because I could pause while taking notes.

Dr. Dimaio's lectures were broken into 3 or 4 modules per lecture that I felt were well-organized and allowed the student to take notes easily. To do well on the exams, you MUST be familiar with all of the lecture slides, they are based heavily (almost 100%) on them. Overall I thought Dr. Dimaio is a professor who you can tell enjoys biochem.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is VERY memorization heavy - basically memorize the lecture slides and you'll ace the exams but if you wait too long you're not gonna make it. He doesn't add much content wise (basically reads off the lecture slides really fast) but he offers a lot of help outside of classes and cares for the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class is graded entirely on 3 out of 4 exams and the material comes entirely from the lecture slides. Go to his office hours because he's really good at answering questions. If you can't go to his office hours then post to the discussion board and he'll reply within a day. If you don't study and then you won't do well �� . DON'T CRAM

Worst professor I've ever had. Talks insanely fast and then tests on the tiniest details of the slides. He doesn't take questions or explain anything past what little he puts on the slides. It's all about memorization and no one leaves this class with true conceptual understanding, but at least we memorized all these random tidbits of info, right?!

Dr. Dimaio is one of the best professors at UW! He makes you work for your grade. He is an amazing lecturer, makes you want to go to lecture, and answers questions so perfectly. He tests on both concepts and memorization (sometimes very detailed information). Take him! Wish he taught 406.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. DiMaio is a spectacular lecturer! He is clear and detailed, loves to answer questions outside of class, very professional, and you can tell he is living for the material. don't get the textbook, make sure you understand every detail on the slides! One of the nicest professors at UW!

Exams are based 100% of stuff on lecture slides, but make sure you know every little detail on the slides, no need for textbook. Pre-lecture quizzes, TA questions, and practice exams are pretty reflective of real exams. A TON of material, review material as you go and start studying wayyy in advance.

Dimaio is a great biochem professor! Uses lots of examples and makes things simple. Unfortunately tests are very memorize-based, so don't wait until the last second (there's a ton of material). Also takes really intense sips of coffee every 2 minutes which cracks me up.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Awesome lecturer - highlights the key concepts you need to know and has a summary slide at the end of his powerpoints with bulletpoints of everything you need to know for tests. Exams are very heavy on memorization and have A LOT of content, so study a weekend or two ahead of the actual test. Make use of the lecture quizzes and practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Was really explicit about what you were expected to know for the exams. Make sure you go to lectures and make a quizlet with all of the material on the lecture slides. Don't leave studying to the weekend before the exam (something I learned the hard way).

Professor Ruiz's class was just okay. It wasn't exactly what I was expecting and I sometimes didn't attend class. Content wasn't super interesting for me personally, but Professor Ruiz made every effort to invest us in the course. Projects were super fun, however.

reviews.comment: I revised an essay from this class for my grad school app. I got in! I still think about the films in this class and the readings were heavy but you can get by skimming. Office hours were so helpful. I think only one other CMS prof goes by Prof/Dr instead of their first name, but that's always felt more respectful to me and what I would want tbh
Horrible. Just horrible.
Her class is interactive, and she really encourages you to participate in the discussion. I like taking her class. You learn a lot in taking her class.

If you want to watch really interesting films & read literature surrounding diverse topics we do not discuss enough in American education, this is a fabulous class. However, the prof is extremely rude outside of lecture, has a superiority complex, and does the bare minimum when it comes to explaining assignments. Praying I never have her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super sweet teacher overall, she explains everything super in depth. Only complaint is that she uses a third-party software that is a little pricey for the homework, but you don't need to read the textbook at all, only study the slides. If you go to lecture easy 4.0

Professor is very kind. She is young and a recent grad student, her info is BASED macro. She doesn't make things overly complicated. You don't really need to attend in person if you're good at teaching yourself. She does not record lectures and sometimes opens zoom if ur sick. I would take again. She really cares about her students.

Talked about basic macro econ information. Used examples to explain the concept. Had midterm and final. But the professor didn't have the past exam. And she did it in a different way than the other professors before.

Homework is REALLY hard (although Maddy Brown was a great TA and helped me), grading on tests is inconsistent, lectures were frequently off-topic, and the prof has a weird obsession with AI. However, the course is interesting, and if you have a good TA to help you with the homework, I do recommend it. Be ready to be time-crunched on the midterm.

He gave unreasonably hard homework but his lectures were very unclear and obviously he did not prepare for lectures and just hand waved the whole thing on the fly. His test was very difficult compared to what he actually taught.
Drusvyatskiy, you should resign so that you no longer sabotage the quality of math education at uw

Professor Drusvyatskiy did not take his students seriously. We can tell that he did not prepare for his lectures at all and he just improvises and teaches very poorly. The class is very unstructured and unorganized. Office hour is deliberately set to a time when students are busy so that he does not have to really meet his students.
He cannot care less about his students
I cannot name another professor who's as irresponsible as he is
He essentially just handed wave the whole class without any real teaching
He was the most ridiculous professor ever. Never took students seriously. Bad teaching, bad grading
Obviously he put very little effort in teaching. The lectures are a mess. I did learn nothing from him.
Worst, really tough grader, no hw and exam answers posted, unclear lecture, unclear grading scale, no one answering questions, worst class that I have ever take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor follows very closely to the textbook. It's as if he copied the book into his lectures verbatim. Oh wait, that's exactly what he did. The tests are based on the HW but no answer keys for the HW provided so we don't even know if we did it right. No answer keys for the exams either. You'd be better off reading the textbook by yourself.

His explanations of topics are very unclear and he expects students to know a lot of information from classes that are not prerequisites. Lectures are very confusing and have little value when doing the homework and exams. If you want to read from the textbook and teach yourself all the material then this is the class for you.

He was good at teaching math308, his quizzes were easy if u took notes and studied a bit, he is also very considerate, he messed up during the first quiz and gave everyone an 100%. Also, for the last quiz he made it optional after 80% of the class rated the class. I would take him again for sure

Great prof for linear algebra, very clear lectures and always explains the concepts very well. Not too much homework and its always relevant to class/quizzes. Tests at least online were weekly and not too difficult, he also drops the three lowest questions from across the quizzes. Overall great prof that I would recommend taking for 308!

For 308 he was a very good prof (don't know about 408, never taken it). Based on just my experience this quarter (ymmv), this prof was very accommodating and helpful (always took time to answer questions). I'm not the best at math so I thought the quizzes were challenging (but not impossible). His attitude is good but his handwriting is awful.

This class is too easy. The hw was too easy. It's not fair, I was expecting higher quality from my first LA class. However, I supposed he must accommodate the ungrateful "technical" students (Engineering, CS, etc). I don't see why the class needs to conform for those who lack potential. I expected more rigor. Take this class if you like easy.

Homework, readings, and the lecture all go hand in hand, reinforcing each other. The quiz structure was an interesting shift from the usual 2 midterms and the final. We only had 9 quizzes on material over the past week, and the quizzes were standard difficulty. The usual math. Excellent professor who enjoys linear algebra; def would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: For Math 308 online he was a great teacher! The class was graded by very few quizzes but they were, in general, not extremely tough, especially if you do the concept problems beforehand. His lectures I found to be extremely engaging and he taught the material well! Great class, and you can tell he cares about his students.
Math 308 (soon to be 208) was well-structured, homework was actually helpful instead of being busy-work.

In short, your experience may vary. Maybe for Math 408 he wasn't as good (judging by the reviews) but for 308 online, he was great. People change over time, so who he was back then isn't who he is now. But based on my experience (and many students will agree) he was very patient and helpful. Online is tough but he made it a pleasant experience.

This professor really knows what he's talking about. He does a great job explaining class content, is obviously passionate about math and various mathematical applications, is humorous at times, and always addresses questions to ensure that his students understand the material.

He put forth a lot of effort to make sure students understood the material. He always pauses during class to address questions. Additionally, the weekly quizzes were based mostly on the webassign homework so as long as you understand the homework, you should do fine on the quiz.

He really cares about students. Always pauses to let students ask questions and he really wants us to understand the material. He never tested us on material that was not covered in class. If hw required a topic that wasn't covered he would extend the deadline. Tests are straightforward but make sure you understand the theory. Overall great prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is more interested in making sure that you understand the material and why you're doing what you're doing. He doesn't have an interest in tests but instead gave weekly quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He really cares about his students and won't continue lecturing until everyone's questions are answered. He's really helpful to talk to and the quizzes he wrote were straightforward, never any gotcha questions. Take him if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Was initially skeptical because the other reviews were very critical of him. However, he deserves the benefit of the doubt. Prof Drusvyatskiy was very helpful (always took the time to answer every student's question), and extremely accommodating in this online quarter. Go to office hours if you need help, he's very nice and easy going.

Very well run class! Manageable workload, and very reasonable weekly quizzes. Grades are skewed strongly toward quiz performance, but some are dropped throughout the quarter. Lectures are quite good, with multiple examples typically ranging from simple to complex, paired with explanation of the theory. Definitely would take again! Great professor.

He knows the material, but he is horrible at teaching it. Youre left confused after every sentence he says. He also doesnt show things, he says things in words and writes them down expecting you to completely understand it with hardly any examples. Also, his tests are very confusing so you would need to understand the theorems incredibly well.

He may know about the materials, but he doesnt know a bit about how to share those with his students, the way he explains something is extremely confused. I study by myself for the whole quarter and all I need is just the book! I was very looking forward to take this class but it is so disappointing. He doesnt even give us the Evaluation paper.

Worst instructor, his lectures have little to do with the homework and the exams. He always simplifies the proof of theorems and never gives examples in class. The most ironic thing is that he considers himself a terrific teacher, even though there are so many students complaining. Avoid him if you want to have a good day.

Definitely the worst class Ive taken at UW. Dont understand any part of it. Lecture is boring and complicated. There are some coding homework with MATLAB but we werent taught on it in lectures. So be prepared to learn how to code on your own. Office hours with him are intimidating. Its better to study by yourself through textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I have taken some math courses about algorithms. But this prof's class is really confused. His lecture and homework are not related in some sense. If you really want to learn something from him, make sure you don't have other difficult courses so you could focus on this one.

The worst professor I've ever had in my 4 college years!!!! Don't take his 408 class. He uses most of the material from the "optional" textbook, and his writing is hard to read if you want to review his lecture note. He changed the material and teaching style from this quarter. He didn't care much on those who failed to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Drusviatsky's class.; he is a really funny lecturer. The homework is harder than class problems, but that's pretty standard honestly because it's WebAssign and he did more UW style things. If anything the class moved annoyingly slow given almost everyone already took AP but he insisted on going very slowly.

Professor Drusvyatskiy definitely knows what he's talking about, but lectures as though the students are able to quickly understand material. He teaches the basics in lectures, then there are three homework assignments a week that are significantly harder than the basics taught in lecture.

Very fast-paced teaching style, so attendance in class and paying attention are musts. Dry, no-nonsense type of personality, but I actually found it quite helpful in that he gives you the information without any misdirections. He can seem intimidating at first due to his accent and curt lectures, but he does throw in jokes on rare occasions :)

He just doesn't teach the material that is on his exams. He is very conceptual and telegraphed one of his questions on the first exam, but his problems are impossible to solve with the way he lectures. He bars you from using concepts you knew from high school if they weren't taught in the class and will give you no credit. Funny guy though.

Angry man, awful prof. I think he spent more time angrily staring and tapping mic at us than teaching anything. Taught content up to the day before the final. Tests were ridiculously hard, WebAssign was useless. If you have to take him get Chegg to do hw and do practice exams instead. Clearly knows his stuff but too advanced for an intro calc class

If he will be teaching something you've never learned before, definitely avoid him. He teaches as if his students are already aware of all the materials. His homework problems are ridiculous since they're nothing like what we do in class. Tried to get help on homework through email, but all he said was we know enough to finish them. avoid him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He is a good teacher, but most of his lecture is made up of examples. The book is not necessary if you attend all the lectures. If English is not your first language, it might be hard to understand him since he speaks with a heavy Russian accent.

Funny and clear lectures. Class notes are posted. No need to read textbook, he'll cover all concepts and go through enough examples.  No quizzes. No clicker question in class. Midterms and final are the same type as the practice exams, so do them before exams. Tests are not hard as long as you take notes and do practice exams. I get 4.0.

Good teacher, definitely covers tons of examples. Tests are about 80% of your grade. Definitely recommend going to the lectures because thats the only way understand topics  Also notation is EXTREMELY important on your tests.   He speaks with a Russian accent but you're able to clearly understand him. And hearing math taught like that is nice :)

Kind professor who knows a lot of information about Chinese History--the information flow can be a lot to process in lecture. Class is organized on doing the textbook readings, and there's a lot of supplemental reading as well. Quizzes have some pure recall elements, so make sure you get your facts and dates down. Good class if you're passionate.

She is really knowledgeable and intelligent, but her teaching style does not work for me. She only has a small amount of items she grades you on, so if you get a bad score on anything your grade is highly affected. Her lectures are not well organized and hard to follow. The information she tests you on doesn't always follow what she lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: God awful class. The grading is terrible, she doesn't grade much on content and argument on paper, but on grammar and wording. Super nitpicky. Also, I think she got lazy after the first couple of lectures because she doesn't make slides anymore and just word-bombs the class for two hours.

Extremely dry and boring lectures. Currently in class while writing this and about to fall asleep. Also, her expectations are unclear, the syllabus doesn't really have anything useful. We were supposed to make discussion posts but she didn't mention anything about it. Less than ten people made a post and gave the rest of the class zeros.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The lectures given are scatterbrained and all over the place with no lecture slides to follow. The grading style is extremely confusing and one is unwilling to see different opinions. The amount of reading is severe, and that will be the only way you can learn anything in this class. Do not take this class unless absolutely necessary.

A lot of people are super harsh on Professor Dong, but she is very clear on her expectations from the beginning and what you need to get done. Her lectures are a little chaotic and all over the place, but if you are reading the material you can do the papers and quizzes easily, which is not a high expectation for a 200 level class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She expects you to read a lot. Her lectures are all over the place, and half the time she talks about herself. You expected to pretty much obtain the information from the readings, which is like 50 pages a week. If you don't read, you can't really participate, and you lose out on huge part of your grade. Engineering capstones are easier than this.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof is very condescending and does not accept any different opinion, she will argue you. Participation is mandatory. Does not have a clear rubric for paper so it is impossible to know what to write. Class overall is not hard but requires some readings each week.

This was one of the best classes I have taken at the university. Prof has real insights. The amount of reading is serious, but it is not 7 full books, just 200 pages/week. There are no exams, just three papers, and the topics are all discussed in detail in class meetings. If you are serious with studying, she goes extra mile to help you.

Please dont take her class, she will ruin your grade, and you will learn nothing. No constructive feedbacks for the papers she graded. No clear direction about what she expects. Your paper wont be graded following the rubric. The rubric she gave is just a very general rubric you can probably find on google and copy and paste.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very unorganized. Learned nothing. Got poor grades for the papers because she does not give clear directions. Lots of reading, it's a 400-level class but it doesn't mean I need to finish at least one thick, dense book a week. Have no idea what's going on in this class. You can't disagree with her, she'll argue with you, or you get bad paper grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: STAY AWAY FROM HER CLASS UNLESS YOU ARE A CHINESE HISTORY EXPERT AND FLUENT IN MANDARIN Have no idea what she expects, no clear rubric on how she grades. Lectures are hard to follow No midterm & finals but 3 paper, 25% each, 10% reading notes (which I think is stupid), 15% active participation. 7 books to read, plus readings on canvas. TOO MUCH!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Pretty decent professor but i wish she would incorporate power points more into her lectures. Sometimes would go on random tangent and made the lectures more confusing than it needed to be which added a degree of unnecessary difficulty to the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Insightful.  New knowledge.
I loved this class! Would definitely recommend!!
Very unclear. Lectures were hard to follow and did not match the prepared visuals. A lot of reading that did not help me learn the material.

Disorganized lectures that jump from topic to topic; it felt like she made them up on the fly. Standards seem arbitrary. Difficult to get in touch with or communicate with. Readings rely heavily on either theoretical jargon or poorly annotated primary sources that are difficult to follow without knowledge of the topic.

Professor Dong is INCREDIBLY intelligent; you'll find that all of the class material connects at the end. Her lectures tend to run long and sometimes don't include breaks. She doesn't rely on powerpoints and instead gives papers with notes outlined. Make sure to raise your hand at least once a class for participation points and for discussion.

Poorly organized lectures, ridiculous grading standards, no clear focus.  I don't know if I learned a single thing in this class.  I got a poor grade on my paper because she disagreed with my thesis.  She starts early, rarely gives breaks during lecture, and always ends late.  Two hours of this class feels like an eternity.
Great class!  Loved the readings and discussions.
Professor Dong is very knowledgeable of the topic and has a passion in teaching it.  I like the way she makes connections between history and contemporary social and political issues in China.
This was the first class I had ever had on China and I loved it.  One of the best history classes I've had at the UW.

Worst teacher I've met in college. Boring and unorganized lectures with a lot of important details missing. I hate people teaching history in a radical and unserious way. Don't take her if you are only taking this class for fun.
This professor was amazing!Best Chinese history teacher I ever had!
It's challenging to attend evening classes, but the professor made her effort.
It's nice to have the opportunity to read some of the classics and talk about them in class.  Prof is nice.

Feels no enthusiasm from her. Good or bad lectures depends on her mood. Personally and literally, I learned zero. Strongly recommend to take another professor if you interested in this area, at least that's a better chance to learn what you expected to learn.

Her idea of teaching is reading off her notes while leaning against a desk for 2 hours. She argues with students and has no idea what she wants you to do for her essay. She always falls behind because she goes off topic all the time. She has no business being a teacher, she should just stick to writing books.
the teaching is very scatter and useless
Really fun class.
My favorite class.
Should not be in the teaching profession. Class not that difficult but teacher has utter contempt for her students.
She is not the one teaching this course.  Have you ever been to the class?  The instructor is a man.

This class was nap time for me. The way she lectured was absolutely boring and she was rather strict with attending section and whatnot. The textbook for the class is very good and just reading that will get you by, but she throws a lot of things on the test not from the textbook. Overall it a bit hard and not really worth it.

Prof Dong is kind & very willing to talk w/you about China stuff outside class. She clearly enjoys the topic & is really cute in an auntie sort of way. The problem is 211's enormous breadth, which sacrifices the depth needed to really "get" certain topics. But it's a req for Chinese majors. You'll live, just GO TO CLASS & ask TAs for writing help!
USELESS

A very difficult grader, but one of the better History professors at UW.  A genuinely nice person, and the, uh, spontaneousness of her lectures can be a turn-off for some, but I found it refreshing compared to your typical cut-and-dry UW professors.  An absurd amount of reading and work though, so be forewarned. Highly recommended.
i had a horrible experience with professor dong. she has unreasonably expectations for her students, and yet comes to class with nothing prepared.

Though the material was interesting, the method of teaching was pretty dry and boring because Prof simply talked the entire time.  There was a ton of reading and materials to cover.  Just read the book and look up the terms for the tests.  Talk alot in quiz session for good grade.  My TA was very willing to help, unlike what others have posted.

Not the most interesting professor.  She seems to be trying to be a good teacher but there was too much information and just went way too fast.  I agree with the other poster that the class seemed to be graded really harshly (for a class I had hoped would be an easy 4.0).

Terrible!  Doesn't have slides or notes.  A lot of stuff on tests was not in the materials. TAs are forbidden from helping you with test prep! Miss section once, you lose 0.3 off the course grade! Expectations for tests NOT presented. Grading was unreasonable.  I had some of the highest grades on tests, got only 3.6 in the class!

The assignment budget he offers is very forgiving. However, you will probably need to attend every lecture to have a firm grasp of the type of film analysis he wants you to employ—I was mostly fine with just the readings, but if you are unfamiliar with esoteric philosophical concepts and abstract thinking you may find this course challenging.

He's nice, but his lectures are SUPER dense. Bi-weekly essays had flexible due-dates but were graded pretty harshly. The material he taught was interesting but the way that it was taught wasn't engaging at all; just lectures, readings, and essays. Highly recommend going to his office hours; he's down to earth & helpful in smaller groups.

This was a very challenging course because the lectures were pretty dense, but I found them to be very engaging. He clearly cared about his students' success and I greatly enjoyed the way he structured the course.

He is super nice and friendly always available when I need help discussing class materials and assignments. I also did writing credit with him. He cares about students' progress and well-being. He is kind of verbose but it's for the clarity of the content. I think he is still experimenting with his teaching methods, but he is very easy to talk to.

Lecture heavy but I personally enjoyed every part of it! He assigns about 1 film and 1 reading per class which is super doable. You can even go without it because he will go over it during class. He's passionate and you can tell he really knows what he's talking about. No graded homework, 1 group project, and 2 exams that are all straightforward.

Doug has a good heart but his lectures are boring and he is not accesible outsde of class. Lectures are mildly relevant to the films we watch for homework, but instead of talking about and discussing the films, he rambles on with overly complicated vocabulary that makes it hard to understand what's going on. Bad lecturer, boring movie picks.

This was the worst class I've ever taken. He is a nice guy, but his prompts and lectures are nonsensical. He is passionate about philosophy -- but you will be essentially penalized for not understanding those abstract concepts in a film HISTORY class. Hard to reach via email. Quizzes every class. Strict paper grading. I would avoid him if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A hellish class experience. Not only was the class boring, the slides were also illogical, requiring students to spend a lot of time organizing notes after class, and then after finishing, they would found that it was him making a simple concept very difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Let me start off by saying that I have an A in the class currently. Lectures are extremely boring, it is hard to stay engaged. The assignments are unnecessarily convoluted. There is no feedback when you lose points on assignments. Graded attendance. The deadlines are inconsistent. Who makes things due at 5 pm?!?!? Overall, wouldn't recommend it.

This class wasnt easy - I've never worked so hard. It's a lot of reading, and it takes time to understand the concepts - philosophy, art, film. It's a difficult course because of the content (we read Heidegger AND had to understand it). But, I have to say: I learned more in this class than in any other class I've taken in CMS. Anderson pushes you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class is EXTREMELY abstract. As the person below said, his feedback is very condescending on the take home exams, and for the weekly responses, the directions are very vague, yet if you lose points on the assignment he does not specify why. An artistic mind is a necessity for this class, and overall it was too all over the place for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: For anyone who isn't trained in english or metaphysical existence, everything that comes out of his mouth is complete gibberish. Today one of the slides said, "World is the clearing of the paths of the essential directives with which every decision complies. This means nothing. His grading responses are also super duper rude and condescending.
Makes the subject way harder than it needs to be. Un-inspirational, dry, & callous.
Not good. You don't know his grading criteria and he could ruin your GPA. Just run away as far and quickly as you can.
The scoring is very strange and there are no scoring criteria.

reviews.comment: Won't take it again
