reviews.comment: not easy to do with and weird professor.

He's really accessible and invested in the students learning. There are visiting speakers too and expert days. the slides are very helpful and so are the videos. The exam preparation is adequate. I would take the class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor set out to understand his students. He provided a coffee with the professor and two to three students sign up to have coffee with him after class for half an hour. At that meeting, he finds out from the student how their learning experience can be improved. The students had expert days and we had visiting speakers. Id take the class.

You would think that a Chinese law class taught by a Chinese professor, with lots of students who are Chinese doing the LLM in Asian law program, would be awesome and really dive deep into Chinese law. You would be wrong. Prof Zang spends the whole class debating American politics and does not bring Chinese students into discussions.

It's pretty clear that Professor Zang teaches this 1L intro core curriculum class (Torts) only because he has to. He doesn't want to teach it. He does a terrible job building a class culture of engaging discussion.
Amazingly enthusiastic human being. Very well respected and one of the most engaging lecturers I've had thus yet. Also super-helpful when talking to one-on-one. Would highly recommend.
Professor Eun is really easy to contact and reply Email in a pretty fast pace as well. In addition, class was heavily project based and if you follow the rubric, it should be a straight A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class is very lax u just do your own thing for the quarter with a few presentations and a longish paper at the end. He knows his stuff and i really enjoyed talking with him. Def does interrupt people when they are presenting, but i would say the presentations are just a more casual thing than people realize. Still annoying.
Disrespectful and irresponsible. Always cut people off when they are speaking and did not make the scoring clear....

Worst prof i've ever seen..........grade came out at last minute and there is no time to argue. HE DID NOT COMMENT ON YOUR PAPER AT ALL, just threw at you a range of grade...did nothing at all. irresponsible.... If there are any other course you can take, don't take his:))))))

DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS if you have other options. Grades came up on the last day for grade reports to be updated, so you have no time to argue. Unclear grading criteria. You spent almost the whole quarter to finish a project, and he gave you no feedback on the paper but just took points off.

One of the worst professors and classes I had in the Econ department. He doesn't care about the students at all and his lectures aren't helpful. It's obvious he doesn't want to teach and all the grades depend on the exams. His grader is very tough.
The most irresponsible Econ professor ever. He never replied to emails and gave low grades.
My grade was so low that for the first time Id like to retake a class but only him teaches 483 so bruh
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worset prof in UW Econ department! Received my lowest GPA ever from him! Need to attend every class and ask questions on every presentation days. Even if you did that, you can never receive 100% participation grade. He teached nothing useful in class and you need to study STATA on your own. No grading weight, no rubric for presentation, ppt, paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He does lecture a bit fast but genuinely cares about his subject matter and how his students are learning. Really helpful when it comes to answering questions and stating concepts in an alternative way. Pretty easy class if you've taken ECON 482 but the paper can be time-consuming if you don't start early.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Extremely helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: He is a great professor who encourages students to explore topics as much as we want. He is also very helpful and accessible outside the class. Even though there is a long paper to write, you can get an A easily if you satisfy all requirements.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Drew explained all the topics well and kept your interest. The tests took a lot of studying in order to do well. A couple of the labs were challenging, but the majority of them were easily understandable. Drew set clear expectations and gave plenty of time and prep for the final project.
Good lectures, but difficult assignments which are generally a lot of work.

Such interesting class; Prof really wants you to succeed and love the material. Lectures are pretty straight forward but in order to fully understand assignments, ATTEND OFFICE HOURS. I switched to the ESS major physics option because this class really captured my interests to earth and space. Assignments 100% of grade. No tests, 1 assign/week.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I love Dru, His lecture might seem a bit long but the class was very easy. Just do the homework and assignment, you will pass with flying grade. I had him for CMST 101. We had a presentation for our final and it was really easy, we are getting graded on whether or not we tried to present, not the fact if our presentation was good enough.

Although Dru puts forth LOADS of effort to make sure his students understand important concepts, he is overly aggressive and intense. He uses intimidation as a technique to maintain order. Having rules is respectable, but making your students feel like they have run over a kitten when -for example-arriving late is unnecessary.

Overall, Dru is great.  He cares about if we learn, allows for class input/creativity, and is very clear and articulate.  He can be harsh at times though, both in grading and personality, but no reason not to take a class from him.  I learned a lot and really improved my public speaking!
His class is interesting, but a lot of work. He really challenges you and can call on you to answer questions at any time. But, he has a good humor. He has good explanations and very articulate.
Not really good at covering concepts. Just skims through the minimum and kinda just expects you to know everything for hw and quiz. The quiz is 40% btw. Definitly NOT a class for beginners.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof gives you an ez practice quiz and then pulls the rug from under ur legs during the actual quiz. Tries to put trick questions that has more to do with syntax issues rather than the logic of course content. If possible, please for your own sake avoid this prof at all costs.

Yes, the course can be a bit challenging, but it's compared to my other courses like organic chemistry, microbiology, endocrinology, its nowhere near that level of difficulty. If you are interested in the content and show up, you should do pretty well. In my opinion, Fitz is an amazing professor, really loved taking the class with them.
cse160 is a hard class for beginners

lectures dont do much at all besides basic python when the homework is expecting much more and only gives vague instructions after the first 2. class as a whole isn't terribly difficult if you use outside resources to help learn. and this is different for every quarter I assume but the TAs were awful; took over a month to grade homework
The worst prof I have had. Does not respond to emails, is very disorganized. Grading takes a lot of a time so the feedback does not come in time. Goes through concepts really fast.

So unclear doesn't explain anything, just expects to understand or have some knowledge on what's going on even though the beginner course homework covers concepts we never talked about in class and wants us to figure it out, and this is the first week of the course.

In my opinion, Fitz was an incredible professor and made me want to continue learning Python. He also had great hair. He cares deeply about his students and is very willing to answer questions both in and outside of class. Go to lecture and start the homework early because its lowkey interesting but overwhelming if you cram it.

Fitz's exams aren't horrible, but follow similar tricky syntax problems presented in lecture (often detailing specifics he didn't cover in class). He's just SO disorganized. He always reposts HW assignments several times (due to forgotten files, incorrect names, or accidentally posting the answers), and each quarter has the exact same problems.

My blue hair king, Fitz was my first CSE class and while it was hard he was there and present in helping students, fast emails, and clear directions on homework. Though, I hated the in person tests that were a little nitpicky, but he does help you prepare well and owns up to his own faults as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I found myself watching panopto recordings all quarter, and i really enjoyed fitz's teaching style. Their lectures were easy to follow, super helpful when it came to hw, and not awful to watch. There's a lot of homework, but its a UW CSE class, heavy workload is part of the syllabus (all profs). Fitz themself was awesome, 12/10 would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: idk why fitz has so many negative reviews. granted this was my first CSE class at uw, but i had an overall great experience. fitz seems like a genuinely nice person who was always willing to stop for questions and help students individually. homework is time-consuming, but if you really invest in this class you can easily get A's.

The lectures were not very good. They moved too fast and assumed we already knew more than we did. But the actual structure and organization of the class was pretty good. The TA section lecture slides were very helpful and the homeworks (while difficult) were great for growing our understanding of the content. The exams were pretty hard though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I'm surprised to see such negative reviews. Andrew was a great professor, the homework assigned was reasonable and the lectures covered enough content to where I didn't really need to study out of class. Lectures were also easy to digest but covered a ton of content. The only downside is that a lot of his lectures were pretty error prone.

Homeworks are very hard and difficult. I'm glad the final project was optional for us since I've been very stressed and exhausted with online classes. We covered a lot of topics which some I enjoyed. The quizzes got harder as they progressed. Definitely go to quiz sections and WPL to ask for help and questions as it gets busy the week hw is due.

don't take cse154 with this prof... his lectures are pretty messy and not gonna lie, the homeworks are graded pretty harshly. also, he expects us to know how to code some stuff when he has never mentioned or taught us before. very hard to get a good grade. i find this class harder than cse142 and 143 so.. that explains it all.

Nothing makes my head hurt more than when I hear the name, Andrew Fitz Gibbons. This quarter has been rough for me, as it is for everyone, because of the pandemic. Andrew refused to be understanding when I needed help. This is a intro class, but since he can't teach, he acts like we're stupid for not knowing and tells us to google it. Do your job.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The absolute GOAT. Amazing lecturer with great informative slides. She is very accessible outside of class and you can tell she really cares about your success. Class material isn't hard and make sure you answer everything using flux reasoning. Ask questions, review notes and homework and you're pretty much set. If you can take her, DO IT!

Dr. Durant is a good and fair teacher. She expects you to know content from class and draws from practice questions to make exams, which I appreciate it. She is always willing to help you succeed as long as you make the effort to go to her. The content fascinates me and wish I could take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Out of my harsh quarter this was a class I really enjoyed! The content is a lot but I would say it's manageable and she makes it easy to understand. The tests are actually based on the content and not curveballs. Your effort is definitely reflected, if you study good you'll get a good grade for sure.

Dr. Durant has no reviews on RMP so I thought I would leave her one! BIOL350 is my first "in-my-major" course and I'm very pleased with how it's going! She is very accessible outside of class and is happy to answer questions in class. The exam material is straightforward, relating to lecture slides, peer-facilitating hours, and discussion section.

Amazing professor!!! Always makes time for students and wants them to do well in class. You can tell that he is passionate about what he does, which makes the lectures interesting. Would 10000% recommend.
One of the kindest professors. Explain the content very well, answer questions with a thorough explanation, and you can tell he truly cares about whether his students understand.
never responds to any emails, is very checked out after teaching for decades, abundant typos in homework, not accessible. pretty average tenured college professor experience.

The content of this class was not difficult to learn. At first glance I thought I would not be prepared because of my poor calculus skills however I learned that the quizzes have a pattern and you can use algebraic formulas and manipulate them to get a numeral answer. The only thing I didn't like was that he was very unresponsive to emails.

The best thing about his class is that he doesn't have midterms but has quizzes! The craziest part is that he reuses quite a few question (word for word) from previous years so if you can ask friends who took him in previous years, you should be set. There's quite a bit of homework which can be difficult. Form study groups and you should be fine!

Gary looks intimidating but he is very nice if you get to know him. His lecture is old fashioned, but I like it. His exams are fair. Make sure your practice exams, HWs, lecture notes, and you'll do well. I was scared of PChem, turned out I actually liked some of the topics. He doesn't reply to emails, find him in-person. Especially DRS things

I love Drobny as a prof and person. He's very traditional and writes on a chalk board. It's recorded on zoom, but you get the most out of class by attending. He has many office hours and give practice quizzes that resemble the real ones. Good guy, tough material and class but he'll get you through it.

The homework is hard and the wording is deceiving. It seems like the problem is asking you to use a simple formula from lecture but then it turns out that the formula isn't on any of the lecture slides.

Definitely one of the best STEM professors I have ever had. His lectures are easy to follow, and he's pretty laid-back. During quizzes, he'll be friendly with students to give a light-hearted atmosphere. If you're taking p-chem, I 100% recommend taking it with Drobny!

Undoubtably the best professor I have had at UW. This guy is extremely intelligent and brings a light-hearted-ness atmosphere to his lectures. Even after 40 years he cares deeply about his students. You can find a lot of his old exams online and if you study those you will 4.0 the class. Pay deep attention to the problems he goes over in lecture.

I would recommend taking notes of the lecture slides before taking his lecture in person, once you're able to follow his speed in class, everything will be much easier. Homeworks each week take ton of time, but after you mastered them, quizzes should be a piece of cake.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Pretty seasoned prof, can tell he loves his subject. Lectures and quizzes/final exam align fairly well. Not a heavy workload, but not an easy breezy class - weekly homeworks will take a couple hours to do, and biweekly quizzes are worth a ton of your grade. It's a math-heavy course, so review basic integrals and derivatives. Get ready for equations

Solid professor. Lectures and notes are pretty helpful. Quizzes are not bad, but be prepared of the final ( A lot questions but we're not given sufficient time). The grading is straight scale so it's pretty stressful. Practice quizzes and exams are not given so find your own practice problems if possible.

Dr. Drobny seriously gives ZERO care about students. He's taught for many decades and seems very burnt out. He acts casual about everything (coming to class 10 min late on the usual,mistakes on HW, and so many typos. When campus went online he made a mistake on the format of the quiz and then blamed students for his mistake and showed no care.

He gives very good lectures and little tricks that make passing quizzes and exams easier. There's a reason for everything he writes on the board so follow along. If you do the homework and go to office hour for problems you get stuck on, you'll do fine. His grading is very fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Drobny is one of the better gems of the chemistry department. His "old-school" chalk-board lectures may not be for everyone, but they get the job done. He also posts annotated lecture notes online a few days in advance. They're great for the online homework. Bi-weekly quizzes on Friday and a final exam. Do the homework and the practice final.

Weekly online homework (done on mastering chemistry), in-class quizzes (every other week), organized and clear lecture notes posted online, answers homework questions during tutorial (optional class). Professor Drobny is very intelligent, knowledgeable, and humorous.

I took him for the B-term summer quarter which was waaaay easier than normal full term pchem one. His quizzes were super easy, way easier than homework it was almost unbelievable. BEWARE OF HIS FINAL. You may fall into a false sense of security but the average grade on the final (w/curve) was a 2.3 and worth 45% of our grade.

Very chill professor and is easily accessible outside of class. He is a very classic lecturer and does all his work on the whiteboard/chalkboard - so it's recommended to print out his lecture notes (or read them beforehand) to follow his lectures. Quizzes are pretty fair - easier than the homework but still tough. Brush. Up. On. Calculus.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He communicates the material, which is inherently very hard to communicate, quite well. More importantly in my opinion, he is a very fair and nice person.

I took this class as a B-term class and honestly, it was waaaay easier than my full term 452. This quizzes were very easy and exactly like the homework with very high averages, and the final was actually a bit hard. I didn't attend class for half the short term bc it was a huge waste. Do the hw and find old material. The textbook is a joke
He is Gandalf reincarnated! Extremely wise and expert in his feild, take a class and you will learn a lot

Review for 452+453, SUMMER Q: quiz on F, written HW on T/W, MChem HW on M/W, book not essential +: Extremely intelligent, very approachable+accommodating, never wastes time. HWs often recycled. Gives examples. -: Difficult class, LOTS of HW. KNOW your calculus. Tricky/difficult exams w/ many conceptual aspects. Keep up. Little practice material.

For homework, he'd give one set of problems that he wrote himself (these were really helpful and relevant) and another set on Mastering Chem. The Mastering Chem problems didn't relate much to lecture, so were difficult. Quizzes were fair and matched his written hw well, with lots of partial credit. Our final was tough; the average was 25/42.

One of the most helpful professors I've had for an upper level science course. Really tries to understand the questions students are asking and always willing to clear points of confusion. Office hours are very helpful. Only negative thing was that the assigned MasteringChemistry problems usually didn't have too much of a relevance for the class.

I have really enjoyed taking P-Chem with Drobny. He's willing to be there for office hours and is reasonable about assigned work and quizzes. All expectations were communicated clearly and nothing was terribly difficult. He was pretty funny too, and I would love taking more classes with him. I didn't actually NEED the textbook but it was helpful.

Not a huge fan of PChem, but I enjoyed Drobny's slight dry humor. Lectures are great, although they do go by fast, so definitely pay attention. The book is mostly just extra info. Weekly homework+quizzes, plus exams. I had tons of fun camping out in his office hours asking questions about both lecture and homework, and he was super helpful!

Drobny did a pretty good job of teaching the material. Lectures are boring if you aren't fascinated with Chemistry, but he does a really good job of slowing down, asking for questions, and answering them clearly. I did not go to office hours but he seemed like a pretty approachable guy and I'll bet that he would help a lot if you needed it.

The key to passing this class is to review his lecture notes, and get ALL his past homeworks and tests. He repeats his test questions ever so often and its easy to get full marks! Note sheet for exam also given.

He answered every question in my class. His teaching is funny and easy to understand. I enjoy going there everyday. The homework was a little bit too much and sometimes it requires exact number (which make you do it over and over again) but aside from that: GREAT!

He loves the history of chemistry and cares about how his students are doing. He's patient in lectures, responds to emails quickly and his exam questions are pretty straightforward. The worksheets he provides in discussion section are very helpful and a good way to prepare for exams.

I really enjoyed his lectures because he talks about interesting real life applications. He also cracks little jokes that are lame but still funny. You can tell that he really cares if the students are doing well because he is very patient when answering questions. He tells you everything that is going to be on his exams. Super straightforward!

I really liked this professor. He clearly wants students to pass and answers questions fully when asked. He likes to go on tangents when lecturing sometimes though. Lectures can be dry, but he makes class more interesting with demonstrations, which help.
The prof obviously love the history of chemistry.

Homework and tests are impossibly hard and he gives very little partial credit. Some problems contain concepts not explained in class or the book, which is very frustrating. Expect to be confused the whole time and learn most of the information from the internet. Tried asking a few questions but was largely not helpful for me. Avoid at all costs!
One of the best chem professors, most of his exam questions are straight forward, and the mean for the final was about 70 percent

I studied every day for hours for this class, yet it never seemed to help. Whenever I thought I got an A on the test, I would get a D. I was very confused because he would always say that the tests are harder than the homework, yet he never gave us any hard practice problems that were like the ones on the test. He also only read from his slides.
Absolute treat. Super interested in his subject. Tests were difficult but exactly what he said they'd be on. Going to the final review was really helpful.
Pretty easy 142 class. Once you learn how to take his tests, you'll do fine for the rest of the year. Did a fairly good job in lectures, but make sure to read the textbook.

Very nice and approachable guy.  Makes excellent slides, but often rambles in class. Made it hard for me to not fall asleep in class, but he is extremely personable and genuinely wants his students to pass. Even scheduled a whole class review for the final and went through each question topic on exam. Self-learning class for sure though.
Rambles a lot. I'm sure he'd be better for a more engaging class, but just look at his slides at home if you need to.

It's a love/hate relationship with this class, particularly because I am able get through this class on "average" (thankfully) but the professor's explanation is pretty much pulled right off the book; reading the book = going to class. Good points: he's very understanding about due dates.
hard!
Not great. Hard to understand. Lectures unclear.

Terrible lecturer.  Posts his notes online so I stopped going to lecture because it was useless to do so.  Recycles both HW and exam questions.  Some questions contain material that aren't covered in lecture notes.  Book also is terrible and confusing.  Understood nothing in class and still managed an A-, so I guess he's considered "easy".

Material is challenging, but if u prepare 4 tests n do HW u will b fine. Allows 1 pg notecard on exams n recycles problems so write his old exams on ur notecard and u should b fine. Very smart guy. He tells history tidbits to make things interesting cuz all the class is is math.More in 453 than 452.

Recycles all material, but doesn't bother to correct errors. Confusing and arrogant. Co-authored mandatory textbook which is even worse than him. Doesn't understand questions asks and wastes class time with history tidbits. Useless course and professor

he is the easiest pchem professor. he recycles his tests, so make sure you know how to do the practice exam problems, b/c you will see some of them in the exam.  You get to use 1 cheat sheet for the exam and he doesn't care if it's hand written or copy..  Your life would be a lot happier if you take his pchem class

This may seem like something so small, but lord his over-pronunciation over every word that isn't in English is like pulling teeth. The way he pronounces Carlos Santana is like nails on a chalkboard. Its like how Disney portrays bilingual speakers. He talks like person from high school who spent a week in Spain and calls it "Barthelona".

Enthusiastic, dedicated steelband instructor. Made the class very accessible and fun for students with no musical background. My one gripe is that we spent 10 weeks on the same two songs, so if you were playing a boring part, there was way too much downtime that he'd spend working with students who were playing more difficult parts.
Lectures were pretty entertaining. Exams and assignments were reasonable. There are required textbook readings but they're very long and not super necessary.
pretty easy, just take notes and do some quick studying (skimming notes and relistening to chorus/part of songs) before the quiz/exams. took in spring 2023

Taken during accelerated summer quarter. Copy down what is written on slides-nothing else. Textbook-I just skimmed and noted that wasn't mentioned in lecture, but most is lecture repeat. Discussion posts, quizzes and exams. Look up the lyrics to the song playing on quizzes/exams, can find all info you need.

I had this class during quarantine so it was all online. If you take notes on all of the lectures, you should do well. I can't speak for the rules in regular classes, but with online classes, we were allowed to use our notes on tests, which made them easy A's.

3 listening quizzes, 2 exams, and 1 reflection paper. Memorization and recognition of specific songs in the list (30 songs/quiz) are the keys to doing well. Exams has an essay portion (no guideline) and was graded very harshly (remember all the dates, specific artists, groups of people, historical context, and random facts). Do not recommend :(
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 162 is an easy A /if/ you have a background in music. Interesting subject material, but he doesn't really accept some student perspectives in class. He's picky about answers to questions, even opinion-based ones if he doesn't agree with your answer or didn't hear a feature of a song that you did, he'll say that you're wrong to the whole class.
Shannon is very passionate and knowledgable about popular music. If you show up to lectures and really study the study guide, you will do fine in his class.

Really cares about his students and puts a ton of time and effort to make his class fun and interesting. Honestly if you go to class and look at his study guide before the exam you will do great in his class. He's a great professor and a good guy.
He doesn't know what he is teaching about.

his "lecture notes" are just dash facts, no slides, so when the 3 exams come up you have NO IDEA what's suppose to be on the exam. He says you don't need the $200 book but writes questions based on the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is not an easy A. Lectures and multiple choice tests. To do well you will need to memorize lots of names and dates, especially for the first test. It helps if you have an ear for music and some music knowledge coming into the class. You aren't required to go to lecture as he posts his lecture notes, but I highly recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took this class for the easy 4.0 but let me tell you, it is not an easy 4.0! there are 3 tests and one tiny essay, the essay is easy but the tests are very specific and cover a lot of material that he had NEVER once gone over in class. To make things worse, he doesn't require the textbook so you have to know things without having heard them

I expected this class to be a gap booster, but it was the exact opposite. Your entire grade is based on three tests because there aren't any homework assignments and the class is not curved. He expects you to know details about songs that he barely talks about or doesn't even mention in class on the tests. I would not recommend this class.

The class used to be known as an easy 4.0 but now it is nothing close. His tests are not fair and have very specific questions on things he barely mentioned in lecture while not including questions on the important main ideas. Tests are also the only part of the grade. Would not recommend. Made me dislike music.

The class is easy work-wise but the tests are oddly specific and there will be questions on things he only mentioned once in lecture. The tests are the 90% of the grade and so it's really hard to get a good grade with the very specific test questions. NOT an easy 4.0 class.
great teacher knows a lot about ethnomusicology. friendly and genuinely cares about his students
I have read a lot on popular music and this teacher was just repeating stuff from other books. He was a bit too friendly with me when he knew how mush I had read, bit shady.

Good professor, I started reading the book, but said forget it. I ended up in the class with a 4.0 with extra points. Went to his office hours and listen to his lecture over again using a voice recorder. My advice to get a 4.0, listen to the lectures over again and formulate questions on the flashcards from the lecture. I did this class Spring 2011

it was a fun class. Unlike most professors, he seems to want the students to do well in his class. But showing up to class isn't really that mandatory. I missed half of his lectures and still got a 4.0. just look over his lecture notes and listening examples and you'll do fine

It seems like he tries to make it so anyone can get a 4.0 (extra credit on tests and opportunities). Just study a few hours before each test and attend lecture.  If you don't expect much, this class will be awesome. He was really nice to our class and extremely accommodating. He's pretty dorky, but in a good way.

Extremely easy and fun class. Lecture is fun and makes studying easier. To do well, before the midterm read up on the songs he posts, like their form, instrumentation, etc, and read his lecture notes. Skimming the book helps to reinforce the concepts too. I got close to 100% (28-29/30) on the midterms because of these tactics.

It was an interesting class but I would not recommend Dudley. He is very passionate about the subject but very disorganized. He always messed up the tests somehow. Also, the tests are extremely tricky. Even if you attend lectures and study hard you still can miss many points on tests.
Very easy class, the second half of the quarter is definitely more interesting. You don't really have to go to lecture, or read the textbook. The tests are easy and not cumulative.
He does not return calls or emails, or give clear answers in his office hours if you are not a priority.
Easiest class ever! I 4.0 it easily and it was also fun. Great music and non-stressful class. I loved it. I wish I could take it again :)

I honestly went to class 4 times the entire quarter and got a 3.9 by spending two solid days before the exams going over the listening portion of the test and the online notes that go along with it.  He is a pretty good teacher and if I had to take another music class I would take him again.  BEWARE OF HIS LOVE OF LATIN MUSIC THOUGH!

during the class, i found myself having a hard time going (mainly because its at eight in the morning). too many lectures on latinos, even though it is his expertise/field. but now that this class is over, i find myself missing it alot. overall, definitely a teacher and class worth taking.

Shannon is an awesome guy, hes really into the material he teaches. tests are pretty easy if you pay attention in lecture. Reading the book def. helps clarify things, but the class is do-able without the readings. Dont skip class though, his lectures are the basis for the tests.
Nice guy, knew his stuff.  A little dorky, but made the class fun and funny.

when i first took this class, i thought it was going to be an easy 4.0. granted, it wasn't hard, but the prof was way confusing. he went off subject way too much, and he made a couple mistakes on the tests.

this wasn't too difficult.. if u go to lectures and take notes it shouldn't be difficult to get a 4.0 without reading ANY of the book .. and only doing the listening examples he assigns before the midterms.. recomended if u need an easy LOW comitment vlpa 5 credit class

Very fun and awesome guy! Loves his job and makes it interesting, even for 750 people at a time AND at 930 in the morning! I strongly recommend this class!  I'd take more classes from him if they were offered!
No Comments
Awesome guy. Material was easy and he made class fun with his sense of humor. I actually wanted to go this class everyday. He also had great guest lecturers which added spice to this class as well!

Professor Dudley is not qualified to teach a class on American Popular Music. I found many instances where he was incorrect. His choices for what is American Popular Music were bad choices. We spent weeks on Latin music but we didn't talk about many of the most popular bands.
a professor in my department; his popular song class was fun and informative, and the tests were super easy.  however, it was a 500 person class.  friendly guy, too!
Hes helpful and consistant on the tests. He asks very specific questions, so there is no room for "bs"ing an answer. Very nice and encouraging

Very interesting class. Great lecturer. The classes were engaging and you can tell there was passion about the subject. Very hard to get a 4.0, but still my favorite class. The exams we had were the most challenging. My biggest critique for the course were the study guides, which were pretty vague.

This class is a standard 200 level class. Duncan likes averages to be ~70% and will curve it up to 70 if it's lower. Questions were fair. Content was kinda hard, but not because of her. It's a mix of in-depth biology, math, and history. Dawgpath says only 3% of students 4.0 this class, but if you genuinely study hard it's possible!

many readings are assigned but you could probably get away with skimming through them if you attend class and pay attention. the TA's were tougher graders on the homework assignments than I would've liked, but if you put a lot of effort into the class you'll be fine.

She's a very nice person, is very straightforward with her expectations, and is extremely passionate about the subject. The only thing I will say is that it's difficult to feel fully prepared for her exams--the study guide for both the second midterm and the final did not include a single practice question and her averages are ~70% per exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the easiest 400 level classes I've ever taken, yet I feel like I learned so much. No tests at all. A couple essays, research projects, and one group project. I was so grateful for a course that was this laid back and low stress. Clear deadlines and rubrics. Extremely fair. Loved this course! Much different than Duncan's other courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! She is a great lecturer with a sense of humor, which made lectures so interesting and engaging. Great class structure. She does cover material quite fast so be prepared to take good notes. Class gets significantly more difficult after the first midterm but you will do better than you think. Wish I took more classes with her!

Professor Duncan is one of the best profs I've had at UW, she genuinely cares about her students and loves what she teaches. I will say she does go a bit fast but going to her office hours or asking some questions after class usually clears things up. Her lab practical final is pretty hard but its such a small part of your grade I wouldn't sweat it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was by far the worst professor I have ever taken a class with at the UW. exams are based on little facts that were mentioned in class maybe once, not good review for exams, lab final was hard, both midterm and final were hard and to top it off she doesn't accommodate to her students, take this class in the summer! someone else teaches it!!!!

Great and informative lectures, the professor is an expert on the class topics and can answer any questions. She is a little unapproachable but the TA is helpful! Midterm and Final are difficult, the Lab final is hard. Lots of studying, reading optional and attendance unfortunately mandatory.

Loved her personality and passion. Only complaint is that slides are uploaded after lectures, making it hard to keep up w/ notes. Most lectures had recordings uploaded next day. If you've taken anatomy/physio and done some basic genetics, this will be a very interesting course that isn't too difficult. 2nd half a bit harder and more content heavy.

I really liked this class! Super interesting material. This class is great if you're REALLY interested in the subject. Make sure you attend lecture as she will do a random poll every week that you can't make up. ASK QUESTIONS. Also (BIGGEST ADVICE) make physical flashcards as that helped me the most on the lab practical!!
The lab practical is harder than any of her tests.

Professor Duncan was great. Did max 5 hours a week of work even tho syllabus said 15. Most quizzes you can take as many times as you want. Teaching format was very well organized. Textbook is not necessary but helps. Lab practical was hard but midterm was pretty easy. Probably best for anthropology majors, may not be interesting to other majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is literally a waste of time with forced participation and unnecessary workloads. Not to mention, the test questions are designed to trick you into thinking you got the correct answer. You are better off taking the community college equivalent of this class since there aren't a lot of other professors at UW that teach this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It is very evident that Dr. Duncan doesn't want students to treat this class as an elective, but to take it seriously. THIS CLASS IS HARDER THAN YOU THINK IT WILL BE! Exams are fairly difficult, and she likes the average to be about 75%. Beware of the lab practical, it is easy to forget about but was super hard. Class average was about 2.8 I think.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Puts passion into 206 despite it being outside her field. Does not do pop quizzes but does PollEv for participation credit (NOT scored), assigns many readings but is clear on what you need to know from readings, and has dense lectures. Incredibly compassionate with extensions, non-exam grading, and extenuating circumstances. So much love to her!

While she moves very fast in lectures and goes a little hard for PollEv, she's super passionate about what she teaches and homework outside of class was super easy and she didn't give much of it. Labs were also really easy, you really just need to show up, but the lab practical was a little rough.

Do NOT take Bioa206 (Plagues and Peoples) with Professor Duncan. She is a nice woman, but a subpar professor and expects you to understand the tiniest details of what she says. Often rushes lecture slides and does not explain concepts well at all. Unfortunately, one of the only BioAnth professors at UW entirely. Take something else for BioA credits
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very interested in the subject which makes her lectures fascinating. You have to go to class. She goes through a lot of information, but it shouldn't bee too difficult. I think the textbook is not really necessary bc she uses a lot of the same graphs/examples. Lab section very useful.

If I'm being honest, this isn't the most helpful class in terms of how helpful the content will be in life. There's so much in lecture to memorize it's literally almost impossible. The exams are tough, you might think you'll pass them but you will end up failing. But if you do your work and attend class, you'll pass this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Only 2 multiple choice exams (midterm and final) as well as a lab practical monitored by the TA. Overall not an extremely difficult course, but the exams are highly specific and require you to memorize nearly everything Duncan lectured on. She's a nice professor and knows her stuff, I just wish the class was graded by more criteria than three exams

she is very knowledgeable in the field, but her lectures are very material heavy and her exam questions are extremely specific and difficult. She expects you to memorize every aspects of her lecture, which is impossible. Her expectations of assignments and exams are unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Conceptually not a hard class, but you have to memorize everything(!) to do well on the tests. It's completely possible though. She definitely let her own interests creep in too much. She was also off-puttingly cynical and kind of mean. I think the best way to succeed is to memorize the content from lecture everyday, rather than putting it off.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very passionate about what she teaches! Lectures are easy to understand but the questions she asks are a little confusing.

Prof Duncan is a nice woman who's pretty passionate about what's taught. The lectures are well informed until it gets to a topic where she will tangent off into her own interests. There is only a midterm and a final which weigh heavily on your grade and are very specific on the most random topics. Lab matters a lot as it isn't recorded. Overall meh
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class and learning about primates and human evolution. To do well, definitely go to quiz section as they were not recorded and covered a lot of important info for the tests. Exams were multiple choice and we had plenty of time to do them.

I really liked Duncan when I took her class in the winter! You have to go to lecture because of pop quizzes that could happen during any day of the week and the labs were a little boring. Despite this, I really liked the class and found the material interesting. To succeed, I found that reading the textbook was really beneficial.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Would NOT recommend. She holds in-class pop quizzes right at the start of class, is not accessible outside of help via email or office hours, & is disagreeable. Her lectures are unclear & contradict themselves (says the exact opposite is true on one slide than that of a previous slide). Unfortunately, she is one of the few BioAnth professors at UW.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took BIOA201 and it was pretty chill. As long as you study her slides and maybe crack open the textbook for review you'll be fine on the midterm/final and the lab practical is just memorization. Also offered some extra credit at the end of the quarter that raised your grade by 0.3. Only thing that sucked was random graded quizzes once a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She's nice and all but BIO A 201 and it was just horrible. There were 2 multiple choice exams. 2 lab exams and a final multiple choice exam and none of them get dropped. She has random pools in the morning so you never know which morning is crucial. weekly video assigned every week or two about an hour long that only have 3-6 questions.

Andrea Duncan is a great lecturer. Her classes are always pretty packed so not a ton of one-on-one interaction, but expectations are made clear. Most of the course is graded on midterm and final exams, so although she doesn't take attendance, attending the lectures is important to do well on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Duncan went on tangets all the time that distracted from lecture. She has two tests, a final and a midterm, that collectively make up 60% of your grade. The tests are all about memorizing tiny details and not about understanding the material. She will use surprise poll everywhere questions. Go to lab to get easy points, and read the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Duncan is one of those professors that genuinely cares about her students doing well and gives many opportunities for extra credit. She has very clear expectations, and if you can't make it to an 8:30am class that's on you. Her lectures are amazing - I have never learned so much in one class before. If you show up and work hard you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The class is only graded on two tests, and you have poll ev. that are graded on accuracy!! (not participation like usual). Do not take this class for general ed. credit, unless you are highly interested in anthropology and it's your anticipated major.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: memorize names, monkeys, phylogenies, and random facts! She posts ALL 6-7 poll Q's at 8:32A SHARP. 1stQ checks if you are physically present -- if you miss this, you get 0/6 for poll that day. No mercy if you have a 1.5hr commute and are late 5 mins. terrible wording on exams. avg70% (W/extra credit), NO CURVE. Would NOT recommend to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Disorganized and unclear of expectations, and doesn't even give clear instructions to her TAs. Slides were crap, and her stories detract from what is pertinent information. Go to class because she weights in class participation off of three or four assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Very nice and approachable but her class was disorganized and expectations weren't clear. She tried to use poll everywhere but didn't know how so they were few and unpredictable, and same for panapto. Hard to get a good grade bc only grades are one midterm and one final which she expects you to memorize very specific and unnecessary info for
I think he knows his stuff but I know he does not know how to teach. You leave class confused wondering what you did in your life to deserve him. Avoid if you can!!!
He gives practice exams that are similar to the real exam but the answer key is often incomplete
So hard

He does not care about students at all. My computer bluescreened the first week of class and I asked for an extension and was not granted one. The homeworks are incredibly difficult and the only way to get through the class is to form a VERY solid study group with 8+ people. Lectures were confusing and pointless, all learning was achieved on own.

Easy material, horrific structure. The lectures are fine, but just watch online. The labs are hell. No instruction from TAs, with labs being on material covered weeks ahead of the lectures, using unfamiliar equipment. Exams weren't bad, they're almost identical to previous quizzes, study those. If you show up to exams early you can start early.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was by far one of the hardest, if not the hardest class I have taken at this school, but Professor Dunham does a fantastic job in giving the resources you need to succeed. He is a very caring professor that always listens to student feedback and wants learning to happen. He is a gem within the EE department.

His lectures were not that great and often doesn't explain things well. The textbook will be more efficient. Also, the exams were pretty difficult and very computationally heavy. However, he is understanding and will try to adjust the class the best he can such as offering to give more time on exams. Overall, not great but not terrible professor
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Homework really bad, one number has 4 trial and each trial will lose 25%. He thinks it's easy to not get wrong and grades are not important for future, Do you think company will hire if the gpa is low for the first job? PLEASE RUN FROM THIS TEACHER

A nice person, but an oblivious professor. Doesn't explain concepts clearly in class, so individu learning from the text is essential. Class organization with labs is also poor: Labs will often require use of new tools with no documentation or guidelines. In last quarter of class, the textbook is no longer used, so lecture notes are all you have. D

Exams were challenging with 60-70% averages on the midterms and 50% average on the final, but partial credit grading was very fair. Reading the textbook is essential and you can do well on the exams with lots of practice problems from the textbook. Explanations in class were not always clear which makes the book so important.

Read the Book. And start your homeworks as early as possible and get as much help as you can get. If you come in armed only with the stuff you know from EE215 and general EE knowledge, this won't be an easy class. The content itself is actually pretty easy, but if you depend solely on lecture and quiz section, you are not going to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He seems to be a nice guy, but also one of the most disorganized professors I have ever seen. He also seemed to be oblivious to the difficulty of his assigned lab reports and homework, which took roughly 8 hours per week EACH.

He is nice and if you asking him questions will always net a response, but he isn't very clear. Labs were individual write-ups despite being group effort, and homework will require at least 6-7 hours a week. This class feels like an 8 credit class with how long the labs / homework is and the exams are difficult. Exam avg: 50. Would not recommend.
Agreeably the worst professor I've had at UW
Excellent researcher, terrible instructor. Arguably one of the worst professors I've ever had.
Super energetic! Very passionate. Weekly "journal" entry, but it can be anything from a written reflection to a creative project. You get what you put into the class. Def recommend!
mind numbing subject coupled with a really overbearing annoying professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Long drawn out boring lectures with talking and rambling that goes in circles. Even worse is that participation is graded. Some of the material is interesting and she is very enthusiastic about it, but her shrill voice is unbearable. Only take the class if you truly love the subject.

Dubrow is knowledgeable and passionate. This is my second time in her class and I enjoyed it just as much the second time. The assignments were very reasonable (borderline easy) and she makes any readings available online in PDFs. She does ramble sometimes but it is interesting. You can skip class but you will be behind in the readings/discussions.

Definitely a lot of heavy reading in this class but it's very doable and interesting to read. The lectures are group discussions about that day's assigned reading. Prof is a good lecturer and makes the class engaging.

She is well-versed in the content she teaches and is extremely enthusiastic about it. Assignments were manageable but she's a hard grader for a class that is only an A&H credit and discussion based. No recordings and the class is longer than necessary. She has high expectations on essays with little guidance and rubric. Good readings though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class is so, so interesting. I took this class thinking it would just be an easy VLPA, but I was absolutely hooked on the literature we read. Prof Dubrow is so knowledgeable and made discussions so fun. Really enjoyed the ghazal unit!! There are some readings, but it is pretty manageable and interesting.

Prof. Dubrow can always find something to compliment about a student while also not making them feel embarrassed if they say something stupid. She has a great attitude and fosters a lot of discussion, maybe too much because it could be hard to get a word in during class (needed for participation grade), but overall an engaging and enjoyable course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is a great professor that really takes the time to delve into the readings, and actually fosters good discussion with her students.

It's a pretty easy chill class, I only took this because I needed a VLPA credit and I ended up getting a 3.9. Class can get boring when no one talks, but the books are good reads, but overall professor is very nice and easy going!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great class overall. Like the last person, i also signed up for the class the last minute but it's one choice i never look back on. The stories ranged from interesting to mundane (i.e. The Namesake which was boring imo but some people are totally gonna hate on me lol). Overall, strongly recommended for someone looking for a decent VLPA. Grading ez.
Liked it a surprising amount, for a class I accidentally signed up for. The class is mostly discussion-based; make sure you do the readings, but overall very light work for a 5 credit class.

When I first took this class, I was skeptical, because I didn't know what I was signing up for, and i needed a VLPA. But the course was very light for a 5 credit class. Readings, essays, short stories, all very easy as long as you follow what they want. Don't hesitate to ask them questions too. I loved the Mushairah at the end of class!

Very easy, yet informative class. Learned quite a bit, and had fun while doing so. There are a few novels that you are required to read, but they are interesting. Essays about the novels and lectures are frequent, but are easy. There is a midterm quiz, but is also VERY easy; I received a 4.0 without really studying. MUST TAKE :)

Easy class. We use the books and discuss them in class so just keep up with the reading (which is not hard and actually interesting). Going to class is your participation so just do it. Easy short responses due every Friday. Two easy 3-4pg double spaced essays plus take home final. She knows her material and is passionate about it! Really enjoyed.

One of the best professors at UW. 
Everything is very straight-forward.

Dr. Arola is a great and charismatic professor. This class was super interesting - I was never bored during lecture. You can tell he is passionate about the subject and cares for his students. Highly recommend!!

Dr. Arola is one of the best lecturers I have had during my entire undergraduate career here at UW. His ability to speak clearly and explain concepts in an easy-to-understand manner makes his lectures engaging. On top of that, he knows his stuff and is able to answer students' questions in great detail. I only wish I had more courses with him.
He is new in the department and actually graduated from UW.  The course was valuable and I can say he is definitely one of the better speakers in MSE.  Has high expectations.

This class I did terrible in. It wasn't like "hard" or anything, the topics were a little difficult to understand but the discussions during class helped. The reason why I got such a crap grade was honestly because of how badly I did on the papers, and for missing a few classes. She takes attendance each class.
In-class discussions were phenomenal, and she is very open to student ideas.  That being said, nothing was graded until the final week of the quarter, which was stressful.

reviews.comment: Politics of Imprisonment was an eye-opening class. Prof. Dwyer wasn't afraid to talk about tough topics, but always went out of her way to make sure everyone felt comfortable. Very supportive for outside-the-box final projects. 10/10 would highly recommend!

Dr. Dwyer's class, The Politics of Imprisonment, is highly recommended. If you want to find out what's actually happening in our society, you must attend. It's a transformative experience. Anyone interested in social justice must experience this class.

If I had to be in dylon's class again, I would drop out. Frankly, he seemed like he couldn't care less for his classes. Many professors grade by few things however they do show you steps on how to succeed but Professor Chow never really cared. He would only teach his material and would never want to solve extra doubts.

Lectures and notes are very unorganized. Goes back and forth with course material. Writing was illegible at first, but got better as the quarter went on. Homework and midterms are pretty easy. There are not a lot of study material available. Final was a lot harder than the midterm and had questions about something he mentioned in a lecture once.

He wasn't very good at explaining the material. Also, 90% of your final grade depends on 2 midterms and the final, so don't mess up! The remaining 10% is homework. He said at the beginning of the quarter that he COULD add weekly quizzes to divide up the grade, but he "didn't want to". I recommend looking for a better-rated prof if you get him.

Surprisingly I really liked this class! Prof Chow has really clear lectures with lots of example problems, and he doesn't make things too conceptual. Grading was test-heavy, but he wasn't a super harsh grader and tests were just like the practice tests. It was 90% for the 2 midterms and final, and 10% for homework, with 1 WebAssign homework weekly.

reviews.comment: Personally, I found Dylon's teaching style very ineffective. In my experience he does not motivate anything he teaches so do not expect to be able to apply many of the concepts in this class. He moved too fast and was too proof heavy for me to effectively learn. I used another professor's lectures to get through this class.

I had math 207 with Dylon. I do really think he is an effective math teacher. He explains concepts and proofs pretty well and goes extensively on answering hw questions. He uploads all lecture notes online which is pretty helpful. It sucks that %90 of grade were based on three tests, you mess one test up and you might as well drop the course.

3 exams make up 90% and homework 10%. Very poor at teaching, never understood his lecture or notes and the panapto recordings were of the worst quality. If you want to pass MATH 207, take anyone but him. I had to study every concept from online resources. He goes too fast and is barely able to clear any doubts.

There are only four assignments for the gradebook (3 being exams) so it is hard to recover your grade in this class. The exams were pretty difficult but people did pretty well so its not curved much. He teaches really fast and and often seems confused on the material himself and when students ask questions. If you're a poor tester you may struggle
